title: 케네스 가드번: 온화함으로 잘 들으십시오 (야고보 1:19-21)

ko.text: 오늘의 성구는 듣는 것과 관련이 있습니다.
온화함이 어떻게 더 잘 듣는 데 도움이 됩니까?
온화함은 듣는 것과 어떤 관련이 있을까요?
그 점을 야고보의 말을 통해 알 수 있는데요.
오늘의 성구가 나오는 야고보 1장을 펴서 19절에서 21절을 읽어 보겠습니다.
모든 사람은 듣기는 빨리 하고, 말하기는 더디 하고, 분노하기도 더디 해야 합니다.
사람의 분노는 하느님의 의를 이루지 못하기 때문입니다.
그러므로 불결한 것과 악의 흔적을 모두 없애 버리고,
하느님께서 여러분 안에 말씀을 심어 주실 때 온화하게 받아들이십시오.
그 말씀은 여러분을 구원할 수 있습니다.”
여기서 야고보는 하느님의 말씀을 듣는 것에 대해 말하고 있습니다.
분노할 것이 아니라 우리는 21절에 나오는 온화를 나타내야 합니다.
온화가 있으면 하느님의 말씀을 빨리 듣고 잘 받아들이는 데 도움이 되죠.
성경에서는 온화한 사람을 가르침을 잘 받아들이는 사람,
하느님의 뜻에 기꺼이 복종하는 사람으로 묘사합니다.
따라서 하느님의 말씀을 잘 들으려면 온화가 꼭 필요합니다.
오늘날 왜 많은 사람들이 성경의 가르침을 들으려 하지 않는지 알 수 있습니다.
“성품이 온화하지 못한 것은 불안하거나 욕구 불만이 있거나
믿음과 희망이 없기 때문이며, 심지어 절망했기 때문일 수도 있다.”
오늘날 세상 상태에 잘 들어맞는 말이 아닙니까?
사탄은 사람들이 스트레스를 받게 만들어서 온화함을 잃게 해 왔습니다.
사람들은 해를 입거나 이용당할까 봐 두려워합니다.
그래서 “합의하려 하지 않고” 남을 신뢰하지 않죠.
또 사탄은 사람들이 좌절감을 느끼게 했습니다.
살면서 불공정한 일을 많이 겪다 보니
반감과 욕구 불만으로 가득 차서 마음의 문을 닫게 됩니다.
이 세상의 많은 조직과 단체는 사람들이 믿음과 희망을 잃게 만들었습니다.
그래서 서로를 믿지 못하고 회의적이 되는 것이죠.
이런 모든 상황 때문에 사람들은 절망과 괴로움과 불안감을 느끼게 됩니다.
온화해지면 하느님의 말씀을 듣기를 빨리 할 것임을 알기 때문입니다.
하지만 여호와의 도움을 받으면 누구나 온화를 길러 나갈 수 있습니다.
온화해야 할 이유를 알려 주시고 그렇게 할 능력도 주십니다.
또 말씀을 통해 우리가 안정감과 평온을 느끼고
강한 믿음과 희망을 가질 이유를 알려 주십니다.
우리는 그분을 신뢰하고 문제를 그분의 손에 맡기게 되죠.
따라서 하느님의 말씀을 잘 들으려면 온화가 꼭 필요합니다.
온화는 마음의 흙을 부드럽게 해서 하느님의 말씀이 심길 수 있게 해 주죠.
또 온화는 잘 듣는 사람이 되는 데도 도움이 됩니다.
예수께서 보이신 훌륭한 본을 보면 그 점을 알 수 있습니다.
예수께선 온화하셨기 때문에 다가가기 쉬운 분이셨습니다.
그래서 사람들의 말을 들으실 기회가 많았죠.
예수께서 얼마나 따뜻하게 말씀하시는지 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
“고생하며 무거운 짐을 진 여러분, 모두 내게로 오십시오.
나는 성품이 온화하고 마음이 겸손하니 내 멍에를 메고 내게서 배우십시오.
그러면 여러분은 새 힘을 얻을 것입니다.”
그래서 사람들은 그분께 쉽게 다가가 이야기할 수 있었죠.
예수께서 오늘은 기분이 어떠실지 걱정하지 않았습니다.
예수께서 자신들의 말을 정말 듣고 싶어 하신다는 걸 느꼈죠.
마르다는 거리낌 없이 예수에게 다가가 자신의 감정을 쏟아내면서
마리아와 마르다는 예수께 자신들의 감정을 거리낌 없이 이야기했습니다.
그들이 예수께 처음으로 한 말이 뭐였죠?
“주께서 여기 계셨더라면 제 오라비가 죽지 않았을 것입니다.”
또 야고보와 요한이 예수께 특별한 은혜를 베풀어 달라고 한 때는 언제였습니까?
예수께서 자신이 고통을 겪고 죽을 것이라고 말씀하신 지 얼마 안 된 때였습니다.
그리고 베드로는 예수를 따로 불러내어 조언을 할 정도로
예수께 편하게 얘기할 수 있었다는 겁니다.
부탁을 하고 감정을 표현하고 걱정거리를 얘기할 수 있었죠.
사람들이 별것 아닌 말을 하거나 무례하게 말하거나 어리석은 말을 하거나
심지어 틀린 말을 해도 그분은 과민 반응 하지 않으셨습니다.
강한 책망이나 조언을 해야 할 때도 그렇게 하셨습니다.
또 놀라운 점은 많은 경우 예수께서 사람들이 무슨 말을 할지 아셨을 거라는 점입니다.
그런데도 그들의 말을 끊지 않고 끝까지 들어 주셨죠.
그들을 존중하시고 생각을 다 말하게 하셨습니다.
우리가 온화하다면 다가가기 쉬운 사람이 될 것입니다.
그러면 다른 사람들의 말을 들을 기회가 많아질 것입니다.
그리고 예수와는 달리 우리는 사람들의 말을 들을 필요가 있습니다.
그래야 어떻게 도울지 알 수 있죠.
그리고 그래야 계속 다가가기 쉬운 사람이 되어서
필요한 조언과 제안을 받을 수 있습니다.
예수께서 온화와 관련해서 본을 보이신 두 번째 부면은
예수께서 과민 반응 하지 않으셨던 건 여호와께 자신을 맡기셨기 때문입니다.
자신이 겪는 모든 불공정을 바로잡아 주실 것임을 아셨죠.
또 사람들이 무슨 말을 하든 자신에 대한 여호와의 생각은
초점을 잃지 않고 문제를 여호와의 손에 맡기셨기 때문에
예수의 본을 묵상해 보면 유익을 얻을 수 있습니다.
우리에 대해 악의적인 이야기를 퍼뜨릴 때 도움이 될 수 있죠.
일상생활에서 대화를 나눌 때에도 도움이 될 수 있습니다.
우리의 동기를 의심하는 듯한 말을 할 수 있습니다.
또는 어떤 사람이 우리가 가진 권위에 도전하는 방식으로 말하거나
우리를 깎아내리는 농담을 할 수도 있죠.
그런 말들을 들으면 낙담하거나 마음의 안정을 잃게 될 수 있습니다.
하지만 여호와에 대한 신뢰심에 근거한 온화함이 있다면
초점을 잃지 않고 과민 반응 하지 않겠죠.
네, 잘 들으려면 온화가 꼭 필요합니다.
온화는 하느님의 말씀을 듣기를 빨리 해서
우리 마음에 심는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
또한 다가가기 쉬운 사람이 되고 과민 반응 하지 않음으로
더 잘 듣는 사람이 되는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.

en.text: So our text is about being quick to listen.
So we’d like to develop the theme
“Listen With Mildness.”
We’ll talk about two points:
Why is mildness essential for listening?
And how can mildness help us
to be a better listener?
Let’s take that first point.
How is mildness connected with listening?
Let’s turn in our Bibles to our text at James chapter 1,
and we’ll read verses 19 through 21
because James makes the connection for us.
James 1:19 says:
“Know this, my beloved brothers: Everyone must be quick to listen,
“slow to speak, slow to anger,
“for man’s anger does not bring about God’s righteousness.
“Therefore, put away all filthiness and every trace of badness,
“and accept with mildness the implanting of the word
that is able to save you.”
So here James is talking about listening to God’s Word,
and he says we need to “be quick to listen.”
That means we have to control our reaction.
We have to be “slow to speak”
because when we start to speak, we stop listening.
And we also have to control our emotions because if we get angry,
that’s not going to work out “God’s righteousness.”
We’ll likely make matters worse.
Instead, the key is what he mentioned in verse 21.
We need to have mildness.
That’s going to help us accept God’s Word
—to listen to it quickly and accept it.
And why is that the case?
Well, mildness involves self-control.
A person who is mild-tempered is humble and they’re patient.
They have a calm and peaceful disposition.
The Scriptures describe a mild-tempered person as teachable
—somebody who is willing and ready to submit to God’s will.
So mildness is essential if we’re to listen to God’s Word.
And doesn’t that explain why so many people today
are not quick to listen to what the Bible says?
The Insight  volume makes this statement.
It says: “Lack of mildness of temper
“is the result of insecurity, frustration,
lack of faith and hope, and even desperation.”
And doesn’t that describe the world that we live in today?
Satan has got people so emotionally wound up that they’re not mild-tempered.
He’s got them feeling insecure.
They feel threatened and afraid of being taken advantage of.
And for that reason, they’re “not open to any agreement.”
They don’t trust other people.
Satan has got people feeling frustrated.
Life in this system is unfair and unjust,
and that hardens people, making them resentful and bitter.
And the institutions in this system of things
have robbed people of their faith and their hope.
And it’s no wonder that people are skeptical and suspicious.
And all of that has left people
feeling despair, distressed, and anxious.
And Satan likes it that way.
He wants people not to be mild-tempered
because he knows if they’re not mild-tempered,
they won’t be quick to listen to God’s Word.
Yet with Jehovah’s help,
anyone can gradually develop a mild temper.
With Jehovah’s Word and his spirit,
he gives us the reason
and the ability to do so.
He gives us the ability to control our reaction.
And through his Word, he gives us the reasons to feel secure,
to feel calm, to have strong faith and hope.
And as a result, we can trust him.
We don’t have to take matters into our own hands.
So mildness is essential to listening to God’s Word.
It’s the quality that loosens the soil of our heart
that allows God’s Word to be implanted there.
But mildness can also help us become a better listener,
and to see that, we have only to look at the wonderful example of Jesus.
Jesus was mild-tempered and, as a result, he was approachable.
He created opportunities for him to listen to other people.
Turn, if you will, in your Bible to Matthew chapter 11.
We’ll read verses 28 and 29.
And notice this warm appeal by Jesus
at Matthew 11:28, 29.
He says: “Come to me, all you who are toiling and loaded down,
“and I will refresh you.
“Take my yoke upon you and learn from me,
“for I am mild-tempered and lowly in heart,
and you will find refreshment for yourselves.”
Yes, Jesus was mild-tempered, and that made him approachable.
People found it easy to talk to Jesus.
They never wondered what kind of mood Jesus was going to be in that day.
Jesus wasn’t touchy or thin-skinned or moody.
People didn’t fear his reaction.
They sensed that Jesus really wanted to listen to them.
So consider some examples of that.
Martha felt free to approach Jesus
and to vent her frustration and complain about her sister, Mary.
Both Mary and Martha felt safe
venting their emotions to Jesus when Lazarus died.
And remember the first words they said to him?
It could have sounded insensitive.
They said: “If you had [only] been here, my brother would not have died.”
Recall the occasion when James and John asked Jesus for special favors.
Now, they did that just shortly after
Jesus said that he would suffer and die.
And although Peter was misguided,
he felt comfortable pulling Jesus aside to offer him some counsel.
What’s the point?
People felt free talking to Jesus
—to ask for things, to express their emotions,
to voice their concerns.
And even though what they said
may have seemed petty, insensitive,
misguided, or even wrong,
Jesus never overreacted.
He always dignified them, dealt with them in a mild way,
even when he had to give them strong reproof or counsel.
And what’s amazing is that Jesus likely often knew
what people were going to say.
And yet he never finished their sentences.
He never interrupted them.
He dignified them.
He let them express themselves.
And what a good lesson for us!
If we’re mild-tempered, that will help us to become approachable,
creating opportunities for us to be quick to listen to other people.
And unlike Jesus, we need to listen to what other people say.
That’s the only way that we’ll know how we can help them.
And it’s the only way that we’ll remain approachable
so that we may receive the counsel and suggestions that we may need.
Now, a second way that Jesus set an example in mildness
is he didn’t overreact to what he heard.
Why was that?
Well, turn in your Bibles, please,
to 1 Peter 2:23,
and note this statement regarding Jesus.
First Peter 2:23 says:
“When he was being insulted, he did not insult in return.
“When he was suffering, he did not threaten,
but he entrusted himself to the One who judges righteously.”
Yes, Jesus kept himself under control
because he entrusted himself to Jehovah.
He knew that Jehovah would deal with all the injustices that he faced.
Jesus knew that there was nothing that anybody could say to him or about him
that would change how Jehovah felt about him,
and that made Jesus feel secure.
He didn’t lose focus.
He didn’t take matters into his own hands.
He didn’t overreact.
Now, meditating on Jesus’ example can help us.
It can help us when we face insulting comments from opposers
or malicious statements by opposers.
But it can also help us deal with day-to-day conversations.
You know, sometimes somebody may say something
that shows that they’ve misunderstood us
or maybe misjudged us.
Or maybe they phrase something in a way
that sounds like they’re challenging our authority,
or maybe they make a joke at our expense.
All of those things can make us feel insecure and frustrated.
But if we have mildness rooted in a relationship with Jehovah,
we’ll stay calm and secure.
We won’t lose our focus.
We won’t overreact.
Yes, mildness is essential for listening.
It will help us to be quick to listen to God’s Word
so that it can be implanted in our hearts.
And it will help us to be better listeners
by helping us to become approachable
and not overreacting to what we hear.

cn.text: 今天的经文鼓励我们要乐于聆听
所以，我们的主题就是
“怀着温和的态度聆听”
我们会谈两点
为什么温和的态度对于聆听很重要？
这种态度怎样帮助我们更乐于聆听？
首先来谈第一点
“温和”和“聆听”有什么关系？
我们先看看门徒雅各是怎么说的
请大家打开雅各书1:19-21
“亲爱的弟兄们
你们要知道
人人都要乐于聆听
不急于说话，不急于发怒
因为人的愤怒并不能伸张上帝的正义
所以，你们要除掉一切污秽和每一丝恶念
你们要用温和的态度接受上帝的话语
让它深深种植在你们心里
上帝的话语能拯救你们的生命”
雅各在这里谈到该怎样聆听上帝的话语
他说，我们要“乐于聆听”
这意味着我们要控制自己的反应
我们不要急于说话
因为我们一开始说话就不再聆听了
我们也要控制自己的情绪
因为就算人生气
也“不能伸张上帝的正义”
反而会让事情变得更糟
相反，我们要像21节所说的那样
要有“温和的态度”
这能帮助我们接受上帝的话语
就是乐于聆听，乐于接受
为什么可以这样说呢？
温和牵涉到自制
温和的人通常都很谦卑，很有耐心
一般来说，他们也都很冷静，很安静
经文说，温和的人很愿意接受教导
这样的人会很喜欢
也很乐于接受上帝的话语
因此可以说
温和对于聆听上帝话语非常重要
这也能帮我们明白
为什么今天有很多人
都不愿意接受上帝的话语
关于这一点，《洞悉圣经》说
“人之所以不够温和
原因在于失意、心里不踏实
信心不足、欠缺希望
甚至完全绝望”
这句话说得非常对
撒但就是让今天世上的很多人
都焦虑不安、很有压力
所以很多人没有温和的态度
撒但让人没有安全感
他们很担心被别人利用
因此他们“不愿意达成协议”
他们也互相不信任
撒但让人生活在绝望当中
这个世上也有很多不公不正的事
所以很多人也变得心怀怨恨
尖酸刻薄
撒但世界的各种制度也让人没有信心
看不到希望
因此，人很容易变得对什么都不信任
而这一切又让人变得很绝望
很焦虑，很抑郁
撒但就是希望人变成这样
他就是希望人变得不温和
因为他知道，人变得不温和
就不会愿意聆听上帝的话语
但靠着耶和华
任何人都能逐渐培养温和的特质
耶和华用他的话语和神圣力量
告诉我们为什么
以及怎么培养温和的特质
他也让我们有能力去控制自己的反应
通过他的话语，他也让我们有安全感
能保持冷静并充满信心和希望
结果，我们就更加信赖他
也不会单靠自己去解决所有问题
可见，要接受上帝的话语
就必须保持温和
它能让我们的内心保持柔软
让上帝的话语能够种植在我们心里
我们保持温和，也会更乐于聆听别人
我们可以看一下
耶稣基督为我们立下的完美榜样
耶稣非常温和，因此他平易近人
他常常给人机会，让人充分表达自己的想法
请大家打开马太福音11章
我们读一下28和29节
耶稣在这里向我们发出一个温暖的邀请
他说
“你们所有辛苦劳碌、背负重担的人啊
到我这里来吧
我会使你们感到舒畅
你们要担起我的担子，向我学习
因为我性情温和，心里谦卑
这样，你们就会感到舒畅”
没错，耶稣性情温和，所以他平易近人
他们跟耶稣说话都感到很轻松
他们都不需要担心耶稣当天情绪怎样
因为耶稣不会情绪多变、喜怒无常
大家都不用害怕他的反应
因为他们知道耶稣很乐意聆听他们说话
我们可以看看几个例子
马大因为妹妹马利亚的事向耶稣抱怨
她丝毫没有压力
拉撒路死后
马利亚和马大在耶稣面前
可以毫不掩饰自己的情绪
你记得她们第一句话怎么说吗？
听起来像在责备耶稣
“要是你当时在这里
我的兄弟就不会死了”
另外
雅各和约翰也曾求耶稣赐给他们特别的地位
实际上，在此之前不久
耶稣刚刚说他会被人折磨至死
使徒彼得也敢把耶稣拉到一边
给耶稣劝告
其实，他的劝告完全不对
要点是什么呢？
人们跟耶稣交谈，感到轻松自在
他们可以说出自己的感受
表达自己的不安
虽然他们说的事很小，很无理
很愚蠢，甚至完全不对
但耶稣从来没有过激的反应
有时候，耶稣也需要提出严厉的劝告
但他总是尊重他们
温和地对待他们
值得留意的一点就是
实际上，很多时候耶稣都知道别人要说什么
但他从来没有打断别人的话
他总是尊重他们
让他们说出自己想说的话
多么好的榜样
如果我们也性情温和
别人就会愿意亲近我们
这也让我们有更多机会聆听别人说话
我们不能像耶稣那样知道别人的想法
我们必须聆听
才会知道怎样帮助他们
另一方面
别人看到我们需要纠正和劝告的时候
才愿意跟我们说
耶稣在温和方面立下的另一个榜样就是
他从来不会反应过激
为什么这样呢？
请大家打开彼得前书2:23
我们来看看
关于耶稣
彼得是怎么写的
彼得前书2:23说
“他被骂却不还口
受苦也不恐吓人
反而把自己交托给施行正义审判的主”
耶稣总是能够保持自制
因为他把自己交托给耶和华
他知道他受到的所有不公的对待
耶和华都会处理
他也知道，不管别人怎么骂他
怎么污蔑他
都不能改变耶和华对他的看法
因此，耶稣没有丝毫的不安
也没有忘记什么最重要
他没有用自己的方式解决问题
也没有反应过激
沉思耶稣的榜样对我们帮助很大
我们不仅知道该怎样面对
反对者的辱骂和他们恶意的攻击
也会知道该怎样面对日常遇到的问题
有时候，别人因为不了解我们
或者误解我们
说了一些伤害我们的话
有时候，别人说的话听起来粗鲁无礼
有时候，他们拿我们开玩笑
这样的时候，人通常都会感到不安和愤怒
但如果我们因为和耶和华
享有亲密的关系而保持温和
我们就会平静面对
我们不会忘记什么最重要
也不会反应过激
没错，温和的特质对于聆听非常重要
它能帮助我们乐于聆听和接受上帝的话语
让它深植心中
也能让我们更乐于聆听别人说话
让我们变得平易近人
并在任何情况都保持冷静

title: 도널드 고든: “그대의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울이십시오” (디모데 전서 4:16)

ko.text: 연구생의 귀로 즉 연구생의 입장에서 말이죠.
때로는 연사의 말이 연구생에게 당혹스러울 수도 있고
딱 맞는 말이라고 느껴질 수도 있습니다.
성서 연구나 재방문을 할 때는 어떻습니까?
우리의 말이 그에게 어떻게 들릴지 생각하면서
우리는 어떤 실수를 하게 될 수 있습니까?
경험 많은 두 명의 순회 감독자가
최근에 형제 자매들의 성서 연구에 다녀온 후에
개선이 필요한 점 몇 가지를 이야기해 주었습니다.
“저는 전도인들이 다른 사람들을 동반하지 않고 혼자 가거나
항상 같은 사람하고만 가는 것을 자주 봅니다.”
이해했다고 생각하고는 넘어가는 경우도 종종 있습니다.”
또한 “이유를 묻는 질문을 더 많이 하면 좋겠습니다.”
「행누」 책의 각 과를 소개하는 항을 살펴보는 데
자신에게도 그처럼 부족한 점이 있다는 것을
봉사하는 면에서 좋은 본이 되는 부부가 있죠.
훌륭한 본을 통해 우리는 많은 걸 배웠습니다.
그는 언변이 좋고 성경에 정통한 사람이었다.
브리스길라와 아굴라가 그의 말을 듣고 그를 데려다가
하느님의 길을 더욱 정확하게 설명해 주었다.”
필요한 도움을 베풀어 개선할 수 있게 해 주는 것이
앞서 순회 감독자가 한 말을 기억하시나요?
“전도인들이 다른 사람을 동반하지 않고 혼자 가거나
항상 같은 사람하고만 가는 것을 자주 본다”고 했죠.
또 이 기록에서 브리스길라가 언급되는 것도
브리스길라가 정말 영적인 여자였다는 걸 느낄 수 있죠.
영적이고 지식이 많고 생각이 깊은 자매들이 많이 있습니다.
많은 자매들이 성서 연구나 재방문을 할 때
오늘의 성구를 어떻게 적용하고 있는지 질문했죠.
정말 멋진 대답들을 들을 수 있었습니다.
먼저 모두가 연구생을 생각하면서 준비하는 게
또 평일 집회 때 배운 것을 잘 적용하고 있었죠.
저는 상대방의 얼굴 표정과 눈을 봐요.
자매는 가르칠 내용을 이미 잘 알고 있기 때문에
무엇을 어떻게 가르쳐야 할지 알 수 있죠.”
연구생에게 어떻게 들릴지 생각해 보는 거죠.
가장 효과적으로 가르치는 방법을 알게 됩니다.
함께 간 사람의 의견을 듣는 게 도움이 돼요.
내가 유의하지 못한 점을 깨닫게 되거든요.
무엇을 피해야 할지 물어보면 큰 도움이 돼요.”
자신이 어떻게 가르치는지 주의를 기울여 잘 듣고
어떻게 발전할 수 있을지 알려 달라고 한 것입니다.
또 다른 자매도 자신이 잘 가르치는 사람이 되기 위해
어색한 침묵이 흐르더라도 기다리는 법을 배웠죠.
그래야 연구생이 그냥 대답만 하는 게 아니라
시간을 주는 건 정말 훌륭한 기술이 아닙니까?
연구 시간이 그를 위한 시간임을 잊지 않으려고 합니다.
우리 자매들이 하느님의 말씀을 최선을 다해
자신의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울이기 위해
제가 아는 세 명의 자매들이 한 말입니다.

en.text: “Pay constant attention
to . . . your teaching.”
In our personal ministry
when making return visits
or conducting a Bible study,
it’s very important for us to listen.
Of course, we’re listening to our student.
But also, are we listening to our teaching?
To illustrate, suppose we’re at the Kingdom Hall,
and we have alongside us, sitting next to us, our Bible student
who is there for his or her first meeting.
Now, as we listen to the public talk,
we’re listening to every point, every sentence,
and maybe every word through the ears of our student.
Sometimes, maybe, it makes us cringe a little bit.
Sometimes we think,
‘Oh, well done —good point—
perfect for my student.’
Well, we can do this because we know our student
—what they understand, what they don’t understand,
their sensitivities on certain subjects, etcetera.
So now with that in mind,
we listen to the speaker through the ears of our student.
When we’re teaching on a Bible study or a return visit,
can we listen to ourselves through the ears of our student?
Are we listening, or paying attention, to our teaching
as our student is hearing our teaching?
What might be some of the challenges we would listen for?
Well, two experienced circuit overseers
who thoroughly enjoy going on Bible studies with our brothers and sisters
mentioned a few challenges that they’ve noted recently.
Here’s one:
“A weakness I see often is
“that publishers rarely invite others to join them
or that they always bring along the same person,”
or another, “Oftentimes, teachers forget
“that the student has gaps in understanding
and assume they know or understand what is taught.”
One mentioned,
“More ‘why’ questions can help students to reason.”
And finally,
“Many friends still spend too much time talking
“and/or dissecting the introductory paragraphs
in the Enjoy Life Forever!  book.”
Well, perhaps we have listened to ourselves,
and we find ourselves challenged
with a few of those same points or others.
What can help us?
Well, for training in the ministry,
we have often turned to the excellent example
of Aquila and Priscilla
as they helped Apollos.
Let’s turn in our Bibles to look at that lesson again.
It’s found in Acts chapter 18,
starting in verse 24.
Acts 18:24 says:
“Now a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria,
“arrived in Ephesus;
“he was an eloquent man who was well-versed in the Scriptures.
“This man had been instructed in the way of Jehovah,
“and aglow with the spirit,
“he was speaking and teaching accurately the things about Jesus,
“but he was acquainted only with the baptism of John.
“He began to speak boldly in the synagogue,
“and when Priscilla and Aquila heard him,
“they took him into their company
and explained the way of God more accurately to him.”
So now, in this example,
we have the case where it is important
for someone else to hear our teaching
and then to render the assistance we need
—make improvements.
Well, do you recall what the circuit overseer observed?
He said: “One weakness I see often
“is that publishers rarely invite others to join them
or that they always bring along the same person.”
You can see how that could be a weakness.
But not in this case.
Aquila and Priscilla were there in the synagogue.
They heard him, and they lovingly pulled him aside
and gave him the help that he needed.
And in this lesson, it is also no surprise
that Priscilla is also mentioned and included in a very respectful way,
working along with her husband and assisting Apollos.
We sense that Priscilla was truly a spiritual woman.
Well, we know it’s no different today.
In our congregations and in our Bethel family,
we have so many spiritually-minded,
knowledgeable, deep-thinking sisters.
It’s truly a blessing.
And when it comes to teaching the Bible on return visits or Bible studies,
well, so many of our sisters are applying themselves
and doing an excellent job.
So I asked a few of our sisters here
how they are applying today’s text
to “pay constant attention to . . . [their] teaching.”
I’m glad I asked because I got wonderful comments.
Here are a few samples.
First, they all mentioned the importance of preparation
—preparation with the student in mind.
And it’s obvious they apply what they are learning at the midweek meeting.
But more specifically, there’s one sister;
she commented about the value of preparation.
She said: “I think it starts with preparing well
“for the return visit or study,
“maybe even overpreparing.
“Then when on the call or study, I’m not focusing on the material
“or distracted by looking for what’s coming up next.
“I can really focus on the person.
“I observe them—their face, their eyes.
“Do they seem confused?
“Are they uncomfortable?
Are their eyes opening up, as if saying, ‘Wow’?”
So our sister, having the material so well in mind,
is now able to focus on the student
and listen to her teaching, as it were,
observing her student.
Another sister with a similar thought stated:
“I have found that preparing myself in advance
“with the householder in mind and wondering,
“‘What would I like to hear if I was in her situation
“with her background?’
helps me know how and what to teach.”
So here she is taking the time during preparation
to listen to the material, as it were,
as it’s going to be heard through her student.
And then she knows the most effective way to teach it.
And how does having someone else with us (along with us) help?
Here’s an observation from one of our sisters:
“I found that having someone with me
“who after the study can critique the conversation
“helps me to understand clues I might have missed.
“Asking my partner what she thinks could be said next time,
“how to say it, and what should be avoided
is a tremendous help to me.”
So we bring along our Aquila and Priscilla
—maybe we bring a variety of Aquilas and Priscillas,
like our circuit overseer recommends.
And to make the point again, the critique was, not on the Bible student,
but on our sister.
It’s for us: “How can I improve?
“You be my ears. Listen for me.
Pay attention to my teaching. Help me improve”
—a beautiful example.
And finally, one of our sisters highlighted
what she tries to implement in an effective teacher
(as an effective teacher).
First of all, not surprisingly, she mentioned all the same things
regarding the value of preparation.
But then she added: “I find it very important
“to allow the student time to express himself.
“I’ve learned not to mind the awkward silence
“that allows him to truly think
“and not to feel pressured just to give an answer
but to give a heartfelt answer.”
Isn’t that beautiful —a beautiful skill—
to be able to give the student time to give a heartfelt answer?
And then she commented:
“I try to take an active interest and remember that this is their time
“and their study.
“Keeping that in mind helps to motivate me
to do my best as a teacher to help them.”
It’s their time; it’s their study
—indeed, very motivating.
Well, these comments help me to appreciate
that our sisters are doing their very best
to teach God’s Word.
We are very proud of all of you
who are trying and doing your best
to pay constant attention to your teaching.
Now, these comments that I mentioned
are just from three sisters I happen to be acquainted with.
But think: Worldwide, there are millions of our sisters
who are skillfully preaching and teaching
the good news of the Kingdom.
This is certainly very encouraging to all of us
paying constant attention to our teaching.

cn.text: “要时刻留意……自己的教导”
我们传道的时候
比如做续访或主持圣经课程
很重要的一点，就是要留心聆听
要留心听学生说话
另外，也要留意自己的教导
为什么呢？
比如说
我们的圣经学生
第一次跟着我们来参加聚会
聚会时他坐在我们的旁边
我们在听公众演讲
我们听到每一个字、每一句话、每个要点
都会想学生会有什么反应
有时，我们觉得讲者的话会让学生尴尬
有时候，我们又想
“很好的要点，很适合我的学生”
因为我们很了解自己的学生
他们明白什么、不明白什么
他们对什么样的话题非常敏感
等等等等
我们仿佛在通过学生的耳朵听公众演讲
我们教导的时候
比如做续访或主持圣经课程的时候
也可以通过学生的耳朵听自己的教导吗？
我们可以换位思考
想想学生对我们的教导有什么感受吗？
我们这样做的话
就会发现自己有哪些毛病呢？
有两位经验丰富的分区监督
他们都很喜欢参加弟兄姐妹的圣经学习
他们都留意到一些需要改善的地方
一个说
“我留意到的一个问题是
有些传道员从来不邀请别人参加他的学习
或者总是带同一个人参加他的圣经学习”
另一个说
“很多时候，传道员都忘记了
其实学生并不是什么都明白
有些地方需要进一步的解释”
一个说
“要多问为什么
这可以帮助学生推理”
另一个说
“很多传道员还是会花太多的时间
跟学生讨论《美好生命》课文的前几段”
如果我们留意自己的教导
可能会发现自己也有刚才谈到的这些问题
或者其他的问题
那该怎么办呢？
我们可以向亚居拉和百姬拉学习
他们在帮助亚波罗的时候做得非常好
为我们树立了很好的榜样
我们来读一下这段记载吧
在使徒行传的18章
我们会从第24节读起
使徒行传18:24
“有一个生在亚历山大的犹太人
名叫亚波罗，到了以弗所
他能言善辩，非常熟悉圣经
受过教导认识耶和华的道路
他充满神圣力量，满腔热诚
正确地讲解和教导关于耶稣的事
可是他只熟悉约翰的浸礼
他在会堂里勇敢地向人传道
百姬拉和亚居拉听过他的话
就私下找他
更准确地向他讲解上帝的道路”
这个例子可以说明
让别人听到我们怎样实行教导
为什么非常重要
他们可以留意到我们的问题
并帮助我们不断进步
你还记得刚才提到的分区监督怎么说吗？
他说
“有些传道员
从来不邀请别人参加他的圣经学习
或者总邀请同一个人参加”
这样做真的不太好
刚才的经文谈到
亚居拉和百姬拉在会堂里听到亚波罗
怎样向人传道
就私下找他，帮助他
你留意到吗？
经文也提到百姬拉
她怀着尊重的态度
跟丈夫亚居拉一起
帮助亚波罗
可以看出，她是一个热心崇拜上帝的女子
今天，情况也一样
不管在会众里还是在伯特利
都有很多成熟的姐妹
她们知识丰富，善于思考
这真的是个福分
在续访别人、主持圣经课程等方面
许多姐妹都努力提高自己的教导技巧
她们都做得非常好
我问了几个姐妹
她们怎样像经文说的那样
“时刻留意……自己的教导”
我很高兴自己问了这样的问题
因为她们都跟我分享了很好的经验
首先，她们都提到
按照学生的需要备课非常重要
看来她们都在运用周中聚会的建议
其中一个姐妹特别谈到
提前准备有哪些益处
她说
“在续访或主持圣经课程前
我都会好好准备
而且准备得越充分越好
这样，到时候我就不用担心要讨论什么内容
或者接下来要讨论什么资料
而是可以专注于对方
我可以观察她们
她们的表情、她们的眼神
她们有点不明白吗？
感觉不舒服吗？
还是她们的眼睛会发亮
仿佛在说：哇哦！”
这位姐妹提前把资料都记在心里
到时她就可以把注意力都放在对方身上
并留意自己的教导
会对学生产生什么样的影响
另一个姐妹有类似的看法
她说
“我准备的时候会想着对方
我会问自己
如果我处于她的情况
有她那样的背景
会对什么感兴趣呢？
这让我知道该说什么
以及怎么说”
所以，这位姐妹在做准备的时候
仿佛就是通过学生的角度
来考虑资料的内容
所以她能够有效地教导别人
那传道同伴可以给我们什么帮助呢？
一个姐妹对此深有体会
她说
“我觉得有传道同伴真的很好
学习之后
她可以告诉我
一些我自己就没有留意到的细节
我也会问同伴
下一次我该说什么
怎么说
什么不要说
这真的对我帮助很大”
有些弟兄姐妹仿佛是我们的亚居拉和百姬拉
要邀请他们参加我们的学习
就像分区监督建议的那样
请记得
这些弟兄姐妹不仅会帮助圣经学生
更重要的是会帮助到我们
可以问问他们
“我可以怎样改善？
我在教导方面有哪些地方需要调整？
请帮助我进步”
这是很好的做法
还有一位姐妹特别谈到
想要成为好老师必须要留意的一件事
她也跟别的姐妹一样
谈到了提前准备有多么重要
另外，她补充说
“要给圣经学生充分的时间思考
如果她思考的时间比较长
也不要担心冷场
不要给她压力匆忙回答
因为我们想听到的不只是一个答案
我们想听到的是她真实的想法”
这真的是一个很好的技巧，对吗？
就是要给学生充分的时间
说出自己真实的想法
这位姐妹还说
“我也努力地关心学生
我提醒自己
这是她们的时间，是她们的学习
记得这一点让我更有动力做个好老师
真诚地帮助学生”
这是她们的时间，是她们的学习
没错，很好的想法！
姐妹们分享的这些经历让我看出
她们都在竭尽全力地
教导别人上帝的话语
我们为你们感到骄傲
因为你们都尽力而为
“时刻留意……自己的教导”
今天跟大家分享的
只是我认识的三个姐妹的经验
请想一想
全球各地有数以百万计的姐妹
都在热心地宣扬上帝王国的好消息
不断提升教导技巧
她们的好榜样
也激励我们所有人
都要“时刻留意……自己的教导”

titles.ko: 도널드 고든: “그대의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울이십시오” (디모데 전서 4:16)

title: JW 방송—2024년 2월

ko.text: 이번 달 프로그램에서는 성경이 어떻게 우리가 더 나은 삶을 살게 도와주고
영구적인 해를 입지 않도록 보호해 주고
다른 사람들과 잘 지내게 해 주는지 알아볼 것입니다.
또한 잘못을 저질렀다 해도 여호와께 다시 돌아갈 수 있다는 확신을 갖는 데
우리는 침례자 요한의 삶을 통해 어떻게 두려움에 대처할 수 있는지,
다른 사람들이 축복을 받을 때 어떻게 기뻐할 수 있는지,
문제를 겪을 때도 어떻게 긍정적인 견해를 유지할 수 있는지 배울 것입니다.
또한 고든 매케이 형제의 이야기를 들으면서
여호와께서는 우리가 ‘그분께 가까이 가기를’ 바라신다는 점을 생각해 볼 것입니다.
그리고 불완전하지만 충실한 그분의 가족으로부터 멀어진 사람들에게
다시 돌아오라는 따뜻한 초대를 담고 있습니다.
우리가 영적인 집에 있다는 것이 얼마나 큰 축복인지 느끼게 될 것입니다.
어렸을 때 저는 어머니가 해 주시는 고구마 파이를 정말 좋아했습니다.
항상 같은 맛이어서 언제 먹어도 맛이 있었습니다.
그러면 어머니는 “항상 똑같은 거 넣는데?” 하고 대답하곤 하셨죠.
네. 뭐가 들어가는지 알려 주진 않으셨지만 어머니만의 요리 방법이 분명히 있었던 겁니다.
성경은 요리책과 비슷하다고 할 수 있습니다.
우리가 영적으로 성공적인 삶을 사는 데 도움이 되는 조리법들이 가득 들어 있죠.
그 조리법들이 어떤 면에서 유익한지 바울이 한 말을 들어 볼까요?
가르치고 책망하고 바로잡고 의로 징계하는 데 유익합니다.
그리하여 하느님의 사람이 온전히 유능하게 되고
모든 선한 일을 할 준비를 완전히 갖추게 해 줍니다.”
하느님의 영감받은 말씀에 담긴 조리법의 한 가지 형태는 성경에 나오는 실제 사례입니다.
그런 예들을 연구해 보면 우리가 본받을 수 있는 특성과 태도들을 알게 되죠.
또 성경에는 여러 특성들이 나열된 조리법도 나옵니다.
예를 들어 갈라디아서 5장에는 하느님의 영의 열매를 이루는 여러 특성들이 언급되죠.
빌립보서 4:8, 9에는 우리가 생각해야 할 좋은 것들이 나옵니다.
그리고 성경에는 우리가 올바른 결정을 내리는 데 도움이 되는 원칙들도 많이 들어 있습니다.
우리는 그러한 원칙들과 특성들과 사례들을 묵상하고 적용해야 합니다.
그러한 조리법을 따르면 영적으로 성공적인 삶을 살 수 있죠.
동료감과 형제 애정과 부드러운 동정심과 겸손을 나타내십시오.”
다섯 가지 훌륭한 특성으로 이루어진 이 조리법을 따르면 영적으로 성공적인 삶을 살 수 있습니다.
같은 생각을 갖기 위해 노력해야 한다는 것이죠.
따라서 우리는 서로 일치된 생각을 갖기 위해,
그리고 특히 여호와와 그분의 조직과 일치된 생각을 갖기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
“너희의 힘은 평온을 유지하고 신뢰하는 데 있을 것이다.”
충실한 종은 바로 이런 태도를 나타내 왔습니다.
따라서 우리도 충실한 종과 일치된 생각을 가지려고 노력해야 합니다.
살면서 어려움을 겪을 때도 평온을 유지하고 여호와를 신뢰해야 하죠.
열왕기하 4장을 보면 예언자 엘리사를 신뢰했던 한 수넴 여자에 관한 내용이 나옵니다.
이 여자는 아주 슬픈 일을 겪었습니다.
하지만 평온을 유지하고 “참하느님의 사람” 엘리사를 신뢰했죠.
우리는 여호와의 대표자를 신뢰한 이 여자를 본받아야 합니다.
4장에서 그 여자가 한 말을 보면 그의 신뢰심이 얼마나 강했는지 알 수 있는데요.
우리도 여호와와 오늘날 지상에서 그분을 대표하는 사람들에게 그런 신뢰심을 갖기를 원하죠.
엘리사는 수넴에 갈 때면 그 부부의 집에 들러 그들을 격려하곤 했습니다.
그는 그 부부가 베풀어 주는 후대를 고맙게 여겼고 그들을 위해 뭔가 해 주고 싶었죠.
열왕기하 4:14-16을 보면 그 여자에게는 아들이 없었고 그의 남편은 나이가 많았습니다.
엘리사는 다음 해에 그 여자가 아들을 안게 될 것이라고 말하죠.
그 예언대로 그 여자는 다음 해에 아이를 낳았습니다.
그 아이는 자랐고 하루는 들에서 일하는 아버지에게 갔습니다.
19절에 보면 아이는 머리가 아프다고 말하다가 결국 죽게 되었습니다.
“수종 한 사람과 나귀 한 마리를 보내 주세요.
그러니까 “그가 뭘 할 수 있겠소?”라고 한 거죠.
여자는 나귀에 안장을 얹고 수종에게 말했다.
‘빨리 모시오. 내가 말하기 전에는 늦추지 마시오.’”
이렇게 여자는 평온하고 신뢰하는 태도를 보이면서 약 30킬로미터를 가서 엘리사를 만납니다.
여자는 엘리사와 잘 아는 사이였고 그를 신뢰했기 때문에 확신을 가질 수 있었습니다.
여자는 슬픈 일을 겪었지만 확신을 잃지 않았습니다.
그래서 “별일 아니에요” 하고 말할 수 있었죠.
엘리사가 여호와에 대해 가진 믿음과 확신 덕분에
여호와를 섬기는 이 여자 역시 힘겨운 일을 겪을 때 평온을 유지하고 확신을 가질 수 있었습니다.
내가 너를 강하게 하고 너를 도와주겠다.
내가 참으로 내 의로운 오른손으로 너를 붙들어 주겠다.”
여호와께서 도와주신다면 모든 것이 잘될 것이라는 확신을 가짐으로
여호와의 조직과 일치된 생각을 갖기 위해 노력해야겠습니다.
네, 영적으로 성공하게 해 주는 조리법에 포함되는 한 가지 재료를 살펴보았습니다.
베드로 전서 3:8에서 베드로는 이어지는 세 가지 재료를 언급합니다.
이런 특성들을 나타내려면 감정 이입이 필요합니다.
감정 이입이란 “다른 사람의 감정을 이해하고 공감할 수 있는 능력”을 가리키죠.
이 세상 제도의 끝이 다가올수록 사탄은 여호와의 백성을 분열시키려고 애쓸 것입니다.
따라서 형제 자매들을 사랑하고 서로에게 감정 이입을 나타내는 것이 더욱 중요해질 것입니다.
여호와의 조직에서 볼 수 있는 감정 이입을 생각해 볼까요?
이곳 지상에서 조직을 인도하는 일을 하는 감독자들도 마찬가지이죠.
그들 중 어떤 사람들은 우리처럼 사별의 아픔을 겪었습니다.
또 어떤 사람들은 병을 앓고 있거나 염려에 시달립니다. 우리처럼 말이죠.
그래서 그들은 우리의 상황에 잘 공감해 줍니다.
사탄이 반역한 이래로 여호와께서는 불완전한 사람들의 행동 때문에
여호와께서는 실제로 그런 감정을 느끼시기 때문에 우리의 감정에 공감해 주실 수 있습니다.
그와 비슷하게, 예수께서도 사탄과 아담과 하와가 일으킨 반역과
그로 인한 결과를 보면서 실망감과 슬픔을 느끼셨습니다.
또 그분은 실제로 인간이 되어 인간이 느끼는 감정을 경험하시면서
우리의 감정을 더 잘 이해할 수 있게 되셨죠.
어떤 세 가지 방법을 통해 다른 사람의 필요와 감정을 더 잘 이해할 수 있는지 알려 줍니다.
우리는 주의 깊이 잘 들음으로 다른 사람들이 어떤 문제에 직면해 있는지를 알게 됩니다.
그들이 마음을 열고 감정을 털어놓을 가능성이 그만큼 더 높아집니다.”
모든 사람이 다 자신이 어떻게 느끼고 있는지
혹은 무슨 일을 겪고 있는지 우리에게 터놓고 이야기하는 것은 아닙니다.
동료 그리스도인이 격려나 실제적인 도움이 필요할 때 그것을 알아차릴 것입니다.’
감정 이입을 하도록 자극하는 가장 강력한 방법은 이렇게 자문해 보는 것입니다.
‘내가 이런 상황에 처해 있다면, 나는 어떻게 느낄 것인가?
나는 어떤 반응을 나타낼 것인가? 나에게는 무엇이 필요할 것인가?’”
네. 동료감, 형제 애정, 부드러운 동정심은 사랑으로 감정 이입을 하는 데 필요한 특성들입니다.
이 특성들은 영적으로 성공을 거두게 해 주는 귀중한 재료들이고
베드로 전서 3:8에서 언급하는 마지막 특성은 겸손입니다.
우리가 여호와와 그분의 조직을 신뢰하려면 겸손해야 합니다.
자신의 힘이나 지혜에 의지해서는 안 되죠.
우리가 겸손하다면 하느님이 어떤 어려움을 허용하시든 잘 인내할 수 있을 것입니다.
우리는 살면서 염려나 압력에 직면할 때 문제가 바로 해결되기를 바랄지 모르죠.
하지만 겸손이 있다면 여호와께서 우리를 위해
언제 어떻게 행동해야 할지 알고 계시다는 점을 신뢰할 수 있을 것입니다.
여호와께서는 그분이 정하신 때에 그분의 방법으로 항상 우리를 도와주십니다.
우리가 겸손하다면 여호와의 생각이 우리의 생각보다 훨씬 더 우월하다는 것을 인정할 것입니다.
하지만 여호와께서는 모든 것을 보고 알고 계시죠.
그분은 우리가 보지 못하는 것을 보실 수 있습니다.
따라서 우리는 그분이 일하시는 방식이 언제나 가장 좋다는 것을 신뢰하죠.
따라서 큰 환난이 다가오는 지금 겸손하게 여호와와 그분의 조직을 신뢰하십시오.
“그러므로 하느님의 강력한 손 아래 자기를 낮추십시오.
때가 되면 그분이 여러분을 높이실 것입니다.”
형제 여러분, “하느님의 강력한 손 아래” 있는 것이 그 어디에 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 낫습니다.
겸손은 우리가 계속 그분의 손 아래 머물 수 있게 해 주는 중요한 재료입니다.
네, 영적으로 성공하게 해 주는 조리법에 들어가는 재료들을 살펴보았습니다.
첫 번째는 일치된 생각을 갖는 것이었죠.

또한 맥이라고 하는 동물도 살고 있는데,
그리고 남아메리카에서 가장 큰 고양잇과 동물인 재규어도 있죠.
수리남은 그 외에도 다양성이 넘쳐 나는 곳입니다.
이곳에 사는 사람들 역시 매우 다양하죠.
여러 가지 관습과 음식이 있어서 수리남의 문화는 아주 다채롭습니다.
숲으로 뒤덮여 있고 다양성을 지닌 수리남에서
3300명이 넘는 우리 형제들이 어떤 어려움을 극복해야 하는지 생각해 보십시오.
사람들을 만나기 위해, 그리고 그들의 언어로 전파하기 위해
수리남 지부는 5개의 언어로 번역하는 일을 감독하고 있습니다.
스라난통가어, 아우카어, 사라마카어, 수리남 수어, 카리브어이죠.
번역 일을 지원하기 위해 2022년에 수리남 베델에서 20명의 번역자,
13명의 전 시간 출퇴근 봉사자, 8명의 원격 봉사자가 일했습니다.
다양한 언어들로 봉사를 하는 우리 형제들을 만나 보실까요?
브라운스버그 회중에 있는 34명의 전도인들은 사라마카어를 사용합니다.
수리남 중부 지역으로 도망친 노예의 후손들이 사용하던 언어이죠.
이 지역에 사는 대부분의 사람들은 수리남의 원주민 중 하나인 아라와크족이죠.
풀루구두 폭포 근처에 있는 풀루구두 회중이 있습니다.
이 지역은 물살이 거세서 배를 타고 다니기가 쉽지 않죠.
나무로 만든 배를 능숙하게 몰고 강들을 다니면서 전파 활동을 합니다.
이 회중의 38명의 전도인은 마룬 아우카어로 봉사합니다.
수리남과 브라운스버그, 아푸라, 풀루구두 회중의 형제 자매들이
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
In this month’s program,
we’ll see how much the Bible can improve our lives,
how it can save us from lasting harm,
how it can help us to get along with one another,
and how it reassures us
that even if we stumble,
Jehovah will help us find our way back.
From the life of John the Baptist,
we’ll learn how to cope with fear,
rejoice when others are blessed, and maintain a positive attitude
even when facing problems.
We’ll see from Brother Gordon Mackay’s experience
that Jehovah wants us to “draw close to [him]”
even if we’ve had a serious spiritual setback.
And our newest music video
extends a warm invitation to all
who find themselves estranged from Jehovah
and his imperfect but faithful family.
It reminds us of what a wonderful blessing
our spiritual home is.
This is the February 2024 edition
of JW Broadcasting.
When I was young, one of my favorite desserts
was my mother’s sweet potato pie.
It always tasted the same.
To me, it was perfect every time.
I’d often ask her, “Ma, what do you put in here
to make it taste so good?”
She’d always respond, “I just use the same stuff every time.”
In other words, number one, she wasn’t going to tell me.
And two, she had a recipe that worked,
so she never changed it.
Well, the Bible is like a cookbook,
full of recipes that work,
that can make our life spiritually successful.
Please note how Paul explains the benefits of these recipes
at 2 Timothy 3:16, 17:
“All Scripture is inspired of God
“and beneficial for teaching, for reproving,
“for setting things straight, for disciplining in righteousness,
“so that the man of God may be fully competent,
completely equipped for every good work.”
Sometimes the recipe from God’s inspired Word
comes in the form of a Bible example.
As we study that example,
we extract qualities and attitudes that we can imitate.
At other times, there’s a list of qualities,
such as the various aspects of the fruitage of God’s spirit
mentioned in Galatians chapter 5
or the list of positive things to consider
at Philippians 4:8, 9.
And, of course, there are numerous Bible principles
that we can use to help us make good decisions.
Meditating on and applying these principles,
qualities, and examples
can be a recipe that contributes to spiritual success.
Let’s consider one example.
It’s recorded at 1 Peter 3:8.
Take note of the ingredients.
“All of you have unity of mind,
“fellow feeling,
“brotherly affection,
“tender compassion,
and humility.”
This is a recipe of five beautiful qualities
that contribute to our spiritual success.
How so?
Let’s discuss the ingredients.
Peter first mentions “unity of mind.”
The footnote says “think in agreement.”
So we must think in agreement with one another
but especially with Jehovah and his organization.
In what way?
The latter part of Isaiah 30:15 says:
“Your strength will be in keeping calm and showing trust.”
That’s exactly what the faithful slave has done.
So let us have unity of mind with them
and have the same calmness and confidence in Jehovah
as we face personal challenges in our life.
In 2 Kings chapter 4,
a Shunammite woman is mentioned
who had confidence in the prophet Elisha.
She suffered a terrible tragedy in her life.
Yet, she remained calm
and showed trust in “the man of the true God,” Elisha.
Her example of trust in Jehovah’s representative
is worthy of imitation.
In fact, there is an expression she uses in chapter 4
that conveys the level of trust
we want to have in Jehovah
and his earthly representatives today.
Let me tell you about this woman.
She and her husband lived in Shunem.
Elisha would regularly make encouraging visits with them
when he was in that city.
Elisha appreciated their hospitality
and wanted to do something kind for them.
What would he do?
Well, verses 14-16
of 2 Kings chapter 4
indicate that she did not have a son
and that her husband was old.
So Elisha told her that the next year
she would be embracing a son.
Well, as Elisha foretold,
she gave birth the next year.
But unfortunately, something drastic happened.
The child grew up and one day went out to work with his father.
In verse 19, the boy complained of a headache,
which led to his eventual death.
Oh my!
What would this woman do?
This was her only son.
Well, she had confidence
in “the man of the true God,” Elisha,
so she says to her husband in verse 22:
“Send me, please, one of the attendants
“and one of the donkeys,
“and let me go quickly
to the man of the true God and return.”
In verse 23, her husband asks:
“Why are you going to see him today?”
In other words, “What can he do for us?”
Ah, note her response
at the end of verse 23 and verse 24:
“However, she said:
“‘Everything is all right.’
“So she saddled the donkey
“and said to her attendant: ‘Go quickly.
Do not slow down for me unless I tell you to.’”
So this calm, trusting woman
rides about 19 miles, or 30 kilometers,
and finds Elisha.
And he ends up resurrecting her son.
Her trusting relationship and association with Elisha
had given her confidence.
Although she experienced a tragedy,
she knew that everything was all right.
Elisha’s faith and confidence in Jehovah
helped this devoted woman also
to remain calm and confident
when facing adversity.
At Isaiah 41:10,
note Jehovah’s assurance:
“Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
So let’s work hard to have unity of mind
with Jehovah’s organization
by keeping calm and showing trust in Jehovah
and by being confident that with Jehovah’s help
everything will be all right.
That’s a beautiful ingredient
in this recipe for spiritual success.
At 1 Peter 3:8,
Peter next mentions three more ingredients.
They are aspects of love:
“fellow feeling,
“brotherly affection,
tender compassion.”
These aspects of love convey empathy.
Empathy is “the ability to understand
and share the feelings of another.”
As this system draws to a close,
Satan will try to divide us from within.
So love for our brothers and sisters
and empathizing with one another
will become ever more important.
It will serve to unify us.
Think of the empathy
of Jehovah’s organization.
We all have personal challenges,
but so do our overseers,
those taking the lead in the organization here on earth.
Some of them have lost loved ones in death
just like us.
Some have experienced sickness and anxiety
just like us.
We love them for their empathy.
Think about the heavenly part of Jehovah’s organization.
Since Satan’s rebellion, Jehovah has been disappointed,
saddened, angered at the actions of imperfect men.
These are real feelings
that our empathetic heavenly Father possesses.
Jesus experienced similar disappointment and sadness
as he also saw the rebellion
of Satan, Adam, and Eve and what’s resulted.
In fact, Jesus’ understanding became deeper
when he became human and began to experience human emotions.
The April 15, 2002, Watchtower  article
entitled “Empathy—Key to Kindness and Compassion”
mentioned three ways we can sharpen our sensitivity
to the needs and feelings of others.
The first: ‘Listen.
‘By listening carefully,
‘we learn what problems others face.
‘And the better we listen,
‘the more likely they will open up their hearts
and reveal their feelings.’
Second: ‘Observe.
‘Not everyone will openly tell us
‘how they feel
‘or what they are going through.
‘A keen observer will notice
‘when a fellow Christian needs encouragement
or some practical assistance.’
Third: “Use Your Imagination.
“The most powerful way to stimulate empathy
“is to ask yourself:
“‘If I were in this situation,
“‘how would I feel?
“‘How would I respond?
What would I need?’”
So fellow feeling, brotherly affection, and tender compassion
are aspects of loving empathy
and are valuable ingredients to our spiritual success
and will benefit others.
The final quality highlighted at 1 Peter 3:8
is humility.
Why do we need humility?
Because we need to trust.
Trust in Jehovah and his organization
requires humility
—not relying on our own strength or wisdom.
Humility helps us to cope
with whatever God permits.
When we face anxiety and pressure in our life,
we may yearn for immediate relief.
But humility helps us to trust
that Jehovah knows precisely when
and how to act in our behalf.
So we wait
patiently.
Jehovah always responds to our needs
in his time and in his way.
Humility helps us to admit that Jehovah’s thoughts
are vastly superior to our own.
We recognize our limited discernment
in comparison
with Jehovah’s all-encompassing perception.
He sees things we do not discern,
and thus we trust that his way of doing things
is always best.
So as the great tribulation approaches,
humbly trust in Jehovah
and his organization.
First Peter chapter 5,
and verse 6 says this:
“Humble yourselves, therefore,
“under the mighty hand of God,
so that he may exalt you in due time.”
Brothers, there is no better place to be
than “under the mighty hand of God.”
Humility is a beautiful ingredient
that helps us to remain there.
So, what were the ingredients
in our recipe for spiritual success?
First was unity of mind.
Be at unity with Jehovah’s organization today
by keeping calm and showing trust.
In the words of the Shunammite woman in 2 Kings chapter 4,
when facing adversity, always know that with Jehovah
“everything is all right.”
Second was fellow feeling,
brotherly affection, and tender compassion
—all aspects of loving empathy.
Remember, we’re all in this together.
The celestial chariot is empathetic toward what we face
and will respond to our personal and organizational needs.
Finally, try always
to include humility
in your recipe for success.
Humility requires trust,
so trust that Jehovah’s way of doing things
is always best.
Psalm 119:105 says
that the Bible “is a lamp to my foot,
and a light for my path.”
So take time to consider
a portion of God’s Word each day.
As situations, decisions, and challenges arise,
search for the right recipe
—Bible example, Christian quality, principle.
When you do, Jehovah will light up
the path ahead of you
and help you to be spiritually successful.
We’ve seen that the Bible’s “recipes”
can make our life spiritually successful
and help us improve our relationships.
In the following interview,
note how applying a recipe of Bible principles
can also undo the damage caused by poor decisions.
We graduated in June, got married in July,
and had a child in November.
So it was a happy time.
At one point, two Witnesses
knocked on my door,
and they showed me Psalm 83:18,
that God’s name is Jehovah.
They offered a Bible study,
but my study only lasted two to three weeks.
We got a car.
We started going to parties
—starting to smoke,
having drugs, getting drunk.
We did all these things
that really tore our marriage apart.
We thought moving away from our town
and our old associates would help.
It was worse then ever.
Baseball was more important to me than even my wife.
I had a real problem with headship.
There were times when I felt like
I was smarter than him,
so I felt like I could make
a better decision than he could make.
In time, Zanna left me for another person,
and that’s what really hurt me.
Zanna had a hard time with drugs and so forth.
That’s when I got custody of the kids.
I decided at that moment that I was done,
and Jehovah
popped into my head.
I remember
getting down
and telling Jehovah,
“Just show me; show me what to do.”
I went through the telephone book
and looked up Jehovah’s Witnesses.
They gave me a book,
a Family Life  book.
I showed him that book,
and I told him,
“Had we applied this in our marriage
“from the beginning,
our marriage would’ve never broken up.”
My mind was going: ‘Really? Really?’
But I’d see she was doing things in a spiritual way.
She stopped doing drugs,
and I just saw her mannerisms change.
In that short period of time, things got better and better.
And then I started studying the Bible with Zanna.
That’s when things started clicking.
One of the scriptures
that helped me to rebuild our marriage
is 1 Corinthians 11:3.
Art is my head; I am not the head.
Knowing that everybody
but Jehovah has a head,
I view that as a protection.
Now I don’t have to make decisions on my own.
Galatians 5:22, 23
—that helped me to show love,
to be a better husband,
a better father.
And I always treat her like a lady,
you know, listen to her viewpoints and things like that.
I remarried Arthur
on April 2, 1979.
I would tell someone who is struggling in their marriage now,
“Apply Bible principles
—apply them.”
We learned to be a family with Jehovah,
and that’s why we can deal with the problems
that we have to face every day.
The second time around
is so much sweeter
with Jehovah in the picture.
Amazing—isn’t it?—
how learning and applying Bible principles
and keeping Jehovah in the picture
made such a difference for Art and Zanna!
That’s why we exert ourselves
to bring God’s Word to as many as possible.
This includes helping people hear the truth
in the language of their heart.
I know you’ll enjoy our next segment
on how a publishing innovation
invented by our brothers years ago
has accelerated the translation of the good news,
leading to the greatest witness in history.
Jehovah’s Witnesses are known
for publishing in hundreds of languages,
with a website recognized
as the most widely translated in the world.
But have you ever wondered how we’re able to release our literature
in print and online in so many languages at once?
The answer involves a cutting-edge publishing system
that our brothers developed more than 40 years ago
—a breakthrough in publishing called MEPS.
But just what is MEPS?
Let’s find out and see how this technology
has helped to unite Jehovah’s people
and has opened the way for us to give the greatest witness in history.
God’s people have long understood
the need to share the truth in as many languages as possible.
Revelation 14:6
prophesied that the good news would be preached
“to every nation and tribe and tongue and people.”
So as far back as the late 1800’s,
the early Bible Students translated our literature
into languages other than English
so that people could learn the truth in their mother tongue.
But for decades, publishing the good news in many languages
was a labor-intensive process.
Imagine yourself working at a Bethel printery decades ago.
It was hot and loud.
Printing required the use of a Linotype machine,
which turned molten lead
into small metal slabs of type called slugs
one line at a time.
Workers had to meticulously compose pages
by arranging the slugs into large metal frames
that were used to make special embossed mats.
Then more hot metal was used to cast printing plates from the mats.
And for long press runs,
the plates then had to be electroplated with nickel to harden them.
Finally, after removing any irregularities,
the plates were ready to be mounted
on a large rotary printing press.
Publishing the same material in another language meant
repeating these prepress steps from beginning to end.
It took months for a single magazine
to be translated from English, typeset, and printed.
For books, it could take years!
The days of hot metal were quickly ending.
The printing industry began adopting the use
of phototypesetting and offset presses.
It was time to modernize operations at Bethel
and make the transition to computers.
But the brothers faced a unique challenge.
At this point, we were already printing literature
in 167 languages.
So we needed a solution
that could handle all those languages and more.
And not one of the commercially available systems could do that.
So in 1979, a group of brothers and sisters
were called to Watchtower Farms in Wallkill, New York,
to develop a Multilanguage Electronic Phototypesetting System,
or MEPS.
So we got to work on building MEPS.
Some brothers and sisters concentrated on the hardware—the actual circuitry.
Other brothers concentrated on the screen itself and building that.
And then others of us concentrated on the software,
the operating system, you might say.
The MEPS team designed and built almost everything
—computers, keyboards, screens, and software.
They had to.
Personal computers with the power needed still weren’t available
and wouldn’t be for another few years.
Another massive part of the project involved creating the fonts
—the individual letters used to make up the pages of text.
Commercial fonts weren’t available or were too expensive
for many of the languages needed.
So brothers and sisters had to draw each character by hand
and scan them into the computer.
For some languages, this meant drawing thousands of characters.
The software then had to be programmed
with all the rules for spacing and hyphenation
so that words and characters could be displayed correctly.
Just three years after the project began,
the first MEPS unit was completed in 1982.
With MEPS, an operator could enter text at a computer workstation
in any supported language.
After this, the workstation could be used to format the text
and compose pages.
This approach allowed the brothers
to use a single-page layout‎
‎to produce the same publication for all languages.
The final pages were then rendered on photographic paper,
transferred to film, and used to make printing plates.
MEPS didn’t do the translation itself.
That was, and still is,
a job for human translators.
But it allowed all the prepress work
to be completed in a fraction of the time.
And MEPS achieved something even more important
than increased speed and efficiency.
It addressed a global spiritual need.
Even before the MEPS project began,
the Governing Body realized
that if Jehovah’s Witnesses worldwide
could somehow study the same material each week at meetings,
it would unite them as never before.
And it was clear that with MEPS,
along with faster presses and other adjustments in production,
this could finally become a reality.
In fact, so much time could be saved in this projected operation
that someday we may be able to bring out The Watchtower
in all principal languages
with each dated issue containing exactly the same spiritual food
for the brothers all around the world.
The April 1, 1984, issue of The Watchtower
became the first to be published in multiple languages simultaneously.
In just the next year, the number of simultaneous languages
grew to 23.
And by 2021, the study edition of The Watchtower
was being published simultaneously
in more than 390 languages!
Almost all of Jehovah’s Witnesses
are now able to study the same spiritual food at our meetings
at the same time
—truly a modern-day miracle!
Today, MEPS does a lot more than typesetting.
It’s grown to become a full set of publishing tools.
MEPS programming paved the way
for Watchtower Library  on CD-ROM
and contributed to the development of the JW Library®  app.
In fact, the MEPS acronym now stands
for Multilanguage Electronic Publishing System
because it drives our publishing both in print and online.
In the end, the story of MEPS
is more than a story of technology;
it’s one of love.
Love moved the Governing Body
to seek better ways to provide spiritual food
to people of every “tribe and tongue.”
As a result of that love and with Jehovah’s holy spirit,
we now enjoy unprecedented unity
and the ability to preach the good news
on a scale never before possible.
From molten metal slabs of type
to computerized publishing,
the development of MEPS has been a real blessing.
It’s helped unify Jehovah’s people
as we preach the good news “in all the inhabited earth
for a witness to all the nations.”
But what if we face a situation
where we personally begin to wonder
if Jehovah is blessing us?
Let’s see how lessons from the life of John the Baptist
can help us remain certain of Jehovah’s love and protection.
I knew this day would come.
True Christians
expect opposition,
but it hurt to see Brother Vasil
get arrested.
After what happened,
I was scared to talk about Jehovah.
Marcos has been looking for work for months.
It’s starting to feel hopeless.
I appreciate that he supports me in the pioneer ministry,
but shouldn’t he focus on finding work?
I was so happy when I heard Nicole got invited to SKE,
but as I kept thinking about it,
I started to feel empty,
disappointed.
Others seem to get so many privileges.
Why not me?
In my Bible reading,
I found an example of courage
to preach boldly despite opposition.
After I told Marcos how I was feeling,
we considered a Bible character who endured with hope.
Jesus said:
“Among those born of women,
“there has not been raised up
anyone greater than John the Baptist.”
Many that listened to him were moved to repent and get baptized,
preparing their hearts to receive the Messiah.
He even baptized
the Son of God.
But as Jesus’ ministry increased,
John’s began to decrease.
When his disciples
pointed that out to John,
he humbly rejoiced at what Jehovah was accomplishing
through Jesus.
However, John faced adversity
just like worshippers of Jehovah today.
John was imprisoned for boldly declaring the truth.
Nothing prevented him from preaching courageously.
As time passed and he remained in prison,
John needed reassurance,
just like I do.
His disciples returned
with a message from Jesus:
Observe what Jehovah
is accomplishing around you.
Now I see what Jehovah
is accomplishing around me.
I can imitate John the Baptist and endure with hope.
I have so many reasons to be joyful,
among them seeing Jehovah use others
to accomplish his will.
People need to learn about Jehovah.
Like John, I can have courage,
no matter what adversity I may face.
Excellent lessons for us all!
One sister was overly concerned
about her husband finding employment.
But she later realized the value
of him keeping up his spiritual routine in the ministry with her.
Another sister felt empty and disappointed,
but she learned to rejoice, as did John,
in seeing Jehovah use others to advance Kingdom interests.
And our brother who faced persecution
learned to overcome his fear and speak up.
Often, in lands where our work is banned,
lies and propaganda are spread
to justify persecution.
But it’s not just in such lands where we face false reports,
misinformation, and outright lies.
In fact, even though we bear the truth,
apostates and others
may cast us as dishonest, as deceivers.
How can we respond to that unfair treatment?
Let’s listen to Brother Seth Hyatt’s recent Morning Worship discussion,
Speaking Truth Though Labeled as Deceivers.
Have you ever been confronted
by a bad report,
a false report,
about Jehovah’s people?
It may be a newspaper article
or a segment on the evening news
or perhaps some subject is brought up in the ministry.
It could be a broad range of subjects:
our neutral stand,
our stand on blood,
our adherence to Jehovah’s elevated moral standards
and appreciation for the sanctity of marriage,
or our insistence on keeping the congregation clean
by disfellowshipping unrepentant wrongdoers.
But whatever the subject,
there are some commonalities.
Such reports
are often characterized by distortions,
inaccuracies,
and sometimes outright falsehood.
And inevitably,
they’re presented with certainty and surety
as though they were fact.
When you’re confronted with such a report,
how do you feel:
disheartened, discouraged,
angry?
Consider the experience of a pioneer sister
who was conducting a Bible study.
In the course of conducting the study,
a woman walked into the house unannounced.
She didn’t ring the doorbell, didn’t knock
and, as it turned out, was an acquaintance of the student.
She walked right in and interrupted the Bible study.
And in her hand was a book
written by a man who at one time had associated with Jehovah’s people.
The woman said to the student,
“You need to read this book.”
Well, an interesting conversation ensued,
and our sister found herself in the position
of being cast in the role of a deceiver.
How did she handle that situation,
and how did the Bible student respond?
Well, before we answer that question,
let’s see how the words of today’s text
and surrounding verses
can help us to have the proper view.
Look, if you would, please, at 2 Corinthians chapter 6,
and notice verse 4.
Paul says: “In every way
we recommend ourselves as God’s ministers.”
Now, what follows is a lengthy series
of circumstances and situations
that the apostle Paul faced in his ministry
and that faithful Christians have faced in their ministry ever since.
In verse 7, the words of today’s text:
“We recommend ourselves as God’s ministers, . . .
by truthful speech.”
Well, we worship Jehovah, “the God of truth,”
and we take delight in that.
And as our Watchtower  comment makes the point,
we’re truthful in things “big and small.”
We love the truth.
We love telling the truth about Jehovah.
So it’s interesting to note
Paul’s words in verse 8.
He says: “Through glory and dishonor,
through bad report and good report.”
And then this intriguing statement:
“We are regarded as deceivers
and yet we are truthful.”
Now, that’s an interesting paradox, isn’t it?
To be truthful
and yet cast in the role of a deceiver.
When we are confronted with a negative report
that does that to Jehovah’s people,
it’s good to remember that Jehovah was the first target
of such an attack.
Look in your Bible at Genesis chapter 3,
beginning in verse 1:
“Now the serpent was the most cautious
“of all the wild animals of the field
“that Jehovah God had made.
“So it said to the woman:
“‘Did God really say
that you must not eat from every tree of the garden?’”
Now, we learn something about Satan’s method.
He didn’t begin with a statement.
He began with a question,
and not just a question,
a question that was designed to sow seeds of doubt:
“Did God really say that . . . ?”
Now, in verses 2 and 3, the woman responds.
Toward the close of verse 3,
she actually quotes Jehovah’s command:
“You must not eat from it, no, you must not touch it;
otherwise you will die.”
So she understood the command,
and she understood the penalty.
But notice in verse 4:
“The serpent said to the woman:
‘You certainly will not die.’”
Now, that was a lie.
But it was presented with certainty and surety
as though it were a fact.
And then in verse 5: “For God knows
“that in the very day you eat from it,
“your eyes will be opened and you will be like God,
knowing good and bad.”
Satan, “the father of the lie,”
cast Jehovah in the role of a deceiver.
Jesus experienced similar attacks
during his earthly ministry,
and the apostle Paul was labeled by his opposers
as a deceiver.
So when we’re confronted
with negative, false reports,
we’re not surprised.
The question is, How will we respond?
Have you ever considered some questions
that Eve could have asked herself
that would have helped her to make a good decision?
Here’s one:
‘What do I know about the person
‘who is the source of this negative report?
‘What is his motive?
‘Does he have my best interests at heart,
or does he have an agenda?’
And another question:
‘Before I accept as truth
‘a negative report from someone I don’t know,
‘is there someone I do know,
‘someone I trust who I can talk with
and get some good advice?’
Well, Eve certainly could have talked with her husband,
and together they could have talked with Jehovah.
And if Eve had asked herself those questions,
the world would likely be a much different place today.
But Eve chose to believe a lie.
How about the pioneer sister
and the Bible student that I mentioned earlier?
How did they handle the situation?
Well, the pioneer sister told us
that she reflected on the fact
that she was a guest in the Bible student’s house.
And so she felt it would be rude for her to interrupt the conversation.
So she chose to say nothing.
What did the Bible student do?
Interestingly, she asked the woman:
“Do you know the man who wrote that book?”
“No.”
“Do you know his motive for writing?
“Why would he write such a book?
“Well, I know this lady who comes and studies the Bible with me,
“and I know her motive is good.
So I don’t think I need to read your book.”
What a beautiful response!
The Bible student got it,
and we get it too.
We know and we’re not surprised
that we will be the target of negative reports.
At times, we may even be cast in the role of deceivers.
Jehovah has frankly told us
that there are some
who are willing to exchange the truth of God for the lie.
But that will never be true of you or me.
Instead, we hold to Jehovah, “the God of truth.”
We continue to “recommend ourselves as God’s ministers . . .
by truthful speech.”
Next, let’s benefit from the experience of a brother
who made significant life changes
when he accepted the truth
only to slip back and stray from it later.
Notice how Jehovah feels about those who stray
and how he extends his loving arm of assistance.
I grew up in the Highlands of Scotland.
It was a beautiful part of the world to grow up in.
My father (when I was growing up, you know),
he and his friends worked very hard, but they also drank a lot.
There was a lot of violence and heavy drinking
and, of course, this sometimes came in to our home life as well.
By the time I was 14, I’d started drinking
and sometimes I fought with my father and my stepfather.
It affected my self-esteem and my view of myself,
and I often went to school feeling low and crushed.
But at times—
The teachers started to read the Bible to us.
Those accounts touched me so deeply,
and it gave me a real sense of hope for the future.
I didn’t want to be fighting and getting into trouble.
I wanted to be a better person.
I had a purpose.
I knew there was more to life than this, and so I joined the army.
The army gave me the opportunity to get out of the environment
and to see the world.
Still, on the weekends, we often
ended up drinking too much and being violent.
When I got into trouble, I always felt deep regret.
I always wanted to change.
So I knew that I needed to escape from that environment and start off fresh.
So I decided to move to Edinburgh.
I was really doing a lot of fitness training at this time,
but really what I had done was
that I had replaced one addiction, which was alcohol,
with another addiction, which was fitness.
So I was smiling on the outside, but I burned out.
I was in a black hole where I couldn’t get out.
I knew that God was the only person that could help me,
and I prayed a lot during that time
so that he would help me to find happiness and a purpose in life.
A colleague came to work alongside me who had been in the marines.
We had gone to a nightclub, and on the way home,
I said that I didn’t like this type of environment.
And to my surprise, this colleague of mine
started to talk to me about the Bible.
But after two or three hours of my questions,
he said, “I will get my dad to speak to you.”
His father was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
He gave me some publications, and he encouraged me to read them
alongside the Bible, looking up the verses in the Bible.
We started to study the Bible with his father.
We started to attend the meetings.
About one and a half years after we’d started,
we both got baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses on the same day.
A few years after I got baptized, I moved to Germany,
and during that time, unfortunately,
I was disfellowshipped from the Christian congregation.
I went to work in the North Sea, and I was so unhappy in this environment
that when I was not working, I was drinking a lot.
If I was not careful, I would end up doing some damage to my health.
So I decided to move to Italy.
Often, when I was out riding my bike and every time I
passed the Kingdom Hall, I would ask the question,
How am I going to return to Jehovah?
I thought, ‘Well, Jehovah will never want me to come back.’
One Saturday morning, the doorbell rang and, sure enough,
it was two of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I knew that Jehovah had sent these two Witnesses.
And Jehovah was saying: “I still love you, you know.
No matter what you have done, I still love you.”
And so for the next few months, I spent a lot of time thinking about that
and accepting Jehovah’s love.
I still had some distractions in my life.
I was training for a race across the Alps.
I was still working on the oil platforms in the North Sea.
I wasn’t making spiritual progress.
One time, the elders in the Kingdom Hall
told me that there was no meeting during the week,
but they encouraged me to go to an assembly in Rome.
What really touched me the most was how clean Jehovah’s people were
compared to the people that I’d been associating with for so many years.
While I was driving home, I remember there was a storm.
I had all these thoughts racing through my mind:
‘How did I manage to leave the congregation?
How did I manage to leave Jehovah?’
On that journey home, I knew that I would never go back to work
on the oil platforms in the North Sea.
I had a lot of free time on my hands, so I read the Bible a lot
and the publications from Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And there was something in those publications that touched me,
because it said: ‘Return to me whole-souled.
Let’s set matters straight between us now.’
I spoke with the elders and told them of my intent
to attend all the meetings and to serve Jehovah whole-souled.
And after a period of time, I was reinstated in the congregation.
When I tried to do things my own way,
my life ended up out of balance—a mess.
I was so unhappy.
But with Jehovah in my life,
it gave me more balance in my life.
It was about learning to accept Jehovah’s love.
And when I did that, I started to make progress
because I was able to accept Jehovah’s love
and I was also able to accept the love
through the brothers in the congregation.
Jehovah’s love is way greater than that.
Jehovah’s love is able to cover everything.
So I realized that Jehovah’s wisdom
is, for me, priceless because
Jehovah is the only one who can turn a negative situation
into something positive and give us
a real sense of purpose and happiness in our life.
Have you, like Brother Mackay, strayed?
Have you become inactive
or even been removed from the congregation?
Consider the following invitation
so warmly brought to life
in our new music video,
Home.
I can feel lost sometimes, Like I’m drifting out to sea,
When troubles in my life Take me far from Kingdom realities.
But I’m never left in the lurch.
Jehovah hears and sends out the search.
He finds me, lifts me up in his arms.
He carries me safely away from harm.
He brings me back to his fold— my home, my family.
I am never alone
when I’m home.
There is no place like this.
It’s a shelter from the storm
Where I find peace and rest
And loving friends who bring out the very best.
So if you find you’re out on your own,
Jehovah will hear your cries to come home.
He’ll find you, lead you back with his voice,
Remind you serving him was your best choice.
He’ll bring you back to his fold— your home, your family.
You are never alone when you’re home.
How we’ll be singing: “You made it back! Welcome home!”
It’s where you belong; And we’re so happy to see you.
Now you’re home.
You are home.
He found you,
lifted you up in his arms.
He carried you
safely away from harm.
He brought you back to his fold.
You’ll never be alone
When you’re home.
Home is with Jehovah and his people.
Home is where we belong.
If you’ve wandered,
come home.
The beauty of our spiritual home
extends across the entire world.
Let’s explore another “room” in that home
by visiting our brothers and sisters in Suriname.
Suriname is a heavily forested country in South America
that’s almost like an island.
It isn’t currently connected by road to any other country.
On its east and west,
it’s bounded by rivers;
on the north,
by the Atlantic Ocean;
and to the south, by tropical rainforests,
savannas, and the mighty Amazon River Basin.
While Suriname may be
one of the smallest countries in South America,
its abundant wild areas host
some of the continent’s largest animals.
The giant anteater, for example,
eats some 35,000 ants and termites a day.
Also found in Suriname are the tapir
(South America’s largest land mammal)
and the jaguar (the largest of South American cats).
Suriname’s rich diversity isn’t limited to wildlife.
Its people are one of the most ethnically diverse in the region.
Their varying customs and foods
enrich the country’s overall culture.
In such a heavily forested and diverse country,
imagine the challenge
our over 3,300 brothers face,
first reaching
and then preaching to people
in their own languages.
While the official language of Suriname is Dutch,
the Suriname branch oversees
translation into five other languages:
Sranantongo, Aukan,
Saramaccan, Surinamese Sign Language,
and Carib.
In 2022, 20 translators in Suriname Bethel
worked with 13 full-time commuters
and 8 remote workers
to meet this need.
Let’s meet some of our brothers working
in the various language fields.
The 34 publishers in the Brownsweg Congregation
speak the Saramaccan language,
used by descendants of escaped slaves
who fled to the country’s interior
almost 400 years ago.
The Apoera Congregation’s 18 Kingdom preachers
conduct 30 Bible studies each month.
Many in the area are Arawak Indians,
among the original inhabitants of Suriname.
Deep in Suriname’s interior
is the Pulugudu Congregation,
located near Pulugudu Falls.
These waters are notoriously difficult to navigate.
Our brothers are adept at using their wooden boats
to carry out the preaching work on the river “roads.”
The 38 publishers preach in the Maroon Aukan language.
The brothers and sisters of Suriname
and the Brownsweg, Apoera, and Pulugudu congregations
send you their love.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

title: 왕국회관 건축보다 더 많은 일을 하는 LDC

ko.text: 열심히 일하는 많은 형제 자매들이 자원해서 전 세계 설계 건축 그룹에서 봉사합니다.
우리 대부분이 잘 알고 있듯이, 그들은 왕국회관과 관련된 일을 합니다.
대회회관, 야외 숙소, 재난 후 재건축을 위해서도 필요합니다.
잠비아에 있는 대부분의 대회 시설은 계속 개선이 필요합니다.
많은 경우 형제 자매들은 바닥에 앉아서 대회를 보고,
대회를 보는 동안 날씨의 영향을 그대로 받습니다.
2023 봉사 연도에 대회 시설과 관련된 10개의 공사를 마쳤습니다.
이 대회장들을 자주 사용하고 있는데 크게 두 가지 문제가 있죠.
그래서 우리는 단열·방음 처리가 된 지붕 패널을 설치해서
이 두 가지 문제를 다 해결할 수 있었습니다.
이제 형제 자매들이 품위 있는 장소에서 모이는 걸 보면 마음이 뿌듯하죠.
새로 지어진 침례장 덕분에 이제는 악어가 많은 강에서 침례를 받지 않아도 됩니다.
건축 프로그램은 형제들을 훈련할 기회가 되기도 합니다.
전문 기술이 있고 건강한 나이 든 형제들을 초대해서
젊은 형제들에게 기술을 전수해 주도록 했습니다.
그 결과 형제 자매들은 기술을 잘 배웠고 ‘격려도 주고받을’ 수 있었죠.
야외 숙소 공사도 매우 중요하다는 걸 깨닫게 됐습니다.
왜냐하면 야외 숙소는 형제들이 일주일에 한두 번 방문하는 곳이 아니라
누군가가 실제로 살면서 먹고 자는 곳이기 때문이죠.
새 야외 숙소에 사는 형제는 말하길,
전기를 쓰려면 다른 형제들의 집까지 멀리 가야만 했다고 했습니다.
열심히 일하는 순회 감독자 부부가 안락한 숙소에서 지내는 것은 정말 중요합니다.
그래야 필요한 휴식을 취할 수 있죠.
또한 적절한 환경에서 그들이 방문할 회중의 유익을 위해
필요한 연구와 준비를 할 수 있습니다.
지난 3년 동안 나이지리아에는 홍수가 여러 차례 있었습니다.
그래서 조정자 위원회를 통해 긴급한 도움을 받았습니다.
그런 다음에 LDC에서 재건축이 필요한 건물이 있는지 파악하고
재해가 닥치면 신권 시설들과 형제 자매들의 집이 영향을 받죠.
일부 형제들은 스스로 집을 다시 짓거나 수리할 수 없습니다.
적절한 사람들이 그러한 공사를 할 수 있도록 마련하는 데 큰 역할을 합니다.
나이지리아는 자연재해뿐 아니라 사람이 초래한 재난으로도 피해를 많이 입습니다.
그런 경우 형제 자매들은 더 안전한 지역으로 피신해야 하죠.
돌아와 보면 안타깝게도 집이 파괴되거나 완전히 불에 타 버린 경우가 있습니다.
그런 일이 생기면 LDC는 안전할 때 가서 어떤 필요가 있는지 파악하고 재건축을 돕습니다.
현재 집 25채를 다시 짓고 18채를 수리해야 합니다.
재난으로 인한 재건축에 참여하고 싶은 분이 있다면 지원서를 작성해야 합니다.
LDC 자원봉사를 할 수 있는 DC-50을 작성하거나
몇 주 또는 몇 달 동안 신권 공사에 자원할 수 있는 A-19 양식을 작성하거나
LDC 프로그램을 전 시간으로 지원할 수 있는 A-8을 작성할 수도 있습니다.
많은 분들이 기도밖에 할 수 없다고 하시지만 사실 기도는 우리가 할 수 있는 최상의 일입니다.
이 모든 공사에는 여호와의 축복이 필요하고,
신권 시설들에서 일하는 자원봉사자들에게도 여호와의 축복이 필요하니까요.
오늘날 진행되고 있는 건축 및 개축 작업은
앞으로 이 땅에 있을 대규모 복구 작업을 준비하는 것입니다.
그때에는 우리 모두가 이 활동에 참여할 수 있을 것입니다.
지금까지 LDC를 통해 이루어진 모든 일들을 돌이켜 보면 정말 흐뭇합니다.
건축자들이 열심히 일해도 헛되다”는 시편 127편의 말씀이 자주 생각납니다.
모든 영예와 영광은 마땅히 우리 하느님께 돌아가야 합니다.

en.text: Hardworking brothers and sisters volunteer to be part
of Local Design/Construction (LDC) groups worldwide.
While working on Kingdom Halls
is the aspect of their work that most are familiar with,
volunteers are also needed
for working on Assembly Halls,
field residences, and with disaster reconstruction.
There is an ongoing need to upgrade
most of our assembly sites in Zambia.
At many of our sites,
the brothers and sisters are sitting on the ground,
and they’re exposed to the elements during the assembly program.
In the 2023 service year,
we completed ten projects related to assembly sites.
In Nigeria, we have 23 Assembly Halls
all over the country.
And, you can imagine,
they are extensively used.
We face two main issues:
heat and also the noise from heavy rain.
So to solve these two issues,
we inserted in the design roof panels that are insulated,
and this really addressed both issues.
To see how our brothers and sisters
can now meet in dignified locations is heartwarming.
With the new baptismal pools,
they don’t have to worry about getting baptized in rivers
that could be crocodile-infested.
The construction programs
are also an opportunity
to train the brothers.
We took advantage of the renovation of the Assembly Hall to invite older brothers
—experts in their trades and in good health—
to pass on their knowledge to the younger ones.
And the truth is, there was a great deal of learning
and “an interchange of encouragement,”
which was then also reflected in the congregations.
For as much as we consider
our Kingdom Halls and our Assembly Halls
as a priority in the program,
we realize that a field-residence project
is always a special one because we are working,
not on a facility that brothers will visit once or twice a week,
but that’s where someone will actually live and sleep and eat.
One brother who benefits from a new field residence commented,
“We used to have to travel long distances
“to brothers’ houses who have electricity
because our mud huts did not have that electricity.”
Now that is a thing of the past.
Having a suitable home base is invaluable
to these hardworking circuit overseers and their wives.
It now enables them to get the rest that they need.
It gives them a suitable environment for the study
and the preparation they need to do
in order to benefit the congregations they’re serving.
In the past three years, Nigeria has been afflicted by flooding
quite a few times.
So after receiving humanitarian assistance through the Coordinators’ Committee,
the LDC comes into the picture
to make sure that if there is
any reconstruction work that needs to be done,
it will be accomplished.
When disasters strike,
our theocratic facilities
and the homes of our brothers are affected.
Some of these brothers can’t rebuild or repair their houses by themselves,
so the LDC really plays a big role
in making sure that we get the information needed
and that we get the right people working on some of these projects.
Apart from natural disasters,
Nigeria has been affected by man-made disasters.
There has been a lot of community crisis,
and usually they have to flee from their region to a safer location.
And when they return, sadly, at times,
they find out that their home has been destroyed
or completely burned down.
So that’s where the LDC,
when it is safe, will go evaluate the needs
and assist with the reconstruction.
Right now, we have 25 houses to be rebuilt
and 18 to be repaired.
If someone wants to get involved
with disaster reconstruction in their branch territory,
they have to fill in their forms.
It could be the DC-50 (which allows them to be LDC volunteers)
or an A-19 form
(where they can volunteer to support theocratic projects
for a couple of months or weeks)
or even an A-8
(where they can come full-time and support the LDC program).
Many might say, “I can only pray.”
But, actually, prayer is the best thing that they can do.
We need Jehovah’s blessings on all these projects,
and we need Jehovah’s blessings on all those who can volunteer
that are working on these theocratic facilities.
The construction and renovation work being done today
is but a preparation
for the grand renovation and rehabilitation of this planet
to happen in the future
at a time when all will be able to participate.
Looking back at all that’s been achieved with this program,
I feel good.
I feel happy and good
in a spiritual sense.
It reminds me a lot of what the psalmist said in Psalm 127,
that “unless Jehovah builds the house,
it is in vain that its builders work hard on it.”
So all the glory and honor obviously go to our God.

每次都要长途跋涉去别的弟兄家里用
现在不用那么辛苦了！
分区监督和他们的妻子
都有了合适而且固定的新宿舍
这样他们就能够好好地休息
专心研读
而且为探访工作做好准备
造福弟兄姐妹
最近三年
在尼日利亚
我们遭受了好几次的洪灾
每次协调委员会都会先开始救灾工作
照顾弟兄姐妹的基本需要
然后LDC就会看看哪些建筑物需要重建
着手落实项目
灾难发生的时候
我们的崇拜设施和弟兄姐妹的家
都有可能受影响
一些弟兄姐妹没有能力自己重建或维修房子
这时LDC就会帮忙
他们会先了解实际的情况和需要
然后派合适的人去现场开展工程
除了前面提到的天灾
尼日利亚还遭受了很多人祸
有不少地方有暴乱
弟兄姐妹不得不逃难
而当他们重返家园的时候往往发现
他们的房子已经被损毁得很厉害
甚至完全烧没了
所以当局势平稳一些的时候
LDC就会去关心这些弟兄姐妹的需要
目前我们有25个房子需要重建
18个房子需要维修
如果你想参与分部地区内的灾后重建工程
就必须填写相关的申请表
比如填写DC-50
可以申请成为LDC的志愿人员
填写A-19可以申请做短期的志愿人员
填写A-8可以申请做全时志愿人员
支援LDC的工作
很多人可能会说
我能做的不多
只能为大家祷告
但其实祷告也是很关键的
因为所有工程项目
都需要耶和华赐福才能成功
而且参与工程的弟兄姐妹
也需要耶和华的帮助
现在我们的建筑还有翻新工作
都是在为将来新世界
更大规模的重建工作做好准备
到时人人都有参与的机会
回顾LDC完成的工程项目
我觉得很好！
我非常开心
感觉跟耶和华更亲近了
就像诗篇127篇说的
“要不是耶和华建造家宅
建造的人就徒劳无功”
所以，所有的荣耀和赞美
都要归给耶和华！

Our past experiences were similar.
