ko.text: 모든 미디어 시설을 한 곳으로 모으는 것입니다.
프로젝트가 시작되면 우린 항상 일이 빨리 진행되길 바라죠.
하지만 실제론 우리가 원하는 만큼 빨리 진행되지 않을 때가 있습니다.
여러 해 동안 계획하고 준비해 오는 과정에서
예상치 못하게 조정을 해야 했던 적이 많이 있었습니다.
뉴욕주에서는 연중 특정한 시기에만 나무를 벨 수 있습니다.
나무를 벨 수 있도록 허락된 기간은 11월에서 3월 말까지입니다.
라마포 타운 위원회는 우리가 나무를 벨 수 있도록 특별 허가를 내주었죠.
우리는 또 다른 기관의 허가를 받아야만
나무를 벨 수 있다는 걸 알게 되었습니다.
원래는 약 12주 안에 모든 벌목 작업을 마칠 계획이었죠.
큰 장비를 사용하는 걸 기준으로 잡은 기간이었어요.
그 기간 안에 못 하면 1년을 더 기다려야 나무를 다 벨 수 있었죠.
그런데 허가장에 있는 어떤 표현이 눈에 확 들어왔습니다.
그걸 보고 나무를 다른 방식으로 자르는 것이 가능하겠다는 생각이 들었죠.
결국 나무를 자를 수 있게 됐습니다.
우리는 외부 업체를 사용해서 4주 만에 나무를 다 자를 수 있었습니다.
벌목 가능 기간이 끝나기 2주 전에 다 끝낸 것이죠.
그 외에도 필요한 허가들을 받기 위해 매일 할 일이 많이 있습니다.
설계가 진행 중이고 공사에 무엇이 필요할지 파악하는 일을 계속하고 있습니다.
작업이 지연되는 동안 기다리고 있던 일부 형제 자매들은
조직 내에서 다른 임명을 수행해야 했습니다.
이 형제 자매들은 기술이 있고 훈련을 받았고 어떤 일이든 할 준비가 되어 있었지만,
우리는 지부와 본부의 여러 부서들과 논의를 했습니다.
도움이 더 필요하다고 기도해 왔다는 걸 알게 되었습니다.
허가가 날 때까지 그 일을 하시다가 다시 원래의 일을 하시게 될 겁니다.”
컴퓨터부 엔지니어링 일을 하게 될 거라고 들었는데,
못 할 것 같았죠. 해 본 게 건축밖에 없었으니까요.
하지만 이 일을 좋아하게 됐어요. 많은 걸 배웠죠.
우리가 라마포에서 일할 수 있었던 건 정말 큰 특권이었습니다.
하지만 지금도 우리는 여호와의 조직의 중심부에서
믿음이 강한 이 형제 자매들은 새로운 임명을 수행하면서
허가를 받기 위해 기다려야 했던 경우들이 있었지만
우리는 기다리는 동안 여러 베델 부서들과 중앙장로회 위원회들,
전문가 형제 자매들과 일할 수 있었습니다.
그들의 조언 덕분에 건물의 설계를 변경할 수 있었죠.
또 어떻게 여러 부서가 공간을 함께 사용해 효율성을 높일지 살펴봤죠.
미술부는 오디오/비디오 관련 부서들과 같은 건물에 있게 될 것입니다.
그렇게 하면 함께 일해야 할 때 훨씬 쉽게 협력할 수 있고
오디오/비디오 작업과 미술 작업을 할 수 있는 최첨단 시설이 될 것입니다.
업계의 기술이 계속 바뀌고 조직의 필요도 계속 변할 겁니다.
그럴 때에도 유용하게 사용할 수 있는 시설이 되도록 설계하고 있습니다.
추후에 최신 기술을 적용하기 위해 조정을 해야 할 수 있죠.
그럴 때에도 건물을 허물 필요가 없도록 설계하고 있고
그렇게 되면 지금뿐만이 아니라 미래에도 잘 사용할 수 있는
미디어 센터의 한 가지 흥미로운 특징은
가상 배경을 보여 주는 비디오 벽이 될 것입니다.
이미 이곳 패터슨에서는 이 신기술을 활용하고 있죠.
비디오 벽을 사용하면 디지털 가상 배경을 만들 수 있고,
그렇게 되면 마치 다른 곳에서 촬영하는 것 같은 효과를 낼 수 있습니다.
중앙장로회는 동영상 제작에 참여하는 형제 자매들의
형제 자매들이 촬영 때문에 장기간 출장을 가게 되면
영적 일과가 방해를 받을 수 있죠.
가상 배경을 활용하면 여행을 하고 일하는 시간이 줄어들어서
영적인 활동이 지장을 덜 받게 될 것입니다.
때때로 어떤 상황 때문에 다른 장소로 이동해서 촬영할 수 없는 경우가 생깁니다.
멈추지 않고 스튜디오에서 촬영을 계속할 수 있을 겁니다.
필요에 맞게 실제 성서 시대 땅처럼 보이도록 배경을 만들 것입니다.

en.text: The specific purpose of the Ramapo project
is to bring all media facilities
under one roof.
As a project begins, we always want things to move fast.
But sometimes the reality is
that it doesn’t happen as fast
as we would like it to.
It’s been several years
of some pretty dynamic planning,
and we’ve seen a lot of twists and turns
and changes along the way.
We’ve had a number of challenges
on the Ramapo project.
In the state of New York,
there’s only a certain season when you can take trees down.
We’re only allowed to remove trees
between November and the end of March.
The town board approved the special permit for us to be able to cut the trees.
However, when we went to exercise that permit,
we realized that another agency
still had to give their permission for us to be able to use it,
which we didn’t get.
Originally we had planned
about 12 weeks to do all of this work.
And that 12 weeks included using mechanized equipment.
If that wasn’t accomplished, we would be waiting an entire year
to be able to cut those trees.
Well, the window started closing from 12 weeks to 8 weeks
all the way down to 6 weeks.
And then somehow, something in the permitting language
opened our eyes to a new possibility
that allowed us to take the trees down in a different way.
We got permission to cut the trees,
but we had to cut the trees all by hand.
And in four weeks,
we used an outside contractor
to take down all the trees that we needed . . .
. . . two weeks early of the end of the tree-cutting season.
Every single day there’s still much work to be done
to get us the needed permits.
The design is continuing,
and the estimating for the project is continuing.
That hasn’t stopped.
That hasn’t slowed up one bit.
Because of some of the delays that we experienced,
there was a need to reassign some of our brothers and sisters
within the organization.
We had these willing volunteers.
They were skilled; they were trained; they were willing to do whatever was needed,
but we just didn’t have the work for them at the time.
We were able to communicate with different departments
in the branch and at headquarters.
And it just so happened that many of these departments
had been praying for additional help.
The brothers had a meeting with us, and they said:
“We know you’re not 100 percent busy like you want to be.
“We’ll be giving a number of you new assignments.
“Most of you will go out for a while
while we get our permits and come back.”
They said that I would be going into CDE,
and I didn’t even know what that was: Computer Department Engineering.
And I thought: ‘That’s way above me.
I’m a construction girl.’
But actually, I’ve loved it.
I’ve learned so much.
And the team that I’ve worked with,
I’ve gotten close to them, and it’s been a wonderful change.
It’s really shown us that Jehovah is going to take care of us.
For us to be at Ramapo
was one of the most amazing privileges we’ve ever had.
But we’re still working for Jehovah
and right in the center of his organization.
These brothers and sisters are real men and women of faith,
helping to advance Kingdom interests in all these other areas.
Obviously, when we hit some of these points where maybe we were waiting on approvals,
the work did not stop.
The time has allowed us to work with the Bethel departments,
to work with the Governing Body committees,
to work with our outside expert audio/video design teams.
And so because of that, the buildings themselves have changed.
It was looked into. How could flexible spaces be created?
And also how could some of these spaces be shared
maybe between different departments
to make the best use of the property that we have?
The Art Department will be in the same building
with the other aspects of media
—the audio part and the video part—
so that when we need to collaborate,
it will be much easier to work together
and we can make the very best possible product.
It’s a state-of-the-art audio/video and art production facility.
The process of designing that and getting it to stay ahead
of not only the ever-changing technologies that we see in the industry
but also the needs for the organization
is a dynamic process.
The facility has been designed
and will be constructed in such a way
that if modifications need to be made later
to keep up with technology,
we won’t have to deconstruct the building
in order to implement those changes.
We’ve developed beautiful studios
that will be functional not only now
but also for future projects.
One exciting feature of the media center
will be the use of video walls for virtual production.
In fact, we’ve already begun filming with this new technology here at Patterson.
With these video walls,
we can create digital backgrounds
that can be used to give the appearance
that we are shooting it in a foreign location.
The Governing Body made it very clear that their focus
was the spirituality of those
who are involved in our productions.
If the friends have to be off-site for long periods of time filming,
it can really disrupt their spiritual routine.
Virtual production will allow us to reduce the need to travel
or to even work hours
that could interfere with spiritual activities.
There are some circumstances that arise
that can sometimes limit our ability to travel to another location.
But with the use of the video wall, we won’t be stopped.
Video production will continue in the studio.
Now we’ll be able to custom-make some backgrounds
that actually look like Bible lands.

cn.text: 拉马波这个建筑工程修建的目的
就是把所有的多媒体设施集中在一起
这个工程开工后
我们一直希望能加速进程
但实际上有时工程进度
并没有我们想象的那么快
我们花了几年的时间
为这个项目做计划和准备工作
但我们不得不多次进行调整
我们在拉马波这个项目上遇到了一些挑战
根据纽约州的政策
每年只有一段特定的时间才可以砍伐树木
政府规定
我们只能在11月到3月底之间砍伐树木
拉马波镇委员会
批准了我们砍伐树木的特别许可证
但是当我们准备好去砍伐树木的时候
才意识到我们还需要另一个机构的许可证
但这个许可证我们还没有
起初
我们计划用12个星期来完成所有这些工作
这还是在有大型机械设备帮助的情况下
如果我们不能在这期间完成
就要再等一年
才能砍伐树木
我们眼看着留给我们的时间
从12个星期到8个星期
再到只剩6个星期了
但这时
我们突然发现
我们已经得到的许可证里
包含一个条目说
我们可以用另一种方式来砍伐树木
所以我们可以去砍伐树木了
但是只能人力砍伐
我们雇用了一个外面的承包商
他们在四个星期内
帮我们砍伐了所有需要的树木
在规定的时间结束前两个星期终于做好了
为了获得各类许可证
我们每天都需要做很多事情
设计工作一直没有间断
我们也在不断评估并准备工程所需的东西
由于我们的工程被一些因素延误了
所以我们不得不调整一些弟兄姐妹的委派
很多弟兄姐妹受过训练，技巧精湛
也乐意去任何需要的岗位
但可惜我们那时没有合适的工作给他们
在跟总部和分部不同部门的弟兄进行沟通时
我们发现刚好其他部门很需要人
很多弟兄一直祷告求耶和华派人去帮助他们
弟兄们跟我们一起开会
他们说
“我们知道你们很想全心投入这个工作
不过你们当中大部分的弟兄姐妹
会被暂时调整岗位
等我们拿到许可证以后再回来工作”
他们说，我会被委派到CDE工作
我甚至不知道那是什么
全称是“网络通讯小组”
我心想
我完全不是这块料啊！
我只会做建筑方面的工作
但后来我很喜欢新的岗位
学到了很多东西
也跟弟兄姐妹成了很好的朋友
我学到耶和华一定会照顾我们的
虽然对我们来说
能在拉马波服务是我们梦寐以求的事
但现在我们还是在为耶和华服务
还是在尽力支持耶和华的组织
这些弟兄姐妹的信心给了我们很大的鼓励
他们在新的岗位上继续全心为耶和华服务
虽然我们正在等待政府批准一些手续
但我们的工作却没有停下脚步
工程推迟的这段时间
我们有机会跟伯特利的不同部门
中央长老团的不同委员会
以及在地区里
有专业建筑设计经验的弟兄姐妹合作
听取了他们的意见后
我们也对建筑的设计作出了调整
我们研究过以下问题
怎样让我们的办公空间更灵活多变
以及怎样让不同部门之间
可以共用这些办公空间
充分善用组织的资源
美术部会跟影音服务部
在同一栋大楼里工作
这样如果这两个部门需要一起合作
就会方便得多
也会让我们制作出更好的成品
这个设施会成为一个现代化的
多媒体制作中心
我们在设计方面要考虑的因素是
科技会更新换代
组织的需要也会调整
所以我们要确保新设施能适应这些改变
虽然这并不容易
但我们满怀期待
新设施的设计和建造方案是
如果日后因为科技的发展
而需要调整的话
我们也不必为了适应这些调整
而对建筑物进行重建
我们已经设计出了既美观又实用的工作室
在现在和未来的项目上都可以使用
这个多媒体中心的一个令人期待的新功能
是使用电视墙制作虚拟场景
事实上
我们已经在帕特森
开始使用这项新技术进行拍摄
有了这些电视墙
我们在工作室拍摄出来的效果
就好像在外面不同的实景拍摄出来的一样
中央长老团非常明确地告诉我们
他们最看重的
就是那些参与制作的弟兄姐妹
跟耶和华的关系
如果弟兄姐妹不得不长时间在异地拍摄
这会打乱他们的崇拜常规
但如果我们在工作室拍摄
弟兄姐妹就不用牺牲聚会和传道的时间
去参与外景的拍摄工作了
有时，一些突发状况

但是随着电视墙的使用
这个问题就得到了解决
我们可以继续在摄影工作室进行拍摄
现在我们已经可以制作出
一些看起来像圣经时代的布景

title: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 자비로우신 “온 땅의 심판관”을 신뢰하십시오

ko.text: 그는 여호와께서 그 도시들을 멸망시키기로 결정하시기 전에
과연 모든 사실을 고려하셨는지 의문을 가졌던 것 같습니다.
“온 땅의 심판관께서 옳은 일을 하지 않으시렵니까?”
아브라함이 그렇게 말한 것은 이해할 만한 일입니다.
여호와 하느님과 우정을 쌓기 시작한 지 얼마 안 되었기 때문입니다.
이제 막 여호와를 알아 가기 시작했으니까요.
나중에 여호와를 훨씬 더 잘 알게 된 뒤에는 그런 질문을 하지 않았을 것입니다.
그런데 혹시 여러분도 진리에 대해 배우면서
비슷한 의문을 가져 본 적이 있으신가요?
‘대홍수 때 죽은 사람은 아무도 부활되지 않는 걸까?
노아에 대해 들어 보지 못한 사람들도 있지 않을까?
부활의 희망이 없이 영원히 멸망된 걸까?
여호와의 천사의 손에 죽은 아시리아 군인 18만 5000명 가운데
기회가 주어졌다면 회개할 가능성이 있었던 사람이
자비로운 “온 땅의 심판관”께서 옳은 일을 하실 것이라는 점입니다.
우리가 그 질문들에 대한 답을 모르는 게 맞나요?
대홍수 때 죽은 사람들이나 소돔과 고모라에서 멸망된 사람들에게
소돔과 고모라에 사는 사람들은 정말 악했고,
하지만 그들이 그게 잘못이라는 걸 알았을까요?
롯과 그의 가족은 그들에게 얼마나 증거했을까요?
그들이 회개하고 여호와에 관한 지식을 얻도록 도왔더라도
아무런 성과가 없었을 것이라고 자신 있게 말할 수 있습니까?
여호와의 표준을 배워 알게 된 뒤에도
소돔 사람 단 한 사람도 회개하지 않았을 것이라고 단정적으로 말할 수 있을까요?
그리고 예수께서 마태복음 11장에서 하신 말씀도 유의해 볼 만합니다.
네 가운데서 행한 기적을 소돔에서 행했더라면,
그곳이 오늘날까지 남아 있었을 것이기 때문이다.
심판날에 소돔 땅이 너보다 더 견디기 쉬울 것이다.”
소돔에서 의로운 사람 10명을 찾으면 그 도시를 멸망시키지 않겠다고 말했습니다.
의로운 사람 10명을 찾을 수 있었을 것이고
그 도시가 멸망되지 않았을 것이라는 뜻이었을까요?
또한 여호와께서 에스겔 16장에서 불충실한 유다에게 하신 말씀도 생각해 볼 만합니다.
소돔 사람들이 부활되지 않는다면 유다 사람은 어떨까요?
그러면 소돔과 고모라가 “영원한 불의 사법적 처벌”을 받았다는 유다의 말은
이 말씀은 그 도시들 자체에, 그리고 아마도 많은 주민들에게 적용되겠죠.
그러면 그 주민들 중 아무에게도 희망이 없는 걸까요?
예수의 말씀을 볼 때 일부 사람들에게 희망이 있는 것 같습니다.
분명한 건 우리가 단정할 수 없다는 겁니다.
하지만 자비로운 “온 땅의 심판관”께서 옳은 일을 하실 것입니다.
이전에는 대홍수 때 죽은 사람들이 부활되지 않을 것이라고 설명했습니다.
그 마음속 생각의 모든 성향이 항상 악했다”고 알려 줍니다.
모두가 노아의 소식을 들을 충분한 기회가 있었습니까?
노아의 가족은 방주를 만드느라 매우 바빴을 겁니다.
전파 활동을 할 시간이 얼마나 있었을까요?
그들에게 격지 봉사를 갈 시간이 있었을까요?
가끔씩 보면 베델 반경 20킬로미터 이내에도 여호와의 증인을 모르는 사람이 있는데요.
노아와 그가 하고 있던 일에 대해 알고 있었다고 단정 지을 수 있습니까?
그리고 당시 사람들 중 누군가에게 충분한 기회가 주어졌더라도
그가 계속 여호와를 배척했을 것이라고 말할 수 있습니까?
물론 여호와께서 그들을 부활시키시지 않는다 해도
그들은 삶을 누렸고, 삶 자체는 누구에게나 과분한 것이죠.
아시는 것처럼 아담과 하와가 죄를 지었을 때
여호와께서는 그들을 곧바로 멸망시키실 수 있었지만
따라서 여러분과 제가 살아 숨 쉬는 모든 순간순간이
여호와의 과분한 친절이라고 할 수 있습니다.
또한 여러 해 동안 우리 출판물에서는
성경에서 조상들과 함께 장사되었다고 알려 주는 사람들이
성경은 그에 대해 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
“솔로몬은 조상들과 함께 잠들어 그의 아버지 다윗의 도시에 장사되었다.”
이전에 우리는 조상들과 함께 장사된 사람들이
그리고 아시는 것처럼 인류의 공통 무덤은 천년 통치 중에 비워질 것입니다.
하지만 이렇게 생각해 볼 필요가 있죠.
성경 필자들이 어떤 사람이 조상들과 함께 장사되었다는 표현을 사용한 것은
그가 받게 될 최종 판결을 밝힌 것입니까?
그들이 어떤 판결을 받게 될지 알려 주신 것입니까?
아니면 성경 필자들은 단순히 그 사람이 어떻게 매장되었는지를 알려 준 것입니까?
성경 시대에는 매장되는 방식이 매우 중요했습니다.
요셉과 야곱은 이집트에 매장되기를 원하지 않았습니다.
대제사장 여호야다는 선한 일을 많이 행했기 때문에
예언자가 어떤 왕이 ‘나귀가 묻히듯 묻히게’ 될 것이라고 말하면
솔로몬은 역사상 두 번째로 지혜로운 사람이었습니다.
여호와께서는 그에게 두 번째로 나타나셨을 때 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
“너희와 너희 자손이 나를 따르지 않고 돌아서[고]
가서 다른 신들을 섬기고 그들에게 몸을 굽히면,
나는 이스라엘을 내가 준 땅에서 끊어 버릴 것이다.”
그는 ‘다른 신들을 섬겼고 그들에게 몸을 굽혔습니다.’
온 땅의 심판관께서는 그를 어떻게 보실까요?
따라서 우리는 조상들과 함께 장사되었다고 언급된 사람들의 미래에 대해
성경 표현은 단순히 그들이 매장된 방식을 알려 주는 것일 수 있죠.
우리가 확실히 알 수 없다는 거죠.
우리는 여호와에 대해 무엇을 알고 있습니까?
예언자 요엘 시대에 하느님의 백성은 영적으로 병들어 있었습니다.
그들은 바알과 금송아지와 신성한 기둥을 숭배했습니다.
무고한 피를 흘리며 고아와 과부를 압제했죠.
분노하기를 더디 하고 충성스러운 사랑이 풍부하여,
재앙에 대해 다시 생각해 볼 것이기 때문이다.”
그렇게 많은 잘못을 했는데도 여호와께서는 자비를 보이려고 하셨습니다.
많은 형제들은 그들이 진리 안으로 들어오기 전에 모르고 저지른 죄를
여호와께서 용서해 주실 것이라는 사실을 전혀 어려움 없이 받아들입니다.
여호와께서 결코 잊지 않고 용서하지 않으실까 봐 걱정하죠.
이스라엘 백성이 여호와께 헌신한 상태에서 죄를 지었는데도 그분은 말씀하셨습니다.
‘너희가 악한 일을 그만두고 옳은 일을 한다면 내가 다시 생각해 보겠다.’
자신의 잘못을 여호와께서 결코 용서하지 않으실 거라고 생각하는 형제 자매들에게
읽어 주기 좋은 구절인 것 같습니다.
“그러나 내가 악인에게 ‘네가 반드시 죽을 것이다’ 하고 말한다 해도,
그 악인이 자기의 죄에서 돌아서서 공의와 의를 행하여, …
그가 지은 죄 가운데 어느 것도 문제시되지 않을 것이다.
그는 공의와 의를 행하였으니, 반드시 계속 살 것이다.”
영적으로 약해져서 어쩌면 잘못을 저지른 사람에게
여호와께서 용서해 주지 않으실까 봐 두려워합니다.
진리 안으로 돌아오고 싶고 여호와께 돌아오고 싶지만
“그가 지은 죄 가운데 어느 것도 문제시되지 않을 것”이라고 하셨습니다.
므낫세왕을 보면 그 점을 알 수 있죠.
그는 헌신한 상태였지만 생애 대부분의 기간 동안 악한 일을 했습니다.
돌이켜서 옳은 일을 하자 여호와께서는 그를 온전히 용서해 주셨습니다.
정말 우리가 섬기는 하느님은 놀라울 정도로 자비로운 분이 아닙니까!
그분이 언제라도 근거만 있으면 자비를 베푸신다는 것을 알 수 있죠.
이제 여호와께서 니네베 사람들을 어떻게 대하셨는지도 살펴보겠습니다.
하지만 여호와께서는 요나보다 훨씬 자비로운 분이셨습니다.
니네베 사람들이 회개하고 돌이키자 그들을 용서해 주려고 하셨습니다.
그들이 “옳고 그른 것조차 구별하지 못했기” 때문입니다.
마태복음 12:41에 나오는 예수의 말씀을 보면 부활될 사람이 있는 것 같습니다.
“심판 때에 니네베 사람들이 이 세대와 함께 일어나 이 세대를 정죄할 것입니다.
그들은 요나가 전파한 것을 듣고 회개했기 때문입니다.
그러나 요나보다 더 큰 이가 여기 있습니다.”
이런 예들을 볼 때 무엇을 알게 됩니까?
니네베 사람들, 므낫세, 그 밖의 사람들은 악했고 잘못을 저질렀습니다.
오늘날에는 심판할 권한이 다른 분에게 주어졌습니다.
심판하는 일을 모두 아들에게 [심판하는 일을 모두 아들에게] 맡기셨습니다.”
예수께서 “산 사람과 죽은 사람을 심판”하실 권한을 받으셨습니다.
우리는 그분이 자비를 나타내실 것임을 확신할 수 있습니까?
“[그는] 자기 눈에 보이는 대로 재판하지 않고
자기 귀에 들리는 대로 책망하지 않을 것이다.
땅의 온유한 자들을 위해 올바르게 책망할 것이다.”
예수께서 받으신 권한에는 죽은 자들을 부활시킬 권한도 포함됩니다.
아시다시피 여호와 하느님께서는 죽은 사람들에 대해 모든 점을 알고 계십니다.
하지만 예수께서 부활시키는 일을 하실 것이기 때문에
그분도 죽은 자와 산 자에 대해 모든 점을 알고 계시다고 결론 내릴 수 있습니다.
그분은 누구를 부활시킬지 정확하게 판단하실 것입니다.
그분이 기름부음받은 자들에게도 부활시킬 권한을 주실 것인지는
이 자리에 없었던 사람에게 어떻게 설명하시겠습니까?
“소돔과 고모라 그리고 대홍수 때 죽은 사람들 중 일부는 부활된대.
누가 부활될지 부활되지 않을지에 대해 단정적으로 말해서는 안 된다는 것입니다.
하지만 우리는 여호와 하느님과 예수 그리스도를 신뢰합니다.

en.text: By means of an angel,
Jehovah God told his dear friend Abraham
that he was going to destroy the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.
The angel said:
“The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah
“is indeed great,
and their sin is very heavy.”
Abraham was troubled.
He apparently wondered
whether Jehovah had taken all of the factors into consideration
before he made that decision to destroy the cities.
So he asked:
“Will the Judge of all the earth not do what is right?”
Well, we can understand why Abraham would ask that question.
It was early days in his relationship with Jehovah God.
He was just beginning to get acquainted with Jehovah,
and we can hardly imagine him asking the same question later
when he knew Jehovah much better.
But have you ever asked a similar question,
maybe when you were just coming into the truth?
Have you ever asked, for example:
“Will none of those who died in the Flood get a resurrection
“—even those who may never have heard of Noah?
“And what about Sodom and Gomorrah?
“Will everyone who died in Sodom and Gomorrah
“sleep an everlasting sleep
“—the women, the children, the babies?
“And was there not one redeemable Assyrian soldier
“in that band of 185,000 who died
at the hand of Jehovah’s angel?”
We don’t have the answer to those questions.
But we do know one thing:
The merciful “Judge of all the earth” will do what is right.
Wait a minute.
Did I hear that right?
We don’t have the answer to those questions?
I thought we did.
In the past, our publications have stated
that there’s no hope of a resurrection
for those who died in the Flood or those destroyed in Sodom and Gomorrah.
But do we really know that?
The men of Sodom and Gomorrah were certainly wicked,
and they deserved to die for what they did.
But did they know any better?
How often did Lot and his family preach to them?
And are we saying that if special pioneers
had been assigned to Sodom,
they would have had no success whatsoever in preaching to the Sodomites,
helping them to turn around and come to a knowledge of Jehovah?
Can we say dogmatically
that not one Sodomite would have repented
if Jehovah’s requirements had been explained?
And then there’s the fascinating statement
made by Jesus found in Matthew chapter 11
—I’ll give you a moment—Matthew chapter 11.
And we’re going to read verses 23 and 24.
This is interesting
—Matthew 11:23, 24:
“And you, Capernaum, will you perhaps be exalted to heaven?
“Down to the Grave you will come;
“because [and notice this] if the powerful works
“that took place in you had taken place in Sodom,
“it would have remained until this very day.
“But I say to you
“it will be more endurable for the land of Sodom on Judgment Day
than for you.”
“It would have remained
until this very day.”
Jehovah’s angel had told Abraham
that if ten righteous men could be found in Sodom,
the city would not be destroyed.
So was Jesus saying that if he had preached
and performed powerful works in Sodom,
ten righteous men would have been found
and the city would have been spared?
It’s also of interest
to consider Jehovah’s words to unfaithful Judah
in Ezekiel chapter 16.
Jehovah said that the citizens of Sodom
were more righteous than the inhabitants of Judah.
So if Sodom is doomed, what about Judah?
But what about the disciple Jude’s statement
that Sodom and Gomorrah would undergo
“the judicial punishment of everlasting fire”?
Well, that certainly will prove true of the cities
and probably many of the inhabitants as well,
but does it mean that there’s no hope for any of them?
Jesus’ statement we just read
would indicate that there is hope for some.
We just can’t be dogmatic.
But again, we can say that the merciful “Judge of all the earth”
will do what is right.
Now let’s talk about the Flood of Noah’s day.
In the past, we’ve said that any who died in the Flood
would not be resurrected.
But does the Bible say that?
Now, Noah’s contemporaries certainly were wicked,
and the Bible says that “man’s wickedness was great on the earth
“and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart
was only bad all the time.”
So those living at that time were sinners,
but did they all get a thorough witness?
Noah and his family must have been very busy building the ark.
How much time did they have for preaching?
And were they able to do seldom-worked territory?
We have found that people who live within ten miles (16 km) of Bethel
have never heard of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
So can we guarantee that everyone living on earth
during that time knew of Noah and what he was doing?
We can’t really say that.
And can we say that if someone had been given an adequate opportunity,
he still would have turned his back on Jehovah?
We just can’t say that.
Now, of course, if Jehovah didn’t bring them back,
they wouldn’t have any grounds for complaint.
They’ve had life,
and life is more than any of us deserves.
As you know, when Adam and Eve sinned,
Jehovah could have destroyed them right away.
But instead, he gave them the opportunity to have sons and daughters.
And as a result, we were born.
So the fact that you and I
have drawn one breath
is pure undeserved kindness on Jehovah’s part.
Now, on the other hand, for many years it was suggested
that all those who the Bible says were buried with their forefathers
were going to have a resurrection.
Solomon was one of those.
The Bible says of him:
“Then Solomon was laid to rest with his forefathers
and was buried in the City of David his father.”
Well, we reasoned that those who were buried with their forefathers
were in the common grave of mankind,
and we know that the common grave of mankind is going to be emptied
during the Thousand Year Reign of Christ.
But we ask ourselves:
‘When Bible writers said that someone was buried with his forefathers,
‘were they really revealing what Jehovah’s final judgment would be?
‘Was Jehovah revealing to them —inspiring them to say—
‘how he was going to settle the case?
‘Or were the Bible writers really saying
‘that this is the way the person was buried
—this is the manner of his burial?’
Remember, in Bible times, the way someone was buried
was very important.
Joseph and Jacob refused to be buried in Egypt.
High Priest Jehoiada was buried with the kings of Judah
because of all the good things he had done.
And when a prophet said that a certain king
was going to have “the burial of a donkey,” that wasn’t good.
Solomon was the second wisest man ever to walk the earth.
Jehovah appeared to him twice, and the second time he appeared to him,
he said: “If you and your sons turn away from following me
“and . . . you go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
I will cut Israel off from the surface of the land.”
What did Solomon do?
He began to “serve other gods and bow down to them.”
How will the “Judge of all the earth” view that?
That’s not for us to say.
So we can’t be dogmatic about the prospects
of those who are said to be buried with their forefathers.
It could be that the Bible
was just indicating the manner of their burial.
Now, that isn’t to say that they won’t be resurrected.
It simply means that we don’t know.
The righteous Judge knows, and we know that he’ll do the right thing.
Well, what do we know about Jehovah?
Why can we trust him to do the right thing?
Well, look at the record.
In the days of the prophet Joel,
God’s people were in a sick spiritual condition.
They were worshipping the Baals and the golden calves and the sacred poles.
They were lying, committing adultery, stealing,
shedding innocent blood, oppressing widows and orphans.
Jehovah had good reason to wipe the whole nation out.
And yet, what do we read at Joel 2:13?
Joel says: “Rip apart your hearts,
“and not your garments, and return to Jehovah your God,
“for he is compassionate and merciful,
“slow to anger and abundant in loyal love,
and he will reconsider the calamity.”
“He will reconsider the calamity.”
After all that, Jehovah was willing to show mercy.
Now, this is very encouraging.
Why?
Many of our brothers have no trouble accepting the fact
that Jehovah will forgive the sins they committed in their ignorance
before they came to a knowledge of the truth.
But if they’ve committed a sin after baptism,
they’re afraid that Jehovah will never forget and he will never forgive them.
And yet, what do we see here?
The nation of Israel was in a dedicated situation before Jehovah,
and yet Jehovah said: ‘If you stop doing what is wrong
and if you start doing what is right, I will reconsider.’
Then you have the encouraging words found in Ezekiel chapter 33.
Let’s read this.
I find that this is a good passage to read to brothers and sisters
who may feel that Jehovah could never forgive them for what they’ve done.
Ezekiel 33:14, 16
—verse 14 first:
“And when I say to the wicked one:
“‘You will surely die,’
“and he turns away from his sin
“and does what is just and righteous, . . .
“[verse 16]
“none of the sins he committed will be held against him.
“For doing what is just and righteous,
he will surely keep living.”
Now, isn’t that encouraging for someone who strayed from the truth,
maybe got involved in some bad conduct?
Far too many of these ones
are afraid that Jehovah will never forgive them.
They would love to come back to the truth, and they would love to come back to Jehovah,
but they’re afraid that Jehovah is not going to accept them.
And yet he says:
“None of the sins he committed will be held against him.”
The case of King Manasseh makes the point.
He was in a dedicated relationship with Jehovah,
and yet for most of his life, he did what was wrong.
But when he repented, turned around,
and started doing what was right,
Jehovah wiped the slate clean.
What a marvelous, merciful God we worship!
It shows that Jehovah will show mercy
whenever he sees a basis for doing so.
Now, consider how Jehovah dealt with the people of Nineveh
in the days of Jonah.
Their conduct was so bad
that Jehovah was determined to destroy the city,
and Jonah was in agreement with that.
‘Yeah, wipe them all out.’
But Jehovah was more merciful than Jonah was,
and when He saw that the people repented and turned around,
He was willing to forgive them.
Why? The Bible tells us why.
They didn’t “know right from wrong.”
They didn’t know any better.
Will some of those Ninevites be back?
Jesus’ words found at Matthew 12:41
seem to indicate that they will.
He said: “Men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment
“with this generation and will condemn it,
“because they repented at what Jonah preached.
But look! something more than Jonah is here.”
So, what do we see from these examples?
The men of Nineveh, Manasseh, and others
—they were wicked, they did bad things,
they repented, they started to do what was right,
and Jehovah wiped the slate clean.
Well, today, power for judging has been given to someone else.
There’s a different judge of all the earth.
And we read about him in John chapter 5
—John chapter 5—
and we’re going to read verse 22.
I’ll give you a moment.
John 5:22:
“For the Father judges no one at all,
“but he has entrusted all the judging
[all the judging] to the Son.”
Jesus has been given authority “to judge the living and the dead.”
Well, can we trust him?
Can we be sure that Jesus will be merciful?
Absolutely!
He’s the exact image of his Father,
and the prophet Isaiah wrote of him:
“He will not judge by what appears to his eyes,
“nor reprove simply according to what his ears hear.
“He will judge the lowly with fairness,
“and with uprightness he will give reproof
in behalf of the meek ones of the earth.”
The authority that Jesus has been given includes the authority to resurrect the dead.
He’s “the resurrection and the life.”
Now, you know, we often say
that Jehovah God knows everything about those who have died,
and that’s true.
But since Jesus is doing the resurrecting,
it’s reasonable to conclude that he also knows everything
about the dead and the living,
and he is going to be able to resurrect them accurately.
Now, whether he’ll share the power to resurrect
with his anointed brothers when they’re raised to heaven
remains to be seen.
We’ll stay tuned.
Well, what’s the takeaway from this talk so far?
How would you explain it to someone who wasn’t here today?
You would not say,
“Some who died in Sodom and Gomorrah
“and in the Flood are going to be resurrected,
and Solomon isn’t going to be resurrected.”
No, no, no. You wouldn’t say that.
What we’re saying is that we shouldn’t be dogmatic
about who will and who will not be resurrected.
We just don’t know.
But we trust Jehovah God,
we trust Jesus Christ,
and they will do what is right.

cn.text: 耶和华上帝
通过天使告诉他的好朋友亚伯拉罕
他准备毁灭所多玛和蛾摩拉
天使说
“指控所多玛、蛾摩拉的声音实在很大
那里的人罪恶深重”
亚伯拉罕很担心
看起来
他担心耶和华在决定毁灭这两个城市之前
是不是已经考虑过了所有的因素
所以他问
“审判全世界的主难道会处事不公正吗？”
亚伯拉罕这样问
其实我们也很理解
那时候
他刚刚开始跟耶和华上帝建立关系
他还需要进一步认识耶和华
随着他对耶和华的认识越来越深
很可能他不会再问这样的问题
你刚开始学习圣经的时候
是不是也问过类似的问题呢？
比如，你有没有问过
所有被大洪水淹死的人
没有一个会复活吗？
如果他们从来没听说过挪亚呢？
所多玛和蛾摩拉又怎样？
这两个城市里所有的人
都不会被复活吗？
那些妇女、小孩，和婴儿呢？
另外
被天使击杀的
那18万5000个亚述士兵呢？
他们当中的每一个人都是罪有应得的吗？
我们不知道这些问题的答案
但我们可以确信
“审判全世界的主”绝不会处事不公正
等等，你刚才说什么？
我们不知道这些问题的答案吗？
我们知道啊
以前，我们的出版物曾经说
所有被大洪水淹死的人
以及所有在所多玛、蛾摩拉被处决的人
都不会复活
但真的是这样吗？
所多玛、蛾摩拉的男子都很邪恶
他们因自己的罪行应该被处决
但是
他们真的知道是非对错吗？
罗得和他的家人常常向他们传道吗？
假设我们派特别先驱到所多玛去
他们努力地向所多玛人传道
教他们认识耶和华
他们也不会取得任何成果吗？
我们可以绝对地说
如果所多玛人了解了耶和华的要求
他们当中也没有一个人愿意悔改吗？
在马太福音11章
耶稣说了一句很有意思的话
不要着急
马太福音11章
我们会一起读一下第23节和第24节
很有意思
“迦百农啊，难道你会被捧到天上去吗？
其实你会被贬到坟墓里去！
因为
［请你留意］
我在你那里施行的奇迹
要是在所多玛施行出来
那座城就会留到今天了
我告诉你们
在审判日，连所多玛遭受的惩罚
也比你遭受的轻呢”
“那座城就会留到今天了”
耶和华的天使对亚伯拉罕说
如果在所多玛找到10个正义的人
就不会毁灭那座城
那耶稣是在说
如果他在所多玛传道、施行奇迹
就会找到10个正义的人
让城不至于被毁灭吗？
请再想一想
耶和华在以西结书第16章
对不忠的犹大国的人说的话
耶和华说
所多玛人比犹大国的人显得更正义
如果所多玛人都没有机会复活
那犹大国的人呢？
那门徒犹大为什么又说
所多玛和蛾摩拉
会“遭受永恒之火的刑罚”呢？
当然
对这两个城市
和里面绝大部分的人来说是这样
但是不是这两个城里没有一个人
有希望复活呢？
我们刚才读过的耶稣的话显示
有些人还是有希望的
我们不能说得那么绝对
但是，我们可以相信
“审判全世界的主”一定会处事公正
我们再来谈谈挪亚时代的人
以前的出版物说
所有被大洪水淹死的人都不会复活
但圣经这样说过吗？
挪亚时代的人都非常邪恶
圣经说，当时的人
“在地上作恶多端，心里总是想着坏事”
可见，当时的人的确都是罪人
但他们都听过挪亚传讲的信息吗？
挪亚和他的家人都忙着修建方舟
他们有多少时间去传道呢？
他们也有机会去不常探访的地区传道吗？
有些生活在伯特利方圆16公里之内的人
都没有听说过耶和华见证人
那么，我们敢肯定
生活在挪亚日子的人
都听说过挪亚和他传讲的信息吗？
我们不能肯定
另外，我们敢说
就算一个人有充分的机会
听到挪亚传讲的信息
他还是会拒绝耶和华吗？
我们也不能肯定
当然，就算耶和华不复活他们
也没有任何的问题
他们都享受过生命
而生命是我们所有人都不配得到的
亚当夏娃犯罪以后
耶和华可以马上就把他们毁灭
但他没有
他让他们有机会生儿育女
结果，我们有机会出生
所以，我们现在能够活着
能够继续呼吸
都是因为耶和华的分外恩典
另外，有很多年的时间
我们的出版物也说
如果圣经说某个人随祖先长眠
他就有机会复活过来
所罗门就是这样
圣经说
“后来，所罗门随祖先长眠
安葬在父亲大卫的城里”
以前，我们认为人随祖先长眠
就意味着他进入人类共同的坟墓
而这个坟墓在基督统治的千年期间
会变得空荡荡的
但是，请再想一想
圣经执笔者说某个人随祖先长眠
他们真的在透露耶和华最终的判决吗？
耶和华向他们启示了
他对某个人最终的审判是什么吗？
还是，这些圣经执笔者
只是简单地记下某个人怎样被埋葬？
请记得，在圣经时代
人怎样被埋葬非常重要
雅各和约瑟不愿意被埋葬在埃及
大祭司耶何耶大
因为自己的善行
而被人和君王埋葬在一起
先知预告有个国王
会被人“像埋葬驴那样埋葬”
真挺惨的
所罗门是有史以来第二个最有智慧的人
耶和华曾向他显现过两次
第二次向他显现的时候对他说
“如果你们和你们的子孙不再跟随我
反而去跪拜敬奉别的神
我就会把以色列人
从我赐给他们的土地上铲除”
那所罗门怎么做呢？
他后来开始“跪拜敬奉别的神”
“审判全世界的主”怎么看？
我们无权妄断
圣经记载的那些随祖先长眠的人
以后会怎样
我们不知道
很有可能
执笔者只是说他们是怎样被埋葬的
当然，这也不是说
他们没有机会复活
我们只是说
我们不知道
但耶和华知道
他一定会作出公正的判决
那关于耶和华，我们知道什么呢？
为什么他行事绝对公正呢？
来看看他以往是怎么做的
在先知约珥的日子
上帝的子民在崇拜方面非常糟糕
他们崇拜巴力、金牛犊、神木
他们撒谎、通奸、偷窃
杀人流血、欺压孤儿寡妇
耶和华有充分的理由毁灭他们
但是，约珥书2:13怎么说呢？
“你们要撕裂内心，而不是撕裂衣服
要回到耶和华你们上帝的身边
因为他体恤人，怜悯人
不轻易发怒，有忠贞的厚爱
他会改变主意，不把灾祸降下”
“他会改变主意”
尽管以色列人罪恶滔天
但耶和华还是愿意表现怜悯
这真的让人很受安慰
为什么呢？
很多弟兄姐妹在认识真理之前
犯过严重的罪
但他们都相信
耶和华会宽恕他们之前犯下的罪
但如果他们受浸之后又犯了罪
他们就认为耶和华永远不会忘记
也永远不会原谅他们
但圣经怎么说呢？
所有的以色列人也都是献身给耶和华的
但耶和华还是说
“如果你们停止犯罪，开始做对的事
我就会改变主意”
以西结书33章的经文也令人很受安慰
有些弟兄姐妹觉得自己犯了罪
所以耶和华永远不会原谅他们
这几节经文对他们会很有帮助
以西结书33章14和16节
14节说
“我对邪恶的人说
你一定死
如果他不再犯罪，反而做公平正义的事”
16节说
“他犯的一切罪，都不会被追究
他做公平正义的事
就一定会活下去”
对那些犯了罪，离开真理的人来说
这几节经文是不是令人安慰呢？
他们很多人都以为
自己永远不会得到耶和华的宽恕
他们很想回到真理中
回到耶和华身边
但他们觉得
耶和华不会接受他们
可是经文说
“他犯的一切罪，都不会被追究”
玛拿西王就是个很好的例子
他已经献身给耶和华
但他几乎一生都在行恶
后来他悔改、回头，开始做对的事
耶和华就把他的罪一笔勾销
我们崇拜的上帝多么伟大，多么仁慈
这也让我们看出
只要有机会，耶和华就会表现仁慈
请再想想
耶和华怎样对待尼尼微城的人
他们作恶多端
所以耶和华决定毁灭这座城
约拿也非常同意
“对！把他们全都消灭”
但耶和华比约拿要仁慈得多
后来，尼尼微城的人悔改、回头之后
耶和华就乐意宽恕他们
原因就是
“他们连是非对错也分不清”
他们犯罪是出于无知
有些尼尼微人会复活吗？
从耶稣在马太福音12:41的话来看
有些人会复活
耶稣说
“审判的时候
尼尼微人会跟这一代人一同起来
而且会定这一代人有罪
因为尼尼微人
听了约拿传讲的信息就悔改了
但你们看
这里有一个比约拿更重要的人”
从这些例子看出什么呢？
尼尼微人、玛拿西，以及其他人
他们都很邪恶，也犯下严重的罪
但他们悔改、回头，开始做对的事
耶和华就把他们的罪行一笔勾销
现在，审判的权力转交给了另一位
这位新的审判官是谁呢？
我们可以读一下约翰福音第5章
约翰福音第5章
我们会一起读一下第22节
约翰福音5:22说
“父亲不审判任何人
倒把审判的事全都交给儿子”
耶和华赐给耶稣权力
让他审判活人和死人
我们可以信赖耶稣吗？
他也会富于怜悯吗？
毫无疑问
因为他完美地反映天父的特质
先知以赛亚说
“他施行审判不单凭眼见
提出责备也不仅凭耳闻
他按照公正审判卑微的人
本着正直提出责备
造福地上谦和的人”
耶稣得到的权力也包括把死人复活过来
他“就是复活，就是生命”
我们常常说
耶和华了解去世的人的一切
没错
但既然现在耶稣做审判的工作
他也应该了解所有的活人
和死人的一切
他会本着公正把人复活过来
当然
他会不会让那些受任命的基督徒
也有能力复活人？
我们还不知道
我们拭目以待
那我们都学到什么呢？
你会怎样向一个没有在场的人解释呢？
你不会说
“所多玛和蛾摩拉的人
以及被大洪水淹死的人
有些会复活
但所罗门不会”
不不不，不是这样的
我们学到的就是
关于谁会被复活，谁不会被复活
我们不能说得那么绝对
因为我们都不知道
但我们知道的是
耶和华上帝和耶稣基督
一定会作出公正的判决

title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 미래에 있을 여호와의 심판에 대해 우리는 어떤 점들을 알고 있습니까?

ko.text: 하늘에 계신 사랑 많은 우리 아버지 여호와께서 온 땅을 자비롭게 심판하는 분이며,
그분의 아들 예수 그리스도도 그러하다는 점을 생각해 보았습니다.
우리는 그분들이 올바른 판결을 내리실 것임을 확신할 수 있죠.
여호와와 예수께서는 사람들의 마음속에 무엇이 있는지 아십니다.
그리고 여호와께서 세우신 완벽한 공의의 표준을 오랜 세월에 걸쳐 지켜 오셨죠.
그러면 앞으로 큰 환난 때 있을 심판은 어떠합니까?
우리가 이해하고 있는 점을 조정할 필요가 있을까요?
그 점을 살펴보기 전에 먼저 생각해 보시죠.
최근 몇 년 동안 큰 환난 중에 일어날 일과 관련해서 몇 가지 이해의 조정이 있었습니다.
진리 안에 오랫동안 계신 분이라면 헷갈릴 때가 있을지 모릅니다.
내가 지금 아는 게 과거의 이해인지 최신 이해인지 말이죠.
그러면 큰 환난 중에 일어날 일들에 관해 우리가 잘 이해하고 있는지
다음 영상을 보면서 함께 복습해 보실까요?
그때에 정치 세력은 거짓 종교 세계 제국에 주의를 돌려
그 상징적인 매춘부에 대한 혐오감을 드러낼 것입니다.
그 결과 모든 거짓 종교 조직이 멸망될 것입니다.
그것이 큰 환난의 최종 부분이 될 것입니다.
여호와와 그분의 왕국과 땅에 있는 그분의 백성을 반대하는 모든 자들과 전쟁을 벌일 것입니다.
이것이 바로 “전능자이신 하느님의 큰 날의 전쟁”입니다.
이제 큰 환난의 시작과 끝에 대해 살펴보았으니까 또 다른 질문에 대해 생각해 보죠.
큰 환난이 시작해서 끝나기까지 얼마나 걸릴 것입니까?
분명한 건 그 시기에 여러 사건들이 일어날 것이라고 예언되어 있다는 점입니다.

에스겔 33:11에서는 ‘여호와께서 악인의 죽음을 기뻐하지 않으신다’고 말합니다.
우리는 여호와와 예수께서 각 사람에게 공정하고 의롭고 자비로운 판결을 내리실 것임을 알고 있습니다.
‘와! 새로 배운 내용이 정말 많네’ 하는 생각이 드시나요?
앞으로 나올 「파수대」에 우리가 오늘 배운 내용이 자세히 실릴 것입니다.
그러면 우리는 앞으로 어떤 일을 계속해야 합니까?
가능한 한 많은 사람들에게 좋은 소식을 계속 전파해야 합니다.
그렇게 계속 전파하면서 심판하는 일은 여호와와 예수께 맡겨야 한다는 점을 기억합시다!
그분들은 언제나 올바르고 자비롭고 공의롭게 일하실 것입니다.

en.text: So, what is the takeaway point up to this time?
I’m sure we got the point.
It’s helped us to think about our loving, heavenly Father, Jehovah,
as the merciful Judge of the entire earth,
and his Son, Jesus Christ.
Yes, we can trust them
to make proper judgments.
We know that Jehovah and Jesus can read hearts.
And they have a long record
of living by the perfect standards of justice that Jehovah has set up.
So, what about the future judgments
during the great tribulation?
Is there something that we can adjust with regard to our understanding?
Well, before we start to do that, let’s be quite frank.
Over the last few years, we’ve had a few changes
with regard to the events that occur during the great tribulation.
And if you’ve been in the truth for a while,
sometimes it’s a bit hard to remember,
‘Was that what we used to believe, or is this what we believe now?’
So to help us to make sure that we’ve got some idea
of some of the events that occur during the great tribulation,
let’s look at this review.
What event starts the great tribulation?
The destruction of Babylon the Great.
That will be the time when the political powers
turn on the world empire of false religion,
showing their disgust for the symbolic prostitute.
This will lead to the destruction
of all false religious organizations.
What event ends the great tribulation?
The battle of Armageddon.
That will be the final part of the great tribulation.
Jesus, along with the resurrected 144,000
and myriads of angels, will battle
with all those who oppose Jehovah,
his Kingdom, and his people here on earth.
This will be “the war of the great day of God the Almighty.”
Now that we have the start
and the end of the great tribulation in mind,
let’s ask a few more questions.
How long will that time period be
from start to finish?
The answer is we don’t know.
We do know that many events
are foretold to happen during that time period.
But these events may all occur
in a reasonably short period of time.
For this discussion, though,
let’s focus on the few events that will occur
toward the end of the great tribulation.
When does the attack of Gog of Magog occur?
It doesn’t occur at the beginning of the great tribulation
but toward the end of that period of time.
This attack on God’s people by a coalition of nations
will lead right into the battle of Armageddon.
So Gog’s attack will occur just prior to Armageddon.
When will the remaining ones of the anointed
be gathered and taken to heaven?
The Bible book of Ezekiel indicates
that when Gog of Magog starts his attack,
some of the anointed will still be here on earth.
However, Revelation 17:14 tells us
that when Jesus battles with the nations,
he will come with those “who are called and chosen,”
that is, all of the resurrected 144,000.
So the final gathering of his chosen ones must occur
after the start of the attack of Gog of Magog
and before the battle of Armageddon.
This means that the anointed will be gathered and taken to heaven
toward the end of the great tribulation, not at the beginning.
When will the final judgment of the sheep and the goats take place?
Again, although we can’t be dogmatic
as to the exact sequence of events,
it appears that the final judgment takes place
at the end of the great tribulation,
not at the beginning.
That will be the time “when the Son of man comes in his glory,
and all [his] angels with him.”
Of course, there are a lot of other events
that are foretold to happen during this time period,
but for now, let’s just focus on these few events,
all of which will happen just before the outbreak of Armageddon.
What do we learn from them?
First, Jesus’ judgment of the sheep and the goats
and the destruction of the wicked
will take place at the end of the great tribulation.
Second, there will be some of the remaining ones
of the anointed on earth
until the start of the attack of Gog of Magog,
right at the end of the great tribulation.
Third, the judgment
of the sheep and the goats
will include their dealings
with Christ’s brothers,
even during the great tribulation.
So that is a review of what we already believe.
So if you were writing down notes (“oh, that’s a new point”),
be careful what you say to others.
But how do these basic facts
(when we look at the things that occur
toward the end of the great tribulation, how do they)
affect our understanding
of Jehovah’s judgments by means of Jesus Christ?
Well, we know that the closer we get to the great tribulation,
the clearer our understanding is of what will occur.
Yes, our understanding is clarified according to the proper time
and also in a way that will help us not only to endure the great tribulation
but also to prosper during that period of time.
So, what we’re going to do
is consider four very interesting questions.
Yes, and I’ve got some time left.
The first question is,
Once the great tribulation starts
(we saw there in the chart
with the destruction of Babylon the Great, so once it starts),
is there a door of opportunity
for nonbelievers to actually join us
in serving Jehovah?
Is there a door of opportunity?
What have we said in the past?
We’ve said, “No, there will not be an opportunity
for people to join us at that time.”
Now, why did we say that?
Well, basically, we viewed the account of the Flood
as being a type and antitype portrayal.
And we thought the fact that the door of the ark was closed
prior to the Flood coming
indicated that the door of opportunity would close
once the great tribulation started.
But, of course, it’s true; Jesus did compare the time of Noah
with the presence of him as a reigning King.
But notice, Jesus didn’t say anything
that indicated this was a type-antitype arrangement,
and he certainly didn’t mention
anything with regard to a door of opportunity closing.
So let’s think about that question again.
Once the great tribulation starts,
is there a door of opportunity still available?
Well, to answer that, looking at this time chart,
remember, the judgment
of the sheep and the goats
—the final judgment—occurs when?
Not at the beginning,
but toward the end of the great tribulation.
So let’s think about some whom we know
—perhaps unbelieving relatives, disfellowshipped ones,
others who have heard the message and perhaps have studied with us.
Could some of them,
once they see the destruction of Babylon the Great,
decide that what Jehovah’s Witnesses were saying
is correct after all?
Could they take a stand for the truth?
Well, if they changed their hearts and joined us,
would we be disappointed?
Now, we can’t be dogmatic,
but we don’t want to be like Jonah
and say: “Oh, no, no. The door is closed, no, no.”
You see, we need to remember other cases in the Scriptures that help us
to understand how Jehovah as a merciful Judge
has dealt with people in the past.
For example, think about the Israelites when they left Egypt.
Please, if you turn with me
to Exodus chapter 12,
Exodus chapter 12,
and we’re going to read the first part of verse 38.
So here it’s describing the Exodus,
and Exodus 12:38 says:
“And a vast mixed company
also went with them.”
Now—do you notice?— there’s a footnote there.
And what does it say?
“That is, a mixed company of non-Israelites,
including Egyptians.”
So, what happened?
Well, during the time when the Ten Plagues came upon the Egyptians,
obviously some of these Egyptians
started to see the distinction
between Jehovah and the false gods that they worshipped.
So when decision time came
and the Israelites were leaving Egypt,
some of these Egyptians joined the Israelites.
Now, isn’t that interesting for us to note?
But, of course, we might be thinking:
‘Yes, well, I understand why we said what we did before,
‘but is it really the case that all these ones whom we’ve studied with
‘or so on (some of them) may have a chance
‘to join us after Babylon the Great is destroyed?
‘Is that fair?
Last-minute repentance.’
But, you see, are we imitating the merciful “Judge of all the earth”?
Really, we shouldn’t be surprised if that were to happen, should we?
And think about it.
As we looked at the time chart, we saw that this is
a time period prior to the final judgment.
So anyone who takes their stand for Jehovah early in the great tribulation
will still face the attack of Gog of Magog,
and that will be a very, very difficult time.
But now, what do we need to note with regard to this?
Well, just as in the first century, in 66 C.E.,
decision time came
and many decided to go and leave Jerusalem at that point.
Now, they made their decision
based on what they already knew and had heard.
So, in a similar way,
our preaching work today is of utmost importance.
Let’s notice what the apostle Paul said,
as recorded in the book of Romans
And as we read this,
think about the context of what we’re talking about
—when Babylon the Great is destroyed.
So the time prior to that, we see it says in verse 13:
“For ‘everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.’
“However, how will they call on him
“if they have not put faith in him?
“How, in turn, will they put faith in him
“about whom they have not heard?
“How, in turn, will they hear
without someone to preach?”
Do you see why our preaching work is so urgent and important today?
Yes, many take the opportunity to make a decision right now.
But could it be that once the great tribulation starts,
many who have heard the message
that Jehovah’s Witnesses have preached
may be in a position then
to make the right decision, the right choice?
Well, again, we can’t be dogmatic,
but we certainly hope that that would be the case.
Now, while we’re talking about this, let’s talk about the elephant in the room.
Hmm, what do we mean?
Well, you know, some of us in the past
(we’re not going to mention names, but yet some of us) have said:
“Oh, you know, my unbelieving relative—
I hope he dies before the great tribulation.”
Aha! We know what you’ve been saying.
We’ve said: “Because if he dies before the great tribulation,
“he’ll have a chance of a resurrection.
But during? Uh-uh.”
But let’s think about that.
You see, does someone’s eternal salvation
depend on when they die?
Or does it depend on, really, their heart condition?
You see, the merciful Judge of the earth
knows their heart condition.
And, really, what are we thinking if we ask that question?
You know, are we imagining Jehovah saying to Jesus: “Look, at this person.
“You know, they really should die forever.
“But look at it!
“They died now before the great tribulation.
Oh, no! We have to resurrect them”?
I mean, really?
Jehovah is the righteous, merciful Judge.
He knows people’s hearts.
You can’t fool him or trick him.
So that was the first question I’m sure you found interesting, yeah?
Once the great tribulation starts,
does the door of opportunity close?
The answer is, well, we’ll have to wait and see.
But according to the Scriptures,
it is a possibility that some can take a stand for the truth.
Second question:
When does the preaching of the good news of the Kingdom finish?
Good question.
For a start, let’s remember
that the good news is only good news to us and to those who accept it.
As Psalm 2 mentions, though, for the rest of the world,
it’s never been good news, has it?
So, what does Matthew 24:14 tell us?
It tells us that ‘the good news is going to be preached,’
and “then the end will come.”
Let’s look at our timeline again.
What is “the end” referred to there?
Well, it’s the final part of the great tribulation.
So that means that during the great tribulation,
the good news of the Kingdom
will still be preached.
And it’s still good news to us
but not to the rest of the world.
That good news will become
more hard-hitting as time goes on,
causing people to make a decision one way or the other,
whether they accept the Kingdom or not.
So isn’t that yet another reason why we shouldn’t be surprised
that some may take a stand for the truth
even during the great tribulation?
The third question:
All those who die during the great tribulation,
will they go into eternal death
and never be resurrected?
Well, initially, we can say the goats
are not going to be resurrected —are they?—
because they’re going to “everlasting cutting off,”
according to what Jesus said.
And in 2 Thessalonians chapter 1,
it speaks of the “punishment of everlasting destruction”
being meted out.
But what time period are we talking about?
Well, let’s look at our timeline again.
You see, this is referring to the time
when Jesus comes with his holy ones.
So looking at our timeline,
what does it show us?
That this is at the very end of the great tribulation
when people are judged as being goats.
Specifically, they have been given this judgment.
But there are some other questions that come up.
You see, these ones who are judged as goats
(those who receive everlasting destruction)
obviously have had adequate opportunity (have had a full opportunity)
to accept or reject the Kingdom.
But what about those prior to that final judgment?
So the great tribulation starts.
We’re not sure how long it goes,
but each day it goes on, there are people who no doubt will die.
Do you realize that every day worldwide
about 150,000 people die
either of natural causes or wars, sicknesses, and so on?
So, what about those ones?
They’re not actually killed by Jehovah as a punishment.
So, what do we need to remember?
The merciful Judge knows who should be resurrected
and who shouldn’t be resurrected.
So we can’t be dogmatic about those ones who may die at that time.
We know that Jehovah and Jesus will do the right thing.
Now, another final interesting question:
Will all those living during the great tribulation
have a full opportunity
to decide either for the Kingdom or against it?
How would you answer?
Don’t say it out loud.
The simple answer is, we don’t know,
and we don’t need to know because we’re not the judges.
It’s above our pay grade.
But now, there may be a little voice in you saying: ‘But why don’t we know?
I mean, I’ve always believed that during that time, that’s it.’
But, you see, each day, as we mentioned,
150,000 people on average die,
but 350,000 new babies are born each day.
So even if the great tribulation was only a few days long,
each day you’ve got more babies being born.
And what about areas where the good news
hasn’t reached to the greatest extent,
maybe in lands where our work is restricted?
We might be wondering, ‘Well, will we get to preach to every individual?’
Matthew 10:23, if you look at it later,
seems to indicate that maybe we won’t.
So, now, here’s an interesting question:
Is it reasonable for us to say that Jehovah and Jesus
automatically label millions of people as goats
even though they have never had a full opportunity to respond?
Interesting question.
If they haven’t had a full opportunity and they die at that time,
is it possible that they may receive a resurrection
as unrighteous persons?
What’s the answer?
We simply don’t know.
We can’t be dogmatic,
and we shouldn’t be dogmatic because we don’t know.
But, rather, let’s take comfort in what we do know.
And what do we know?
We know that Jehovah and Jesus are merciful,
that they will always do the right thing.
At Ezekiel 33:11, what does it say?
‘Jehovah takes no delight in the death of a wicked person.’
He wants them to change.
And we know that Jehovah and Jesus will judge each individual
in a balanced, righteous, and merciful way.
Well, now, at this point, you think:
‘Wow! That’s a lot to take in.’
Maybe your hand is a little tired from taking notes.
Don’t worry.
An upcoming Watchtower
is going to give us all the details on this, so stay tuned.
But in the meantime, what do we need to keep doing?
We need to keep preaching the message to as many people as possible.
We have no idea what results may come from that.
And as we keep on preaching, remember,
leave the judging to Jehovah and Jesus!
They will always  do the right thing,
the merciful and just thing.
Of that we can be absolutely confident!

因为那些以前跟我们学习过圣经的人
他们看到大巴比伦被毁灭之后才想要悔改
想要加入我们
这不公平

但不要忘记，审判全世界的主非常仁慈
如果他让人那时有机会悔改
我们也不该惊讶
请想想，我们看时间表的时候会留意到
我们讨论的是最终审判之前的一段时间
如果有人决定
在大患难开始的时候支持耶和华
他们还是要面对歌革的攻击
这也是一个很大很大的考验

比如在公元1世纪
在公元66年
很多人要决定
要不要离开耶路撒冷
什么帮助他们作出明智的选择呢？
就是他们听到的事和已经了解到的情况
同样的道理
我们今天传讲的信息也非常重要
请看看使徒保罗是怎么说的
在罗马书
读的时候，请你记得
我们讨论的时间就是
大巴比伦被毁灭之前
经文说
“所有呼求耶和华圣名的人，都会得救

你明白为什么今天的传道工作

一直以来都听到耶和华见证人传讲的信息
大患难开始之后

作出明智的选择
正确的决定呢？
我们不完全清楚
但我们肯定希望会有这样的人
说到这里

我们当中有一些人
我们不会提你的名字，放心好了
有些人心里会这么想

我们知道你心里是怎么想的

一个人能否得救

还是根据的是他的内心情况呢？
审判全世界的主了解所有人的内心情况
而且你不觉得期待家人早点死

你能够想象耶和华对耶稣说

但是

这有可能吗？
耶和华是仁慈而公正的审判官
他能够看透人心，你根本骗不倒他
这就是我们要讨论的第1个问题
也就是大患难开始之后
得救的大门还会开着吗？
答案就是

但根据圣经的记载

诗篇第2篇指出

马太福音24:14是怎么说的呢？
经文说
“好消息会传遍天下
到时末日就会来到”

经文说的“末日”指的是什么时候呢？
指的是大患难的最后阶段
也就是说
在大患难期间
我们还需要继续传讲上帝王国的好消息

这也可以帮助我们理解

我们从时间表还能看出什么呢？

很显然

是接受还是拒绝上帝的王国

平均来讲

但可以肯定耶和华和耶稣
一定会作出公正的审判
现在，我们就来到了最后的一个问题
所有在大患难期间活着的人

你会怎么回答？
不要那么大声
简单来说

我们不需要知道
因为我们不是审判官
这跟我们没有关系
但也许你的心里有个声音在说
“为什么我们不知道？
我一直觉得到了大患难，过了就过了”
刚才提到
平均每天全球都会有15万人死去
另外
平均每天全球还会有35万个婴儿出生
所以，就算大患难只会持续几天
每天还是会增加很多新生的婴儿
另外，在世界上的有些国家、地区
我们还不能做彻底的见证
比如我们的活动受限制的地区
我们可能会想
我们有机会向每一个人传道吗？
你以后可以看一下马太福音10:23
看来我们做不到
这就带来了一个问题
如果有数以百万计的人还没有充分的机会
对王国的信息作出反应
耶和华和耶稣会自动地
给他们贴上山羊的标签吗？
值得想想
如果他们没有充分的机会作出回应就死了
那他们有机会
作为不正义的人被复活过来吗？
你怎么回答？
简单来说
我们不知道
我们不想说得那么绝对
因为我们
真的不知道
但我们可以因为自己知道的事而感到安慰

就是耶和华和耶稣非常仁慈
他们永远都会处事公正
以西结书33:11是怎么说的？
耶和华“绝不喜欢邪恶的人死亡”
我们可以确信
耶和华和耶稣
会本着合理、公正、仁慈的原则
对每个人作出判决
到这里，你可能会想
“哇，太多要点了吧！”
可能你的手记笔记都记酸了
别担心
以后会有《守望台》的文章
详细地解释这些要点
敬请期待
与此同时，我们需要继续怎么做呢？
我们需要继续向更多的人传道
我们不知道还有多少人会接受真理
而我们传道的时候也要记得
要把审判的事交给耶和华和耶稣

titles.ko: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 미래에 있을 여호와의 심판에 대해 우리는 어떤 점들을 알고 있습니까?

titles.cn: 杰弗里·杰克逊：关于将来的审判，我们知道什么？

title: 제프리 윈더: 어떻게 빛이 점점 밝아집니까?

ko.text: 최근 몇 년간 연례 총회에서는 성경 진리에 대한 새로운 이해가 발표되었습니다.
많은 경우 여호와께서는 연례 총회를 통해 새로운 이해를 알려 주셨습니다.
오늘도 빛이 더 밝아지는 일이 있을까요?
오늘 프로그램에서 어떤 내용이 다루어질지 기대해 보시기 바랍니다.
여호와께서는 성경에 대한 조정된 이해, 즉 새로운 빛을 오늘날에 어떻게 밝혀 주십니까?
중앙장로회는 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”으로서 함께 모여서 어떻게 일합니까?
어떤 과정을 거쳐 빛이 더 밝아지나요?
여호와께서는 이해의 조정이 필요할 때 충실하고 슬기로운 종을 어떻게 사용하십니까?
먼저 성경에서 뭐라고 알려 주는지 볼까요?
첫 번째로 여호와께서는 무엇을 사용해 새로운 빛을 비춰 주십니까?
“하느님께서는 그것들을 자신의 영을 통해 바로 우리에게 계시하셨습니다.
영은 모든 것, 심지어 하느님의 깊은 것까지 살핍니다.”
여호와께서는 무엇을 사용해 새로운 빛을 비추십니까?
바로 성령이죠. 여호와의 영은 진리가 밝혀지는 데 매우 중요한 역할을 합니다.
두 번째로 여호와께서는 누구에게 조정된 이해를 밝혀 주십니까?
그들에게 제때에 양식을 나누어 주게 한 충실하고 슬기로운 종은 과연 누구입니까?”
보신 것처럼 그리스도께서는 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 임명하셨고,
여호와께서는 그리스도를 통해 임명된 그 종을 사용하여 영적 양식을 공급하십니다.
이렇게 해서 두 가지 점을 살펴보았는데요.
여호와께서 영적인 진리, 즉 새로운 이해를 어떻게 전달하시는지 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
그분은 성령을 사용하여 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 통해 그러한 진리를 알려 주시죠.
여호와께서는 언제 새로운 빛을 비춰 주십니까?
종이 “제때에 양식을 나누어” 줄 것이라고 했죠.
여호와께서 언제 빛을 비춰 주시는지 알 수 있지 않나요?
그리고 우리가 그분의 뜻을 수행하는 데 도움이 되는 때에 조정된 이해를 밝혀 주십니다.
네 번째로 여호와께서는 어떤 속도로 새로운 빛을 밝혀 주십니까?
한 번에 쏟아 내십니까, 아니면 서서히 알려 주십니까?
그 질문에 대한 답을 알기 위해 잠언 4장을 펴 보실까요?
“그러나 의로운 자의 길은 아침의 밝은 빛과도 같으니, 한낮에 이르기까지 점점 밝아진다.”
여기 보면 한낮에 이르기까지 밝아지는 빛을 언급하는데요.
자신의 목적을 점진적으로 밝혀 주신다는 점을 잘 보여 줍니다.”
한낮에 이르기까지 빛이 점점 밝아지는 것처럼
성경 진리에 대한 이해도 우리에게 필요할 때,
우리가 그것을 받아들이고 적용할 수 있을 때 점진적으로 밝혀집니다.
실제로 빛이 점점 밝아지면 우리 눈이 적응하기가 쉽습니다.
아브라함 시대에 여호와의 뜻에 대한 온전한 이해가 밝혀졌다면
그가 그것을 받아들이고 이해할 수 있었을까요?
이스라엘 12지파, 모세 율법, 그리스도에 대한 지식, 대속 희생, 1세기 그리스도인 회중,
하늘 희망, 마지막 날, 큰 환난에 대한 세부점 같은 것들 말입니다.
그럴 리가 없었을 겁니다. 그런 지식이 필요하지도 않았죠.
하지만 아브라함은 당시에 여호와를 올바로 섬기는 데 필요한 점들은 알고 있었습니다.
우리는 “참지식이 풍부하게 될 것”이라고 예언된 마지막 때에 사는 특권을 갖고 있습니다.
하지만 그렇다 해도 참지식은 우리가 그것을 받아들이고 적용할 수 있는 속도에 맞추어 밝혀지죠.
우린 그 점에 대해 여호와께 감사합니다.
이렇게 해서 우리가 성경과 경험을 통해 알고 있는 점,
즉 오늘날 진리의 빛이 어떻게 더 밝아지는지 살펴보았습니다.
여호와께서는 성령을 사용하여 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 통해 진리를 밝히십니다.
이러한 점들을 알고 있기 때문에 우리는 필요한 조정을 하는 것에 대해 부끄러워하지 않으며
이전에 정확하게 이해하지 못했다고 해서 사과해야 한다고 생각하지도 않습니다.
우리는 여호와께서 진리를 어떻게 밝히시는지 알고 있습니다.
또한 중앙장로회 성원들은 불완전한 사람들이며, 그들의 말은 성경처럼 영감받은 것도 아닙니다.
따라서 교리나 조직상의 지침과 관련해 실수를 할 수도 있습니다.
그 형제들은 그 시점에 자신들이 알고 있는 것을 근거로 최상의 결정을 내리려고 노력하지만,
그것을 기꺼이 받아들이고 형제 자매들에게도 알려 줍니다.
그럴 때 우리는 여호와께서 정하신 때라는 것을 알기 때문에 그러한 조정을 기꺼이 받아들입니다.
그럼 처음에 했던 질문으로 돌아가 볼까요?
성경에서 알려 주는 그런 점들은 이해가 되죠.
그러면 중앙장로회 형제들이 함께 모일 때
여호와께서는 그들이 더 정확한 이해를 갖도록 어떻게 도와주십니까?
여호와께서는 그러한 과정을 비밀스럽게 감춰 두지 않으시기 때문이죠.
초기 그리스도인 회중에서 이해가 조정된 일에 관한 기록을 남겨 두셨습니다.
한 가지 예로 기원 49년경에 구원에 필요한 조건에 대한 정확한 이해를 할 필요가 있었습니다.
문제가 된 것은 이방인 남자들이 구원을 받기 위해
할례를 받고 모세 율법을 지켜야 하는가 하는 점이었습니다.
이것은 회중을 분열시킬 수도 있는 중요한 문제였기 때문에
당시의 중앙장로회였던 사도들과 연로자들이 그 문제를 다루게 되었죠.
갈라디아서 2:2을 보면 바울은 자신이 “계시를 받았기 때문에”
그 문제를 예루살렘의 형제들에게 가져갔다고 말합니다.
그러니까 그리스도께서 이 중요한 교리적인 문제를 인도하는 형제들이 해결하도록 마련하신 겁니다.
그리고 사도행전 15장에서 여호와께서는 우리가 그 모임이 어떻게 진행되었는지 볼 수 있게 해 주십니다.
그들이 어떤 말을 주고받았는지, 성령이 그들을 어떻게 인도했는지,
그들이 어떻게 하느님의 말씀을 사용했고 어떻게 결론에 이르게 되었는지,
그리고 그 결정이 어떻게 회중들에 전달되었는지 말이죠.
그럼 그때 어떤 일이 있었는지 사도행전 15장을 보실까요?
“사도들과 장로들이 이 문제를 검토하려고 함께 모였다.”
네, 중요한 문제였기 때문에 당시의 중앙장로회가 검토하게 된 거죠.
그리고 7절을 보면 “열띤 토론이 있었다”고 알려 줍니다.
형제들은 존중심 있는 태도로 자유롭게 이야기하면서 문제에 대한 다양한 생각과 의견을 말했습니다.
아마도 이 삽화가 그 장면을 묘사한 것 같습니다.
베드로는 이야기를 시작하면서 자신이 고넬료와 관련하여 직접 겪은 일에 대해 말하죠.
12절을 보면 베드로의 말에 형제들이 수긍한 것 같습니다.
형제들의 겸손을 느낄 수 있지 않나요?
누구도 자기 의견만을 고집하면서 그것을 받아들이도록 강요하지 않았기 때문입니다.
그들은 한마음으로 여호와의 인도를 따르고자 했습니다.
이런 일이 있은 다음 바울과 바나바가 자신들의 경험을 이야기하기 시작합니다.
더 많은 사실과 증거들을 검토하게 된 거죠.
13절을 보면 이어서 야고보가 성경을 사용해 형제들이 올바른 결론에 이르도록 돕습니다.
그는 여호와께서 ‘이방 사람들 가운데서 자신의 이름을 위한 백성을 모으시려고
그들에게 주의를 돌리셨다’고 말하면서 아모스 9:11, 12을 인용합니다.
25절을 보면 형제들이 만장일치로 결정했다는 점을 알 수 있습니다.
22절에서는 그러한 조정된 이해를 회중들에 알리기 위해 형제들을 보냈다고 알려 줍니다.
또한 성령이 당시에 인도하는 일을 하던 형제들 위에 작용했죠.
살펴보신 것처럼 결정을 내리는 과정은 비밀스럽게 감추어져 있지 않습니다.
오늘날에도 비슷한 과정을 통해 우리의 이해가 조정됩니다.
‘우리 시대에 어떤 영적인 것을 명확히 밝힐 때가 되면,
성령은 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 이전에는 이해하지 못했던 깊은 진리들을 분별하도록 돕습니다.
중앙장로회 전체가 제안된 조정 사항을 함께 고려합니다.
그들은 알게 된 점을 모두의 유익을 위해 간행물에 싣습니다.’
이해를 조정할 때 보통 이런 과정을 거칩니다.
중앙장로회 성원이 개인 연구를 하거나 성경 읽기를 하다가 의문점을 발견할 수 있죠.
혹은 영적 양식을 준비하거나 번역하다가 검토가 필요한 의문점이 생길 수도 있습니다.
또는 세계 사건들 때문에 특정한 예언을 좀 더 자세히 검토해야 할 수도 있죠.
그리고 그 질문은 중앙장로회가 다룰 안건이 되죠.
형제들은 그 문제에 대해 더 깊이 조사할 필요가 있는지 판단을 내립니다.
우리의 이해가 어떻게 조정되어야 하는지 최종적으로 결정을 내리는 것이 아니라
더 깊이 조사할 필요가 있는지 판단하는 거죠.
그럴 필요가 있다고 판단되면 조사 팀이 배정되며
중앙장로회가 검토할 제안 사항과 그와 관련된 자료를 준비하죠.
그러한 조사에는 그 문제에 대해 우리 조직에서 설명해 온 모든 내용,
즉 1879년 이후로 「파수대」에 실린 모든 내용을 정리하는 것이 포함됩니다.
또한 정확한 의미를 파악하기 위해 문맥을 고려하기도 합니다.
만일 평행 기록이 있는 경우라면 그 기록이 우리의 이해에 어떤 영향을 미치는지도 살펴봅니다.
뿐만 아니라 히브리어와 그리스어 원어가 우리의 이해에 어떤 영향을 미치는지도 고려합니다.
조사가 다 끝나면 그 자료를 중앙장로회에 제출하여 검토할 수 있게 합니다.
중앙장로회 성원 각자는 모임에 참석하기 전에 기도하면서 그 자료를 살펴보고 깊이 생각합니다.
그런 다음 중앙장로회 전체가 함께 모여 여호와의 성령을 구하는 기도를 하고 문제를 검토합니다.
중앙장로회 성원들은 토의를 할 때 서두르거나 빨리 결정을 내리자고 재촉하지 않습니다.
자신의 의견이나 생각, 자신이 묵상하거나 조사한 점을 자유롭게 이야기하죠.
그 누구도 자신의 의견을 고집하거나 그것을 받아들이도록 강요하지 않죠.
중앙장로회의 모든 형제들은 여호와께서 그 문제를 어떻게 인도해 주시는지,
그들이 무엇을 하기를 바라시는지 알기를 간절히 바랍니다.
때로는 최종적으로 결정된 내용이 처음에 조사를 할 때 제시된 제안과는 상당히 다른 경우도 있죠.
분명한 건 여호와의 영이 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”에게 작용하여
형제들의 의견이 만장일치가 안 되면 아직 때가 되지 않은 것일 수 있죠.
그러면 다음에 그 문제를 토의하기로 합니다.
나중에, 심지어 몇 년 뒤에 그 문제를 다시 검토할 때는 모두가 동의하는 결정을 내리게 될 수 있죠.
혹은 조정을 하기로 결정하는 과정에서 전에는 알지 못했던 중요한 점들을 알게 되기도 합니다.
형제들은 기도하면서 이런 과정을 거쳐 만장일치로 어떤 결론에 이르게 되면
그것을 여호와의 인도로 받아들이고 형제 자매들에게 알려 줍니다.
이렇게 해서 우리는 오늘날 어떻게 빛이 더 밝아지는지 그 과정을 살펴보았습니다.
우리의 이해가 명확해지는 과정을 아는 것도 흥미로운 일이지만
우리에게 정말 감동을 주는 건 왜 이해가 조정되는가 하는 점입니다.
자신의 내밀한 일을 자신의 종인 예언자들에게 밝혀 주지 않고서는 아무것도 행하지 않는다.”
여호와께서 우리를 신뢰한다는 점이 느껴지지 않습니까?
그분이 얼마나 사랑이 많고 충성스러우신지 느껴지지 않나요?
여호와께서는 자신의 백성을 가르치는 일에 적극적으로 관여하시면서
앞으로 일어날 일에 대비해 우리를 준비시키십니다.
적절한 때에 필요한 점을 이해할 수 있게 해 주시죠.
끝이 점점 더 가까워지고 있고, 사탄의 증오와 그의 공격도 갈수록 거세지고 있습니다.
큰 환난이 점점 더 다가오고 있고, 사탄의 악한 세상 제도가 멸망될 때가 가까워지고 있죠.
따라서 우리는 우리 하느님 여호와께서 우리에게 필요한 지침과 이해를
계속 충성스럽게 베푸실 것임을 확신할 수 있습니다.
우리는 인도를 받지 못해 어떻게 해야 할지 모르는 상태로 있지 않을 것입니다.
우린 어둠 속을 헤매지 않을 것입니다.
“의로운 자의 길은 아침의 밝은 빛과도 같으니, 한낮에 이르기까지 점점 밝아진다.”

en.text: In recent years, the annual meeting has been an occasion
where clarified understanding of Bible truths, new light,
has been announced and explained.
Of course, it’s not at every annual meeting that this takes place,
but when Jehovah makes something known,
often it’s at the annual meeting where it is announced.
Now, will there be new light today?
I think Brother Cook already spilled the beans a bit,
but we look forward to seeing
what is in store for our program.
But have you ever wondered, though,
‘How exactly does Jehovah reveal
‘clarified understanding of the Scriptures,
new light, in modern times?’
When the Governing Body is meeting together
as “the faithful and discreet slave,”
how does it work?
How exactly does the light get brighter?
How does Jehovah use that arrangement
to clarify our understanding?
Well, first of all, what do we know from the Scriptures?
Let’s look at four points.
The first one is this:
By what means does Jehovah reveal new light?
Well, for that, we can turn to 1 Corinthians chapter 2
and read together 1 Corinthians 2:10:
“For it is to us God has revealed them
“through his spirit,
“for the spirit searches into all things,
even the deep things of God.”
So clearly— By what means does Jehovah reveal new light?
It’s by his spirit.
We recognize the key role
that Jehovah’s spirit has in revealing the truth.
Point two:
To whom does Jehovah reveal clarified understanding?
Well, for that we can turn to the book of Matthew chapter 24
and read together Matthew 24:45:
“Who really is the faithful and discreet slave
“whom his master appointed over his domestics,
to give them their food at the proper time?”
So clearly, Christ has appointed “the faithful and discreet slave,”
and it is through this channel that Jehovah, through Christ,
works to provide spiritual food.
So just with those first two points,
it’s very clear to us how spiritual truth, new understanding,
is communicated from heaven to earth by means of the holy spirit
through the channel of “the faithful and discreet slave.”
Question number three:
When does Jehovah reveal new light?
Well, we just have to look back to verse 45 of Matthew chapter 24.
The slave will provide the “food at the proper time.”
There’s a clear timing element indicated there, isn’t there?
And so Jehovah reveals clarified understanding at his time
when it is needed and when it will help us to carry out his will.
Number four:
At what rate does he reveal new light?
Is it all at once, like a dump truck?
Or is it metered out, like a trickle?
Well, the answer to that is found in the book of Proverbs chapter 4
and verse 18
—Proverbs 4:18:
“But the path of the righteous is like the bright morning light
that grows brighter and brighter until full daylight.”
So the Bible here uses the illustration of daylight.
And what does that teach us?
Well, The Watchtower  said: “These words aptly apply to the way
in which Jehovah reveals his purpose to his people—gradually.”
So just as daylight grows brighter and brighter gradually,
a proper understanding of Bible truths comes gradually
as we need it and as we are able to absorb it and use it.
And we appreciate that, don’t we?
It’s easier on our eyes when literal light gets brighter gradually.
And so it is with the understanding of Jehovah’s purpose as well.
For example, think about Abraham.
Could Abraham have handled and absorbed a complete understanding
of Jehovah’s will at his time
—how he would use the 12 tribes of Israel,
the Mosaic Law, the understanding of Christ, the payment of the ransom,
the first-century Christian congregation, the heavenly hope,
the last days, and details about the great tribulation?
No way. He couldn’t handle all of that.
He didn’t need it.
But Abraham had what he needed
to serve Jehovah acceptably during the time that he lived.
Well, we have the privilege to live during the last days
when “true knowledge” was foretold to “become abundant.”
But even still, it is released and made known
at a pace that we can absorb,
that we can handle, and that we can use.
And we thank Jehovah for that.
So this is what we know from the Scriptures and from our own experience as well
about how the light gets brighter in modern times.
It comes about by means of the holy spirit,
through his channel of “the faithful and discreet slave,”
He reveals it gradually, and at a time that it is needed.
Well, knowing this, then, we are not embarrassed about adjustments that are made,
nor is an apology needed
for not getting it exactly right previously.
We understand that this is how Jehovah operates.
He reveals matters gradually when it is needed.
And also the Governing Body is neither inspired nor infallible.
And so it can err in doctrinal matters or in organizational direction.
The brothers do the best they can with what they have
and what they understand at the time
but are happy if Jehovah sees fit to clarify matters,
and then that can be shared with the brotherhood.
And when that happens,
we understand it’s because it’s Jehovah’s time for that to happen,
and we eagerly accept that.
But now let’s go back to our original question.
OK, we understand these things from the Scriptures.
But, really, how does it work?
When the brothers are meeting together, how does Jehovah help them
come to a better understanding of things?
Well, that’s an appropriate question because Jehovah does not intend for it to be
a mystery or overly secretive.
In fact, in his inspired Scriptures,
he reveals examples of when understanding
was clarified in the Christian era.
And a notable example was around 49 C.E.
when clarification was needed regarding the requirements for salvation.
And specifically, the question was this:
Would Gentile males first need to be circumcised
and submit to the Mosaic Law in order to be saved?
This was a significant matter that could have divided the congregation,
and so it was referred to the apostles
and the older men, the governing body, at that time.
And in fact, at Galatians 2:2,
Paul states that “as a result of a revelation,”
he brought the matter to the brothers in Jerusalem.
So Christ himself directed that this important doctrinal matter
be settled by the brothers taking the lead.
And in Acts 15, Jehovah allows us to look in on that meeting
(to be a fly on the wall, as it were) to hear their discussion
—to see how the holy spirit worked with them, how they used God’s Word,
how they came to a conclusion, and then the result
that was sent and conveyed to the congregations.
And the process is not entirely different today.
So let’s take a look at what happened if we turn together to Acts chapter 15.
Acts chapter 15 and beginning in verse 6, it says:
“The apostles and the elders gathered together to look into this matter.”
So this is an important matter.
It’s brought before the governing body of that day.
And then in verse 7,
it mentions that there was “much intense discussion.”
So it was a lively conversation.
The brothers felt free to express themselves respectfully,
but they were sharing their thoughts and opinions
about the different sides of the issue.
And in verse 7, Peter stands.
And maybe this is the point that is reflected in our artwork here.
And Peter begins to speak and relates his comments
based on his real-life experience with Cornelius.
So they’re considering some facts.
And if you look in verse 12, Peter’s words strike a chord
because “the entire group [becomes] silent.”
And in this, we see humility —don’t we?—
because none of the brothers were trying to force their personal opinion
or get their idea approved.
They were collectively looking to Jehovah for direction on the matter.
Well, this makes way, then, for Paul and Barnabas
to begin to explain their experiences.
So there were more facts, more evidence, that they could consider.
And then in verse 13, James speaks up
and he uses the Scriptures to help the brothers
draw a proper Scriptural conclusion.
He applies Amos 9:11, 12, saying that Jehovah
would turn “his attention to the nations
to take out of them a people for his name.”
Well in verses 19-21, he recommends a decision.
Verse 25 indicates that that decision was unanimous.
And then in verse 22, it mentions that they sent the brothers out
to inform the congregation of this clarified understanding.
So in the whole process described there, we see the use of God’s Word,
we see the leadership of the Christ, and the operation of the holy spirit
working through the brothers taking the lead at that time.
And so we can see the process is not intended
to be a mystery or to be overly secretive.
And the process today is not much dissimilar than that.
In 2010, The Watchtower  explained it this way.
It said: “When the time comes to clarify a spiritual matter in our day,
“holy spirit helps . . . ‘the faithful and discreet slave’ . . .
“to discern deep truths that were not previously understood.
“The Governing Body as a whole considers adjusted explanations.
What they learn, they publish for the benefit of all.”
So generally the process happens this way:
First of all, a question comes up.
And so it could be that a Governing Body member in his personal study
or his personal Bible reading notices something that then raises a question.
Or it could be that a question comes up during the preparation
or translation of spiritual food
that requires more consideration.
World events might put the spotlight on a particular prophecy
that then gets closer attention.
So in one way or another, a question comes up.
And that question is then put on
the Governing Body’s agenda for discussion.
And the question is,
Does this require, or warrant,
additional research?
The brothers are not making a final decision on what the new understanding will be
but are just asking, “Does it warrant additional research?”
And if the answer is yes, then a research team is assigned to provide
recommendations and research for the Governing Body to consider.
And this research includes a summary of everything that we have said
(the organization has said) on the subject since 1879
—all of The Watchtowers  on what we have said.
Also, it includes what the context of the verse indicates about its meaning.
Further, what bearing do parallel accounts
have on the understanding of the account, if there are any parallel accounts?
And finally, what impact does the original Hebrew or Greek
have on our understanding of the verse?
Well, once that whole research package is compiled,
it’s placed back on the Governing Body’s agenda for review.
And, of course, once it goes on the agenda,
then each individual member of the Governing Body under prayer
reviews the information and thinks about it in preparation for the meeting.
And then it’s discussed as a group
at the Governing Body meeting again under prayer,
relying on Jehovah’s holy spirit.
Now, when this matter is discussed, the discussion is not rushed,
nor is the decision forced.
But often, like in the first century, it’s a lively discussion
as the brothers feel free to share their opinions and their thoughts
and the results of their meditation and their research.
But there’s also humility there because, again, none of the brothers
are trying to force their idea or are trying to get their thoughts approved.
But there is this collective, unified desire
to see Jehovah’s direction on the matter and where he is steering things.
The goal is to discern Jehovah’s direction on the matter.
And often (or at times, we could say),
the final result might be quite different
than what the research package originally recommended.
But that’s Jehovah’s spirit working through “the faithful and discreet slave”
to bring us to the right decision.
And the brothers are looking for a unanimous decision.
At times, it may seem like this is a solid adjustment,
but if it’s not unanimous,
it just might not be time yet for it to be revealed.
And so it’s not forced.
The matter is set aside.
And it could be that sometime later, even some years later,
the matter comes back up and then it sails right through.
Or maybe it does get approved but now with a couple of key points
discerned that weren’t discerned earlier.
Well, with this thorough process under prayer
and when there is unanimous accord,
then the brothers take that as Jehovah’s direction
and then are happy to share it with the brotherhood.
So this helps us to understand the process,
understand how light gets brighter in modern times.
And while it is interesting to us
how our understanding is clarified,
what really touches our heart is why it’s clarified.
Turn with me, please, to the book of Amos chapter 3.
And notice what Amos 3:7 says:
“For the Sovereign Lord Jehovah will not do a thing
“unless he has revealed his confidential matter
to his servants the prophets.”
Doesn’t that convey Jehovah’s confidence in us?
Doesn’t it indicate his love and his loyalty?
Jehovah is actively involved in teaching his people,
preparing us for what lies ahead.
He’s providing us with the understanding that we need when we need it.
And that is reassuring —isn’t it?—
because as we progress deeper into the time of the end,
as Satan’s hatred intensifies
and his attacks increase,
as we draw closer to the great tribulation
and the destruction of Satan’s wicked system of things,
we can be confident that Jehovah God, our God,
will continue to loyally provide us
with the direction and the understanding that we need.
We will not be left without guidance, unsure where to go or what to do.
We will not be left to stumble in the dark
because Jehovah has said:
“The path of the righteous one is like the bright morning light
that grows brighter and brighter until full daylight.”

cn.text: 最近这几年
我们通常都会在年会上
向大家澄清一些圣经真理
并跟大家分享一些最新的理解
当然，不是每个年会都会这样
但每当耶和华帮我们更明白真理
我们通常都会在年会跟大家分享
那这次年会也会这样吗？
库克弟兄刚才已经剧透了
所以我们真的非常期待观看接下来的节目
你有没有想过这个问题？
在今天，耶和华是怎样帮助我们
更清楚地了解圣经的真理呢？
每当中央长老团
作为忠信睿智的奴隶聚集在一起的时候
他们怎么做呢？
他们怎样在耶和华的帮助下
更清楚地理解圣经的真理
让真理之光变得越来越亮呢？
我们先来看看圣经是怎么说的
我们会讨论4个问题
第一个问题
耶和华用什么揭示真理呢？
为了回答这个问题
请打开哥林多前书第2章
哥林多前书2:10说
“但上帝用他的神圣力量
向我们揭示了这一切
这股神圣力量能显露万事
连上帝高深的事也能显露出来”
很清楚，耶和华用什么揭示真理呢？
就是神圣力量
我们可以看出
在揭示真理方面
神圣力量发挥了多么重要的作用
第二个问题
耶和华向谁揭示真理呢？
请大家打开马太福音第24章
我们会一起读一下24:45
“到底谁是忠信睿智的奴隶
受主人委派管理他的仆役
在适当的时候给他们食物呢？”
经文说得很清楚
基督任命了忠信睿智的奴隶
耶和华让基督通过这个奴隶
向我们提供滋养信心的食物
现在我们讨论完了两个问题
我们简单总结一下
耶和华用神圣力量
通过忠信睿智的奴隶
帮我们对圣经真理有了更清楚的理解
第三个问题
耶和华什么时候进一步揭示真理呢？
我们可以再看一下马太福音24:45
经文说奴隶会“在适当的时候”提供食物
可见耶和华会按照自己的时间表
在最需要的时候
让我们对圣经真理有更深的理解
这也能帮我们继续遵行他的旨意

title: M. 스티븐 레트: 여호와의 하늘 수레가 전진하고 있습니다

ko.text: 사무엘하 15:1에 따르면 압살롬은 왕위를 빼앗으려는 음모를 꾸미던 중에
자기를 위해 왕이 타는 것과 같은 병거를 마련했습니다.
위풍당당한 말들이 끌고 50명이 그 앞에서 호위하게 했죠.
많은 사람의 눈에는 그 병거와 거기 탄 사람이 인상적으로 보였겠지만
에스겔 1장에 나오는 하늘 수레에 비하면 어떠합니까?
압살롬의 병거는 속도도 느리고 볼품없는 고물 같을 것입니다.
아시다시피 에스겔 1장에 나오는 그 하늘 수레는
여호와께서 자신의 뜻과 목적을 이루기 위해
사랑으로 자신의 조직의 활동을 인도하고 계시기 때문입니다.
그 하늘 수레 바퀴의 “테에 빙 둘러 눈이 가득”합니다!
모든 것을 보시는 여호와께서 모든 것을 인도하고 계시는 것입니다.
압살롬의 병거는 시속 72킬로미터까지 달릴 수 있었을 것입니다.
에스겔 1:14에서는 그 하늘 수레가 움직이는 모습을 묘사하고 있는데요.
그 모습이 마치 “번개가 번쩍이는 것 같았다”고 말합니다.
번개가 번쩍일 때 나오는 빛은 초속 30만 킬로미터로, 매우 빠르게 움직입니다.
하지만 생각해 보면 여호와의 수레는 그보다 훨씬 더 빠르죠.
사실 그 수레는 생각의 속도로 움직입니다.
우리로서는 측정할 수 없을 정도로 빠를 겁니다.
물론 우리는 하늘에서 일어나는 일을 볼 수 없습니다.
조직의 하늘 부분을 엄청난 속도로 움직이시는 모습을 볼 수 없죠.
하지만 우리는 여호와의 조직의 보이는 부분이
얼마나 빠르게 움직이는지는 관찰할 수 있습니다.
여호와의 조직의 지상 부분은 하늘 부분과 밀접한 연관이 있고,
사실 하늘 부분에서 일어나는 일을 그대로 반영하기 때문입니다.
이 점을 염두에 두고 아까 쿡 형제가 언급하신
두 가지 프로젝트의 최신 진행 상황에 대해 얘기해 보겠습니다.
여호와께서 인도하시는 두 프로젝트 모두 매우 빠른 속도로 진척되고 있죠.
오늘 제가 속도 얘기를 참 많이 하죠.
진행 상황을 보면 여호와께서 인도하고 계시다는 것을 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
오디오 비디오 시설 건축 공사의 상황에 대해 이야기해 보겠습니다.
이 시설은 협회가 원래 소유하고 있던 부지에 건설되고 있습니다.
워릭에 있는 세계 본부에서 3킬로미터밖에 떨어지지 않은
중앙장로회는 이 부지를 팔려고 여러 해 동안 많은 노력을 했습니다.
그러다가 이 부지가 우리에게 꼭 필요한 시설을 짓기에
현재 여러 곳에서 진행되는 오디오, 비디오, 미술 작업이
한 곳에서 이루어질 수 있도록 모든 미디어 시설을 전부 합치는 겁니다.
여호와의 눈이 모든 걸 살핀다는 것을 보여 주는 또 다른 예죠.
“내가 네게 통찰력을 주고 네가 가야 할 길을 가르치며
네게서 눈을 떼지 않고 충고를 베풀겠다.”
여호와께서는 분명 모든 일을 인도하고 계십니다.
여러분 모두 현재 라마포 공사가 어떻게 진행되고 있는지 궁금하실 텐데요.
그 점을 보여 주는 동영상을 함께 보시겠습니다.
라마포 공사의 구체적인 목적은 모든 미디어 시설을 한 곳으로 모으는 것입니다.
프로젝트가 시작되면 우린 항상 일이 빨리 진행되길 바라죠.
하지만 실제론 우리가 원하는 만큼 빨리 진행되지 않을 때가 있습니다.
여러 해 동안 계획하고 준비해 오는 과정에서
예상치 못하게 조정을 해야 했던 적이 많이 있었습니다.
뉴욕주에서는 연중 특정한 시기에만 나무를 벨 수 있습니다.
나무를 벨 수 있도록 허락된 기간은 11월에서 3월 말까지입니다.
라마포 타운 위원회는 우리가 나무를 벨 수 있도록 특별 허가를 내주었죠.
우리는 또 다른 기관의 허가를 받아야만 나무를 벨 수 있다는 걸 알게 되었습니다.
원래는 약 12주 안에 모든 벌목 작업을 마칠 계획이었죠.
큰 장비를 사용하는 걸 기준으로 잡은 기간이었어요.
그 기간 안에 못 하면 1년을 더 기다려야 나무를 다 벨 수 있었죠.
작업이 가능한 기간은 점점 짧아져서 12주에서 8주, 결국 6주가 되었습니다.
그런데 허가장에 있는 어떤 표현이 눈에 확 들어왔습니다.
그걸 보고 나무를 다른 방식으로 자르는 것이 가능하겠다는 생각이 들었죠.
결국 나무를 자를 수 있게 됐습니다.
우리는 외부 업체를 사용해서 4주 만에 나무를 다 자를 수 있었습니다.
벌목 가능 기간이 끝나기 2주 전에 다 끝낸 것이죠.
그 외에도 필요한 허가들을 받기 위해 매일 할 일이 많이 있습니다.
설계가 진행 중이고 공사에 무엇이 필요할지 파악하는 일을 계속하고 있습니다.
작업이 지연되는 동안 기다리고 있던 일부 형제 자매들은
조직 내에서 다른 임명을 수행해야 했습니다.
이 형제 자매들은 기술이 있고 훈련을 받았고 어떤 일이든 할 준비가 되어 있었지만,
우리는 지부와 본부의 여러 부서들과 논의를 했습니다.
놀랍게도 마침 많은 부서에서 도움이 더 필요하다고 기도해 왔다는 걸 알게 되었습니다.
허가가 날 때까지 그 일을 하시다가 다시 원래의 일을 하시게 될 겁니다.”
