“하느님께서 곧 모든 고통을 없애실 것이라는 점을 들어 보셨나요?”
“지구의 환경이 회복될 것이라는 점을 알고 계셨나요?”
사람들은 적절한 때에 간단한 진리를 듣기만 해도
예수께서는 양들이 자신의 목소리를 들을 것이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
우리가 진리를 간단명료하게 전해 줄 때 진리를 분별할 것입니다.
부록 나는 대화를 계속 이어 나갈지 결정하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
이 새로운 팜플렛에서 배우는 점을 연습해 볼 것입니다.
미리 정해진 주제와 성구를 소개하는 데 초점을 맞추지 않을 것입니다.
학생이 구역 사람들이 관심 있을 만한 주제를 선택해서
우리는 각 사람의 관심사와 필요에 맞게
자연스럽게 대화를 시작하는 기술을 발전시킬 수 있을 것입니다.
우리는 제자 삼는 활동을 더 쉽고 효율적으로 하게 될 것입니다.
과에서 강조하는 특성을 어떻게 나타낼 수 있는지
친절하게 행동하면 왕국 소식을 전할 기회가 생길 수 있습니다.
사람들이 자신의 생각을 말할 때 관심을 갖고 잘 들어 주십시오.
적절한 때에 간단한 진리를 알려 주십시오.
우리의 목표는 외워서 말하는 것이 아니라
만나는 모든 사람에게 그리스도와 같은 사랑을 나타내는 것입니다.
사랑을 나타내는 것만으로도 봉사에서 기쁨을 발견할 수 있을 것입니다.
다른 사람에게 사랑을 적극적으로 표현하는 것이
제자 삼는 일을 하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
효과적으로 봉사하는 데 도움이 되는 이 새로운 도구를 주신 여호와께
이 멋진 새로운 팜플렛을 언제쯤 받을 수 있을까요?
기쁘게도 모든 회중에서 11월 6일에 이 팜플렛을 전자 형태로 받을 수 있고,
또 대부분의 지역에서는 그때에 인쇄본으로도 받아 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
뿐만 아니라 네 부분으로 이루어진 이 심포지엄 전체가
모든 형제 자매들이 이 심포지엄의 내용을 동시에 듣게 될 것입니다.
여러분 모두 팜플렛과 동영상들을 빨리 보고 싶으실 겁니다.
방금 본 소개 동영상에서 들으신 것처럼
중앙장로회는 1월부터 평일 집회에서 이 새로운 팜플렛을 사용할 마련을 했습니다.
우리는 이 팜플렛의 내용을 바로 적용해 볼 기회를 갖게 될 겁니다.
먼저 플리글 형제는 우리가 왜 여호와를 사랑하는지,
또 어떻게 그 사랑이 그분을 찬양할 마음을 갖게 하는지 설명했죠.
자원해서 나실인이 된 사람들 사이의 차이에 대해 알려 주었습니다.
회중 전도인이 더는 야외 봉사 시간을 보고하지 않는다고 해서
제자 삼는 일을 해야 할 우리 각자의 책임이
줄어드는 것은 아니라는 점을 일깨워 주었습니다.
사람들에게 사랑을 나타내고 그들을 제자로 삼는 데 도움이 되는
이사야 60:17의 말씀이 성취되는 것을 보는 놀라운 경험을 하고 있습니다.
의를 너의 작업 임명자로 삼을 것이다.”
이미 좋은 것이 더 좋은 것으로 점진적으로 대체된다는 의미입니다.
그게 지금 바로 우리가 목격하고 있는 일이죠.
축음기와 증거 카드를 가지고 다니면서 정말 열정적으로 봉사했습니다.
축음기를 틀어 주거나 증거 카드를 보여 주었습니다.
같이 봉사하던 파이오니아 자매가 문을 열고 나온 남자에게
아무 말도 하지 않고 증거 카드를 내밀었습니다.
청각 장애인들인데 뭐 하고 싶은 말이 있나 봐.”
그분은 우리에게 효과적인 증거 방법을 가르쳐 주셨습니다.
성경을 사용해서 사람들과 대화하는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
최근에는 「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」라는 놀라운 도구 덕분에
성서 연구를 훨씬 더 잘 사회할 수 있게 되었습니다.
그리고 이번에 나온 팜플렛은 우리가 사람들에게 초점을 맞추고
그들이 관심을 가진 것에 대해 대화하도록 도와줄 것입니다.
그렇게 하는 것은 그들의 마음을 감동시켜 제자가 되게 하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
이러한 조직상의 변화가 있을 때마다 우리는 분명히 볼 수 있었죠.
좋은 것이 더 좋은 것으로 바뀌는 것을요.
그러한 것들도 그 점을 잘 보여 주지 않습니까?
좋은 것이 훨씬 더 좋은 것으로 바뀌었죠.
여호와께서 우리가 그분의 백성으로서 장성하도록 돕고 계신다는 걸
우리가 단지 봉사 시간이나 전한 출판물 개수를 보고하는 데만
우리가 봉사에서 느슨해지고 있다는 의미가 아닙니다.
큰 환난이 다가오고 있는 이때에 우리가 손을 늘어뜨리고 있다는 뜻이 아니죠.
현재 왕국 전파자 학교에 참석하기 위해 지원서를 제출한 사람들의 수가
우리는 새로운 선교인, 새로운 특별 파이오니아,
임시 특별 파이오니아, 수많은 새로운 정규 파이오니아들을 임명하고 있습니다.
놀랍게도 올해 필리핀의 전도인 수가 9퍼센트 증가하여
그러므로 이 점을 꼭 기억하시기 바랍니다.
우리의 전파 활동은 결코 느슨해지지 않았습니다.
우리의 전파 활동은 그 어느 때보다도 지금 중요합니다.
전파 활동을 수행하는 우리의 동기가 더욱 분명해졌다는 것을 의미합니다.
네, 우리가 전파 활동을 수행하는 이유는
따라서 지금은 여호와의 일을 부지런히 수행할 때입니다.
예수께서 말씀하신 주인과 세 종에 관한 비유가 기억나시나요?
그 비유는 우리가 끝이 오기를 기다리면서
무엇을 해야 하는지를 가르쳐 주기 위한 것입니다.
셋 중 두 종은 열심히 일했고 주인의 돈을 두 배로 불렸습니다.
우리도 그들처럼 열심히 부지런히 일하기를 원합니다.
물론 장로와 봉사의 종과 파이오니아들이 봉사에 앞장설 것입니다.
하지만 우리 모두는 더 열정적으로 봉사하면서
각자가 세운 목표를 이루기 위해 계속 최선을 다할 것입니다.
더 많은 사람들이 우리와 함께 여호와를 섬기기를 진심으로 바랍니다.
여호와께서는 자신의 백성이 보이는 충실함과 관대함에 대해
여호와께서 여러분 모두에게 상을 주실 때가 가깝습니다.
그분은 우리가 멋진 하느님 여호와를 사랑하고 제자 삼는 일을 하기 위해 바친
모든 시간과 노력에 대해 풍성한 상을 주실 것입니다!
1부에서 우리는 여호와의 증인의 역사에 남을 정말 중요한 내용을 들었는데요.
이번 달 방송을 마치기 전에 아드리아해에 접해 있는 작은 나라인 알바니아로 가 보겠습니다.
알바니아는 여러 나라의 침략을 받으면서 혼란스러운 시기를 겪었습니다.
그러면서 다양한 민족과 문화와 종교가 이 나라에 들어오게 되었죠.
알바니아는 호수와 강이 많은 아름다운 나라입니다. 해안선에는 멋진 해변들이 많이 있죠.
그중에는 스노클링 명소인 아쿠아리움 비치도 있습니다.
알바니아에서 가장 큰 호수인 카라바스타 호수에는 달마티안 펠리컨이 살고 있습니다.
펠리컨 중에서 가장 덩치가 큰 이 새는 몸길이가 최대 1.8미터에 달하죠.
로마서 15장에서 사도 바울은 자신과 동료들이 “좋은 소식을 철저히 전파했다”고 말합니다.
그들은 로마 속주 “일리리쿰에 이르기까지” 여행했는데, 그곳에는 오늘날 알바니아의 일부도 포함되어 있었죠.
당시에 그곳의 일부 사람들이 그리스도인이 되었을 가능성이 있습니다.
역사에 따르면 1세기에 알바니아에서 그리스도교가 자리를 잡았기 때문이죠.
1920년대에 미국에 살던 몇몇 알바니아인들이 성경 진리를 배웠습니다.
그중 일부 사람들이 침례를 받고 알바니아로 돌아가 가족과 친구들에게 귀중한 진리를 열심히 전했죠.
1928년에 라자르 나손과 페트로 스타브로가 미국에서 알바니아로 와서 “창조 사진극”을 상영했습니다.
많은 사람이 진리를 받아들였고 정치적 혼란, 경제 문제,
극심한 반대에도 불구하고 왕국 선포자들의 수가 계속 증가했습니다.
현재 5400명 이상의 전도인들이 89개 회중에서 봉사하고 있죠.
수도인 티라나에 있는 지부 사무실에서 알바니아의 활동을 돌보고 있습니다.
또한 북동쪽의 이웃 나라 코소보의 228명의 전도인도 지원하고 있죠.
알바니아 중서부에 있는 도시인 루슈녀로 가 볼까요?
루슈녀 베리우 회중은 이 도시의 약 3분의 1에 해당하는 지역과
형제 자매들은 이 마을들에서 봉사하면서 좋은 성과를 거두고 있고,
어떤 전도인들은 도시 밖의 마을들에서 살고 있지만 대면 집회에 기꺼이 참석합니다.
루슈녀 베리우 회중에 있는 77명의 전도인들이 여러분에게 그리스도인 사랑과 인사를 전합니다!
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting® for November 2023!
On October 7,
the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society
of Pennsylvania
held its annual meeting.
Usually, you would be viewing
this portion of the program
in January 2024.
However, you are now able to enjoy four talks this month,
November 2023.
These talks have been especially prepared at the direction of the Governing Body.
They want the worldwide brotherhood
to be aware of the content as soon as possible.
Please pay close attention and enjoy the program!
Well, it’s an absolute delight to be here today, isn’t it?
And you’re going to get happier as the morning goes along.
The annual meeting
—as an example, I’m going to pick the year of 2013.
Now, that annual meeting has been called landmark.
We’ve even stated that; we called it a landmark annual meeting.
You might think that all annual meetings are landmark,
and many of us here would agree with that.
But that one was very special.
At that meeting, the revised edition
of the New World Translation in English was released
—a very special annual meeting.
And that landmark Bible release continues to be a blessing
for many people around the earth
as more languages are added.
Now, ten years later,
exactly ten years later,
we have arrived at another truly landmark annual meeting.
This time, Jehovah has helped “the faithful and discreet slave”
to discern deeper principles
and understanding
from that very same Word of truth.
And this understanding is now going to be passed on to you.
Are you ready?
Are you excited to hear it?
Let’s listen very carefully to this next symposium.
And again, each speaker will introduce
the next one on the program.
Please pay close attention to Brother Gage Fleegle
as he begins with the talk entitled
“Love Jehovah—Praise Jehovah.”
The day was Nisan 11, 33 C.E.
Jesus was busy in the temple
teaching just a few days prior to his death.
He silenced the scribes and the Pharisees
with his irrefutable logic,
at the same time sharing some of the most profound teachings
of his earthly ministry
—for instance, “pay back . . . Caesar’s things to Caesar,
but God’s things to God.”
Then one of the scribes came forward
and asked Jesus,
What is “the greatest commandment”?
How did Jesus respond?
His response would have far-reaching implications
even down to our day
for anyone claiming to be a Christian.
We find his response in Mark chapter 12.
I invite you to turn there.
Mark chapter 12—and notice, please, with me verses 29 and 30,
“Jesus answered:
“‘The first [or the most important commandment
“‘—the greatest commandment] is,
“‘“Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah,
“‘“and you must love Jehovah your God
“‘“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
and with your whole mind and with your whole strength.”’”
“You must love Jehovah.”
Love God.
It sounds simple, right?
Well, billions of people claim to love God,
but they love pleasures more,
or they’re willing to fight and kill their fellow man,
or they refuse to live by God’s moral standards.
All such things contradict their claim to love God.
Well, Jesus demonstrated that love of God requires
more than a feeling of affection.
Jesus stressed how completely we must love God
—with our whole heart, with our whole soul,
with our whole mind, with our whole strength.
Does that leave anything out?
our eyes?
our ears? our hands?
Well, the study notes on verse 30 help us to understand
that this includes our emotions, desires, and feelings.
It includes our intellectual faculties and power of reason.
It includes our physical and mental strength.
Yes, our whole being —all that we are—
we must devote to our love to Jehovah.
Love for God must govern a person’s entire life.
Nothing is left out.
Well, shortly after emphasizing the greatest commandment
—and again we’re thinking of Jesus— he’s there in the temple.
Shortly after emphasizing the greatest commandment,
Jesus shines a light on both bad and good examples
of love for God.
First, he sharply condemned the scribes and the Pharisees
for their pretense of love for God.
Now, if you want the full condemnation, it’s found in Matthew chapter 23.
Those hypocrites
—they even gave the tenth, or a tithe, of small, tiny herbs,
but they ignored “the weightier matters of . . .
justice and mercy and faithfulness.”
That was the bad example.
But then Jesus gave his attention
to an outstanding example of love for God.
If you’re still there in Mark chapter 12,
notice starting in verse 41:
“And [Jesus] sat down with the treasury chests in view
“and began observing how the crowd was dropping money into the treasury chests,
“and many rich people were dropping in many coins.
“Now a poor widow came and dropped in
“two small coins of very little value.
“So he called his disciples to him and said to them:
“‘Truly I say to you that this poor widow put in more than all the others
“‘who put money into the treasury chests.
“‘For they all put in out of their surplus,
“‘but she, out of her want, put in everything she had,
all she had to live on.’”
The coins of the needy widow were worth about 15 minutes of wages.
Yet, Jesus expressed his Father’s view of her worship.
He commended her whole-souled sacrifice.
What do we learn?
Well, clearly, the lessons go far beyond material giving.
Motive in our worship of Jehovah is important to him.
Jehovah doesn’t compare us with others
or even previous versions of ourselves —younger versions of ourselves.
Jehovah simply wants love for him
with our whole heart, soul, mind, and strength,
not as they were 10 or 20 years ago,
but as they currently are now.
Now, a question in reference to love for Jehovah,
Is it reasonable for Jehovah to expect us to love him
with our whole heart, soul, mind, and strength?
Is it reasonable?
Yes, absolutely.
Why can we say that?
Because Jehovah loves us
with his whole heart, soul, mind, and strength.
How so?
Well, let’s turn to Isaiah chapters 40 through 44,
and there we’ll consider
a few of the many reasons we have to love Jehovah.
And at the same time, we’ll consider some examples
of the depth of Jehovah’s love for us.
So our first example is in Isaiah chapter 40, and notice, please, verse 11.
Isaiah 40:11—there it says:
“Like a shepherd he will care for his flock.
“With his arm he will gather together the lambs,
“and in his bosom he will carry them.
He will gently lead those nursing their young.”
Here we find a beautiful word picture of Jehovah.
Jehovah is a tender Shepherd.
At Ezekiel 34:15, 16, Jehovah says:
“I myself will feed my sheep . . .
“The lost one I will search for, the stray I will bring back,
“the injured I will bandage [as we notice in the illustration],
and the weak I will strengthen.”
What a touching picture of compassion and tender care!
If we fall and hurt ourselves
or if we stumble in the briar patch, so to speak,
Jehovah bandages us.
He helps us to heal.
When we seek his help, he doesn’t reproach us:
“You should have known better.”
No.
But he does try to help us not to stray in the future
with reminders from his Word.
And what is the effect on the sheep?
Well, as we saw in the illustration, he feels secure in Jehovah’s care.
How do we feel in Jehovah’s care, his compassionate care?
We too feel secure.
We might say that Jehovah loves us
with all his heart—his compassion.
Doesn’t that increase your love for him?
Let’s consider a second reason that we have to love Jehovah.
Isaiah chapter 40 —notice verses 28 and 29.
Verse 28 says:
“Do you not know? Have you not heard?
“Jehovah, the Creator of the ends of the earth,
“is a God for all eternity.
“He never tires out or grows weary.
“His understanding is unsearchable.
“He gives power to the tired one
and full might to those lacking strength.”
With Jehovah’s mighty holy spirit,
he created everything
—beginning with his firstborn Son
to myriads of mighty spirit creatures
to the vast universe
with its trillions upon trillions of stars
to this beautiful earth
with its endless variety of plant and animal life
to the human body

Our ministry involves much more
than counting time.
For this reason,
we are pleased to announce that beginning
November 1, 2023,
congregation publishers will no longer
be asked to report the amount of time
they spend in the ministry.
Nor will publishers be asked to report their placements,
the videos they show, or their return visits.
Instead, the field service report will simply have a box
that will allow each publisher
to indicate that he or she shared
in any form of the ministry during the month.
There will be one more box where publishers
report the number of different Bible studies they conduct.
This simplified report serves a valuable purpose.
It will allow us to know the number
of active publishers in each land.
It will also help us to know whether certain territories
are producing Bible studies
and where there is a greater need for pioneers,
special pioneers, missionaries, and Kingdom Halls.
Although publishers will no longer report their time in the ministry,
we all want to follow faithfully the words
of Colossians chapter 3,
verses 23 and 24:
“Whatever you are doing,
“work at it whole-souled
“as for Jehovah,
“and not for men,
“for you know that it is from Jehovah
“you will receive the inheritance as a reward.
Slave for the Master, Christ.”
The Governing Body is confident that you dear ones
will continue to render whole-souled service to Jehovah
by doing all that you can in his service.
And just as Jehovah richly blessed faithful Israelites
who generously supported the tithing arrangement,
he will richly bless your “sacrifice of praise.”
But wait!
What about the Nazirite arrangement?
Is there a similar provision in the modern-day organization?
Certainly!
We all do well to imitate the Nazirites’ example
of self-sacrifice and courage.
However, as Brother Lösch explained,
the Nazirites had to meet certain requirements
that were not expected of Israelites in general.
The same is true of modern-day pioneers.
They have volunteered to devote a certain number of hours
to spend in the ministry.
Thus, auxiliary and regular pioneers,
special pioneers, missionaries,
and circuit overseers and their wives
will continue to report the number of hours
they spend in the ministry,
along with the number of different Bible studies they conduct.
As you know, the Governing Body recently reduced the hour requirements
for auxiliary pioneers, regular pioneers,
special pioneers, field missionaries,
and circuit overseers and their wives.
It gave us great joy to do that,
and we are convinced that as a result,
even more will be able to join the ranks of the pioneers.
Why are we so confident of that?
Because of what it says at Psalm 110:3:
“Your people will offer themselves willingly
on the day of your military force.”
Yes, Jehovah promises that his people,
and young ones in particular,
will reach out to do more in this time of the end.
Many pioneers eventually attend the School for Kingdom Evangelizers;
they become special pioneers, field missionaries,
and even circuit overseers who serve with their wives.
We thank Jehovah for those who reach out
to serve as pioneers.
But let’s think for a moment
what this adjustment will mean for all of us.
Isn’t it true that reporting our field service activity each month
has served as a reminder?
Our monthly report reminded us to be regular in the ministry,
to use our various publications and videos,
and to make return visits.
But what about now?
Will we still be conscientious
about having an active share in the ministry each month?
Remember that with the tithing arrangement,
each individual was responsible to give their full tithe to Jehovah.
Likewise, each of us will want to set personal goals
to make sure we have a zealous share in the ministry.
Love for Jehovah will move us to have a schedule
to make sure the ministry
continues to take priority in our lives.
What will these adjustments in reporting our ministry
mean for you elders and circuit overseers?
It will be even more important
that you brothers be discerning shepherds.
You will have to know the flock well.
For example,
evaluating a congregation’s spiritual health
or a brother’s qualifications to serve as an elder or ministerial servant
will not simply be a matter of computing averages
—time spent in the ministry, literature placements, and so forth.
No, you will have to know the brothers.
What is their attitude toward the ministry?
Are they zealous for pure worship?
What is their reputation in regard to the ministry?
Do they take advantage of opportunities to give a witness?
Do they help others to do so, including the members of their family?
As we have discussed,
Jehovah clearly deserves our best,
and we demonstrate our love for him
by exerting ourselves in the ministry
and in all other aspects of our worship.
Jehovah loves you for that.
And we love you for that.
We know you will continue to manifest
the spirit expressed at Psalm 54:6.
It says:
“I will sacrifice to you willingly.
“I will praise your name, O Jehovah,
for it is good.”
So we have no doubt that you will continue to give Jehovah
your very best in the disciple-making work.
But is there still more we can learn from the Scriptures
about the way we conduct our ministry?
If so, are additional adjustments
appropriate at this time?
To find out, let us give our attention to Brother Mark Sanderson,
a member of the Governing Body,
who will share the final talk in this symposium,
entitled “Love People—Make Disciples.”
Well, brothers and sisters, hasn’t this been an amazing program?
This is truly a historic day
in the history of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And maybe our hearts right now are more full of love and appreciation
for our wonderful God, Jehovah, than ever before.
We’ve deepened our understanding of Jehovah’s mercy,
his compassion, and his patience.
And what about that announcement about our field service reporting?
Jehovah is dignifying us.
He has confidence in us.
You see, why do we go from house to house?
Why do we do cart work?
Why do we make telephone calls and write letters
and make return visits and start Bible studies?
Why do we do all of these things?
It’s because we truly love
our amazing and wonderful God, Jehovah.
As Brother Fleegle emphasized in his talk,
at Matthew 22:37,
Jesus identified the greatest and first commandment.
Do you remember what he said?
“You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart
and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.”
But is there something else
that moves us to make disciples?
Yes.
It’s what Jesus said was the second greatest commandment.
Jesus said: “You must love your neighbor
as yourself.”
So we must love God,
but we must also love people.
Now, why is love for people so important?
Well, because when we see
that someone cares about us,
we are moved even if we don’t know that person.
For example, maybe someone you’ve never met before does a kind deed for you.
Maybe they open a door for you,
they pick something up that you’ve dropped,
or they help you carry a heavy load.
How do you feel?
Well, you appreciate  their kindness, don’t you?
And as a result, you’re more inclined to want to listen
to what that person might want to say to you.
You see, when we sense that someone has love for us,
we open up our hearts.
Well, unselfish love is so powerful.
It touches the hearts
of those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
And Jesus said
that his true disciples would be identified
—they’d be recognized—
by the love that they had in their midst.
Well, isn’t it true that so often brothers and sisters
say that what it was that drew them to the truth
was the love they felt from their Bible teacher
or from the congregation
when they began to attend meetings?
Well, very likely that same love
was what drew you
to want to become a disciple of Christ Jesus.
Well, for that reason, at the 2017 annual meeting,
the Governing Body encouraged us to begin to think more
about conversing with people.
And at that same meeting, you’ll remember that we simplified
our Teaching Toolbox so that we could become more familiar
with the various tools that we use in the ministry.
You see, we want to carefully consider
each individual’s personal situation
—the concerns that they have, the interests that they have—
and then be flexible in choosing a topic
that we want to discuss with them.
Well, for several years now,
our midweek meetings have provided us with sample conversations,
with suggested scriptures,
and even with a suggested link
to help us to continue the conversation at a later time.
But is there a challenge sometimes with a memorized presentation?
You know, I think back to when I was a brand-new pioneer.
One day, I was out with this sister in the ministry.
As we were going to the door, you know, she was actually mouthing her presentation.
She had it perfectly memorized.
And suddenly, this woman came to the door.
She opened the door, and here she was
—a beautiful older lady with her hair done, makeup on, beautifully dressed—
looking like she was just going out.
And the sister was so flustered that she said:
“Oh, I’m sorry. Did we get you out of bed?”
Yeah, memorized presentations are not always good.
Well, maybe we’ve memorized presentations,
and sometimes we feel like we’re giving a talk when we’re at the door.
But what if the person has a very specific interest?
What if they have some special need
or they’re facing some terrible challenge just at the time when we’re calling?
Well, we want to look to the example of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He set the perfect example for us.
He showed love for people
by choosing subjects that were appropriate
for each individual.
And his personal interest in individuals
attracted people to the message.
Well, for example, do you remember the time when Jesus had a conversation
with the Pharisee Nicodemus?
Now, Nicodemus was impressed by Jesus’ miracles,
and he approached Jesus at night
probably because he was afraid of the Jews.
Now, as a Pharisee and a teacher,
Nicodemus evidently must have had
a very great knowledge of the Hebrew Scriptures.
So, what did Jesus do?
Well, he shared something with Nicodemus that was completely new.
You see, he talked about new truths
—about being “born again” and about seeing “the Kingdom of God.”
He explained to Nicodemus that he had ‘descended from the heavens’
and that he was the “only-begotten Son” of God
and that he was the way to everlasting life.
Well, I’m sure you’d agree that even though Nicodemus was a teacher,
he received quite an education from Jesus on that night.
But now, does that mean
that Jesus took exactly that same approach
with everyone that he met?
Well, no, not at all.
You see, on another occasion, when Jesus spoke to the Samaritan woman,
his approach was completely different.
Evidently, the Samaritan woman
had a very basic knowledge of the Hebrew Scriptures.
So, what did Jesus do?
Well, he noted the things she was interested in,
like obtaining water and why Jesus as a Jew
would speak with a Samaritan.
Well, Jesus also took an interest in her family situation.
He noted that she was very concerned about why Jews
worship in one location and Samaritans in a different location.
What did Jesus do?
Well, he talked with her
about the things that interested her and that were of concern to her.
He helped her to see that worshipping with “spirit and truth”
was more important than the location where individuals would worship.
And how did that woman respond?
Well, the Bible says she “left her water jar” there at the well,
she “went off into the city,”
and she gave a powerful witness about Jesus.
She was so effective
that the Samaritans invited Jesus to stay
and many put faith in him.
So, now, what do we learn from these two simple accounts?
Well, Jesus did not use a memorized presentation.
He just talked with people,
and he shared with them the truths
that he knew would touch their hearts.
He was very quick to choose topics and words
based on the interests and the concerns
of the person whom he was speaking to.
Well, now, with all of this in mind,
you may be wondering
(well, you’re supposed to be wondering):
‘How can I display that same love for the people whom I meet?’
Wouldn’t it be wonderful to have a little bit more help
to see how we can show love for people and make disciples?
Wouldn’t it be wonderful to have a publication
that would help us to be more flexible and more responsive
to the different needs and interests of the people whom we meet?
And what if that publication
highlighted specific ways that Jesus
and other first-century evangelizers
showed their love as they made disciples?
Well, you will be happy to know
that Jehovah’s organization
has produced just such a publication.
It’s a 32-page brochure entitled
Love People—Make Disciples.
Well, now, would you like to see a little preview
of what this brochure contains?
Please watch the following video.
This new publication, Love People—Make Disciples,
is being made available in both print
and digital formats in over 400 languages.
How is the brochure designed
to help us show love for people we meet?
Unlike the tools we’ve used in the past,
this new brochure does not give us expressions to memorize;
nor does it put the emphasis on leaving literature.
Rather, it features 12 lessons
that focus on qualities we need to cultivate
to make disciples.
All the lessons are based on Bible accounts
in which Jesus or another first-century evangelizer
displayed a specific quality in the ministry.
The lessons will help us see how we can imitate the qualities
they demonstrated as we make disciples.
Each lesson contains a video
that brings the account to life.
A woman of Samaria came to draw water.
Give me a drink.
By cultivating an interest in people,
we can talk about things that are on their minds.
What truths might we share with people once a conversation is started?
Appendix A highlights basic Bible truths that we love to teach.
Make it your goal to learn these basic truths
and the scriptures that support them.
If you do,
you will be more effective in starting conversations
and in making disciples.
For example, a conversation can be started
by asking a simple question, such as:
“Have you heard that God will soon end all suffering?”
or “Did you know that the earth’s environment will be restored?”
Sharing a simple truth at the right time is powerful.
Jesus said his sheep would listen to his voice.
In other words, “rightly disposed” ones
will recognize the truth when they hear it expressed simply.
Appendix B helps us to determine whether to continue a conversation.
Appendix C provides practical suggestions
on how to conduct Bible studies in Enjoy Life Forever!
What if you don’t feel comfortable starting conversations?
Don’t worry!
Beginning in January 2024,
the “Apply Yourself” portion of each midweek meeting
will help us to practice the points we are learning in this new brochure.
The meeting will no longer focus on presenting
a predetermined topic and scripture.
Rather, students will select topics for their assignments
that they know are on the minds of those in their community.
By means of realistic demonstrations,
audience discussions,
and talks,
our meetings will assist us to develop skills
that will help us start conversations naturally
and adapt to each person’s concerns and needs.
By focusing on people,
we will become more comfortable
and more effective as we make disciples.
As you consider each lesson,
think carefully about how you can demonstrate
the highlighted qualities when conversing with people in your community.
Ask yourself, ‘What are their concerns and needs?’
As you go about your activities, be observant.
Look for appropriate opportunities to help people in practical ways.
Acts of kindness can open the door to share Kingdom truth.
Show that you care by listening to others when they express themselves.
Share a simple truth at the right time.
Remember, our goal is not to memorize a presentation
but to demonstrate Christlike love to everyone we meet.
This will require patience,
perseverance,
and commitment.
No matter where we live
or under what circumstances we are preaching,
simply showing love will help us to find joy in our ministry.
More than any specific technique,
actively expressing our love for others
will help us make disciples.
So we indeed thank Jehovah for this wonderful new tool
to make us more effective in our ministry.
Of course, the question you may be wondering is,
When will you receive your copy of this new brochure?
Well, you’ll be pleased to know that it’s going to be made available
to all congregations in electronic format
and in most places in printed format
by November 6.
In addition, this entire four-part symposium
will be posted on jw.org on November 6
so that all of our brothers and sisters
will hear the information in the symposium at the same time.
Isn’t that great?
Of course, we’re all going to want to read the brochure.
We’re going to want to watch the videos.
But wasn’t it wonderful to hear in this video
that the Governing Body has arranged to make use of this new publication
beginning in the month of January during our midweek meeting?
So we’re going to get the opportunity to put this into practice right away.
So, what have we learned in this four-part symposium?
In Part One, Brother Fleegle reminded us why we love Jehovah
and how our love motivates us to want to praise him.
In Part Two, Brother Lösch explained the differences
between most Israelites
and those who volunteered to be Nazirites.
In Part Three, Brother Herd helped us to see
that although congregation publishers
will no longer report their time in the ministry,
this in no way
diminishes our individual responsibility to make disciples.
And finally, in this part, we received a new tool
that will help us to show our love for people
and to make disciples.
It’s really amazing to witness as Jehovah’s people
the fulfillment of Isaiah 60:17.
You’ll remember the prophecy there.
It says:
“Instead of the copper I will bring in gold,
“and instead of the iron I will bring in silver,
“instead of the wood, copper,
“and instead of the stones, iron;
“and I will appoint peace as your overseers
and righteousness as your task assigners.”
Well, what’s the point of the prophecy?
You see, it outlines that good materials
would gradually be replaced by even better ones.
And that’s exactly what we have seen.
You think back to the 1930’s when our brothers
became so zealous in the ministry
that they went out with phonographs and testimony cards.
But, of course, at that time, they didn’t speak.
Either the record did the speaking or people read the card.
My mother loved to tell the story
about being in the service with her pioneer partner.
The door opened, she handed the man the testimony card
and, of course, didn’t say anything.
The man started to read it.
Suddenly, his wife called out, “Who’s at the door?”
The man said: “I don’t know.
There are two deaf women here, and I’m trying to figure out what they want.”
Well, that was the reality.
We weren’t speaking.
But how Jehovah improved the situation!
He trained his people how to give an effective witness.
And then we had publications, like Reasoning From the Scriptures,
that helped us to learn how to use the Bible to reason with people.
And more recently, Jehovah has given us
this marvelous tool Enjoy Life Forever!
so that we can conduct much more quality Bible studies.
And now, with the release of this brochure,
we’re going to focus on people
and talk about the things that are of interest to them
and, in that way, endeavor to reach their heart
so that they can become disciples.
Well, it’s true
that with each of these organizational adjustments,
we went from something good to something better.
And I think with the things that were announced today,
isn’t it true that we’re seeing that again?
We’re going from something that was good to something even better.
And I think we’d agree, too,
that Jehovah is helping us to mature as a people.
He has confidence in us
that our concern is not merely the number of hours
or the publications that we place that we’re going to put on a report.
We love Jehovah, we love people,
and we want to make disciples.
So, what does all of this mean,
and what does it not mean?
Well, first,
these adjustments do not
—they do not—
mean that we are in any way slacking off in our ministry.
It does not mean that we are slowing down
as we approach the great tribulation.
Nothing could be further from the truth.
Right now we have more than 50,000 applications
from students who want to attend the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
We’re appointing new missionaries, new special pioneers,
temporary special pioneers,
and an army of new regular pioneers.
And in some lands, like the Philippines
(sorry, I have to mention the Philippines),
we are experiencing record growth.
Can you imagine a 9 percent increase this year
with a new peak of 253,876 publishers
and 12,954 baptized
just in this last year?
Isn’t that amazing?
So please know —please know—
that in no way is the work slowing down.
Our ministry has never
been more important than it is now.
So, what, then, do these adjustments mean?
Well, they do mean that our motivation
for carrying out the ministry
has been even more clarified.
You see, we share in the ministry
because we love Jehovah and because we love people.
So this is the time when we want to be busy
in Jehovah’s work.
Do you remember Jesus’ parable of the master and the three slaves?
That parable was designed to teach us
what we need to be doing while we’re waiting for the end to come.
Two of those slaves were industrious,
and they doubled the master’s money
and, as a result, they were blessed.
We want to have that same
industrious, diligent spirit.
We want elders and ministerial servants and pioneers
to take the lead in the ministry.
But all of us
in our personal ministry want to be even more zealous
in what we want to accomplish in our ministry.
What an exciting time this is!
The Governing Body sincerely hopes
that many more will come to join us
in serving Jehovah before the end comes.
And remember:
Jehovah delights in rewarding his people
for their faithfulness and for their generosity.
So with the great tribulation fast approaching,
have no doubt that Jehovah will soon richly reward you
as we all give generously of our time and our effort
to love our amazing God, Jehovah,
and to make disciples!
As you were able to see,
Part 1 is of historical proportions and most exciting!
Part 2 will be available on jw.org in January.
Our postcard for this month is from Albania,
a small country on the Adriatic Sea.
For much of its tumultuous past,
foreign powers have come and gone,
each bringing with it a different mix of peoples,
cultures, and religions.
Albania is a beautiful land, scattered with lakes
and crisscrossed by rivers.
Idyllic beaches dot the coastline,
such as the aptly named Aquarium Beach,
a beautiful spot for snorkeling.
The Karavasta Lagoon, the largest in the country,
is the home of the Dalmatian pelican,
the largest of its kind,
measuring up to 1.8 meters (6 ft) long.
In Romans chapter 15, the apostle Paul reported
that he and his companions had “thoroughly preached the good news.”
They had traveled “as far as Illyricum,”
a Roman province that included part of what is today Albania.
It is likely that some in the region became Christians at that time,
for secular history reports that Christianity
took root in Albania in the first century.
In the 1920’s,
some Albanians learned Bible truth
while living in the United States.
After getting baptized, some returned to Albania,
eager to share these precious truths
with family and friends.
In 1928, Lazar Nasson and Petro Stavro
traveled from the United States back to Albania
to show the “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
Many responded,
and despite political turmoil, economic reversal
and, at times, vigorous opposition,
the number of Kingdom proclaimers has grown steadily.
Today, there are more than 5,400 publishers
serving in 89 congregations.
From Tirana, the capital,
the branch office cares for the work in Albania
and the 228 publishers in its northeast neighbor, Kosovo.
Let’s visit the city of Lushnjë, located in west-central Albania.
The Lushnjë Veriu Congregation preaches in a territory
that covers around one third of the city
as well as 21 villages in the Myzeqe Valley.
The preaching work in the villages yields good results,
and meeting attendance regularly averages over 130 percent.
They are happy to host a Romany-language group.
Though some publishers live in villages outside the city,
they are happy to attend the meetings in person,
some walking one hour from their home to the Kingdom Hall.
The 77 publishers of the Lushnjë Veriu Congregation
send you their Christian affection and greetings!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

10月7日
宾夕法尼亚州守望台圣经书社举行了年会
按以往的习惯
你可能会在2024年1月
才能看到这个节目
然而这一次你在这个月
就能看到年会的其中4个演讲了
中央长老团特别指示
要在这个月播放这些节目
他们希望全世界的弟兄姐妹
都尽早地看到这些年会的内容
请大家好好享受接下来的节目
今天我们真的非常高兴来到这里
我相信你们今天会越来越高兴
我们的年会通常都被称为
具有历史性意义的会议
比如，很多人说2013年的年会
是具有历史性意义的年会
我们的出版物也这样说
你可能会说所有的年会都很重要
这样说也没错
但那次年会真的很特别
因为我们在那次年会上发行了
英语《圣经新世界译本》（修订版）
真的是很特别的年会
现在《新世界译本》（修订版）
被翻译成越来越多的语言，也让更多人受益
10年过去了
整整10年过去了
现在我们又迎来了另一次重要的年会
耶和华帮助忠信睿智的奴隶
更加明白他的话语圣经
也更深入地理解圣经中所蕴含的一些原则
我们想把这一切分享给你们
你准备好了吗？
你准备好自己的心了吗？
接下来请好好享受一个系列演讲
每一位讲者都会介绍下一位讲者
首先有请盖奇·弗莱格尔弟兄
他演讲的题目是
《要爱耶和华——赞美耶和华》
这一天是公元33年尼散月11日
耶稣在圣殿里教导别人
再过几天他就会被处死
耶稣以无可反驳的论证
回答了抄经士和法利赛派的人
而同时他也把握机会告诉了我们
很多重要的道理，比如
“属于凯撒的要给凯撒
属于上帝的要给上帝”
然后有一个抄经士走上前来问耶稣
“诫命中哪一条是最重要的呢？”
耶稣怎么回答呢？
从那时直到今天
耶稣的话对所有自称是基督徒的人
都有深远的影响
他的回答记录在马可福音12章
请打开马可福音12章
我们一起读一下第29和30节
耶稣回答说
“最重要的”
或者说这是最大最重要的诫命
“最重要的是，以色列啊，听吧！
耶和华我们的上帝是独一的耶和华
你要全心，全意，全力
用全部生命爱耶和华你的上帝”
你要爱耶和华
爱上帝，听起来很简单
今天世上有亿万的人都说自己爱上帝
但他们更爱享乐
他们也愿意拿起武器去杀死别人
他们也不愿意遵守上帝所定的道德标准
他们的行为证明他们根本不爱上帝
耶稣指出
对上帝的爱不只是一种感情而已
他强调我们应该怎样爱上帝
就是要全心，全意，全力
用全部生命去爱他
那其他的部分又怎么样呢？
我们的眼睛
我们的耳朵
我们的手呢？
《精读本》在第30节有一个注释
帮助我们明白
这包括我们的感情、愿望和感觉
也包括我们的头脑和理解力
以及身体和思维的能力
没错，也就是我们拥有的所有的一切
都该用来爱耶和华

en.text: On this account I say to you: Stop being anxious

or what you will drink,
or about your bodies as to what you will wear.
Does not life mean more than food
and the body than clothing?
Observe intently the birds of heaven;
they do not sow seed or reap
or gather into storehouses,
yet your heavenly Father feeds them.
Are you not worth more than they are?

title: 좋은 소식에 담긴 모든 내용을 선포하십시오

ko.text: 혹시 얼마 전 광고한 특별 전파 활동을 생각하고 있었니?
제가 드리는 말씀 오해하진 말아 주세요.
우리가 전하게 될 소식이 너무 강한 것 같아요.
내 생각은 좀 다르지만 아주 직접적인 소식이긴 하지.
안 그래도 사람들이 자기들 생각이랑 다른 이야기를 하면 싫어하는데

말해 준 적 있나 모르겠는데 우리 가족은 퀘벡 출신이야.
우리 아버진 1940년대에 강력한 증거 활동에 참여하셨지.
아버지는 그 지역 종교 지도자들의 위선을 폭로하는 전도지를 전해야 하셨어.
종교 지도자들이 추종자들을 선동해서 증인들을 폭행하고
형제들은 거짓 고발을 당해 체포되거나 수감되기도 했지.

나도 생각을 해 봤는데 출애굽기의 내용이 떠오르더라고.

또 우리가 어느 편인지도 보여 주고요.
돌이켜 보면 이스라엘 백성이 한 일은
내가 너를 강하게 하고 너를 도와주겠다.
내가 참으로 내 의로운 오른손으로 너를 붙들어 주겠다.”

en.text: Good morning.
Sorry I was running a little behind this morning,
but at least I come bearing gifts.
Oh. No worries.
Thank you. I could really use it today.
Were you also thinking
about that announcement about the special preaching campaign?
Yeah-yeah, I was.
Don’t take what I’m going to say the wrong way,
but
don’t you think the message we’ll be preaching
is pretty harsh?
No, I wouldn’t say that,
but it’s definitely very direct.
I mean, people already get defensive
whenever you challenge their beliefs,
and this is going to be the next level.
This isn’t going to be the easiest message to deliver.
But, you know, it’s not the first time we’ve done this.
Really?
Absolutely.
I don’t know if you remember me telling you
that my family is originally from Quebec,
and my dad was part of an incredibly hard-hitting witness
back in the 1940’s.
I looked this up last night.
He had to distribute a tract that called out
the local religious leaders as hypocrites.
What were they doing?
They were inciting their followers
to mob violence against the Witnesses,
telling them to vandalize our properties,
even getting brothers falsely arrested
and imprisoned.
Wow, and they had to distribute that tract during the violence?
They had to.
Jehovah wanted to show how unjust their actions were.
But I remember my dad telling me—
He said that initially he was pretty terrified.
Yeah, I mean, that’s how I feel.
I’m-I’m terrified.
It’s normal to feel that way.
I’ve been thinking about it myself,
and I thought of an account in Exodus.
It’s where Moses tells the Israelites
to splatter the blood of a ram on their doorposts
in order to avoid the effects of the last plague.
And I thought about how some of the Israelites
might have felt about doing that back then.
That’s all Moses told us.
And everyone has to do this? Every family?
Rams are sacred to the Egyptians!
Yeah, this would be an affront to Amon-Ra.
How are the Egyptians going to react?
I know. I’ve thought about that too.
Does Moses know what he’s asking us to do?
Brothers, I don’t know if we have anything to worry about.
We don’t have anything to fear.
Think of how Jehovah has protected us with these last plagues.
And as for the blood,
it’s not a matter of offending them;
it’s a matter of protecting us.
It’s showing whose side we’re on
—Jehovah’s side.
Looking back, what the Israelites did
was actually good news.
It meant their deliverance,
and it’s the same with any message we bear today.
Let me show you one of my favorite scriptures
at Isaiah 41:10.
It says: “Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
The fear we feel is natural.
But remember,
Jehovah was with the Israelites,
he was with my dad,
and he will be with us.
The message we are sharing is good news.

cn.text: 早啊！
不好意思，我今天来得有点晚
但我带了咖啡
哦，没关系
谢谢！
我现在真的很需要咖啡
你也在想着
跟特别传道活动有关的事吗？
嗯，对
你不觉得
这次要传的消息
太严厉了吗？
你不会误解我的意思吧？
对吧？
我明白你的意思
是，这次的内容是很直接
我们之前传道的时候
他们的反应就已经很糟了
这次
反应应该会更大吧？
传讲这样的信息
确实很不容易
但我们以前也传讲过类似的信息啊！
是吗？
是的
我以前有跟你说过吗？
我们家本来住在魁北克
20世纪40年代，我们受到猛烈的反对
包括我爸爸在内
我昨晚找到了这个
那时候，他分发这张传单
让人知道那些宗教领袖有多么虚伪
发生了什么事？
这些宗教领袖煽动暴民
袭击耶和华见证人
破坏弟兄姐妹的家
他们甚至还诬告我们、拘捕我们
哇，他们在这样的情况下
还要分发传单？
是的
因为耶和华想让大家都知道
宗教领袖的恶行
我爸爸曾对我说
刚开始的时候
他也觉得很害怕
嗯，我懂
我也感觉
很害怕
这很正常
我有时也有这种感觉
我最近想起出埃及记里的记载
当时摩西告诉以色列人
要宰杀羊羔
把羊血洒在门柱上
这样才能躲过最后一场灾殃
我想到
有些以色列人听到这个消息后
可能有什么反应
这就是摩西的吩咐
每家人、每个人都要这样做？
但对埃及人来说，羊羔就是神呐！
对，这等于攻击阿蒙瑞呀！
埃及人会怎么想？
我知道，我也想到了
摩西真的知道这意味着什么吗？
弟兄们
我觉得我们没什么好担心的
没什么好害怕的
前几场灾殃
耶和华不是一直保护我们吗？
至于羊羔的血
这不是要冒犯他们
而是要保护我们自己
这能表明我们支持谁
就是耶和华啊
现在回头看
以色列人听到的是好消息
这为他们带来了拯救
我们今天宣扬的消息也能带来拯救
想给你看一下我最喜欢的一段经文
以赛亚书41:10
这里说
“你不要怕
因为我与你同在
你不要忧虑
因为我是你的上帝
我要使你坚强
我一定会帮助你
一定会用我伸张正义的右手扶持你”
感到害怕
是很正常的
但别忘了
耶和华与以色列人同在
他也与我爸爸同在
他也会与我们同在
我们传讲的消息是好消息！

title: 지부 보고: 나이지리아와 카메룬

ko.text: 나이지리아는 아프리카에서 인구가 가장 많은 나라입니다.
이 나라에서 여호와의 이름을 전파하고 있습니다.
약 570명이 그곳에서 전 시간으로 일하고 있죠.
그에 더해 100명의 형제 자매들이 지부 개축 공사를 하고 있습니다.
어떤 점을 배울 수 있을지 궁금했습니다.
여러 가지가 있겠지만 특히 감명 깊었던 건
그들이 어려움 속에서도 기쁨에 넘쳐 있다는 것이었습니다.
왕국이 가져올 축복에 초점을 맞추기 때문이죠.
지난 9월과 10월에 여러 지역에서 큰 홍수가 있었습니다.
그들은 카누를 타고 함께 「파수대」 연구를 하면서
많은 형제들이 집을 떠나야 했지만 기쁨을 잃지 않았죠.
재해를 겪은 건 당연히 힘든 일이지만
혼자가 아니라는 걸 알고 있었기 때문입니다.
기꺼이 도와주는 형제 자매들이 많이 있고
이런 문제가 곧 사라질 것임을 알았던 거죠.
형제 자매들이 기뻐하는 모습을 보면서 큰 격려를 받았습니다!
형제들은 다른 어려움을 인내하면서도 계속 기쁨을 나타냅니다.
자신이 사는 마을과 이웃 마을 사이에 충돌이 있었을 때
저는 성경을 사용해서 제 양심상 어느 한쪽 편을 들 수 없다고,
그러면 여호와께서 불쾌하게 여기실 것이라고 설명했습니다.
그러자 사람들은 저를 때리고 묶어서 마을 밖으로 추방했습니다.
그런데 형제들이 제가 지낼 곳을 마련해 주고
저를 격려해 주고 여러 가지 방법으로 저를 도와주었죠.
양 치는 방문도 여러 번 받았어요.
여호와께서 저를 보고 계시다는 걸 분명히 느꼈습니다.
기쁨을 유지하고 있는 한 자매를 만나 보겠습니다.
루키 보라로 자매는 23살일 때 갑자기 시력을 잃었습니다.
그 무렵에 그는 진리를 배우게 되었죠.
자매가 처음 집회에 갔을 때 어떤 점을 느꼈는지,
기쁨을 유지하는 데 어떻게 도움이 되는지 들어 볼까요?
시각 장애인들은 불안감을 느낄 때가 많아요.
그런데 처음 집회에 갔을 때는 사랑을 느낄 수 있었어요.
다들 저를 정말 편안하게 대해 줬어요.
그 사랑 덕분에 제가 소중한 존재라는 느낌이 들어요.
제 삶을 사용해 여호와를 섬길 수 있으니까요.
사람들에게 여호와에 관해 이야기해 주면 정말 뿌듯해요.
마음이 기쁘고 사랑하는 여호와를 위해 더 많이 봉사하고 싶어지죠.
여호와의 기쁨을 자신의 산성으로 삼고 있습니다.
우리는 그런 모습을 보면서 정말 큰 격려를 받았죠.
우리가 다음으로 간 곳은 이웃 나라인 카메룬이었습니다.
카메룬은 흔히 아프리카 대륙의 축소판이라고 불립니다.
매우 다양한 지리적, 문화적 특징을 가지고 있기 때문이죠.
카메룬 지부가 관할하는 구역에서 좋은 소식을 전하고 있는데요.
형제 자매들은 전파하고 성서 연구를 사회하는 것을 정말 좋아합니다.
우리는 베델 정문 바로 앞에 전시대를 세워 둡니다.
출근하기 전 이른 아침과 퇴근 후 저녁
그리고 주말에 베델 가족들이 전시대 옆에 서서 봉사합니다.
사람들과 좋은 대화를 나눌 때도 많고
성서 연구도 여러 건 시작할 수 있었습니다.
또한 매년 지부에서는 특별 전파 활동을 조직해서
거의 봉사되지 않은 구역과 임명되지 않은 구역에서 봉사합니다.
많은 형제 자매들이 기꺼이 이 활동에 참여합니다.
휴가철을 그렇게 보내는 분들이 많이 있습니다.
저는 특별 전파 활동에 참여하는 게 정말 좋아요.
특별한 방법으로 표현할 수 있는 좋은 기회니까요.
우리가 가는 구역에서 무슨 일이 있을지는 전혀 알 수 없죠.
하지만 여호와께서 우리를 어떻게 지원해 주시는지는 늘 볼 수 있습니다.
특별 전파 활동 기간에 우리는 먼 곳까지 가기 때문에
우리는 일찍 일어나서 어제보다 더 멀리 가서 전파하죠.
이런 특별 전파 활동에 빠지지 않고 참여할 겁니다.
형제 자매들은 이런 전파 활동에 참여하면서
진리에 관심을 가진 사람들을 많이 만납니다.
데이브 모모 형제는 외딴 지역의 전도인들을 만나러 갔다가
인근 마을에 사는 관심자인 니컬러스에 대해 알게 되었습니다.
니컬러스는 자기가 사는 마을에서 여러 사람과 성서 연구를 했습니다.
그래서 우리는 니컬러스에게 어떻게 우리 출판물을 구했고
어떻게 「파수대」 연구를 사회하는 법을 배웠는지 물어보았죠.
그랬더니 클레멘트라는 사람이 두 달에 한 번씩 왔었다고 하더라고요.
그리스도인 집회를 조직하는 법을 가르쳐 주었던 겁니다.
그래서 우리는 그 이웃 마을에 가서 클레멘트를 만났습니다.
도착해 보니 클레멘트도 자기 마을에서 전파하고 있었고
모임 장소까지 지었다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
이 사람들은 아직 여호와의 증인이 아니었는데도
관심자들을 돕기 위해 특별 파이오니아가 그 지역에 파견되었습니다.
우린 그날 오후부터 바로 성서 연구를 사회하기 시작했고,
다음 날엔 니컬러스가 사는 마을을 방문했죠.
관심자들은 우리에게 추장을 꼭 만나 보라고 했어요.
왕국회관을 지을 부지를 받을 수 있을까 해서였죠.
놀랍게도 추장은 그렇게 해 주겠다고 했습니다.
니컬러스는 침례를 목표로 잘 발전하고 있습니다.
아름다운 영적 특성들을 정말 많이 갖고 있습니다.
특히 나이지리아 형제들의 기쁨과 카메룬 형제들의 열심은
우리에게 큰 감동을 주었으며 우리는 그들을 정말 사랑하게 되었습니다.
그들을 섬기고 여호와께서 그 충실한 종들을 사용해
이 지역의 왕국 활동을 돌보시는 것을 직접 볼 수 있어서

en.text: Nigeria is by far the most populous nation in Africa,
with over 200 million inhabitants.
Over 389,000 Kingdom publishers
are giving a witness to Jehovah’s name in this country.
The branch office is in Igieduma,
where approximately 570 full-time members care for the work
along with an additional 100 working on the renovation of the branch.
We wondered
what we would come to love about the friends in Nigeria.
What beautiful qualities would stand out?
Well, many could be mentioned,
but we were especially touched by the joy they display
despite challenges.
Our brothers remain joyful
because their focus
is on future Kingdom realities,
not on the present unfavorable conditions.
In the month of September and October,
a number of states experienced severe flooding.
Even with this unwelcomed challenge,
the brothers ensured that they would not miss the spiritual food.
Thus, they had the Watchtower  Study in a canoe over flooded areas,
joyfully attending and commenting despite obstacles.
Even though many had to leave their homes,
they still had joy,
not because of their lives being turned upside down,
but joyful because they were not alone,
joyful because they knew they had a supportive brotherhood behind them
and they knew the real solution is soon to come.
How encouraging to see the friends’ joy
despite the hardships that natural disasters bring!
We also see this quality shine through
when the brothers endure other hardships.
Brother Russel Odhozor endured persecution
when he took a neutral stand involving a conflict with the neighboring village.
I explained to them from the Scriptures
that my conscience will not allow me
to show support
and that it will offend Jehovah.
So they flogged me, tied me,
and that led to my banishment from the community.
I did not have any plan of where I would stay,
and the brothers welcomed me,
they encouraged me, and they supported me in various ways.
I received several shepherding calls.
It showed me that Jehovah takes note of me personally.
He cares about me.
Brother Odhozor continues to find joy in his ministry
in spite of these challenges.
Next, note the example of a sister who is able to maintain her joy
despite physical limitations.
Sister Ruky Kpohraro suddenly lost her eyesight
when she was 23 years old.
Around that time, she came into contact with the truth.
Listen to what impressed her at her first meeting with Jehovah’s people.
Notice, too, how her zeal in the ministry affects her joy.
Without a doubt,
God’s people in Nigeria
are making ‘the joy of Jehovah their stronghold.’
And that left an indelible mark on our hearts.
Our next stop was the neighboring country of Cameroon.
Cameroon is often referred to as Africa in miniature
because of its geographical and cultural diversity.
Over 50,000 publishers are preaching the good news in this branch territory,
which includes Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.
The branch office is located in Douala,
where about 70 full-time workers care for the work.
We wondered the same about Jehovah’s people in Cameroon.
What would we come to love about them?
What beautiful qualities would stand out?
Well, it is difficult to narrow it to just one.
But we could say that a quality that stood out plainly
was their zeal in serving Jehovah.
The brothers and sisters
just love to preach
and conduct Bible studies.
This can be seen among the Bethelites.
Right outside the Bethel gate, we set up a literature cart.
Early mornings before work, evenings after work,
and on weekends, Bethelites man the cart.
We have had wonderful conversations,
and several Bible studies have been started.
Also, every year,
preaching campaigns are organized by the branch
to cover seldom-worked and unassigned territories
all over the branch territory.
Thousands of brothers and sisters answer this call,
including many young ones.
For many of the friends, it is their yearly vacation.
I love participating in campaigns
because they are a great opportunity
to express one’s faith in Jehovah in a remarkable way.
We almost never know what awaits us in the territory where we are going.
However, we always see how Jehovah supports us.
During campaigns,
we cover long distances to preach,
and sometimes we return exhausted.
But surprisingly,
the next day we are up early and ready to go
and preach farther than the previous day.
This is proof that it is Jehovah who gives us strength.
I am determined to participate in all campaigns
until the preaching work stops.
When participating in these preaching campaigns,
the friends are finding great interest in the truth.
When visiting publishers in a remote area,
Brother Dave Momo learned of Mr. Nicholas,
an interested man in a nearby village.
Mr. Nicholas studied the Bible
with a number of people in his village.
So we asked Mr. Nicholas how he got the publications
and how he learned to conduct the Watchtower  Study.
Mr. Nicholas explained to us
that Mr. Clement came every two months.
He was the one who brought him the publications,
and he was the one who taught him
how to organize Christian meetings.
We traveled to the next village to meet Mr. Clement.
When we arrived,
we found that Mr. Clement was also preaching in his village.
And he had even built a place of worship.
Although these men were not yet Jehovah’s Witnesses,
they were already preaching in remote villages.
A special pioneer was sent to follow up on the interest.
When we arrived in Mr. Clement’s village,
interested ones came to visit us immediately.
We began to conduct Bible studies that afternoon
and played videos into the night.
The next day, we visited Mr. Nicholas in his village.
Those interested in the good news insisted that we meet with the chief
with the hope that he would give us land to build a Kingdom Hall.
To our surprise, the chief agreed.
Now Mr. Clement is baptized,
and Mr. Nicholas is progressing toward baptism.
Much more could be said
about the beautiful spiritual qualities these friends exhibit.
But the joy we found in Nigeria
and the zeal of the friends in Cameroon
are two of the qualities that touched our hearts
and endeared the friends to us.
It was a privilege to serve them
and to see how Jehovah is using these faithful servants
to care for his Kingdom work in this part of the world.

cn.text: 尼日利亚（奈及利亚）
是非洲人口最多的国家
它的人口超过两亿
在这里有38万9000多位传道员
正热心地为耶和华的圣名作见证
分部办事处位于伊吉杜马
大约有570位全时伯特利成员在这里服务
另外，还有100多位志愿人员
在参与分部的扩建工程
出发前，我和妻子都在想
尼日利亚的弟兄姐妹是什么样的人呢？
他们身上有什么显著的特质呢？
他们的确有很多美好的特质
但最让我们印象深刻的
就是他们虽然面对很多考验
却保持喜乐
弟兄们能保持喜乐
因为他们专注的不是目前的困难
而是未来王国的福分
9月和10月，有一些州受洪水重创
尽管如此，弟兄们还是作出安排
确保大家能参与崇拜活动
他们甚至在小船上
举行了《守望台》研究班聚会
很多人都喜乐地参与和评论
尽管他们不得不撤离，但弟兄们还是很喜乐
这当然不是因为他们失去了一切
而是因为他们知道自己并不孤单
也知道他们的身后
有个全力支持他们的弟兄团体
而且难题很快就会彻底解决
虽然遭遇天灾，但弟兄们依然保持喜乐
这真的让我们很受鼓励
我们也看到，弟兄们在面对其他考验时
同样保持喜乐
拉塞尔弟兄就曾因保持中立受到迫害
当时，他所在的村庄和邻近的村庄发生冲突
我用经文向他们解释
我的良心不容许我支持任何一方
因为我不想得罪耶和华
于是，他们就把我毒打了一顿
并把我从村子里赶走
我不知道自己可以住在哪里
但弟兄们为我提供了住处
他们鼓励我
也用各种方法支持我
长老们也好几次牧养探访我
这都让我看出
耶和华真的很关心我，很爱我
尽管面对考验
拉塞尔弟兄依然喜乐地参与传道活动
接下来，请听听一位姐妹的经历
罗吉姐妹在23岁的时候突然失去了视力
大概在那个时候，她也接触到了真理
第一次参加耶和华见证人的聚会
给她留下了深刻的印象
请听听她讲述这段经历
以及热心地参与传道，怎样带给她喜乐
我们盲人通常都很缺乏安全感
跟不熟悉的人在一起时就更是这样了
但我第一次参加聚会时
就感受到弟兄姐妹都很有爱心，也很快乐
他们和我一起笑，拥抱我
让我觉得轻松自在
他们的爱真的让我感到他们很关心我
我失去视力后
觉得自己变成了个没用的人
但现在我不这样想了
因为我可以献出自己为耶和华服务
我可以出去向人传道
这让我觉得自己做的事很有价值
我非常快乐
我也更爱耶和华，想多为他服务
毫无疑问
尼日利亚的弟兄姐妹
因“耶和华赐的喜乐”就充满了力量
这也给我们留下了深刻的印象
接下来，我们就到了尼日利亚的邻国喀麦隆
因为多样的地理环境和文化
喀麦隆也被称为小非洲
喀麦隆分部
共督导5万多位传道员的传道活动
他们督导的地区也包括赤道几内亚和加蓬
喀麦隆分部位于杜阿拉
这里有大约70位全时伯特利成员
我们也在想
喀麦隆的弟兄姐妹是什么样的人呢？
他们身上有什么显著的特质呢？
实际上，他们也有很多美好的特质
但最令人印象深刻的就是
他们在为耶和华服务时表现出来的热心
喀麦隆的弟兄姐妹真的很喜欢传道教人
伯特利成员就是一个例子
就在伯特利大门口，我们放了一个手拉车
每天上班前、下班后，还有周末的时候
都有伯特利成员在这里作手拉车见证
我们遇到不少对真理感兴趣的人
也建立了好几个圣经课程
另外，分部每年都会组织特别传道运动
让大家去分部范围内那些
未分配地区和传道员很少的地区去传道
很多弟兄姐妹都积极参与
包括很多孩子在内
很多弟兄姐妹都利用年假参与特别传道运动
我很喜欢参与传道运动
也喜欢以这种特别的方式
表明自己对耶和华的信心
虽然，我们从来不知道传道时会遇到什么
但我们总能感受到耶和华的支持
参加特别运动时
我们每天都会去很多地方传道
一天下来总觉得精疲力尽
但没有想到的是
第2天我们还是能早早起床
去更多地方传道
这一切都证明，是耶和华在给我们力量
我决心要参与所有的传道运动
直到耶和华说可以停下来了
弟兄姐妹在参与这些传道活动时
找到了很多对真理感兴趣的人
戴夫弟兄在一个偏远的地区传道时
听说邻近的村子里有一个对真理感兴趣的人
名字叫尼古拉斯
尼古拉斯和村子里好几个人学习圣经
我们问他，谁给他出版物
教他安排《守望台》聚会的
尼古拉斯说，是一个叫克莱门的人
克莱门住在附近的村子
每两个月来看望尼古拉斯一次
克莱门送给他出版物
也教他怎样安排基督徒聚会
我们就到另一个村子去找克莱门
我们到达的时候
发现克莱门正在村子里传道
他还搭了一个棚子，用来举行崇拜活动
虽然他们还没有受浸成为耶和华见证人
却已经开始热心地传道
后来，弟兄们派一个特别先驱
去照顾这些感兴趣的人
那天下午，我们一到达克莱门的村子
就有很多感兴趣的人来围住我们
我们马上就开始跟他们学习圣经
还给他们播放了很多短片
直到晚上，还有很多人留在那里看短片
不愿意离开
第2天，我们到尼古拉斯的村子去看望他
那些对真理感兴趣的人
让我们去找村长
看看他会不会给我们拨一块地
让我们修建王国聚会所
没想到村长真的答应了
现在克莱门已经受了浸
尼古拉斯也朝着受浸的目标不断进步
我们在这些弟兄姐妹身上
看到很多美好的特质
尼日利亚的弟兄姐妹身上的喜乐
喀麦隆的弟兄姐妹表现出来的热心
让我们印象最深刻，也让我们更爱他们
能够和他们并肩服务，让我们深感荣幸
看到耶和华正在任用这些忠心的人
在他们各自的地区宣扬王国
也让我们大受鼓励

title: 지부 보고: 필리핀

ko.text: 필리핀 제도는 7000개가 넘는 섬으로 이루어져 있습니다.
대도시에서 사람들은 흔히 지프니라고 하는 교통수단을 이용하죠.
넓은 시골 지역 사람들은 일반적으로 농사를 짓거나 물고기를 잡습니다.
여러 가지 해산물과 야채, 그리고 망고스틴,
잭프루트, 두리안 같은 독특한 과일도 즐겨 먹습니다.
필리핀 제도에서 여호와의 이름이 어떻게 영광스럽게 되었습니까?
“죽은 자는 어디 있는가?”라는 제목의 연설을 했습니다.
약 1000명이 참석하여 연설을 주의 깊이 들었다.”
35년 뒤인 1947년에 처음으로 길르앗 학교 졸업생들이 도착했습니다.
1954년에는 레이먼드 리치와 덴턴 홉킨슨이 필리핀에 왔습니다.
홉킨슨 형제는 22세에 순회 활동을 시작했고 현재는 지부 위원으로 일하고 있습니다.
제가 필리핀에 처음 왔을 때는 전도인 수가 2만 명이었습니다.
제로니모 라스티마 형제는 위험한 산악 지역에서 진리의 소식을 전했습니다.
사람들의 목을 잘라 죽이는 사람 사냥꾼이 있으니까요”라는 말을 들었죠.
그 말대로 한 덕분에 제 머리가 아직 이렇게 있네요.
자매들은 그 지역 사람들에게 진리를 잘 가르쳤습니다.
시간이 흘러 그 사람들도 침례를 받고 파이오니아가 되었죠.
그들은 그곳의 문화를 잘 알았고 효과적으로 증거할 수 있었습니다.
그 중에는 노라 파하르도 자매가 있습니다.
저와 다른 자매, 그렇게 둘밖에 없었지만
우리는 정말 용감하게 좋은 소식을 전했어요.
여호와께서 우리에게 힘을 주신 게 분명합니다.
그 덕분에 제자 삼는 일을 할 수 있었죠.
이러한 노력을 기울인 결과 전도인 수가 계속 증가하여
2022년 11월에는 야외 봉사 보고를 제출한 전도인의 수가 최초로 24만 명을 넘었습니다!
그리고 21만 건이 넘는 성서 연구가 사회되었습니다!
코로나19 팬데믹이 아직 끝나지 않은 상황에서 이러한 증가가 이루어진 것이죠.
최근에 스테파니라는 소녀는 전시대에서 우리 서적과 잡지를 보았습니다.
스테파니는 어머니에게 전에 전시대에서 가져간 출판물을 이미 다 읽었다고 말했죠.
스테파니는 「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」책을 가져가고 싶다고 했습니다.
그리고 부모님의 허락을 받아 성서 연구를 시작했습니다.
후에 하느님의 이름이 여호와라는 걸 알게 되었고
지금은 기도할 때마다 그 이름을 사용합니다.
메트로 마닐라 대회회관에서 특별 모임이 있었습니다.
거의 3년 만에 대면으로 열린 대규모 모임이었죠!
전도인 수보다 약 10만 명이 더 참석한 것이죠!
모임이 끝난 뒤에는 특별 식사와 음악 공연이 있었습니다.
필리핀 베델 가족은 행복하고 활기에 넘쳤습니다.
우리는 매일 함께 교제하고 숭배를 드리고 맛있는 음식도 먹었습니다.
또 각 부서들을 방문하여 격려를 베풀기도 했습니다.
서로를 사랑하고 연합되어 있는 세계적인 가족에 속해 있다는 건 정말 행복한 일이죠!
‘사람들이 바다의 섬들에서도 여호와의 이름을 영광스럽게 할 것이다!’

en.text: The Philippines archipelago is composed
of over 7,000 islands.
It spans an area
of about 1,850 kilometers (1,150 mi)
from north to south
and some 1,125 kilometers (700 mi)
from east to west.
In the large cities,
people often crowd into jeepneys
for public transportation.
In the vast rural areas,
farming and fishing are common occupations.
Rice is normally served at every meal.
Seafood too is very common, along with vegetables
and such unique fruits as mangosteen, jackfruit, and durian.
How has Jehovah’s name been glorified in these islands?
In 1912, C. T. Russell stopped in Manila
and gave a talk on the subject “Where Are the Dead?”
The Watchtower  reported:
“There were present about 1,000 Filipino young men,
“ages from 18 to 30, who understand English,
and who gave the very closest attention.”
Several decades later, in 1947,
the first Gilead graduates arrived.
Raymond Leach and Denton Hopkinson also arrived.
Brother Hopkinson entered the circuit work at age 22
and now serves on the Branch Committee.
Brother Geronimo Lastima helped to spread the truth in the mountains,
even though there were dangers.
The sisters were effective in teaching the truth to the local people.
Then, in turn, the locals were baptized and became pioneers.
They understood the culture of their own people
and knew how to witness effectively.
Sister Nora Fajardo was among them.
Through such efforts,
the number of publishers continued to increase,
surpassing 77,000 by 1975.
In November 2022, for the first time,
over 240,000 publishers
reported field service activity!
Also, over 210,000 Bible studies were conducted!
All of this as we were coming out
of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Recently, when a girl named Steffanie
saw the books and magazines at a literature cart,
she told her mother that she’d already finished reading
the publications they’d picked up previously.
Steffanie asked for a copy
of Enjoy Life Forever!
A Bible study was offered,
and with her parents’ permission, Steffanie accepted.
Later, she learned God’s personal name, Jehovah.
Now every time she prays, she uses God’s name.
Steffanie continues with her study of the Bible.
From January 16-27, 2023,
the Philippines received a branch visit.
In connection with the visit,
a special meeting was held at the Metro Manila Assembly Hall
on Sunday, January 22.
This was the first large, in-person event in nearly three years!
The total attendance was 341,643,
around 100,000 more than the number of publishers!
After the program we enjoyed a special meal
and musical program.
The Philippines Bethel family is happy and colorful.
Each day we enjoyed association, worship, and delicious food.
We also met with each of the departments
to provide encouragement.
What a joy it is to be part
of our united, loving international family!
How true are the words of Isaiah 24:15:
“In the islands of the sea they will glorify the name of Jehovah”!

title: 2023 중앙장로회 보고 제7보

ko.text: 이번 보고에서 알려 드릴 흥미로운 점들이 있는데요.
이번 달이면 2013년 연례 총회에서 영어 「신세계역」 개정판이 발표된 지
140만 명이 넘는 사람이 현장에서 또는 인터넷으로 그 프로그램을 즐겼습니다.
하지만 그리스도인 그리스어 성경 전체 또는 일부만 번역된 언어 수까지 합치면
그 수를 모두 다 합하면 총 279개에 달합니다.
「신세계역」 개정판이 봉사에서 큰 도움이 되고 있지 않습니까?
이제 중앙장로회는 성경의 강력한 소식을 빠르게 찾아 보는 데 도움이 되는
우리는 하느님의 말씀에 위로하고 인도하는 힘이 있다는 걸 믿죠.
그래서 다들 좋아하는 성구가 있고 그걸 몇 번이고 찾아 봅니다.
그런데 어떤 성구의 일부분만 기억이 나서
또는 흔히 들어 보지 못한 성구로
그러시다면 이제 여러분이 좋아하실 만한 새로운 도구를 발표합니다.
이 출판물은 여러 면에서 과거 1965년에 발표된
「‘모든 사물을 확인하고 훌륭한 것을 굳게 잡으라’」라는 책과 비슷합니다.
“122개의 주요 표제 아래 … 성구들을 편찬한 것이다”라고 알려 줍니다.
“이러한 제목에 대한 성서의 가르침을 확인하고자 할 때, …
또한 당신의 믿음에 이의를 제시하는 사람들에게 대답하기 위하여
이 책을 사용할 수 있다”라고 말합니다.
각 주제마다 많은 성구들이 나열되어 있어서
중요한 성경 원칙을 찾아 보고 이해하는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
우린 많은 분이 성경에 대해 대화하기 좋아하는 지역에서
한번은 어떤 여자가 대화 중에 부자와 나사로 이야기를 꺼냈어요.
그래서 우린 「확인」 책의 지옥불 제하에서 그 내용을 찾아
이 책은 전쟁, 중립, 세상과 벗하는 일에 관해
제가 더 분명히 이해하는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
새로운 출판물인 「그리스도인 생활을 위한 성경 구절들」에도
100개가 넘는 주제에 관한 많은 성구들이 들어 있습니다.
이 출판물의 목적은 디모데 후서 2:15에서 권하는 것처럼
우리가 “진리의 말씀을 올바로 다루”도록 돕기 위한 것입니다.
이 새 출판물의 특징을 간단히 살펴보겠습니다.
어려움에 대처하고 사람들을 격려하는 데 도움이 되는
성경 구절들과 기록을 쉽게 찾을 수 있게 해 줍니다.
이 출판물은 특정 주제에 대한 모든 성구를 나열하지는 않지만
어려움, 행실, 회중, 생활, 가족, 영성, 특성입니다.
원하는 주제가 어떤 카테고리에 있는지 잘 모르겠다면
각 주제 아래에는 굵은 글씨로 된 부분이 있습니다.
참조된 성구들은 굵은 글씨로 된 부분을 뒷받침하거나 그에 대한 대답이 됩니다.
어떤 경우에는 부가적인 성구나 관련된 성경 기록도 나와 있습니다.
이 출판물을 어떻게 활용할 수 있을까요?
주로 야외 봉사에서 사용하도록 만들어진 「확인」 책과는 다르게,
이 책은 우리가 참그리스도인으로서 겪는 어려움에 대처하도록 돕기 위해 마련되었습니다.
양 치는 방문을 하거나 연설을 준비할 때
이 새로운 출판물이 아주 유용한 자료가 될 것입니다.
가족 숭배를 할 때 이 자료를 사용해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
개인 성서 연구를 할 때 이 자료를 사용해 볼 수 있습니다.
또한 성서 연구생이 결정을 내릴 때
성경 원칙을 알아보고 적용하도록 돕기 위해서 사용할 수도 있습니다.
이 출판물은 300개가 넘는 언어로 번역되도록 승인되었습니다.
지금 볼 수 있다는 것을 기쁘게 알려 드립니다.
한동안 이 출판물을 “새로운 내용”에서 찾아 보실 수 있습니다.
서책을 눌러 찾아 보실 수도 있습니다.
중앙장로회는 「그리스도인 생활을 위한 성경 구절들」 책이 큰 도움이 되길 바랍니다.
모든 선한 일을 할 준비를 갖추게” 되기를 바라죠.
그렇게 하는 것은 이 악한 세상의 끝이 가까워 올수록
지난 몇 년 동안 두려움을 느낀 적이 있으신가요?
어쩌면 자연재해나 박해나 전쟁을 겪었을 수 있습니다.
아주 오랫동안 두려움 속에서 지냈을지 모릅니다.
두려움을 느낀다는 건 믿음이 부족하다는 뜻일까요?
과거의 충실한 사람들도 때때로 두려움을 느꼈죠.
이스라엘에선 아무 곳도 다윗에게 안전하지 않았죠.
당연히 그곳 사람들은 다윗을 좋아하지 않았습니다.
“가드 왕 아기스를 매우 두려워했다”고 알려 줍니다.
다윗은 인생의 그 위험한 시기에 시편 56편을 지었습니다.
물과 음식이 있어야 살 수 있죠.
단지 여호와께서 그것들을 뺏어 버리기만 하시면
“당신은 내가 떠돌아다니는 것을 낱낱이 살피고 계시니,”
“내 눈물을 당신의 가죽 부대에 담아 주십시오.
그것이 당신의 책에 기록되어 있지 않습니까?”
자신이 때때로 눈물을 흘리고 두려워했다는 사실을
다윗은 힘든 상황에서도 슬픔에 휩싸여 있지 않았습니다.
그의 눈물이 책에 기록된 것과 같았죠.
그를 울게 한 사람들을 여호와께서 벌하실 것이라고 말입니다.
여호와께서 우리의 눈물에 무관심하지 않으시다는 사실이
그 상황에서 할 수 있는 일이 있다면
만약 어떤 상황 때문에 두려움을 느끼게 된다면
우리에게 비밀 무기가 있다는 걸 기억하십시오.
하지만 어떻게 해야 하는지 알려 주죠.
내년에는 이 말에 대해 생각해 볼 기회가 많을 것입니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome!
We have some exciting things
to share with you in this update.
I’m sure you’ll find it very encouraging.
This month makes the ten-year anniversary
of the release of the revised English New World Translation
at the annual meeting in 2013.
That historic program
was streamed to 31 lands,
and over 1.4 million attended in person
or via Internet stream.
The complete New World Translation
is now available in 158 languages.
But if we take into consideration those languages
that have the complete Christian Greek Scriptures
or part of the Christian Greek Scriptures,
that brings the total
to 279 languages.
We’ve found this revision to be so helpful in our ministry, haven’t we?
And now the Governing Body has approved of adding yet another tool
to help us quickly access the powerful message in the Bible.
We all believe in the power of God’s Word
to give us comfort and guidance.
Because of that,
we have our favorite scriptures that we refer to over and over again.
However, do you ever partially remember a Bible verse
but you’re not sure where to find it?
I know that happens to me.
Or do you want to comfort someone
with a verse that perhaps they don’t often hear?
If so, you will be pleased to know
that a new tool is being released.
It has the title
Scriptures for Christian Living.
This publication is similar in a number of ways
to one that was released back in 1965, the book
“Make Sure of All Things; Hold Fast to What Is Fine.”
The title page described that book
as “a compilation of scriptures from the Holy Bible
under one hundred and twenty-three main headings.”
Its purpose?
The title page said:
“This book may be used to assure yourself of the Bible teaching on these subjects,
and also to answer those who challenge your faith.”
Make Sure  was a well-loved publication.
Notice what two publishers enjoyed about it.
I love this book.
Its comprehensive lists of scriptures
under topics ranging from angels to work
helped me to understand and identify important Bible principles.
Well, when the Make Sure  book came out,
we were pioneering in the Bible Belt
where we often had doctrinal discussions.
I remember one time talking with a woman,
and she brought up the rich man and Lazarus.
So we went to that section in the Make Sure  book on hellfire,
and we were able to reason with her on the matter.
I was in the Air Force when I got the truth,
and so this book helped me to understand a lot more clearly
issues relating to war, neutrality, and friendship with the world.
To this day, I keep my copy handy.
I would say that it was a teaching tool of the time.
And as pioneers, we never left home without it.
Like the Make Sure  book, which is no longer available in print,
the new publication, Scriptures for Christian Living,
is a compilation of scriptures on more than 100 topics.
The purpose of this publication
is to help us as we’re instructed at 2 Timothy 2:15,
that is, to handle “the word of the truth aright.”
Let’s briefly outline key features of this new publication
using  JW Library®.
Scriptures for Christian Living,
which we’ll refer to as scl,
makes it easy to locate
Bible verses and accounts
to help you deal with challenges
and to encourage others.
It doesn’t list all the scriptures
on a given topic.
Instead, it groups
the various subjects by category.
To find a subject,
use the search box in  JW Library
or browse the categories.
SCL is divided into seven categories:
Challenges, Conduct, Congregation,
Daily Life, Family,
Spirituality, and Qualities.
Select a category,
and then scroll down the list of topics.
If you’re not sure which category
might have the subject you’re looking for,
select All.
Many of the subjects have these features:
Under each topic,
you’ll see a number of statements
or questions in bold.
The cited verses
support the statement or answer the question.
In some cases, there are “See also” verses
or “Relevant Bible account(s)” listed.
How can the scl  be used?
Unlike the Make Sure  book,
which was designed primarily for use in the field ministry,
scl  is designed to guide us
as we face the challenges of living as true Christians.
Elders, you will find this new publication
to be a valuable resource on shepherding calls
and when developing talks.
Family heads, you may want to use the material
as the basis for some of your Family Worship sessions.
And congregation publishers,
you can use this material
not only as a basis for some personal Bible study projects
but also to help your Bible students
learn and apply Bible principles
when making decisions.
SCL has been approved in over 300 languages.
How can you get a copy?
And the big question: When can you get a copy?
We’re happy to inform you that scl
is now available in  JW Library
and will later be available in print.
For a period of time,
scl  will be available in “What’s New.”
And you’ll also be able to find it
by selecting the Library option
at the bottom of the screen
and then selecting Books.
Some languages will be available
at the same time as English,
with more languages to follow.
It’s the Governing Body’s hope that Scriptures for Christian Living
will help all of us to do as 2 Timothy 3:17 says
and use God’s Word to become “fully competent,
completely equipped for every good work.”
This is especially important
as we get deeper into the last days.
Have you ever been afraid during the past few years?
afraid you’d get sick?
afraid you’d lose your job?
afraid you wouldn’t be able to feed your family?
Maybe you’ve faced a natural disaster,
persecution, or war.
For what seems like an eternity,
you’ve been living with fear.
If so, what does it mean?
Does being afraid indicate a lack of faith?
Not at all.
Faithful men of the past have been afraid at times.
Take David, for example.
King Saul had put a price on David’s head.
As a result, no place in Israel was safe for David,
so he decided to leave the country.
Where did he go?
To Gath, the hometown of Goliath.
As you can imagine, David wasn’t very popular there.
As a result, the Bible says
that “David . . . became very much afraid
of King Achish of Gath.”
It was during that dangerous time in David’s life
that he composed the 56th Psalm.
Let’s look at a few verses, starting with verse 1.
“Show me favor, O God,
because mortal man is attacking me.”
Now, that’s good to remember.
No matter how powerful a ruler may seem to be,
he is still a “mortal man.”
He needs water and food to live.
All Jehovah has to do is to take that away,
and that man is a goner!
Now let’s look at verse 8.
David says:
“You keep track of my wandering.”
No matter where David went,
he was never out of Jehovah’s sight.
Then he continues:
“Do collect my tears in your skin bottle.
Are they not recorded in your book?”
David, that courageous warrior,
wasn’t embarrassed to admit that he shed tears at times
and that he was afraid at times.
Still, David didn’t allow himself
to be overwhelmed by grief.
He was confident that Jehovah noticed his tears
and that God understood the reason why David was crying.
It’s as if his tears were recorded in a book.
David was sure that one day that book would be opened
and that Jehovah would repay the men who had made David cry.
Isn’t it reassuring to know that Jehovah
is not indifferent to our tears?
When you get into a difficult situation, pray.
If there’s something you can do about it,
pray for wisdom.
If there’s nothing you can do about it,
pray for peace.
When a situation arises that makes us fearful,
remember that we have a secret weapon.
It’s a powerful weapon—prayer.
If we pour out our hearts to Jehovah,
he will listen to us and he will help us.
Now, that brings us back to verse 3.
It’s a simple statement, but it’s very meaningful.
“When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.”
That’s realistic.
It acknowledges the fact that sometimes we’re afraid,
but it tells us what to do about it
—to put our trust in Jehovah.
Next year, we’ll have many opportunities to meditate on that statement
because the Governing Body has chosen it
as our yeartext for 2024!
Once again,
that’s Psalm 56:3:
“When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.”
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.
