en.text: Are you amazed when you see the work
Jehovah is accomplishing
through the earthly part of his organization?
Each year, more individuals
are being reached with the good news.
We are blessed with a variety of new spiritual food.
Worldwide construction work is ongoing,
and relief aid is provided
to victims of disasters.
The Governing Body has asked me
to convey their deep appreciation for the gifts you give
of your time, energy, and resources
to assist with this work.
You may wonder, ‘How do we make sure
‘that we have the financial means needed
to care for all of this activity?’
Following the principle at Luke 14:28,
each year, branch offices of Jehovah’s Witnesses
“calculate the expense”
of the projects needed
and prepare a budget to ensure funds will be available.
Your kind donations play a significant role
in this budgeting process.
You’re following the principle at 1 Corinthians 16:2.
Here the first-century congregation
was encouraged to plan their financial contributions.
They were told:
“On the first day of every week,
“each of you should set something aside
according to his own means.”
Your generous and consistent practice of ‘setting something aside’
helps us to be confident that the work that’s planned
can be accomplished with Jehovah’s blessing.
In the following video,
notice how throughout the history of Jehovah’s modern-day organization,
brothers and sisters have benefited
from the practice of setting something aside.
Throughout the years,
various arrangements have been used
to set something aside.
Starting in the early 1890’s, an insert was provided
in the December 15 issue of The Watch Tower.
Brothers and sisters could send this insert to the branch office
to indicate how much they hoped to be able to contribute
to the “Good Hopes Fund” in the coming year.
Regarding this method of giving,
The Watch Tower  of December 15, 1896, stated:
“Knowing in advance
“what the friends wish and hope to do
“enables us the better to regulate the work
economically and efficiently.”
However, The Watchtower  of May 1, 1959,
made it clear that this indication
was not an obligation.
It said: “This is not a pledge
“but merely a statement
“of what one hopes to be able to contribute
during the coming year.”
Today, using donate.jw.org,
there are various donation methods available to contribute
what one has set aside.
Recurring donations help
to provide an indication of funds that are available.
There’s also an arrangement where one can set up
a legally executed will
to stipulate what they wish to give
to the organization, and this helps the organization
plan better for the future.
They can cancel or change the arrangement
according to their circumstances,
but it gives them an opportunity to experience Jehovah’s joy in giving.
When I participated
in the disaster relief work,
I was really moved to see with my own eyes
how the donations were actually being used.
Because I wanted to express my appreciation for these activities,
I set up an online donation.
From the monthly appreciation letters,
we learn that the real needs of our brothers around the world
are being cared for through our donations.
Those letters make me feel
that I’m working unitedly with Jehovah’s organization.
The important decision we made
was to follow the advice of the apostle Paul, to really put aside
a specific value.
So we planned: We calculated our cost,
we analyzed the situation, we prayed on the subject.
And then we saw the importance
of making a will.
Jehovah gave us everything,
so I think we’re just returning what Jehovah gave us.
I have come to realize that, in general,
contributions are not a pocket condition but a heart condition.
Contributing to Jehovah’s organization
makes me happy.
It helps me to set a reminder each month to contribute,
because there is a lot that could cause me to forget.
So setting the reminder
helps me to remember
to contribute toward Jehovah’s organization.
It doesn’t matter whether we contribute a lot or a little,
but what is important is that we contribute with our whole heart.
That makes Jehovah very happy.
It is heartwarming to see how Jehovah’s people follow the principle
at 1 Corinthians 16:2
and “set something aside” regularly
to show their Christian love for the worldwide association of brothers.
These last days are bringing economic challenges to many of us.
But please be assured
that Jehovah values what you do in his service,
no matter how small it may seem in your own eyes.
It’s our prayer that Jehovah continues to bless your practice
of setting something aside.
Thank you for all you’ve done and continue to do.

ko.text: 함께 성경을 펴서 요한 계시록 7장을 살펴보실까요?
7장에 나오는 매우 흥미진진한 예언에 관한 몇 가지 요점에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
그렇게 하면 여러 가지 임명을 수행하면서 여호와를 위해 열심히 일하려는 우리의 열망을
어떻게 강화할 수 있는지 알게 될 것입니다.
요한 계시록 7:1-3을 보면 요한이 무엇을 보고 어떤 말을 들었는지 알게 됩니다.
네 천사가 파괴적인 바람을 붙잡아 땅과 바다를 해치지 못하게 하죠.
지금 우리 눈에 보이지는 않지만, 강력한 천사들이 큰 환난의 파괴적인 바람을 붙잡고 있습니다.
뭘 기다리는 걸까요? 3절을 보면 어떤 중요한 일을 기다리고 있는지 알 수 있습니다.
14만 4000명 중 땅에 남아 있는 자들이 하늘의 상을 위해 최종 인장을 받게 될 때를 기다리고 있는 거죠.
4-8절을 보면 영적 이스라엘에 속한 모든 자들이 인장을 받을 것임을 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
생각해 보십시오. 머지않아 그들은 통치를 시작할 준비를 갖추게 될 것입니다.
그러면 사탄의 제도는 사라지고 새로운 정부가 들어설 것입니다.
새로운 왕국 정부가 온 땅을 통치하는 거죠.
그러면 땅에서 살 희망을 가진 사람들의 경우는 어떠합니까?
“그 후에 내가 보니, [아마도 요한은 외경심을 느끼고 흥분해서 이렇게 말합니다]
아무도 셀 수 없는 큰 무리가 모든 나라와 종족과 민족과 언어에서 나와 왕좌 앞과 ‘어린양’ 앞에 희고 긴 옷을 입고 서 있었다.
그들의 손에는 야자나무 가지가 있었다. 그들은 계속 큰 소리로 외쳤다.
‘우리의 구원은 왕좌에 앉아 계신 우리 하느님과 “어린양”에게 있습니다.’”
그리고 오늘의 성구인 14절을 보면 이렇게 나오죠.
“이 사람들은 큰 환난에서 나오는 사람들입니다.” 이 예언은 어떤 점을 알려 줍니까?
오늘날 모든 나라와 종족과 언어에서 나온 셀 수 없이 많은 사람들
즉 큰 무리가 모아들여지고 있으며 그들은 다가오는 큰 환난을 생존할 것이라는 점을 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
물론 우리가 아는 것처럼, 1935년에 여호와의 백성이 이 예언의 의미를 명확하게 이해한 후로
많은 형제 자매들이 궁금하게 생각한 점이 있었습니다. 이 큰 무리가 얼마나 많을 것인가 하는 점입니다.
우린 여전히 이 점에 관심이 많죠. 오늘날 큰 무리의 수는 800만 명이 넘습니다.
그리고 매년 늘어나고 있죠. 2016 봉사 연도부터 2020 봉사 연도까지 지난 5년간
130만 명 이상이 침례를 받았다는 사실을 아십니까?
지난 5년간 매일 평균 750명이 넘는 사람들이 새로운 제자가 되었다는 뜻입니다!
그리고 2021 봉사 연도 초반의 보고만 보더라도 “밭이 희어져 수확하게 되었다”는 말씀이
여전히 참되다는 것을 알 수 있죠.
최근에 봉사 위원회 사무실에 들어온 두 가지 격려적인 보고를 들려 드리고 싶은데요.
그 지부가 감독하는 구역에는 전파되지 않은 구역이 많고 전도인 비율이 2만 명 대 1명입니다.
“팬데믹에도 불구하고 야외에서 꾸준히 성장이 이어져 큰 격려를 받았습니다.
국가에서 팬데믹으로 인한 제한 조치를 시행하고 도움을 주기 위해 외국에서 온 많은 형제들이 떠났는데도,
이 지부는 2020 봉사 연도에 관할 구역에서 전도인이 5퍼센트 증가했다고 보고했습니다.
“성서 연구 건수가 꾸준히 증가해 왔습니다. 집회 참석자 수도 점점 증가하고 있습니다.
2021년 기념식 참석자 수는 작년보다 20퍼센트 증가했는데, 전도인 수의 세 배가 넘는 사람들이 참석한 것입니다.”
또한 이 지부는 그 나라의 주요 언어들 중 한 언어 구역에서 사람들이 극심한 가난, 영양실조, 문맹,
빈약한 전기와 인터넷 시설에도 불구하고 성경에 큰 관심을 보인다고 보고했습니다.
이 지역의 한 회중에서 들어온 보고를 말씀드리죠.
이 회중에는 30명의 전도인이 있고 그중 4명은 임시 특별 파이오니아인데요.
성서 연구 건수가 126건이나 됩니다. 그런데 더 놀라운 사실이 있습니다.
이 지부의 보고에 따르면, 많은 경우 그러한 연구에는 한 번에 8명에서 10명의 연구생이 함께 그룹으로 연구를 한다고 합니다.
그리고 전도인이 30명인 이 회중에서 올해 기념식에 2200명이 넘는 사람들이 참석했습니다.
성서 연구생들은 각자 여러 명의 연구생들을 가르치고 있고, 그 연구생들도 다른 사람들에게 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
지부의 보고에 따르면 이 구역 사람들은 성경에 대해 배우려는 열망이 아주 강합니다.
예수의 말씀처럼 눈을 들어 밭을 보면 무엇이 보입니까?
큰 무리의 수가 지금보다 더 많이 늘어날 가능성이 크다는 것을 알 수 있죠.
그런데 이 같은 보고는 왕국 소식이 전해지지 않은 곳에서만 들어오는 것이 아닙니다.
유럽의 한 큰 지부에서는 지부에 소속된 12개 나라 중 8개 나라에서
2021년 기념식 참석자 수가 신기록을 달성했다고 보고했습니다.
해당 지부 사무실이 위치한 나라의 경우, 마지막으로 기념식 참석자 수 신기록을 달성한 때는
현재 그 나라에서는 전도인 수와 파이오니아 수도 신기록을 달성했으며,
재활동을 시작한 전도인의 수도 증가했고 무활동이 되는 전도인들의 수는 줄어들었습니다.
네, 밭을 보면 무엇을 볼 수 있습니까?
끝이 오기 전에 더 많은 사람들이, 수십 만명, 어쩌면 수백만 명이 더 우리와 함께 참숭배를 드리게 될까요?
사도 요한이 환상에서 큰 무리를 “아무도 셀 수 없었다”고 말하기는 했지만,
여호와와 예수께서는 누가 자신에게 속한 사람들인지 아신다는 것입니다.
2002년에 “사람들이 ‘어떻게 들을 수 있겠습니까?’”라는 제목의 기사에서 충실한 종은 다음과 같이 말했습니다.
“이 활동에 대한 책임은 여호와께 있으며, 그분은 자신의 천사들을 사용하여 이 일을 감독하고 계십니다.
모든 나라에 어느 정도나 증거할 것인지를 결정하실 분은 바로 그분입니다.
여호와께서는 원하시기만 하면 더 많은 사람들이 ‘좋은 소식의 말씀을 듣고 믿도록’
우리가 전혀 예상하지 못했던 방법으로 왕국 소식이 널리 전해지게 하실 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 하시는 일은 그분이 어떤 분이냐 하는 사실,
즉 사랑이 많으시고 지혜로우시며 공정하신 하느님이라는 사실과 온전히 조화를 이룰 것입니다.”
1세기에 예수께서는 사람들이 ‘목자 없는 양처럼 내버려진’ 것을 보셨습니다.
성경은 그분이 그들을 불쌍히 여기셨다고 알려 주죠.
그분은 그런 깊은 감정에서 우러나와 사람들을 돕기 위해 행동하셨습니다.
그분은 땅에 계실 때 제자들에게 두 번이나 이렇게 말씀하셨죠.
그러고 나서 “수확하는 주인에게 수확할 일꾼들을 보내 달라고 청하라”고 하셨습니다.
오늘날의 수확 활동에 대해 여호와와 예수께서는 어떤 생각을 갖고 계실까요?
그분들은 무엇이 필요한지 아시고 중앙장로회와 전 세계 지부 위원회를 통해
이 점은 우리가 임명을 수행하면서 그들을 지원하도록 어떻게 힘을 줍니까?
예수께서 제자들에게 하신 말씀은 우리가 수확하는 주인이신 여호와께
수확할 일꾼들을 보내 달라고 계속 청해야 한다는 점을 일깨워 줍니다.
수확하는 이 일이 여호와께서 원하시는 만큼 이루어지게 해 달라는 우리의 기도는 분명히 응답될 것입니다.
예수처럼 우리도 수확하는 일꾼이 됨으로 그 기도에 대한 응답이 될 수 있습니다.
지금까지 살펴본 이런 흥미로운 점들을 생각하면 정말 힘이 납니다.
베델이나 야외에서 우리가 하는 일이 결코 헛되지 않다는 것을 느끼게 해 주죠.
오늘도 우리에게는 간절하게 기도하고 전파하고 가르치는 일을 하고
다양한 방법으로 왕국 활동을 지원할 수 있는 특권이 있습니다.
우리 모두 그러한 일들을 최선을 다해 수행해야겠습니다.
그렇게 한다면 큰 무리의 수가 더욱더 많아지게 하는 데 기여할 수 있을 것입니다.

en.text: Well, this morning I invite you to open up
your Bible with me to Revelation chapter 7.
Let’s review a few highlights
of this extremely exciting prophecy
in its context.
Doing so will help us
to see what will strengthen
our desire to work hard for Jehovah
in our various assignments.
As you look at Revelation 7:1-3,
you’ll notice quickly what John saw and heard
—four angels holding back destructive winds
from harming the earth and the sea.
What does it teach us?
Right now, though invisible to our eyes,
powerful angels are holding back
the destructive winds of the great tribulation.
What are they waiting for?
Verse 3 indicates that one key event
involves the confirmation that the remaining ones on earth
of the 144,000
have been finally sealed for their heavenly reward.
Verses 4 to 8 go on to give us assurance
that the full number of spiritual Israel
will be sealed.
Think of that.
Soon the full staff making up our heavenly government will be installed.
Then it will be out with the old
and in with the new
—the new Kingdom government ruling over the entire earth.
But now, where do those with an earthly hope
fit in to this prophecy?
Let’s read together verses 9 and 10 of Revelation chapter 7:
“After this I saw
“[and perhaps with a measure of excitement and awe, John says],
“and look! a great crowd, which no man was able to number,
“out of all nations and tribes and peoples and tongues,
“standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes;
“and there were palm branches in their hands.
“And they keep shouting with a loud voice, saying:
“‘Salvation we owe to our God, who is seated on the throne,
and to the Lamb.’”
Our day’s text (in verse 14) goes on to explain
that “these are the ones
who come out of the great tribulation.”
Well, what does the prophecy remind us of?
It clearly indicates that today a great crowd
—an unnumbered multilingual,
multinational, multitribal crowd of people—
are being gathered who will survive the coming great tribulation.
Of course, as we’ve researched and read,
we know that after this prophecy was clarified
for Jehovah’s people in 1935,
a common question circulated among Jehovah’s people:
How great will the great crowd turn out to be?
You know, that is still an intriguing question.
Today, the great crowd numbers over eight million.
But it’s growing every year.
Did you know that during the last five service years,
from 2016 through 2020,
over 1.3 million new disciples were baptized?
During the last five service years —that’s an average
of over 750 new disciples every day!
And early indications for this year,
the 2021 service year,
are that the fields continue to be
very “white for harvesting.”
I thought it would be encouraging to share with you two examples
that we received in the Service Committee Office recently.
In April 2021, a branch office
with much untouched territory
and a ratio of 1 publisher to over 20,000 persons
submitted this report:
“Despite the pandemic, we have been greatly encouraged
“to see sustained and accelerated growth in the field.
“We have observed publisher peaks
“continue for 27 months in a row
“in spite of a nationwide lockdown
and the exodus of need-greaters.”
The same branch territory reported during the 2020 service year
a 5 percent publisher increase.
The report goes on:
“The number of Bible studies has steadily increased.
“Meeting attendances have also progressively increased.
“The 2021 Memorial attendance
“was a 20 percent increase over 2020,
which is more than three times the number of publishers.”
In one of their main language fields,
the branch reports that in spite of extreme poverty,
malnutrition, illiteracy, lack of electricity and Internet,
they are seeing an explosion of interest in the Bible.
Consider the report from just one congregation in this region.
One congregation with 30 publishers,
which includes four temporary special pioneers,
is reporting 126 Bible studies.
But we have to look a little deeper to get the full story.
The branch reports that a Bible study in this congregation
is often a group of eight to ten Bible students
studying the Bible together.
They have over 300 regularly attending the meetings.
And at the Memorial this year, the congregation of 30
had more than 2,200 in attendance.
Each Bible student
is conducting dozens of his or her own Bible studies,
and they, in turn, are conducting their own studies.
People in this area, the branch reports,
are desperately hungering and thirsting for spiritual truth.
What an encouraging report!
Like Jesus, as we lift up our eyes
and we view the fields, what do we see?
Tremendous potential for the great crowd
to be even greater than it is today.
Brothers and sisters, such reports of increase
are not isolated to lands with virgin territory.
One of the larger branches in Europe recently reported
that for the 2021 Memorial this past spring,
they experienced all-time peaks
in 8 of the 12 countries they oversee.
In the country where the branch office is located,
the last time they experienced a peak
for the Memorial was in 1994
—27 years ago!
Now that same country is reporting
all-time peaks in publishers and pioneers,
an increase in the number of reactivated publishers,
and a decrease in the number of publishers going inactive.
Again, what do we see
when we look at the fields?
You know, we have to ask the question,
Will hundreds of thousands more
—could millions more—
join us in true worship before the end comes?
Well, we’ll have to wait and see.
But what do we know?
Though the apostle John in his vision reported
that “no man was able to number” the great crowd,
we know that Jehovah and Jesus know who belong to them.
Back in 2002, in an article entitled “How Will They Hear?,”
notice the comment made by the faithful slave:
“Jehovah is responsible for this work
“and is using his angels to oversee it.
“He is the one to determine to what extent
“the witness is to be given to all the nations.
“If Jehovah chooses, he can see that the Kingdom message
“is spread in ways that we cannot yet imagine
so that many more people may ‘hear the word of the good news and believe.’”
In conclusion, the article says:
“What Jehovah does will be in full harmony with who he is
—a loving, wise, and just God.”
You know, in the first century when Jesus saw the crowds of people
that “were thrown about like sheep without a shepherd,”
the Bible reports that he felt pity
—deep-seated emotion—
that moved him to action.
On two occasions when he was with his disciples here on the earth,
he said: “The harvest is great, but the workers are few.”
And then he encouraged us to “beg the Master of the harvest
to send out workers into his harvest.”
Well, how do we think Jehovah and Jesus
feel about the harvest work today?
They see the need, and they’re responding to the need
through the Governing Body and through the oversight
of branch committees worldwide.
How does this strengthen us to support them in our assignments?
Well, Jesus’ words to his disciples back then
remind us that we want to keep begging the Master of the harvest, Jehovah,
to send out workers into his harvest.
Our prayers for this work
to be accomplished to the extent and on the scale that Jehovah desires
will be answered.
But there’s something more.
Like Jesus, we can be the answer to that prayer
by being workers in the harvest.
All of this is very encouraging and exciting
—a reminder that our work here at Bethel or in various field assignments
is not in vain, brothers and sisters.
So may we today view our privileges
—the privilege to pray earnestly, the privilege to preach and teach,
the privilege to support the Kingdom work in various ways—
to move us to do our part
to contribute to the great crowd
turning out to be very great.

cn.text: 今天早上
我们会一起看看启示录第7章
我们会讨论一下
这个令人兴奋的预言和它的上下文
我们越是理解圣经的预言
就越渴望
在各自的岗位上热心地为耶和华服务
我们先看一下启示录7:1-3怎么说
这里告诉我们使徒约翰看到什么、听到什么
就是四个天使正抓住大地四方的风
不让它们伤害地和海
这告诉我们什么呢？
虽然我们看不见
但大能的天使正抓住大患难那带来毁灭的风
天使在等什么呢？
第3节的经文告诉我们其中一个重要的原因
就是要等到14万4000个
受任命的基督徒当中
那些还在地上的人盖印完毕
紧接着4到8节的经文向我们保证
上帝以色列的全数将会盖印完毕
想想看
我们天上政府的所有成员很快就会集结起来
到时旧的会消逝
新的将开始
就是上帝的王国将会统治整个地球
有希望在地上得享永生的人会怎样呢？
我们来继续读启示录7:9,10
经文说
“之后，我看见一大群人
［可能当时约翰也很惊讶、很兴奋］
没有人能数得过来
是从所有国族、部族、民族、语言来的
他们站在宝座和绵羊羔面前
身穿白袍，手拿棕榈枝
他们不断大声说
我们得救
全靠宝座上我们的上帝
以及绵羊羔”
然后第14节的经文解释说
“这些人是从大患难中出来的”
预言告诉我们什么呢？
它清楚地指出
今天正有一大群人被聚集起来
他们来自不同的国家
不同的语言、不同的民族
这群人有机会渡过将临的大患难
我们研读的时候就会知道
耶和华的子民更加明白了这个预言的含义
从那时起
很多人心里都有这个疑问
经文说的“大群人”到底会有多少人呢？
我们都想知道这个问题的答案
今天“大群人”的数字已经超过了八百万
而且每年都还在增长！
你知道吗？
在过去的五个工作年度
就是从2016年到2020年
有超过130万人受浸
也就是说在这段时间
平均每天都有超过750个人受浸
就在今年
就是2021年工作年度的上半年
我们看到田地依然是变白的
可以收割了！
传道委员会办事处最近收到很多报告
我想跟大家分享其中的两个例子
2021年4月我们收到一个分部提交的报告
这个分部督导的地区里
很多地方都没有传道员探访过
传道员和人口的比例呢?
是1比2万多
报告说
虽然现在是疫情
但我们的传道活动却非常稳定
并不断扩展
虽然整个国家都被封锁
很多扩大服务的弟兄姐妹也离开这里
但在过去的27个月里
传道员的数字每月都创新高
这个分部报告说

title: 해럴드 코컨: 다른 사람들과 그들이 하는 일을 소중히 여김으로 하느님을 본받으십시오 (히브리 6:10)

ko.text: 오늘의 성구 내용을 살펴보기 위해 히브리서 6:10을 다시 한번 보시겠습니다.
여러분이 행한 일과 그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑을 잊지 않으십니다.’
잠깐, 여호와께서 불의하지 않으시다는 점에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
누군가가, 이 경우엔 여호와께서 언제나 옳은 일을 하신다는 것이죠.
늘 공정하시고 항상 옳은 일만 하시죠.
신명기 32:4에서 하느님에 대해 이렇게 말하는 바와 같습니다.
“반석이신 그분의 모든 길은 공의로우니 그분의 활동은 완전하다.
결코 불공정하지 않으신 충실한 하느님, 의롭고 올바른 분이다.”
그가 소돔과 고모라에 관해 여호와와 나눈 대화를 기억하시죠?
아브라함은 여호와의 의로움에 대해 무엇이라고 말했습니까?
‘주께서 이렇게 행하시어 의로운 사람을 악한 사람과 함께 죽이신다는 것은
그런 다음 “온 땅의 심판관께서 옳은 일을 하지 않으시렵니까?”라고 말했습니다.
그러니까 오늘의 성구를 통해 알 수 있는 매우 격려적인 사실은
그 점을 생각하면 정말 안심이 되죠.
그리고 우리도 여호와를 본받기 위해 최선을 다합니다.
우리는 동료 형제 자매들이 하는 일을 눈여겨보고
그렇게 하는 데 무엇이 도움이 될까요?
함께 성경을 펴서 베드로 전서 3:8을 보겠습니다.
우리가 여호와를 본받아 다른 사람들에게 존중심과 감사를 표현하는 데
어떤 특성들이 도움이 되는지 유의해 보시죠.
동료감과 형제 애정과 부드러운 동정심과 겸손을 나타내십시오.”
이런 특성들이 여호와를 본받는 데 어떻게 도움이 됩니까?
먼저 동료감에 대해 잠시 이야기해 보겠습니다.
이 특성은 우리가 형제 자매들의 수고를 당연하게 여기지 않는 데 어떻게 도움이 됩니까?
우리는 열심히 일하는 형제 자매들을 관찰하면서
자신에게 몇 가지 질문을 해 볼 수 있습니다.
‘내가 저 형제나 자매의 임명을 맡았다면 어떤 느낌이 들까?
어떻게 저렇게 비이기적으로 일할 수 있지?
똑같은 임명을 저렇게 오랫동안 수행하다니, 정말 대단해.’
또 이렇게 자문해 볼 수 있죠.
누군가가 알아주고 칭찬해 주면 어떤 느낌이 들까?’
이런 생각도 해 볼 수 있죠.
다른 형제들에게도 필요하다는 것을 알게 됩니다.
“그러므로 무엇이든지 사람들이 여러분에게 해 주기를 바라는 것을
여러분도 사람들에게 해 주어야 합니다”라고 했죠.
일을 더 잘하도록 동기를 부여해 주는 한 전문가가 한 말이 떠오르는데요,
그 사람은 고용주와 고용인의 관계에 대해 이야기한 적이 있습니다.
물론 우리는 그런 관계가 아니라 동료 일꾼이지만, 배울 점이 있습니다.
고용인들이 고용주에게 칭찬을 거의 듣지 못한다고 불평하는 경우가 많다고 말했습니다.
그리고 관찰해 보니 실제로 그런 경우들이 있다고 했죠.
고용주가 자신에게 관심이 없다고 느꼈기 때문이다.”
형제들에게 관심을 나타내고 그들을 소중한 존재로 여기게 될 것입니다.
형제들에게 말하는 방식, 그들을 대하는 태도가 달라지겠죠.
그들을 존중하고 소중히 여기고 있음을 나타내게 될 것입니다.
그렇게 하면 매번 고맙다는 말을 못해도
형제들은 우리가 그들을 대하는 방식을 통해 사랑과 존중을 받는다고 느낄 것입니다.
형제 애정과 동료감과 부드러운 동정심을 갖는다면 어떻게 하게 될까요?
“선한 사람은 자기 마음에 선한 것을 쌓아 두었다가 선한 것을 … 냅니다.
마음에 가득한 것을 입으로 말하는 법입니다.”
우리는 서로를 소중히 여긴다는 것을 자연스럽게 표현하게 될 것입니다.
그리고 그렇게 할 때 언제나 우리를 올바르게 대하시는 여호와를 본받게 되죠.
그러면 이제 이런 점도 생각해 볼까요?
때로는 칭찬하는 것이 적절하지 않아 보이는 상황이 있을 수 있습니다.
우리의 동료 중 누군가를 예로 들어 보죠.
형제일 수도, 자매일 수도 있지만 형제라고 해 보겠습니다.
열심히 일하고, 신뢰할 수 있고, 영적인 사람이죠.
그래서 조언을 듣고 어쩌면 징계를 받아
그런 상황에서 형제는 어떤 감정을 느낄까요?
이 경우에 우리의 동료인 그 형제는 겸손한 사람이라고 해 보겠습니다.
그는 계속 여호와를 섬기기 위해 필요한 변화를 하고 있습니다.
포기하지 않으면서 훌륭한 태도를 보이고 있죠.
그러면 이 상황에서 무엇에 대해 칭찬할 수 있을까요?
하지만 여호와께서는 그 형제에게서 무엇을 보실까요?
정직, 겸손, 참을성을 나타내고 계속 변화하려고 했습니다.
그처럼 힘든 시기를 겪는 사람들에게 이렇게 말씀하십니다.
여러분이 걷는 길을 계속 곧게 하십시오.
이런 점을 살펴보면 죄를 지은 다윗왕이 생각나는데요,
시편 40:12을 보면 그가 어떤 감정을 느꼈는지 알 수 있죠.
“내가 저지른 많은 잘못에 짓눌려 앞을 볼 수 없으니
그것이 내 머리카락보다 많아 나는 낙심하고 말았습니다.”
“당신은 나의 충절 때문에 나를 붙들어 주시니,
나를 영원히 당신 앞에 두실 것입니다.”
어려움 속에서도 좋은 태도를 나타내는 그런 형제들에게 무엇이 필요할까요?
우리도 여호와처럼 그들을 사랑한다는 걸 알려 줄 필요가 있죠.
그들이 나타내는 정직함, 겸손함, 끈기를 칭찬해 줄 수 있습니다.
우리는 여호와께서 그들과 특히 그들이 나타내는
좋은 태도를 소중히 여기신다는 걸 알고 있습니다.
그들은 하늘에 보물을 많이 쌓아 왔습니다.
그런데 잘못을 저질렀다고 해서 여호와께서 그 보물을 버리셨을까요?
그들이 계속 하늘에 보물을 쌓기를 바라십니다.
심각한 죄를 저지른 한 남자가 회개했을 때
바울이 고린도 회중에 한 말과 같습니다.
“그 사람은 여러분 대다수에게서 충분히 꾸짖음을 받았습니다.”
“그러므로 여러분이 그를 사랑하고 있음을 그에게 확신시켜 주기를 권합니다.”
그렇게 할 수 있는 한 가지 방법은 알맞은 때에
훌륭한 태도를 나타내고 포기하지 않은 것에 대해 칭찬할 수 있죠.
이러한 예는 여호와께서 자신의 종들의 수고를 잊지 않으신다는 점을 잘 보여 줍니다.
따라서 여호와를 본받아 항상 올바르고 공정하게 행동하기 위해 노력해야겠습니다.
동료감, 동정심, 사랑을 갖기 위해 계속 노력하도록 합시다.
자신이 필요한 존재이고 소중히 여겨지고 있다고 느끼게 될 것입니다.
우리가 그들을 얼마나 소중히 여기는지 이야기해 줄 수 있습니다.
그렇게 함으로 자신의 종들이 하는 일을 소중히 여기시고
언제나 그들에게 올바른 일을 하시는 하느님을 본받아야겠습니다.

en.text: To begin our discussion of the text,
we invite you to go back to Hebrews 6:10.
And let’s look at the early part of that verse.
Hebrews 6:10 says:
“For God is not unrighteous
“so as to forget your work
and the love you showed for his name.”
For a few moments, we’d like to talk about Jehovah
not being unrighteous.
The opposite of unrighteous would be righteous.
Well, what does “righteous” mean?
It’s a person who, in the case of Jehovah,
always does the right thing.
He’s never acting in an unjust manner.
He’s always fair.
He’s always going to do the right thing.
And that’s the point that Deuteronomy 32:4 shares with us:
“The Rock, perfect is his activity,
“for all his ways are justice.
“A God of faithfulness who is never unjust;
righteous and upright is he.”
So we concur with the feelings of Abraham.
Remember his conversation with Jehovah about Sodom and Gomorrah?
What did Abraham say about Jehovah doing the right thing?
He said in Genesis chapter 18:
“It is unthinkable
“that you would act in this manner
by putting the righteous man to death with the wicked.”
And he said it again: “It is unthinkable of you.”
And then he says: “Will the Judge of all the earth not do what is right?”
So one of the most encouraging aspects of this text is
that Jehovah can be relied on.
He doesn’t change.
He is not going to forget
and act in a way other than what is the right and the fair thing to do.
And that reassures us greatly, doesn’t it?
And we do our very best to imitate Jehovah
in this matter of recognizing to the proper degree
and commending to the proper degree
our fellow workers and showing appreciation.
What can help us do this?
We invite you to open your Bibles
to the book of 1 Peter chapter 3,
and let’s look at verse 8.
That’s 1 Peter 3:8.
Notice some qualities that are essential
to our being able to imitate Jehovah
in showing respect and appreciation.
It says: “Finally, all of you have unity of mind,
“fellow feeling, brotherly affection,
tender compassion, and humility.”
Now, how will these qualities help us to imitate Jehovah?
Well, let’s talk just for a moment about fellow feeling.
How could that help us not take for granted
what our brothers and sisters do as our fellow workers?
Well, we might begin to ask ourselves some questions
as we observe our hardworking fellow workers.
We could pick out someone and say:
‘How would I feel if I had that assignment?
‘How hard that must be!
‘Look at the unselfishness that they show.
‘How tired they must be at times!
Look at how long they’ve been handling the same assignment for so long.’
And then we could ask ourselves,
‘If I had that assignment to perform,
how would I feel if someone recognized me with proper commendation?’
And then we could ask ourselves,
‘How would I feel if no one ever said anything?’
That fellow feeling helps us to understand
what we would need
and how our brothers would need the same.
It reminds us of Matthew 7:12, doesn’t it?
“All things, therefore, that you want men to do to you,
you also must do to them.”
Now, in this connection,
there was a motivational trainer who worked in the secular field,
and he talked about the relationship between employers and employees.
Well, we’re not employers and employees; we’re fellow workers.
But there’s a principle here.
He said that often when dealing with companies,
he would often hear the complaint from the employees
that their employer rarely, if ever, commended them.
And he said in his studies that is sometimes legitimate.
But he said, “What bothered the employees the most was
that they felt there was a lack of personal interest.”
Well, how does that relate?
Well, when we have fellow feeling and brotherly affection,
we’re going to take a personal interest in our brothers
and we’re going to view them as having value and worth.
It will affect how we talk to them, how we treat them,
how we show them that we honor them and respect them and we value them.
When we do that,
we don’t always have to say thank you.
They know that we love them and appreciate them
by the way we deal with them.
However, the fact is,
if we have brotherly affection and fellow feeling
and tender compassion in our heart for our fellow workers,
what’s going to happen?
What does Luke 6:45 say?
“A good man brings good out of the good treasure of his heart, . . .
[and] out of the heart’s abundance his mouth speaks.”
So we can’t help but just express how we feel
about each other when those qualities are in our heart.
And in this way, we’re imitating Jehovah,
who always does the right thing in dealing with us.
Well, now let’s take a few moments to talk about a situation
where we may not always think that recognition or commendation
would be appropriate.
Let’s take, for example, one of our fellow workers.
It could be a brother or sister, but in this case,
we’re going to use a brother.
And this brother has served faithfully for many years
—conscientious, trustworthy, spiritual.
He’s poured his heart into his assignment.
And then because of negligence,
a lapse in good judgment,
or caving in to a fleshly weakness,
he is counseled,
perhaps even disciplined,
and even loses a privilege of service.
Now, what might that person be going through?
Well, in this case, let’s say that this person,
our fellow worker, is humble.
He was honest.
He admitted his mistake.
He sought help.
He accepted the counsel.
But now he’s having to deal with ‘putting his hand to the plow’ and moving ahead.
He doesn’t want to stop.
He has a great attitude.
Well, now, what could be commended in this situation?
Well, we certainly wouldn’t want to commend the negligence
or lack of good judgment or failing to exercise self-control.
But what does Jehovah see in this person now
with the good attitude that we described:
the honesty, the humility, the endurance, the determination to move forward?
Well, Jehovah loves that person.
Jehovah loved that person when He disciplined them.
And then, at Hebrews 12:12, 13,
Jehovah says to those who have gone through a difficult time like that
to “strengthen the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,
“and keep making straight paths for your feet,
so that . . . [you] may be healed.”
So Jehovah still loves that person.
And, you know, this reminds us, too, of King David
after his sins.
At Psalm 40:12, notice the feeling that he had.
He said: “So many of my errors
“overwhelm me that I cannot see my way;
they are more numerous than the hairs of my head, and I have lost heart.”
But then in the next psalm, Psalm 41, he says:
“As for me, you [Jehovah] uphold me
“because of my integrity;
you will keep me in your presence forever.”
So, what do our brothers need at a time like that when their attitude is good?
They need to be reminded that we love them just as Jehovah loves them.
And we commend them for their honesty and their humility
and their stick-to-itiveness and not quitting.
And we know that Jehovah views them as precious,
especially with their good attitude.
And all those treasures that they had stored up in heaven
prior to their difficulty—
Has Jehovah thrown those treasures out?
No.
He still retains them, and he’s more than happy for them
to start putting more treasures up in heaven
because he appreciates it very much.
So it’s like Paul said to the congregation in Corinth,
at 2 Corinthians 2:6-8,
after the man who sinned seriously was repentant.
What did Paul say?
“This rebuke given by the majority is sufficient for such a man.”
And then he goes on to say:
“I therefore exhort you to confirm your love for him.”
And one way we can do that is by appropriately,
and to the proper degree at the right time,
commend him for his excellent attitude and his willingness not to stop.
Well, that’s just another example
of how Jehovah doesn’t forget works of his servants,
and neither should we.
So in imitation of Jehovah,
let’s always strive to do the right thing, the fair thing.
Let’s have the fellow feeling as we do; continue with it
—the compassion and the love for each other.
And then that would automatically make others feel needed, wanted, and appreciated.
And we can add to that by expressions from our heart,
telling them directly how much we value them.
By doing this, we will be imitating our appreciative God,
who always does the right thing to those who serve him.

cn.text: 我们先来读一下
希伯来书6:10上半部分的经文
希伯来书6:10
经文说
“上帝并非不义
他不会忘记你们所做的工作
和你们为他的名字显出的爱心”
我们先讨论一下这句话
“上帝并非不义”
不义的反义词就是正义
那“正义”是什么意思呢？
就是一个人总是做对的事
耶和华上帝就是这样的
他绝不会做不公正的事
他总是公平正义，也一直会做对的事
申命记32:4就是这样描绘他的
“他是磐石，所做的完美无瑕
他做的事全都公正
他是信实可靠的上帝
大公无私，又正义又正直”
我们都会认同亚伯拉罕的话
他曾跟耶和华谈到所多玛和蛾摩拉的事
他完全相信耶和华一定会做对的事
你记得他是怎么说的吗？
在创世记第18章
亚伯拉罕这样说
“你绝对不会把正义的人
和邪恶的人一起处死！”
他还说
“你是绝对不会这样做的
审判全世界的主难道会处事不公正吗？”
这段记载给人很大的鼓励
包括让我们确信我们可以信赖耶和华
他永不会改变，他绝不会忘记什么是公正
也绝不会做出任何不公正的事
这给我们很大的安慰，对吗？
我们要尽己所能向耶和华学习
就是要留意到弟兄姐妹付出的努力
并用适当的方法称赞他们
可以怎么做呢？
请打开圣经到彼得前书第3章
我们会读一下彼得前书3:8的经文
这节经文列出了一些美好的特质
培养这些特质，能帮助我们效法耶和华
尊重和珍视别人
经文说
“最后，你们人人都要思想一致，将心比心
怀有弟兄之情、怜恤之心，为人谦卑”
这些特质怎样帮助我们效法耶和华呢？
我们先谈一谈“将心比心”这句话
如果我们将心比心
就不会把弟兄姐妹付出的努力视为理所当然
怎么做呢？
看到弟兄姐妹勤奋工作时
我们可以问自己一些问题
比如，我们可以问问自己
“我做这份工作的话，会有什么感受呢？
这份工作太不容易了！
但他们多么无私啊！
他们一定有时候很累
这么长时间，他们一直做同样的工作”
可以问问自己
“如果我做这份工作
别人称赞和鼓励我，我会有什么感受呢？”
然后再问问自己
“如果从来没有人称赞我又怎么样呢？”
如果我们将心比心
就会知道自己需要什么
也会理解别人的感受
这就是马太福音7:12的话，对吗？
“无论什么事，你们希望别人怎样对待你们
你们就要怎样对待别人”
我们举个例子
有一位从事职业培训的专业人员
有一次谈到了老板和员工之间的关系
当然了，我们不是老板和员工
我们是弟兄姐妹
但我们也可以参考他说的话
他说，他常常听到员工们抱怨说
他们的老板很少
甚至从来都不会称赞他们
他说，这样的情况有时是可以理解的
但最让员工感到不舒服的是
他们觉得老板不关心他们
可以学到什么呢？
如果我们将心比心、怀有弟兄之爱
就会真诚地关心我们的弟兄姐妹
珍视他们和他们的服务
这会影响到我们怎样对待他们
怎样跟他们说话，也会让我们更加尊重他们
把他们视为宝贵的人
这样做，有时甚至不需要说“谢谢你”
弟兄姐妹就知道我们珍视他们、爱他们
另外还有一点
如果我们将心比心
心里充满了弟兄之情、怜恤之心
会怎么样呢？
路加福音6:45说
“良善的人心里积存良善，就发出良善……
因为人心里充满什么，他的口就说出什么”
所以很自然地
如果我们心里充满了这些美好的特质
我们就会向别人表达出来
这样做，我们就是在效法耶和华
而他总是用正确的方式对待我们
接下来我们讨论一种情况
我们可能会觉得在这种情况下
称赞和鼓励对方并不是那么恰当
举例来说，有一个基督徒
他可能是个弟兄，也可能是个姐妹
我们以弟兄为例
这位弟兄很多年都很忠贞
他很勤奋，很值得信任，也很爱耶和华
他全心投入在工作上
但由于疏忽大意
或者缺乏判断力
又或者由于一时的软弱
他受到了劝告
甚至被管教
因此失去了服务的机会
那他会有什么感受呢？
假设例子中提到的这位弟兄非常谦卑
他很诚实
他承认自己的过错、寻求帮助
也接受劝告
现在他就要“手扶着犁”继续前进
他不想停下来
他真的有很好的态度
那我们可以称赞这位弟兄吗？
我们当然不想称赞他疏忽大意、缺乏判断力
或者没有保持自制
但耶和华看到这位弟兄
非常诚实
非常谦卑、保持忍耐
又决心继续前进
他会有什么感受呢？
耶和华很爱他
耶和华很爱他所以管教他
耶和华对处于这种情况的人说
“要让下垂的手变得强壮
使软弱的膝变得有力
不断修直你们脚下的道路……得到医治”
可见耶和华还是很爱这样的人
这让我们想起大卫王
犯罪之后，他在诗篇40:12这样写道
“许多罪过压倒我，我看不到出路
我的罪过比我的头发还多
我不禁灰心丧气”
然后在诗篇第41篇，大卫说
“我是忠义的，所以你扶持我
让我永远侍立在你面前”
我们可以怎样对待犯了错
但有很好态度的弟兄呢？
我们可以让他们知道
我们像耶和华一样，很爱他们
我们可以称赞他们很诚实、很谦卑
坚守忠义，毫不放弃
我们知道，耶和华很珍视他们
很赏识他们的态度
那这些弟兄在犯过之前
在天上积存的财宝又怎样呢？
耶和华会把它们扔出去吗？
不，他会继续保存
他很高兴看到这些弟兄继续在天上积存财宝
因为他真的很爱他们
你还记得保罗写给哥林多会众的信吗？
会众里有一个人犯下严重的罪
但后来悔改
在哥林多后书2:6-8，保罗怎么说呢？
“这样的人受过大多数人的谴责，也就够了”
然后他又说
“我劝你们，要让他确实知道你们爱他”
我们可以怎么做呢？
就是要在恰当的时间、用恰当的方式
称赞这些悔改的人
称赞他有很好的态度
也称赞他不放弃真理
这个例子很好地说明
耶和华不会忘记他的忠仆
我们也不会
我们要效法耶和华
努力做对的事
做公平公正的事
所以，让我们继续将心比心
怀有怜恤之情
彼此相爱
我们这样做，就会让别人感到
受重视、有价值
我们还可以怎么做呢？
就是直接告诉他们
我们有多么珍视他们
这样做，我们就是在效法耶和华上帝
他总是珍视那些忠心崇拜他的人！

ko.text: 이번 달 방송에서 우리는 좋은 소식이 무엇인지, 그것이 왜 축복인지 살펴볼 것입니다.
또한 성경 시대와 현대의 훌륭한 본들이
우리가 좋은 소식에 담긴 모든 내용을 담대하게 선포하도록 어떻게 격려하는지 알아볼 것입니다.
그리고 르완다의 한 충실한 형제를 통해 박해를 받고 투옥되어도
어떻게 계속 열심히 좋은 소식을 전할 수 있는지 살펴볼 것입니다.
우리가 사람들에게 좋은 소식을 전하면서 얼마나 큰 기쁨을 누리는지 보여 줄 것입니다.
여호와의 증인인 우리에게는 놀라운 특권이 있습니다.
그러면 그 좋은 소식에는 무엇이 포함됩니까?
그 점을 아는 것이 우리가 좋은 소식을 더 열심히 선포하려는 마음을 갖는 데 어떻게 도움이 될까요?
이 질문들에 대한 답을 함께 생각해 보시죠.
성경에서 이 표현이 어떻게 사용되었는지 살펴보면 그 답을 알 수 있습니다.
“평화의 좋은 소식”, “영원한 좋은 소식”이라는 표현이 나옵니다.
따라서 좋은 소식이란 하느님의 왕국이 통치하는 것과
예수에 대한 믿음을 통해 구원받는 것을 가리킨다고 할 수 있습니다.
또한 여기에는 예수께서 말씀하시고 제자들이 기록한 모든 진리가 포함되죠.
좋은 소식이 전파되는 것에 관해 말씀하셨습니다.
이사야의 예언은 특히 메시아가 오시는 시점부터 전파될 좋은 소식의 목적과
이사야 61:1, 2에 나오는 이러한 내용에 유의해 보십시오.
“주권자인 주 여호와의 영이 내 위에 있다.
여호와께서 나에게 기름을 부으셔서 온유한 사람에게 좋은 소식을 전하게 하셨다.
그분은 나를 보내셔서 마음이 찢긴 사람을 싸매 주고,
갇힌 사람의 눈을 활짝 열어 주게 하셨다.
여호와의 선의의 해와 우리 하느님의 복수의 날을 공포하고,
이 좋은 소식은 듣는 사람들에게 좋은 영향을 미칠 것이었습니다.
“마음이 찢긴 사람을 싸매 주고, … 슬퍼하는 모든 사람을 위로”할 것이었죠.
이것은 우리가 봉사할 때 아주 자주 이야기하는 좋은 소식과 비슷합니다.
낙원이 된 땅에서 하느님의 왕국의 통치를 받으며
그들이 여호와를 사랑하려는 마음을 갖게 해 줍니다.
하지만 좋은 소식에는 또 다른 것도 포함됩니다.
우리가 봉사에서 자주 이야기하지 않는 내용이죠.
“우리 하느님의 복수의 날”이라는 표현에 유의해 보셨습니까?
“여호와의 선의의 해”에 관한 소식만 포함되는 것이 아닙니다.
그 점을 요한 계시록 14:6, 7에 기록된 말씀을 통해 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
“나는 또 다른 천사가 하늘 한가운데를 날고 있는 것을 보았다.
그는 땅에 사는 사람들, 곧 모든 나라와 종족과 언어와 민족에게 선포할
그러므로 하늘과 땅과 바다와 샘들을 만드신 분을 숭배하여라.’”
몇몇 참고 문헌에 따르면, 여기서 “심판”으로 번역된 원어는
하느님께서는 사람들의 행동을 면밀히 관찰하고 계십니다.
모든 거짓 종교 즉 큰 바빌론과
사탄의 세상 제도의 나머지 모든 부분에 대한
하느님의 심판을 선언하고 집행하는 일이 둘 다 있게 됩니다.
물론 큰 바빌론과 이 세상 제도의 나머지 부분은 이미 심판을 받았습니다.
하지만 그 심판은 아직 집행되지 않았죠.
마지막 날이 절정에 이를 때에 있을 것입니다.
그렇기 때문에 오늘날 사람들의 행동이 매우 중요한 것입니다.
하느님께서 심판을 집행하실 때가 빠르게 다가오고 있으므로
우리는 좋은 소식에 담긴 심판의 내용을
그러면 심판에 관한 내용이 왜 좋은 소식이라고 말할 수 있습니까?
그 심판을 통해 모든 불공정과 폭력을 비롯해 악이 사라질 것이기 때문에
올바른 마음을 가진 사람들에게 그것은 좋은 소식이죠.
악한 사람들의 행동으로 인해 고통을 겪고 있는 사람들에게
이 심판은 큰 위안이 될 것입니다!

봉사에서 이 방법을 빨리 사용해 보고 싶으실 것입니다.
좋은 소식에 대해 묵상하면 기회가 있을 때마다 그 소식을 전하고 싶은 마음이 드실 것입니다.
물러서지 않고 그 소식을 알리고 싶어지죠.
바로 이것이 이번 달 뮤직비디오의 주제입니다.
우리의 전파 활동으로 사람들이 좋은 소식을 받아들일 수 있다는 건 정말 행복한 일이 아닙니까?
그들은 또 다른 사람들에게 그 소식을 전할 것입니다. 그리고 그들의 삶도 완전히 달라지게 되죠!
지난달에 우리는 「훌륭한 믿음의 본」이라는 새로운 연재 동영상의 첫 번째 이야기를 보았습니다.
아브라함의 삶에 관해 볼 수 있었죠.
성경에서는 아브라함을 가리켜 “믿음을 가진 모든 사람의 아버지”라고 부릅니다.
아브라함은 살면서 또 어떤 일들을 겪었을까요?
그의 아내 사라가 아들을 낳을 것이라는 말씀이었죠.
사라가 기적적으로 임신을 하여 이삭을 낳은 일은
여호와의 말씀이 항상 이루어진다는 것을 잘 보여 주었습니다.
하지만 방주 안의 여덟 명은 안전하게 있었지.
여호와께서 노아의 가족을 보호해 주신 거야.
그래서 지금 우리가 이렇게 살아 있지.
그 후에도 무서운 일들이 많이 있었지.
하지만 여호와께선 언제나 그분의 약속을 이루셨단다.
파라오가 엄마를 아내로 삼으려고 했을 때
그분이 어떻게 보호해 주셨는지 생각해 보렴.
롯을 구출하기 위해 천사들을 보내 주기도 하셨지.
넌 내 아들이지만 여호와께서도 너의 아버지이시지.
그분은 자신의 목적을 이루는 데 널 사용하실 거야.
늘 여호와를 신뢰할 수 있다는 걸 기억하렴.
여호와께서 우리 가족에게 하신 약속 기억하니?
‘나는 네가 사는 땅을 너와 네 뒤를 이을 자손에게
영속하는 재산으로 주고 그들의 하느님이 되겠다.’
이 영적인 가정에도 힘든 일들이 일어났습니다.
모두가 널 비웃고 있어. 내가 첫째야.
널 좋아하는 사람이 있을 것 같아?
이스마엘의 행동 때문에 사라는 마음이 몹시 아팠죠.
사라가 그 아이와 너의 여종에 대해 너에게 하는 말을 언짢게 여기지 마라.
너의 자손이라고 불릴 자는 이삭을 통해서 있을 것이다.
내가 그 여종의 아들도 한 민족을 이루게 할 것이니,
어려운 일이었지만 아브라함은 순종하여 하갈과 그의 아들 이스마엘을 내보냈습니다.
부디 너의 아들, 네가 그토록 사랑하는 너의 외아들 이삭을 데리고
모리아 땅으로 가서, 내가 너에게 일러 줄 산에서 그를 번제물로 바쳐라.
과거에 아브라함은 하느님의 판결과 결정에 대해
하지만 그분과 더 가까워지고 그분에 대한 믿음이 더 커지면서
자네들은 나귀와 함께 여기에 머물러 있게.
아이와 나는 저기로 가서 숭배를 드리고 돌아오겠네.
여기 불과 나무는 있는데, 번제물로 바칠 양은 어디 있습니까?
아들아, 하느님께서 친히 번제물을 위한 양을 마련하실 것이다.
네가 너의 아들, 너의 외아들까지 나에게 아끼지 않았으니,
네가 하느님을 두려워하는 줄을 이제 내가 알았다.
너의 자손을 통해 땅의 모든 민족이 스스로 축복을 얻을 것이다.
아브라함과 사라와 이삭은 여호와를 온전히 신뢰했습니다.
여호와께서 그들에게 하신 약속은 우리에게도 희망을 줍니다.
우리가 이미 잘 알고 있는 성경 기록들을 깊이 묵상해 보면 그러한 기록들을 더 가치 있게 여기게 됩니다.
또 그런 기록에서 배운 점을 적용해 보고 싶은 마음이 강해지죠.
이번 달에는 아프리카 남쪽에 있는 나라인 레소토에 있는 형제들을 만나 보겠습니다.
레소토는 해발 고도가 1000미터가 넘으며, 그 나라에 있는 일부 산의 정상들은 높이가 그보다 3배나 높습니다.
약 200만 명의 인구 중 대다수가 바소토족 사람들이며 주로 시골 지역에 삽니다.
많은 사람이 생계를 위해 가축을 기르거나 농사를 짓죠.
레소토의 산간 지역에서는 날씨가 급격히 변할 수 있기 때문에 갑작스러운 추위에 대비하고 있어야 합니다.
그래서 바소토족 사람들은 담요를 두르고 다니는 것으로 잘 알려져 있습니다.
특히 겨울에 산들이 눈으로 뒤덮일 때 매우 유용하죠.
우리 형제들은 추위나 고지대에도 불구하고 지난 80여 년 동안 좋은 소식을 널리 전해 왔습니다.
남아프리카 공화국에서 진리를 배운 두 명의 바소토족 증인이 1942년에 레소토로 돌아가
이 어려움이 많은 구역에서 열정적으로 전파했습니다.
9년 뒤에는 작은 회중이 5개 있었고 63명의 증인들이 있었죠.
1960년대와 1970년대에는 열심 있는 복음 전파자들이 지칠 줄 모르고 노력한 덕분에 전파 활동이 계속되었습니다.
현재 3700명이 넘는 전도인들이 매달 4500건 이상의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
레소토 사람들이 험난한 지역에 널리 퍼져 살고 있기 때문에
우리 형제들은 사람들이 사는 곳이면 어디든 찾아가 전파하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
이곳의 많은 형제들은 집회에 가기 위해 가파른 길을 올라가야 합니다.
모코틀롱 회중에 있는 78명의 전도인들이 특히 그러하죠.
그들은 아프리카 남부에서 가장 높은 곳에 있는 왕국회관에서 집회를 봅니다.
레소토에서 가장 높은 곳에 있는 모코틀롱 회중의 형제 자매들이 여러분에게 따뜻한 인사를 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
In this month’s program,
we’ll examine what “the good news” is
and why it’s such a blessing.
We’ll consider how examples from
from the Bible and our modern history encourage us
to declare all of the good news boldly.
We’ll learn from a faithful brother in Rwanda
how we can maintain our zeal for the good news
despite persecution and imprisonment.
And we’ll enjoy a new music video that reminds us
how much joy we can have sharing the good news with others.
This is JW Broadcasting
for October 2023.
As Jehovah’s Witnesses, we have a wonderful privilege
—the privilege of “declaring the good news”!
But just what does that good news include?
If we know the answer,
how will that motivate us
to be even more zealous as we declare the good news?
Let’s consider the answers to those questions.
First of all, what is the good news?
We get an idea by looking at how this expression
is used in the Bible.
For example, we read of “the good news of the Kingdom,”
“the good news of God,”
“the good news about Jesus Christ,”
“the good news of the undeserved kindness of God,”
“the good news of peace,”
and the “everlasting good news.”
So we can say that the good news refers
to the rule of God’s Kingdom
and salvation by faith in Jesus.
This includes all the truths about which Jesus spoke
and the disciples wrote.
Through the prophet Isaiah,
Jehovah spoke about the preaching of the good news.
Isaiah’s prophecy described the purpose
and effect of the good news to be preached,
particularly from the time of Messiah’s coming.
Notice what’s recorded at Isaiah 61:1, 2:
“The spirit of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah is upon me,
“because Jehovah anointed me to declare good news to the meek.
“He sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,
“to proclaim liberty to the captives
“and the wide opening of the eyes to the prisoners,
“to proclaim the year of Jehovah’s goodwill
“and the day of vengeance of our God,
to comfort all who mourn.”
This good news would have a positive effect
on those who listened to it.
It would “bind up the brokenhearted”
and “comfort all who mourn.”
This is likely the kind of good news
that we talk about most in our ministry.
The prospect of enjoying everlasting life in an earthly paradise
under the rule of God’s Kingdom
provides hope to our listeners
and motivates them to love Jehovah.
However, the good news also includes something else,
something that we may not talk about as readily in our ministry.
You may have noticed in Isaiah the expression
“and the day of vengeance of our God.”
So there’s more to the good news
than just “the year of Jehovah’s goodwill.”
We see this clearly in the words recorded
at Revelation 14:6, 7:
“And I saw another angel flying in midheaven,
“and he had everlasting good news
“to declare to those who dwell on the earth,
“to every nation and tribe
“and tongue and people.
“He was saying in a loud voice:
“‘Fear God and give him glory,
“‘because the hour of judgment by him has arrived,
“‘so worship the One who made the heaven
“‘and the earth and the sea
and the springs of water.’”
Evidently, the “everlasting good news”
also includes a judgment message.
What is “the hour of judgment” mentioned in this verse?
According to some reference works,
the original language term here rendered “judgment”
refers to a “legal process of judgment,”
a “scrutiny of conduct.”
So God is looking closely at conduct —how people act.
That is the basis for judgment.
“The hour of judgment” mentioned in this verse
includes both the pronouncement
and the execution of divine judgment
against all false religion —Babylon the Great—
and all other parts of Satan’s system of things.
Of course, Babylon the Great and this world’s institutions
have already been judged.
However, their sentence has yet to be carried out.
When will that happen?
Toward the end of “the hour of judgment,”
which will conclude at the climax of the last days
with the destruction of the present wicked system.
That’s why the actions of people today matter so much.
It’s increasingly urgent that we proclaim
the judgment aspect of the good news to them
because the time when God will execute judgment
is fast approaching.
Why, though, can we say that this judgment message
is good news?
It’s good news for honesthearted ones
because it means the end of wickedness,
including all forms of injustice and violence.
For those who are suffering as a result of the bad actions of the wicked,
this judgment will bring great relief!
It will be a clear demonstration of Jehovah’s love and justice.
However, it will be bad news for those who stubbornly refuse
to live by Jehovah’s righteous standards.
In Bible times,
Jehovah warned of various acts of judgment
that he would bring against those
who deliberately disobeyed his commands.
In each case, he informed the affected people
well in advance
and instructed them to make changes
that were in harmony with his will.
To encourage the right response,
he often used his loyal servants on earth
to announce his judgments
and to convey a sense of urgency.
For example, think of Noah.
For years, he fearlessly warned
the immoral and violent people of his day
about a coming global Flood.
He also told them they needed to do to survive.
What about Moses and Aaron?
Jehovah used them to warn Pharaoh and his servants.
For example, think about the specific warning Jehovah gave
regarding the seventh plague, a devastating hailstorm.
At Exodus 9:18, 19,
we read that Moses and Aaron
gave the people the time and the information they needed
to protect themselves from the storm.
Yes, Jehovah always makes sure
that people have sufficient opportunity to heed his warnings.
Second Peter 3:9 says:
“He does not desire anyone to be destroyed
but desires all to attain to repentance.”
The good news we are now preaching informs people
not only of the marvelous hope for the future that Jehovah offers
but also of what we must do to enjoy that hope.
That’s why we need to let people know
about Jehovah’s soon-to-come judgment.
Notice how the preaching of the good news is tied to divine judgment
at Matthew 24:14:
“And this good news of the Kingdom
“will be preached in all the inhabited earth
“for a witness to all the nations,
and then the end will come.”
Note how the good news serves as “a witness”
to everyone who hears it.
Depending on what they do with it,
it will result in their eventual acquittal
or condemnation.
Just as a court takes time to hear all the facts
and to weigh all the evidence,
Jesus is wisely using his time now
to judge people fairly.
Both he and Jehovah continue to analyze the conduct of individuals
and how they respond to the good news that we’re preaching.
How should what we’ve just considered about the good news affect us?
For one thing, we will not hold back
from sharing all of the good news.
We will talk about the future blessings God has promised
as well as God’s judgment of the wicked,
which will make these blessings possible.
Imagine for a moment that you knew that a dangerous storm
was bearing down on where you lived.
What would you do?
Wouldn’t you try to be as prepared as possible
so that you could successfully weather the storm?
Wouldn’t you warn your family, friends, even neighbors
and try to help them to do the same?
In a similar way,
we try to help as many people as possible
to prepare for the impending execution
of Jehovah’s judgments on this world.
While being tactful,
we do not hold back from letting people know
what they need to do to be saved.
For example, we help our Bible students
to understand what they need to do.
In a frank yet kind way,
we help them to see what changes they need to make
to harmonize their lives with Jehovah’s standards.
Our new study tool, Enjoy Life Forever!,
is designed to help us do such teaching.
It includes several features to help our Bible students qualify
to preach the good news as soon as possible.
For example, at the end of each section,
there is a review with questions, some of which are quite pointed.
Considering these questions with our students
can help them to see what they need to do
to apply what they’ve been learning in their Bible study.
We’ll have an opportunity to watch a video later on in this program
that will demonstrate some of the features in Enjoy Life Forever!
and how we can use them to help our Bible students.
Understanding the importance of the good news
will also motivate us to preach and teach it with urgency!
We’ll strive to have a full share
in all aspects of the ministry available to us.
Rather than taking a casual approach,
we’ll be zealous and “work at it whole-souled as for Jehovah.”
Why?
Because we realize that people’s lives are at stake;
they urgently need to hear the good news
and respond to it.
Of course, we all have different circumstances and abilities.
We know that Jehovah and Jesus take this into account.
In Jesus’ illustration of the talents,
not all the slaves were given the same number of talents.
Rather, the talents were distributed ‘according to their ability.’
This reminds us that Jehovah and Jesus
are aware of our personal situations.
They know what we can reasonably do,
and they never expect anything beyond that.
Nor do they compare us to our fellow brothers and sisters.
Knowing this is very comforting
because we may not always be able to do
all that we want to do in the preaching work.
That’s often the case with our dear older ones
and others who cope with serious limitations.
However, we can all feel confident
that as long as we do our personal best,
Jehovah will be pleased with us.
He’ll never ‘forget our work and the love that we show.’
So may each of us continue to do all that we can
to share the good news —all of the good news!
By doing so, we will experience great joy and contentment
as we participate in this lifesaving work,
helping as many as possible before it’s too late.
Do you sometimes worry, though, how people might react,
especially to a stronger judgment message?
Facing this fear is not new.
God’s people in ancient and modern times have dealt with it too.
In the following demonstration,
let’s see what one brother is moved to do
after meditating on their examples.
Good morning.
Sorry I was running a little behind this morning,
but at least I come bearing gifts.
Oh. No worries.
Thank you. I could really use it today.
Were you also thinking
about that announcement about the special preaching campaign?
Yeah-yeah, I was.
Don’t take what I’m going to say the wrong way,
but
don’t you think the message we’ll be preaching
is pretty harsh?
No, I wouldn’t say that,
but it’s definitely very direct.
I mean, people already get defensive
whenever you challenge their beliefs,
and this is going to be the next level.
This isn’t going to be the easiest message to deliver.
But, you know, it’s not the first time we’ve done this.
Really?
Absolutely.
I don’t know if you remember me telling you
that my family is originally from Quebec,
and my dad was part of an incredibly hard-hitting witness
back in the 1940’s.
I looked this up last night.
He had to distribute a tract that called out
the local religious leaders as hypocrites.
What were they doing?
They were inciting their followers
to mob violence against the Witnesses,
telling them to vandalize our properties,
even getting brothers falsely arrested
and imprisoned.
Wow, and they had to distribute that tract during the violence?
They had to.
Jehovah wanted to show how unjust their actions were.
But I remember my dad telling me—
He said that initially he was pretty terrified.
Yeah, I mean, that’s how I feel.
I’m-I’m terrified.
It’s normal to feel that way.
I’ve been thinking about it myself,
and I thought of an account in Exodus.
It’s where Moses tells the Israelites
to splatter the blood of a ram on their doorposts
in order to avoid the effects of the last plague.
And I thought about how some of the Israelites
might have felt about doing that back then.
That’s all Moses told us.
And everyone has to do this? Every family?
Rams are sacred to the Egyptians!
Yeah, this would be an affront to Amon-Ra.
How are the Egyptians going to react?
I know. I’ve thought about that too.
Does Moses know what he’s asking us to do?
Brothers, I don’t know if we have anything to worry about.
We don’t have anything to fear.
Think of how Jehovah has protected us with these last plagues.
And as for the blood,
it’s not a matter of offending them;
it’s a matter of protecting us.
It’s showing whose side we’re on
—Jehovah’s side.
Looking back, what the Israelites did
was actually good news.
It meant their deliverance,
and it’s the same with any message we bear today.
Let me show you one of my favorite scriptures
at Isaiah 41:10.
It says: “Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
The fear we feel is natural.
But remember,
Jehovah was with the Israelites,
he was with my dad,
and he will be with us.
The message we are sharing is good news.
The faithful record of God’s servants, ancient and modern,
strengthens us to carry out our preaching work
and declare the good news.
Meditating on Jehovah’s unfailing support
can help us overcome any fear we may have.
Our Bible students face many challenges
as they learn about the good news.
They may need to make drastic changes to harmonize their lives
with Jehovah’s standards.
This can be difficult.
How can we help them make these changes
so that they can begin sharing the good news alongside us?
Enjoy Life Forever!
has been designed to help us do just that.
Let’s see encouraging evidence
that this powerful tool is really working.
When I heard about the new publication,
the Enjoy Life Forever!  book,
I was very nervous.
It was a change, and sometimes
I don’t like change.
But I knew that it was for the best.
I just needed to try it out.
I hadn’t had a progressive Bible study in years.
But the book—
The way it was designed was to help me as a teacher.
Once the features of this new publication
were explained,
that it was going to help us to help our Bible students
begin preaching in the ministry
as well as help our Bible students make changes in their everyday lives,
we were really excited
about using those features to help our students to do so.
I like the “Some People Say” section
at the bottom of the lesson
because that helps prepare her for informal witnessing.
It helps them to formulate in their own words
how to defend their faith
or how to preach informally
or use those opportunities
to share what they’ve just learned.
This was her way of learning how to feel comfortable
talking to others about Jehovah
and teaching others about Jehovah.
You’re right away,
from lesson 01 and lesson 02,
encouraging them to recognize
that it’s not just about what they’re learning
but it’s also about what they can share with others.
As the Bible teacher,
it helps us to round out the rough edges
so that when they do speak to others, it’s tactful.
I put her in that place,
like: “What would you say if someone told you that Jesus was God?
How would you answer that question?”
And that went to her heart, and she was able to answer the question.
“Well, I would tell them this. I would say this.”
Because that’s exactly what happened.
She was telling her family about the lessons that she was learning,
the things that she learned from the Bible,
so all along she was informally witnessing
and not realizing that’s what she was doing.
So when you see that connection
between what they’re learning and how they can use what they learn,
it’s just a wonderful feeling
because you recognize that now they’ll be able to teach somebody else.
One thing that the book also does
is that it progressively helps the student
to make changes in their personal life in order to live by Jehovah’s standards.
The section review is a series of questions
that usually has a key question
or a key verse related to that lesson.
So before going on to the next section,
it’s almost like a filter.
It stops them, helps them to review,
and helps the teacher realize,
‘Hmm, they don’t quite understand that point.’
They are excellent
because they can get the expressions from your student,
and now you can really focus
on what exactly the issues are that they’re having.
I was able to see if she had any gray areas,
if there was a problem, or if she didn’t understand something.
Are they saying, “The book says” or “You taught me this”?
Then you know, ‘OK,
they need to be reminded of the Scriptures,’
and you need to seed that truth
a little bit deeper into their heart.
That’s when I saw my student express herself
and let me know things she was thinking
or things that were bothering her
or that she realized that she needed to make changes with.
The questions are a bit more personal than maybe you would have asked in the past.
They’re a bit more pointed than maybe we have the habit of of asking.
In comparing my questions I used in the past with what’s in the Enjoy Life Forever!  book,
I mean, I wasn’t getting anywhere before.
These questions really help the students speak from their heart,
and I’m so glad they’re there.
It takes time.

to let them make those changes so they can qualify

This publication, the Enjoy Life Forever!  book,
is like no other.

That book has helped a lot. It has definitely boosted my confidence.
It was designed to just bring people
right into the truth.
She said the book was made especially for her.
When the time came for her
to do the door-to-door ministry, she was ready.
My student has already started
several Bible studies.
This study program has trained him now
to be a Bible teacher.
If you follow everything that’s in the book, it’s like a complete study.

It’s all there.
Enjoy Life Forever! has many well-worded questions,
some of which are quite pointed,
to help our students reason on God’s Word
and to think deeply about the changes
they need to make to please Jehovah.
The publication also shows them how to preach informally
and stresses how important it is for all of us
to share what we know with others.
Everyone who serves Jehovah has the responsibility
to declare all of the good news.
Paul reminded us at 1 Thessalonians 2:2
that we would need boldness to preach the good news
“in the face of much opposition.”
How can we do that?
Let’s learn from
Brother Gaspard Rwakabubu’s experience and see how
he maintained his zeal through persecution
and imprisonment.
During the 1970’s,
the preaching work
was not recognized in Rwanda.
When my family and I
received a letter of invitation
to go serve there,
we were living a good life.
We had some concerns,
but praying to Jehovah
and asking him for direction helped us.
I discussed it with my wife,
and we were both positive about it.
We made a request for legal recognition in 1982,
but instead, I
and two other brothers
were thrown into prison.
One day, on a Sunday,
the archbishop came to the prison,
and he announced,
“Beware of those Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
As a result of that,
he raised the curiosity of his listeners.
The prisoners wanted some explanations from us
because they could not understand what he meant.
Many began to join our meetings.
The archbishop was not happy.
He grew even angrier.
And in order to stop our activities,
he told his close followers to beat us up
when we attended the following meeting.
Two young prisoners approached us,
and they said,
“Today they plan to beat you up.”
When our meeting time came,
we didn’t show up.
Another religious group came and took our place that night,
so they were the ones who got beaten up.
From that time on, no one disturbed us any longer.
We continued preaching and attending meetings peacefully.
After spending two years in prison,
we were freed.
Outside of prison, the brothers were not free to preach.
Many more brothers and sisters kept being arrested and imprisoned.
Later, I was put in prison again,
and the imprisoned brothers
rejoiced over my presence, saying,
“We now have our circuit overseer visiting us.”
They were very happy.
We started working together
in harmony and preaching.
Each one was assigned a territory.
Some were discouraged,
but I tried to strengthen
and encourage them to hold on to Jehovah.
Then brothers from all over the world
started to write to the head of state.
Letters were coming in huge quantities!
Those letters had a good impact because,
finally, one day
an announcement was made on the radio
by the president himself
saying that he pardoned Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The people on the street started shouting at us:
“Jehovah has won!
“Jehovah has won!
He has won!”
The work of Jehovah’s Witnesses
was legally recognized in 1992.
Sadly, in 1994,
during the time of genocide,
some of our brothers died
and others faced serious challenges.
Some fled to Goma as refugees.
I received the assignment
to oversee the relief funds that were coming from Kinshasa.
One day,
I had just collected the relief money
for our refugee brothers,
and I was stopped by two policemen.
They possibly thought
that they could get that money.
So they asked me to go with them
to their superior.
As we were walking,
I remembered a prayer
that our daughter Deborah said
during the genocide.
While the whole family was praying silently,
she prayed out loud,
pouring her heart out to Jehovah.
Thanks to that, they refrained from killing us.
This moved me to pray in my heart too.
As soon as I said “Amen,”
the two policemen turned right
and went to meet their colleague.
I also saw in front of me a brother
holding a black suitcase,
looking exactly like the one I had with the money.
I handed him mine, full of money,
and he gave me his with literature inside.
Then without delay, the policemen said:
“Let’s go now.
Let’s go.”
We walked all the way to the chief of police,
but they found nothing.
They were holding their chins in their hands,
saying: “This is a miracle!
How could the money we saw turn into books?”
In all the trials I’ve encountered,
I really saw Jehovah’s powerful hand!
As a house built on a rock
that is struck by storms
(hit by anything)
but remains firm,
we too met with many trying challenges,
but Jehovah continued to make us firm,
just like a house built on a rock.
A scripture found at Isaiah 54:17
explains that in reality
all those fighting against us,
no matter who they are,
will never succeed.
Up until this moment,
although my physical strength is gradually fading,
I feel that the power to serve Jehovah
is growing so much.
In fact, I feel more powerful than ever.
My determination is that no matter the situation,
I will continue to serve Jehovah.
I’ve met Brother Rwakabubu
and personally heard many of his amazing experiences,
some of which he acted out for me.
The experience of his daughter’s prayer can be found
on pages 198 and 199
of the 2012 Yearbook of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Brother Rwakabubu’s daughter was six years old
when she prayed in front of a group of soldiers.
The soldiers were planning to kill the entire family,
including Brother Rwakabubu’s five children.
However, her innocent and earnest prayer
touched the hearts of those hardened soldiers.
Today, Brother Rwakabubu deals with various health issues
that resulted from his persecution and imprisonment.
However, Brother Rwakabubu’s reliance on Jehovah
and his love of the good news
has enabled him to maintain his zeal
—even as he’s grown older.
Sharing the good news informally
can have powerful results.
But to be effective, we need to be prepared.
How?
As we’ll see in this following morning worship,
we can learn from the example of the Great Teacher, Jesus.
Jesus, as the Great Teacher,
created opportunities to witness to others.
And of course, an excellent example of that
is found in John chapter 4.
So if you turn with me, please,
to John chapter 4,
let’s analyze how Jesus was able
to do informal witnessing,
and we’ll see what lessons we can learn from it.
So in looking at John chapter 4, to get the background,
we see that in verses 3-6 it mentions
that Jesus left Judea,
and he was going toward Galilee.
But he decided to go through Samaria
and ended up in Sychar.
In looking at the study note,
we notice that this was a journey
that involved an ascent of some 3,000 feet (914 m).
Now, that’s a very high elevation to climb up to.
In rough terms, we could say it’s like going up
300 floors, or stories, in a building.
Imagine how you would feel at the end of that.
So if Jesus and his apostles had made that journey that morning,
it’s no wonder that in verse 6, it says that he was “tired out.”
He was sitting there, and it mentions in verse 6, too,
it was the sixth hour, or about midday.
So imagine the setting: Jesus is in Samaria,
he’s tired, and it’s about midday
—not the best circumstances for starting to witness.
So, what’s the first lesson we learn from this?
Jesus didn’t wait for the perfect opportunity
to informal witness.
No, he used whatever opportunity came up and created opportunities.
So, of course, the woman comes along.
Notice in verse 7 how Jesus introduced,
or started, this conversation.
He simply said: “Give me a drink.”
He didn’t dive into some deep spiritual discussion,
but rather, he just started talking to the woman.
Well, what lesson do we learn from that?
You see, if we’re interested in witnessing to others informally,
perhaps all it takes is just greeting them, saying hello.
And of course, if they’re not even willing to start talking to us,
it’s very hard to go much further.
So that’s the first lesson.
How did the woman respond?
Well, we’ll notice as we go through John chapter 4,
there were at least four potential problems that Jesus had to avoid
as he continued this discussion.
The first of these problems is recorded in verse 9.
There straightaway she says,
‘You’re a Jew, and I’m a Samaritan woman.
How come you’re talking to me?’
So she referred to his appearance, his background.
Well, in a similar way today,
sometimes someone may take a look at us
and refer to our color or racial background or nationality.
And that could be a negative thing.
But what did Jesus say?
Well, he didn’t respond and say: ‘You know, I’m a nice person.
That’s how come I’m willing to talk to you.’
No, he completely avoided that whole issue
and focused on the spiritual message
that he wanted to convey to her.
So we notice that in verse 10,
he speaks “of the free gift of God,”
and he also mentions that this woman could get “living water,”
not just the water that she was interested in at that point.
Now, when we analyze how the conversation went,
we can see clearly that Jesus laid the foundation here at this point
for what he was going to say later.
You see, he started with water.
Then he mentions God’s gifts and “living water,”
and we’ll see how he develops that a little further as we go on.
Well, what happened at that point when he offered this “living water”?
Well, in verse 11, notice she says: “You do not even have a bucket.”
So in other words, she was basically saying:
‘I don’t believe you.
The well is very deep.’
The study note says it’s maybe about 75 feet (23 m) deep.
So this is a negative reaction on her part,
followed up by something else that was very controversial in Jesus’ day.
She says, ‘Do you think you’re better than our forefather Jacob?’
Now, that was very controversial
because the average Jew in those days would have objected to that comment,
saying that she wasn’t a relative of Jacob.
So here we have another two possible problems.
How did Jesus handle it?
Well, he just focused back on the spiritual message.
As we mentioned, as recorded in verse 10,
he started with water, God’s gift, and “living water.”
And then if we look at verse 14,
he speaks about drinking water
so that you would “never get thirsty at all” again.
And then he introduces the concept, or thought,
of everlasting life.
So obviously, Jesus had in his mind
a plan of action, or a little outline,
of how he could develop a certain theme.
And that was to do with water leading to everlasting life.
Well, how did the woman respond at that point?
Notice, in verse 15, she says: “Sir, give me this water.”
Now, was she saying, ‘Please, I really want it’?
Or was she perhaps a little cynical, maybe even a little sarcastic?
Well, it’s hard for us to tell.
It doesn’t seem until later that she fully believed Jesus.
But whatever the case,
it perhaps could, in a modern setting, be like her saying,
‘That sounds good, but it’s too good to be true.’
Did that stop Jesus?
No.
Jesus then basically changes the direction of the conversation
and gives her an opportunity to show her honesty.
Jesus realized that she was coming at that time of the day
to avoid perhaps others seeing her.
Why?
Well, in verse 16, Jesus says to her: “Call your husband.”
She says: “I do not have a husband”
—a very honest comment to a stranger.
Then Jesus said: “You are right.
“You have had five husbands,
“and the man you now have is not your husband.
This you have said truthfully.”
Well, now, what do we learn from this?
You see, although Jesus knew
that she was living in an immoral relationship,
still, that wasn’t the focus.
He gave her an opportunity to express herself,
and then what did he do?
He commended her.
So in a similar way, it’s good for us to always try to find points
that we can commend the person for,
even if they say something that is totally opposite
to what the Bible says.
We can at least thank them for expressing their viewpoint
and being honest about it.
So as we continue on, we then see, at this point,
the woman has really taken notice because she says:
“Sir, I see that you are a prophet.”
But then the next problem, the fourth problem, comes in.
What does she say?
‘Well, we worship here at Mount Gerizim,
but you Jews, you say we should worship in Jerusalem.’
So, basically, it’s the modern equivalent of saying,
‘I have my own religion, and it’s different from yours.’
Well, how did Jesus deal with that potential problem?
Well, when we look at verse 21,
it’s interesting to see how he starts the answer by saying:
“The hour is coming when neither on this mountain
nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.”
So, basically, Jesus was just allaying her concern
and saying: ‘Look, don’t worry.
‘In the future, this is not going to be an issue,
whether it’s here or there.’
And then he goes on to explain that the important thing is
to “worship the Father with spirit and truth.”
So, what do we see from that?
Jesus tried to help her to see
that what she perceived as being a problem
really wasn’t an issue at all.
It wasn’t something they had to go through and explain all the details.
Of course, he did mention that “salvation [began] with the Jews,”
but then he showed her very clearly what she needed to do.
Now, why was that so important?
Well, if we turn
to the book of Acts 8:14,
there’s a very interesting study note there
that tells us that what Jesus did on this occasion,
in witnessing to this woman and then to various ones in her community,
laid the basis for what Philip the evangelizer
would later do when he moved to Samaria
and helped many there to become Christians.
And ultimately they became anointed Christians.
So Jesus’ conversation here with this woman
certainly was very, very successful.
So, what have we learned from this discussion looking through John chapter 4?
First of all, Jesus didn’t wait for the perfect opportunity;
he created that opportunity.
Second, he wasn’t distracted, or sidetracked,
by the various issues —some of them controversial—
that this woman raised,
but he focused on a spiritual theme.
He had something in mind where he would use water
to eventually describe everlasting life.
And then he commended her for her honest remarks
and showed her what she needed to do.
What an excellent lesson this is for all of us
as we try to witness to others!
Start simple, have a theme in mind,
and commend the person.
What a simple formula!
I’m sure you’ll want to try this approach as soon as possible.
When we meditate on the good news,
we can’t help but want to share it
at every possible opportunity.
We just can’t hold back!
That’s the theme of this month’s music video.
The signs we see are clear; The end of this world is near.
But how will they know the way to go Without a chance to hear?
The truth we cannot hide. Our fear we must set aside.
Look to God, and pray to fan the flame, And let it burn inside.

We know we can’t hold back.
So let’s keep it burning bright And spread his glorious light.
We know we can’t hold back.
We can’t hold back.
So let’s do all we can. Soon these words of hope will end.
When that time has come, we’ll stand as one;
God’s name we will defend.
With this fire in our bones, We’ll make his message known.
We know we can’t hold back.
So let’s keep it burning bright And spread his glorious light.
We know we can’t hold back.
We can’t hold back.
So keep the fire burning; keep it burning strong.
Jehovah’s day is near; it won’t be long.
Let’s carry on.
With this fire in our bones, We’ll make his message known.
We know we can’t hold back.
So let’s keep it burning bright And spread his glorious light.
We know we can’t hold back.
We can’t hold back.
We can’t hold back.
We can’t hold back.
Isn’t it wonderful how our preaching efforts
may help people accept the good news?
In turn, they’ll be moved to share it with others.
And what a difference it makes in their lives!
Last month, the first episode
in the new series Imitate Their Faith
brought to life much of Abraham’s story.
But what happened next in the life of this man
who the Bible refers to
as “the father of all those having faith”?
Let’s find out in Part 2.
One year ago,
Jehovah told Abraham something
that seemed impossible.
His wife, Sarah, would have a son.
Our son, Isaac.
Sarah’s miraculous pregnancy and Isaac’s birth
were proof that Jehovah’s word
always comes true.
As the rains came down,
there they were, eight souls,
safe on the ark.
Jehovah protected Noah’s family.
That’s why we’re alive today.
And you know, that’s not the only time.
There have been many things that seemed scary.
But Jehovah always
makes sure his promises come true.
Think how he helped to protect your mother
when Pharaoh wanted to take her as his wife.
Think how he sent angels to save Lot.
Remember he caused your birth.
I’m your father, but Jehovah is your Father too.
You are part of his purpose, Isaac.
Hard things are going to happen,
but remember we can always trust Jehovah.
Because he always keeps his promises.
That’s right!
Remember the promise Jehovah made to our family?
“I will give to you
“and to your offspring after you
“the land in which you lived as a . . . lasting possession,
and I will be their God.”
Come here.
Hard things did happen,
even in this spiritual household.
I am the star. I am the firstborn.
Everybody hates you. Nobody likes you.
Our father loves me. The joke is on you, Isaac.
I am the firstborn.
No one cares about you, not even God.
The dancing is for me.
Everybody hates you. Nobody likes you.
This wasn’t just sibling rivalry.
Ishmael’s abusive behavior had broken Sarah’s heart.
Please, please, please,
drive out that slave girl and her son.
Do not be displeased
by what Sarah is saying to you
about the boy and about your slave girl.
Listen to her,
for what will be called your offspring
will be through Isaac.
As for the son of the slave girl,
I will also make a nation out of him,
because he is your offspring.
Though it was hard,
Abraham obediently sent Hagar
and his son Ishmael away,
trusting that Jehovah had his eyes upon them.
Abraham!
Here I am!
Take, please, your son,
your only son whom you so love, Isaac,
and travel to the land of Moriah
and offer him up there as a burnt offering
on one of the mountains that I will designate to you.
Let’s go.
In the past,
Abraham had asked God questions
about some of his judgments and decisions,
but now his friendship and trust in Jehovah
had grown.
He didn’t ask anything at all.
You stay here with the donkey,
but the boy and I will go over there
and worship and return to you.
Father!
Yes, my son!
Here are the fire and the wood,
but where is the sheep
for the burnt offering?
God himself will provide the sheep
for the burnt offering, my son.
Abraham, Abraham!
Here I am!
Do not harm the boy,
and do not do anything at all to him,
for now I do know that you are God-fearing
because you have not withheld your son,
your only one, from me.
And by means of your offspring
all nations of the earth
will obtain a blessing for themselves
because you have listened to my voice.
Abraham
and Sarah
and Isaac
all knew they could have full faith in Jehovah.
His promises to them are promises to us.
When we immerse ourselves in familiar Bible accounts,
we gain an even deeper appreciation for their power
and more firmly embed in our hearts
the lessons we learn from them.
In this month’s postcard, we’ll visit our brothers in Lesotho,
a country in the south of Africa.
Lesotho is over 1,000 meters,
or 3,280 feet, above sea level,
with some of its mountain peaks rising three times as high.
The majority of its two million people,
called Basotho, live in rural areas.
Many herd animals or farm for a living.
Weather conditions can change quickly in Lesotho’s mountainous terrain,
calling for protection from sudden cold.
So the famous Basotho blanket comes in quite handy,
especially in winter
when the mountains are blanketed in snow.
Of course, the good news must be spread despite cold or heights
as our brothers there have been doing for over 80 years.
two Basotho Witnesses who learned the truth in South Africa
returned to preach enthusiastically in this challenging territory.
Nine years later, there were five small congregations
with 63 Witnesses.
In the 1960’s and 1970’s,
the work continued thanks to the tireless efforts
of zealous evangelizers.
Today, over 3,700 publishers
conduct over 4,500 Bible studies
each month.
Because Lesotho’s population is widely spread across a challenging terrain,
our brothers exert themselves to preach
wherever the people live.
Many of our brothers here climb steep paths
to get to their meetings
—especially the 78 publishers
of the Mokhotlong Congregation,
who meet in the highest Kingdom Hall in southern Africa.
From the heights of Lesotho,
the brothers and sisters of the Mokhotlong Congregation
send you their warmest greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

title: 우울증이 있어도 평화를 누리는 우리 형제들

ko.text: 이제 막 일을 시작해서 부담감도 있었지만
우울증이 있다고 알려 주시는 것 같았어요.
운동을 하고 몸에 좋은 음식을 먹는 게
일기장에 내게 나타나는 다양한 우울증 증상들을 써 봤죠.
그리고 각 증상에 맞는 성구들과 기사들을 적어 놨어요.
또 출판물에 들어 있는 삽화와 그림들을 보는 것도 많은 도움이 됐죠.
집회 갈 준비를 하고 옷을 입을 땐 괜찮았어요.
주체할 수 없이 두렵고 슬픈 감정이 밀려와서
전 어쩔 줄 몰라서 울기 시작했어요.
제가 정말 나쁜 선택을 하게 될 것 같았죠.
사실 장로들한테 우울증 얘기를 한 적은 없었거든요.
그런데 저를 찾아오신 장로 형제 중에 한 분도
병원에서 치료를 받아보는 게 어떠냐고 제안했죠.
사실 전 예전부터 병원은 정말 가고 싶지 않았어요.
하지만 다른 사람의 도움이 필요할 때가 있어요.
우울증을 숨겨야 하는 나쁜 병이라고 말하고,
치료를 받는 것을 아주 부끄러운 일이라고 생각하죠.
의사의 도움을 받아야 된다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
모두가 치료를 받아야 되는 건 아니지만
‘이게 다 무슨 소용이야. 아무도 살리지 못하고,
아무도 도울 수 없잖아’ 하는 생각이 들었죠.
인내할 수 있게 평화를 달라고 간청했죠.
우울증으로 힘들어하는 형제 자매들을 도울 때면
여호와께서 저를 사용하고 계시다는 느낌을 받아요.
또 여호와께서 만드신 작은 창조물들을 보면서도

en.text: My mom has always told me
that I’ve always been
a caregiver ever since I was a little girl;
it was just part of who I was.
I don’t like to see people suffer;
it’s very difficult for me.
I remember that when I first started working as a nurse,
I would always cry.
I cried—
Literally I cried every day that I had to go to work.
Not only was I overwhelmed being a new nurse
but also
I was battling my depression.
I was feeling so sad.
I really needed Jehovah’s help to figure out what was going on with me.
And I remember
that the 2009 article about depression came out.
And I realized: ‘OK, Jehovah, you’re telling me
‘this is what I have.
‘So now that I realize I have this,
I’ve got to figure out how I can manage it.’
So I changed my eating habits.
I started exercising a lot more.
I realized that exercising and eating healthy really, really did help.
Also, I made a journal.
And I made different sections
of the different aspects of my depression that I dealt with.
In each section, I would put scriptures;
I would put articles.
And the illustrations, the pictures,
they speak a lot without saying anything.
Jehovah hears us.
Jehovah cares.
Exercising, changing my diet,
the publications, journaling
—that was my lifeline.
That really actually helped me for a long time.
But it came to a point where it
stopped working as effectively.
I remember getting ready, dressing for the meeting,
and I was fine.
I was getting dressed for the meeting, about to walk out the door, but I couldn’t.
There was this overwhelming fear that came over me
and an overwhelming sadness that came over me.
And I just lost it; I just started crying.
I couldn’t get myself together.
It was bad.
It got really bad; my depression got really bad.
So it was very difficult for me to approach the brothers to ask them for help.
But at that time, I knew that if I didn’t,
that something bad would happen.
So I decided: ‘You know what?
I’m going to ask for a shepherding call with my brothers,’
because I’d never talked about my depression with the elders at all.
This was my first time speaking with them.
And there was one brother, one of the elders,
who also battled depression.
And he suggested,
“Have you thought about seeking medical help?”
Seeking professional help was something I never wanted to do.
I thought that I didn’t need to do it,
but sometimes there comes a point
where you need additional help
and what you’re doing is not enough.
In this world, they make you feel that it’s a bad thing,
that depression is a dirty word,
or that seeking medical help is something that you don’t do.
But I realized also that seeking medical help
was part of my being able to worship Jehovah effectively.
That’s me doing my part.
Not everyone needs to take that step, but for me, this is what I need to do.
And I’m glad I did it because of the fact
that I’ve never ever felt this good
in my life.
At first, it started with one floor,
then it went to another floor,
and then the whole entire hospital.
Every floor had COVID patients.
That was some of the hardest nursing
that I’ve ever done in my life
in all of my years of nursing.
And we lost a lot of good nurses
who were right in the trenches with me
who were in there doing their best.
We lost a lot of good people.
Even though I was on medication to help me,
it still didn’t take the depression away.
You’re like: ‘What’s the point?
‘I can’t save anyone.
I can’t, I can’t help anyone.’
It was devastating.
It truly, truly was devastating.
And at those times I just cry to Jehovah,
talk to Jehovah about how I’m feeling,
and just ask for his peace to help me to deal.
When I’m able to help people who are battling depression,
I feel like Jehovah is using me in that way,
and it makes me happy that I can be of use to Jehovah.
It’s good to feel—
It’s so nice to feel good again,
to feel happy again, to be able to smile,
to be able to take in enjoyment in the small things,
you know, in Jehovah’s creation
—and, you know, just be happy that I’m alive.
So yeah,
yeah.
