then you need to make your decisions accordingly.”
It was like a light went on in my head.
Now I was sure about what I needed to do.
I had to speak to her.
One day, I prayed to Jehovah and got up the courage.
I told her that it couldn’t continue with us.
Of course, explaining that to my classmates
and to my teachers was a little hard.
I mean, it was difficult for them to understand.
Sure, I explained it, but they said, “Why would you do that?”
For whoever is in the same situation that I was in,
the best thing to do
is to talk to someone you trust, tell them how you feel,
and ask for help.
Our Creator, Jehovah, is the one who thinks about me and loves me most.
He hasn’t deprived me of anything good.
He always helps us and never leaves us.
I’m so grateful to Jehovah.
Dilan and Isaac both admitted that the pressure they faced
was almost too much, almost got the best of them.
What helped them turn the corner?
Isaac said that it was reaching out and getting help.
If you’re facing similar pressures in school, don’t keep it to yourself.
Talk to someone you trust
—that can open the door to getting just the help you need.
Now we’d like to share something special with you:
a recent discovery that has rewritten a part of our theocratic history.
Enjoy the following story, more than 80 years in the making.
Jehovah’s Witnesses love the Bible.
Long before taking on the monumental task
of Bible translation,
they acquired licenses
to print already existing translations of the Bible.
And then in the 1950’s,
the Watchtower Bible and Tract Society
printed the first Bible ever to be translated by Jehovah’s Witnesses
—the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.
At least we thought it was the first Bible
ever to be translated by Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Well, in the fall of 2017,
the World Headquarters Museum Department
received a Bible donated
by a brother in Germany.
Accompanying the Bible was a letter referring
to a rare Bible printed in 1934
at Magdeburg, the location
of the Watchtower Bible and Tract Society’s
Germany Branch and printery at that time.
Little was known about this Bible,
and to those who did know of it, it was thought of as something
unapproved by the then-president of the Society, J.F. Rutherford.
By 1934, Adolph Hitler’s campaign against Jehovah’s Witnesses
was well underway.
Our religious activities were banned,
65 tons of literature had been seized
and burned by Nazi authorities, and the branch office and printery
at Magdeburg had already been confiscated and released several times.
And this may explain why the Magdeburger Bible
doesn’t have a typical publishers’ page listing
of who published it, who translated it, when and where it was printed.
But on the bottom of one of the last pages,
there is just one line in small letters, and it reads:
“Printed: Watchtower Bible and Tract Society, Magdeburg.”
Interestingly, on September 13, 1934,
the Ministry of the Interior of the German government
granted permission for the Magdeburg office
to resume the printing and distribution of Bibles.
However, everybody knew that the facilities could be shut down again,
perhaps permanently, at any time.
What really could be accomplished in the limited time they had?
The Magdeburg office informed Rutherford
that they had possession
of a New Testament manuscript ready for printing and, additionally,
a translation of the Old Testament was nearly complete.
In October 1934,
Rutherford approved the printing of 100,000 copies.
But time was running out.
Brother Rutherford received the following letter dated August 6, 1935,
and it says: “In the afternoon of July 10th
“a number of officials of the secret Police of Berlin and Magdeburg
“appeared and sealed the factory,
“rooms and offices at Magdeburg, closed all factory rooms,
“attached the property
“and money of the Society . . .
“Several thousand Bibles
“were just been bound
and the rest is printed.”
Sadly, only a small number
of those Bibles actually made it out of the printery.
In November 2017,
after a careful search,
we were able to obtain three copies of the Magdeburger Bible.
Little did we know what a treasured place
in our organization’s history of Bible translation
and printing this Bible deserves!
It’s not a mere compilation of existing translations
but a fresh, unique translation of the Bible.
Jehovah’s name is used extensively
in the text of the Hebrew Scriptures
as well as in footnotes of the Christian Greek Scriptures.
The Magdeburger Bible was also
cited in German-language editions of The Watchtower.
And nearly a century later,
the text can still be easily understood
by the German reader.
This Bible translation truly has a remarkable story.
It’s print run was small by normal Bible-printing standards,
and its distribution was even smaller.
And although it was produced in record time
and under highly dangerous circumstances, its story
lay forgotten for decades until it was rediscovered.
The Magdeburger Bible is the first-known Bible
to be translated and published by Jehovah’s Witnesses,
predating the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures.
It was able to survive in a time of Nazi government opposition
and is now part of our Bible Museum at Warwick.
This Bible truly is a testimony
to the words we find at Isaiah 40:8:
“Aber Jehovas Wort bleibt ewiglich!”
Not even the threat of Nazi oppression
stopped our brothers in Germany
from doing what they could to make the Bible more available.
Why not?
Because as Jehovah’s Witnesses,
we love the Bible and love teaching others about it.
But what does it take to be a good teacher of God’s Word?
In a Morning Worship program,
Brother Geoffrey Jackson discussed
what we can learn from the apostle Paul
and how to reach the heart.
How would you define a good teacher?
That’s an interesting question, isn’t it?
For many of us,
perhaps we might answer by saying
what we think a good speaker is like.
We might say,
“The brother uses many illustrations in his talk”
or “He was able to highlight a scripture that I’ve read many times,
“and yet for the first time, I’ve seen something interesting
in that that I’ve never seen before.”
Or perhaps we might say,
“He was able to keep my interest right through the 60 minutes.”
Well, there are all sorts of different ways
we could say that someone is a good teacher.
Of course, the best compliment someone could receive is if they’re told
that their teaching is similar to that of Jesus Christ,
because we know he set a wonderful example for all of us.
But as we’re thinking about the qualifications
for someone to be a good teacher,
let’s turn our attention to the words of the apostle Paul.
And if you turn with me, please,
to 1 Thessalonians 2:7, 8,
here we see, in addition to some of the matters that we just discussed,
other aspects or other qualities that are required
for someone really to be an effective teacher.
So that’s 1 Thessalonians 2:7, 8:
“On the contrary, we became gentle in your midst,
“as when a nursing mother tenderly cares for her own children.
“So having tender affection for you,
“we were determined to impart to you,
not only the good news of God but also our very selves.”
Do you notice some of the qualities, or attributes,
here that the apostle Paul mentions
as being very important with regard to our teaching?
In verse 8, it mentions “tender affection.”
So love is very much connected
with someone having the ability to be a good teacher.
In fact, to reach the heart of the student,
we have to display love as well, don’t we?
Without reaching the heart of the student we’re trying to teach,
it’s like enjoying a meal in a dream.
There really is no benefit at all.
So if we teach but don’t reach the heart of the student,
then it really is of very little value to the student.
Then looking on, notice it says that Paul
was “determined to impart”
not just the message of the good news
but his very self.
In other words, he put his whole heart into teaching others.
But let’s look up at verse 7.
Now, I feel quite confident in saying that probably none of us
would have listed this quality as being essential for a good teacher.
How does he start?
“We became gentle in your midst.”
Now, honestly, that probably isn’t the first quality
that would come to your mind with regard to a teacher.
But what’s meant by this expression to be “gentle”?
Well, one Bible scholar made this comment.
He said that this word that’s translated “gentle”
“was frequently used by Greek writers
“as characterizing a nurse with trying children
or a teacher with refractory scholars.”
Now, I had to look up the word “refractory” and add it to my vocabulary.
It means, basically, “difficult to control,
resisting authority, unmanageable, unresponsive.”
Well, do we see an interesting thought here?
This gentleness has a firmness and stability about it
that isn’t rocked or shaken easily
by the negative response of the one that’s being taught.
Isn’t that an interesting quality?
And no doubt we’ve all tried to display that,
perhaps as we’re trying to teach someone something about the Scriptures
and come across the thought that this person doesn’t really accept it.
We state the fact,
we show our scripture, but they still may have a problem.
Well, how do we react?
You see, if we were to demand that they accept what we say
because we said it or because the Scriptures say it
without reasoning with that person,
then, really, we don’t have that gentleness
that the apostle Paul is referring to here.
So that stability under pressure
in a loving way convinces someone
of something that perhaps they’re not so responsive to.
Doesn’t that open our minds
to another aspect of what is involved with good teaching?
Now, by contrast, if we look back at 1 Thessalonians chapter 2,
we’ll see that the apostle Paul in verses 5 and 6
gives us a contrast about the type of things
that we wouldn’t want to do as a teacher.
Let’s read that in verses 5 and 6:
“In fact, you know that we never used flattering speech
“or put on any false front with greedy motives;
“God is witness!
“Nor have we been seeking glory from men,
“either from you or from others,
though we could be an expensive burden as apostles of Christ.”
So, what are these negative things that we certainly would want to avoid
if want to be an effective teacher?
Well, notice that first one, “flattering speech.”
Now, this reminds us of another scripture.
Let’s turn across to Proverbs 28:23,
and this is a good reminder for all of us.
It says: “Whoever reproves a man
“[or corrects his thinking]
“will afterward find more favor
than someone who flatters with his tongue.”
Do we see the point that is being made there?
That flattery is not really an effective way
for us to gain someone’s confidence,
but, rather, it’s by honestly correcting the thinking of someone else.
So with our Bible students or whatever level of teaching that we’re doing,
we need to remember that part of the process of teaching involves
giving counsel or direction in correcting wrong viewpoints.
For us not to do that in a loving way
really shows that we don’t love the person properly
because we don’t really want them to change their wrong thinking.
So avoiding “flattering speech” is very important.
Going back to 1 Thessalonians chapter 2,
what’s the second point that Paul mentions?
A “false front with greedy motives.”
So a false front is pretending to be someone that you’re not.
So none of us would ever want to put across
a self-righteous viewpoint
to try to convince others that we are holier than they are,
but as it says here, it’s to not have that “false front.”
And then it mentions “greedy motives.”
You see, there’s a marginal reference
that takes us across to Acts 20:33.
There the apostle Paul says:
“I have desired no man’s silver or gold or clothing.”
So certainly as a teacher of the good news,
we wouldn’t want to expect some benefits or something
that would come back to us by means of our teaching.
There the apostle Paul sets a good standard for us.
And then in verse 6,
he said that he wasn’t ‘seeking the glory of men,’
or as one translation says, “insisting on our own dignity.”
So it could be that if we’re a teacher,
we may feel that we deserve a certain measure of respect.
Yes, our position is a little higher than the student.
If we really feel that way deep inside,
that’s going to affect our attitude
with regard to being gentle, won’t it?
Because if someone questions what we say
or if it looks like they’re not dignifying us in a proper manner,
then we will lose that firm gentleness
that helps correct the thinking of others.
Well, when we think about all these various attributes and qualities
that are needed for us to be a good teacher,
perhaps we might feel that there’s a lot we can work on, I’m sure.
I feel that way as well.
It’s a continual battle —isn’t it?—for us to continue
to try to be effective teachers.
Here is one word of encouragement we gain from the book of Philippians.
As a final scripture,
Philippians 2:13:
“For God is the one who for the sake of his good pleasure energizes you,
“giving you both [notice] the desire
“[yes, so the desire for us to impart the truth
“in a loving manner to others and then also]
and the power to act.”
So as we consider our teaching abilities,
don’t just think of techniques.
But always remember that when we’re a good teacher,
we need to be gentle in the midst of others
and help them in a loving way to correct wrong thoughts.
Like Jesus, Paul put his whole heart into his teaching.
His concern for others moved him
to share the good news with as many as possible.
In modern times, many have shown that same spirit,
moving them to preach even in the face of opposition.
One of those sisters is Maria Kaloyanoff.
So my mother was born in the country of Bulgaria in 1922,
and in the early 1950’s,
my family emigrated from Germany to the United States.
We settled in New York City,
and it was there that my mother
learned the truth.
That is the first time I opened a Bible.
I went and opened Revelation chapter 21.
But what hit me was the point
that there will not be sickness,
sorrow, and death anymore.
Anyone that comes into the truth
wants to share that with their family.
I had a desire,
really, to tell them the truth,
how they can get free
from oppression and sickness and death.
So she very much saw the need and desired
to have literature in the Bulgarian language.
She was able to ask the brothers in Brooklyn,
specifically offering if she could
translate some literature into Bulgarian.
The brothers approved for her to do that,
starting out with some of the tracts.
So Bulgaria was behind the Iron Curtain, a Communist country.
Literature about God and the Bible
is not acceptable and banned,
so you can’t just mail it.
So as literature became available, people have to take it in.
My family was one of those families that volunteered to do that.
We traveled into Bulgaria by train.
We had a lot of luggage because every time we would go to Bulgaria,
we stayed two and a half months.
That was the summer vacation.
In that luggage, in various places,
we put literature.
Traveling into a country with banned literature
is not without its problems or dangers.
They knew that we had some literature, and that was the tracts.
My mother realized that we were going to be searched.
We had the ability
to take the literature out of each luggage that we had hidden it in
and to put it into one small briefcase.
And what we couldn’t,
like unfolded tracts,
we put around our arm
with our overcoats over it.
I was only worrying about how I can
hide that literature so he cannot find it.
Because if he finds it,
then there really are consequences.
So as the guards would search through the luggage,
they would rifle through it.
They didn’t straighten anything out,
so my mother quickly thought and asked them,
“Can I now go over there and straighten out
what you’ve messed up?”
And they said, “OK.”
I took my tracts,
which I had around my hand,
and I put them in the already checked bag over there.
One of the guards gets to the point that it’s my little briefcase.
He says,
“This is so small;
nothing could be in here!”
And he just takes it over there.
The man who was looking was getting very nervous
because he knew we had something,
but he was not able to find it.
So in one trip years later, my mother was on her own.
The officials at the border of Bulgaria found literature.
They arrested her.
They put her in prison.
They interrogated her for two weeks or more every day.
And in time, the Bulgarian government changed their mind
and decided that as a foreign national,
they would just expel her from the country.
To this day, my mother continues her spiritual routine
of worshipping Jehovah
—being at the meetings, preparing for the meetings, reading her Bible,
and zealously sharing the truth with others.
It helps me practically
every minute in my life.
And I want to use my last bit of energy
to make his will known.
Once Sister Kaloyanoff heard the Bible’s message,
she just had to share it with those in her home country.
As she’s gotten older, her circumstances have changed,
but not her determination.
She still wants to do whatever she can,
using her ‘last energy,’ as she put it,
to make God’s will known.
Do you have faithful ones like Sister Kaloyanoff in your congregation?
Keep them in mind as you enjoy this month’s music video.
It’s called Two Small Coins.
Two small coins Are all that she can give.
As she waits, The courtyard echoes with bountiful gifts.
Lost in the crowd, Like a single grain of sand,
Will her Father take note Of the two small coins in her hand?
No matter how small, Don’t wonder at all,
‘Does he notice my sacrifice?’
It’s not hard to believe If we see how he sees—
If we see through Jehovah’s eyes—
Two small coins.
Would she have thought Of all she’d given before—
Of easier times When she had the means to give so much more?

But for Jehovah God, This small gift made a thunderous sound.
No matter how small, Don’t wonder at all,
‘Does he notice my sacrifice?’
It’s not hard to believe If we see how he sees—
If we see through Jehovah’s eyes—
Two small coins.
He looks far beyond what you and I see.
He knows who we really are underneath.
He sees all we can be.
No matter how small, Don’t wonder at all,
‘Does he notice my sacrifice?’
It’s not hard to believe If we see how he sees—
If we see through Jehovah’s eyes—
Two small coins.
Do you see through Jehovah’s eyes?
What a beautiful reassurance
that no matter what our limitations may be,
our gifts have great value in Jehovah’s eyes!
For this month’s video postcard,
let’s travel to a land of incredible scenic beauty
—New Zealand.
New Zealand is made up primarily of two main islands
about 1,600 kilometers, or more than 1,000 miles,
southeast of Australia.
On those islands, you’ll find snowcapped mountain ranges,
crystal clear lakes,
miles of beaches, and a sweeping coastline
with many harbors and fjords.
It’s also an area
of dramatic geothermal activity,
with active volcanoes, geysers,
bubbling mud pools,
and one of the largest hot springs in the world,
the fittingly named Frying Pan Lake.
Residents of New Zealand are often nicknamed “Kiwis”
—a nod to one of the country’s most unique indigenous birds,
the long-billed and flightless kiwi.
The good news first reached New Zealand in the late 1890’s
when one local reader of the Watch Tower publications
started preaching on his own.
A few years later,
colporteurs from Australia and the United States arrived,
and the good news began to spread.
The early Witnesses in New Zealand
were intrepid preachers,
crossing rugged terrain on foot, horseback,
and bicycle to reach remote towns.
One New Zealander
who became a zealous preacher in those early days
was William Barry,
who read the six volumes of Studies in the Scriptures  in 1909
and immediately recognized he had found the truth.
He diligently taught the truth to his children.
And in 1975, his son Lloyd Barry
became a member of the Governing Body.
The truth has also spread quickly among the Maori,
the indigenous people of New Zealand.
The first Maori-language convention was held in 1928.
Today, we have many Maori brothers and sisters
who enjoy sharing their rich culture with others.
Altogether, there are now more than 15,000 publishers in New Zealand,
preaching in 18 different languages,
including New Zealand Sign Language.
Here on the South Island is the seaside town of Picton
—home to the Picton Congregation.
With a busy waterfront and ferry terminal,
Picton welcomes many tourists
and international workers,
so there are plenty of opportunities
for public witnessing.
To reach those living in homes around the many bays of Picton,
the preaching work involves using boats owned by brothers.
The 39 publishers and the pioneers in the Picton Congregation
send their love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is, yes, this is JW Broadcasting!

title: 지부 보고: 브라질과 파라과이

ko.text: 아마존 우림, 비옥한 농경지, 아름다운 해안을 볼 수 있죠.
브라질과 국경을 맞대고 있는 파라과이는 남아메리카에서 여덟 번째로 큰 나라입니다.
다양한 지형을 볼 수 있는데 큰 강들, 드넓은 평원, 비옥한 농경지가 있죠.
우린 두 나라의 베델 가족들이 약 2년 반의 팬데믹 기간을 보낸 후
델링거 형제 부부와 저희 부부는 워릭 베델에서 출발해서
하지만 최근에 있었던 대통령 선거 후로 상파울루에서 대규모 시위가 있어서
공항에서 지부 사무실까지 가는 길을 포함해 주요 도로들이 꽉 막혔습니다.
여호와께선 전혀 예상치 못한 방법으로 해결해 주셨죠.
한 증인 가족의 관대한 지원 덕분에
우리는 공항에서 지부까지 순식간에 올 수 있었습니다.
브라질 지부는 시골 지역에 있고 약 1200명의 자원봉사자들이 살고 있습니다.
방문 기간에 베델 가족 전체가 식당에서 아침 숭배와 아침 식사를 즐겼습니다.
중앙장로회의 지시에 따라 브라질 지부는 작년에 65개 언어로 출판물을 인쇄했습니다.
브라질은 창고 역할을 하는 지부이기도 합니다.
브라질 지부는 출판물을 인쇄하고 보관하고 각 회중에 직접 발송합니다.
파라과이, 아르헨티나, 우루과이, 볼리비아, 칠레, 페루로 보내죠.
콜롬비아, 멕시코, 미국, 남아프리카 공화국, 독일, 일본 지부이죠.
이곳에서 브라질에서 사용되는 다른 언어들로 우리 출판물을 번역합니다.
브라질 지부에는 두 개의 박물관이 있습니다.
하나는 성경 번역의 역사에 관한 것이고
다른 하나는 브라질의 증인 역사를 보여 주는 박물관이죠.
브라질 지부는 또한 패터슨에 있는 미술부에 우리 출판물을 위한 사진과 삽화를 제공합니다.
아마 이런 장면들이 기억이 나실 겁니다.
또 브라질 지부에는 본부 오디오/비디오 봉사부의 감독을 받는 지역 비디오 제작 팀이 있습니다.
이 모든 활동을 수행하고 90만 명이 넘는 전도인들을 지원하기 위해
많은 출퇴근 베델 봉사자들이 보시는 것처럼 이 공사에 기쁘게 참여하고 있죠.
베델 가족과의 특별 저녁 식사도 기억에 남습니다.
베델 성원들의 합창과 전통적인 춤을 즐기고, 격려적인 야외 봉사 경험담도 들었습니다.
정말 이곳의 야외 봉사를 직접 체험해 보고 싶었습니다.
실제로 해 보니까, 들은 대로 시골 지역에서나 도시에서나 사람들이
친절하고, 쉽게 대화할 수 있고, 왕국 소식을 잘 들었습니다.
이 큰 나라에서 아직도 더 많은 사람이 여호와의 조직에 들어올 수 있겠다는 생각이 들었죠.
지부 시설 안에 있는 대회회관에서 베델 가족,
그리고 인근 회중 형제 자매들과 특별 프로그램을 즐겼습니다.
베델 가족과 마지막 식사를 하고 이제 작별 인사를 하려니 감정이 북받쳐 올랐습니다.
그런데 떠나기 직전에 길이 더 막힌다는 소식을 들었습니다.
상파울루에 가서 제시간에 비행기를 탈 수 있었을까요?
우리는 파라과이 베델에 도착해서 예상치 못한 큰 환영을 받고 감동을 받았습니다.
파라과이 지부는 수도인 아순시온에서 아주 가까운 곳에 있습니다.
지부 바로 옆에는 아름다운 새 대회회관과 왕국 전파자 학교 시설이 완공되어 가고 있었습니다.
우리는 건축 자원봉사자들의 열심을 느낄 수 있었죠.
우리가 방문을 마치고 나서 몇 주 후에 대회회관과 학교 시설이 완공되었습니다.
파라과이 베델 가족은 약 100명이며 이들은 이 나라에 있는 1만 1000명의 전도인을 지원합니다.
번역부 형제 자매들은 우리의 출판물과 웹사이트를
과라니어로 번역하기 위해 많은 노력을 기울이죠.
나라 전역의 마음이 정직한 사람들이 그로 인해 큰 유익을 얻어 왔습니다.
과라니어를 사용하는 앙헬리나라는 여자를 예로 들어 보죠.
앙헬리나는 팬데믹 기간에 휴대폰으로 성서 연구를 했습니다.
하지만 외딴 곳에 살았기 때문에 전기 공급이 불안정했습니다.
성서 연구를 위해 휴대폰을 충전하려고 매번 4킬로미터나 되는 거리를 오갔습니다.
발전하면서 집회에도 접속하기 위해 그 거리를 더 자주 오갔습니다.
현재 앙헬리나는 침례받은 증인이고 남편도 성서 연구를 하고 있습니다.
우리는 봉사에서 사람들의 반응이 어떨지 궁금했습니다.
한 공원에서 봉사했는데 거의 모두가 친절하고 겸손하고 대화하려고 했죠.
다음날 코로나19 중에도 우리는 특별 모임을 즐길 수 있었습니다.
전파 활동과 관련된 격려적인 경험담들도 즐겼습니다.
분명 더 많은 파라과이 사람들이 왕국 소식에 반응을 보일 것입니다.
베델 가족과 특별 식사를 하면서 우리는 맛있는 음식도 먹고 전통 춤과 노래도 즐겼습니다.
팬데믹 기간 중에 편지와 전화로 증거한 베델 성원들의 좋은 경험담도 들었죠.
네, 브라질 지부와 마찬가지로 파라과이 베델 가족들도 연합되어 있고 기쁨에 넘치고 있습니다.
많은 베델 가족이 “이 방문이 정말 좋았고 꼭 필요한 것이었”다고 말했습니다.
이런 방문은 중앙장로회가 전 세계 베델 가족을 사랑으로 돌본다는 증거입니다.
상상이 가시겠지만 사랑하는 우리 형제 자매들과 작별하기가 정말 힘들었습니다.
하지만 지난 몇 년 동안 여호와께서 어떻게 그들을 사랑으로 돌보셨는지 알게 되어 기뻤습니다.
우린 형제 자매들을 잊지 못할 겁니다.
두 지부의 베델 가족이 중앙장로회에게 따뜻한 안부를 전합니다.

en.text: Brazil is the largest country in South America
—from the Amazon rain forest
to the rich farmland
and the beautiful coastline.
Paraguay borders Brazil
and is the eighth largest country in South America.
Its diverse geography includes major rivers,
vast plains,
and fertile farmland.
We wondered how the Bethel families in those countries were doing
after some two and a half years of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Brother Dellinger and I, along with our wives, Lourdes and Angela,
began our journey from Warwick Bethel
with a flight to São Paulo, Brazil.
But after the recent presidential election,
large protests in São Paulo were blocking key roads,
including the road from the airport to the branch office.
But Jehovah provided
an unexpected solution.
Thanks to the generosity of a Witness family,
we were transported from the airport in record time.
We had no problem finding a parking space
on the Bethel soccer field.
The branch is located in a rural area
and serves as a home to some 1,200 volunteers.
During our visit, the entire Bethel family
enjoyed morning worship and breakfast in the dining room.
Irmãos, bom dia!
Are you excited to be here for the branch visit?
We are too.
One of the first stops on our tour was the large printery.
In harmony with the Governing Body’s desire to provide printed material,
Brazil produced publications in 65 languages last year.
Brazil also serves as a warehousing branch.
What is that?
It means Brazil can print, stock, and ship literature directly
to individual congregations
in Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay,
Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.
Brazil also ships publications to branches
in Colombia, Mexico, the United States,
South Africa, Germany, and Japan.
In addition, there are ten remote translation offices
that translate our publications into other languages spoken in Brazil.
Brazil Bethel has two museums;
one is devoted to the history of Bible translation
and the other shows the history of Jehovah’s people in Brazil.
The Brazil branch also provides the Art Department in Patterson
with photos and artwork for our publications.
Perhaps you recognize some of these scenes.
Under the oversight of Audio/Video Services at headquarters,
Brazil has a regional video team.
Ready, set, action!
With all of this activity and over 900,000 publishers to support,
the branch is being renovated and modernized.
Many commuter Bethelites are sharing in this project
and, as you can see, all are happy to help.
Another highlight of our visit was the special dinner with the Bethel family,
which featured the Bethel chorus,
traditional dancing,
and some excellent field service experiences.
Naturally, we couldn’t wait to see for ourselves
what field service was like.
And, sure enough,
we found that, both in the rural areas and in the city,
people were polite, easy to talk with,
and receptive to the Kingdom message.
We couldn’t help but think that many more
may yet come into Jehovah’s organization in this large country.
At the Assembly Hall on the branch property,
we were able to enjoy a special program
with the Bethel family and nearby congregations.
Over 2,000 attended.
After our final meal with the Bethel family,
it was hard to hold back the tears as we said our farewells.
But just before our departure, we heard of more road blockages!
Would we be able to get to São Paulo in time for our flight?
Absolutely.
Upon our arrival at Paraguay Bethel,
we were surprised and overwhelmed.
What a welcome!
The Paraguay branch is located
just outside the capital city of Asunción.
Just a block down the street,
a beautiful new Assembly Hall
and School for Kingdom Evangelizers facility
were nearing completion.
The enthusiasm of the construction volunteers was contagious.
Just a few weeks after our visit,
the Assembly Hall and school facility were completed.
There are about 100 members in the Paraguay Bethel family,
which cares for the 11,000 publishers in the country.
The largest department at the branch is Translation.
These dear brothers and sisters devote much effort
to translate our publications and our website
into the Guaraní language.
This has proven to be a blessing
for honesthearted ones throughout the country.
For example, we learned of a Guaraní-speaking woman named Angelina.
During the pandemic, Angelina studied the Bible by cell phone.
But because she lives in a remote location,
electricity is unreliable.
But that did not deter Angelina.
For her Bible study, Angelina walked four kilometers,
or two and a half miles, round-trip to charge her cell phone.
As she progressed, she walked that distance more often
so that she could connect to our meetings.
Was it worth the effort?
Today, Angelina is now baptized
and her husband is studying the Bible!
We were curious about what we would find in the ministry.
In one city park, virtually everyone we spoke with
was polite, humble, and willing to talk.
The next day, despite an outbreak of COVID-19,
we enjoyed a special meeting
that was transmitted to all congregations throughout the country.
The program featured experiences
that highlighted the progress of the preaching work.
No doubt many more
will respond to the Kingdom message in Paraguay.
For the special meal with the Bethel family,
we enjoyed delicious food
along with traditional dancing and singing.
We also enjoyed hearing nice experiences of Bethelites
who witnessed by letter and telephone during the pandemic.
Yes, as was true of Brazil,
the Paraguay Bethel family is united and joyful.
Many in the Bethel family said,
“We did not realize how much we needed this visit.”
Truly, these visits are evidence of the Governing Body’s love
in caring for our Bethel families worldwide.
As you can imagine,
it was hard to tear ourselves away from our dear brothers and sisters.
But we rejoiced in seeing
how Jehovah has so lovingly cared for them
during the past few years.
We will remember them fondly.
Both Bethel families send their warm love to the Governing Body.

title: 콩고 (킨샤사) 지부 보고

ko.text: 분명 콩고는 세계적으로 인기 있는 관광지는 아니지만
전파 활동을 하기에는 아주 좋은 곳입니다.
그에 더해 여호와의 증인들은 높은 도덕 표준과 성경 교육 활동으로 잘 알려져 있습니다.
증인이 아닌 부모들이 증인들에게 자신의 자녀와 성경 공부를 해 달라고 요청하는 경우가 흔히 있는데,
자녀가 더 나은 사람이 되고 학교에서 공부를 더 잘하도록 돕고 싶어서이죠.
그 결과, 성서 연구 건수가 전도인 수의 약 세 배나 됩니다.
그리고 기념식 참석자 수는 전도인 수의 거의 다섯 배나 되죠.
콩고는 인터넷 연결이 도시에서도 상당히 불안정하고
그래서 팬데믹 기간에 대체 방식으로 집회를 보고 전파 활동을 하는 데 큰 어려움이 있었죠.
우리는 형제 자매들이 제때에 영적 양식을 얻고 전파 활동에 활동적으로 참여할 수 있도록
조직이 마련해 준 부가적인 방법들에 감사합니다.
예를 들면, JW 위성 TV 채널, JW 박스,
그리고 미리 녹음된 공개 강연을 지방 라디오 방송국을 통해 송출한 마련이 있었죠.
그에 더해, 전도인들은 아주 실용적인 전파 방법들을 생각해 냈습니다.
예를 들어, 내륙 깊숙이 있는 므페시라는 시골 회중에서는
세계적으로 많은 생명을 앗아 가고 있는 전염병에 관한 뉴스를 들었지만
그런 소식이 큰 주의를 끌지 못했습니다.
하지만 에마뉘엘이라는 임시 특별 파이오니아 형제는
조직에서 마련한 코로나19 지침을 따르기로 결심했습니다.
그런데 인터넷 연결도 안 되고 연구생이 스마트폰도 갖고 있지 않은데
어떻게 성서 연구를 계속 할 수 있었을까요?
그의 집에는 앞문도 있고 뒷문도 있었기 때문에 그는 뒷문을 열어 놓고
성서 연구생들에게 한 명씩 뒷문으로 들어오라고 했습니다.
각자 자기 의자를 갖고 와서 방 안에 있는 것은 아무것도 만지지 말고
거실로 통하는 문 앞에 앉게 했습니다. 그 문은 닫혀 있었죠.
에마뉘엘 형제는 앞문으로 들어가 닫힌 문 반대편 거실에 앉아 성서 연구를 사회했습니다.
정부에서 시행한 코로나19 제한 조치 때문에 많은 형제 자매들이 큰 타격을 입었습니다.
안 그래도 수입이 얼마 되지 않았는데 하루 아침에 그마저도 수입이 없게 된 것이죠.
우리 지부는 승인을 받아 약 3천 톤의 기본 식품을 20만 명이 넘는 사람들에게 공급했습니다.
113개의 재해 구호 위원회가 단지 4개월 만에 이 인도주의적 구호 물품을 나누어 주었습니다.
식품을 실은 트럭들이 왕국회관에 도착해 수백 명의 사람들이 구호 물품을 받는 것을 보고
증인이 아닌 많은 사람들이 깊은 인상을 받았습니다.
그들은 여호와의 조직이 다른 종교 단체들과 얼마나 다른지 또 한 번 체험했습니다.
팬데믹 중에 많은 목사들과 전도사들이 교회 신자들에게 자기들을 경제적으로 도와 달라고 한 반면,
증인들은 도움이 필요한 지역 주민들에게 무료로 물품을 나누어 주었습니다.
분명 “[콩고의 밭은] 희어져 수확하게 되었고” 수확하는 사람들은 기뻐하고 있습니다.

en.text: Congo is certainly not among
the most popular travel destinations
for tourists around the world,
but it is definitely a preaching paradise.
In general, very few people have reservations
to discuss their personal spiritual convictions with strangers.
In addition, Jehovah’s Witnesses are well-known for their high moral standards
and their consistent Bible education.
It is not uncommon for non-Witness parents
to even solicit the services of a Witness Bible teacher
in order to help their children become better persons
and improve their performance in school.
As a result,
the number of Bible studies is about three times
the number of active Witnesses.
And Memorial attendance figures
amount to almost five times the number of publishers.
As you can imagine,
in a country where Internet connections are pretty unstable in urban areas
and almost unavailable in more remote places,
it was a tremendous challenge for the friends to adapt
to the alternative COVID-19 meeting and preaching methods.
Our branch benefited from many additional arrangements
that have been kindly put in place to assist these brothers and sisters
to keep up-to-date with spiritual food and stay active in the ministry,
such as the JW satellite TV channel,
the JW Box network,
and prerecorded public talks
broadcast on local radio stations.
In addition, publishers came up with some
very practical alternative preaching methods themselves.
For example,
in a rural congregation called Mpeshi deep in the interior,
the news of a worldwide pandemic costing hundreds of thousands of lives
hadn’t been perceived as more than background noise.
Still, a temporary special pioneer called Emmanuel
was determined to apply theocratic COVID-19 instructions.
But how could he continue to conduct his Bible studies
in a place with no Internet coverage
and with students who don’t even possess smartphones?
This is what he came up with:
As his house has a main entrance and a back door,
he advised his Bible students to come one by one
and enter through the back door,
which he left open
(each one with his own chair not touching anything in the room),
and sit down next to the closed door leading to the living room.
Emmanuel himself used the main door,
sat on the other side of that closed door in the living room,
and conducted his studies, so to speak, behind a closed door.
So let’s go back to the urban areas.
Here government-imposed COVID-19 restrictions
had a great impact
on thousands of our self-employed brothers and sisters
who overnight were cut off
from their already meager sources of income.
Our branch was authorized
to provide about 3,000 tons of staple food
for more than 200,000 beneficiaries.
One hundred thirteen Disaster Relief Committees
distributed this humanitarian aid
in only four months.
As food trucks pulled up at Kingdom Hall properties
and later hundreds of individuals left with care packages,
many onlookers were deeply impressed.
Once more, they realized how different Jehovah’s organization is
from all the other religious entities around them.
While many pastors and preachers urged their church members
to help them financially during the pandemic,
the Witnesses distributed free goods to needy ones in their community.
Definitely “the fields [in Congo] are white for harvesting,”
and the reapers rejoice.

cn.text: 对全球爱好旅游的人来说
刚果绝不会是他们想去的地方
但这里绝对是一个传道的乐园
可以说，刚果人几乎都不会拒绝
跟别人谈论与信仰有关的事
耶和华见证人因为遵守崇高的道德标准
和推广圣经教育
而在当地广为人知
有些做父母的，虽然自己不学习真理
但却愿意让自己的孩子跟传道员学习圣经
他们希望传道员可以教导孩子
并帮孩子提高学习成绩
结果，现在圣经学生的数字
差不多是传道员数字的3倍
参加纪念聚会的人数
几乎达到了传道员数字的5倍
在刚果，很多偏远的地区几乎都没有网络
而城市里的网络也很不稳定
所以你不难想象
在疫情期间，弟兄姐妹要参加聚会和传道
有多么不容易
我们作出了一些额外的安排
好帮助弟兄姐妹继续收到滋养信心的食物
也能够继续参与传道工作
这些安排包括使用JW卫星电视
使用JW盒子
以及在当地电台播放事先录制好的公众演讲
另外，弟兄姐妹也发挥想象力
想到了很多传道的方法
比如，刚果内陆的深处有一群会众
几乎与世隔绝
虽然疫情蔓延全球
夺去了很多人的生命
但当地人对这样的新闻都毫不在意
不过
会众里一位叫埃玛纽埃尔的临时特别先驱
还是决心遵守组织的防疫规定
当地没有网络
而他的一些圣经学生甚至都没有手机
埃玛纽埃尔该怎么主持圣经课程呢？
他想到一个办法
他的房子有两个门
前门和后门
他让学生一个一个地来
他会先打开后门，自己使用前门
学生来的时候，都会自己带着凳子
从后门进来后
就在起居室的门前停下来坐好
埃玛纽埃尔自己就坐在起居室门的另一面
隔着门主持圣经课程
他还特别提醒学生
什么东西都不要碰
住在城市里的弟兄姐妹，情况又怎样呢？
当地政府为了防止疫情蔓延
作出了很多限制和规定
很多弟兄姐妹都自己做小生意
他们的收入原本就很微薄
那时候他们的情况就更加艰难了
我们得到批准，购买了3000吨食物
分发给20多万个传道员
113个救灾委员会只用了四个月的时间
就把这些物资分发出去了
我们用卡车把这些物资
送到不同的王国聚会所
之后，会众里的弟兄姐妹就会过来领取
这让很多当地人都很惊讶
他们再一次看出
耶和华的组织跟其他的宗教团体
真的有天壤之别
很多教会里的牧师和神父
在疫情期间都要求信徒为自己提供经济援助
但耶和华见证人却为传道员免费分发食物
没错，刚果的田地“已经变白了”
收割的人都很喜乐

title: 편견이 뭘까?

ko.text: 혹시 이 바이러스에 감염된 적 있니?
지금까지 정말 많은 사람들이 이 바이러스에 걸렸어.
그런데 우리는 누구나 편견을 가질 위험이 있고
어쩌면 이미 가지고 있을 수도 있어.
편견을 없애려면 그게 뭔지부터 알아야 해.
편견은 누군가에 대해 좋은 쪽이든 나쁜 쪽이든 한쪽으로 치우친 생각을 하는 거야.
뭐 때문에 다른 사람을 편견을 갖고 대하게 될까?
아니면 그냥 뭔가가 나랑 다르기 때문일 수도 있고.
근데 누군갈 잘 알지도 못하면서 겉모습이나 배경으로 판단하는 건
마치 어떤 음식을 먹어 보지도 않고 싫어하는 것과 같지
편견에 사로잡히면 어떤 사람은 잘해주고 어떤 사람은 멀리하게 돼.
또 자신이 잘났다고 생각해서 자기랑 다른 사람은 무시하게 될지도 몰라.
“교만하면 파멸이 따르고, 영이 거만하면 걸려 넘어지게 된다”고 말해.
그런 태도를 나타내면 진짜 친구를 사귈 수 없어.
나한테 편견이 있다는 걸 알게 되었다면 어떻게 해야 할까?
니 주위 사람들에 대해 더 알아보는 거야.
그들이 살면서 어떤 경험을 했고, 어떤 재능이 있는지 알아 봐.
다른 사람의 장점을 아는 건 편견을 없애는 아주 좋은 치료제거든.
그리고 니가 누구랑 친한지 생각해 봐.
친구들이 다들 외모도 생각도 행동도 너랑 비슷하니?
그럼 성경 고린도 후서 6:13에서 조언하는 것처럼 “넓히”는 게 어떨까?
너랑 다른 다양한 사람들을 친구로 사귀는 거지.
그런데 나쁜 행동을 하는 친구가 있다면 어떻게 해야 할까?
너도 똑같이 나쁜 행동을 하게 될 수 있으니까.
넌 그런 편견에 물들지 않을 수 있어.
사람들을 섣불리 나쁘게 보는 일을 피하고
다른 사람을 더 잘 알기 위해 노력하고
나와는 다른 다양한 사람들을 친구로 사귀는 거지.
나랑 달라서 끌리지 않던 차이점도 매력으로 느껴지게 될 거야.

en.text: Have you been infected?
No, no, not with an actual virus,
but with something that has infected people throughout history,
something that no one is completely immune to
—prejudice.
‘Whoa! Whoa!’ you may think,
‘Prejudice—me?
‘That can’t be right.
I like all kinds of people!’
The truth is that all of us are capable of
or even guilty of prejudice to some degree.
But it can be hard to recognize in ourselves.
So, what is prejudice?
To overcome prejudice, you have to understand what it is.
Prejudice often means having a biased opinion,
either good or bad, of someone you don’t even know.
We can be prejudiced against people and even treat them badly
simply because of their age,
where they’re from,
what they look like,
how much money they have,
or because of other things that make people different from us.
But judging others based on appearances or superficial traits
before getting to know them would be unfair and unreasonable.
It would be like hating a food before you’ve even tried it.
Prejudice can lead us to give special treatment to some people
and exclude others.
It can make us act like we’re smarter
or better than people who are different.
But that can be dangerous.
The Bible says at Proverbs 16:18
that “pride is before a crash,
and a haughty spirit before stumbling.”
Having a superior attitude can keep us from having real friends.
That can take the joy out of life.
If you recognize prejudice in your heart,
what can you do?
Try these steps:
Learn more about those around you.
What have they experienced in their life?
What are their talents?
When you appreciate others’ strengths,
it can be a powerful antidote to prejudice.
Next, take a look at your friends.
Do they all look, think,
and act a lot like you?
If so, follow the Bible’s advice
at 2 Corinthians 6:13 and “widen out.”
Make friends with people who are different from you.
But what if you discover
that some of them practice bad things?
In that case, stay away!
Their bad conduct can make you act badly.
In this world, prejudice is everywhere.
But we don’t have to let it control our thinking.
We can overcome prejudice
if we avoid reaching negative conclusions about people
before we get to know them,
make an effort to learn about others,
and try to make friends with people who are different from us.
The more we know about the people around us,
the more we can appreciate the things that make us different.

cn.text: 你被感染了吗？
No！No！No！
我说的可不是病毒
有个东西，感染力超强
几乎没有人能抵抗得了
那就是偏见
你可能会想
我？偏见？
没有吧！
我跟谁都合得来啊！
其实我们或多或少
都会对别人有偏见
只是我们没有发现而已
怎样才算是对人有偏见呢？
想要抵抗它
就要先知道偏见是什么
偏见通常是对不认识的人
有先入为主的看法
不论是好是坏
我们对人有偏见
甚至欺负他们
原因可能是他们的年龄
文化背景
长相
有没有钱
只要是跟我们不一样的地方
都可能是产生偏见的原因
但如果我们还没认识一个人
就用外在条件评断他
这样既不公平也不合理
就好像你还没尝过一道菜
就觉得它难吃
如果我们有偏见
就会对人有差别待遇
我们也可能觉得自己很了不起
瞧不起别人
但这样的心态可能会害到自己
“骄傲自大是失败的开始
心高气傲是跌倒的起因”
如果觉得自己高人一等
就很难结交真正的朋友
生活也不那么丰富多彩了
如果你被偏见感染了
可以怎么做呢？
首先，要多认识周围的人
比如他们有什么样的经历？
有什么样的才艺？
当你懂得欣赏别人
就可以加强对偏见的抵抗力
接着，想想你跟怎样的人做朋友
他们的打扮、想法和行为
都跟你一样吗？
如果是这样
你可以按照哥林多后书6:13说的
“开阔心胸”
扩大你的交友圈
但如果你发现有的人会做坏事
那就要离他们远一点
因为他们可能会把你带坏
虽然这个社会充满偏见
但你还是可以保护好自己
不受感染
我们来复习一下吧
打败偏见的方法是
不要对人有先入为主的看法
要多认识别人
要扩大自己的交友圈
我们更认识别人
就会发现差异不是问题
反倒会拉近彼此的距离

title: 시련을 인내하는 사람들을 위해 열렬히 기도하십시오

ko.text: 저는 매일 아침 일이나 봉사를 하러 가기 전에
의자에 앉아 커피를 한잔 하면서 jw.org를 살펴봅니다.
그렇게 하면 우리 형제들이 어떻게 지내는지 최신 소식을 잘 알 수 있죠.
우리 형제 자매들이 시련을 겪고 있다는 내용을 읽게 되면
그 형제 자매들을 돕기 위해 뭔가 하고 싶은 마음이 생겨요.
언론에서는 우리에 대해 부정적이거나 사실이 아니거나
사실이 아닌 믿을 수 없는 정보였어요.
사도 바울은 시련을 겪을 때 형제들에게
‘나를 위해 하느님께 기도하는 일에 힘써’ 달라고 부탁했습니다.
그들이 얻을 수 있는 모든 지원과 도움을 필요로 합니다.
끝이 매우 가까웠기 때문에 자녀들은 우리가 어떤 일을 겪게 될 수 있는지 알아야 합니다.
다른 사람을 위해 기도하는 것에 관한 동영상과
조직에서 마련해 준 자료들을 활용할 수 있죠.
가족 숭배 때 같이 학습 자료를 해 봤어요.
그 형제들은 모르겠지만 우리가 그들을 위해 기도하면 여호와께서 기뻐하세요.
용기가 있는 그 형제들을 저도 본받고 싶어요.
저는 우리 자녀가 다른 사람들이 어떤 시련을 겪는지 아는 게 중요하다고 생각해요.
아이들이 그 형제들을 생각해 보고 그들을 위해 기도한다면
그 형제들이 충실하도록 도와주고 있는 거죠.
저는 다른 사람을 위해 기도하면 언제나 힘이 나요.
그렇게 하면 실제로 여호와와 더 가까워지는 것 같거든요.
다른 사람들이 어려움을 겪으면서 어떻게 충실을 유지하는지 생각해 보면
제 믿음이 강해지고 그들의 믿음을 본받고 싶어져요.
교통사고를 당했는데 그 뒤로 제 삶이 크게 달라졌어요.
우리 웹사이트를 살펴보다가 뉴스룸을 보게 되었어요.
거기서 우리 형제 자매들이 어떤 어려움을 겪고 있고,
그 모든 형제 자매들이 어려움 속에서도 포기하지 않는다면 저도 포기해서는 안 되죠.
이제는 기도할 때 다른 사람들을 위해 먼저 기도하고
다른 사람들을 위해 기도하면 여호와에 대한 믿음과 신뢰심이 강해집니다.
그분이 우리 형제 자매들을 도와주셨고 우리도 도와주실 걸 아니까요.
러시아에서 박해가 심해지자 무슨 일이 생길지 몰라서 많이 불안했죠.
jw.org에 실린 뉴스를 보고 전 세계 우리 형제들이 러시아의 상황을 알고 있다는 걸 깨달았어요.
다른 나라 형제들이 우릴 위해 뭐라고 기도하는진 몰랐지만
관심을 갖고 우리를 위해 기도해 준다는 건 알았어요.
형제들이 우리를 위해 기도해 준다는 사실은
형제 자매들이 겪는 문제를 잘 알면 마음에서 우러나온 더 진실한 기도를 할 수 있습니다.
모든 기회를 이용해서 기도할 거예요. 형제 자매들을 위해 기도하는 걸 멈추지 않을 겁니다.
우리가 여호와의 목적과 일치하게 기도할 때 그분은 우리의 기도를 들어 주십니다.

en.text: Before I go to work or go witnessing,
I wake up, grab a coffee,
sit in my chair, and I check jw.org.
I think it’s important because it helps us to keep informed
with what our brothers are going through.
When I read about my brothers and sisters facing trials,
I just feel I want to do something
to help these brothers and sisters.
When Jehovah’s Witnesses were banned in Russia,
a lot of negative, false, and questionable information about us
began to appear in the media.
It was all so unreal. It was hard to believe.
When the apostle Paul was facing a trial, he was asking the brothers
to ‘exert themselves in prayer to God for me.’
For our brothers going through jail
or through natural disasters,
they need all the support and help
that they can get.
We’re so close to the end;
we want our children to understand what we might face.
We’ve done the videos on praying for others,
and the brothers have given us good worksheets.
For family worship, we did some worksheets.
They might not know
that we are praying for them,
but Jehovah feels happy when I pray for them.
They have courage, and I want to be like them too.
As a mother, I think it’s really important
for our children to know what’s going on
with others’ trials.
And if they can stop and really feel for those brothers
and then offer a prayer,
they’re taking part in them being faithful.
It’s always encouraging
to pray for others
because you’re actually building
your relationship with Jehovah.
When you stop and consider what others are going through
and how they’re being faithful, that’s really built my faith,
and then I want to imitate their faith.
I was involved in a car accident,
and that impacted my life.
I have pain every day.
I was feeling lonely and depressed.
And while I was scrolling through the website,
I came across the Newsroom,
and I read about our brothers and sisters
—the things that they were going through, the challenges they were facing.
If they didn’t give up going through all those difficult times,
then I don’t have to give up either.
My sequence of prayer now is to pray for others first
and then for myself last.
When we pray for others, it helps us
to build our faith in Jehovah and trust in him
because we know that he has helped our brothers and sisters
and he will also help us.
When the persecution in Russia began to grow,
a sense of uncertainty arose
about what was happening.
When we saw the news on jw.org,
we realized that our brothers all over the world
knew about the situation in Russia.
Although we did not hear how brothers from other countries were praying for us,
we knew that they were doing it and cared about us.
The knowledge that the brothers were praying for us
really strengthened us.
I knew that everything was under control.
When you know the problems that a brother or sister is facing,
then our prayers are more sincere
and they truly come from the heart.
I must use every opportunity.
I must not let up to pray for my brothers and sisters.
When we pray
and it’s for his name, Jehovah answers our prayers.

title: 크리스토퍼 메이버: 자신의 동기를 점검하십시오 (잠언 16:2)

ko.text: 해설자들이 말한 것처럼 오늘 우리가 생각해 볼 주제는 아주 개인적이고 민감할 수 있는 문제입니다.
동기는 우리 마음속 깊은 곳에 자리잡고 있죠.
오늘의 성구는 동기에 관해 우리에게 주의를 주면서 그에 대한 여호와의 견해를 가져야 한다고 말합니다.
함께 성경을 펴서 잠언 16:2의 성구 전체를 읽어 보겠습니다.
우리가 이러한 경고를 받는 이유는 이미 살펴봤듯이 동기엔 강력한 힘이 있기 때문이죠.
동기는 우리가 하느님의 눈에 옳은 일을 하게 할 수도 있지만,
잘못된 일을 하도록 우리를 속일 수도 있습니다.
이 점에 대해 잠언 16:2은 이렇게 말합니다.
“사람의 길이 자기가 보기에는 모두 옳지만, 여호와께서는 동기를 살피신다.”
우리가 자신을 위해 좋은 목표를 세우거나 좋은 일을 한다고 생각할지 모르지만,
성구에서 알려 주는 것처럼 우리의 방법이나 생각이 좋아 보인다 해도 여호와께서 그것을 살피십니다.
그리고 우리의 동기가 순수하지 않거나 그분의 뜻과 온전히 일치하지 않은 걸 보시게 되면
우리는 그분의 승인을 얻지 못하고 심지어 그분의 분노를 사게 될 수도 있습니다.
그러면 어떻게 우리의 동기가 순수하고 여호와께 기쁨이 되게 할 수 있습니까?
그 점을 알기 위해서는 우리의 마음에 대해 잘 알아야 합니다.
예레미야 17:9은 마음에 대해 중요한 점 한 가지를 알려 줍니다.
“마음은 그 무엇보다도 더 믿을 수 없고 무모하다. 누가 그 속을 알 수 있겠는가?”라고 했죠.
마음은 우리를 속여서 자신의 잘못을 정당화하게 만들 수 있습니다.
또 여호와께 드리는 봉사를 이용해 자신의 개인적인 이익을 추구하는 행동을 정당화하게 만들 수도 있습니다.
바로 그런 예가 아까 본 잠언의 상호 참조 성구인 사무엘상 15:13, 14에 나오는데,
성경을 펴서 그 부분을 함께 살펴보겠습니다.
여호와 하느님은 사울왕에게 그가 뭘 하기 원하시는지 아주 분명한 지시를 하셨습니다.
아말렉 사람들을 가장 작은 자에서 가장 큰 자까지 모조리 죽이라는 것이었습니다.
5절에서 7절을 보면 사울은 그 임무를 받아들이고 꽤 잘 수행했습니다.
여호와께서 하라고 하신 그대로 아말렉 사람들을 멸망시키고 있었죠.
9절. “그러나 사울과 백성은 [왕인] 아각을 비롯하여 양 떼와 소 떼와 살진 짐승과 숫양들 중에서,
또 모든 좋은 것들 중에서 제일 좋은 것들을 남겨 두었다. 완전히 멸망시키기를 원하지 않았던 것이다.
이 임무, 즉 여호와께 드리는 봉사를 이용해 뭘 하려는 거였죠?
자신의 영광을 구하고 이익을 얻는 것이었습니다.
사실 12절을 보면 그는 갈멜까지 가서 자신의 기념비를 세웠습니다.
아말렉을 상대로 거둔 큰 승리에 대한 영광을 자신에게 돌리는 거였죠.
아각왕을 일종의 전리품처럼 데리고 와서 자신이 아말렉을 정복했다는 것을 과시했습니다.
그리고 그들에게 큰 도움이 될 가장 좋은 동물들을 남겨서 이익을 취했습니다.
사울의 동기가 순수하지 않다는 것을 꿰뚫어 보셨죠.
그래서 그분은 사무엘을 사울에게 보내셔서 그분이 그를 정죄하셨고,
그가 여호와의 승인을 잃었기 때문에 더 이상 왕으로 통치하지 못할 것이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
하지만 사울은 그런 정죄의 말씀을 듣기 전에 자신이 여전히 여호와를 기쁘시게 하고 있다고 생각했고,
백성 앞에서 하느님의 충실한 종인 것처럼 보이려고 했습니다.
“여호와께서 당신을 축복하시기 바랍니다. 나는 여호와의 말씀대로 행했습니다.”
당신은 여호와의 영광이 아니라 자신의 영광을 구하고 있어요”라고 했죠.
이 기록에서 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
이 기록은 기억해 둘 만한 좋은 예인데,
오늘의 주제인 동기가 정말 중요하다는 것을 아주 잘 보여 주기 때문입니다.
사울의 동기는 순수하지 않았고, 여호와를 삶에서 첫째 자리에 두지 않았습니다.
네, 그는 동기가 순수하지 않았기 때문에 하느님께 불충실하게 되었고, 그분께 강한 질책을 받게 되었습니다.
우리가 마음속에 불순한 생각이나 동기를 갖게 되는 심각한 실수를 피하려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
성경 말씀처럼 우리의 마음에 그런 문제가 있다는 걸 어떻게 알 수 있습니까?
여호와께선 우리가 자신의 마음 상태와 동기를 파악하게 도와주십니다.
히브리 4:12을 보면 여호와께서는 우리가 그렇게 할 수 있는 놀라운 도구를 주셨습니다.
“하느님의 말씀은 살아 있고 힘을 발휘하며 어떤 쌍날칼보다 더 날카로워서,
사람 속을 꿰찔러 영혼과 영을 가르고 관절과 골수를 가르기까지 하며, 마음에 품은 생각과 의도를 분별해 냅니다.”
따라서 충실한 종이 우리에게 하느님의 말씀인 성경을 매일 읽으라고 권하는 것도 당연합니다.
성경은 우리의 불완전한 마음의 단단한 껍데기를 꿰뚫고 들어가 마음을 쪼개서
그 속에 실제로 무엇이 들어 있는지 드러내 줍니다.
그러면 우리는 문제를 바로잡을 수 있죠.
지난 주에 우리는 정말 유익한 「파수대」 기사를 공부했습니다.
이 「파수대」 기사는 하느님의 말씀에서 힘을 얻는 방법만이 아니라
우리가 우리 마음속에 무엇이 있는지 알아보는 쉽지 않은 일을 할 수 있는 방법도 알려 주었습니다.
이 기사의 요점은 성경을 읽기 전에 기도를 해서 여호와의 영의 인도를 구하라는 것입니다.
그리고 성경을 읽은 다음에는 내가 실제로 그 자리에 있고 성경 인물의 입장이라고 상상해 볼 수 있습니다.
우리의 마음 상태가 실제로 어떤지 확인하십시오.
이 내용이 나에게 어떻게 적용되는지 생각해 보고 실제로 적용하십시오.
그렇게 한다면 우리는 우리의 마음 상태가 어떤지 알 수 있으며,
필요하다면 우리의 잘못된 동기를 바로잡기 위해 조처를 취할 수 있습니다.
아마 젊은 형제들은 회중에서 봉사의 특권을 받기 위해 노력하고 있을 것입니다.
봉사의 종이나 장로가 되기 위해 노력하는 것은 좋은 일입니다.
바로 그럴 때 우리가 살펴본 네 단계를 따를 수 있죠.
봉사의 종이나 장로에 대한 성경의 자격 조건을 모두 읽어 보십시오.
알게 된 점들을 생활에 적용하고 이렇게 자문해 보십시오.
‘내가 그 특권을 받고 싶은 이유는 뭘까?
다른 충실한 성경 인물이 되어 하느님의 백성을 위해 여호와의 뜻을 행하는 데 온 힘을 쏟아붓고
때로는 사람들에게 무시를 당한다고 상상해 보세요.
사실 신권 임명을 받기 원하는 모든 사람은 방금 살펴본 방법으로 우리의 마음을 점검해야 합니다.
우리의 동기가 우리와 그런 임명에 대한 여호와의 뜻과 일치하는지 확인하는 거죠.
그렇게 해 보면 우리에게 사울처럼 여호와께 드리는 봉사를 이용해 자신의 이익을 추구하고
자신을 돋보이게 하려는 동기가 있다는 걸 알게 될 수 있습니다.
“충성심을 약화시키는 것을 멀리하십시오” 심포지엄을 기억하실 겁니다.
영상에 나온 한 장로는 많은 일을 하고 있었지만 마음속에 문제가 있었습니다.
그는 다른 장로에게서 조언을 받았을 때 자신이 나타낸 반응을 보고 마음에 문제가 있음을 깨달았죠.
그는 여호와께 기도했고 회중에서 눈에 띄지 않는 일들을 했습니다.
때로는 아무도 없는 시간에 왕국회관에 가서 사람들의 주목을 받지 못하는 일을 했습니다.
하지만 그건 하느님의 뜻과 목적을 이루기 위해 꼭 필요한 일들이었죠.
영상에서 보셨던 것처럼 그러한 변화는 그 장로가 지하실에서 형제들을 인도하는 데 도움이 됐고
그리고 여호와께서는 큰 환난 중에 양들을 돌보는 데 그를 사용하셨습니다.

en.text: As our commenters bring out,
our focus today is on something
that is actually very private
and perhaps very sensitive,
and that is our motives.
Motives dwell deep within our figurative hearts.
They really are described as “the impelling force behind our conduct”
and decision-making.
But today, our text puts us on alert about these motives,
and we need to have Jehovah’s viewpoint of them.
Let’s consider the full scripture.
Open your Bibles, please, to Proverbs 16:2.
We’re alerted to this because, as we’ve already discussed,
motives are an impelling force.
They can help us do what is right in God’s eyes,
but they also can deceive us into doing what is wrong.
Notice what the Bible says about this;
Proverbs 16:2 says:
“All of man’s ways seem right to him,
but Jehovah examines the motives.”
Interesting.
We could set a very good goal for ourselves
—be involved in what appears to be very good things.
But if, as the Bible says,
our ways or our thoughts may appear good
but Jehovah examines them
and he sees that our motives are not pure,
or not in total harmony with his will,
well, we could meet up with his disapproval
and even sharp judgment.
How, then, can we make sure that our motives are pure
and that they are pleasing to Jehovah God?
In order to understand that, we have to understand our hearts
because this is where our motives reside —in our figurative hearts.
An important aspect of our hearts
is brought out for us in Jeremiah 17:9.
Remember, it says there that “the heart is more treacherous
“than anything else and is desperate.
Who can know it?”
You see, our imperfect figurative hearts are inherently selfish.
It thinks of only one thing, and that is itself.
And our hearts could deceive us into justifying errors on our part
or even justifying self-seeking actions,
using Jehovah’s service
for our own personal benefit.
Now, this is a dangerous thing.
A case in point is brought out for us.
If you look at the cross-reference to this scripture
at 1 Samuel 15:13, 14—
In fact, let’s open our Bibles to that portion of the scripture.
It’s the account of King Saul,
and Jehovah God gave King Saul very definite directions
on what he wanted him to do,
and that was to completely annihilate the Amalekites
from the greatest to the least of them.
He was to get rid of them.
Now, if we look at verses 5 through 7,
we see that Saul took on this assignment, and he was doing rather well.
He was doing exactly what Jehovah had told him to do,
and that was to annihilate the Amalekites.
But in verse 9, we see that something went wrong
—something changed.
In verse 9, it says: “However, Saul and the people
“spared Agag [who was the king] and the best of the flock, the herd,
“the fattened animals, the rams, and all that was good.
“They did not want to devote them to destruction.
“But all the goods that were worthless and unwanted,
these they devoted to destruction.”
So we see something happened here.
Saul developed, or had, his motives for one point only:
using Jehovah’s service —this commission—
to do what?
To glorify himself, to benefit himself.
In fact, if you look in verse 12, he even went so far as to go to Carmel
and erect a monument to himself
—glorifying this great victory that he performed over the Amalekites
and bringing King Agag back with him (as perhaps a trophy)
to show everyone that he dominated this nation, got rid of them,
and enriched himself by these beautiful animals
that would no doubt benefit the herds that they had.
Well,
was Jehovah fooled by this?
Obviously not. Jehovah saw right through it.
He saw right to the core of the matter that Saul’s motives were not pure.
And so when he sent Samuel to the camp,
he told Samuel to tell Saul he had basically been condemned,
ripping the rulership away from him.
He was no longer pleasing to Jehovah God.
Saul, though, before he heard this denunciation from Jehovah,
thought he was still in good stead with God,
and he was putting on a big show
of being a servant of God, a faithful man.
He said in verse 13:
“May Jehovah bless you [when he saw Samuel].
I have carried out the word of Jehovah.”
And Samuel set him straight:
‘No you didn’t. You were lying.
You were seeking your own glory and not Jehovah’s glory.’
Well, what can we learn from this account?
It’s a very good account to have in mind
because it’s a sharp contrast, or an acute example,
of what we’re discussing here today about motives.
We see that Saul’s motives were not pure.
He was not putting Jehovah first in his life,
and, in fact, his impure motives
moved him to an unfaithful course with God,
meeting up with his strong judgment against him.
How can we avoid making such a terrible mistake
in succumbing to perhaps impure reasonings or motives
that we might have in our hearts?
How can ‘we even know it’ —as the Bible says—
that it’s there?
Well, Jehovah does help us read our motives
and understand what’s going on.
At Hebrews 4:12,
we can see that Jehovah has given us a marvelous tool to do that.
It says: “For the word of God is alive
“and exerts power and is sharper than any two-edged sword
“and pierces even to the dividing of soul and spirit,
“and of joints from the marrow,
and is able to discern thoughts and intentions of the heart.”
So it’s no wonder that we are given strong admonition from the faithful slave
to read God’s Word, the Bible, every day.
It’s by means of this amazing tool
that can pierce through and slice through the hard shell
of our figurative, imperfect hearts
that it is revealed what’s really there.
And then we can do something about it.
You see, as we learned in this past week’s Watchtower—
What a wonderful article it was!
And what beautiful guidance it gave us
about how to gain strength from God’s Word
and also how to accomplish
this very difficult assignment, if you will,
of knowing what’s in our hearts!
Here we are told that before we read God’s Word,
we should pray, ask Jehovah’s spirit to guide and direct us,
and then after reading it, imagine that we are there
in the very account that we’re reading
—in the shoes of the ones that we’re talking about.
Meditate on these things.
Understand what is truly going on in our hearts.
How does this information apply to me personally?
And then apply what we learn.
And you see, by doing that, well, then we can not only reveal
what’s going on inside of our hearts
but then we can take steps to correct our motives
if they need correcting.
Perhaps as young brothers,
we desire to reach out for service as a privilege in the congregation.
It’s a wonderful thing to reach out to be a ministerial servant, to be an elder.
But what are the true motives?
Why do we want this assignment?
Well, this is where following
this four-step procedure that we learned can help.
Why not read all the qualifications
that a ministerial servant or an elder should have?
Meditate upon them.
Apply these things in our life and ask ourselves:
‘Why do I really want to be a servant in the congregation?
‘Is it to glorify myself, to promote myself,
or to actually do the work?’
Imagine ourselves being Timothy or Paul
or other faithful men mentioned in the Bible
who expended themselves and poured themselves out
on behalf of God’s people in doing Jehovah’s will,
even perhaps being looked down upon
both by those in the congregation as well as on the outside.
Are we willing to do that?
Actually, all of us who desire theocratic assignments
should go through this kind of procedure
to make sure that our hearts
—our motives, really—
are in harmony with Jehovah’s will
for this assignment as well as what he wants for us.
Doing this, perhaps maybe we find
that we may be harboring a Saul-like motive
and perhaps want to use Jehovah’s service
for self-interests and to promote ourselves.
I think it was interesting several years ago back in 2016
at the “Remain Loyal to Jehovah” convention
—perhaps you recall the the symposium “Avoid What Erodes Loyalty”—
and there it gave the experience of an elder who was taking the lead,
how he was revealed.
His motives were revealed by some counsel that an elder had given him,
and he saw that he wasn’t responding correctly.
So, what did he do?
He prayed to Jehovah,
and then he took on assignments in the congregation that no one ever saw,
working after hours, perhaps when no one was at the Kingdom Hall,
doing things that would not put him in the limelight.
Yet, it was necessary work
—work that needed to be done to carry out God’s will and purpose.
This eventually changed his heart.
And as we understand from that video
and that brother in the basement taking the lead with the brothers there,
it actually saved his life to make these changes and helped.
And Jehovah used him to appropriately shepherd the flock
during the great tribulation.
Well, that’s a good example for us.
That’s what we want to do, and we can.

cn.text: 在今天的演讲里
我们要讨论的这个话题
对有些人来说可能很敏感
就是我们的动机
我们的动机藏在我们内心深处
但它会推动我们采取某些行动
作出某些决定
今天的经文给了我们很好的提醒
让我们用耶和华的观点来看待动机
我们先读一下经文
请打开圣经到箴言16:2
就像刚才讨论的一样
我们必须提高警觉
因为动机很有推动力
它既能推动我们做上帝看为对的事
也能骗我们作出错误的事
请看看经文是怎么说的
箴言16:2说
“人认为自己的行为都是正确的
但耶和华察验人的动机”
有意思
我们可能为自己制定了一些很好的目标
追求一些看起来很好的事
但就像这节经文说的
我们的行为、我们的想法可能看起来很好
但耶和华察验的时候
却发现我们的动机其实并不纯正
跟他的旨意也不吻合
如果是这样，我们就会让耶和华不悦
甚至令他生气
那怎么确保我们的动机是纯正的？
是令耶和华上帝喜悦的呢？
要做到这一点
我们就需要先了解自己的内心
因为我们的动机发自内心
耶利米书17:9
指出关于我们内心的一个事实
经文说
“人心比什么都诡诈
不顾一切
谁能看透呢？”
我们生来就不完美
心里充满自私的念头
总是只想着自己
我们的心会骗我们
让我们为自己的过错找借口
或者为自私的行为找理由
我们甚至会利用服务机会
来追求自己的利益
这真的很危险
来看个例子
箴言16:2有一节参考经文
就是撒母耳记上15:13,14
请打开你的圣经
我们来读一下这段经文
这里谈的是扫罗王
耶和华给扫罗王
一个非常清楚的指示
要他消灭亚玛力人
灭尽他们和他们的一切
无论男女老幼都要杀掉
如果我们看一下5-7节会发现
扫罗接受任务之后，执行得很不错
他完全按照耶和华给他的吩咐
消灭了亚玛力人
但我们在第9节却看到
有些事好像不太对劲
第9节说
“可是扫罗和民众放过了亚甲
［就是亚玛力人的王］
以及上好的牛羊、肥壮的家畜、公绵羊
和一切好东西，不想灭尽
至于不值钱、没人想要的东西
他们都灭尽了”
发生了什么事呢？
扫罗怀着自私的动机
利用为耶和华服务的机会去做什么呢？
让自己得荣耀、得益处
12节的经文甚至提到
扫罗去了迦密
为自己立了一座纪念碑
纪念自己在和亚玛力人交战中
取得的巨大胜利
他还把亚甲王作为俘虏，带了回来
好让人知道他彻底消灭了亚玛力人
扫罗还带回来很多肥壮的牛羊
归自己所有
让他自己变得更加富有
但耶和华当然不会被扫罗骗倒
他了解一切
他清楚看出扫罗的动机并不纯正
所以他派撒母耳先知去营地告诉扫罗
耶和华不再悦纳他，并且从他手里收回王权
耶和华弃绝了扫罗
但扫罗在听到撒母耳的话之前
还以为自己做得很好
他还假装自己非常忠诚
对耶和华非常忠心
他见到撒母耳的时候甚至说
“愿耶和华赐福给你！
耶和华的命令我已经执行了”
撒母耳直接了当地说
“没有
你在撒谎
你希望自己得到荣耀
而不是让耶和华得到荣耀”
我们从这件事可以学到什么呢？
这个记载是个发人深省的好例子
能够清楚地说明
人怀着怎样的动机真的很重要
我们看到扫罗的动机并不纯正
他没有把耶和华放在首位
正是因为他的动机不纯正
所以他不再忠于耶和华
也受到耶和华严厉的判决
那我们怎样才能避免犯下类似的大错呢？
我们怎么知道自己内心的动机
是不是纯正呢？
或者像圣经说的
我们怎么能够看透自己的内心呢？
耶和华的确帮助我们了解
自己内心的情况是怎样的
从希伯来书4:12，我们就能知道
耶和华给了我们一个很好的工具
经文说
“上帝的话语是活的，是有力量的
比任何两刃的剑更锋利
连外表和内心、关节和骨髓都能刺穿分开
甚至心里的意念和打算都能辨明”
所以，忠信睿智的奴隶总是鼓励我们
要天天阅读上帝的话语圣经
因为通过深入地研读圣经
我们就能够
“刺穿分开”自己内心坚硬的外壳
看看里面的情况到底是怎样的
并把不纯正的部分清除出去
2021年3月刊《守望台》里的这篇文章
说得非常好
文章提出的建议
不仅可以帮助我们从圣经获得力量
也能够帮助我们完成这个非常艰难的任务
就是了解自己的内心
文章建议我们在研读之前
先要祷告
求耶和华用神圣力量指引我们
研读之后
要想象自己就身处圣经记载中的那个环境
就是圣经中的那个人物
要这样认真地沉思
要了解自己内心真正的想法
这段记载对我个人有什么帮助呢？
然后把学到的运用出来
我们这样做
就不仅能够了解自己内心真正的想法
也能够采取必要的行动
来纠正自己不纯正的动机
比如说，年轻的弟兄很想多为会众服务
很想成为助理仆人或者成为长老
有这样的想法真的非常好
但我们真正的动机是什么呢？
为什么想这样做呢？
这时候
我们就可以使用《守望台》文章
提到的四个步骤
我们要先了解一下
助理仆人和长老的资格是什么
然后认真地沉思，并把学到的运用出来
我们也可以问自己这样的问题
“我为什么很渴望受到委任呢？
是想让我自己得到荣耀吗？
还是很想为大家服务呢？”
可以想象自己就是提摩太或者保罗
或者圣经中记载的其他忠心的男子
他们都愿意献出自己，遵行耶和华的旨意
全心全意为弟兄姐妹服务
这样做
他们甚至可能会被会众里面
和外面的人都看不起
我们愿意做这样的牺牲吗？
实际上，所有渴望多为耶和华服务的人
都要采取这些步骤
用耶和华的观点看待这个工作
了解他对我们的期待
并确保自己的动机和他的旨意一致
我们也许很惊讶地发现
自己怀有跟扫罗类似的动机
我们想利用为耶和华服务的机会
寻求自己的利益，抬高自己
我记得几年前
“对耶和华忠贞不渝”的大会上
有一个系列演讲
题目是《避免破坏忠贞的行为态度》
里面谈到一个长老
他留意到自己的动机有问题
另一个长老给了他一些建议
他发现自己的反应很不好
他意识到自己的动机出了问题
他怎么做呢？
他向耶和华祷告
然后他就参与会众里面
一些无人留意到的工作
比如，在没有人的时候去打扫王国聚会所
这样的工作没有任何人会注意到
但这些工作都是必要的
是我们遵行上帝的旨意必须要做的工作
他的动机得到了纠正
我们从短片里看到
后来在地下室的时候
这位长老是带头的弟兄
他作出的调整拯救了自己的生命
在大患难的时候，耶和华也任用他
照顾会众里的人
他真的为我们立下好榜样
而我们也可以这样做

titles.ko: 크리스토퍼 메이버: 자신의 동기를 점검하십시오 (잠언 16:2)
titles.en: Christopher Mavor: We Must Examine Our Motives (Prov. 16:2)
titles.cn: 克里斯托弗·梅弗：我们必须察验自己的动机（箴16:2）

title: 로널드 커잔: ‘연합하여 함께 거하십시오!’ (시 133:1)

ko.text: 여러분과 저를 포함해 약 850만 명에 달하는 여호와의 증인들이
“보라! 형제들이 연합하여 함께 거하는 것이 얼마나 좋으며 얼마나 즐거운가!”
우리는 이 조직에 속해 있는 것이 정말 기쁘고 자랑스럽습니다.
여호와께서는 우리 각자를 이 연합된 조직으로 이끄셨습니다.
정부들과 종교들이 연합되어 있지 않고 모두 분열되어 있습니다.
세상의 상태를 묘사하려면 성구의 표현을 이렇게 바꿔야 할 겁니다.
‘보라! 연합되지 않고 함께 거하는 것이 얼마나 나쁘며 얼마나 불쾌한가!’
하지만 우리가 전하는 희망의 소식은 그들의 상황을 바꿀 수 있습니다.
그러면 여호와의 조직을 그토록 다르게 만드는 것은 과연 무엇입니까?
우리가 말하는 언어와 우리가 입는 옷 때문입니다.
먼저 스바냐 3:9을 통해 우리를 연합시켜 주는 언어가 무엇인지 함께 보시겠습니다.
“내가 민족들의 언어를 순결한 언어로 [다시 말해 성경 진리로] 바꾸어서,
그들이 모두 여호와의 이름을 부르고 어깨를 나란히 하여 하느님을 섬기게 하겠다’
따라서 이 땅에서 형제 자매들과 어깨를 나란히 하여 일하는 것은 놀라운 특권입니다.
우리는 수가 늘어나고 갈수록 더 연합되고 있죠.
하지만 지상 부분만 본다면 시야가 좁은 것입니다.
어떻게 여호와의 조직의 하늘 부분과 어깨를 나란히 하여 일하고 있는지도 보아야 하죠.
예를 들어 본다면, 여호와의 능력을 의미하는 손은 그분의 조직의 하늘 부분을 움직이고 있습니다.
이것을 하늘 수레에 비할 수 있습니다.
여호와의 영이 직접 이 수레를 움직입니다.
여호와의 뜻과 그분이 원하시는 방향대로 말이죠.
그리고 바로 여기에 여호와의 조직의 지상 부분이 연결됩니다.
그래서 여호와께서 하늘 부분을 움직이시면 지상 부분도 똑같이 따라 움직이죠.
우리는 여기에 달려 있는 클립과 같습니다.
그래서 여호와께서 그분의 조직을 움직이시면 하늘에 이어 땅 부분까지 움직이고 우리도 따라가게 됩니다.
하지만 어떤 땐 여호와께서 자신의 조직을 움직이시면 우리도 흔들리다 충격을 받을 때가 있죠?
네, 우리가 아는 것처럼 에스겔은 환상에서 “바퀴야!”하고 부르는 음성을 들었습니다.
그러자 바퀴가 움직이면서 여호와의 조직의 하늘 부분이 움직이기 시작했습니다.
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 통해 우리는 여호와로부터 필요한 모든 것을 받고 있습니다.
그 덕분에 우리는 하늘 부분과 조화를 이루면서 연합해서 굳건하게 여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리고 있죠.
우리는 동일한 영적 양식을 섭취하고 동일한 성경의 표준을 따르며
전파하고 제자를 삼는 중요한 활동에 동일하게 참여합니다.
이 모든 것은 여호와의 백성이 어깨를 나란히 하여 연합하게 해 주죠.
우리는 여호와의 조직을 통해 영적으로 잘 먹고 있습니다.
중앙장로회는 「파수대」, 크고 작은 대회, 평일 집회, JW 방송을 통해 영적 양식을 공급하죠.
이 모든 것들이 우리를 하나의 백성으로 연합시킵니다.
예를 들어 JW 방송을 생각해 보면 아마 기억하시겠지만 첫 방송이 나간 것은 2014년 10월이었습니다.
처음엔 영어 하나였지만 중앙장로회의 승인을 얻어 언어 수를 늘렸습니다.
그리고 아시는 것처럼 길르앗 학교 졸업식과 연례 총회가 방송에 추가되었습니다.
사실 처음에는 전 세계의 번역자들이 매달 꼭 해야 하는 번역을 하다 보면
길르앗 학교 졸업식이나 연례 총회는 번역할 여력이 없었습니다.
그러던 중, 중앙장로회는 그 프로그램들을 월간 방송에 포함시켰죠.
지금은 162개 언어로 길르앗 졸업식의 깊은 영적 진리를 들을 수 있죠.
여러 해 동안 영어로만 즐길 수 있던 영적 양식을 많은 형제 자매들이 동일하게 즐길 수 있게 된 것입니다.
이처럼 여호와의 조직은 움직이고 있고 연합되어 있습니다.
나는 하늘과 땅이 연합된 이 조직에서 어떻게 하고 있는가?’
앞서 말한 것처럼 우리가 말하는 언어, “순결한 언어”와 우리가 입는 옷이 중요합니다.
함께 골로새서 3:14을 보시죠. 3장 14절에서는 ‘사랑을 입어야 한다’고 말합니다.
바울은 12절에서 이 옷에 무엇이 포함되는지를 알려 줍니다.
동정심 어린 부드러운 애정, 친절, 겸손, 온화, 참을성이죠.
“다른 사람에 대해 불평할 이유가 있더라도 계속 서로 참고 서로 기꺼이 용서할 것입니다.”
“여호와께서 여러분을 기꺼이 용서하신 것처럼 여러분도 그렇게 해야 합니다”라고 했죠.
그분의 아들 예수는 사랑을 포함해 하느님의 특성을 완벽히 본받으셨습니다.
그리고 예수께서는 자신의 제자들이 사랑으로 식별될 거라고 하셨죠.
따라서 우리 각자는 어떻게 연합에 기여할 수 있을까요?
방금 읽은 것처럼 우린 동정심, 친절, 겸손, 온화, 참을성, 용서와 같은 경건한 특성들을 길러야 합니다.
이런 특성들은 우릴 결속시켜 주고 계속 연합을 유지할 수 있게 해 줍니다.
아까 말씀드린 예를 다시 생각해 보면, 어깨를 나란히 해서 일하다가 문제가 생길 수 있죠.
함께 일하다 보면 여기 이 클립처럼 우리의 모양이 일그러질 수 있습니다.
방금 말한 특성들, 용서, 동정심, 양보하는 태도가 필요하죠.
그리고 우리 조직을 더 많은 책임을 맡기 위해 사다리를 올라가야 하는 곳으로 보지 말아야 합니다.
우리는 모두 각자의 자리에서 연합해서 함께 일해야 합니다.
제가 클립에 대해 조사를 좀 해 봤는데요,
물론 클립은 모양과 크기나 색깔이 다양하지만 주된 용도가 무엇일까요?
종이를 한데 모아 끼워 두는 것이죠.
가정에서, 회중에서, 여기 베델에서, 여호와의 조직의 어디에서든 연합시켜 주는 역할을 해야 합니다.
흥미롭게도 클립을 설계할 때는 “항복 응력”이라는 것을 고려하는데,
항복 응력이란 “철사의 모양을 영구적으로 변형시키는 데 필요한 힘”입니다.
그 힘이 너무 강하면 클립을 벌려서 종이를 한데 끼우기가 어려울 겁니다.
반대로 항복 응력이 너무 약하면 힘이 없어서 종이를 제대로 끼워 둘 수가 없죠.
이와 비슷하게 우리는 때때로 확고한 태도를 나타내야 할 때가 있습니다.
하지만 우리는 그리스도인 특성을 나타내어 양보하고 평화를 이루어야 합니다.
바울이 고린도 전서 1:10에서 말한 것도 그 점인데요.
“완전한 연합의 띠”를 갖는다는 건 연합되고 분열되지 않는다는 것이죠?
“형제 여러분, 우리 주 예수 그리스도의 이름으로 여러분에게 권고합니다.
모두 일치되게 말하고 여러분 가운데 분열이 없게 하여
같은 정신과 같은 생각으로 온전히 연합하십시오.”
따라서 사탄 마귀가 분열을 일으켜 우리를 여호와에게서
그리고 그분의 조직의 하늘 부분과 지상 부분에서 멀어지게 하도록 허용하지 마십시오.
우리는 그리스도인 특성들인 새 인간성을 입지 않아서 분열을 일으키는 사람이 되기를 결코 원하지 않습니다.
앞서 보신 클립처럼 우리가 모양이 일그러질 때가 있다면 고린도 후서 13:11의 바울의 말대로
그리고 우리 모두는 자기를 낮춘 정신으로 양보하고
참을성을 보임으로 ‘남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여겨야' 합니다.
우리가 그렇게 한다면 하늘 부분과 지상 부분으로 이루어진 여호와의 조직과 연합하게 됩니다.
‘형제 자매들이 연합하여 함께 거하는 것은 정말 좋고 정말 즐거운 일입니다!’

en.text: When we think about it,
eight and a half million Jehovah’s Witnesses,
like you and me,
are in the process of fulfilling
our text for today.
And that is taken from Psalm 133:1.
It says:
“Look! How good and how pleasant it is
for brothers to dwell together in unity!”
So we are so privileged and proud to be part of this organization.
Jehovah has drawn each one of us
to be part of this unified organization.
Now, in contrast, what do we see in the world?
Their governments and their religions are all divided.
It’s disunited.
So maybe rephrasing the scripture,
this is what they’re experiencing now:
‘Look! How bad and how unpleasant it is
to dwell together in disunity!’
It’s a sad reality,
but our hope that we share with them
could change that very quickly.
So, what is it that makes Jehovah’s organization (our organization)
so different, so special?
Two things:
It’s the language we speak
as well as the clothes we wear.
What do we mean by that?
Well, let’s go to Zephaniah 3:9
to see the language that we have and are unified with.
At Zephaniah 3:9, it reads:
“[And] I will change the language of the peoples
“to a pure language [and we know that is a Scriptural truth],
“so that all of them may call on the name of Jehovah,
to serve him shoulder to shoulder”
—or, as the footnote says, “worship him in unity.”
So the privilege for us to work shoulder to shoulder
with all those on earth is amazing!
And we see how we’re growing and how much more united we are becoming.
But, really, if we’re just looking at the earthly part,
we’re short-sighted.
We need to look at the heavenly part as well
and how we’re united with Jehovah’s heavenly organization
shoulder to shoulder.
In fact, just to illustrate this,
we know that Jehovah’s hand of applied power
is steering his heavenly organization, right?
So we have this magnet here that could be the celestial chariot.
Jehovah’s spirit directly has that chariot move
based on what he wants and what he directs with his holy spirit.
And connected to that is
the earthly part of his organization.
And as Jehovah moves the heavenly part,
the earthly part is directly connected with it.
Well, where do we fit in?
Well, we can be likened to these
paper clips.
So as Jehovah moves his organization,
what happens from heaven down to the earth?
We are following right along with it.
But sometimes —isn’t it true?—
as Jehovah moves his organization,
there’s a little bit of a whiplash happening with all of us.
So we appreciate when Ezekiel
in his vision heard, “Wheelwork!”
That’s when the wheels went to work,
and that’s when Jehovah’s heavenly organization was on the move.
But we appreciate that we need to be on the move as well.
And by means of “the faithful and discreet slave,”
we are getting from Jehovah everything we need
to be unified, to be strong,
to worship Jehovah in pure worship
in harmony with his heavenly organization.
So we feed on the same spiritual food,
we hold to the same Scriptural standards of conduct,
and we share in the same vital work of preaching
and disciple-making work.
All of this unites Jehovah’s people
shoulder to shoulder.
Now, through Jehovah’s organization,
we have been fed so well by the Governing Body
through our Watchtower,  through conventions,
assemblies, midweek meetings, through JW Broadcasting®.
All of these have served to unite us as a people.
In fact, you might remember, just talking about JW Broadcasting,
that it was October of 2014
when the first broadcast aired, and that was with Brother Lett.
And we know that was only in one language.
And now what do we have?
With the approval of the Governing Body,
they have increased the languages starting first in English.
Now, we know that the Gilead graduation has been added
and the annual meeting has been added
to the broadcast throughout the year.
Well, originally, the translators around the world
were doing their best to keep up with all
the other translation that was needed,
and they were not able to do the Gilead graduation or the annual meeting.
But interestingly, the Governing Body now has put those on as monthly broadcasts.
What has that done for the organization?
It has united us.
In 2016, there were only 34 languages
able to translate the Gilead graduation.
Now 162 languages
have that deep spiritual truth.
And the same is true with the annual meeting.
Now thousands of our brothers and sisters have that same spiritual food,
that feeding program that we have been enjoying for many years.
So Jehovah’s organization is on the move.
It is united.
But the question is:
What about me?
Where do I fit in
to this unification of heaven and earth?
It really comes down to, again,
the language that we speak —the “pure language”—
as well as the clothing that we wear.
What do I mean by that?
Let’s go to Colossians chapter 3,
and notice verse 14.
Colossians 3:14 says
that we should “clothe [ourselves] with love.”
That’s the clothing.
And what does that help us with?
“For it is a perfect bond of union.”
Paul goes on to say in verse 12 what this clothing entails.
It’s “tender affections of compassion, kindness,
humility, mildness, and patience.”
What it means, if we’re wearing this,
is that we will continue to “[put] up with one another,
“[forgiving] one another freely
“even if anyone has a cause for complaint against another.
“Just as Jehovah freely forgave you,
you must also do the same.”
So love is the “perfect bond of union.”
Unity is based on love.
We worship Jehovah.
“God is love.”
His Son, Jesus, perfectly represented him,
mirrored every aspect of Him with love.
And Jesus said that his disciples would be identified with love.
So in what ways can we be a unifying factor?
Well, as we just read, we need to cultivate those godly qualities
of compassion, kindness, humility,
mildness, patience, forgiveness.
These are the qualities that hold us together
and keep us together unitedly.
Now, when we think about that little illustration I used there,
working shoulder to shoulder could have its problems.
Sometimes we could be bent out of shape
when we are working shoulder to shoulder.
Well, what do we need to keep in mind?
Again, it’s those qualities
of forgiveness, compassion, being yielding,
and not looking at our organization
as a way to climb some sort of ladder to get more responsibility.
It’s everyone working in their place, working together unitedly.
When we think about paper clips (I did a little research on this),
paper clips come, of course, in different shapes, sizes, and colors.
But what’s the purpose of a paper clip?
Isn’t it to hold pieces of paper together?
Isn’t that the same with you and me?
The purpose that we have as Jehovah’s Witnesses
is to unite, to be a uniting factor,
in our family, in the congregation,
here at Bethel, or in any aspect of our organization.
And it’s interesting that the engineers of paper clips
actually have something that is called “yield stress,”
or “the amount of stress needed to permanently reshape the wire.”
If it has too much stress,
that means it’ll be hard to open and unite the paper.
If it has too low of a yield stress, then it becomes wimpy,
and it won’t hold anything together.
So we can see where you and I
need to have some rigidness in us.
We need to stand firm,
but we need to have those Christian qualities
to be yielding and to be peaceable.
And that’s what Paul was saying at 1 Corinthians 1:10,
if you would turn there with me.
Having this “perfect bond of union”
means having unity but not divisions and disunity.
First Corinthians 1:10 reads:
“Now I urge you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
“that you should all speak in agreement
“and that there should be no divisions among you,
“but that you may be completely united in the same mind
and in the same line of thought.”
So, again, don’t allow a place for Satan the Devil to cause divisions,
to distance us from Jehovah and from his organization
both in heaven and on earth.
And we never want to be one who will be a disuniting factor
by not putting on that new personality, those Christian qualities.
And if we do get bent out of shape from time to time,
like our little paper clip here,
Paul says at 2 Corinthians 13:11
that we should “continue to . . . be readjusted.”
And we need to have that same lowliness of mind,
‘considering others as superior to us’
by being yielding and being patient.
And if we do this, we are aligning ourselves
with Jehovah’s organization, both in heaven and on earth.
Well, there is our theme scripture for today.
We will be happy,
because ‘how good it is and how pleasant it is
to dwell together in unity!’

cn.text: 每当我们想到
850万个耶和华见证人
包括你和我
正在应验今天经文的预言
都会感到很振奋
那就让我们来看一下今天的经文
“看哪！弟兄团结同住
多么美善，多么可喜！”
我们非常荣幸和自豪能属于这个组织
耶和华吸引我们每个人
成为这个团结的国际大家庭的一员
相比之下
世界的情况是怎样的呢？
世上的政府和宗教四分五裂
完全不团结
如果我们把刚才的经文改一下
就是世人现在的情况
“看哪！一群人不团结地住在一起
多么糟糕，多么痛苦！”
事实的确如此
但我们跟他们分享的希望
可以改变他们的处境
那么是什么让耶和华的组织
我们的组织
与众不同、独一无二呢？
两方面
就是我们说的语言
还有我们穿的衣服
这是什么意思呢？
让我们来看一下西番雅书3:9
看看把我们团结在一起的“语言”
指的是什么
西番雅书3:9
经文说
“我要教导所有民族的人改说纯洁的语言
（也就是圣经真理）
让他们都可以呼求耶和华的名
并肩敬奉他”
这里的脚注说的是
“团结一致地崇拜他”
我们有幸跟全球的弟兄姐妹并肩工作
真的是很大的福分！
我们看到崇拜耶和华的人越来越多
而且也越来越团结
但实际上
如果我们只看到地上的部分
就没有看到全貌
我们也要看到天上的部分
也就是我们要跟耶和华组织的天上部分
肩并肩，团结一致
关于这一点
我们可以用一个比喻
我们知道耶和华的手在操控天上的战车
我们可以把战车比作这块磁铁
耶和华会用他的神圣力量
以他想要的方式直接指挥战车移动
这个战车就是耶和华组织的天上部分
与之相连的
就是他组织的地上部分
耶和华移动组织的天上部分时
地上的部分也会同步并进
在这个比喻中
我们在什么位置呢？
我们就好比这些
回形针（回纹针）
当耶和华的手指挥战车移动
会发生什么情况呢？
我们也会跟着移动
不过大家感觉到了吗？
有时耶和华的组织移动的时候
我们会跟着前后摇晃
所以，这让我们想到
以西结在异象中听到“旋转的轮子啊！”
这句话的时候
他就知道耶和华组织的天上部分正在行动
这就意味着
我们也要与之同步并进
耶和华通过“忠信睿智的奴隶”
为我们提供所需的一切
让我们变得更团结、更坚强
这样就能跟耶和华组织的天上部分
团结一致地支持正确崇拜
弟兄姐妹享用同样的滋养信心的食物
谨守同样的圣经标准
传讲同样的拯救信息
教导人做基督的门徒
所有这些都让我们紧紧地团结在一起
并肩工作
今天，忠信睿智的奴隶
为我们提供丰盛的食物
包括《守望台》杂志、周中聚会、大会
还有JW电视
不断滋养我们的信心
所有这些都帮助我们团结一心
举个例子，大家可能还记得
第一期JW电视的播出时间
是在2014年10月
莱特弟兄是那一期的主持人
当时还只有英语一种语言
现在又怎样了呢？
在中央长老团的指引下
我们又增加了许许多多的语言
首先只有英语
但现在我们可以在JW电视上以不同的语言
看到每期的基列毕业典礼和年会的节目
刚开始的时候
世界各地的翻译员
都要付出很大的努力翻译各种资料
这样就没有精力
翻译基列毕业典礼和年会的节目了
但从近几年开始
中央长老团批准
把这些节目作为每月节目播出
这对组织有什么影响呢？
这促进了我们的团结
2016年，基列和年会的节目
只被翻译成34种语言
但现在，我们可以用162种语言
享受这些节目
这样，全球的弟兄姐妹
都能通过这些打动人心的节目
接受来自耶和华的教导
所以，耶和华的组织正在不断前进
而且越来越团结
但问题是
我自己又怎样呢？
我在耶和华的宇宙组织里
处于怎样的位置呢？
答案就在于
我们所讲的语言
“纯洁的语言”
以及我们穿的衣服
“衣服”指的是什么呢？
让我们看一下歌罗西书第3章
请留意第14节
歌罗西书3:14
经文说
我们应该“穿上爱”
这就是衣服
爱有怎样的作用呢？
“爱能完美地维系团结”
保罗在第12节继续说这衣服是怎样的
它是“温暖的怜恤之情
仁慈、谦卑、温和、耐心”
这意味着，如果我们穿上这件“衣服”
我们会“继续彼此包容，彼此甘心宽恕”
即使有理由对人不满
就像耶和华甘心宽恕我们一样
我们也要甘心宽恕别人
是的，“爱能完美地维系团结”
爱是团结的基础
我们崇拜耶和华
耶和华就是爱
他的儿子耶稣基督完美地反映了
耶和华的特质，尤其是爱
耶稣说，他的门徒会以爱心作为标志
那么我们每个人可以怎样维系团结呢？
就像刚才我们读到的经文说的那样
我们需要培养怜恤之情
仁慈、谦卑、温和、耐心、宽恕等特质
这些特质让我们团结在一起
并肩崇拜耶和华
我们再来用回形针的比喻说明这一点
我们跟弟兄姐妹并肩工作时
可能会产生问题
我们有时
会像回形针一样弯曲变形
那么，我们需要记住什么呢？
还是这些特质
宽恕、怜恤之情
以及乐意让步
我们不会仿效世人的做法
利用这个组织向上爬
追求个人的利益
而会谨守各自的岗位
并肩服务，团结一致
关于回形针，我还做了一点研究
回形针有不同的形状、大小和颜色
但回形针的用途是什么？
就是把纸张夹在一起
你和我也是一样
我们作为耶和华见证人
也会起到团结的作用
我们在家里，在会众里
在伯特利或者其他地方
都能成为团结的纽带
有意思的是
回形针在设计的时候需要遵循一个物理法则
叫做“屈服应力”
也就是重塑铁丝形状所需的应力
如果闭合太紧
就很难把它打开
把纸张夹在一起
如果太松，就会失去作用
不能把任何东西夹在一起
通过这个例子我们学到
我们有时的确需要一些硬度
我们需要坚定不移
但同时
我们也需要乐意让步、促进团结
这就是保罗在哥林多前书1:10所说的
请大家跟我一起翻开
“完美地维系团结”
意味着同心同德而不是彼此分裂
下面我们来看一下哥林多前书1:10
经文说
“弟兄们，我凭着我们主耶稣基督的名
劝你们大家说话要一致
不可分裂
好让你们的思想意念也都一致
完全团结”
所以，我们不要让魔鬼撒但有机可乘
制造分裂
使我们远离耶和华和他在天上和地上的组织
如果我们不穿上美好的基督徒特质
就可能被撒但利用，引起分裂
我们绝不想变成这样
如果有时我们真的像回形针一样弯曲变形了
就要像保罗在
哥林多后书13:11说的那样
我们应该“继续……接受纠正”
保持耐心，乐意让步，表现谦卑
看别人比自己优秀
如果我们这样做
就是在跟耶和华天上地上的组织同步并进
所以，今天的主题经文真的给我们很大鼓励
我们能团结地生活在一起
这多么美善，多么可喜！

title: 진화의 산물인가? 인체의 산소 운반

ko.text: 우리가 숨을 쉴 때마다 생명에 꼭 필요한 산소를 들이마십니다.
산소가 있어야 먹은 음식을 에너지로 바꿀 수 있기 때문에
몸 전체에 있는 수많은 세포로 어떻게 전달됩니까?
그런 다음 적혈구라는 세포가 몸의 곳곳으로 산소를 운반합니다.
산소를 꼭 필요한 때에 꼭 필요한 곳으로 전달할 수 있습니다.
양면의 가운데가 오목한 원반 모양을 하고 있기 때문에
구부러지거나 접혀져서 아무리 비좁은 혈관도 통과할 수 있습니다.
적혈구는 다른 세포들이 생존하는 데 꼭 필요한
중요한 성분을 더 많이 수용할 수 있습니다.
헤모글로빈 분자는 적혈구가 폐를 지나갈 때
가능한 많은 양의 산소를 흡수하는 작은 기계와 같습니다.
산소 분자와 결합할 수 있는 네 개의 지점이 있습니다.
하나의 산소 분자가 그러한 지점에 결합하면 놀라운 일이 벌어집니다.
꼭꼭 접혀 있던 헤모글로빈의 구조가 변하면서
최대 세 개의 산소 분자를 더 흡수할 수 있게 되는 것입니다.
언제 어디로 산소를 운반해야 하는지 어떻게 압니까?
몸의 한 부분을 활발하게 움직이면 더 많은 산소를 쓰게 됩니다.
혈액이 몸을 순환하면서 산소가 필요한 조직들을 지나게 되는데,
산소와 헤모글로빈이 결합한 부분에 변화가 생깁니다.
대부분 혈장이 화학적으로 변화시킨 후 운반해 갑니다.
하지만 일부 이산화탄소는 헤모글로빈과 결합해 폐로 돌아갑니다.
다시 숨을 들이쉬면 산소가 새로 공급되어 몸 전체로 운반됩니다.
혈관을 타고 몸 구석구석을 끊임없이 돌아다니는 적혈구는
매초 최대 200만 개의 새로운 적혈구를 계속 생산합니다.
그리고 간은 수명을 다한 적혈구를 분해하여
수많은 적혈구를 사용하는 인체의 산소 운반 체계는 진화된 것입니까,

en.text: Every day, we take around 25,000 breaths of air.
And each breath contains a gas essential for life
—oxygen.
We need a steady supply of oxygen
because our body cells use it to produce energy from the food we eat.
But how does oxygen get from your lungs
to the trillions of individual cells throughout your body?
When you take a breath,
oxygen passes from your lungs
into your bloodstream,
where it’s transported
by the workhorses of oxygen transport
—red blood cells.
Their unique shape and composition
make these cells perfectly suited
to deliver oxygen precisely where and when it’s needed.
Each one is a tiny disk
with its center curved inward on both sides.
This shape lets the cells bend and fold themselves
so that they can squeeze through even the narrowest blood vessels.
Red blood cells are unusual in other ways.
They don’t have a nucleus
or the specialized structures that other cells need to survive.
For this reason,
red blood cells don’t use up any of the oxygen they transport.
And their unique makeup
leaves more room for their most important component
—hemoglobin.
Each red blood cell contains
over 250 million hemoglobin molecules.
Hemoglobin molecules work like tiny machines
absorbing as much oxygen as possible
when red blood cells pass through the lungs.
Each hemoglobin molecule has four locations
where an oxygen molecule can attach.
As soon as an oxygen molecule binds to one of those locations,
something remarkable happens:
The tightly folded structure of the hemoglobin changes,
making it possible for as many as three more oxygen molecules
to be absorbed.
But how does the hemoglobin
know when and where to deliver the oxygen?
When a part of the body is exerted,
it uses more oxygen.
So as blood travels through your body,
it passes by tissues that need oxygen
and that release carbon dioxide
as waste into the blood.
In the presence of carbon dioxide,
hemoglobin’s bond to oxygen changes.
The oxygen molecules that have been riding along
can then break free to be absorbed by other body cells.
As for the carbon dioxide that needs to be removed,
most of it is chemically changed
and carried by the blood’s plasma.
But some also attaches to the hemoglobin molecules
and returns to the lungs,
where, along with the carbon dioxide unloaded from plasma,
it can be exhaled
and where the very next breath
brings in a fresh supply of oxygen
ready for transport.
Constantly zipping through your body’s thousands of miles of blood vessels,
red blood cells wear out after only about four months.
But healthy bone marrow continuously produces
up to two million new red blood cells every second as replacement cells.
And the liver breaks down the worn-out cells
and recycles the iron found in the hemoglobin molecules.
It’s an amazing system
of delivery, pickup, and disposal.
What do you think?
Did the oxygen transport system in our bodies,
with its trillions of red blood cells, simply evolve?
Or was it designed?

cn.text: 我们每一天都会呼吸大约2万5000次
每一口气里都含有维持生命所需的氧气
我们需要不断吸入氧气
这样细胞才能够将我们吃进去的食物转换为能量
但氧气怎样从肺部被运送到身体的亿万个细胞呢？
我们每吸一口气
氧气就会从肺部进入到血管里
接着就有搬运工负责运送氧气
它们就是红细胞（红血球）
红细胞的形状和构造非常特殊
让它们能够及时地将氧气运输到有需要的地方
红细胞的形状就像中间凹陷的小圆盘
这样的形状让红细胞可以灵活地弯曲
就连最细的血管也能通过
红细胞还有一个独特的地方
它们没有细胞核，也没有其他细胞器
因此红细胞不会消耗掉它们所运输的氧气
因为这样的结构
它们有更多空间可以容纳血红蛋白
它是运送氧气的关键部分
每个红细胞有超过2亿5000万个血红蛋白分子
因为有血红蛋白的关系
当红细胞经过肺部就可以接收更多的氧气
血红蛋白有4个点可以跟氧气结合
只要有一个氧分子跟血红蛋白结合
奇妙的事情就会发生
血红蛋白原本紧密的结构会改变
让它更容易跟其他3个氧分子结合
不过血红蛋白要怎么知道要在何时何处释放氧气呢？
当身体某个部位的活动量增加时
它需要的氧气也会更多
这时，需要氧气的身体组织
会把二氧化碳排放到流经的血液当中
遇到二氧化碳，血红蛋白对氧的亲和力会改变
原本附着在血红蛋白上的氧分子会被释放
然后被其他细胞吸收
至于二氧化碳，大部分会发生化学改变
被血浆带走
但有些二氧化碳会跟血红蛋白分子结合回到肺部
跟着血浆带回来的二氧化碳一起被排出去
我们再次吸气的时候
氧气又进入肺部，供红细胞运输
红细胞在身体长长的血管里不断流动穿梭
但它的生命周期只有大约4个月
不过健康的骨髓每秒会制造200万新的红细胞
肝脏则会把已经衰老的红细胞分解
然后把血红蛋白中的铁回收再利用
运输氧气、排放废物
这整个过程十分精妙
你认为呢？
血管内亿万红细胞运输氧气的机制是进化而来的
还是经过设计的呢？
