title: 로버트 시렌코: 징계는 여호와에게서 옵니다 (고린도 전서 5:11)

ko.text: 오늘은 제명 처분 마련을 생각해 보겠습니다.
우선 제명 처분의 성경적인 근거를 읽어 보죠.
그 점이 고린도 전서 5장에 나오는데요, 함께 성경을 펴서 5:9부터 읽어 보겠습니다.
“나는 편지에서 여러분에게 성적 부도덕을 저지르는 자들과 더는 어울리지 말라고 썼습니다.
그 말은 이 세상의 성적 부도덕을 저지르는 자들이나 탐욕스러운 자들이나 강탈하는 자들이나
우상 숭배자들과 전혀 어울리지 말라는 뜻이 아닙니다.
그렇게 하려면 여러분이 아예 세상 밖으로 나가야 할 것입니다.”
그리스도인들은 증인이 아닌 사람들을 피해 다니지 않습니다.
이웃, 직장 동료, 학교 친구들과 일상적인 접촉을 하고 그들에게 증거도 합니다.
부도덕한 생활을 하는 사람들도 있지만 그들을 완전히 피할 순 없죠.
하지만 형제가 그렇게 산다면 얘기가 달라집니다.
“형제라고 하는 사람이 성적 부도덕을 저지르는 자이거나 탐욕스러운 자이거나 우상 숭배자이거나 욕하는 자이거나
술 취하는 자이거나 강탈하는 자이거든 더는 어울리지 말고 그런 사람과는 함께 먹지도 말라는 것입니다.”
이 영감받은 교훈이 제안이 아니라 명령의 형태로 되어 있다는 것에 유의하십시오.
이 점이 “제명 처분이 사랑의 마련인 이유”라는 2015년 4월 15일호 「파수대」 기사에 이렇게 잘 설명되어 있습니다.
자신의 종들이 달하기를 바라시는 거룩함의 표준을 가지고 계십니다.
예를 들어 여호와께서는 우리가 성적 부도덕, 우상 숭배, 도둑질, 강탈, 살인,
영매술과 같은 심각한 죄를 저지르지 않을 것을 요구하십니다.
여호와의 깨끗한 표준이 합리적이고 우리에게 보호가 된다는 점에 동의하지 않으십니까?
평화롭고 행실이 바른 신뢰할 만한 사람들과 함께하는 삶을 좋아하지 않을 사람이 누가 있겠습니까?
우리는 영적 형제 자매들과 함께할 때 그런 삶을 누립니다.
하느님께 헌신할 때 그분의 말씀에 나오는 지침에 따라 살겠다고 우리 모두가 약속했기 때문입니다.”
그런데 침례받은 그리스도인이 심각한 죄를 저지르면 어떠합니까?
성적 부도덕, 우상 숭배, 도둑질, 강탈, 살인, 영매술과 같은 죄를 저지르면 회중에서 제명됩니까?
같은 「파수대」 기사에 따르면 두 가지 요건이 모두 갖춰질 경우에만
여호와의 증인의 한 사람을 제명하게 됩니다.
‘첫 번째는 침례받은 증인이 심각한 죄를 짓는 것이고, 두 번째는 그가 자신의 죄를 회개하지 않는 것이죠.’
따라서 어떤 사람이 죄를 짓고 회개하지 않을 때에만 제명됩니다.
그리고 장로들이 그가 진정으로 회개했다고 확신하기 전까지는 회중으로 복귀되지 않습니다.
사랑하는 친구나 가족이 제명되었을 때 정말 힘들 수 있죠.
그런 경우, 우리는 문제를 다루는 장로들의 결정을 받아들일 것입니까?
우리는 장로들이 상황을 더 객관적으로 볼 수 있다는 점을 인정해야 합니다.
결정하기 전에 많이 기도하고 죄를 지은 사람을 회복시키기 위해 최선을 다합니다.
하지만 그가 회개하지 않는다면 장로들은 회중을 보호해야 합니다.
그런 경우라도 복귀하는 데 필요한 절차를 친절하고 분명하게 설명해 주고,
주기적으로 제명된 사람을 방문해서 여호와께 돌아오는 방법을 일깨워 줍니다.
죄를 지은 사람이 여호와에게서 오는 징계로부터 유익을 얻도록 돕는 것입니다.
징계가 여호와에게서 오는 것임을 깨닫는 것이 중요하죠.
“또 여러분은 아들에게 하듯이 여러분에게 하신 이러한 권고를 완전히 잊어버렸습니다.
‘내 아들아, 여호와로부터 오는 징계를 가볍게 여기지 말고 그분에게 시정을 받더라도 포기하지 마라.
사실 그분은 아들로 받아들이는 모든 사람을 채찍질하신다.’”
“사실, 어떤 징계도 당시에는 기뻐 보이지 않고 고통스럽지만,
나중에는 그것으로 훈련받은 사람들에게 평화를 이루는 열매인 의를 가져다줍니다.”
제명 처분이라는 징계로 훈련받은 사람들은 그 마련을 통해 영적으로 회복하도록 도움을 받았습니다.
따라서 제명된 사람에게 어떻게 하는 것이 가장 좋을까요?
고린도 전서 5:11에서 이미 읽어 본 것처럼 그런 사람과는 “더는 어울리지 말고 …
그리고 그런 사람에 관해 사도 요한은 요한 2서 10절에서
“그를 집에 받아들이지도 말고 그에게 인사하지도 마십시오”라고 했죠.
이런 상황에서 우리가 제명된 사람이 아니라 하느님께 충성하는지가 드러납니다.
하느님께서는 우리가 제명된 사람과 어울리지 말라는 그분의 명령을 지키는지 보고 계십니다.
일부 여호와의 백성은 이 마련이 너무 가혹하고
제명된 친구나 가족과 계속 연락하는 것이 친절한 일이라고 생각할지 모르죠.
그렇게 하면 우리의 마음이 편해질 수는 있지만 그것은 제명된 사람에게 할 수 있는 최악의 행동일 것입니다.
예수께선 마태복음 11:19에서 “지혜는 그 결과로 의롭다는 것이 증명된다”고 하셨죠.
가족이 제명된 사람과 어울리지 말라는 여호와의 명령에
확고하고 충성스럽게 고착해서 훌륭한 결과를 거둔 예를 많이 찾아볼 수 있습니다.
한 아버지는 자신의 아들이 나쁜 행동을 하기 시작했을 때
그의 생활 방식 때문에 두 사람 사이가 단절되었다고 말했습니다.
아버지는 그렇게 단절된 것이 여호와 때문이 아니라 아들 때문이란 걸 인식한 것이죠.
10년쯤 뒤에 아들은 잘못된 생활을 정리하고 회중으로 돌아왔습니다.
“제명되고 나니 내 생활 방식이 초래한 결과를 뼈저리게 느끼게 되더군요.
여호와의 표준에 따라 살아가는 데 도움이 되지요.
고통스럽기는 해도 장기적으로 좋은 결과를 가져옵니다.
내가 나쁜 행실을 관용했다면 그 아이는 결코 회복되지 못했을 겁니다.’
‘제명된 여동생과 모든 교제를 단절한다는 것은 하느님의 마련에 대한 우리의 충성에 시험이 되었어요.
이 일로 여호와의 길이 최상의 길이라는 확신을 나타낼 기회가 생겼죠.’
복귀된 여동생은 후에 언니에게 이렇게 말했습니다.
“만일 언니가, 내가 제명된 것을 대수롭지 않게 여겼더라면, 나는 그렇게 빨리 복귀하려는 조처를 취하지 않았을 거예요.
사랑하는 가족들 그리고 회중과의 긴밀한 접촉으로부터 완전히 단절되자 회개하고 싶은 열망이 생겼죠.
내 행동이 얼마나 나빴는지, 여호와께 등을 돌린 것이 얼마나 심각한 일이었는지 깨닫게 되었어요.”
제명된 친구나 가족과 어울리지 말라는 하느님의 명령을 어기고 싶은 유혹을 받는다면
앞서 언급한 기사는 또한 이렇게 말합니다.
회중에 더 이상 속하지 않게 되면 그는 자신이 잃은 것이 무엇인지 깨닫게 될지 모릅니다. …
죄짓는 행로로 인한 쓰디쓴 결과를 경험하고 여호와와 그분의 백성과 좋은 관계를 누리던 행복한 …
추억을 떠올리면 정신을 차리게 될 수 있습니다.”
제명된 사람과 전혀 어울리지 말라고 기록하게 하신 데는 그분의 큰 지혜가 담겨 있습니다.

en.text: Well, let’s talk
about the disfellowshipping arrangement.
To begin, it would be good to read
the Scriptural basis for disfellowshipping.
It is found in 1 Corinthians chapter 5,
so if you would like to open
your Bibles there,
we will start reading with verse 9
of 1 Corinthians 5.
It says (and this is the apostle Paul writing under inspiration):
“In my letter I wrote you to stop keeping company
“with sexually immoral people,
“not meaning entirely
“with the sexually immoral people of this world
“or the greedy people or extortioners or idolaters.
Otherwise, you would actually have to get out of the world.”
Well, Christians do not hold themselves aloof from non-Witnesses.
We have normal contacts with neighbors,
workmates, schoolmates, and others, and we witness to them.
Even if some of them are living immoral lives,
we cannot avoid them completely.
It is different, though, with a brother who lives like that.
Verse 11 continues:
“But now I am writing you to stop keeping company
“with anyone called a brother who is sexually immoral
“or a greedy person or an idolater
“or a reviler or a drunkard or an extortioner,
not even eating with such a man.”
And so at the end of verse 13,
he adds: “Remove the wicked person
from among yourselves.”
Notice that this inspired instruction
is worded as a command, not a suggestion.
This matter was nicely explained in the article
“Why Disfellowshipping Is a Loving Provision”
in the April 15, 2015, issue of The Watchtower.
It said: “Although Jehovah does not demand perfection from us,
“he does have a standard of holiness that he expects his servants to meet.
“For example, Jehovah insists that we avoid such serious sins
“as sexual immorality, idolatry, thievery,
“extortion, murder, and spiritism.
“Would you not agree that Jehovah’s clean standards
“are reasonable and that they serve to protect us?
“Who does not prefer to live among peaceful, decent people who can be trusted?
“We find such an environment among our spiritual brothers and sisters,
“thanks to the promise we make at the time of our dedication to God
to live in harmony with the guidelines found in his Word.”
But now, what if a baptized Christian
commits a serious sin?
Does the congregation
disfellowship people because they commit sexual immorality,
idolatry, thievery, extortion,
murder, spiritism, or something else?
Well, there’s more to it than that.
And the same article explains
that two factors must coincide
that result in the disfellowshipping of one of Jehovah’s Witnesses:
“First, a baptized Witness commits a serious sin.
Second, he does not repent of his sin.”
So individuals are disfellowshipped
only when they are unrepentant of the sins they have committed,
and they cannot be reinstated into the congregation
until the elders are convinced
that they are genuinely repentant.
Well, this presents a challenge to each of us
when it is a beloved friend or relative who is disfellowshipped.
Will we be submissive and yield
to the judgment of the elders who handle the matter?
We should accept the fact that they are in a position
to be more objective than we are.
The elders pray hard about these decisions,
knowing that “they will render an account” to God,
and that’s why they make every effort to recover the erring one if possible.
But if that fails,
they must protect the congregation and keep it morally clean.
But even then, they kindly and clearly explain
the steps needed to be reinstated.
And they may periodically visit the disfellowshipped person
to remind him or her of the way back to Jehovah.
Now, if we yield to and support the elders’ judgment,
we will actually be helping a wrongdoer to benefit
from the discipline as coming from Jehovah.
And that’s so important for them to realize.
Look at Hebrews chapter 12.
Hebrews 12 starting with verse 5
—it says: “And you have entirely forgotten
“the exhortation that addresses you as sons:
“‘My son, do not belittle the discipline from Jehovah,
“‘nor give up when you are corrected by him;
“‘for those whom Jehovah loves he disciplines,
in fact, he scourges everyone whom he receives as a son.’”
And then verse 11:
“True, no discipline seems for the present to be joyous, but it is painful;
“yet afterward, it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness
to those who have been trained by it.”
So for disfellowshipped ones who have been trained by the discipline,
it has helped them to become spiritually restored.
So, what is the very best thing we can do for those who are disfellowshipped?
We already read it at 1 Corinthians 5:11:
“Stop keeping company with [them] . . . ,
not even eating with [them].”
And speaking of the same sort of person,
the apostle John wrote at 2 John 10:
“Do not receive him into your homes or say a greeting to him.”
Now, our loyalty is on the line,
not to the disfellowshipped person, but to God,
who is watching to see whether we will abide by his command
not to have contact with those who are disfellowshipped.
Some of Jehovah’s people may think this is too drastic
and that their keeping in contact
with the disfellowshipped friend or relative is a kindness.
But they could not be more wrong about that.
You see, it may salve their own feelings,
but they would be doing the worst possible thing
for the disfellowshipped person.
And Jesus did point out at Matthew 11:19:
“Wisdom is proved righteous by its results.”
We can share with you many fine examples
of the good that has resulted when a family firmly and loyally
upholds Jehovah’s decree not to associate
with disfellowshipped ones.
One father said that when his son began behaving
in a way that was unacceptable,
his lifestyle had put up a barrier between them.
Now, note that the father recognized that it was his son
who had created the barrier, not Jehovah.
After some ten years, the young man cleaned up his life
and returned to the congregation, and he admitted:
“Being disfellowshipped brought me face-to-face
“with the consequences of my lifestyle.
I needed that sort of discipline.”
His father added: “Disfellowshipping is an arrangement that we need,
“one that helps us live according to Jehovah’s standards.
“In the long run, despite the pain, it brings good results.
Had I been tolerant of my son’s bad conduct, he would never have recovered.”
In another case, a sister admitted: “Cutting ourselves off completely
“from all association with [my disfellowshipped sister] . . .
“tested our loyalty to [God’s] arrangement.
“It gave [us] opportunity to show
that we really believe that Jehovah’s way is best.”
And her reinstated sister later told her:
“If you had viewed the disfellowshipping lightly,
“I know that I would not have taken steps
“toward reinstatement as soon as I did.
“Being totally cut off from loved ones and from close contact with the congregation
“created a strong desire to repent.
“I realized just how wrong my course was
and how serious it was to turn my back on Jehovah.”
We should think of these comments
if ever we are tempted to violate God’s command
not to associate with disfellowshipped friends or relatives.
The article I have quoted from also says:
“Disfellowshipped ones who are no longer members of the . . . congregation . . .
“may come to realize what they have lost.
“The bitter fruits of their sinful course,
“together with the memories of happier days
“when they enjoyed a good relationship with Jehovah and his people,
could bring them to their senses.”
Well, Jehovah knew what he was doing
when he inspired the anointed apostles to write what they did
about not having any contact
with disfellowshipped wrongdoers.
Let’s always believe that.

cn.text: 今天我们会讨论一下开除的安排
首先，我们来读一下
这项安排所根据的经文
就是哥林多前书第5章
请打开你的圣经
到哥林多前书第5章
我们会从哥林多前书5:9读起
这是使徒保罗在上帝指引下写的
“我曾经写信告诉你们
不要再跟淫乱的人来往
这不是说，你们要跟这个世界上淫乱的
贪心的、敲诈人的
拜偶像的人断绝来往
要是这样，你们就非离开世界不可了”
所以，基督徒还是会跟那些
没有学习真理的人来往
我们会接触到邻居、同事、同学等等
我们也会向他们作见证
他们有些人过着不道德的生活
但我们还是会接触到他们
但如果一个弟兄过着不道德的生活
情况就不同了
11节的经文说
“可是我现在写信告诉你们
凡是称为弟兄的人
如果是淫乱的、贪心的
拜偶像的、辱骂人的
醉酒的、敲诈人的
就不要再跟他来往
连跟他一起吃饭也不可以”
13节的经文最后也说
“要把邪恶的人从你们当中除掉”
保罗在上帝指引下写的这段话
不是一个建议，而是一条命令
2015年4月15日刊的《守望台》里
有一篇文章
《为什么开除的安排是仁爱的？》
文章解释得很清楚
文章说
“虽然耶和华没有期望他的仆人十全十美
却要求他们符合他的圣洁标准
上帝告诫他们不要触犯严重的罪
例如淫乱、拜偶像、偷窃
敲诈、杀人和通灵
相信你会同意
耶和华的圣洁标准不但合情合理
而且能保护上帝的子民
我们都会喜欢跟一些友善和蔼
品行端正和值得信任的人来往，不是吗？
会众的弟兄姐妹大都有这些美德
因为我们献身给耶和华时
都承诺遵从圣经的指引生活”
那如果受了浸的人犯下严重的罪
会怎么样呢？
如果一个人犯下淫乱、拜偶像
偷窃、敲诈、杀人或通灵等罪行
就一定会被会众开除吗？
这样的情况有点复杂
《守望台》文章解释
一个人会不会被开除，取决于两个因素
这两个因素必须同时存在
第一，受了浸的耶和华见证人犯了严重的罪
第二，当事人没有悔改
只有在犯了严重罪的人不愿意悔改的时候
他们才会被开除
另外，会众的长老必须确信
被开除的人已经衷心悔改了
才会考虑重新接纳他们
这就带来一个问题
如果我们的亲朋好友当中有人被开除了
对于长老们作出的这个决定
我们愿意接受并表现服从吗？
我们要相信
长老们是很客观地作出这个决定的
他们一定为此恳切地祷告
因为他们要为自己做的决定向上帝负责
他们也会尽力帮助犯过的人改正
如果犯过者不愿意接受
他们就必须保护会众的洁净
就算作出开除的决定
他们也会清楚仁慈地解释
怎样被重新接纳
另外，他们也会定期看望那些被开除的人
让他们知道怎样重新回到耶和华身边
如果我们服从并支持长老们的决定
我们就是在帮助犯过者从管教获益
管教其实是来自耶和华的
这一点，犯过者必须明白
来看一下希伯来书第12章
我们会从第5节读起
经文说
“你们完全忘了上帝劝你们
像劝儿子一样，说
儿子啊，你不要轻看耶和华的管教
被他纠正也不要放弃
因为耶和华管教他所爱的人
鞭打他接纳的每一个儿子”
第11节又说
“人被管教，当时自然不会快乐
只会觉得痛苦
日后，从管教中受到磨炼的人
却会获得让人安宁的成果，也就是正义”
所以，被开除的人如果愿意接受管教
他们就一定能恢复与耶和华的关系
我们怎么做
对被开除的人来说就是最好的呢？
我们已经读过了
哥林多前书5:11说
“不要再跟他来往
连跟他一起吃饭也不可以”
在约翰二书第10节
约翰给我们的建议也类似
“绝不可请他进你们家里去
也不可向他问好”
这样的时候，我们要忠于的是上帝
而不是被开除的人
上帝在观察
看我们有没有按照他的吩咐去做
就是停止与那些被开除的人来往
有些弟兄姐妹可能觉得
这样的要求太苛刻了
他们以为仁慈的做法
就是继续与被开除的亲朋好友来往
但是，他们的想法完全错了
这样做，可能他们自己觉得好受一些
但对于那些被开除的人来说
这是最糟糕的做法
耶稣在马太福音11:19指出
“智慧是由行为来证实的”
我们有很多例子都能说明
如果一家人坚定而忠贞地遵守耶和华的吩咐
断绝与被开除的亲朋好友来往
结果通常都是好的
有一个作父亲的说
他的儿子做了一些基督徒不该做的事
结果破坏了他们父子之间的关系
但这位父亲意识到
破坏他们父子关系的
是他的儿子，而不是耶和华
大概10年之后，他的儿子洗心革面
被会众重新接纳
儿子承认说
“被会众开除使我知道
要承担错误行为所带来的后果
我需要这样的管教”
这位父亲说
“会众必须开除不悔改的人
这个安排能提醒我们
生活要跟耶和华的标准一致
虽然开除使人痛苦，但长远来看却有好处
假如我纵容儿子，他就不会改过自新了”
还有一个姐妹也说
“与被开除的妹妹断绝一切来往
表明我们忠贞地支持耶和华的安排
也让我们一家人有机会表明
自己相信耶和华的行事方式是最好的”
她的妹妹后来对她说
“如果你把开除的事一笑置之
我知道，我就不会采取行动
尽快回到会众里了
由于家人和会众里的弟兄姐妹
都与我断绝关系
这推动我要悔改回头
我意识到我之前做的事有多么地错误
也看出背弃耶和华有多么严重”
如果我们还是很想跟被开除的亲朋好友来往
就最好记得这些弟兄姐妹的话
《守望台》文章还说
“犯过的人被开除后
就不再是会众大家庭的成员
他会看出自己失去了什么福分
被开除的人尝到犯罪的苦果
回想以往跟耶和华和弟兄姐妹有亲密的关系
日子过得多么快乐，可能会醒悟过来”
是的，耶和华在圣经里通过使徒吩咐我们
不要再跟那些被开除的人来往
他这样做很有智慧
愿我们都记得这一点

ko.text: 혹은 “저는 제 나름대로 하느님을 섬기니까 종교가 필요 없어요.”
많은 사람들은 특정한 종교의 신도가 될 필요가 없으며
단지 하느님과 개인적인 관계를 맺기만 하면 충분하다고 생각합니다.
많은 종교가 거짓 숭배를 조장해 왔습니다.
종교들은 신도들을 부당하게 대하거나 많은 돈을 요구해 왔으며
성경에서 정죄하는 행동을 용인하거나 심지어 조장해 왔습니다.
물론 그들이 조직되어 있는 것 자체에는 문제가 없습니다.
여호와께서는 자신의 백성이 조직되어 있기를 바라십니까?
성경을 보면, 초기 그리스도인들은 조직되어 있었습니다.
1세기 회중에서 교리와 관련된 한 가지 문제가 발생해
각자가 자신이 원하는 대로 믿기만 하면 된다고 결론 지었습니까?
그렇게 했다면 당시에 설립된 지 20년도 채 안 된 그리스도인 회중이 분열되었을 겁니다.
“그래서 바울과 바나바 두 사람과 그들 사이에 심한 의견 충돌과 논쟁이 있었다.
형제들은 그 문제 때문에 바울과 바나바와 다른 몇 사람을
예루살렘에 있는 사도들과 장로들에게 올라가도록 마련했다.”
예루살렘에 있는 사도들과 장로들은 그 문제에 대해 결정을 내렸습니다.
얼마 후 사도 바울과 디모데는 회중들을 방문했습니다.
예루살렘에 있는 사도들과 장로들이 정한 규정들을
1세기에 예루살렘에 있는 사도들과 장로들은 하느님의 백성을 위해
영적 양식과 지침과 실제적인 도움을 주었습니다.
모든 일을 적절하게 마련에 따라 하십시오.”
조직은 우리가 여호와를 그분이 원하시는 방식으로 숭배하는 데 큰 도움이 됩니다.
첫째, 숭배를 위해 함께 모이려면 조직되어 있어야 합니다.
우리가 서로를 모르고, 함께 모일 장소나 시간도 정해져 있지 않고,
집회를 위한 프로그램도 없다면 어떻게 함께 모이겠습니까?
둘째, 우리가 하나로 연합된 신앙을 가지려면 조직되어 있어야 합니다.
우리 모두는 회중 집회와 대회에서 동일한 교육을 받으며
성경에 근거한 출판물과 동영상들을 통해 성경을 이해하도록 도움을 받습니다.
고린도 전서 1:10의 교훈처럼 “일치되게 말”하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
셋째, 우리가 세계적인 형제 관계를 누리려면 조직되어 있어야 합니다.
우리가 “연합된 형제들”과 한 무리를 이루고 있다고 알려 주죠.
누가 우리의 영적 가족인지 어떻게 알아볼 수 있겠습니까?
넷째, 우리가 모든 나라와 민족과 언어의 사람들에게
좋은 소식을 전파하려면 조직되어 있어야 합니다.
어떻게 철저하면서도 효과적으로 왕국 소식을 전파할 수 있겠습니까?
다섯째, 우리가 구호 활동을 하려면 조직되어 있어야 합니다.
초기 그리스도인들이 다른 지역의 어려운 형제 자매들을

영적 양식과 지침과 실제적인 도움을 베풉니다.

en.text: Have you ever heard someone say:
“I’m not religious, but I am spiritual”
or “I don’t need to belong to a religion;
I worship God in my own way”?
Many people believe that they don’t need to be associated
with a specific religious organization
—that it’s good enough simply to have
a personal relationship with God.
It’s not surprising that they feel that way.
Many religious organizations have promoted false worship.
They’ve mistreated their followers
or demanded large sums of money from them
and tolerated or even promoted conduct
that the Bible condemns.
Of course, it’s the fruitage of those organizations that’s bad,
not the fact that they are organized.
But we might still ask,
‘Does Jehovah want his people to be organized?’
What does his Word say?
The Bible reveals that the early Christians were organized.
Consider what’s recorded in Acts chapter 15.
An issue arose
—an issue involving doctrine, or belief,
that caused disagreement among those in the congregation.
How would they settle that issue?
Did they conclude that it was enough
for each Christian to have his own relationship with God
and for each person to believe what he personally wanted?
No.
That would have divided the young Christian congregation,
which at this point was less than 20 years old.
At Acts 15:2, we read:
“But after quite a bit of dissension
“and disputing by Paul and Barnabas with them,
“it was arranged for Paul, Barnabas,
“and some of the others to go up to the apostles
and elders in Jerusalem regarding this issue.”
The apostles and elders in Jerusalem
made a decision that resolved the issue.
Thereafter, they made their decision known to the congregations.
This helped to restore peace and unity.
That wasn’t an exceptional case.
Sometime later, the apostle Paul and Timothy visited the congregations.
What did they accomplish?
Acts 16:4 says:
“As they traveled on through the cities,
“they would deliver to them for observance
“the decrees that had been decided on
by the apostles and the elders who were in Jerusalem.”
The apostles and elders in Jerusalem
consistently provided spiritual food, direction,
and practical help for God’s people in the first century.
They acted as a governing body.
What was the result of such organization?
Note the next verse.
It says: “Then, indeed,
“the congregations continued to be made firm in the faith
and to increase in number day by day.”
That organization in the first century helped the early Christians to be united,
productive, and happy.
In like manner, Jehovah’s people today are organized.
This reflects Jehovah’s personality.
First Corinthians chapter 14,
verses 33 and 40 says in part:
“God is a God not of disorder
“but of peace. . . .
Let all things take place decently and by arrangement.”
Think about it: Organization really helps us
to fulfill Jehovah’s requirements for true worship.
Consider five examples.
First, we must be organized to meet together for worship.
How could we do so if we didn’t know one another,
didn’t have designated places and times to gather together,
and didn’t have a scheduled program for each meeting?
Second, we must be organized to be united in belief.
All of us receive the same instruction at congregation meetings,
assemblies, and conventions,
and we’re helped to understand the Scriptures
through Bible-based publications and videos.
These provisions require organization,
and they help us to worship unitedly and,
as 1 Corinthians 1:10 counsels us,
to “speak in agreement.”
Third, we must be organized
to form a worldwide brotherhood.
First Peter 2:17 reminds us
that we belong to an “association of brothers.”
If we weren’t organized,
how could we even identify those
who are truly part of our spiritual family?
Fourth, we must be organized to preach the good news
to people of different nations, tribes, and languages.
How could we possibly declare the Kingdom message
thoroughly and effectively
if we weren’t associated with an organization?
Fifth, we must be organized to provide disaster relief.
Just as the early Christians had an arrangement to supply financial aid
to their needy brothers and sisters in other lands,
so we are organized to help our brothers and sisters
as soon as possible after a disaster,
disease outbreak, or other emergency.
As was the case in the first century,
the Governing Body today provides spiritual food, direction,
and practical help for God’s people around the world.
Jesus has appointed that Governing Body to be “the faithful and discreet slave.”
How grateful we are that Jehovah, through our Leader, Jesus Christ,
has organized us so that we can do God’s will
as a united brotherhood!

cn.text: 你可能听人说过
我不信教，但我相信有神！
或者
为什么要入教？
我自己也能崇拜上帝！
很多人认为
他们没必要正式加入一个宗教组织
他们觉得
只要心里相信有上帝就够了
他们这样想也不奇怪
很多宗教组织宣传错误的教义
他们剥削信徒
要求信徒捐很多钱
有的还宽容圣经谴责的行为
甚至鼓吹这样的事
这些组织的行为确实很恶劣
但这不意味着组织起来崇拜上帝是错的
我们也许会想
耶和华真的希望他的子民组织起来吗？
圣经怎么说呢？
圣经显示
1世纪的基督徒是有组织的
使徒行传15章提到
当时有一个跟教义有关的争议
这件事在各群会众中吵得沸沸扬扬
他们是怎样解决问题的呢？
他们有没有觉得
只要信上帝就好了
有不同的看法无所谓
想信什么就信什么吧！
没有！
当时基督徒会众才成立不到20年
他们要是这样想
会众就分裂了
使徒行传15:2说
耶路撒冷的使徒和长老
开会解决了这个问题
然后他们把决定告诉各群会众
这维护了组织的团结与和睦
后来又怎么样呢？
让我们看看
使徒保罗带着提摩太去探访会众时
还做了什么
使徒行传16:4说
这说明
耶路撒冷的使徒和长老
一直为上帝的子民
提供滋养信心的食物
指引和实际的帮助
他们就是1世纪的中央长老团
这样的组织安排带来了什么成果呢？
接着看第5节
经文说
因为有组织
1世纪的会众才能这么地团结
喜乐和兴旺！
同样，上帝的子民今天也要组织起来
这就是耶和华做事的风格
因为在哥林多前书14:33,40说
为什么说
只有组织起来
才能按照耶和华喜欢的方式崇拜他呢？
请看五个方面
首先，有组织才能聚集起来崇拜他
这样，我们才能认识彼此
有合适的崇拜场所
固定的聚会时间
才知道聚会要学什么内容
第二，有组织才能在信仰上保持一致
我们通过会众聚会、分区大会和区域大会
受到同样的教导
通过书刊和影片更明白经文的含义
这些都需要组织的安排！
有了这些安排，我们才能团结合一
像哥林多前书1:10说的那样
“说话……一致”
第三，有组织才能组成一个国际大家庭
彼得前书2:17说
我们都属于同一个“弟兄团体”
要是没有组织
我们怎么分辨出
谁才是我们真正的弟兄姐妹呢？
第四，有组织才能做好传道工作
向不同国族、语言的人作见证
如果没有组织
我们怎么可能用有效的方式
把好消息传遍普天下呢？
第五，有组织才能统筹救灾工作
1世纪的基督徒组织起来
为受灾的弟兄姐妹运送救援物资
今天，要是发生天灾
传染病或其他紧急情况
我们也会尽快组织起来
救援弟兄姐妹
跟1世纪一样
今天的中央长老团
也会为上帝的子民
提供滋养信心的食物
指引和实际的帮助
他们就是耶稣任命的“忠信睿智的奴隶”
耶和华通过我们的领袖耶稣基督
把我们组织起来
团结一致地敬奉他
我们多么感谢他！

title: JW 방송—2023년 7월

ko.text: 이번 달 방송에서는 어떤 내용을 살펴보게 될까요?
나쁜 일을 하게 만드는 강한 유혹을 받았지만
하느님의 도덕 표준에 따라 살기로 결심한 두 청소년들의 이야기를 들어볼 것입니다.
새로운 뮤직비디오는 하느님의 백성이 어떻게 연합을 이루고
서로에 대한 사랑을 나타내는지를 보여 줄 것입니다.
다음으로 한 형제가 여호와를 중심으로 살아가는 것이
진정한 행복의 비결이라는 점을 어떻게 깨닫게 되는지 살펴볼 것입니다.
이제 JW 방송을 시작하겠습니다. 2023년 7월 방송을 함께 시청해 보시죠.
예수께서는 아버지께 기도하면서 제자들을 지켜 달라고 요청하셨습니다.
“제가 아버지께 요청하는 것은, 그들을 세상에서 데려가 주시라는 것이 아니라
악한 자로부터 그들을 지켜 주시라는 것입니다.
제가 세상에 속해 있지 않은 것처럼 그들도 세상에 속해 있지 않습니다.”
예수께서 여호와와 진리의 힘을 확신하셨다는 사실을

따뜻하고 친근한 태도를 보이고, 대화를 이어 나가고, 더 알고 싶게 만드십시오.

우린 관심을 보인 사람 모두를 주저 없이 방문하길 원하기 때문이죠.

진리에 대한 사랑은 또한 우리가 동료 숭배자들을 돕고자 하는 마음을 갖게 합니다.
그래서 우리는 때때로 조언을 해 주기도 하죠.
다음 아침 숭배에서 스플레인 형제가 그 점에 대한 훌륭한 제안을 해 줄 것입니다.
하느님의 말씀에는 많은 것이 들어 있습니다.

그런 다음, 갈라디아서 6:1의 표현을 하나씩 분석해 보겠습니다.
한 구절에 많은 게 들어 있죠.
“형제 여러분, 어떤 사람이 미처 알지 못하고 걸음을 잘못 내디딜지라도,
영적 자격을 가진 여러분은 그런 사람을 온화한 영으로 바로잡기 위해 노력하십시오.
그리고 여러분도 유혹에 빠지지 않도록 자신을 계속 살피십시오.”
처음 나오는 표현은 “형제 여러분”인데, 복수로 되어 있습니다.
이 점과 관련해서는 잠시 후에 다시 말씀드리죠.
이어서, “어떤 사람이 미처 알지 못하고 걸음을 잘못 내디딜지라도”라는 표현이 있는데,
길을 걷고 있는 한 남자를 떠올린 것입니다.
생각해 보면, 바울이 갈라디아서에서 걷는 것을 언급한 건 이것이 처음이 아닙니다.
그러면 육적인 욕망에 따라 행동하는 일이 결코 없을 것입니다.”
“그러나 여러분이 영의 인도를 받고 있다면, 여러분은 율법 아래 있는 것이 아닙니다.”
또 25절을 보면 “우리가 영을 따라 살고 있다면, 계속해서 영을 따라 걸어갑시다”라고 했는데,
그런 다음 6:1에서 ‘어떤 사람이 걸음을 잘못 내디딜지라도’라고 한 겁니다.
따라서 바울은 어떤 그리스도인이 똑바로 걸어가다가 갑자기 걸음을 잘못 내딛는 모습을 생각한 것입니다.
그런데 걸음을 한 번 잘못 내딛는 것이 그렇게 큰 문제인가요?
컬럼비아 하이츠의 울퉁불퉁한 길을 걸어가 보신 분은 아실 것입니다.
길을 걸어가다가 걸음을 잘못 내딛어서 발목을 삐거나 허리를 다치기 쉽다는 것을 말이죠.
네, 한 걸음만 잘못 내디뎌도 위험할 수 있습니다.
농구를 하다가 실수로 발을 한 번만 헛디뎌도 몇 주 동안이나 목발을 짚게 될 수 있다는 것을 아실 겁니다.
따라서 한 번만 걸음을 잘못 내디뎌도 심각할 수 있습니다.
‘걸음을 잘못 내딛다’로 번역된 그리스어는 다양한 의미가 있습니다.
큰 잘못 즉 큰 죄를 의미할 수도 있죠.
오늘의 해설에서는 갈라디아서 6:1이 심각한 죄에 적용된다는 것을 알려 줍니다.
다시 갈라디아서 6:1의 표현을 보면 “미처 알지 못하고 걸음을 잘못 내디딜지라도”라고 했죠.
여기 사용된 그리스어는 죄가 고의적이 아님을 알려 줍니다.
이 사람은 그날 심각한 죄를 지을 생각으로 집을 나선 것이 아닙니다.
나쁜 친구들과 시간을 보냈을 수 있습니다.
그러다 갑자기 자신이 계획하지 않은 일을 하게 된 것이죠.
단지 고의로 죄를 지은 것이 아닐 뿐입니다.
하지만 그는 도움을 받을 수 있습니다.
성구에 “영적 자격을 가진 여러분은”이라고 했는데, 갈라디아 사람들은 그 자격이 어떤 것인지 알았을 것입니다.
왜냐하면 5:22, 23에서 사도 바울이 영의 열매의 아홉 가지 부면을 나열했기 때문이죠.
따라서 그들은 영적 자격이 어떤 것들인지 알았을 겁니다.
조언을 하는 사람은 성령의 인도를 받아 그렇게 해야 합니다.
짜증이 나거나 화가 나서 조언을 해서는 안 되죠.
거의 반사적으로 또는 순간 욱해서 조언하면 안 됩니다.
성령이 우리를 움직여서 조언을 하게 해야 합니다.
또 흥미로운 표현이 있는데 “영적 자격을 가진 여러분은 … 노력하십시오”라고 했죠.
제가 알기론 「신세계역」 외에는 “노력하라”는 이 표현을 쓴 성경 번역판이 하나밖에 없습니다.
대부분의 번역판은 「킹 제임스 성경」을 따르는데 거기엔 ‘영적인 너희는 그를 회복시키고’라고 했죠.
노력을 의미할 수도 있고 직접적인 행동을 의미할 수도 있죠.
번역 위원회는 상대방을 바로잡으려고 시도하더라도 그 결과가 상대방의 반응에 따라 달라질 수 있다는 걸 알았습니다.
조언을 받아들일 수도, 그렇지 않을 수도 있죠.
그리고 여호와의 증인들이 아마도 조언을 하고 사람들을 돕는 일을 누구보다 많이 하기 때문에
이 구절에 노력한다는 표현을 포함시키는 것이 필요하다고 본 것일 수 있습니다.
자, 어떤 사람이 걷다가 걸음을 잘못 내딛습니다.
걸음을 잘못 내딛으면 어떻게 될 수 있죠?
여기 사용된 그리스어가 어긋난 뼈를 맞추는 것을 가리키는 의학 용어라는 것을 아실 것입니다.
여러분이 길을 걷다 걸음을 잘못 내디뎌서 뼈가 어긋났다면 그것을 바로잡아야 합니다.
바로잡을 때 중요한 것은 성구 표현처럼 “온화한 영”입니다.
이것이 중요한 이유는 장로들은 때때로 아주 역겨운 일을 한 사람에게 조언을 해야 할 때가 있고,
그러다 보면 화가 많이 날 수 있기 때문입니다.
거친 말로 혼을 내고 싶을 수도 있겠지만 장로들은 그러지 않죠.
장로들은 성령을 주셔서 온화를 보이게 해 달라고 기도하죠.
심각한 죄를 저지른 사람은 스스로 큰 부끄러움을 느낄 수 있습니다.
장로들에게 오기까지 엄청난 용기가 필요했을지 모르죠.
따라서 그런 사람을 친절하게 대해야 합니다.
“온화한 영” 얘기를 하고 나서 다음 표현으로
그런데 지금은 조언을 하는 사람 각자에게 이야기하고 있는 것입니다.
따라서 우리는 자기 검토를 해 보아야 합니다.
우리 중 많은 분이 오늘 아침 해설자들의 말에 공감할 것입니다.
조언을 많이 해 보신 분들은 때때로 과거를 돌아보며 후회할 때가 있습니다.
‘더 친절하고 더 온화하게 조언했어야 하는데’ 하고 말이죠.
그래서 우리는 때때로 “내가 다른 사람에게 조언을 할 때 그는 어떤 느낌을 받는가?” 하고 자신을 검토해 보는 것이 좋습니다.
바울은 단수형을 사용해서 우리 각자에게 말하고 있는 것입니다.
장로들인 여러분과 저에게 이렇게 말하고 있는 것이죠.
“형제의 조언이 사람들에게 어떤 느낌을 주고 있는지 자신을 검토해 보세요.”
끝으로 살펴볼 표현은 “여러분도 유혹에 빠지지 않도록”인데요, 무슨 뜻일까요?
어떤 죄를 지었는지 자세히 듣게 되면 자신도 그 일을 하고 싶은 유혹에 빠질 수 있다는 뜻일까요?
바울이 말하고자 하는 것은 우리 모두가 불완전하다는 겁니다.
다른 사람보다 우월하다고 생각지 말고, 조언을 할 때 독선적이 되지 말라고 한 것이죠.
우리는 불완전하기 때문에 언젠가는 입장이 바뀌어 조언을 받게 될 수도 있다고 말한 것입니다.
우리는 그런 상황에서 상대방이 온화한 영으로 조언해 주기를 바랄 것입니다.
우리도 불완전하다는 것을 기억한다면 잘못한 사람에게 온화한 태도로 부드럽게 말하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
“형제 여러분, 어떤 사람이 미처 알지 못하고 걸음을 잘못 내디딜지라도,
영적 자격을 가진 여러분은 그런 사람을 온화한 영으로 바로잡기 위해 노력하십시오.
그리고 여러분도 유혹에 빠지지 않도록 자신을 계속 살피십시오.”
조언하는 사람은 성령의 인도를 받아 온화한 태도로 조언해야 한다는 것입니다.
조언을 해야 하는 경우라면 반드시 온화한 영으로 조언해야 합니다.
앞서 얘기한 것처럼, 진리는 우리를 행동하게 만듭니다.
상상할 수 있는 거의 모든 문화와 배경에서 나왔습니다.
하지만 우리는 많은 사람이 현대의 기적이라고 생각하는 평화를 누리고 있습니다.
이번 달 뮤직비디오가 그 내용을 담고 있는데요,
여호와의 증인인 우리에게 연합은 단순한 꿈이 아닙니다.
대회를 위해 함께 모였을 때나 어려운 상황에서
서로를 도울 때 우리의 사랑과 연합을 분명히 볼 수 있습니다.
땅에 대한 하느님의 뜻이 온전히 이루어지고
문자적으로 이 땅에 있는 모든 사람들이
함께 연합하게 될 때 어떤 모습일지 한번 상상해 보십시오.
이번 달 방송에서는 진리에 대한 사랑이 우리 삶 전체에 영향을 주어야 한다는 점을 살펴봤습니다.
그 사랑은 우리가 하느님의 표준을 따르고, 그것을 자신의 것으로 만들고,
효과적인 재방문을 함으로 관심 있는 사람들을 돕고,
많은 사람이 피지에서 볼 수 있는 아름다운 열대 지방의 모습을 떠올릴지 모르는데,
우리가 이번에 가 볼 곳이 바로 피지입니다.
피지는 남태평양에 있는 300개가 넘는 섬으로 이루어져 있으며,
그러한 섬들에 가면 울창한 우림, 건조한 초원 지대,
산호초에 둘러싸인 아름답고 깨끗한 석호를 볼 수 있습니다.
섬 안쪽으로 들어가면 험하고 가파른 지형을 만날 수 있는데
거의 100만 명의 사람들에게 좋은 소식을 전하고 있습니다.
피지의 가장 큰 두 섬 사이에 있는 코로라는 작은 섬에서
우리 형제들은 구역의 대부분을 걸어서 봉사합니다.
멀리 떨어진 구역으로 갈 때에는 트럭을 빌리기도 합니다.
그러면 노인들도 아이들도 모두 여러 마을로 가서 봉사할 수 있죠.
회중의 많은 사람은 봉사를 하지 않을 때는 농사를 지어서 가족을 부양합니다.
생계를 위해 피지의 전통적인 방식으로 돗자리를 만드는 사람들도 있습니다.
돗자리는 열대 지방에서 자라는 판다누스 나무의 가늘고 긴 잎으로 만듭니다.
잎을 말리고 진흙 속에 넣어 염색을 한 뒤 부드럽게 만들어 돗자리를 짭니다.
많은 가족들은 돗자리를 팔아서 순회 대회와 지역 대회에 갈 경비를 마련합니다.
형제 자매들은 12시간을 배를 타고 거칠기로 유명한 바다를 건너
피지의 가장 큰 섬인 비티레부에서 열리는 대회에 다녀옵니다.
그것은 그때까지 남반구에서 관측된 가장 강력한 태풍이었습니다.
작은 마을인 난간다무에 있는 대부분의 집이 완전히 파괴되었고
그곳의 우리 형제 자매들은 가진 것 대부분을 잃었습니다.
증인들의 훌륭한 평판을 잘 알고 있었던 마을의 촌장은
왕국회관 주변에 형제 자매들이 집을 다시 짓도록 땅을 마련해 주었습니다.
현지 형제들은 재해 구호 자원봉사자들과 함께
회중의 모든 사람을 위해 14채의 새 집을 지었습니다.
현지 형제들은 집회를 볼 때도, 그리고 봉사를 할 때도 최신 기술을 잘 사용합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Hello, and thank you for joining us!
What can we look forward to in this month’s broadcast?
We’ll hear from two young people
who chose to live
by God’s moral standards
even when their resolve
was seriously challenged by temptation.
A new music video
celebrates the ways
that God’s people demonstrate
their unity and express their love
for one another.
And we’ll see how one brother learned
that a life centered on Jehovah
is the key to true happiness.
Welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
This is the program for July 2023.
The evening before he died,
Jesus Christ asked his Father in prayer
to watch over his disciples.
His request is recorded at John 17:15-17.
Read it with me.
Jesus said: “I do not request
“that you take them out of the world,
“but that you watch over them
“because of the wicked one.
“They are no part of the world,
just as I am no part of the world.”
Jesus’ confidence in Jehovah
and in the power of the truth
can be seen clearly in what he asks of his Father in verse 17:
“Sanctify them by means of the truth;
your word is truth.”
When we accept the truth
and make a personal dedication to God,
in a general sense,
we are sanctified, or set apart, from the world
because we no longer fit into its mold.
People view us differently
because our values have changed.
We live by the standards of Bible truth,
and doing so honors Jehovah God,
gives our life meaning, and brings us great happiness.
With those thoughts in mind,
how should we feel about the sayings of God
and the Bible truths that we have learned?
We feel the way the psalmist did.
At Psalm 119:140,
he said to Jehovah God:
“Your saying is thoroughly refined
“[which means that it’s clean and pure;
and then he said], and your servant loves it.”
Isn’t that how we feel about the truth?
We love it!
It would be wonderful if everyone would respond to the truth of God’s Word
and love it.
However, the sad fact is that the majority of the world rejects it.
There are many people who do not believe that truth is attainable.
Some ancient philosophers made the teaching of doubts
virtually their life’s work.
Human philosophy is built on pride of intellect
and a warped pleasure of endless speculation
that leaves Jehovah God, the Creator,
completely out of the picture.
By removing God,
philosophers wander in a maze of ideas and theories
that fascinate the mind and inflate the ego
but never arrive at the truth.
If truth were not attainable,
why would Jesus Christ say
as recorded at John 8:31, 32:
“If you remain in my word,
“you are really my disciples,
“and you will know the truth,
and the truth will set you free”?
Are we not experiencing the freedom that Jesus spoke of?
And why would the apostle Paul write at 1 Timothy 2:4
that God’s “will is that all sorts of people
should be saved and come to an accurate knowledge of truth”?
Why does the word “truth” occur over a hundred times
in the Christian Greek Scriptures?
Jesus not only pointed out that the truth is attainable,
but he showed that finding it is required
if our worship is to be approved by God.
When a Samaritan woman wondered
what the true form of worship was
—the worship practiced by the Jews in Jerusalem
or that practiced by the Samaritans on Mount Gerizim—
Jesus did not answer by saying:
‘Truth is unattainable, and you don’t need to worry about it,’
or ‘You can believe whatever you want to believe.’
No, Jesus did not view the truth as relative
—that whatever you want to believe is the truth.
That is nonsense
and has nothing to do with the realities of life.
At John 4:23, 24,
Jesus made a specific reference to truth,
God’s spirit, and pure worship.
At John 4:23, 24, he said:
“True worshippers
“will worship the Father with spirit and truth,
“for indeed, the Father is looking for ones like these
“to worship him.
“God is a Spirit, and those worshipping him
must worship with spirit and truth.”
Jesus was talking about being guided in our worship
by God’s holy spirit
and said that we do not need the use of temples, images,
or other physical objects in true worship.
And the truth that Jesus referred to
is an accurate knowledge of Bible truths.
True faith is much more than just belief in God
—that he exists;
it also means an acceptance of God’s Word,
obtaining an intellectual understanding of that Word,
and then manifesting a heartfelt reliance upon it.
As genuine Christians,
we view the Bible as the inspired Word of God,
beneficial for teaching and disciplining mankind.
Psalm 119:160 says of Jehovah God:
“The very essence of your word is truth.”
When Jesus Christ stood before Pontius Pilate
and told him that he had come to earth to speak the truth,
Pilate responded with the words: “What is truth?”
Likely, Pilate was cynical.
His words reveal a skeptical view of truth.
But the truth that Jesus had in mind was about God’s Kingdom
and Jesus’ role as its King.
That was the very theme, the core,
of Jesus’ teaching while he was on earth.
That’s why when Pilate asked Jesus if he was a king,
Jesus replied:
“You yourself say it.”
In other words, ‘Yes, I am,’
but he added that his Kingdom was “no part of this world.”
The truth is that his Kingdom will sanctify Jehovah’s name,
vindicate his sovereignty,
and restore faithful mankind to happy, eternal life.
Genuine Christians embrace this truth.
Since Jesus’ role in the fulfillment of all of God’s promises is so pivotal
and since all of God’s prophecies
become “Amen,” or true, because of him,
Jesus could well say, as recorded at John 14:6:
“I am the way and the truth and the life.”
And as 2 Corinthians 1:20 declares:
“For no matter how many the promises of God are,
“they have become ‘yes’ by means of him.
“Therefore, also through him
is the ‘Amen’ said to God.”
Jesus used the word “amen”
to affirm the truthfulness of what was said,
but he did so in a unique way.
We usually say “amen” after a prayer is said
to show our agreement with it.
However, rather than use it
to reply to a prayer or a statement,
he used “amen”
to introduce pronouncements of truth.
At times, he repeated the word,
saying “amen, amen” and then made his statement,
which would be like saying
“most truly I say to you.”
Yes, by using this expression,
he assured his listeners that his words were the absolute truth.
Jesus could speak with such certainty
because he was the one authorized
to make all of God’s promises come true.
To us, the exhilarating good news of God’s Kingdom
under the rulership of Jesus Christ
is more, far more, than mere information.
That truth moves us to action;
it compels us to live by it and share it with others.
To the first-century Christian congregation,
the way of life they adopted as followers of Christ
was sometimes known simply as “the truth”
or “the way of the truth.”
Read with me 3 John verse 4, where it says:
“No greater joy do I have than this:
“that I should hear that my children
go on walking in the truth.”
Isn’t that how parents feel about their children
who are serving Jehovah faithfully?
Absolutely!
However, not all young ones
raised in a believing household have stuck with the truth.
The same is true about many with whom we’ve studied the Bible.
Is their situation hopeless?
No, not at all.
There’s still time for them to act
and to show Jehovah that they love him
and that they love the truth.
The end of this system is fast approaching.
It is going to happen and soon.
We encourage such ones to give serious thought
to their relationship with Jehovah God,
because he genuinely loves them
and wants them to have life.
We pray that such ones take whatever steps are necessary
to return to Jehovah before it’s too late.
It’s a Scriptural fact
that people need to love the truth in order to be saved.
This is the point that the apostle Paul makes
at 2 Thessalonians 2:10,
where it reads in part that people will perish
“because they did not accept the love of the truth
in order that they might be saved.”
Our prayer is that honesthearted people everywhere
will respond to Jehovah’s invitation
to draw close to him and love the truth.
This world is heading for an abrupt end
at the battle of Armageddon.
To survive that battle,
we must have knowledge of Jehovah God
and live in harmony with his Word,
which includes the teachings of Jesus Christ.
Earth wide we are proclaiming the good news
that God’s Kingdom has been established in the heavens.
That proclamation
is the foretold “witness to all the nations”
that soon the accomplished end of this world’s system will come.
No, no, not the end of our planet,
because another basic truth is that “the earth remains forever”
as stated at Ecclesiastes 1:4.
These are absolute truths that we preach,
and we love them.
Knowing the truth sets us free from lies,
delusions, and superstitions.
And when we live by it,
the truth strengthens us to endure hardships.
God’s truth is so reliable and well-founded,
and it so inspires us with hope
that it enables us to stand up under any test.
We see our brothers in lands where they are mistreated and persecuted
doing just that, and they do it with joy.
To dismiss truth as relative or nonexistent
is to miss out on the most thrilling
and fulfilling quest that life offers.
To find the truth is to find hope;
to know and love it is to know and love the Creator of the universe
and his only-begotten Son;
to live by it is to live with purpose and peace of mind,
now and forever.
There’s no question
that when we live the truth,
we stand out as different from the world around us.
That’s not easy for any of us.
But if you’re a teenager, it’s especially hard.
Young ones, we know your faith is tested every day.
Your peers question your belief in God,
look down on Bible teachings,
and make fun of your lifestyle.
For your faith to remain strong,
it’s not enough simply to believe what you’ve been taught.
You need solid reasons for what you believe.
That’s why we’re pleased to introduce
a brand-new video series just for you
called Reasons for Faith.
In each episode, young Witnesses like you
talk about why they have faith
and how they keep it strong in a world
that has little or no respect for God’s Word.
Why was it difficult to uphold God’s moral standards at school?
I remember that in high school it was complicated
because my classmates made fun of me.
They often said I acted holier-than-thou and other similar insults
because I didn’t go to nightclubs, I didn’t curse, I didn’t smoke.
It was unbearable because they often tried to push me to the limit.
I had a one-hour bus ride to get to high school,
and I wanted the bus to make a U-turn and avoid going to high school.
I had all the time to think
of what could happen to me and what they could say to me,
and I admit that I sometimes felt alone.
The environment at school often exposed me to immorality.
For example, girls would wear short skirts.
I received instant messages
from people I had never met before.
They would send me photos,
a phone number, or invitations that I could have just simply accepted.
So I could have easily committed sexual immorality.
Sometimes I felt like I was missing out on something important
when I heard my classmates talking about what they were doing
on their evenings and weekends
and about drinking alcohol and new drugs they were trying
or girls they had slept with.
I started to become curious.
What did you do to strengthen your faith?
During family worship with my parents,
we studied the example of Daniel.
Far from his family
among people that didn’t serve Jehovah,
he succeeded in remaining faithful,
and I wanted to do the same.
To strengthen my faith,
I started reading the Bible.
I had to take the metro to get to school,
so every morning I took the opportunity to read a few verses.
I thought about the verses I had read.
By praying to Jehovah,
having a kind of constant conversation with him,
Jehovah would put me in a little bubble.
I started feeling comfortable inside,
and I was no longer under the bad influence of others.
And the fact that I prayed more also made me feel closer to Jehovah.
It was a bit like Psalm 63:7,
which describes how Jehovah shelters us under his immense wings.
Well, that’s exactly how I felt.
Prayer allowed me to face any temptation.
Why do you believe that Jehovah’s standards are beneficial?
I closely observed the young ones in the world,
and I realized that they are suffering from the standards they follow.
I closely stick to the moral standards that Jehovah has given me.
I’m aware that they are there for my benefit,
because with the experiences I’ve had in school,
I’ve observed the painful consequences that my classmates have suffered.
Some got into trouble with the law
or got sick.
They’ve had health problems caused by their lifestyle.
A girl in school did something immoral with a boy,
and it started circulating around the school.
Because of that,
the girl didn’t come to school anymore,
and she started having suicidal thoughts.
I understood that Jehovah protects us with his principles, his standards.
And if I had compromised even once with his standards,
I would have regretted it sooner or later.
And for me, there is nothing worse than regret.
I’m 100 percent sure that Jehovah gave me
these moral principles for my own good
so that I could be morally clean.
He also helps me to be positive.
For example, he helped me to see my classmates
as potential disciples,
and we were able to have conversations about the Bible together.
I am really convinced that Jehovah’s standards are good for me.
Being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses is the best life possible.
What gave Clara and Hugo the courage
to live by God’s standards when under pressure that, as Clara said,
‘was sometimes unbearable’?
You heard them.
They are absolutely convinced
that Jehovah’s standards are for their own good.
Is that how you feel?
Why not follow their advice
and dig deeply into God’s Word
to strengthen your confidence in it
and pray to Jehovah for his help
when you face those same pressures?
Real faith has the power to improve people’s lives
in ways they couldn’t have imagined
before learning the truth.
Take our brother Jason Worilds.
He learned that what the world offers
pales in comparison to what Jehovah freely gives us.
News overnight
—Steelers’ linebacker Jason Worilds
is walking away from the NFL
in the prime of his NFL career.

that give us the best chance for a successful return visit.
The first step is to be warm and friendly.
So focus on just getting yourself relaxed.
That way you can be warm and friendly when you greet them.

conversing with someone we don’t know well.
But if we’ve prepared well ahead of time,
we can now take a deep breath,
focus on the value of the message, and smile.
This can help us to relax,
and often our smile is contagious.
I’m Laura.

Yeah, that’s right.

I want to answer the question that I left with you last time:

Why does God allow suffering?

to be able to answer your question the next time that I come.
Does that sound OK?
Sure, that’s fine.

We can simply ask if it would be OK to continue our current discussion
so we can do some research and return with a better answer.

that’s fine.

but, if necessary, we can always adjust it.
And here’s our last tip:
Leave them wanting more.

Set up a question for the next visit.
Huh, that’s interesting.

could I maybe come back Saturday?

Three easy steps that can help us be more comfortable
and also help us make successful return visits:
Be warm and friendly,
continue our discussion,
and leave them wanting more.
I know these tips have helped me,
and I sure hope they help you

What do you think?

That’s our hope,

Our love for the truth
also impels us to help our fellow worshippers.
Sometimes we do so by giving corrective counsel.

Brother Splane shares some valuable advice along those lines
in the following morning worship.
Well, God’s Word is so rich.
There’s so much in it,
and Galatians 6:1 is no exception.
So, please, let’s turn there,
and we’re going to read the whole thing.
And then we’re going to analyze
Galatians 6:1 phrase by phrase;
there’s a lot in this one verse.
So at Galatians 6:1,
Paul writes:
“Brothers, even if a man takes a false step
“before he is aware of it,
“you who have spiritual qualifications
“try to readjust such a man in a spirit of mildness.
“But keep an eye on yourself,
for fear you too may be tempted.”
Now, the first word is “brothers.”
And we notice that that is in the plural.
That may be significant, and we’re going to come back to that in a few minutes.
Now, Paul says: “even if a man takes a false step.”
So, what’s the metaphor here?
What is Paul thinking about?
Walking.
He sees a man who is walking down a path.
And all of a sudden, he “takes a false step.”
Now, come to think of it,
this isn’t the first time that Paul mentions walking
in his letter to the Galatians.
Cast your eye on chapter 5,
and notice verse 16:
“But I say, Keep walking by spirit
and you will carry out no fleshly desire at all”;
and again, verse 18:
“Furthermore, if you are being led by spirit,
you are not under law”;
and once again, verse 25:
“If we are living by spirit,
let us also go on walking orderly by spirit”
—literally walking in a straight line;
and then at chapter 6, verse 1:
“brothers, even if a man takes a false step.”
So Paul sees a Christian who is walking along,
walking in a straight line,
but all of a sudden, he takes a false step.
Question: Is one false step so serious?
Well, those of us who have tried to walk down
the uneven pavement on Columbia Heights
and have taken a false step
as we stepped off the curb
and wrenched something or put something out,
we can testify that one false step can be serious.
And what about you young brothers, you basketball players?
You know that sometimes when you’re on the basketball court,
you take one false step
and you end up on crutches for a few weeks.
So the fact is that one false step can be serious and, interestingly,
the Greek word that’s translated “false step” here
allows for a variety of meanings.
It can apply to a minor infraction,
but it can also apply to a major transgression
—a major sin.
And you’ll notice in the comment today when we read it
that Galatians 6:1 is being applied to a serious sin.
So it can be applied to both.
Let’s carry on.
He “takes a false step before he is aware of it.”
Now, what does that mean?
Well, the Greek word here
indicates that the sin is not deliberate.
He didn’t leave home that day with the idea
that he was going to commit a serious sin.
It came upon him unawares.
He was surprised.
Perhaps he got into the wrong crowd,
and all of a sudden, he ended up doing something
that he really hadn’t planned to do.
It is not deliberate,
but that doesn’t mean that the sin isn’t serious.
It just means that it was not intentional.
Now, here’s help; help is on the way.
It says: “you who have spiritual qualifications.”
Well, come to think of it, the Galatians would know what these are
because at chapter 5, verses 22, 23,
the apostle Paul outlined
the nine aspects of “the fruitage of the spirit,”
so they would know what the spiritual qualifications are.
But here’s the point, as Brother Devine brought out:
Those who give counsel
need to be motivated by the holy spirit,
not by frustration, not by anger.
This is no knee-jerk reaction,
a flash of anger or something.
No, the holy spirit
has to move us to give the counsel.
Now, the next word is interesting.
It says: “You who have spiritual qualifications try”
—“try.”
Now, you won’t find that word in many Bibles.
I think there’s only one other besides the New World Translation
that says “try.”
Most of the Bible translations follow the King James Version.
And the King James Version  says: ‘You who are spiritual restore the man.’
Now, the Greek allows for both.
It allows for an attempt,
or it can be a direct action.
So, now, the translators have to choose.
The original New World Bible Translation Committee chose “try.”
Why?
Well, they realized that while there would be an attempt to readjust,
the outcome would depend on the person who was being readjusted.
Would he really want to change?

probably do more in giving counsel

the translation committee saw the subtlety
at Galatians 6:1.
Well, now, we have a man walking along.

for setting a fractured bone in place.

something gets out of joint, and now you have to be readjusted.

“in a spirit of mildness.”

—“yourself.”

who was called upon to give counsel.

to the comment that was given this morning.

a self-examination from time to time.

By using the singular,
Paul is talking to each and every one of us.
If you are an elder,

and he’s saying: “Examine yourself.

Is he saying that if you hear the details of what the person has done,
you may want to do the same thing?
No, what he’s reminding us of
is that we are all imperfect.
Paul is saying to us: “Don’t get on your high horse.
“Don’t be self-righteous when you’re giving counsel to others.

In a spirit of mildness.
Keeping our own limitations in mind
will help us to moderate our tone,
to speak to the offender in a spirit of mildness.

“Brothers,
“even if a man takes a false step
“before he is aware of it,
“you who have spiritual qualifications
“try to readjust such a man
“in a spirit of mildness.
“But keep an eye on yourself,
for fear you too may be tempted.”

by those who are moved by holy spirit,
this discussion will have been worth having.

Jehovah’s people speak hundreds of languages
and come from almost every imaginable culture and background,
yet we enjoy a peace that is viewed by many
as a modern-day miracle.

Earth cries out ev’ry day. So many have lost their way.

Jehovah is there and lovingly shares Peace that flows like a river,

One faith, one God, Peace on earth,
One mind, one voice Throughout the universe
When all hearts sing as one.
Under the Prince of Peace, Freedom will never end.
When sorrow is gone and death is undone,
Every knee will bend To Jehovah, our King.
One faith, one God, Peace on earth,
One mind, one voice Throughout the universe—
One faith, one God, Peace on earth,
One mind, one voice Throughout the universe
When all hearts sing as one,
God’s will on earth is done!
Among Jehovah’s Witnesses,
unity isn’t just an ideal.
It’s a reality!
Whether we’re gathering at a convention
or helping each other in a crisis,
our love and unity are so clear to see.
And just imagine what it will be like
when God’s will for the earth is fully accomplished
and we’ll be at unity with literally everyone on earth.
In this program, we’ve seen how important it is
for our love for the truth to permeate our lives.
That love moves us to hold to God’s standards
and make them our own,
to help interested ones
by making effective return visits,
and to remain united at all times.
When you hear the word “paradise,”
what do you think of?
For many, it might bring to mind
the tropical beauty found in Fiji
—the location for this month’s video postcard.
Fiji is made up
of more than 300 islands
in the South Pacific Ocean,
about 100 of which are inhabited.
On those islands you’ll find lush rain forests,
dry grasslands,
and pristine lagoons ringed by coral reefs.
If you travel inland, the terrain is steep and rugged,
with peaks over 1,300 meters high.
That’s more than 4,200 feet.
In this beautiful setting,
there are 3,186 publishers
preaching the good news
to nearly one million people.
On the small island of Koro,
which lies between Fiji’s two main islands,
our brothers cover much of the territory on foot.
To reach some outlying areas,
they may hire a truck,
allowing older and younger ones to travel to different villages
to have a share in the ministry.
When they’re not in the ministry,
many in the congregation support their families through farming.
Others engage in the traditional Fijian art
of mat making.
The mats are woven from the long, narrow leaves of the pandanus,
a tree native to the tropics.
The leaves are dried,
dyed by burying them in the mud,
and then softened for weaving.
Selling the mats
helps many families pay for travel to circuit assemblies
and regional conventions.
That trip involves a 12-hour boat ride
over notoriously rough seas
to Viti Levu,
Fiji’s largest island.
Back in 2016,
Cyclone Winston ravaged Fiji.
At the time,
it was the most powerful storm ever recorded
in the Southern Hemisphere.
In the small village of Naqaidamu,
most of the homes were virtually flattened
and our brothers and sisters lost almost everything they had.
The only building that survived was the Kingdom Hall.
But a village chief, aware of the Witnesses’ good reputation,
granted them a block of land
right around the Kingdom Hall
to rebuild all their homes.
Local brothers worked with disaster relief volunteers
to build 14 new homes
to house the entire congregation.
The Kingdom Hall at Naqaidamu
is entirely solar powered,
and the local brothers make good use of technology at the meetings
and in the field.
The 38 publishers
of the Naqaidamu Fijian Congregation
would like to pass on their loloma  —that’s Fijian for love—
to all in their spiritual family.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

问题是失足真的有那么严重吗？
请想象一下
如果我们走在崎岖不平
或者有许多台阶的路上
我们迈了一步，一脚踩空了
扭伤了脚或者摔倒了
相信我们那时候就会理解
失足可能会产生多么严重的后果
相信你们这些喜欢打篮球的年轻弟兄
都能理解
如果一个人在篮球场上不小心失足了
那就有可能要拄着拐杖好几个星期
所以，一次失足完全有可能导致严重的后果
这里翻译成“失足”的希腊语词
有许多不同的含意
它可以指轻微的过犯
但也可以指严重的过犯
也就是严重的罪
在今天经文的评论中
加拉太书6:1指的是严重的过犯
所以，失足这个词可以指两种情况
继续往下看
经文说“不知不觉失足了”
这意味着什么呢？
这里的希腊语词
表明
这不是故意犯罪
这就好比一个人在出门前
并没有打算犯严重的罪
但后来他却犯了罪
他犯的罪显然不是蓄意的
这也出乎他的意料
也许他跟一些不良的友伴在一起
突然之间他就做了一些他本来没想做的事情
他不是蓄意去做的
但这并不意味着罪不严重
这只意味着他不是蓄意去做这件事的
不过，他是可以得到帮助的
脚注说“受神圣力量引导而有资格的人”
我们留意上下文就会发现
加拉太人可以明白经文指的是什么
使徒保罗概述了神圣力量果实的九个方面
所以经文说的资格一定跟这些果实有关
就像刚才评论的弟兄说的那样
提供帮助的人需要受到神圣力量的激励
而不是出于
本能的反应
或者出于怒气、批评以及指责的态度
所以，我们必须受到神圣力量的感动
才能向人提出忠告
接下来有一个词很有意思
经文用的是“设法纠正他”
“设法”
相信你不会在许多圣经版本中找到这个词
我了解到，除了新世界译本
只有一个版本用了这个词
大部分的圣经译本都遵循了《英王钦定本》
说的是
“你们属灵的人，就当把他挽回过来”
这里的希腊语词可以指两种情况
既可以指设法这样做，也可以指直接做
翻译员必须作出选择
新世界圣经翻译委员会
选择加上“设法”这个词
为什么呢？
他们看出，虽然一个人会设法帮助别人
但最终结果取决于那个被帮助的人
他真的想改变吗？
所以，这样的帮助可能有效果，也可能没有
也许因为耶和华见证人
在提出劝告和帮助方面比其他人做得更多
所以翻译委员会认为
加拉太书6:1有必要加上“设法”这个词
这就好像一个人走着走着突然失足了
失足可能会导致怎样的结果呢？
他的骨头可能会错位
这就引出了“纠正”这个词
刚才的经文说：“设法纠正他”
也许大家知道
这个词是一个医学术语
意思是把错位的骨头复位
这一点与经文描述的情况非常一致
一个人走着走着，失足跌倒了
某些关节错了位
所以必须把它复位或者矫正才行
现在让我们再来看看前面一句话
“就要用温和的态度”
这是很好的提醒
因为有些需要被劝告的人做了一些
让长老们感到恶心的事情

他们会通过祷告求神圣力量
神圣力量果实的一个方面是什么？

ko.text: 성경은 모든 사람을 위한 하느님의 소식이 담겨 있는
하지만 성경의 모든 기록은 조화를 이루며
필자들의 정신에 자신의 생각을 넣어 주셨습니다.
따라서 “모든 성경은 하느님의 영감을 받은 것입니다.”
첫 다섯 권은 모세 오경이라고도 불리는데,
고대 이스라엘 민족의 초기 역사를 다룹니다.
이스라엘 민족이 약속의 땅으로 들어간 일,
하느님께 불충실하여 그로 인해 유배된 일,
그 후 고국으로 돌아오기까지의 일들을 다룹니다.
생활에 적용할 수 있는 지혜가 들어 있습니다.
하느님의 백성을 위한 지침과 경고가 나옵니다.
예수의 지상 생애와 봉사에 대한 기록이 담겨 있습니다.
성경은 그 이름을 어떤 이름보다도 많이,
여호와의 목적은 지성 있는 모든 창조물이
그분의 통치 아래 영원히 사는 것입니다.
여호와의 주권, 즉 그분의 통치할 권리에
왕국을 통해 자신의 통치권을 회복하시는 것이
한편 여호와께서는 구원자 즉 메시아를 통해
메시아는 하느님의 왕국의 왕이 될 것이었습니다.
영의 몸을 가진 하느님의 아들 예수께서
예수께서는 하느님의 주권을 지지하지 않는 자들 모두를
예수 그리스도가 다스리는 하늘 왕국을 통해
성경의 각 책이 어떤 관련이 있는지

en.text: An introduction to the Bible.
The Bible is a collection of ancient writings, or books,
that contain God’s message for all people.
This message was put down in writing
by approximately 40 different men.
It was written in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek
using Hebrew letters and Greek letters.
The writers came from many different backgrounds
and lived in various places throughout the ancient Near East
and southern Europe.
Yet everything in the Bible harmonizes
—there are no contradictions.
By various means, God put his thoughts
into the minds of these writers.
That is why the Bible says that “all Scripture is inspired of God.”
Bible writing began in 1513 B.C.E.
It continued for the next 1,600 years.
The last books of the Bible to be written
were completed about 98 C.E.
The Bible’s 66 books
are grouped into two main sections:
the Hebrew Scriptures,
often called the Old Testament,
and the Christian Greek Scriptures,
commonly called the New Testament.
The Hebrew Scriptures make up the first 39 books of the Bible.
The Pentateuch, or first five books,
describe the creation of all things
and the founding of the ancient nation of Israel.
The historical books show how,
after the nation of Israel enters the Promised Land,
Israel is unfaithful to God
and is taken into exile but eventually returns to its homeland.
The poetic books feature sacred songs
and practical wisdom for daily living.
The prophetic books foretell future events
and contain instructions and warnings for God’s people.
The last 27 books of the Bible make up the Christian Greek Scriptures.
First, there are the four Gospels
—a history of Jesus’ earthly life and ministry.
Then Acts of Apostles
narrates the history of the early Christian congregation.
There are 21 letters that contain practical counsel
and encouragement for Christians.
The last book, Revelation,
contains a series of prophetic visions.
In the Bible, God identifies himself as the Creator,
outlines his purpose,
and reveals his personal name, Jehovah
—shown here in ancient Hebrew lettering.
Did you know?
Unlike any other book,
the Bible magnifies God’s name, Jehovah.
It mentions his name over 7,000 times,
more than any other name.
Jehovah’s purpose is for all intelligent creatures
to live forever under his rulership.
But early in human history,
Jehovah’s sovereignty, or right to rule,
was challenged
by a rebellious spirit creature called Satan,
who spoke by means of a snake.
How Jehovah will clear his name
and restore his rulership by means of his Kingdom
is the theme of the Bible.
To answer Satan’s accusations,
Jehovah allows humans to pursue their own course.
Centuries of disastrous human rule follow.
Meanwhile, Jehovah arranges to accomplish his purpose
by means of a Savior —the Messiah—
who will eventually become King of God’s Kingdom.
In time, Jehovah reveals
who this Messiah will be.
Jesus, a spirit son of God,
is miraculously born as a human.
He teaches people about Jehovah
and sacrifices his life to save mankind.
God then resurrects Jesus
back to heavenly life.
The Bible says that Jesus rids the heavens
of all those who do not support God’s sovereignty.
As King of God’s Kingdom,
Jesus is joined by 144,000 corulers,
“who have been bought from the earth.”
God’s Kingdom will restore the earth to ideal conditions.
Jehovah’s purpose will be fulfilled:
All faithful intelligent creatures will unitedly worship him forever
as their one true God and Sovereign.
As you read and study the Bible,
note its internal harmony and practical wisdom
as well as how each book contributes to its overall theme:
the vindication of Jehovah’s name,
which will be accomplished by means of his heavenly Kingdom
in the hands of his only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ.

cn.text: 圣经是由许多经卷集合而成的
里面记载了上帝给全人类的信息
圣经是由大约40个人
以希伯来语、阿拉米语以及希腊语写成的
运用的是希伯来语和希腊语字母
写圣经的人来自不同的背景
也生活在不同的地方
有些住在古代的近东
有些在欧洲南部
虽然如此
圣经的信息首尾一贯、没有矛盾
上帝通过不同的方式把他的想法传达给这些写圣经的人
因此可以说“圣经全都是上帝指引人写下来的”
圣经写作始于公元前1513年
写作时间长达1600多年
最后几卷书是在大约公元98年完成的
圣经共有66卷书
可以分为两个部分
《希伯来语经卷》，也称《旧约》
以及《希腊语经卷》，也称《新约》
圣经的头39卷书属于《希伯来语经卷》
头五卷书，又称摩西五经
讲述了从创世到古代以色列国建立的记载
接下来的历史书
描述了以色列人进入上帝承诺赐予的土地
后来他们对上帝不忠，结果被流放
但最终返回故土
接下来的部分是神圣的歌集和智慧之言
先知书记录了跟上帝子民有关的预言
也包含了一些指引和警告
后27卷书属于《希腊语经卷》
首先是四福音书
记录了耶稣的生平事迹和传道工作
使徒行传记载了关于早期基督徒会众的历史
接下来是写给基督徒的21封书信
里面有鼓励和劝勉的话
最后一卷书是启示录
记录了一连串有预言意义的异象
上帝通过圣经告诉我们他是创造主
他的旨意是什么，以及他的名字耶和华
你在这里看到的是上帝的名字
是用古希伯来语拼成的
你知道吗？
在所有书中
只有圣经强调了上帝的名字耶和华
耶和华这个名字出现了7000多次
远远超过其他名字
耶和华原本的旨意
是要天使和人类在他的统治下永远活下去
不过，在人类的历史初期
上帝的至高统治权被一个叛逆的天使质疑
他就是撒但，他还通过一条蛇说话
但是耶和华会通过天上的王国
维护他的圣名和至高统治权
这就是圣经的主题
为了回答撒但的质疑
耶和华允许人类自行统治
几千年下来，事实证明
人类的统治彻底失败
为了实现自己的旨意
耶和华上帝安排了一位救主，他就是弥赛亚
他会成为上帝王国的君王
后来耶和华逐步透露了弥赛亚是谁
上帝施行奇迹
让他的一个灵体儿子耶稣降世为人
他在地上时教导人们认识耶和华
还为了拯救人类，牺牲了自己的生命
上帝后来将他复活到天上
圣经提到
耶稣把那些不支持上帝统治的灵体从天上赶了出去
作为上帝王国的君王
耶稣会跟14万4000人一起统治
这些人都是“从地上买来的”
上帝的王国会将地球恢复成最佳的状态
耶和华的旨意会彻底实现
天上地上会团结起来
一起崇拜这独一的真神、至高的主宰耶和华

title: M. 스티븐 레트: 위대한 선생님을 본받으십시오

ko.text: 또 많은 사람을 먹이고 사람들을 부활시키셨습니다.
그분이 주로 전파하고 가르치는 데 노력을 쏟으셨기 때문입니다.
예수께선 그러한 기적이 일시적인 유익을 줄 뿐이라는 걸 아셨습니다.
누군가를 악귀에게서 풀어 주거나 치료하거나 먹이거나 부활시킨다 해도
그럼 어떻게 영원한 유익을 줄 수 있으셨나요?
그렇게 하는 유일한 방법은 그분의 아버지이신 여호와에 관해 가르치는 것이었습니다.
그 지식이 사람들의 생명을 구할 것이었죠.
그분은 요한 17:3에서 하신 이러한 말씀이 참되다는 걸 잘 아셨죠.
‘영원한 생명에 이르는 길은 오직 한 분의 참하느님이신 아버지와 그분이 보내신 예수 그리스도를 알아 가는 것입니다.’
네, 예수께선 놀라운 기적을 많이 행하셨지만,
그분은 주로 전파하고 가르치는 일에 초점을 맞추셨고
그로 인해 인류 역사상 가장 위대한 선생님이 되셨습니다.
한번은 경비병들이 그분을 잡으러 왔을 때
그들은 “이제까지 그 사람처럼 말한 사람은 아무도 없었습니다”라고 말했죠.
그들은 예수의 가르침에 깊은 감명을 받아 그분을 체포할 수 없었습니다.
큰 무리가 여러 날 동안 먹지도 않고 그분을 따라다닌 적도 있었죠.
사도 바울이 한밤중까지 연설을 아주 길게 했다고 알려 줍니다.
어쩌면 자기 책임도 좀 있다고 생각했을 수 있죠.
하지만 바울은 위대한 선생님만큼 잘 가르치진 못했습니다.
한 형제가 제게 농담으로 한 말이 생각나는데요.
푹 자고 개운하게 일어날 수 있거든요.”
네, 바울과 같이 우리 중 그 누구도 위대한 선생님이신 예수만큼 잘 가르칠 수 없습니다.
그런데 베드로 전서 2:21은 뭐라고 알려 주죠?
완벽할 순 없어도 우리가 할 수 있는 한
하지만 특히 곧 졸업하실 길르앗 학생 여러분들은
전파하고 가르치는 일을 최우선 순위에 두어야 합니다.
우리는 최선을 다해 가르치는 기술을 향상시켜야 합니다.
오늘 이 연설에서 다루는 대부분의 내용은
하지만 그중 많은 부분은 개인을 가르치거나 회중에서 가르칠 때도 적용할 수 있을 것입니다.
특히 형제 여러분은 여호와의 양을 개인적으로 가르치거나 회중 집회 때 연단에서 가르칠 때
예수께서 가르칠 때 사용하셨던 방법을 본받기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
그러면 예수께서는 어떻게 위대한 선생님이 되셨습니까?
성경에서는 그분이 셀 수 없이 오랜 기간 동안
“숙련된 일꾼”으로 여호와 곁에 있으면서 아버지를 주의 깊이 관찰하고 본받았다고 알려 줍니다.
그렇게 하면서 훌륭하게 가르치는 기술을 얻게 되셨죠.
가장 위대한 선생님께 배워 자신도 위대한 선생님이 된 것입니다.
예수께선 하늘의 아버지께 배웠고, 그 모든 영광을 그분께 돌렸습니다.
자신의 말하고 가르치는 능력에 대해 어떻게 아버지께 합당한 영광을 돌렸는지 보시죠.
“내가 아무것도 내 뜻대로 하지 않는다는 것을 알게 될 것입니다.
나는 아버지께서 가르쳐 주신 대로 말합니다.”
네, 예수께선 아버지를 본받으셨고, 우린 예수를 본받기를 원합니다.
그럼 예수께서 배워 사용하신 가르치는 방법들에는 어떤 것들이 있습니까?
첫째로, 그분은 열정과 확신을 가지고 가르치셨습니다.
“그분이 서기관들과는 달리 권위 있게 가르치셨기 때문이다.”
네, 가르칠 때 권위, 열정, 확신이 있으셨죠.
따라서 우리가 봉사에서나 연단에서 가르칠 때
열정이 없다면 듣는 사람들이 배우는 내용에 어떻게 열정을 갖겠습니까?
우리는 가르칠 때 성의 없어 보인다는 인상을 주기를 원하지 않습니다.
방 안에서 한 사람이 하품을 하면 곧 모두가 하품을 하죠.
성의 없는 가르침도 그와 같을 수 있습니다.
그렇다고 너무 과장된 느낌으로 말하지 않도록 조심해야 합니다.
마치 사람들 앞에서 연극이라도 하는 것처럼
너무 과한 몸동작이나 얼굴 표정을 지어서 그런 느낌을 주는 일이 없도록 말입니다.
우리 자신에게 주의를 끌 수 있기 때문입니다.
이제 예수께서 사용하신 두 번째 방법을 생각해 보겠습니다.
“[여호와께서는] 내 귀를 깨우셔서 가르침받은 자처럼 듣게 하신다.
주권자인 주 여호와께서 내 귀를 열어 주시니, 나는 거역하지도 않고 등을 돌리지도 않았다.”
여호와께서 귀를 열어 주시고 잘 듣도록 훈련을 베푸셨습니다.
그래서 예수께서는 이 땅에 오셨을 때 어린 시절부터 계속해서 잘 들으셨습니다.
요셉과 마리아는 예수를 3일간 찾은 끝에 마침내 발견합니다.
기록에 따르면 성전에서 “교사들 가운데 앉아서” 그들의 말을 듣기도 하고 그들에게 질문을 하기도 했습니다.
따라서 그분이 30세에 제자 삼는 활동을 시작했을 때 잘 듣는 습관이 몸에 배어 있었습니다.
그러니까 그분은 그 누구보다 알려 주실 게 많았지만,
잠시 멈추어 사람들이 의견을 말하게 하고 그들의 말을 들어 주는 것이 중요하다는 점을 아셨습니다.
특히 여러분은 졸업한 후에 알려 줄 게 많을지 모릅니다.
봉사에서 짝이 집주인과 대화할 때가 있는데요.
공감한다는 뜻으로 고개를 자주 끄덕일 수 있을 것입니다.
“흥미롭네요”와 같은 말을 해 줄 수도 있죠.
무슨 뜻인지 다시 물어볼 수도 있습니다.
따라서 봉사할 때 집주인에게 말하든 짝으로 옆에 서 있든
길거리에 무슨 일이 있는지 쳐다보고 있다면 어떨까요?
이보다 주위를 더 산만하게 만드는 일은 없을 겁니다.
두 번째, 세 번째 방법이 서로 관련이 있죠?
상대방의 생각을 더 많이 들을 수 있으니까요.
그런데 만약 우리가 질문을 잘 사용하려 하지 않는다면 어떻게 될 수 있을까요?
우리만 계속 말해서 상황을 통제하려고 한다면요?
물론 우리만 계속 말을 하는 게 효과적이진 않지만 그렇게 하는 게 더 쉽다고 생각할 수 있죠.
집주인에게 질문을 하고 대답을 듣는 것은 길쭉한 타원형의 럭비공을 튕기는 것과 같습니다.
둥근 농구공은 어디로 튈지 알 수 있죠.
하지만 사람들은 럭비공처럼 우리의 질문에 다양한 반응을 보일 수 있습니다.
여러분은 그들의 반응에 맞추어 기꺼이 잘 대처할 수 있어야 합니다.
어떤 사람들은 예상치 못한 답변을 피하려고 말을 혼자 다 하죠.
하지만 그렇게 하는 건 위대한 선생님을 본받아 질문을 사용해 가르치는 것에 비할 때
그다지 효과적이라고 말할 수 없을 것입니다.
여러분은 수업 시간에 질문을 잘하는 것이 중요하다는 걸 느끼셨을 겁니다.
강사들이 질문을 잘 사용하니까 수업 내용을 이해하기가 훨씬 쉬우셨을 겁니다.
질문을 능숙하게 사용하는 것이 더 효과적인 이유는 무엇일까요?
한 가지는 듣는 사람을 대화에 참여시킬 수 있기 때문입니다.
이야기를 듣기만 하는 것과 대화에 참여하는 것 중에
또 다른 점은 그 사람에 대한 중요한 정보를 얻을 수 있다는 것인데,
그러면 그 사람을 더 잘 도울 수 있죠.
어떤 질문을 해 볼 수 있을까요?
예를 들어 예수께서는 마태복음 18:12에서 이렇게 질문하셨습니다.
어떤 사람에게 양 100마리가 있는데 그중 한 마리가 길을 잃는다면 …”
사람들은 자기 생각을 이야기하면서 더 즐겁게 대화하게 될 겁니다.
답을 고를 수 있는 질문을 사용할 수도 있을 것입니다.
그렇게 하면 집주인이 대답하기가 더 쉬울 수 있죠.
예를 들어 예수께서는 마태 17:25에서 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다.
“시몬, … 땅의 왕들이 누구에게서 관세나 인두세를 받습니까?
우리가 사용하는 전도지들 다수가 선택형 질문으로 되어 있습니다.
그들과 대화를 계속 이어 나갈 수 있습니다.
예를 들어 상대방이 당신들은 예수를 안 믿는다고 한다면 물어보는 겁니다.
이런 단순한 질문들을 하면 대화가 계속되고
그 사람을 돕는 데 필요한 중요한 정보를 얻을 수도 있습니다.
한 형제는 파이오니아 학교 때 이 질문들이 중요하다는 점을 강조받았습니다.
그는 봉사 중에 한 여자를 만났고, 여자는 이렇게 말했죠.
그러면 성서 연구를 사회할 때 생각을 자극하는 질문을 어떻게 사용할 수 있습니까?
새로운 연구용 서적에는 생각을 자극하는 질문이 많이 있습니다.
때로는 부가적인 질문들을 해야 할 수도 있습니다.
잘 가르치는 연구 사회자는 성서 연구 때 질문 형태로 말한다는 것을 기억하십시오.
저도 그렇게 하기 위해 노력을 많이 했습니다.
내가 말하려고 했던 걸 연구생이 말하게 해 보는 거야.’
그렇게 하는 게 더 효과적이지 않을까요?
보통 연구생에게 성구를 설명해 주는 것보다
연구생이 직접 성구를 설명하게 하는 것이
얼른 뭔가를 말해야겠다는 생각이 들지 모릅니다.
가장 위대한 선생님께 배우신 예수께서는 가르칠 때 비유를 효과적으로 사용하셨습니다.
그분의 가르침에서 비유는 강력한 힘을 발휘했습니다.
마태 13:34은 그분이 ‘비유가 아니면 말씀하지 않으셨다’고 알려 줍니다.
예수께서는 사용하고자 하는 비유를 즉석에서 생각해 내셨을까요?
좋은 비유를 빨리 생각해 내는 데 도움이 되었을 겁니다.
하지만 그분은 비유를 효과적으로 사용하는 능력을 발전시키기 위해 노력하셨던 것 같습니다.
예를 들어, 그분은 양 떼를 돌보는 목자를 보고 이렇게 묵상하셨을지 모릅니다.
‘어떻게 이 상황을 활용해서 중요한 진리를 가르칠 수 있을까?’
또한 그분은 그물을 내리고 있는 어부들이나
탑을 짓고 있는 인부들을 봤을 때도
‘어떻게 이런 상황들을 비유로 들어 중요한 진리를 가르칠 수 있을까?’
그분은 새, 백합, 등불, 가죽 부대,
간단한 것들을 보고서도 이렇게 생각하셨을 겁니다.
‘어떻게 이 간단한 것들을 사용해 중요한 진리를 가르칠 수 있을까?’
그래서 그분의 비유는 큰 힘이 있었죠.
우리 주변에는 좋은 비유로 사용할 수 있는
얼마 전에 한 형제가 아기를 보았는데
‘그리스도교국 사람들을 묘사할 때 저 비유를 잘 사용할 수 있겠어.
그 사람들은 자기들이 배우는 것에 아무런 영적 영양분이 없는데도 그냥 만족하잖아.
하지만 우린 그에 만족하지 못하는 사람들을 찾고 있어.
자기들의 영적 필요를 느끼는 사람들 말이야.’
조심해야 할 점들도 몇 가지 있는데요.
비유가 너무 길거나 복잡해서는 안 된다는 것입니다.
효과가 있으려면 비유가 청중에게 친숙하고 딱 맞는 것이어야 한다는 점입니다.
호주의 일부 지역에서는 좋은 비유가 될 수 있겠죠.
그 지역 사람들은 수컷 오리너구리의 특징을 잘 알고 있습니다.
무해하고 순진해 보여도 뒷발에 며느리발톱과 연결된 독샘이 있다는 걸 말이죠.
따라서 해롭지 않아 보여도 아주 위험합니다.
정말 큰 효과를 발휘할 수 있습니다.
생각과 행동을 변화시키도록 마음을 움직일 수도 있죠.
좋은 비유는 여러 해가 지나도 기억이 납니다.
가장 위대한 선생님에게서 배우신 네 가지 가르치는 방법을 살펴보았는데요.
우리는 그 방법들을 최선을 다해 따르기를 원하죠.
여러분이 앞으로 섬기게 될 회중과 구역에서
그분의 가르치는 방식을 따라야겠다는 마음이 더욱 강해지셨을 겁니다.
효과적인 비유를 사용하기 위해 노력하도록 합시다.
이와 같은 가르치는 기술들을 사용하기 위해 열심히 노력한다면
훨씬 더 능숙하게 듣는 사람의 마음을 움직이게 될 것입니다.
우리 형제 자매들의 생명이 달려 있습니다.
우리는 위대한 선생님에게서 배운 “가르치는 기술”을 사용해서

뿐만 아니라 우리 구역에 사는 마음이 정직한 사람들의 생명도 구하기를 원합니다.
너무 늦기 전에 그들을 찾아야 하죠.
우리는 위대한 선생님에게서 배운 가르치는 기술을 사용해서
여호와의 조직의 보호 아래로 들어오도록 그들의 마음을 움직여야 합니다.
사람들을 가르치는 방법을 배우기 위해 지금 우리가 하고 있는 일들은

우리는 부활되어 돌아오는 수많은 사람들을 가르칠 것입니다.
그러니까 지금은 몸을 풀고 있는 거죠.
얼마 안 있어 있게 될 사상 최대 규모의 교육 활동에 뛰어들기 위해서 말입니다.

여러분은 그에 대해 학교에서 많이 배우셨죠.
여호와께서 곧 졸업할 사랑하는 학생 여러분을 계속 축복해 주시기를 바랍니다.
여러분이 위대한 선생님을 본받기 위해 노력하면서
길르앗 학교에서 배운 훌륭한 가르침을 적용할 때

en.text: During his earthly ministry,
Jesus expelled demons.
He healed the sick.
He fed multitudes.
He even raised the dead.
But was he known
as the Great Demon-Expeller,
the Great Healer,
the Great Feeder-of-Multitudes,
or the Great Resurrector?
No.
But he was known as the Great Teacher.
Why?
Because he primarily focused his efforts
on the preaching and teaching work.
But now, why did he do this?
Well, he knew physical miracles
would only bring temporary benefits.
He knew ones freed from the demons,
ones that were healed, fed, and even resurrected
would eventually grow old and die.
So how could he help people permanently?
Well, he knew he could only do it
by teaching them the life-saving knowledge
about his Father, Jehovah.
He well knew the truthfulness
of what he stated as recorded at John 17:3:
‘This means everlasting life,
‘their coming to know you, the only true God,
and the one He sent, Jesus Christ.’
So even though he did many amazing things,
he focused primarily on the preaching and teaching work,
becoming the greatest Teacher ever to walk this earth.
In fact, when officers were sent to arrest him,
do you remember what happened?
They came back empty-handed.
Why?
Well, they said: “Never has any man spoken like this.”
They were so awestruck by his teaching,
they couldn’t even bring themselves to arrest him.
Large crowds would stick with him for days,
even without eating in order to listen to his teaching.
In contrast to the quality of Jesus’ teaching,
Acts chapter 20 tells us about the apostle Paul
giving a long, long talk.
And during that talk, you’ll remember that the young man Eutychus
sank into a deep, deep sleep
and even fell out of the third-story window of a building.
Now, of course, Paul resurrected him,
but probably he felt responsible
for putting him to sleep like that.
But, no offense to Paul, I’m sure he was doing the best he could.
But, obviously, his teaching
was not on a par with that of the Great Teacher.
And that makes me think of what a brother said to me in a teasing way.
He said: “Brother Lett, I always look forward to your talks.
I know I’m going to wake up totally refreshed.”
Well, it’s really true that none of us, like Paul,
can begin to match the quality of teaching of the Great Teacher.
But what are we told at 1 Peter 2:21?
We are told “to follow his steps closely.”
We can’t do it perfectly,
but we’re told to do it as closely as we can.
So that means all of us.
But especially as we’re talking to you,
dear Gilead students, soon-to-be-graduates,
you must make the preaching and teaching work
a priority.
And we must do our best
and you must do your best to improve in your teaching.
And how can you do that?
By imitating the Great Teacher.
During this talk (even though much of what we will talk about
will concern the public ministry),
what we’re going to discuss (much of it)
would be applicable to teaching on a personal level
and in the congregation.
So especially you brothers (but all of us),
want to imitate Jesus’ teaching methods
as we shepherd Jehovah’s sheep on a personal level
and as we do so on a congregational level
from the platform.
Now, here’s a question:
How did Jesus become the Great Teacher?
Well, the Bible tells us that for aeons and aeons of time,
as “a master worker” beside Jehovah,
he carefully observed and he imitated his Father.
And he thereby acquired amazing teaching skills.
He learned from the greatest Teacher.
And no wonder he became the Great Teacher.
He learned from his heavenly Father,
and he appropriately gave credit where it belongs.
Go to John chapter 8, please,
and notice how he gave the credit for his
speaking and teaching where it belongs.
John 8 and the B  part of verse 28:
“I do nothing of my own initiative;
“but just as the Father taught me,
I speak these things.”
Yes, he imitated his Father.
Now we want to imitate him.
But what specific teaching methods
did he utilize and did he learn from the greatest Teacher?
Well, let’s discuss four.
Now, one, he taught with enthusiasm
and conviction.
Matthew 7:29:
“For he was teaching them
“as a person having authority,
and not as their scribes.”
So doesn’t that indicate enthusiasm, conviction,
and authority is what he taught?
So if we’re not enthusiastic about what we teach
in the ministry or from the platform,
how could we expect our listeners to be enthusiastic about it?
So never would we want to come across halfhearted in our teaching.
Just like enthusiastic teaching is contagious,
halfhearted teaching is contagious too, isn’t it?
You could perhaps liken it to yawning.
One person yawns in a room, and pretty soon everybody is yawning.
And that could be the way with halfhearted teaching.
But as a caution, we don’t want to be
theatrical in our speaking.
That means we wouldn’t want to use extreme gestures
or dramatic expressions
—overly theatrical or even theatrical.
Why?
Because now you end up drawing attention to yourself
—don’t you?— rather than to what you’re teaching.
And that’s emphasis in the wrong place, isn’t it?
But now let’s talk about a second method the Great Teacher utilized.
He was a good listener.
Where did he learn this pattern of being a good listener?
Well, open up to Isaiah chapter 50, please,
and notice what is prophetically said about Jesus
and where he learned to be a good listener.
Notice in chapter 50 and right at the end of verse 4.
Let’s begin there: “He [Jehovah]
“awakens my ear to listen
“like the taught ones.
“The Sovereign Lord Jehovah has opened my ear,
“and I was not rebellious.
I did not turn in the opposite direction.”
So Jehovah opened his ear,
trained him to be a good listener, and he responded well, did he not?
And that’s why when he became a human,
from childhood on,
he continued his pattern of being a good listener, didn’t he?
Do you recall the account in Luke chapter 2
when Joseph and Mary finally found Jesus
after three days when he was only 12 years old?
Where did they find him?
It says that he was “sitting in the midst of the teachers” there in the temple
and listening to them
and then also asking them questions.
Then when he began his career as a disciple-maker at age 30,
it was second nature—wasn’t it?— to be a good listener.
Now, think of this: Even though he had more to say
than any other human has ever had to say,
he knew the value of pausing, drawing out his audience,
and then really listening to them.
And the same is true with us.
You may think especially after Gilead School that you’ve got a lot to say.
But if we’re going to imitate the Great Teacher,
we have to use self-control.
We have to pause and draw people out
and then really listen to them.
And when we serve as an assistant, which sometimes is half the time,
we want to be active listeners.
What does that mean (to be an active listener)?
Well, maybe you would nod periodically in agreement.
Or maybe you would add some little comment, such as, “Well, that’s very interesting.”
You might even ask for clarification.
People like to clarify what they’re saying.
It shows you’re really interested in what’s happening.
So whether we’re the one presenting
or the one who is an assistant, we want to be an active listener.
There’s probably nothing more distracting
than having your assistant playing with the dog
or maybe looking down the street to see what’s happening down the street.
Pretty soon, your householder is looking down the street to see what’s happening.
Be an active listener.
Well, let’s get our third method the Great Teacher used.
He used thought-provoking questions.
And methods two and three do go hand in hand —don’t they?—
because if you ask good questions,
you’re likely going to have more to listen to.
But what if some of Jehovah’s people tend to shy away,
perhaps, from using questions?
What if they just like to present information
and kind of control everything?
Well, if you think about it, it’s probably easier just to present information
even though it’s not nearly as effective.
When you ask questions
and then you get a response from the householder,
it’s kind of like bouncing a football.
Now, when you bounce a basketball, it’s predictable—isn’t it?—but not a football.
And it’s the same way with people.
They come back with all kinds of responses,
and you’ve got to be willing and able
to adapt according to their responses.
Some don’t like that uncertainty, so they would rather just present information.
But as we said, that’s not going to be nearly as effective
as those who have learned to imitate the Great Teacher
and effectively teach with questions.
Now, you Gilead students
have certainly seen the value of good questions during class.
It made it so much more enjoyable —didn’t it?—
and it enhanced your learning tremendously
when your instructors used these good questions.
Why is that more effective,
to proficiently use questions?
Well, for one thing, you involve your listener
in the conversation.
And what do you enjoy more?
Being given a sermon or being involved in a conversation?
The answer is obvious, isn’t it?
So involve the listener. It’s more enjoyable.
Another thing is that you gain valuable information about your listener,
which you can use to really help that one.
Well, what are types of questions we can use?
You can use “what do you think” questions.
Jesus used them.
As an example, Matthew 18:12:
“What do you think?
If a man has 100 sheep and one of them strays . . . ”
—we know the rest of the illustration.
But he started out with: “What do you think?”
And people generally like to give their opinion
and, in a sense, there’s no wrong answer —is there?—
because whatever they say, that’s what they think.
That’s what you asked for, right?
You asked, “What do you think?”
And people like to give their opinion.
It makes it enjoyable.
You can also use multiple-choice questions.
That sometimes makes it easier for the householder to answer.
Jesus gave an example in Matthew 17:25.
He said: “[Simon,] from whom do the kings of the earth
“receive duties or head tax?
From their sons or from the strangers?”
Many of our tracts use multiple-choice questions—don’t they?—
and we can effectively use those.
And if you think about it, the right question
can often enable us
to overcome potential conversation stoppers
and keep the conversation going.
For example, if a person says, “You people don’t believe in Jesus,”
we might say: “Well, may I please ask, why do you say that?
Did someone tell you that about us?”
Harmless questions can keep that conversation going
until you get valuable information
that perhaps you can use to help the person.
A person says, “I don’t believe in the Bible.”
“May I please ask why you feel that way?
May I ask how long you have felt that way?”
Keep it going.
One brother said that during pioneer school
he had those questions drilled into his head:
“Why do you feel that way?
How long have you felt that way?”
A woman came to the door and said, “I can’t talk; I’m pregnant.”
And he said, “Well, may I ask how long you’ve felt that way?”
Don’t do that.
Like we said before, you’ve got to be a good listener.
But then what about using thought-provoking questions
when conducting a Bible study?
As you well know, our new study book
is loaded with thought-provoking questions —isn’t it?—
and we certainly want to fully utilize them.
But occasionally we may need to add auxiliary questions.
But remember, most of what a good teacher says during a Bible study
is in the form of questions.
I know for myself, I’ve really tried hard to train myself
when I’m about ready to make a statement, say something.
‘Wait a minute; let me change that.
‘Let me change it to a question,
and let me draw out from the student what I was about to say.’
That’s going to be more effective, isn’t it?
It’s normally much better
than explaining a scripture
to a student to have the student explain it to you.
And don’t be afraid of a little silence.
If you ask a question and there is silence,
some of us think that we have to quickly fill in the gap by saying something.
But if they’re thinking, let them think.
Of course, you have to know your student.
If they have no clue what the answer is,
then don’t let them just sit there and sizzle.
Throw them a rope.
Throw them an auxiliary question.
But now we’re going to go to our fourth method
that the Great Teacher learned from the greatest Teacher:
He effectively used illustrations.
And that was certainly a powerful teaching tool indeed.
Matthew 13:34:
“Without an illustration
[Jesus] would not speak.”
But here’s a question:
Do you think that Jesus’ illustrations
were the product of spur-of-the-moment thinking?
Well, there’s no doubt about it that his perfect brain certainly helped
to be able to come up with amazing illustrations.
But nevertheless, the indication is
that he cultivated the ability
to effectively use illustrations.
If he saw a shepherd, for example, taking care of his sheep,
he likely meditated, ‘Now, how can I use this situation
to teach vital truths?’
He did the same when he saw, for example, a fisherman letting down his nets,
a farmer sowing seed,
or maybe builders constructing a tower.
‘How can I use this
to make powerful illustrations that teach vital truths?’
Even with simple items
like birds, lilies, a lamp on a lampstand,
a wineskin, leaven, a mustard seed, salt, the young child
he thought, ‘How can I use these simple items
to teach vital truths?’
And it was amazing how he did that.
And the same is true with us.
All around us, if we train ourselves to think that way,
there are circumstances, there are situations,
there are even items that we can use
and make them into powerful illustrations.
And we can powerfully elevate the quality of our teaching.
Now, here’s an example.
Some time ago, a brother noticed a little baby
with a pacifier.
This pacifier had been dipped in sugar water and put in the baby’s mouth.
And he was thinking: ‘You know, that’s a very good illustration
‘of many, many in Christendom.
‘They’re satisfied with what they have,
‘even though they have no real spiritual nourishment.
‘But we’re looking for those who are not satisfied,
those who are conscious of their spiritual need.’
And he was able to use that in a talk.
What are cautions regarding the use of illustrations?
Well, here are just a couple.
An illustration should not be too long or complicated.
If it is, simplify it or discard it.
That’s what the School Guidebook  tells us.
Here’s another caution: To be effective,
the illustration must be familiar to
and fit your audience.
For example, what if you used the illustration
that Satan’s system is like a male platypus?
Now, in some parts of Australia, that might be a good illustration
because they know a male platypus
looks harmless, he looks innocent,
but his hind legs are armed with ankle spurs
connected to venom glands.
So he looks harmless, but he could be very dangerous.
But that only works if you’re dealing with people that are familiar
with that particular animal.
But skillfully selected and used,
illustrations are very effective.
They stimulate thinking,
they arrest and hold attention,
they motivate the heart and conscience of our listener,
and they serve as powerful memory aids.
A good illustration
is going to be remembered years later
along with (and this is the important thing)
a point that it was designed to highlight.
Well, there we have four teaching methods
utilized by the Great Teacher
that he learned from the greatest Teacher, as we said.
And we want to do our best to copy, or imitate, his way of teaching.
And I know you Gilead students have an enhanced desire to do that
in the congregation and also in your territory
that you’re going to be working in.
So let’s work hard
to teach with enthusiasm and conviction,
let’s be a good listener,
let’s use thought-provoking questions,
and let’s use effective illustrations.
If you work hard, you dear students, almost graduates,
to employ these same teaching techniques,
then you’re going to be a lot more skillful
in reaching the hearts of your listeners.
And there’s a lot at stake, isn’t it?
I mean, if you think about it, the lives of our brothers and sisters are at stake.
And with the “art of teaching” learned from the Great Teacher,
we want to help as many of them as we can
to make it into that new world.
And then also the lives of honesthearted ones in our territory
hang in the balance, don’t they?
So we want to find them before it’s too late.
And using the art of teaching learned from the Great Teacher,
we want to motivate them to come into the safety
of Jehovah’s organization.
And if you think about it, it’s good to remember
that what we’re doing now in the way of learning to teach
is really preparing us
for the greatest teaching campaign
ever in all human history —the teaching of billions
who will be coming back in the resurrection.
You could say our work now is like a warm-up, isn’t it?
It’s a warm-up for that greatest teaching campaign
that is just around the corner.
So please continue to observe carefully
the teaching of the Great Teacher,
and you learned a lot about that in school, no doubt about it.
And may Jehovah continue
to bless you most beloved Gilead students, almost graduates.
May he bless you as you apply
all the wonderful things you’ve learned during this school,
and that includes learning
to imitate the Great Teacher.
