en.text: “This book of the Law
“should not depart from your mouth,
“and you must read it
“in an undertone day and night,
“in order to observe carefully
“all that is written in it;
“for then your way will be successful
and then you will act wisely.”
The Bible is enjoyed in many different formats,
one of which is the audio edition of the New World Translation.
“The good news according to Matthew.”
But how is it produced?
Let’s take a closer look.
When we first heard that the Governing Body wanted to record
the revised edition of the New World Translation,
I think all of us knew that it was going to be a big job.
The narrator is one voice,
and all the other characters
are different voices.
It’s not a dramatic Bible reading,
but it’s a reading with a high level of realism.
There’s no music, no sound effects, just voices.
We were surprised to find out how many characters there were in the Bible.
The Bible is a really big book.
I don’t think any of us realized how big of a job it would be.
This is not a little project.
This is huge!
The research really is one of the items
that is very fundamental, basic.
It is very important to get the facts together.
The Bible is true life;
it’s what really happened to real people.
We had to break down who the voices were.
And then we had to give each character a unique name to identify him.
If he’s not named in the Bible, . . .
We have to just give them descriptions that are in the context,
like “Third Jew” or “First in the crowd.”
We were given a room
—a fair-sized room.
And we used it to make a list
of all of the characters in all four Gospels.
We began with the book of Matthew,
and we had to determine the parallel accounts
between the different Gospel writers.
You’ll have to use the same voice for a character.
If he appears in one book, he needs to be the same voice in the other books.
Like in Matthew chapter 21,
we have this report where Matthew simply says,
well, the disciples say that ‘the fig tree has withered.’
But who are the disciples?
Did they all say it at the same time?
So if you check in Mark, for example, Mark is very specific.
He says that Peter said: “The fig tree . . . has withered.”
The Art Department took those maps and charts in the appendix
and blew them up into poster size for us as we were deciding
who said what and where they were and how to name the characters.
It was very helpful to have that.
All that gets put into a database, what kind of attributes they had
—age, where they were from,
what kind of traits they were expressing in their quotations.
When the Bible talks about Jehovah speaking,
well, was it really Jehovah himself who spoke?
Well, something we know is that at least
on three occasions it was Jehovah who spoke.
This was when Jesus was on earth.
We compiled most of the research,
and then it was forwarded on to Writing Research.
We have a large library here at Bethel
that is focusing especially on Biblical subjects.
And we’re using this quite a bit
because we need to make sure that what we say is solid.
We are a people for Jehovah, and we are really—
Everything we say, it’s based on the Bible.
We don’t want to read too much into Bible accounts.
And we don’t want to read it in a way that steers incorrectly.
To start with, Who’s at Bethel?
We have an audition bank
here in Audio/Video.
We poured through hundreds of auditions.
We had a brother from Africa that we auditioned over the Internet.
He’s sitting there reading into a mic;
I’m watching him.
By the time we tallied all of the characters for the entire Bible,
we realized we had about a thousand characters.
So a thousand voices that we’ll need to find.
There was a reading seminar at which we were taught
every aspect of reading.
And that was very effective because it reminded us of a lot of things:
dos and don’ts for effective reading.
It really gave me the confidence and understanding that I think I can do this.
Some of the roles are very small.
Those short, very short passages
—those one-sentence lines
that we would call a person in for—
were some of the hardest to coach.
When I initially was asked to participate in the Bible reading,
I was so excited.
And then I saw that it was one line, and I thought:
‘OK, well, it won’t be too bad. It will be easy.’
And then I listened to the Bible reading seminar,
and it really helped me to take it more seriously.
We would even ask the readers to study this over.
You only have one sentence, but study all about this character.
I read the chapter. I read the Insight  book.
And I realized that this is more
than just saying one line.
What we have found is that it’s a good idea
to provide the reader with a script that has been customized.
I have the word written out phonetically
so that you would know better how to pronounce it.
I would say, “Sulomon.”
Sulomon? Who’s he?
It’s that kind of thing.
So anyway, they helped you pronounce “Solomon.”
And they were very careful to make sure the pronunciation was accurate.
And that it would be consistent and accurate
all the way through the Bible reading from beginning to end.
So when the character comes in,
we try to help them to kind of think about the context.
Of course, they have already done that in their own research and practice
but a little bit more about, maybe, the motive of the character.
How would they have felt in this particular instance?
How would they say this line?
But we also want to make sure the brothers and sisters feel really comfortable,
and it often takes a long time to get them to relax.
In the control room,
there are basically three roles and the reader.
The follower is responsible to make sure that all of the content is there
—to make sure that no words are missing.
During the recording, the audio engineer is listening for anything
that will distract the listeners: stomach noises or shirt noise
or if the brother is wearing suspenders.
The coach is responsible for the quality of teaching.
I love watching the coach try to get the right emotion out of the reader.
So then, you might read a line,
and he’ll say, “Can you say that again with a smile?”
And it’s amazing because then it sounds more joyful.
And then once you capture the emotion, then it naturally comes out.
You’re not trying to copy what he’s told you to say.
What we usually have a person do is start with one emotion
—that you’re sad— and then add each emotion on top.
That ends up getting a very complex delivery of a line.
There are so many possible ways to say one line,
and I didn’t even realize how many.
You think you know how the character said it,
and then the coach will give you a suggestion.
So the editing process actually begins during the recording.
And then when we get done recording, perhaps a chapter,
we’ll take down the best takes of every verse
because the reader and the coach can then listen back and see,
“OK, do we like how it sounds?”
We use professional software to do the editing,
and that means we do all the spacing that’s needed;
we pull in all the characters for a specific chapter.
Because we record each voice individually,
it’s not a group of people around the microphone having the conversation.
So each character is done,
and then if there are multiple voices in a chapter,
then we pull them all together.
Once we started editing these chapters together,
a beautiful artwork of truth
as you’re seeing the context jump out,
and for us to then feel it
and move us as the reader of God’s Word,
hearer of God’s Word.
The comment I’ve heard over and over again is,
“It’s brought the Bible to life in my mind and heart.”
And it has encouraged us
to meditate deeper into God’s Word.
Having the different characters read the voices
is going to be such a comfort to all of us.
I think that this is really going to make Bible reading exciting.
So now the Bible is alive, and what a difference it makes!
I think they’re going to love it!

title: 기념식 아침 숭배—새뮤얼 F. 허드: 매년 “나를 기억하여 이 일을 계속 행하십시오” (누가 22:19)

ko.text: 전 세계에 계신 여호와의 백성과 또 함께하신 분들을 뵙게 되어 기쁩니다.
오늘 해가 지면 약 2천만 명의 사람들이 다양한 회중과 집단에서 그리고 개인적으로
예수의 죽음을 기념하기 위해 모일 것입니다.
이야기를 시작하기 전에 출판 위원회의 보조자이신 도널드 고든 형제가 오늘의 성구를 읽어 주시겠습니다.
2000만 명이 넘는 사람이 오늘 저녁에 모이는 이유는 무엇입니까?
한 가지 이유는 오늘의 성구인 누가 22:19의 말씀 때문이죠.
그때 예수께서는 그분의 죽음의 기념식을 제정하고 계셨습니다.
그분은 방금 누룩이 들지 않은 빵을 떼어 자리에 있는 각자에게 주셨습니다.
누룩이 들지 않은 빵은 예수의 완전하고 죄없는 몸을 상징했죠.
그분은 자신에게 믿음을 나타내는 모든 사람의 영원한 유익을 위해 죽으심으로 자신의 몸을 내주실 것이었습니다.
바로 이 시점에서 누가 22:19의 말씀을 하신 것입니다.
계속 포도주와 빵을 사용하여 예수의 죽음과 그것이 이룰 일을 기억하라는 것입니다.
그분이 하신 말씀 그대로 계속하라는 것이죠.
앞으로도 계속해서 그 일을 하라는 것입니다.
얼마나 자주 그 일을 하라는 뜻이었을까요?
어떤 종교에서는 매주 빵과 포도주를 먹습니다.
각 교회에서 얼마나 자주 이 의식을 행할지 결정하게 하는 종교도 있습니다.
그런가 하면 1년에 네 번 지키라고 가르치는 종교도 있죠.
그런데 왜 여호와의 증인은 다른 종교와는 다르게 1년에 단 한 번 예수의 죽음을 기념합니까?
사실 해마다 어떤 일이 있었던 바로 그 날짜에 그 일을 기념하는 것은 논리적입니다.
결혼기념일을 결혼 날짜가 아닌 다른 날 지키거나 1년에 여러 번 지키는 사람이 과연 있을까요?
분명 결혼기념일을 매주, 또는 매일 지키는 사람은 없을 겁니다.
흥미롭게도, 기념일에 해당하는 영어 단어는 어떤 중요한 사건이나 일이 일어난 특정한 날을
그런데 1년에 한 번 기념하는 것은 논리적일 뿐 아니라 성경에 근거한 것이기도 합니다.
예수께서는 사실상 이렇게 말씀하신 것이나 다름없습니다.
“나를 기억하여 [1년에 한 번, 내 죽음을 기념하는 날에] 이 일을 계속 행하십시오.”
1년에 단 한 번 기념해야 한다는 어떤 성경적인 근거가 있습니까?
누가복음 22장에 들어있는 오늘의 성구의 문맥을 함께 보시죠.
예수와 사도들이 그 날짜에 식사를 하려고 모인 원래 이유는 무엇이었을까요?
그 날은 당시의 유대력, 또는 음력으로 니산월 14일이었습니다.
“유월절 제물을 바쳐야 하는 무교절 날이 되자 예수께서는 베드로와 요한을 보내시며
당시 유대인의 법에 따라 예수께서는 1년에 한 번 충실하게 유월절을 지키셨습니다.
“시간이 되자, 그분이 사도들과 함께 식탁에 앉으셨다.
‘내가 고난을 당하기 전에 여러분과 함께 이 유월절 식사를 하기를 간절히 바랐습니다.
여러분에게 말하는데, 이것이 하느님의 왕국에서 성취될 때까지 내가 다시는 이 식사를 하지 않을 것이기 때문입니다.’
그분은 잔을 받으신 뒤 감사를 드리고 말씀하셨다.
방금 14절에서 17절을 읽어 본 것처럼, 예수께서는 기념식을 제정하기 바로 전에 유대인의 유월절을 지키셨던 것입니다.
1세기 당시에는 유월절 식사에 참석한 사람들에게 관례에 따라 네 잔의 포도주를 돌렸습니다.
17절에 나오는 잔은 아마도 유월절을 기념하는 세 번째 잔이었을 것입니다.
그분은 자신의 죽음의 기념식을 제정하기 위해 네 번째 잔을 남겨 두셨을 것입니다.
그러면 유월절은 얼마나 자주 지켜야 했습니까?
출애굽기 12장을 보면 여호와께서는 이스라엘이 이집트를 떠나도록 준비시키실 때
그 중요한 일을 기념하도록 유월절을 제정하셨습니다.

내가 날마다 성전에 앉아서 가르쳤는데도, 여러분은 나를 붙잡지 않았습니다.
그러나 이 모든 일이 일어난 것은 예언자들의 글이 성취되기 위한 것입니다.”
그때에 제자들은 모두 그분을 버리고 달아났다.
역사상 가장 큰 두 가지 사랑이 표현되기까지 있었던 상황을 보여 주는 중요한 성구들이죠.
여호와와 예수께서는 과거 에덴동산에서 아담과 하와와 함께 시작된
마귀의 일을 없애기 위해 함께 협력하셨습니다.
기름부음받은 자이건 다른 양들이건 우리 모두는 완전한 인간이셨던 예수의 대속 희생 덕분에
영원한 생명을 누릴 놀라운 희망을 갖게 됐습니다.
우리 모두를 위한 예수의 죽음을 기념하는 뜻깊은 저녁이 되기를 진심으로 바랍니다.

en.text: I am delighted to address Jehovah’s people
and their friends worldwide today!
After sundown,
some 20 million of us will have gathered
in various congregations,
groups, and even as individuals
to commemorate the death of Jesus.
Before we begin our discussion,
we will have the text for today read
by Brother Don Gordon, a helper to the Publishing Committee.
Today is Tuesday, April 4.
“‘Keep doing this in remembrance of me.’
Why would over 20 million people gather together this evening?
One reason is our Scripture text for today,
Luke 22:19.
Jesus was in the process of inaugurating
the Memorial of his death.
He had just broken the unleavened bread
and passed it to each one present.
The unleavened bread pictured Jesus’ perfect, sinless body
that he would surrender in death
for the everlasting benefit to all exercising faith in him.
It is at this point that Jesus said the words
of Luke 22:19:
“Keep doing this in remembrance of me,”
meaning keep using the wine and bread
as the way to remember my death
and all that it will accomplish.
Why would he say that: “Keep doing this”?
He meant exactly what he said: “Keep doing this.”
Yes, keep doing it on into the future.
How often did he intend that we “keep doing” it?
Some religions partake of the bread and wine weekly.
They call it communion.
Other religions let the individual congregations determine
how often they would perform this activity.
Still others instruct that it should be done four times a year.
Why do Jehovah’s Witnesses remember Jesus’ death in this special way,
just once each year on the anniversary of Jesus’ death?
Well, there is some logic to celebrating an anniversary annually
on the precise date of the original event,
much like a wedding anniversary.
Why would you celebrate a wedding anniversary
on any other day of the year
or multiple times a year?
Certainly, you would not celebrate your wedding anniversary
every week or every day.
Interestingly, the English word “anniversary”
is defined as “the annual recurrence of a date
marking an event or occurrence of notable importance.”
Jesus’ death is certainly “of notable importance.”
However, not only is it logical to do so once a year
but there is a Biblical indication
that this is what Jesus was requesting,
in effect saying:
“Keep doing this
“[once a year on the anniversary of my death]
in remembrance of me.”
What is the Biblical indication
that it should be memorialized just once a year?
Let’s look at the context of our text for today
in Luke chapter 22.
Please locate that text.
Our day’s text is verse 19.
But what was the initial purpose
of Jesus and his apostles gathering together
for a meal on that date?
The date was Nisan 14
according to the Jewish, or lunar, calendar of that time.
Please look at Luke 22:7, 8.
It says:
“The day of the Unleavened Bread now arrived,
“on which the Passover sacrifice must be offered;
“so Jesus sent Peter and John, saying:
‘Go and get the Passover ready for us to eat.’”
According to Jewish law at the time,
Jesus had faithfully observed the Passover once each year.
Now read verses 14 through 17:
“So when the hour came,
“he reclined at the table
“along with the apostles.
“And he said to them:
“‘I have greatly desired
“‘to eat this Passover with you
“‘before I suffer;
“‘for I tell you,
“‘I will not eat it again
“until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.’
“And accepting a cup,
“he gave thanks and said:
“‘Take this and pass it from one to the other
among yourselves.’”
Just prior to instituting the Memorial,
Jesus celebrated the Jewish Passover, as we just read
in verses 14 through 17.
By the time of the first century,
it was the custom to pass four cups of wine
to those seated for the Passover meal.
The cup mentioned in verse 17
was likely the third cup of the Passover celebration.
Evidently, Jesus was saving the fourth cup
for instituting the Memorial of his death.
So the question is,
How often was the Passover to be celebrated?
In Exodus chapter 12,
when Jehovah was preparing the Israelites to depart Egypt,
he instituted the Passover
to remember this event of notable importance for the nation.
At Exodus 12:14,
Jehovah instructed Moses:
“This day will serve as a memorial for you,
“and you must celebrate it
“as a festival to Jehovah
“throughout your generations.
“As a lasting statute,
you should celebrate it.”
He repeated in verse 17:
“And you must keep this day
“throughout your generations
as a lasting statute.”
So it is that Jews observe the Passover
once a year “as a memorial”
on the annual anniversary of their Exodus from Egypt.
So after celebrating the last valid Jewish Passover,
when Jesus instituted the Memorial of his death
and he said “keep doing this,”
his apostles would have known the intent.
Instead of observing the Passover once a year on that date,
they would now remember the death of Jesus
once a year on that same date.
That seems pretty logical, straightforward,
and has a Scriptural precedent.
But many nominal Christian religions seem to think
that memorializing the event more often during the year
must be even better.
In part, this is because of a misunderstanding
of the intent of 1 Corinthians 11:25.
In most English translations of the Bible,
it is rendered something like this:
“Keep doing this, as often as you drink it,
in remembrance of me.”
Some feel that the word “often”
indicates that Christ’s death should be commemorated frequently
in the sense of as many times as possible.
The New World Translation also rendered the verse similarly
prior to the revised edition being released.
The wording is an accurate way of rendering the verse.
However,
its intent is easily misinterpreted by many.
For example,
just commemorating the Lord’s Evening Meal once a year
is often
when you consider that it is approaching 2,000 years
since Jesus instituted it.
That in itself is often.
But, more precisely,
in the context of 1 Corinthians 11:25, 26,
Paul was discussing, not how often,
but how the Memorial should be observed.
In the original language, he did not use the Greek word
that means “often,” or “frequently.”
Rather, he used a different Greek word
that means “as often as,”
or it could be expressed “whenever”
or “every time that you do.”
Paul was saying: ‘Every time that you do this,
you keep proclaiming the death of the Lord.’
To make that even clearer to the reader,
the revised New World Translation
now renders the text at 1 Corinthians 11:25 this way:
“Keep doing this, whenever you drink it,
in remembrance of me.”
And as discussed already,
Jesus intended that it be
a once-a-year replacement
for the annual Passover observance
on the anniversary of Jesus’ death.
To be clear,
following the process Jesus instituted with the bread and wine
just once a year
does not mean we only think
about Jesus’ death on one day of the year.
No!
Those of you
who are dedicated and baptized Witnesses of Jehovah know
that we think of Jesus’ sacrificial death
every day of the year.
It is mentioned in our regular congregation meetings
and in our family worship.
And every prayer we say
acknowledges Jesus’ presenting
the value of his sacrificial death
in our behalf.
At the end of every prayer, we acknowledge to God
that we are praying in Jesus’ name.
Amen.
Being imperfect,
we do not have direct access to Jehovah.
Instead, he readily accepts our prayer
if we say it
in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ.
Most of you viewing this program
are well-aware of the fact
that the Memorial is primarily
for those chosen by God for heavenly life.
It signifies their being party to the new covenant
to share in the Kingdom with Christ.
However, all who gather together tonight
will benefit greatly from being in attendance.
All of us are imperfect,
and we benefit from Jesus’ ransom sacrifice,
which is the basis for forgiveness of sins.
And all of us have the prospect
of everlasting life in the future,
whether that is in heaven for the few anointed ones
or in a paradise earth
for the millions of others serving Jehovah.
So only the few anointed ones
will actually partake of the bread and wine tonight.
Because of the high percentage of those in attendance with an earthly hope,
very few by comparison will partake of the emblems.
In most congregations, there will likely not be any partakers;
in others, maybe one or two.
If that is the case,
why do we pass the emblems to each one in attendance?
Why not just invite any of the anointed to the stage
to partake of the bread and wine?
It would save a lot of time
instead of passing the emblems to all in the audience.
The foremost reason the emblems are passed before all
is because that follows the pattern set by Jesus.
However, if an anointed one
makes clear his heavenly hope by partaking,
what about those of you
who pass the emblems by without partaking?
You too are going on public notice
that your hope is to live forever
in a marvelous paradise here on earth.
And think about it:
For humans, that is the best life ever!
It is what Jehovah originally intended for mankind
when he created the first couple in the garden of Eden.
What could be better for a human than that?
All of us eagerly look forward to the time soon to come
when the evil influence of Satan is taken away from the earth.
He and all of his demon followers
will be hurled into an abyss of inactivity
for 1,000 years.
The resurrected anointed ones
will share with Christ in bringing that about.
And those alive on earth during the Thousand Year Reign of Jesus
will share in bringing the earth back
to the condition Jehovah originally intended.
Extending our thoughts even further into the future,
after the Thousand Year Reign of Christ,
mankind will have reached perfection,
similar to Adam and Eve after their creation
and before their plunge into sin.
First Corinthians 15:24 says:
“Next, the end,
“when he hands over the Kingdom
to his God and Father.”
By then the Messianic Kingdom will have fulfilled its role
to have an earth filled with perfect people.
Then, after a final test by Satan,
any dissenters will be eliminated
and Satan and his demons
will be forever destroyed.
At that time, Jehovah’s original purpose for the earth
will be fully realized.
The entire planet will be full of beautiful people,
all worshippers of the Universal Sovereign,
our precious Father, Jehovah God.
Brother Gordon, will you please read the Watchtower  comments for today’s text?
“Jesus spoke to his 11 faithful apostles
“about two covenants, or agreements
“—the new covenant and the Kingdom covenant.
“These covenants opened up the way
“for those apostles and a limited number of others
“to become kings and priests in heaven.
“Only the anointed remnant, who are in these two covenants,
“may partake of the bread and the wine
“at the Memorial.
“Jehovah has given them a remarkable hope
“—to enjoy immortal and incorruptible life in heaven,
“to serve alongside the glorified Jesus Christ
“and the rest of the 144,000
“and, above all, to be in the very presence of Jehovah God!
“The anointed recognize
that they must remain faithful until their death.”
Thank you, Don.
For the past few days, our Bible reading has covered
the Bible accounts leading up to Jesus’ death.
We invite you to follow along with the reading for today.
The specific verses will appear on screen in your language.
Along with the reading, enjoy the new artwork
that has been prepared this year.
“On the first day of the Unleavened Bread,
“the disciples came to Jesus, saying:
“‘Where do you want us to prepare for you
“to eat the Passover?’
“He said:
“‘Go into the city to So-and-so
“‘and say to him, “The Teacher says:
“‘“‘My appointed time is near;
“‘“‘I will celebrate the Passover
“with my disciples at your home.’”’
“So the disciples did as Jesus instructed them
and prepared for the Passover.”
“The day of the Unleavened Bread now arrived,
“on which the Passover sacrifice must be offered;
“so Jesus sent Peter and John, saying:
“‘Go and get the Passover ready for us to eat.’
“They said to him:
“‘Where do you want us to get it ready?’
“He said to them:
“‘Look! When you enter into the city,
“‘a man carrying an earthenware water jar
“‘will meet you.
“‘Follow him into the house that he enters.
“‘And say to the landlord of the house,
“‘“The Teacher says to you:
“‘“‘Where is the guest room
“‘where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’”
“‘And that man will show you
“‘a large, furnished upper room.
“Get it ready there.’
“So they left and found it just as he had told them,
and they prepared for the Passover.”
“When evening came,
“he was reclining at the table with the 12 disciples.
“While they were eating, he said:
“‘Truly I say to you, one of you will betray me.’
“Being very much grieved at this,
“each and every one began to say to him:
“‘Lord, it is not I, is it?’
“In reply he said:
“‘The one who dips his hand with me into the bowl
“‘is the one who will betray me.
“‘True, the Son of man is going away,
“‘just as it is written about him,
“‘but woe to that man
“‘through whom the Son of man is betrayed!
“‘It would have been better for that man
if he had not been born.’
“Judas, who was about to betray him, replied:
“‘It is not I, is it, Rabbi?’
“Jesus said to him:
“‘You yourself said it.’
“As they continued eating, Jesus took a loaf,
“and after saying a blessing, he broke it,
“and giving it to the disciples, he said:
“‘Take, eat. This means my body.’
“And taking a cup, he offered thanks
“and gave it to them, saying:
“‘Drink out of it, all of you,
“‘for this means my “blood of the covenant,”
“‘which is to be poured out in behalf of many
“‘for forgiveness of sins.
“‘But I say to you:
“‘I will by no means drink again
“‘any of this product of the vine
“‘until that day when I drink it new with you
in the Kingdom of my Father.’
“Finally, after singing praises,
“they went out to the Mount of Olives.
“Then Jesus said to them:
“‘All of you will be stumbled
“‘in connection with me on this night,
“‘for it is written: “I will strike the shepherd,
“‘and the sheep of the flock will be scattered about.”
“‘But after I have been raised up,
“I will go ahead of you into Galilee.’
“But Peter, in response, said to him:
“‘Although all the others
“‘are stumbled in connection with you,
“I will never be stumbled!’
“Jesus said to him:
“‘Truly I say to you,
“‘on this night, before a rooster crows,
“you will disown me three times.’
“Peter said to him:
“‘Even if I should have to die with you,
“I will by no means disown you.’
“All the other disciples also said the same thing.
“Then Jesus came with them
“to the spot called Gethsemane,
“and he said to the disciples:
“‘Sit down here while I go over there and pray.’
“And taking along Peter
“and the two sons of Zebʹe·dee,
“he began to feel grieved
“and to be greatly troubled.
“Then he said to them:
“‘I am deeply grieved, even to death.
“Stay here and keep on the watch with me.’
“And going a little way forward,
“he fell facedown, praying:
“‘My Father, if it is possible,
“‘let this cup pass away from me.
“Yet, not as I will, but as you will.’
“He returned to the disciples
“and found them sleeping,
“and he said to Peter:
“‘Could you not so much as keep on the watch
“‘for one hour with me?
“‘Keep on the watch and pray continually,
“‘so that you may not enter into temptation.
“‘The spirit, of course, is eager,
“but the flesh is weak.’
“Again, a second time, he went off and prayed:
“‘My Father,
“‘if it is not possible for this to pass away
“‘unless I drink it,
“let your will take place.’
“And he came again and found them sleeping,
“for their eyes were heavy.
“So leaving them,
“he again went off and prayed for a third time,
“saying once more the same thing.
“Then he returned to the disciples and said to them:
“‘At such a time as this,
“‘you are sleeping and resting!
“‘Look! The hour has drawn near
“‘for the Son of man to be betrayed
“‘into the hands of sinners.
“‘Get up, let us go.
“Look! My betrayer has drawn near.’
“While he was still speaking,
“look! Judas, one of the Twelve, came
“and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs,
“sent from the chief priests
“and the elders of the people.
“Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying:
“‘Whoever it is I kiss, he is the one;
“take him into custody.’
“And going straight up to Jesus, he said:
“‘Greetings, Rabbi!’
“and gave him a tender kiss.
“But Jesus said to him:
“‘Fellow, for what purpose are you present?’
“Then they came forward and seized Jesus
“and took him into custody.
“But look! one of those with Jesus
“reached out his hand and drew his sword
“and struck the slave of the high priest,
“taking off his ear.
“Then Jesus said to him:
“‘Return your sword to its place,
“‘for all those who take up the sword
“‘will perish by the sword.
“‘Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father
“‘to supply me at this moment
“‘more than 12 legions of angels?
“‘In that case,
“‘how would the Scriptures be fulfilled
“that say it must take place this way?’
“In that hour Jesus said to the crowds:
“‘Did you come out to arrest me
“‘with swords and clubs as against a robber?
“‘Day after day I used to sit in the temple teaching,
“‘and yet you did not take me into custody.
“‘But all of this has taken place
“for the writings of the prophets to be fulfilled.’
Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.”
Those were significant verses leading up
to the two greatest acts of love of all time.
Jehovah and Jesus cooperated together to undo
the works of the Devil that were initiated
back in the garden of Eden with Adam and Eve.
Whether of the anointed or of the other sheep,
we all have the marvelous hope of everlasting life
based on the ransom sacrifice
of the perfect man Jesus.
We hope all of you enjoy your evening
commemorating Jesus’ death
in behalf of all of us!

cn.text: 我很高兴今天有机会
跟弟兄姐妹以及其他的朋友谈一谈
日落以后
在全世界将会有大约2000万人
纪念耶稣的死亡
有些人是自己一个人
有些人和小组或会众的弟兄姐妹在一起
但首先
我们会邀请
出版委员会助手唐纳德∙戈登弟兄
为我们读出今天的经文
4月4日星期二
“你们要不断这样做来纪念我”
路加福音22:19
为什么今天晚上
会有2000多万人聚集起来呢？
今天的经文，就是路加福音22:19
告诉我们其中一个原因
当时，耶稣正在创立纪念他死亡的聚会
他刚刚把无酵饼掰开
递给在场的每个人
无酵饼象征耶稣完美无罪的身体
耶稣会牺牲自己的生命
让所有对他有信心的人能够永远获益
就是在这个时候
耶稣说了路加福音22:19的话
意思就是
你们要用饼和酒来纪念我的死亡
和我的死亡成就的事
他为什么要说“要不断这样做”呢？
他要表达的意思就是要不断这样做
是的，之后也要继续这样做
但耶稣希望我们多么经常这样做呢？
有些教会每周都会吃饼喝酒
他们说这是圣餐
还有一些教会让每个教堂自己决定
多经常这样做
还有一些教会一年4次吃圣餐
为什么耶和华见证人
只是在耶稣牺牲生命的那一天
才纪念他的死亡呢？
这就跟我们只会在某件事情发生的那一天
纪念这件事一样
比如，结婚周年纪念日
你不会在一年其他时候庆祝结婚纪念日
也不会一年纪念很多次，对吗？
你也不会每一天
每个星期都庆祝你的结婚周年
实际上，按照字典的解释
“周年纪念”这个词
意思就是
每年在重要事件发生的这一天
举行纪念活动
耶稣的死亡绝对是重要的事件
另外
每年一次举行纪念活动
不仅仅合乎逻辑
而且按照圣经
这也是耶稣给我们的吩咐
耶稣相当于在说
“要不断地，每年在我死亡的这一天
这样做来纪念我”
每年一次纪念耶稣的死亡
有哪些圣经根据呢？
我们可以再看一下今天的经文
在路加福音22章
我们今天的经文是第19节
你记得
当天耶稣和他的门徒聚在一起吃晚餐
原本是为了什么目的吗？
按照犹太历
当天是尼散月14日
我们读一下路加福音22:7,8
经文说
耶稣每年一次
都按照摩西法典的规定守逾越节
我们再读一下14到17节的经文
就像14到17节的经文所说的
看来，耶稣在创立牺牲纪念聚会前
先庆祝了逾越节
在公元1世纪
犹太人在庆祝逾越节的时候
通常会喝4杯红酒
17节中提到的这杯红酒
看来是当天晚上逾越节晚餐中的第3杯
很显然
耶稣留着第4杯红酒
用来创立纪念他牺牲的聚会
那么
逾越节是多久庆祝一次呢？
在出埃及记12章
耶和华在带领以色列人离开埃及之前
他创立了逾越节
来纪念这个有重要意义的日子
在出埃及记12:14
耶和华吩咐摩西说
第17节的经文也说
由此可见，犹太人每年一次守逾越节
纪念他们摆脱奴役
从埃及出来的日子
这是最后一次按上帝的吩咐守逾越节
之后，耶稣就创立了纪念他死亡的聚会
他吩咐门徒
“要不断这样做”
所以，门徒很清楚他的意思
他们会在每年原本要守逾越节的这一天
纪念耶稣基督的死亡
这既清楚又合理
而且还有圣经的根据
很多所谓的基督教会都认为
每年越经常纪念耶稣的死亡越好
这很可能是因为他们误解了
哥林多前书11:25的意思
许多英语的圣经译本都把这节经文翻译成
“要不断这样做
要经常喝这杯，来纪念我”
因此，很多人觉得
要经常纪念耶稣基督的死亡
而且越经常越好
英语《圣经新世界译本》在修订之前
也是这样翻译的
其实，这个译法的措辞也是对的
但是，它的意思却很容易被误解
比如
从耶稣创立主的晚餐纪念聚会以来
已经差不多2000年过去了
就算是每年举行一次
也可以说是很经常的
但更准确地说
从哥林多前书11:25,26的
上下文来看
使徒保罗想强调的不是频率
而是纪念聚会举行的方式
在圣经原文里
保罗在这里使用的词
不是“常常”或“经常”
他使用的是一个跟“经常”很类似的词
但这个词的意思是
“每当”、“每逢”或者“每一次”
意思就是
“每次你们这样做
你们都是在显扬主的死亡”
为了让意思更清楚
《新世界译本》修订版
把哥林多前书11:25的经文翻译成
就像之前提到的一样
耶稣让他的门徒每年一次
在他牺牲生命那一天纪念他的死亡
这会取代之前一年一度的逾越节
当然
我们每年一次按照耶稣创立的方式
用饼和酒来纪念他的死亡
并不意味着我们一年当中
只会在这一天才想到他的死亡
不是的
所有献了身受了浸的耶和华见证人都知道
我们在一年当中的每一天
都会想到耶稣的牺牲
无论是在会众聚会里还是在家庭崇拜里
我们都会提到他
我们每一次祷告
也都承认耶稣基督献出的宝贵生命
是为了我们的益处
我们每一次都会奉耶稣基督的名献上祷告
然后再说
“阿们”
因为我们都不完美
所以我们无法直接亲近耶和华
但如果我们奉他的儿子耶稣基督的名祷告
耶和华就会垂听
很多观众都知道
牺牲纪念聚会主要是为那些
受上帝任命的基督徒举行的
这些基督徒是新约的立约方
会跟基督一起作王
但是
今天晚上所有参加的人都会得到益处
因为我们都不完美
都需要靠着耶稣基督的赎价
让自己的罪得到赦免
另外
我们都有机会在未来得到永远的生命
为数不多的
受任命的基督徒会到天上去
亿万崇拜耶和华的人
会在地上的乐园里得享永生
今天晚上
只会有很少的人会吃饼喝酒
跟那些希望在地上享受永生的人相比
领食象征物的人非常地少
在绝大部分会众里
可能都不会有领食的人
有些会众，也许有一两个人
既然如此
为什么我们还要所有人
都传递这些象征物呢？
为什么不邀请那些受任命的基督徒
到台上来吃饼喝酒呢？
这样做可以节省很多时间
也不用麻烦大家一个一个地传啊！
我们传递饼和酒
最主要的原因是
要跟从耶稣创立的模式
如果受任命的基督徒吃饼喝酒
是为了表明自己有希望到天上去
那其他人为什么也要传递象征物呢？
这样做是要公开表明
自己希望永永远远活下去
就在地上的乐园里
请想一想
对人类来说，这是最好的生活
这也是耶和华原本创造亚当夏娃时
对人类所定的旨意
对人来说，还有比这更美好的希望吗？
我们所有人都热切地期待未来到来
到时，撒但将不能再影响地上的人
他和手下的所有邪灵
将会被扔进无底深渊里
被囚禁1000年
完全不能活动
复活到天上的基督徒会和基督
一起成就这件事
在耶稣千年统治期间
所有在地上生活的人
都有机会将地球恢复成乐园
像耶和华原先定意的那样
让我们把目光看得更远一些
基督千年统治之后
人类将会恢复完美
就像亚当夏娃刚刚被创造
还没有犯罪时的状态一样
哥林多前书15:24说
到那时，弥赛亚王国会实现它的目标
就是让地上布满完美的人类
接着，在撒但最后的引诱之后
所有反叛的人都会被毁灭
而撒但和他手下的邪灵也会被永远消灭
到时
耶和华对地球所定的旨意将会完全实现
地球上的每个角落
都住着正义的人
他们都会崇拜宇宙至高的统治者
我们仁爱的天父耶和华上帝
戈登弟兄
请你为我们读出今天的《守望台》评论
耶稣跟11个忠心的使徒提到了两个约
也就是新约和王国之约
这两个约让这11个忠心的使徒
和一小群数目有限的基督徒
有机会到天上去做君王和祭司
受神圣力量任命而且仍然在世的基督徒
是这两个约的立约人
所以，只有他们可以在纪念聚会里吃饼喝酒
耶和华赐给他们的希望非常奇妙
他们会在天上享有不死不朽的生命
会跟耶稣基督以及其余复活去天上的基督徒
一起施行统治
更重要的是，他们会亲眼看见耶和华上帝！
受神圣力量任命的基督徒必须忠心至死
谢谢你！
过去几天，我们阅读的经文
记载的都是耶稣牺牲前发生的事
接下来，我们一起阅读今天的经文
要阅读的经文范围会出现在屏幕上
读的时候
你也可以欣赏我们这次特意准备的图画
无酵节的第一天
门徒来问耶稣说
“你要我们在哪里准备逾越节的晚餐呢？”
他说
“你们进城去见某某人
对他说
老师说
我的时候快到了
我要在你家里跟门徒过逾越节”
门徒照耶稣吩咐的去做
就准备好了逾越节的晚餐
无酵节到了
在这一天要宰杀逾越节的祭牲
耶稣派彼得和约翰出去
说
“你们去，为我们准备逾越节的晚餐”
他们说
“你要我们在哪里准备呢？”
他说
“你们进了城
就会遇见一个人拿着一个水瓶
你们要跟着他
到他进去的那个房子
你们要对房子的主人说
老师对你说
我跟门徒一起吃逾越节晚餐的客房
在哪里呢？
那个人
就会带你们去看楼上一个宽敞的房间
里面家具齐全
你们就在那里准备吧”
他们去了
发现情形正如耶稣对他们说的一样
他们就把逾越节的晚餐准备好了
到了晚上
耶稣跟12个门徒一起用餐
他们吃的时候，耶稣说
“我实在告诉你们
你们有一个人会出卖我”
门徒就非常忧愁
一个一个地问他说
“主啊，不是我吧？”
他回答说
“跟我一起把手伸进同一个碗里的
就是出卖我的人
正如圣经说的
人子固然要离去
可是出卖人子的人有祸了！
那个人没有出生倒好”
打算出卖耶稣的犹大就说
“老师，不是我吧？”
耶稣对他说
“你自己心里清楚”
他们还在吃的时候
耶稣拿起饼来
祷告之后就掰开，递给门徒说
“你们拿去吃吧
这指的是我的身体”
他拿起杯来
祷告感谢之后，递给他们说
“你们全都喝这杯酒吧
这指的是我的立约之血
是要为许多人流出来的
使罪得到宽恕
可是我告诉你们
从今以后
我绝不再喝这葡萄酒
直到我跟你们在我父亲的王国里
喝新酒的那一天”
最后
他们唱了赞美歌
就离开那里，前往橄榄山
那时耶稣对他们说
“今天晚上
你们全都会因我的事而离弃我
因为圣经上写着
我要打击牧人
羊群就会四散
可是我复活以后
要比你们先到加利利去”
彼得却对他说
“即使其他人全都因你的事而离弃你
我也绝不会离弃你！”
耶稣对彼得说
“我实在告诉你
在今天晚上，鸡叫以前
你会三次不认我”
彼得对他说
“即使我必须跟你一起死
也绝不会不认你”
其他的门徒也全都说了同样的话
那时耶稣跟他们来到
一个叫客西马尼的地方
他对门徒说
“你们坐在这里
我到那边去祷告”
他带了彼得和西庇太的两个儿子一起去
当时他忧愁起来，极其难过
于是对他们说
“我心里非常忧愁，几乎要死
你们要留在这里
陪我一起守望”
他稍往前走
跪在地上下拜，祷告说
“我的父亲啊
要是可能，愿这个杯离开我
可是不要照我的意思
而是要照你的意思”
他回到门徒那里
看见他们睡着了
就对彼得说
“你们连跟我守望一小时也不能吗？
你们要不断守望，不断祷告
免得陷入引诱
心灵固然是热切的
肉体却是软弱的”
他第二次又去祷告说
“我的父亲啊
要是这个杯不可能离开我
非要我喝不可
就愿你的旨意实现吧”
他再次回来，看见门徒又睡着了
因为他们困得眼睛都睁不开了
他就离开门徒，第三次去祷告
把同样的话又说了一遍
接着他回到门徒那里
对他们说
“在这样的时候
你们还在睡觉
还在休息！
看！
时候快到
人子要被人出卖
落在罪人手里了
起来，我们走吧
看！
出卖我的人快到了”
他还在说话
十二使徒之一的犹大忽然来了
有一大群人带着刀剑棍棒跟着他
他们是祭司长和民众的长老派来的
出卖耶稣的那个人事先给了他们一个暗号
说
“我吻谁，谁就是你们要的人
你们要拘捕他”
犹大直接走到耶稣跟前
说
“老师，你好！”
然后非常亲切地吻他
耶稣对他说
“你这个人来这里做什么？”
于是他们上前
抓住耶稣，拘捕了他
不料，跟耶稣同行的人当中
有一个伸手拔剑
向大祭司的奴隶砍去
削掉了他一只耳朵
于是耶稣对那个门徒说
“把剑收回原处！
使用刀剑的，都会死在刀剑之下
难道你以为我不能求我的父亲
立刻给我派12个军团以上的天使来吗？
要是这样
圣经说事情必然这样发生
又怎能实现呢？”
当时，耶稣对那群人说
“你们带着刀剑棍棒出来捉拿我
像对付强盗一样吗？
我天天坐在圣殿里教导人
你们却没有拘捕我
可是所有这些事发生
是要应验众先知写下来的话”
那时门徒全都抛下他逃跑了
经文记载的事发生之后不久
人类就见证了有史以来
最有爱心的两个行动
耶和华和耶稣一起粉碎了魔鬼的作为
消除了他在伊甸园里
引诱亚当夏娃犯罪所带来的恶果
受任命的基督徒和另外的绵羊
都有希望永永远远地活下去
我们能享有这个希望
都是因为耶稣基督献出的赎价牺牲
愿你们所有人
今天晚上
都可以好好享受
耶稣牺牲纪念聚会！

title: 브라질 지부 개축 공사

ko.text: 오늘은 이 아름다운 지부의 개축을 위해 진행되고 있는 일들을 보여 드리고자 합니다.
현재 브라질 베델에는 1150명 이상의 베델 봉사자들이 살고 있고
1997년에 마지막 증축이 있은 이후로 아직까지 건물의 개축이 이루어진 적이 없습니다.
그에 더해 이곳에서 일이 수행되는 방식에 많은 변화가 있었습니다.
그리고 이 기간에 브라질의 전도인 수는 두 배 가까이 증가해서 90만 명을 넘어섰습니다.
건물들이 잘 관리되고는 있지만 일부 기계, 전기, 컴퓨터 시스템이 노후해서
필요한 일을 수행하는 데 제약이 따릅니다.
이러한 이유와 그 밖의 이유들 때문에 조직의 현재와 미래의 필요를 돌보려면
베델을 개축하는 것이 좋겠다는 결론을 내리게 되었습니다.
개축 공사는 이미 시작됐습니다. 220명이 넘는 자원봉사자들을 위한 임시 숙소가 마련됐습니다.
이 숙소들은 건축 팀이 사용할 것입니다.
마감을 새로 하고 설비 및 전기 시스템을 교체했습니다.
교체한 창문은 단열 및 방음 성능이 뛰어나고, 자연광을 더 들어오게 해서 자원을 절약하는 데 도움이 되죠.
절약과 간소화를 위해 베델 성원 각자는 직접 자신의 옷을 세탁하게 될 것입니다.
숙소동들 전체에 걸쳐 29개의 세탁실을 짓고 있습니다.
또한 사실상 모든 사무실을 현대적으로 완전히 리모델링할 것입니다.
현재 사무 공간은 약 500명을 수용할 수 있는 규모인데,
개축 후에는 거의 900명이 일할 수 있는 규모가 될 것입니다.
사무 공간은 필요 시 구조를 바꾸어 많게는 1050개가 넘는 작업 공간을 배치할 수 있게 설계했습니다.
또한 지부에 있는 대부분의 공용 공간을 현대식으로 개축하여
더 좋은 환경에서 일을 하고 생활할 수 있도록 할 계획입니다.
개축 공사를 위해 매일 350명에서 400명의 자원봉사자들이 일하게 될 것입니다.
그런데 베델 개축 공사에 초대받게 된 거예요.
전 전기 팀에서 일해요. 15살 때 전기 과정을 이수했는데 사실 기술은 여기 베델에 와서 다 배운 거죠.
저희 부부가 함께 참여하는 첫 임무죠.
저는 엔지니어링부에서 설계 일을 돕고 있어요.
벽돌 쌓는 일을 하는데 처음 해 봐요.
하루 일을 끝마칠 즈음에는 정말 큰 만족감과 성취감을 느끼죠.
이 공사가 끝날 즈음에는 이 건물들이 더 효율적이고
미래의 필요를 더 잘 돌볼 수 있도록 준비되어 있기를 바랍니다.
여러분이 드리는 기도와 세계적인 활동을 위한 기부는 큰 도움이 됩니다.
또한 여러분의 상황이 허락한다면 이 건축 공사나
다른 건축 공사에 자원해서 직접 참여해 보는 것은 어떻겠습니까?

en.text: Welcome to the Brazil branch!
Today we will show you the work
that’s being carried out
in the renovation of this beautiful branch.
Our buildings house more than 1,150 Bethelites
and also provide work space
for an additional 600 commuters.
The last branch expansion finished in 1997,
and since then, there has not been a renovation of its buildings.
In addition, the way in which much of the work is done here
has changed a lot.
During this period,
the number of publishers in Brazil
has almost doubled,
reaching to more than 900,000.
Although our buildings are very well cared for,
some mechanical, electrical, and computer systems are outdated,
which limits their usefulness.
For these and other reasons,
the renovation is necessary for Bethel to continue caring
for the present and future needs of the organization.
The renovation has already started.
Temporary accommodations have been created
for more than 220 volunteers.
These accommodations will be used by the construction team.
This is a renovated apartment.
Along with new finishes, the mechanical and electrical systems have been replaced.
The new windows have better thermal and acoustic insulation,
letting in more natural light and serving to economize resources.
Each of the over 650 apartments at the branch will be renovated.
While on the subject of economizing and simplifying,
now each Bethelite will wash their own clothes.
Twenty-nine new laundry rooms are being constructed
throughout the residential blocks.
In addition, practically all of the offices
will be completely renovated and modernized.
We currently have office space for approximately 500 workers.
The renovation will create room for almost 900.
The new layout will also provide the option to reconfigure the office space
to more than 1,050 workstations.
Also, the project includes plans to renovate and modernize
most of the public areas throughout the branch,
creating a nicer environment to work and live.
In order to accomplish this, we plan to have
between 350 and 400 workers per day at the renovation.
I am 23 years old.
I’ve always had the dream of serving in construction.
Then I had the privilege of being called to serve in the construction
going on here at Bethel.
It’s amazing.
I work on the electrical crew.
I took an electrical course when I was 15,
but the truth is, I really learned this profession here in Bethel.
This is my wife, Nathalia.
And this is my husband, José.
And this is our first assignment together.
I’m serving in the Engineering Department in the design sector.
I’m in masonry, something I’ve never done before.
At the end of the day when I finish work,
I feel like I’ve really accomplished something.
We hope that at the end of this project,
these buildings will become a place that’s even more efficient
and better prepared to care for the future needs.
Would you like to have a part in this project?
If so, know that your prayers
and your contributions to the worldwide work
are a great help.
Also, if your circumstances permit,
then why not make yourself available to come
and serve as a volunteer on this or another construction project?

cn.text: 欢迎来到巴西分部！
今天我们会向大家介绍
在这个美丽的分部进行的整修工程
超过1150位伯特利成员
在这里工作和生活
另外还有600多位通勤人员在这里工作
上一次分部翻新还是在1997年
从那时起，这里的设施就没有再整修过
另外
这里的工作方式也发生了很大的改变
在这段时期
巴西的传道员人数几乎翻了一倍
达到了90多万
虽然分部的建筑都得到很好的维修保养
但有些机械设施、电力设备
以及电脑系统都太老旧了
由于这些因素以及其他原因
我们需要对巴西分部进行整修
好让它能继续满足组织的发展和需要
整修工程已经开始了！
我们为220多位志愿人员
准备了临时住处
志愿建筑人员会住在这些房子里
这是一个翻新好的房间
房间里的机械和电力设施
全部都换新的了
新窗户可以起到更好的保温和隔音效果
房间里采光也更好了
这可以节约能源
伯特利的650多个房间
每一个都会这样翻新
为了节省开支、简化工作
每一个伯特利成员都会自己洗衣服
我们在宿舍楼一共修建了29个洗衣房
另外
所有的办公场所都会被重新设计和改造
目前的办公空间只能供大约500人使用
但整修之后将能供超过900人使用
我们甚至能灵活地调整办公空间
让1050多位弟兄姐妹在这里工作
另外，分部里所有的公共空间
都会重新设计和装修
为大家创造更加舒适的工作和生活环境
为了完成整修工程
我们每天都需要

title: 케네스 쿡 2세: 속임수를 피하고 왕국을 따르십시오 (예레미야 10:23)

ko.text: 오늘 해설은 사탄이 여호와에 대한 사람들의 시각을 어떻게 흐리게 만들어 왔는지 알려 줍니다.
배교적인 가르침을 통해 그리고 성경의 많은 사본들에서 하느님의 이름을 없애 버림으로
사탄은 사람들을 영적으로 눈멀게 해 왔습니다.
오늘 아침에는 이와 관련된 이야기를 해 보겠습니다.
주의하지 않으면 사탄의 세상에서 현재와 미래에 일어나는 어떤 일들이 하느님의 왕국에 대한
우리의 시각을 흐리게 만들 수 있습니까?
각각의 일들을 예레미야 10:23에 나오는 원칙과 연결 지어 생각해 보겠습니다.
“오 여호와여, 사람의 길이 자기에게 있지 않다는 것을 제가 잘 압니다.
발걸음을 인도하는 것은 걷는 사람에게 있지 않습니다.”
이 원칙을 염두에 두고 곳곳에서 일어나는 시위들, 정치적인 약속들, 평화와 안전에 대한 선언들이
어떻게 하느님의 왕국에 대한 우리의 시각을 왜곡시킬 수 있는지 생각해 보시죠.
어떤 시위가 한 나라를 휩쓸 때 누군가가 설득력 있는 큰 목소리로 군중을 이끄는 모습을 볼 수 있습니다.
그런 목소리는 보통 많은 사람들이 불공정하다고 여기는 문제에 대한 것입니다.
시위 규모가 수백 명이든 수천 명이든, 대부분의 시위 참여자들은 주동자를 따라
문제는 그들이 제시하는 해결책이 인간의 해결책이라는 것입니다.
하지만 예레미야의 말처럼 “발걸음을 인도하는 것은 걷는 사람에게 있지 않습니다.”
그리스도인들은 왜 그런 시위들을 조심해야 합니까?
그리스도인들이 인기 있는 시위의 영향을 받아 그들의 메시지를 지지하거나 마음속으로라도 동조한다면
하느님의 왕국에 대한 시각이 흐려질 위험이 있기 때문입니다.
세상 사람들의 경우 분명한 인도나 희망이 없을 때 흔히 분노하거나 과격해지는 걸 볼 수 있습니다.
하느님의 백성도 왕국에 대한 초점을 잃으면 그러한 태도를 나타내게 될 수 있죠.
다윗왕의 아들 압살롬을 따른 사람들에게 어떤 일이 있었는지 잠깐 생각해 보겠습니다.
성경은 압살롬이 아버지 다윗의 통치권에 반기를 들었다고 알려 줍니다.
사실 압살롬은 교활한 말과 행동으로 지지 세력을 모으기까지 했죠.
그가 한 행동에 대해 사무엘하 15:2-6에서 읽을 수 있습니다.
그는 사람들에게 공의를 약속했죠. 6절은 “압살롬이 이스라엘 사람들의
다시 말해 사람들은 그의 말에 설득당하고 있었던 것이죠.
압살롬 편에 가담한 사람들은 과격해졌고 처참한 결과가 있었습니다.
네, 여호와를 숭배하는 사람들의 마음도 도둑질당할 수 있습니다.
다시 말해 마음이 설득당하거나 오늘의 성구 표현처럼 잘못 인도될 수 있습니다.
사탄도 그 점을 잘 알고 있습니다.
분명 사탄은 진정한 해결책인 하느님의 왕국에서 사람들의 주의를 돌리기 위해
여러 가지 항의 시위를 사용하고 있습니다.
사탄은 여호와의 백성의 마음을 빼앗기 위해 가능한 모든 수단을 사용할 것입니다.
그러한 시도를 피하고 왕국에 초점을 맞추려면 예수에 관한 이사야 42:1의 약속들을 꼭 기억해야 합니다.
그 구절에서는 “그가 민족들에게 공의를 베풀 것”이라고 했죠.
왕국의 왕으로서 바로 예수께서는 죄 많은 인간이 결코 이룰 수 없는 진정한 공의를 가져오실 것입니다.
왕국에 대한 우리의 시야를 흐리게 만들 수 있는 두 번째는 정치적인 약속들입니다.
사람들은 권력을 얻기 위해 끊임없이 거짓 약속들을 늘어놓죠.
설령 약속들을 지키려고 하는 정치인들이 있다 해도 그렇게 할 수 있는 지혜와 능력이 부족한 경우가 많습니다.
정치인들은 기껏해야 일시적인 해결책만을 내놓을 수 있을 뿐입니다.
흔히 그들은 부도덕한 것이라도 대중들이 좋아하면 받아들이죠.
그들의 생각은 왜곡되어 있어서 옳고 그른 것을 잘 구별하지 못합니다.
그들은 사회 불안과 같은 해결하기 힘든 문제들에 직면해 있죠.
완전히 해결할 수도 없고 많은 돈을 들인다고 해서 해결되는 것도 아닙니다.
다시 한번 예레미야의 말처럼 “발걸음을 인도하는 것은 걷는 사람에게 있지 않습니다.”
고대 로마의 통치자들은 사회 불안을 잠재우기 위해 사람들에게 많은 것을 무료로 제공했습니다.
음식이나 오락, 많은 서비스들이 무료이거나 매우 쌌습니다.
그런 방식으로 사람들을 달래고 그들의 충성을 얻어 낸 것입니다.
하지만 오늘날의 정부들처럼 로마 제국도 점차 쇠퇴해 갔습니다.
그들이 만든 해결책은 장기적인 것이 아니라 임시방편에 불과했습니다.
로마와 그 밖의 지역에 살던 초기 그리스도인들도 제국이 제공한 혜택을 어느 정도 누렸을 것입니다.
음식, 물, 좋은 도로와 같은 것들 말이죠.
그렇더라도 초기 그리스도인들은 주와 그분의 약속된 왕국에 계속 초점을 맞출 필요가 있었습니다.
그렇지 않으면 사물에 대한 그들의 시각이 왜곡될 수 있었고, 제국에 부당한 영광을 돌림으로
믿음을 타협하게 될 위험에 처할 수 있었습니다. 근시안적이 될 수 있었던 것이죠!
사실 로마 제국은 결국 그리스도인들을 박해하기 시작했습니다.
오늘날 우리도 정부들이 하는 일 때문에 혜택을 누릴 수 있지만, 초기 그리스도인들처럼 우리의 정신과 마음에서
왕국에 대한 초점이 흐려지는 일이 결코 없어야 합니다.
여호와와 그분의 아들이 인간의 미래를 책임지고 있다는 걸 명심하는 것입니다.
두 분의 약속들은 반드시 성취될 것입니다.
그 점을 계속 기억한다면 인간이 만든 제도가 하느님의 백성을 공격할 때 우리는 영향을 받지 않을 것입니다.
성경 말씀대로 우린 하느님의 통치와 충돌하지 않는 한 인간의 통치권에 복종하지만, 그렇다고 해서
우리의 미래를 정치적인 약속들이나 정부가 베푸는 혜택에 맡기지 않습니다.
우리는 우리의 미래를 하느님의 왕국에만 맡기죠.
나라들이 정치적인 약속들을 통해 사람들의 환심을 사려고 할수록 우리는 진정한 해결책인
하느님의 왕국에 더욱더 초점을 맞추어야 합니다.
하느님의 왕국에 대한 우리의 시야를 흐리게 만들 수 있는 세 번째는 나라들이 앞으로 “평화롭다, 안전하다” 하고
말할 그때에 갑작스러운 멸망이 순식간에 그들에게 닥칠 것”이라고 예언합니다.
나라들은 왕국 소식을 듣고도 문제를 해결하기 위해 자신들을 신뢰하는 것을 멈추지 않을 것입니다.
정치 세력은 어느 시점엔가 거만하게도 “평화롭다, 안전하다”라고 말할 것이고,
언제 어떻게 그 일이 있을 것인지 여호와께서는 아시죠.
나라들이 얼마나 큰 목소리로 “평화롭다, 안전하다”라고 외치든,
“발걸음을 인도하는 것은 걷는 사람에게 있지 않다”라는 사실은 변하지 않습니다.
인간이 단지 날갯짓을 흉내 낸다고 해서 날 수 없는 것처럼 인간은 스스로를 다스릴 능력이 없습니다.
따라서 큰 환난이 가까워 올수록 우리는 나라들의 말과 주장이 얼마나 설득력 있게 들리든
세상의 문제들에 대한 인간의 해결책을 제시하는 인기 있는 시위들의 영향을 받거나 관여하지 않고,
세상의 정치적인 약속들에 신뢰를 두지 않고,
“평화롭다, 안전하다”라는 나라들의 말에 속지 않음으로 그럴 수 있습니다.
사탄의 세상이 뉴스나 소셜 미디어나 그 밖의 매체를 통해 어떤 선전을 하든,
사람들에게 왕국의 좋은 소식과 앞으로 있을 일에 대한 경고의 소식을 계속 전파하십시오.
인간의 미래를 책임지고 있는 분은 여호와와 그분의 아들임을 잊지 마십시오.
사탄과 세상이 믿음을 약하게 하고 왕국에 대한 시야를 흐리게 하지 못하게 하십시오.
그리고 이사야 26:3, 4의 말씀을 늘 마음에 새기시기 바랍니다.
“당신은 당신을 온전히 의지하는 자들을 지켜 주시고 그들에게 지속적인 평화를 주실 것입니다.
그들이 당신을 신뢰하기 때문입니다. 너희는 여호와를 영원토록 신뢰하여라.

en.text: Today’s printed comments consider
how Satan has blurred
people’s view of Jehovah.
Satan has blurred their view,
or blinded people, by means
of apostate teachings and by seeing to it
that God’s name has been removed from many copies of the Bible.
For this morning’s discussion, we want to consider a related concern,
and that is, What current and future events in Satan’s world
could blur our view of God’s Kingdom if we’re not careful?
With each point, we’ll tie in the principle
found in these words at Jeremiah 10:23,
where it says:
“I well know, O Jehovah,
“that man’s way does not belong to him.
It does not belong to man who is walking even to direct his step.”
With this in mind, we’re going to look at how widespread protests,
political promises, and claims of peace and security
could distort our view of God’s Kingdom if we’re not careful.
First is widespread protests.
When protests sweep through any country,
there’s often someone leading the way
with a very loud or persuasive voice, true?
And their message usually touches on something
that many see as an injustice.
Whether the protest involves dozens, hundreds, or thousands of people,
most of the protesters are followers,
and they repeat a message, or slogan.
The problem is that the solutions they seek
are human solutions.
Recall Jeremiah’s words:
“It does not belong to man . . . even to direct his step.”
What danger do such protests pose for true Christians?
The danger is this: If we get caught up in the spirit of popular protests
—even slightly supporting a cause,
even silently within our heart—
we could find our view of God’s Kingdom growing dim.
What, in turn, could that lead to?
Well, when people in the world lack clear direction or hope,
their hearts often start to be filled with anger and rage.
A servant of God can feel such things too
if he or she loses sight of the Kingdom.
Consider for a moment what happened to those
who followed after King David’s son Absalom.
The Bible explains that Absalom objected to his father’s rulership,
but he did more than that.
Through cunning words and actions, he gathered a following.
You can read about what he did
at 2 Samuel 15:2-6.
He promised the people justice.
And verse 6 says that “Absalom kept stealing
the hearts of the men of Israel.”
In other words, the people got caught up in his message.
Eventually, those who joined him turned violent,
and the outcome was disastrous.
Yes, even the hearts of those who worship Jehovah
can be stolen, or captured, or as today’s text says,
‘led astray’ for a misguided, or bad purpose.
So that is the danger, and we can be certain that Satan knows it.
There’s no question that Satan is right now using
various messages of protest
to direct people away from the real solution, God’s Kingdom.
And Satan will cast his net wide
to try to capture some of Jehovah’s people, if possible.
To avoid that and remain focused on the Kingdom,
we must not forget what Isaiah 42:1
promises about Jesus.
There it foretells that “he will bring justice to the nations”
—he will, not humans.
As King of God’s Kingdom,
Jesus is the one who will bring what sinful humans can never bring
—real justice for people.
A second thing that can blur our view of the Kingdom
if we’re not careful is political promises.
Is there no end to the false promises
that people will make when they want power?
And even when politicians try to fulfill some of their promises,
they often fall short on the wisdom and the resources to do it effectively.
Political powers can only provide
short-term human solutions at best.
They often cave in to popular and immoral thinking.
Their thoughts are so distorted
that they have difficulty seeing right from wrong.
They face long-term problems, including social unrest,
that they cannot permanently solve,
and no amount of money can fix it for them.
Again, we recall Jeremiah’s words:
“It does not belong to man . . . even to direct his step.”
When the rulers of ancient Rome tried to put down social unrest,
they gave many things to the people for free.
Food, entertainment, and many services
were free or very cheap.
They called it “bread and circuses.”
See, that was their formula to appease the people and gain their allegiance.
But like the governments of today,
that man-made empire was in gradual decline.
And the humans in charge had no long-term answers,
only short-term offerings.
Now, it’s likely that the early Christians in Rome and elsewhere benefited
from some of the things that the empire provided:
food, water, good roads, and so forth.
Still, those early Christians needed to remain focused
on the Lord and on his promised Kingdom;
otherwise, their view of things could have become distorted
and they might have been pulled into compromising their faith
by giving undue glory to the empire.
How shortsighted that would have been!
That empire in Rome would eventually,
and did eventually, turn against those Christians.
Today, we too may benefit from some of the things
that the nations are doing, but like the early Christians,
we must never allow the Kingdom
to become out of focus in our minds and hearts.
What will help us to do this?
We’re helped when we remember that Jehovah and his Son
are in charge of man’s future.
The solutions they offer are permanent.
The promises they have made will be fulfilled.
If we keep that focus,
then when this man-made system turns against God’s people,
it will have no hold on us.
As God’s Word directs, we submit to man’s rulership
where it does not conflict with God’s rule.
But in following that direction,
we’re not entrusting our future to political promises and favors.
We entrust our future to God’s Kingdom alone.
The more that the nations try to appease the people through political promises,
the more determined we must be
to keep the Kingdom in focus as the real solution.
That leads us to the third thing that could blur, or distort,
our view of God’s Kingdom, namely,
when the nations are saying “peace and security.”
At 1 Thessalonians 5:3, God’s Word foretells
that “whenever it is that they [the political powers] are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
then sudden destruction is to be instantly on them.”
Why will sudden destruction come?
Because human governments are not the solution.
Despite having heard the Kingdom message,
the nations will not stop trusting in themselves to solve their problems.
At some point,
the political powers will be arrogantly saying
“peace and security” in a way
that fulfills 1 Thessalonians 5:3.
Jehovah knows how and when that will prove to be.
Yet, no matter how much or how loudly
the nations will be saying it,
they cannot change this fact:
“It does not belong to man who is walking even to direct his step.”
Just as humans cannot simply flap their arms and fly,
so, too, humans cannot rule themselves successfully.
So as things move ahead toward the great tribulation,
we must not allow ourselves to be fooled no matter how convincing
the speeches and boasts from the nations may sound.
And we will not be fooled
if we refuse to get caught up in popular protests
that seek human solutions to the world’s problems,
if we refuse to place our trust in political promises,
and if we refuse to be fooled by the nations saying
“peace and security.”
So no matter what Satan’s world promotes in the news,
on social media, or elsewhere, we’re convinced
that God’s Kingdom alone is the solution.
What can we do to keep that focus?
Keep preaching the good news of the Kingdom to people,
including the warning about what is coming;
remember that Jehovah and his Son
are the ones who are in charge of man’s future;
and never allow Satan and his world to weaken your faith
and blur your view of God’s Kingdom.
And always have this in mind:
it’s stated at Isaiah 26:3, 4,
where it says of Jehovah:
“You will safeguard those who fully lean on you;
“you will give them continuous peace,
“because it is in you that they trust.
“Trust in Jehovah forever,
for Jah Jehovah is the eternal Rock.”

cn.text: 今天，我们会谈谈
撒但用什么方式让人无法正确认识耶和华？
撒但已经蒙蔽了很多人的思想
他的手段
就是通过错误的教义
或者从圣经经卷中删去上帝的名字
今天早上，我们要讨论一个相关的问题
那就是在目前和未来
撒但会用哪些事
来误导我们对上帝王国的看法
讨论每一点的时候
我们都会引用
耶利米书10:23的经文
“耶和华啊，我清楚知道
人不能掌握自己的道路
人行走也无法确定该走的方向”
我们会结合经文谈谈
世界各地的抗议活动
政治承诺还有和平安全的主张
会怎样误导我们对上帝王国的看法
首先是世界各地的抗议活动
人们发起抗议活动的时候
都会用强硬的态度喊出他们抗议的口号
他们的抗议大多跟不公的事有关
不管参加抗议活动的
是几十人、几百人还是几千、几万人
大多数的抗议者会重复喊出一个信息或口号
不过
他们寻求的解决方法是出于人的想法
我们再回头想想耶利米书的话
“人行走无法确定该走的方向
为什么这些抗议活动
对基督徒来说
非常危险呢？
因为如果我们被卷入这些抗议活动
哪怕是在心里有支持这些活动的倾向
都可能对上帝的王国慢慢失去信心
如果失去信心和希望
人会受到什么影响呢？
世人因为看不到希望和方向
心里往往充满愤怒
上帝的仆人如果不专注于上帝的王国
也会有这样的感觉
现在我们来看看
在大卫王的儿子押沙龙死后
那些跟随押沙龙的人
落得了怎样的下场
圣经说，押沙龙想篡夺他父亲的王位
用一些诡诈的手段
来笼络人心
达到了自己的目的
撒母耳记下15:2-6说
押沙龙承诺要为人民主持公道
第6节说
“押沙龙暗中得了以色列人的心”
换句话说，这些人听信了押沙龙的话
后来，那些跟押沙龙一起谋反的人
参战攻打大卫
结果损失惨重，一败涂地
的确，崇拜耶和华的人
有时也会被错误信息腐化
就像经文说的“被误导”
这很危险，因为撒但也清楚知道这点
毫无疑问
撒但正用各种各样的抗议活动
试图让人偏离真正能解决问题的途径
就是上帝的王国
撒但会千方百计捕获上帝子民的心
我们想要避开陷阱
专注于上帝的王国
就要牢记以赛亚书42:1中
关于耶稣的承诺
经文预告“他要在列国中主持公道”
只有他能做到，人做不到
作为上帝王国的君王
耶稣会为人类带来完美的公正
这是不完美的人类永远无法做到的
第二个模糊我们视线的因素就是政治承诺
为了得到权力
政客们会作出一个又一个的虚假承诺
就算他们试图兑现一些承诺
也往往缺乏有效解决问题的智慧和资源
人类政府最多只能为人类
提供短期的解决方案
他们常常会迎合世上流行的不道德想法
这些想法会扭曲人的思想
让人很难辨别是非对错
他们面对很多长期的问题
例如社会动荡不安
但他们没办法彻底解决
再多的钱也解决不了这些问题
我们再想想耶利米书的经文
“人行走无法确定该走的方向”
古代罗马的统治者为了平息社会动乱
就给人提供免费的或者非常便宜的生活服务
饮食和娱乐
来拢络人心
有人把这种方式称为“面包和娱乐”
他们觉得这样可以安抚人心
让人民效忠政府
但就像世上其他政府一样
强大的罗马帝国也逐步走向衰落
人类政府没办法从根源解决问题
只能提供暂时的方案
罗马和其他地方的早期基督徒
很可能受益于当时政府的福利
比如食物、水、便利的交通等等
不过
这些早期的基督徒需要保持目光专注
专注于上帝的王国
否则他们很可能被误导和蒙蔽
被罗马政府提供的看得见的福利
削弱了对上帝王国的信心
被眼前的利益蒙蔽很不明智
因为罗马帝国
后来开始反过来迫害这些基督徒
今天，我们也可能像早期的基督徒一样
受益于政府提供的福利
但我们千万不要分心
要专注于上帝的王国
我们怎样才能做到呢？
我们要时刻提醒自己
将来统治全球的是耶和华和耶稣
他们会从根源彻底解决所有问题
他们的承诺一定会实现
这样，人类政府攻击上帝子民时
我们就会坚定不移
要谨守圣经原则
如果当权者的统治跟圣经没有冲突
我们就要顺服当权者
当然，顺服当权者
并不代表我们把未来寄托在政治承诺上
上帝的王国才是我们唯一的希望
政府越是极力通过政治承诺来安抚人心
我们就要越坚定地提醒自己
只有上帝的王国才能解决所有问题
第三个模糊我们视线的因素
就是各国政府会宣布“和平安全了”
让我们看一下
帖撒罗尼迦前书5:3
是怎样预告的
人，也就是世上的政府
正说“和平安全了”的时候
突如其来的毁灭就立刻临到他们
为什么会有突如其来的毁灭呢？
因为世上的政府无法彻底解决问题
他们虽然听到王国的好消息
但仍然坚信自己有能力解决问题
在未来的某个时候
世上的政府会高傲地宣布
“和平安全了”
就像刚才的经文说的一样
但这件事何时发生、怎样发生
只有耶和华知道
关于和平安全
无论各国政府怎样宣传
呼声有多高，都无法改变一个事实
就是“人行走无法确定该走的方向”
正如人类没有能力像鸟一样自如地飞翔
人类也没有能力成功地统治自己
我们现在越来越接近大患难
不管世上政府的言论听起来多么令人信服
我们都要保持清醒，不要上当
弟兄姐妹们
如果我们拒绝被卷入各种抗议活动
不听信政治承诺
也不被和平安全的宣布所迷惑
我们就不会被误导
无论撒但的世界通过新闻
社交媒体或其他方式宣传什么
我们都要确信
只有上帝的王国才能解决所有的问题
我们怎样才能不分心呢？
要向人传讲上帝王国的好消息
也包括将来发出的警告信息
要记得
掌控人类未来的是耶和华和耶稣基督
不要让撒但和他统治的世界误导你
削弱你的信心
我们要经常提醒自己
以赛亚书26:3,4的经文
“你会保护完全依靠你的人
你会赐他们长久的安宁
因为他们信赖的是你
你们要永远信赖耶和华
因为耶和华
耶和华是永恒的磐石”

title: 이삭 머레이: 언제나 은혜롭게 말하십시오 (골로새 4:6)

ko.text: 우리가 늘 어떻게 말해야 하는지를 알려 줍니다. 6절.
“여러분은 소금으로 맛을 내듯 언제나 은혜롭게 말하십시오.”
두 번째로, 은혜롭게 말하는 것이 왜 그렇게 중요합니까?
세 번째로, 은혜롭게 말하는 법을 어떻게 배울 수 있습니까?
사도 바울은 그의 편지에서 이 그리스어 단어를 100번이 넘게 사용했습니다.
이 내용을 바울이 에베소서 4장에서 한 말과 비교해 보겠습니다.
에베소서 4:29 하반절에 보면 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
“오직 필요에 따라 세워 주는 선한 말만 하여
그런데 이 구절 첫 부분에서는 어떻게 알려 주나요?
“썩은 말은 입 밖에 내지 말고”라고 했죠.
아마 여러분의 냉장고에서 음식이 상한 적이 있을지 모릅니다.
하지만 뚜껑을 열어 보니 악취가 코를 찌릅니다.
얼굴을 홱 돌리고 뚜껑을 닫은 다음 얼른 갖다 버립니다.
이제, 친한 친구와 대화를 나눈다고 생각해 보시죠.
격려적이고 좋은 얘기를 듣게 될 줄 알았는데
다른 사람이나 어떤 마련에 대해 얘기하는 겁니다.
정말 악취가 심한 말이지만, 고개를 홱 돌릴 수가 없습니다.
그렇게 하다간 내가 험담의 대상이 될 수 있으니까요.
그냥 조용히 대화의 뚜껑을 닫아 버립니다.
사실 우리 모두는 분명 썩은 음식과 같은 말을 하거나
은혜롭게 말하는 것이 왜 그렇게 중요합니까?
혀는 우리 지체 가운데서 불의의 세계를 대표합니다.
혀는 온몸을 더럽히고 인생행로 전체를 불태우며
“당신들에게 말하는데, 사람들은 자기들이 하는 모든 무익한 말에 대해
그런데 여호와께서는 우리의 속사람을 보고 심판하시는 게 아닌가요?
맞습니다! 34절 뒷부분에서 무엇이라고 알려 주는지 보실까요?
우리가 하는 말이 머리에서 나오는 것 같아 보이지만
그리고 우리의 말이 사람들에게 주는 영향을 보고 심판하시죠.
사실 여호와께서는 친절하고 은혜롭게 말하는 면에서 최고의 본을 보이십니다.
스가랴 1장을 보면 12절에서 여호와의 천사가 여호와께 이야기합니다.
그 내용을 보면, 이 천사는 몹시 괴로워하는데, 거짓 숭배가 우세해져서
참숭배가 뒤로 밀려나는 것처럼 보이기 때문입니다.
여호와께서 은혜롭고 친절하게 말씀하신 건 분명하죠.
은혜롭게 말하는 법을 어떻게 배울 수 있습니까?
이제 살펴볼 첫 번째 원칙은 에베소서 5:1에 나옵니다. 5:1입니다.
“그러므로 사랑받는 자녀로서 하느님을 본받는 사람이 되십시오.”
그리고 부모를 위해 뭔가 하는 것을 아주 좋아합니다.
어린 여자아이가 엄마한테 선물을 줄 때가 있죠.
물론 그건 비싸거나 아주 좋은 선물은 아니지만
관대하게 주는 어머니를 보고 따라 하는 거죠.
우리가 그분을 본받을 때 그분은 정말 기뻐하십니다.
사실 이 모든 게 감사하는 마음에서 나오죠.
고맙고 감사하는 마음을 표현하는 가장 좋은 방법은
따라서 날마다 여호와께서 해 주시는 모든 일에 대해 감사하십시오.
우리는 그분이 해 주시는 모든 일을 다 알지는 못하죠.
날마다 잊지 않고 그분이 해 주신다고 느끼는 일에 감사한다면
여호와께 감사하는 마음이 갈수록 더 깊어질 것이고 사랑도 깊어질 겁니다.
그리고 여호와를 더욱더 사랑할수록 그분을 본받기가 더 쉬워질 것입니다.
자신이 무가치하다고 느끼면서 이렇게 말하면 안 되죠.
아닙니다! 감사하는 마음만 있다면 누구나 여호와를 본받을 수 있습니다.
두 번째로 우리가 살펴볼 원칙은 오늘의 성구에 들어 있는데,
우리의 말을 “소금으로 맛을 내”야 한다는 것입니다.
그래서 사람들은 음식을 보존하기 위해 소금을 사용했습니다.
음식이 상하지 않도록 소금을 사용했던 것입니다.
마치 소금이 음식을 보존해 주는 것처럼 은혜로운 말은 다른 사람의 품위를 지켜 줍니다.
그리고 은혜로운 말은 사랑과 우정을 지켜 주어
우리가 하는 이런 은혜로운 말은 감사하는 마음에서 우러나옵니다.
따라서 다른 사람들에게서 좋은 점을 찾아 보고,
그 좋은 특성들을 더 길러 나가도록 격려의 말을 해 주십시오.
우리는 사랑하는 사람들에게 아주 좋은 말을 해 주지 않습니까?
어떤 어려움이 있든, 우리의 기분이 어떻든, 항상 은혜롭게 말하십시오.
선하고 친절한 말을 하는 것은 언제나 올바른 일입니다.
“내 입의 말과 내 마음의 묵상이 당신에게 기쁨이 되기를 바랍니다,
오 나의 반석, 나의 구속자이신 여호와여.”

en.text: The text for today here at Colossians 4:6
sets a standard for us in our speech.
It says: “Let your words always be gracious,
seasoned with salt.”
So we will consider three questions.
The first one:
What is gracious speech?
Second:
Why are gracious words so important?
And third:
How can we learn to speak graciously?
So for that first one (what is gracious speech?),
the word “gracious” has a special meaning.
The apostle Paul used this Greek word
more than 100 times in his writings.
So, what is so special about this word?
This word is also translated
as “undeserved kindness,”
and in some cases it is translated as “a kind gift.”
So apply it to the words in this text:
‘Let your words always be a kind gift.’
We can compare this concept
with the words of Paul in Ephesians chapter 4.
It says at Ephesians 4:29,
the second part of the verse,
“only what is good
“for building up as the need may be,
to impart what is beneficial to the hearers.”
But now note what he says in the first part of this verse:
“Let a rotten word
not come out of your mouth.”
Now, that’s a strong concept.
Maybe you have had in your refrigerator
some food that went off.
On the outside it looks fine.
But when you open that lid and that putrid smell comes out,
you turn your head away,
you close the lid, and you get rid of it as fast as you can.
Now, think of a conversation you have with your close friend.
You’re expecting to hear something really good and upbuilding from him,
but out come these critical, nasty,
and negative comments about somebody else
or about some arrangement.
How disappointing!
The smell is just overwhelming,
but you cannot react as you would with that container of food
in case you become the next target.
So, what do you do?
Just quietly put a lid on that conversation and throw it away.
Now, I’m sure all of us
have been there at some time on either side of the conversation.
But now we come to the second part.
Why is it so important to have gracious speech?
Consider the words here in James —James chapter 3.
Now, here it says in verse 6,
James 3:6:
“The tongue is also a fire.
“The tongue represents a world of unrighteousness
“among our body members, for it defiles all the body
“and sets the whole course of life on fire,
and it is set on fire by Gehenna.”
So who is ‘liable to Gehenna’?
It’s the one misusing their tongue.
Jesus said the same thing.
Consider his words here in Matthew
—Matthew chapter 12.
And here Jesus says in verse 36
—he says:
“I tell you that men will render an account
“on Judgment Day
for every unprofitable saying that they speak.”
We may ask, ‘But is Jehovah not judging us
on the person we are on the inside?’
Exactly!
Look what it says in verse 34, the second part of verse 34:
“For out of the abundance of the heart
the mouth speaks.”
So words seem to appear from the top of the head,
but they really come from the heart.
And Jehovah judges a person on the inside
and on the impact their words
might have on other people.
Of course, Jehovah sets the most beautiful example for us
of kind and gracious speech.
Look at this example in Zechariah
—Zechariah chapter 1.
And here in Zechariah chapter 1,
an angel of Jehovah is speaking to Jehovah
in verse 12.
Now, this angel is very distressed
because it seems that false worship
is gaining the upper hand
and true worship is being pushed aside.
And he says here in verse 12:
“O Jehovah of armies,
“how long will you withhold your mercy from Jerusalem
“and the cities of Judah,
with whom you have been indignant these 70 years?”
Now, look at verse 13:
“Jehovah answered the angel who was speaking with me,
with kind and comforting words.”
Now, the account does not say what Jehovah said,
but we know Jehovah is gracious and kind.
So now we come to our third question:
How can we learn
to be gracious and to have gracious speech?
Well, there are two principles we’ve got to highlight,
because this is a very complicated subject.
And the first one we would like to highlight
is at Ephesians 5:1
—Ephesians 5:1.
And there it says:
“Therefore, become imitators of God,
as beloved children.”
Now, we know children imitate their parents.
They just find it so enjoyable
to do something for their parents.
They imitate them.
See this little girl?
She gives a gift to her mother.
Now, it is not the best gift
or the greatest gift ever,
but to the mother it is wonderful.
Why?
Because she’s imitating her.
She probably saw her being generous to other people;
she imitates that.
And that makes her feel very, very good.
The same with Jehovah.
When we imitate him,
we bring joy to his heart.
Now, it’s all a matter of appreciation, isn’t it?
Nothing builds appreciation
more than being grateful,
to say thank you.
So thank Jehovah
for everything he does for us every day.
Now, we probably don’t even know the half of what he really is doing for us.
But if we thank him all the time
—every day make it a point to thank him for the things we see he does for us—
it will engender in our hearts
an appreciation for Jehovah
and we will admire him.
And the more we admire Jehovah,
the more we will be inclined to imitate him.
And there is no need to feel unworthy, saying,
“Oh, well, I cannot imitate Jehovah.”
No!
The only qualification needed
is to have an appreciative heart.
The second principle we would like to highlight
is contained in our text for today,
which says our words should be “seasoned with salt.”
Now, in Bible times they didn’t have refrigeration.
So in order to preserve food, they would salt it.
They would season it with salt
to make sure that the food was not spoiled.
Our words —our gracious words—
should preserve the dignity of other people;
they should preserve love and friendships
that will last forever.
These words that we speak
will come from an appreciative heart.
So look for the good in other people
and say the right thing
to strengthen the good in them.
And we do say the nicest things to those we love, don’t we?
So in conclusion,
regardless of what we go through or how we feel,
always be gracious.
It is never wrong to do good and be kind.
Don’t give up.
And make this the standard, as it says at Psalm 19:14:
“Let the sayings of my mouth
“and the meditation of my heart
“become pleasurable before you,
O Jehovah my Rock and my Redeemer.”

cn.text: 我们怎样说话才能令人舒畅呢？
秘诀就在今天的经文歌罗西书4:6
经文说
“你们说话应该总是仁慈体贴
仿佛用盐调味”
今天我们就来讨论三个要点
第一
什么样的话才是仁慈体贴的？
第二
为什么说话仁慈体贴很重要？
第三
我们怎样才能说出仁慈体贴的话？
什么样的话才是仁慈体贴的呢？
歌罗西书4章6节中
译作“仁慈体贴”的希腊语词
意思很特别
在保罗执笔的书信中
这个词出现了100多次
为什么说这个词的意思很特别呢？
这个词也被译作“分外恩典”
或者“救济”一类的善事
如果把这类的意思套用在
歌罗西书4:6
经文也可以说成
“你们说的话，总应该像捐赠的礼物一样”
我们可以把这个意思
跟保罗写的以弗所书第4章的经文做个比较
以弗所书4:29的后半部分
是怎么说的呢？
经文说
“要按照需要说鼓励人的好话
让听见的人受益”
不过请留意
他在4:29的前半部分说
“有害无益的话一句也不可出口
“有害无益”这个词
直译为“腐烂”
这会让你联想到什么呢？
假设你的冰箱里有些食物坏掉了
虽然看起来没什么问题
但当你打开盖子
闻到一股腐烂的气味
你一定会马上把头转过去
盖上盖子，赶紧把食物扔掉
想想看
如果你跟一个好友聊天
你肯定想从朋友那里听到鼓励的话
而不是一些批评和难听的话
或是针对个人或会众安排的不满
这样的话很让人沮丧
就像腐烂的食物一样
但是你却
不能表现得像闻到坏掉的食物那样
如果你那样做
他下一次可能就会说你的坏话
那么你应该怎样做呢？
就是默默地把这些像腐烂食物的话
盖上盖子，然后把它扔掉
我相信大家都听到过，也说过这样的话
现在我们来谈谈第二点
为什么说话仁慈体贴
这么重要呢？
来看一下雅各书
雅各书的第3章
第6节
经文是这样说的
“舌头就是火
在我们身体各部分中
舌头就是一个不正义的世界
它玷污全身
被欣嫩谷的火点着
使人的一生着起火来”
所以哪些人
会被扔进“欣嫩谷”呢？
就是没有善用舌头的人
耶稣也说过类似的话
他的话在马太福音
马太福音的12章
耶稣说
“我告诉你们，在审判日
人要为自己说过的每一句无益的话负责”
你可能会想
耶和华不是根据我们内在的为人
来审判我们吗？
说得没错
我们看看
12章34节的后半部分是怎么说的
这里说
“心里所充满的，口里就说出来”
就算一个人说了一些有口无心的话
他的话也能反映出
他内心的想法
耶和华审判人不但会根据内在为人
也会根据一个人的言谈对别人的影响
在言谈方面，耶和华上帝以身作则
是说话仁慈体贴的典范
我们来看一个例子
在撒迦利亚书1:12
撒迦利亚书1:12
记载了一个天使对耶和华说的话
这个天使很沮丧
因为反对者看起来一直在阻止忠贞的犹太人
用正确的方式来崇拜耶和华上帝
在第12节，这个天使说
“天军的统帅耶和华啊
这70年来
你一直向耶路撒冷和犹大国的城镇发怒
你要到什么时候才怜悯他们呢？”
在第13节
经文说
“耶和华就用仁慈的话
去安慰跟我说话的天使”
经文虽然没有说耶和华说了什么
但我们知道耶和华说了仁慈体贴的话
下面让我们来看一下
我们可以怎样
对人仁慈体贴
并说出仁慈体贴的话
这方面的原则有很多
不过今天我们强调两个
第一个原则，在以弗所书的5:1
以弗所书5:1
经文说
“所以，你们既然是蒙爱的儿女
就要效法上帝”
我们都知道孩子会模仿父母
他们真的很喜欢为父母做点事情
他们愿意模仿父母
那么想一想，一个小女孩儿
她把一个礼物送给了妈妈
这个礼物本身可能很普通
但对于妈妈来说
却是非常宝贵的
为什么呢？
因为女孩儿在模仿妈妈
她可能看到妈妈对别人慷慨
女孩儿也这样做
妈妈看到后
就会感到很开心
很自豪
耶和华也是一样
如果我们效法他，他也会很高兴
所以第一个原则
就是要心怀感激
我们常常记得对人说
“谢谢”
就会变得
更有感恩之心
所以我们每天
都要感谢耶和华为我们所做的一切
耶和华上帝真的为我们做了很多
我们能感受到的只是一小部分而已
但如果我们还是为这些事
每天感谢耶和华
就会激发我们的感恩之心
我们就会敬畏耶和华
我们越敬畏他，就越想要让他高兴
也会越渴望
效法他的美好品格
千万不要觉得
我没办法效法耶和华
我做不到
其实你只需要做到一点就能效法他
那就是培养一颗感恩的心
我想强调的第二个原则
今天的文章里也提到了
那就是我们说话要用盐调味
圣经时代
人们还没有冰箱
他们会用盐来保存食物
也就是在食物里加适量的盐
来防止食物变质
正如盐可以保存食物
我们说话仁慈体贴
也能维护别人的尊严
并且一直守护爱心
巩固友谊
我们心怀感激
就会说出仁慈体贴的话
特别是对我们所爱的人
所以要努力多看别人的优点
说鼓励人心的话，帮助他们培养好品格
不管我们面对什么难题
内心有怎样的感受
都要尽力说话仁慈体贴
做事良善仁慈永远都不会错
要坚持这样做
为我们树立了一个很好的目标
经文说
“耶和华，我的磐石，我的救赎主啊
愿我口中所说的话、心里沉思的事
都让你喜悦”

title: 필릭스 테래저스와 마이라 테래저스: 시련을 겪더라도 강한 믿음을 유지하십시오

ko.text: 강한 믿음을 유지한 많은 본들이 있는데요.
필릭스 테래저스 형제와 마이라 테래저스 자매의 미리 녹화된 인터뷰 영상을 보시겠습니다.
매우 힘든 일을 겪고 계신 것으로 알고 있습니다.
약 1년 반 전부터 가슴에 가끔씩 통증이 느껴지기 시작했습니다.
얼마 뒤에 악성 종양이 있다는 진단을 받았습니다.
수술을 받고 나서 좋은 소식을 듣기를 기다리고 있었습니다.
그런데 몇 주 뒤에 의사로부터 결코 듣고 싶지 않았던
저에게 남은 시간이 몇 달뿐이라는 거였죠.
누구나 그렇겠지만 저희도 기도를 많이 드렸습니다.
좋은 결정을 내릴 수 있도록 지혜를 달라고 간청했습니다.
제게 남아 있는 시간을 최대한 잘 활용하고
여호와께 가장 좋은 걸 드리기 위해서였죠.
자매는 남편을 정말 잘 지원해 주셨는데요.
고린도 후서 1:7의 말씀처럼 저희는 지금 ‘고난을 겪고’ 있죠.
하지만 그 구절에선 ‘위로도 받을’ 거라고 알려 줍니다.
지금 바로 그런 경험을 하고 있어요.
전 우리 부부가 낙원에서 함께 걸으며
여호와의 창조물을 보고 즐거워하는 모습이 생생하게 그려져요.
이 희망 덕분에 기쁨과 평화를 누립니다.
필릭스 형제는 어떻게 기쁨을 유지할 수 있었나요?
지금 저는 그 어느 때보다도 여호와와 가까운 관계를 누리고 있습니다.
제가 지금 기쁨을 유지하고 있는 건
여호와와 누리는 그런 가깝고 친밀한 관계 때문이라고 생각합니다.
‘하느님의 평화가 마음을 지켜 줄’ 것이라고 알려 줍니다.
기도가 없었다면 결코 이런 평화를 누리지 못했을 겁니다.
저는 지금 부활에 대한 강한 확신을 갖고 있습니다.
잠언 12:25의 말씀과 같다고 할 수 있습니다.
좋은 말은 마음을 북돋아 준다”고 했죠.
사랑과 관심과 염려를 표현하는 말을 정말 많이 해 주었습니다.
저희 부부는 형제들이 해 주는 그런 좋은 말을 통해
그리고 제가 지금 처한 상황 때문에
가족들에게 왕국 진리를 전할 좋은 기회가 많이 생겼습니다.
어머니와 성서 연구를 할 수 있어서 정말 행복했습니다.
이런 일을 겪으면서 여호와에 대한 믿음이 어떻게 강해지셨습니까?
남편이 얼마 못 살 거라는 말을 들은 날이었죠.
그날 베델 가족 연구 때 살펴본 기사의 제목이
이어서 “여호와의 영원한 팔에 계속 안겨 있으십시오”라는 강의가 있었죠.
여호와께서는 바로 그날 우리에게 꼭 필요했던 내용을 들려주셨습니다.
우리의 기도에 대한 응답인 것 같았어요.
그분이 아무 걱정할 필요 없다고 말씀하시는 것 같았죠.
이 일을 통해 여호와께서 “훨씬 더 넘치게” 해 주시는 분이라는 믿음이 강해졌습니다.
계속 우리를 돌보고 인도해 주실 것임을 확신하게 되었죠.
미래에 관한 약속도 반드시 이루어 주실 것이라는 점도요.
앞으로 살 수 있는 날이 얼마 남지 않았다는 것을 알게 되면
하지만 여호와께서는 그분의 손으로 우리를 꽉 붙잡아 주셨습니다.
그 덕분에 쓰러지지 않을 수 있었죠.
이 시련을 겪으면서 여호와의 사랑을 분명히 느꼈습니다.
그분은 우리가 결정을 내리고 한 걸음 한 걸음 내디딜 때마다
수술을 받고 얼마 살지 못할 거라는 말을 들을 때까지
제 믿음이 정말 강해졌다고 분명히 말할 수 있습니다.
잠깐 동안 잠을 자게 될 겁니다.
제가 여호와의 모든 약속을 믿는다는 걸 그분께 보여 드리고
끝까지 충절을 온전히 지킬 수 있다는 건 정말 영예로운 일입니다.
두 분은 믿음의 살아 있는 본이십니다.
이 인터뷰를 정말 많이 봤지만 볼 때마다 감동적입니다.
그들이 얼마나 강한 믿음을 가지고 있었고
여호와께 가장 좋은 것을 바치기를 열망했는지를 직접 보셨을 겁니다.
마이라 자매는 지금도 훌륭한 믿음을 나타내면서 잘 인내하고 있습니다.
필릭스 형제의 어머니는 영적으로 계속 잘 발전하고 계십니다.

en.text: Well, we have many fine examples
of those who have maintained their focus
during extreme life events.
Consider the experience of Felix and Mayra Terrazas
in the following prerecorded interview.
Well, it’s a privilege to be with Felix and Mayra Terrazas,
serving at Wallkill.
We understand
it’s been a very difficult year.
Could you share some of the details of your medical condition?
Well, about a year and a half ago,
I started developing an infrequent pain in my chest,
which led me to seeing several doctors.
Soon thereafter, I was diagnosed with a malignant tumor
that was only going to be treatable by its complete removal.
After the surgery, we were hoping to hear good news moving forward.
Then, a few weeks later,
one of my doctors conveyed to us some of the most difficult words
that one could imagine hearing
—a life expectancy of just a few months.
Wow!
That had to have been difficult to hear.
How were you able to get your mind wrapped around that?
Well, as you can imagine, after many intense and tearful prayers
asking Jehovah to give us peace of mind
and to give us a calm heart and wisdom to make a good decision,
we decided on a treatment of hospice care
that would allow me to make the most of the time that I had left
and to be able to give my very best to Jehovah.
That’s remarkable, Felix.
And, Mayra, you’re such a supportive wife.
How have you been able to be so positive?
I have to say that it is my hope in Jehovah.
That is what has helped me.
At the moment, we are ‘sharing in the sufferings’
mentioned at 2 Corinthians 1:7.
But the verse concludes that ‘we will also share in the comfort,’
and we are also experiencing that right now.
I have no doubt that I’ll see Felix again in the resurrection.
When I look to the future,
I can vividly picture us walking through the Paradise earth,
enjoying Jehovah’s beautiful creation.
This is the life, “the real life,” that Jehovah promises.
And it’s this hope that gives me joy and peace.
Beautifully expressed.
Thank you.
And, Felix, how have you been able to be so joyful?
My relationship with Jehovah has never been stronger than it is right now.
And I believe that it’s this closeness and this intimacy with him
that is providing me the joy that I’m experiencing.
Now, Philippians 4:6, 7
assures me that “by prayer and [by] supplication,”
it says that “the peace of God . . . will guard your hearts.”
Prayer has been so indispensable
in bringing me peace during this process,
and it’s also amplified my appreciation for the resurrection
like I’ve never experienced before.
Proverbs 12:25, I think,
perfectly illustrates our current situation.
There it says: “Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down,
but a good word [it says that it] cheers it up.”
Both Mayra and I have benefited
from what we feel is an enormous storehouse
of good words received in the way of concern,
of love and compassion, from the brotherhood.
And last, my current circumstances
have opened up such a wonderful opportunity
to share Kingdom truths with family members,
including the beautiful privilege of being able to study the Bible
with my mother during the past few months.
Wow!
Amazing!
Tell us, how has this experience
affected your faith and trust in Jehovah?
Well, we have seen Jehovah’s hand from the very beginning,
but one time sticks out in my mind.
It was the day we received Felix’s prognosis.
That evening, the Bethel family Watchtower  Study
considered the article “Keep Calm and Trust in Jehovah,”
and this was followed by a lecture
entitled “Remain in Jehovah’s Everlasting Arms.”
Jehovah provided us exactly what we needed to hear
that very day.
We felt it was an answer to our prayers,
as if to reassure us that he has everything under control.
This has strengthened my faith in that Jehovah will continue
to “more than superabundantly” provide for us care and guidance
as we face new challenges
and will without a doubt fulfill his promises for the future.
I think when you come to understand that you only have a short time to live,
you know, that’s something that can very easily knock you right off of your feet.
But we know that we have been grasped
by Jehovah’s caring hands right now,
and that is what’s stabilized us.
You know, throughout this ordeal, we have seen Jehovah’s love
—his care and assistance—
in every decision, in every step, that we’ve taken.
From the first visits to the doctors, through surgery,
and into the most difficult part of the prognosis,
we have lacked nothing.
I absolutely know that my faith
has only been strengthened by the challenges of this trial.
So now as I prepare to close my eyes
and fall asleep for just a brief time,
it is a privilege for me to demonstrate to Jehovah my trust
in all of his promises
and to maintain complete integrity right down to the end.
What an outstanding expression of faith!
Thank you both so much for sharing
those deeply personal and motivating expressions.
You are a living example of faith in action,
and we love you.
I can’t tell you how many times I’ve seen that, and it’s so moving each time.
On June 8, 2021, our dear brother Felix went to sleep in death,
just seven weeks after this interview.
And any, frankly, that were around the Terrazas during this time
would see firsthand
the power of faith
and their focus on wanting to give Jehovah their absolute best.
It was tremendous!
Mayra, dear Mayra, continues to show
that same faith and endurance even now.
And Felix’s mother
—she has continued to progress spiritually, we understand.
Felix will be so happy to hear that.

cn.text: 很多弟兄姐妹都在非常困难的情况下
依然信心坚定、保持专注
接下来我们会看看一个提前录制好的访谈
是关于特拉萨斯弟兄姐妹的经历
费利克斯、梅拉
我很荣幸能跟你们一起在华基尔服务
我们知道你们度过了非常困难的一年
费利克斯，可以告诉我们
你目前的身体状况吗？
大约一年半以前
我开始觉得胸口常常很痛
就去看了几个医生
不久后
医生就诊断出我得了一种恶性的肿瘤
一定要动手术
完全切除才行
手术之后
我们希望从医生那里听到好消息
谁知道几个星期后
一位医生告诉我们
一个令人
难以接受的事实
那就是，我的生命
只剩下几个月了
哇！这真的像晴天霹雳一样
那当时你怎样应付这种艰难的情况呢？
我们好多次非常恳切地
流着泪跟上帝祷告
希望耶和华可以赐给我们内心的安宁
和智慧做正确的决定
后来我们决定接受临终的安宁疗护
这样我就可以在我离开前
把自己最好的献给耶和华
费利克斯，你真的很鼓励我们
梅拉，你一直忠贞地支持丈夫
那你是怎样保持积极的呢？
真正能帮助我的就是
信赖耶和华
在哥林多后书1:7说
我们同受苦难
后面说，我们也同得安慰
经文说的，正是我们所经历的
我确信我们一定会在乐园里重聚
这一切仿佛近在眼前
我们一起散步
一起欣赏耶和华创造的奇妙万物
这才是耶和华承诺赐给我们真正的生命
这个希望让我感到安宁和喜乐
我们也非常期待，谢谢你
那么费利克斯
你是怎样让自己保持喜乐的呢？
我跟耶和华的关系
从来没有像现在这么紧密
一定是因为这个原因
我才能在这么艰难的情况下
