title: 제152기 길르앗 졸업식—결론 연설 및 임명

ko.text: 오늘 졸업식 프로그램의 주요 연설을 들으실 시간이 되었습니다.
새뮤얼 허드 형제의 연설을 들으실 텐데요.
허드 형제가 준비하신 연설의 제목이 아주 흥미롭습니다.
여러분은 이제 임지로 가게 될 것입니다.
임신한 여자처럼 여러분의 배는 만삭이 되었습니다.
여러분의 배가 많이 불렀으니 이제 곧 아기가 태어날 것입니다.
언제 나오냐고 물어보자 의사는 “언제든요” 하고 대답하죠.
여러분의 정신과 마음도 비유적으로 영적인 것을 출산할 준비가 되었습니다.
네, 오늘이 바로 여러분이 출산하는 날입니다.
여러분에게서 나오는 빛은 주변을 밝게 비춥니다.
도시가 산 위에 있으면 숨겨질 수가 없습니다.
사람들은 등불을 켜서 통으로 덮어 두지 않고 등잔대 위에 둡니다.
그러면 집 안에 있는 모든 사람에게 빛이 비칩니다.
이와 같이 여러분의 빛을 사람들 앞에 비추어,
그들이 여러분의 훌륭한 행실을 보고 하늘에 계신 여러분의 아버지께
우선 집 안에 있는 여러분의 영적인 형제 자매들에게 빛을 비추십시오.
하지만 그들에게만이 아니라 다른 사람들에게도 빛을 비추십시오.
여러분은 지난 5개월 동안 여호와의 성품을 공부했고
물론 인간은 여호와의 모습을 실제로 볼 수는 없습니다.
여호와 하느님께서 영적인 언어로 자신을 묘사하신다면
그것은 마치 눈먼 사람에게 색깔을 설명하는 것과 같을 것입니다.
여러분은 길르앗에서 공부할 때 여호와께 도움을 구했고
그분의 도움이 없었다면 여러분은 졸업하지 못했을 겁니다.
여러분의 가족과 성서 연구생과 영적인 형제 자매들에게
하지만 너무 밝고 세게 빛을 비춰서 주위 사람들의 눈을 멀게 하지는 마십시오.
길르앗 수업을 들으면서 이런 내용도 배웠어요.
중앙장로회 성원이 강의 때 특별히 강조해 준 내용이거든요.”
길르앗에 오기 전에도 여러분은 많은 걸 알고 있었죠.
그것이 유일무이한 독특한 이름이라는 걸 알고 있었습니다.
제 이름은 샘, 새뮤얼, 새미라고도 하죠.
샘이라는 삼촌의 이름을 따라 지은 건데
‘엉클 샘’ 하면 미국분들은 왜 웃긴지 아시죠?
제 이름은 제가 지은 게 아닙니다.
“엄마, 제가 태어나면 새미라고 불러 주세요”라고 할 순 없죠.
전능한 하느님께서는 자신의 이름 여호와를 직접 선택하셨습니다.
곧 길르앗을 졸업하실 여러분들은 여호와를 알지만 완전히 아는 것은 아니죠.
다 아는 것이 아니라 언저리만 알 뿐입니다.
옷 끝에 달려 있는 옷 술 장식을 보는 것과 비슷하다고 할 수 있습니다.
그것만으론 전체 옷을 알 수 없죠.
“오, 하느님의 부와 지혜와 지식은 참으로 깊습니다!
참으로 그분의 판단은 헤아릴 수 없고, 그분의 길은 찾아낼 수 없습니다!
‘누가 여호와의 생각을 알게 되었고, 누가 그분의 조언자가 되었습니까?’
또 ‘누가 그분에게 먼저 드린 것이 있어서 보답을 받아야 하겠습니까?’
모든 것이 그분에게서 나왔고, 그분에 의해,
그분에게 영원토록 영광이 있기를 바랍니다. 아멘.”
“참으로 하느님은 우리가 알 수 있는 것보다도 더 크시고,
우리가 지금까지 아무리 많은 지식을 쌓았다 하더라도
그것은 바닷가에 있는 모래 알갱이 하나에 불과합니다.
영원이란 말은 “끝없이, 끊임없이, 중단 없이”라는 뜻이죠.
불완전한 인간은 영원이란 개념을 가늠조차 할 수 없지만
그분은 순종하는 사람들에게 영원한 끝없는 생명을 약속하십니다.
성경의 어느 곳인지를 알려 드리지 않고 성구를 하나 읽어 드리겠습니다.
지난 1956년에 제 관심을 사로잡은 성구 중 하나입니다.
“그때에 나는 왕좌에서 나오는 큰 음성이 이렇게 말하는 것을 들었다.
그분이 그들과 함께 거하실 것이며, 그들은 그분의 백성이 될 것이다.
하느님께서 친히 그들과 함께 계실 것이다.
그분은 그들의 눈에서 모든 눈물을 닦아 주실 것이다.
더 이상 죽음이 없고, 슬픔과 부르짖음과 고통도 더는 없을 것이다.
이전 것들이 다 사라져 버린 것이다.’”
지금은 우리의 두뇌가 배우고 이해할 수 있는 지식의 양에 한계가 있습니다.
하지만 우리는 오늘날보다 훨씬 더 많은 것을 알게 될 것입니다.
잘된 일인데 그래야 잘난 척할 일이 없을 테니까요.
여러분은 이제 빛을 비출 때가 되었습니다.
현재 우리가 할 일은 하늘의 정부인 하느님의 왕국이
많은 고통과 죽음을 초래하고 있는 인류의 문제들에 대한
길르앗에서 배운 지식의 빛을 너무 세게 비춰서
빛이 조금만 있어도 사람들이 어디로 가야 할지 보는 데 충분할 겁니다.
오래전에 독일에서 제가 군인으로 복무할 때
그 트럭 뒤에는 M101이라는 대포가 달려 있었습니다.
우리는 깜깜한 밤에 라이트도 켜지 않고 이동했습니다.
앞서가는 차의 뒷부분에 달린 라이트만 보고 따라갔습니다.
여러분이 알고 있는 모든 걸 배울 만큼 충분한 시간이 남아 있지 않을 수 있습니다.
그들에게 너무 많은 진수성찬을 차려 주기 보다는
입맛을 돋우는 가볍고 맛있는 음식을 주십시오.
나라들은 이제 곧 언제라도 그들의 인도를 구하는 사람들이
마침내 평화가 이루어졌다고 생각하게 만들 것입니다.
나라들의 지도자들은 이미 평화의 필요성에 대해 이야기하고 있습니다.
우리는 “평화롭다, 안전하다!”라는 거짓 외침에 속지 않을 것입니다.
임신한 여자에게 해산의 고통이 닥치는 것처럼 갑작스러운 멸망이 순식간에
그들에게 닥칠 것이며, 그들은 결코 피하지 못할 것입니다.”
여호와께서는 이 세상의 정치 세력이 큰 바빌론을 공격하게 하실 것입니다.
성구에선 그 여자에게 갑작스러운 멸망이 닥친다고 하죠.
그러면 그 여자의 지지자들은 슬퍼하며 이렇게 말할 것입니다.
“하늘아, 거룩한 자들과 사도들과 예언자들아, 그 여자로 인해 기뻐하여라!
하느님께서 너희를 위해 그 여자에게 심판을 선언하셨기 때문이다.”
그 여자의 멸망을 기뻐할 준비가 되셨나요?
나라들이 우리에게 총부리를 겨눌 때 여호와께서 보호해 주실 것입니다.
준비가 되었는지는 그때 가서 확실히 알게 되겠죠.
지금은 여호와께서 우리를 사랑하신다는 확신과 믿음을 계속 강하게 할 때입니다.
5개의 매끄러운 돌을 주머니 안에 가지고 있었습니다.
돌 하나만 사용했지만 만약의 경우를 대비해 더 갖고 있었던 거죠.
우리가 성경을 읽고 묵상할 때 우리의 마음은 하느님의 말씀을 흡수합니다.
마치 비유적인 돌들을 마음에 넣는 것처럼,
하느님의 말씀을 흡수하면 지금 왕국 소식을 전파하고
가까운 미래에 강력한 심판의 소식을 선포할 내적 힘을 얻게 됩니다.
곧 언제라도 구원의 날은 끝날 수 있습니다.
노아는 방주 안에서 필요한 모든 식품과
여호와께서 지정해 주신 모든 생물을 모은 다음
모든 부류의 육체의 수컷과 암컷이 들어갔다.
그 후에 여호와께서 그의 뒤에서 문을 닫으셨다.”
구원의 문을 닫는 것은 우리가 할 일이 아닙니다.
여호와께서 닫으신 문을 우리가 다시 열어
어머니나 다른 누군가를 들여보낼 수 없습니다.
다른 많은 형제 자매들이 받을 수 없는 훈련을 받았습니다.
“내가 가르치는 것은 나의 것이 아니고 나를 보내신 분의 것입니다.”
우린 여호와께서 여러분을 길르앗에 보냈다고 생각합니다.
무엇보다 여러분이 가르치는 것이 여호와께 속한 것임을 늘 기억하고
곧 언제라도 밤이 오기 전에 그렇게 하십시오.
학생들은 연설이 마음에 안 들어서 나가는 게 아니라
그런데 오늘처럼 프로그램에서 두 명의 제프리가 연설하는 건 처음이네요.
새뮤얼 허드 형제는 이름은 흔하지만 우리에겐 하나뿐인 분이죠.
몇 가지 통계 수치를 말씀드리도록 하겠습니다.
특별 전 시간 봉사 평균 연수는 14.4년이며
이번 프로그램부터 달라진 점이 하나 있는데요.
jw 스트림을 통해 생중계로 졸업식을 시청하고 계신 분들이 몇 분이나 되는지
그래서 현재 얼마나 많은 분들이 졸업식을 시청하고 계신지 말씀드리려 합니다.
참석자 수를 집계하는 데 도움을 주신 모든 분들께
현지 사무실을 포함해 미국 베델에서 5463명이 참석하셨습니다.
오늘 연사 분들은 참석자 수를 몰랐던 게 다행이시죠?
먼저 오스트랄라시아 지부에서 따뜻한 사랑과 안부를 전했습니다.
그 구절에서 이스라엘 백성은 이렇게 말합니다.
“우리가 한 모든 일도 당신이 우리를 위해 이루어 주신 것입니다.“
영국 지부는 학생들이 앞으로도 계속될 우정과 아름다운 추억을 만들어
오랫동안 소중히 간직하게 될 거라고 말했습니다.
중앙아프리카 공화국 지부는 그 지부에서 처음으로
한 부부가 길르앗 학교에 참석할 수 있었던 것에 대해
체코-슬로바키아 지부의 베델 성원 115명이 사랑과 안부를 전했고
또 편지를 보내 준 지부들로는 도미니카 공화국, 프랑스, 아이티, 일본, 카자흐스탄,
강한 믿음을 나타낸다면 임지에 있는 형제 자매들에게
분명 큰 위로의 원천이 될 것입니다.
전쟁이 계속되는 지난 몇 달 동안 우리 지부 구역에서 볼 수 있었듯이
그렇게 하는 것은 이 세상 제도 마지막 날의 끝부분에 특히 중요합니다.
이제 드디어 학생들에게 졸업장을 나눠 드릴 시간이 되었습니다.
교습 위원회 보조자인 데이비드 셰이퍼 형제가 아주 중요한 일을 맡으셨는데요.
이번에 학교를 졸업하는 형제 자매들의 이름을 불러 드릴 겁니다.
어떤 분들의 이름은 발음하기가 좀 쉽지 않은데요.
그래도 잘하실 거라고 믿습니다, 셰이퍼 형제.
봉투 주실 때 헷갈리시면 안 됩니다.
네, 이즈지 형제 부부는 튀르키예 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
마루슈카 형제 부부는 체코-슬로바키아 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
음쿠부켈리 형제 부부는 남아프리카 공화국 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
우에드라오고 형제는 베냉 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
펠라에스 형제 부부는 페루 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
페르 형제 부부는 프랑스 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
피스코포 형제 부부는 오스트랄라시아 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
라모스 형제는 미국 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
살바두 형제 부부는 모잠비크 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
소힌토 형제 부부는 베냉 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
수아상트 형제 부부는 중앙아프리카 공화국 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다
수아레스 형제 부부는 콜롬비아 지부로 돌아갈 것입니다.
수고해 주신 셰이퍼 형제는 워릭으로 돌아갈 것입니다.
여러분께 152기 길르앗 학급 졸업생들을 소개해 드리게 되어 정말 기쁩니다.
오스트랄라시아 지부로 돌아가는 제이슨 피스코포 형제가
”여호와께서 주신 모든 좋은 것에 대해 내가 무엇으로 보답할 수 있겠습니까?”
이 뜻깊은 졸업식 날 우리 모두가 느끼는 감정을 잘 표현해 줍니다.
우리의 마음은 사랑 많은 위대한 스승이신 여호와 하느님에 대한 감사로 벅차오르고 있습니다.
우리는 하늘에 계신 아버지와 가까운 관계를 발전시키기 위해 노력했습니다.
하느님의 말씀을 연구하면서 그분의 성품을 더 깊이 알게 되었고
하느님이 얼마나 영광스러우신 분인지 더 선명히 보게 되었습니다.
우리는 여호와께서 이유 없이 행동하시는 분이 아니며
다양한 방법으로 뛰어난 지혜를 참을성 있게 나타내시는 분,
되게 하시는 분이라는 점을 알게 되어 정말 행복했습니다!
우리가 배운 점들에 대해 생각해 보면 욥처럼 이렇게 말하게 됩니다.
또 사랑하는 중앙장로회 여러분께 배울 수 있었던 것은 특별한 경험이었습니다.
여러분은 말과 행동을 통해 겸손, 겸허, 연합,
여호와와 양들에 대한 깊은 사랑을 분명히 보여 주셨습니다.
우리는 그 모습에 큰 감동을 받았습니다!
바쁜 일정 가운데서도 기꺼이 시간을 내어 우리를 가르쳐 주시고 격려해 주셨습니다.
자신의 조직의 지상 부분을 놀랍게 인도하고 계신다고 확신합니다.
여러분이 임명을 성공적으로 수행할 수 있도록
여호와께서 계속 강력한 성령을 공급해 주시기를 기도합니다.
우리는 강사 형제들을 정말 사랑하게 되었습니다.
여러분은 우리를 교실 내에서만 가르쳐 준 게 아닙니다.
”나를 보고 내가 하는 그대로 하십시오” 라고 말한 기드온처럼,
여러분은 가르친 내용을 직접 본으로 보여 주셨습니다.
귀중한 교훈이 담긴 경험을 많이 이야기해 주셨습니다.
또 우리는 미국 베델에서 일하는 형제 자매들을 정말 사랑합니다.
훈련은 교실에 첫발을 들여놓기도 전에 시작되었는데
여러분은 우리가 도착한 그 순간부터 사랑과 후대를 나타내 주셨죠.
길르앗에 오기 전에도 여러분의 사랑에 대해 들었지만
이번엔 직접 보고 느낄 수 있었습니다.
형제 자매 여러분은 정말 여호와께서 주신 선물입니다.
고린도 후서 6:1에서 사도 바울이 한 이러한 말을 마음에 새길 것입니다.
그 목적에서 빗나가는 일이 없도록 하십시오.”
우리는 길르앗 성서 학교의 목적 대로
우리는 사도 바울처럼 우리가 배운 것만이 아니라
하늘에 계신 우리 아버지 여호와께 돌아가기를 바랍니다.
여러분에 대한 우리의 따뜻한 사랑을 받아 주시기 바랍니다.
학생 여러분을 직접 만나고 강의도 할 수 있어서 큰 특권이었습니다.
연설을 할 수 있어서 매우 기쁩니다.
마지막 연설에서는 어떤 내용을 살펴보게 될까요?
오늘 졸업식 프로그램에서 좋은 내용들을 이미 아주 많이 들으셨죠?
잘 듣지 못한 부분들이 있다는 생각이 드실 수 있지만,
열심뿐 아니라 참을성도 나타낼 필요가 있다는 점을 살펴봤죠.
그 임무를 생활에서 첫째 자리에 두어야 한다는 것을 겸손히 인정하심으로
그 결과 그 여자는 정말 큰 축복을 받았죠!
또 로마군 장교와 사마리아 여자도 마찬가지입니다.
예수의 구역에 포함되어 있지 않은 사람들이었죠.
하지만 그들은 예수께 도움을 청했기 때문에 놀라운 축복을 받았습니다.
예수의 봉사를 통해 유익을 얻었던 몇 사람을 더 생각해 보겠습니다.
물론 빌라도가 예수와 대화를 나눈 후에 그로부터 유익을 얻었다는 말은 아닙니다.
하지만 그에게는 정말 놀라운 기회가 있었습니다.
망설임 없이 누군가를 처형하라는 명령을 내릴 수도 있는 사람이었습니다.
예수를 처형하라는 명령을 내리지 않으려고 했습니다.
혹시 이때 예수께서 그리스어나 다른 언어로 말씀하셨을까요?
분명한 건 그가 깊은 인상을 받았다는 거죠.
또 그 옆에서 대화를 듣고 있던 사람들도 많았습니다.
기억하시겠지만 나중에 예수께서 숨을 거두시던 때
그는 예수께서 하느님의 아들이라는 것을 인정했습니다.
연구 노트는 그가 예수께서 재판받으실 때 빌라도와 함께 있었을 수 있다고 말합니다.
어쩌면 그가 형 집행을 조직했을지 모르죠.
그분의 증언을 듣고 엄청난 유익을 얻은 겁니다.
이스라엘 사람은 아니었지만 유익을 얻은 거죠.
천사가 돌을 굴려 내는 것은 보았습니다.
그 사건은 그들의 삶에 아주 큰 영향을 미쳤을 겁니다!
지금까지 살펴본 점들에 대해 생각해 보면
임지로 돌아가면 모든 일을 다 하려는 마음이 들 것입니다.
그러니까 배를 구해서 90개나 되는 섬들을 방문하려고 하는 거죠.
최대한 많은 사람을 돕고 싶은 그런 마음은 여전히 강하게 들 것입니다.
여러분에게 특정한 임무가 있고 그걸 첫째 자리에 두어야 한다는 겁니다.
길르앗에서 배운 것만이 아니라 졸업식에서 들은 모든 내용도 적용하십시오.
한 중앙장로회 성원이 한 말이 기억이 나는데요
그 형제는 어려운 상황이 생길 때면 침착하게 이렇게 말했죠.
임지로 떠나는 여러분에게 여호와의 축복이 있기를 바랍니다.

en.text: Well, in any graduation program,
we get to the point when the principal talk, or the main talk, is given.
And this time, we have a special privilege
of having a longtime member of the Governing Body,
Brother Samuel Herd, speak to us.
And the subject that he has is a very interesting subject:
“Any Day Now.”
Brother Herd, please.
You will be going home or to a new assignment.
We want you to know that you will be missed.
It was good for the Bethel family to have you with us.
It was a blessing from Jehovah.
Like a pregnant woman, your bellies are swelled to the limit.
All the signs tell you
that a baby is about to be born.
You’re rushed to see the doctor.
He examines you.
And you ask, “When?”
He says, “Any day now.”
Your minds and hearts are about to burst
with spiritual things to deliver to others.
Yes, this is a day for delivering.
Your spirituality is contagious.
When you walk into a room, you bring sunshine with you.
Notice what Jesus said to some of his followers
—Matthew 5:14-16:
“You are the light of the world.
“A city cannot be hid
“when located on a mountain.
“People light a lamp and set it,
“not under a basket,
“but on the lampstand,
“and it shines on all those in the house.
“Likewise, let your light shine before men,
“so that they may see your fine works
“and give glory to your Father
who is in the heavens.”
First of all, your spiritual brothers and sisters
are in the house with you.
Shine on them, but don’t limit it to them.
We want others to see the light.
For the past five months,
you have been studying the personality of Jehovah
and talking to him by means of prayer.
It’s true
that humans cannot see the literal Person, Jehovah.
For Jehovah God to set down
a description of himself in spirit terms
would be like trying to explain colors
to a person born blind.
You have been asking for him to help you in your studies,
and he has helped you.
Without his help, you would not be graduating.
Now you’re ready as never before
to let your light shine
on your fleshly family members,
your Bible students,
and your spiritual brothers and sisters.
But don’t make it so bright and intense
that you put out the eyes of those around you.
Turn the wick down in your lamp.
There is no need to say every time:
“We were taught this in Gilead.”
“We were taught this in one of our Gilead classes.”
“A member of the Governing Body called this to our attention
in a lecture he gave.”
You knew some things before you came to Gilead.
You knew that God’s name is Jehovah
and that it is unique,
meaning the only one of its kind.
My name is Sam,
Samuel, or Sammy.
It is not unique.
There are many others with the same name.
I was named after my father’s brother
—Uncle Sam.
Did you get that, Uncle Sam?
I did not name myself.
A baby doesn’t say, after eight months in his mother’s womb,
“Mommy, when I get out, call me Sammy.”
God Almighty chose his name, Jehovah.
He named himself.
That is different; that is unique.
You Gilead students, soon to be a Gilead graduates,
know Jehovah but not completely,
not the whole Person, just the fringe.
Compare what you see to an ornamental edging
of hanging threads of a garment.
You don’t see the whole garment.
Romans 11:33-36 says:
“O the depth
“of God’s riches and wisdom and knowledge!
“How unsearchable his judgments are
“and beyond tracing out his ways are!
“For ‘who has come to know Jehovah’s mind,
“or who has become his adviser?’
“Or, ‘who has first given to him,
“so that it must be repaid to him?’
“Because from him and by him and for him
“are all things.
“To him be the glory forever.
Amen.”
tells us: “Yes, God
“is greater than we can know;
“the number of his years
is beyond comprehension.”
No matter how much knowledge we have accumulated in our brain,
it amounts to a grain of sand on a seashore
when we live forever.
“Forever”?
That is an interesting word.
It is defined as “never-ending,
“incessantly,
ceaseless.”
That’s enough to blow an imperfect man’s mind away
but not Jehovah’s mind.
And he promises obedient humans
everlasting, never-ending, life.
I’m going to read a scripture to you without revealing
where it is found in the Bible.
It is one of the first that captured my attention
back in 1956.
Now, that was before any of you were born.
“With that I heard a loud voice
“from the throne say: ‘Look!
“‘The tent of God is with mankind,
“‘and he will reside with them,
“‘and they will be his people.
“‘And God himself with be with them.
“‘And he will wipe out every tear from their eyes,
“‘and death will be no more,
“‘neither will mourning nor outcry
“‘nor pain be anymore.
The former things have passed away.’”
Where is it in the Bible?
Revelation 21:3, 4.
I knew you would know that one.
We are limited to how much knowledge our brains
can understand and sort out correctly.
Yes, one day
we will know much more than we know today.
But we will not know it all.
That’s good.
You will never be a know-it-all.
Now is the time to let your light shine.
Our work at the present
is to inform people that the Kingdom of God,
a heavenly government,
is the only remedy
to the woes of mankind, which are causing
so much suffering and death.
Inform people of the Kingdom,
but don’t blind them with your bright light
of knowledge learned at Gilead.
A little light will be enough
for them to see where to go.
When I was in the army in Germany years ago,
I drove a truck with five men inside
and an M101 howitzer artillery gun
attached to the rear of the truck.
We traveled during a pitch-dark night with no lights used.
We could only see the tail light
of the vehicle in front.
That was enough light to follow.
Keep in mind,
there may not be enough time left
for your students and new brothers and sisters
to learn all that you know.
Feed them not a heavy meal
of steak and baked potatoes
but an appetizer
to stimulate the juices in the mouth.
Any day now
nations will cause the peoples
who are looking to them for guidance to think
they have finally established peace.
The need for peace is already being talked about by national leaders.
We are not fooled by this sham cry
of “Peace and security!”
First Thessalonians 5:3 says:
“Whenever it is that they are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
“then sudden destruction
“is to be instantly on them,
“just like birth pains
“on a pregnant woman,
and they will by no means escape.”
Jehovah will have the political powers of this world
turn against Babylon the Great
(that’s false religion).
After they see the handwriting on the wall for her
and destroy her
(“sudden destruction” instantly
—it won’t take long),
her supporters will cry out,
weeping and mourning, and say,
“Too bad, too bad!”
But we will be thinking,
‘I’m glad; I’m glad!’
Revelation 18:20 says:
“Be glad over her, O heaven,
“also you holy ones
“and apostles and prophets,
“because God has pronounced his judgment
on her in your behalf!”
Are you ready?
Are you ready to “be glad over her” destruction?
I think you are.
But I can’t make that determination.
We will know if we were ready
as Jehovah protects us
when the nations turn their guns on us.
Now is the time
for us to continue strengthening our faith and trust
in Jehovah’s love for us.
Study, meditate,
associate, and preach the Kingdom.
Young David, when facing Goliath,
had five smooth stones in his pouch,
the pouch of his shepherd’s bag.
He only used one,
but he was prepared in case he needed more.
When we read the Bible and meditate on it,
our figurative heart absorbs God’s Word.
Like putting symbolic stones
in our figurative heart,
this gives us the inner strength we need
to preach the Kingdom message now
and to proclaim the hard-hitting judgment message
that we may deliver in the near future.
The day for salvation will be closed
any day now.
When Noah had gathered all the creatures
that Jehovah had designated,
along with all necessary food
needed for all in the ark,
they went into the ark.
Note, it was Jehovah who closed the door, not Noah.
Genesis 7:16 says:
“So they went in, male and female
“of every sort of flesh,
“just as God had commanded him.
“After that Jehovah
shut the door behind him.”
We don’t take it upon ourselves
to close the door to salvation.
Jehovah shuts the door,
and we can’t push it open to let Mom or anyone else in.
You Gileadites are professional preachers and teachers.
You have received training that not many of your brothers and sisters
will have the privilege to receive
on this side of Armageddon.
Yes, without a doubt, you are wiser now
than you used to be
but not as wise as Jesus was
when he said: “What I teach is not mine,
but belongs to him who sent me.”—John 7:16.
We believe Jehovah sent you to Gilead.
Keep foremost in mind
that what you teach belongs to Jehovah,
and conduct yourselves in a manner that displays that.
Let your light shine, not too brightly,
but just a flicker, as needed before nightfall
—any day now.
Don’t worry, Brother Herd,
those weren’t people leaving because they were upset with your talk.
Those are the students going backstage.
Brother Herd, we loved the talk.
It was classic Herd,
and we really enjoyed the points you brought out.
It was very comforting for me because this is the first time
we’ve had two Geoffreys on the same program.
But speaking on behalf of the other members of the Governing Body,
we know there is only one, unique, Samuel Herd,
and we love you for it.
Well, now we have this part where we give you some statistics
before we get into the really interesting things.
The number of students in this class is 24;
the average age, 42.8;
the average years baptized, 26.5;
the average years in full-time service, 19.4;
the average years in special full-time service, 14.4;
and then the number of languages spoken by the 24 students,
That’s very interesting.
Another interesting feature to our program today
is that we have for the first time the opportunity to find out
how many are tied in with the live stream
on JW Stream.
So we can actually give you some idea
of how many were listening live to the program.
And we thank those that are tied in
for taking the time to put in the attendance figures.
So first of all, from Canada Bethel,
we had 398 in attendance.
From the United States Bethel, including the remote offices,
we had 5,463;
then the live audience via JW Stream,
in 132 countries.
So that makes for a total of 48,419.
Probably most of us on the program
are so glad we didn’t know so many were listening.
We have some greetings from near and far.
We’ll just quickly go through some of the comments.
The Australasia branch sends their warmest love and Christian greetings.
The Benin branch refers to Isaiah 26:12,
and there they quote Jehovah saying, “Everything we have— ”
Sorry, not Jehovah, but the Israelites were saying:
“Everything we have done you have accomplished for us.”
And that captures the thought, doesn’t it?
Britain mentions how the students
will have beautiful memories
and new friendships that will continue on,
and they’ll treasure them for many years.
Central African Republic expresses their deepest gratitude
because for the first time,
a couple from the Central African Republic
has been able to attend Gilead.
The Czech-Slovak branch of 115 Bethelites there
send their love and greetings
—also the Dominican Republic, France,
Haiti, Japan, Kazakhstan (the list goes on and on),
Mozambique, Peru, the Philippines, Senegal,
South Africa, Spain, Turkey,
and also our brothers in Ukraine.
Let me read what they say:
“As you put your increased knowledge
“and strengthened faith to work,
“you will certainly prove to be a source of great comfort
“to your fellow believers in your assignments.
“This is all important
“in these very last days of this system of things,
“as we have witnessed in our branch territory
“in the recent months of the ongoing war.
We wish you Jehovah’s rich blessing.”
Don’t we appreciate those greetings?
Now we’ve gotten to the point where we have the opportunity
to present the diplomas, and Brother David Schafer,
a helper to the Teaching Committee, is here
with this high-pressure job.
And he has the very interesting assignment
of naming the families, the brothers and sisters.
Some of them have a little bit difficult names to pronounce,
but I’m sure you’ll be good, Dave.
And then he has to give me the envelopes to pass on.
So I’m handing it over to you.
So first we have Brother and Sister İzci.
They’ll return to the Turkey branch.
Brother İzci has been appointed to serve on the Branch Committee.
Brother and Sister Maruška will return to the Czech-Slovak branch.
Brother and Sister Mkubukeli will return to the South Africa branch.
Brother Ouedraogo will return to the Benin branch.
Brother and Sister Peláez will return to the Peru branch.
Brother and Sister Peyre will return to the France branch.

Well, I have the pleasure now to introduce you
to the graduates of the 152nd class of Gilead.
And at this point, we have a letter that’s going to be read
by Brother Jason Piscopo, who is returning to Australasia,
and he’s reading this letter on behalf of this class.
“Dear brothers of the Governing Body and the Bethel family:
“‘With what will I repay Jehovah for all the good he has done for me?’
“How fittingly these words of Psalm 116:12
“describe the sentiments of each one of us
“at the end of this wonderful journey!
“Our hearts are simply bursting in appreciation
“to our loving Grand Instructor, Jehovah.
“Prior to coming to Gilead,
“we strived to develop a close relationship with our heavenly Father.
“However, over the past five months,
“our eyes have been opened even further to God’s glory
“as we have delved into the deeper facets of his personality
“through the pages of his Word.
“How fascinating it has been
“to see how Jehovah is not a God of random acts,
“but One who causes to become,
“patiently revealing his diversified wisdom
“in so many ways!
“As we contemplate the things we have learned,
“our feelings are like those of Job, who said:
“‘My ears have heard about you,
“but now I do see you with my eyes.’
“What a privilege it has been to be instructed by you,
“dear brothers of the Governing Body!
“Your humility, modesty, unity,
“and deep love for Jehovah and his sheep
“were clearly evident in both your words and demeanor.
“How touching it was for us to see!
“Although you are so busy,
“you selflessly took out time out of your schedules
“to teach and encourage us.
“We are convinced that Jehovah is using you, dear brothers,
“in a powerful way to direct the earthly part of his organization.
“And it is our prayer that He continue to provide you
“with his dynamic holy spirit to carry out your assignment.
“We have developed a special fondness for those selected to teach us.
“Their teaching did not limit itself to the classroom.
“Like Gideon, who said: ‘Watch me and do exactly what I do,’
“they were living examples of the things they taught.
“Their counsel was always given in love,
“and their experiences always accompanied valuable life lessons.
“We love you, dear brothers,
“and will treasure the time we had with you.
“We also love and treasure
“the dear brothers and sisters of the United States Bethel family.
“Our training began even before ever stepping foot in the classroom.
“From the moment we arrived, we experienced your love and hospitality.
“Prior to coming to Gilead, we’d heard about your love.
“But now we have seen and felt it.
“You, brothers and sisters, truly are a gift from Jehovah,
“and we thank you from the bottom of our hearts.
“Now, as we move on to our various assignments,
“the words of the apostle Paul
“at 2 Corinthians 6:1
“echo in our minds and hearts,
“as he urged fellow Christians
“‘not to accept the undeserved kindness of God and miss its purpose.’
“The purpose of Gilead
“is to strengthen and stabilize the brotherhood,
“and that is our determination.
“Like the apostle Paul,
“we are determined to impart to our brothers
“not only the things that we have learned
“‘but also our very selves,’
“all to the glory and honor of our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
“Please accept this expression of our warm love for you.
Your brothers, the 152nd class of Gilead.”

and that he put that assignment first in his life.
But he also showed wonderful balance, didn’t he?

because of her expression of faith and accepting him as the Messiah,
he was willing to be flexible.
And what a wonderful blessing she got!
And then the Roman officer and the Samaritan woman
—all these people were ones who, really,
technically weren’t part of his territory.
And yet they got wonderful blessings
because they asked specially for some help.
Well, what are the lessons for us?
Well, maybe before we go on to the lessons,
we can think of some of the other non-Israelites
who gained some benefit from Jesus’ ministry.
Who else would you think of?
What about Pontius Pilate
and those in his court?
When he had all these discussions,
well, now, I’m not telling you
that Pontius Pilate benefited from it.
But we do see that he had a wonderful opportunity
—didn’t he?— because he was a sort of person
who was a very violent man,
a person who at the drop of a hat would have someone executed.
And yet what do we see?
Over and over again,
he seemed to try and avoid sentencing Jesus to death.
Well, we know that something impressed him.
Again, is this one of the times
when Jesus spoke in Greek to him or some other language?
Who knows?
I’m not speculating,
but we do know that he was very impressed.
And what about those who were there listening?
There was a lot going on.
Well, remember later when Jesus actually died,
there was a centurion.
And this centurion acknowledged that this was the Son of God.
The study note, if you check it later,
says maybe he was there with Pontius Pilate.
Makes sense, doesn’t it?
He was perhaps in charge of organizing this.
So that man got a tremendous benefit
from at least seeing Jesus and hearing his testimony
—a non-Israelite but someone who gained benefit.
And then finally, what about those two Roman soldiers
who witnessed the resurrection?
Now, they didn’t have a chance
to talk to Jesus, as far as we know,
but they did see the angel
roll back the stone.
What an impact that would have had
on their lives!
So thinking about these ones that we’ve just discussed,
what do we see?

as we mentioned, there’ll be the temptation
to get yourself involved with everything that is going on
—to visit the 90 islands, to get a ship.
No, I know you’re not going to do that,
but the temptation will be there
to sort of see the need to help as many people as possible.
But what’s the point?
Remember, you have an assignment.
Each one of you now has a specific assignment.
Put that first.
Be faithful and loyal to Jehovah.
Apply all these things that you’ve not only heard in Gilead
but also in today’s program.
And then be patient.
Leave it to Jehovah. Remember, it’s Jehovah’s work, isn’t it?
I remember one dear brother of the Governing Body
made a comment once, you know, when he was facing a difficult situation.
He just looked and said, “It’s Jehovah’s problem.”
Yeah, and that’s what we need to recognize.
Some things we leave to Jehovah.
So as you go, we wish you Jehovah’s blessing.
Remember, be enthusiastic but also be patient.

title: 잘못된 정보로부터 나를 보호하려면 어떻게 해야 할까?

ko.text: 요즘에는 사방에서 수없이 많은 정보들이 계속 쏟아져 나오지.
물론, 정보를 얻는 건 좋은 거야.
그런데 문제는 우리가 보고 듣는 게 전부 다 사실은 아니라는 거지.
어떤 경우엔 사실처럼 꾸민 거짓말일 수도 있지.
그런 잘못된 정보들은 부정확하기만 한 게 아니야.
중요한 경고를 무시하게 만들 수 있거든.
그러면 어떻게 잘못된 정보로부터 자신을 보호할 수 있을까?
어떤 음식을 먹는데 맛이 이상하다면 삼키기 전에 뱉을 수 있잖아.
마찬가지로 어떤 이야기를 믿거나 다른 사람에게 전달하기 전에
그렇게 하는 방법이 두 가지 있어.
첫 번째 방법은 그 정보의 출처를 확인하는 거야.
그 정보가 제일 처음에 어디에서 나온 건지 알고 있니?
온라인 게시물은 겉으로는 믿을 수 있는 것처럼 보여도
실제로는 단지 소문이나 자기 생각을 퍼뜨리는 것일 수 있지.
그리고 부정직한 사람들은 ‘딥페이크’라는 합성 기술을 사용해서
사실과 완전히 다른 자료를 만들기도 해.
그래서 많은 사람에게 알려진 정보라 해도,
보고 들은 내용이 사실인지 다른 자료들과 비교해서 한번 확인해 봐.
두 번째 방법은 그 정보의 의도를 생각해 보는 거야.
특정한 집단이 끔찍한 일이나 혼란을 일으키려고
그런 음모론은 흔히 편견과 증오를 조장할 의도로 만들어져.
하지만 그건 근거 없는 주장일 뿐이야.
누군가가 의도적으로 꾸며낸 거짓 정보일 수도 있어.
하지만 보고 들은 내용을 확인하는 데 시간과 노력을 들이기 전에
생각해 봐야 할 중요한 질문이 있어.
자극적인 제목은 별거 아닌 뉴스도 중요한 것처럼 보이게 만들 수 있어.
하지만 눈에 보이는 모든 정보에 관심을 갖다 보면,
사실보다는 추측에 가까운 보도에 스트레스를 받거나
너무 많은 정보에 압도될 수 있지.
만약 그렇다면 알림 설정을 꺼 놓는 게 좋아.
그리고 내가 꼭 필요할 때만 정보를 찾는 거지.
물론, 잘못된 정보는 인터넷으로만 퍼지는 게 아니야.
친구들이 좋은 의도로 들은 말을 그냥 옮길 수도 있어.
슬기로운 자는 한 걸음 한 걸음을 신중히 살핀다.”
다시 말하면, 들은 내용을 아무 생각 없이 전부 믿어선 안 돼.
그렇다고 그 누구도 그 무엇도 믿어서는 안 된다는 말은 아니야.
보고 들은 내용 때문에 불안하거나 의심이 생기면,
경험 많고 신뢰할 만한 사람에게 물어봐.
그 내용이 사실인지 확인할 수 있게 도와줄 거야.
꼭 필요하지 않은 정보들에 정신을 빼앗기지 않는다면
잘못된 정보가 아니라 정확한 정보를 얻게 될 거야.
그러면 좋은 결정을 내리고 안전하게 지낼 수 있지.

en.text: In today’s world, there’s a constant flood of information
coming at you from just about everywhere.
It’s good to stay informed.
The problem is that not everything you hear or see is true.
Some of it is misinformation:
opinions,
half-truths,
conspiracy theories,
and even outright lies dressed up as facts.
Misinformation isn’t just inaccurate;
it can also be dangerous!
It can cause people to make bad decisions
or to ignore important safety warnings.
So how can you protect yourself from misinformation?
At Job 12:11,
the Bible says that we should “test out words
as the tongue tastes food.”
When you taste something new,
you can spit it out if it’s bad
before you swallow it.
In the same way,
before you believe a story or repeat it to others,
you should put it to the test.
Here are two ways you can do that.
Test number one: Consider the source of the information.
Do you know where the information originally came from?
Don’t be fooled by appearances.
An online post may look official.
But behind the scenes,
the author may just be repeating rumors
or spreading his own opinions.
And with something called deepfake technology,
dishonest people can even do things
like swap the faces and voices in a video
to create a completely fake report.
So even if a story is widely repeated,
follow the Bible’s advice
of 1 Thessalonians 5:21
and “make sure of all things.”
Compare what you hear with other sources
to verify the information.
Test number two: Consider the purpose of a story.
Is it really to present the facts
or to promote just one side of an issue?
Some reports spin the news,
emphasizing certain details and downplaying others
to sway your opinion.
Some reports may even be conspiracy theories
—claims that certain groups have secretly plotted
to cause a tragic event or crisis.
The purpose is often to promote prejudice and hatred.
Such theories have a way of spreading like wildfire.
But they are just that —theories.
And sometimes they’re based on deliberate lies,
so don’t be fooled.
But before you spend time and effort testing everything you hear,
there’s an important question you need to ask yourself,
‘Is the story really that important to me?’
Splashy headlines can make even trivial news items seem important.
But if you follow every bit of information that pops up,
you just may hit information overload
or get stressed out about reports
that are more speculation than actual news.
If you feel overwhelmed,
it may help to turn off some notifications
and just search for the information you need
when you need it.
Of course, even if you’re not online,
misinformation can spread by word of mouth.
Even well-meaning friends
may just repeat what they’ve heard.
So whether you read something,
hear it from another person,
or it’s forwarded to you by a friend,
remember the words of Proverbs 14:15:
“The naive person believes every word,
but the shrewd one ponders each step.”
In other words, don’t just believe everything you hear
without thinking it through.
But that doesn’t mean we can’t trust anything or anyone.
If you hear something that makes you anxious or suspicious,
go to someone you trust
—someone with more experience
who can help you evaluate the truth behind it.
By taking the time to evaluate information sources,
by considering the purpose behind the reports you hear,
and by not getting bogged down with news you don’t really need,
you’ll be well-informed instead of misinformed,
and that will help you make good decisions and stay safe.

title: 제152기 길르앗 졸업식—인사이드 스토리

ko.text: 일부 졸업생들을 더 잘 알게 되고
사회자는 길르앗 강사들 중 한 분인 리처드 칠턴 형제입니다.
일반적으로 책에는 시작, 전개, 결말이 있습니다.
그리고 그 책이 우리 손에 들어올 시점엔
각 장의 내용이 잘 짜여져서 마무리되어 있습니다.
우리의 이야기가 이미 완성됐다고, 끝났다고 느끼십니까?
여호와를 섬기는 일에서 내가 무언가 새로운 걸 시작하기엔
이번 「인사이드 스토리」에 나오는 형제 자매들이 하는 말에
토마시 마루슈카 형제와 에바 마루슈카 자매입니다.
이번 「인사이드 스토리」에서 두 분을 만나 뵙게 되어 반갑습니다.
두 분은 우리의 활동이 금지된 나라에서 성장하셨다고 들었는데요.
네, 제가 어렸을 땐 우리의 활동이 금지되어 있었죠.
금지되어 있을 땐 모든 게 지금과 아주 달랐어요.
예를 들면, 지금처럼 공개적으로 열리는 대회들이 없었습니다.
대회도 없고 왕국회관도 없는데, 어떻게 집회를 보았나요?
형제들의 집에서 작은 집단으로 모여 집회를 봤던 게 기억납니다.
흔히 저녁 늦은 시간에 집회를 보았죠.
그래서 저 같은 어린이들은 집회 때 졸지 않고 깨어 있기가 정말 힘들었습니다.
그런 상황에서 출판물은 어떻게 구할 수 있었나요?
전 「나의 성서 이야기 책」을 보며 자랐는데,
그 책엔 성서 이야기가 글로만 들어 있고
그래서 우린 그 모든 이야기들을 머릿속으로 상상해야 했죠.
자매 쪽 이야기도 좀 해 주시겠어요?
이런 환경에서 두 분은 어린 시절을 보내셨는데,
출판물을 만드는 방에 들어갈 수 있었나요?
어렸을 때라 저흰 호기심이 아주 많았어요.
그 방에 뭐가 있는지 정말 궁금했습니다.
온갖 비밀스러운 장비들이 그 방에 숨겨져 있었거든요.
형제 자매들이 집회에 가져가거나 숨겨 놓기가 쉬웠죠.
비밀의 방에서 출판물을 만드는 일에 더해
그러니까 자동차 뒷좌석 뒷부분에 숨겨 놓으셨죠.
자매랑 언니 오빠들은 출판물이 거기 있단 걸 알았나요?

왜냐하면 남편이 말한 것처럼, 일반적으로 우리 나이에 베델 봉사에 초대되는 경우는 거의 없거든요.
그럼 페루 베델에 계신 지는 얼마나 되셨나요?
그러면 몬트리올을 떠나신 지는 몇 년 정도 되신 거죠?
10년이요. 파피노 형제가 1, 2년만 해 보라고 했을 때 두 분이 이렇게 될 줄 알았을까요?
저희가 페루에서 봉사하면 축복을 많이 받을 거란 건 분명히 아셨겠죠.
일단 1년만 봉사를 해 보고 그 다음에 상황을 보라고 하신 조언이
지금까지 살아오면서 많은 조정을 하셨는데 그런 결정들에 대해 어떻게 느끼시나요?
정말 감사 하게도, 남편과 저의 가족들이 모두 처음부터 우리를 지원해 줬어요.
그리고 파피노 형제 부부처럼 본이 되는 형제 자매들이 있어서 정말 좋았죠.
우리에게 어떻게 예상하지 못한 축복을 주시는지 경험했어요.
우리의 삶이라는 책에 새로운 페이지들이 더해진 거죠.
네, 지금까지 우리에게 도움을 준 모든 형제 자매들께 진심으로 감사드리고 싶습니다.
아내가 말한 것처럼 우린 전혀 후회하지 않아요.
이 봉사를 좀 늦게 시작하긴 했지만, 여호와께선 우리에게 적절한 때를 알고 계셨죠.
그리고 뒤돌아 보면 여호와께서 우리에게 주신 축복들이 너무 많아서
정말 감사하고 기쁘다고밖에 말할 수 없어요.
우린 여호와께 더 많은 봉사를 드리기에 너무 늦은 나이는 없다고 확신합니다.
많은 조정을 해 오신 두 분의 이야기를 들으니 격려가 되네요.
그리고 여호와께서 두 분과 계속 함께 계시면서 축복해 주셨다는 것도 알 수 있었고요.
오늘 나와 주신 네 분은 모두 살면서 여러 가지 조정을 하고
네 분의 이야기를 통해 우리는 봉사를 확장하는 데 너무 늦은 나이는 없다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
우리가 이 두 부부처럼 믿음을 나타낼 때 여호와께서는 우리에게 어떻게 해 주실 것입니까?
이 산더러 ‘여기서 저기로 옮겨 가라’ 해도 옮겨 갈 것이고,
또 여러분에게 불가능한 일은 아무것도 없을 것입니다.”
아직 내용을 수정하거나 새 이야기를 쓸 시간이 있습니다.
여러분이 믿음을 나타낸다면 여호와께서는 산을 옮겨 주시겠다고
그리고 불가능한 일은 아무것도 없을 거라고 약속하십니다.
칠턴 형제와 인터뷰에 참여한 모든 분들께 진심으로 감사합니다.
보신 것처럼 어떤 사람들은 십 대에 파이오니아를 시작하지만
좀 더 나이 들어서 파이오니아를 시작하는 사람들도 있죠.
따라서 새로운 걸 시작하기엔 너무 늦었다고 생각하지 마십시오.

en.text: In recent years, we’ve enjoyed watching The Inside Story,
and it really has helped us to get to know some of the students a little better
and to get “the inside story.”
So let’s enjoy this presentation of The Inside Story
as presented by one of the other lecturers,
or the instructors, in Gilead, Brother Richard Chilton.
All of us have a story.
But how is that story written?
A literal book contains a beginning, a middle, and an end.
And by the time we hold that book in our hand,
each chapter has been carefully analyzed and locked-in.
That story is done, finished.
Well, what about us?
Do you ever feel that your story
is pretty much locked-in, finished?
that the opportunity to make changes
in connection with your service to Jehovah has passed you by?
If so, please pay special attention
to what our guests have to share with us today
on this edition of The Inside Story.
The first couple we would like to introduce
is Tomáš and Eva Maruška from Slovakia.
Well, Tomáš and Eva, it is so nice to have you with us
on this edition of The Inside Story.
Welcome!
Thank you very much.
Now, we understand that you both grew up in a country that was under ban.
Can you tell us a little bit about that?
We remember growing up when the group was under ban,
and a change came later in 1989, at the end of the year.
And then finally in 1993,
the work was officially registered as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
During a ban,
all the things are very different from what we know today.
For example, there are no assemblies
and no conventions at all held publicly like today.
Of course, no Kingdom Halls were available at that time.
So how did you hold your meetings
if there were no assemblies and no Kingdom Halls?
So I remember
that they were held in small groups in the private homes of our brothers,
and usually they were held very late in the evening.
So as children,
we really struggled to stay awake
and not to fall asleep during a meeting.
Under those circumstances,
how did you handle the matter of literature?
So there were no officially printed
and imported publications from our organization.
It was forbidden under ban.
However, we had homemade publications.
I remember growing up with the book My Book of Bible Stories.
It was a transcript of the stories but with no pictures.
So we had to really use our imagination and just imagine all those stories.
That was also in our family.
Tell us a little bit about your side of that story too.
Yeah, it’s very similar, I think.
My parents were involved in literature production.
It was either by typing or by photography.
Now, when you were both children and growing up under this environment,
were you allowed into these rooms where this printing was taking place?
So we were very curious as kids.
And, of course, we still tried to figure out what was inside.
We called it the secret room because all the secrets were kept there,
and there was this equipment
for making copies of literature.
A simple camera took a photo, and then with a magnifier,
they could make a different size of the publication—smaller.
It was easier for the friends to carry to meetings
and also easier to hide, of course.
Now, Eva, it went beyond
this secret room in the attic in your house.
There was another method
that your parents used in connection with this literature.
Can you tell us about that?
Yeah, actually, this literature needed to be transported somehow
to the groups that were using the publications or to the families.
So my parents did it in a way
where they put the publications in the back seat of the car,
behind the back seat of the car.
Now, did you and your siblings know this literature was in the car?
No, we had no idea.
You didn’t know.
They couldn’t tell us.
And there was also a way where they put it under our feet.
And actually, we are six kids, and I am the youngest,
so they put like four or five
or six of us in the back seat of the car.
We were sitting there patiently
and, you know, those cute little faces don’t look like smugglers.
Well, it’s obvious your parents
were thinking it through to protect everyone and to keep the work going.
That must have been very interesting, growing up under those circumstances.
Let’s move now into your teen years
and your early adult life.
What were some of the circumstances
that you had observed that affected your view, or attitude,
toward regular pioneering and just the full-time service in general?
So when I was growing up, we had no regular pioneers at all
in our congregation and just very few in our area.
Was there any particular reason why
there were so few pioneers in your area?
I would say that it took time to introduce and to understand the concept of pioneering.
Sometimes other spiritual goals were considered as more important
because during a ban, nobody was really preaching publicly.
So it took time to understand this concept
and to really have pioneers in the congregation.
And I remember that the first one whom I really met
and had the chance to work with was when I was 16.
At the time,
three special pioneers were assigned to our congregation:
one couple and one single brother.
And that single brother was accommodated in our home.
So for us, as two boys, it was really
like having an older brother at home,
a spiritual single brother pioneering.
So we could really see our first pioneer in flesh and blood
(to see him alive), and we could observe his goals.
And he spent a lot of time with us.
So about how old were you then, Tomáš,
when you started regular pioneering yourself?
So it was three years later.
It was when I was 19.
I was the first one in our congregation.
I tried, but at the time, there was still very little support.
We had just four regular pioneers in the whole circuit.
So then after several months,
I was struggling with the quota and several challenges came.
So I decided to quit pioneering
because I came to the conclusion
that it’s not really for me, so it’s probably for others.
What about in your case, Eva?
Actually, I never—
Growing up, I never had really any idea what pioneering meant.
So I didn’t have a real need
to start pioneering.
The first time I started pioneering was when we were already married,
and I set a goal to do it for one year.
But then also I stopped after one year.
OK, now you’re in your adult life here.
What came next?
So I would say that this was a turning point in our country
—when we got several couples as missionaries.
And they really brought zeal, the pioneer spirit from congregations
where they were pioneering for decades.
And this had a really nice influence on the congregations
and also the circuits.
You had mentioned, Eva, that when the missionaries came,
you mentioned a specific effect they had on the rest of you.
You want to tell us about that?
Well, I think it was huge.
They just woke us up.
They showed us what pioneering means
—that you can really enjoy the ministry.
Yeah, we remember their enthusiasm for the ministry.
And it was really catchy to hear these missionaries,
and they were struggling with the language.
So they were just learning Slovak —speaking broken Slovak.
But they identified young couples and really invested their time and energy.
They gave us a lot of their free time, not just during the ministry.
We made great friendships with them,
and until today, we have great relationships with them.
And you had mentioned when you were out in the ministry with them,
what was something that they showed you
was OK that added to your joy?
Well, this is a very important thing.
They showed us that we can drink coffee during the ministry
—yeah, good Italian coffee.
Oh, good.
They made it fun for you.
So where did that lead to?
So then later when we moved to another congregation
and with the nice spirit and support of the missionaries,
we decided to start as a couple pioneering.
I was around 28 or 29 at this time,
and we decided to start in the new service year.
We really saw and really understood what it means
that pioneers produce other pioneers
because within two years, we had 25 or 26 regular pioneers.
That’s amazing!
And they were supporting, really, every day the field service meetings.
You never— Sorry.
You were never searching for service partners.
Anytime you wanted to go in the ministry, you had a person to go with.
And Jehovah blessed it because after a while, we had a couple of Bible studies.
We were afraid, but after we started, it was a nice result
that Jehovah blessed pioneers in our congregation.
Then what was the next change for you after you started pioneering?
What came next?
Well, I felt that some change needed to be done
because I was a little tired of everything.
I was working eight hours a day secularly.
It was full-time work.
It was an international company
where everybody was just concerned about their career growth
and everything was about the efficiency in the work.
I was a little afraid to even go—
Nobody ever asked about reducing their working hours.
It was like, like the more you worked, it’s better.
So we started to pray about it, and finally I went and they granted me
that I could work from eight o’clock in the morning to noon.
But the amazing thing was that they gave me almost the same salary
as I had for eight hours,
like, for full-time work.
So your salary basically doubled while doing half the work, right?
Exactly.
How did you take advantage of that?
Well, at the time, the RTO was open.
Yeah, and I was helping with the construction of that RTO in our Kingdom Hall,
and I started to commute for the RTO to take care of some technical stuff.
And you were helping us at the RTO as a commuter.
Yes, I was working with food service
and with lunch,
but I needed to be there at lunchtime.
So I needed to go back to my employer
and ask to move my work time
to early morning hours.
So I would wake up at 4:30 a.m. and work until 10:00 a.m.
Actually, when they also granted this thing to me,
we saw that it was Jehovah behind it
because it was nothing normal in this environment.
So now with that change, you were able to fully support the assignment at the RTO.
Yeah, I could commute.
Where did that lead to next?
We were very happy at the time because we were pioneering.
We were doing a little bit of pioneering
and a little bit of Bethel because of the RTO,
and we felt that we were doing a lot
because we had to work and were supporting where we could.
But then we decided to apply for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
and we submitted our application.
There was a convention, and a couple from Bethel came,
and the brother asked us one question.
We still remember that question:
“Are you willing to serve anywhere?”
And we were like, “Yes, of course we are willing.”
And he asked us, “What about Bethel service?”
Well, we never thought about Bethel.
It was quite surprising for us.
But then we thought about this encouragement,
we prayed about it, and we decided to submit our applications for Bethel.
And surprisingly, within several months,
we were invited to serve at Bethel.
And so approximately what were your ages
around this time when you’re finally now entering Bethel service?
I was 31 or 32.
OK.
And she was younger.
OK, she was younger. We’ll leave it at that.
Real good.
So when you look back
on your life now,
how do you feel about the adjustments
that you made in your service to Jehovah?
We never regretted any of those decisions,
setting spiritual goals
—start pioneering, support the RTO, or apply for Bethel service.
Maybe there’s one change we would make.
What is that?
We would start earlier if we could.
Definitely.
Well, there are probably a number of us that would feel similarly.
But we’re glad that you did make those adjustments,
and it’s obvious that Jehovah has blessed you for doing so.
Thank you so much for taking time
to share your wonderful story with us.
It really touched our hearts, and we appreciate that.
Our pleasure. Thank you.
Next, we’ll enjoy the company
of José and Andreina Peláez.
Welcome to The Inside Story for Gilead class 152.
Did you think you would ever hear those words in your lifetime?
No. No, never.
In fact, being at Gilead
is the surprise of our lives.
Yes, it is definitely a surprise we never thought of.
Well, we are certainly happy to have you with us.
So you came to Gilead from Peru Bethel.
But before that, your home was Montreal, Canada.
How did that happen?
So I was born in Caracas, in Venezuela,
and that’s where I learned the truth.
When I was born,
my grandmother was a Witness, so she taught me the truth.
Eventually, my mother got baptized,
so she continued raising me in the truth.
And when I was ten years old,
my family decided to move, to immigrate, to Montreal, Canada.
So we arrived there
—it was my mother, my brother, and my unbelieving stepfather.
OK, so you go from Caracas, Venezuela,
to Montreal, Canada, at ten years of age.
How did you wind up in Montreal, José?
I was born in Lima, Peru,
and I heard about Jehovah when I was a child.
The Witnesses would come to my house,
and some of my older brothers even studied the Bible.
Then when I was a teenager,
because of the political and economic situation of the country,
my parents decided
to move to Canada, to Montreal, Canada.
My older brother was already living in Canada, and he was already a Witness.
But suddenly, sadly, soon after we arrived
—a few months after— my father died.
I’m sorry to hear that.
Thank you. Thank you.
So my mom and I stayed with my brother, and at that time,
the congregation helped us a lot to progress and get baptized.
So I made it a goal to share my relationship with Jehovah.
Then at the right moment of my life,
I met Andreina and eventually we got married.
What happens next with you two now that you’re married?
So when we got married,
we were not regular pioneers, but we had spoken about it.
We definitely wanted to make ourselves available.
What were you doing then if you weren’t regular pioneering at that point?
We both had our full-time jobs, and we were,
I mean, we were comfortable
and enjoyed both of our jobs—secular jobs.
So the idea of regular pioneering was there, like I said.
It was a goal that I previously had,
but, you know, we had a long way to go.
Now, you had mentioned to me earlier
that you were about 16 years old or so
when you first had this goal to pioneer.
Yes.
From 16 to what point do you finally now reach
entering the pioneer service?
Yes, so we started—
I was in my late 20’s when we started.
I was in my mid-30’s when I started.
We wanted to— Like we said before,
we wanted to increase our service to Jehovah,
but there were different challenges there and different adjustments we wanted to make.
And a turning point happened at that time
when we wanted to expand our ministry (service)
to be more useful in the hands of Jehovah.
The circuit overseer at that time
was Brother John Pappino and his wife, Sister Carla Pappino,
and they encouraged us very much to take on regular pioneering.
Yes, I remember being with them
out in the ministry during the week when they would come to the congregation,
and we’d always make a stop and go for coffee.
And we would enjoy their experiences
and just that happiness that we would see in them.
After each visit,
for family worship, we would discuss and see
how we could then simplify our lives.
Because that was it
—we needed to simplify our lives.
And we started by, you know, regularly auxiliary pioneering.
And we became—
Then eventually, we started this new chapter of our lives:
We became regular pioneers.
Now you’re in your early to mid-30’s; you’re in your late 20’s;
and now with that encouragement, you’re entering the pioneer service.
That’s good.
So did pioneering—?
Once you started pioneering, is that what now stirred your desire
to want to serve where the need was greater?
Oh no, not at all.
I mean, we always thought that serving in another country
or where the need is greater even in the country we were in
was maybe an experience from the Yearbook,
but not for us.
And we thought that we just had waited too long probably
to make those types of decisions.
So it was not something
that we thought we could do.
Correct, that’s it.
Many times we thought that we had waited too long
to start regular pioneering.
So the idea of serving in another country
never came to our mind.
However, another turning point in our life
was the encouragement of Brother John Pappino and his wife.
Now, you had mentioned to me earlier
that Brother Pappino gave you an illustration . . .
Yes.
. . . that really got you thinking.
What was that?
Yes.
When we were deciding to move,
there were always fears
(certain fears),
despite the fact that we had kind of made the decision to go.
So I mentioned this to Brother Pappino —about the fears we had.
So he gave me an illustration.
He told me:
“Imagine there’s a father, and in front of him is a table.
“And on top of the table is his child —his baby child of two years old.
And then all of a sudden, imagine that the child jumps to the floor.”
And he asked me,
“What do you think the father is going to do?”
And I said, “Well, he’s going to right away try to grab his baby
to help him to avoid hitting his face on the floor.”
And he told me,
“Well, that’s exactly what Jehovah is going to do if you jump to Peru,
if you step over to Peru.”
So that was beautiful.
And that gave us the strength, you can say,
to achieve
and make our decision to move to Peru.
So, what an illustration to get your minds and hearts thinking on it!
Yeah.
Like he said, there were many fears.
And also we had our lives in Canada, our families.
We had never been away from our families,
but the encouragement we received definitely made a good impression.
And then we prayed about it.
And yes, we thought that it was possible for us.
But it was not easy.
We still needed to make certain adjustments.
So Brother Pappino
was always encouraging us.
Yes, he said: “Just try it for one year or two, just to try it.
“If something doesn’t work, then you can always come back.
But you can taste what it is.”
What difference did that make for you —for him to give you that encouragement
to just put it in the context of just a year or two?
Did that affect your decision at all?
In a way, yes because, you know,
the idea of moving was a big change.
It was a big decision for us.
And having in mind that we could go for one year
—try it out and then come back—
kind of smoothed the fears, you know.
So that was a good example for us.
And we made the decision to move.
We made certain adjustments in our life,
in our secular work.
We sold our belongings, and we set a date.
We had a date.
We said, “By the end of this year
(that was in 2012) we need to go to Peru.”
Yeah.
So you got down there, and where did you go once you arrived there?
We arrived in Lima, and just a few weeks after,
we moved to Tacna.
This is a city in the south of Peru, bordering with Chile.
We took a bus from Lima to Tacna.
That was 22 hours of travel —a trip of 22 hours.
So the south of Peru is desert.
So you could imagine that after five hours, six hours, seven hours, ten hours,
all I saw on my left was sand, on my right was sand,
in the back was sand, and in the front was sand.
So I said to Andreina, “Where are we going?”
We had no idea it was like that at all.
But eventually, after 22 hours,
we could see the city.
We arrived, and yes, we were not going to live just on sand.
There was actually a city there.
And that was going to be our new home.
It started at the beginning, since the first day,
that Jehovah was proving to us that he was going to be there with us.
And then another door opened for us, and that was
to apply for the Bible School for Christian Couples back then.
So when that door opened,
we knew that the idea of just one year or two in Peru
was going to change.
And that’s what happened.
We attended school
one and a half years after we arrived in Tacna.
That’s when we were invited.
And then we had received an assignment.
Yes, they gave us the assignment
to serve as temporary special pioneers in Abancay,
which is in the Andes area of Peru.
So you went from the desert to the mountains?
Yes.
So how long were you there in your special pioneer assignment?
It was in total maybe five months.
Yes.
Why so short?
The branch office called us again,
telling us that now we were going to receive another assignment
to work in the circuit work —serve in the circuit work—
but the circuit work was going to be in Lima.
So you still had yet another course adjustment ahead of you.
How long were you there in the circuit work in Lima?
So after two years of serving in that circuit,
the branch office called me
and the brother told me
that they wanted to see us at the branch the next Monday.
So we said: “Fine, we can go there.
We can be there next Monday at 8:00 a.m.”
And he said, “Just make sure to bring your things to stay two weeks with us.”
Two weeks?
What was going through your mind when they told you that?
We actually had no idea.
They told us it’s training.
Training.
So we went for two weeks.
Yes.
And then
at the end of the two weeks, they told us that they extended us
for up to a month.
After one month, they extended us two months.
After two months, they extended us six months.
And then when all this happened,
I said, “Wait a minute
“—two weeks, one month, two months, six months—
am I entering Bethel in my mid-40’s?”
Yes.
So it was surprising for us.
Yes, and after six months—
Maybe Andreina can say this.
Yes, after six months, we received a letter that
that was our new assignment, and we could not believe it.
I mean, like he said, we had passed that age or reached that age
when normally you don’t start serving at Bethel.
And so how long have you been there in the Bethel in Peru?
It’s been six years.
Six years.
Yes.
So how many years, then, has it been since you left Montreal?
Almost ten years.
Almost ten.
Do you think Brother Pappino knew what he was doing
when he told you to just try it
for a year or two?
He definitely knew the blessings
that we were going to enjoy in Peru.
And I think the best counsel that he gave us
was to just give it a try for one year and see how it goes;
it was the best.
And a whole decade has passed since then.
When you look back over those
life course adjustments, how do you feel about the decisions you’ve made?
Well, we don’t regret any of these decisions.
We just feel so grateful because from the beginning,
both of our families supported us.

title: 재방문: 기도—요1 5:14

en.text: It’s good to see you again, Isabel.
The last time we spoke,
I left you with the question, What can we pray about?
The Bible answers that question for us at 1 John 5:14.
Would you mind reading that aloud for us, please?
Sure.
It says: “And this is the confidence that we have toward him,
that no matter what we ask according to his will, he hears us.”
Thank you.
You know, people believe different things regarding prayer.
But based on this verse, do you think God would answer our prayer
if we asked him for a million dollars?
Probably not.
Why not?
“No matter what we ask . . .”
“. . . according to his will . . .”
That’s right.
We can pray for anything in harmony with God’s will.
What about asking him to give us wisdom to do what’s right?
Sure.
We can ask him for that.
Yes, that’s certainly in harmony with God’s will, right?
The next time we talk, let’s discuss how God answers our prayers.
I’d like that.

title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: “온유한 자들은 땅을 차지할 것이다” (시 37:11)

ko.text: 미래에 대한 희망을 갖도록 사람들을 돕기 위해 자주 사용하는 성구죠.
우리의 주이신 예수께서 마태복음 5:5에서 하신 말씀을 살펴보겠습니다.
그리스어로 기록된 예수의 말씀에 살짝 다른 표현이 사용되었는데요.
연구 노트를 보면, 이러한 흥미로운 해설이 나옵니다.
“여기에 사용된 그리스어 단어는 겁이 많거나 약하다는 의미가 아니다.
예수께서 원래 히브리어로 말씀하셨지만 그리스어로 기록되었기 때문이죠.
“온화”라는 말은 “온유”의 의미를 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
온화하다는 건 성격이 불 같거나 너무 차가운 것이 아닙니다.
어떤 일에 반응을 나타낼 때 균형 잡혀 있습니다.
“해를 입은 것에 대해 흥분하거나 노여워하거나 앙심을 품어 보복하지 않고
죄 많은 이 세상에서 “태어날 때부터 온유한 사람은 없다”고 말합니다.
계속 발전시키기 위해 노력해야 할 특성이죠.
예를 들어, 오늘의 해설에서는 모세를 언급하죠.
그런데 성구에서는 단지 “모세가 온유했다”라고만 하지 않습니다.
모세가 단지 “가장 온유한 사람이었다”라고만 하지도 않죠.
우린 누구나 그런 평판을 얻고 싶지 않나요?
이스라엘 백성이 모세를 몹시 실망시키고 화나게 했기 때문에,
또 그들이 언제나 여호와의 말씀을 배척하는 것처럼 보였기 때문이죠.
우리는 어떤 교훈을 얻을 수 있습니까?
우리도 그처럼 온유를 나타내기 어려운 상황에 처할 수 있습니다.
사람들을 대하면서 크게 실망할 수 있죠.
또는 우리가 살고 있는 이 어려운 시기에
식품이나 의약품이 부족한 상황이 생길 수 있습니다.
쇼핑 카트에 식료품과 그 밖의 물품을 잔뜩 가져가는 것을 보게 될지 모릅니다.
그가 필요한 것보다 훨씬 더 많이 가져가는 바람에
우리에게는 필요한 물품이 부족하게 될 수도 있습니다.
그러면 우리의 온유가 시험받을 수 있죠.
그리고 정치인들이 무슨 말을 하고 무엇에 대해 다투는지를 보면서
그리고 우리가 살면서 겪는 편견과 불공정,
이와 같은 요인들 때문에 모세와 같은 반응을 나타내게 될 수 있죠.
온유함을 나타내는 면에서 시험받을 수 있는 겁니다.
우리가 온유를 기르고 유지하는 데 무엇이 도움이 됩니까?
온유를 기르고 유지하는 데 그 무엇보다 중요한 것은
여호와에 대한 신뢰심을 강화하고 그분께 희망을 두는 것입니다.
이제 우리가 앞에서 살펴보았던 시편 37편을 다시 보겠습니다.
즉 현재와 미래에 우리의 온유를 시험할 수 있는 상황들을 생각하면서
“여호와 앞에서 잠자코 있고 그분을 간절히 기다려라.”
여호와께 희망을 두는 자들은 땅을 차지할 것이다.
조금만 더 있으면 악한 자들이 더는 없으리니,
그들이 있던 곳을 살펴보아도 없을 것이다.
풍부한 평화 가운데 더없는 기쁨을 얻을 것이다.”
특히 오늘날 이 시대를 살고 있는 우리에게 더 깊은 의미가 있지 않습니까?
우리의 하느님 여호와를 온전히 신뢰해야 합니다.
여호와께서 미래에 하실 일들을 통해서만 해결될 수 있습니다.
우리가 살펴본 시편 37편에 나와 있는 것과 비슷한 사상이
로마서 12장에 나와 있는 걸 볼 수 있습니다.
모든 사람이 좋게 여기는 일을 고려하여 행하십시오.
가능하다면 여러분이 할 수 있는 대로 모든 사람과 평화롭게 지내십시오.
사랑하는 여러분, 스스로 복수하지 말고 진노에 맡겨 두십시오.
이 성구에서 “진노에 맡겨 두라”는 말은 무슨 뜻입니까?
여호와 하느님께서 지금 벌어지는 모든 나쁜 일들을
주제넘게 나서서 잘못된 것을 바로잡으려고 하고
우리 주위에서 벌어지는 나쁜 일들에 부정적인 반응을 보여서는 안 되겠습니다.
그분이 해결해 주실 때까지 기다려야 합니다.
겸손을 기르기 위해 적극적으로 노력해야 한다는 것입니다.
그런데 각주에는 이 표현들이 “겸손”, “겸손한”으로 되어 있죠.
이 점을 통해 우리는 온화와 온유가 겸손과도 관련이 있다는 점을 알 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 문제를 해결하실 때를 기다리는 겁니다.
어떤 사람이 아주 어려운 상황에 처하게 됩니다.
상황이 잘못되어서 심각한 문제가 생긴 겁니다.
“내 아들아, 네가 이웃의 손에 걸려들었으니 이렇게 하여 벗어나라.”
이런 상황에서 벗어나기 위해 어떻게 해야 할까요?
흥미롭게도, 여기서 “자신을 낮추다”에 해당하는 히브리어 단어의 문자적인 의미는
모세와 같은 시험을 받게 될 때 우리는 어떻게 해야 합니까?
여호와를 온전히 신뢰하고 그분께 희망을 둔다면,
그분은 분명 우리를 온유한 사람으로 여기실 것입니다.

en.text: “The meek will possess the earth.”
We’re all familiar
with those words, aren’t we,
from Psalm 37:11?
No doubt, we’ve used them in the ministry
to help others have a hope for the future.
But what does it really mean for someone to be meek?
Well, we get help with regard to the definition
if we turn to the words of our Lord Jesus,
as recorded at Matthew 5:5.
So Matthew 5:5,
and here Jesus is recorded as saying:
“Happy are the mild-tempered, since they will inherit the earth.”
You’ll notice there’s a slightly different expression
that Jesus used here as recorded in Greek
and that is being mild-tempered.
If we look at the study note, we’ll notice a very interesting comment.
It says: “The Greek term
“does not imply cowardice or weakness.
“In the Septuagint, the word was used
“as an equivalent for a Hebrew word
that can be translated ‘meek’ or ‘humble.’”
So we see that because even though Jesus spoke in Hebrew
but it was recorded in Greek,
this translation of the word “mild-tempered” is there in the text.
And “mild-tempered” helps us a little to understand the word “meek.”
Mild-tempered means not hot-tempered
and doesn’t mean saying someone is cold either.
It just means that they’re balanced
with how they handle their reaction to things.
The Insight  volume makes the comment
that being meek or mild-tempered
‘enables a person to endure injury with patience,
‘without irritation, without resentment,
or vindictive retaliation.’
So that’s what’s involved with being meek.
The Watchtower from which the comments are taken
reminds us that no one in this sinful world
is born with meekness.
It’s something that we need to develop,
and it’s something that we need to keep on working on.
For example, our text refers to Moses.
Now, you notice there in the Scripture
that it doesn’t just say: “Moses was meek.”
It doesn’t just say:
“Moses was the meekest man.”
What does it say?
He “was by far the meekest” man.
Now, that’s very interesting.
We’d all like to have that said of us, wouldn’t we?
But when we look at what happened
just toward the end of the 40 years in the wilderness,
we see that Moses reacted badly.
And what was it that caused him to do so?
It was because of his reaction
to persons who frustrated him, irritated him,
those who, it seemed, always rejected the word of Jehovah.
So, what’s the lesson in this for us today?
Well, our meekness too
can be challenged in a similar way.
It can be the frustrations of dealing with others.
Or even in these difficult times in which we’re living now
in seeing shortages of food and medicine.
And perhaps seeing persons with their shopping trolleys
full of items that we know they shouldn’t have got
—so many things— but here they are,
getting away with all this produce, and so on.
And yet here we are, we don’t have enough.
Well, that can be a test of meekness.
Looking at television programs
and seeing what the world leaders are saying,
what politicians are arguing about,
can also be a test of meekness.
Seeing prejudice and unfairness in our lives,
all these things
can be just like the situation with Moses.
We can be tested with regard to our meekness.
So now, here’s the question:
What will help us to remain meek?
What will help us to develop meekness?
Well, the first thing we’d like to mention is a very important thing,
and that is for us to strengthen our trust in Jehovah
and to put our hope in him.
So let’s go back to the words that we mentioned in the beginning
taken from Psalm 37.
Let’s read the context,
thinking of what we just discussed
about the tests that we may face now
or even in the future
that might test our meekness.
So in Psalm 37,
let’s read verses 7-11:
“Keep silent before Jehovah
and wait expectantly for him.”
Do we see the key to maintaining meekness?
Yes, waiting on Jehovah.
Then he goes on to say: “Do not be upset by the man
“who succeeds in carrying out his schemes.
“Let go of anger and abandon rage;
“do not become upset and turn to doing evil.
“For evil men will be done away with,
“but those hoping in Jehovah
“will possess the earth.
“Just a little while longer, and the wicked will be no more;
“you will look at where they were, and they will not be there.
“But the meek will possess the earth,
“and they will find exquisite delight
in the abundance of peace.”
When we read these words,
particularly at this time in which we’re living now,
don’t they take on deeper meaning for us?
Yes, for us to show meekness,
we have to trust fully in Jehovah, our God.
We have to leave things to him.
Some things we know will only be corrected
by what Jehovah does in the near future.
So with that in mind, let’s look at the book of Romans.
If we turn there together to Romans chapter 12,
we notice that a similar thought
to the one described in Psalm 37
is also here in Romans chapter 12,
and let’s read together verses 17-19:
“Return evil for evil to no one.
“Take into consideration what is fine
“from the viewpoint of all men.
“If possible, as far as it depends on you,
“be peaceable with all men.
“Do not avenge yourselves, beloved,
“but yield place to the wrath;
“for it is written: ‘Vengeance is mine;
I will repay,’ says Jehovah.”
Now, when it says “yield place to the wrath,” what does that mean?
Well, we know that The Watchtower
has helped us to see that that’s Jehovah’s wrath.
In other words, it’s his right
to rectify all these bad things that are happening.
So rather than presumptuously trying to jump in and right the wrong
and try to react in a negative way
to all these bad things that are happening around us,
some things we realize we have to leave to Jehovah
and allow him to correct the situation.
So that’s the first point:
Strengthen our trust in Jehovah.
Yes, make sure our hope is in him.
The second point is
that we need to actively develop humility.
Now, later, if you check the book
of Zephaniah 2:3,
it mentions there that we need to “seek meekness,”
and it mentions “meek ones of the earth.”
But the footnote to that verse
mentions “humility,” the “humble ones.”
So obviously, then, humility is also connected
with having a mild temper and being meek.
How so?
Well, humility means we respect others.
And of course, included in that is our respect of Jehovah,
allowing him to do what he needs to do
rather than us presumptuously stepping in.
And our final thought we can find in Proverbs chapter 6.
At Proverbs 6:1-3,
here it describes a person who is in a difficult situation.
In this case, they ‘have put up a security for [their] neighbor,’
and now it hasn’t worked out well.
But what does it say to do in verse 3?
“Do this, my son, and free yourself,
for you have fallen into the hand of your neighbor.”
Now, how should we react in a situation like that?
It says: “Go and humble yourself
and urgently plead with your neighbor.”
Now, interestingly, the Hebrew expression here,
“humble yourself,” literally means “stamp yourself down.”
So do we see the lesson?
When we’re faced with a test like Moses was faced with,
what should we do?
Stamp ourselves down!
Yes, hold off that hot temper.
Yes, have full trust and hope in Jehovah,
and in that way, we can be sure
that he will view us as a meek person.

cn.text: “谦和的人必拥有大地”
诗篇37:11的话
我们大家都非常熟悉
在传道的时候
我们也用这几节经文
告诉别人未来美好的希望
那么到底什么样的人
可以算作谦和的人呢？
主耶稣基督说的话
可以帮助我们明白
谦和是什么意思
我们可以看一下马太福音5:5
马太福音5:5
在这里耶稣说
“性情温和的人有福了
因为他们会承受大地作为产业”
你可能留意到
耶稣用的词跟诗篇的词有一点不同
耶稣说的是“性情温和的人”
但我们可以看一下精读本的注释
注释说
译作“性情温和”的希腊语词
并没有懦弱、胆小的意思
在《七十子译本》中
这个希腊语词用来翻译意思为
“谦和”或“谦卑”的希伯来语词
耶稣应该是用希伯来语说的
但马太把它用希腊语记了下来
耶稣说的“性情温和”
可以帮助我们明白
“谦和”这个词到底是什么意思
性情温和的人不会行事急躁
也不会非常冷漠
他们在遇到问题时不会反应过激
而会保持平衡
《洞悉圣经》谈到“谦和”
或“性情温和”的人时这样写道
“谦和的人就算被人伤害
也能耐心忍受
不含怒，不怨恨，不报复”
我们从这个解释可以看出
谦和的人是这样的人
相关的《守望台》文章也提醒我们
我们生来都不完美
不会自动变得谦和
我们所有人都需要学习
并且不断地付出努力培养这种特质
比如说，圣经谈到摩西时
你记得吗？
经文不是说“摩西很谦和”
也不是说“摩西是最谦和的人”
圣经怎么说呢？
“摩西比地上任何人都要谦和”
很高的评价！
我们也希望自己得到这样的评价
但是我们都记得
以色列人在旷野流浪40年快结束的时候
摩西犯下了大错
是什么让他当时有那样的反应呢？
就是因为以色列人
他们让摩西很失望、很生气
而且他们总是拒绝听从耶和华的话
那我们可以从中学到什么呢？
我们也可能面对类似的情况，变得不谦和
跟别人打交道的时
就会遇到这种情况
或者我们所生活的时代
也让我们不容易保持谦和
比如我们缺乏必要的食物和药物
但我们去购物的时候却看到
别人的购物车里堆满了东西
而我们知道
其实他们根本不需要这么多的东西
而我们呢？
我们却缺乏基本的必需品
这有可能让我们变得不谦和
或者我们看电视节目的时候
看到世上的领袖彼此攻击、互相争吵
这都可能让我们变得不谦和
又或者我们自己看到
或经历过偏见和不公平的情况
这都可能让我们受到跟摩西类似的考验
就是变得不再谦和
那问题来了
什么能帮助我们培养并保持谦和呢？
要谈到的第一件事
也是最重要的事
就是要增强信心
信赖耶和华
我们必须要仰望耶和华
现在，让我们再来看一下
演讲起头提到的诗篇37篇
我们看一下上下文
同时也想想我们刚才谈到过的考验
并思考一下现在
或者将来有哪些情况会让我们变得不谦和
诗篇37篇
我们会从第7节读到第11节
“你要在耶和华面前静默，热切等候他”
保持谦和的秘诀是什么呢？
就是要等候耶和华
我们继续看
“不要因别人计谋得逞就气愤
要化解怒气，弃绝盛怒
不要气愤，以免作恶
作恶的人必被铲除
仰望耶和华的人却必拥有大地
还有片刻，恶人就不再存在
你到他们的地方去
也看不到他们了
谦和的人必拥有大地
饱享平安
满心喜乐”
这几节经文对生活在这个时代的我们来说
是不是更具有意义呢？
没错，对我们来说
要保持谦和
就必须全心信赖耶和华
把一切都交在他手里
有些事情只有耶和华
能在不久的将来纠正过来
我们可以再看一下罗马书的经文
请打开罗马书到第12章
罗马书的经文说的意思
跟诗篇37篇表达的意思差不多
我们会读一下罗马书12:17-19
“对谁都不要以恶报恶
所有人认为美好的事，你都要重视
只要自己做得到
就要尽可能跟所有人和睦相处
亲爱的朋友，不要自己报复
要让上帝降怒
因为圣经说
我会惩罚，我会治罪，这是耶和华说的”
经文鼓励我们
“要让上帝降怒”
《守望台》的文章也强调
要把一切交在耶和华手里
因为只有耶和华
才有权利最终拨乱反正
所以我们不会越权行事
看到身边发生恶事的时候
也不会想要用自己的方式来解决问题
我们会把一切都交在耶和华手里
让他来纠正事态
这是我们学到的第一点
就是要全心信赖耶和华
只有他能给我们真正的希望
第二点就是
我们要努力培养谦卑这种特质
如果你查看一下西番雅书2:3
你会发现这节经文谈到
“为人谦和”“力求谦和”
按照脚注
“谦和”又可以翻译成“谦卑”
所以很显然
谦卑的人同时也是性情温和、谦和的人
为什么这样说呢？
谦卑的人会尊重别人
当然，这也包括尊重耶和华
把事情交在他手里
而不是用自己的方式来处理问题
还有一点
我们可以看一下箴言第6章
箴言6:1-3提到一个人
他陷入了困境当中
这个人为别人作保
结果情况进展得并不顺利
第3节提出了什么建议呢？
“你就落入别人手中了
儿子啊，你只好这样自救”
怎么做来自救呢？
第3节说
“要放下架子，赶紧央求别人”
被译作“放下架子”的希伯来语原文
字面意思是“践踏自己”
我们学到什么呢？
如果我们遇到跟摩西类似的情况
该怎么做呢？
要践踏自己
千万不要轻易动怒
要全心信赖和仰望耶和华
我们这样做
耶和华就会把我们视为谦和的人

title: 세스 하이엇: 시련 가운데서도 ‘인내로 열매를 맺으십시오’ (누가 8:15)

ko.text: 아름다운 올리브나무 숲이 있는 것으로 유명합니다.
가장 오래된 올리브나무들 중 일부가 그리스와 중동에 있습니다.
어떤 올리브나무들은 수천 년이나 된 것으로 여겨집니다.
그 올리브나무들은 병이 돌 때도 잘 견디고
제대로 돌봄을 받지 못하고 방치되어 있어도
가뭄이 여러 해 지속되면 올리브나무는 열매를 맺지 못합니다.
예수께서 다양한 종류의 흙에 씨를 뿌린 사람에 관해
“좋은 흙에 있는 씨는 훌륭하고 선한 마음으로 말씀을 들은 뒤에,
마태와 마가의 기록에는 들어 있지 않죠.
여호와의 말씀에 마음을 쏟음으로 그렇게 합니다.
즉 성경에 들어 있는 희망이 우리에게도 힘을 주며
여호와께서 우리에게 주신 일을 계속 충실히 수행하려는
오늘의 성구가 발췌된 「파수대」 기사에 나오는 한 가지 어려움은
린달 형제는 캐나다에 있을 때 진리를 배웠는데,
침례받은 지 얼마 안되어 파이오니아를 시작했습니다.
당시에 그는 임지에서 계속 충실히 봉사하기 위해
얼마나 많이 인내해야 할지 몰랐을 겁니다.
그 기간에 그가 전파한 단 한 사람도 진리의 편에 서지 않았습니다.
그는 그곳에 있은 지 7년이 된 때인 1936년에
단 한 명도 반응을 보이지 않았다고 말했습니다.
그는 ‘몇몇 사람들이 진리에 반대하는 입장을 취했지만,
그런 임지에서 봉사하는 데 인내가 필요했을까요?
린달 형제는 그 임지에서 봉사하며 충실히 인내했습니다.
그런가 하면 전파하는 걸 어렵게 만드는 다른 장애물들도 있습니다.
세계 일부 지역의 우리 형제 자매들은
박해를 받고 있거나 활동에 제한을 받고 있습니다.
하지만 그들은 계속 “인내로 열매를 맺”고 있습니다.
그는 선교 봉사 짝인 스탠리 존스와 함께
킹 형제는 1958년에 수감되어, 5년 동안 독방에 감금되었습니다.
오랫동안 외로움을 느끼고 낙담하게 되기가 쉬웠을 겁니다.
킹 형제는 그러한 상황을 어떻게 헤쳐 나갔습니까?
그가 그동안 쌓아 온 성경 지식이
킹 형제도 최대한 많은 성구를 기억해 냈습니다.
이미 쌓아 두었던 성경 지식을 사용해
교도소에서 영적으로 버틸 수 있었던 겁니다.
지역 대회 일요일 오전 심포지엄에서 소개되었던 형제가 생각나실 텐데요.
그는 수감되어 있는 동안 500개의 성구를 적을 수 있었습니다.
우리가 그러한 상황에 놓인다면 몇 개의 성구를 적을 수 있을까요?
성경 지식을 쌓아 두는 것이 얼마나 중요한지 알 수 있죠?
체포되기 전에 성서 연구를 진지하게 그리고 부지런히 하지 않았다면
그들이 어떻게 영적으로 버틸 수 있었겠습니까?’
그가 “열매를 맺”는 데도 도움이 되었다고 할 수 있습니다.
아침에 봉사를 하면서 가상의 인물들과 대화를 나누었습니다.
그는 가상의 인물인 카터 부인을 만나
여러 차례 재방문을 한 후 성서 연구를 시작했죠.
가상의 인물들에게 전하는 소식을 듣기 위해서였습니다.
이처럼 우린 ‘말씀을 간직하고 인내로 열매를 맺습니다.’
우리가 인내하고 있는 것이 또 있죠.
이전에 경험해 보지 못한 방식으로 인내하고 있지 않습니까?
봉사할 때 이전에 썩 좋아하지 않았던 증거 방식을
한 순회 감독자의 아내가 이에 대해 흥미로운 이야기를 했습니다.
“우리는 전화 증거를 하면서 정말 놀라운 경험을 하고 있어요.
솔직히 말해서 처음에는 조금 겁이 났죠.
하지만 여호와께서 이 활동을 축복하고 계신 게 분명합니다.
회중들에서 성서 연구가 거의 두 배로 늘었고
재방문도 감당할 수 없을 정도로 많이 생겼죠.
네, 여호와께서는 이 활동을 축복하고 계십니다.
그분은 우리가 계속 인내로 열매를 맺을 수 있게 해 주시죠.
“여러 가지 시련을 만날 때에 그것을 온전히 기쁘게 여기라”고 하면서
그리고 그는 “인내가 그 일을 온전히 이루게 하라”고 했습니다.
아무것에도 부족함이 없게 될 것’이기 때문입니다.
우리는 결코 비성경적인 방법으로 시련을 피하려고 하지 않습니다.
다음의 왕국 노래가 우리의 결심을 잘 표현합니다.

en.text: The Mediterranean region is well-known
for its beautiful olive groves
and delicious olive oil.
Some of the oldest olive trees are found
in Greece and in the Middle East.
It’s thought that some of the trees
are thousands of years old,
and yet they continue to “bear fruit,”
and they endure.
They endure
epidemic disease,
they endure drought,
they endure abuse
and even neglect,
and they “bear fruit.”
But there’s one thing that is required
for an olive tree to produce fruit
—water.
In years of drought, olive trees don’t produce fruit.
So, what do we learn from the olive tree,
and how does that relate to today’s text?
Turn with me, please, to Luke chapter 8,
and let’s read verse 15 in its entirety.
Here, Jesus concludes his discussion
of the man who sowed seed that fell on different types of soil.
“As for that on the fine soil,
“these are the ones who,
“after hearing the word with a fine and good heart,
[number one] retain it.”
They ‘retain the word,’
and, number two, they “bear fruit
with endurance.”
Now, we’re glad Luke included that detail
that neither Mark nor Matthew included in their accounts.
Bearing fruit as faithful disciples of Christ
would require endurance.
And what is the key to endurance?
Well, the answer is in the verse.
Do you see it?
By ‘retaining the word,’
we “bear fruit with endurance.”
So, like the olive tree, you and I want to be fruitful.
Like the olive tree, you and I will experience hardships,
challenges, disappointments,
and discouragement at times.
And how is it that we “bear fruit with endurance”?
By having a heart attachment
to Jehovah’s Word.
We need to read it every day
and meditate on it
—digest it spiritually.
Why?
Because the hope that we share with others
is the same hope that sustains us
and strengthens our determination
to continue faithful in the work Jehovah has given us to do.
The Watchtower from which today’s text is drawn,
discussed one challenge
—unresponsive territory.
And certainly, that can be a challenge.
I couldn’t help but think of Brother Georg Lindal.
Brother Lindal
lived in Canada when he learned the truth,
and shortly after his baptism, he began to pioneer.
And Brother Lindal had a skill.
He could speak Icelandic.
So he decided to move to Iceland.
He did that in 1929 at the age of 40.
Now, little did he know
how much endurance would be required
to stick to his assignment.
For 18 years
he was the only Witness in Iceland.
And during those years, not one person to whom he preached
took a stand for the truth.
Now, in 1936,
after he had been there for seven years,
he commented that he had placed tens of thousands of books,
and yet not one person responded.
He said, ‘Some have taken a stand against the truth,
but the majority continue to be indifferent.’
Would such an assignment call for endurance?
Absolutely!
And Brother Lindal did endure faithfully in that assignment.
Now, there are other challenges
that can make bearing witness difficult.
For example, we have brothers and sisters in the world
who are facing persecution
and restrictions on the work.
And in some places, the work is banned,
and yet they continue
to “bear fruit with endurance.”
I thought of Brother Harold King
who, along with his missionary partner Stanley Jones,
served in China during the 1950’s
and early 1960’s.
In 1958, Brother King was sentenced
to five years of solitary confinement.
Now, that would be,
it seems, a recipe for a long period of loneliness
and possible discouragement.
But how did Brother King address it?
How did he approach it?
And what sustained him?
Well, it was the reservoir
that he had built up of Bible knowledge.
And just like his partner, Brother Jones,
Brother King remembered as many Bible verses as he could.
And he drew on that reservoir to sustain himself spiritually
during his years of imprisonment.
We might think of the brother featured in the Sunday morning symposium
on our regional convention program
who was able to write down 500 Bible verses.
How many could we write
if we found ourselves in that situation?
It emphasizes the importance of building up a reservoir.
The Watchtower  asked this interesting question:
‘If the two brothers, King and Jones,
‘had failed to make a serious and diligent study of the Bible
‘before their arrest,
what would have sustained them spiritually?’
Well, it’s a good reminder for us.
Now, the verses that Brother King recalled
also helped him to “bear fruit,” in a way.
In solitary confinement,
he still went out in the ministry in the mornings,
talking to imaginary people.
Eventually, he met Mrs. Carter
who, after a series of return visits, agreed to a Bible study.
Now, in the course of his ministry,
Brother King says that he spoke out loud.
Why?
So that he could hear with his ears
the hope that he was sharing with his imaginary audience,
and Jehovah’s Word sustained him.
So we ‘retain the word,’
and we “bear fruit with endurance.”
There’s one other thing that we are enduring
—a pandemic.
And would you agree that it calls for endurance
in ways that we haven’t experienced before?
For example, in our ministry,
we’ve been forced to consider avenues of witnessing
that we might not have been attracted to before.
A circuit overseer’s wife shared some interesting comments in that connection.
She said: “We’re having some of the best experiences
“through telephone witnessing.
“I have to say, it was somewhat intimidating when we started.
“But it is so obvious how Jehovah is blessing this work.
“In the congregations, Bible studies have almost doubled,
“and we have more return visits than we can handle.
It is so wonderful.”
Well, it is wonderful because Jehovah is blessing the work,
and he is enabling us
to keep bearing fruit with endurance.
In his letter, James said that we should ‘consider it all joy,
‘when we meet with various trials,
‘knowing as we do that the tested quality of our faith
works out endurance.’
But James continues:
‘Allow endurance to complete its work.’
Why?
‘So that you and I will be complete and sound in all respects,
not lacking in anything.’
That is our determination, isn’t it?
We would never seek to escape a trial
by some unscriptural means.
No, we’re determined to “retain” God’s Word
and to “bear fruit.”
As one of our Kingdom songs so well states:
“We will not give up nor see the need for doubt or fear.
“Faithfully we’ll serve until Jehovah’s day is here.
“Let’s keep on enduring.
That time is very near.”
Yes, you and I are determined to be amongst those
who will “retain” God’s Word
and “bear fruit with endurance.”

en.text: Many people wonder if God really listens to prayers.
What are your thoughts?
I think he does.
I believe so too because of what it says here in the Bible.
Notice how God is described at Psalm 65:2:
“O Hearer of prayer, to you people of all sorts will come.”
So how is God described in this verse?
As a “Hearer of prayer.”
Yes.
What a difference from many people
in positions of authority who are inaccessible!
And based on what we read,
do you think God expects us to pray to him in a specific language?
Hmm, I don’t think so.
That’s exactly right.
This verse says that God hears the prayers of “people of all sorts,”
or people who speak different languages.
No matter what language we pray in,
we can express to him what’s in our heart,
and he understands us.
As our Father, he cares about each one of us.
This publication discusses other important aspects of prayer.
If you’d like to read it, I’d be happy to leave it with you.
Sure.
And the next time I’m here,
we can discuss the kinds of things we can pray about.
When can I speak with you again?

en.text: Many people feel that it takes blind faith to believe in God.
They say that they only believe in what they can see.
And often what they see is human suffering.
God, they cannot see.
‘If God is real,’ they ask,
‘why do bad things happen to good people?’
Does believing in God make a person gullible or naive?
At Hebrews 11:1, the Bible says:
“Faith is . . . the evident demonstration of realities
that are not seen.”
“The evident demonstration of” God’s existence
is all around us.
Some of it we can see,
and some of it we can’t.
For example, our sun emits ultraviolet rays.
How are we protected from their harmful effects?
Our earth has a protective shield
—a layer of ozone gas that filters out
most of the harmful radiation.
If the radiation increases,
so does the protective ozone.
It’s reasonable to ask:
Is there an intelligence behind the earth’s processes
and the things we observe in nature?
At Hebrews 3:4,
the Bible says:
“Every house is constructed by someone,
“but the one who constructed
all things is God.”
Where there is design,
there is a designer.
That makes sense.
Wouldn’t that same logic apply to our complex earth?
Even if you can accept the possibility of a Creator,
you might wonder,
‘How do we explain suffering?’
If you see a house in ruins,
would you conclude that it had no builder?
Or could there be a more plausible explanation?
Why deny God’s existence because of suffering?
Instead, let your questions lead to further investigation.
To learn more about what the Bible says
on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.

en.text: Life had changed for Naomi, For she had lost her sons.
Though Ruth was sad, she comforted Naomi with her love.
Ruth truly was a friend On whom Naomi could depend.
Ruth said when needed most: “Where you go I will go.”
“Where you go I will go.”
They stuck together side by side, Living for the truth.
Jehovah saw and blessed the love That was shown by Ruth.
There is so much to learn from them, Like how to be a loyal friend.
These words I will echo: “Where you go I will go.”
When my friends are sad, I’ll stick to them.
That’s when I’m needed most.
I’ll be a shoulder to cry on, Someone to rely on.
I’ll be a true friend.
“Where you go I will go.”
“Where you go I will go.”
