title: JW 방송—2022년 12월: 제152기 길르앗 졸업식

ko.text: 코로나19 제한 조처가 완화될 때까지 참을성 있게 기다려야 했습니다.
형제 자매들을 강화하려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?
길르앗 졸업식 프로그램 제1부에서 이 질문들에 대한 답을 알아보겠습니다.
미소 짓는 여러분들을 보니까 기대로 가득 차 있는 것 같습니다.
벌써 졸업할 때가 되었다는 게 믿기지 않으실 겁니다.
여러분은 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아가든 새로운 임지로 가든
임지에 가서 섬길 생각에 열심과 열정으로 가득 차 있습니다.
지난 여러 달 동안 여러분은 많은 것을 배우셨습니다.
이제는 여러분의 임지로 가서 그것을 실천할 준비가 되었습니다.
하지만 주의할 점은 열심과 열정으로 가득 차는 것에 더해
따라서 “열심뿐만 아니라 참을성도 나타내십시오” 라는 주제로
배운 모든 것을 적용하고 실천하고 싶은 마음이 들 겁니다.
하지만 하루만에 세상을 바꿀 순 없죠.
사실 한 번에 너무 많은 것을 하려고 하다 보면 쉽게 압도될 수 있습니다.
그렇기 때문에 열심을 나타내는 것에 더해 참을성도 필요한 것이죠.
예수께서는 이 면에서 훌륭한 본을 세우셨습니다.
예수께서 이 땅에 오셨을 때 온 세상에 그분의 소식이 전해져야 했습니다.
여호와의 시간표에 따라 약 30년을 기다리셔야 했습니다.
세상을 둘러보시면서 당장 해야 할 모든 일들을 생각하셨을까요?
“나는 오직 이스라엘 집의 잃어버린 양들에게만 보냄을 받았습니다.”
예수께서는 제한적이고 특정한 임무가 있다고 말씀하십니다.
몇 장 앞으로 가서 마태복음 10장을 함께 보실까요?
10:5, 6을 보면 예수께서는 사도들을 보내시면서 이렇게 말씀하십니다.
오히려 이스라엘 집의 잃어버린 양들에게 계속 가십시오.”
그들에게도 제한적이고 특정한 임무가 있다고 말씀하신 것이었습니다.
그들은 한 번에 모든 일을 하려고 해서는 안 되었습니다.
이스라엘 집의 잃어버린 양들에게만 전파해야 했습니다.
그러면 이 성구들을 통해 우리는 어떤 점을 배울 수 있습니까?
물론, 온 세상이 좋은 소식을 들을 필요가 있었지만
예수께서는 어떻게 하셨고 사도들에게 무엇을 기대하셨습니까?
그들이 자신처럼 특정한 임무가 있다는 것을 인식하길 바라셨죠.
사도들이 한 번에 온 세상을 바꾸려고 했다면 압도되고 말았을 것입니다.
좋은 소식이 널리 전해지게 하실 것임을 확신하셨습니다.
여러분이 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아가거나 새로운 임지로 가게 되면
다른 사람을 도울 수 있는 기회가 아주 많아질 것입니다.

가서 여러분의 형제들을 돕는 임무를 완수하겠다고 굳게 결심하시기 바랍니다.
여러분이 오랫동안 기억할 만한 아주 격려적인 연설이었습니다.
그 말이 이렇게 유행어가 될 줄은 몰랐네요.
이걸 알았더라면 서두에 제 연설을 할 때도 이렇게 말했을 겁니다.
“우린 예수의 본을 따라야 하는데 마태 16:14을 보면 사람들은 예수를
이 연설들은 길르앗 졸업생들을 위한 것이지만 우리 모두에게도 유익한 내용이었습니다.
미국은 매우 넓은 영토와 다양한 풍경을 지니고 있습니다.
큰 산들, 구불구불한 협곡들, 열대 섬들, 광활한 사막들이 있죠.
하지만 이곳에 살고 있는 사람들은 훨씬 더 다양합니다.
가능한 그들 모두를 돕기 위해 120만 명이 넘는 전도인이
사람들의 마음을 감동시키기 위해 노력하고 있죠.
아이티 크레올어는 미국에서 많은 사람이 사용하는 언어 중 하나입니다.
미국 지부 구역에는 아이티 혈통을 가진 사람들이 약 100만 명이 있고,
아이티인들은 활동적인 사람들인데, 생동감 있는 춤, 화려한 옷,
맛있는 음식에서도 그 점을 볼 수 있습니다.
플로리다주 마이애미 바로 북쪽에는 “리틀 아이티”라고 불리는 구역이 있습니다.
이곳에서 웨스트 아이티 크레올어 회중에 속한 80명의 전도인들이
그들은 공원과 거리에서 증거하고 연구생의 가족들에게 편지를 씁니다.
회중 성원들은 평균 126건의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다!
플로리다주 마이애미에 있는 웨스트 아이티 크레올어 회중의 형제 자매들이
전 세계에 있는 여러분에게 사랑과 안부를 전합니다!

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting® for December 2022!
On September 10th,
24 students reached a milestone
and graduated from the 152nd class of Gilead.
Many of the students were initially invited to attend the school,
but they patiently waited until COVID-19 restrictions eased.
Now, after five months of intensive study,
how will they apply their training?
How can they succeed in their assignments?
And how can they strengthen their brothers and sisters?
These questions and more are answered
in Part 1 of this Gilead graduation program.
Well, this day has arrived for you students.
I see you there smiling and looking forward to this program.
I’m sure it’s hard for you to believe that we’ve actually gotten to graduation day.
But we also know that you’re very keen and enthusiastic to get to your assignments,
whether you’re going back to where you came from
or you’re going to a new assignment.
Over the last few months, you’ve learned so much, haven’t you?
You’ve crammed that information into your mind and heart,
and now you have that ready to implement it
when you go to your assignments.
But we need to be careful
not only to be enthusiastic, keen, and zealous,
but also we need to be patient.
So we’d like to talk to you for a few moments about this theme
“Be Enthusiastic but Be Patient” as well.
Why so?
Well, when you go to your assignments with all this that you’ve learned,
you’re going to be tempted to try and implement it everywhere.
But remember, you’re not going to change the whole world in one day
or even the whole branch.
You see, it’s so easy to become overwhelmed
if we try to take on too much all at one time.
So that’s why it’s important to be enthusiastic
but also patient.
Our Lord Jesus Christ was an excellent example of this.
When Jesus came into the world,
the whole world needed to hear his message.
And yet, he had to wait some 30 years,
growing up according to Jehovah’s timetable, before he started his ministry.
So that took patience on his part, didn’t it?
But what about when Jesus started his ministry?
What was his focus?
You can imagine him looking around,
seeing all the things that needed to be done in the world at that point.
But let’s turn in our Bibles.
If you turn with me, please, to Matthew chapter 15
—Matthew 15:24,
and here Jesus said to his apostles:
“I was not sent to anyone
except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
That’s interesting.
Jesus here mentions he had a specific, limited assignment.
What was the assignment?
To go “to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
Now, if you turn back just a couple of chapters,
in chapter 10 of Matthew,
you’ll notice in verses 5 and 6 that when Jesus sent out his apostles,
what did he say to them?
“Do not go off into the road of the nations,
“and do not enter any Samaritan city;
“but instead, go continually
to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
So as Jesus sent out his apostles
in this particular instance,
what was he reminding them of?
He was telling them
that they likewise had a limited assignment,
a specific assignment.
They weren’t supposed to try
and do everything all at once
—to go to the Samaritans and to the Gentiles.
They were to focus
just on “the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
So when we think about this,
what do we learn from these two verses?
Well, first of all,
yes, the whole world needed to hear the message.
But what did Jesus do, and what did he expect of his apostles?
That they would recognize that they had a specific assignment.
They weren’t to be overwhelmed
by trying to think of changing the whole world at that point.
Jesus showed great trust in Jehovah.
He knew that Jehovah would gradually expand the message
and the reach of the message.
And, of course, we realize that at Pentecost there was an expansion
and then in 36 C.E., another expansion.
So, what does that mean for you?
You see, when you return to your assignment or you go to the new one,
there’s going to be an endless number of possibilities
where you can help others
—to stabilize and strengthen everyone.
But if you try to take everything on at once,
you’re going to wear yourself out
and probably wear out a whole lot of other people as well.
You know the English idiom “Don’t bite off more than you can chew.”
You see, gradually do the things that Jehovah has assigned you to do.
If you try to be too broad in what you do,
you may end up not accomplishing much at all
except just wearing yourself out.
But be patient just as Jesus was,
and recognize that each one of you will have a specific assignment.
And then try to work at that,
trusting that Jehovah will allow
your good example to benefit others,
and gradually the effects of your work will spread to others.
Now, an example of this is in the South Pacific,
if I could just tell you about that now.
When missionaries arrived in the South Pacific—
Let’s take, for example,
you might end up in a country
that has 100 inhabited islands.
Now you’re a new missionary.
I remember the feeling.
And then you find out there are only ten islands
that have Jehovah’s Witnesses on them
—ten islands that have publishers and congregations.
So there are 90 that don’t.
So, what do you think the normal enthusiastic response is?
“Oh, let’s get a boat. We have to get a boat!
“We must visit all the 90 islands.
Oh, that needs to be done now, immediately!”
Well, usually you’re assigned to one congregation
in one area.
Now, what’s the point?
What normally happens?
Well, you see, if you were to get a boat
(and there’s nothing wrong with getting a boat
or visiting other islands)
and if that becomes your focus and you neglect your assignment,
how can you follow up on all the interest that you may find on those 90 islands?
It’s not just enough to go and give them some magazines,
but you need to be there with them,
build them up, and form congregations.
So normally what happens?
Well, it’s amazing to see missionaries and others
who work in maybe larger city areas;
they work diligently at their assignments.
But then maybe others from different islands
come to visit that city the missionaries are in,
and they get contacted.
They show an interest, they start to study,
and they return to their home islands.
And what happens?
Gradually, the work spreads out to all these islands.
So, what’s the point?
Don’t feel that you have to take on everything.
Focus as Jesus did on the limited assignment you have.
But then along the way, you may be surprised at what happens.
Now, that’s exactly what happened to Jesus.
Let’s go back to Matthew chapter 15.
Remember, what was the assignment that Jesus had?
In verse 24,
he mentioned “Israel.”
Now, looking at this map, we see at that time
there was actually a border around that area
that we could say was his territory assignment.
But when Jesus said these words,
where was he?
Do you remember?
Let’s look in verse 21:
“Jesus now went into the region
of Tyre and Sidon.”
So when you look at the map,
where was Tyre and Sidon?
What do you notice?
You see, he wasn’t in his territory.
He was out among the Gentiles.
Why?
Well, when we look at the parallel account
that’s mentioned in Mark chapter 7,
it tells us that Jesus wanted some time alone with his apostles,
some downtime because there were so many crowds;
they were so busy.
Now, I’m sure all of us can understand that feeling Jesus had.
So he took them out of that general area
to this territory
that was beyond what he would normally preach in
to have some quiet time together.
But what happened?
Well, the account tells us that there was a Syrophoenician woman,
perhaps (as the study notes help us to see)
from a Greek background
as far as her nationality went,
but maybe she was a citizen
or an inhabitant of that area,
the Syrophoenician area.
So this woman approached Jesus, pleading with him.
Now, she didn’t look like a Jewish person.
She probably didn’t even speak Hebrew.
She certainly wasn’t in the category
of the lost ones of the house of Israel.
So Jesus,
initially when she started to make these efforts to talk to him,
mentioned this to his apostles in verse 24:
‘That’s our assignment.’
But notice that this was a little different
in the sense that this woman
showed an appreciation for who Jesus was.
Notice in verse 22, she said:
“Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David.”
Now, here’s a Gentile woman.
Should she really know who David was?
And by saying “Son of David,”
as the study note indicates, perhaps she was showing faith
in the fact that Jesus is the Messiah.
So she wasn’t your average Syrophoenician person.
What did Jesus do?
Well, he tested her a little.
He did emphasize the fact that in a household
you first of all feed the children, the family,
and then the little dogs get fed afterward.
And perhaps he was playing on words there.
It’s interesting.
We’re not sure what language Jesus was speaking to her.
The Watchtower  did say that Jesus
perhaps did understand Greek and use it at times.
Why, his apostles obviously understood some Greek.
They wrote some of the books of the Bible in Greek.
But whatever the case, the record of this is written
—the inspired record— in Greek,
and it uses this term “little dogs.”
Was that offensive?
No.
As it’s mentioned, it was an affectionate term
like saying “puppies” or “pets.”
So whatever the case,
he must have looked very friendly, perhaps had a smile on his face,
because she was not deterred.
What was Jesus’ reaction?
Well, he acknowledged his territory, his assignment.
But then in verse 28, he said,
“O woman, great is your faith;
let it happen to you as you wish.”
Is this the only time that Jesus did something like this
for a non-Jewish person?
Remember in John chapter 4,
not only do we have this case of the Syrophoenician woman,
but in John chapter 4, we’re told about the Samaritan woman.
This non-Jewish person was witnessed to,
and then even members of her village
accepted Jesus as the Messiah.
And then what about the Roman army officer
that Jesus was able to help?
And Jesus mentioned
that he hadn’t even seen
that type of faith in all of Israel.
So, what lesson do we learn from this?
Well, Jesus focused on his assignment.
He always acknowledged what he was assigned to do.
But when opportunities came up along the way
to help those who weren’t necessarily in his assignment,
he still gave them some help
because they were genuine persons who needed help.
Yes, although Jesus realized it wasn’t yet the time to expand the work,
he was willing to reach out to these ones as well.
So, what’s the lesson for all of us?
Well, when you go to your assignments, you will have specific assignments.
Now, if it’s in a Bethel or in the field,
you’ll know what your assignment is.
So don’t start looking at all the other assignments that are around
and how you can help them and what you need to do
and say, “Oh, why don’t they change?”
I mean, you’ve changed a lot in the last few months;
but remember, they haven’t.
And they survived without you.
So, what’s the key?
Focus on your assignment.
Be zealous, be enthusiastic,
but also be patient.
Yes, have trust in Jehovah
that if you focus on your assignment, you work hard,
you take up whatever opportunities come your way along the way,
then you can be sure you will be blessed
because you’re enthusiastic but also patient.
Well, now with those thoughts in mind,
we have a very interesting program ahead of us.
First up, we have Brother Kenneth Cook, a member of the Governing Body.
And Brother Cook is going to talk to you on the theme
“Follow the Steps That Lead to Blessings.”
Brother Cook, please.
To begin, I’d like to share a personal experience with you.
When I was told that I was appointed to be a member of the Governing Body,
one of the brothers who informed me said:
“With this assignment, you’ll experience
“a great increase in responsibility.
“But you’ll also see a corresponding increase
“in Jehovah’s spirit to help you.
It will not be too much for you.”
Well, those words were very, very reassuring to me.
And the fact is that all of us
(no matter who we are) serving Jehovah faithfully
must rely on his help
to succeed in serving him.
Now, how do we show this and receive his help?
There are a number of ways.
We’re going to focus on three of them.
They are these: Follow direction, show faith,
and use common sense, or the thinking ability,
that Jehovah has given to us.
So let’s consider the first step.
Sometimes all that’s required to receive Jehovah’s blessing on our work
is to follow simple, clear direction.
Now, here’s a Bible example of that.
It’s found in Mark chapter 14
—Mark chapter 14.
Now, you’ll recall from this account
that God’s Son directed two of his disciples
to go into Jerusalem and to prepare a large,
furnished upper room for the Passover.
His directions were specific.
For instance, Jesus said that they would meet
‘a man carrying a large, earthenware jar,
and they were to follow him.’
And then starting in verse 14, Jesus added this,
he said: “Wherever he goes inside, say to the master of the house,
“‘The Teacher says: “Where is the guest room
“where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
“And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready.
“Prepare it for us there.
“So the disciples went out, and they entered the city
“and found it just as he said to them,
and they prepared for the Passover.”
So the directions were simple, right?
They were told where they should go,
who they should follow, what they were to say,
and what they were to do.
And the two disciples promptly followed that direction,
and of course, their obedience brought many blessings, as we know.
Well, what practical lesson can you draw from this?
The lesson: Sometimes all that is needed in serving Jehovah
is to follow simple, clear direction.
You’ll have many opportunities to do so in your assignments.
Follow clear direction, and look for Jehovah’s blessing on it.
But now, on the other hand, you might be asked to care for something
that’s far more involved than that.
For example, what if you’re asked to assist someone
who’s known to be difficult to deal with?
Or you’re asked to care for a work-related problem
that others have not been able to solve.
You’re the one selected because you’ve had the training.
In such a case, what will help you?
Your strong faith—the next step.
The fact is that at times we need to show added faith to fulfill our assignments.
True?
Consider the example of Ananias.
Now, he too was a man of faith,
but he faced a challenge that required even more of him,
and we read about it in Acts chapter 9.
We’ll begin with verse 10 —Acts 9:10—
it says: “There was a disciple named Ananias in Damascus,
“and the Lord said to him in a vision: ‘Ananias!’
“He said: ‘Here I am, Lord.’
“The Lord said to him: ‘Get up, go to the street called Straight,
“‘and look for a man named Saul, from Tarsus,
“‘at the house of Judas.
“‘For look! he is praying,
“‘and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias
“come in and lay his hands on him so that he may recover sight.’
“But Ananias answered: ‘Lord,
“‘I have heard from many about this man,
“‘about all the harm he did to your holy ones in Jerusalem.
“‘And here he has authority from the chief priests
“to arrest all those calling on your name.’
“But the Lord said to him: ‘Go! because this man
“‘is a chosen vessel to me to bear my name to the nations
“‘as well as to kings and the sons of Israel.
“‘For I will show him plainly how many things
he must suffer for my name.’”
Well, the direction was clear.
Where should Ananias go? To the street called Straight.
Who was he looking for? A man named Saul.
What house is he in? The house of Judas.
Ananias was even told what Saul was doing.
He was praying.
Then Ananias was told what he should do.
He was to lay his hands on him so that he would recover sight.
Simple, right?
Jesus would do the rest.
What a great example of giving clear direction!
But here is where Ananias needed to stir up more faith.
The man he was to visit had severely persecuted
the holy ones in Jerusalem.
And speaking to the Lord, Ananias added
that this man “has authority from the chief priests
to arrest all those calling on your name.”
Well, talk about stating the obvious to Jesus.
The point is that Ananias had a moment
where he was overwhelmed by the weight of the assignment.
That’s just what happened.
What would help him? More faith.
And Jesus knew how to draw it up in that dear man.
Look again at Jesus’ reply.
He simply restated his command: “Go.”
Then Jesus said that “this man is a chosen vessel to me
“to bear my name to the nations
as well as to kings and the sons of Israel.”
Now, Jesus added something there, didn’t he?
He pointed to the future.
What was he doing?
He was helping Ananias to look ahead, see.
And doing this evidently prompted Ananias
to show even more faith, which is what he needed.
How do we know this?
Well, look at what he said to Saul.
On meeting Saul, verse 17 tells us
that Ananias called him “brother.”
His initial hesitation had changed
into putting his full faith and trust
in Jesus’ direction.
Well, like Ananias, as you face challenges in the future
(and they will come; they come upon all of us),
have strong faith that Jehovah sees what is needed,
and he and his dear Son will help you.
Keep the big picture in mind,
and look to the blessings ahead for your hard work.
Jehovah will always bless your strong faith in him.
Well, so far we’ve looked at the need to follow clear direction
and to show strong faith.
Now we’re going to add another step:
Use common sense, or thinking ability.
Our Bible example—Elijah.
In this account, Elijah has traveled to Zarephath,
a Phoenician coastal town.
What was his business there?
Well, the land was in the grip of a long drought,
and Jehovah would help his prophet
by means of someone in that town.
Elijah was told: “Look!
I will command a widow there to supply you with food.”
It appears that he gave no other details about the widow than that.
So how would Elijah find her?
Would Elijah look for the wealthiest widow to care for his needs?
Or would he use common sense and thinking ability along with his faith?
Let’s see what Elijah does at 1 Kings chapter 17.
And we’re going to read verse 10 —First Kings 17:10,
it says: “So he [Elijah] rose up and went to Zarephath.
“When he came to the entrance of the city,
“there was a widow gathering pieces of wood.
“So he called to her and said:
‘Please, bring me a little water in a cup so that I may drink.’”
So then what did Elijah do?
Evidently, he approached the very first widow he met.
And she was not a wealthy widow, but a poor one.
In fact, it says Elijah had not yet passed
beyond the entrance of the city.
What does this tell us about Elijah?
First, he showed no prejudice
in following through on Jehovah’s direction, did he?
And second, he added thinking ability
to his obedience and faith.
How so?
Well, common sense would tell him to show his faith
and start looking with the very first widow he met.
Elijah obviously had confidence
that Jehovah would make his choice clear.
His obedience, faith, and good sense were rewarded
because that widow was Jehovah’s choice.
Now, surely holy spirit guided Elijah,
but we can’t ignore the faith and clear thinking ability
that Elijah developed as he obediently did God’s will.
After all, prior to that widow, Jehovah used birds
to carry food to his prophet.
Surely Jehovah could use a poor widow as well.
What’s the lesson for you and for all of us?
Sometimes we’re given much to go on
when we receive an assignment
and, at other times, frankly, maybe not so much.
In such a case, our faith and clear thinking ability
remind us to trust in Jehovah
and to look for his guidance as we go forward in doing his will.
Jehovah will always help you dear friends at the right time.
So then, as our examples show, promptly obey,
show strong faith, and use common sense and thinking ability
in our service to our dear heavenly Father.
Remembering such lessons will help you
as you support Jehovah’s work
in your respective branches.
Jehovah gives power beyond what is normal
to those who rely on him
and follow the steps that lead to blessings.
And we are confident that this will always be true of you.
Thank you very much, Brother Cook.
You clearly helped us to see the steps that are needed
for us to gain blessings.
Well, now our next speaker on the program
is Brother Jeffrey Winder, who is a helper to the Personnel Committee.
And Brother Winder is going to discuss with us this very interesting question,
“How Close Can You Be?”
How would you students answer this question:
Do you feel closer to Jehovah now
than you did before your Gilead training began?
The answer is a resounding yes, isn’t it?
Maybe you can relate to these comments
of graduates of past classes of Gilead.
One brother said: “Absolutely, yes!
“I believe I now experience more fully
“what it means to walk with God
“and know and rely upon him as a close Friend,
not merely someone I turn and look up to in prayer.”
A sister said: “Gilead definitely drew me closer to Jehovah.
“The way we studied the Scriptures with intensity
truly made me feel like the Bible was a letter Jehovah wrote to me.”
Another brother said: “Jehovah communicated with such clarity,
“which made it real and personal.
“It made me feel closer to Jehovah than ever before,
and that feeling will never be forgotten.”
Well, unquestionably, your deep study of God’s Word during Gilead
drew you closer to Jehovah.
But here’s the question,
How close can you be?
How close can your relationship with Jehovah get?
You saw it leap forward in five months of deep Bible study, but is there a limit?
Is there more? Will you ever get done?
Consider two points that answer that question.
The first one is found in the book of James chapter 4,
and let’s read together the first part of verse 8.
And let’s read it with that question in mind:
Is there any limit to how close our relationship with Jehovah could be?
James 4:8 says:
“Draw close to God,
and he will draw close to you.”
So is there any limit indicated here?
Well, it is true that in English this phrase to “draw close to” someone
could be applied in a physical sense
—actually standing next to someone.
And in that case, there is a limit.
You can only stand so close to someone.
But that’s not really the sense of James 4:8, is it?
Rather, it’s in this sense: When we talk about our close friends,
we’re not talking about those that are nearest in proximity.
We’re talking about the depth of our relationship,
the closeness of our friendship.
And so then to “draw close to God” then means
to strengthen our relationship, strengthen our friendship, with him.
And then looking at the verse, does it appear that there’s any limit
to how close that relationship can get?
The implication is that as long as we keep drawing close to Jehovah,
then he’ll keep drawing close to us.
And that takes us to our second point,
and that is the real life example of God’s Son,
because Jesus drew close to Jehovah.
Clearly, he was taught by Jehovah.
Remember Isaiah 50:4,
regarding Jesus’ prehuman existence, where he said:
“He awakens me morning by morning;
he awakens my ear to listen like the taught ones.”
Does that sound a bit like your Gilead training?
‘Morning by morning Jehovah was awakening your ear.’
Yet, Jesus wasn’t instructed by Jehovah for five months;
he was instructed for billions of years.
And during all that time,
his relationship with his Father continued to grow and deepen.
So, then, we put it all together.
You saw your relationship with Jehovah grow significantly
in five months of deep Bible study.
James 4:8 encourages us to just keep drawing close to Jehovah.
And Jesus did so for billions of years,
and look at how close his relationship with Jehovah is.
So, then, what’s the answer?
How close can you be to Jehovah?
The potential for your relationship with Jehovah to deepen
is endless.
Well, that’s just wonderful to contemplate, isn’t it?
But let’s make some application
because this really becomes a very important overall lesson
that you take with you from your Gilead experience:
That is how your deep Bible study
affected your relationship with Jehovah.
And one of the reasons why this is such an important lesson
is because your success in your assignment
is directly connected to the depth of your relationship with Jehovah.
Your success in your assignment
is directly connected to the depth of your relationship with Jehovah.
Now, why can we say that?
It’s because of what takes place
when we draw close to Jehovah through a study of his Word.

“was song number 38, ‘He Will Make You Strong.’
“I made that song more personal
“by replacing the pronoun ‘you’ with ‘me.’
“This song helped me never to give up.
“I had no Bible.
“So each day, I meditated on Bible teachings
“such as everlasting life in Paradise and a resurrection hope.
“These meditations gave me deep inner joy
“and a calm that cannot be described.
“At times, I thought about the possibility of facing death,
but the fear of death did not consume me.”
Yes, she thought about the possibility of facing death,
but the fear of death did not consume her.
The fearsome Warrior, Jehovah, was marching with her.
No prison walls, no bars can block Jehovah from marching with her.
And our sister was recently released from prison.
So whatever your trials,
we don’t know what trials you’re going to face.
You don’t know. We don’t know.
But reflect on how Jehovah supports you.
Stay in the battle.
And when you reflect on how Jehovah supports you,
it’s tangible, it’s real, it’s concrete.
Think about that.
Jehovah will never stop marching with you.
And remember, you are part of a large army.
You’re not alone.
Therefore, when you see a fellow worshipper struggling,
don’t ignore them.
Help them not to fall behind.
Help them.
Help them.
You’re part of an army.
You’ve been trained to do this.
That’s what school taught you:
not to be independent, but to be interdependent,
not independen—interdependent with your brothers and sisters.
That’s your job.
Be quick to help them back up.
Keep marching with Jehovah.
And although you don’t know what challenges lie ahead,
you are prepared.
So with your marching orders in hand,
be courageous and strong,
knowing that each trial you face, each trial you endure,
will make you stronger for the next one.
Be confident that you will always have the fearsome Warrior,
the mighty Soldier marching by your side.
He’s there, Jehovah.
So now go
wherever the battle may take you.
Go,
and be determined to fulfill your commission
to support your brothers
as you march on with Jehovah.
What a powerful encouragement
—one that I’m sure you’ll remember for many years to come!
And students, maybe I need to apologize.
I didn’t realize Anathoth was going to be the buzz word.
You see, if I had realized that in the beginning in my introduction,
I would have said, “We need to follow the example of Jesus,
“who according to Matthew 16:14
people thought was Jeremiah, who was from Anathoth.”
But anyway, you can take note of that.
But thank you again, Brother Noumair.
That was a very encouraging and stimulating talk.
Although these talks were directed to the Gilead graduates,
they contain beneficial lessons for all of us.
We hope you enjoyed Part 1.
Parts 2 and 3 will be available on jw.org later this month.
Our postcard is from the United States.
It’s a large territory encompassing a variety of landscapes.
There are majestic mountains,
twisting ravines,
tropical islands,
and vast deserts.
Across this varied land resides an even greater diversity of people.
To help all they can,
over 1.2 million publishers preach in 114 languages!
Whether native speakers or learners of a new language,
publishers try to reach the heart.
One of the largest language groups in the United States is Haitian Creole.
There are approximately one million people of Haitian descent in the branch territory
with over 10,000 publishers.
Haitians are a vibrant people as expressed
in their energetic dances, their colorful clothing,
and their delicious food.
Just north of Miami, Florida,
there’s a community referred to as “Little Haiti.”
It’s here where the 80 publishers of the West Haitian Creole Congregation
search for lovers of truth.
They have witnessed in parks and on street corners.
They have written letters and focused
on the family members of their Bible students.
The congregation now
conducts on average 126 Bible studies!
With love, the brothers and sisters
of the West Haitian Creole Congregation of Miami, Florida,
send their greetings to the worldwide brotherhood!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

ko.text: 그에 보조를 맞추는 것의 중요성에 대해 살펴보겠습니다.
우선 최근 소식 몇 가지를 전해 드리죠.
또한 본부 대표자들이 지부들을 방문하도록 마련하죠.
순회 감독자가 회중들을 방문하는 것과 비슷한데요.
다른 점은 중앙장로회 성원과 본부 대표자가
방문한 사람과 방문을 받은 사람 모두가
순회 대회 때 파이오니아들과 갖는 특별 모임에 관한
“오늘 퀸스 대회회관에서 3년 만에 대면 방식으로 열린 파이오니아 모임에 참석했습니다.
우리가 팬데믹 기간에 겪은 일들을 우리 아버지께서 깊이 이해하고 계신다는 사실에
분명 전 세계의 많은 파이오니아들도 이분과 똑같이 느끼고 계실 것입니다.
지역 설계 건축과 관련된 일도 순조롭게 재개되고 있습니다.
왕국회관 건축 그룹의 활동이 다시 시작되었습니다.
현재 새로 짓거나 대대적으로 개축해야 하는 왕국회관이
대면 집회를 위해 이러한 왕국회관들이 꼭 필요하죠!
전 세계에서 1600건 이상의 공사가 계획되어 있습니다.
대면 방식의 순회 대회와 신권 학교들에 사용할 시설들을 준비하기 위해 수고하고 있습니다.
여러분도 신권 건축을 지원하는 일에 참여할 수 있습니까?
그렇다면 회중 장로들에게 더 자세한 점을 문의해 보실 수 있습니다.
현재 많은 젊은 형제 자매들이 이 일에 참여하고 있습니다.
아마겟돈 후에 있을 대규모 건축 활동에
“그리고 여러분은 내 이름 때문에 모든 사람에게 미움을 받을 것입니다.”
유럽에서 우리의 숭배의 자유를 보호하는 일을 감독할 것입니다.
‘이미 수십 년간 유럽에서 잘 활동해 왔는데, 그런 부서가 필요한가?’
등록된 모든 종교에 지급하는 국가 보조금을
여호와의 증인에게만 더는 지급하지 않기로 결정했습니다.
여호와의 증인의 법적 인가가 취소될 수도 있다는 편지를 받고,
여호와의 증인은 노르웨이에서 120년 넘게 좋은 소식을 활발히 전파해 왔죠!
사실 여호와의 증인은 2 차 세계 대전 당시
과거에 노르웨이 종무부에서 일했던 한 관리는
유일한 종교 단체라는 것을 인정하며 이렇게 말했습니다.
특히 이 사실은 젊은이들에게 유익할 겁니다.’
우리는 항상 좋은 시민으로 알려져 왔습니다.
700개가 넘는 종교 단체에는 계속 보조금을 지급하면서도
노르웨이에서 종교의 자유를 침해하는 전례 없는 행위입니다.
새로 설립된 숭배의 자유 사무실의 도움을 받아
우리는 이러한 상황이 원만하게 해결되기를 기도하고 있습니다.
성경에 근거한 우리의 제명 처분 마련 때문에
여호와의 증인에 대한 법적 인가를 취소하겠다고 위협하고 있습니다.
우리의 숭배의 자유를 제약하려고 할 것입니다.
우리의 성경적 교리를 바꾸도록 압력을 가할지 모르죠.
하지만 우린 결코 그렇게 하지 않을 것입니다!
우리는 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
여러분들도 이 문제를 위해 기도해 주시기를 꼭 부탁드립니다.
팬데믹이 끝나 가면서 많은 활동들이 신속히 재개되고 있습니다.
여호와의 하늘 수레는 번개처럼 빠르게 움직이기 때문입니다.
이 점이 에스겔 1:16, 17에 어떻게 묘사되어 있는지 살펴보겠습니다.
에스겔은 외경심을 불러일으키는 하늘 수레를 보게 됩니다.
“바퀴들의 모습과 구조는 귀감람석이 빛나는 것 같고,
그 모습과 구조는 마치 바퀴 안에 바퀴가 있는 것처럼 보였다.
바퀴들은 움직일 때에 방향을 바꾸지 않고
여호와의 우주 조직의 하늘 부분을 보여 주는
그 수레를 제어하시는 하느님의 대처 능력과 합리성을 완벽하게 반영합니다.
필요에 따라 무엇이든 되실 수 있습니다.
··· 하느님이 우리에게 필요한 조처를 제때에 빨리 취하지 못하실까 봐 염려하거나
그분의 조직이 이 급변하는 세상에서 발생하는 새로운 문제에
잘 대처하지 못할까 봐 걱정할 필요도 없습니다.
여호와의 조직이 계속 움직이면서 활동하고 있다는 사실을 잊지 마십시오.”
우리는 팬데믹 기간에 이 내용이 사실임을 직접 경험했습니다.
여러분 모두가 이러한 변화들에 적응하면서 보여 주신 훌륭한 태도에 감사합니다.
팬데믹 초기에 우리는 직접 만날 수 없었습니다.
하지만 하늘 수레의 인도를 충실히 따르면서 우리는 잘 적응했고,
집회와 봉사를 위해 화상 회의 프로그램을 사용했습니다.
다시 서로를 직접 볼 수 있어 정말 기쁩니다.
대면 집회 참석과 관련된 광고를 낭독하도록 마련했습니다.
여호와께서 이 마련을 축복하고 계시다는 점을 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
우리는 형제 자매들과 직접 만나서 인사를 나누고,
함께 어우러져 여호와께 찬양의 노래를 부르고,
그 밖의 방법으로 그리스도인 사랑을 표현할 수 있는 기회를
다시 한번 갖게 된 것에 대해 여호와께 감사드립니다.
2년이 넘는 기간 동안 왕국회관에 함께 모이지 못하게 되면서,
우리에게 힘을 주고 믿음을 강하게 해 주는 대면 집회의 소중함을 다시금 깨닫게 되었습니다.”
“일부 사람들은 노령이나 질병 또는 그 밖의 다른 상황으로 인해
대면 집회에 참석하기가 어려울 수 있습니다.
히브리서 6:10에 나오는 이러한 사랑에 찬 말씀을 꼭 기억하시기 바랍니다.
여러분이 거룩한 자들을 섬겼고 지금도 섬기면서 행한 일과
그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑을 잊지 않으십니다.’”
여호와께서는 여러분의 충실한 봉사를 결코 잊지 않으실 것입니다!
여러분은 줌 집회에 정기적으로 참석하고 참여하면서
하느님의 이름에 대한 사랑을 계속 나타내고 계십니다.
여러분의 그런 모습은 회중에 큰 격려가 되죠.
줌으로 모든 일들을 하는 데 익숙하실 겁니다.
팬데믹 기간에 여호와께서 제가 그렇게 집회를 보기를 바라셨기 때문이었죠.
대면 집회가 재개되면서 저는 다시 왕국회관에 갈 수 있어 정말 행복했습니다.
우리 형제 자매들을 직접 대면해서 만나는 것보다 더 좋은 일은 아무것도 없죠.
물론 어떤 분들은 그렇게 하실 수 없지만,
이제, 왕국회관에서 다시 대면 집회에 참석하게 된
집회가 열리지 않을 거라는 광고를 들었을 때
영적 양식을 받을 수 없게 되었으니까요.
우리가 라디오를 통해 집회를 들을 수 있게 마련해 주었죠.
다른 형제들 집에 가서 집회를 들어야 했어요.
그러다 장로들이 줌으로 집회를 볼 수 있게 마련했습니다.
회중 형제 자매들의 집에 가야 했습니다.
어떤 때는 그분들 인터넷 데이터가 다 떨어져서
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 대면 집회를 재개하기로 결정했다는 소식을 들었을 때
팬데믹 기간에 보지 못했던 형제 자매들을
예전처럼 영적 양식을 즐길 수 있게 되어
왕국회관에 갈 수 없게 돼서 정말 힘들었어요.
줌으로 영적 양식을 계속 공급받을 수 있었어요.
다시 대면 집회가 열린다고 들었을 때
사탕 가게에 들어가는 아이같이 정말 신이 났죠.
그러니까 우리 모두가 다 격려를 받아야 하죠.
왕국회관에서 그런 격려를 받을 수 있으니까
저보다 연로한 분들도 있고 청소년들도 있어요.
너무 기뻐서 저절로 미소를 짓게 돼요.
여호와께서는 우리가 그렇게 형제 자매들과 함께하면서
왕국회관에 가면 바로 그런 기분을 느낄 수 있어서 정말 좋습니다.
우리는 대면 집회에 대한 정말 많은 긍정적인 보고들을 받고 있죠.
최근에 부룬디 지부에서 이런 보고가 있었습니다.
인터넷으로 집회를 보기 위해 다들 최선을 다했지만,
인터넷으로 집회를 보기가 매우 어려운 상황이었습니다.
전국적으로 집회 참석자 수가 엄청나게 증가한 걸 볼 수 있었습니다.
한 회중에서는 인터넷으로 집회를 볼 때 집회 참석자 수가 140명이었는데,
왕국회관에서 대면 집회가 열리기 시작한 이후로는
집회 참석자 수가 크게 늘어 현재 227명이 참석하고 있습니다.”
앞서 그 광고 내용으로 다시 돌아와서,
모두가 유의해야 할 한 가지 점을 더 살펴보죠.
노령이나 질병 또는 그 밖의 다른 상황으로 인해
대면 집회에 참석하기가 어려운 분들이 계실 수 있다는 걸 인정한 다음,
광고에서는 생각해 볼 만한 다음과 같은 점을 언급했습니다.
정기적으로 참석하기가 더 유리한 상황에 있을 수 있습니다.
왕국회관에 직접 참석할 수 있는 상황인데도
화상 회의 방식으로 집회를 보려는 경향이 관찰되었습니다.”
우리가 계속 깊이 생각해 볼 만한 점이죠.
우리는 대면으로 순회 대회와 지역 대회를 열기 위해 준비하고 있죠.
따라서 지금이야말로 대면 집회에 대한 우리 자신의 태도를 점검해 볼 좋은 때입니다.
물론 대면 집회 참석이 어려운 분들도 계시겠지만,
우리 각자가 자신의 상황을 정직하게 점검해 보는 데 무엇이 도움이 됩니까?
그 광고는 3개의 성구를 묵상해 보라고 권했는데요.
이 중요한 문제에 대한 여호와의 생각을 우리에게 알려 주죠.
“내가 당신의 이름을 내 형제들에게 선포하고, 회중 가운데서 당신을 찬양하겠습니다.”
“회중 가운데서” 여호와를 찬양할 수 있는 기회를
“점점 더 나빠지는 세상 상태에 대처하려면 강한 믿음과 인내가 필요합니다.
이 기회를 통해 소중한 형제 자매 여러분을 따뜻하게 칭찬합니다.
여러분은 우리의 영광스러운 하느님 여호와를 찬양하려는 진심 어린 열망을 나타내며
특히 우크라이나에 있는 우리 형제 자매들은
최근에 우크라이나의 비교적 안전한 지역에 있는 약 100개의 회중이
대면 집회를 재개하도록 중앙장로회의 승인을 받았습니다.
형제 자매들은 이 소식에 정말로 기뻐했습니다.
그들이 대면 집회에 참석해 얼마나 기뻤고,
“저는 대면 집회가 다시 열릴 거라는 광고를 들었을 때
가장 먼저 여호와께 진심으로 감사하다는 기도를 드렸어요.
왕국회관 집회에 참석할 때면 힘과 마음의 위로를 얻어요.
형제 자매들과 포옹을 하고 대화를 나누면
특히 지하실에 몇 시간씩 숨어 폭탄이 터지는 소리를 듣다가 집회에 가면 더욱 그렇습니다.”
“온라인 집회에 참석하는 건 작은 구명정에 타고 있는 것에 비할 수 있죠.
그런데 대면 집회에 참석하니까 대형 유람선에 타고 있는 것처럼 느껴져요.
전쟁으로 모두가 신체적, 감정적으로 너무 지치지만
팬데믹 기간에 침례를 받은 스타니슬라우 형제는
왕국회관 집회에 한 번도 참석해 본 경험이 없었습니다.
하지만 왕국회관에 직접 가서 집회를 보니까
그 내용을 기억하는 데도 더 도움이 되더라고요.”
많은 어려움 속에서도 대면 집회에 참석하기 위해 노력하는 모습을 보면
그들의 말은 시편 122:1의 말씀을 생각나게 해 줍니다.
“‘여호와의 집으로 가자’ 하고 사람들이 말했을 때에 내가 기뻐했다.”
우리는 여호와의 수레가 움직일 때 그에 발맞춰 같은 방향으로 움직여야 합니다.
그렇게 하려면 집회에 참석하고 야외 봉사에 참여하는 것에 더해
정기적인 개인 연구를 통해 최신 지식을 섭취하기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
우리는 여호와의 수레와 계속 보조를 맞춤으로
그분에 대한 우리의 존중심과 신뢰심을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
시편 29:11의 말씀을 직접 경험하게 될 것입니다.
“여호와께서 자신의 백성에게 힘을 주시고 여호와께서 자신의 백성을 평화로 축복하시리라.”
우리가 계속 여호와의 조직에 속해 있는다면,
오직 그분만이 우리에게 주실 수 있는 힘과 평화를 맛보는 축복을 누리게 됩니다.

en.text: Welcome!
In this program,
we’re going to talk about the importance
of adapting as Jehovah’s chariot moves.
But first, here are a few updates.
Earlier this year, the Governing Body approved for branch visits
to resume during the 2023 service year.
The Service Committee
assigns Governing Body members
to make shepherding visits on branches.
It also assigns headquarters representatives
to visit branches.
This is similar to when circuit overseers
visit congregations,
except that the Governing Body members
and headquarters representatives
visit branches.
As of November 28,
over 15 of these visits
have already taken place this service year.
These visits have resulted
in a tremendous
“interchange of encouragement”
for all involved
and have strengthened our unity.
We have also heard positive comments
about the special meetings with pioneers
that are held in conjunction with circuit assemblies.
One pioneer in New York said:
“I attended the first in-person pioneer meeting
“in three years at the Queens Assembly Hall today.
“I couldn’t hold back tears a couple of times
“because our Father deeply understood
“what we went through during the pandemic.
Jehovah is good indeed.”
No doubt many of our pioneers around the globe feel similarly.
It’s also encouraging to hear
that the Local Design/Construction work
is moving ahead.
Where there are no government restrictions,
Kingdom Hall construction groups have restarted.
What theocratic construction is on the horizon?
We now need over 15,700 new Kingdom Halls
and major renovations around the world.
We need these Kingdom Halls
for our in-person meetings!
To begin addressing these needs,
over 1,600 projects worldwide
are planned for this year alone.
And branches are also working hard
to prepare facilities
for in-person circuit assemblies and theocratic schools
starting in January 2023.
Can you make yourself available
to help with theocratic construction?
Ask your congregation elders for more information.
It’s wonderful to see young people
assisting with the work.
Think of the training they’re receiving now
that they’ll be able to use during the great rebuilding work
after Armageddon.
We have another exciting update regarding freedom of worship.
As Jesus foretold at Matthew 10:22,
we face much opposition.
Jesus said:
“And you will be hated
by all people on account of my name.”
To assist Jehovah’s people,
we have recently established the Freedom of Worship Office
at the Central Europe branch.
This headquarters department
will coordinate our efforts to defend our worship in Europe.
Now, you might be wondering:
‘The work has been established throughout Europe for many years,
so is this really needed?’
Yes, it is.
For example, recently, the government of Norway
decided that Jehovah’s Witnesses
would no longer receive certain state benefits
that are provided to all registered religions.
Here to explain more about this
is Brother Jørgen Pedersen.
We were shocked when we received a letter
from government authorities in Oslo, Norway,
threatening to remove our registration
as a religious community.
Jehovah’s Witnesses have been actively preaching the good news in Norway
for more than 120 years!
In fact, Jehovah’s Witnesses
suffered for their faith
under the Nazi occupation of Norway
during World War II.
Commenting on how Jehovah’s Witnesses
were the only religious group
who stood firm against the Nazis,
a previous minister for religion exclaimed:
‘People throughout the country should know about this
—especially young ones would benefit from this information.’
We’ve always been known as good citizens.
In fact, a public report stated
that Jehovah’s Witnesses
‘are careful to obey the laws of the land.’
Now they’ve suspended our grants,
while there are over 700 religious communities
who continue to receive such state benefits.
This decision is unconstitutional
and an unprecedented attack
on religious freedom in Norway.
With the assistance
of the newly established Freedom of Worship Office,
we’re pursuing legal remedies.
At the same time,
we’re pursuing dialogue with government officials.
And we pray that this situation will be amicably resolved.
Thank you, Brother Pedersen.
The authorities in Norway
have threatened to remove our legal registration
because of our Scriptural beliefs and practices
regarding disfellowshipping.
In the future, various governments
will challenge our freedom of worship.
They may pressure us to change our Scriptural beliefs.
But we’re certainly not going to do that!
As Brother Pedersen mentioned,
efforts are being made to address this issue.
In the meantime,
please make it a matter of prayer.
At the beginning of the pandemic,
many activities were quickly suspended.
But now, as we’re coming out of the pandemic,
many activities are quickly resuming.
And this is no surprise because Jehovah’s celestial chariot
moves swiftly, like lightning.
Notice how this is described at Ezekiel 1:16, 17.
Here Ezekiel gets an awe-inspiring glimpse of the chariot.
He describes it this way:
“The wheels and their structure
“appeared to glow like chrysolite,
“and the four of them looked alike.
“Their appearance and structure looked
“as though a wheel were within a wheel.
“When they moved,
“they could go in any of the four directions
without turning as they went.”
What an amazing vision of the heavenly part
of Jehovah’s universal organization!
The Pure Worship  book explains:
“Jehovah’s chariot perfectly reflects the reasonable,
“adaptable God who is in control of it.
“As his very name suggests,
“he can become anything that is needed
“in order to accomplish his purpose. . . .
“Never should we . . . worry
“that our God will be late in responding to our needs
“or that his organization will fail to adapt to some new challenge
“arising in the volatile world around us.
“We do well to remember
“that Jehovah’s organization is active,
ever on the move.”
We’ve certainly experienced the truth of these words
during the pandemic.
Thank you for the fine spirit you show
as we all adapt to these changes.
Earlier in the pandemic,
we couldn’t meet together in person.
But as a result of faithfully following the chariot,
we adapted and used videoconferencing
for our meetings and ministry.
Thankfully, circumstances are different now.
We rejoice to be able to meet in person again.
Back in July, the Governing Body prepared an announcement
that was read in all congregations about attending in-person meetings.
Do you recall some of the key points from that announcement?
The announcement began:
“In reviewing the results of resuming
“in-person congregation meetings . . . ,
“it is evident that Jehovah
“is clearly blessing this arrangement.
“We thank Jehovah for the opportunity
“to greet our brothers and sisters face-to-face,
“sing songs of praise to Jehovah harmoniously,
“and make other appropriate expressions
“of Christian affection once again.
“After more than two years
“of not being able to meet together at our Kingdom Halls,
“we have renewed appreciation for in-person Christian meetings
“that lift our spirits and strengthen our faith
during these difficult times.”
The announcement continued:
“We acknowledge that because of advanced age,
“infirmities, or other circumstances,
“some may be limited in their ability to attend meetings in person.
“For such ones, please keep in mind
“the loving reminder at Hebrews 6:10:
“‘God is not unrighteous so as to forget your work
“‘and the love you showed for his name
by ministering and continuing to minister to the holy ones.’”
Jehovah will never forget you and your faithful service!
You continue to show your love for his name
as you regularly attend and participate in meetings on Zoom.
And this is such an encouragement to the congregation.
Now, some of us got used to doing everything on Zoom.
I know for me,
only for Jehovah would I have done what we needed to do
during the pandemic.
As soon as we could,
I was so happy to go back to the Kingdom Hall.
There really is nothing like being together
with our brothers and sisters in person.
I appreciate that others can’t.
But I was happy to get back to the hall.
Many feel the same way.
Let’s hear how some of our brothers and sisters feel
about being back in person at the Kingdom Hall.
I was so sad when they announced
that we would stop having meetings
at the Kingdom Hall because of COVID.
I felt trapped
because I couldn’t go to the Kingdom Hall anymore
to be fed spiritually.
For two years, the faithful slave made arrangements
for us to listen to the meetings over the radio.
Since I did not have a radio,
I went to different brothers’ homes to listen to the meetings.
Then the elders arranged to start having meetings on Zoom.
I do not have a smartphone,
so I had to go to the homes of those in the congregation.
Sometimes after arriving,
I would find out that their Internet data bundle was used up.
This made the pandemic very difficult for me.
When I heard the news that “the faithful and discreet slave”
decided to resume in-person meetings,
I was just so happy!
Now I can see the brothers and sisters
that I had not seen during the pandemic.
I am back at the Kingdom Hall;
I am back where I can have my spiritual food
the way I have always enjoyed it.
To not be able to go to the hall
was a challenge for me.
It wasn’t easy.
But I appreciated Zoom
because we kept being fed spiritually
and that was a blessing.
But still, I missed the people.
When I heard we were going back in person, I was so excited.
I was like a child going into a candy store.
I was so excited.
It was great. It really was energizing.
You felt alive again.
We all have challenges.
We’re tired.
So who doesn’t need to be energized?
We all do.
And so to come to the Kingdom Hall
—there’s no question that I am going to the meeting.
You’re with the older friends, even older than me,
and younger ones.
Little children come running up to you.
That just brings joy to your heart and a smile on your face.
And I think that’s the experience
Jehovah wants us to have as a brotherhood.
So I feel more fulfilled by being at the Kingdom Hall.
I’m happy.
It’s heartwarming to hear their expressions.
We’ve received many positive reports about in-person meetings.
For example, the Burundi branch recently wrote:
“The decision to return to in-person meetings
“has been a great blessing to our brothers and sisters in Burundi.
“Although they did what they could to connect virtually,
“the reality was that many
“just did not have the circumstances to do so.
“Since resuming in-person congregation meetings,
“our attendance has increased tremendously throughout the country.
“For example, in one congregation,
“the attendance was 140 persons
“when the meetings were held virtually,
“but after resuming in-person meetings at the Kingdom Hall,
the attendance is now 227.”
Continuing with the announcement,
we want to draw your attention to this one comment.
After acknowledging those with advanced age,
infirmities, and other circumstances
that may prevent them from attending meetings in person,
the announcement included this thought-provoking statement:
“On the other hand, some brothers and sisters
“—younger and in good health—
“have more favorable circumstances
“that may allow them to attend Christian meetings regularly
“at the Kingdom Hall.
“However, it has been observed
“that some have developed a tendency
“to attend meetings on a videoconference when,
“according to their circumstances,
they could be physically at the Kingdom Hall.”
That’s what the announcement said.
It’s something we can continue to reflect on.
The chariot is moving!
We’re getting ready for in-person circuit assemblies
and regional conventions.
So now is an excellent time
to evaluate our attitude about in-person meetings.
Again, we appreciate that some cannot attend in person.
But on the other hand, maybe some could.
What will help each of us to honestly evaluate
our personal circumstances?
Well, the announcement drew our attention to three verses
that express Jehovah’s thinking on this important matter.
Let’s read just one of those verses
at Psalm 22:22:
“I will declare your name to my brothers;
in the midst of the congregation I will praise you.”
How we cherish our opportunities
to be “in the midst of the congregation”
at in-person meetings!
The announcement concluded by saying:
“Strong faith and endurance are required
“to face deteriorating world conditions.
“So, we take this opportunity
“to warmly commend you dear brothers and sisters
“for your faithfulness, love, and heartful desire
“to praise our glorious God, Jehovah.
We love you very much!”
Our brothers and sisters in Ukraine
have faced especially challenging circumstances
when it comes to holding in-person meetings.
Recently, approximately 100 congregations in Ukraine
were approved to resume in-person meetings
where it was safe to do so.
The brothers and sisters responded enthusiastically.
Notice some of their expressions, which highlight the joy and benefits
of in-person meetings.
A sister named Svitlana says:
“When the announcement was read about the return to in-person meetings,
“the first thing I did
“was thank Jehovah in fervent prayer.
“Meetings at the Kingdom Hall refresh and give emotional strength.
“The hugs and conversations
“improve my mood and give me the needed support.
“This is especially the case after spending hours in basements
and hearing bombs explode.”
Nadia states:
“I compare online meetings
“to rescue boats helping us to stay afloat.
“Attending in-person meetings
“feels like being aboard a huge cruise ship.
“The war is taking an emotional and physical toll on all of us,
“but when I am in the Kingdom Hall,
I forget about my problems, my worries, and even the war.”
Brother Stanislav who got baptized during the pandemic
without ever having attended a meeting at the Kingdom Hall says:
“I am a modern person and found our Zoom meetings OK.
“But I did not expect that the atmosphere
“in the Kingdom Hall would be so overwhelming.
“I also find it easier to follow
the presented material and to remember it.”
We’re encouraged by the determination
of our brothers and sisters in Ukraine
to attend in-person meetings
despite the many challenges they face.
Their expressions echo the words of Psalm 122:1:
“I rejoiced when they said to me:
‘Let us go to the house of Jehovah.’”
What have we learned from this update?
As we’ve seen from Ezekiel’s vision,
we must always be ready to adapt
when Jehovah’s chariot moves.
We do so not only by attending meetings
and participating in the field ministry
but also by staying up-to-date
with our spiritual feeding program.
By keeping pace with Jehovah’s chariot,
we show that we respect and have confidence in Jehovah.
As a result, we enjoy what is stated
at Psalm 29:11:
“Jehovah will give strength to his people.
Jehovah will bless his people with peace.”
Yes, by being part of Jehovah’s organization,
we share in the strength and peace
that only he can provide.
May we all continue to adapt as Jehovah’s chariot moves
and enjoy his rich blessing.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

title: “창조극”—잊지 못할 드라마

ko.text: 많은 사람에게 감동을 준 이 영상물은
약 1만 명의 사람이 베를린 경기장에 모였습니다.
이 극에 담긴 희망의 소식을 최대한 많은 사람에게 전하기 위해
당시 성경 연구생으로 알려져 있던 여호와의 증인은
사람들의 관심을 끌어 성경 진리를 가르치기 위해,
그들은 녹음된 강연을 슬라이드와 활동사진과 결합한
여러 해 동안 사용한 “사진극”의 일부 유리 슬라이드가 파손되었습니다.
성경 연구생들은 여전히 많은 사람에게 소식을 전하기를 원했습니다.
그래서 많은 지역에서 성경에 근거한 프로그램을
이런 방법으로 왕국 희망을 알리는 것을 금지했습니다.
독일의 형제들은 “창조 사진극”과 비슷한 영상물을 사용하는 것이
사람들에게 소식을 전하는 가장 좋은 방법이라는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
1927년에 한스 데커 형제가 “창조 사진극”의 대본을 개정했습니다.
그는 새로 나온 「창조」 책에 근거해 대본을 개정하고
빌헬름 슈만 형제는 최신 출판물에 나오는 그림들을 사용해
새로운 여러 슬라이드에 손으로 직접 그림을 그렸습니다.
음악가인 에리히 프로스트 형제가 영상에 곁들일 음악을 작곡했습니다.
몇 부로 나누어 며칠 저녁에 걸쳐 상영되었습니다.
당시 독일은 심각한 경제 공황 상태에 있었고,
사람들에게는 어려움을 이겨 낼 희망이 필요했습니다.
그 무렵 아돌프 히틀러가 이끄는 국가 사회당 즉 나치당이라는
새로운 정당이 세력을 키워 가고 있었습니다.
“창조극”의 소식을 최대한 많은 사람에게 전하기 위해
그 후 5년 동안 수백 차례에 걸쳐
히틀러가 성경 연구생들의 전파 활동을 반대했지만,
여호와의 백성은 계속 용기 있게 전파했습니다.
1931년에 스위스 베른에 있는 중부 유럽 지부의 형제들은
그와 비슷한 영상물을 유럽의 다른 지역에서
사용할 수 있게 해 달라고 요청했습니다.
여호와의 증인에게 가해진 박해에 대한 정보를
교직자들이 히틀러의 나치당과 손을 잡았다는 사실도
중립 입장 때문에 체포되었다는 사실도 추가되었습니다.
“창조극” 상영에 관해 지금까지 알려진 마지막 보고입니다.
몇 달 후 제2차 세계 대전이 발발했습니다.
성경의 소식을 배우는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
사람들의 정신과 마음에 지울 수 없는 인상을 남겼습니다.
많은 사람이 잊지 못할 드라마였다고 말했습니다.
“창조극”은 하느님의 약속에 관해 알려 주기만 한 것이 아니라,
왕국 희망에 대한 믿음을 많은 사람의 마음에 심어 주었습니다.
수많은 여호와의 증인들에게 큰 힘이 되었습니다.
계속해서 사람들에게 미래에 대한 성경의 약속을 가르쳤습니다.

en.text: In the late 1920’s,
Jehovah’s servants in Germany
produced a Bible-based presentation
that attracted huge crowds.
It was called the “Creation Drama.”
Some 10,000 people came to see it
at the Berlin Sports Palace.
But what exactly was the “Creation Drama”?
And what efforts were made so that its message of hope
might reach as many as possible?
The “Creation Drama” was the successor
to a previous work called the “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
Early in the 1900’s,
the Bible Students, as Jehovah’s Witnesses were then known,
wanted to reach as many as possible with the Bible’s message.
To attract people and teach them Bible truths,
they combined recorded lectures with visual aids
in the form of slides and motion-picture film.
they began showing the “Photo-Drama of Creation”
in city after city,
and it was seen by over nine million people
in just the first year after its release.
But by the 1920’s, after years of use,
some of the “Photo-Drama’s” glass slides were broken.
The film was deteriorating,
and the equipment was wearing out.
The Bible Students still wanted to reach large audiences.
So in many lands
they began broadcasting Bible-based programs on the radio.
But in Central Europe,
governments restricted this means of advertising the Kingdom hope.
The brothers in Germany realized
that a motion-picture presentation
similar to the “Photo-Drama”
would be the best way for them to reach people.
Little did they know how timely their efforts would be.
Brother Hans Decker updated the “Photo-Drama” script
with information from a new book entitled Creation,
even adopting the name “Creation Drama.”
Brother Wilhelm Schumann hand painted many new slides
using pictures from recent publications.
New film was also added.
Erich Frost, a skilled musician,
composed music to accompany the program.
When it was released,
the “Creation Drama” was eight hours long
and designed to be presented over several evenings.
At that time, Germany was suffering severe economic depression,
and people needed hope to deal with the difficult conditions.
And the new political party,
the National Socialist, or Nazi party,
was gaining strength under the leadership of Adolf Hitler.
What efforts were made
so that the “Creation Drama’s” message might reach as many as possible?
the brothers in Germany
began showing the “Creation Drama.”
In the five years after its release,
they showed it hundreds of times to over a million people.
Hitler opposed the preaching work of the Bible Students,
but Jehovah’s people kept on preaching courageously.
Martin Poetzinger reported:
‘One evening in Weissenburg, Bavaria,
‘people were coming in droves to see the drama,
‘but the police blocked their entry.
‘And even though hundreds went to demonstrate in front of the town hall,
‘the police continued blocking them.
‘The next evening,
‘storm troopers showed up
looking to destroy the equipment.’
Jehovah’s Witnesses in Germany
continued showing the “Creation Drama”
until April 1933,
when the government started
imposing bans on their work.
In fact, in the last six months
that it was shown in Germany,
the brothers hosted 160 performances
with a total of nearly 300,000 attendees.
the brothers at the Central Europe branch
in Bern, Switzerland,
recognized the success
of the “Creation Drama”
and requested permission to develop similar programs
for use in the rest of Europe.
Even after the preaching work was banned in Germany,
the Witnesses continued to show the “Creation Drama”
in such places as Switzerland, France,
the Netherlands, Austria,
Czechoslovakia, and Yugoslavia.
As conditions changed across Europe,
the “Creation Drama” was updated
to include new developments.
For example,
when a brave family smuggled information
from Germany into Switzerland
about the persecution of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this news was added to the “Creation Drama.”
As the clergy aligned themselves
with Hitler’s Nazi party,
this fact was also included in the drama.
And when Jehovah’s Witnesses
were arrested for taking a neutral stand,
this too was added.
The brothers in Switzerland reported
the last known use of the “Creation Drama.”
there were 20 performances
with a total attendance of 19,000.
Months later,
the Second World War began.
Back in 1914, just before the First World War,
the “Photo-Drama of Creation”
had acquainted millions with the Bible’s message.
From 1928 to 1939,
as the Second World War approached,
the “Creation Drama” was shown
just in time to make an indelible impression
on the minds and hearts of those who saw it.
Many described it as unforgettable.
It did more than just inform people
of God’s promises;
it motivated many
to put faith in the Kingdom hope
in spite of the dark shadows of war.
The “Creation Drama” also encouraged
thousands of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Europe.
When they were persecuted and imprisoned,
they continued to teach others
about the Bible’s promises for the future.

title: 로버트 루시오니: 자신의 영을 잘 지키고 배신하지 마십시오 (말라기 2:15)

ko.text: 말라기 시대의 일부 유대인 남자들은 아내와 이혼함으로 아내를 배신했습니다.
사소한 이유로 이혼하기도 했는데, 흔히 더 젊은 여자와 결혼하기 위해서였죠.
여호와께서 이에 대해 어떻게 느끼시는지가 16절에 이렇게 분명히 나와 있습니다.
잠언 2:22은 “배신자들이 땅에서 뽑힐 것”이라고 알려 줍니다.
누군가 이렇게 배신행위를 하는 경우는 거의 없습니다.
남편과 아내 사이가 아주 좋았다 해도 점점 나빠질 수 있습니다.
부부 사이뿐 아니라 어떤 관계에서든 그럴 수 있죠.
아주 친한 두 친구 사이나 우리와 조직 사이나
그런 일이 생기지 않도록 어떻게 해야 하는지 알려 주십니다.
“그러므로 너희는 자신의 영을 잘 지키고 … 배신하지 마라.”
어떻게 하다가 사랑하는 남편이나 아내를 배신하는 지경에 이를 수 있습니까?
어떻게 아주 친한 두 친구의 우정이 깨지게 될 수 있습니까?
어떻게 형제나 자매가 여호와의 조직에 등을 돌리게 될 수 있습니까?
그런 일이 있기 오래전부터 마음속에서 이미 문제가 자라고 있었던 거죠.
그래서 성경은 “영을 잘 지키라”고 말하는 겁니다.
계속해서 분을 품거나 거친 말을 하거나 오해를 풀지 않거나
관계가 점점 나빠져서 상황이 심각해질 수도 있기 때문입니다.
이제 성경에 나오는 두 배신자의 예를 통해,
그 점을 더 자세히 살펴보도록 하겠습니다.
사울이 다윗을 죽이려고 한 때부터 다윗이 왕이 될 때까지
압살롬이 반역하고 왕위를 찬탈하려고 했을 때도
그는 다윗의 다른 아들인 아도니야가 왕위를 차지하려고 할 때 그의 편에 섰습니다.
아비아달의 마음속에 풀리지 않은 감정이 남아 있었던 겁니까?
대제사장인 아비아달의 아버지와 다른 84명의 제사장들을 죽였습니다.
다윗이 아비아달의 아버지에게 가서 빵과 칼을 달라고 요청했기 때문이죠.
그래서 아비아달은 다윗에 대해 풀리지 않은 감정이 있었던 걸까요?
‘다윗이 우리 가족에게 오지만 않았어도 아버지가 죽지 않았을 거야’
경쟁 관계에 있는 것처럼 보이는 사람이 있었는데,
역대기상 12:28은 그가 “용맹스러운 젊은 용사”였다고 알려 줍니다.
하지만 그는 사울이 죽을 때까지 사울 밑에서 일했고
그 후로 아비아달과 사독은 함께 다윗을 위해 일했습니다.
사실 두 사람은 대개 함께 언급되는데,
흥미롭게도 사독의 이름이 언제나 먼저 나옵니다.
혹시 아비아달이 마음속에 사독에 대한 시기심과 반감을 품고 있었던 것은 아닐까요?
사울이 제사장들을 전부 죽일 때 죽지 않았는데,
처음부터 다윗을 충실하게 섬긴 아비아달 못지않게
두 사람 사이에 어느 정도 경쟁심이 자라게 된 것입니까?
어떤 이유였든 아비아달은 자신의 영을 잘 지키지 않았기 때문에
유다는 최악의 배신자, 배신의 대명사라고 할 수 있죠.
그는 한때 분명 예수를 매우 사랑했고 그분과 아주 가까운 관계를 누렸을 것입니다.
그가 사도로 임명된 걸 보면 그 점을 알 수 있죠.
또한 유다는 예수와 12사도들이 사용하는 자금을 관리하는 책임을 맡았습니다.
이 점을 보면 예수께서 그를 신뢰하셨다는 걸 알 수 있는데,
특히 재무 관리 경험이 있는 마태에게 그 일을 맡기지 않으신 걸 보면 그렇죠.
우리는 유다가 처음엔 예수의 말씀을 잘 듣고
그분과 함께 먹고 웃는 모습을 그려 볼 수 있습니다.
그런데 어느 시점엔가 그의 영에 변화가 생기기 시작했습니다.
많은 제자들이 예수의 살과 피에 대한 그분의 말씀을 듣고 걸려 넘어져서
우린 흔히 베드로가 한 충성스러운 대답에 초점을 맞춥니다.
그런데 이 시점에 예수께서는 유다의 마음속에서
반감이 자라기 시작하는 걸 보신 것 같습니다.
그분은 가룟 시몬의 아들 유다에 대해 말씀하신 것이다.”
유다가 예수에 대해 수군거리는 사람들의 말에 귀를 기울이기 시작한 것은 아닐까요?
그는 돈궤에서 돈을 꺼내 가곤 했죠.
자금과 관련해 마음에 들지 않는 결정이 내려지는 걸 보면서부터였을까요?
마리아가 예수께 향유를 붓는 걸 보면서 유다의 반감은 극에 달했던 것 같습니다.
예수께서는 모든 사람 앞에서 그를 크게 질책하셨습니다.
그 자리를 떠나 며칠 후 예수를 배반하고 그분을 제사장들에게 넘깁니다.
강한 징계를 받거나 사람들 앞에서 창피를 당하거나
다른 누군가의 특권에 대해 시기심이 생길 수 있습니다.
우리 모두는 살면서 언젠가는 이런 일들을 겪게 됩니다.
그런 일을 겪을 때마다 우리 마음에 작은 씨앗이 떨어진다고 할 수 있죠.
조처를 취하지 않는다면 유독한 뿌리가 자라나서
우리가 결국 배신자가 되게 만들 수 있습니다.
심지어 여호와를 배신하게 될 수도 있죠.
“하느님의 과분한 친절을 얻지 못하는 사람이 없도록 주의하십시오.
그리하여 유독한 뿌리가 나서 문제를 일으키고
그것 때문에 많은 사람이 더럽혀지는 일이 없게 하십시오.”
어떻게 하면 유독한 뿌리를 뽑아낼 수 있습니까?
성경에 담긴 훌륭한 원칙들을 적용할 수 있습니다.
문제나 오해가 생길 때 대화로 해결하려고 노력하십시오.
해결하지 않은 채 묻어 두지 말고, 형제나 자매를 얻으려고 하십시오.
과거로 돌아가서 내가 남편이나 아내와 사랑에 빠진 이유를 생각해 보십시오.
어떻게 내 친구와 이렇게 가까운 사이가 되었는지 떠올려 보십시오.
또 어떻게 진리를 확신하게 되었는지도 생각해 보세요.
우리는 유독한 뿌리를 하나씩 뽑아내서 그것이 자라지 못하게 하는 것입니다.
이것은 우리가 끊임없이 계속 해 나가야 할 일이죠.
따라서 우리의 영을 잘 지키겠다고 결심하도록 합시다.
우리는 결코 그 어떤 유독한 뿌리도 우리 안에서 자라게 해서는 안 됩니다.
사랑하는 사람들과 여호와께 충성을 유지할 수 있을 것입니다.

en.text: Malachi 2:15:
“Do not deal treacherously
with the wife of your youth.”
Now, in Malachi’s day,
apparently Jewish husbands
were dealing treacherously with their wives
by divorcing them,
sometimes on frivolous grounds
and perhaps so as to marry younger women.
And the term “treacherously” was very appropriate.
Here the Hebrew word means
to “deal deceitfully, . . . unfaithfully.”
A form of this verb means to be a traitor.
And how Jehovah feels about this
is no wonder that he says what he does in verse 16,
where he says: “For I hate divorce.”
Jehovah hates treacherous, deceitful conduct.
Jehovah hates traitors.
At Proverbs 2:22, it says that “the treacherous
will be torn away from [the earth.]”
Well, happily, the majority of marriages in Jehovah’s organization
do not experience such treachery.
However, caution is still needed.
You see, it’s possible for even a once beautiful relationship
to begin to sour.
And not only in marriage,
but in any relationship: between two very close friends,
between us and the organization, even between us and Jehovah.
Well, in Malachi chapter 2,
Jehovah here gives us a formula for never letting things get to that point.
Look again at the latter part of verse 15.
He says: “So guard yourselves respecting your spirit,
and do not deal treacherously.”
Verse 16, the latter part of it says:
“And guard yourselves respecting your spirit.”
So you think about it.
How does somebody get to the point where they begin to deal treacherously
with their beloved husband or wife?
How does somebody get to the point
where two friends can no longer speak civilly with each other?
How does somebody get to the point
when they turn against Jehovah’s organization?
Well, see, long before they get to that point,
something has been brewing under the surface.
Thus the comment: “Guard yourselves respecting your spirit.”
And why is that appropriate?
Well, grudges, harsh words, unresolved misunderstandings,
questioning decisions that are made,
see, this can begin to fester
and begin to rot a relationship from the inside out
if left unchecked.
Now, we can see this by looking at (illustrate this by looking at) the example
of two traitors in the Bible,
Abiathar and also Judas.
Now, Abiathar was a high priest who stuck with David right from the beginning
when Saul was trying to kill him through David’s kingship.
Even when Absalom turned traitor and tried to take over the kingship,
Abiathar was faithful to David.
But later in life, Abiathar became a traitor.
He sided with David’s other son Adonijah
when he tried to take over the kingship.
What happened?
Were there some unresolved issues that Abiathar buried?
In 1 Samuel chapter 22, it’s recorded
where King Saul had Doeg kill Abiathar’s father, who was the high priest,
and 85 other priests because David went to Abiathar’s father
and asked him for some bread and also a sword.
Only Abiathar escaped, and he joined David’s camp.
Well, was this an unresolved issue with Abiathar?
Did he secretly always have in his mind,
‘You know, if David had never involved my family,
perhaps my father would still be alive’?
And then there could be what could be seen as a rivalry,
or a competition, between Abiathar and Zadok.
Now, Zadok was also a priest and a prophet.
At 1 Chronicles 12:28,
he’s called “a mighty and courageous young man.”
However, he served with Saul until Saul’s death,
and then after Saul’s death, he joined David’s camp.
Well, from then on, David used Abiathar and Zadok together.
In fact, they’re usually listed together,
but it’s of interest that Zadok is always listed first,
even though Abiathar was the high priest.
Did Abiathar secretly maintain
some feelings of jealousy or animosity toward Zadok?
See, Zadok, though he was a priest,
he wasn’t killed when Saul exterminated the priests.
Zadok sided with Saul,
and now he’s the favored one in David’s camp
next to Abiathar, who had been faithful to David
right from the beginning!
See, were there some seeds of competition that grew between these two men?
Whatever it was, what aspect of Abiathar’s spirit
did he not guard
that caused him to eventually turn traitor against David?
Now, another example is that of Judas.
He showed the ultimate betrayal and treachery.
Now, no doubt, Judas at one time loved Jesus dearly
and enjoyed a very close relationship with him.
His very appointment as an apostle indicates that.
Judas was also entrusted
with caring for the finances of Jesus and the Twelve.
And this also reflects favorably on him,
especially when you consider that this assignment
wasn’t given to Matthew, who had experience in handling the finances.
And we can just picture Judas there in the beginning,
listening to Jesus words, eating with him, laughing with him and the others.
But somewhere along the line,
something started to develop in his spirit.
Now, if you look in John chapter 6,
we read in that account when many of the disciples
were stumbled by Jesus’ words regarding his flesh and his blood,
and they left off following him.
In verse 61, John 6:61, it says that ‘the disciples began to murmur.’
In verse 67, Jesus asks the Twelve,
he says: “You do not want to go also, do you?”
And we often focus on Peter’s beautiful words of loyalty.
But we also—
It seems that at this point, Jesus was starting to see
seeds of bitterness starting to grow in Judas.
Look at what it says at John 6:70, 71:
“Jesus answered them: ‘I chose you twelve, did I not?
“Yet one of you is a slanderer.’
He was, in fact, speaking of Judas the son of Simon Iscariot.”
You see, was Judas starting to listen
to those who were beginning to murmur against Jesus?
At John 12:6, we’re told that Judas “was a thief.”
He would take money from the money box.
Well, when did that start?
Was that after he saw some decisions made with the finances
that he didn’t quite agree with?
According to Matthew’s and Mark’s accounts,
it appears that seeing Mary pour the perfumed oil on Jesus
was the last trigger for Judas.
He strongly objects,
and Jesus strongly rebukes Judas on that occasion
right in front of everybody.
And Judas, no doubt stung by these words, leaves,
and just a few days later, he betrays Jesus to the priests.
Well, what is the point?
Things happen in our life:
an injustice, a misunderstanding,
strong discipline, being embarrassed in public,
maybe feelings of jealousy over privileges that somebody else has.
See, these things happen to all of us
at one time or another in our life or through our life.
And each time this happens,
it drops a little seed, if you will, into our heart.
And if left unchecked, a poisonous root can begin to grow
that eventually can cause us to become a traitor
against our marriage mate, against our close friend,
against the organization, or even against Jehovah.
So, what do we do?
Malachi 2:15: “Guard yourself respecting your spirit.”
And notice what it says at Hebrews 12:15
—Hebrews 12:15.
It says: “Carefully watch that no one fails to obtain
“the undeserved kindness of God,
“so that no poisonous root springs up
to cause trouble and many are defiled by it.”
Well, how do we go about digging up poisonous roots?
Well, by following the beautiful principles we have in the Bible
at Matthew 5:23, 24 and Matthew 18:15.
When there are problems, when there are misunderstandings,
talk it out.
Work it out.
Do not leave them buried and unresolved.
Seek to gain our brother or sister.
Matthew 18:35: “Forgive [our] brother from [the] heart.”
Forgive and let go and move on.
John 13:34: “Love one another.”
Think back to when we fell in love with our husband or wife.
What caused us to fall in love with them?
What caused us to develop that close bond between us and our best friend?
What was it that convinced us that this is the truth?
Think back to that.
And, see, every time we do these things,
we’re pulling out one of those poisonous roots
and stopping it from growing.
It’s an ongoing process that we do over and over again.
So may all of us be determined to guard ourselves respecting our spirit.
Now is not the time
to allow any poisonous roots to begin to grow within us.
Keep our love for and our relationship with our mate (if we’re married),
with our friends, with the organization,
and with Jehovah strong.
And this will help us to stay loyal to loved ones
and to Jehovah now and in the days to come.

cn.text: 玛拉基书2:15说
不要用诡诈的手段对待自己年轻时娶的妻子
在玛拉基的时代
犹太人会用诡诈的手段跟妻子离婚
有时只是为了一些鸡毛蒜皮的小事
目的也许是想娶更年轻的女子
“诡诈”这个词用得非常恰当
译作“诡诈”的希伯来语词
有“欺骗、不忠贞”的意思
这个词在原文中也有“叛徒”的意思
在第16节
让我们看看耶和华对离婚有什么看法
耶和华说
我憎恨离婚
耶和华憎恨诡诈、欺骗的行为
也憎恨背信弃义的人
箴言2:22说
背信弃义的人会从地上被消灭
虽然在耶和华的组织里
基督徒的婚姻很少出现背叛的行为
但我们还需保持警惕
因为就算感情一直都很好的夫妻
也会出现问题
不只在婚姻当中
在其他方面也是一样
比如朋友之间、我们跟耶和华的组织之间
甚至我们跟上帝之间
在玛拉基书第2章
耶和华告诉我们怎样做才能
避免这样的事发生
在15节的后半部分，他说
你们要保护自己的心，不要用诡诈的手段
16节的后半部分也说
你们要保护自己的心
我们可以想想以下问题
为什么一个人开始用诡诈的方式
对待深爱的配偶？
是什么原因让亲密无间的朋友关系破裂？
又是什么原因让一个人走到了
背叛耶和华组织的地步？
在事情变得严重之前
往往会发生一些不起眼的小事
这会潜移默化地影响人
所以圣经说
要保护自己的心
这个提醒很重要
一个人如果一直心怀怨恨、说话苛刻
迟迟不愿化解矛盾，或者质疑组织的决定
他跟别人和上帝的关系就会开始出现裂痕
为了说明这一点
接下来让我们看看圣经中两个叛徒的例子
一个是亚比亚他，另一个是加略人犹大
亚比亚他是个大祭司
从扫罗追杀大卫到大卫作王
他一直都忠贞地跟随大卫
就算在押沙龙想篡夺王位的时候
他依然忠于大卫
不过，后来当大卫的另一个儿子亚多尼雅
试图篡夺王位时
他却背叛了大卫，转而支持亚多尼雅
为什么会这样？
是不是由于大卫做过的某些事
让他耿耿于怀呢？
在撒母耳记上22章
这里说扫罗王
让多益杀了亚比亚他的父亲
以及85个祭司
因为大卫
向当时还是大祭司的亚比亚他的父亲
要了食物和剑
后来只有亚比亚他逃了出来，投靠了大卫
亚比亚他是不是还在为这件事耿耿于怀呢？
他会不会总是在心里想
要是当时大卫没来
我的父亲也许还活着
另外，我们可以看到亚比亚他和撒督之间
可能也存在竞争
撒督是一个祭司，也是一个先知
历代志上12:28把他称作
“年轻的勇士”
不过，他之前一直跟随的是扫罗
扫罗死后他就投靠了大卫
从那时起
亚比亚他和撒督经常被大卫一起任用
在圣经中，他们也经常被一起提到
值得留意的是，虽然亚比亚他是大祭司
但先被提到的总是撒督
请大家想想看
亚比亚他会不会在心里
对撒督心怀嫉妒和敌意呢？
撒督虽然是祭司
但在扫罗杀害祭司的时候却没有被杀
撒督曾经站在扫罗的一边
而现在他却支持大卫
像一直忠于大卫的亚比亚他那样受到重用
有没有可能在这两个人的心里
滋生了竞争的念头？
可是不管是出于什么原因
亚比亚他没有保护好自己的心
最终背叛了大卫
另一个人就是犹大
在背信弃义方面，他是一个非常典型的例子
毫无疑问，犹大曾经忠于耶稣
跟耶稣的关系非常亲密
这一点从他被选为使徒就能看出来
另外，犹大被委任
为耶稣和十二使徒看管财物
想想看
连在这方面非常有经验的马太
都没有被委派做这个工作
耶稣多么信任犹大！
犹大当初听从耶稣的教导
跟耶稣一起吃饭
也跟耶稣和其他门徒一起度过快乐的时光
但后来他的心改变了
我们来看一下约翰福音第6章的记载
当时很多门徒听到耶稣说吃他的肉
喝他的血
都离开了耶稣
约翰福音6:61说门徒开始“私下议论”
在第67节，耶稣对十二使徒说
你们也想走吗？
我们都一定记得彼得忠贞而坚定的回答
不过，我们从耶稣接下来的话也能看出
他留意到犹大的心开始变得邪恶了
约翰福音6:70,71说
耶稣就对他们说
我不是挑选了你们12个人吗？
但现在你们有一个人好像魔鬼一样
其实他说的是加略人西门的儿子犹大
犹大是不是听到门徒的私下议论
心就开始动摇了呢？
约翰福音12:6说
犹大是个贼，他会从钱盒里偷钱
他是从什么时候开始的呢？
是不是他不同意某些财务方面的决定
之后就心怀恶念了呢？
马太福音和马可福音都提到了
马利亚为耶稣倒馨香油这件事
这显然是犹大出卖耶稣的导火线
当时犹大表示强烈反对
而耶稣却当着众人的面直接地反驳了犹大
犹大就生气地离开了
几天后，他就去找祭司出卖了耶稣
我们能学到什么呢？
类似的事也可能发生在我们身上
遭遇不公、误解、严厉的管教
当众遇到尴尬的情况
或者嫉妒别人拥有的服务机会
在我们的日常生活中
大家都会经历这样的事
每次经历这样的事
我们的心里就可能种下一颗不好的种子
如果我们没有及时除去毒根
任由种子生长
最终就可能会背叛自己的配偶
亲密的朋友、耶和华的组织
甚至是耶和华
我们要怎样做呢？
玛拉基书2:15说
要保护自己的心
接着，我们再来看一下希伯来书12:15
经文说
你们要小心
免得有人得不到上帝的分外恩典
这样毒根才不会长起来
危害你们玷污许多人
我们怎样才能拔掉毒根呢？
答案就在
我们要把这些原则用出来
问题出现时要跟对方说出想法
一起解决问题，不要憋在心里
要主动跟弟兄姐妹和解
马太福音18:35说
要“从心里宽恕弟兄”
要把事情放下，让它过去，向前看
约翰福音13:34说要“彼此相爱”
回想一下
当初你跟配偶怎样坠入爱河？
是什么让你爱上对方？
你们怎样建立了亲密的关系
并成为最好的朋友？
也要想想
当初你为什么确定自己学到的是真理
我们经常回想这样的问题
就仿佛在拔掉心里的毒根
阻断种子的生长
这是一个持续的过程
我们必须不断这样做
愿我们所有人都下定决心保护自己的心
现在
绝不是让有害的种子
在我们心里扎根的时候
要加深对配偶和朋友的爱
也要加深对耶和华和他的组织的爱
这样我们就能对耶和华和别人保持忠贞
直到永远
