텐트를 설치해 또는 야외에서 열린 대회들도 있었는데,
1908년에 오하이오주의 여름 휴양지인 푸트인베이에서 그런 대회가 열렸죠.
3500명이 넘게 참석한 것으로 추산되는 당시까지 가장 큰 대회였습니다.
남녀노소할 것 없이 형제 자매들 모두가 영적으로 힘을 얻고, 함께 시간을 보내고,
함께 웃고 먹고, 진정한 우정과 사랑을 쌓는 좋은 기회가 되었죠.
1918년에 약 5천만 명의 목숨을 앗아간 치사적인 전염병 때문에 몸살을 앓았습니다.
그 대회는 러더퍼드 형제와 동료들이 석방된 뒤 열린 첫 대규모 대회였습니다.
성경 연구생들은 마침내 안전하게 모이게 되어 기뻐했고
참석자가 계속 몰려들어 전체 프로그램을 야외에서 진행해야 했습니다.
이 대회에는 하루 평균 약 1만 명이 참석했습니다.
이 대회는 하느님의 백성이 더 큰 열심으로 전파 활동을 수행하도록 힘을 주었죠.
하느님의 백성이 훨씬 더 강한 연합을 이루는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
일례로 1931년 오하이오주 콜럼버스에서 열린 대회가 있죠.
사람들이 박람회장에 있는 경기장으로 들어서는 모습을 상상해 보십시오.
프로그램에는 JW라는 두 글자가 크게 인쇄되어 있었습니다.
처음 이틀 동안 참석자들은 그 글자들의 의미를 알아내려고 애썼습니다.
형제는 연설 마지막 부분에서 발표한 결의문에서 다음과 같이 말했습니다.
“우리는 그 이름 즉 여호와의 증인으로 알려지고 불리기를 원하는 바이다.”
1940년대에 발발한 2차 세계 대전은 많은 나라들을 황폐시키고 분열시켰지만
여호와의 증인은 그 수가 늘어나고 더욱더 연합되었습니다.
오하이오주 클리블랜드에서 열린 “즐거운 백성” 신권 대회에 모였습니다.
일부 사람들은 텐트와 트레일러에서 숙박을 했습니다.
그 시대에는 큰 대회 때 이런 모습을 흔히 볼 수 있었죠.
영적 가족의 수가 증가하면서 1950년대에는 세계 전역에서
심지어 경제적으로 어려운 나라에서도 큰 대회들이 열렸습니다.
국제 대회가 얼마나 큰 규모로 열리게 되었는지를 보여 주는 두드러진 예는
123개국에서 25만 명이 넘는 사람들이 그 대회에 참석했습니다.
이것은 한 도시에서 열린 가장 큰 대회였습니다.
양키 스타디움과 근처에 있는 폴로 그라운드가 가득 찼죠.
참그리스도인 역사상 가장 큰 대회가 오늘 열리고 있습니다.
하지만 하느님의 백성이 이러한 대회에서 연합된 것은
격려적인 연설, 실용적인 심포지엄, 새로운 발표물,
실감 나는 성경 드라마와 같은 영적 양식이 제공되었습니다.
이러한 영적인 선물에 더해 새로운 친구와 옛 친구를 만나는 기쁨은
대회가 진정한 축복이 되게 해 주었습니다.
하지만 대회를 여는 것이 늘 쉽지는 않았습니다.
트빌리시 교향악단 콘서트홀에서 열 계획을 했습니다.
대회가 열리기 불과 일주일 전에 계약을 취소했습니다!
농장 부지 두 곳을 대회장으로 바꾸어 놓았습니다.
연단과 긴 의자들을 만들고 음향 장치도 설치했습니다.
첫 회기가 시작할 시간이 되었을 때 모든 준비가 끝나 있었고,
대회가 방해 없이 순조롭게 진행되었을 뿐 아니라
참석자들은 예상치 못한 축복에 크게 기뻐했습니다.
조지아어로 신세계역이 발표되어 현지 형제 자매들은
전 세계 형제들과 연합돼 있다는 것을 더 깊이 느끼게 되었습니다.
오늘날 이처럼 특별 지역 대회와 국제 대회가
그리고 직접 만날 수 없을 때에는 온라인으로도 대회를 봤죠!
하느님의 모든 백성을 위한 즐거운 영적 행사입니다.
대회들은 우리를 격려하고, 형제 자매로서 연합시켜 주고,
가장 중요한 점으로 여호와와 가까워지게 해 줍니다.
우리가 영적 가족으로 연합될 때 여호와께 찬양이 돌아갑니다.
또 그러한 연합은 우리가 서로 사랑하는 가족이라는 증거죠.
누가 감정을 상하게 해서 참을성이 시험받을 때 특히 그렇죠.
하지만 여호와의 도움으로 손상된 관계를 회복할 수 있습니다.
방송을 더 유익하게 즐길 수 있는 기능을 소개해 드리고자 합니다.
여러 언어로 자막을 볼 수 있는 기능입니다.
동영상에 여러분의 언어로 자막이 들어 있다면
화면 아래의 톱니바퀴 모양의 아이콘을 클릭해서 자막을 끄거나 켤 수 있습니다.
이제 「그때처럼 우리 다시」라는 뮤직비디오를 함께 보시죠.
이러면 안 된단 걸 나도 아는데.
이번 달 방송은 참을성이라는 아름다운 특성에 초점을 맞추었습니다.
기대와 다르게 행동하는 사람에게 참을성을 보이는 법을 배웠죠.
우리가 나쁜 습관과 싸울 때 여호와께서 참을성을 보이신다는 점과
우리의 참을성과 사랑이 다른 사람에게 유익을 준다는 점도 배웠습니다.
이번 달에는 중앙아메리카에 있는 과테말라로 가 보겠습니다.
정글, 해변, 산, 아니면 열대 우림인가요?
과테말라에는 이 모든 게 다 있습니다.
과테말라 남부에는 27개나 되는 화산이 몰려 있습니다.
1958년 무렵에는 세 개의 순회구에 700명 이상의 증인들이 있었죠.
1980년대에 정부가 무장한 시민 순찰대를 조직하면서 어려움이 생겼습니다.
일부 형제들은 시민 순찰대에 가입하지 않으면 죽이겠다는 위협을 받았습니다.
오늘날 약 4만 명의 전도인이 850개 이상의 회중에서 봉사하고 있습니다.
그들은 상황에 맞는 다양한 방법으로 봉사하죠.
과테말라의 공식 언어는 스페인어이지만 20개가 넘는 토착어도 사용되고 있습니다.
20개 회중에 있는 500명 이상의 전도인이 맘어로 좋은 소식을 전하고 있습니다.
케트살테낭고에 있는 우스툰칼코 맘어 회중의 형제 자매들입니다.
이 형제 자매들의 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Greetings, and welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
Here are a few highlights from this month’s program.
Samuele was torn between his career and the truth.
How did he resolve this conflict,
and what steps did he take to reach his spiritual goals?
Perhaps you’ve been impatient with someone
because they’re not handling a situation the way you would.
In a new dramatization,
Neeta and Jade learn how to cultivate patience.
In this episode of Our History in Motion,
we’ll see how conventions strengthen the unity
and love among Jehovah’s people.
This is JW Broadcasting for November 2022!
In our broadcast for this month,
we’re going to discuss the quality of patience.
Think of how many situations we encounter
that require patience:
waiting in rush-hour traffic,
dealing with a difficult coworker,
raising a child, overcoming marital problems,
coping with the illness of a loved one,
or maybe coping with an illness of our own.
Clearly, all of us face situations
that require us to display a measure of patience each day.
If we don’t have patience, we can become frustrated,
tired, and discouraged.
But no matter what our circumstances are,
all of us can develop this quality.
How do we know?
Because according to Galatians 5:22,
patience is an aspect of the fruitage of God’s spirit,
and with its help,
we can make this quality an integral part of our personality.
For this to happen, let’s now answer two important questions.
First, How can being patient
help us to express our love for Jehovah?
And second, How can being patient improve
our relationship with others?
Let’s start with our first question:
How can being patient help us to express our love for Jehovah?
Let’s consider what is stated in 1 Corinthians chapter 13.
This chapter gives us a description of how love manifests itself.
Please follow along as I read verse 4:
“Love is patient and kind.
“Love is not jealous.
It does not brag, does not get puffed up.”
Of all the many qualities that stem from love,
did you note which one is listed first?
Patience.
It is an integral aspect of love.
We need both love and patience in order to be successful
and ensure we’re on the right course, which includes pleasing Jehovah.
If we think of situations where a lack of patience was a factor,
we can usually identify where a lack of love was evident.
Take, for example, God’s chosen people, the nation of Israel.
In Psalm 106,
written many years after Israel’s deliverance from Egypt,
the psalmist indicates that they continued acting with a similar disposition.
Despite that,
Jehovah extended patience to them for many years.
Please follow along as I read Psalm 106:7, 8:
“Our forefathers in Egypt
“did not appreciate your wonderful works.
“They did not remember your abundant loyal love,
“but they rebelled at the sea, by the Red Sea.
“But he saved them for the sake of his name,
to make his mightiness known.”
And what was the result?
Let’s read verse 13:
“But they quickly forgot what he did;
they did not wait for his counsel.”
How sad!
The people “did not wait.”
They were not patient.
And that highlights that they did not appreciate
Jehovah’s patience and loyal love.
Love for God should have caused them
to think about the consequences of their actions.
They should have remembered how Jehovah cared and provided for them.
That should have moved them to be patient
and wait on Jehovah’s direction.
But time and again,
their actions showed that they really didn’t love Jehovah as they should have.
And it cost them.
They eventually tested Jehovah’s patience to the limit
and, as a nation, lost his favor.
What can you and I learn from their example?
Never would we want to become independent of Jehovah,
trusting in our own thinking
and not patiently waiting for Jehovah’s counsel
to direct the decisions we make.
Think about how well we’ve been guided recently regarding the pandemic,
natural disasters,
and the organizing of our ministry.
Even if we didn’t fully understand
or even fully agree with all the decisions,
our love for God helped us to take the time
to think about Jehovah’s care for us and trust him.
By doing so, we learn that if we’re patient
and submit to Jehovah’s direction,
we won’t go off course
and we’ll benefit ourselves and others.
And in doing so,
we ultimately express our love for Jehovah.
Let’s now answer the second question:
How can being patient improve our relationship with others?
If we go back to 1 Corinthians 13:4,
the study note states:
“Patience is a quality that Jehovah and Jesus
“constantly show in their dealings with humans.
“As imitators of Jesus and Jehovah,
Christians are to show patience to others.”
So if Jehovah and Jesus are patient with us,
it would follow that we imitate their example and be patient with others.
Let’s start with the greatest example, Jehovah.
Think about the patience he’s shown
in waiting to bring an end to this system.
Jehovah has a fixed day and hour when that will take place,
and he’s patiently waiting until that arrives.
He’s bound himself to his own timetable.
Now rest assured,
Jehovah is well aware of how we feel as his servants.
He knows that we wish the end of this system to come as soon as possible
and that we long to see the fulfillment of all his promises.
And he longs to fulfill them.
But he will not become impatient
and act before his appointed time.
Why should we appreciate Jehovah’s patience in that regard?
Please follow along as I read 2 Peter 3:15:
“Furthermore, consider the patience
“of our Lord as salvation,
“just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote you
according to the wisdom given him.”
Isn’t that a powerful point?
Jehovah’s patience is the means for our salvation.
Think about the number of people who are learning the truth every year.
Even during the pandemic,
when we weren’t able to engage in our typical house-to-house witnessing,
tens of thousands of individuals still got baptized worldwide.
Perhaps some of those included your Bible students,
family members, close friends,
or maybe even you yourself.
And think about this:
If Jehovah had impatiently brought the end of this system
5, 10, or 20 years ago,
would you have learned the truth?
So we appreciate that Jehovah
is still patiently waiting for his day to arrive
and has allowed so many to attain to repentance
and develop a relationship with him.
How should this affect our relationship with others?
Perhaps it can help us to be more patient with a progressive Bible student
who still may be struggling with a problem.
Or maybe it’s still difficult for some of our relatives to see us
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses and to adjust to our beliefs and lifestyle.
But in imitation of Jehovah’s patience,
we won’t give up on them.
And, of course, reflecting on Jehovah’s patience should move us
to continue to have a full share in the ministry,
earnestly looking for those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life”
and helping them to love Jehovah and serve him.
Then they too can benefit from Jehovah’s patience,
just as we have.
We can also learn from the example of Jesus.
He demonstrated tremendous patience when his disciples
were arguing among themselves as to who was the greatest.
This apparently happened on a number of occasions.
And no doubt, it saddened Jesus to hear this.
But Jesus was patient with them.
He showed empathy for them.
He knew how much the culture and the environment
in which they had been raised affected their thinking and attitude.
That knowledge caused him to react kindly.
Note one beautiful example.
Please read with me Mark chapter 9
“And they came into Capernaum.
“Now when he was inside the house,
“he put the question to them:
‘What were you arguing about on the road?’”
Well, we know the answer.
They had been arguing about who among them was the greater.
Look at verse 35:
“So he sat down and called the Twelve and said to them:
“‘If anyone wants to be first,
he must be last of all and minister of all.’”
Did you note what Jesus did?
He patiently waited for the right time
to correct them kindly.
He didn’t make a scene on the road.
Verse 33,
he waited until “he was inside the house,”
verse 35, ‘sitting down.’
He calmed the situation.
He didn’t push them.
Instead, he led them patiently by instruction
and by example.
What a great example in avoiding becoming provoked
and, instead of acting immediately,
waiting for the right time to address matters,
even when our patience is tested!
What else can we take away from Jesus’ example of patience?
If you’re a parent,
can you imitate the way that Jesus dealt with his apostles?
It may be frustrating if your children don’t respond immediately to your counsel
or if they’re slow in correcting their shortcomings.
Or perhaps you’re an elder
and someone you’re trying to help may be slow
in responding to Bible-based counsel.
But remember Jesus’ example.
He never gave up on his apostles.
He kept looking for the good,
expressing confidence in them,
and he patiently repeated lessons that they needed
so that they could draw closer to Jehovah.
If we do the same, not giving up,
our patience may eventually be rewarded as well.
So to review:
How can being patient help us to express our love for Jehovah?
It stops us from running ahead of Jehovah,
demonstrating our loyal love for him.
Waiting patiently for Jehovah’s direction and guidance
ensures that our course is pleasing to him.
And second, How can being patient improve our relationship with others?
It helps us to avoid acting rashly
and to look for the good in others
and express confidence in them.
Hopefully, this discussion will help us appreciate
the benefit of displaying patience in our lives.
With the increasing pressures of these last days,
we’ll need to display patience more than ever before!
Imitating the patience of Jehovah and Jesus
will help us keep the right attitude.
We won’t become overly discouraged or overwhelmed
by the present wickedness in this system
or even be impatient about when it will end.
Instead, we’ll stay on the right course:
keeping busy, working to develop a closer relationship with Jehovah,
and keeping active in our ministry,
helping others to learn about Jehovah
and benefit from his patience.
May all of us keep working
to make the quality of patience a dominant part of our personality.
As we do,
we will demonstrate how much we value and appreciate this wonderful quality
and bring all praise and honor to Jehovah!
To give Jehovah their best,
some of our brothers give up lucrative and prestigious careers.
Making this decision may take time and patience
as we’ll see in our first video.
I played in the Series A, which is the top league in Italy.
I was on the National Youth Team,
and I went all the way up to the Men’s National Team.
Just the fact that you are good
at your job is gratifying,
and then there is also the financial aspect.
My mom and dad were Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and so was my older brother.
At a certain point,
I felt conflicted,
especially when I decided to draw closer to the truth.
It was no longer a “family” thing.
In time, something started to develop in me
—a fire, a small fire.
Gradually, I came to the point of dedication to Jehovah,
although I still played.
But maybe —not maybe, definitely—
I wasn’t giving Jehovah my best, my energy.
I was fitting my spiritual life around my work life
and not the other way around.
I excused myself, saying:
“I’m just working.
“It’s a profession.
“Yes, it’s time-consuming,
but it’s of short duration because athletes retire earlier.”
The closer I drew to Jehovah,
the stronger my inner conflicts became.
The circuit overseer who served the area I was associated with helped me.
I had known him since I was a child.
When we met again, the first thing he asked me was,
“Are you happy with what you are doing?”
It seems like a simple question, right?
But this question went deeper.
I’m very grateful to him and his wife for all the time they devoted to me.
They were very busy,
but even on their day off or in the evenings
after long days of activity,
they spent time with me.
In time, I moved to different cities and changed to various teams.
So he entrusted me, so to speak,
to two other families.
They poured themselves out for me,
sacrificing their time,
without ever making me feel bad for what I did.
With regard to decisions about basketball,
they never told me what to do.
I had to reach that decision on my own,
whether I should continue playing or not.
It was their way of life that corrected me, so to speak.
Their example
—their lifestyle, the priorities they set,
and the joy they had in doing what they did—helped me.
It was more their example
than their words.
It helped me understand
what I really wanted from my life.
I started in 1995
and continued until April 2008
when I played my last match.
I, let’s say, made a cut and quit playing basketball.
I’m glad I made it.
Sometimes I say to myself:
‘If only you’d done it earlier!
If only you’d had the courage earlier!’
I had the privilege of serving as a regular pioneer
for two and a half years.
I was asked if I would like to apply for Bethel service.
And to my surprise, I was invited to the Italy branch
and served there for five years.
A few months after leaving Bethel,
I had the privilege of attending the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
It was wonderful!
This sport —basketball—
it’s great, it’s thrilling, it’s exciting,
but it’s not the source of true happiness.
It’s true that the world can give you a measure of satisfaction,
but everything comes at a cost.
But it took me a long time to understand this.
Knowing that I am giving Jehovah my best
has made me happy.
Yes, there is a team,
a large one, and we all play for Jehovah.
And its goal is beautiful, it’s exciting,
and its success is sure.
Samuele said he wished he had given up basketball earlier
to pursue spiritual goals.
From that we learn that decisions to spend time on personal interests
take away from time we should give to Jehovah.
The sooner we appreciate Jehovah’s patience,
the sooner we enjoy the blessings which make us truly rich.
We are happy that Jehovah exercised patience with Brother Podestà
and helped him to regain his balance.
If you’re facing a career decision,
be assured that when we focus first
on serving Jehovah and teaching others his Word,
we’re happier!
Samuele was influenced by the patience and good example of loving brothers.
When we see how others are handling situations,
we may not be as patient as we’d like to be.
That’s what happens to Neeta and Jade in the following dramatization.
How do they learn to be more patient with each other?
You’re late!
Hmm?
I said, “You’re late.”
Sorry.
You work here now?
Yeah, just a— Just a few weeks.
You look great.

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—성경 번역의 발전

ko.text: 많은 언어로 쉽고 명확하게 번역한 덕분에
전 세계의 진실한 마음을 가진 사람들이
여호와의 말씀을 이해할 수 있게 되었습니다.
나중에 노어 형제의 연설을 들어 보니
여호와의 증인의 신권 통치 증가 국제 대회에서
이것은 시간과 노력이 많이 드는 작업이었죠.
번역자가 성경 번역 팀에서 일하도록 임명을 받게 되면
여러 날 동안 잠을 자지 못하고
어떤 음식을 조리법에 따라 요리하려고 하는데
원래와 똑같은 맛과 풍미를 내야 하는 겁니다.
원재료인 히브리어와 그리스어 단어들을 사용할 수 없죠.
원래 구절에 담긴 의미와 감정을 동일하게 전달해야 하는 겁니다.
중앙장로회는 이 일의 중요성을 잘 알고 있습니다.
여호와의 지원에 대해 확신을 갖게 해 줍니다.
모든 성경 번역 팀들이 볼 수 있도록
성경을 구하기가 어렵다는 사실을 알게 되었습니다.
성경 개정 작업이 최근에 마무리되었음을 발표하게 되어 기쁩니다.
아주 유용하다는 걸 아시게 될 겁니다.
우리가 새로 받은 성경을 활용하는 데 말이죠.
의미에 더 초점을 맞추는 데 도움이 됩니다.
“여러분이 돌보아야 할 하느님의 양 떼를 치십시오.
더 오래된 베드로 전서의 사본이 발견되었고,
같은 사람이 장로이면서 감독자일 수 있다는 거죠.
감독자는 그보다 훨씬 더 높은 직급입니다.
그러니까 직급이 낮은 사제가 주교일 수는 없는 겁니다.
그들이 가진 번역판이 가장 좋은 번역판일 거야.’
형제 자매들의 기쁨에 찬 얼굴을 볼 때면
그들의 감정에 쉽게 공감할 수 있습니다.
저도 그렇게 느껴 본 적이 있으니까요.
도착하지 않을 것처럼 보이는 때도 있습니다.
발표하기 바로 전날 도착한 경우도 몇 번 있었습니다.
질 낮은 성경 번역판을 사지 않아도 된다고 생각하니
그 일에 필요한 도구들을 마련해 주십니다.
“이와 같이 여호와의 말씀은 위력 있게 자라 가고 힘을 떨치고” 있습니다.

en.text: The Governing Body and the Writing Committee
take the responsibility of translating God’s Word very seriously.
As we will see in this report,
the Bible translation done by Jehovah’s people
has played a key role in making Jehovah’s Word
widely available in simple, clear language
that touches the hearts of sincere people.
In 2021, we reached an exciting milestone.
The New World Translation  is now available
in whole or in part
in well over 200 languages.
Let’s look at a few key landmarks
along the way.
In 1950, my mother and her family
were at Yankee Stadium
when Brother Knorr
released the New World Translation.
It was something unforgettable for them.
Years later, when I heard the recording of Brother Knorr’s talk,
I understood why.
But now by Jehovah’s undeserved kindness,
I have the extreme pleasure of releasing
to the international Theocracy’s Increase Assembly of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
the New World Translation
of the Christian Greek Scriptures.
No wonder he said: ‘It gives me extreme pleasure
to release the New World Translation.’
Brother Knorr was overjoyed to release a translation
that was not tainted with false religion
and that restored Jehovah’s holy name
to its rightful place.
And it was translated by anointed brothers of Christ.
Back then, most English-speaking people
used the King James  Bible.
It used old-fashioned words
like “thee” and “thou” that were hard to understand.
The New World Translation was so much clearer.
And it restored Jehovah’s name to its rightful place
7,000 times.
The same need existed in other languages too.
So work began to produce the New World Translation
in additional languages.
It was a slow, painstaking process.
Some early editions
of the New World Translation
were taking over 20 years to complete.
But since 1989,
the Governing Body always assigns a team of translators
who encourage each other to keep moving
through the 66 books
and over 31,000 verses.
When a translator learns
that he has been assigned
to work with a Bible translation team,
he is overwhelmed.
One said: “I couldn’t sleep for many nights.
I even had nightmares.”
It is a tremendous challenge
to fully understand
the meaning of every part of the text
before he starts translation.
Imagine trying to replicate a food recipe,
but you do not have the original ingredients.
You need to use substitutes
but still create the same taste and flavor.
Translating the Bible is something like that.
You cannot use the original ingredients
—the Hebrew and Greek words.
However, using the words in your language,
you want to re-create the same meaning
and emotional impact as the original verse.
The Governing Body recognizes what a responsible project this is,
so they arrange specialized training
to guide translators
and to assure them of Jehovah’s support.
More than 130,000 questions
from Bible translators have been answered in the past 30 years or so.
And these answers are not only provided
to the teams that ask the questions
but to all Bible translation teams.
This approach made the translators’ work much easier,
but the focus on Bible translation was about to intensify.
The Governing Body became aware
of some difficult problems
that some of our brothers were facing,
particularly with certain language groups.
You had just one Bible
for a family or group or even for a congregation,
and they had to share that one Bible.
In addition to that, some languages did have
new translations of the Bible that were available,
but they not only took Jehovah’s name out
but they replaced it with the name of a local deity.
So back in 2004, the Governing Body decided
to expand Bible translation work
so that more and more languages could have the New World Translation.
With the Governing Body’s clear direction,
Bible translation picked up speed.
Then came the landmark 2013 annual meeting.
And we’re pleased to announce at this annual meeting
that the work on this revision recently was completed.
You don’t have to wait at all! Here it is!
The revised edition of the New World Translation.
We think you’re going to find that this application
is going to be the ideal digital companion
to the Bible that you now have in your hand.
The simpler 2013 English text
sets a pattern for translators
because it places greater emphasis on meaning rather than on words.
Let’s look at 1 Peter 5:2.
I’m going to read it
from the previous edition
of the New World Translation,
and on the screen you’ll see the revised version:
“Shepherd the flock of God in your care,
not under compulsion, but willingly.”
Did you notice anything different?
“Serving as overseers” has been added.
We never had those words in the New World Translation  before
because the word translated “serving as overseers”
didn’t appear in the Greek text that was used as the basis for it.
However, since then, an older copy of 1 Peter was uncovered,
and it does contain the word.
It appears that the word was removed
from some later manuscripts of the fourth century.
Why would anyone remove the word?
Scholars have suggested a possibility.
In verse 1, Peter addresses the elders,
and then in verse 2, he calls them overseers.
That proves that the same person can be both an elder and an overseer.
The Catholic church disagrees.
In the Catholic church, an elder is equated with a priest
and an overseer is much more important.
He’s equated with a bishop, and to them, a priest
—a lowly priest— can’t also be bishop.
So when the Catholic copyists came to verses 1 and 2,
they must have thought that the church couldn’t be wrong,
so the Bible must be wrong.
And they took it out.
To Jehovah’s people, if there’s a difference
between what we believe and what the Bible says,
we will change.
We leave the Bible alone.
When I think back to the very evening
when I realized
that I had been given the truth,
I recall thinking to myself,
‘Jehovah’s Witnesses have the truth,
and so they must have the very best Bible translation.’
And so that was the first thing I asked for.
I wanted my own copy of the New World Translation.
And so now when I have the privilege to release a new language edition
of the New World Translation
and I see the joy on the faces of the friends,
I can connect directly to that because that’s exactly how I felt.
I just love releasing the New World Translation
in another language.
Sometimes it’s very exciting because the brothers don’t think they’re able
to even receive the printed copy
in time for the release.
In a couple of cases,
they received the shipment of Bibles
just the day before the release talk.
So you can imagine, the brothers were totally excited,
and then when they received it, that excitement was really enhanced.
The day I had the privilege to release the Ewe New World Translation  in Ghana,
we traveled to the Assembly Hall for the program.
As we neared the Assembly Hall,
here there were many people with little stands alongside the road
trying to sell things to the brothers.
Many were selling Bibles
because our brothers did not have the New World Translation.
It made me so happy
to think that this was the last day
our brothers would be forced to buy an inferior-quality Bible translation.
Now they would have the New World Translation.
Every copy of the New World Translation that is printed or downloaded
has the potential to change someone’s life.
Our preaching and teaching work is more important than ever.
Jehovah provides the tools we need.
As we use them, we make Bible truths
widely available in hundreds of languages.
We help people to understand the truth
and let it reach their hearts.
“Thus in a mighty way,
the word of Jehovah [keeps] growing and prevailing.”

cn.text: 中央长老团和写作委员会
都非常重视圣经翻译的工作
在这个报告里
我们会看到《新世界译本》圣经
在传播上帝的话语方面
发挥了多么大的作用！
因为它很简单、很清楚
能够打动很多人的心
2021年是一个非常重要的里程碑
《新世界译本》全书和部分经卷
已经被翻译成200多种语言
我们来回顾一下
这段历史中的重大事件
1950年，我妈妈和她的家人
在洋基体育场
听到诺尔弟兄宣布发行《新世界译本》
当时的场景对他们来说非常难忘！
很多年后
我听到诺尔弟兄演讲的录音才明白为什么
凭着耶和华的分外恩典
我非常荣幸
在耶和华见证人的这个
“神治国的扩展”国际大会上
宣布发行《希腊语经卷新世界译本》
难怪诺尔弟兄说
我非常荣幸宣布发行《新世界译本》
因为这个译本没有被错误的宗教道理玷污
而且在原文中所有出现上帝名字的地方
这个名字都被翻译出来了
此外，这个译本的翻译员
都是上帝用神圣力量任命的基督徒
当时大部分说英语的人
读的是《英王钦定本》
这个译本用了很多古旧的词
让人很难读懂
相比之下，《新世界译本》就简单多了
而且耶和华的名字
在这个译本里出现了7000多次
其他语言也需要一个这样的译本
于是组织开始翻译其他语言的
《新世界译本》圣经
这是一个漫长又艰难的过程！
有些早期翻译的《新世界译本》
用了20多年才完成
但从1989年开始，中央长老团决定
圣经翻译项目
一定要由小组而不是一个人完成
这样他们就能彼此鼓励
尽快翻完66卷书，共31000多节经文
有些翻译员听说
组织要委派自己参与圣经的翻译工作
就觉得要崩溃了
有个翻译员说
我好多天都睡不着觉，还做恶梦
这的确是个挑战！
因为在开始翻译圣经之前
翻译员需要透彻地理解每一节经文的意思
比如说，你要照食谱做一道菜
但你没有食谱里的材料
只能用别的材料代替
但你还要做出同样的味道来
翻译圣经就是这样
你不能用原材料
就是希伯来语和希腊语
你要用你自己的语言
表达跟原文一样的意思
传达同样的感情
中央长老团知道翻译圣经是一项重大的责任
所以他们会给翻译员一些特别的培训
让他们感受到耶和华上帝的支持
过去30多年来
总部回答了超过13万个
跟圣经翻译有关的问题
而且不仅是提问的小组能看到这些答复
所有圣经翻译小组都能看到
总部的协助减轻了翻译员的负担
但还是有许多语言版本的圣经急需出版
中央长老团发现有些弟兄姐妹
根本没有自己的圣经
有时整家人只有一本圣经
甚至整群会众只有一本
弟兄姐妹只能轮流看
另一种情况是
有些语言虽然有现代的圣经译本
但这些译本不仅删除了上帝的名字
还把上帝的名字换成当地神明的名字
所以在2004年
中央长老团决定加速圣经翻译的工作
这样《新世界译本》就能以更多语言发行了
由于有中央长老团清晰的指示
圣经翻译工作进展迅速
2013年年会是历史性的一刻！
我们很高兴宣布
修订版的工作已经完成了！
就在今天，就在这里！
请看，这是我们的《新世界译本》修订版！
我们相信，你们一定会发现
这个电子工具
是你们手中这本圣经的最佳拍档
英语2013修订版的措辞很简单
这样其他语言的翻译员
就更容易用自然的方式表达经文的意思了
来看看彼得前书5:2
我会读以前的译本
画面上是修订版的经文
你留意到不同之处吗？
以前的《新世界译本》
没有“负起监督的责任”这句话
这是因为
以前我们翻译根据的4世纪的希腊语文本里
没有收录
不过，后来发现了更古老的抄本
这个抄本里是有这句话的
这说明是4世纪的一些抄本删去了这句话
为什么他们要这么做呢？
有些学者这么认为
在第1节，彼得是对一些长老说话
到了第2节，他称他们为监督
所以，一个人既可以是长老
也可以是监督
天主教会不认同这点
因为在天主教会里
长老等同于神父
但监督的地位高得多
监督等同于主教
而神父是无法与主教相比的
所以当天主教的抄经士
抄到第1和第2节的时候
他们觉得教会不可能错
错的一定是圣经
那就把这句话删掉吧！
但对上帝的子民来说
如果我们相信的跟圣经不一样
我们就会调整想法
但绝对不会改变经文！
我记得
我意识到自己学到的是真理的那天晚上
我对自己说
耶和华见证人既然教的是真理
他们的圣经译本一定是最好的
所以我马上问一个弟兄
我能不能有一本自己的《新世界译本》呢？
现在，当我有机会宣布发行
一种语言的《新世界译本》时
看到弟兄姐妹脸上洋溢着笑容
我真的很有共鸣，想起了当年的自己
我真的很喜欢宣布发行《新世界译本》！
有时弟兄们觉得
他们不可能在发行的那一天
收到印刷版的圣经
但有好几次，就在宣布发行的前一天
印刷版的圣经及时送到了！
所以你可以想象
弟兄们有多兴奋！
在他们拿到圣经的那一刻
他们真的开心得不得了！
有一次，我要在加纳宣布发行
埃维语的《新世界译本》
在去大会场的路上
快到目的地的时候
我们发现，路两边有很多人在兜售东西
很多商贩向弟兄们兜售圣经
因为弟兄们还没拿到《新世界译本》
当时我特别高兴
因为这是最后一天有这种情况了！
以前弟兄们要花钱买劣质的圣经译本
但马上他们就会有自己的《新世界译本》了
每一本被分发出去的圣经
无论是印刷版的还是电子版的
都可以改变人的一生
传道教人的工作非常紧急！
耶和华给我们提供合适的工具
只要我们善用这些工具
就可以帮助说各种语言的人认识耶和华
我们帮助别人认识真理、打动他们的内心
这样耶和华的话语
就会“不断传开，节节得胜”！

ko.text: 몇 가지 기쁜 소식을 전해 드리겠습니다.
또한 재해 구호 활동과 관련된 새로운 소식을 알려 드리겠습니다.
우리가 급변하는 세상에 살고 있기 때문에
매우 중요하다는 점도 함께 살펴볼 것입니다.
성서 연구를 제안하는 특별 활동을 수행했습니다.
더는 마스크를 쓸 필요가 없다는 광고였습니다.
형제 자매들 개개인이 내리는 결정을 존중합니다.
신권 학교, 순회 대회, 지역 대회에서도
물론 정부의 방역 지침을 철저히 지켜야 하겠죠.
베델 견학과 손님 초대 마련과 같은 일부 활동들은
이제 여러분께 알려 드릴 기쁜 소식이 있습니다.
특별 지역 대회를 대면으로 재개하게 될 것입니다.
대회가 열리는 장소와 일자에 관한 자세한 점이
여러분에게 이러한 좋은 소식들을 전할 수 있게 되어 정말 기쁩니다.
위로가 되는 성경의 소식을 전해 준 적이 있을 것입니다.
사별한 사람을 위로하는 데 도움이 되는
새로운 동영상을 발표하게 되어 정말 기쁩니다.
“사별의 아픔을 겪고 있는 사람들을 위한 위로의 소식”입니다.
우리를 이해해 줄 수 있는 누군가로부터
가족과 친구와 가슴 아프게 사별을 하신 적이 있습니다.
그리고 더 많은 걸 해 주고 싶어 하셨죠.
여호와께서 모든 얼굴에서 눈물을 닦아 주실 것이다.”
예수께서도 미래에 대한 이러한 아름다운 약속을 하셨습니다.
그의 음성을 듣고 나올 때가 오고 있기 때문입니다.”
사랑하는 사람과 사별해서 힘들어하고 있는 모든 분들께
이 소식이 위로가 되기를 진심으로 바랍니다.
이 동영상을 쉽게 찾을 수 있도록
즐겨찾기에 이 동영상을 추가해 둘 수도 있습니다.
이제 우리의 재해 구호 활동과 관련된
미국과 캐나다의 일부 지역에 사는 형제 자매들이
형제들을 영적으로 격려하고 도와주기 위해 최선을 다하고 있습니다.
우리는 자연재해로 피해를 입은 모든 형제들과
구호 활동에 참여하는 모든 형제들을 위해
우크라이나와 러시아의 형제들이 어떻게 지내는지 궁금하실 겁니다.
전쟁이 단지 몇 주나 몇 달 만에 끝날 것이라고 생각했습니다.
전쟁 때문에 다른 나라로 피신해 있다면,
그러면 우리는 어떤 도움을 베풀고 있습니까?
중부 유럽 지부의 보고를 시청해 보도록 하겠습니다.
재해 구호 위원회의 감독 아래 일하게 하라는 지침을 주었습니다.
정기적으로 영적 활동에 참여하고 스스로 필요를 돌보도록 도와주고 있죠.
새로운 숙소와 일자리를 구할 수 있었습니다.
정부의 지원을 받은 형제 자매들도 있죠.
더 빨리 새로운 집에 정착하고 일자리를 구하고 회중과 연합할수록,
더 빨리 안정된 일상을 누리게 된다는 점을 알게 되었습니다.
형제들은 영적으로, 신체적으로, 감정적으로 유익을 얻고 있죠.
여호와께서 우리의 노력을 축복하시는 게 분명합니다.
어떤 자매의 소개로 아파트를 보러 가게 되었습니다.
몇몇 현지 형제들과 통역자 한 명이
부동산 중개인은 그 모습에 감동을 받아 이렇게 말했습니다.
이런 종교 단체가 있다는 게 정말 놀랍습니다!”
집을 둘러보고 난 다음 그 가족은
그 집을 계약할 수 있냐고 중개인에게 물어보았습니다.
이 집에 관심 있어 하는 사람이
나중에 중개인은 여호와의 증인과 우리의 활동에 대해 더 물어보았습니다.
그 아파트를 볼 수 있게 해 주겠다고 말했습니다.
대피한 형제들이 정부로부터 아파트 임대료를 지원받을 수 있도록
이처럼 많은 형제들이 열심히 일하고 있는 모습은 정말 격려적입니다.
새로운 상황에 잘 적응하고 가진 것으로 만족하고 있습니다.
앞으로 있을지 모르는 에너지 부족 현상을
더 잘 대비할 수 있도록 돕고 있습니다.
회중들에 도움과 지침을 베푸는 중요한 일을
중단 없이 계속 수행할 수 있을 것입니다.
이 세상의 장면이 변하고 있다는 사실에 동의하실 것입니다.
이 세상에서 상대적으로 평온하게 지내 왔던 곳들도
“슬기로운 자는 위험을 보면 몸을 숨기지만, 경험 없는 자는 그대로 가다가 대가를 치른다.”
‘헤롯이 어린 예수를 찾아 죽이려 했기’ 때문입니다.
“예루살렘이 진을 친 군대에게 포위되는 것을 보거든, 그 도시가 황폐되는 일이 가까이 온 줄을 아십시오.
그때에 유대에 있는 사람들은 산으로 도피하고,
시골에 있는 사람들은 그 도시로 들어가지 마십시오.”
자신이 가진 소유물의 일부 혹은 전부를 포기해야 할지 모릅니다.
우크라이나와 러시아에 사는 많은 형제 자매들은
‘나도 전쟁을 피해 다른 곳으로 가야 하나?’
결정을 내리기가 정말 어려울 수 있습니다.
예수나 천사가 우리에게 대피하라고 말해 주지는 않을 것입니다.
위험한 상황에 처했을 때 어떻게 행동했는지
비상 물품을 준비하고 대처 방안을 세워 두는 것에 대해
우리는 전쟁이 일어나고 폭격이 발생하면 집을 떠나기로 미리 결정해 두었죠.
우리는 각자 비상 물품을 준비해 두었습니다.
그리고 눈에 잘 보이는 곳에 두었죠.
저는 아이들에게 비상 가방 외에 꼭 필요한 것만 챙기라고 말했어요.
아이들은 갈아입을 옷을 한 벌씩만 챙겼습니다.
차에 기름 채워 둔 적이 한 번도 없었죠.
떠나는 게 과연 안전할지 고민이 되었습니다.
장로 형제들이 전화로 생각해 볼 수 있는 점을 알려 주었죠.
그리고 얼마 안 있어 폭발이 일어났습니다.
단 몇 분 만에 떠날 준비가 끝났죠.
집을 떠나는데 주유소마다 차들이 길게 늘어서 있었어요.
우리는 국경 근처에서 기름을 한 번만 더 채우기만 하면 됐죠.
여호와께서 베푸시는 지침이 언제나 가장 유익하다는 걸 여러 번 느꼈어요.
때로는 이해가 되지 않더라도 그 지침을 항상 따라야 하죠.
늘 그렇듯, 순종하면 축복을 받게 됩니다.
개인의 결정에 따라 신속히 떠날 수 있었습니다.
우리는 재난과 급변하는 상황에 잘 대처할 수 있도록
정신적으로, 신체적으로, 영적으로 미리 대비하고 있어야 합니다.
지금 다른 형제들이 겪고 있는 그 일이
내일은 우리가 겪는 일이 될 수도 있습니다.
지금은 우리가 서로를 도와야 할 때입니다.
우리가 드리는 신성한 봉사의 중요한 부분입니다.
사람이 거주하는 온 땅에 곧 큰 기근이 들 것이라고 영을 통해 예언했다.
그 일은 실제로 클라우디우스 때에 일어났다.
유대에 사는 형제들에게 구호금을 보내기로 결의했다.”
“그리스도인들이 다른 지역에 사는 그리스도인들을 위해 구호 활동을 한 것은 기록상 이 경우가 처음이다.”
연구 노트는 계속 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
그리스도인의 봉사의 직무에 2가지 부면이 있다는 것을 알 수 있다.
이 구절에 언급된 것처럼 동료 그리스도인들을 위한 봉사이다. …
그리스도인 봉사의 직무의 다양한 부면이 모두 ‘신성한 봉사’라는 것을 알 수 있다.”
여러분이 관대하게 지원해 주시는 것에 대해
여러분은 음식을 마련해 주고 집과 왕국회관을 고쳐 주고 있습니다.
집으로 데려가 숙식을 제공해 주고 있죠.
그들에게 필요한 것들을 마련해 주고 있습니다.
이 모든 일은 꼭 필요한 일들이며
형제 자매들에게 큰 도움이 되고 있습니다.
매우 사랑한다는 것을 기억해 주시기 바랍니다.
여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome, dear brothers and sisters.
In this program, it’s my pleasure
to share reports
about our in-person activities.
We’ll also provide updates
about our disaster relief efforts.
And, finally,
in view of the rapidly changing world scene,
we’ll discuss the need
for decisive action
when we are confronted with dangerous circumstances.
Since September 1, 2022,
we’ve resumed
the house-to-house ministry.
And we also had a worldwide campaign
to offer Bible studies,
using the Enjoy Life Forever!  brochure.
Many honesthearted ones are responding
to this “good news of something better.”
Since our last update,
it was announced that as of October 1,
we are no longer strongly recommending mask wearing
while attending in-person meetings.
So unless it’s a governmental requirement,
it is a personal choice
whether to wear a mask while participating
in theocratic activities.
We respect the individual decisions
of our brothers and sisters on this matter.
This direction will also apply
to our in-person theocratic schools,
circuit assemblies,
and regional conventions when they resume
By January 1, 2023,
if it is Jehovah’s will,
we hope to have returned to most
of our prepandemic arrangements,
in harmony with local governmental regulations.
There are some activities
that have not yet been approved to resume,
such as Bethel tours and guests.
But what about beyond January 1?
We’re excited to inform you
that, Jehovah willing,
we’ll resume in-person special conventions
starting January 1, 2024.
More information on the specific locations and dates
will be announced soon.
We’re very happy to share these
positive developments with you.
During the pandemic, tragically,
many of us have lost loved ones
to COVID-19.
Sadly, others have lost loved ones because of war,
natural disasters,
or other painful circumstances.
In recent times,
likely you’ve shared the Bible’s message of comfort
with a coworker,
a neighbor, or a relative.
To help us in such situations,
we’re pleased to announce the release
of a new video.
It is entitled
Comfort for Those Who Mourn.
We’re confident that this video
will be a valuable tool
to help us comfort our relatives and other acquaintances
—even those who may not be
religiously inclined.
Please enjoy watching this comforting video.
Our family and friends are precious to us.
They show us love.
They are there when we need them.
So when we lose a loved one in death,
we want comfort from someone who understands.
God and his Son, Jesus, understand.
While on earth,
Jesus experienced the pain of losing family and friends.
After the death of a close friend named Lazarus,
Jesus’ grief was intense.
He felt what others felt.
The pain was crushing.
Yet, his empathy
moved him to comfort others.
Still, he wanted to do more.
Jesus spoke with his Father and brought his friend back to life.
Jehovah God and Jesus have not changed.
They feel pain when people die.
They feel your pain
and have promised to eliminate death.
“[God] will swallow up death forever . . .
“Jehovah will wipe away the tears
from all faces.”
Jesus also gave this beautiful promise for the future.
“Do not be amazed at this,
“for the hour is coming
“in which all those in the memorial tombs
will hear his voice and come out.”
A special magazine entitled
“Help for Those Who Grieve”
has been prepared to provide comfort.
You can download your copy free of charge at jw.org.
We are sorry for your loss
and hope that this message will provide you comfort
during this difficult time.
This video is now available
on jw.org
and in JW Library®.
You can find it under What’s New
and also under VIDEOS >
OUR MEETINGS AND MINISTRY >
TOOLS FOR THE MINISTRY.
In order for you to have easy access to this video
in JW Library®,
you may choose to add it to your favorites.
We also have some updates
about our disaster relief efforts.
As reported on JW News,
Hurricanes Fiona and Ian
have affected our brothers and sisters
in the Caribbean and in parts of Canada and the United States.
Sadly, one brother in Cuba died.
Between the two storms,
over 3,600 of our brothers’ homes
and over 100 Kingdom Halls
were damaged or destroyed.
The branch offices are working hard to provide assistance
and spiritual encouragement.
We continue to pray
for all those affected by natural disasters
and for all those who are providing relief.
You may also be wondering,
‘How are our brothers in Ukraine and Russia doing?’
Since February,
over 26,000 brothers and sisters
have chosen to flee areas affected
by the war in Ukraine.
Because of recent events,
thousands of people are fleeing Russia.
This includes some of our brothers.
At the outset, some thought the war might last
for only a few weeks or months.
But this is not the case.
If you have fled the war to another country,
please know that we want to help you to regain
a sense of normalcy in your lives
as soon as possible.
What are we doing to assist?
Well, let’s watch the following report
from the Central Europe branch.
In our branch territory,
over 8,500 brothers and sisters
arrived as refugees.
In March, the Coordinators’ Committee
directed that we appoint case monitors
to work under the direction of Disaster Relief Committees.
Case monitors work along with elders
to help individuals and families
to maintain their spiritual routine
and become self-sufficient.
Some publishers have been able to make personal arrangements
to obtain accommodations and employment.
Others have been able to benefit from government programs.
We have found that the sooner we can help our brothers
to get settled into their own home,
to find employment, and to associate with a local congregation,
the sooner they feel a sense of normalcy.
This benefits them spiritually,
physically, and emotionally.
Jehovah is really blessing these efforts.
It’s encouraging to hear
how so many are working hard
to help our refugee brothers
get back to a more normal life.
And we’re so proud of our refugee brothers
for being flexible
and for having realistic expectations.
We are also working to assist various branch offices around the world,
especially in Europe,
to be better equipped to deal
with potential energy shortages.
This may be in the form of adding solar panels,
generators, and battery backups.
This will help branches to continue their vital work
of delivering spiritual food
and giving support and direction
to congregation activities.
But now, for the next few minutes,
let’s discuss the theme
“When You See Danger, Act Quickly!”
No doubt you’d agree
that “the scene of this world is changing.”
The relative stability we’ve experienced in various parts of the world
seems to be rapidly disappearing.
There are so many natural disasters,
increased unrest, war,
threats of food shortages,
energy shortages, and more.
What should we do
when we are personally confronted
with such dangers?
Well, please turn with me to Proverbs chapter 22,
and let’s read together verse number 3.
“The shrewd one sees the danger
“and conceals himself,
“but the inexperienced keep right on going
and suffer the consequences.”
Yes, when we see danger,
we’re wise to conceal ourselves.
But we must act quickly!
This is true now, and it was true in Bible times too.
Consider a few examples.
When David faced threats of attack from Saul or others,
he quickly got up and ran away.
In the first century,
Jehovah’s angel told Joseph
to take newborn Jesus and Mary
and flee to Egypt because
“Herod is about to search
for the young child to kill him.”
So Joseph and Mary
left that night.
Later, Jesus told Christians
to flee when they saw Jerusalem
surrounded by armies.
Let’s read that at Luke chapter 21,
and we’re going to read together verses 20 and 21:
“However, when you see Jerusalem
“surrounded by encamped armies,
“then know that the desolating of her
“has drawn near.
“Then let those in Judea
“begin fleeing to the mountains,
“let those in the midst of her leave,
“and let those in the countryside
not enter into her.”
What’s the point?
When we see danger,
we don’t need to panic,
but we do need to act quickly.
That may mean fleeing the area where we live
and saying goodbye to some
or even all of our possessions.
Many of our brothers and sisters in Ukraine and Russia
are facing this question:
Should I flee because of the war?
That can be a very difficult decision to make.
Unless the government directs us to flee,
it’s a personal decision.
We do not expect Jesus or an angel
to tell us to leave.
But Jehovah does expect us
to use our “power of reason.”
He wants us to act wisely.
Let’s see how one family from Ukraine
responded when they realized
they were in danger.
Even before the war started,
there had been warnings.
We had family worship
and studied an article from the Awake!  magazine.
There was a lot of advice about emergency kits
and having a plan of what you will do.
We made a firm decision that if war broke out
and there were explosions, we would not stay.
Each one of us had our own emergency kit ready.
We had put them in the hallway before everything started.
I told the children:
“Aside from your backpack, take only what you really need.”
Each child took only one extra change of clothes, and that’s it.
And we had filled up the tank in the car.
Up to that moment, before the war, we had never had a full tank.
We thought, ‘Let there never be war, but at least we’ll have a full tank.’
We were ready and waiting, but what next?
Was it safe to go or not?
The elders called and told me to weigh the pros and cons.
Then there was an explosion.
The windows and the doors shook, and I thought,
‘No, we have to leave; that will be safer.’
So the whole family —me, my wife, and our five children—
took our backpacks to the car.
It took us just a few minutes to get the car ready.
And when we were leaving, all the gas stations
were crowded and there were huge queues.
Our tank was full, so we only had to fill up again near the border.
We were at the border for 21 hours.
It took 21 hours moving the car little by little.
Time and again we are convinced
that Jehovah’s advice is always for the best
—even if we don’t understand why, we should follow it always—
and that obedience brings blessings.
That’s how it works.
Being prepared allowed them
to make the personal decision to leave quickly
when they saw the danger.
Ahead of time, they obediently followed the direction
to have go bags and a full tank of gas in the car.
Dear brothers and sisters,
because of the instability of the world,
we have to be prepared mentally,
physically, and spiritually
for disasters
and rapidly changing circumstances.
Today, it’s affecting these brothers,
but tomorrow it may be affecting us.
But we can be sure
that we will all stand together and help one another
through whatever challenges we may face.
This is a time for us to support one another.
And, really, relief work
is a vital part of our sacred service.
Please turn with me to Acts chapter 11.
We’re going to take a look at verses 28 and 29:
“One of them named Agabus
“stood up and foretold through the spirit
“that a great famine
“was about to come on the entire inhabited earth,
“which, in fact, did take place in the time of Claudius.
“So the disciples determined,
“each according to what he could afford,
“to send relief
to the brothers living in Judea.”
The study note on verse 29
helps us appreciate
that “this is the first recorded instance
“of Christians sending relief aid to fellow Christians
living in another part of the world.”
The study note goes on to explain:
“The Greek word di·a·ko·niʹa,
“often rendered ‘ministry,’
“is also used in the sense of ‘relief work’
“at Ac 12:25
“and ‘relief ministry’ at 2Co 8:4.
“The use of the Greek word di·a·ko·niʹa
“in the Christian Greek Scriptures
“shows that Christians have a twofold ministry.
“One aspect is . . . the preaching and teaching work.
“The other aspect involves their ministry
“in behalf of fellow believers, as mentioned here.
“Paul . . . showed that these different aspects of the Christian ministry
all constitute ‘sacred service.’”
So we see that relief work
is sacred service.
It is a vital part of our ministry.
We often say thank you,
but we want you to know
how very much we appreciate
that you are generously supporting
our relief efforts.
You’re providing food
and rebuilding homes and Kingdom Halls.
When refugees come,
you’re welcoming them at border crossings
and into your homes.
You’re helping our brothers
rebuild their lives
and providing them what they need.
All of this is greatly needed
and deeply appreciated.
Thank you for what you’re doing.
And please know
that we love you all very much.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

title: 마크 샌더슨: 그들은 흠 없는 사람들이었다 (열왕기상 15:5)

ko.text: 우리는 사람들을 여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 봅니까?
성경을 읽다 보면 그런 질문이 떠오를 수 있습니다.
“그 당시 사람들 가운데 흠 없는 사람”이었다고 알려 줍니다.
우리는 노아가 불완전한 사람이었다는 것을 알고 있습니다.
그런데 성경은 왜 노아가 “흠 없는” 사람이었다고 말합니까?
이 점에 관한 흥미로운 설명이 나옵니다.
노아와 욥과 같은 사람들에 관해 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
즉 그들의 불완전성과 무력함을 참작한 요구 조건에
그들이 온전히 달하였다는 의미로 그러하였음이 명백하다.”
「통찰」 책은 도공의 예를 들면서 계속 이렇게 말합니다.
특별히 정제한 진흙으로 빚을 때 만들어지는 꽃병과는
그러한 충실한 사람들은 육체의 불완전성 때문에
그러므로 그들이 도달할 수 있는 한계 내에서
하느님이 그들의 경우에 요구하시는 바를 충족시켰다.
[그들에 대해] 흠을 잡는 것은 정당할 수가 없었다.”
“성서는 그가 동시대인들의 관점에서 흠 없는 사람이 아니라
동시대인들 가운데 흠 없는 사람이었다고 말한다는 데 유의하십시오.
바꾸어 말해, 노아는 하느님이 보시기에는 흠 없는 사람이었지만
대홍수 전 세상의 사람들이 보기에는 이상한 사람이었던 것입니다.”
노아에 대해 할 말이 좀 있었을지 모르겠습니다.
그들이 무슨 말을 했을지 한번 상상해 보시죠.
성서 연구생도 그런 질문을 할지 모릅니다.
우리도 노아에 대해 하고 싶은 질문이 있을 수 있죠?
하지만 여호와의 관점에서 그는 “흠 없는” 사람이었습니다.
여호와께서 그에게 바라시는 모든 일을 했습니다.
여기서 우리는 한 가지 중요한 사실을 알 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 사람들을 보시는 방식과 우리가 사람들을 보는 방식에는
여호와께서 보시는 방식으로 사람들을 보기 위해
우리가 알고 있는 다윗의 잘못을 먼저 떠올리는 것이
우리 불완전한 인간의 경향일 수 있습니다.
그런데 열왕기상 15장에서 어떻게 알려 주는지 읽어 보시죠.
평생 그분이 명령하신 어떤 것에서도 벗어나지 않았기 때문이다.”
벗어나도 너무나 벗어난 것처럼 보이지 않습니까?
아내들이 그의 마음을 기울어지게 하여 다른 신들을 따르게 했다.
그의 하느님 여호와에 대해 온전하지 않았다.”
이처럼 여호와께서 보시기에 다윗은 마음이 온전했습니다.
여호와께선 왜 다윗의 마음이 온전하다고 보셨습니까?
“다윗도 … 심각한 잘못을 몇 가지 범한 사람이었지만,
책망을 받아들여 자신의 길을 시정하였기 때문이다.
자기 마음에 여호와 하느님에 대한 진정한 사랑을
이처럼 여호와께서는 노아의 경우이든 다윗의 경우이든
그들에게서 좋은 점을 보실 수 있었습니다.
다윗을 온전한 마음을 가진 사람으로 보셨죠.
우리도 여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 사람들을 봅니까?
우리 인간은 다른 사람의 단점이나 불완전함을 찾고
“검은 점이 보인다”고 하는 것이 인간의 경향이죠.
우리가 사람들을 볼 때도 그런 경향이 있습니다.
우린 흔히 다른 사람의 단점을 즉시 알아봅니다.
그리고 검은 점과도 같은 그러한 단점에 초점을 맞추면
그 단점이 보면 볼수록 점점 더 크게 보일 것입니다.
그래서 결국 우리 형제들의 좋은 점은 조금도 보이지 않고,
오로지 그들의 나쁜 점만 보이게 될 것입니다.
그런데 실제로 그 사람과 대화해 보면 무엇을 알게 될 수 있죠?
그 사람은 자기 자신을 어떻게 봅니까?
아주 작은 점 하나뿐이라고 생각할 수 있습니다.
그런데 우리가 계속 그의 단점에만 초점을 맞추면 어떤 영향을 줄 수 있죠?
그 밝은 점 하나마저 없어지게 만들 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 사람들을 보는 법을 배워야 합니다.
그분처럼 사람들을 보기 위해 아주 많은 노력을 기울여야 하죠.
그러기 위해 우린 좋은 점을 찾고
그런데 좋은 점이 얼른 눈에 띄지 않는다면,
형제들을 더 잘 알기 위해 힘써 노력해야 합니다.
그러면 우리는 그들의 아름다운 특성을 분명히 보고
그들을 여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 보게 될 수 있을 것입니다.
미게일이라는 형제의 경험을 듣고 큰 감동을 받았습니다.
그는 교도소에서 봉사하다가 에스메랄도라는 남자를 만났는데,
그 남자는 미게일의 손자를 죽인 사람이었죠.
그가 자신도 죽이려고 할까 봐 두려웠습니다.
그에게 즉시 성경 진리를 알려 주기 시작했습니다.
들은 내용에 깊은 감동을 받은 에스메랄도는
다른 형제가 그 장면을 멀리서 보고 있었는데,
그는 미게일에게 에스메랄도와 성서 연구를 시작해 보라고 권했습니다.
그 형제는 에스메랄도가 미게일의 손자를 죽였다는 걸 몰랐죠.
미게일은 에스메랄도와 함께 성서 연구를 하기로 했습니다.
에스메랄도는 침례를 받고 그리스도인 형제가 되었습니다.
미게일이 여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 에스메랄도를 보기 위해
얼마나 많은 노력을 기울였을지 상상이 되십니까?
우리가 여호와께서 보시는 것처럼 사람들을 보는 법을 배우면
그들의 좋은 특성에 초점을 맞출 수 있습니다.
그러면 그들이 발전하도록 돕고 싶은 마음을 갖게 되고,
그들과 함께 여호와 하느님을 영원히 섬기는 기쁨을 누리게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Well, here is a question:
Do you see people as Jehovah sees them?
Now, that’s a very practical question
that comes up when we read in the Scriptures
that they describe Noah
as being “faultless among his contemporaries.”
Now, we all know that Noah was an imperfect human.
So why would the Bible make the comment
that Noah was “faultless”?
Well, if you go to Insight, Volume 2,
page 604, under the article “Perfection,”
there’s a very, very interesting discussion of this,
and I want to read some of it to you.
It says, when talking about men like Noah and Job and others, it says:
“It is clear that such men were ‘faultless’ and ‘blameless’
“in the sense of measuring up fully
“to God’s requirements for them,
requirements that took into account their imperfection and disability.”
Now, “even as a potter
“[this is the illustration the Insight  book uses, even as a potter]
“would not expect the same quality
“when molding a vase from common clay
“as he would when forming one
“from special refined clay,
“so Jehovah’s requirements take into consideration
“the weakness of imperfect humans.
“Though committing errors and wrongs because of their fleshly imperfection,
“such faithful men nevertheless manifested
“‘a complete heart’ toward Jehovah.
“Thus, within the limits possible for them to attain,
“their devotion was complete, sound,
“satisfying the divine requirements in their case.
“Since God the Judge was pleased with their worship,
“no human or spirit creature
could rightly find fault with [them].”
Isn’t that an interesting quote from the Insight  volume?
The June 1, 2008, Watchtower
just adds one more thought.
It says: “Notice that the Bible says he was faultless
“among, not from the viewpoint of, his contemporaries.
“In other words, he was faultless in the eyes of God,
“but to the people of the pre-Flood world,
Noah was odd.”
Well, that’s an interesting comment, isn’t it?
Well, maybe even the members of Noah’s family
might have had some interesting comments about Noah.
Maybe those were some of the questions Sister Denyse Ekrann mentioned,
some questions her Bible student would like to ask.
Maybe we’d like to ask some questions like that about Noah.
Did he have some annoying habits?
Did he snore?
Noah was imperfect, right?
But from Jehovah’s standpoint, he was “faultless.”
He did everything that Jehovah expected him to do,
given his imperfection.
Well, that highlights a very important truth,
which is that there is a difference
between the way that Jehovah sees people
and the way that we see people.
But it should always be our desire
to try to see people
the way that Jehovah can see them.
Well, now, think of some examples.
Let’s start with King David.
Now, if you had to describe David’s life course,
what would you say?
Well, would you begin by describing some of the major sins
that David had committed during his life?
See, maybe that’s our human tendency,
to right away think of the failure
that we know about David.
But what does 1 Kings chapter 15 say?
Let’s read this together —1 Kings chapter 15
and verse 5.
It says: “For David did what was right
“in the eyes of Jehovah,
“and he did not turn aside from anything
“that He had commanded him all the days of his life,
except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.”
Now, isn’t that an interesting description of David?
Probably for us, that’s a pretty big “except,” isn’t it?
And yet, how did Jehovah see David?
How did he view him?
Well, again, let’s look at 1 Kings chapter 11
and verse 4.
It says: “In Solomon’s old age,
“his wives inclined his heart to follow other gods,
“and his heart [now, notice this, and his heart]
“was not complete with Jehovah his God
like the heart of David his father.”
So from the standpoint of Jehovah,
David had a complete heart.
Now, why was that?
Why was it that Jehovah could see David as having a complete heart?
Insight, Volume 1, page 1211,
under the article on “Integrity,”
says this:
“David . . . committed several serious wrongs,
“but he, nevertheless, ‘walked with integrity of heart,’
“for he accepted reproof and corrected his way.
“He thereby proved that his heart
still retained genuine love for Jehovah God.”
Well, whether we’re speaking about Noah
or we’re speaking about David,
Jehovah could see good in these men.
He could view Noah as “faultless” and David as having a complete heart.
Well, now, how do we view others?
We know how Jehovah sees people, but how do we view them?
Well, the human tendency is always to look
for flaws and imperfections
and then to focus on these.
Well, now, let me show you— Let me show you this.
What do you see here?
Well, now, there are two ways you could answer.
You could say a piece of paper,
or you could say a spot.
Well, our human tendency would be to answer, “I see a spot.”
And that’s the way we tend to look at other people.
We tend to immediately identify their weaknesses.
And by focusing on those spots, or blemishes,
what happens?
Well, often they tend to get bigger
and bigger and bigger
so that now,
instead of seeing the good things about our brothers,
we become completely focused on their negative qualities.
Yet, if we were to actually speak to the individual involved
(the actual person, maybe), how do they see themselves?
Well, maybe it’s sort of like this.
You see, they see themselves
as all black with just that one —one small spot—
maybe just one small, bright spot in their life.
And by focusing constantly on negatives and imperfections,
what’s the effect?
Well, we could even close out that one bright spot.
Brothers, what’s the solution?
We have to learn
to see people the way Jehovah sees them.
We have to learn from our heavenly Father
and work very, very hard to be able to see them as he does.
That means we have to look for the good;
we have to emphasize the good.
And if we don’t see it initially or immediately,
then we have to work hard to get to know our brothers better
so that we can identify clearly their beautiful qualities
so we come to see them the way Jehovah does.
When I served in the Philippines,
I was deeply moved by the experience of a brother named Miguel,
who while preaching in a prison
met a man named Esmeraldo,
who had killed Miguel’s own grandson.
Now, Miguel was afraid that when he met Esmeraldo in the prison,
he would try to kill him.
So immediately when Esmeraldo approached him,
Miguel began to explain to him truths from the Bible.
Well, Esmeraldo was so moved by what he heard
that he admitted that he had committed the murder,
and he apologized to Miguel for doing so.
Another brother was watching this scene from a distance,
and he encouraged Miguel to start a Bible study with Esmeraldo.
The brother had no idea of the connection between the two men.
Well, even so, Miguel did agree
to study the Bible with Esmeraldo.
And on February 1, 2010,
Esmeraldo was baptized as our Christian brother.
Can you imagine?
Can you imagine how much effort it would have taken for Miguel
to be able to see Esmeraldo
in the way that Jehovah would come to see him?
But he was willing to make the effort.
Although it will never ever be easy,
if we can learn to see others in the way that Jehovah sees them,
we’ll focus on their good qualities.
We’ll be eager to help them to improve,
and we may even have the joy of being able to serve
our wonderful God Jehovah forever along with them.

cn.text: 问大家一个问题
你会像耶和华那样看待别人吗？
比如圣经说
挪亚“在同时代的人当中无可指责”
我们读到这样的记载
可能会有一些疑问
因为我们都知道挪亚是不完美的人
但圣经为什么说挪亚是“无可指责”的呢？
如果你查看一下
《洞悉圣经》（下册）434页
“完美”这个词条
这里有一些很好的解释
我想给大家读出来
在谈到挪亚、约伯等古代忠仆时
“圣经称这些人
纯全无疵
无可指责
显然是指他们完全达到了
上帝的要求而已
即达到了上帝对不完美
有欠缺的人的要求”
接着《洞悉圣经》用了一个比喻
“正如陶匠不会期望一个粗糙的泥瓶
能跟一个优质的陶瓶媲美或质量相同
同样
耶和华知道不完美的人有种种欠缺
不会对他们有过分的要求
上帝的忠仆虽然身心不完美
经常犯错
却全心归向耶和华
换言之
他们在自己的能力范围内
达到了上帝的要求
就是全心全意爱上帝，完完全全忠于他
既然审判人的主耶和华
悦纳这些忠仆对他的崇拜
任何人或天使就没有理由挑剔他们了”
《洞悉圣经》的解释非常好，对吗？
《守望台》2008年6月1日刊
还提到另外一点
文章说
“请留意圣经说挪亚在那一代人当中
而不是在那一代人眼中纯全无疵
换句话说，挪亚在上帝眼中纯全无疵
但在当时的世人眼中
却是个怪人”
说得很有意思，对吗？
甚至挪亚的家人
可能都会觉得他这个人比较古怪
就像埃克兰姐妹刚才评论的一样
有些圣经学生也会问这样的问题
甚至我们也会问类似的问题
挪亚有令人讨厌的习惯吗？
他睡觉会打鼾吗？
挪亚并不完美
但从耶和华的角度来看
他是“无可指责”的
虽然不完美
但耶和华让他做什么
他都照着做了
这也帮助我们看出一个重要的事实
我们对别人的看法跟耶和华对人的看法
有时候并不一致
实际上我们所有人
都应该努力
用耶和华的观点去看待别人
我们可以举几个例子
比如大卫王
如果请你描述大卫的一生
你会怎么说呢？
很有可能一提到大卫
你首先想到的就是
他犯下的大罪
这就是人自然的倾向
我们提到大卫首先会想到他犯下的罪
但列王纪上15章怎么说呢？
我们一起读一下吧
列王纪上15章
第5节说
“因为除了赫提人乌利亚那件事以外
大卫总是做耶和华眼中正确的事
一生都没有违背上帝的任何吩咐”
很高的评价对吗？
可我们会首先想到乌利亚的事
但耶和华上帝是怎样看待大卫的呢？
请再看一下列王纪上
第11章第4节
“所罗门年老的时候
他的妻妾使他的心离开上帝去崇拜别的神”
请留意接下来的话
“他不像父亲大卫那样
全心忠于耶和华他的上帝”
从耶和华的角度来说，大卫全心忠于他
为什么这样？
为什么耶和华觉得大卫全心忠于他呢？
在“忠义”这个词条下说
“大卫……屡次犯下大罪
但由于他乐意接受管教
改过自新”
所以圣经说
他“怀着纯洁正直的心敬奉”耶和华上帝
无论是挪亚还是大卫
耶和华都留意他们的优点
在他看来，挪亚是“无可指责”的
大卫是全心忠于他的
那我们怎么看待别人呢？
我们知道耶和华怎样看待人
但我们呢？
作为不完美的人，我们很容易就想到
并总是留意别人的缺点和毛病
我想给大家看一个东西
你看到了什么呢？
你可以说
“我看到了一张白纸”
你也可以说
“一个黑点”
我们人很容易都会说
“我看到了黑点”
我们也很容易这样看待别人
我们很容易马上想到他们的缺点
如果我们总是
想着别人的缺点和毛病
会怎样呢？
他们的缺点和毛病
在我们眼中就变得越来越大
最后我们就看不见弟兄姐妹身上的优点
而只是留意他们身上的缺点
但如果我们
跟这样的弟兄或姐妹聊聊天
会发现他们是怎样看待自己的呢？
很可能是这样的
他们很可能觉得自己全身上下都是毛病
只有一个小小的亮点，或者说优点
如果我们总是
留意他们的缺点和毛病会怎样呢？
我们可能会把他们仅有的亮点都抹杀了
那我们可以怎样做呢？
我们要用耶和华的观点看待别人
我们要效法天父的榜样
努力地用他的观点看待身边的弟兄姐妹
这意味着我们要找到别人的优点
多留意别人的优点
如果我们刚开始不容易看出对方有什么优点
就要多认识我们的弟兄姐妹
这样我们就能清楚看出
他们有哪些美好的特质
也能够用耶和华的观点看待他们
我在菲律宾服务期间
听到了米格尔弟兄的经历
他的经历很感人
米格尔在监狱里传道时
遇到了埃斯梅拉尔多
这个男子杀死了
米格尔的孙子
所以
米格尔很担心他碰到埃斯梅拉尔多的时候
会想要杀死对方
后来埃斯梅拉尔多向他走过来的时候
米格尔就马上向他传讲圣经的真理
圣经的真理深深打动了埃斯梅拉尔多
他承认自己杀害了米格尔的孙子
并为自己的罪行向米格尔道歉
一位弟兄从远处看见这一幕
就鼓励米格尔
帮助埃斯梅拉尔多学习圣经
这位弟兄根本不知道
他们两个人之间发生的事
但尽管如此
米格尔还是同意跟埃斯梅拉尔多学习圣经
在2010年2月1日
埃斯梅拉尔多受浸
成为我们的弟兄
你能够想象米格尔需要付出多大的努力
才能用耶和华的观点看待埃斯梅拉尔多吗？
但他很愿意这样做
尽管不容易做到
我们还是要努力
用耶和华的观点看待别人
我们多留意别人的优点
就会渴望帮助他们继续进步
我们甚至有机会
永远地跟他们一起喜乐地崇拜
我们伟大的上帝耶和华

title: 로널드 커잔: 여호와의 모든 마련에 대해 감사를 나타내십시오 (시 116:1)

ko.text: 우리 대부분은 수년 또는 수십 년 동안 집회에 참석해 왔습니다.
다음과 같은 자문을 해 보는 것이 좋습니다.
우리에게 아주 큰 의미가 있는 중요한 질문입니다!
이 질문은 우리 마음속의 동기와 목표를 드러내 줍니다.
우리와 여호와 그리고 다른 사람과의 관계에도 영향을 주죠.
오늘 우리가 고려하는 「파수대」 기사의 제목은 이러합니다.
“집회에 참석해야 하는 이유”라는 제목의 네모 안에
3가지로 분류해 놓은 걸 볼 수 있습니다.
집회에서 우리는 교육을 받고 격려를 받습니다.
여호와와 더 가까워지고 더 나은 삶을 살게 됩니다.
두 번째는 “다른 사람들에게 어떻게 도움이 되는가?”입니다.
여호와께서 마땅히 받으셔야 할 것을 드립니다.
또한 우리가 여호와와 예수와 가까워지길 원한다는 걸 보여 드립니다.
끝으로 우리가 하느님의 주권을 지지한다는 걸 나타냅니다.
하지만 이 이유들을 중요한 순서로 다시 배열한다면
우리가 왕국회관에 가는 가장 중요한 이유죠.
물론, 자신과 다른 사람들이 유익을 얻는 것도 중요합니다.
하지만 잠시 멈추어서 생각해 보시기 바랍니다.
집회에 가는 가장 중요한 이유를 생각해 보아야 합니다.
그리고 여호와를 더 많이 섬기기 위해 할 수 있는 일에 대해 생각했죠.
그는 시간을 내서 여호와께서 해 주신 모든 일을 묵상했습니다.
그러면 성경이나 전자 기기로 시편 116편을 찾아보실까요?
이 시에서 필자는 여호와에 대해 놀라운 점들을 알려 주며,
우리가 겪고 있는 문제들에 어떻게 잘 대처할 수 있는지도 알려 줍니다.
이 시가 “감사의 노래”라고 되어 있는 걸 볼 수 있죠?
시편 필자는 다음과 같이 감사를 표현합니다.
“내 목소리를, 도와 달라는 간청을 들어 주시니.”
각주에 따르면 “몸을 굽혀 내 말을 들어 주시니.”
여호와와 그러한 관계를 누리고 그분을 사랑했다고 해서
많은 분이 그의 감정에 공감하실 겁니다.
우리도 죽음에 직면한다면 시편 필자처럼 느낄 겁니다.
이 말은 그가 낙심하고 마음이 약해지고
어떤 상황인진 몰라도 그는 이렇게 느꼈습니다.
하지만 그는 많은 어려움과 시련을 겪으면서도
즉 그분이 마땅히 받으셔야 할 찬양을 드리고
살아 있는 한 그렇게 한다고 했죠.
여호와께서 과거의 충실한 종들과 자신을 위해 해 주신
시편 필자가 여호와를 자신을 지켜 주시고 구출해 주시는 신뢰할 수 있는 분,
친절하고 동정심 많은 아버지로 느꼈다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
이와 같은 여호와에 대한 사랑과 애착은 그에게 어떤 영향을 미쳤죠?
10절을 보면, 그는 강한 사랑이 있었기 때문에
하느님을 위해 말하고 그분을 찬양할 확신을 갖게 되었습니다.
하지만 여호와께서 늘 곁에서 그를 지원하고 위로하고
그가 인내하면서 포기하지 않도록 도움을 베푸셨습니다.
이제 그는 여호와께서 지난 세월 동안
어떻게 자신을 돌봐 오셨는지 생각해 본 뒤,
우리도 때때로 이러한 자문을 해 본다면 좋을 것입니다.
“여호와께서 내게 해 주신 모든 좋은 것에 대해
그는 이러한 점을 깊이 생각해 보았죠.
여호와께 한 나의 서원을 지킬 것입니다,
그분의 모든 백성 앞에서, 여호와의 집 뜰에서,
또 그가 얼마나 여호와와 가까운지 느낄 수 있죠?
여호와께선 그의 말을 들어 주시고 그를 도우셨습니다.
그 결과, 시편 필자와 여호와의 관계는 더욱 튼튼해졌습니다.
자신의 약속과 서원에 따라 살기로 결심했습니다.
우리가 어떻게 여호와께 보답할 수 있습니까?
그분이 해 주신 모든 일에 대해
우리가 그분께 받은 걸 다 갚는 건 불가능하죠.
매일 매일 헌신에 따라 살아갈 수 있죠.
우리의 형제 자매들과 함께 그렇게 할 수 있죠.
또한 우리는 오늘날 여호와의 조직에서 공급하는 많은 것들에 대해서도
연구 노트, 동영상, 삽화, 도표가 있어서
저처럼 시각 자료를 통해 배우기를 좋아하는 사람들이
그분이 바라시는 것을 배우는 데 큰 도움이 되죠.
그에 더해 jw.org와 JW 방송도 있고
이러한 마련들은 우리가 여호와에 대한 사랑을 강화하고
그분을 우리의 삶에서 첫째 자리에 두는 데 도움이 됩니다.
그럼 이 모든 마련을 통해 온전히 유익을 얻으려면,
우선, 우리가 활용할 수 있는 것들에 익숙해져야 합니다.
이러한 도구들을 자신의 유익과 여호와께 드리는 숭배와
다른 사람의 유익을 위해 사용해야 합니다.
간단한 예를 한 가지 생각해 보겠습니다.
아마 많은 분들이 핸드폰이 있으실 텐데요.
다양한 기능이 있는 스마트폰을 쓰시는 분들도 있을 겁니다.
그런데 그러한 다양한 기능들을 익히려면 시간과 노력이 필요합니다.
사진과 동영상을 찍고 개인 연구를 하고
정말 많은 일을 할 수 있습니다.
우리 가족들의 얼굴을 보면서 화상 통화도 할 수 있습니다.
하지만 이 기능들을 잘 활용하려면 우리는 어떻게 해야 합니까?
그리고 이러한 스마트폰과 같은 전자 기기들은
충전이 되어야만 우리가 사용할 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 우리가 무엇을 하기를 원하시는지 이해해야 합니다.
또한 강력한 성령이라는 전원에 우리를 연결시켜야 하죠.
그렇게 한다면 우리는 여호와께서 마땅히 받으셔야 할 숭배를 드리고,
다른 사람들에게도 유익을 줄 수 있습니다.

en.text: Most of us have been attending meetings
for years—some for decades,
others for our entire life.
But isn’t it good to stop and pause
from time to time and think to ourselves
and ask ourselves,
‘Why am I attending meetings?’
It seems like such a simple,
basic question but how profound
because it has huge meaning for us!
It really shows our motives, what’s inside, and it shows our goals.
It affects our relationship with Jehovah as well as others.
Our Watchtower  article under consideration for today is entitled
“Why Should We Meet Together for Worship?”
So there’s our clue, “for worship.”
And the Watchtower  article featured a box entitled
“Reasons to Attend Meetings.”
As shown on the monitor,
the box listed eight reasons.
And they were grouped into
three basic categories.
The first is how you are personally affected.
So we receive education at the meeting
and also encouragement.
They bring us closer to Jehovah
through his holy spirit,
and we can tap into that powerful spirit.
The second area is how others are affected.
So we have an opportunity
to show our brothers and sisters
that we love them
and that we want to encourage them.
And the last category
is how Jehovah is affected.
As we go to the meetings
and we have good meeting attendance,
it really gives us an opportunity
to give Jehovah what he deserves
—our heartfelt praise, our worship.
It shows Jehovah that we want
to draw close to him and his Son, Jesus.
And last, it demonstrates
that we support God’s sovereignty.
Now, this is the way The Watchtower  listed
these subjects, these categories.
But if you were to rearrange these,
how would you put these
in order of importance?
Isn’t it true that worshipping Jehovah
is the most important reason
why we go to the Kingdom Hall?
These other reasons are good.
We benefit; others benefit.
But as we meditate and we stop and think,
‘Are meetings a priority in my life
‘even if I’m tired, even if I’m full of anxiety,
or if I’m going through some difficult times?,’
we need to stop, think, and meditate
on why we go to meetings.
It’s to worship Jehovah.
And that’s exactly what the composer of Psalm 116 did.
He paused, he stopped,
and he thought about his relationship with Jehovah
and what he could do to serve Jehovah more in the future.
He saw how Jehovah helped him through the difficult times
as well as the good times.
He took this time, in Psalm 116, to reflect on all that Jehovah did for him,
and it’s good for us to do the same.
So please open your Bibles or your tablets with me to Psalm 116.
And as we find that psalm,
we will see that the psalmist
really tells us some wonderful things about Jehovah
and how we can cope with our issues.
We see here this psalm is referred to as “a song of gratitude.”
And we see this right away in verse 1,
where the psalmist makes this thankful saying,
this expression of gratitude: “I love Jehovah.”
Well, there are many reasons why he loved Jehovah,
but he starts out by saying “because he hears my voice,
my pleas for help”
and in verse 2: “He inclines his ear to me,”
and the footnote says: “Or [he] ‘bends down to listen.’”
Now, just because the psalmist had this relationship with Jehovah
and he loved Jehovah, it did not mean that his life was carefree,
that it was stress free, or that he had an easy life.
No, by no means.
In fact, it’s quite the opposite.
He had many problems, and he had many trials.
And many of us can relate
to some of the things that we’ll be reading in Psalm 116,
what this psalmist went through.
Notice there in verse 3,
it says that he faced death.
Well, if we were to face death, we would feel the same way as the psalmist.
It caused him distress; it caused him grief.
There in verse 6: “[He] was brought low.”
Well, this could mean that he felt downhearted, weak, depressed.
Whatever the circumstances he was in, this is how he felt.
In verses 10 and 11, he said: “[He] was greatly afflicted.”
This caused him to panic, to become anxious.
Now, although he was going through some difficult times and he had these trials,
he made a vow to Jehovah.
He promised in verses 2 and 4
to “call on” Jehovah, to give Him the praise that He deserves,
to rely on Him in prayer.
And he would do this for how long?
For as long as he lived.
And this is just what he did.
And as the psalmist reflected
on all that Jehovah had done for his loyal servants in the past
as well as what he had done for the psalmist himself,
it really helped him to come to the conclusion in verse 5
that the God that he worships is one who “is compassionate,”
one who “is . . . righteous,” one who “is merciful.”
And in verses 6-8, we’ll notice that Jehovah,
in the eyes of the psalmist, is viewed as a trusted Guardian,
Savior, Rescuer, a kind and compassionate Father,
who always provides comfort and guidance to his children.
And all of this —this love, this attachment to Jehovah—
what did it do for the psalmist?
Notice there in verse 10.
That strong love gave him strong faith.
It gave him the confidence to speak up and to praise his God.
His problems did not disappear, but neither did Jehovah.
Jehovah was always there to back him, to give him the comfort,
and to help him endure, to never give up.
Now, after meditating on all the ways that Jehovah cared for him over the years,
the psalmist asked himself a question
(maybe it’s a question we need to ask from time to time)
in verse 12:
“With what will I repay Jehovah
for all the good he has done for me [personally]?”
So he thought about that; he pondered.
And what was the conclusion?
Notice verse 17.
He said: “I will offer to you [Jehovah] the sacrifice of thanksgiving;
“I will call on the name of Jehovah.
“I will pay my vows to Jehovah in the presence of all his people,
“in the courtyards of the house of Jehovah,
“in your midst, O Jerusalem.
Praise Jah!”
So we can see the determination in the psalmist and his closeness to Jehovah.
Jehovah inclined his ear to listen to him, to help him.
Well, this really strengthened the bond
between the psalmist and Jehovah.
He was resolved to do his best to give thanks back to Jehovah
and live up to his promises and his vows.
It was his desire.
It was his goal to always praise Jehovah,
and he would do this for the rest of his life.
And where would he do this?
“In . . . the house of Jehovah.”
And who would he worship “in . . . the house of Jehovah” with?
With “all [of Jehovah’s] people.”
So we see a pattern for us today.
How can we possibly pay, or repay, Jehovah?
How can we show our appreciation for all the provisions,
all that he has done for us?
Well, we can never fully repay Jehovah; that’s impossible.
But what we can do is show him our love and our appreciation.
We can live up to our dedication every day.
We can give back to Jehovah praise every week at our meetings
and in the ministry and doing so
with our brothers and our sisters.
We can also show appreciation for the many provisions
that are available to Jehovah’s organization today,
like our revised Bible.
What a treasure that is for us!
And then we have the Study Bible  with all those study notes,
the videos, the pictures, the charts
—all of these helping us visual people
to understand what Jehovah’s righteous ways are,
how he wants us to act and serve him.
We also have the many printed publications.
We have jw.org, JW Broadcasting®,
and the beautiful music and videos
that are being produced for our benefit today.
Now, these provisions will help strengthen our love for Jehovah
and keep Jehovah as the number one thing in our life.
But to fully benefit from all of these provisions,
what is needed on our part?
Well, first of all, we need to be acquainted with what is available.
We need to learn how to use them.
And then we need to take the time, slow down,
and use these tools to our benefit,
to the worship of Jehovah, and to benefit others.
Now, thinking about it (just a really simple illustration),
many of us have a phone.
Some of us have these things called smartphones
(you need to be smart to even use these smartphones).
But it takes time; it takes effort to learn all the different features on these phones.
They can take pictures and videos.
We can study on these.
We can go on the Internet, and we can do all kinds of wonderful things.
We could talk to our families
through Skype or different means.
We can talk (use it as a phone).
How amazing!
But with all these things, what is needed on our part?
First of all, we need to understand how to use it, right?
And this phone or some of these tablets would never work
if we would not plug it into a power source.
It has to be charged in order to be useful to us.
And isn’t that the same when we think about what we need to do for Jehovah?
We need to be at the meetings.
We need to understand what he wants us to do
to work in accord with his will, his purposes.
But we also need to plug ourselves into his powerful holy spirit.
And if we do that, we will be able to give Jehovah the worship he deserves,
we will benefit, and then we will be beneficial to others.

cn.text: 我们当中很多人已经参加聚会
好几年、几十年，甚至一辈子了
但是，我们还是可以时不时停下来
想一想，问问自己
“为什么我要参加聚会？”
看起来这是一个简单又基本的问题
但却非常深刻
而且对我们有重大意义
因为答案能反映我们的内心、动机和目标
也会影响到我们跟耶和华
以及跟其他人的关系
今天的资料节选自一篇《守望台》文章
题目是《为什么要参加聚会？》
从这篇文章，我们可以看出
是为了崇拜
这篇《守望台》的文章也有一个附栏
题目是“参加聚会的理由”
请看画面上这个附栏列出的八个理由
我们可以把它们分为三个类别
第一个类别跟我们自己有关
我们在聚会时接受教导，也受到鼓励
耶和华的神圣力量也会引导我们
第二个类别跟其他人有关
我们参加聚会就有机会
向弟兄姐妹表达我们很爱他们
很想鼓励他们
第三个类别跟耶和华有关
我们参加聚会
就是把上帝应得的崇拜给他
包括我们发自内心的赞美
我们参加聚会就是向耶和华表明
我们很想亲近耶和华和他的儿子耶稣
另外，我们参加聚会也表明
我们支持上帝的至高统治权
《守望台》的文章列出了这些类别
但是，如果我们按照重要性
重新排列这些内容，你会怎样做呢？
当然，聚会让我们和其他人都获得益处
但我们参加聚会最重要的原因
肯定是崇拜耶和华
所以我们可以认真想一想
“我有没有把聚会放在生活的首位？
就算我面对很大压力、身心疲惫
或者正在经历难题
我还是会重视聚会吗？”
我们需要停下来，认真想想
“我为什么要去参加聚会？”
就是为了崇拜耶和华
诗篇第116篇的执笔者就是这样做的
他花时间认真想一想自己和耶和华的关系
以及他日后可以怎样为耶和华做更多服务
他想到了无论面对顺境还是逆境
耶和华是怎样帮助他的
在经文中我们可以看到
他特意抽出时间来沉思
耶和华为他所做的一切
这真的很重要
请大家打开手中的圣经或者平板电脑
到诗篇第116篇
在这首诗里我们会看到
诗篇执笔者怎样描述耶和华的奇妙作为
以及我们可以怎样应付生活中的难题
在内容大纲里
这首诗被描述为“感恩之歌”
我们在第1节就可以看出这点
诗篇执笔者说了这句发自内心的感恩的话
“我爱耶和华”
他有很多理由爱耶和华，但他一开始就说
“因为他垂听我的声音、我的恳求”
在第2节他继续说
“他侧耳听我说话”
脚注说
又译“俯身垂听”
虽然这个诗篇执笔者跟耶和华有亲密的关系
而且深爱耶和华
但这不意味着他生活是无忧无虑
没有压力、一帆风顺的
情况刚好相反，他有很多问题
也有很多考验
相信我们当中很多人
都有过跟这个诗篇执笔者类似的感受
接下来我们会具体看一下
第3节，执笔者说
他面对死亡的威胁
苦难和悲痛把他压垮了
如果我们面对死亡的威胁
也可能会有类似的感觉
第6节说他“沮丧无助”
看来当时他很痛苦、很虚弱，感到绝望
无论当时他的处境如何，这就是他的感觉
在第10和第11节中
他说自己“非常痛苦”
这让他非常恐慌以及焦虑
尽管他正在经历这些考验，处境这么艰难
但他还是向耶和华许下承诺
第2节和第4节说，要呼求耶和华
也就是献给上帝他应得的赞美
并且通过祷告加强信心
他会这样做多久呢？
只要他活着就会这样做
而这也正是他所做的
当诗篇执笔者沉思耶和华在过去
为他的忠仆所做的一切
以及耶和华为这个执笔者所做的一切
他就得出结论
在第5节中，他说
他所崇拜的上帝耶和华
“体恤世人，处事正义
充满怜悯之情”
在6-8节中我们留意到
耶和华在这个执笔者眼中是一位
守护者、拯救者
也是仁慈而富有怜悯之情的父亲
总是为他的孩子们提供安慰和指引
诗篇执笔者深爱耶和华
跟他有亲密的关系
这对他产生了怎样的影响呢？
请留意第10节
这种强烈的爱给了他坚定的信心
这样的信心推动他衷心赞美他的上帝
虽然他的难题没有消失
但耶和华也没有消失
耶和华一直在他身边支持他，给他安慰
帮助他忍耐，永不放弃
诗篇执笔者沉思了耶和华多年来
怎样在各个方面帮助他
然后他在12节问自己一个问题
这也许是我们需要时常问自己的问题
经文说
“耶和华赐给我一切恩惠
我拿什么报答他呢？”
他开始认真沉思这个问题
他的答案是什么？
请留意，从17节开始
他说
“我要向你献上感谢的祭牲
还要呼求耶和华的圣名
我要在上帝的所有子民面前
履行我向耶和华许下的誓愿
耶路撒冷啊，我要在你中间
在耶和华殿宇的院子里履行誓愿
要赞美耶和华！”
我们可以看到诗篇执笔者的决心
以及他跟耶和华有多么亲密的关系
耶和华也侧耳倾听他的声音
这真的加强了诗篇执笔者
跟耶和华之间的关系
他决心尽最大努力回报耶和华
并履行他的承诺和誓言
这是他的愿望
他的目标是永远赞美耶和华
他在余生中都会这样做
他会在哪里这样做呢？
在“耶和华的殿宇”
他会跟谁一起在那里崇拜耶和华呢？
跟耶和华的所有子民
这也是我们在今天所做的事
那么我们怎样做才能报答耶和华上帝呢？
他一直悉心地照顾我们
我们怎样才能感激他为我们所做的一切呢？
我们永远无法完全报答他的厚爱
但我们能做的
就是向他表达我们的爱和感激之情
我们每天都可以履行我们的献身誓愿
每周都可以通过聚会和传道
来赞美耶和华上帝
跟我们的弟兄姐妹一起并肩敬奉他
我们还可以对耶和华的组织
为我们所做的一切表达感恩之心
例如我们修订版的圣经
这真的是非常宝贵的礼物！
还有我们的精读本圣经
里面有精读本注释、影片、图片、图表
这些视觉教材都能帮助我们
正确理解关于耶和华的真理
以及他希望我们怎样崇拜他和行事为人
我们还有各种各样的印刷出版物
以及JW电视、jw.org®网站
还有许许多多美妙的音乐和影片
满足我们的不同需要
这些资料都能帮助我们加深对耶和华的爱
也让耶和华成为我们生活中最重要的一位
但是，为了能从这些资料充分受益
我们需要做些什么呢？
首先，我们需要熟悉这些资料
我们需要学习怎样运用这些资料
然后我们需要花时间，静下心来
使用这些工具来让自己受益
来崇拜耶和华，以及用这些资料帮助别人
我想用一个简单的比喻来说明这一点
我们大部分人都有手机
其中有些人有智能手机
这样的手机有很多不同功能
但我们都知道
学习这些手机上的各种不同功能
需要付出努力
我们可以用它来拍照、录像
用它学习，也可以用它来上网
或者做各种有意思的事情
我们可以通过Skype或其他方式
跟家人聊天
也可以把它当作电话来通话
多么神奇！
虽然它有这么多功能，我们需要怎样做呢？
首先，我们需要了解怎样使用它
如果我们不先充电
我们的手机或平板电脑
就没办法正常工作
想要让它们发挥作用
首先必须有电才行
在我们为耶和华服务方面也是一样
所以我们需要参加聚会
我们需要明白怎样遵行耶和华的旨意
按照他的意思处事为人
我们也需要让他强大的神圣力量为我们充电
我们这样做
就能用正确的方式崇拜耶和华
我们自己会受益
也会让其他人得到益处

title: 사별의 아픔을 겪고 있는 사람들을 위한 위로의 소식

ko.text: 우리를 이해해 줄 수 있는 누군가로부터 위로를 받고 싶어 집니다.
하느님과 그분의 아들 예수께서 바로 그런 분이십니다.
가족과 친구와 가슴 아프게 사별을 하신 적이 있습니다.
다른 사람들의 슬픔도 이해하시고 그들을 위로해 주셨습니다.
그리고 더 많은 걸 해 주고 싶어 하셨죠.
예수께서는 아버지께 기도를 드리신 다음 나사로를 부활시키셨습니다.
여호와께서 모든 얼굴에서 눈물을 닦아 주실 것이다.”
예수께서도 미래에 대한 이러한 아름다운 약속을 하셨습니다.
“이 말에 놀라지 마십시오. 기념 무덤에 있는 모든 사람이
그의 음성을 듣고 나올 때가 오고 있기 때문입니다.”
“사별의 아픔—이겨 낼 수 있을까?”라는 잡지가 여러분에게 위로가 될 것입니다.
사랑하는 사람과 사별해서 힘들어하고 있는 모든 분들께
이 소식이 위로가 되기를 진심으로 바랍니다.

en.text: Our family and friends are precious to us.
They show us love.
They are there when we need them.
So when we lose a loved one in death,
we want comfort from someone who understands.
God and his Son, Jesus, understand.
While on earth,
Jesus experienced the pain of losing family and friends.
After the death of a close friend named Lazarus,
Jesus’ grief was intense.
He felt what others felt.
The pain was crushing.
Yet, his empathy
moved him to comfort others.
Still, he wanted to do more.
Jesus spoke with his Father and brought his friend back to life.
Jehovah God and Jesus have not changed.
They feel pain when people die.
They feel your pain
and have promised to eliminate death.
“[God] will swallow up death forever . . .
“Jehovah will wipe away the tears
from all faces.”
Jesus also gave this beautiful promise for the future.
“Do not be amazed at this,
“for the hour is coming
“in which all those in the memorial tombs
will hear his voice and come out.”
A special magazine entitled
“Help for Those Who Grieve”
has been prepared to provide comfort.
You can download your copy free of charge at jw.org.
We are sorry for your loss
and hope that this message will provide you comfort
during this difficult time.

cn.text: 我们都很珍惜家人和朋友
因为他们很爱我们
也在我们需要的时候，陪在身边
要是失去了他们
我们希望有人可以了解我们的痛苦
安慰我们
上帝和他儿子耶稣就了解我们的感受
耶稣在地上的时候
也经历过失去家人和朋友的痛苦
耶稣的好朋友拉撒路过世时
耶稣非常悲痛
他完全明白失去亲友的痛苦
因此，他即使悲痛欲绝
也很想安慰别人
但他做的不只这些
耶稣向天父祷告，让他的朋友死而复生
现在，耶和华和耶稣看到有人死去
还是感到很难过
他们知道你内心的痛苦，也承诺会消灭死亡
耶稣也保证死去的人会复活过来
《如何面对丧亲之痛？》这本杂志
可以给你带来安慰
你可以在jw.org网站免费下载
你遭遇这样的事，一定很不容易
我们希望这本杂志的内容
可以给你帮助和希望

title: 재방문: 성경—계 21:3, 4

en.text: The last time we were here, we promised to return
and show you a scripture that can give us real hope.
Yeah, I’m interested in seeing that.
Great.
It’s here at Revelation 21:3, 4.
Susan, would you please read that?
Sure.
“With that I heard a loud voice from the throne say:
“‘Look! The tent of God is with mankind,
“‘and he will reside with them, and they will be his people.
“‘And God himself will be with them.
“‘And he will wipe out every tear from their eyes,
“‘and death will be no more,
“‘neither will mourning nor outcry nor pain be anymore.
The former things have passed away.’”
Thank you.
So, what does this say that God will do?
It says that he’ll wipe out our tears,
take away death, and take away pain.
Exactly.
All of the problems that can make life seem hopeless today
—such as poverty, injustice, sickness, even death—
will no longer exist.
Have you ever read those words?
No! I’ve never seen them before.
Many people aren’t aware of the gems contained in God’s Word
because they feel it’s too difficult to understand.
The next time, I’d like to discuss the question,
How can we understand the Bible?
Would next Friday evening work for you?
Yeah, I should be home.
Great.
Before we go, perhaps we can exchange our contact information.
