title: 이삭 머레이: 여호와의 사랑이 담긴 징계를 받아들이십시오 (히브리 12:6)

ko.text: 우리는 자신이 불완전하다는 걸 쉽게 인정합니다.
그런데 시정을 받을 때에는 왜 받아들이기가 어려울까요?
우리는 올바른 태도가 무엇인지 잘 알죠.
“의로운 자가 나를 치더라도 충성스러운 사랑에서 나온 행동이요,
나를 책망하더라도 내 머리에 기름을 붓는 것과 같으니,
어쩌면 우리는 징계에 대한 이 세상의 견해에 영향을 받았을지 모릅니다.
한 사전에서는 징계를 “통제하기 위해 벌을 주는 것”으로 정의합니다.
다른 사전에서는 징계를 “사람들이 규칙에 순종하지 않을 경우 처벌하는 행위”로 정의하죠.
여호와께서는 자녀에게 권고하듯 우리에게 “내 아들아” 하고 말씀하시죠.
이처럼 징계를 좋은 것으로 묘사하고 있습니다.
간단히 말해, 징계는 훈련의 한 형태입니다.
여호와를 더 잘 알 수 있게 해 주기 때문입니다.
이제 징계를 받을 때 흔히들 나타내는 반응 세 가지를 살펴보도록 하겠습니다.
우리 모두 그런 반응을 나타낸 적이 있을 겁니다.
수치심을 느끼고 마음의 상처를 입는 것이죠.
어린아이들은 부모에게 꾸중을 들을 때 아주 시무룩해지곤 합니다.
슬픈 표정을 짓고 또 입을 삐쭉 내밀기도 하죠.
하지만 그리스도인이고 성인인 우리는 물론 그렇게 행동하지는 않겠죠?
사실, 징계는 아주 고통스러울 수 있는데,
우리 내면에 있는 매우 민감한 무언가를 드러내기 때문입니다.
징계를 기꺼이 받아들이는 것이 훨씬 더 좋습니다.
“징계를 거절하는 자는 자신의 생명을 가볍게 여기는 자이고.”
네, 시정이나 징계를 받아들이지 않으면 삶이 불행해집니다.
여호와를 두려워하는 것은 지혜로워지게 해 주는 훈련이고
따라서 교훈을 받아들이고 여호와께 훈련을 받으십시오.
강한 충고를 받기 전에, 우리에게 나쁜 결과가 닥치기 전에
우리가 나타낼지 모르는 두 번째 부정적인 반응은 조언을 무시하는 것입니다.
‘그 조언은 나한테 맞지 않아. 왜 그런 조언을 하는 거지?
난 그렇게 나쁘진 않다고. 전체 상황을 알지도 못하면서 왜 조언을 하는 거야?
그리고 조언은 그런 식으로 하는 게 아니지.’
보통 우리가 그런 반응을 나타내는 이유는
조언을 통해 우리가 나쁜 것을 사랑한다는 것이 드러나기 때문입니다.
그래서 그 점을 숨기려고 조언을 해 준 사람이 자격이 없다고 비난을 하게 되는 겁니다.
하지만 사실은 우리가 전체 상황을 모르는 거죠.
어쩌면 알고 싶지 않은 것일 수도 있습니다.
우리가 여호와의 생각이 아니라 자신의 생각에 의존하는 것일 수 있죠.
누군가가 우리에게 조언이나 충고를 해 줄 때
잠언 25:12에 나오는 이러한 태도를 나타내는 것이 어떻겠습니까?
“지혜롭게 책망하는 자는 잘 받아들이는 귀에 금귀걸이 같고 정금 장식 같다.”
우리에게 조언을 해 준 사람에게 비유적인 의미에서 금 장식을 해 줄 수 있습니다.
하느님의 사랑을 분별하고 우리가 받은 시정과 징계를 사랑하십시오.
조언을 받을 때 우리가 나타낼지 모르는 세 번째 반응은 기분 나빠하거나 화를 내는 겁니다.
자신이 보기에 뭔가 나보다 못한 사람일 수도 있습니다.
진리 안에서 얼마 안 되었거나, 지식이 적거나, 나이가 어리거나 하는 이유일 수 있죠.
잘 가르는치는 사람이 아니라서 그를 얕볼지 모릅니다.
실제로는 여호와께서 우리에게 말씀하고 계시다는 점을 기꺼이 인정합니까?
아마도 여호와께서 우리에게 조언하도록 그 사람을 선택하신 데에는
아주 중요한 이유가 있을 수 있습니다.
여호와의 조언을 ‘가볍게 여겨서는 안 된다’고 알려 줍니다.
그런데 이런 생각이 들 수 있죠.
‘만약 여호와께서 오셔서 직접 조언해 주신다면 난 당연히 잘 들을 거야.’
하지만 우리가 받은 조언이 여호와께서 직접 해 주신 말씀이 아닙니까?
다윗은 시정을 배척하지 않고 나단에게 화를 내지 않았습니다.
그는 충고를 받아들였고 “내가 여호와께 죄를 지었습니다” 하고 말했습니다.
조언을 배척하지 말고 마음을 다해 받아들이십시오.
우리는 여호와의 가족으로서 즉 여호와의 자녀로서 많은 조언과 많은 충고를 받게 됩니다.
여호와께서 주시는 모든 조언과 모든 충고는 우리의 유익을 위한 겁니다.
여호와께서는 그분이 원하시는 사람이 되도록 우리 각자를 틀 잡고 계십니다.
따라서 오늘 우리는 우리에게 징계가 필요한가가 아니라
우리가 징계에 대해 어떤 태도를 가져야 하는가를 살펴보았습니다.
히브리서 12장에 나오는 바울의 말은 잠언에서 인용한 것입니다.
잠언 3:18에는 여호와께서 우리 모두에게 하시는 애정 어린 권고가 들어 있습니다.
잠언 3:18에서 징계에 관해 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
“지혜는 붙잡는 이들에게 생명나무가 되니, 그것을 굳게 잡는 이들은 행복하다고 여겨질 것이다.”

en.text: It is easy to admit that we are imperfect.
But why is it that it is so painful
when we receive correction?
We all know the right attitude
we should have,
as outlined here at Psalm 141:5.
Shall we read that?
Psalm 141:5—it says:
“Should the righteous one strike me,
“it would be an act of loyal love;
“should he reprove me, it would be like oil on my head,
which my head would never refuse.”
So maybe we are affected
by a worldly view of discipline.
One dictionary says that discipline is
“punishment to gain control.”
Another dictionary says that “discipline is to make people obey
and to punish when they don’t.”
It’s so different from Jehovah God’s point of view, isn’t it?
In our text for today, here in Hebrews,
it says that Jehovah invites us as his children.
He says in verse 5 “my son”
and then in verse 6: “For those whom Jehovah loves
he disciplines.”
So it puts discipline in a very appealing light, doesn’t it?
So the bottom line is
discipline is a form of training.
It’s actually a very exciting process
because it helps us to get to know Jehovah even better.
So, what we would like to do now is discuss
three common reactions to discipline.
I guess all of us have been guilty of them at one time or another.
The first one is to feel very crushed
—embarrassed—
and we have this pain in our heart.
And this is very natural.
We see this even in little children
—that they can feel very crushed
when they experience the displeasure of their parents.
And they react with a long face,
and maybe they even start pouting.
But we as Christians, mature grown-ups,
we don’t react that way, do we?
Now the question is, How do we react?
What should be the proper reaction?
First of all, do not be so overwhelmed
by the emotion.
Do not feel sorry for yourself.
Another important point is
that it is painful
because the discipline exposes
something very sensitive inside us.
It is much better to respond positively toward the discipline
because the counsel is given for our benefit.
Let us read the words here at Proverbs 15:32
—Proverbs 15:32.
It says: “Anyone refusing discipline
despises his life.”
Yes, it is a miserable life
while fighting our correction, or discipline.
And then it goes on to say: “But whoever listens to reproof
“acquires understanding.
“The fear of Jehovah is a training in wisdom,
and before glory there is humility.”
So let us learn the lessons and be trained by Jehovah.
Get the sense
before strong counsel comes
and before some of the bad consequences
come upon us.
The second negative reaction we may have
is that of dismissing the counsel:
‘Well, the counsel is wrong for me.
‘It’s inappropriate.
‘I’m not that bad, and the person who counseled me
‘does not see the full picture.
And by the way, they can improve in their way of giving counsel.’
Now, usually when we have this reaction,
it is because the counsel exposed
that we love what is wrong,
and we cover that
by accusing the bearer of the message as unqualified.
The reality is we  don’t see the big picture.
Well, maybe we don’t want to see the big picture.
And could it be that we rely on our own understanding
instead of Jehovah’s view?
How about having this attitude here at Proverbs 25:12
as an attitude toward the counselor
when he gives us counsel and advice?
Proverbs 25:12
—it says: “Like an earring of gold
“and an ornament of fine gold
is a wise reprover to the receptive ear.”
So we can dignify the process
by adorning the bearer of the message —the counselor—
with gold, as it were.
So we need to respond with love.
Truly see God’s love,
and love the correction and the discipline we have.
Now, the third reaction,
we may be irritated
or angered by the counsel,
‘Who do they think they are?’
Maybe it’s a peer.
Maybe it is someone, in our opinion, who is in a lower status than we are.
‘They have not been in the truth as long.’
‘They do not know as much.’
‘They are younger,’ or whatever reason we may have.
We may look down on them because they are not good teachers.
The question is, Are we willing to admit
that Jehovah knows better
—that it is really Jehovah talking to us?
And there may be a very important reason
why Jehovah selected that person or that agency
to come to us and give us the advice.
Now, the scripture for our day text here at Hebrews 12:5
says that we must not despise
Jehovah’s counsel.
It says we must not “give up
when [we] are corrected by him.”
Now, we may say, “Well, if Jehovah comes to me
“and he gives me this counsel directly,
of course I will listen.”
But isn’t this Jehovah’s way
of speaking to us directly?
Think of the case of David.
When Nathan came to him,
David didn’t rebel.
He was not angry with Nathan.
He accepted the counsel,
and he said: “I have sinned against Jehovah.”
So, what is the point?
Do not dismiss counsel;
accept the counsel wholeheartedly.
So in summary, see the big picture.
When we are part of Jehovah’s family,
as we hopefully are,
all of us will receive much counsel, much advice.
All the advice, all the counsel, that comes from Jehovah
is for our good.
Jehovah is shaping us individually
to become the kind of person he wants us to become.
So this is not really a discussion
about the need of discipline,
but it is a discussion of our attitude toward discipline.
Paul’s words in Hebrews 12
are taken from Proverbs.
And in Proverbs chapter 3, it discusses discipline.
But there toward the end of the discussion
at Proverbs 3:18,
it gives this beautiful invitation to all of us.
Proverbs 3:18
—it says about discipline:
“It is a tree of life
“to those who take hold of it,
“and those who keep firm hold of it
will be called happy.”
So joyfully accept the counsel;
view it as an embrace from Jehovah God.

cn.text: 我们都承认自己是不完美的
但为什么受到劝告时
却很不容易接受呢？
我们知道正确的反应应该是
像诗篇141:5说的那样
我们一起读一下诗篇141:5
经文说
“就算义人责打我
也是出于忠贞的爱
即使他责备我
也像把油抹在我头上
我的头不会闪避”
很有可能
我们对管教的看法
都受到了这世界的影响
一本字典说
管教就是通过惩罚来控制别人
另外一本字典说
管教就是要求别人服从
当别人不服从时就惩罚他们
但耶和华上帝的看法
却多么不同啊！
就像今天的经文所说的那样
耶和华上帝把我们看作他的孩子
希伯来书12:5说
“儿子啊”
在第6节又说
“耶和华管教他所爱的人”
可见，管教对我们来说是很有帮助的
基本上来说
管教就是一种培训
我们接受来自耶和华的管教
就能够更加认识耶和华上帝
我们会讨论一下
受到管教时常有的三种反应
我们或多或少都有过这种反应
第一种反应就是感到灰心丧气
尴尬
内心觉得很痛苦
这是很正常的
我们看到小孩子也是这样
当父母管教他们的时候
他们就变得很不高兴
他们甚至会嘟着小嘴、拉长脸
但我们都是成年人
是成熟的基督徒
我们不会这样，对吗？
但问题是
应该有什么反应呢？
正确的反应应该是怎样的呢？
首先，不要被那些情绪所左右
不要觉得自己很可怜
另外，很重要的一点就是
管教会让我们觉得痛苦
是因为管教
会把我们心里一些很敏感的东西暴露出来
但我们还是应该对管教有积极的反应
因为管教是为了我们的益处
我们来一起读一下箴言15:32
经文说
“拒绝管教的，鄙视生命”
不接受纠正或管教
生活多么糟糕啊！
经文接着说
“听从责备的，求取悟性
敬畏耶和华，使人学习智慧
荣耀之前，必有谦卑”
所以，如果我们接受耶和华的培训
从管教中吸取教训
就不需要在以后接受更严厉的管教
也不需要承担非常糟糕的后果
对管教常见的第二种不好的反应就是
不理会管教
“这个劝告不适合我”
“这个劝告不太对”
“我没有那么糟糕啊！”
“提出劝告的人看法一点都不客观”
“另外，他提出劝告的方式也太差了”
如果我们是有这样的反应
通常是因为劝告让我们发现
自己喜欢错误的东西
所以我们急着找借口
指责提出劝告的人没有资格
但实际上是我们的看法不客观
或者说我们不想客观地看待自己
这样，我们就没有耶和华的观点
而是信赖自己的理解力
当别人给我们提出建议或劝告的时候
我们可不可以
像箴言25:12说的那样看待他们呢？
“智者的责备在愿意听的人耳中
好像黄金耳环，有如纯金饰物”
我们应该尊重提出劝告的人
把他提出的责备
看作黄金耳环
或纯金饰物
并怀着爱心作出回应
因为这是耶和华爱我们的表现
我们也要爱受到的劝告和管教
受到劝告时，第三种反应就是
我们变得非常生气
“他以为他是谁啊？”
提出劝告的人可能是我们的同辈
也可能从我们的角度来看
比我们资历浅
“他们在真理的时间还没我长呢！”
“他们知道的很有限”
“他们太年轻了！”
或其他理由
我们可能因为对方没有教导能力
而看不起他们
但问题是
我们会不会承认耶和华了解的更多
而提出劝告的实际上是耶和华呢？
而且很可能
耶和华是基于一个非常重要的理由
选择这个人向我们提出劝告
今天的经文
就是希伯来书12:5说
我们绝不应该轻看耶和华的管教
经文也说我们被他纠正也不要放弃
但我们可能会说
“如果是耶和华亲自向我提出劝告
当然我肯定会听”
但现在是不是也是耶和华
在向我们提出劝告呢？
请想想大卫的例子
当拿单来找他的时候
大卫没有变得叛逆
他没有生拿单的气
而是接受了劝告
大卫说
“我犯了罪，冒犯了耶和华”
要点是什么呢？
不要不理会劝告
而是要衷心地接受劝告
总结一下
要有全面的看法
当我们成为耶和华大家庭的成员时
希望我们都是
我们所有人都会受到劝告和责备
所有这些来自耶和华的责备和劝告
都是为了我们的益处
耶和华正在塑造我们每一个人
成为他希望我们成为的样子
我们今天讨论的不是
我们需不需要管教
而是在受到管教时
我们应该怀有怎样的态度
保罗在希伯来书12章的话
引自箴言
箴言3章前面的部分
讨论的就是管教
在这个讨论结尾的部分
箴言3:18向我们所有人发出了邀请
箴言3:18谈到管教
经文这样说
“人持守智慧
智慧就是他们的生命树
谨守智慧的，会被称为有福的人”
我们要喜乐地接受劝告
并把它当成来自耶和华的拥抱

titles.ko: 이삭 머레이: 여호와의 사랑이 담긴 징계를 받아들이십시오 (히브리 12:6)
titles.en: Izak Marais: Benefit From Jehovah’s Loving Discipline (Heb. 12:6)
titles.cn: 艾扎克·马雷：从耶和华仁爱的管教获益（来12:6）

title: 케네스 쿡 2세: “너희가 가지고 있는 것을 내가 올 때까지 굳게 잡고 있어라” (계시록 2:25)

ko.text: 우선, 예수의 진심 어린 감사의 기도는
그 후 있었던 일을 이렇게 기록합니다.
주께서 감사를 드리고 사람들에게 빵을 먹이신 곳
예수께서 전날 기적을 행하신 곳 근처일 뿐 아니라
근처이기도 했다는 점을 말하고 있는 겁니다.
사도 요한은 영감을 받아 이 점을 수십 년 뒤에 기록했습니다.
그분이 행한 기적만을 보고 기억한 게 아니란 걸 알 수 있습니다.
분명 예수의 제자들은 그분의 좋은 본을 따랐습니다.
여러 가지 훌륭한 특성 중 두 가지를 살펴보겠습니다.
예수께선 깊이 감사하는 마음이 있으셨기 때문에
그 점을 어떻게 알 수 있죠?
예수께서 극심한 시련을 겪으셨을 때 하신 말씀을 통해 알 수 있습니다.
자신이 신성 모독죄와 선동죄로 처형당하는 것 때문에
하늘에 계신 아버지께 모독이 돌아가는 것을
심지어 이런 식의 죽음을 피하게 해 달라고 하셨죠.
“제 뜻이 아니라 아버지의 뜻대로 하십시오”라고 하셨습니다.
이렇게 용기 있게 말씀하실 수 있었던 이유는 무엇입니까?
히브리서 12:2에서 그 답을 찾을 수 있습니다.
수치를 대수롭지 않게 여기시고 형주를 인내하셨다”고 알려 줍니다.
예수께서 하느님의 뜻을 받아들이는 데 무엇이 도움이 되었죠?
무엇보다도 충절을 지킴으로 여호와께 영예를 돌리는
그분과 그분의 아버지께 모독을 돌리려고 했지만,
수치를 대수롭지 않게 여기시고 기쁨을 찾으셨죠.
자신의 뜻보다 하느님의 뜻을 앞자리에 두셨습니다.
“제 뜻이 아니라 아버지의 뜻대로 하십시오”라고 하셨죠.
하느님의 뜻을 행하기 위해 힘써 노력합니다.
그리고 우리의 형제들이 부당한 투옥을 당할 때
그들을 변호하고 무엇보다 그들을 위해 기도합니다.
예수처럼 우리는 여호와를 알고 숭배하는 특권에 대해 감사하고
우리가 누리는 놀라운 형제 관계라는 축복에 대해
용기를 가지고 하느님의 뜻을 행해야 합니다.
감사하는 마음이 우리 안에서 자라게 해야 합니다.
그분은 기적을 행하실 때나 제자들을 가르치실 때나
예수께선 자신에게 결코 주의를 이끌지 않으셨습니다.
그분은 다른 사람을 섬길 수 있는 것에 대해 감사하셨고
사람들이 나타내는 모든 긍정적인 반응에 대해서도 감사하셨습니다.
마지막 저녁에 있었던 일을 생각해 보겠습니다.
그리고 그들을 위해 아주 특별한 일을 해 주셨습니다.
예수께서 그들에게서 무엇을 보셨는지 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
“여러분은 내가 시련을 받는 동안 내 곁에 머물러 온 사람들입니다.
내 아버지께서 나와 계약을 맺으신 것처럼 나도 왕국을 위해 여러분과 계약을 맺습니다.”
예수께선 그들의 좋은 점을 보시고 기억해 주셨죠.
‘그분이 시련을 받는 동안 그분 곁에 머물러 왔다’고 하셨습니다.
그분은 아주 놀라운 겸손을 나타내지 않으셨습니까!
예수께선 자신을 너무나 큰 존재로 생각해
제자들의 좋은 점을 아무것도 아닌 것처럼 여기지 않으셨습니다.
그분은 겸손하셨고 제자들의 좋은 점을 소중히 여기셨죠.
우리 역시 형제들의 불완전성을 볼 때에도 겸손과 감사하는 태도를 나타냅니까?
예수께서는 제자들이 분명한 잘못을 했을 때에도
과민 반응을 보이지 않으셨다는 점을 기억하십시오.
그리고 언제나 그들의 좋은 점을 찾으려고 하셨고
우리도 서로에게 그렇게 해 주어야 합니다.
지금 우리는 이전 어느 때보다 서로가 필요하지 않습니까?
우리가 순결한 숭배를 드릴 수 있는 것에 감사한다면
다른 사람에게서 언제나 좋은 점을 찾으려고 할 것입니다.
다른 사람을 격려하기 위해 최선을 다할 것입니다.
예수께선 “여러분은 내가 시련을 받는 동안 내 곁에 머물러 온 사람들입니다”라고 하셨죠.
우리도 적절할 때는 언제나 다른 사람에게 진실한 칭찬을 해야 합니다.
예수의 진실한 감사의 기도를 기억했다는 점을 살펴보았죠.
그분의 기도는 그분의 기적만큼 기억에 오래 남았죠.
요한복음 11:41에서도 그러한 예를 또 볼 수 있습니다.
예수께선 나사로를 부활시키실 때 이러한 말로 기도를 시작하셨죠.
하지만 예수의 감사의 기도도 제자들의 기억에 새겨졌죠.
또한 우리는 용기와 겸손과 같은 훌륭한 특성이
우리가 어떻게 그런 특성들을 나타낼 수 있는지도 알아보았습니다.
분명 여호와의 백성은 실제로 그렇게 하고 있습니다.
현재 정말 많은 사람들이 집회에 참석하고 있는 것을 보면,
얼마나 감사하고 있는지를 알 수 있습니다.
우리는 현 세상 제도가 언제 끝날지 알 수 없지만,
모든 고통의 원인을 영원히 없애실 것입니다.
여호와를 섬기면서 그분의 뜻을 행할 기회가 생길 때
언제나 그 기회를 붙잡을 준비가 되어 있어야 한다는 것입니다.
사람들이 여호와의 편에 서도록 돕는 게 포함되죠.
우리가 그렇게 할 수 있도록 힘을 줄 것입니다.

en.text: Well, throughout his earthly ministry,
Jesus expressed and showed gratitude.
Let’s look at what we can learn
from what he said and what he did
as a thankful person.
First, Jesus’ heartfelt prayers of thanks
had an effect on others.
Consider what happened the day after Jesus
miraculously fed thousands
near Bethsaida along the Sea of Galilee.
At John 6:23, we read
that “boats from Tiberias . . . arrived near the place where they ate the bread
after the Lord had given thanks.”
That added comment, “after the Lord had given thanks,”
must be in there for a reason.
For one thing, this tells us that the boats arrived
not just near the place where a miracle had occurred the day before,
but it also tells us that the boats arrived near the place
where the Lord had given thanks.
That fact was recorded under inspiration many years later by the apostle John.
And this shows us that Jesus’ true disciples
saw and remembered more
than the miracle itself.
They also witnessed and remembered
Jesus’ heartfelt prayer of thanks.
No doubt Jesus’ disciples followed his good example.
Let’s look at two of the many fine qualities
that Christians who imitate Jesus’ good example display,
namely, courage and humility.
We begin with courage.
Jesus was moved by a deep sense of gratitude
to be courageous.
Why can we say this?
For one thing, because of something that he said
during a very critical time for him.
You’ll recall that in the garden of Gethsemane,
Jesus prayed out of great concern
over the reproach that his death
as one being charged with blasphemy and sedition
would bring to his heavenly Father.
In fact, Jesus implored Jehovah
that a death of this sort might pass away from him.
Yet, despite such intense feelings, he said:
“Not as I will, but as you will.”
What helped Jesus to make that courageous statement,
knowing what it would lead to?
We find the answer in Hebrews 12:2,
where it says in part of Jesus
that “for the joy that was set before him
he endured a torture stake, despising shame.”
So, what helped Jesus to accept God’s will for him?
“The joy that was set before him.”
That joy included his hope, yes,
but above all his privilege to honor Jehovah
by keeping his integrity.
No matter how much his enemies opposed him, mocked him,
or tried to heap shame on him and his heavenly Father,
Jesus put that out of his mind,
despising shame and finding joy.
“For the joy that was set before him” he gratefully and courageously
accepted the privilege of putting God’s will ahead of his own.
“Not as I will, but as you will,” he said.
Do God’s people today imitate Jesus’ grateful and courageous example?
Absolutely!
Jesus’ true followers today strive to do God’s will
despite threats of imprisonment, actual imprisonment,
torture, verbal abuse, loss of livelihood, and so forth.
And when our brothers are unjustly imprisoned,
we do all that we can for them,
including speaking up in their behalf
and, of course, praying for them.
Like Jesus, gratitude for the privilege
to know and worship Jehovah
and for the blessing of serving in this marvelous brotherhood that we have
should move us to have and show courage
in doing God’s will today.
And we allow gratitude, not shame,
to take root and grow within us.
The second quality that we want to look at is this:
Grateful Christians are humble people.
Again, we’ll consider Jesus’ example.
Every miracle that he performed
and every teaching that he passed on to his disciples
was carried out in humility.
Jesus never sought to draw attention to himself, did he?
Instead, what do we see?
We see that he was grateful for the privilege to serve others
and grateful for every positive response
that he saw in others.
And what he saw went beneath the surface.
With that in mind, think about what happened
during Jesus’ last evening with his faithful apostles
when their imperfections were on full display, you could say.
For instance, out of all of them,
only Jesus would wash the feet of the others.
Yet, despite this, Jesus saw what?
He saw the good in them,
and he was motivated to do something extraordinary for them.
Take note of what Jesus saw in them
as we read Luke chapter 22,
and verses 28 and 29,
where Jesus said this to them:
“However, you are the ones who have stuck with me in my trials;
“and I make a covenant with you,
“just as my Father has made a covenant with me,
for a kingdom.”
What moved Jesus to do this for them?
Gratitude.
You see, Jesus saw the good in them —didn’t he?—and he remembered it.
“You are the ones who have stuck with me in my trials,” he said.
What a wonderful gift he was offering to them
by inviting them to share in his Kingdom,
and what outstanding humility he displayed in doing this!
Jesus did not view himself as so great in his own eyes
that he could overlook the good that was in his disciples.
He was humble, he appreciated the good,
and he truly “loved them to the end.”
Do we likewise show humility and gratitude
though faced with the imperfections of our brothers?
We must remember that Jesus never overreacted
to the obvious faults of his disciples.
Instead, he was grateful for their support.
And he always looked for and found
—and found—the good in them.
We should want to do the same for one another
—all of us need it.
In fact, we need one another now more than ever, don’t we?
The gratitude that we feel for being in pure worship
should move us to seek the good in one another always.
Along with this, we should be moved to reach out
and encourage one another in any way that we can.
This includes giving sincere commendation that stems from gratitude.
As Jesus said: “You are the ones
who have stuck with me in my trials.”
He was commending them, acknowledging the good in them.
He was thankful for it.
We too should give sincere commendation
to others when appropriate and do it out of gratitude.
We really mean it from the heart.
So, what have we considered this morning?
We looked at how Jesus’ sincere prayers of thanks
were long remembered by his disciples.
In fact, his prayers were remembered as much as his miracles.
As another example, think of what we read at John 11:41,
where—when resurrecting Lazarus— Jesus offered a prayer
and started off by saying: “Father,
I thank you that you have heard me.”
That resurrection was astounding!
But Jesus’ prayer of thanks was also remembered.
We also reviewed how Christlike qualities, such as courage and humility,
grow out of a grateful heart.
And we considered ways in which we can show such qualities.
And Jehovah’s people are definitely doing this.
The numbers that we hear about of those now attending our meetings
are proof of the grateful spirit found in God’s people
and in those who see the wisdom of returning
while there’s still time.
We don’t yet know when this present world situation will end,
but we do know this: Jehovah’s purpose will not fail.
Jehovah and his Son will make certain
that all causes for harm disappear forever.
And aren’t we grateful for that?
Our job is this:
We need to make certain that we are ready to accept the opportunities
that may yet present themselves in doing Jehovah’s will
before the complete end arrives.
This includes giving everything we’ve got
to help others come over to Jehovah’s side.
The gratitude and humility and the courage
that result from a thankful spirit
will help us to do this.

en.text: I don’t remember when our routine service day
became so,
well,
routine.
Our zeal wasn’t what it used to be.
And we were finally starting to notice.
Not everyone wants to listen.
We just didn’t want to be the reason.
It didn’t take much research to find
great ideas and set a few simple goals, . . .
. . . like working with those who encourage us.
With Ryota and Ami, we’re always talking
about how we can reach the heart.
We got back to basics:
Be friendly,
listen,
let the conversation progress naturally,
try to share an appealing Scriptural thought,
and keep trying.
Our zeal
can attract an honest person
to the truth.
We’d made some good changes,
but we weren’t done.
I asked Yuri what she planned to talk about.
That started the usual scramble.
Then we got it—the sample conversation.
That’ll do.
But for that to work, I had to remember the scripture.
We were both a little forgetful that morning.
Yeah, we needed to prepare better.
We’d been relying on our experience
and not enough on Jehovah.
So first we prepared our hearts.
Then we prepared our minds
and found new ways to use our preaching tools.
Even a little preparation for initial calls
and our returns visits
went a long way.
They seemed nice.
I knew what Yuri was thinking.
I wanted to start a conversation,
but I didn’t want to bother them either.
And when an opportunity came,
I just froze.
Then I was in a rush to give a witness.
It felt forced.
It helped to hear that we’d all been there.
Our past experiences were similar.
Whenever we didn’t put pressure on ourselves
and just looked for something in common to talk about,
we could usually find a moment when we could say something about the Bible.
She was curious why we were dressed up.
It turns out that she’d never talked
to Jehovah’s Witnesses before.
Ami left a great question for her next visit.
Return visit! Mrs. Iwata!
I told her I’d visit this morning.
I just didn’t schedule the time.
I could at least stop by on the way back.
I missed her again.
If I didn’t try something different,
I was just going to keep missing her.
First, I wanted her
to know I hadn’t forgotten her.
Dear Mrs. Iwata,
I hope you’re doing well.
I promise to come by early next week.
By the way, your flowers are so beautiful!
Then I made a plan for my service day.
Following through is just too important
to leave to chance.
Mrs. Iwata was doing great.
We were already on Lesson 10.
I really hoped she’d come to a meeting soon.
We talked about Hebrews 10:24, 25
and watched the video.
Did I miss something?
I guess I did.
I was too focused on our progress with the lessons
instead of her progress and what she needed.
Mr. Iwata said going to meetings would dishonor the family.
He wanted her to quit the study.
She didn’t want to quit,
but whenever she tried to talk about it, they argued.
We showed her where to look for help
and made time during our studies
to talk about it more.
And we all prayed for Jehovah
to bless her efforts.
We did our best to share the good news of peace,
and Jehovah did the rest.

title: 온 우주의 평화가 반드시 이루어질 것입니다!—희망을 잃지 마십시오

ko.text: 우리는 “대처하기 어려운 위급한 때”에 살고 있습니다.
여호와의 종들도 시련을 피할 수는 없습니다.
또 깊은 감정적 상처를 입거나 믿음 때문에 수감될 수도 있습니다.
여호와를 충실하게 섬겼던 욥은 너무 큰 슬픔에 빠진 나머지
“어찌하여 내가 태어날 때 죽지 않았던가?” 하고 말하기까지 했습니다.
그와 같은 심정이 들었던 적이 있을지 모릅니다.
하지만 우리는 왜 희망을 잃지 말아야 합니까?
지금 당장 없애 주지는 않으실지 모릅니다.
하지만 신세계에서 그 모든 문제가 사라질 때까지
우리가 인내하도록 그분이 도와주실 것을 확신할 수 있습니다.

en.text: We are living
in “critical times
hard to deal with.”
Many people have lost all hope,
and servants of Jehovah
are not free from trials.
We may face loss of property,
loss of health,
loss of loved ones.
We may experience deep emotional trauma
or even imprisonment for our faith.
Our trials are similar to those of Job,
a faithful servant of Jehovah
who was so saddened that he once asked,
‘Why didn’t I die at birth?’
Perhaps we’ve had moments like that.
But why should we not lose hope?
Because with every trial comes Jehovah’s support
—support received in many forms:
material support,
emotional support,
and spiritual support.
And while Jehovah
will not remove all our trials now,
we trust that with his support,
we can endure them
until they disappear in “the real life” to come.
Psalm 34:17, 18 says:
“They cried out, and Jehovah heard . . .
He saves those who are crushed in spirit.”

cn.text: 我们生活在难以应付的非常时期
许多人对未来感到绝望
崇拜上帝的人
也要面对各种考验
我们可能失去财产
失去健康
失去所爱的人
我们也许因此悲痛欲绝
也有可能因为信仰而失去自由
我们所受的考验跟古代的约伯类似
他是耶和华的忠贞仆人
他曾在极度的痛苦中问耶和华
“我为什么没有一出生就死？”
也许我们也有类似的感受
不过我们不必感到绝望
因为每当我们遭遇考验
耶和华都帮助我们
这些帮助包括
尽管耶和华现在不会除去我们的所有考验
但靠着他的帮助
我们一定可以忍耐到底
最终得到真正的生命

title: 온 우주의 평화가 반드시 이루어질 것입니다!—동영상 주요 장면

ko.text: 니가 할 수 있는 일이 없는 것 같지?
술람미 소녀에 대해 배웠던 거 기억나니?
더 잘 대처할 수 있을 거야.
전 옳은 일을 해서 마음의 평화를 지킬 거예요.
간수가 바울에게 어떻게 했는지 생각해 봐.
하지만 바울은 간수의 고통을 먼저 생각했을 거예요.
제가 성경 구절 하나만 보여 드릴게요.
너무 잘난 척하는 거 같지 않으세요?
헤일리가 올려 놓은 걸 다 본 건 아니지만 …
실리아 자매도 헤일리에 대해 그렇게 생각했으면
자매도 누구한테 꼭 용서받고 싶었던 때가 있지 않았어?
형제 자매들을 잘 알 때 커지게 됩니다.
두 분은 진짜 사이가 좋으신 것 같아요.
이건 장로의 회에서 만장일치로 결정된 문제라고요.
필 형제는 팀 형제와 제가 어떤 상황인지 몰랐죠.
여호와께 충성을 지킨 고대 성경 인물들의 본이 …
쉽진 않았지만 대화로 문제를 풀어 나갔습니다.
그리고 여호와의 도움으로 평화를 이룰 수 있었죠.
계속 감옥에 갇혀 있게 될 거란 말을 듣는데
마치 뭔가에 머리를 맞은 것 같았죠.
그런데 엘리베이터 문이 열렸는데 그 앞에 …
제가 힘이 다 빠졌다고 느낄 때면
이 모든 일을 통해 제가 배운 건
평화가 내가 처한 환경에 달려 있는 게 아니라는 거예요.

en.text: Hey, everyone, Brooke here.
Guess who just walked in?
Olivia.
And there’s Jake.
Would she ever?
No, she would never; she’s an angel.
It feels out of your control, doesn’t it?
Remember when we studied about the Shulammite girl?
Who was really in control?
She was.
You have the same power.
If you believe that, it’ll change how you handle the pressure.
My peace comes from doing the right thing.
“I am a wall.”
You’re just a coward.
Take your trash.
Think about what the jailer had done to Paul.
He could have hated him for it.
Yeah, he could have.
But I guess he saw the jailer’s pain instead of just his own.
Let me show you just one scripture.
All right, one scripture.
Jehovah has taught us to love,
and he’s given our family
peace.
Hello, everyone.
Haley from DeNure Design here.
You don’t think she’s showing off?
Is this just about Haley?
Can you believe her?
I haven’t seen all her posts.
If Celia agrees that Haley is doing something she shouldn’t,
you should talk to her.
I’ve noticed
your posts lately on QuicPost.
What about them?
Some people might think you’re bragging.
Who would think like that? You?
I didn’t want to upset you. Jake said that I needed to take . . .
Jake! So everyone thinks my posts are inappropriate?
That’s not what I am saying at all.
You are such . . .
Think back to a time
when you wanted forgiveness.
“Love is patient and kind.”
It’s not jealous.
I’m sorry, Haley.
Genuine affection fights peace wreckers.
And affection grows when we really know
our brothers and sisters well.
I was always impressed
with how close you two were.
Well, it wasn’t always that way.
No.
What started as a small disagreement just exploded.
You! You’re the problem.
I needed a lot of help from Jehovah
to make things right with Nick.
There was a misunderstanding
that got blown all out of proportion.
And I didn’t handle it the best.
That’s when our peace was really put to the test.
The body decided, unanimously, that he should no longer serve.
Because you pushed them!
Phil didn’t know just how tense things were between Tim and I.
I found comfort in accounts of Jehovah’s servants.
They helped me realize that
being at peace with my brothers
was more important than any appointed position.
It wasn’t easy,
but we talked it out.
And we were able to make peace with Jehovah’s help.
Without peace,
I don’t know how we could’ve managed what was to come.
At that moment when you hear the verdict
that you’ll stay in prison,
it’s like you’ve been knocked unconscious.
But then
the doors of the elevator opened up,
and in front of us . . .
That’s Jehovah.
When you’re just about to lose all your strength,
Jehovah does that something for you.
The Russian brothers and sisters, I pray for them constantly
because they are going through a very tough time.
What I’ve learned from all of this
is peace isn’t from what’s outside,
from what’s going on, or from what you’re experiencing.
I’ve learned that peace is on the inside,
and that comes from Jehovah.

title: 평화를 뿌리고 거둔 사람들

ko.text: 두 분은 진짜 사이가 좋으신 것 같아요.
그러다가 함께 하던 사업에 문제가 생겼습니다.
둘 사이에 벽이 생긴 것 같았습니다.
상처가 아무는 데는 시간이 오래 걸렸죠.
결국 우린 다시 사이좋게 지내게 되었습니다.
팬데믹이 그렇게 길어질 줄은 아무도 몰랐죠.
야! 회사에서 아무도 마스크 안 써.
그래서 걸린 사람 하나라도 있는 줄 알아?
형제들이 우리를 보호하려고 하는 건 알겠는데요.
일주일 후에 우리 집단의 형제 한 명이
젊고 방역 수칙도 잘 지키던 형제였죠.
우리 가족은 바이러스에 걸리지 않을 거라고 안심하지 마십시오.
형제들이 우리를 정말 보호하려고 한다는 걸 깨달았어요.
내 결정이 다른 사람들에게 어떤 영향을 주는지도요.
내 결정으로 해를 입을 수 있었죠.
그래서 그땐 할 일이 정말 많았는데도
식품 나눠 주는 일을 조직하신다고 들었어요.
오늘 나눠 드릴 건 다 실었어요.
그치만 이렇게 전화 줘서 정말 고마워요.
레이 형제, 미안한데 이제 출발해야 해서요.
레이 형제는 정말 열심히 일하는 사람이었어요.
레이 형제에게 일할 사람이 충분하다고 했을 때
그러니까 제가 이 일에 참여할 자격이 안 된다는 말씀이시죠?
어머니 돌봐 드리느라 너무 힘드실 것 같아서 …
형제가 안 그래도 어머니 돌보느라 힘든데
바이러스에 노출될 만한 상황을 만들고 싶지 않았어요.
우린 형제 어머니가 계속 건강하셨으면 좋겠어요.
어머니 따라가려면 아직 먼 거 알죠?
사실 형제는 우리에게 정말 본이 돼요.
그리고 어머니를 위해 하는 모든 수고를 보면서
작은 일이라도 도울 일이 있으면 알려 주세요.
그러면 이 문제에 대한 형제 생각을 물어 보고 싶어요.
우리가 항상 긍정적이 될 수 있었죠.
아내는 사람들을 친하게 만드는 재주가 있죠.
회중에 두 명의 파이오니아 자매가 있었죠.
아무리 봐도 저 자매는 봉사 좀 신경 써야 될 것 같아.
베키 자매를 보면 사실 자매 생각이 나요.
베키 자매는 정말 뭐든 열심히 하고
우리 셋이 한 번 모이면 어때요?
그다음 주에 두 사람을 저희 집에 초대했어요.
두 사람은 서로에 대해 잘 알게 되었습니다.
잠언을 보면 “혀가 아픔을 낫게 한다”고 하죠.
아내 덕분에 그 의미를 분명히 알게 됐어요.
여호와의 도움으로 우리는 연합을 이룰 수 있었습니다.
우린 감옥에 있을 때 데이비드를 처음 만났죠.
여러분처럼 평화롭게 지내는 사람은 처음 봤어요.
우리에게는 그보다 더 강한 것이 있으니까요.
제 자신을 변호하는 데 급급하다 보니
이건 뭔가 착오가 있는 것 같아요.
상황이 그렇게 나빠질 거라곤 생각하지 못했습니다.
필 형제는 이제 장로로 섬기지 않습니다.
다음 몇 달 동안 정말 힘들었어요.
몇 가지 사실이 더 밝혀졌을 때
여호와의 조직에 속해 있다는 거 자체가
얼마나 큰 특권인지 깨닫게 해 주었죠.
그 이후에 닥칠 어려움을 인내할 수 없었을 겁니다.
필 형제는 팀 형제와 제가 어떤 상황인지 몰랐죠.
필 형제 자격에 대해 다시 검토해야 할 것 같아요.
장로 회에서 이미 장로 자격이 없다고
이건 장로의 회에서 만장일치로 결정된 문제라고요.
압력을 받아야겠어요! -어떻게 그런 말을 할 수 …
그 후로도 우린 올바로 행동하지 못했습니다.
이 이야기를 필 형제에게 다 해 줬어요.
믿음의 두 눈 환히 비춰 주네,
쇠창살도 여러분을 가두지 못하는 것 같았어요.
여러분이 하느님의 축복을 받는 사람들이라는 걸요.
어떻게 그렇게 다른 건지 알고 싶었습니다.
필 형제가 그 답을 알려 줬죠.
“그리고 여러분은 진리를 알게 될 것이며, 진리가 여러분을 자유롭게 할 것입니다.”
형제가 감옥에 있을 때 겪은 일들과
여호와께서 늘 함께 해 주신 경험 말이에요.
칼 형제가 한 번은 이렇게 말했었는데,
나중에 우리가 요셉 형제랑 식사하게 되면
여러분 한 분 한 분의 이야기를 듣고
제 이야기를 좀 더 해 드려도 될까요?

en.text: And every morning
—and I mean every morning—
there’s Jeremy singing at the top of his lungs.
OK, I wasn’t the only one.
No, but you were the loudest.
Spoken like a true big brother.
I was always impressed with how close you two were.
Hmm.
Well, it wasn’t always that way.
No.
I mean, it started out that way.
Nick and I—we weren’t just brothers;
we were friends.
But then the family business ran into trouble,
and what started as a small disagreement just exploded.
You don’t even understand at all how our business works!
Instead of criticizing, could you just once . . .
Jeremy!
Do you have any idea what this is going to cost us?
I didn’t have a choice. You went behind my back!
What’s your problem?
You! You’re the problem.
We tried to work it out.
But things just got worse.
It was like a door had slammed shut between us.
On the outside, I acted like everything was fine.
But inside, I couldn’t let it go.
I felt like a total hypocrite,
and that had to change.
I needed a lot of help from Jehovah
to let go
—to move on—
and make things right with Nick.
It took a long time for the wounds to heal . . .
. . . and for us to trust each other the way we used to.
But we did.
I’m so grateful that we made peace
before the world turned upside down.
You see,
the pandemic lasted longer than any of us expected,
and all the conflicting news reports just added to the stress.
Then my sister lost her job and had to move in with us.
So, yeah, it was me
and Kelly, Nicole, and Dad.
Twenty seconds, Son
—twenty seconds.
I’ll see you later.
Yeah.
Uh, where’s your mask?
Don’t worry.
Here, you can use this one.
I won’t get near anyone.
Gary.
Listen!
Nobody at the warehouse is wearing masks.
And do you know how many people have actually gotten sick?
Zero.
So far.
You saw the last Governing Body update.
We can’t let down our guard.
Not now.
Dad, I get it.
OK?
Look, I think it’s great that the brothers are trying to keep us safe.
But . . .
But what?
Don’t you think that they’re, you know, overreacting?
But, of course, it wasn’t the brothers who had the problem.
It was me.
A week later, I found out that a friend in our service group
was in the hospital with COVID-19.
He was young, and he had been taking all the right precautions.
I had really let my guard down.
Now is not the time
to slacken our hand when it comes to safety.
Don’t let your guard down.
Don’t think the virus can’t affect you or your family.
I saw how the organization was really trying to protect us
and how much my decisions were affecting others,
including the people I love the most.
As the pandemic dragged on,
I learned the importance of being humble and obedient.
Following Jehovah’s direction didn’t just help us stay safe,
it brought us peace.
And you know how Jehovah’s people are.
When there’s a need,
our brothers step up.
So even though we had
a lot of work to do back then,
we always had willing workers
—so many workers that some started to feel like they were being overlooked.
Hey, Ray! What’s up?
Hey, Matt,
I hear you’re organizing the food distribution for our congregation.
Yeah, I’m trying my best.
Yeah, well, can I give you a hand? My truck is all ready to go.
We actually just finished loading up for the day, so I think we’re good.
But, wow, yeah, thank you very much for offering.
OK. When’s the next run?
You know what, Ray?
We’re about to pull out right now.
Is it OK if I call you back?
Yeah. Yeah, sure.
Ray was such a hard worker,
more than most of us even realized.
He put his heart into every assignment.
Who was that?
But when I told him
we already had all the help we needed,
it didn’t go the way I hoped.
Ray, I think you’re muted.
So, what you’re saying is you don’t think I’m qualified to help out.
No, no, we just—
We know how hard you’re working caring for your mom.
We didn’t want to . . .
Isn’t Paul Thompson on your crew?
Yeah, but—
And Oliver Kagan?
Oliver’s my assistant, yes, but—
So how does this work, Matt?
I mean, you just use your friends,
and you shut the rest of us out.
Don’t you think I notice how you brothers ignore me?
Ray, I owe you an apology.
I’m so sorry.
I should’ve spoken with you about this right from the start.
You’re working so hard taking care of your mom.
The last thing we wanted to do was make things harder for you.
But even more than that,
we didn’t want to have to ask you to do something
that would put you or your mother at higher risk.
I know.
I worry about that too.
You know,
your mom —we wouldn’t want anything to happen to her.
She’s one of our congregation treasures.
I know.
And you’re not so bad either.
Seriously, you’re such a good example.
Think how Jehovah must feel when he sees
all that you’re doing for us and for your mom.
Thank you.
That means a lot to me.
If something comes up that I can help with then
—even just a little— and I can do it from home—
Well, that’s a good point.
Maybe I can get your thoughts on something, if that’s OK?
And later on,
when things got even more intense,
that’s when our peace was really put to the test.
Yeah, but, Tim, you always found a way to keep us positive.
Well, I learned a lot about that from my better half.
Amy has always had a way of bringing people together.
For example, just before the pandemic,
there were these two pioneer sisters in our congregation.
Becky was energetic, industrious, and fearless in her ministry,
and Lena was experienced, self-sacrificing,
and such a good Bible teacher.
But they didn’t exactly get along.
Are you ready to go?
Are you OK?
It’s just— It’s Becky.
She’s just such a phantom pioneer.
We never see her.
I’m sorry, but she just needs to be more serious
about her ministry.
Well, she’s been doing metro witnessing and . . .
I know, I know, and LDC too, right?
She does plumbing?
Concrete.
She does have a lot of energy!
Do you remember when we used to be like that?
I don’t know that I was ever like Becky.
No, you weren’t.
You were Beckyer than Becky.
I couldn’t keep up with you
—those long service days in your little red car.
That feels like a long time ago.
Yeah.
You know, Becky reminds me a lot of you
—I mean both of us—
twenty years ago.
She’s working so hard,
and she’s made so many sacrifices
for the truth, just like you have.
I think we should get together
—the three of us.
You should get to know her better.
The next week, I had them both over to the house.
And the more those two got to know each other,
the closer they became.
You know that proverb: “The tongue of the wise is a healing”?
Amy taught me what that verse really means.
OK, everyone out!
When everything changed
and we suddenly found ourselves locked up together,
I tried to show that same spirit
so that we could stay united.
And with Jehovah’s help,
we did.
The first time we met David,
we were in chains!
I’d seen a lot of things during my time as a guard,
but nothing like the peace that you all had.
Prison chains may be strong,
but we all had something much stronger.
But we had to work for that peace.
Right, Phil?
That’s right.
See, there was a misunderstanding
that got blown all out of proportion.
And I didn’t handle it the best.
The more I tried to defend myself, the worse it became.
Brothers, there must be some mistake.
This isn’t true.
You know me!
I wasn’t prepared for how far it would go.
There’s one more announcement.
Brother Philip Kim is no longer serving as an elder.
Well, that brings our meeting to a close.
Now we can stand.
The next few months were a real struggle.
But when more details came to light,
I thought I’d be reappointed,
but I wasn’t.
Phil!
I couldn’t understand why.
Phil, come on . . .
I felt bitterness growing inside.
Phil, you know . . .
Everything became about me
—how I felt, what I deserved.
It was like a fog that stopped me from seeing what Jehovah deserved,
and I really needed his help.
I found comfort in accounts of Jehovah’s servants
who were either misunderstood or misjudged
but maintained their loyalty to Him.
They helped me realize that it’s a privilege
just to be in Jehovah’s organization.
Being at peace with my brothers
was more important than any appointed position.
Without peace, I don’t know how we could’ve managed what was to come.
Is your arthritis bad today?
Then I’ll be your secretary
just like Baruch was to Jeremiah.
I don’t know what I’d do without you.
But you know, there is more to the story.
Phil didn’t know just
how tense things were between Tim and I.
No idea.
We never talked,
I mean really talked, about it
until it was too late.
Look!
We need to talk.
I think we need to seriously reconsider Phil’s qualifications.
You know he’s not the type of brother that . . .
Enough. Enough! Enough about Phil.
I know he’s your friend, . . .
Friend?
. . . but the body agreed that he no longer qualified to serve as an elder.
Friend? Friend?
He’s worked with us for years!
The body decided, unanimously,
that he should no longer serve.
Because you pushed them!
Excuse me?
It’s enough that we have those outside the congregation
putting pressure on us; we do not need more in here!
Do you seriously think . . .
The conversation —the argument—
it was terrible.
We both said things we didn’t mean.
And after that, we both handled the situation poorly.
We needed to make things right.
It wasn’t easy,
but we talked it out.
And we made peace with Jehovah’s help.
Can you imagine what it would have been like in that cellblock if we hadn’t?
We finally told Phil the whole story once we were all roommates.
Wow!
We’re ready!
Let’s go sing.
Like an island of calm In dark stormy seas,
God’s people are living in peace.
With our eyes of faith, We see beyond the clouds
And know that the storm soon will cease.
To the ends of the earth, There’ll be peace at last
For all eternity.
From the valleys below . . .
There’s one more story to tell.
I didn’t know it at the time,
but seeds of truth
were being planted in my heart.
You were all so different.
I couldn’t understand it.
You were prisoners, yes,
but you felt free
—truly free.
After you were released,
it became clear to me
that you have God’s blessing,
and I wanted to know why.
Phil helped me find the answer.
“And you will know the truth,
and the truth will set you free.”
Phil encouraged me to make the truth my own.
I had real trouble at first.
With all the turmoil going on at the time,
the idea of being peaceable
and waiting on God’s Kingdom
—it was hard to grasp.
But with Jehovah’s help
and the patience of these good people,
I was baptized before the start of the great tribulation.
Joseph, during our time in prison,
the story of your life
—your time in prison
and how Jehovah was always with you—
became a real source of strength
for us.
I remember one day,
Carl said—
What did you say?
I said, “One day, we’ll have a meal with Joseph,
and we’ll say ‘thank you.’”
And here we are!
Really, it’s I who should thank you.
Each and every one of your stories
touches my heart.
You know a lot about my life,
but would it be all right if I shared a few more stories?
Please!
We have so many questions.
Can you tell us about Egypt?
What was Pharaoh really like?
Dreams!
We have to talk about those dreams.
You do have many questions!
And I have many details to share.
And thanks to our God, Jehovah,
we have all the time we need.

ko.text: 회중의 영적 깨끗함과 연합을 유지하길 원하죠.
성경에서 금지하는 종교 의식이나 숭배 행위에 참여하지 않아야 한다는 것입니다.
둘째로, 다른 종교들의 숭배 행위에 참여하지 않는 것에 더해
우리의 결정으로 인해 회중에 있는 누군가가
걸려 넘어지지는 않을지 생각해 봐야 합니다.
우리는 누가복음 17:2의 성경 원칙을 기억하기 때문에
세 번째로 생각해 보아야 할 점은
우리가 주의 깊이 고려해야 할 한 가지 성경 원칙은
장로들이 다른 사람을 도울 때에도 적용됩니다.
회중 형제 자매들에게 도움을 베풀 수는 있지만,
따라서 증인들이 주관하지 않는 장례식에 참석하는 문제와 관련해
각자 성경 원칙에 근거해 결정을 내린다면
자유롭고 평화로운 분위기가 조성될 수 있습니다.
지역 관습이 아니라 성경 원칙을 따르는 것도
화상으로는 하객들의 행동을 통제할 수가 없잖아요.
누군가의 양심을 불편하게 할 수 있는 상황들을 예상해 보았죠.
저희는 저희 상황에 맞는 성경 원칙들을 미리 생각해 봤어요.
또 장성한 장로 형제와 상의한 것도 큰 도움이 됐죠.
그 형제는 잠언 14:15의 원칙을 알려 주시면서
성경 원칙과 일치하게 진행되게 할 책임은
많은 일들은 저희 나름대로 결정할 권리가 있었지만
저희는 형제들이 그 결정을 어떻게 받아들일지도 신경을 썼습니다.
저희는 결혼식에 참석한 사람 중 누구도
충분히 즐거운 결혼식을 올릴 수 있었습니다.
혹시나 누가 불편했을까 봐 걱정되는 일이 하나도 없었죠.

en.text: In Japan,
religious rituals are associated with each stage of life
and with each season of the year.
As Jehovah’s Witnesses,
we want to keep the cleanliness and unity
of the congregation.
In this regard, one of the most delicate areas
is the decision on whether to attend a non-Witness funeral or not.
The first thing we must consider regarding funerals is not to be involved
in religious rituals and acts of worship that are condemned by the Bible.
In harmony with the principle
at 2 Corinthians 6:14,
we need to keep completely separate
from pagan acts of worship.
Next, even if we don’t participate in the worship of other religions,
we need to consider if our decisions could stumble someone in the congregation.
When we consider the Bible principle
at Luke 17:2,
we do not want our decisions to hinder
the faith of someone in the congregation.
The third point to think about is our conscience.
We need to seriously think about the Bible principle
at Galatians 6:5, where it says
that each must “carry his own load.”
This Bible principle
also applies when elders want to support others.
Of course, those in the congregation can ask the elders for support
in issues related to funerals.
However, in matters of conscience,
elders cannot force decisions on others.
So it would be wrong to make some kind of rule
regarding attending non-Witness funerals.
If each person can make
decisions based on Bible principles,
we can have a truly peaceful
and free atmosphere
where each individual’s differing situation
is respected.
This would really contribute to the unity of the congregation.
And all can maintain a clean conscience
and serve happily before Jehovah.
In my culture,
specifically the Namibian Oshiwambo culture,
like in many African cultures,
there are many spiritistic customs related to weddings
that are included in wedding celebrations.
Unfortunately, my family is not in the truth.
So obviously, for Ben and I,
that was one of the main concerns.
They don’t understand our worship of Jehovah,
and they don’t understand that we apply Bible principles
and not the traditions of men.
We got engaged before the pandemic,
but obviously, now that our wedding was to be over videoconferencing,
it meant that we didn’t have control over many things.
We tried to imagine situations
that could stumble our brothers or disrupt
the unity in the congregation.
We had to, in advance,
think of Bible principles that would apply in our case,
but particularly what we also found helpful was speaking to a mature elder.
He gave us a principle at Proverbs 14:15.
He told us to be very careful when people say,
“I will do this” or “I won’t do this” at your wedding.
Basically, it was up to us to make sure that the proceedings
or things that happen at our wedding
would be in order and in harmony with Bible principles.
Another principle that came to mind was
1 Corinthians 10:23.
So obviously, we knew that we had the right to do many things,
but we were also very conscious
of how our brothers would view our wedding.
We didn’t want anybody to be at our wedding and feel embarrassed
or even stumbled to be there.
Now looking back at our wedding,
we look back with fond memories.
So applying Bible principles didn’t restrict our fun.
Also, it contributed to the unity among our brothers
because all of us —those present, those who were invited—
were able to enjoy the wedding.
You’re not worried about thinking, ‘Oh, did that thing offend anybody?’
So you’re able to enjoy the day without any bad memories.

title: 어려움 속에서도 평화를 누리는 우리 형제들

ko.text: 우리 모두는 평화를 빼앗아 갈 수 있는
그리고 이겨 내기 위해 어떻게 힘써 노력했는지
평화를 되찾고 유지하기 위해 어떻게 했는지 유의해 보십시오.
여호와께서 그들을 어떻게 도우셨는지 확인해 보십시오.
이제 보게 될 동영상에 나오는 사람들과
비슷한 어려움을 겪고 있다는 걸 알고 있습니다.
이 동영상에 나오는 형제 자매들의 본이
전 그런 본을 보면서 많은 걸 배워요.
어릴 때는 엄마 아빠랑 같이 살았는데
다음 날이 되면 또 아프고 그랬어요.
그리고 형사소송법 책 같은 걸 펴 놓고
저 혼자서 수사관과 판사 역할을 다 하는 거예요.
어렸을 때 전 친척들과 다 같이 살고 싶었어요.
뉴욕에 왔을 때 제 마음은 슬픔으로 가득했어요.
그래서 그날 아침에 대피하라는 전화를 받았을 땐
우리 마을 전체가 그렇게 하루 사이에
산불이 나기 직전 집회 때, 회중의 필요에서
재해가 발생했을 때 어떻게 해야 하는지를 다뤘지요.
그래서 교통경찰이 우회전을 하라고 했을 때,
이제 막 일을 시작해서 부담감도 있었지만
여호와께서 일자리를 찾게 도와주실 거라고 믿었죠.
그런데 아무리 노력해도 직장을 구할 수가 없었습니다.
그렇게 느끼는 것은 전혀 이상한 일이 아닙니다.
때로는 살면서 예상하지 못한 문제들이 생겨서
마거릿, 펠릭스, 미겔, 니키, 그리고 앤트워넷은
그렇게 말할 수 있는 이유를 살펴보시겠습니다.
어떻게 본받을 수 있는지 유의해 보십시오.
왜 불공정과 고난을 허용하시는지에 대해 의문이 생겼습니다.
전 모든 불공정을 바로잡아야 한다고 생각했습니다.
저에게 진리에 대해 아주 열정적으로 말했습니다.
따뜻한 아버지가 계시다는 게 어떤 건지 느끼게 됐어요.
침례 받는 날 진짜 너무 기분이 좋았어요.
형제 자매들이 절 사랑한다는 걸 느낄 수 있었죠.
계속해서 좋은 일들이 일어나는 것 같았습니다.
무장한 요원 여럿이 우리 집에 들이닥쳤습니다.
그런데 이제 그들과 사법 기관들 때문에
제가 불공정한 일을 당하게 된 겁니다.
어릴 적 제가 병 속에 넣어 두었던
마치 제가 그런 벌레가 된 기분이었죠.
계속 감옥에 갇혀 있게 될 거란 말을 듣는데
마치 뭔가에 머리를 맞은 것 같았죠.
귀에서는 윙 하는 소리가 들리기 시작했습니다.
그러고 나선 수갑이 채워진 채로 끌려갔습니다.
절 위해 박수를 쳐 주고 있었습니다.
제가 힘이 다 빠졌다고 느낄 때면
그 덕분에 계속 달릴 수 있었어요.
아마 계속 제 병 걱정만 했겠죠.
음식은 좋은 대화 소재인 것 같아요.
음식 이야기만 나오면 다들 할 말이 정말 많죠.
머리사랑 같이 병원에 가는 날은 정말 신나요.
머리사랑 같이 있으면 항상 웃게 돼요.
친구들은 정말 제게 큰 힘이 돼요.
“진정한 친구는 항상 사랑하니 그는 고난의 때를 위해 태어난 형제이다”
속마음을 털어놓을 수 있는 친한 친구에게
어쩌면 지금 변화가 필요한 시기일지도 몰라.
좀 단순한 일을 해 보면 어때?
가족 부양을 할 수 있게 될 거야.”
아내가 가족이 먹을 빵을 만드는 걸
여보, 나 이제 그 빵 만들어서
거리에 나가서 사람들한테 빵을 팔겠다고 하니까요.
그러곤 요리사 모자 같은 걸 썼죠.
빵을 다 판 걸 보고 아내는 깜짝 놀랐습니다.
다음번에 빵을 또 팔러 나가려고 하는데
남자가 다른 사람 집에 가서 옷을 다려 주는 건
그래서 사람들이 좀 이상하게 보기도 했어요.
하지만 전 가만히 팔짱 끼고 앉아서
우울증이 있다고 알려 주시는 것 같았어요.
운동을 하고 몸에 좋은 음식을 먹는 게
일기장에 내게 나타나는 다양한 우울증 증상들을 써 봤죠.
그리고 각 증상에 맞는 성구들과 기사들을 적어 놨어요.
또 출판물에 들어 있는 삽화와 그림들을 보는 것도 많은 도움이 됐죠.
제가 제발 충성을 지킬 수 있게 도와 달라고 말씀드렸습니다.
저에게 좀 더 잘해 주기 시작했죠.
제가 그 감방에서 떠나게 됐을 때
“누가 너 건드리면, 그 놈한테 내가 꼭 찾아간다고 전해라.”
수감자들이 제 물건을 들고 우르르 나와서
그걸 본 교도관은 조용히 문을 닫았습니다.
“보통은 저 감방에서 사람들한테 두드려 맞다가 쫓겨 나와.
밖에 던져 버리는 경우가 더 많지.”
그는 보고도 믿을 수 없었던 거죠.
집회 갈 준비를 하고 옷을 입을 땐 괜찮았어요.
주체할 수 없이 두렵고 슬픈 감정이 밀려와서
전 어쩔 줄 몰라서 울기 시작했어요.
제가 정말 나쁜 선택을 하게 될 것 같았죠.
사실 장로들한테 우울증 얘기를 한 적은 없었거든요.
그런데 저를 찾아오신 장로 형제 중에 한 분도
병원에서 치료를 받아보는 게 어떠냐고 제안했죠.
사실 전 예전부터 병원은 정말 가고 싶지 않았어요.
하지만 다른 사람의 도움이 필요할 때가 있어요.
우울증을 숨겨야 하는 나쁜 병이라고 말하고,
치료를 받는 것을 아주 부끄러운 일이라고 생각하죠.
의사의 도움을 받아야 된다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
모두가 치료를 받아야 되는 건 아니지만
제가 다시 감옥에 갇힐 수 있다는 걸 알고 있었죠.
그래서 그때까지 시간을 최대한 잘 사용하기로 했습니다.
“당신의 법을 사랑하는 이들에게는 풍부한 평화가 있습니다.”
암이 다 나았다는 말을 들었을 때
“와, 드디어 이제 나도 친구들이 하는거 뭐든지 다 할 수 있어.
그래서 지금은 사실 할 수 있는 게
그럴 땐 그런 감정을 억누르려고 하지 마세요.
전 늘 건강 문제를 안고 살아가고 있지만,
제 상황에만 몰두하지 않는 법을 배웠어요.
그들이 겪고 있는 문제들을 생각하려고 해요.
다른 사람과 그들이 겪는 어려움에 대해 초점을 맞추면
앤트워넷, 우리가 만나서 대화할 수 있다는 말을 들었을 때
형제를 만나 대화할 수 있다고 해서
교도소에 있을 때 정말 힘드셨을 것 같아요.
감옥에 있을 때 형제들이랑 이런 말을 했어요.
“‘상황이 지금보다 나빠지기야 하겠어?’ 하고 묻는 사람은 곧 그 답을 알게 된다.”
분명히 곧 나쁜 일이 생긴다는 거죠.
유죄 판결을 받았을 때 우린 이랬죠.
몇 시간 동안 모욕적인 대우를 받았어요.
‘이게 다 무슨 소용이야. 아무도 살리지 못하고,
아무도 도울 수 없잖아’ 하는 생각이 들었죠.
상황이 안 좋다고 느꼈던 적이 있습니까?
시련을 만날 때마다 그러한 시련을 여호와를 의지할 기회로 여깁니다.
이제 이 동영상의 마지막 부분을 보면서
여호와께서 어떻게 이 형제 자매들에게 힘을 주셨는지.
그리고 그분과의 우정을 강하게 해 주셨는지 유의해 보십시오.
여호와께서 여러분이 시련을 인내하도록 어떻게 도우셨는지 떠올려 보십시오.
그리고 그분이 앞으로도 계속 그렇게 하실 것이라는
인내할 수 있게 평화를 달라고 간청했죠.
꼭 다시 만나게 해 달라고 기도했습니다.
결국 안전한 곳으로 올 수 있었습니다.
순종했기 때문에 그분이 절 구해 주신 거예요.
전 사람들에게 짐이 되고 싶지 않았어요.
저의 집과 다른 집들을 다 고쳐 주었지요.
이 모든 형제 자매들이 나를 도와주러 온 거예요.
그 모습을 보고 있으면 이런 생각이 들어요.
우울증으로 힘들어하는 형제 자매들을 도울 때면
여호와께서 저를 사용하고 계시다는 느낌을 받아요.
또 여호와께서 만드신 작은 창조물들을 보면서도
저는 제가 추방될 거라는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
아내는 누군가 자기한테 달려오는 걸 보고
저는 세상에서 가장 사랑하는 아내를 꼭 끌어안았습니다.
자매가 우리와 러시아 형제 자매들을 위해
신세계에 가면 뭘 할지 상상하곤 해요.
한 번도 못 먹어본 음식도 먹어 보고
질병, 위험, 박해, 경제 문제가 없는 상태가 아니예요.
그분의 말씀과 약속들을 묵상할 때 얻을 수 있는 거죠.
이 모든 일을 통해 제가 배운 건
평화가 내가 처한 환경에 달려 있는 게 아니라는 거예요.
여호와를 섬기는 일에 계속 초점을 맞추었고,
그리스도인 특성을 나타내야 한다는 걸 알고 있었죠.
자신이 아니라 다른 사람을 돕는 일에
자신이 할 수 있는 일에 초점을 맞추십시오.
시련 그 자체보다 더 나쁜 영향을 줄 수 있습니다.
여호와 하느님과 아주 가까운 관계를 유지하고 있습니다.
인터뷰에 응해 주신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.
또한 이 코로나19 팬데믹 기간 중에
여러분은 욥의 인내에 관해 들었으며, 여호와께서 주신 결과를 보았습니다.
여호와는 애정이 매우 부드럽고 자비로운 분이십니다.”
우리가 시련을 인내하면서, 여호와께 받는 축복들은
우리를 강하게 해서 미래에 대비시켜 주고,
우리가 여호와께서 바라시는 사람이 되도록 도와줄 수 있습니다.
우리가 누리고 있는 마음의 평화와 기쁨은 여호와께서 주시는 선물입니다.
동영상에 나온 세계 각지의 형제 자매들을 통해 배운 것처럼,
하늘에 계신 훌륭한 우리 아버지 여호와께서
자신을 사랑하는 사람 모두를 축복해 주실 것임을 온전히 확신해야겠습니다.

en.text: As long as we live in Satan’s world,
all of us will face situations
that can rob us of our peace.
Regaining that peace can be difficult
but not impossible.
In this video, we will hear
from three sisters and two couples
who will speak candidly about their trials
and how they struggled to cope with them.
But in spite of what they have endured,
please take note of their smiles, their joy,
and what they did to regain and maintain their peace.
And take special note of how Jehovah helped them.
The Governing Body knows that many of you
are suffering circumstances
not unlike the ones we will hear about,
and they trust that the examples in this video
will help each of you to maintain your peace
as you endure various trials.
Brothers and sisters all over the world are facing
natural disasters,
economic collapse,
illness,
and persecution.
Despite all that,
they keep joy and peace.
I can learn a lot from them.
My name is Antoinette.
I live here in Las Vegas, Nevada,
with my supermom
and my troublemaking sister.
Family and friends have always been important to me.
As a child, I lived with my mom and dad
and I was very close to my dad’s side of the family.
It was very loving, unified, and fun.
I was pretty happy.
But I already was starting to feel the effects of my cancer.
We just didn’t know what it was really.
One day I was OK, and then the next day I started feeling bad, you know.
In my childhood,
I played an unusual game.
I would catch insects,
put them in a jar, and then bring them home.
Then, I would get books, such as the Criminal Procedural Code,
open them up, and start judging one of the bugs.
I would play the role of investigator and judge at the same time.
I was born into a family where everyone,
starting with my grandparents,
was either wearing an officer’s uniform or a judge’s robe.
That’s why I had this strong sense of justice.
But in 1989,
my mother was in a tragic car accident,
and
she got severe burns
on her face, hands, and body.
And then my father,
at seeing my mom’s condition,
decided to leave us.
Yeah.
And it was at that moment, I guess,
that my world, my ideals,
they crumbled.
As a little kid, I always wanted, like, one big happy family.
Once we moved to New York for my treatment,
I no longer had that big family bond anymore.
What I was feeling back then in New York was
just sadness,
never really peace.
Here in California,
we’re used to fires.
But when I got the call to evacuate that morning,
I never knew that by that evening,
the whole town of Paradise would be gone.
Just before the fire, we had the needs of the congregation
where they instructed us what to do in the case of a disaster.
I had the truck full of gas,
I had my go bag ready,
and I had a map of where I was going.
I was ready.
The brothers, also in their instructions,
said to obey the traffic instructors.
The instructor told us to turn right,
and I didn’t want to turn right,
but they said obey them.
So I turned right,
though I thought it would be really bad.
The smoke got darker and darker,
and finally it got black.
You couldn’t see anything.
My mom has always told me
that I’ve always been
a caregiver ever since I was a little girl;
it was just part of who I was.
I don’t like to see people suffer; it’s very difficult for me.
I remember that when I first started working as a nurse,
I would always cry.
I cried— Literally I cried
every day that I had to go to work.
Not only was I overwhelmed being a new nurse
but also
I was battling my depression.
I was the treasurer
for a prestigious bank in Nicaragua,
and I was the father of a one-year-old son.
We were very happy.
But then I lost my job.
So I said, ‘I have the experience,
and Jehovah will help me find another job, something similar.’
And I kept looking for jobs, but doors kept closing.
I felt very tense;
it made me feel very useless,
like
I couldn’t even provide for my family.
It was something very difficult for me.
These dear brothers and sisters
faced serious challenges.
They may have had moments when they felt like Job
when he said: “I loathe my life.”
That is not an unusual human emotion.
Sometimes things in life
don’t work out as we had hoped,
and it can hurt us deeply.
Does this mean that we are helpless victims of our circumstances?
Not at all!
Please pay close attention
and take note of why we can say
that Margaret, Feliks,
Miguel, Nikki, and Antoinette
are not helpless victims.
To the contrary,
they are conquerors.
As you watch and listen,
look for specific actions they took
to maintain their peace
and please give thoughtful attention
to ways that you can imitate their faith.
Growing up, I wondered,
‘Why does the Supreme Judge, God,
allow injustice and suffering?’
And inside of me, I had this need to restore justice.
It was such a burning desire within me.
And with that in mind,
I moved to Russia to stay with my sister.
She started to study the Bible
and was overflowing with the truth.
We talked for hours till late into the night.
So that’s when my special relationship with Jehovah began.
That’s when I got a taste of what it’s like
to have a caring Father.
It had been a while since I was able to feel that.
My baptism date was very exciting.
The spiritual family I inherited was very vast.
You can instantly feel the love.
I got baptized, and it seemed like miracles happened
one after the other.
We had a great life.
And then
the persecution started with Brother Christensen,
and then there was a ripple effect of arrests, one after the other.
Then it was our turn.
In June of 2018,
a huge group of armed men came to us, to our home.
They represented the ideals of my childhood.
But now these people,
this judicial system,
became the source of injustice to me.
I was sitting in a cage, the same way my bugs used to be in a jar.
I guess I felt like they did.
In your head at that moment when you hear the verdict
that you’ll stay in prison,
it’s like you’ve been knocked unconscious.
You’ve been hit in the head with something,
and there’s just a ringing sound in your ears.
And so I was taken away in handcuffs.
Of course, I wasn’t in the best mood.
But then
the doors of the elevator opened up, and in front of us,
a lot of brothers and sisters
were clapping their hands as hard as they could.
And some were crying,
but not crying because they felt sorry for me.
They cried because they loved us
and because they were proud of us.
That’s what always happens.
When you’re just about to lose all your strength,
Jehovah does that something for you that gives you a second wind.
And so, the applause, the love,
the tears,
the shouts, “Hang in there; everything will be OK!”
—they gave me a second wind.
And with renewed strength, I could run the next part of the race.
One of the guards was so surprised that he said,
“Now that’s some support you’ve got!”
Yeah.
Without friends, I would be very lonely.
I would constantly be focusing on my illness.
The day I met Marissa was at a convention.
She’s a really great friend, a spiritual friend.
When she’d take me to my hospital appointments,
we would eat out.
I think food is just the common language between everyone, you know.
When you talk about food, you know, it’s like:
“Ah! Yes, we have something to talk about,” you know.
I would be excited when she would take me to my hospital appointment.
She always makes me laugh, you know.
She always helps me have a good time no matter what.
Again, friends really help encourage me.
Proverbs 17:17 says:
“A true friend shows love at all times
and is a brother who is born for times of distress.”
And I have seen this come true in my life.
When I lost my job at the bank,
well, I felt very depressed, troubled, tense.
And I have a good friend who I can talk to,
and when I told him how I was feeling, he told me:
“Look, Miguel, don’t look for the same
“line of work.
“Maybe what you need to do is make a change in your life.
“Why don’t you find some simple work outside of an office for a time?
“That can help you to keep your eye simple
and allow you to provide for your family.”
I watched my wife make bread for our family,
and one day I told her:
“I’m going to make that bread, but not for our family.
I’m going to make it to sell.”
So she told me, “No, are you crazy?”
It was a big change—right?—
from having a position at a bank
and handling a lot of money
to selling on the street.
So I told her, “Look, I’m going to put this hat on,”
and I put like a chef’s hat on.
And I told her,
“I’ll be back in less than an hour, whether I sell or not.”
And that’s what happened.
And to her surprise, I came back without any bread.
So when I got ready to leave the second time to sell,
she said: “OK. Go, but leave the hat here.”
I also started to iron clothes for people in their homes,
and it looked strange because normally where we live
that type of work is done by a woman.
But for a man to go and iron clothes at someone’s home,
you don’t see that.
But I didn’t want to just sit back with my arms crossed
and see what would happen.
No!
I had to put my hands to work to earn a living for my family.
So I would preach one day, and the next day I would iron clothes.
The next day I would preach, and the day after that I would go out and sell bread.
So my mind was always occupied on doing something,
either for the Kingdom or my family.
And that helped me a lot.
I was feeling so sad.
I really needed Jehovah’s help to figure out what was going on with me.
And I remember
that the 2009 article about depression came out.
And I realized: ‘OK, Jehovah, you’re telling me this is what I have.
‘So now that I realize I have this,
I’ve got to figure out how I can manage it.’
So I changed my eating habits.
I started exercising a lot more.
I realized that exercising and eating healthy
really, really did help.
Also, I made a journal,
and I made different sections
of the different aspects of my depression that I dealt with.
In each section, I would put scriptures;
I would put articles.
And the illustrations, the pictures,
they speak a lot without saying anything.
Jehovah hears us.
Jehovah cares.
After some time in prison,
they transferred me to a different cell.
In it were inmates who followed the orders
of the investigators.
They did everything they could to other inmates
to make life unbearable.
Why did they do this?
To break a person
so that they would start to collaborate with the investigators,
confess to everything, and then be able to get transferred to another area.
Psalm 37:3: “Trust in Jehovah and do what is good.”
I said: “Jehovah, please help me to stay loyal to you.
Please help me.”
My prayers were really simple
—actually like two words: “Jehovah, help!
Jehovah, help! Jehovah, help!”
Despite how they treated me,
when I dealt with others, I tried to treat them with kindness.
These people,
they made life
uncomfortable, unbearable,
but when they were treated kindly,
they started to soften.
They began to treat me differently.
When I was being transferred
out of that cell,
the inmate who ran the area called me over to him and said,
“Come sit beside me.”
And I sat down.
Then he said, “If anybody in this prison touches you,
tell him that I’ll come looking for him.”
Then he said, “Get his things”
(he told the other prisoners).
The cell doors opened
and the guards saw
a crowd of inmates
grabbing my things and putting them out into the hallway.
I left the cell without having to carry a thing!
The guard quietly closed the door.
And before the inmates returned to their cells,
they even said goodbye, hugged me, and said: “Hang in there!
You’re going to be OK.”
They went into the cell, and the guard closed the door and asked me,
“Boy, how long have you been in there?”
I said, “Three weeks.”
He said: “Well, normally people leave this cell beaten up,
“and they’re thrown out by the other inmates.
“They have to carry their own things, and that’s if the other inmates
haven’t thrown their stuff out the door.”
He couldn’t believe what had just happened.
That’s Jehovah.
Exercising, changing my diet,
the publications, journaling —that was my lifeline.
That really actually helped me for a long time.
But it came to a point where it stopped working as effectively.
I remember getting ready, dressing for the meeting,
and I was fine.
I was getting dressed for the meeting and about to walk out the door,
but I couldn’t.
There was this overwhelming fear that came over me
and an overwhelming sadness that came over me.
And I just lost it; I just started crying.
I couldn’t get myself together.
It was bad.
It got really bad; my depression got really bad.
So it was very difficult for me
to approach the brothers to ask them for help.
But at that time, I knew that if I didn’t,
that
something bad would happen.
So I decided: ‘You know what?
I’m going to ask for a shepherding call with my brothers,’
because I’d never talked about my depression with the elders at all.
This was my first time speaking with them.
And there was one brother, one of the elders,
who also battled depression.
And he suggested,
“Have you thought about seeking medical help?”
Seeking professional help was something I never wanted to do.
I thought that I didn’t need to do it,
but sometimes there comes a point where
you need additional help
and what you’re doing is not enough.
In this world, they make you feel that it’s a bad thing,
that depression is a dirty word,
or that seeking medical help is something that you don’t do.
But I realized also
that seeking medical help
was part of my being able to worship Jehovah effectively.
That’s me doing my part.
Not everyone needs to take that step, but for me, this is what I need to do.
And I’m glad I did it because of the fact
that I’ve never ever felt this good
in my life.
About a year later,
we were released.
But my wife and I understood
that they could put me back in prison again,
so
we needed to use the time until then to the full
in the best way possible.
So, what did we do?
“Abundant peace belongs to those who love your law.”
We had family worship,
read the Bible, and prayed together.
That’s how I spent my four months of freedom.
Then I was put into prison
for three years.
When they told me about my cancer being gone,
I was really happy; I was ecstatic.
I was like: ‘Finally I’m going to get to do normal things
‘that a kid my age should be able to do.
I don’t need to be afraid or anxious anymore.’
Unfortunately, I did relapse again,
and basically right now my present condition is
there’s nothing really more to do.
They’re just waiting to let nature take its course basically,
and that’s it.
In harmony with Ephesians 4:26,
I had to let myself process the news
and let myself be sad and be angry.
Let yourself feel those feelings;
do not try to repress them.
But you can control your thoughts and your actions.
Pretty much my whole life has revolved around my illness,
but I’ve learned how to shift focus.
I just don’t focus on myself all the time.
I focus on others and their trials,
which are different but just as hard.
You read the stories on jw.org in the Newsroom.
The Russian brothers and sisters,
I pray for them constantly because
they are going through a very tough time.
“There is [definitely] more happiness in giving than receiving.”
And in our situation, this proved true.
I would say
this really helps to relieve your pain.
If you focus on yourself, your pain gets worse.
When you focus on others and on their problems,
your pain lessens, diminishes.
Hello!
Hello!
Antoinette, I was so—
When I was told that we would talk with each other,
this was something very special for me.
Same for me too.
When the brothers told me as well
about meeting you, I was really excited.
Thank you for your prayers in behalf of the brothers in Russia.
They are precious.
We can learn so much from you.
Thank you.
It’s really nice of you to say that.
We’ve both been through very many hardships.
I’m sure prison was super hard.
You know, in prison, us brothers had a saying,
“If you ask: ‘How much worse can it get?’
you won’t have to wait long to find out.”
Or in other words, when you think, ‘How much worse can it get?’
for sure something worse is bound to happen.
And when we received our sentence, we thought:
‘Well, that’s it. That’s the worst that could happen.’
And then, of course, it got worse.
Upon arrival at the prison,
we were beaten up
and for hours we were humiliated.
We thought, ‘How much worse can it get?’
Then the next day, we were told,
“You are going to the punishment cell.”
We thought,
‘Well, how much worse can it get?’
At first, it started with one floor,
then it went to another floor, and then the whole entire hospital.
Every floor had COVID patients.
That was some of the hardest nursing that I’ve ever done in my life
in all of my years of nursing.
And we lost a lot of good nurses
who were right in the trenches with me who were in there doing their best.
We lost a lot of good people.
Even though I was on medication to help me,
it still didn’t take the depression away.
You’re like: ‘What’s the point?
‘I can’t save anyone.
I can’t, I can’t help anyone.’
It was devastating. It truly, truly was devastating.
Have you ever felt as Feliks did when he asked,
“How much worse can it get?”
Nevertheless, a spiritual person
can see each new challenge
as an opportunity to rely on Jehovah.
As we watch the concluding part of this video,
please take note of how Jehovah strengthened
these brothers and sisters
and deepened their friendship with him.
Think about your own circumstances
and the ways that Jehovah has helped you through trials,
and have full confidence
that he will continue to do so.
And then I decided that I was going to stop asking,
“How much worse could it get?”
I asked Jehovah for endurance
and joy for that day—just for that day.
And at those times, I just
cry to Jehovah,
talk to Jehovah about how I’m feeling,
and just ask for his peace to help me to deal.
I’ve talked to Jehovah very intimately and personally
but never like I have when I was so alone there.
I realized that I was going to die.
I asked Jehovah if he saw enough good in me,
that he would just resurrect me
and that I’d love to be in his new world
and see my husband again and my children.
And I thanked him so much for the life that I had.
And I felt such a peace
like I’d never felt before.
And then
I just knew it was Jehovah getting me out.
The obedience, just doing what we were told,
it came from Jehovah, and it was so simple.
That gave him something to bless, and it may have saved my life.
I just never wanted to be a burden on people,
but
the brothers and sisters had come from all over the country
to do work for this house and the other houses—all of them.
They made me feel wanted,
and they made me feel loved.
To feel like Jehovah cared enough to give attention to me,
I
just felt so unworthy.
And here all these people
are here taking care of me.
And you just look at them, and then you think:
‘I’m part of this organization. I’ve got to do better.
I’ve got to be like them and make other people happy.’
When I’m able to help people who are battling depression,
I feel like Jehovah is using me in that way,
and it makes me happy that I can be of use to Jehovah.
It’s good to feel— It’s so nice to feel good again,
to feel happy again, to be able to smile,
to be able to take in enjoyment
of the small things, you know, in Jehovah’s creation
—and, you know, just be happy that I’m alive.
So
yeah, yeah.
Now I have a stable job.
I work at a hardware store.
And I feel at peace.
The adversities have made me stronger,
and overall, I have a much closer relationship with Jehovah.
But I’m still making bread.
And at home, yeah, I’m the one who irons the clothes.
After a while, I found out that I was being deported.
I remember getting off the train.
They took me through the back door,
but my wife, Zhenya, was standing at the main entrance.
She was on the phone. She couldn’t see me.
She was looking at the main entrance.
And I threw my bag down as I ran to her.
She could see from the corner of her eyes someone was running.
She was a little confused, even scared.
And there I was
hugging the person I loved the most.
It was one of the most beautiful days of my life.
Hi.
Privet.
Hello.
When I heard that you were praying for us
and for the brothers and sisters in Russia,
it really encouraged me and Feliks.
It’s such an example for me personally.
We mentioned it in our prayer yesterday;
Feliks was saying
that you are a great example of how we need
to genuinely care for our brothers and sisters.
We love you very much.
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
It was nice meeting you.
Goodbye.
My cancer is uncurable,
but I know the cure is in the new system.
So that’s the cure!
I like to imagine, ‘When that time happens, what will I be doing?’
Obviously, I’m going to be jumping for joy
because I’m going to be rid of my cancer.
I’m going to enjoy food that we never really got to enjoy,
and I’m going to have so many animals.
I’m going to make a house. I’m going to learn how to make a house.
Peace in this world is not the absence
of illness,
danger,
persecution,
or economic problems.
Peace in this world is listening to Jehovah’s guidance,
praying to Jehovah constantly,
meditating on Jehovah’s Word and his promises.
Peace in this world is also
having good friends by our side
and having a good sense of humor.
What I’ve learned from all of this
is peace isn’t from what’s outside,
from what’s going on, or from what you’re experiencing.
I’ve learned that peace is on the inside,
and that comes from Jehovah.
These examples we’ve just seen
are of ordinary people
“with feelings like ours.”
Yet, they felt peace
even when confronting serious trials.
How did they do it?
When Miguel lost his job,
he kept his focus on serving Jehovah
and he was not too proud to do humble work
to provide for his family.
Margaret was prepared for a natural disaster,
and throughout her ordeal,
she prayed to Jehovah.
While struggling with depression,
Nikki did research using our publications
and asked for help from the elders.
Even when facing brutal persecution,
Feliks showed kindness to his persecutors.
He knew that the way he responded
would reflect Christian qualities.
And dear Antoinette,
despite her diagnosis,
focuses not on herself
but on helping others.
As she said, the cure for her
—as it is for all of us—
is God’s Kingdom.
If you are experiencing trials,
focus on what you can control,
help others,
be grateful,
and rely on Jehovah and his organization.
If you are not experiencing serious trials,
do what you can to prepare for them
by building yourself up spiritually.
Do not be anxious.
Fear of what might happen
is often worse than the trial itself.
Trust in Jehovah, and be assured
that he will never abandon his friends.
The dear brothers and sisters whom we’ve just listened to
are doing well spiritually.
We thank them for participating in these interviews.
We’d also like to thank all our brothers and sisters
working in the medical field
who have gone the extra mile during this pandemic.
James 5:11 reads:
“We consider happy those who have endured.
“You have heard of the endurance of Job
“and have seen the outcome Jehovah gave,
that Jehovah is very tender in affection and merciful.”
The blessings we receive by enduring trials
can strengthen us for the future
and help us to become the kind of person
that Jehovah wants us to be.
The inner peace and joy we experience
is a gift from Jehovah.
As these brothers and sisters from around the world
have reminded us,
we need never doubt
that our wonderful heavenly Father will bless
all those who continue loving him.

en.text: I prayed to Jehovah,
“If it is your will, I would be happy
to enter pioneer service.”
But I had to work really hard to provide for the needs of my family
because my father had died when he was 45 years old.
The elder that I talked to
gave me advice not to be picky about what kind of job I could get.
He reminded me of Matthew 6:33, and told me
not to be overly anxious.
Because of our good communication within the family,
we were able to find solutions.
My other siblings realized that they also shared
responsibility in providing for the needs of the family.
After one year of pioneering, I was encouraged to apply for Bethel service,
and now I am in Bethel.
I feel that Jehovah really cares for me, loves me,
and appreciates all my efforts.
Because they love me, my cousins pressured me to choose a secular career.
If I went against
their wishes, it would hurt them
and put a strain on our relationship.
I was really anxious.
I wanted to show my trust in Jehovah by pioneering
and give him an opportunity to show me that I can be happy in his service.
I tried to express my appreciation for my cousins by what
I said and did
and showed them love.
They’ve realized that I have changed for the better.
I show more concern for others now.
Now they understand that we have been learning good things and that we have
a happier and more meaningful life.
I wanted to try serving
where the need was great.
When I first arrived,
I thought it was so cool being there.
I had expected the poverty, but when I saw it,
it hit home more than what I had expected.
So then I started to feel really homesick.
But my brothers and sisters—
I’d go to the Kingdom Hall and they were able to cope with the challenges
that they were facing because they had Jehovah in their life.
So their example really helped me to see that my circumstances
don’t need to change for my attitude to change.
Proverbs 15:15 stood out to me,
which is about having “a cheerful heart”
and being able to have “a continual feast” no matter what my circumstances are.
And I found an article about that scripture.
And so from there, I decided to ask myself, ‘How can I use my situation
and what I’m learning to help others?’
And I got to start helping with a foreign-language group there.
That whole experience
just made my love for people grow so much
and definitely changed my life.

cn.text: 我向耶和华祷告说
“如果这是你的旨意
我就开始做先驱”
但我身上的担子很重
要非常努力工作养家
因为我爸爸在他45岁的时候去世了
一个长老告诉我
对于要做什么工作
不要太过挑剔
他用马太福音6:33的经文提醒我
不要过度忧虑
我跟家人好好地沟通以后
我们找到了解决问题的办法
我的弟弟妹妹也意识到
他们也要分担养家的责任
做先驱一年之后
弟兄们鼓励我申请伯特利服务
所以现在我在伯特利工作
耶和华真的很照顾我
他很爱我
也很欣赏我为他做的一切
出于对我的关心
我的几个亲戚给我压力
要我找份好的工作
如果我没有照着他们的期待去做
他们会很受伤
我们之间的关系也会变得紧张
这给我很大的压力
我想做先驱
表明我信赖耶和华
并且证明为耶和华服务是很开心的事情
我努力让我的亲戚知道我很重视他们
也用行动表明我对他们的爱和关心
他们现在看出我成为了一个更好的人
我比以前更关心别人了
他们也明白圣经的教导真的对人有益
可以让我们的生活过得快乐也充满意义
我想去更需要的地区服务
刚到那里的时候
我觉得这地方太棒了
我去之前就知道那里的经济条件很差
但我到了那里，才发现比我想的更糟
所以我非常想家
但我去王国聚会所的时候
看到弟兄姐妹靠着耶和华
应对生活中遇到的各种挑战
他们的榜样让我看出
需要改变的不是我的环境
而是我的想法和态度
箴言15:15说得很有道理
只要我们“心境愉快”
不论面对什么样的环境
我们都可以好像“常享宴席”
我找到了一篇跟这节经文有关的文章
看完后我问问自己
我可以怎样善用我的情况
和我学到的东西去帮助别人？
我开始在当地的其他语言小组服务
这次的经历让我学会更爱别人
也改变了我的生活

titles.ko: 청소년 여러분, 평화를 가져다주는 목표를 추구하십시오!
titles.en: Young People—Choose a Path That Leads to Peace!
titles.cn: 年轻人——要追求快乐安宁的生活！

title: 가짜 평화에 속지 마십시오!—테아 판 레이우언

ko.text: 이게 예수님의 복음과 어떻게 부합한단 말입니까?
하지만 목사는 한마디 답도 하지 못했어요.
그래서 전 정치에서 답을 찾으려고 했죠.
당시에 평화 운동 단체들이 많이 생겼고
내가 바라는 건 사람들을 추앙하는 게 아니라
하루는 커피 한 잔 하려고 친구 집에 갔는데
성경에 대해 알려 주러 왔다고 했어요.
그 후 정말 친절한 여자 분이
이 조직이야말로 평화를 진정으로 갈망하는 조직이야’ 하고 생각했어요.
그랬더니 다들 저를 미친 사람 보듯 쳐다보았죠.
전 새로운 인생을 살게 되어 정말 기뻤어요.
이사야 14:7의 말씀은 제 인생에 큰 영향을 주었습니다.
하느님께서 평온하고 평화로운 세상을 가져오겠다고 약속하시기 때문입니다.

en.text: My father always taught me that we needed God in our life
in order for there to be peace.
And he always wanted to know,
Can Christians go to war?
How is this consistent with the Gospel of Jesus Christ?
But the pastor could never give us an answer,
and so I thought I’d have to look to politics to find it.
A lot of peace movements were being formed at that time,
so I joined one of them.
We decided where the protest marches would be
and which pamphlets we would use.
But after the protests were over,
everyone was so excited
and they all started applauding
and cheering for the leaders.
I thought: ‘That’s not what I wanted.
‘I don’t want to honor people.
‘I want to have world peace.
And that still hasn’t happened yet.’
Then I started to feel very alone,
and it made me feel unsafe in this world.
With no peace in sight,
I thought, ‘What is the purpose of life?’
While visiting friends for coffee, I saw a man I’d never met before.
My friends told me he wanted to talk to us about the Bible.
So I asked him:
“Sir, what do you think?
Can Christians join the military?”
And the man said, “No, that’s not allowed
because the Bible says you should ‘love your [enemy].’”
It made me think about what my father always said
—that we need God to bring peace.
Then a really nice lady came to my door,
and she had an orange book in her hand.
And it said: True Peace and Security.
After reading it, I thought:
‘This is it!
This is the organization that truly wants peace.’
So I went to those involved in the peace movement.
I told them that I believe that God will change this world
into a beautiful earth where there’ll be true peace.
They all looked at me like I had lost my mind.
I was so happy with my new life.
I felt like I was part of a family
who truly cared about one another
and really wanted peace with each other.
Isaiah 14:7 had a major impact on my life
because there God promises
a calm and peaceful world.

cn.text: 我爸爸常说
我们要有世界和平就必须依靠上帝才行
他一直很想知道
基督徒能不能参与战争
参与战争真的符合耶稣基督的教导吗？
牧师并不能给我们合理解释
所以我觉得只有通过政治途径来追求和平
当时有很多和平运动
我就加入了其中一个
我们会策划要在哪里游行
还有要分发什么册子
但是抗议游行结束之后
大家都很兴奋，情绪高涨
为那些带头的人鼓掌欢呼
我想，这并不是我想要的
我不想要推崇人
我只想要和平安宁
但它并没有实现
我开始感到非常无助
得不到安全感
我觉得和平安宁是不可能实现的
于是我想
“活着到底是为了什么？”
我去朋友家的时候
看到了一个我从没有见过的人
朋友说，这个人想跟我们谈谈圣经
我就问他
“基督徒能加入军队吗？
你觉得怎么样？”
他回答说
“不行，因为圣经说，要爱你的敌人。”
这让我想到我爸爸说的
只有上帝才能带来和平
后来有一位友善的女士来找我
她手里拿着一本橘色的书
书上写着“真正的和平安全”
读完后，我就想
这是我要找的！
这个组织是真正在追求和平的组织
我就去找那些以前跟我一起游行抗议的朋友
我跟他们说
上帝会把这个世界变得非常美好
他会让这个地球充满和平和安宁
他们都惊讶地看着我
觉得我疯了
现在我过得非常快乐
我很高兴我属于一个温暖的大家庭
大家都彼此关心，追求和睦
以赛亚书14:7的经文
对我的人生有很大的影响
因为上帝保证
大地会安宁太平

titles.ko: 가짜 평화에 속지 마십시오!—테아 판 레이우언
