title: 게리트 뢰시: “평화​를 찾아 그것​을 추구​하십시오”—말​이라는 선물​을 지혜​롭게 사용​함​으로

ko.text: 어떤 강력한 힘이 우리가 그렇게 하지 못하게 막기 때문인데,
말은 강력한 힘이 있어서 큰 유익을 줄 수 있지만
우리의 불완전성 때문에 큰 해를 입힐 수도 있습니다.
이러한 내용이 성경 잠언에 잘 묘사돼 있습니다.
“생각 없이 하는 말은 칼로 찌르는 것과 같지만, 지혜로운 자의 혀는 아픔을 낫게 한다.”
“죽고 사는 것이 혀의 권세에 있으니, 혀를 사용하기 좋아하는 자는 그 열매를 먹는다.”
깊은 상처를 받은 적이 있을 것입니다.
사려 깊은 말을 하면 아픈 마음을 달래 주고 관계를 회복할 수 있습니다.
우리 모두는 불완전하기 때문에 혀를 제어하는 데 어려움이 있습니다.
배가 아무리 크고 또 거센 바람에 밀려가도,
아주 작은 불이 얼마나 큰 숲을
“그러나 혀를 길들일 수 있는 사람은 아무도 없습니다.
우리의 가정 환경도 큰 영향을 줄 수 있습니다.
가정 환경 역시 혀를 오용하게 만드는
어떤 사람들은 쉽게 합의하지 않고 자제하지 않고
우리 각자는 “평화를 찾아 그것을 추구”할 수 있습니다.
예수께서는 말이라는 선물을 지혜롭게 사용한 훌륭한 본이 되십니다.
그분은 말로 사람들을 격려하고 위로해 주셨습니다.
“주권자인 주 여호와의 영이 내 위에 있다.
온유한 사람에게 좋은 소식을 전하게 하셨다.
그분은 나를 보내셔서 마음이 찢긴 사람을 싸매 주고,
갇힌 사람의 눈을 활짝 열어 주게 하셨다.”
연기 나는 심지를 끄지 않을 것이다.”
이러한 성구들은 중요한 교훈을 가르쳐 줍니다.
해를 입힐 수도 있고 치유해 줄 수도 있다는 것을 아셨습니다.
우리는 예수를 더 밀접히 본받을 수 있습니까?
말을 어떻게 지혜롭게 사용할 수 있는지
아, 요즘 겨울 시즌 준비 중인데
왜 최근에 네가 올린 거 있잖아.
이것도 니가 좋은 아이디어를 줘서 그렇지 뭐.
“넌 그분의 집에 정말 귀중한 보물이 될 거야.
너도 드릴 수 있는 …” -어우, 나 목소리 왜 이러니.
근데 이 노래 잘하는 사람은 따로 있죠, 우리 회중에.
자기가 노래 엄청 잘하는 줄 알잖아요.
너무 잘난 척하는 거 같지 않으세요?
자매가 헤일리가 걱정이 돼서 정 마음에 걸리면
그런 건 얘기를 해 줘야 한다고 하셨는데 ···
파이오니아가 그러면 안 되는 거 아니에요? -별 것 아닌 줄 알았던 일이
걷잡을 수 없이 커졌죠. -헤일리, 내 말은 그게 아니야.
꼭 용서받고 싶었던 때가 있지 않았어?
혹시 저만 이렇게 생각하는 거 아니죠?
그 자매는 사람들 후대를 진짜 잘하지 않아?
그 자매가 만든 카레 먹어 봤어?
아니, 안 먹어 봤는데. -아, 그 자매 완전 프로야, 프로.
또한 누군가가 우리에게 화를 낼 때
온화하게 대답하면 화를 누그러뜨릴 수 있습니다.
“온화한 대답은 격노를 가라앉히지만, 거친 말은 분노가 치밀게 합니다.”
계속 서로 격려하고 서로 세워 주십시오. …
때때로 우울한 감정을 느낄 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 그들을 소중히 여기신다는 것을 깨닫도록
구체적이고 진심 어린 칭찬을 해 주십시오.
“마음이 찢긴 자들”과 “영이 꺾인 자들”을 위한 여호와의 진실한 관심과 사랑을 보여 주는
그들의 슬픈 마음을 위로할 수 있습니다.
그들이 가치 있고 소중한 존재라는 점을
아픈 사람에게 큰 힘을 줄 수 있습니다.
형제 자매들의 문제를 해결해 줄 수는 없을지 몰라도
우리가 그들을 사랑하고 아낀다는 점을 알려 줄 수 있습니다.
그들과 함께 시간을 보낼 기회를 만들 수 있습니다.
또한 성경 말씀으로 그들을 강하게 해 줄 수도 있습니다.
회중의 형제 자매들이 그들을 사랑한다는 것을
우리의 말에 담긴 진심과 확신을 그들이 느끼게 해 주십시오.
많은 점을 생각해 볼 수 있었습니다.
평화를 추구하는 게 늘 쉽지만은 않다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
평화를 추구하려면 노력을 기울여야 한다는 점도 알게 되었죠.
우리는 앞으로 “평화를 찾아 그것을 추구”하기 위해
우리 모두 계속 평화를 추구하기 위해
여러분의 노력을 풍성히 축복해 주시기를 바랍니다!

en.text: Why is it challenging to use our gift of speech wisely?
Because something powerful constantly works against us.
What is it?
Imperfection.
The tongue is powerful.
It can do much good, but because of imperfection,
it can also cause much harm.
This thought is well expressed in the Bible book of Proverbs.
For example, Proverbs 12:18 says:
“Thoughtless speech is like the stabs of a sword,
but the tongue of the wise is a healing.”
And Proverbs 18:21 states:
“Death and life are in the power of the tongue;
those who love to use it will eat its fruitage.”
Words have power,
so we need to be careful about what we say
and how we say it.
Perhaps you can recall when someone spoke unkindly to you
and hurt you deeply.
On the other hand, thoughtful speech
can mend an aching heart and heal friendships.
Because of imperfection, we all have difficulty
controlling our tongue.
This was true even of the first-century disciple James.
He humbly acknowledged the challenge that all humans face
in the third chapter of his inspired letter.
Notice how James described this
at James 3:3-6, 8:
“If we put bridles in the mouths of horses
“to make them obey us,
“we guide also the whole body.
“Look also at ships: Although they are so big
“and are driven by strong winds,
“they are steered by a very small rudder
“wherever the man at the helm is inclined to go.
“So, too, the tongue is a small part of the body,
“and yet it makes great brags.
“See how small a fire it takes
“to set a great forest ablaze!
“The tongue is also a fire.
“The tongue represents a world of unrighteousness
“among our body members, for it defiles
“all the body and sets the whole course of life on fire,
and it is set on fire by Gehenna.”
And verse 8: “But no human can tame the tongue.
“It is unruly and injurious,
full of deadly poison.”
In addition to inherited imperfection,
our upbringing could also be a factor.
The Watchtower  of September 15, 2006,
page 21, paragraph 6 states:
“In addition to human imperfection,
“family environment plays a role in the misuse of the tongue.
“Some people were raised in homes
“where parents were ‘not open to any agreement, . . .
without self-control, fierce.’”
Despite such challenges, it is possible for each one of us
to “seek peace and pursue it.”
Jesus set a good example
in using the gift of speech wisely.
He used his speech to encourage and comfort others.
While on earth, he applied to himself the words
found at Isaiah 61:1,
which states the following:
“The spirit of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah is upon me,
“because Jehovah anointed me to declare good news to the meek.
“He sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,
“to proclaim liberty to the captives
and the wide opening of the eyes to the prisoners.”
As recorded at Matthew 12:20, Matthew applies the words
of Isaiah 42:1-3 to Jesus.
At Matthew 12:20, he stated:
“No bruised reed will he crush,
“and no smoldering wick will he extinguish,
until he brings justice with success.”
We learn an important lesson from such verses.
Jesus recognized that the tongue has power
—power to harm and power to heal.
The Watchtower  of February 15, 2015,
page 13, and paragraph 11, thus stated
that “Jesus showed discernment
in all he said and did.”
Can we imitate Jesus more closely?
If so, what will you do the next time an opportunity arises
for you to use your gift of speech wisely?
In the following dramatization,
notice how the wise use of the tongue helps to heal.
I just need a bit of help.
What do you think I should do for my winter collection?
Well, I don’t know, but I love what you did with your new stuff,
especially
this set.
Oh, thanks.
You’ve all given me so many great ideas.
Yeah, but you make them.
Yeah.
OK, girls.
You love it.
Oh, this is my song.
Mine too.
“You have a treasured place
“in Jehovah’s house;
“He’ll help you out [out].
And you have . . .”
Oh, I sing like a crow.
No, stop!
I’ll tell you who else thinks it’s her song, but you’d better have earplugs handy
—Veronica.
Oh, my goodness! She’s in love with her own voice.
Ever sit near her at the hall?
It’s like she’s the only one that can sing.
And she’s such a diva.
My first thought: ‘Oh, no! Here we go again!
I’ve seen this movie before.’
You don’t think she’s showing off?
Is this just about Haley?
It seems it’s all about Haley.
Is there just a little bit of envy in there?
I’ve lived it.
If it’s a case of her being more careful how she comes across,
that’s another matter.
What did she suggest?
That I should tell her that she needs to stop.
Can you believe that?
Especially as a pioneer, what kind of example is she setting?
How quickly it snowballs out of control!
That’s not what I am saying at all.
You are such . . .
Wow! I can’t believe you.
Are you that lonely that you’ve got nothing better to do?
Haley!
How difficult it can be to unravel!
I’m sorry.
I shouldn’t have judged you so harshly.
I shouldn’t have judged you at all.
A chance to forgive is a chance to imitate Jehovah.
Think back to a time when you wanted forgiveness.
Has anyone ever tried talking to her about her singing?
You know what I love about Veronica?
She’s probably the most hospitable person I know.
It’s always open house at her place.
And can she cook!
Have you tried her curry?
I haven’t tried it yet.
Yeah, it’s so good.
It’s so good.
I really look forward to that.
It’s really good.
OK, I’ll ask her.
She does these curry nights.
Oh, you’re going to love it.
We should use our gift of speech
to honor God and to benefit others.
And if somebody gets angry at us,
our mild reply can diffuse the situation.
As Proverbs 15:1 says:
“A mild answer turns away rage,
but a harsh word stirs up anger.”
We can also use our gift of speech
to console and encourage others.
First Thessalonians 5:11, 14 states:
“Therefore, keep encouraging one another and building one another up,
“just as you are in fact doing. . . .
“On the other hand, we urge you, brothers,
“to warn the disorderly, speak consolingly
“to those who are depressed,
support the weak, be patient toward all.”
Yes, even faithful servants of Jehovah
may at times struggle with depression.
How can we help such ones?
Offer specific, genuine commendation
to help them see their own value in Jehovah’s eyes.
Share with them the powerful words of Bible texts
showing that Jehovah truly cares about and loves those
who “are broken at heart” and “crushed in spirit.”
We can also use the power of our tongue
to provide much needed encouragement to others.
Has a fellow believer lost a loved one in death?
Sympathetic words expressing our care and concern
can comfort a grieving heart.
Is an elderly brother or sister feeling unneeded?
A thoughtful tongue can reassure older ones
that they are valued and appreciated.
Is someone struggling with a chronic illness?
Kind words shared on the phone or in person
can do much to lift the spirits of one who is sick.
How pleased our Creator must be
when we use the power of speech to utter sayings
that are “good for building up”!
We may not be able to fix their problems,
but we can let them know that we love them
and we care about them.
For example, you can arrange to spend time with him or her.
Additionally, we can use God’s Word
to strengthen them.
Or you may notice that someone in the congregation
is discouraged or depressed.
You could read an encouraging Bible verse
and even offer to say a prayer.
Reassure such ones
that their brothers and sisters in the congregation love them.
And speak in a way that shows
that you really mean and believe what you say.
This symposium has given each one of us
much to think about, has it not?
We have been reminded that seeking peace is not always easy.
We have also learned that the pursuit of peace
requires effort.
In what specific ways are you resolved
to “seek peace and pursue it”
in the days ahead?
May we all continue to pursue peace
(1) by not quickly taking offense,
(2) by apologizing,
(3) by forgiving freely,
and (4) by using our gift of speech wisely
to encourage and comfort others.
And may Jehovah, “the God of peace,”
bless you abundantly for doing so!

cn.text: 为什么我们想要说话明智很不容易呢？

title: 레너드 마이어스: “평화​를 찾아 그것​을 추구​하십시오”—기꺼이 용서함으로

ko.text: 한 아버지와 십 대인 딸이 있었습니다.
예수께서는 그분이 누구인지 모른 채 그분의 손과 발에 못을 박았던
나중에 그분께 믿음을 나타낸 사람들을 염두에 두셨을지 모르죠.
화가 나거나 앙심을 품게 될 수 있죠.
분명, 평화롭고 용서하는 사람이 되는 것은
그에 대해 듣고 욥을 위로하러 왔습니다.
그들은 “7일 동안 밤낮으로 그와 함께 땅바닥에 앉아 있었지만 …
근거 없는 비난으로 욥에게 심한 상처를 주었기 때문입니다.
그런데 한 가지 흥미로운 기록이 있는데요.
“내 종 욥이 너희를 위해 기도할 것이다.
욥이 여호와께 “제게 그러한 말을 한 사람들을 용서하라는 건가요?”라고 말했나요?
다른 사람을 용서해서 어떤 결과가 있었죠?
‘전에 가졌던 것의 두 배를 주셨다’고 알려 줍니다.
그냥 요새 에밀리가 시도 때도 없이 연락을 해서요.
꼭 용서받고 싶었던 때가 있지 않았어?
실리아가 정말 좋은 얘기를 해 줬죠!
따라서 누군가가 우리에게 잘못을 할 때
여호와께서 욥에게 친구들을 위해 기도하라고 하신 것을 기억하실 겁니다.
그 덕분에 욥은 그들을 용서할 수 있었죠.
“누군가 다른 사람에 대해 불평할 이유가 있더라도
계속 서로 참고 서로 기꺼이 용서하십시오.
“과분한 친절”이나 “은혜”로 자주 번역되는 단어와 어근이 같습니다.
여호와께서는 우리가 그분처럼 다른 사람을 기꺼이 용서할 것을 요구하십니다.
그냥 지나쳐 주는 게 가장 좋습니다.
사랑은 “해를 입은 것을 기억해 두지 않는다”고 했죠.
‘잘못을 지나쳐 주는 게 아름다운 일’이라고 했습니다.
하지만 어떤 형제나 자매의 잘못에 대해
우선 기도로 여호와께 인도를 구해야 합니다.
그의 말에 다 동의하지 않더라도 말입니다.
그 형제의 좋은 점에 대해 이야기하고
평화를 이룰 또 다른 기회를 찾으십시오.
우리가 할 수 있는 일을 해야 합니다.
때로는 용서하기가 쉽지 않다는 것에 동의하실 것입니다.
하지만 앞서 자신의 딸을 용서하지 않은 아버지처럼 되어서는 안 됩니다.
누군가를 용서할 기회는 여호와를 본받을 기회입니다.
이제 중앙장로회 성원인 게리트 뢰시 형제가 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.
제목은 “‘평화를 찾아 그것을 추구하십시오’ —말이라는 선물을 지혜롭게 사용함으로”입니다.

en.text: It’s a simple fact that to be at peace with others,
we must be willing to forgive.
Please notice two examples:
A father and his teenage daughter didn’t get along.
Minor disagreements often developed into shouting matches.
Finally, the tension got so bad
that the daughter was asked to leave the house.
Eventually, she recognized that she was at fault
and asked for her father’s forgiveness.
But instead of overlooking her mistakes,
her father rejected her efforts.
He was unwilling to extend forgiveness to his own daughter.
Now, let’s contrast that with another example.
A blameless man was condemned to die for a crime he didn’t commit.
Shortly before he died, the innocent man stated:
“Father, forgive them,
for they do not know what they are doing.”
Those words of Jesus are recorded at Luke 23:34,
and he may have been referring to the Roman soldiers
who drove the nails into his hands and feet
and who didn’t know who he really was.
Or Jesus may have had in mind some in the crowd
who demanded his execution
but would later exercise faith in him.
The point is that Jesus was willing to forgive freely.
How do we measure up with regard to forgiveness?
Are we like Jesus, willing to forgive others freely?
Or at times, do we tend to be more like the man who was unwilling to forgive?
Granting forgiveness isn’t always easy.
Imperfection exerts a powerful influence over us,
sometimes robbing us of compassion.
When someone hurts us,
we may become resentful, or hold a grudge.
And perhaps some of us were taught not to forgive others.
Little wonder that cultivating a peaceful, forgiving spirit
can be difficult.
Still, the Bible encourages us to forgive freely.
Let’s consider another example of forgiveness in the man Job.
Now, we’re familiar with his trials:
loss of his possessions and ten children,
a loathsome disease, and his wife told him to curse God and die.
Three companions heard about Job’s calamities,
and they agreed to go comfort him.
Job 2:13 states that when they arrived,
“they sat . . . with him for seven days and seven nights,”
but they didn’t say “a word to him.”
Now, maybe that was a good thing
because when they finally opened their mouths,
they deeply hurt Job with their baseless accusations.
But notice something interesting about this account.
Please turn with me to Job chapter 42.
At the end of Job’s trials, Jehovah asked Job
to do something regarding these false accusers.
Notice Jehovah’s words there at Job 42, the B  portion of verse 8:
“And my servant Job will pray for you.
“I will surely accept his request
not to deal with you according to your foolishness.”
Did you notice that after all the false accusations,
Jehovah asked Job to pray for the men who had tormented him?
Now, would Job tell Jehovah,
“Jehovah, after what they said to me, I’m not going to forgive them”?
Would Job be resentful?
Notice the latter portion of verse 9:
“And Jehovah accepted Job’s prayer.”
Job followed Jehovah’s instructions.
What was the result of Job’s integrity and his forgiving spirit?
Verse 10:
“After Job had prayed for his companions,
“Jehovah removed Job’s tribulation and restored his prosperity.
Jehovah gave him double what he had before.”
The account goes on to say that Job had ten more children.
He lived for 140 more years,
and verse 17 states:
“Finally Job died, after a long and satisfying life.”
Job was blessed for his forgiving spirit,
and he set a good example for us to forgive freely.
In the following dramatization with Celia and Haley,
notice why Haley finally decides to forgive freely.
Hey, it’s me.
I’ve been thinking of you.
Great broadcast.
How did you like the new original song?
Give us a call.
I wish she’d give it a rest.
Sorry?
Oh, nothing.
Sorry, it’s just Emily for the millionth time.
What’s the problem, love?
There’s no problem.
It’s just . . .
. . . difficult to let her back in?
Not that simple?
Not that simple.
You want to forgive . . .
. . . but not get burned again.
Keep in mind
that a chance to forgive is a chance to imitate Jehovah.
We wouldn’t want to miss that opportunity.
I never thought about it like that.
Think back to a time when you wanted forgiveness
—when it meant everything.
How did it feel?
. . . just like your Nana does as well.
She really deeply cares about you.
You feel awful
that you’ve let everyone down.
You’re very precious.
Thank you.
Then they forgive you,
and suddenly everything is OK.
Emily, sorry I haven’t been back to you.
Have plans for tomorrow?
What good reasoning on the part of Celia!
Did you notice the expression that really touched Haley’s heart?
“A chance to forgive is a chance to imitate Jehovah.
We wouldn’t want to miss that opportunity.”
So when we’ve been wronged, we don’t want to miss the opportunity
to imitate Jehovah by forgiving freely.
Please notice how this is highlighted at Colossians 3:13.
When we considered Job’s example, remember that Jehovah
instructed him to pray for his companions.
And that helped Job display a forgiving spirit.
Well, notice here what Jehovah instructs us to do at Colossians 3:13:
“Continue putting up with one another
“and forgiving one another freely
“even if anyone has a cause for complaint against another.
“Just as Jehovah freely forgave you,
you must also do the same.”
The Greek verb used here for “freely forgive”
is related to a word often rendered
“undeserved kindness” or “favor.”
When used in the sense of forgiving,
this verb conveys the idea of doing so
freely, generously
—just as when you, out of generosity, give a gift to someone.
Jehovah requires that we freely forgive others in imitation of him.
Did you notice the end of the verse?
“You must  also do the same.”
Now, if the offense is minor, it’s best to overlook it.
First Corinthians 13:5 states
that love “does not keep account of the injury.”
And Proverbs 19:11 tells us
that “it is beauty . . . to overlook an offense.”
However, if we feel that we need to talk to our brother or sister
about an offense that was committed against us,
what’s the best way to handle that?
First, we should ask Jehovah in prayer for his guidance.
Then with the brother’s good qualities in mind,
graciously tell him that we want to make peace.
Listen carefully and empathetically.
We shouldn’t interrupt, even if we don’t agree with everything being said.
It may be that his viewpoint is wrong, but it is his viewpoint.
Then when it’s our turn to speak, we want to be gracious.
Tell the brother what we appreciate about him;
apologize for any part that we played in the misunderstanding.
If our humble efforts result in good, thank Jehovah.
If they don’t, keep asking Jehovah for guidance
while we look for another opportunity to make peace.
When we truly forgive,
we make a heartfelt decision to let go of resentment.
And what peace that can bring us!
Now, forgiving doesn’t mean that we approve of a wrong action,
consider it unimportant, or pretend it didn’t happen.
Also, if we’ve been treated unjustly and have a cause for complaint,
we do what we can to pursue peace and resolve the matter.
And then we confidently leave it in Jehovah’s hands.
Brothers and sisters, what will you take away from this consideration?
I’m sure you’ll agree that it can be a challenge at times to forgive.
But rather than be like the man we spoke of earlier
who refused to forgive his own daughter,
may we follow the examples of Jehovah, Jesus, Job, and Haley
by forgiving freely, generously.
Remember, a chance to forgive
is a chance to imitate Jehovah,
and we wouldn’t want to miss that opportunity.
May all of us pursue peace
by being willing to forgive freely.
Brother Gerrit Lösch, a member of the Governing Body,
will now present the final talk of this symposium,
“‘Seek Peace and Pursue It’ . . . By Using Our Gift of Speech Wisely.”

cn.text: 我们要跟别人有和睦的关系
就必须甘心宽恕别人
请考虑两个例子
一个爸爸跟他十几岁的女儿关系很不好
他们经常为了小事情而吵架
他们的关系越来越糟
爸爸最后把女儿赶出家门
后来，女儿看出自己做得不对
就请求爸爸原谅
可是爸爸抓着过去的事不放
不理会女儿的道歉
他不想原谅自己的亲生女儿
现在，再想另外一个例子
一个人被判处死刑
但他却没做错什么事
在临死之前，这个无辜的人说
父亲啊，求你宽恕他们
因为他们不知道自己在做什么
这是耶稣在路加福音23:34说的话
他说的人很可能就是
把他手脚钉在柱上的罗马士兵
他们不知道耶稣的身份
也可能是人群中那些极力要求处死他的人
他们有些人后来成了信徒
重点是耶稣愿意甘心宽恕他们
我们有多愿意宽恕别人呢？
我们像耶稣一样
乐意宽恕别人吗？
还是有的时候
像那个爸爸一样不愿意宽恕呢？
甘心宽恕并不容易
不完美对我们有很大的影响
有时让我们不容易体谅别人
当我们受到伤害时
可能容易记仇或怀恨在心
也许我们的文化背景教我们不要原谅对方
这些都会让我们很难宽恕别人，追求和睦
不过，圣经鼓励我们要甘心宽恕
我们来看看另外一个例子，就是约伯
我们都知道他的遭遇
他失去了财产和孩子
染上了严重的疾病
他的妻子叫他去死了算了
约伯的三个朋友听说了他的遭遇
就一起去安慰他
约伯记2:13说
他们到了以后
跟约伯一起坐了七天七夜
但谁也没有说话
这也许也不是坏事
因为他们后来说的话
深深地伤害了约伯
他们无理指控他
值得留意的是后面发生的事
请打开约伯记42章
在约伯的考验结束时
耶和华要约伯为这些伤害他的人做一些事
留意耶和华在约伯记42:8
后半部分怎么说
我的仆人约伯会为你们祷告
我一定会答应他的恳求
不会因为你们的愚昧而惩罚你们
请留意，虽然那些人伤害约伯
但耶和华却要约伯为那些人祷告
约伯会不会回答说
耶和华，他们那样说我
我不可能原谅他们
约伯有没有怀恨在心呢？
请留意第9节的最后怎么说
耶和华听允了约伯的祷告
约伯按照耶和华的吩咐去做
约伯保持忠贞，乐意宽恕
结果怎么样呢？
10节说
约伯为他的朋友祷告之后
耶和华让约伯不再受苦
再次兴旺起来
耶和华让约伯拥有的是以前的双倍
经文说约伯后来又有了十个孩子
再活了140年
在第17节说

请看看接下来的这部短剧

对不起一直没回你

ko.text: 사과하는 것은 정말 힘들 수 있습니다.
상대방이 화를 내거나 비난하거나 외면할까 봐
‘이미 잘못을 했으니 사과해도 달라지는 건 없다’고 생각할 수도 있죠.
우리가 화가 났기 때문일 수도 있습니다.
자신이 관련된 사고로 부상을 당한 사람에게 유감을 표현하면
사고에 대한 책임을 경감해 주는 법안을 통과시켰습니다. …
사과를 하면 법원에서 유죄를 시인한 것처럼 해석될까 봐
사과하기를 꺼린 것이 자주 관찰되었기 때문입니다.”
성경에 나오는 충실한 종인 사도 바울은
바울이 유대인들에게 고발당한 이유를 알고 싶어 합니다.
명령을 내려 고등 법원인 산헤드린을 소집하죠.
바울이 옳은 것을 담대하게 변호하는 모습이 인상적일 것입니다.
하느님 앞에서 온전히 깨끗한 양심으로 살아왔습니다.’
당신이 율법에 따라 나를 재판하려고 앉아 있으면서도
나를 치라고 명령하여 율법을 어긴단 말입니까?’
“너는 네 백성의 지도자를 비방해서는 안 된다”고 기록되어 있습니다.’”
재판관이 폭력을 써서는 안 된다는 그의 말은 옳은 말이었습니다.
젊은 자매들에게 ‘건전한 정신을 갖도록’ 조언하는 모습을 보게 될 것입니다.
평화를 추구하는 모습도 보게 될 것입니다.
이런 일이 벌어져서 나도 마음이 아파.
어떻게 절 그렇게 보실 수 있죠?
자, 둘 다 이러지 말자, 응?
할머니 때문에 먼저 좀 가 볼게요.
그리고 두 젊은 자매가 평화를 이루도록 도와주었죠.
사과를 하려면 용기와 겸손과 결심이 필요합니다.
오히려 겸손하게 남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기십시오.”
또한 우리가 옳다는 것을 이미 확신한 상태로 대화를 시작해서도 안 됩니다.
그것은 자기중심적인 태도라고 할 수 있죠.
오히려 이 성구에서 알려 주는 원칙에 따라
우리의 목표는 평화를 추구하는 것이 되어야 합니다.
여호와께서 우리의 숭배를 받아 주시기 때문입니다.
예수께서는 그 점을 이렇게 분명히 알려 주셨습니다.
거기서 당신의 형제가 당신에게 반감을 품고 있는 것이 생각나거든,
예물을 거기 제단 앞에 두고, 가서 먼저 그 형제와 평화를 이루십시오.
한 성서학자는 그 장면을 이렇게 묘사합니다.
여러 개의 뜰 곧 이방인의 뜰,
그 너머에는 평신도가 들어갈 수 없는
자기 제물을 제사장에게 넘겨줄 준비를 하고 있다.”
그는 형제가 자기에게 반감을 품고 있는 것이 생각납니다.
예수께서는 ‘예물을 거기 제단 앞에 두고 형제에게 가라’고 말씀하셨습니다.
예수께서는 예물을 바치는 것보다 뭐가 더 중요하다고 말씀하셨죠?
화해 즉 평화를 이루는 것이 희생 제물보다 중요하다는 것입니다.
우리가 형제 자매들을 어떻게 대하는지는 하느님과 누리는 관계에 직접적인 영향을 줍니다.
“보이는 형제를 사랑하지 않는 사람이 보이지 않는 하느님을 사랑할 수 없습니다.”
우리가 어떤 형제나 자매의 마음을 상하게 했다는 것을 알게 된다면
우리는 솔선해서 그 형제나 자매에게 다가가야 합니다.
더는 동물 희생을 바칠 필요가 없습니다.
양쪽 다 어느 정도 책임이 있을 것입니다.
두 사람 다 불완전하고 실수를 하기 때문이죠.
문제를 해결하려면 양쪽 모두 노력해야 합니다.
세속 법정에 데려간다는 말을 들었을 때
“왜 차라리 부당한 일을 그냥 당하지 못합니까?
형제 자매들과 누리는 평화가 누가 옳고 그른지 가리는 것보다 더 중요합니다.
우리에게 잘못이 있다고 생각하는 사람에게 사과하기가 더 쉬울 것입니다.
이제 집필 위원회의 보조자인 레너드 마이어스 형제가
이 심포지엄의 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.

en.text: “I am so sorry.”
“It’s my fault, please forgive me.”
No matter how we phrase it,
it can be difficult to apologize.
Why is that so challenging?
There are many reasons:
We may fear confrontation, blame, or rejection.
Perhaps we feel embarrassed, and we’re too proud to apologize.
We may reason, ‘Apologizing will not undo the blunder I’ve already made.’
And it may even be that we are angry.
This is such a matter of concern
that “in July 2000,
“the California State Legislature in the United States
“passed a bill designed to relieve people of liability
“if they express sympathy to an individual who was injured in an accident
“in which they themselves were involved. . . .
“It was noted that . . . people often hesitate to extend an apology
“[out of concern that] it could be construed in court
as an admission of guilt.”
The Bible provides an account of a faithful servant,
the apostle Paul,
who was a good example of one who apologized.
The account is in the book of Acts chapter 23.
The setting: A Roman military officer
wanted to know why Paul was being accused by the Jews.
So he brought Paul to the Jewish chief priests
and commanded the Sanhedrin, the high court, to assemble.
As we read Acts 23:1-5 together,
we can’t help but be impressed
by Paul’s boldness as he stands for what is right.
But at the same time, please take note of his humility.
Acts 23:1: “Looking intently at the Sanhedrin,
“Paul said: ‘Men, brothers,
“‘I have behaved before God
“with a perfectly clear conscience down to this day.’
“At this the high priest Ananias
“ordered those standing by him to strike him on the mouth.
“Then Paul said to him:
“‘God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall.
“‘Do you sit to judge me according to the Law
“‘and at the same time violate the Law
“by commanding me to be struck?’
“Those standing by said:
“‘Are you insulting the high priest of God?’
“And Paul said: ‘Brothers,
“‘I did not know he was high priest.
“‘For it is written, “You must not speak injuriously
of a ruler of your people.”’”
Paul immediately admitted his error.
What he had said,
that the one appointed as judge should not resort to violence, was right.
Yet, he apologized.
In the following dramatization,
we will see an older sister
applying the inspired words of Titus 2:3-5
in order to advise younger sisters “to be sound in mind.”
We will also observe how one of the younger sisters
avoids further problems and pursues peace
by humbly apologizing.
I don’t know how this happened
but, Haley, I’m sorry.
It hurts me to see you so upset.
I can’t believe you two.
First,
what you heard
was not what I said.
Well, I thought that was how you felt.
And even if I got that part wrong, all this drama?
Now stop!
Come on, girls.
Haley, come closer.
“Love is patient and kind.”
It’s not jealous.
It doesn’t become provoked,
even when things become difficult.
So, what are we going to do?
I just thought if—
No,
I’m sorry, Haley.
I’m sorry.
I shouldn’t have judged you so harshly.
I shouldn’t have judged you at all.
And I’m sorry for dragging you into this by twisting what you said.
It’s OK; things happen.
I’ve been on both ends.
I should never have spoken that way to you, Celia
—I mean, to either of you.
I’ve got to get home to Nana.
I’ll call you tomorrow.
Bye.
The older sister apologized, even though she was not in the wrong.
She also urged the two younger sisters to make peace.
It takes courage, humility, and determination to apologize.
It’s interesting to note what’s stated
at Philippians 2:3:
“Do nothing out of contentiousness or out of egotism,
but with humility consider others superior to you.”
That means our determined effort is not to win an argument,
which could be contentious,
nor do we want to start a discussion
with the primary thought being that we are in the right.
That could mean that we are self-concerned, or egotistical.
Rather, in harmony with the principle of that scripture
we want to act with humility.
Our aim should be to pursue peace.
Even if we think the other person is being unreasonable,
we apologize.
Why is it so important to do so?
Because that is what makes our worship to Jehovah acceptable.
At Matthew chapter 5,
verses 23, 24,
Jesus makes it very clear:
“If, then, you are bringing your gift to the altar
“and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
“leave your gift there in front of the altar,
“and go away.
“First make your peace with your brother,
and then come back and offer your gift.”
“One Bible scholar describes the scene this way:
“‘The worshipper has entered the Temple;
“‘he has passed through [a] series of courts,
“‘the Court of the Gentiles,
“‘the Court of the Women, the Court of the Men.
“‘Beyond that there lay the Court of the Priests
“‘into which the layman could not go.
“‘The worshipper is standing at the rail,
“ready to hand over his [living animal] to the priest.’ . . .
“At that [critical] moment,
the worshipper remembers that his brother has something against him.”
What is he to do?
“Leave your gift there in front of the altar,”
Jesus explains, “and go away.”
What does Jesus say is more important than offering up a sacrifice?
‘First, make peace with your brother.
‘Then when you have come back,
offer up your gift.’
The expression rendered “make your peace”
means “to reconcile.”
Jesus’ words teach a crucial lesson:
Reconciliation, or peace,
comes before sacrifice.
The way we treat fellow worshippers
has a direct bearing on our relationship with God.
First John 4:20 pointedly says:
“For the one who does not love his brother, whom he has seen,
cannot love God, whom he has not seen.”
If we find ourselves in a situation where we have offended a fellow worshipper,
we want to apply Jesus’ counsel.
We want to take the initiative
to approach our brother or sister.
We may need to acknowledge their hurt feelings.
We may also need to ask, “What can I do to make amends?”
Often a sincere apology is all that is needed.
Although our worship today no longer includes animal sacrifices,
what Jesus was teaching
emphasizes that there is a connection
between peace with our brother
and acceptable worship to God.
When two humans are at odds,
there may be a measure of blame on both sides,
since both are imperfect and prone to error.
This usually calls for mutual concessions.
Even if only the one apologizing is right,
the issue is not so much who is right and who is wrong
but who will take the initiative to make peace.
When the apostle Paul heard that the Christians in Corinth
were taking fellow servants of God
to secular courts over personal differences,
he said:
“Why [do you] not rather let [yourself] be wronged?
Why do you not rather let [yourself] be defrauded?”
The principle is clear.
Peace among fellow believers is more important than proving
who is right and who is wrong.
Keeping this in mind makes it easier to apologize for a wrong
that someone thinks we’ve committed against him or her.
A heartfelt apology can open the way
to a constructive conversation.
It can minimize problems
and restore peace.
Brother Leonard Myers,
a helper to the Writing Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“‘Seek Peace and Pursue It’ . . .
By Forgiving Freely.”

cn.text: “真的非常对不起”
“是我的错，请原谅我”
不论我们用什么措辞
道歉都是不容易的
为什么会这样？
原因有很多
我们可能害怕面对问题
怕被指责或被拒绝
我们也可能觉得尴尬
或者太骄傲不想道歉
我们可能想
道歉也弥补不了已经发生的事
或者是因为我们还在气头上
不过，道歉很重要
美国加利福尼亚州议会通过一条法案
容许造成事故的人减轻责罚
条件是，他要慰问伤者
向对方表示歉意
肇事者往往不愿意道歉
因为在法庭上
表示歉意很可能被理解为
肇事者已经认罪
圣经记载了一位忠心崇拜上帝的人
就是使徒保罗
他在道歉方面立下了很好的榜样
这个经历记载在使徒行传23章
背景是
一个罗马将军想知道
保罗到底为什么被犹太人指控
他就把保罗带到祭司长那里
让公议会
也就是犹太最高法庭审问他
在读使徒行传23:1-5时
我们会禁不住赞叹
保罗在维护真理时
表现出的勇气
但是这次
请留意保罗的谦卑
“保罗注视着公议会的人，说
各位弟兄，我在上帝面前
向来都本着良心处事为人
无愧于心，直到今天
大祭司亚拿尼亚一听见
就吩咐站在旁边的人打他的嘴
保罗对他说
你这个虚伪的人，上帝要打击你
你一边坐着根据法典审判我
一边又违反法典下令打我吗？
站在旁边的人说
你竟敢侮辱上帝委任的大祭司？
保罗说
弟兄们，我不知道他是大祭司
圣经上写着
不可侮辱人民的首领”
保罗马上承认了错误
他说的话并没有错
审判官的确不该动手打人
不过，保罗还是道歉
在接下来的短剧中
一位年长的姐妹
实践提多书2:3-5的原则
帮助年轻的姐妹培养健全的思想
我们也会看到，年轻的姐妹
怎样寻求和睦
谦卑地道歉
没有让矛盾变严重
我也不知道
事情为什么会变成这样
海莉
真对不起
看到你这么伤心
我也很难过
你们真的太过分了
首先
你听到的
跟我说的
完全不一样
我以为你就是那个意思
就算我有一部分理解错了
－她也不应该……   －好了
你们听我说
海莉
坐过来点
爱，有耐心，又仁慈
爱，不会嫉妒
也不会轻易动怒
即使在不容易的情况下也一样
那你们打算怎么做？
我当时只是觉得……
对不起，海莉
对不起
我不应该那样批评你
是我的态度有问题
对不起
我不应该扭曲你的意思
还把你卷进来
没问题
可以理解
我以前也这样做过
我不应该那样说你
对你那么凶
也许……
对你们两个都不该
我要回家了，奶奶在等我
明天我给你打电话
再见
年长的姐妹并没有错
但她还是道歉了
她也劝两位年轻姐妹要保持和睦
道歉需要谦卑、勇气
也需要决心
腓立比书2:3的内容
很值得我们留意
“做什么都不要争强好胜
不要自命不凡
要谦卑
看别人比自己优秀”
这意味着我们的目标不是要吵赢架
不是要争胜
我们去找对方谈的目的
也不是要证明
自己有理
这样的人很自私
只想到自己
相反，刚才的经文提醒我们
要表现谦卑
我们的目标是追求和睦
即使我们觉得这件事情错不在自己
也可以道歉
为什么这么做很重要？
因为这关系到耶和华是否接纳我们的崇拜
在马太福音5:23,24
耶稣清楚地说
“所以，你把礼物带到祭坛来的时候

title: 존 에크란: “평화​를 찾아 그것​을 추구​하십시오”—성급하게 화내지 않음으로

ko.text: 이 제목은 베드로 전서 3:11에 근거해 있는데요.
“악에서 떠나 선을 행하고, 평화를 찾아 그것을 추구하십시오.”
바람이 불어서 휙 날아가 버린 적이 있나요?
어느 순간 휙 날아가 버릴 수 있고
평화를 추구하는 네 가지 방법을 살펴볼 것입니다.
“성급하게 화낸다”라는 말에 대해 한번 생각해 보시죠.
우리는 사실을 확인해 보지도 않고 성급하게 결론을 내려서는 안 됩니다.
예수의 충실한 사도들도 성급하게 화를 낸 적이 있었습니다.
그때 야고보와 요한이 예수께 이렇게 말했습니다.
“주여, 우리가 하늘에서 불을 불러 내려 저들을 모두 없애 버릴까요?”
그러자 예수께서는 그들의 경솔한 태도를 꾸짖으셨습니다.
예수께서 화가 난 야고보와 요한을 말리지 않으셨더라면
어떤 심각한 결과가 있었을지 생각해 보십시오.
사마리아 사람들이 왕국 소식에 편견을 가졌을 것입니다.
예수께서는 평화를 추구하는 쪽으로 문제를 해결하셨죠.
성경에 따르면 그들은 그저 “다른 마을로 갔습니다.”
그러면 우리는 어떤 일로도 기분이 상해서는 안 됩니까?
요점은 우리가 모든 사실을 듣기도 전에 성급하게 결론을 내려서는 안 된다는 것입니다.
“사실을 듣기도 전에 문제에 대답하는 것은 어리석고 수치스러운 일이다.”
한 자매가 다른 사람의 잘못을 어떻게 지나쳐 주는지 유의해 보시죠.
자매도 뒤에서 제 얘기나 떠들고 다니셨어요? -헤일리!
근데 지금 정말 크게 오해하는 거야.
일단 좀 차분하게 가라앉히고 얘기하자, 응?
근데 사람들은 뒤에서 제 얘기나 하고 있고.
자매가 요새 이렇게 힘든데 신경도 못 써 줬네.
우리가 헤일리처럼 기분이 상하는 일이 있을 때
어떻게 하면 성급하게 화내지 않을 수 있을까요?
“성급하게 화내지 마라. 화내는 것은 어리석은 자의 품에나 머무르는 것이다.”
또 무엇을 모르고 있는지 생각해 보아야 합니다.
우리가 어떤 말을 전해 들었을 때
그에 관한 모든 점을 알고 있습니까?
실리아가 실제로 무슨 말을 했는지 물어보지도 않았죠.
또한 우리는 어떤 말을 들을 때
무슨 의도로 그 말을 했는지도 알고 있습니까?
헤일리가 자기 “영상에 대해 이야기했냐”고 물었을 때
즉시 헤일리는 그게 부정적인 말이었을 거라고 단정했습니다.
다른 사람을 잘못 판단할 수 있죠.
실리아의 말을 들어 보지도 않고 말이죠.
헤일리는 실리아가 자신이 좋아하는 훌륭한 자매라고 말했지만,
무슨 생각을 하고 어떤 말을 할지
잠시 멈추어 생각해 보지 않은 겁니다.
힘든 하루를 보냈기 때문일 수 있습니다.
반면 실리아는 우리에게 좋은 본이 됩니다.
할머니도 돌봐 드려야 한다고 말했을 때,
시간을 내서 충분히 생각해 보는 것에 더해
그 점을 기억하는 것이 특히 더 중요합니다.
뒤에서 어떤 차가 우리 차를 받았습니다.
여호와께서 모든 것을 지켜보고 있다는 사실에서
마음의 평화를 누릴 수 있다는 점을 잘 보여 줍니다.
여호와께서 그날 모든 것을 지켜보고 계셨다는 사실에서
큰 위로를 받을 수 있을 것입니다.
우리는 주변 사람들의 부정적인 말이나 행동 하나하나에 화를 내거나
우리가 옳다는 것을 매번 입증하려고 노력할 필요가 없습니다.
그렇게 하면 감정적으로 몹시 지치게 되고
주변 사람들과 그리 친하게 지내지 못할 것입니다.
사소한 잘못은 기꺼이 지나쳐 주어야 합니다.
잘못을 지나쳐 주는 것은 그의 아름다움이다.”
우리에게 불평할 만한 심각한 이유가 있다면
여호와의 지침에 따라 그 문제를 처리하십시오.
그 돈보다 훨씬 더 가치가 있습니다.
그것을 다시 얻기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
하느님께 영광을 돌리고 평화를 추구할 수 있을 것입니다.
이제 인사 위원회 보조자인 랠프 월스 형제가 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.

en.text: The title of this series of four talks is “Seek Peace and Pursue It,”
and it’s based on 1 Peter 3:11.
Let’s read that together
—1 Peter 3:11:
“Let him turn away from what is bad and do what is good;
let him seek peace and pursue it.”
Yes, we have to pursue peace, and pursuit requires effort.
Have you ever had to chase a piece of paper that was in your hands
and got blown away by the wind,
and just once you get to it, the wind blows it away again and again?
It can really take quite some effort
to retrieve and get that paper back in your hands.
Just standing there and watching the paper blow farther and farther away
is not going to get it back.
Well, peace can be a lot like that paper.
At some point, it can get blown away,
and we have to then chase,
or pursue, it to get that peace back again.
This series of talks will help us to pursue peace in four ways:
by not quickly taking offense,
by apologizing,
by forgiving freely,
and by using our gift of speech wisely.
Let’s consider our first way to pursue peace:
Avoid quickly taking offense.
Now, because we are imperfect,
we might misjudge others and quickly take offense.
Notice that we say quickly take offense.
That’s an important word.
We need to avoid jumping to conclusions quickly
before we actually have the facts.
Even faithful men like Jesus’ apostles have taken offense too quickly.
You may recall the time that Jesus and his apostles
were looking for lodging in a Samaritan village.
Now, the Samaritans in that village rudely denied them lodging.
At Luke 9:54-56,
the apostles—James and John— say to Jesus:
“Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven and annihilate them?”
But Jesus rebukes them for their rash and rather violent suggestion.
Think of the serious consequences
had Jesus yielded to the violent temper of James and John.
The Samaritans could have become prejudiced against the Kingdom message.
Instead, Jesus pursues a peaceful solution.
The account says ‘they simply went to a different village.’
Now, does this mean we’re saying we can never take offense?
No, you may have a legitimate “cause for complaint.”
The key point is that we should not quickly draw conclusions
before we hear all the facts.
Proverbs 18:13 says:
“When anyone replies to a matter before he hears the facts,
it is foolish and humiliating.”
In the following dramatization,
note what helps one sister to overlook an offense.
And I expected more from you.
Haley, what are you talking about?
Gossiping about my posts!
Are you that lonely that you’ve got nothing better to do?
Haley,
wait, please!
I don’t know what’s happening.
Did you talk to Emily about my posts?
Yes, we did . . .
So you gossiped about me.
No, I would . . .
I looked up to you!
I would never . . .
You’re supposed to be the mature one,
and you’re just like Emily, busy running your mouth.
Haley!
Look, I can see you’re upset,
but trust me, this is a huge misunderstanding.
I love you.
I would never ever say anything behind your back.
So please calm down.
Sometimes I just feel so alone
—between Nana and work—
and then knowing all of you are talking about me.
I promise, that’s not what happened.
You’re just really tired and overwhelmed.
So why don’t we just slow things down a little.
You know, meetings always make me feel better,
even on my worst days.
Why don’t we go inside,
clean up a little, and enjoy the program together.
Then afterward, we can all talk.
I promise, it’ll be OK.
Haley really was upset.
She had already concluded that she was being gossiped about by everyone.
If we find ourselves like Haley feeling offended,
how can we avoid quickly taking offense?
Well, we must stop and think.
Let’s read Ecclesiastes 7:9
for some very good advice in these situations
—Ecclesiastes 7:9:
“Do not be quick to take offense,
for the taking of offense lodges in the bosom of fools.”
Like Celia said in the parking lot to Haley,
“Please calm down.”
So in those situations,
you need to think about what you know
and, just as important, what you don’t know.
Now, you know what you were told happened,
but what was really said?
In the video, Haley quickly believed what she was told.
She did not even ask Celia what she really said.
Or you may know what was said,
but do you know what was really meant by it?
Haley asked, “Did you talk about . . . my posts?”
And Celia said, “Yes.”
And immediately, Haley assumed the worst.
Or perhaps we misjudged the person who hurt us.
Haley misjudged Celia on the spot by saying,
‘You’re just as bad as Emily.’
She had not even heard from Celia yet.
Haley said to Celia that she was the mature one,
the one she looked up to,
yet she was quick to believe the worst about her.
Haley had not stopped and really thought about what
she was thinking and saying.
Perhaps she was having a hard day.
Well, Celia really set a fine example for us.
Even though Haley spoke harshly to her,
Celia was calm and listened to Haley.
As Haley explained how she was feeling lonely,
dealing and caring for her grandmother,
you can see the love and concern that Celia had for Haley,
even though just moments before she had spoken really harshly to her.
Well, besides taking time to think things through,
we also need to remember that it is Jehovah’s opinion of us
that matters the most.
Now, that’s an important point, especially when we deal
with misunderstandings or false accusations.
Think about it: Jehovah is an eyewitness to everything.
To illustrate that, I want you to imagine
you had a traffic accident.
Now, you were just sitting at the stop sign,
but another car ran straight into you.
The police come, and the person that ran into you
says that you ran into them, and the police believe them.
You take the matter to court.
The judge listens as the other person says that you ran into them;
however, before you can say anything,
the judge says: “No, that is not what happened.
“I was there walking on the sidewalk across the street that day,
and I saw the whole thing.”
Well, it’s extremely unlikely that you can go to court and expect
the judge for your case to have been an eyewitness.
This does illustrate, though, the peace of mind that we can have
knowing that Jehovah is an eyewitness to all that happens.
So when falsely accused or when we have a misunderstanding
that we cannot seem to clear up, it is of great comfort for us to know
that Jehovah was there that day and saw the whole thing.
We don’t need to take offense at every negative thing
that is said or done around us
or feel we have to defend ourselves as being right on every occasion.
We would surely wear out emotionally
and probably not have very many friends.
We should be willing to overlook minor transgressions.
Let’s look at Proverbs 19:11
—Proverbs 19:11.
What can help us?
“The insight of a man certainly slows down his anger,
and it is beauty on his part to overlook an offense.”
So can you “overlook an offense”?
As the proverb said, that ‘is beauty on our part.’
If not and you have a serious cause for complaint,
handle matters according to Jehovah’s direction.
Show insight.
Slow down any anger.
Think carefully, and listen patiently
to make sure you clearly have all the facts
before you become offended or take action.
Remember that piece of paper that you had in your hands
and got blown away by the wind?
What if it was a hundred-dollar bill?
Well, you would make every effort
to pursue it and get it back because it’s valuable.
Our peace with our brothers is far more valuable than paper money.
When our peace with our brothers or sisters
is blown away by misunderstandings, mistakes, or sin,
then we should pursue peace and try hard to get it back.
Yes, we glorify God and promote peace
when we avoid quickly taking offense.
Brother Ralph Walls, a helper to the Personnel Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“‘Seek Peace and Pursue It’ . . . By Apologizing.”

cn.text: 这个系列演讲的主题是
寻求和睦，不断追求
这是根据彼得前书3:11
让我们一起读这节经文
请打开圣经到彼得前书
我们读3:11
“要弃恶从善
也要寻求和睦
不断追求”
经文说要追求和睦
这意味着要付出努力
你有没有遇到过你手上拿的纸
突然被一阵大风吹走
当你好不容易快捡到的时候
纸却被风吹得更远
你必须要费好一番功夫
才能把那张纸捡回来
只是站在那里
看着纸被风吹得越来越远
那张纸是回不来的
和睦就像那张纸
有的时候它会被吹走
我们要付出努力去追求
才能把它追回来
这个系列演讲
会告诉我们追求和睦的四个方法
分别是：不轻易动怒
主动道歉
甘心宽恕
还有留意我们的言谈
追求和睦的第一个方法是
不要轻易动怒
因为我们都不完美
可能会误会别人，马上就生气
我们说不轻易动怒
这个词很重要
我们在了解全部事实前
不该轻易下结论，让自己动怒
就连耶稣的忠心使徒也曾经轻易动怒
有一次耶稣和使徒
到撒马利亚的村庄找留宿的地方
那个村庄的人无礼地拒绝他们
在路加福音9:54-56
雅各和约翰对耶稣说
“主啊，你要我们叫火从天上降下来
消灭他们吗？”
但耶稣斥责他们
没有允许他们冲动行事
假如耶稣真的容许他们这样做
后果会多么严重
撒马利亚人可能因此就不想接受王国信息
不过耶稣追求和睦
经文说他们就到别的村庄去
这是不是说，我们都不可以生气呢？
不是，有的时候你可能有理由生气
重点是我们在没有了解全部事实的时候
不该太快下结论
“还没听到事实就回应
不仅愚蠢，而且丢脸”
请看以下短剧
留意一位姐妹
怎样不轻易动怒
我还以为你很成熟
海莉
你在说什么？
别装了，你自己知道
你是不是太闲了
都没有别的事可做？
海莉
等等我
你到底怎么了？
你和珍妮在背后说我发的东西
我们只是……
你们在背后说我坏话
没有，我……
亏我还把你当榜样呢！
我绝没有……
我一直把你当成熟的人
没想到你跟珍妮一样
就只会在背后说人坏话
海莉
我知道你现在很生气
但请你相信我
你真的误会了
我很爱你
我从来没有在背后说过你坏话
我们先冷静一下
好不好？
有时候
我觉得很无助
要照顾奶奶，要工作
然后
你们还在背后议论我
我向你保证
事情不是你想的那样
我知道你压力很大
生活不容易
我们先冷静下来好不好？
海莉
聚会总是对我很有帮助
哪怕是我最痛苦的时候
我们先进去吧
整理一下
好好参加聚会
聚会结束后
我们三个聊一聊
我保证
一切都会没事的
海莉非常生气
她已经认定
所有人都在背后说她的坏话
如果我们像海莉一样感觉受冒犯
什么能帮助我们不轻易动怒呢？
我们要停下来，想一想
传道书7:9给了我们很明智的建议
我们来读一下
传道书7:9
“你不要轻易动怒
因为怒气留在愚昧的人怀里”
就像莱雅在停车场对海莉说
我们冷静一下
在这样的情况
要想想我们知道什么
也要想想我们不知道什么
想想我们听到的内容
就是事情的全貌吗？
在短剧中，海莉马上就相信了珍妮的话
她没有问莱雅
这是不是事实
我们可能听到别人说了什么
但会不会误会了他的意思呢？
海莉跟莱雅说这件事
但莱雅还没有解释，海莉就认定
莱雅说自己的坏话
我们也有可能错怪了别人
海莉马上认定，莱雅跟珍妮一样
在背后说人的坏话
她没有给莱雅机会解释
海莉说莱雅是个成熟的人
是她的榜样
但她却马上认定莱雅在背后议论她
海莉没有停下来想一想
就把怒气发泄出来
也许那天她心情很不好
莱雅为我们立下了很好的榜样
即使海莉对她很凶
她还是冷静地听海莉说话
当海莉说到自己孤单无助
要照顾奶奶的时候
我们可以看到莱雅对海莉的爱和关心
莱雅没有在意海莉刚才对她的态度
除了要仔细想想事情的全貌
我们也要记得
耶和华怎么看我们才是最重要的
尤其是被误会
或受到无理指责的时候
更要记得这一点
不要忘记
耶和华看到，也知道一切
有一个比喻可以说明这一点
请想象一个情况
你开着车，停在路口
有一辆车开过来，撞上了你
警察来了
开车撞你的人说
是你撞了他
警察也相信了他
事情闹到法庭上
那个司机又跟法官说
是你撞了他
在你开始为自己辩护之前
法官突然说
不，事情不是这样
我那天正好就在马路边
看到了整个事故的经过
当然，这种情况不太可能发生
法官不太可能刚好目击了你遇到的事情
但这个比喻说明
我们可以享有内心安宁
因为知道耶和华能看到一切
当我们被误解
或受到指责时
我们可能没办法澄清
但我们知道耶和华当时在场
看到了一切
就会感到很安慰
我们不需要
为别人冒犯我们的每一件事情生气
也不需要每一次
都证明自己是清白的
这样做会耗尽我们的精力
也可能会让我们失去很多朋友
我们要学会不计较别人微小的过失
我们来看箴言19:11
什么能帮助我们呢？
“人洞悉事理
就不轻易发怒
不追究过失
就是他的美德”
你可以“不追究过失”吗？
经文说这样做是一种“美德”
如果事情比较严重，不能不追究
就要按照圣经原则来处理
要洞悉事理
不轻易发怒
要认真想想，也要耐心聆听
在了解全部事实之前
不要定下结论
还记得演讲开始提到被风吹走的那张纸吗？
如果那是一百美元的钞票呢？
你会尽一切努力把它追回来
因为它很有价值
我们跟弟兄姐妹的和睦
比一百美元贵重多了
当我们之间的和睦
被误会、过失或不完美“吹走”时
我们要尽一切努力
把它追回来
我们不轻易动怒
就能促进和睦
也能为耶和华带来荣耀
人事委员会助手拉尔夫·沃尔斯弟兄
会发表系列演讲的下一部分
寻求和睦，不断追求——主动道歉

title: 케네스 쿡 2세: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—제어되지 않은 분노

ko.text: 성경은 사탄이 “몹시 화가 났다”고 알려 줍니다.
그는 악의적이고 제어되지 않은 분노를 표출합니다.
하느님을 두려워하고 건전한 정신을 가진 사람이
제어되지 않은 분노를 ‘벗어 버리기로’ 굳게 결심합니다.
그러면 제어되지 않은 분노 말고도 분노는 다 나쁜 걸까요?
성경은 모든 분노가 다 나쁘다고 하지 않습니다.
성경에서 정죄하는 분노는 부당하거나 제어되지 않은 분노입니다.
때때로 우리는 뭔가가 잘못되었다고 느낄 때가 있죠.
그럴 때 우리는 화가 나거나 기분이 상해서
그건 잘못된 분노라고 할 수 있습니다.
그러한 분노는 우리가 건전한 정신을 가지고 행동하지 못하게 할 수 있죠.
계속 분노를 터뜨리는 사람은 구원을 얻지 못할 것입니다.
하느님의 왕국을 상속받지 못하게 하는 “육체의 일” 가운데 “격분”을 언급합니다.
그런 사람은 하느님의 신세계에 들어가지 못합니다.
우리와 다른 사람의 평화를 깨뜨리는지 생각해 보면
그 점을 더 잘 이해할 수 있습니다.
제어되지 않은 분노는 당사자뿐 아니라 주위 사람들에게도 해로운 영향을 끼칩니다.
그리고 그에 더해 “범법을 많이 저지른다”고 알려 줍니다.
그중 하나는 모욕적인 말을 하는 것입니다.
자제력을 나타내기 위해 노력할 필요가 있습니다.
우리는 해로운 감정을 반드시 제어해야 하죠.
모욕적인 말, 조롱, 멸시, 미움에 찬 분노는 잘못입니다.
우리가 다른 사람 그리고 여호와와 누리는 소중한 관계를 해칠 수 있습니다.
화산이 폭발하는 것에 비할 수 있는데요.
그 주위에 있는 사람들이 피해를 입는 것처럼,
격렬한 분노를 터뜨리는 사람은 주위 사람들에게 큰 해를 입히게 됩니다.
화를 표출하게 되면 종종 더욱더 화가 치밀어 오릅니다.
그처럼 제어되지 않은 분노는 우리 마음의 평화를 빼앗아 가죠.
나중에 후회할 행동을 하게 될 수도 있습니다.
또한 건강에도 해가 될 수 있습니다.
제어되지 않은 분노는 고혈압과 호흡기 질환을 일으킬 수 있습니다.
소화기에도 여러 가지 장애를 일으킬 수 있습니다.
우리가 화가 나게 되면 차분하게 생각하기가 어렵게 됩니다.
분노를 폭발하고 나면 기분도 우울해질 수 있습니다.
제어되지 않은 분노가 얼마나 파괴적인 결과를 가져오는지 보여 주는
바로 족장 야곱의 아들들인 시므온과 레위에 관한 기록입니다.
자신들의 누이인 디나가 세겜이라는 남자에게 강간을 당했다는 것을 알게 되자
창세기 34:7에 따르면 “그들은 감정이 상하고 몹시 화가 났습니다.”
하지만 그 화가 너무 지나쳐서 제어되지 않은 정도가 됩니다.
그들은 속임수를 써서 세겜의 도시에 있는 모든 남자를 공격해 죽입니다.
그 도시를 약탈하고 여자와 아이들을 포로로 사로잡아 갑니다.
분명 야곱도 디나가 겪은 끔찍한 일 때문에 마음이 아팠겠지만
아들들이 제어되지 않은 분노를 나타낸 것을 꾸짖었습니다.
시므온과 레위는 자신들의 행동을 정당화하려고 했지만,
시므온과 레위의 자손이 이스라엘 지파들 가운데
흩어지게 될 것이라는 예언을 했던 것입니다.
그들은 제어되지 않은 분노를 나타냈기 때문에
하느님의 은혜와 아버지 야곱의 승인을 잃었습니다.
그러한 분노가 초래하는 해를 피하도록 해야겠습니다.
한 자매가 어떻게 분노를 터뜨릴 위험에 처하게 되는지 보시겠습니다.
너 맨날 바빠서 시간 내기도 힘들잖아.
지금 하는 게 나을 것 같은데.
아 그게, 최근에 네가 올린 영상들 말이야.
어 ··· 파이오니아가 그런 영상 올리는 거, 좀 그렇지 않아?
그냥 내가 만든 물건 광고하려는 건데 뭐가?
니가 관심 끌고 싶어서 안달 난 것처럼 보일 수 있다는 ···
나 말고도 실리아 자매도 그렇게 생각하셔.
내 뒷담화하고 다니니까 그렇게 좋아? -뒷담화가 아니고 ···
분노가 제어되지 않으면 어떤 일이 일어날지 우리 모두가 알기 때문이죠.
그로 인해 어떤 일이 생길 수 있는지 살펴봤는데요.
제어되지 않은 분노를 어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있는가 하는 것입니다.
우리는 먼저 제어되지 않은 분노의 위험성을 인식해야 합니다.
“자기를 제어하지 못하는 자는 성벽이 다 헐린 도시 같다.”
고대의 도시들은 튼튼한 성벽이 없으면 침략자들에게 쉽게 함락당할 수 있었습니다.
자기를 제어하지 못하는 사람이 바로 이와 같다는 것이죠.
자제력을 잃으면 나쁜 생각들이 아주 손쉽게 우리의 마음에 침입하게 됩니다.
그런 생각은 자신과 다른 사람들에게 해를 입힐 수 있죠.
제어되지 않은 분노는 그만큼 위험한 것입니다.
분노 때문에 나중에 후회할 일을 하기 전에
화가 끓어오른다면 시므온과 레위에게 있었던 일을 생각해 보도록 하십시오.
그리고 우리가 방금 본 동영상의 내용도 떠올려 보시면 도움이 되실 것입니다.
고통스러운 일을 피할 수 있지 않았을까요?
따라서 잠언 17:14의 말씀을 기억하는 것이 좋습니다.
이 점을 기억하면서 이렇게 자문해 보십시오.
‘나는 모든 사실을 알지 못하면서 속단하는 경향이 있는가?
그렇다면 분노가 더 자라기 전에 그 자리를 피해
그 분노를 떨쳐 버릴 수 있는가?’
야고보서 1:19의 영감받은 조언이 그렇게 하는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다.
이 말씀을 적용하기 위해 진지한 노력을 기울여야 합니다.
제어되지 않은 분노를 벗어 버릴 수 있는 간단한 방법들을 찾아 보실 수 있습니다.
우리가 여호와께 “듣기는 빨리 하고, 말하기는 더디 하고, 분노하기도 더디 하게” 도와 달라고 요청한다면
제어되지 않은 분노를 벗어 버리도록 그분이 도와주실 것입니다.
우리의 노력이 성공을 거두려면 교제의 대상을 지혜롭게 선택해야 합니다.
교만하고 독선적이고 쉽게 화를 내는 사람들과 어울린다면
분노를 제어하기 위해 우리가 기울이는 노력과 여호와의 도움이 효과를 거두지 못할 수 있습니다.
쉽게 화를 터뜨리는 사람에 대해 잠언 22:25에서 경고하는 것처럼,
곧 있을 이 악한 세상의 심판을 생존하는 데 도움이 되는
시기심, 부정직, 남에 대한 해로운 이야기,
평화를 깨뜨리는 특성들을 계속 벗어 버리기 위해 최선을 다해야 합니다.
만약 우리에게 개선해야 할 점이 조금이라도 있다면,
여호와의 도움을 청하고 변화하기 위해 열심히 노력하십시오.
우리는 형제 자매들과의 평화를 추구하기 위해 진지하게 노력함으로
“여호와의 날”과 그분이 약속하신 신세계를 간절히 기다리고 있음을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
그러한 노력은 우리의 마음에 영향을 줄 것이고,
하늘의 아버지께서도 우리의 노력을 눈여겨보실 것입니다.
그리고 그분과 또 동료 숭배자들과 “평화”를 누리는 사람으로 여겨 주실 것입니다.

en.text: Satan is the main peace wrecker.
The Scriptures tell us that he is driven by “great anger.”
His anger is malicious and uncontrolled.
Would any sound-minded, God-fearing person
allow himself to reflect Satan’s vicious anger?
Of course not!
That is why all true servants of God are determined
to “put away” uncontrolled anger.
But apart from uncontrolled anger, is all anger bad?
The Bible does not condemn all anger.
It teaches us that anger is wrong when it is uncontrolled or unjustified.
At Ephesians 4:26, God’s Word tells us:
“Be wrathful, but [it adds] do not sin.”
At times, anger may simply be a strong feeling
that comes into us because of being upset or annoyed
by something that we see as being wrong.
That in itself is not bad.
But what makes anger bad is when it fills a person’s heart
and he or she just loses control of it.
When that happens,
it may cause a person to act without a sound mind.
Those who continue to lash out in anger will not gain salvation.
Galatians 5:20 lists “fits of anger”
among “the works of the flesh” that will prevent a person
from inheriting God’s Kingdom.
There will be no place for such ones in God’s new world.
A brief review of how uncontrolled anger
wrecks peace for ourselves and others
will highlight why this is so.
Uncontrolled anger
harms both the angry person as well as those around him.
We read at Proverbs 29:22
that an angry person “stirs up strife,”
adding that he “commits many transgressions.”
One of these many sins is abusive speech.
We must work to show restraint when speaking with workmates,
with strangers in the ministry,
with our brothers and sisters in the congregation,
and with our family members.
Bad feelings must be controlled.
Abusive speech, ridicule, contempt,
and hateful anger are wrong.
Giving vent to such feelings can destroy precious friendships
with other people and with Jehovah.
Don’t be like a volcano that will not quiet down.
Just like an erupting volcano will harm those living around it,
so too a person who expresses intense anger
will harm those living around him.
He also damages himself.
In what way?
Acting on anger often leads to even more aggression,
so uncontrolled anger can also affect our own peace.
It can cause us to do something that we will later regret.
It can have a negative effect on our health.
Medical studies show that uncontrolled anger
can cause high blood pressure and respiratory problems.
It can also affect the liver and pancreas,
and such anger can cause digestive problems.
When a person becomes angry,
he or she will not always think clearly.
After a fit of rage, a person may become depressed.
No wonder we read at Proverbs 14:30
that “a calm heart gives life to the body.”
The disastrous consequences of uncontrolled anger
are illustrated in God’s Word
by the actions of Simeon and Levi,
sons of the patriarch Jacob.
When they learned that their sister, Dinah,
was violated by a man named Shechem,
we read at Genesis 34:7
that “they were offended and very angry.”
Now, they had a valid reason to be angry,
but they took their anger too far.
It was uncontrolled.
Simeon and Levi took vengeance on Shechem.
Using deception, they attacked and killed
every male in Shechem’s city.
Then, along with the other sons of Jacob,
they plundered it and took the women and little children captive.
Dinah’s tragic experience must have grieved Jacob greatly.
Yet, he condemned his sons’ uncontrolled anger.
Simeon and Levi tried to justify their actions,
but that was not the end of the matter,
because Jehovah was also displeased.
For this reason, Jacob later foretold
that the descendants of Simeon and Levi
were to be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
Their uncontrolled anger brought disfavor
from God and from their father, Jacob.
We’re wise to pay attention to such Scriptural accounts
and put away uncontrolled anger and all of the harm that it brings.
In the following dramatization,
notice how a person might be tempted to give in to anger.
Yes, Nana?
Don’t forget eggs, dear.
No, no, I didn’t forget.
Are you sure, love?
No, I won’t forget. OK.
Thank you so much.
OK. Love you.
Bye.
No!
Haley, finally, I’ve caught you.
Do you have a minute?
Hi, Emily.
Can we talk later?
I’m really struggling this morning.
You know, it’s just that you’ve been so busy, and I’ve been waiting for the right moment;
I’d really just like to address it.
OK. What’s up?
It’s just that I’ve noticed your posts lately on QuicPost.
What about them?
Well, do you really think they’re something that a pioneer should be posting?
What? What are you talking about?
Some people might think you’re bragging.
Some people? What people?
It’s a business account. I’ve got to show off my products.
I know. I get that.
It’s just— I don’t know.
It could feel like you’re drawing a little too much attention to yourself.
Who would think like that? You?
No, not just me; Celia felt the same.
You spoke to Celia about this?
I didn’t want to upset you.
Jake said that I needed to take . . .
Jake! So everyone thinks my posts are inappropriate?
Not everyone, Haley.
That’s not what I am saying at all.
You are such . . .
Wow! I can’t believe you.
Who else have you spoken to?
You are just such a gossip!
I’m not gossiping. I was trying to . . .
You are!
I’m just trying to help you, if you would just listen to me.
You’re so jealous!
If you’d just listen to me.
Oh yeah, listen to this.
And I expected more from you.
Haley, what are you talking about?
Gossiping about my posts!
Are you that lonely that you’ve got nothing better to do?
Haley,
wait, please!
Were you left feeling a bit tense?
If so, you know what uncontrolled anger can lead to.
Now that we’ve defined uncontrolled anger
and considered what it can lead to,
the next question is,
How can we put away uncontrolled anger?
First, we need to recognize the danger of uncontrolled anger.
Proverbs 25:28 states
that “as a city broken through, without a wall,
is the man who cannot control his temper.”
Strong city walls were vital in ancient times.
Without them a city would quickly fall to invaders;
likewise, so will those who cannot control their temper.
By losing control, they make themselves vulnerable
to the invasion of wrong thoughts
—thoughts that can cause them to hurt themselves and others.
Uncontrolled anger can do just that.
Next, after recognizing the danger,
we must pause and then deal with the anger
before it causes us to do something that we will regret.
When anger grows within us,
we’re wise to recall what happened with Simeon and Levi.
We might also recall what happened
in the video dramatization that we just viewed.
You see, in each case,
pausing before reacting out of anger
may have spared much pain and heartache, true?
That is why we have this warning
at Proverbs 17:14:
“Before the quarrel breaks out, take your leave.”
With that in mind, each of us should ask himself:
‘Do I tend to jump to conclusions
‘when I don’t have all the facts?
‘If so, can I take my leave and put away anger
before it starts to build up?’
The inspired advice
found at James 1:19 will help us to do so
—but only if we make a sincere and determined effort
to apply what it says.
Let’s read that verse—James 1:19.
And here we find some simple steps
to help us put away uncontrolled anger.
It says: “Know this, my beloved brothers:
“Everyone must be quick to listen,
slow to speak, slow to anger.”
If we ask Jehovah to help us with this,
namely to “be quick to listen,
slow to speak, slow to anger,”
he will assist us to do so.
He will help us to see the facts of the matter,
show understanding, and then put away uncontrolled anger.
A word of caution, though:
To succeed in doing our part,
we must choose our associates wisely.
We could undermine all of our good work
and Jehovah’s help in controlling our anger
if we choose associates who are arrogant,
opinionated, or quick to become angry.
Regarding someone who is disposed to rage,
Proverbs 22:25 warns:
“Never learn his ways.”
Well, we’ve enjoyed another outstanding series of talks
that should help us to keep awake,
maintain fine conduct,
and escape the judgment that will soon come on this world.
As this symposium has emphasized,
we must do our utmost to continue to put away peace wreckers
such as inappropriate boasting, envy,
dishonesty, harmful gossip,
and uncontrolled anger.
If we have a problem with any of the peacemaking qualities
that we have discussed in this symposium,
seek Jehovah’s help to change and then work at it.
Our sincere efforts to pursue peace
with our brothers and our sisters
will influence how earnestly we are awaiting “Jehovah’s day”
and his promised new world.
Yes, our genuine efforts will affect our hearts
and will be noticed by our heavenly Father.
Then, in his great mercy,
Jehovah will consider us to be, as his Word says,
“spotless and unblemished and in peace”
—both with him and with our fellow worshippers.

자신의 건강 문제가 남에게 알려지기를 바라지 않을 수도 있습니다.

히브리어 성경을 들어 자신의 말을 뒷받침했죠.

그 결과 회중의 평화가 크게 위협받을 수 있었죠.

파이오니아가 그러면 안 되는 거 아니에요?
저 박스 옮기는 것 좀 도와줄 수 있을까요?
걱정이 돼서 한 말인 건 아는데,
한쪽 편의 얘기만 듣게 될 때가 있죠.
섣불리 판단하지 않는 게 좋지 않을까요?
그리고 아내가 헤일리에게 직접 말해 보게 할게요.
앨리스터 형제가 잠언 18:17을 근거로 생각해 보도록 친절하게 도와주었을 때
그는 그런 생각은 못 해 봤다고 했죠.
헤일리 자매에 대해 부정적인 말을 하기 전에
따라서 애초부터 그런 해로운 이야기를 하지 않으려면

다른 사람에 대해 나쁜 말을 하기 전에
긴 시간을 묵상해야 하는 것은 아닙니다.
부정적인 말을 옮기지 않을 수 있었을까요?
이런 질문을 해 볼 수 있었겠죠.

자기가 퍼뜨린 말을 주워 담고 싶겠죠.
말이 퍼지려면 말하는 사람과 듣는 사람이 있어야 합니다.
해로운 남의 이야기를 듣는 것이 잘못일까요?
속이는 자는 악의적인 혀에 귀를 기울인다.”
우리가 해롭고 악의적인 말에 귀를 기울이면
우리도 그 일에 큰 책임이 있다는 것입니다.
우리가 그런 말을 듣고 있으면 계속하라고 부추기는 것입니다.
이런 이야기를 하는 게 저는 좀 불편하네요”
남의 이야기를 하기 좋아한다는 걸 알게 된다면
그와 더는 가깝게 어울리지 않는 것이
“남의 이야기를 하기 좋아하는 자와는 사귀지 마라.”
우리의 소중한 평화와 연합을 지키게 될 것입니다.
이제 중앙장로회 성원인 케네스 쿡 형제가
이 심포지엄의 마지막 연설을 할 것입니다.
제목은 “평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—제어되지 않은 분노”입니다.

en.text: Do you gossip?
No.
Well, whenever we share any news about others,
that is a form of gossip.
Because we are interested in others, we might say,
“I am really concerned about Brother Smith’s health,”
or “Did you hear about Sister Brown’s experience in the ministry?”
Is this type of gossip harmful?
Generally not.
Still, we need to be careful.
At 1 Timothy 5:13,
Paul spoke out against certain sisters
who were “gossipers and meddlers in other people’s affairs.”
We do not need to know and share everything we know
about what’s happening in other people’s lives.
What if, for example, Brother Smith did not want others
to know details about his health problem?
We need to respect the privacy of others.
Or what if talking about Sister Brown’s experience turns into,
“Oh, you know, she always brags about her success in the ministry.”
When our talk about others turns negative,
it can develop into slander.
Slander is making deliberate, false statements
that damage another’s reputation.
Let’s now consider how harmful gossip wrecks peace.
If you have spread harmful gossip about someone and he hears about it,
when you see him the next time,
what will be the look on his face?
Please read with me Proverbs 25:23:
“The north wind brings a downpour,
and a gossiping tongue brings an angry face.”
The north wind in Palestine
brought dark clouds and rain.
Likewise, when the one you gossiped about
catches wind of this and he sees you,
he will have a gloomy, angry face.
There will be a storm and a chilled relationship.
Now, when that happens,
you may feel very badly and apologize,
but you may have damaged his reputation
in a way that may be difficult to undo.
Listen to this old Jewish story:
‘A man went about town slandering the town’s wise man.
‘Later, the malicious gossiper realized his wrong
‘and went to the wise man and asked for his forgiveness.
‘He offered to do whatever was needed to make amends.
‘The wise man made one request.
‘He told the gossiper to take a feather pillow,
‘cut it open, and scatter the feathers to the wind.
‘Well, the gossiper was puzzled by this request,
‘but he did as instructed.
‘Then he returned to the wise man.
‘“Am I now forgiven?” he asked.
‘“First, go and gather all the feathers,” the wise man responded.
‘“But, how can I?
‘The wind has already scattered them.”
‘The wise man replied,
‘“It is as difficult to repair the damage done by your words
as it is to recover the feathers.”’
Yes, once spoken, hurtful words cannot be retrieved.
Let’s not scatter feathers in the wind.
If we spread rumors,
it can seriously disturb the peace of many in the congregation.
We find an example of this
at Acts 21:20, 21.
The older men of the Jerusalem congregation explained to Paul
that some Jews had spread a rumor among Jewish Christians
that he had been teaching an apostasy,
speaking against the Law of Moses.
Of course, this was a twisting of the facts.
Paul never spoke disrespectfully of the Law.
He even went to synagogues
where he reasoned on the basis of the Hebrew Scriptures.
Such stories could have led some newly converted Jewish Christians
to think that Paul did not respect God’s arrangements,
and this could have seriously disrupted the peace of the congregation.
In the following dramatization,
notice the effect that harmful gossip can have
on the peace in a congregation.
Can you believe that?
Especially as a pioneer,
what kind of example is she setting?
Has Emily stopped following her?
No, not yet, but she probably will.

About what?
Haley’s posts on QuicPost.
Is there a problem?

—my clothes, my hair, my makeup.”

I know that I’ve done that and realized later
that I was wrong.
Yeah, that’s a good point.
Listen, I don’t want to pull you away,
but if you have a minute, would you mind giving me a hand with these boxes?
Sure.
Thanks for your help.
No problem.
Jake, back in the hall, I know you were just expressing concern,
but here’s something to consider.
This principle is one of my favorites.
It’s found at Proverbs
chapter 18 and verse 17.
“The first to state his case seems right,
until the other party comes and cross-examines him.”
I’m not sure I understand.
It just means that sometimes
we only hear one side of a story.
And until we personally hear both,
it’s best not to draw any conclusions.
And even then, if it’s something negative,
we wouldn’t want to spread it
any more than we’d want something spread about ourselves.
I guess I hadn’t considered that.

and have Emily talk directly to Haley.
Good idea.
Did you notice what Jake said
after the elder graciously helped him reason
on Proverbs 18:17?
He said, “I had not considered that.”
Yes, Jake just did not stop and think
before he said those negative things about Haley.
So how can we “put away” harmful gossip
before it begins?
Let’s read Proverbs 15:28:
“The heart of the righteous one meditates before answering,
“but the mouth of the wicked
blurts out bad things.”
So before we say bad things about others,
we need to meditate.
No, this does not mean a long-drawn-out process.
It just requires a little thought.
What thoughts could have stopped Jake
from repeating his wife’s negative view of Haley’s post?
He could have asked himself:
‘Is what I am about to say true?
‘Is it kind, loving?
‘How will Harry and Marie view Haley
if they hear those negative things about her?’
Another principle that will help us to put away harmful gossip
is the so-called Golden Rule,
as recorded at Luke 6:31.
Jesus said: “Just as you want men to do to you,
do the same way to them.”
This means showing empathy,
putting ourselves in the place of the other person,
and asking ourselves, ‘How would I feel
if someone said this about me?’
One situation that may tempt us to engage in harmful gossip
is when we believe we have been wronged by someone.
Instead of applying the counsel
at Matthew 5:23, 24
to talk to the person privately,
we could start talking about it to others who are not involved.
Imagine if after finally talking with the person
you find out he actually did not wrong you at all.
You will have made the situation much worse.
But whether we are right or wrong,
engaging in hurtful speech
will never improve a situation.
Gossip requires a speaker and a listener.
Is it wrong to listen to harmful gossip?
Yes!
Note what Proverbs 17:4 says:
“A wicked man pays attention to hurtful speech,
and a deceptive man listens to a malicious tongue.”
Think about that.
In God’s eyes if we listen to hurtful,
malicious speech, we too bear a heavy responsibility.
By listening to the gossiper,
we are encouraging him to go on.
So, what should you do?
Without taking on an air of self-righteousness,
you could simply say, “Let’s change the subject,”
or “I don’t really feel comfortable talking about this;
after all, she is not here to defend herself.”
And if we find that a brother or sister
likes to gossip,
we may find it easier to avoid harmful gossip
by stopping close association with that person.
Proverbs 20:19 frankly counsels:
“Do not associate with one who loves to gossip.”
So, dear friends, let’s put away harmful gossip.
Doing so, we will maintain
our precious peace and unity.
Brother Kenneth Cook,
a member of the Governing Body,
will now present the final talk of this symposium,
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers —Uncontrolled Anger.”

cn.text: 你说闲话吗？
不说吗？
其实闲聊的时候要是不小心
就会变成说闲话
我们很关心弟兄姐妹
可能会说
“我真的担心张弟兄的身体”
或者
“你有没有听说过王姐妹的传道经历呢？”
这样闲聊有害吗？
一般不会
但我们还是要小心
在提摩太前书5:13
使徒保罗说
有些姐妹“好说闲话，多管闲事”
我们不该总是打听别人的事
或把我们知道的跟别人有关的事都说出来
比如说
张弟兄可能并不想让别人知道
他具体得了什么病
那我们就该保护他的隐私
或者我们本来想说王姐妹的传道经历
说着说着就成了
“她就是这样，总是炫耀自己的传道成果”
要是我们聊别人的时候越讲越负面
就可能变成诽谤
诽谤就是故意歪曲事实
这样做会破坏别人的名声
请想想，为什么闲话会破坏和睦呢？
要是你说了别人的闲话
后来传到了那个人的耳朵里
下次你们见面时
你觉得他脸上会有怎样的表情呢？
让我们一起看箴言25:23
“北风阵阵，带来倾盆大雨
闲言闲语，使人怒容满面”
就像巴勒斯坦的北风
会带来乌云和暴雨
同样，你说别人的那些闲话
也会传到他耳朵里
他再见到你时
一定会沉着脸、怒气冲冲
你们俩的关系会瞬间降到冰点
这种情况下
你肯定会觉得很难堪、很惭愧
但就算你道歉
也很难弥补你对他名声造成的破坏
犹太人有一个古老的故事
有个人在镇上
到处诽谤一个有智慧的人
后来那个说闲话的人意识到自己做错了
就去请求对方原谅
说自己愿意尽力弥补过失
那个有智慧的人提了一个要求
要那个说闲话的人划破一个枕头
把枕头里的羽毛撒在风中
说闲话的人很困惑
但他还是照着做了
然后回去问那个有智慧的人
“你原谅我了吗？”
有智慧的人说
“你先去把那些羽毛收回来给我吧”
“那怎么可能？羽毛都被风吹散了！”
有智慧的人说
“要弥补你说闲话造成的那些伤害
就像要收回那些羽毛那么困难！”
伤人的话一旦说出口
就再也收不回来了
千万不要把羽毛撒在风中！
要是我们说闲话
就会在许多弟兄姐妹之间造成不和
就有这样一个典型的例子
耶路撒冷会众的一些长老
告诉使徒保罗
有人在犹太裔的基督徒当中造谣
他们说
使徒保罗教导人背弃摩西法典
这当然是歪曲事实
保罗从来没有说过任何诋毁法典的话
他在犹太会堂里
甚至会引用希伯来语经卷跟人推理
这些谣言
会让那些新受浸的犹太裔基督徒以为
保罗不尊重耶和华上帝的安排
这会严重破坏会众的和睦
在接下来的短剧中
让我们看看说闲话
会怎样破坏会众弟兄姐妹之间的和睦
你们看过吗？
她是先驱欸
先驱应该做好榜样才对吧？
珍妮还在订阅她的频道吗？
我觉得，她早晚会取消订阅
艾理弟兄，你觉得呢？
觉得什么？
海莉的频道和影片啊
有什么问题吗？
珍妮告诉我
影片都是，你看我
我的衣服，我的头发，我的脸
连莱雅都觉得有问题
其实，社交网站的东西比较片面
很容易让人误解
我以前也觉得别人有问题
但后来发现，我完全错了
嗯，确实会这样
对不起
我不是想打断你们
但如果你有空
可以帮我搬这些书吗？
好吧
谢谢你帮忙
别客气
雷克，刚刚说的事情
我知道你是出于担心
不过还有一个原则
这个原则是我常常提醒自己的
这节经文在箴言18:17
先说案情的人，看起来有理
另一方来对质，就真相大白
我不太懂你的意思
意思是
如果我们只听了一个人的想法
在还没有了解事情的全貌之前
就最好不要太快下结论
而且，就算某个人真的有问题
我们也不该说出去
因为我们也不希望别人这样对待我们
我真的没想到这个，谢谢
我会让他们知道我不该那样说
也要请珍妮直接找海莉谈谈
太好了
长老用箴言18:17
给了雷克一个善意的提醒后
你还记得雷克怎么说吗？
他说
“我真的没想到这个”
没错
他说出那些消极的话之前
确实应该好好想一想
那么
怎样才能除掉闲话
不让它萌芽呢？
看看箴言15:28怎么说
“义人的心经过沉思才回答
恶人的口却涌出种种奸恶”
要是我们想说一些关于别人的负面的话
就要先三思
这并不是说你要用很长时间去思考
只是开口前先想一想
雷克开口前
可以想想哪些问题
就不会像他妻子那样抱怨海莉姐妹呢？
比如他可以想想
我说的这些话是真的吗？
这么说仁慈吗？有爱心吗？
别人听我这样说海莉姐妹
会对海莉有什么看法呢？
另一个能帮助我们除掉闲话的圣经原则
就是耶稣的一句名言
记在路加福音6:31
耶稣说
“你们希望别人怎样对待你们
你们就要怎样对待别人”
意思也就是
要设身处地为别人着想
问问自己
要是别人这么说我
我会有什么感受呢？
还有一种情况也很容易让我们说闲话
就是我们认为别人做了对不起我们的事
有时我们没有按照
以及18:15说的那样
跟对方私下沟通
反而把事情告诉不相干的人
向他们诉苦
想想看
要是你跟对方沟通后
发现他其实并没有做什么对不起你的事
那时你可就追悔莫及了
不管我们是对是错
说别人闲话
只会让问题变得更糟糕
闲话有人说
也得有人听
听别人讲讲闲话也是不对的吗？
当然不对
因为箴言17:4说
“恶人仔细听害人的嘴说话
骗子侧耳听恶毒的舌发言”
想想看
要是我们听别人说恶毒害人的话
在耶和华看来
我们不就成了那个人的帮凶吗？
我们听别人说闲话
就是鼓励他继续说下去
那该怎么办呢？
我们不用批评说闲话的人
但可以转换一下话题
或者你也可以说
“不好意思
你这样说让我有点不舒服
因为他并不在场
我们也不知道他是怎么想的”
如果我们发现某个弟兄或姐妹
很爱说闲话
那最好的方法
可能就是
跟他保持适当的距离
不要聊得太多
箴言20:19说得很坦白
“爱说闲话的， 不可跟他来往”
亲爱的弟兄姐妹
让我们除掉一切闲话
这样就能维系彼此间的团结、促进和睦
中央长老团成员肯尼思·库克弟兄
会发表系列演讲的最后部分
除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——发泄怒气

titles.ko: 패트릭 래프랜카: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—남에 대한 해로운 이야기
titles.en: Patrick LaFranca: “Put Away” Peace Wreckers—Harmful Gossip
titles.cn: 帕特里克·拉弗朗卡：除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——说闲话

title: 가유스 글로켄틴: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—부정직

ko.text: 또 아나니아와 그의 아내도 생각나실 텐데요.
거룩하신 하느님 여호와께서는 우리도 거룩하기를 바라시기 때문에
성경 레위기 19:11에서 고대 이스라엘 사람들에게 권고하셨습니다.
다른 사람을 속여서는 안 된다고 말이죠.
고의적으로 다른 사람이 잘못된 결론에 이르게 하는 행동.
다른 사람과의 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있습니다.
어떻게 부정직이 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있다는 것입니까?
평화와 평화로운 관계는 신뢰심에 기반을 두고 있습니다.
우리가 누군가를 신뢰하는 마음을 갖게 되면
또 서로에게 진실을 말할 때 생깁니다.
성경 표현처럼 “구부러진 말”을 하지 않는 사람들입니다.
그가 하는 모든 말에 의심이 생기게 될 겁니다.
단 한 번의 부정직한 행동도 해로울 수 있죠.
부정직은 그보다 훨씬 더 심각한 해를 초래할 수도 있습니다.
부정직은 전염성이 아주 높은 바이러스에 비유할 수 있습니다.
부정직은 단 하나의 인간관계만 해치는 것이 아니라
한 집단 전체의 연합과 평화를 깨뜨릴 수도 있습니다.
창세기에 나오는 라반과 야곱 사이에 있었던 일들을 보면 그 점을 알 수 있습니다.
하지만 야곱에게는 그 기간이 “단지 며칠” 같았습니다.
레아도 야곱을 속이는 일에 가담한 것입니다.
야곱은 라반이 자신을 속였다는 것을 알게 되었고,
부정직 때문에 그들 사이에 평화가 깨지면서
라헬을 얻기 위해 또다시 7년을 일한 기간은
그리고 라반은 더욱더 뻔뻔하게 야곱을 계속 속였습니다.
부당하게도 야곱의 품삯을 열 번이나 바꾸었죠.
이제 앞 연설에서 봤던 영상의 이어지는 장면을 시청해 보시죠.
두 자매가 카페에서 계속 대화 중입니다.
젊은 자매가 어떻게 진실을 왜곡하고 싶은 유혹을 느끼는지에 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
자매를 이해 못 하는 게 아니야.
헤일리가 올려 놓은 걸 다 본 건 아니지만
에밀리, 자매는 정말 예쁘고 영적인 자매야.
아, 실리아 자매한테 말하지 말 걸 그랬나?
아니 뭐, 잘 물어본 것 같은데?
헤일리가 올린 걸 다 보지는 못하셨대.
그런 건 얘기를 해 줘야 한다고 하셨는데,
실리아 자매도 헤일리에 대해 그렇게 생각했으면
오늘도 저희 부부를 사랑으로 보살펴 주시고 ···
에밀리 자매가 자기가 듣고 싶은 말만 들은 것에 유의하셨나요?
자매는 남편에게 말할 때 모든 사실을 말하지 않았죠.
헤일리 자매가 올린 영상을 실리아 자매는 이상하게 생각하지 않는다는 점을 빼놓았습니다.
실리아 자매는 헤일리에게 조언이 필요하다고 말하지 않았죠.
형제 자매들은 진실을 알 권리가 있습니다.
하지만 에밀리 자매는 진실을 말하지 않았죠.
여호와께서는 평화를 깨뜨리는 이러한 부정직을 우리가 벗어 버리기를 바라십니다.
그러면 어떻게 부정직을 벗어버릴 수 있을까요?
우리가 정직해야 하는 이유를 알려 줍니다.
“여러분은 거짓을 버렸으므로 각자 이웃에게 진실을 말하십시오.
우리가 거짓을 버리고 서로에게 진실을 말해야 하는 이유가 무엇이라고 했죠?
바울은 “우리가 서로에게 속한 지체들이기 때문”이라고 했죠.
그러니까 부정직한 행동은 다른 형제들에게 영향을 미치고
우리가 그들과 누리는 관계에도 영향을 미친다는 것입니다.
어떻게 부정직을 벗어 버릴 수 있을까요?
부정직의 결과와 정직의 결과를 주의 깊이 생각해 보는 겁니다.
바로 이게 옳은 일을 하는 데 도움이 되죠.
당장에는 부정직한 행동이 손쉬운 해결책처럼 보일 수 있지만
정직할 때 우리는 좋은 친구들을 얻게 됩니다.
그 친구들 역시 평화를 누리고 싶어 하고
그래서 자기가 신뢰할 수 있는 사람과 친구가 되고 싶어 하죠.
우리는 선한 양심을 갖게 되고 “하느님과 평화를” 누리게 됩니다.
그러므로 우리 모두 작은 일에서도 항상 진실하게 행동함으로
여호와께서는 불완전한 우리에게 이것이 늘 쉽지는 않다는 것을 아십니다.
우리가 신뢰와 평화를 쌓고 그것을 깨뜨리지 않으려고 노력할 때
우리의 모든 노력을 분명히 축복해 주실 것입니다.
이제 인사 위원회 보조자인 패트릭 래프랜카 형제가
이 심포지엄의 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.
제목은 “평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’ —남에 대한 해로운 이야기”입니다.

en.text: What comes to your mind when you hear the word “dishonesty”?
Maybe you think of Satan, “the father of the lie.”
Or Ananias and his wife come to your mind.
They lost their lives because of lying.
We do not want to imitate such ones.
We avoid lying.
Is that, though, as far as our honesty goes?
Our holy God, Jehovah, wants us to be holy as well,
and that is why he urged the ancient Israelites
not to deceive others
as mentioned at Leviticus 19:11.
Does this not add some color to honesty?
Dishonesty includes (and please take note of this definition)
intentionally leading someone to a wrong conclusion.
For example, by twisting the truth
or by providing only certain details,
we endanger our peace with others.
Why can we say so?
How does dishonesty wreck peace?
Peace and a peaceful relationship
are built on trust.
Trusting someone makes you feel safe and secure
and puts you at ease.
There is no peace without trust.
How do we develop trust?
Trust is the result of spending time together,
speaking the truth with one another.
We trust people who act unselfishly
and do not use “crooked speech,” as the Bible puts it.
If someone deceives us only once or is dishonest in another way,
we might start to question everything they say.
One single act of dishonesty may be enough.
It can ruin their reputation.
As bad as this is, dishonesty has the potential
to create even greater damage.
Dishonesty can be compared
with a highly contagious virus.
Dishonesty breeds dishonesty.
People who have contact with deceitful, dishonest persons
are in danger of being infected.
Dishonesty might not only wreck one relationship
but multiple relationships,
putting the unity and peace of the whole group at risk.
This reminds us of the relationship
between Laban and Jacob in the Bible book of Genesis.
Based on the agreement with Laban,
Jacob worked hard for seven years
in order to marry Laban’s daughter Rachel.
And despite this high price that Jacob had to pay,
those years seemed for him
just like “a few days.”
Sadly, instead of Rachel,
he received the older daughter, Leah, as a wife.
So now Leah was also part of the deception.
What was the result after Jacob had found out
that Laban tricked him?
The trust was gone.
The relationship had suffered to a great degree.
Dishonesty wrecked the peace in those relationships,
and so the following seven years of work for Rachel were bitter.
And Laban’s dishonesty emboldened him to continue in his course.
He unfairly changed Jacob’s wages ten times.
He deceived Jacob.
Because of Laban’s dishonesty,
the peace in the whole family was disrupted.
Let us now continue to watch the next segment of the dramatization.
We left Emily and Celia sitting in a coffee shop.
Please watch carefully, and notice
how Emily is tempted to alter the truth.
You pioneer together.
I know, and that’s why I’m concerned.
Concern is good,
but
is there just a little bit of envy in there?
I thought you would understand.
I think I understand your feelings.
But not about Haley?
I haven’t seen all her posts.
There’s nothing immoral, is there?
No.
Good. That’s not like her.
Now, if
it’s a case of her being more careful how she comes across,
that’s another matter.
Why don’t you talk to her?
Maybe.
Emily, you are a beautiful, spiritual sister.
You know,
for years,
I had a bad habit of comparing myself to others.
My own insecurity hurt me
and my closest friends.
So you don’t think I should’ve spoken to Celia?
No, I’m glad you asked Celia about it
—someone you trust.
What did she say?
Well, she definitely understands how I feel.
Good.
And about Haley’s posts?
Well, she hasn’t seen everything she has out there.
Hmm.
She did say that Haley
needs to be more careful
how she comes across.
What did she suggest?
That I should tell her that she needs to stop,
but I’m too worked up.
Look,
if Celia agrees that Haley is doing something she shouldn’t,
you should talk to her.
You’ll find the right time.
Thanks for understanding.
I’m hungry.
Can you say the prayer?
Sure.
Jehovah, we’d like to praise you
for your generosity and kindness . . .
Did you notice how Emily just heard what she wanted to hear?
In talking to her husband, Jake, she painted an incomplete picture.
She did not relay that Celia had no opinion
about the social media posts of Haley.
And contrary to what she told her husband,
Celia did not encourage her to tell Haley to stop.
Our brothers and sisters deserve the truth.
But Emily didn’t relay that, did she?
She was dishonest, something that can have
a damaging effect, as we will see later.
Jehovah wants us to put away
this peace wrecker, dishonesty.
He wants us to always be truthful,
even in small matters.
Therefore, how do we put away dishonesty?
Let us please turn to Ephesians chapter 4.
Here the apostle Paul reminds us
of a reason to be honest.
This is Ephesians chapter 4,
and we want to read verse 25:
“Therefore, now that you have put away deceit,
“each one of you speak truth with his neighbor,
because we are members belonging to one another.”
Did you notice why we put away deceit
and speak truth with one another?
Paul says: “Because we are members belonging to one another.”
In other words, Paul reminds us of the fact
that dishonesty affects others
—our brothers and our relationship with them.
So, then, knowing this,
how can we put away dishonesty?
The answer is:
By considering the consequences of dishonesty and honesty.
This will help us to do the right thing.
Now, what are the consequences of dishonesty?
As we’ve seen in the case of Laban and Jacob,
it will disrupt the peace with others.
And since Jehovah hates dishonesty,
it will also disrupt our peace with Jehovah.
On the other hand,
what are the consequences of honesty?
While dishonesty might seem in the moment to be the easier way out,
in the long run,
honesty will enable us to have good friends.
They want to enjoy peace as well,
and therefore they are also searching
for someone they can trust.
And in this way, we are
like ‘body members belonging to one another.’
And even more important,
we will enjoy a good conscience
and “peace with God.”
Let us, therefore, put away this peace wrecker (dishonesty)
by sticking to the truth even in small things.
Dear brothers and sisters, Jehovah knows
that for us imperfect humans
this is not always easy.
Yet, he promises to help us
and to bless every step we take
to build trust and peace
and not to wreck it.
Brother Patrick LaFranca, a helper to the Personnel Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers—Harmful Gossip.”
