titles.ko: 가유스 글로켄틴: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—부정직
titles.en: Gajus Glockentin: “Put Away” Peace Wreckers—Dishonesty
titles.cn: 盖乌斯·格洛肯汀：除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——不诚实

title: 세스 하이엇: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—시기심

ko.text: 시기심이 어떻게 나타나는지 알아차리는 것은 중요한 일입니다.
그런 감정을 방치하면 우린 영적으로 죽게 될 수 있습니다.
한 가지는 우리 모두가 잘 아는 것이죠.
시기심이 있으면 다른 사람이 가진 것을 탐내게 됩니다.
사실 이 두 번째가 더 위험하다고 할 수 있는데요.
시기심은 다른 사람이 가진 것을 탐내는 데서 그치지 않습니다.
그 사람이 그것을 갖지 못하게 되기를 바라죠.
예수가 사람들에게 정말 많은 사랑을 받았기 때문입니다.
하지만 그들은 사람들을 대하는 자신들의 방식을 바로잡으려 하지 않고
그분의 좋은 평판을 망치려고 그렇게 한 것이죠.
예수께서 가지셨던 것을 탐낸 것만이 아니라
여러 가지 “육체의 일”들 중 하나로 언급되는 것도 놀라운 일이 아닙니다.
시기심은 사람 간의 관계를 약화시키거나 손상시키고 심지어 파괴합니다.
그 점을 보여 주는 한 가지 예는
야곱은 열두 아들 중 한 아들을 특히 사랑했는데
그래서 요셉의 형들은 요셉을 시기하게 됩니다.
그는 요셉 때문에 여러 해 동안 슬퍼했습니다.
시기심 때문에 정말 끔찍한 일이 일어난 겁니다!
사랑, 동정심, 친절 같은 특성을 나타내지 못한다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
미움, 분쟁, 격분과 같은 해로운 특성들이 채워지게 됩니다.
시기심이 회중의 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있을까요?
고라와 다단과 아비람의 예를 생각해 보겠습니다.
그 세 사람은 이스라엘 회중 가운데서 모세와 아론을 시기했습니다.
그들은 여호와의 대표자들에 대해 부정적이고 비판적으로 말하기 시작했는데,
심지어 모세가 군왕 노릇을 하며 다른 사람들 위에 자신을 높인다고 비난했습니다.
사실 여호와께서 모세와 아론에게 책임 있는 위치를 맡기셨는데
한동안 회중에서는 평화를 찾아볼 수가 없었죠.
여호와께서 시기심을 어떻게 보시는지 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
‘내가 다른 사람에게 해를 입히면서까지 뭔가를 원하는 일은 절대 없을 거야.’
자기도 모르게 시기하게 될 수 있죠.
시기심이 어떻게 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있는지 보시겠습니다.
너무 잘난 척하는 거 같지 않으세요?
전에도 그 얘기 했던 거 같은데.
그 자매는 헤일리 자매의 동기를 의심했죠.
또한 헤일리 자매의 평판에 해가 될 수 있는 말을 했습니다.
그럼 우리는 어떻게 시기심을 물리칠 수 있습니까?
두 가지 아름다운 특성들을 기르기 위해 노력하는 것입니다.
먼저, 겸손에 관한 성경 말씀을 살펴보시죠.
자신을 실제보다 더 중요하게 생각하는 것입니다.
이 면에서 예수 시대의 종교 지도자들은 어땠을까요?
그들이 자신을 실제보다 더 중요한 사람으로 여겼을까요?
하지만 우리 중 누구라도 그렇게 될 수 있습니다.
“겸손하게 [또는, 자기를 낮추는 정신으로] 남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기라”고,
다시 말해 자신보다 남을 더 중요한 사람으로 여기라고 말합니다.
우리가 이런 정신 태도를 가질 때
4절의 이러한 말씀과 같이 할 수 있게 됩니다.
“여러분 자신의 일에만 관심을 갖지 말고 다른 사람들의 일에도 관심을 가지십시오.”
네, 겸손한 사람은 다른 사람들에게 관심을 갖습니다.
자신이 남보다 더 나은 대우를 받아야 한다고 생각하지 않죠.
그에 더해 자기가 가진 것으로 만족하는 태도도 중요합니다.
자신의 특권이나 소유물을 다른 사람이 가진 것과 비교하지 않는 거죠.
여호와의 도움으로 우리는 이 아름다운 특성들을 기를 수 있습니다.
그러면 시기심이 들어설 자리가 없을 것입니다.
또한 우리의 평화가 더 커질 것입니다.
마음의 평화는 물론, 가정과 회중에서 더 큰 평화를 누리게 될 겁니다.
여호와께서는 분명 그것을 보시고 정말 기뻐하실 것입니다.
이제 출판 위원회 보조자인 가유스 글로켄틴 형제가
이 심포지엄의 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.

en.text: What is envy?
Do you know?
It’s important that we be able to identify the symptoms of envy.
Why?
Because envy is an expression of hatred.
It’s an enemy of peace.
And if left unchecked,
it can result in spiritual death.
As described in the Bible, envy has two symptoms.
The first is probably more familiar.
An envious person wants
what someone else has.
It’s the second symptom
that makes envy especially dangerous.
An envious person not only wants what someone else has,
but he also doesn’t want the other person to have it.
Here’s an example:
In the first century, Jewish religious leaders envied Jesus
because Jesus was much appreciated by the common people.
Jesus dealt with people,
including lowly ones, in a way that dignified them.
As a result, he was appreciated.
The religious leaders envied him.
But rather than adjusting their own way of dealing with people,
they attacked Jesus verbally
in an effort to destroy his good reputation.
They spread malicious slander.
Not only did they want what Jesus had,
but also they didn’t want Jesus to have it.
No wonder envy is listed as one of “the works of the flesh”
at Galatians 5:21.
It’s a dangerous quality
that we need to avoid.
How does envy disrupt peace?
Envy undermines, damages,
or even destroys relationships
in the family and in the congregation.
Consider the example of Jacob
and his 12 sons.
Jacob had special affection for one of his sons, Joseph.
As a result, Joseph’s brothers became envious.
How did the envy manifest itself?
What was the fruitage?
Well, they dealt treacherously with Joseph, selling him into slavery.
And as if that weren’t bad enough, they compounded their wrong
by lying to Jacob,
telling him that Joseph was dead.
According to the Bible account,
Jacob “refused to be comforted.”
He mourned Joseph for years.
What a terrible consequence of envy!
It’s clear that envy
allows no room for love,
compassion, or kindness.
Those qualities go out the window.
And they’re replaced by qualities
such as hatred, strife, fits of anger.
Can envy disrupt the peace of a congregation?
Consider the examples of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
They envied Moses and Aaron
in the congregation of Israel.
How did that envy manifest itself?
Well, they began to speak negatively—critically—
of Jehovah’s representatives, even accusing Moses
of playing the prince and lifting himself up above the others.
They forgot that Jehovah
had put Moses and Aaron in their positions of responsibility.
How did Jehovah react
to that manifestation of envy?
He destroyed those three men and all who supported them.
For a time, the congregation was robbed of its peace,
and the accounts certainly provide some insight
into Jehovah’s view of envy.
Now, by this point, you’re no doubt thinking,
‘I would never want something so badly that I would
damage someone else to get it.’
But we’re all imperfect.
We have a treacherous heart,
and envy is insidious.
In the following dramatization,
notice how envy threatens to disrupt peace.
Really?
Bad news?
She’s a sweetie.
It reminds me that I want to speak to her about a necklace.
You too?
You don’t think she’s showing off?
No.
Everyone thinks she’s “Miss Wonderful”;
she’s starting to agree.
Is this just about Haley?
It seems it’s all about Haley.
Your tea is getting cold.
And you’re changing the subject.
No,
but you’ve brought this up before.
What is it?
You’re friends; you pioneer together.
Yeah, and that’s why I’m concerned.
Concern is good,
but
is there just a little bit of envy in there?
What did you notice?
Well, Emily is suffering from an onset of envy.
Did you notice how she questioned Haley’s motives
and potentially called Haley’s reputation into question?
It could happen to any one of us.
So how do we battle and conquer envy?
By cultivating two beautiful qualities,
humility and contentment.
Let’s see what the Bible has to say about humility.
Turn with me, please, to Philippians chapter 2,
and we’re going to begin reading in verse 3
—Philippians 2:3:
“Do nothing out of contentiousness
or out of egotism.”
What is egotism?
Well, it’s having an exaggerated opinion of oneself.
Do you think that the religious leaders in Jesus’ day,
Joseph’s brothers,
Korah, Dathan, and Abiram
had this affliction?
Did they have an exaggerated view of themselves?
Without question!
But it’s an affliction that could affect any one of us.
What is the solution?
Well, Paul continues:
“But with humility [or, lowliness of mind]
consider others superior to you”
—or consider others
as more important than yourself.
Now, that kind of mindset
allows a person to do what’s stated in verse 4:
“As you look out not only
“for your own interests,
but also for the interests of others.”
A humble person
looks out for others.
He doesn’t feel that he deserves
more than others.
Contentment—a content person is satisfied with what he has.
He doesn’t compare his privilege or his possession
with another person’s privilege or possession.
He’s content.
Humility, contentment
—with Jehovah’s help we can cultivate these beautiful qualities—
qualities that leave no room for envy.
And in doing so, we promote peace
—inner peace, peace in our family,
and peace in the congregation.
And you can be sure that Jehovah appreciates that.
Brother Gajus Glockentin, a helper to the Publishing Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers—Dishonesty.”

cn.text: 你知道妒忌是什么意思吗？
我们看出自己有没有妒忌别人
其实很重要
为什么呢？
因为妒忌是仇恨的一种表现
是和睦与安宁的敌人
要是不改变这种心态
就肯定会破坏我们跟耶和华的关系
我们看圣经就知道
妒忌别人的人有两种症状
第一种大家都知道
就是很想要得到别人拥有的东西
不过妒忌的第二种症状
就比第一种更危险
这种妒忌心
不仅让他想要得到别人拥有的东西
还希望对方失去这些东西
一个例子是
在1世纪犹太宗教领袖妒忌耶稣
因为耶稣深受平民百姓的爱戴
耶稣很愿意跟民众来往
关心弱势群体
很尊重他们
这就是大家喜欢耶稣的原因
宗教领袖们却妒火中烧
他们没有检讨自己对待民众的方式
反而到处说耶稣的坏话
散播谣言
诽谤耶稣
想用这种手段来破坏他的名声
他们不仅想像耶稣那样受人欢迎
还想让耶稣被人唾弃
难怪加拉太书5:21
把妒忌列为顺应罪性的行为
我们千万要避免这种恶劣的心态！
为什么妒忌会破坏和睦呢？
因为妒忌会造成人与人之间的裂痕
甚至完全毁掉
我们跟家人和弟兄姐妹的关系
让我们想想雅各和他的12个儿子之间的事
雅各特别宠爱其中一个儿子——约瑟
这让约瑟的哥哥们十分妒忌
结果怎么样？
他的哥哥们做了什么事呢？
他们很残忍，把约瑟卖给人做奴隶
而且他们不知悔改、错上加错
还合伙骗父亲雅各
说约瑟死了
圣经说雅各
“不肯接受安慰”
伤心欲绝
他为约瑟哀悼了很多年
妒忌带来多么可怕的后果啊！
妒忌心会让人没有办法显出
爱心、怜恤、仁慈
这些美德都离他而去了
取而代之的，是一些恶劣的品行
比如仇恨、争吵和愤怒
那妒忌会破坏会众的和睦吗？
让我们想想可拉、大坦和亚比兰的例子
他们非常妒忌摩西和亚伦
羡慕他们在会众里的地位
结果他们做了什么事呢？
他们用恶毒的话批评耶和华的这两个代表
还指控摩西
说他作威作福
把自己凌驾于会众之上
他们完全忘了
是耶和华给摩西和亚伦职责
去带领会众的
耶和华怎样处置这群充满妒忌心的人呢？
他消灭了那三个人和他们的党羽
他们破坏会众的和睦
让人人都不得安宁
这段记载确实让我们看出
耶和华对妒忌的看法
说到这里
你可能会想
我才不会为了想要得到某个东西
而去伤害别人呢！
可是我们都不完美
人心比什么都诡诈
妒忌心是不容易察觉的
在接下来的短剧
请注意妒忌会怎样破坏和睦
又来了！
怎么了？
她好可爱
我正想找她买一条项链
什么？
你不觉得她太高调了吗？
还好吧
大家都觉得她超级完美的
她自己也没有否认
你找我就是因为她？
那还能是因为谁？
这家店的奶茶不错
你是在转移话题吗？
不是
但这不是你第一次说她的事了
你怎么了？
你们不是好朋友
一起做先驱吗？
是啊，所以我才这么关心她
关心没有错
但其中有没有掺杂一点妒忌呢？
你注意到了吗？
珍妮姐妹开始出现妒忌的症状了
我们看到她质疑海莉姐妹的动机
而且
还说了一些
可能会破坏海莉名声的话
我们也可能会犯同样的错误
那么
我们应该怎样克服妒忌的倾向呢？
就是培养两种美好的品格
谦卑和知足
关于谦卑，让我们看看圣经怎么说
请跟我一起翻开腓立比书第2章
我们会从第3节开始读
腓立比书2:3
“做什么都不要争强好胜，不要自命不凡”
自命不凡
也就是以为自己有多么多么了不起
你觉得
耶稣时代的宗教领袖
约瑟的哥哥们
可拉、大坦和亚比兰
有这种症状吗？
他们一个个都自命不凡
以自我为中心
要是我们
也不小心变成这样
那该怎么办呢？
保罗接着劝勉我们说
“要谦卑，看别人比自己优秀”
也就是
把别人看得比自己还要重要
我们有这种心态
就会按照第4节说的去做
“不要只关心自己，也要关心别人”
谦卑的人
会为人着想
他不会觉得自己得到的
应该要比别人多
还有知足
一个知足的人会因为自己拥有的而感到满足
他不会眼红别人有什么东西
或是有什么服务机会
他会知足
谦卑、知足
有耶和华的帮助
我们一定能培养这两种美德
这样就可以把妒忌拒之门外
我们培养这些美德就能享有内心的安宁
也能维系家人和会众的和睦关系
耶和华也一定会为你付出的努力感到高兴！
出版委员会助手
盖乌斯·格洛肯汀弟兄

除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——不诚实

titles.ko: 세스 하이엇: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—시기심

title: 해럴드 코컨: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—합당하지 않은 자랑

ko.text: 아마 이러한 표현들이 연상되실 수 있는데요.
“여러분은 이전의 행로를 따르며 기만적인 욕망에 이끌려 썩고 있는
네, 우린 “옛 인간성을 벗어 버”려야 했습니다.
하지만 이렇게 벗어 버리는 것에 더해
“여러분은 자신을 지배하는 정신 태도를 계속 새롭게 하고”.
특히 옛 인간성에 속한 특성들 중 일부는 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있기 때문입니다.
다시 입지 말아야 할 그러한 특성
각 연설에서 다음 요점을 살펴볼 것입니다.
첫째, 각 특성들은 정확히 무엇을 가리킵니까?
둘째, 그 특성들이 어떻게 평화를 깨뜨리며,
셋째, 그 특성들을 어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있습니까?
우리가 첫 번째로 살펴볼 특성은 무엇입니까?
“네 입이 아니라 남이 너를 칭찬하게 하고,
네 입술이 아니라 다른 사람이 너를 칭찬하게 하여라.”
교만하면 다른 사람들 위로 우리 자신을 높이게 되죠.
그 회중이 겪고 있는 분열과 평화가 깨진 상태에 대해 이야기했습니다.
바울, 아볼로, 게바와 같은 사람을 두고요.
자신과 다른 사람들에게 지나치게 주의를 기울이고 있었던 겁니다.
예를 들어 여러 명이 모여 있는데
이런 말이 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있을까요?
어떤 성과에 대해 여호와께 감사를 드리는 것은 잘못이 아닙니다.
하지만 자신이 한 일에 대한 합당하지 않은 자랑은
사람들이 정말 자기 자랑을 많이 하지 않나요?
사람들은 소셜 미디어에 올리는 것을 통해
자기가 대단한 사람인 것처럼 보이고 싶어 합니다.
또 호화로운 휴가 같은 것들을 말이죠.
합당하지 않게 자랑해서 평화를 깨뜨리는 것은 정말 해로울 수 있습니다.
성경에 나오는 하만의 예가 그걸 잘 보여 주죠.
아주 높은 자리에 앉힌 것을 자랑합니다.
뿐만 아니라 그는 분노에 차 있었습니다.
그가 모르드개를 매달려고 세운 바로 그 기둥에
이사야 29:20에서 이렇게 알려 주는 바와 같습니다.
우리 자신과 다른 사람에게 아주 해로운 영향을 미치기 때문에
우리는 자랑한다는 인상조차 주지 않으려 하죠.
한 자매의 행동이 어떻게 자랑하는 것으로
그런데 본의 아니게 그렇게 될 수 있습니다.
형제 자매들을 잘 알 때 커지게 됩니다.
내가 이걸 그냥 혼자 할 수가 없어서.
어떤 패션에도 매치하시기가 너무 좋으세요. -허, 이거 봤어?
이런 제품들 더 알아보고 싶지 않으세요?
자신의 할머니를 참을성 있게 잘 보살폈죠.
이 광고를 다른 한 자매가 봤죠.
생각해 봐야 한다는 점을 교훈해 줍니다.
어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있는가 하는 것입니다.
그러기 위해 항상 기억해야 될 점이 있습니다.
사실, 당신이 가진 것 가운데서 받지 않은 것이 무엇이 있습니까?
받은 것이라면 왜 받지 않은 것처럼 자랑합니까?”
우리가 가진 좋은 것에 대해 여호와께 모든 영예를 돌려야 한다는 겁니다.
다윗왕은 이 모든 것을 다 가지고 있었죠.
또 그분의 뜻을 이루는 데 그분께 사용될 수 있는 영예에 대해 자랑하라는 것입니다.
다른 형제 자매들이 가진 훌륭한 특성들에 대해 이야기하는 것입니다.
겸손하고 겸허한 사람은 자기에 대해 자랑하지 않고
여호와께서 그분의 일에서 어떻게 그들을 사용하고 축복하고 계신지 보려고 합니다.
그러므로 합당하지 않은 자랑이라는 이 특성을 벗어 버리고
우리가 이룬 일에 대해 여호와께 감사와 영예를 돌리고
형제 자매들이 훌륭한 특성들을 가진 것과
여호와께서 그들을 사용하시는 것에 대해 칭찬하는 것입니다.
또 형제들과 누리는 소중한 평화를 유지하게 될 것입니다.
이제 봉사 위원회 보조자인 세스 하이엇 형제가 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.

en.text: What comes to your mind when you hear the expression “put away”?
You may think of related expressions
such as “cast aside,” “dispose of,”
“discard,” “get rid of.”
What did we have to put away to become a Christian?
The Bible in the book
of Ephesians 4:22 provides the answer.
That’s Ephesians 4:22:
“You were taught to put away the old personality
“that conforms to your former course of conduct
and that is being corrupted according to its deceptive desires.”
So we had “to put away the old personality.”
But it’s one thing to put it away;
it’s something else to keep it away.
And that’s why in the very next verse, verse 23,
Paul encourages us to do this:
“And you should continue to be made new
in your dominant mental attitude.”
It’s so important to keep it away,
because the old personality has traits
that can become peace wreckers.
This symposium will consider five peace wreckers
that we should put away and keep away.
Each talk will include the following main points:
(1) It will define the peace wrecker,
(2) it will explain how it wrecks peace,
and (3) we will consider how to put it away.
What is the very first one that we’re going to talk about?
It is inappropriate boasting.
What is inappropriate boasting?
Basically, it’s self-praise,
and the Bible condemns self-praise
Notice Proverbs 27:2:
“Let someone else praise you,
“and not your own mouth;
others, and not your own lips.”
Self-praise is an evidence of pride
that causes one to elevate himself above others.
Some might develop an unhealthy pride
about their accomplishments, even in the ministry.
It happened in the first century.
Paul had to write to the Corinthian congregation
about the dissensions that they were having,
the lack of peace they were experiencing.
Why?
Well, some in the congregation were “puffed up with pride” about themselves
or other men,
such as Paul, Apollos, Cephas.
They were giving too much attention to themselves
and to other men.
Well, how could that happen today?
Well, let’s imagine a group of brothers talking,
and one in the group says,
“With Jehovah’s help and with diligent prayer and effort,
I finally got a Bible study.”
But right away, another one in the group proudly declares,
“I have four Bible studies;
two are attending meetings, and one will soon be baptized.”
Could such a statement be a peace wrecker?
How does inappropriate boasting wreck peace?
Well, it’s not wrong to take pleasure in our work
and to thank Jehovah for the success that we may have.
But inappropriate boasting about our accomplishments
can stir up competition, envy, and rivalry.
We must remember that self-promotion
does not originate with our heavenly Father, “the God of peace.”
Where does it originate?
First John 2:16 says:
“The showy display of one’s means of life
“does not originate with the Father,
but originates with the world.”
And would you not agree that the world is filled with self-praise?
Even on their social media, we see this.
Some of the material that people post on social media
is designed to make one appear very important.
And it is a showy display
of their accomplishments, their material possessions,
or their expensive vacations that they enjoy.
In other words, it’s all about “look at me.”
Well, we want to avoid getting caught up
in the world’s spirit of self-promotion
that wrecks peace.
To illustrate just how devastating
the peace wrecker’s inappropriate boasting can be,
let’s briefly consider the Bible character Haman.
He was a proud and haughty man,
and he boasted a lot.
Esther chapter 5 tells us
that he was boasting with his family and friends
about his wealth, his many sons,
how the king had promoted him to a high station,
that he was above all the other servants,
and that he’d had a special meal, or banquet,
with the king and queen.
But Haman was hateful and arrogant.
And he was plotting to kill Jehovah’s faithful servant Mordecai.
But his scheme and his attitudes were exposed.
And what happened?
The very stake that Haman had built
to hang Mordecai on he was hung on.
And it reminds us —doesn’t it?—
that at Isaiah 29:20, the Bible says:
“The boaster will come to his finish.”
So because of the devastating effects
that improper boasting can have on ourselves and others,
we do not even want to give the impression of boasting.
In the following dramatization,
notice how a sister’s actions
are misunderstood as boasting.
“Put away from yourselves every kind
“of malicious bitterness, anger, wrath,
“screaming, and abusive speech,
as well as everything injurious.”
Did anyone start the day thinking,
‘I believe I’ll show malicious bitterness to my brother today’?
Of course not!
And yet the potential is there, isn’t it?
But genuine affection fights peace wreckers.
And affection grows when we really know our brothers and sisters well.
We remember their joys
and pains,
their selfless zeal,
how they came to love Jehovah,
and what they endure.
I’ll get back as soon as I can.
Love you. Bye.
Oh, no!
Haley, love?
So sorry, I’ve got to run.
OK. I’ll ring you about this week.
Thanks. Love you both.
See you!
The afternoon would look better.
Nana!
Hello, Haley, darling.
I’m so, so sorry.
Oh, it’s not too bad.
I’ve got this.
Oh.
How are you though?
Thank you. I’m so sorry.
Oh, poor thing.
Let me clear this up.
Thank you.
Oh, Nana, it’s Sunday today, isn’t it?
This one.
It’s felt like such a long day, hasn’t it?
It has felt like a long day.
Thanks.
Sleep well.
Hello, everyone.
Haley from DeNure Design here,
helping you to be effortlessly elegant.
I want to welcome my new followers and thank everyone
for subscribing to this channel.
So first up, I’ve got this gorgeous earring and necklace set.
And as you can see, the first disc I’ve done is in this warm nude tone,
and that’s great because it goes . . .
Can you believe her?
Haley’s business feed?
But what makes this set is really special.
It’s giving you that understated elegant look.
If you haven’t done so already, please hit the subscribe button below.
Because as you know,
when you look this good, you feel great.
Was the sister in this video boasting inappropriately?
No, she was a humble servant of Jehovah,
kindly and patiently helping her elderly relative.
But do you recall her business website
and the presentation she made about her jewelry products?
She said,
“When you look this good, you feel great.”
Her Christian sister was upset
and took those comments and her actions
to be boastful.
Well, this video reminds us
to think about how our words and our actions
may appear to others.
So now we’re going to get to the question:
How do we put away inappropriate boasting?
A key point that we must always remember
to help us to do just that is recorded in the book
of 1 Corinthians 4:7,
1 Corinthians 4:7:
“For who makes you different from another?
“Indeed, what do you have that you did not receive?
“If, in fact, you did receive it,
why do you boast as though you did not receive it?”
What’s the point of this scripture?
We do not want to boast about ourselves
but give all credit to Jehovah for the good that we can do.
Now, some people are proud about their good looks,
their popularity, their wealth, their position,
their physical strength, their musical ability.
But remember, King David of ancient Israel
had all of those assets.
But throughout his entire life,
he never became a boastful person.
He remained humble.
Why?
At Psalm 113:5-8,
David gave all credit to Jehovah.
He said that in his case Jehovah stooped down
and took this “lowly” one and raised him up
to “sit with nobles.”
And on every occasion that he had,
David would always say, ‘Praise Jehovah,
boast about his holy name.’
Well, we, like David, should “boast in Jehovah.”
The apostle Paul encouraged us to do that at 1 Corinthians 1:31:
“The one who boasts, let him boast in Jehovah.”
What does that mean?
It means that we boast in the privilege of knowing the true God
and of being able to be used by him to accomplish his will.
Now, another way that we can put away improper boasting
is to not talk about ourselves,
but to acknowledge the good and the fine qualities
that our fellow workers have.
Humble and modest people don’t brag about what they do,
but they turn their attention to their fellow workers
and see how Jehovah is using them
and blessing them in his service.
And when we do that,
that creates a very peaceful, happy environment.
Well, may we continue to put away and keep away
inappropriate boasting—self-praise.
How?
By giving praise and thanks and honor to Jehovah for our accomplishments
and by commending our fellow workers for all the good qualities they have
and for how Jehovah is using them in his service.
By doing so, we will preserve our precious possession of peace
with Jehovah and with our brothers.
Brother Seth Hyatt, a helper to the Service Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers—Envy.”

cn.text: 听到“除掉”这个词语
会让你想到什么呢？
你可能会想到一些词语
例如“扔掉”
“清理”
“丢掉”
“抛弃”
作为基督徒，我们要除掉什么呢？
圣经的以弗所书4:22告诉我们答案
以弗所书4:22说
“你们学过，要除掉旧品格
这旧品格与你们以往的行为一致
随着骗人的欲望而渐渐腐化”
所以我们必须除掉旧品格
但只是除掉并不够，还要避免再捡回来
这也就是为什么保罗在23节
鼓励我们这样做
他说:“要不断更新你们的思维模式”
根除旧品格很重要
因为旧品格会大大破坏
人与人之间的和睦关系
这个系列演讲会讨论
五种破坏和睦的旧品格
这些都是我们应该除掉的
每个演讲都会包含三个要点
1. 这种旧品格指的是什么？
2. 为什么这种品格会破坏和睦？
3. 这种品格该怎样除掉？
那么，第一个
我们想谈谈的旧品格是什么呢？
就是自夸
自夸是什么意思呢？
简单来说，就是吹捧自己
圣经谴责这种行为
请留意箴言27:2
“要让别人称赞你，不要自卖自夸
等其他人赞赏你，不要自吹自擂”
吹捧自己是骄傲的表现
这样的人觉得自己高人一等
比别人厉害
他们也许因为自己的成就
或传道方面的成果
就自以为了不起
1世纪就有这样的情况
当时的哥林多会众充满纷争
弟兄姐妹彼此不合
所以保罗必须写信给他们
会众里有些人自高自大
或者喜欢吹捧别人
例如吹捧保罗、亚波罗和矶法
他们把太多注意力放在自己和别人身上
今天也会有这样的情况吗？
想象一下，一些弟兄在聊天
其中一个说
“我一直努力、一直祷告
耶和华终于让我有一个圣经学生了！”
这时另一个弟兄马上自豪地说
“我有四个圣经学生
两个已经在参加聚会
还有一个快要受浸了！”
他这样讲会不会破坏和睦呢？
想一想，为什么自夸会破坏和睦呢？
当然
如果耶和华帮助我们取得了一些成就
为此高兴并没有什么不对
不过，夸耀自己的成就
很容易导致竞争、嫉妒和分裂
我们要记得“赐人和睦的上帝”不会自夸
那这种精神是从哪里来的呢？
约翰一书2:16说
“炫耀财物的行为
不是源于天父的
而是源于世界的”
的确，这个世界上有很多人
都喜欢炫耀自己
这在社交平台上也很常见
有些人在社交平台上发布东西
主要是为了炫耀和突显自己
他们炫耀自己的成就
自己拥有的东西
或自己的假期有多豪华、多享受
他们好像在说
“看我，看我”
我们都想避开这种世界的精神
不自吹自擂、破坏和睦
那么自夸这种精神
到底会带来多严重的后果呢？
让我们来看看一个圣经人物
哈曼
他目中无人，很爱吹嘘
以斯帖记第5章提到
哈曼向家人和朋友炫耀
自己多么荣华富贵、儿子众多
又炫耀国王怎样提拔他
让他超越其他人
他还说
国王和王后为他摆设了特别的宴席
其实他心胸狭窄
一心只想杀死耶和华的忠仆末底改
但是哈曼的诡计被揭穿了
结果怎样呢？
他想用一根木柱处死末底改
没想到死在上面的却是他自己
这让我们想到以赛亚书29:20
经文说
自夸的人会“消失”
也就是被消灭
既然自夸会对自己和别人
造成严重的影响
我们真的不想让人以为
我们是爱自夸的人
在接下来的短剧里
我们来看看一个姐妹做了什么
让别人误以为她很爱自夸
你们要除掉一切恶毒
怒气、愤恨、叫骂、伤人的话
以及一切有害的事
你会不会早上一起床就想
今天我要用恶毒的方式来对待弟兄姐妹?
肯定不会
但如果我们不小心就可能伤害别人
培养温情能帮助我们促进和睦
而我们越认识弟兄姐妹
就越容易对他们表现温情
因为我们知道他们经历过什么
受过什么伤
也知道他们怎么认识真理
怎样表现热心
以及正在面对什么考验
好的，我马上回去
别着急
哎呀，真是的……
海莉要走了吗？
对，我有事要先走
我再给你打电话
－那我走了   －拜拜
那我们先约下午
－奶奶！   －你回来了
我又弄成这样，真对不起
没关系的，奶奶
我来收拾
你真好
你没事吧？
我没事，真对不起
真的没关系，奶奶
奶奶，今天是星期天
要吃这个
好，我知道了
累了吧，早点休息
晚安
哈喽，大家好
我是你的美丽顾问海莉
让你从头到脚都美丽
我想欢迎关注我的新朋友
谢谢你们订阅我的频道
首先要向你推荐的是
这款个性又百搭的耳环
我特地选择了现在最流行的莫兰迪色系
她在做什么？
不就是在卖东西吗？
戴上这副耳环会让你与众不同
魅力四射，充满女人味
还没有订阅我频道的朋友们
抓紧机会，赶快订阅
只要你光鲜亮丽
就能跟我一样充满自信
短片中的海莉姐妹是个爱自夸的人吗？
不是
她其实很谦卑
非常体贴而耐心地照顾她的奶奶
不过
你记得她怎样在网上
介绍自己制作的首饰吗？
她说
“只要你光鲜亮丽
就能跟我一样充满自信！”
这让另一个姐妹很不舒服
觉得海莉姐妹说的做的都是在炫耀自己
这个短片提醒我们
要想想自己的言行会给人留下什么印象
那么，让我们考虑一下这个问题
怎样除掉自夸这种旧品格？
有一点很重要，值得我们谨记
这句话就在哥林多前书4:7
一起来看哥林多前书4:7
经文说
“使你跟别人不同的是谁呢？
你有什么不是领受的呢？
既然都是领受的
为什么还要夸耀，好像不是领受的呢？”
经文要强调什么呢？
我们不该夸耀自己
而是应该把全部的功劳都归给耶和华
今天有些人很爱夸耀自己长得好看
受人欢迎、很有钱
社会地位高、体力好
或有音乐才华
其实，这一切以色列王大卫都有
但他一生都很谦卑，从来不夸耀自己
大卫是怎样做到的呢？
大卫把功劳都归给耶和华
他说
耶和华上帝“俯身察看”寒微的他
“扶起”他，让他跟尊贵的人同坐
大卫一有机会
就会对别人说
“要赞美耶和华，夸耀他的圣名”
我们也要像他一样“夸耀耶和华”
保罗在哥林多前书1:31这样鼓励我们
“夸耀的人应该因耶和华而夸耀”
这是什么意思呢？
就是我们夸耀的理由
应该是自己有幸认识上帝
而且受他任用去达成他的旨意
我们还能怎样除掉自夸这种旧品格呢？
不要老把话题转到自己身上
要多欣赏弟兄姐妹的美好品格
也要称赞他们
谦虚的人不会吹嘘自己做了什么
反而会关注弟兄姐妹
留意耶和华怎样任用他们
怎样帮助他们取得成功
我们这样做就能营造出和睦愉快的气氛
愿我们不断努力
彻底根除自夸这种旧品格
我们可以怎么做呢？
在取得成就时要赞美、感谢、尊荣耶和华
也要欣赏弟兄姐妹的好品格
留意耶和华怎样任用他们，为此称赞他们
我们这样做
就能好好维护
与弟兄姐妹和耶和华之间
宝贵的和睦关系
传道委员会的助手塞斯·海厄特弟兄
会发表系列演讲的下一部分
除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——妒忌

titles.ko: 해럴드 코컨: 평화를 깨뜨리는 특성을 ‘벗어 버리십시오’—합당하지 않은 자랑
titles.en: Harold Corkern: “Put Away” Peace Wreckers—Inappropriate Boasting
titles.cn: 哈罗德·科克恩：除掉破坏和睦的旧品格——自夸

title: 2022 ‘평화를 추구하십시오!’ 대회: 토요일 오후 회기—1부

ko.text: 여러분 한 분 한 분을 따뜻하게 환영합니다.
대회 프로그램의 토요일 오후에 해당하는 이 회기에서는
우리 각자가 할 수 있는 일을 알아볼 것입니다.
우리 자신의 평화와 다른 사람의 평화가 깨질 수 있죠.
어떤 특성들을 피해야 하는지를 살펴볼 것입니다.
출판 위원회의 보조자인 해럴드 코컨 형제의 연설을
아마 이러한 표현들이 연상되실 수 있는데요.
“여러분은 이전의 행로를 따르며 기만적인 욕망에 이끌려 썩고 있는
네, 우린 “옛 인간성을 벗어 버”려야 했습니다.
하지만 이렇게 벗어 버리는 것에 더해
“여러분은 자신을 지배하는 정신 태도를 계속 새롭게 하고”.
특히 옛 인간성에 속한 특성들 중 일부는 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있기 때문입니다.
다시 입지 말아야 할 그러한 특성
각 연설에서 다음 요점을 살펴볼 것입니다.
첫째, 각 특성들은 정확히 무엇을 가리킵니까?
둘째, 그 특성들이 어떻게 평화를 깨뜨리며,
셋째, 그 특성들을 어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있습니까?
우리가 첫 번째로 살펴볼 특성은 무엇입니까?
“네 입이 아니라 남이 너를 칭찬하게 하고,
네 입술이 아니라 다른 사람이 너를 칭찬하게 하여라.”
교만하면 다른 사람들 위로 우리 자신을 높이게 되죠.
그 회중이 겪고 있는 분열과 평화가 깨진 상태에 대해 이야기했습니다.
바울, 아볼로, 게바와 같은 사람을 두고요.
자신과 다른 사람들에게 지나치게 주의를 기울이고 있었던 겁니다.
예를 들어 여러 명이 모여 있는데
이런 말이 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있을까요?
어떤 성과에 대해 여호와께 감사를 드리는 것은 잘못이 아닙니다.
하지만 자신이 한 일에 대한 합당하지 않은 자랑은
사람들이 정말 자기 자랑을 많이 하지 않나요?
사람들은 소셜 미디어에 올리는 것을 통해
자기가 대단한 사람인 것처럼 보이고 싶어 합니다.
또 호화로운 휴가 같은 것들을 말이죠.
합당하지 않게 자랑해서 평화를 깨뜨리는 것은 정말 해로울 수 있습니다.
성경에 나오는 하만의 예가 그걸 잘 보여 주죠.
아주 높은 자리에 앉힌 것을 자랑합니다.
뿐만 아니라 그는 분노에 차 있었습니다.
그가 모르드개를 매달려고 세운 바로 그 기둥에
이사야 29:20에서 이렇게 알려 주는 바와 같습니다.
우리 자신과 다른 사람에게 아주 해로운 영향을 미치기 때문에
우리는 자랑한다는 인상조차 주지 않으려 하죠.
한 자매의 행동이 어떻게 자랑하는 것으로
그런데 본의 아니게 그렇게 될 수 있습니다.
형제 자매들을 잘 알 때 커지게 됩니다.
내가 이걸 그냥 혼자 할 수가 없어서.
어떤 패션에도 매치하시기가 너무 좋으세요. -허, 이거 봤어?
이런 제품들 더 알아보고 싶지 않으세요?
자신의 할머니를 참을성 있게 잘 보살폈죠.
이 광고를 다른 한 자매가 봤죠.
생각해 봐야 한다는 점을 교훈해 줍니다.
어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있는가 하는 것입니다.
그러기 위해 항상 기억해야 될 점이 있습니다.
사실, 당신이 가진 것 가운데서 받지 않은 것이 무엇이 있습니까?
받은 것이라면 왜 받지 않은 것처럼 자랑합니까?”
우리가 가진 좋은 것에 대해 여호와께 모든 영예를 돌려야 한다는 겁니다.
다윗왕은 이 모든 것을 다 가지고 있었죠.
또 그분의 뜻을 이루는 데 그분께 사용될 수 있는 영예에 대해 자랑하라는 것입니다.
다른 형제 자매들이 가진 훌륭한 특성들에 대해 이야기하는 것입니다.
겸손하고 겸허한 사람은 자기에 대해 자랑하지 않고
여호와께서 그분의 일에서 어떻게 그들을 사용하고 축복하고 계신지 보려고 합니다.
그러므로 합당하지 않은 자랑이라는 이 특성을 벗어 버리고
우리가 이룬 일에 대해 여호와께 감사와 영예를 돌리고
형제 자매들이 훌륭한 특성들을 가진 것과
여호와께서 그들을 사용하시는 것에 대해 칭찬하는 것입니다.
또 형제들과 누리는 소중한 평화를 유지하게 될 것입니다.
이제 봉사 위원회 보조자인 세스 하이엇 형제가 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.
시기심이 어떻게 나타나는지 알아차리는 것은 중요한 일입니다.
그런 감정을 방치하면 우린 영적으로 죽게 될 수 있습니다.
한 가지는 우리 모두가 잘 아는 것이죠.
시기심이 있으면 다른 사람이 가진 것을 탐내게 됩니다.
사실 이 두 번째가 더 위험하다고 할 수 있는데요.
시기심은 다른 사람이 가진 것을 탐내는 데서 그치지 않습니다.
그 사람이 그것을 갖지 못하게 되기를 바라죠.
예수가 사람들에게 정말 많은 사랑을 받았기 때문입니다.
하지만 그들은 사람들을 대하는 자신들의 방식을 바로잡으려 하지 않고
그분의 좋은 평판을 망치려고 그렇게 한 것이죠.
예수께서 가지셨던 것을 탐낸 것만이 아니라
여러 가지 “육체의 일”들 중 하나로 언급되는 것도 놀라운 일이 아닙니다.
시기심은 사람 간의 관계를 약화시키거나 손상시키고 심지어 파괴합니다.
그 점을 보여 주는 한 가지 예는
야곱은 열두 아들 중 한 아들을 특히 사랑했는데
그래서 요셉의 형들은 요셉을 시기하게 됩니다.
그는 요셉 때문에 여러 해 동안 슬퍼했습니다.
시기심 때문에 정말 끔찍한 일이 일어난 겁니다!
사랑, 동정심, 친절 같은 특성을 나타내지 못한다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
미움, 분쟁, 격분과 같은 해로운 특성들이 채워지게 됩니다.
시기심이 회중의 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있을까요?
고라와 다단과 아비람의 예를 생각해 보겠습니다.
그 세 사람은 이스라엘 회중 가운데서 모세와 아론을 시기했습니다.
그들은 여호와의 대표자들에 대해 부정적이고 비판적으로 말하기 시작했는데,
심지어 모세가 군왕 노릇을 하며 다른 사람들 위에 자신을 높인다고 비난했습니다.
사실 여호와께서 모세와 아론에게 책임 있는 위치를 맡기셨는데
한동안 회중에서는 평화를 찾아볼 수가 없었죠.
여호와께서 시기심을 어떻게 보시는지 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
‘내가 다른 사람에게 해를 입히면서까지 뭔가를 원하는 일은 절대 없을 거야.’
자기도 모르게 시기하게 될 수 있죠.
시기심이 어떻게 평화를 깨뜨릴 수 있는지 보시겠습니다.
너무 잘난 척하는 거 같지 않으세요?
전에도 그 얘기 했던 거 같은데.
그 자매는 헤일리 자매의 동기를 의심했죠.
또한 헤일리 자매의 평판에 해가 될 수 있는 말을 했습니다.
그럼 우리는 어떻게 시기심을 물리칠 수 있습니까?
두 가지 아름다운 특성들을 기르기 위해 노력하는 것입니다.
먼저, 겸손에 관한 성경 말씀을 살펴보시죠.
자신을 실제보다 더 중요하게 생각하는 것입니다.

하지만 그 화가 너무 지나쳐서 제어되지 않은 정도가 됩니다.
그들은 속임수를 써서 세겜의 도시에 있는 모든 남자를 공격해 죽입니다.
그 도시를 약탈하고 여자와 아이들을 포로로 사로잡아 갑니다.
분명 야곱도 디나가 겪은 끔찍한 일 때문에 마음이 아팠겠지만
아들들이 제어되지 않은 분노를 나타낸 것을 꾸짖었습니다.
시므온과 레위는 자신들의 행동을 정당화하려고 했지만,
시므온과 레위의 자손이 이스라엘 지파들 가운데
흩어지게 될 것이라는 예언을 했던 것입니다.
그들은 제어되지 않은 분노를 나타냈기 때문에
하느님의 은혜와 아버지 야곱의 승인을 잃었습니다.
그러한 분노가 초래하는 해를 피하도록 해야겠습니다.
한 자매가 어떻게 분노를 터뜨릴 위험에 처하게 되는지 보시겠습니다.
너 맨날 바빠서 시간 내기도 힘들잖아.
지금 하는 게 나을 것 같은데.
아 그게, 최근에 네가 올린 영상들 말이야.
어 ··· 파이오니아가 그런 영상 올리는 거, 좀 그렇지 않아?
그냥 내가 만든 물건 광고하려는 건데 뭐가?
니가 관심 끌고 싶어서 안달 난 것처럼 보일 수 있다는 ···
나 말고도 실리아 자매도 그렇게 생각하셔.
내 뒷담화하고 다니니까 그렇게 좋아? -뒷담화가 아니고 ···
분노가 제어되지 않으면 어떤 일이 일어날지 우리 모두가 알기 때문이죠.
그로 인해 어떤 일이 생길 수 있는지 살펴봤는데요.
제어되지 않은 분노를 어떻게 벗어 버릴 수 있는가 하는 것입니다.
우리는 먼저 제어되지 않은 분노의 위험성을 인식해야 합니다.
“자기를 제어하지 못하는 자는 성벽이 다 헐린 도시 같다.”
고대의 도시들은 튼튼한 성벽이 없으면 침략자들에게 쉽게 함락당할 수 있었습니다.
자기를 제어하지 못하는 사람이 바로 이와 같다는 것이죠.
자제력을 잃으면 나쁜 생각들이 아주 손쉽게 우리의 마음에 침입하게 됩니다.
그런 생각은 자신과 다른 사람들에게 해를 입힐 수 있죠.
제어되지 않은 분노는 그만큼 위험한 것입니다.
분노 때문에 나중에 후회할 일을 하기 전에
화가 끓어오른다면 시므온과 레위에게 있었던 일을 생각해 보도록 하십시오.
그리고 우리가 방금 본 동영상의 내용도 떠올려 보시면 도움이 되실 것입니다.
고통스러운 일을 피할 수 있지 않았을까요?
따라서 잠언 17:14의 말씀을 기억하는 것이 좋습니다.
이 점을 기억하면서 이렇게 자문해 보십시오.
‘나는 모든 사실을 알지 못하면서 속단하는 경향이 있는가?
그렇다면 분노가 더 자라기 전에 그 자리를 피해
그 분노를 떨쳐 버릴 수 있는가?’
야고보서 1:19의 영감받은 조언이 그렇게 하는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다.
이 말씀을 적용하기 위해 진지한 노력을 기울여야 합니다.
제어되지 않은 분노를 벗어 버릴 수 있는 간단한 방법들을 찾아 보실 수 있습니다.
우리가 여호와께 “듣기는 빨리 하고, 말하기는 더디 하고, 분노하기도 더디 하게” 도와 달라고 요청한다면
제어되지 않은 분노를 벗어 버리도록 그분이 도와주실 것입니다.
우리의 노력이 성공을 거두려면 교제의 대상을 지혜롭게 선택해야 합니다.
교만하고 독선적이고 쉽게 화를 내는 사람들과 어울린다면
분노를 제어하기 위해 우리가 기울이는 노력과 여호와의 도움이 효과를 거두지 못할 수 있습니다.
쉽게 화를 터뜨리는 사람에 대해 잠언 22:25에서 경고하는 것처럼,
곧 있을 이 악한 세상의 심판을 생존하는 데 도움이 되는
시기심, 부정직, 남에 대한 해로운 이야기,
평화를 깨뜨리는 특성들을 계속 벗어 버리기 위해 최선을 다해야 합니다.
만약 우리에게 개선해야 할 점이 조금이라도 있다면,
여호와의 도움을 청하고 변화하기 위해 열심히 노력하십시오.
우리는 형제 자매들과의 평화를 추구하기 위해 진지하게 노력함으로
“여호와의 날”과 그분이 약속하신 신세계를 간절히 기다리고 있음을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
그러한 노력은 우리의 마음에 영향을 줄 것이고,
하늘의 아버지께서도 우리의 노력을 눈여겨보실 것입니다.
그리고 그분과 또 동료 숭배자들과 “평화”를 누리는 사람으로 여겨 주실 것입니다.
이 점이 어떻게 오늘날 우리의 믿음을 강하게 해 줍니까?
모든 인종의 평화를 위해 노력해 왔죠.
미래 세대를 위한 평화의 토대를 놓기 위해
아이들이 깨끗하고 평화로운 세상에서 자라는 것입니다.
건강, 안전, 복지와 같은 것들을 누리기가
지금도 마음의 평화를 누릴 수 있죠.
네가 걸어가야 할 길로 너를 인도하는 이다.
네가 나의 명령에 주의를 기울이기만 한다면!
그러면 네 평화가 강처럼 될 것이다.”
그분은 우리가 평화를 누릴 수 있는 방법을 계속 알려 주십니다.
“모든 이해를 뛰어넘는 하느님의 평화”를 주심으로 그렇게 하십니다.
과거에도 힘든 시기를 산 사람들이 있었죠.
성경에는 그에 대한 기록이 많이 나옵니다.
우리를 평화로 인도하시는 여호와 하느님을 신뢰하는 데 도움이 되는
그분이 미래에도 도움과 인도를 베푸실 것임을 확신하게 됩니다.
요나는 니네베에 관한 소문을 들었기 때문에
이 임명을 받고 큰 두려움을 느꼈습니다.
아시리아 사람들은 잔인한 전사들로 알려져 있었고,
요나는 누가 이 폭풍을 보냈는지 알았죠.
그래서 그는 이게 다 자기 때문이라고
바로 나 때문에 이 사나운 폭풍이 불어온 겁니다.
사람들이 자기 때문에 죽는 걸 막기 위해서였죠.
제가 감사의 목소리로 당신께 희생을 바치고
내가 너에게 말하는 소식을 그 도시에 선포하여라.
자기를 보호해 주실 거라고 믿지 않았습니다.
하지만 두 번째로 기회가 주어졌을 때는
여호와께서 자기를 보호해 주실 것을 신뢰합니다.
처음에 니네베로 가지 않고 멀리 도망쳤을 때
요나는 여호와께서 그분을 신뢰하고 그분께 순종하는 사람들을
요나의 기록이 그 점을 보여 주죠.
요나가 심판의 소식을 전한 때로부터 약 100년 뒤에
특히 그가 손에 넣고 싶어 한 곳은
히스기야는 참숭배를 위해 많은 일들을 했지만
하지만 산헤립의 군대는 공격을 멈추지 않고
여호와께서 산헤립의 상대가 되지 않는다고 거들먹거렸습니다.
이스라엘 군인들은 정말 겁이 났을 겁니다.
형제 여러분, 여호와께서는 과거에 하신 것처럼
성전, 예루살렘, 우리 목숨도 다 잃을 겁니다.
셉나, 나도 어떤 상황인지 잘 압니다.
여호와의 것을 우리 손으로 넘길 순 없습니다.
여호와께서 그분의 백성을 구출하실 수 있다는 점에 초점을 맞추었습니다.
너희 왕이 대체 무슨 생각인지 모르겠구나.
자길 구해 줄 거라고 믿는 거지?
히스기야는 막다른 길에 이른 것 같을 때도
우리가 보기에 어떤 상황은 막막해 보일지 모르죠.
우린 확신을 가지고 그분의 인도를 따를 수 있죠.
아시리아의 공격을 무사히 넘길 수 있었습니다.
거짓 신의 조각한 형상을 두기까지 했죠.
그 거짓 신들에게 희생으로 바치기까지 했습니다.
그토록 열심히 이룩해 놓았던 하느님과의 평화가
그의 아들의 행동으로 무너져 내린 겁니다.
그 때문에 여호와께서는 므낫세를 엄하게 벌하셨습니다.
아시리아 왕이 그를 바빌론으로 사로잡아 갔죠.
그들이 여호와와 바알을 같이 섬길 수 있다고
우상 숭배를 없애는 대대적인 활동을 벌입니다.
이 나라의 거짓 신은 전부 이렇게 될 겁니다.
신성한 목상, 형상, 금속 상을 부서뜨렸습니다.
우상 숭배를 뿌리 뽑으려는 결의에 차 있었죠.
참숭배를 옹호하는 사람들이 거의 없을 때
자신이 옳은 일을 하고 있는 것인지
그는 네 위에서 희생의 연기를 올리는 산당의 제사장들을
사람들의 뼈를 네 위에서 태울 것이다.”
그 예언은 300년도 더 전에 분명히 확증해 주었죠.
성전을 보수하는 일까지 해 나갈 수 있었을 겁니다.
그 땅에 다시 평화가 찾아오게 되었습니다.
예레미야는 바빌론이 유다를 정복할 것이라고 예언했습니다.
70년 동안 바빌론 왕을 섬기게 될 것이다.
다니엘은 예레미야의 이 말을 직접 들었을 수 있습니다.
유다 지파의 탁월한 가문 출신인 젊은 다니엘은
고향에서 잡혀 와 가족과도 떨어져 지내야 했습니다.
다니엘은 더 큰 어려움들을 겪게 됩니다.
다니엘이 유다에서 여호와를 섬기며 살던 삶과
바빌론 주민들이 얼마나 큰 안정감을 느꼈을지 상상해 보십시오.
느부갓네살왕은 그 도시가 누리는 번영과 안전이
그런데 이 거짓 신들과 그 제사장들의 무능함이 드러납니다.
내가 꾼 꿈과 해석을 같이 알려 주지 못하면,
가서 하나냐, 미사엘, 아사랴를 데려와 줘.
이 명령 때문에 다니엘과 그의 친구들도
그 왕은 당시 가장 강력하고 난폭한 왕이었습니다.
그런데 그 무시무시한 왕이 갑자기 명령하는 겁니다.
그가 꾼 꿈의 내용과 그 의미를 알려 달라는 거죠.
폐하의 꿈과 그 의미를 알려 주실 겁니다.
다니엘은 이전에 꿈을 해석해 본 경험이 없었죠.
이전에는 여호와로부터 꿈의 해석을 받은 적이 없었습니다.
그렇게 한 건 바로 믿음 때문이었는데,
당시에 구할 수 있었던 성경 책들을 연구해서 갖게 된 믿음이었습니다.
그리고 그 밖의 예언자들의 기록이 있었을 겁니다.
따라서 느부갓네살의 꿈에 대해 전혀 몰랐지만
그는 여호와께서 그 꿈과 해석을 알려 주시고
그가 “책들”을 읽었다는 것은 알 수 있습니다.
그는 여호와께서 충실한 사람들을 축복하신 기록을 보았습니다.
그러니까 느부갓네살에게 시간을 달라고 했을 때,
다니엘은 그저 조금 더 목숨을 부지하려고 한 게 아니라
꿈을 밝혀 주실 거라고 확신하기는 했지만,
그는 그저 손 놓고 상황을 바라보기만 하지 않았습니다.
당신만이 비밀을 밝히실 수 있다는 것을
꿈을 해석할 수 있는 사람을 찾았습니다.
그래, 네가 정말 내가 꾼 꿈과 그 해석을 알려 줄 수 있겠느냐?
하늘에는 비밀을 밝히시는 분인 하느님이 계십니다.
폐하께 말일에 일어날 일을 알려 주셨습니다.
그 형상은 폐하 앞에 서 있었습니다.
네 번째 왕국은 철같이 강할 것입니다.
그 왕국이 일부는 강하고 일부는 약할 것입니다.
다니엘은 정말 엄청난 믿음과 용기를 나타냈습니다.
우리도 위험한 상황에 처할 수 있죠.
우리는 여호와께 마음을 쏟아 놓으며 기도할 수 있습니다.
우리도 여호와의 소식을 전할 임명을 받았습니다.
막막하고 막다른 상황에 직면할 수 있죠.
하느님이 주시는 가장 강력한 힘에 의지할 수 있습니다!
우리는 확신을 가지고 그 일들을 직면할 수 있습니다.
단지 바빌론 제국의 미래에만 적용된 것이
그 예언들은 지금 일어나고 있는 일들뿐만 아니라
바로 지금 우리 눈앞에서 벌어지고 있습니다!
우리의 충절이 어떻게 여호와의 목적에 기여하는지 기억하고
이 의미심장한 영상의 제2부를 보게 될 것입니다.

en.text: We extend a warm welcome to one and all.
In this session, which corresponds
to the Saturday afternoon portion of the program,
we will learn what we individually can do
to pursue peace with others.
We will begin with a music-video presentation.
The video will encourage us to welcome others
into our peaceful worldwide brotherhood.
Please enjoy.
Please join in singing song number 29, entitled
“Living Up to Our Name”—song number 29.
At times, our imperfections can disrupt our peace
and that of others.
During the next symposium,
we will consider things we must avoid
in order to cultivate peaceful relationships.
Please give your attention to Brother Harold Corkern,
a helper to the Publishing Committee,
as he develops the theme
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers —Inappropriate Boasting.”
What comes to your mind when you hear the expression “put away”?
You may think of related expressions
such as “cast aside,” “dispose of,”
“discard,” “get rid of.”
What did we have to put away to become a Christian?
The Bible in the book
of Ephesians 4:22 provides the answer.
That’s Ephesians 4:22:
“You were taught to put away the old personality
“that conforms to your former course of conduct
and that is being corrupted according to its deceptive desires.”
So we had “to put away the old personality.”
But it’s one thing to put it away;
it’s something else to keep it away.
And that’s why in the very next verse, verse 23,
Paul encourages us to do this:
“And you should continue to be made new
in your dominant mental attitude.”
It’s so important to keep it away,
because the old personality has traits
that can become peace wreckers.
This symposium will consider five peace wreckers
that we should put away and keep away.
Each talk will include the following main points:
(1) It will define the peace wrecker,
(2) it will explain how it wrecks peace,
and (3) we will consider how to put it away.
What is the very first one that we’re going to talk about?
It is inappropriate boasting.
What is inappropriate boasting?
Basically, it’s self-praise,
and the Bible condemns self-praise
Notice Proverbs 27:2:
“Let someone else praise you,
“and not your own mouth;
others, and not your own lips.”
Self-praise is an evidence of pride
that causes one to elevate himself above others.
Some might develop an unhealthy pride
about their accomplishments, even in the ministry.
It happened in the first century.
Paul had to write to the Corinthian congregation
about the dissensions that they were having,
the lack of peace they were experiencing.
Why?
Well, some in the congregation were “puffed up with pride” about themselves
or other men,
such as Paul, Apollos, Cephas.
They were giving too much attention to themselves
and to other men.
Well, how could that happen today?
Well, let’s imagine a group of brothers talking,
and one in the group says,
“With Jehovah’s help and with diligent prayer and effort,
I finally got a Bible study.”
But right away, another one in the group proudly declares,
“I have four Bible studies;
two are attending meetings, and one will soon be baptized.”
Could such a statement be a peace wrecker?
How does inappropriate boasting wreck peace?
Well, it’s not wrong to take pleasure in our work
and to thank Jehovah for the success that we may have.
But inappropriate boasting about our accomplishments
can stir up competition, envy, and rivalry.
We must remember that self-promotion
does not originate with our heavenly Father, “the God of peace.”
Where does it originate?
First John 2:16 says:
“The showy display of one’s means of life
“does not originate with the Father,
but originates with the world.”
And would you not agree that the world is filled with self-praise?
Even on their social media, we see this.
Some of the material that people post on social media
is designed to make one appear very important.
And it is a showy display
of their accomplishments, their material possessions,
or their expensive vacations that they enjoy.
In other words, it’s all about “look at me.”
Well, we want to avoid getting caught up
in the world’s spirit of self-promotion
that wrecks peace.
To illustrate just how devastating
the peace wrecker’s inappropriate boasting can be,
let’s briefly consider the Bible character Haman.
He was a proud and haughty man,
and he boasted a lot.
Esther chapter 5 tells us
that he was boasting with his family and friends
about his wealth, his many sons,
how the king had promoted him to a high station,
that he was above all the other servants,
and that he’d had a special meal, or banquet,
with the king and queen.
But Haman was hateful and arrogant.
And he was plotting to kill Jehovah’s faithful servant Mordecai.
But his scheme and his attitudes were exposed.
And what happened?
The very stake that Haman had built
to hang Mordecai on he was hung on.
And it reminds us —doesn’t it?—
that at Isaiah 29:20, the Bible says:
“The boaster will come to his finish.”
So because of the devastating effects
that improper boasting can have on ourselves and others,
we do not even want to give the impression of boasting.

But genuine affection fights peace wreckers.

We remember their joys
and pains,
their selfless zeal,
how they came to love Jehovah,
and what they endure.

A key point that we must always remember

1 Corinthians 4:7:

What’s the point of this scripture?
We do not want to boast about ourselves

Now, some people are proud about their good looks,

Well, may we continue to put away and keep away

and by commending our fellow workers for all the good qualities they have
and for how Jehovah is using them in his service.
By doing so, we will preserve our precious possession of peace
with Jehovah and with our brothers.
Brother Seth Hyatt, a helper to the Service Committee,

“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers—Envy.”
What is envy?
Do you know?
It’s important that we be able to identify the symptoms of envy.
Why?
Because envy is an expression of hatred.
It’s an enemy of peace.
And if left unchecked,
it can result in spiritual death.
As described in the Bible, envy has two symptoms.
The first is probably more familiar.
An envious person wants
what someone else has.
It’s the second symptom
that makes envy especially dangerous.
An envious person not only wants what someone else has,
but he also doesn’t want the other person to have it.
Here’s an example:
In the first century, Jewish religious leaders envied Jesus
because Jesus was much appreciated by the common people.
Jesus dealt with people,
including lowly ones, in a way that dignified them.
As a result, he was appreciated.
The religious leaders envied him.
But rather than adjusting their own way of dealing with people,
they attacked Jesus verbally
in an effort to destroy his good reputation.
They spread malicious slander.
Not only did they want what Jesus had,
but also they didn’t want Jesus to have it.
No wonder envy is listed as one of “the works of the flesh”
at Galatians 5:21.
It’s a dangerous quality
that we need to avoid.
How does envy disrupt peace?
Envy undermines, damages,
or even destroys relationships
in the family and in the congregation.
Consider the example of Jacob
and his 12 sons.
Jacob had special affection for one of his sons, Joseph.
As a result, Joseph’s brothers became envious.
How did the envy manifest itself?
What was the fruitage?
Well, they dealt treacherously with Joseph, selling him into slavery.
And as if that weren’t bad enough, they compounded their wrong
by lying to Jacob,
telling him that Joseph was dead.
According to the Bible account,
Jacob “refused to be comforted.”
He mourned Joseph for years.
What a terrible consequence of envy!
It’s clear that envy
allows no room for love,
compassion, or kindness.
Those qualities go out the window.
And they’re replaced by qualities
such as hatred, strife, fits of anger.
Can envy disrupt the peace of a congregation?
Consider the examples of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
They envied Moses and Aaron
in the congregation of Israel.
How did that envy manifest itself?
Well, they began to speak negatively—critically—
of Jehovah’s representatives, even accusing Moses
of playing the prince and lifting himself up above the others.
They forgot that Jehovah
had put Moses and Aaron in their positions of responsibility.
How did Jehovah react
to that manifestation of envy?
He destroyed those three men and all who supported them.
For a time, the congregation was robbed of its peace,
and the accounts certainly provide some insight
into Jehovah’s view of envy.
Now, by this point, you’re no doubt thinking,
‘I would never want something so badly that I would
damage someone else to get it.’
But we’re all imperfect.
We have a treacherous heart,
and envy is insidious.

What comes to your mind when you hear the word “dishonesty”?

not to deceive others
as mentioned at Leviticus 19:11.

Dishonesty includes (and please take note of this definition)
intentionally leading someone to a wrong conclusion.
For example, by twisting the truth
or by providing only certain details,
we endanger our peace with others.
Why can we say so?
How does dishonesty wreck peace?
Peace and a peaceful relationship
are built on trust.
Trusting someone makes you feel safe and secure
and puts you at ease.
There is no peace without trust.
How do we develop trust?
Trust is the result of spending time together,
speaking the truth with one another.
We trust people who act unselfishly
and do not use “crooked speech,” as the Bible puts it.
If someone deceives us only once or is dishonest in another way,
we might start to question everything they say.
One single act of dishonesty may be enough.
It can ruin their reputation.
As bad as this is, dishonesty has the potential
to create even greater damage.
Dishonesty can be compared
with a highly contagious virus.
Dishonesty breeds dishonesty.
People who have contact with deceitful, dishonest persons
are in danger of being infected.
Dishonesty might not only wreck one relationship
but multiple relationships,
putting the unity and peace of the whole group at risk.
This reminds us of the relationship
between Laban and Jacob in the Bible book of Genesis.
Based on the agreement with Laban,

So now Leah was also part of the deception.
What was the result after Jacob had found out
that Laban tricked him?
The trust was gone.
The relationship had suffered to a great degree.
Dishonesty wrecked the peace in those relationships,
and so the following seven years of work for Rachel were bitter.
And Laban’s dishonesty emboldened him to continue in his course.
He unfairly changed Jacob’s wages ten times.
He deceived Jacob.
Because of Laban’s dishonesty,
the peace in the whole family was disrupted.

Do you gossip?
No.
Well, whenever we share any news about others,
that is a form of gossip.
Because we are interested in others, we might say,
“I am really concerned about Brother Smith’s health,”
or “Did you hear about Sister Brown’s experience in the ministry?”
Is this type of gossip harmful?
Generally not.
Still, we need to be careful.
At 1 Timothy 5:13,
Paul spoke out against certain sisters
who were “gossipers and meddlers in other people’s affairs.”
We do not need to know and share everything we know
about what’s happening in other people’s lives.
What if, for example, Brother Smith did not want others
to know details about his health problem?
We need to respect the privacy of others.
Or what if talking about Sister Brown’s experience turns into,
“Oh, you know, she always brags about her success in the ministry.”
When our talk about others turns negative,
it can develop into slander.
Slander is making deliberate, false statements
that damage another’s reputation.
Let’s now consider how harmful gossip wrecks peace.
If you have spread harmful gossip about someone and he hears about it,
when you see him the next time,
what will be the look on his face?
Please read with me Proverbs 25:23:
“The north wind brings a downpour,
and a gossiping tongue brings an angry face.”
The north wind in Palestine
brought dark clouds and rain.
Likewise, when the one you gossiped about
catches wind of this and he sees you,
he will have a gloomy, angry face.
There will be a storm and a chilled relationship.
Now, when that happens,
you may feel very badly and apologize,
but you may have damaged his reputation
in a way that may be difficult to undo.
Listen to this old Jewish story:
‘A man went about town slandering the town’s wise man.
‘Later, the malicious gossiper realized his wrong
‘and went to the wise man and asked for his forgiveness.
‘He offered to do whatever was needed to make amends.
‘The wise man made one request.
‘He told the gossiper to take a feather pillow,
‘cut it open, and scatter the feathers to the wind.
‘Well, the gossiper was puzzled by this request,
‘but he did as instructed.
‘Then he returned to the wise man.
‘“Am I now forgiven?” he asked.
‘“First, go and gather all the feathers,” the wise man responded.
‘“But, how can I?
‘The wind has already scattered them.”
‘The wise man replied,
‘“It is as difficult to repair the damage done by your words
as it is to recover the feathers.”’
Yes, once spoken, hurtful words cannot be retrieved.
Let’s not scatter feathers in the wind.
If we spread rumors,
it can seriously disturb the peace of many in the congregation.

where he reasoned on the basis of the Hebrew Scriptures.
Such stories could have led some newly converted Jewish Christians
to think that Paul did not respect God’s arrangements,
and this could have seriously disrupted the peace of the congregation.

Brother Kenneth Cook,
a member of the Governing Body,
will now present the final talk of this symposium,
“‘Put Away’ Peace Wreckers —Uncontrolled Anger.”
Satan is the main peace wrecker.
The Scriptures tell us that he is driven by “great anger.”
His anger is malicious and uncontrolled.
Would any sound-minded, God-fearing person
allow himself to reflect Satan’s vicious anger?
Of course not!
That is why all true servants of God are determined
to “put away” uncontrolled anger.
But apart from uncontrolled anger, is all anger bad?
The Bible does not condemn all anger.
It teaches us that anger is wrong when it is uncontrolled or unjustified.
At Ephesians 4:26, God’s Word tells us:
“Be wrathful, but [it adds] do not sin.”
At times, anger may simply be a strong feeling
that comes into us because of being upset or annoyed
by something that we see as being wrong.
That in itself is not bad.
But what makes anger bad is when it fills a person’s heart
and he or she just loses control of it.
When that happens,
it may cause a person to act without a sound mind.
Those who continue to lash out in anger will not gain salvation.
Galatians 5:20 lists “fits of anger”
among “the works of the flesh” that will prevent a person
from inheriting God’s Kingdom.
There will be no place for such ones in God’s new world.
A brief review of how uncontrolled anger
wrecks peace for ourselves and others
will highlight why this is so.
Uncontrolled anger
harms both the angry person as well as those around him.
We read at Proverbs 29:22
that an angry person “stirs up strife,”
adding that he “commits many transgressions.”
One of these many sins is abusive speech.
We must work to show restraint when speaking with workmates,
with strangers in the ministry,
with our brothers and sisters in the congregation,
and with our family members.
Bad feelings must be controlled.
Abusive speech, ridicule, contempt,
and hateful anger are wrong.
Giving vent to such feelings can destroy precious friendships
with other people and with Jehovah.
Don’t be like a volcano that will not quiet down.
Just like an erupting volcano will harm those living around it,
so too a person who expresses intense anger
will harm those living around him.
He also damages himself.
In what way?
Acting on anger often leads to even more aggression,
so uncontrolled anger can also affect our own peace.
It can cause us to do something that we will later regret.
It can have a negative effect on our health.
Medical studies show that uncontrolled anger
can cause high blood pressure and respiratory problems.
It can also affect the liver and pancreas,
and such anger can cause digestive problems.
When a person becomes angry,
he or she will not always think clearly.
After a fit of rage, a person may become depressed.
No wonder we read at Proverbs 14:30
that “a calm heart gives life to the body.”
The disastrous consequences of uncontrolled anger
are illustrated in God’s Word
by the actions of Simeon and Levi,
sons of the patriarch Jacob.
When they learned that their sister, Dinah,
was violated by a man named Shechem,
we read at Genesis 34:7
that “they were offended and very angry.”
Now, they had a valid reason to be angry,
but they took their anger too far.
It was uncontrolled.
Simeon and Levi took vengeance on Shechem.
Using deception, they attacked and killed
every male in Shechem’s city.
Then, along with the other sons of Jacob,
they plundered it and took the women and little children captive.
Dinah’s tragic experience must have grieved Jacob greatly.
Yet, he condemned his sons’ uncontrolled anger.
Simeon and Levi tried to justify their actions,
but that was not the end of the matter,
because Jehovah was also displeased.
For this reason, Jacob later foretold
that the descendants of Simeon and Levi
were to be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
Their uncontrolled anger brought disfavor
from God and from their father, Jacob.
We’re wise to pay attention to such Scriptural accounts
and put away uncontrolled anger and all of the harm that it brings.
In the following dramatization,
notice how a person might be tempted to give in to anger.
Yes, Nana?
Don’t forget eggs, dear.
No, no, I didn’t forget.
Are you sure, love?
No, I won’t forget. OK.
Thank you so much.
OK. Love you.
Bye.
No!
Haley, finally, I’ve caught you.
Do you have a minute?
Hi, Emily.
Can we talk later?
I’m really struggling this morning.
You know, it’s just that you’ve been so busy, and I’ve been waiting for the right moment;
I’d really just like to address it.
OK. What’s up?
It’s just that I’ve noticed your posts lately on QuicPost.
What about them?
Well, do you really think they’re something that a pioneer should be posting?
What? What are you talking about?
Some people might think you’re bragging.
Some people? What people?
It’s a business account. I’ve got to show off my products.
I know. I get that.
It’s just— I don’t know.
It could feel like you’re drawing a little too much attention to yourself.
Who would think like that? You?
No, not just me; Celia felt the same.
You spoke to Celia about this?
I didn’t want to upset you.
Jake said that I needed to take . . .
Jake! So everyone thinks my posts are inappropriate?
Not everyone, Haley.
That’s not what I am saying at all.
You are such . . .
Wow! I can’t believe you.
Who else have you spoken to?
You are just such a gossip!
I’m not gossiping. I was trying to . . .
You are!
I’m just trying to help you, if you would just listen to me.
You’re so jealous!
If you’d just listen to me.
Oh yeah, listen to this.
And I expected more from you.
Haley, what are you talking about?
Gossiping about my posts!
Are you that lonely that you’ve got nothing better to do?
Haley,
wait, please!
Were you left feeling a bit tense?
If so, you know what uncontrolled anger can lead to.
Now that we’ve defined uncontrolled anger
and considered what it can lead to,
the next question is,
How can we put away uncontrolled anger?
First, we need to recognize the danger of uncontrolled anger.
Proverbs 25:28 states
that “as a city broken through, without a wall,
is the man who cannot control his temper.”
Strong city walls were vital in ancient times.
Without them a city would quickly fall to invaders;
likewise, so will those who cannot control their temper.
By losing control, they make themselves vulnerable
to the invasion of wrong thoughts
—thoughts that can cause them to hurt themselves and others.
Uncontrolled anger can do just that.
Next, after recognizing the danger,
we must pause and then deal with the anger
before it causes us to do something that we will regret.
When anger grows within us,
we’re wise to recall what happened with Simeon and Levi.
We might also recall what happened
in the video dramatization that we just viewed.
You see, in each case,
pausing before reacting out of anger
may have spared much pain and heartache, true?
That is why we have this warning
at Proverbs 17:14:
“Before the quarrel breaks out, take your leave.”
With that in mind, each of us should ask himself:
‘Do I tend to jump to conclusions
‘when I don’t have all the facts?
‘If so, can I take my leave and put away anger
before it starts to build up?’
The inspired advice
found at James 1:19 will help us to do so
—but only if we make a sincere and determined effort
to apply what it says.
Let’s read that verse—James 1:19.
And here we find some simple steps
to help us put away uncontrolled anger.
It says: “Know this, my beloved brothers:
“Everyone must be quick to listen,
slow to speak, slow to anger.”
If we ask Jehovah to help us with this,
namely to “be quick to listen,
slow to speak, slow to anger,”
he will assist us to do so.
He will help us to see the facts of the matter,
show understanding, and then put away uncontrolled anger.
A word of caution, though:
To succeed in doing our part,
we must choose our associates wisely.
We could undermine all of our good work
and Jehovah’s help in controlling our anger
if we choose associates who are arrogant,
opinionated, or quick to become angry.
Regarding someone who is disposed to rage,
Proverbs 22:25 warns:
“Never learn his ways.”
Well, we’ve enjoyed another outstanding series of talks
that should help us to keep awake,
maintain fine conduct,
and escape the judgment that will soon come on this world.
As this symposium has emphasized,
we must do our utmost to continue to put away peace wreckers
such as inappropriate boasting, envy,
dishonesty, harmful gossip,
and uncontrolled anger.
If we have a problem with any of the peacemaking qualities
that we have discussed in this symposium,
seek Jehovah’s help to change and then work at it.
Our sincere efforts to pursue peace
with our brothers and our sisters
will influence how earnestly we are awaiting “Jehovah’s day”
and his promised new world.
Yes, our genuine efforts will affect our hearts
and will be noticed by our heavenly Father.
Then, in his great mercy,
Jehovah will consider us to be, as his Word says,
“spotless and unblemished and in peace”
—both with him and with our fellow worshippers.
Thank you, brothers, for helping us to strengthen our bond of unity.
Since the rebellion in Eden,
peace among mankind as a whole has been lost.
Despite this, Jehovah has given peace
to those who trust in him.
How has he done so in the past,
and how does this strengthen our faith in him today?
We invite you to enjoy Part 1 of the documentary
Jehovah Guides Us in the Way of Peace.
Our military forces are committed to peace.
We have chosen peace.
Our wish, our prayer, is for peace.
We yearn for peace.
We pray for peace.
For thousands
of years, humans have tried
to find peace
—peace as individuals,
peace as families,
peace for the entire human race.
We want to lay the foundation of peace for generations to come.
We want to do the hard work now
so our children and our grandchildren can grow up in a peaceful world.
The future we want:
opportunity and security for our families,
a rising standard of living,
a sustainable, peaceful planet for our kids
—all that is within our reach.
Yet, despite humans’ best efforts,
peace
has been elusive.
For millenniums,
rulers and governments have tried to achieve peace
through treaties,
resolutions,
summits
and, ironically, war.
Our peace as humans is more fragile than ever.
Man’s efforts to bring about lasting peace
have failed time and time again.
This isn’t surprising to us.
Jeremiah 10:23 tells us:
“It does not belong to man . . . to direct his step.”
Humans were simply not designed to rule themselves.
Good health, safety, overall well-being
—these are becoming harder to find
as we move further into what the Bible
refers to as “the last days.”
As long as human rule continues,
disunity will continue.
It’s true that global peace
cannot be obtained by human efforts alone.
But those who are close to God
can find peace of mind right now.
Isaiah 48:17, 18 says:
“I, Jehovah, am your God,
“the One teaching you to benefit yourself,
“the One guiding you
“in the way you should walk.
“If only you would pay attention
“to my commandments!
“Then your peace
would become just like a river.”
It’s only Jehovah
who has the ability to guide humans
to real, lasting peace.
He promises he will bring this about.
Until this happens,
Jehovah continues to provide ways
for us to experience peace now.
How does he do that?
By giving us “the peace of God that surpasses all understanding.”
We aren’t the only ones whose peace has been challenged.
God’s Word is filled with accounts of faithful servants
whose peace was challenged
by the dominating forces of their day.
As we study and meditate on these accounts,
the lessons we learn from them
help us to trust in Jehovah as he guides us to peace.
Understanding how these accounts relate to Jehovah’s purpose to bring peace
by means of his Messianic Kingdom gives us confidence
that his purpose never fails
and he will support and guide us on into the future.
One of Jehovah’s prophets
who learned this lesson firsthand was Jonah.
Jonah lived in the ninth century B.C.E.
Jehovah assigned Jonah to go to Nineveh,
a city of the Assyrian Empire.
Based on what he knew about Nineveh,
Jonah considered this to be
an intimidating and threatening assignment.
The Assyrians were known as fierce warriors,
and Nineveh itself was later described
as a “city of bloodshed.”
So you can understand Jonah’s trepidation when Jehovah asks him
to proclaim a judgment message
against this imposing city
and its pagan inhabitants.
In an attempt to find peace,
Jonah decides to go far away from Nineveh
and boards a boat headed for Tarshish.
Tarshish is generally associated
with modern-day Spain.
So from Israel,
this is the complete opposite direction
of Nineveh.
Jonah found anything but peace.
Look!
By the gods.
Furl the sail!
Now, this was no ordinary storm.
It was so severe that the ship
was in danger of being wrecked.
Captain, we’re taking on too much water!
This storm is from the gods!
Baal!
Eshmun!
The crew cried out to their gods,
but Jonah knew the true Source of the storm.
And now he accepts
personal responsibility for the situation.
Lift me up
and throw me into the sea,
and the sea will calm down for you;
for I know that it’s because of me
that this violent storm has come upon you.
Can you imagine the courage it took
for Jonah to make this request?
He had no way of knowing if Jehovah would save him,
but he did not want others to perish on his account.
In his mercy, Jehovah spares Jonah’s life.
How am I still alive?
What will become of me?
When faced
with a difficult assignment,
Jonah “got up to run away from Jehovah
to Tarshish.”
Jonah’s conscience had to bother him;
he had to be questioning his decision.
He tried to take matters into his own hands,
tried to find his own peace.
Where does he find himself?
In the belly of a fish!
Yet he calls to Jehovah in a moment of despair.
O Jehovah,
out of the depths of the Grave,
I cry to you for help.
Please hear my voice.
What I have vowed, I will pay.
Jonah could have reasoned
that this was the end of his assignment as Jehovah’s prophet.
After all, he did disobey direction.
So likely, he was surprised
to hear the word of Jehovah come to him
a second time.
Jonah!
Get up,
go to Nineveh the great city,
and proclaim to her
the message that I tell you.
Yes.
Yes.
Thank you.
At first, Jonah trusted in himself
and didn’t understand
that Jehovah would protect him from the violent Assyrians.
But after being given a second chance, what happens?
Well, then he puts aside
his human concerns
and looks to Jehovah for protection.
In just 40 days more,
Nineveh will be overthrown.
Jehovah, the true God, has spoken.
This city will be destroyed.
Nineveh will be overthrown.
The true God will overthrow Nineveh.
The true God has spoken.
Eventually, the king himself repents
and orders everyone
in Nineveh to do the same.
Jonah learned a valuable lesson
from this experience.
By originally running away from Nineveh,
he chose to trust in himself
rather than putting his trust in Jehovah.
Are you Jonah?
I am.
Mommy says you saved us.
No, Jehovah saved you.
I was just—I was just a messenger.
Jonah learned
that without a doubt
Jehovah protects those who trust and obey Him.
If Jehovah has asked you to do something,
if he’s asked me to do something,
if he’s leading us,
he absolutely will guide us through it.
Jonah’s account proves this.
Although the Ninevites were spared
because they repented (that’s true),
Assyria later
returned to its evil, wicked ways.
About a century
after Jonah’s judgment message,
King Sennacherib of Assyria brought
his armies against the cities of Judah,
including the city he wanted most
—Jerusalem.
King Hezekiah of Judah
was an outstanding king
who “held fast to Jehovah.”
From the beginning of his reign,
he proved to be zealous for true worship
not only in Judah but in all of Israel.
Hezekiah had done so much to stand up for pure worship,
yet now he is faced with the prospect
of a siege against Jerusalem
by Sennacherib’s armies.
Hezekiah agrees to pay Sennacherib
a tribute in return for peace.
Yet, the armies continue their conquests,
as Sennacherib and his men besiege
the strongly fortified city of Lachish.
From here,
Sennacherib sends a part of his army
as well as military chiefs to Jerusalem
in an attempt to demand surrender.
The spokesman for the group was the Rabshakeh,
who spoke Hebrew fluently.
He loudly ridiculed Hezekiah
and taunted Jehovah,
boasting that Jehovah was no match against King Sennacherib.
Imagine what these soldiers
must have been thinking.
Sennacherib’s armies were on a warpath,
taking city after city.
To Hezekiah, this was a defining moment.
He had to decide if he would trust in himself
or trust in Jehovah.
My brothers,
we must remember that Jehovah
is fully able to rescue us,
just as he has in times past.
God’s Word . . .
King Hezekiah,
will you not even now face the facts?
We are trapped!
The Assyrians are at our gate,
and you cling to the belief
that nothing bad will happen.
You will destroy everything
you so hope to preserve
—the temple, Jerusalem,
our very lives.
Shebna, I am not blind
to the dangers that we face.
I too am afraid.
But if Jehovah
allows Jerusalem to fall,
so be it.
How can we give up what belongs to Jehovah?
So as a man of faith,
Hezekiah focused on Jehovah’s ability
to save His people
despite Sennacherib’s continued advances toward Jerusalem.
I’m curious about this king of yours.
Who does he think
will come to save him from me?
Jehovah, your God,
is weak!
He will cringe before my god Asshur.
Hezekiah remained
determined to trust in Jehovah.
This decision required a tremendous amount of faith,
especially with more than
185,000 Assyrian soldiers
headed toward Jerusalem.
Instead of trusting in himself,
he continued to look
for Jehovah as the Source of true peace
even as an attack seemed imminent.
And Jehovah again
showed just how insignificant
human rulers are in comparison to him.
Hezekiah learned
that when a way out seems impossible,
trusting in Jehovah always leads to success.
Jehovah rewarded that trust with victory over the Assyrians.
This is a lesson we can apply now and in the near future.
There may be situations when true worshippers seem trapped,
but never forget that Jehovah is all-powerful.
He’s leading his people,
and we can follow his guidance with full confidence.
Jehovah will protect those who trust in him at Armageddon.
Jerusalem remained safe
against attack for the time being,
but peaceful conditions didn’t last long.
Hezekiah’s son Manasseh
did what was detestable
in the eyes of Jehovah.
He brought back Baal worship
and personally took its vilest practices
to extremes,
even putting a carved image of a false god
right inside Jehovah’s temple.
So here you have a king
who’s supposed to be protecting the people from idolatrous influence
doing the exact opposite —building altars to false gods.
He even went so far as to pass his own sons through the fire,
sacrificing them to these gods.
The peace with God that Hezekiah
worked so hard to achieve for the nation
is now reversed by the actions of his son.
Because of this,
Jehovah punished Manasseh severely.
He allowed the king of Assyria
to take him captive to Babylon.
While in captivity,
Manasseh ultimately repented.
He humbled himself,
and he stayed faithful
right to the end of his life.
Grandfather!
We can imagine him impressing
the importance of faithfulness
to Jehovah on his young grandson Josiah.
Listen to me.
Jehovah is holy,
and you must serve him
the way he wants us to.
All other gods
are powerless.
Yet, in spite of all this,
the people still thought
that they could serve Jehovah and Baal.
So after becoming king,
Josiah started a campaign against idolatry.
I’ve seen these cheaper.
Take it or leave it.
We start here!
No!
This is what we will do to every false god in the land.
He tore down altars used for false worship,
sacred poles, images, and statues.
He was intent on cleansing the land of idolatry.
Now, he showed remarkable courage
to stand up for true worship at a time when few were doing so.
There’s no doubt this was a difficult task.
At times, he may have even wondered
if he was doing the right thing.
It’s possible Jehovah provided Josiah
with assurance from the prophet Jeremiah.
This is what Jehovah says: “Look!
“A son named Josiah
“will be born to the house of David!
“He will sacrifice on you
“the priests of the high places,
“those making sacrificial smoke on you,
and he will burn human bones on you.”
That prophecy
made over 300 years earlier confirmed
that Josiah was the one prophesied to act against false worship.
This may have given Josiah even greater incentive and courage
to continue his campaign,
which now included repairing the temple.
These actions contributed
to the peaceful conditions
that elevated pure worship.
Josiah did so much
to restore pure worship.
That is why we love him.
Yet, the peoples’ heart condition remained polluted,
so the nation required severe discipline.
Jeremiah prophesied
a conquest of the Babylonians
against Judah.
All this land
will be reduced to ruins,
and this land and its inhabitants
will have to serve the king of Babylon
for 70 years.
Daniel himself may have heard
Jeremiah speak those words.
And he certainly
saw it come true as he and his family were exiled to Babylon.
Talk about peace being interrupted!
Daniel was a young Judean prince taken
from his homeland
and separated from his family.
But being chosen to receive special training
in the court of King Nebuchadnezzar
presented another set of challenges.
The entire way
of Babylonian life was contrary to what Daniel knew growing up in Judah.
But Daniel was determined not to pollute himself
with foods Jehovah would not approve of.
And Jehovah blessed
Daniel’s determination to be faithful,
as he was selected to serve
as one of King Nebuchadnezzar’s wise men.
Nebuchadnezzar was a warrior-king
intent on building a great empire.
After he officially
took the throne in 624 B.C.E., his domain
grew with each conquest.
Babylon became an epicenter of trade and commerce.
Nebuchadnezzar undertook
huge building projects throughout the city,
which made the city seem impregnable.
Imagine the sense of security the inhabitants of Babylon must have felt,
locked safely behind the city’s walls.
Nebuchadnezzar
attributed the prosperity
and security all around him
to the power of his false gods.
The chief of these false gods was Marduk, the god of war.
Yet, these false gods and their priests would prove to be worthless.
One night,
King Nebuchadnezzar had a strange dream.
Call the wise men!
O king, may you live on forever.
Relate the dream to your servants.
We will tell the interpretation.
No!
If you don’t make the dream known to me
along with the interpretation,
you’ll be dismembered,
and your houses will be turned into public latrines.
There is not a man on earth
who can do what the king demands.
What the king is asking is difficult.
No one exists
who could tell this to the king except
—except the gods.
Seize them!
Kill them!
Jerah.
You’re in danger.
Why? What happened?
I didn’t hear everything,
but the wise men angered the king.
Everyone is to be executed by dawn.
Bring Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah here.
I’ll try to learn more.
This edict to kill all the wise men
would also include Daniel and his companions.
So let’s look at this from Daniel’s perspective.
Here he is, a young man in a foreign land,
serving in the court of one of the most powerful and violent men alive.
And that man is now demanding
that someone, in effect, read his mind:
“Tell me my dream,
and tell me what it means.”
O king,
interpretations belong to my God, Jehovah.
He knows your dream and what it means.
Well, where is your God?
Where?
I believe that he— I know that he will reveal it to me.
Please, give me time.
Daniel is not acting
on previous experience.
He hasn’t received interpretations of dreams from Jehovah.
Instead, he is acting on faith
—faith that he had learned
by studying the sacred books of his time.
These books
likely included the inspired writings
of Moses, David, Solomon, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and other prophets.
Oh, we can only imagine
Daniel poring over these scrolls,
opening up his heart to Jehovah,
begging Jehovah to give him wisdom and understanding.
He loved it.
There’s no doubt that
as Daniel studied these accounts,
his faith was strengthened
and his bond with Jehovah drew even closer.
So even though Daniel knew nothing of King Nebuchadnezzar’s dream,
he was fully convinced
that Jehovah would reveal the dream
and its interpretation
and prove to be Daniel’s salvation.
Do we know exactly which accounts
Daniel was able to draw from at this time?
It’s impossible to say for a certainty,
but we do know he had access to “the books.”
He references the prophecies of Jeremiah.
Daniel could see how Jehovah blessed faithful, obedient men in the past.
So by asking Nebuchadnezzar for time,
he wasn’t looking to buy himself
another day of life;
he was allowing Jehovah to reward his faith
by revealing the dream to him.
Daniel strikes a balance here.
Although he is confident
that Jehovah will reveal the dream to him,
he isn’t casual in the way he handled the situation.
He did what any God-fearing man
would do here.
He approached Jehovah in prayer.
O Jehovah,
surely you didn’t bring us here just to die.
What will people say?
We told them
that you are the God of the heavens,
the only God who can reveal secrets.
Please, vindicate yourself.
I have found a man from the exiles of Judah
who can make known
the interpretation to the king.
I know who he is.
Can you really make known to me
the dream that I saw
and its interpretation?
There is a God in the heavens
who is a Revealer of secrets,
and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar
what is to happen
in the final part of the days.
This is your dream:
You saw an immense image.
That image
was standing in front of you.
You yourself are the head of gold.
But after you another kingdom will rise,
inferior to you.
Then another kingdom, a third one, of copper,
that will rule over the whole earth.
As for the fourth kingdom,
it will be strong like iron.
The kingdom will be divided.
And as the toes of the feet
were partly of iron and partly of clay,
so the kingdom will be partly strong
and partly fragile.
This took a tremendous amount of faith
and courage on the part of Daniel.
Now, we may find our peace threatened,
our very lives might be on the line.
In that moment, we can turn to Jehovah God in prayer,
opening up our hearts, confident that he will support us.
Like both Daniel and Jonah,
we’ve been given an assignment
to proclaim a message.
This requires courage to speak out boldly
concerning Jehovah’s judgments
against those who oppose his sovereignty.
Both of these prophets are excellent examples
of Jehovah backing those who trust in him.
Jehovah will always be with us as long as we have faith in him.
When we face situations that seem impossible,
as in the case with Hezekiah,
we have the ability to tap
into the most powerful force there is!
As this system comes to a close,
we will find ourselves in situations
that test our courage and threaten our peace.
We will have to stand up for pure worship
just like Josiah, and this will be unpopular.
But with Jehovah on our side,
we can face those situations with confidence.
He’s all-powerful,
and he’s going to help us through it.
Now, here’s the interesting thing:
Some of the prophecies that Daniel recorded
applied not only to the future of the Babylonian Empire
but also outline world events
to our day and beyond.
And these events are being fulfilled
right before our very eyes!
What a motivating presentation!
Even when our peace is threatened,
we can focus on how our integrity relates to Jehovah’s purpose,
and we can endure with joy.
We look forward to watching Part 2 of this important consideration
during the final session of our convention.
Now let’s sing together song number 130,
entitled “Be Forgiving.”
That’s song number 130.
