title: 로버트 시렌코: “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오—잘 준비하십시오

ko.text: 제가 이 연설을 하려고 여러분 앞에 섰는데
사실은 연설 준비를 전혀 하지 않았다면
주요점을 뒷받침하는 성구들도 제대로 기억하지 못한다면요?
연설을 하는 저도 엄청 긴장이 될 겁니다.
그리고 여러분은 제가 왜 시간과 노력을 들여 연설을 준비하지 않았는지 의아해하실 겁니다.
할 말을 미리 준비하지 않는 것도
집주인은 우리를 다시 만나고 싶어 하지 않겠죠.
우리는 봉사를 하기 전에 시간을 내어 잘 준비해야 합니다.
우리가 전하는 소식이 가장 중요한 소식인 “평화의 좋은 소식”이기 때문입니다.
따라서 우리는 사람들이 이 소식을 듣고 싶은 마음이 들도록 최선을 다해야 합니다.
예수께서는 제자들이 봉사 준비를 하도록 도와주셨습니다.
구역에서 만나게 되는 사람들의 다양한 반응에
예수께서 제자들을 그처럼 잘 준비시켜 주셨기 때문에
더 침착하고 열정적인 태도로 즐겁게 봉사할 수 있습니다.
어떤 좋은 결과가 있는지 유의해 보십시오.
아내에게 무슨 말을 할 거냐고 물어봤어요.
늘 그렇듯 서둘러 할 말을 생각했죠.
봉사 도구를 활용할 방법을 잘 생각해 볼 필요가 있습니다.
우리는 사도 바울과 같은 목표를 가져야 합니다.
“좋은 소식을 다른 사람들에게 전해 주려고 좋은 소식을 위해 모든 일을 한다”고 썼습니다.
그러면 이제 봉사를 어떻게 잘 준비할 수 있는지 살펴보겠습니다.
먼저, 사람을 직접 만나든 전화로 증거하든
첫 방문에서 할 말을 어떻게 준비할 수 있을까요?
매번 도움이 되는 대화 방법 제안이 실립니다.
물론 그 제안을 조정하거나 완전히 바꿔서 사용할 수도 있겠죠.
지나간 달에 사용된 주제나 다른 성구가 구역에 더 호소력이 있을 수도 있습니다.
특히 대화를 어떻게 시작할지를 잘 준비해야 합니다.
처음 꺼내는 말이 흥미를 불러일으키지 않는다면
집주인에게 인사를 한 뒤 이어서 어떤 말을 할지
미리 한두 문장을 잘 준비해 둔다면
더 효과적으로 봉사할 수 있을 것입니다.
“이 점에 대해 어떻게 생각하세요?” 라고 할 수 있을 것입니다.
그런 다음 구역 사람들이 관심 있을 만한 주제로
집주인의 생각을 이끌어 낼 수 있는 질문을 미리 잘 준비해야겠죠.
사실 재방문 준비는 첫 방문에서 시작됩니다.
첫 방문을 마칠 때 집주인이 생각해 볼 만한 질문을 남기는 거죠.
「집회 교재」에 나오는 첫 방문과 재방문 대화 방법 제안이 그런 식으로 되어 있죠.
매번 방문을 마칠 때마다 생각해 볼 만한 질문을 남긴다면
집주인은 우리와 계속 대화를 하고 싶은 마음이 들 것입니다.
그 모든 차량들이 함께 움직이게 해 주는 것은 무엇입니까?
그 차량과 그 뒤의 차량을 연결시켜 줍니다.
모든 차량이 선로를 따라 함께 움직이는 것입니다.
첫 방문에서 이렇게 질문할 수 있을 것입니다.
그 점에 대해 이야기를 나눈 뒤
“하느님은 우리가 겪는 고통에 대해 어떻게 느끼실까요?”
재방문에서 그 답을 알려 준 뒤에
이런 질문을 또 남길 수 있겠죠.
다음 방문 때 답을 알려 줄 수 있겠죠.
재방문을 하기 전에 미리 시간을 내서 목표를 정할 수 있겠죠.
그 질문에 대한 성경의 답을 보여 주는 것도 목표가 될 겁니다.
「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」 팜플렛으로 성서 연구를 시작하는 것입니다.
연구 준비는 어떻게 할 수 있습니까?
우리가 내용을 아무리 잘 알고 있다 해도
연구생의 관점과 필요에 대해 생각해 보고
미리 예상해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
어떤 점을 이해하거나 받아들이기 어려워할지 생각해 볼 수 있겠죠.
다루게 될 과의 내용도 미리 잘 살펴봐야 합니다.
낭독 성구를 찾아서 적용점을 생각해 보십시오.
연구 중에 보게 될 동영상도 미리 시청해 보고
연구생에게 특히 어떤 내용이 도움이 될지 생각해 보십시오.
이렇게 함으로 연구를 사회하기 위해 잘 준비할 수 있을 것입니다.
연구생을 잘 도울 수 있게 해 달라고 기도해야 합니다.
우리가 봉사의 직무를 효과적으로 수행하는 데 도움이 되는 것 한 가지는
우리의 웹사이트와 「JW 라이브러리」에 새로 실리는 내용을 잘 알아 두는 것입니다.
이 도구들을 능숙하게 사용하는 법을 익히십시오.
성경의 가르침 탭에 있는 “성경 질문과 대답”
그리고 안내 탭에 있는 “자주 하는 질문”이 특히 도움이 됩니다.
이 내용은 앱에 있는 “연재 기사” 항목에서도 볼 수 있습니다.
그가 그리스도인 제자들을 세우는 비유적인 의미의 건축을 했기 때문이죠.
우리도 봉사의 직무에 참여할 때 같은 일을 하는 것입니다.
하지만 이 건축 활동을 잘하려면 도구를 잘 사용할 줄 알아야 합니다.
특히 우리의 주된 도구인 하느님의 말씀을 사용하는 기술을 발전시켜야 합니다.
봉사 도구함에 있는 출판물들도 잘 사용할 줄 알아야 하죠.
건축가가 일을 시작하기 전에 미리 준비한다면
실수하거나 후회하는 일을 피할 수 있을 것입니다.
‘간단히 준비하기만 했는데도 큰 도움이 되었다’고 했습니다.
“그대 자신을 승인받은 사람으로, 진리의 말씀을 올바로 다루며
아무것도 부끄러워할 것이 없는 일꾼으로 하느님께 바치기 위해 최선을 다하십시오.”
“평화의 좋은 소식”을 전하기 위해 잘 준비한다면
지금 진행되고 있는 영적 건축 활동에서 큰 기쁨을 맛보게 될 것입니다.
이제 중앙장로회 성원인 앤서니 모리스 형제가 할 다음 연설의 제목은
“‘평화의 좋은 소식’을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오 —적극적으로 대화를 시작하십시오”입니다.

en.text: What would you think and how would you feel if I showed up to give this talk
but had done nothing to prepare what to say to you
—if I had not bothered to study the outline I was given,
could not remember the theme, had no idea what the main points are,
and would have to guess at what scriptures to use to support them,
and then, as I spoke, I would ramble incoherently?
I’d make a very bad impression.
I know how I would feel.
I would be a nervous wreck,
and you would wonder why I did not think enough of you
to put all the time and effort that was necessary
into preparing the talk so that you could get the most benefit from it.
Can you see where I’m going with this?
Could the same things be said
if you engaged in the ministry without first preparing what to say?
If you did not review the sample conversations that had been provided,
could not think of how to start a conversation,
and did not know what scripture to share,
how nervous would you be?
And what would the householder think of you?
It would likely be a very short, uncomfortable conversation.
And the other person may not care to have you call again.
We should take some time to prepare well before we preach.
Why?
Because we have the best message ever
—“the good news of peace” to share with people—
and we should do our best so that they will want to listen to what we have to say.
Jesus helped his disciples to prepare for the ministry.
Luke chapter 10 reports that before sending out 70 disciples to preach,
he shared with them a pleasant way to greet each householder,
he told them what to talk about (the Kingdom of God),
and he told them how to respond to the varied reactions
they would get in their territory.
As a result, because the disciples
were fully prepared for the ministry,
they enjoyed some thrilling experiences.
When we are prepared,
we are more poised and enthusiastic and can truly enjoy the ministry.
As you watch the following video,
notice the good results of preparing well.
We’d made some good changes,
but we weren’t done.
I asked Yuri what she planned to talk about.
That started the usual scramble.
Then we got it—the sample conversation.
That’ll do.
But for that to work, I had to remember the scripture.
We were both a little forgetful that morning.
Yeah, we needed to prepare better.
We’d been relying on our experience
and not enough on Jehovah.
So first we prepared our hearts.
Then we prepared our minds
and found new ways to use our preaching tools.
Even a little preparation for initial calls
and our returns visits
went a long way.
The husband said, “Yeah, we needed to prepare better.”
Have you ever thought that about your ministry?
Like the couple in the video,
we can first prepare our heart and our mind
and then see how best to use our preaching tools.
Our goal should be the same as that of the apostle Paul.
At 1 Corinthians 9:23,
he wrote that he wanted
to “do all things for the sake of the good news,
in order to share it with others.”
So let’s think about some specific things that we can do to prepare well,
beginning with what we can say on the initial call,
whether that is done in person or over the telephone.
Each issue of the Christian Life and Ministry—Meeting Workbook
provides us with sample conversations that give us some helpful ideas.
Of course, you may modify the samples or use something entirely different.
Perhaps a subject from a previous month
or a different scripture would have wider appeal in your territory.
Your opening words may be the most important part of the presentation,
so think it through.
If the introduction does not arouse interest,
the other person may terminate the conversation
before we can give a witness.
We will be more effective if we carefully prepare
the first sentence or two that we will say after giving a customary greeting.
We might say, “Many people are concerned about . . . ”
or “I would like to get your opinion on . . . ”
or say something else.
Then pick a topic that is of local interest
and ask a well-worded viewpoint question
that would draw the person into the conversation.
Now, what about preparing for our return visits?
That actually begins on the initial call by leaving a question
for the person to think about until you call again.
That is how the sample initial calls and return visits
are set up in the Meeting Workbook.
By leaving a thought-provoking question at the end of every visit,
we can keep the chain of conversations going as long as possible.
We can illustrate it this way:
Imagine a freight train with an engine at the front,
a caboose at the rear, and many cars in between.
What keeps all of those cars moving together down the train track?
There is a device called a coupler at the back of each train car
that latches onto the coupler at the front of the car behind it.
By being coupled, or linked, together,
the cars all run as a unit along the track.
So the question that we leave with a householder at the end of one visit
is what we can latch onto at the beginning of our next visit
so that we can keep the train of thought going from one conversation to the next.
For example, on the initial call you could ask,
“Why is there so much suffering in the world?”
After discussing that, raise the question,
“How does God feel about our suffering?”
But don’t answer the question until your next visit.
After answering that question on the first return visit,
leave the person with this question, “What will God do to end our suffering?”
This will be discussed on your next visit.
It is also important to have an objective in mind for each return visit.
Before making the call,
think about what you want to accomplish on that call.
If you raised a question the last time,
you’re objective will surely include answering that question from the Bible.
Of course, the ultimate objective is to try to start
a Bible study in the Enjoy Life Forever!  brochure.
Now, what about preparing for the Bible studies that we conduct?
Even if we know the material very well,
we should prepare for each study session with our student in mind.
That means thinking about and anticipating
the views and needs of that individual.
What points might he struggle to understand or accept?
It also means getting familiar with the lesson
to be covered in our interactive Bible course.
Read the lesson carefully,
look up the “read” scriptures to see how they apply,
watch the videos that will be shown during the lesson,
and review the items in the “Explore” section
so that you will know which of those will be especially helpful to your student.
Then you will be well-prepared to conduct the study.
Since it is ‘God who makes the seed of truth grow’ in a person’s heart,
we should ask for Jehovah’s blessing on our preparation for the study
so that we can best help the student spiritually.
And we will be more effective in our ministry
if we stay up-to-date with the latest material
and features found on jw.org and on JW Library®.
So learn how to navigate the website and the app.
Two very helpful features on the website
are “Bible Questions Answered” under the Bible Teachings tab
and “Frequently Asked Questions” under the About Us tab.
They can also be found on the app under “Article Series.”
The apostle Paul described himself at 1 Corinthians 3:10
“as a skilled master builder.”
That is because he was engaging
in a spiritual construction work to build Christian disciples.
And we are doing the same sort of work when we engage in the ministry.
But to build effectively, we must learn to use our tools well.
We especially need to develop skill in using our principal tool, God’s Word,
as well as learn how to make effective use of the publications
in our Teaching Toolbox.
A builder who prepares before starting to work
avoids mistakes and frustration.
Remember what the brother said at the end of the video?
‘Even a little preparation goes a long way.’
And that is what will help you to do your best in the ministry.
Just as Paul recommended at 2 Timothy 2:15
—please follow along in your Bible, if you will—
it’s 2 Timothy 2:15:
“Do your utmost to present yourself approved to God,
“a workman with nothing to be ashamed of,
handling the word of the truth aright.”
Then you will experience great joy in the spiritual building work
that is taking place now because you will be ready
and well-prepared to share “the good news of peace.”
Brother Anthony Morris, a member of the Governing Body,
will now present the next talk of the symposium,
“Be Ready to Share ‘the Good News of Peace’ —Take the Initiative.”

title: 케네스 플로딘: “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오—열정을 계속 유지하십시오

ko.text: 이 심포지엄은 “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전하는 것에 관한 내용입니다.
겸손한 사람들이 여호와와 평화를 누리게 돕는 것은 정말 큰 영예죠.
그리스도인의 “온전한 갑주” 중에 발에 대한 내용이 나옵니다.
먼 거리를 행군하는 경우가 정말 많았습니다.
“발에는 평화의 좋은 소식을 전할 준비의 신 [준비의 신]을 신고 굳게 서십시오.”
네, 모든 적절한 경우에 “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있어야 합니다.
전파하고 가르칠 준비를 갖추는 다섯 가지 방법을 살펴볼 것입니다.
먼저 열정을 유지하는 것이 왜 중요한지 살펴보시죠.
우리는 흔히 열정을 불에 비하기도 하죠.
“나는 그리스인과 외국인, 지혜로운 사람과 무분별한 사람 모두에게 빚진 사람입니다.
그래서 나는 … 좋은 소식을 전하기를 간절히 바랍니다.”
열정적인 전파자들은 좋은 소식을 전하기를 간절히 바랍니다.
사람들이 여호와와 평화를 누리기를 바라는 것입니다.
그런데 그런 열정이 약해질 수도 있을까요?
평화를 바라는 사람들을 찾을 준비가 돼 있는 상태,
네, 살면서 이런저런 문제들을 겪다 보면
생활의 염려 때문에 그럴 수 있습니다.
이러한 문제들도 불에 비할 수 있는데요.
미국 서부 지역에 해마다 큰 피해를 가져오는 산불과도 같다고 할 수 있죠.
우리의 열심과 열정이 식을 수 있습니다.
산불이 번지는 것을 막는 한 가지 좋은 방법은 맞불을 놓는 것입니다.
그러면 그 일대가 맞불에 의해 다 타버립니다.
더 태울 것이 없어서 이내 꺼져 버리죠.
봉사에 대한 열정이 활활 타오르게 하십시오.
사람들이 하느님과 평화를 누리며 영원히 살도록 도울 기회를 놓치게 될 수 있습니다.
“그대 자신과 그대의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울이십시오.”
다시 말해, ‘자신의 열정과 자신의 가르침에 주의를 기울이라’는 말이죠.
이렇게 하면 그대 자신과 그대의 말을 잘 듣는 사람들을 구원하게 될 것입니다.”
봉사에 대한 열정이 많이 식어 있었습니다.
이제 어떻게 그 불씨에 부채질을 해서
모든 사람이 우리의 소식을 듣는 건 아니지만
좋은 소식을 듣기 싫어하면 안 되잖아요.
당장 실천할 만한 목표들도 세울 수 있었죠.
호소력 있는 성경 소식을 알려 주는 겁니다.
그리고 계속 그렇게 해 보는 거죠.
이 부부는 어떤 불같은 문제들 때문에
앞서 언급한 네 가지 문제 중에
봉사에 대한 이 부부의 열정을 식게 만든 것은
또 영상 첫 부분에서 남편이 피곤해 보였죠.
이 부부는 어떻게 해서 불은 불로써 다스려야 한다는 걸 깨닫게 되었을까요?
“사람들이 듣지 않는 이유가 우리의 태도 때문이면 안 된다”고요.
이 부부는 열정이란 맞불을 놓기로 한 겁니다.
남편이 기도할 때 로마서 12:11의 표현을 사용했을까요?
부부가 “영으로 타오르도록” 도와 달라고 여호와께 기도했을 수 있습니다.
“언제부터인가 우리의 봉사는 좀 타성에 젖어 있었어요.”
이 외에도 부부가 열정을 되살리기 위해 어떻게 했죠?
활기를 불어넣는 데 도움이 되는 제안들을 찾았습니다.
봉사할 때 왜 인내해야 하는지 기억하는 데도 도움이 됩니다.
전파 활동에 대한 예수의 태도를 연구해 보십시오.
또 불같은 반대에도 사도들이 얼마나 담대하게 증거했는지,
아굴라와 브리스길라가 어떤 태도를 나타냈는지 살펴보면
우리도 그들과 비슷한 열정을 갖게 될 것입니다.
여러 통의 전화를 걸었는데 아무도 안 받는 경우가 있습니다.
이건 마치 호별 방문을 하는데 집에 아무도 없는 것과 같죠.
그렇다면 사람들이 집에 있을 만한 시간에 증거해 보는 것이 어떻습니까?
그리고 다양한 형태의 봉사에 참여해 보십시오.
전화 봉사도 하고 편지 봉사도 했죠.
이제 우리는 다양한 방법으로 봉사하고 있습니다.
그 덕분에 봉사에 대한 열정과 열심을 유지할 수 있죠.
영상에 나오는 부부가 어떤 목표를 세웠는지 기억나시나요?
그리고 전화 봉사를 하든 공개 증거를 하든,
봉사하는 중간중간에 격려적인 내용으로 대화를 나눴습니다.
여호와께서 잊지 않겠다고 하신 건 우리의 재방문 건수가 아니죠.
그분이 잊지 않겠다고 하신 건 우리가 사회하는 성서 연구 건수도 아닙니다.
여러분의 “일[즉 노력]과 그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑”입니다.
우리가 여호와와 예수를 깊이 사랑한다는 것을 보여 줍니다.
우리의 봉사가 좀 타성에 젖어 있다는 생각이 드십니까?
이제 집필 위원회 보조자 로버트 시렌코 형제가
이 심포지엄의 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.
제목은 “‘평화의 좋은 소식’을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오—잘 준비하십시오”입니다.

en.text: This symposium is about sharing “the good news of peace.”
What a privilege it is to help humble people find peace with Jehovah!
At Ephesians 6:15,
in describing a Christian’s “complete suit of armor,”
it mentions our feet.
Now, back at that time,
thinking of Roman soldiers, Paul knew that often they marched
for hundreds of miles on Roman highways,
crisscrossing the empire.
So at Ephesians 6:15, he said this:
“Having your feet shod in readiness
[in readiness] to declare the good news of peace”
—yes, ready to share “the good news of peace”
on every suitable occasion.
In this symposium, we’ll discuss five ways
to remain ready to preach and teach.
We’d first like to discuss why it’s important to maintain your zeal.
Now, as an analogy,
zeal has often been linked to fire.
We even use the expression —don’t we?—
“He has a fiery zeal for his beliefs.”
But what does “a fiery zeal” indicate?
Please find Romans 1:14, 15,
and here it does not actually use the word “zeal,”
but the sense of the word is evident.
You say: “We’re on fire,” “We’re stoked up,” “We are ready.”
Did you find it?
Romans 1:14, 15:
“Both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to wise and to senseless ones,
“I am a debtor; so I am eager
“[you see, ready with fiery zeal, eager]
to declare the good news.”
Zealous evangelizers are eager to declare the good news—they’re “on fire.”
They want others to find peace with Jehovah.
But is there something that can dampen that flame,
something that could even extinguish the eager desire
—the readiness— to find those who
even unknowingly yearn for peace?
Yes,
it can be difficult to remain eager with fiery zeal
when we face such problems as
an unresponsive territory,
criticism, or outright opposition to the work
—and then there are the pressures of daily life.
Those issues can also be likened to a fire,
to destructive fires like the wildfires
that have plagued the western part of the United States year after year.
Those problems can threaten our zeal and enthusiasm.
So, what can we do?
Well, there’s an English expression that originates with firefighters.
The expression is “Fight fire with fire.”
In the path of a raging wildfire,
one technique is to ignite a controlled fire.
That controlled fire consumes combustible materials.
So when the wildfire advances to that point,
there’s no fuel left and the wildfire goes out.
Fight fire with fire.
Keep your zeal for the ministry burning brightly.
And now please find 1 Timothy 4:16.
If our zeal fades—the flame smolders—
we might miss out on opportunities to help others to gain life,
a life of peace with God.
Look at 1 Timothy 4:16 with me.
It says: “Pay constant attention to yourself and to your teaching”
—you see, the flame, the temperature.
‘Pay attention to your zeal and teaching.’
It says: “Persevere in these things,
“for by doing this you will save both yourself
and those who listen to you.”
Yes, share “the good news of peace” with zeal.
Now, in the following video, note how a couple realized
that the flame had gone out.
They still had some glowing embers left,
but they now find a way to fan the coals
and regain their fiery zeal.
I don’t remember when our routine service day
became so,
well,
routine.
Our zeal wasn’t what it used to be.
And we were finally starting to notice.
Not everyone wants to listen.
We just didn’t want to be the reason.
It didn’t take much research to find
great ideas and set a few simple goals,
like working with those who encourage us.
With Ryota and Ami, we’re always talking
about how we can reach the heart.
We got back to basics:
Be friendly,
listen,
let the conversation progress naturally,
try to share an appealing Scriptural thought,
and keep trying.
Our zeal
can attract an honest person
to the truth.
In the video, what wildfires, or problems,
did the couple face that sucked the oxygen out of their ministry?
Well, of the four we mentioned earlier,
it seems the couple’s zeal was waning
because of seemingly unresponsive territory.
And as tired as the husband looked in that first scene,
the pressures of daily life might have been having a toll on him.
So how did they come to realize
that they needed to fight fire with fire?
Do you remember their kitchen-table talk?
The husband mused that “not everyone wants to listen.”
But then he added, “We just didn’t want to be the reason,”
you see, the reason for them not listening.
They decided to fight fire with fire.
They reignited their own controlled fire of zeal
to counteract the problems they were succumbing to.
Well, what were some of the techniques they used?
The first was to pray to Jehovah.
Could it be that the husband borrowed the words of Romans 12:11 in his prayer?
Yes, he may well have asked Jehovah to help them
as a couple to “be aglow with the spirit.”
Remember he said earlier,
“I don’t remember when our routine service day
became so, well, routine.”
Fight the wildfire by, again, becoming “aglow with the spirit.”
Ensure that any lack of response
is not due to our lackluster approach.
Well, what else did you notice they did to rekindle their zeal?
They did some research, looking for suggestions
to invigorate their ministry.
Yes, and regular Bible study helps us to remember
why we endure in the disciple-making work.
For example, review Jesus’ attitude toward the ministry.
The apostles’ bold witnessing despite fiery opposition
and the disposition of Paul, Aquila and Priscilla, Stephen,
and other Bible characters
—these can infuse us with similar zeal.
Next, keep your ministry fresh.
Well, what does that mean?
Instead of having a number of phone calls that go unanswered,
which is similar to having no one at home when in the door-to-door work,
change the time of day for witnessing
to when more people are home.
Participate in various forms of the ministry.
You know, ironically,
the pandemic more or less forced some of us
who were staunch door-to-door Witnesses to branch out.
We tried phone witnessing and letter writing.
And now we have a variety of preaching activities,
and this can keep us more fully engaged and enthused.
And did you notice what the couple in the video set as a goal?
Periodically, they decided in advance
to share in the ministry with someone specific.
And then they determined to talk about encouraging subjects
when in between calls, whether in phone witnessing
or in the public ministry.
Jehovah values our work in the ministry
regardless of the response we receive.
Hebrews 6:10—are you familiar with that?
Of course you are.
It does not say
that Jehovah does not forget the number of return visits you make.
It does not say he does not forget how many Bible studies you conduct.
No, it says he does not “forget your work [your effort]
and the love you showed for his name.”
Our zeal for the ministry demonstrates
that we have a deep love for Jehovah and Jesus.
If (like the couple in the video) you detect that your
routine of service is becoming, well,
very routine, then fight fire with fire.
Maintain that fiery zeal.
Be ready to share “the good news of peace.”
Brother Robert Ciranko, a helper to the Writing Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“Be Ready to Share ‘the Good News of Peace’ —Prepare Well.”

cn.text: 你准备好宣扬关于和睦的好消息了吗？
能帮助人跟上帝建立和睦的关系
是我们的荣幸
以弗所书6:15
描述基督徒的“全副盔甲”时
提到了鞋子
在保罗的日子
当时的罗马士兵为了执行任务
会在广大的帝国境内走好几百公里
所以，在以弗所书6:15
保罗这样说
“要准备好宣扬关于和睦的好消息
仿佛把鞋穿上”
我们要准备好在任何适当的场合宣扬
关于和睦的好消息
这个系列演讲会讨论五个方法
帮助我们为传道教人做好准备
我们会先谈谈保持热心的重要性
很多人会用火来比喻热心
比如我们会说
他有一颗火热的心，传道时很积极
那这是一种怎样的热心呢？
来看看罗马书1:14,15
经文没有使用“热心”这个词
但表达的意思是相似的
就像有些人说
我卯足了劲，准备火力全开！
“无论是希腊人，还是非希腊人
是有智慧的人，还是不明事理的人
我都欠了他们的债
所以我热切盼望”
也就是热心、渴望
“向你们宣扬好消息”
热心的传道员盼望宣扬好消息
他们的心好像有火在燃烧
很想帮助人跟上帝和好
不过，有些事会打击我们
让我们心中的火渐渐熄灭
不再那么想帮助人跟上帝和好
你想到哪些情况呢？
比如
传道地区里的人反应冷淡
被人批评和反对
还有生活压力大
这些事都可能会让我们
很难继续保持热心
我们也可以把这些难题比喻成火
破坏力很大的火
就像美国西部最近几年发生的森林大火那样
生活上的难题
可能会使我们失去热心和热情
那该怎么办呢？
遇到森林大火时
消防员有一种方法
这种方法叫做“以火攻火”
在大火烧过来之前，他们怎么做呢？
就是点燃另一把火
把一定范围内的可燃物质都烧掉
所以当大火烧过来的时候
这里已经没有燃料了，大火就熄灭了
我们也要以火攻火
用热心的火来对抗如火的考验
请看提摩太前书4:16
如果我们不再热心，让火熄灭
我们很可能错失帮助人亲近上帝
得到永生的机会
我来读提摩太前书4:16
“你要时刻留意自己和自己的教导”
我们也可以说
要留意自己有没有保持热心
“要坚持不懈地做这些事
因为这样做既可以救你自己
也可以救听你的人”
热心宣扬好消息真的很重要！
我们会在接下来的影片看到
一对夫妻发觉自己不再那么热心了
他们的火快要熄灭了
不过他们找到把火煽旺的方法
找回了对传道的热情
不知道从什么时候开始
我们的传道
变得
好像例行公事
我们
不像以前那么热心了
我们应该认真面对这个问题
虽然不是每个人都愿意听
但我们不希望
他们拒绝是因为我们的态度
查考一些资料
定下小的目标
其实没有想的那么难
比如，约热心的人一起传道
跟良太和雅美一起传道的时候
我们常常谈到怎样打动别人的心
我们从基本做起
对人亲切
耐心聆听
自然地交谈
尽量分享合适的经文
还有不要放弃
我们的热心
能吸引有正确态度的人
认识真理
在影片里
是什么“火”，什么难题
削弱了这对夫妻对传道的热情呢？
前面我们提过四种情况
看来，这对夫妻
是因为传道地区里的人反应冷淡
才失去热心
还有，那个丈夫在第一幕里看起来很累
很可能是生活的压力把他压得喘不过气
后来这对夫妻怎么看出自己必须
以火攻火呢？
还记得他们在餐桌上的对话吗？
丈夫说
“虽然不是每个人都愿意听
但我们不希望
他们是因为我们的态度才拒绝”
这对夫妻开始反省自己
于是决定要以火攻火
他们重新燃起热心的火焰
用这把火来对抗自己的难题
那么他们怎么做呢？
首先向上帝祷告
这个丈夫在祷告里提到
罗马书12:11吗？
有可能
也许他求耶和华帮助他们
“靠着神圣力量满腔热诚”
记得他怎么说吗？
“不知道从什么时候开始
我们的传道变得好像
例行公事”
所以要以火攻火，靠神圣力量充满热诚
这样，就算地区里的人反应不佳
也不是因为我们缺乏热情
后来，这对夫妻还做了什么呢？
他们查找资料
唤起自己对传道工作的热情
经常研读圣经确实会帮助我们记得
自己为什么要坚持不懈地传道
比如，我们可以研究耶稣怎样热心传道
使徒们怎样在反对下勇敢地作见证
还有保罗、亚居拉、百姬拉
司提反和其他人物的榜样
研读这些记载会让我们
变得更热心
另外，要保持新鲜感
这是什么意思呢？
就像我们挨家挨户时
常常没有人应门那样
我们做电话见证时
是不是也常常没有人接呢？
可以试试换个时间在住户方便时向他们传道
我们要参与不同形式的见证工作
有意思的是
在疫情之前
有些人只习惯挨家挨户的传道方式
疫情之后反而学会了电话和书信见证
从事不同形式的传道工作
让我们更有新鲜感，变得更投入了
你注意到影片中的夫妻定下什么目标吗？
他们预先计划
找一些比较热心的弟兄姐妹一起传道
而且也决定
不论是挨家挨户时
或做电话见证时
都跟同伴聊一些鼓励人心的话题
不论地区里的人反应怎样
耶和华都很看重我们的传道工作
希伯来书6:10
很熟悉吧？
经文不是说
耶和华不会忘记你有多少个圣经学生
也不是说他不会忘记你做了多少个续访
而是说他不会忘记你们所做的工作
你们的付出跟你们为他的名字所显出的爱心
我们热心传道就表示
我们真的深爱耶和华和耶稣
如果你像这对夫妻那样
发现自己的传道工作
好像在例行公事
有点“公式化”
就要以火攻火
点燃你的热心之火吧！
做好准备宣扬关于和睦的好消息！
写作委员会助手罗伯特·斯朗科弟兄
会发表系列演讲的下一部分

title: 믿음으로, 많은 일을 할 수 있는 문으로 들어가십시오—여호와의 일을 위해 “얼마를 따로 모아” 둠으로

ko.text: 그 지역 형제 자매들이 나타낸 태도에
이 정도는 헌금할 수 있을 것 같아요.
더 많이 줄 수 있는 입장이었습니다.
더 많은 일을 할 수 있을까요?

en.text: When a disaster struck in the north of the country,
we immediately answered the call for help.
Seeing our brothers and sisters in need was heartbreaking.
But what really touched our heart was the spirit
of the local brothers and sisters.
They were like the Macedonians.
They didn’t have much, but they gave generously from the heart.
When we got home,
Madeline and I resolved to show the same kind of spirit.
First, our appreciation led us
to review our contribution to the worldwide work.
I’ve come up with this figure.
Is this right?
Yeah.
Let’s just thank Jehovah.
We looked for ways to be generous
to those around us.
We discovered that we had
the means to give more, so we didn’t hold back.
And then, our congregation was invited to help
with a special preaching campaign.
. . . reach as many as possible with the good news.
Do you think we could do a bit more?
Could we push ourselves a bit further?
I’d really like to.
It was within our power to help,
and that’s exactly what we did!
I’m bringing too much?
No, of course not.

cn.text: 北部发生地震时
我们马上报名去支援灾区
看到弟兄姐妹们受到灾害的影响
我们很难过
但是当地的弟兄姐妹表现出来的精神
却深深地打动了我们的心
他们就像马其顿人一样
拥有的不多，却非常慷慨
回家以后
我和妻子决心要表现同样慷慨的精神
首先，我们仔细计算
可以怎样通过捐款更加支持全球的传道工作
我觉得可以捐这么多，行吗？
好！
我们做个祷告吧
我们寻找机会对周围的人表现慷慨
我们发现，其实我们有能力做得更多
我们就努力这样做
后来我们会众受邀请
参与一个特别的传道活动
我们要让更多人听到好消息
你觉得我们可以调整一下
为耶和华做更多吗？
当然可以
我们有能力行善，就努力这样做了
我是不是带得太多了？
没有，怎么会！

title: 2022 ‘평화를 추구하십시오!’ 대회: 토요일 오전 회기—1부

ko.text: 오늘의 회기도 음악 영상으로 시작될 것입니다.
이 영상을 통해 우리가 누릴 많은 축복을 생각하면서
이 소중한 진리를 사람들에게 전할 마음이 강해질 것입니다.
프로그램의 토요일에 나오는 연설과 동영상들을 즐길 것입니다.
이 두 회기의 주제 성구는 베드로 후서 3:14입니다.
“점도 없고 흠도 없이 평화 가운데 ··· 나타날 수 있도록 최선을 다하라”고 권고합니다.
“평화를 추구”하기 위해 우리 각자가 할 수 있는 일을
“평화의 하느님”에 관해 증거하고 왕국을 선포하는 것을
관심을 가진 사람이 잘 발전하도록 도울 수 있습니까?
이번 회기의 첫 번째 심포지엄에서 그 점을 알아볼 것입니다.
교습 위원회 보조자인 케네스 플로딘 형제가 해 주실
“‘평화의 좋은 소식’을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오
이 심포지엄은 “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전하는 것에 관한 내용입니다.
겸손한 사람들이 여호와와 평화를 누리게 돕는 것은 정말 큰 영예죠.
그리스도인의 “온전한 갑주” 중에 발에 대한 내용이 나옵니다.
먼 거리를 행군하는 경우가 정말 많았습니다.
“발에는 평화의 좋은 소식을 전할 준비의 신 [준비의 신]을 신고 굳게 서십시오.”
네, 모든 적절한 경우에 “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있어야 합니다.
전파하고 가르칠 준비를 갖추는 다섯 가지 방법을 살펴볼 것입니다.
먼저 열정을 유지하는 것이 왜 중요한지 살펴보시죠.
우리는 흔히 열정을 불에 비하기도 하죠.
“나는 그리스인과 외국인, 지혜로운 사람과 무분별한 사람 모두에게 빚진 사람입니다.
그래서 나는 … 좋은 소식을 전하기를 간절히 바랍니다.”
열정적인 전파자들은 좋은 소식을 전하기를 간절히 바랍니다.
사람들이 여호와와 평화를 누리기를 바라는 것입니다.
그런데 그런 열정이 약해질 수도 있을까요?
평화를 바라는 사람들을 찾을 준비가 돼 있는 상태,
네, 살면서 이런저런 문제들을 겪다 보면
생활의 염려 때문에 그럴 수 있습니다.
이러한 문제들도 불에 비할 수 있는데요.
미국 서부 지역에 해마다 큰 피해를 가져오는 산불과도 같다고 할 수 있죠.
우리의 열심과 열정이 식을 수 있습니다.
산불이 번지는 것을 막는 한 가지 좋은 방법은 맞불을 놓는 것입니다.
그러면 그 일대가 맞불에 의해 다 타버립니다.
더 태울 것이 없어서 이내 꺼져 버리죠.
봉사에 대한 열정이 활활 타오르게 하십시오.
사람들이 하느님과 평화를 누리며 영원히 살도록 도울 기회를 놓치게 될 수 있습니다.
“그대 자신과 그대의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울이십시오.”
다시 말해, ‘자신의 열정과 자신의 가르침에 주의를 기울이라’는 말이죠.
이렇게 하면 그대 자신과 그대의 말을 잘 듣는 사람들을 구원하게 될 것입니다.”
봉사에 대한 열정이 많이 식어 있었습니다.
이제 어떻게 그 불씨에 부채질을 해서
모든 사람이 우리의 소식을 듣는 건 아니지만
좋은 소식을 듣기 싫어하면 안 되잖아요.
당장 실천할 만한 목표들도 세울 수 있었죠.
호소력 있는 성경 소식을 알려 주는 겁니다.
그리고 계속 그렇게 해 보는 거죠.
이 부부는 어떤 불같은 문제들 때문에
앞서 언급한 네 가지 문제 중에
봉사에 대한 이 부부의 열정을 식게 만든 것은
또 영상 첫 부분에서 남편이 피곤해 보였죠.
이 부부는 어떻게 해서 불은 불로써 다스려야 한다는 걸 깨닫게 되었을까요?
“사람들이 듣지 않는 이유가 우리의 태도 때문이면 안 된다”고요.
이 부부는 열정이란 맞불을 놓기로 한 겁니다.
남편이 기도할 때 로마서 12:11의 표현을 사용했을까요?
부부가 “영으로 타오르도록” 도와 달라고 여호와께 기도했을 수 있습니다.
“언제부터인가 우리의 봉사는 좀 타성에 젖어 있었어요.”
이 외에도 부부가 열정을 되살리기 위해 어떻게 했죠?
활기를 불어넣는 데 도움이 되는 제안들을 찾았습니다.
봉사할 때 왜 인내해야 하는지 기억하는 데도 도움이 됩니다.
전파 활동에 대한 예수의 태도를 연구해 보십시오.
또 불같은 반대에도 사도들이 얼마나 담대하게 증거했는지,
아굴라와 브리스길라가 어떤 태도를 나타냈는지 살펴보면
우리도 그들과 비슷한 열정을 갖게 될 것입니다.
여러 통의 전화를 걸었는데 아무도 안 받는 경우가 있습니다.
이건 마치 호별 방문을 하는데 집에 아무도 없는 것과 같죠.
그렇다면 사람들이 집에 있을 만한 시간에 증거해 보는 것이 어떻습니까?
그리고 다양한 형태의 봉사에 참여해 보십시오.
전화 봉사도 하고 편지 봉사도 했죠.
이제 우리는 다양한 방법으로 봉사하고 있습니다.
그 덕분에 봉사에 대한 열정과 열심을 유지할 수 있죠.
영상에 나오는 부부가 어떤 목표를 세웠는지 기억나시나요?
그리고 전화 봉사를 하든 공개 증거를 하든,
봉사하는 중간중간에 격려적인 내용으로 대화를 나눴습니다.
여호와께서 잊지 않겠다고 하신 건 우리의 재방문 건수가 아니죠.
그분이 잊지 않겠다고 하신 건 우리가 사회하는 성서 연구 건수도 아닙니다.
여러분의 “일[즉 노력]과 그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑”입니다.
우리가 여호와와 예수를 깊이 사랑한다는 것을 보여 줍니다.
우리의 봉사가 좀 타성에 젖어 있다는 생각이 드십니까?
이제 집필 위원회 보조자 로버트 시렌코 형제가
이 심포지엄의 다음 연설을 할 것입니다.
제목은 “‘평화의 좋은 소식’을 전할 준비를 갖추고 있으십시오—잘 준비하십시오”입니다.
제가 이 연설을 하려고 여러분 앞에 섰는데
사실은 연설 준비를 전혀 하지 않았다면
주요점을 뒷받침하는 성구들도 제대로 기억하지 못한다면요?
연설을 하는 저도 엄청 긴장이 될 겁니다.
그리고 여러분은 제가 왜 시간과 노력을 들여 연설을 준비하지 않았는지 의아해하실 겁니다.
할 말을 미리 준비하지 않는 것도
집주인은 우리를 다시 만나고 싶어 하지 않겠죠.
우리는 봉사를 하기 전에 시간을 내어 잘 준비해야 합니다.
우리가 전하는 소식이 가장 중요한 소식인 “평화의 좋은 소식”이기 때문입니다.
따라서 우리는 사람들이 이 소식을 듣고 싶은 마음이 들도록 최선을 다해야 합니다.
예수께서는 제자들이 봉사 준비를 하도록 도와주셨습니다.
구역에서 만나게 되는 사람들의 다양한 반응에
예수께서 제자들을 그처럼 잘 준비시켜 주셨기 때문에
더 침착하고 열정적인 태도로 즐겁게 봉사할 수 있습니다.
어떤 좋은 결과가 있는지 유의해 보십시오.
아내에게 무슨 말을 할 거냐고 물어봤어요.
늘 그렇듯 서둘러 할 말을 생각했죠.
봉사 도구를 활용할 방법을 잘 생각해 볼 필요가 있습니다.
우리는 사도 바울과 같은 목표를 가져야 합니다.
“좋은 소식을 다른 사람들에게 전해 주려고 좋은 소식을 위해 모든 일을 한다”고 썼습니다.
그러면 이제 봉사를 어떻게 잘 준비할 수 있는지 살펴보겠습니다.
먼저, 사람을 직접 만나든 전화로 증거하든
첫 방문에서 할 말을 어떻게 준비할 수 있을까요?
매번 도움이 되는 대화 방법 제안이 실립니다.
물론 그 제안을 조정하거나 완전히 바꿔서 사용할 수도 있겠죠.
지나간 달에 사용된 주제나 다른 성구가 구역에 더 호소력이 있을 수도 있습니다.
특히 대화를 어떻게 시작할지를 잘 준비해야 합니다.
처음 꺼내는 말이 흥미를 불러일으키지 않는다면
집주인에게 인사를 한 뒤 이어서 어떤 말을 할지
미리 한두 문장을 잘 준비해 둔다면
더 효과적으로 봉사할 수 있을 것입니다.
“이 점에 대해 어떻게 생각하세요?” 라고 할 수 있을 것입니다.
그런 다음 구역 사람들이 관심 있을 만한 주제로
집주인의 생각을 이끌어 낼 수 있는 질문을 미리 잘 준비해야겠죠.
사실 재방문 준비는 첫 방문에서 시작됩니다.
첫 방문을 마칠 때 집주인이 생각해 볼 만한 질문을 남기는 거죠.
「집회 교재」에 나오는 첫 방문과 재방문 대화 방법 제안이 그런 식으로 되어 있죠.
매번 방문을 마칠 때마다 생각해 볼 만한 질문을 남긴다면
집주인은 우리와 계속 대화를 하고 싶은 마음이 들 것입니다.
그 모든 차량들이 함께 움직이게 해 주는 것은 무엇입니까?
그 차량과 그 뒤의 차량을 연결시켜 줍니다.
모든 차량이 선로를 따라 함께 움직이는 것입니다.
첫 방문에서 이렇게 질문할 수 있을 것입니다.
그 점에 대해 이야기를 나눈 뒤
“하느님은 우리가 겪는 고통에 대해 어떻게 느끼실까요?”
재방문에서 그 답을 알려 준 뒤에
이런 질문을 또 남길 수 있겠죠.
다음 방문 때 답을 알려 줄 수 있겠죠.
재방문을 하기 전에 미리 시간을 내서 목표를 정할 수 있겠죠.
그 질문에 대한 성경의 답을 보여 주는 것도 목표가 될 겁니다.
「행복한 삶을 영원히 누리십시오!」 팜플렛으로 성서 연구를 시작하는 것입니다.
연구 준비는 어떻게 할 수 있습니까?
우리가 내용을 아무리 잘 알고 있다 해도
연구생의 관점과 필요에 대해 생각해 보고
미리 예상해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
어떤 점을 이해하거나 받아들이기 어려워할지 생각해 볼 수 있겠죠.
다루게 될 과의 내용도 미리 잘 살펴봐야 합니다.

결과로 인해 여러분의 결정이 “의롭다는 것이 증명”되는 것입니다.
예상하지 못한 문제를 겪게 되는 것입니다.
‘이렇게 힘들 줄 정말 몰랐어’ 하는 생각이 들 수 있죠.
그런 문제들에는 여러 가지가 있을 수 있습니다.
새로 함께 살게 된 사람에게 적응해야 할 수도 있고,
성격 차이 때문에 힘들 수도 있고,
향수병으로 어려움을 겪게 될 수도 있죠.
이 점과 관련해서 야고보가 뭐라고 말했는지 찾아 보실까요?
시련이 가져오는 좋은 결과에 대해 언급하고 있습니다.
그러면 여러분이 온전해지고 모든 면에서 건전해져서
여기서 야고보가 한 말의 의미는 무엇일까요?
이런 속담을 들어 보신 적이 있으신가요?
분명 근육에 통증을 느끼기도 할 것입니다.
또 그 과정에서 자존심에 상처를 입게 될 수도 있습니다.
실력을 키우고 목표를 이루려면 포기해서는 안됩니다.
영적인 목표를 달성하는 것도 마찬가지라고 할 수 있습니다.
시련을 겪다 보면 약점이 드러나는 경우가 많습니다.
우리의 성품에서 개선해야 할 부면이 있을 수도 있죠.
또는 여호와와의 관계를 더 발전시켜야 할 수도 있습니다.
믿음을 강화하거나 신뢰심을 키워야 할지 모릅니다.
그러니까 그분에 대한 사랑, 믿음, 신뢰심이 계속 자라 갈 것입니다.
따라서 시련을 겪을 때 [반드시 겪게 되겠죠]
쉽게 전 시간 봉사를 그만두지 마십시오.
포기하지 말고 계속 인내하면서 앞으로 나아가십시오!
비슷한 어려움에 성공적으로 대처한 형제 자매들에게 조언을 구하십시오.
여러분도 분명 잘 해낼 수 있을 것입니다.
전 시간 봉사자들이 세 가지 어려움,
즉 경제적인 염려, 다른 사람들의 압력, 예상하지 못한 문제에도 불구하고
어떻게 진정한 평화를 누리게 되었는지 유의해 보십시오.
제게 일자리를 너무 가리지 말라고 조언해 주셨어요.
또 가족들과 함께 솔직하게 이야기를 나누면서
제 수고를 가치 있게 여기신다고 느낍니다.
형제 자매들의 모습을 볼 수 있었습니다.
그 형제 자매들의 훌륭한 본을 보면서
내 태도는 바꿀 수 있다는 걸 깨달았어요.
그 성구에 관한 기사를 읽고 나서
다른 사람을 돕는 데 어떻게 활용할 수 있을까?’
증인이 아닌 가족이 여러분에게 좋은 직장을 구하거나
돈을 많이 벌어야 한다고 말할지 모릅니다.
여러분을 사랑하기 때문에 여러분이 잘되라고 하는 말이겠죠.
전 시간 봉사를 하다 보면 물론 어려움을 겪게 될 수 있죠.
하지만 그와는 비교도 할 수 없는 큰 축복을 누리게 될 것입니다.
영상에 나온 형제 자매들이 어떤 경험을 했는지 생각해 보십시오.
할리는 자신의 결정 덕분에 베델에 가게 되었고,
여호와께서 자신을 정말 사랑하신다고 느끼게 되었습니다.
그 덕분에 다른 사람들에게 더 많은 관심을 기울이게 되었고,
이제 친척들도 그가 좋은 결정을 내렸다고 생각합니다.
칼리는 어려움이 생겼을 때 포기하지 않았습니다.
오히려 사람들을 더 사랑하는 법을 배웠고,
더 강한 그리스도인, 더 훌륭한 그리스도인이 되었습니다.
청소년 형제 자매 여러분, 우리가 확신하는 이유가 뭘까요?
전 시간 봉사를 하면 여러분이 행복한 삶을 살게 될 것이라고 왜 확신할까요?
우리 중 많은 사람이 젊은 시절에 그런 결정을 내렸기 때문입니다.
아까 말씀드린, 어떤 결정을 내려야 할지 고민하던
저도 전 세계의 많은 형제 자매들과 마찬가지로
곧바로 전 시간 봉사를 시작한 겁니다.
저는 그 결정을 내린 걸 한 번도 후회한 적이 없습니다.
앞으로도 그 결정을 내린 걸 결코 후회하지 않을 것입니다.
그분은 여러분이 정말 멋진 삶을 살기를 바라시죠.
가능하다면 전 시간 봉사의 길을 선택하십시오.
우리의 멋진 하느님 여호와와 평화를 누리며
어릴 때부터 전 시간 봉사를 추구하도록
따뜻하게 격려해 주신 샌더슨 형제, 감사합니다.

en.text: We extend a warm welcome to all.
Today’s session will begin with a music-video presentation
that will remind us of the many blessings in store for Jehovah’s servants
and motivate us to share these precious truths with others.
Please enjoy.
During this session and the next,
we will enjoy the talks and videos
under the Saturday heading on your program.
The scripture theme for these two sessions
is taken from 2 Peter 3:14,
where we are admonished
“to be found . . . spotless and unblemished and in peace.”
These sessions will highlight
what we can individually do to ‘pursue peace with others.’
To begin, please join in singing song number 58,
“Searching for Friends of Peace.”
That’s song number 58.
As Jehovah’s people,
we are proud to witness about “the God of peace”
and to proclaim his Kingdom.
How can we give an effective witness
and help interested ones to progress?
Our first symposium for this session will address these questions.
Brother Kenneth Flodin, a helper to the Teaching Committee,
will deliver the first talk of the symposium,
“Be Ready to Share ‘the Good News of Peace’ —Maintain Your Zeal.”
This symposium is about sharing “the good news of peace.”
What a privilege it is to help humble people find peace with Jehovah!
At Ephesians 6:15,
in describing a Christian’s “complete suit of armor,”
it mentions our feet.
Now, back at that time,
thinking of Roman soldiers, Paul knew that often they marched
for hundreds of miles on Roman highways,
crisscrossing the empire.
So at Ephesians 6:15, he said this:
“Having your feet shod in readiness
[in readiness] to declare the good news of peace”
—yes, ready to share “the good news of peace”
on every suitable occasion.
In this symposium, we’ll discuss five ways
to remain ready to preach and teach.
We’d first like to discuss why it’s important to maintain your zeal.
Now, as an analogy,
zeal has often been linked to fire.
We even use the expression —don’t we?—
“He has a fiery zeal for his beliefs.”
But what does “a fiery zeal” indicate?
Please find Romans 1:14, 15,
and here it does not actually use the word “zeal,”
but the sense of the word is evident.
You say: “We’re on fire,” “We’re stoked up,” “We are ready.”
Did you find it?
Romans 1:14, 15:
“Both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to wise and to senseless ones,
“I am a debtor; so I am eager
“[you see, ready with fiery zeal, eager]
to declare the good news.”
Zealous evangelizers are eager to declare the good news—they’re “on fire.”
They want others to find peace with Jehovah.
But is there something that can dampen that flame,
something that could even extinguish the eager desire
—the readiness— to find those who
even unknowingly yearn for peace?
Yes,
it can be difficult to remain eager with fiery zeal
when we face such problems as
an unresponsive territory,
criticism, or outright opposition to the work
—and then there are the pressures of daily life.
Those issues can also be likened to a fire,
to destructive fires like the wildfires
that have plagued the western part of the United States year after year.
Those problems can threaten our zeal and enthusiasm.
So, what can we do?
Well, there’s an English expression that originates with firefighters.
The expression is “Fight fire with fire.”
In the path of a raging wildfire,
one technique is to ignite a controlled fire.
That controlled fire consumes combustible materials.
So when the wildfire advances to that point,
there’s no fuel left and the wildfire goes out.
Fight fire with fire.
Keep your zeal for the ministry burning brightly.
And now please find 1 Timothy 4:16.
If our zeal fades—the flame smolders—
we might miss out on opportunities to help others to gain life,
a life of peace with God.
Look at 1 Timothy 4:16 with me.
It says: “Pay constant attention to yourself and to your teaching”
—you see, the flame, the temperature.
‘Pay attention to your zeal and teaching.’
It says: “Persevere in these things,
“for by doing this you will save both yourself
and those who listen to you.”
Yes, share “the good news of peace” with zeal.
Now, in the following video, note how a couple realized
that the flame had gone out.
They still had some glowing embers left,
but they now find a way to fan the coals
and regain their fiery zeal.
I don’t remember when our routine service day
became so,
well,
routine.
Our zeal wasn’t what it used to be.
And we were finally starting to notice.
Not everyone wants to listen.
We just didn’t want to be the reason.
It didn’t take much research to find
great ideas and set a few simple goals,
like working with those who encourage us.
With Ryota and Ami, we’re always talking
about how we can reach the heart.
We got back to basics:
Be friendly,
listen,
let the conversation progress naturally,
try to share an appealing Scriptural thought,
and keep trying.
Our zeal
can attract an honest person
to the truth.
In the video, what wildfires, or problems,
did the couple face that sucked the oxygen out of their ministry?
Well, of the four we mentioned earlier,
it seems the couple’s zeal was waning
because of seemingly unresponsive territory.
And as tired as the husband looked in that first scene,
the pressures of daily life might have been having a toll on him.
So how did they come to realize
that they needed to fight fire with fire?
Do you remember their kitchen-table talk?
The husband mused that “not everyone wants to listen.”
But then he added, “We just didn’t want to be the reason,”
you see, the reason for them not listening.
They decided to fight fire with fire.
They reignited their own controlled fire of zeal
to counteract the problems they were succumbing to.
Well, what were some of the techniques they used?
The first was to pray to Jehovah.
Could it be that the husband borrowed the words of Romans 12:11 in his prayer?
Yes, he may well have asked Jehovah to help them
as a couple to “be aglow with the spirit.”
Remember he said earlier,
“I don’t remember when our routine service day
became so, well, routine.”
Fight the wildfire by, again, becoming “aglow with the spirit.”
Ensure that any lack of response
is not due to our lackluster approach.
Well, what else did you notice they did to rekindle their zeal?
They did some research, looking for suggestions
to invigorate their ministry.
Yes, and regular Bible study helps us to remember
why we endure in the disciple-making work.
For example, review Jesus’ attitude toward the ministry.
The apostles’ bold witnessing despite fiery opposition
and the disposition of Paul, Aquila and Priscilla, Stephen,
and other Bible characters
—these can infuse us with similar zeal.
Next, keep your ministry fresh.
Well, what does that mean?
Instead of having a number of phone calls that go unanswered,
which is similar to having no one at home when in the door-to-door work,
change the time of day for witnessing
to when more people are home.
Participate in various forms of the ministry.
You know, ironically,
the pandemic more or less forced some of us
who were staunch door-to-door Witnesses to branch out.
We tried phone witnessing and letter writing.
And now we have a variety of preaching activities,
and this can keep us more fully engaged and enthused.
And did you notice what the couple in the video set as a goal?
Periodically, they decided in advance
to share in the ministry with someone specific.
And then they determined to talk about encouraging subjects
when in between calls, whether in phone witnessing
or in the public ministry.
Jehovah values our work in the ministry
regardless of the response we receive.
Hebrews 6:10—are you familiar with that?
Of course you are.
It does not say
that Jehovah does not forget the number of return visits you make.
It does not say he does not forget how many Bible studies you conduct.
No, it says he does not “forget your work [your effort]
and the love you showed for his name.”
Our zeal for the ministry demonstrates
that we have a deep love for Jehovah and Jesus.
If (like the couple in the video) you detect that your
routine of service is becoming, well,
very routine, then fight fire with fire.
Maintain that fiery zeal.
Be ready to share “the good news of peace.”
Brother Robert Ciranko, a helper to the Writing Committee,
will now present the next talk of this symposium,
“Be Ready to Share ‘the Good News of Peace’ —Prepare Well.”
What would you think and how would you feel if I showed up to give this talk
but had done nothing to prepare what to say to you
—if I had not bothered to study the outline I was given,
could not remember the theme, had no idea what the main points are,
and would have to guess at what scriptures to use to support them,
and then, as I spoke, I would ramble incoherently?
I’d make a very bad impression.
I know how I would feel.
I would be a nervous wreck,
and you would wonder why I did not think enough of you
to put all the time and effort that was necessary
into preparing the talk so that you could get the most benefit from it.
Can you see where I’m going with this?
Could the same things be said
if you engaged in the ministry without first preparing what to say?
If you did not review the sample conversations that had been provided,
could not think of how to start a conversation,
and did not know what scripture to share,
how nervous would you be?
And what would the householder think of you?
It would likely be a very short, uncomfortable conversation.
And the other person may not care to have you call again.
We should take some time to prepare well before we preach.
Why?
Because we have the best message ever
—“the good news of peace” to share with people—
and we should do our best so that they will want to listen to what we have to say.
Jesus helped his disciples to prepare for the ministry.
Luke chapter 10 reports that before sending out 70 disciples to preach,
he shared with them a pleasant way to greet each householder,
he told them what to talk about (the Kingdom of God),
and he told them how to respond to the varied reactions
they would get in their territory.
As a result, because the disciples
were fully prepared for the ministry,
they enjoyed some thrilling experiences.
When we are prepared,
we are more poised and enthusiastic and can truly enjoy the ministry.
As you watch the following video,
notice the good results of preparing well.
We’d made some good changes,
but we weren’t done.
I asked Yuri what she planned to talk about.
That started the usual scramble.
Then we got it—the sample conversation.
That’ll do.
But for that to work, I had to remember the scripture.
We were both a little forgetful that morning.
Yeah, we needed to prepare better.
We’d been relying on our experience
and not enough on Jehovah.
So first we prepared our hearts.
Then we prepared our minds
and found new ways to use our preaching tools.
Even a little preparation for initial calls
and our returns visits
went a long way.
The husband said, “Yeah, we needed to prepare better.”
Have you ever thought that about your ministry?
Like the couple in the video,
we can first prepare our heart and our mind
and then see how best to use our preaching tools.
Our goal should be the same as that of the apostle Paul.
At 1 Corinthians 9:23,
he wrote that he wanted
to “do all things for the sake of the good news,
in order to share it with others.”
So let’s think about some specific things that we can do to prepare well,
beginning with what we can say on the initial call,
whether that is done in person or over the telephone.
Each issue of the Christian Life and Ministry—Meeting Workbook
provides us with sample conversations that give us some helpful ideas.
Of course, you may modify the samples or use something entirely different.
Perhaps a subject from a previous month
or a different scripture would have wider appeal in your territory.
Your opening words may be the most important part of the presentation,
so think it through.
If the introduction does not arouse interest,
the other person may terminate the conversation
before we can give a witness.
We will be more effective if we carefully prepare
the first sentence or two that we will say after giving a customary greeting.
We might say, “Many people are concerned about . . . ”
or “I would like to get your opinion on . . . ”
or say something else.
Then pick a topic that is of local interest
and ask a well-worded viewpoint question
that would draw the person into the conversation.
Now, what about preparing for our return visits?
That actually begins on the initial call by leaving a question
for the person to think about until you call again.
That is how the sample initial calls and return visits
are set up in the Meeting Workbook.
By leaving a thought-provoking question at the end of every visit,
we can keep the chain of conversations going as long as possible.
We can illustrate it this way:
Imagine a freight train with an engine at the front,
a caboose at the rear, and many cars in between.
What keeps all of those cars moving together down the train track?
There is a device called a coupler at the back of each train car
that latches onto the coupler at the front of the car behind it.
By being coupled, or linked, together,
the cars all run as a unit along the track.
So the question that we leave with a householder at the end of one visit
is what we can latch onto at the beginning of our next visit
so that we can keep the train of thought going from one conversation to the next.
For example, on the initial call you could ask,
“Why is there so much suffering in the world?”
After discussing that, raise the question,
“How does God feel about our suffering?”
But don’t answer the question until your next visit.
After answering that question on the first return visit,
leave the person with this question, “What will God do to end our suffering?”
This will be discussed on your next visit.
It is also important to have an objective in mind for each return visit.
Before making the call,
think about what you want to accomplish on that call.
If you raised a question the last time,
you’re objective will surely include answering that question from the Bible.
Of course, the ultimate objective is to try to start
a Bible study in the Enjoy Life Forever!  brochure.
Now, what about preparing for the Bible studies that we conduct?
Even if we know the material very well,
we should prepare for each study session with our student in mind.
That means thinking about and anticipating
the views and needs of that individual.
What points might he struggle to understand or accept?
It also means getting familiar with the lesson
to be covered in our interactive Bible course.
Read the lesson carefully,
look up the “read” scriptures to see how they apply,
watch the videos that will be shown during the lesson,
and review the items in the “Explore” section
so that you will know which of those will be especially helpful to your student.
Then you will be well-prepared to conduct the study.
Since it is ‘God who makes the seed of truth grow’ in a person’s heart,
we should ask for Jehovah’s blessing on our preparation for the study
so that we can best help the student spiritually.
And we will be more effective in our ministry
if we stay up-to-date with the latest material
and features found on jw.org and on JW Library®.
So learn how to navigate the website and the app.
Two very helpful features on the website
are “Bible Questions Answered” under the Bible Teachings tab
and “Frequently Asked Questions” under the About Us tab.
They can also be found on the app under “Article Series.”
The apostle Paul described himself at 1 Corinthians 3:10
“as a skilled master builder.”
That is because he was engaging
in a spiritual construction work to build Christian disciples.
And we are doing the same sort of work when we engage in the ministry.
But to build effectively, we must learn to use our tools well.
We especially need to develop skill in using our principal tool, God’s Word,
as well as learn how to make effective use of the publications
in our Teaching Toolbox.
A builder who prepares before starting to work
avoids mistakes and frustration.
Remember what the brother said at the end of the video?
‘Even a little preparation goes a long way.’
And that is what will help you to do your best in the ministry.
Just as Paul recommended at 2 Timothy 2:15
—please follow along in your Bible, if you will—
it’s 2 Timothy 2:15:
“Do your utmost to present yourself approved to God,
“a workman with nothing to be ashamed of,
handling the word of the truth aright.”
Then you will experience great joy in the spiritual building work
that is taking place now because you will be ready
and well-prepared to share “the good news of peace.”
Brother Anthony Morris, a member of the Governing Body,
will now present the next talk of the symposium,
“Be Ready to Share ‘the Good News of Peace’ —Take the Initiative.”
For this part of the symposium,
“Share ‘the Good News of Peace,’”
we’re going to discuss the need to take the initiative.
Now, we’re going to look
at why we should take the initiative,
how to take the initiative,
and then a concluding thought about who’s helping
in directing us in our preaching work.
Now, first of all, why take the initiative?
Well, think about it.
One thing about being Jehovah’s Witnesses
is that we’re never off duty.
We never stop being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
—wherever we are or whatever we’re doing.
So it isn’t just when we’re out
in the formal preaching work with a congregation group
—we are one of Jehovah’s Witnesses all the time.
There’s no such thing as being off duty
when we’re one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Now, to give you an idea of how
significant this is with informal witnessing,
I will tell you a statistic: A survey was taken some years ago
(and you’d be surprised, possibly),
and one group of over 200 baptized Witnesses,
now notice, over 40 percent
had been contacted by informal witnessing.
Isn’t that amazing?
So the door-to-door work is crucial.
Of course, during COVID-19 that’s been inhibited
—letter writing has its place and also phone witnessing.
But the point is, there are other times
when we can do some witnessing informally.
Now, let’s examine how to do it?
And the best example of how to do informal witnessing
is, of course, Christ Jesus.
And there’s an account that all of us are familiar with in the Bible book of John.
So please find John chapter 4,
and we’re going to take a look at how Jesus took the initiative
and then imitate him
—do just as he did.
Now notice here in John chapter 4
(we get the context), they’ve been traveling through Samaria.
And then verse 6, we’ll read:
“In fact, Jacob’s well was there.
“Now Jesus, tired out as he was from the journey,
“was sitting at the well.
It was about the sixth hour.”
Now, that’s interesting, is it not?
Jesus was tired.
He was a perfect man, but human,
and his journey tired him out.
And he’s there about noon sitting at the well.
And now notice what happens in verse 7:
“A woman of Samaria came to draw water.
Jesus said to her: ‘Give me a drink.’”
Real simple—“Give me a drink.”
Well, what do we learn from this?
As you noticed, Jesus was tired.
We get tired
because of being imperfect.
If a perfect man gets tired out, certainly we get tired.
Sometimes you may feel: ‘Well, you know, maybe I could witness
‘to this person —take the initiative.
But I just don’t feel like it. I’m tired.’
Not with Jesus.
See, to imitate Jesus, even in the case when you’re tired,
you’re thinking of others.
You want to take the opportunity to start a conversation.
That’s the initial goal.
Now, notice something else here
that we learn in the 9th verse
of John chapter 4:
“So the Samaritan woman said to him:
“‘How is it that you, despite being a Jew,
ask me for a drink even though I am a Samaritan woman?’”
And then we learn more here in parentheses:
“For Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.”
And it went both ways.
That’s the way prejudice was —“no dealings”—

and when we refuse to give up, we become stronger.
We become stronger in our spirituality
and our relationship with Jehovah
—our love for him, our faith in him, our trust in him
just continues to grow.
As James says there in verse 4,
we become “complete and sound in all respects,
not lacking in anything.”
So when those trials come
—and they will come—
don’t look for a quick way out.
Endure, keep going, don’t give up!
Seek advice from brothers and sisters who have successfully coped
with similar challenges, and you too will be successful.
In the following video,
notice how some full-time servants have found real peace
despite those three obstacles: financial concerns,
pressure from others, and unexpected challenges.
I prayed to Jehovah,
“If it is your will, I would be happy
to enter pioneer service.”
But I had to work really hard to provide for the needs of my family
because my father had died when he was 45 years old.
The elder that I talked to
gave me advice not to be picky about what kind of job I could get.
He reminded me of Matthew 6:33, and told me
not to be overly anxious.
Because of our good communication within the family,
we were able to find solutions.
My other siblings realized that they also shared
responsibility in providing for the needs of the family.
After one year of pioneering, I was encouraged to apply for Bethel service,
and now I am in Bethel.
I feel that Jehovah really cares for me, loves me,
and appreciates all my efforts.
Because they love me, my cousins pressured me to choose a secular career.
If I went against
their wishes, it would hurt them
and put a strain on our relationship.
I was really anxious.
I wanted to show my trust in Jehovah by pioneering
and give him an opportunity to show me that I can be happy in his service.
I tried to express my appreciation for my cousins by what
I said and did
and showed them love.
They’ve realized that I have changed for the better.
I show more concern for others now.
Now they understand that we have been learning good things and that we have
a happier and more meaningful life.
I wanted to try serving
where the need was greater.
When I first arrived,
I thought it was so cool being there.
I had expected the poverty, but when I saw it,
it hit home more than what I had expected.
So then I started to feel really homesick.
But my brothers and sisters—
I’d go to the Kingdom Hall and they were able to cope with the challenges
that they were facing because they had Jehovah in their life.
So their example really helped me to see that my circumstances
don’t need to change for my attitude to change.
Proverbs 15:15 stood out to me,
which is about having “a cheerful heart”
and being able to have “a continual feast” no matter what my circumstances are.
And I found an article about that scripture.
And so from there, I decided to ask myself, ‘How can I use my situation
and what I’m learning to help others?’
And I got to start helping with a foreign-language group there.
That whole experience
just made my love for people grow so much
and definitely changed my life.
Some of your non-Witness family members
might offer you secular or financial advice.
We know they mean well
and they feel that they’re giving you the best advice
because they love you.
But, young brothers and sisters,
we are convinced that the blessings of full-time service
far outweigh any challenges
that might go along with it.
Just think of the experiences that we heard in the video.
Harley’s choices allowed him to go to Bethel
and helped him to feel that Jehovah really loved him.
Anjil’s choices took courage,
but those choices helped him to be more concerned about other people
and helped his relatives to see
that he had made a good decision.
And Carlee did not give up when the trials came.
Instead, she learned to love other people even more
and became a more powerful, strong Christian.
Brothers and sisters, why are we so convinced
that full-time service will lead you young ones
to a wonderful life?
Well, it’s because that’s the decision
that so many of us made when we were young.
Do you remember that 18-year-old young brother
who was trying to decide which path to take?
Well, that was me some years ago.
I’m so glad
that with the help of Jehovah and my parents
and other mature friends in the congregation,
I made the decision
just like so many other brothers and sisters around the world
to turn down that scholarship,
to give up university,
and to go directly into the full-time service.
That is a decision that I have never regretted;
that is a decision that I will never regret.
Young people, Jehovah loves you.
He wants you to have a wonderful, awesome life.
Choose the path of full-time service if you can.
You will never regret it.
It will put you on a path that leads to joy and peace
with our marvelous, wonderful God, Jehovah.
Thank you, Brother Sanderson,
for the warm encouragement to pursue full-time service
from an early age.
Now we invite all to join in singing song number 135,
“Jehovah’s Warm Appeal: ‘Be Wise, My Son.’”
That’s song number 135.

ko.text: 팬데믹 때문에 여전히 학급이 열리지 않고 있습니다.
학급이 재개되었을 때 검토될 수 있도록
또한 봉사 훈련 학교나 독신 형제 성서 학교 졸업생으로서
여전히 독신으로 전 시간 봉사를 하고 있는 사람들도
이제 왕국 전파자 학교에 지원할 수 있음을
어려움을 겪을 때 여호와께서 어떻게 우리의 필요를 채워 주십니까?
여호와의 축복으로 평화를 누린 형제 자매들의 경험을 보게 되실 것입니다.
「어려움 속에서도 평화를 누리는 우리 형제들 —반대, 질병, 경제적 어려움, 자연재해」
우리 모두는 평화를 빼앗아 갈 수 있는
그리고 이겨 내기 위해 어떻게 힘써 노력했는지
평화를 되찾고 유지하기 위해 어떻게 했는지 유의해 보십시오.
여호와께서 그들을 어떻게 도우셨는지 확인해 보십시오.

저는 그 문제를 따지지 않기로 했어요.
그 자매와 일주일을 같이 살아야 하니까요.
자매가 저와 지내다 보면 제가 나쁜 뜻으로 말한 게 아니라는 걸 깨달을 거라고 생각했죠.
월요일에 우리가 떠날 때는 자매와 정말 친한 사이가 됐죠.
자매는 절 안아 주었고, 그 문제는 언급하지 않았습니다.
자매의 영적인 특성을 볼 수 있었습니다.
마지막으로, 여호와의 평화의 길로 걸은 것이 그분과 평화를 누리는 데 어떻게 도움이 되셨나요?
여호와께서 저 자신을 위해 행동하시는 걸 여러 번 경험하면 그분의 승인을 받고 있다는 느낌이 들죠.
저희 부부는 이제 나이가 많이 들었는데요.
오랫동안 저희 목표였던 베델 봉사를 할 수 있도록 여호와께서 마음의 소원을 들어주셨다는 생각이 듭니다.
제가 충실을 유지하는 한 여호와께서 저에게 마음의 평화를 주실 거라고 확신합니다.
여호와께서 자매에게 그렇게 해 주실 것이라고 저희도 확신합니다.
저희를 위해 격려적인 이야기를 들려주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
이제 세 번째 요점을 생각해 볼까요?
여호와의 평화의 길로 계속 걷기 위해 어떻게 할 수 있습니까?
문자적인 길을 가다 보면 길의 상태가 달라지거나 날씨가 나빠져서 조정을 해야 할 수도 있습니다.
마찬가지로 여러분도 평화의 길을 걷다 보면 자신의 생각과 행동을 조정해야 할 때가 있을 겁니다.
최근에 한 순회 감독자가 우리의 생각과 태도에 관해 흥미로운 이야기를 해 주었는데요.
우리의 생각과 태도가 감옥이 될 수도 있고, 여권이 될 수도 있다고 했죠.
감옥이 되는 경우는 우리의 생각과 행동이 우리를 제한하거나 가두는 경우가 되겠죠.
여권이 되는 경우는 우리가 가야 할 곳으로 갈 수 있게 해 주는 경우입니다.
우리는 지금 생명의 길에 있어야 하고, 그 길에 머물러야 합니다.
그러기 위해서는 우리가 계속 영적으로 발전해야겠죠.
우리의 생각과 행동이 우리가 발전하지 못하게 가두거나 제한하는 일이 없도록 필요한 조정을 해야 합니다.
그러면 어떤 부면에서 발전할 필요가 있을까요?
바울이 고린도 후서 13장에서 한 말을 살펴보시겠습니다.
“끝으로 형제 여러분, 계속 기뻐하고 자신을 바로잡고 위로를 받고 일치된 생각을 하고 평화롭게 지내십시오.
그러면 사랑과 평화의 하느님께서 여러분과 함께 계실 것입니다.”
어떤 세 가지 부면에서 조정할 수 있다고 했는지 유의하셨습니까?
살면서 생기는 걱정거리에 지나치게 신경 쓰다 보면 평화와 기쁨을 잃게 됩니다.
따라서 기쁨을 유지하기 위해, 슬픔을 주는 것보다는 기쁨을 주는 것에 초점을 맞춰 보십시오.
몸이 좋지 않거나 만성 질환에 시달리고 있다면 병이 사라질 것이라는 하느님의 약속에 초점을 맞출 수 있을 것입니다.
믿음 때문에 반대를 받는 경우라면 어떠합니까?
우리를 위해 기도하고 우리를 지원하는 영적 가족에 초점을 맞추십시오.
또 여러 영적 마련들이 우리를 강하게 해 주고 있다는 점도 생각해 보십시오.
세계의 사건들 때문에 낙담이 된다면, 우리에게 미래에 대한 희망이 있다는 점을 떠올리며 기뻐할 수 있습니다.
이 모든 것이 곧 끝나고 더 나은 미래가 올 거니까요.
요점은 부정적인 생각이 여러분의 발전을 제한하게 해서는 안 된다는 것입니다.
그렇게 해서 앞으로 나아가고 기쁨을 유지하십시오.
11절에 언급된 조정해야 할 또 다른 부면을 생각해 보죠.
1세기 회중들의 일부 성원들은 배교적인 생각을 퍼뜨리고 있었습니다.
논쟁이 될 만한 말을 하는 사람들도 있었죠.
그들의 말은 성경에 정면으로 위배되지는 않았지만 분열을 일으켰습니다.
그 결과 회중에 말다툼과 논쟁이 일어났고, 영적으로 좋지 않은 분위기가 형성되었습니다.
계속 일치된 생각을 하는 데 무엇이 도움이 될까요?
물론 우리는 여호와의 도덕법에 분명하게 위배되는 문제에 있어서는 단호한 입장을 취합니다.
하지만 성경 원칙을 어기는 경우가 아니라면 개인의 의견을 내세우지 않는 것이 좋습니다.
논쟁을 일으키거나 논쟁에 휘말리지 않도록 최선을 다해 노력하십시오.
우리가 조정을 할 수 있는 세 번째 부면은 계속 “평화롭게 지내”는 것입니다.
아까 회견에서 두 자매가 평화를 위협하는 상황에서 어떻게 대처했는지 기억하십니까?
그리고 성경의 교훈을 깊이 묵상해 보았죠.
그런 다음 그런 교훈을 자신의 상황에 어떻게 적용할 수 있는지 잘 생각해 보았습니다.
그 결과 마음의 평화를 얻었고 다른 사람들과도 평화를 누릴 수 있었습니다.
모든 사람에게 사랑과 관대함을 나타내어 평화를 유지하기 위해 계속 노력하십시오.
특히 가족을 대할 때 그렇게 하십시오.
오늘이 매우 중요한 날이라는 점을 다시 한 번 말씀드리고 싶습니다.
시간을 내어 오늘이 여러분에게 어떤 의미가 있는지 깊이 생각해 보십시오.
여러분은 여호와께 헌신하기로 한 여러분의 결정을 결코 후회하지 않으실 것입니다.
침례를 받는다고 해서 여러분의 여정이 끝나는 것은 아닙니다.
생명의 길에 계속 머무르기 위해 최선을 다하시기 바랍니다.
첫째로, 여호와의 평화의 길로 걷는 것을 포기하지 마십시오.
둘째로, 생명의 길의 경계 내에 머무르십시오.
여러분은 목적을 가지고 이 길을 걸어가고 있습니다.
그리고 이 길의 목적지는 여호와와 영원히 평화로운 관계를 누리는 것입니다.
마지막으로, 필요하다면 여러분의 생각과 태도와 행동을 계속 조정해 나가십시오.
그렇게 해서 여호와와, 그리고 다른 사람들과 평화를 누리십시오.
이러한 일들을 계속한다면 여러분은 평화를 누리게 될 것입니다.
그에 더해 고린도 후서 13:11에서 알려 주는 것처럼
“사랑과 평화의 하느님께서 여러분과 함께 계실 것입니다.”
여호와께서 평화의 길로 계속 걷는 사람들에게 하신 이 약속을
올해에도 침례를 받는 상황이 장소에 따라 다를 것입니다.
지역 상황에 따라 적절한 마련을 해 놓았을 것입니다.
지원자들은 이번 회기가 마친 다음 침례를 받게 될 것입니다.
우리는 이 회기에서 즐긴 시기 적절한 영적 양식에 대해 여호와께 감사합니다.
우리가 어떻게 평화를 깨뜨리는 일들을 피할 수 있는지 알아볼 것입니다.
어떤 일들을 할 수 있는지도 살펴볼 것입니다.
그리고 성경 드라마 제1부를 시청할 것입니다.
이제 이 회기를 마치는 노래를 함께 부르실까요?
노래를 부른 후 따로 마치는 기도를 하실 수 있습니다.

en.text: Have you applied to the School for Kingdom Evangelizers
but not been invited?
Or have you wanted to apply
but wondered if the time was right?
You are not alone.
Because of the pandemic, classes are still suspended.
But if you are a pioneer between the ages of 23 and 65
and would like to attend a future class of SKE,
please contact your congregation secretary
and fill out the online application
so that it can be considered when classes resume.
As a reminder, your application is active for one year.
Therefore, you must apply each year that you desire to be considered.
Additionally, we are pleased to inform you
that graduates of the Ministerial Training School
or the Bible School for Single Brothers
who are still single and in full-time service
may now apply for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Is it possible to maintain our peace
when dealing with intense trials and pressures?
How does Jehovah care for our needs when we are in distress?
The following video will introduce us to brothers and sisters
who have been blessed by Jehovah with peace.
The title is
How Our Brothers Are Enjoying Peace
Despite . . . Opposition, Illness,
Economic Problems, Natural Disasters.
As long as we live in Satan’s world,
all of us will face situations
that can rob us of our peace.
Regaining that peace can be difficult
but not impossible.
In this video, we will hear
from three sisters and two couples
who will speak candidly about their trials
and how they struggled to cope with them.
But in spite of what they have endured,
please take note of their smiles, their joy,
and what they did to regain and maintain their peace.
And take special note of how Jehovah helped them.
The Governing Body knows that many of you
are suffering circumstances
not unlike the ones we will hear about,
and they trust that the examples in this video
will help each of you to maintain your peace
as you endure various trials.
Brothers and sisters all over the world are facing
natural disasters,
economic collapse,
illness,
and persecution.
Despite all that,
they keep joy and peace.
I can learn a lot from them.
My name is Antoinette.
I live here in Las Vegas, Nevada,
with my supermom
and my troublemaking sister.
Family and friends have always been important to me.
As a child, I lived with my mom and dad
and I was very close to my dad’s side of the family.
It was very loving, unified, and fun.
I was pretty happy.
But I already was starting to feel the effects of my cancer.
We just didn’t know what it was really.
One day I was OK, and then the next day I started feeling bad, you know.
In my childhood,
I played an unusual game.
I would catch insects,
put them in a jar, and then bring them home.
Then, I would get books, such as the Criminal Procedural Code,
open them up, and start judging one of the bugs.
I would play the role of investigator and judge at the same time.
I was born into a family where everyone,
starting with my grandparents,
was either wearing an officer’s uniform or a judge’s robe.
That’s why I had this strong sense of justice.
But in 1989,
my mother was in a tragic car accident,
and
she got severe burns
on her face, hands, and body.
And then my father,
at seeing my mom’s condition,
decided to leave us.
Yeah.
And it was at that moment, I guess,
that my world, my ideals,
they crumbled.
As a little kid, I always wanted, like, one big happy family.
Once we moved to New York for my treatment,
I no longer had that big family bond anymore.
What I was feeling back then in New York was
just sadness,
never really peace.
Here in California,
we’re used to fires.
But when I got the call to evacuate that morning,
I never knew that by that evening,
the whole town of Paradise would be gone.
Just before the fire, we had the needs of the congregation
where they instructed us what to do in the case of a disaster.
I had the truck full of gas,
I had my go bag ready,
and I had a map of where I was going.
I was ready.
The brothers, also in their instructions,
said to obey the traffic instructors.
The instructor told us to turn right,
and I didn’t want to turn right,
but they said obey them.
So I turned right,
though I thought it would be really bad.
The smoke got darker and darker,
and finally it got black.
You couldn’t see anything.
My mom has always told me
that I’ve always been
a caregiver ever since I was a little girl;
it was just part of who I was.
I don’t like to see people suffer; it’s very difficult for me.
I remember that when I first started working as a nurse,
I would always cry.
I cried— Literally I cried
every day that I had to go to work.
Not only was I overwhelmed being a new nurse
but also
I was battling my depression.
I was the treasurer
for a prestigious bank in Nicaragua,
and I was the father of a one-year-old son.
We were very happy.
But then I lost my job.
So I said, ‘I have the experience,
and Jehovah will help me find another job, something similar.’
And I kept looking for jobs, but doors kept closing.
I felt very tense;
it made me feel very useless,
like
I couldn’t even provide for my family.
It was something very difficult for me.
These dear brothers and sisters
faced serious challenges.
They may have had moments when they felt like Job
when he said: “I loathe my life.”
That is not an unusual human emotion.
Sometimes things in life
don’t work out as we had hoped,
and it can hurt us deeply.
Does this mean that we are helpless victims of our circumstances?
Not at all!
Please pay close attention
and take note of why we can say
that Margaret, Feliks,
Miguel, Nikki, and Antoinette
are not helpless victims.
To the contrary,
they are conquerors.
As you watch and listen,
look for specific actions they took
to maintain their peace
and please give thoughtful attention
to ways that you can imitate their faith.
Growing up, I wondered,
‘Why does the Supreme Judge, God,
allow injustice and suffering?’
And inside of me, I had this need to restore justice.
It was such a burning desire within me.
And with that in mind,
I moved to Russia to stay with my sister.
She started to study the Bible
and was overflowing with the truth.
We talked for hours till late into the night.
So that’s when my special relationship with Jehovah began.
That’s when I got a taste of what it’s like
to have a caring Father.
It had been a while since I was able to feel that.
My baptism date was very exciting.
The spiritual family I inherited was very vast.
You can instantly feel the love.
I got baptized, and it seemed like miracles happened
one after the other.
We had a great life.
And then
the persecution started with Brother Christensen,
and then there was a ripple effect of arrests, one after the other.
Then it was our turn.
In June of 2018,
a huge group of armed men came to us, to our home.
They represented the ideals of my childhood.
But now these people,
this judicial system,
became the source of injustice to me.
I was sitting in a cage, the same way my bugs used to be in a jar.
I guess I felt like they did.
In your head at that moment when you hear the verdict
that you’ll stay in prison,
it’s like you’ve been knocked unconscious.
You’ve been hit in the head with something,
and there’s just a ringing sound in your ears.
And so I was taken away in handcuffs.
Of course, I wasn’t in the best mood.
But then
the doors of the elevator opened up, and in front of us,
a lot of brothers and sisters
were clapping their hands as hard as they could.
And some were crying,
but not crying because they felt sorry for me.
They cried because they loved us
and because they were proud of us.
That’s what always happens.
When you’re just about to lose all your strength,
Jehovah does that something for you that gives you a second wind.
And so, the applause, the love,
the tears,
the shouts, “Hang in there; everything will be OK!”
—they gave me a second wind.
And with renewed strength, I could run the next part of the race.
One of the guards was so surprised that he said,
“Now that’s some support you’ve got!”
Yeah.
Without friends, I would be very lonely.
I would constantly be focusing on my illness.
The day I met Marissa was at a convention.
She’s a really great friend, a spiritual friend.
When she’d take me to my hospital appointments,
we would eat out.
I think food is just the common language between everyone, you know.
When you talk about food, you know, it’s like:
“Ah! Yes, we have something to talk about,” you know.
I would be excited when she would take me to my hospital appointment.
She always makes me laugh, you know.
She always helps me have a good time no matter what.
Again, friends really help encourage me.
Proverbs 17:17 says:
“A true friend shows love at all times
and is a brother who is born for times of distress.”
And I have seen this come true in my life.
When I lost my job at the bank,
well, I felt very depressed, troubled, tense.
And I have a good friend who I can talk to,
and when I told him how I was feeling, he told me:
“Look, Miguel, don’t look for the same
“line of work.
“Maybe what you need to do is make a change in your life.
“Why don’t you find some simple work outside of an office for a time?
“That can help you to keep your eye simple
and allow you to provide for your family.”
I watched my wife make bread for our family,
and one day I told her:
“I’m going to make that bread, but not for our family.
I’m going to make it to sell.”
So she told me, “No, are you crazy?”
It was a big change—right?—
from having a position at a bank
and handling a lot of money
to selling on the street.
So I told her, “Look, I’m going to put this hat on,”
and I put like a chef’s hat on.
And I told her,
“I’ll be back in less than an hour, whether I sell or not.”
And that’s what happened.
And to her surprise, I came back without any bread.
So when I got ready to leave the second time to sell,
she said: “OK. Go, but leave the hat here.”
I also started to iron clothes for people in their homes,
and it looked strange because normally where we live
that type of work is done by a woman.
But for a man to go and iron clothes at someone’s home,
you don’t see that.
But I didn’t want to just sit back with my arms crossed
and see what would happen.
No!
I had to put my hands to work to earn a living for my family.
So I would preach one day, and the next day I would iron clothes.
The next day I would preach, and the day after that I would go out and sell bread.
So my mind was always occupied on doing something,
either for the Kingdom or my family.
And that helped me a lot.
I was feeling so sad.
I really needed Jehovah’s help to figure out what was going on with me.
And I remember
that the 2009 article about depression came out.
And I realized: ‘OK, Jehovah, you’re telling me this is what I have.
‘So now that I realize I have this,
I’ve got to figure out how I can manage it.’
So I changed my eating habits.
I started exercising a lot more.
I realized that exercising and eating healthy
really, really did help.
Also, I made a journal,
and I made different sections
of the different aspects of my depression that I dealt with.
In each section, I would put scriptures;
I would put articles.
And the illustrations, the pictures,
they speak a lot without saying anything.
Jehovah hears us.
Jehovah cares.
After some time in prison,
they transferred me to a different cell.
In it were inmates who followed the orders
of the investigators.
They did everything they could to other inmates
to make life unbearable.
Why did they do this?
To break a person
so that they would start to collaborate with the investigators,
confess to everything, and then be able to get transferred to another area.
Psalm 37:3: “Trust in Jehovah and do what is good.”
I said: “Jehovah, please help me to stay loyal to you.
Please help me.”
My prayers were really simple
—actually like two words: “Jehovah, help!
Jehovah, help! Jehovah, help!”
Despite how they treated me,
when I dealt with others, I tried to treat them with kindness.
These people,
they made life
uncomfortable, unbearable,
but when they were treated kindly,
they started to soften.
They began to treat me differently.
When I was being transferred
out of that cell,
the inmate who ran the area called me over to him and said,
“Come sit beside me.”
And I sat down.
Then he said, “If anybody in this prison touches you,
tell him that I’ll come looking for him.”
Then he said, “Get his things”
(he told the other prisoners).
The cell doors opened
and the guards saw
a crowd of inmates
grabbing my things and putting them out into the hallway.

Well, let’s go back to our illustration of the road.
On a literal road, travelers may need to make adjustments
in response to changing road conditions
or bad weather.
Similarly, as you go on walking in the way of peace,
you will need to readjust your actions and thinking from time to time.
Recently, a circuit overseer shared an interesting point
regarding our thoughts and attitudes on matters.
He said that they could either serve
as a prison or a passport:
a prison, in that our thoughts and actions
can confine or restrict us
or a passport,
in that they can take us where we need to be.
Well, right now, we need to be
and stay on this road to life.
So we want to make sure that any needed adjustments are made
in our thoughts and our actions
so that we’re not confined or restricted
in making spiritual progress.
Well, what might be some areas
that we’ll need to make adjustments?
Notice, please, Paul’s words in 2 Corinthians chapter 13.
And we’ll read 2 Corinthians 13:11.
Paul says: “Finally, brothers,
“continue to rejoice, to be readjusted,
“to be comforted, to think in agreement,
“to live peaceably;
and the God of love and of peace will be with you.”
Did you notice three areas in this verse
where Paul states we can make adjustments?
First, he says: “Continue to rejoice.”
We can lose our peace and joy
if we become overwhelmed by the anxieties of life.
So in order to rejoice,
can you make it a goal to focus on things
that bring joy rather than sadness?
So if you’re not feeling well or coping with chronic pain,
you can focus on God’s promise of when no one will say:
“I am sick.”
If you’re facing opposition for your beliefs,
focus on the fact that we’re part of a brotherhood
—a brotherhood that supports and prays for us—
and arrangements are in place to keep us spiritually strong.
If you’re discouraged by world events,
you can rejoice in the fact
that you have a hope for the future,
and we know how this all ends.
We know that better times are ahead.
The point is, Don’t let negative thoughts
restrict or limit your progress.
Instead, make the needed adjustments
so that you can move forward and continue to rejoice.
Note another area for readjustment that Paul mentions in verse 11.
There he says: “Continue . . .
to think in agreement.”
There were members of the congregation
back in the first century that were promoting apostate ideas.
Others were introducing controversial ideas
that were not directly unscriptural,
but they were divisive.
This resulted in bickering and arguments over words,
really creating a spiritually unhealthy atmosphere.
Well, what’s going to help us
to continue to think in agreement?
Remember Paul’s words at 2 Timothy 2:23
to “reject foolish and ignorant debates,
knowing that they produce fights.”
Of course, we react strongly when facing issues
that clearly violate Jehovah’s moral laws.
But if no Scriptural principle is being violated,
we’re wise to abstain from promoting our personal opinions.
We want to do all we can to avoid starting
or being drawn into disagreements
that can disrupt the peace of the congregation.
Now, back in verse 11,
a third area where we can make adjustments
is to continue “to live peaceably.”
Did you notice from the interview with our sisters
what they both did when challenged,
when faced with a challenge that threatened their peace?
They took the matter to Jehovah in prayer.
They reflected on scriptures found in God’s Word.
And then they looked to see how they could apply those verses
in their particular situation.
It helped them to not only have inner peace
but peace with others as well.
So let your spiritual qualities shine through.
Continue to work on keeping peace,
showing those qualities of being loving and generous toward all,
but especially with our close family members,
whether they are Witnesses or not.
Well, we want to conclude by reminding you baptism candidates
that today marks a significant milestone
in your journey in your relationship with Jehovah.
So take the time to appreciate
what this day means for you.
We’re so proud of all of you.
You will never regret the decision you have made
to dedicate your life to Jehovah.
But keep in mind that after today and beyond,
the journey is not yet over.
Really, it’s just the beginning.
So we encourage you to do all you can
to stay on the road to life.
Keep in mind the points we considered today.
First, do not give up on walking in Jehovah’s way of peace.
Your life depends on it.
Allow Jehovah to guide your steps.
Second, stay within the boundaries on the road to life.
Remember, you’re walking with a purpose,
and that will lead you to your destination
—peaceful friendship with Jehovah forever.
And finally, keep making any needed adjustments
in your thoughts, attitude, and actions
so that you can maintain peace with Jehovah and peace with others.
If you continue to do these things,
not only will you have peace
but as the last part of 2 Corinthians 13:11 says:
“The God of love and of peace
will be with you.”
May you always remember that promise,
which Jehovah makes to those
who go on walking in the way of peace.
Thank you, Brother Turner.
Similar to last year,
the arrangements for baptism will vary in each location.
Each local congregation’s elders have made suitable provisions
in accord with local circumstances
for candidates to be baptized after the conclusion of this session.
We thank Jehovah for the timely spiritual food we enjoyed
during this session of the convention.
Our next session will show us how to avoid
common pitfalls to pursuing peace.
It will highlight specific activities
that peacemakers excel at.
We will also enjoy part one of the feature Bible drama.
But now, let’s sing together the closing song for this session,
song number 54, “‘This Is the Way.’”
After the song, you may have your own concluding prayer.
That’s song number 54.
