因为彼此亲如一家”
在真理中进步的一个方法是
努力找机会对别人行善
包括对弟兄姐妹和基督徒会众以外的人行善
疫情期间我们有很多机会这样做
我们常常打电话关心别人
也给他们送食物和其他必需品
另外，我们的弟兄姐妹一次又一次
努力帮助受天灾影响的人
所以要花点时间想想你周围的情况
你可以怎样对所有人行善呢？
有没有人需要帮忙买菜或做其他事呢？
有没有人心情低落，需要听到鼓励的话呢？
有没有人要应付失去亲友的伤痛
特别需要得到安慰
或有人听他们倾诉呢？
你显出耶和华喜爱的特质
比如仁慈、体恤、好客、慷慨施与
就会得到耶和华丰厚的奖赏
也会感到很满足
你这样做会让耶和华很开心
因为他看出你行走通往生命之路的目的
不仅仅是要救自己，也是要帮助别人
现在来看看第三个相似之处
无论是实际的路，还是通往生命的路
我们都有想要到达的终点或目的地
一条实际的路最终会把你带到一个目的地
身为耶和华见证人，我们踏上的这条路
这个旅程，也会把我们带到一个目的地
就是跟耶和华享有和睦的关系，直到永远
当然，我们都很向往上帝的新世界
但就算是现在
只要我们尽心尽力地为上帝服务
就能享有很多福分和内心的安宁
现在我们很高兴访问赫德姐妹
赫德姐妹受浸超过70年了
她和丈夫从事特别全时服务多年
有很多美好的经历
她的丈夫是中央长老团成员赫德弟兄
赫德姐妹，我们知道你一路走来
得到了很多福分
但也肯定遇到过不少困难
多年来，你在不同的岗位上为耶和华服务
行走他的平安之路
什么帮助你一直保持内心的安宁呢？
这么多年来，我学到
如果耶和华给你一个任务
他就一定会帮助你完成这个任务
我们从探访会众的监督和他们的妻子
学到很多
我很荣幸能跟这些忠贞的弟兄姐妹一起服务
我小的时候
其中一些就是探访我们会众的监督
看到他们这么忠贞，这么快乐
内心有真正的安宁，对我帮助很大
我从他们身上学到很多
很想效法他们的榜样
有这些榜样，真是个福分
还有什么帮助了你呢？
常常向耶和华祷告也帮助我享有内心的安宁
很多次我们钱不多，甚至根本没钱
但我们从来没有饿过肚子
也从来没有错过聚会和大会
我们从这些经历学到
就算没有钱，也难不倒耶和华
我们的祷告他都听到了，也回应了
有时候福分就好像从天上掉下来的一样
祷告的力量真的很大，谢谢分享
那么行走耶和华的平安之路
怎样帮助你跟别人和睦相处呢？
我跟很多姐妹一起工作过，甚至一起住过
她们都有不同的性格
我学到要运用罗马书12:18的原则
经文说
“只要自己做得到
就要尽可能跟所有人和睦相处”
我学到，有时候为了跟别人和睦相处
我必须自己作出调整
这样的事常常发生
我记得有一次
我们星期二早上搬到一个姐妹家
我说了一些话，让她很不高兴
她非常生气
当时我决定先不解释太多
因为还要在她家住一个星期
我打算用我的行为让她看出
我的话绝对不是她想的那个意思
时间一天一天过去
我们的关系不那么紧张了
到周一我离开的时候
我们已经成了好朋友
她给了我一个大大的拥抱
那件事就过去了
这个问题你处理得很好
看得出来你有非常美好的特质
最后，行走上帝的平安之路
怎样帮助你跟上帝享有和睦的关系呢？
当你看到耶和华
一次又一次地帮助你、指引你
你就会感受到他是认可你的
现在我们夫妻俩年纪都大了
耶和华真的把我们心里渴求的赐给了我们
让我们在伯特利服务
这是我们多年来的心愿
我知道，只要我一直忠于耶和华
他就会继续赐给我内心的安宁
对，我们知道他一定会的
谢谢你，赫德姐妹
谢谢你接受访谈
我们真的受到很大的鼓励
让我们来谈谈第三个问题
我们怎样做
就能继续行走耶和华的平安之路？
让我们回到之前的比喻
走在实际的路上时
我们可能需要根据路况或天气
作出相应的调整
类似地，当你继续行走平安之路时
也需要时不时调整自己的思想和行为
最近，有个分区监督
跟我讲了一个很有意思的比喻
他是这么说的
我们的思想和行为既可以是监狱
也可以是护照
是监狱
意思是我们的思想和行为
可以束缚或限制我们
是护照
意思是可以带我们去想要去的地方
现在我们必须踏上
并且继续行走这条通往生命的路
所以，我们要作出必要的调整
目的是确保我们的思想和行为
不会束缚或限制我们
使我们停滞不前
我们可能在哪些方面需要作出调整呢？
请留意保罗在哥林多后书13章说的话
我们会看哥林多后书13:11
“最后，弟兄们，你们要继续欢欣喜乐
接受纠正，接受安慰
思想一致，和睦共处
这样，充满爱心、赐人安宁的上帝
就会与你们同在”
保罗提到了三个方面
我们可以努力在这三方面作出调整
首先，他说
“要继续欢欣喜乐”
如果我们被生活的忧虑压倒
就会失去内心的安宁和喜乐
为了继续欢欣喜乐
你能不能多想想让你快乐
而不是悲伤的事呢？
如果你感觉不舒服或长期有病痛
就要多想想上帝承诺将来没有人会说
“我病了”
如果你正因为信仰而遭受反对
就要多想想
我们的弟兄团体都在支持你、为你祷告
也要想想组织为了帮助你保持坚定
而做的一切
要是你因世界的情况而沮丧
就要想想未来的希望
这能帮助你保持喜乐
这一切很快就会结束
美好的日子就在前头
重点是
不要让消极负面的思想
限制或阻碍你的进步
相反，要作出必要的调整
这样你就能继续前进，继续欢欣喜乐
请留意保罗在11节提到的另一个方面
他说
“要继续……思想一致”
在公元1世纪的基督徒会众里
有一些人鼓吹叛道的思想
另一些人提出的主张
虽然没有直接违背圣经真理
却造成了分裂
结果，有些弟兄姐妹常常为字眼争辩
严重破坏了会众的团结
什么能帮助我们继续思想一致呢？
保罗在提摩太后书2:23说
“要弃绝愚蠢无知的辩论
因为知道这种行为会引起争吵”
对于那些明显违反上帝道德标准的事
我们当然会表明立场
不过，如果事情没有违反圣经原则
我们就最好不要到处发表个人见解了
我们要尽力避免挑起纷争
也要避免卷入任何争议
这样就不会破坏会众的和睦
让我们回到哥林多后书13:11谈到的
第三个方面，就是要继续“和睦共处”
还记得，刚才访问的两位姐妹
她们在不容易的情况下
做了什么去保持内心的安宁呢？
她们祷告，向耶和华倾诉
她们沉思圣经中相关的经文
然后想想可以怎样运用这些原则
来解决自己遇到的问题
这不但带给她们内心的安宁
也帮助她们跟别人和睦相处
要让你的基督徒特质清楚可见
要继续努力跟人和睦相处
要仁慈慷慨地对待所有人
尤其是我们亲爱的家人
不管他们是不是耶和华见证人
最后，我们想对所有即将受浸的朋友说
在你跟耶和华建立友谊的这个旅程上
今天是个重要的里程碑
所以要花时间认真想想
今天对你有什么意义
我们为你们骄傲
你们决定把自己的一生献给耶和华
绝对不会后悔
不过要记得，今天只是个开始
旅程还没有结束
我们鼓励你们
要竭尽全力留在这条通往生命的路上
请记住我们学到的要点
第一
要继续行走上帝的平安之路，不要放弃
这是生死攸关的
要让耶和华引导你的脚步
第二，走在这条路上时，不要越出界限
要记得，你走这条路是有目的的
而你要到达的终点或目的地就是
跟上帝享有和睦的关系，直到永远
最后，要继续在思想、态度和行为上
作出必要的调整
这样，你就能跟上帝和别人都有和睦的关系
如果你们继续这样做，就不仅会享有安宁
也会像哥林多后书13:11说的
“充满爱心、赐人安宁的上帝
就会与你们同在”
愿你每天都记得
耶和华对你许下的这个承诺
永远行走他的平安之路！
谢谢你，特纳弟兄
跟去年一样
每个地点的浸礼安排都会有所不同
在这部分的节目结束之后
每群会众的长老都会根据本地的情况
为打算受浸的人做浸礼的具体安排
我们感谢耶和华在这部分大会节目中
赐下适时的滋养信心的食物
星期六下午的节目会帮助我们看出
怎样避开破坏和睦的事
以及我们可以怎样促进和睦
另外，我们也非常期待观看圣经影剧的上集

ko.text: 호별 봉사를 제외한 모든 형태의 공개 봉사를 재개할 것이라는 소식을 알렸습니다.
공개 증거를 재개하게 되어 매우 기뻐했습니다.
“자전거 타는 법을 쉽게 잊지 않는 것처럼
몇몇 사람들과 함께 재방문 봉사를 했습니다.
팬데믹 이후로 직접 만나지 못한 사람들을 재방문한 것이었습니다.
형제는 재방문에서 좋은 대화를 나눈 뒤에
집으로 찾아가서 사람들과 직접 대화를 나누니까
한 자매가 그 여자를 방문하도록 마련했습니다.
형제들이 가두 증거를 하고 있는 것을 보고
그리고 자기 승객들에게 전도를 해 달라고 요청했습니다.
버스에 타고 있던 모든 승객들이 잘 듣고
여호와의 증인이 수행하는 번역 작업에 있어
어떤 언어들에서는 그리스어 성경 전체가 발표되었고,
한 주말에 가장 많이 발표된 성경 번역판의 숫자가 6개였습니다.
이런 소중한 선물을 주신 여호와께 감사합니다!
유럽 인권 재판소는 21개 사건에서 여호와의 증인에게 호의적인 판결을 내렸습니다.
하루에 가장 많은 법적 승리를 거둔 종전 기록은
그때 우리는 미국 대법원에서 심리한 12개 사건에서 승소했습니다.
이런 큰 승리를 가져다주신 여호와께 영광을 돌립니다.
이번에 판결이 난 21개 사건 중 20개의 사건은
여호와의 증인을 박해하는 러시아 당국에 대한 역사적이고도 중요한 판결이었습니다.
세계 본부의 법률부에서 일하는 형제들이 그에 대해 알려 줄 것입니다.
러시아가 우리 형제들을 박해하고 우리의 숭배를 금지하는 데 사용한 거짓말을
사전에 계획된 무자비한 공격을 계속 감행한 것이
“여호와의 증인이 믿음을 포기하고 다른 사람들이 증인 단체에 가담하지 못하도록 고안된 ··· 편협한 정책을 [추진해 왔다]”고 밝혔습니다.
물론 그 정책은 전혀 성공을 거두지 못했죠.
우리가 우리의 신앙을 진리로 여긴다는 이유로
“어떤 종교 단체든 신자 개인이든 자기들의 교리가 참되며 우월하다는 주장을 하고 그것을 변호할 권리가 있다”고 판결했습니다.
재판소는 우리가 가진 다음의 권리를 확증해 주었습니다.
부모가 자녀가 여호와를 섬기도록 가르칠 권리,
수혈을 거부하고 효과적인 대체 치료법을 선택할 권리,
전적으로 평화롭고 종교의 자유권에 의해 보호를 받는다고 결론 내렸습니다.
또한 재판소는 러시아 당국에 이렇게 명령했습니다.
유럽 인권 재판소에 이 사건들을 제소하기 위해
지칠 줄 모르고 열심히 일한 많은 형제 자매들에게
러시아 당국이 이 판결을 따를 것인지는
이 판결은 유럽 인권 재판소의 관할 아래 있는
이 일로 이 지역에 살고 있는
유럽 인권 재판소는 깊이 존중받는 재판소이기 때문에
이번 결정은 전 세계의 상급 법원들에 큰 영향을 줄 것입니다.
우리는 유럽 인권 재판소를 통해 이런 역사적이고 압도적인 승리를 가져다주신 여호와께 감사합니다!
우리는 세속 권위들이 어떤 일을 하든
“‘너를 치려고 만들어진 어떤 무기도 소용이 없고,
재판에서 너를 거슬러 일어나는 모든 혀도
지금은 물론 영원히 계속될 그분의 지원을 확신하게 해 줍니다.
평화와 영적인 번영을 빼앗지 못할 것입니다.
과거 구소련에서 박해를 받던 우리 형제들을
그 점을 분명히 알 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 그 시기에 자신의 백성을 보호해 주신
몇 가지 실제 경험담을 살펴볼 것입니다.
우리 모두가 이런저런 다양한 반대에 직면하고 있으니까요.
‘내가 그런 일들을 겪었다면 난 어떻게 했을까?
이 형제 자매들이 여호와께 계속 충실을 유지하는 데 무엇이 도움이 되었는가?’
남편과 결혼하면서 리투아니아에 와서 살게 되었죠.
얼마 후 배 속에 있던 아기가 유산됐습니다.
말도 잘 통하지 않는 외국 땅에서
그곳 교도관들은 죄수들을 잔인하게 구타하곤 했고
가족과 영적 형제 자매들과 떨어져 지내는 것이었습니다.
그중에서도 아내와 떨어져 지내는 게 가장 힘들었죠.
저에게 정말 큰 힘이 되어 주었습니다.
거의 매일 제게 편지를 써 주었죠.
다른 재소자 30명이 받은 편지를 다 합한 것보다
편지에 성경 구절과 출판물의 내용을 포함시켰어요.
눈에 띄지 않게 잘 적어 보낼 필요가 있었죠.
저는 그리스도인 집회를 통해 큰 힘을 얻었고
어느 날은 저희 집에서 집회를 보고 있었는데
그 후 법원에 출두하라는 명령을 받았죠.
법원 심리가 있던 날 정말 걱정이 됐어요.
하지만 여호와께서 마음을 평온하게 해 주셨고
하지만 그 일로 전 위축되지 않았고
그 후로도 집회에 절대 빠지지 않았습니다.
그곳에 있는 사람들에게 증거할 기회를 잘 활용했습니다.
제 이야기를 들으려고 모일 때도 있었죠.
제가 믿는 신앙에 대한 근거를 설명할 수 있었습니다.
저는 항상 여호와께서 제가 시련 가운데서도 충실을 지키기를 원하시는 이유에 초점을 맞췄고,
이건 여호와께서 도와주신 거라고 말할 수밖에 없는 상황들이 참 많았습니다.
우리 자신이 어떻게 시련을 인내할 것인지가 아니라,
여호와께서 어떻게 우리를 도와주실 것인지에 대해 생각하세요.
그분은 모든 것을 인내할 힘을 주실 겁니다.
그런 일들은 우리의 믿음을 단련하고 강하게 해 줍니다.
우리는 여호와께 끝까지 충실하겠다고 결심해야 합니다.
두 분의 충실한 인내에 큰 격려를 받았습니다.
박해를 받기 전과 박해를 받을 때,
전파 활동에 참여하는 것이 얼마나 중요한지
두 분을 통해 배울 수 있었네요.
우리가 흔들림 없이 믿음을 강하게 유지하도록 도와줍니다.
다시 만날 수나 있을까 하고 생각했죠.
제가 계속 여호와께 충실을 유지하도록 힘을 주었습니다.
배지도 달지 않고 타이도 매지 않고,
성구들을 외울 수 있도록 가르쳐 주셨습니다.
또 일주일에 세 번 열리는 집회에
저는 해설에 참여하는 걸 정말 좋아해서
형제들이나 부모님을 배신하라는 압력을 받을 때
저희는 성경 출판물을 조금 챙겨올 수 있었고
그 영적 양식들이 얼마나 소중했는지 모릅니다.
하지만 여호와의 주권 쟁점에 관해 묵상한 덕분에
또 전 인내하고 충실을 유지할 힘을 달라고
어떤 상황에서도 결코 타협하지 않는 데
2년 후에 남편은 몰도바 대법원에서 재판을 받고
한 살 된 아들과 단둘이 남겨졌습니다.
제 마음에 의심의 씨앗을 심으려 했어요.
다음 몇 해 동안 저는 사진으로만,
또 아내가 일 년에 두 번 면회 올 때에만
커 가는 아들의 모습을 볼 수 있었습니다.
특히 저는 아내가 새로운 신발을 넣어 줄 때가
남편에게 전해 줄 잡지 내용을 옮겨 적었습니다.
신발 한 켤레에 잡지 7부를 넣을 수 있었습니다.
그분의 목적과 왕국에 관해 이야기할 기회를
현재 가진 것에 초점을 맞추도록 도와주시는데
그게 저한테 큰 기쁨과 위로가 됩니다.
박해를 이겨내는 데 무엇이 도움이 되었죠?
부모에게 좋은 훈련을 받은 것에 더해
여호와의 주권 쟁점에 항상 초점을 맞추었고
“여호와가 나를 돕는 분이시니 내가 두려워하지 않겠다.
사람이 내게 무엇을 할 수 있겠는가?”
그 형제들은 그 시기에 정말 모진 박해를 당했지만
충실히 인내했고 오히려 그 수가 증가했습니다.
하지만 현재는 그 나라들의 전도인 수가
소련에 속한 국가들에 있던 형제들과 긴밀히 일했습니다.
여호와께서 그들을 도우시는 많은 방법을 목격했죠.
여호와께서는 그들에게 필요한 영적 양식을 항상 마련해 주셨습니다.
그 형제들은 집회 참석의 중요성을 한시도 잊지 않았기 때문에
또 신권적인 노래들을 부르는 것을 좋아했고
여호와의 조직은 결코 해산시킬 수 없습니다.
북방 왕은 결국 어떻게 될 것입니까?
“그가 끝에 이르고 말 것이니, 그를 도와줄 자가 아무도 없을 것이오.”
네, 북방 왕을 도울 자는 아무도 없을 것입니다.
무슨 일이 있어도 여호와를 온전히 신뢰하고

en.text: Brothers and sisters,
welcome to our update!
Since our last report,
there have been some exciting developments.
the Governing Body informed all Branch Committees
that we would now resume all forms
of our public ministry except house-to-house work.
Around the world, our brothers and sisters were thrilled
to resume public witnessing.
After resuming in-person preaching,
one sister said: “It was like we were resurrected.
“We were gone, and then we were back.
It was unifying.”
And a brother said: “It was like riding a bicycle.
It all came back quickly, and we had a great time.”
A member of the Branch Committee in the United States
was working with a small group making return visits
that they hadn’t made in person since before the pandemic.
He said: “I was worried that people would be standoffish
“or that they’d be worried about the virus.
But that just wasn’t the case at all!”
After having a good discussion with his return visit,
the brother said, “It was so refreshing
to actually witness to someone in person at the door.”
Recently, I had a similar experience when sharing in street work.
A young woman noticed that the brother with me had Watchtower magazines,
and she stopped us.
She said that she was so happy to see Jehovah’s Witnesses.
That led to a good discussion,
and arrangements were made for a sister to contact her.
It was such a pleasure to be in street work again!
In Zambia, a public bus driver stopped the bus
when he saw our brothers street witnessing,
and he received a magazine from the brothers.
He asked them to preach to his passengers.
All of the passengers on the bus gladly listened and took magazines.
The weekend of June 25, 2022,
was a milestone for our translation efforts.
Thirteen language editions
of the New World Translation
were released in one weekend!
Some of the releases were of individual Bible books,
others were the complete edition of the Greek Scriptures,
and some were of the complete Bible.
Previously, the largest number of Bibles
released in a single weekend was six.
We thank Jehovah for these precious gifts!
On June 7, 2022,
the European Court of Human Rights
ruled in favor of Jehovah’s Witnesses in 21 cases
—all in one day!
Our previous record for court victories awarded in one day
was on May 3, 1943,
when we won 12 cases in the United States Supreme Court.
We praise Jehovah for these fine victories.
Twenty of the twenty-one cases this month
form a historic judgment
against Russia for persecuting Jehovah’s Witnesses.
What did the court decide?
In the following video,
brothers working with the World Headquarters Legal Department
answer these questions.
Brothers, this decision is truly historic!
In fact, the court consolidated 20 of our cases into one decision
and ruled conclusively in our favor in all of them.
Throughout the 196-page decision,
the court meticulously dismantles the lies
that Russia has used to persecute our brothers and ban our worship.
Shane, in what way specifically did the court condemn Russia?
Well, the decision
unambiguously declares that Russia
is guilty of carrying out a premeditated
and relentless attack on innocent worshippers and on pure worship.
For example, in paragraph 254 of the decision,
the European Court states that the Russian authorities had pursued
“a policy of intolerance . . .
“designed to cause Jehovah’s Witnesses to abandon their faith
and to prevent others from joining it.”
Of course, that policy was entirely unsuccessful.
In fact, this judgment
completely exonerates Jehovah’s Witnesses.
For example, Russia claimed
that our publications and website
are extremist simply because we believe that we have the truth.
In response, the European Court ruled
that “any religious entity or individual believers
“have the right to proclaim and defend their doctrine
as the true and superior one.”
Shane, what else did the court say in our favor?
The European Court confirms our right to engage
in our door-to-door preaching,
for parents to teach their children to worship Jehovah,
to own and use our places of worship,
to refuse military service,
to refuse blood transfusions and choose effective alternatives,
and to be politically neutral.
In all of these areas,
the European Court concludes that our religious beliefs and activities
are entirely peaceful and are protected
by the right to freedom of religion.
Among other things,
the decision orders Russia to stop persecuting Jehovah’s Witnesses,
restore our legal status, release those who are in prison,
allow us to use our literature and website,
and either return the properties that were confiscated
or pay us the equivalent of over 65 million dollars (U.S.).
Outstanding!
We are just so grateful
to the many brothers and sisters who worked tirelessly
to bring these cases before the European Court of Human Rights.
Time will tell whether Russia will comply with this decision.
But even if it does not,
this decision is legally binding on the 46 countries
who have submitted to the jurisdiction of the European Court.
Thus, the rights of over one and a half million Jehovah’s Witnesses
who live in these lands are better protected than ever.
But even more,
because the European Court is held in such high regard,
this decision will have great weight before high courts worldwide.
We thank Jehovah
for this historic victory —this resounding victory—
from the European Court!
We’re confident that, regardless of what the secular authorities do,
Jehovah is going to continue to be with our brothers.
Why do we know that?
Because of what is stated at Isaiah 54:17.
There we read:
“‘No weapon formed against you will have any success,
“‘and you will condemn any tongue
“‘that rises up against you in the judgment.
“‘This is the heritage of the servants of Jehovah,
and their righteousness is from me,’ declares Jehovah.”
Yes, our “heritage” from Jehovah assures us
of his constant support now and forever.
With that assurance,
no opposition will weaken our faith
or deprive us of the peace and spiritual prosperity
we enjoy as God’s servants.
This is clearly seen when we consider how Jehovah helped our brothers
during the persecution in the former Soviet Union.
In the rest of this update,
we’re going to consider some examples
of how Jehovah looked after his people during that time.
We know this will be so encouraging not only for our brothers in Russia
but also for all of us,
since we are all facing opposition in one way or another.
As we watch the following interviews,
ask yourself: ‘If this happened to me,
‘what would I do?
‘What helped these brothers and sisters
to remain loyal to Jehovah?’
I was baptized at the age of 15.
A few weeks later,
the school administration discovered
that I am one of Jehovah’s Witnesses and decided to try to readjust me
and our family so that we would renounce our faith.
They did not stop pressuring us for three years.
At the age of 18, I received a conscription to the Soviet army,
but I refused and was sentenced to two years of imprisonment.
After serving the sentence,
I married a lovely and faithful sister, Lidija.
Soon after, I received a second call to join the army.
This time, the court rendered
a sentence of three years in a unit of strict regime.
I was born in Ukraine.
When I got married, I moved to live with my husband in Lithuania.
Seven months later, my husband received a prison sentence.
Emotionally, this was so difficult that I ended up in a hospital.
Soon we lost our unborn baby,
and here I was alone in a foreign land,
unable to speak the local language.
In view of the imprisonment of my husband, I was not able to find a job.
Prison guards were cruel and would often beat the prisoners.
I suffered such mistreatment as well.
More than that, I was isolated from my family
and from my spiritual brothers and sisters.
The hardest part was the separation from my dear wife, Lidija.
Even so,
Lidija was a special source of support for me.
Almost every day,
she wrote me letters.
I received more letters
than all the other 30 inmates combined.
To support my husband spiritually,
in my letters I would include verses from the Scriptures
and quotations from the publications,
trying to put them in a way that the censorship
would not be able to spot them.
Christian meetings were a source of strength for me.
I never missed them.
On one occasion, when we held a meeting in our home,
a group of militia and KGB broke in.
As a result, I received a call to appear before the court.
On the day of the court hearing, I was very worried,
but Jehovah gave me such calmness
that fear and nervousness disappeared.
I was sentenced to pay a fine of 50 rubles.
At the time, it was a large sum of money,
but I was not intimidated
and never stopped attending meetings.
I used opportunities to give a witness to others in the prison.
There were instances
when an audience of dozens of prisoners would listen to me.
When they asked questions that were more difficult to answer,
I would analyze them and ponder over them
so as to be able to explain the grounds for my beliefs.
Prayer was a constant companion.
I saw how Jehovah responded to them.
Sometimes he would answer in a way I did not expect.
I always stayed focused on the reason why Jehovah wants me
to remain faithful to him through all these difficulties,
and this helped a lot.
There were many occasions when the help I received
could not have come from any other source but Jehovah.
Therefore, he became my best Friend.
He would always come to the rescue.
The weaker I was,
the more help that came from Jehovah.
Let us not think about how we are going to endure tests;
think about how Jehovah will help us.
He will give us strength to endure everything.
Enduring the things Jehovah allows us to experience is not in vain,
but it is beneficial for us.
It fortifies and tempers our faith, so to speak.
What we need is the right, positive attitude toward
the difficulties we face.
And we have to be determined
to stay faithful to Jehovah to the end.
We appreciate your faithful endurance, Brother and Sister Pudžiuvys.
You reminded us how vital it is
to regularly attend meetings and share in the ministry
—both before and during times of persecution.
This helps to stabilize us and keep our faith strong.
In our next interview, notice how parental training,
regularly taking in spiritual food,
and remaining determined never to compromise
helped Iósif and Véra Rúsu to endure persecution.
I dealt with persecution
when I was six years old.
My father and older brother
were sentenced to 25 years in prison
as conscientious objectors.
I wondered if I would ever see them again.
However, thankfully, they were released two years later.
Their example has strengthened me
to remain faithful to Jehovah.
I also faced persecution when I was a child.
At school, I was often beaten because I preached,
I didn’t wear the Soviet star and tie, and I didn’t sing patriotic songs.
From an early age,
my parents taught me to love Jehovah,
to read from the Bible,
to sing praises to him,
and to learn verses by heart.
They took us with them to the meetings that were held three times a week.
I loved to participate.
I always had my hand up.
My parents taught me how to respond to those who would put pressure on us
to betray my brothers or my parents.
The love and trust in Jehovah that my parents planted in my heart
helped me to cherish him and to want to remain loyal to him.
When I was 15,
our family was deported to Siberia by train.
In these difficult conditions,
I found comfort and joy in the spiritual food
that we managed to take from home.
Those were the most important things.
All the way there on the train, we sang songs.
Ten years later,
when I was in Kazakhstan,
I was arrested and sentenced to five years.
Oftentimes, the prison guards pressured me
to compromise and renounce my faith.
But meditating on the issue of Jehovah’s sovereignty
helped me to stay firm.
I prayed to Jehovah for the strength to endure
and to remain faithful.
Reading the Bible helped me to endure trials
and not to make any compromises, no matter what.
After I finished my prison sentence,
I returned to Moldova.
Then, in 1967,
Véra and I got married.
Two years later, Iósif
was tried by the Supreme Court of Moldova
and sentenced
to ten years in a maximum-security camp.
Suddenly, I was left alone at 18 with a one-year-old boy.
I was often called by the KGB and interrogated for hours,
sometimes for five hours.
They told me many lies and attempted to sow doubts in my mind.
The next few years,
I saw my son grow up only in photographs
and when Véra would visit me twice a year.
One of the things I especially looked forward to receiving from her
was a new pair of boots.
The other brothers and sisters and I wrote the magazines
on very thin sheets of paper that had the shape of a sole.
We removed the soles of the boots, filled them with magazines,
and then nailed the soles back on.
It was possible to fit seven magazines in one pair of boots.
During persecution,
your relationship with Jehovah becomes closer, more real.
Jehovah is kind.
He is giving me “the power beyond what is normal.”
In my life, the greater the trials,
the more opportunities Jehovah gave me to talk about his purpose and his Kingdom.
The way Jehovah helps me focus on what I have
and not on the hardships that I have endured
brings me so much joy and comfort.
I have no reason not to be happy.
Thank you, Brother and Sister Rúsu, for sharing your experience with us.
Did you notice what helped them prepare for and face persecution?
In addition to good parental training,
they regularly took in spiritual food
and learned Bible verses by heart
and they kept clearly in mind the issue of Jehovah’s sovereignty,
remaining determined never to compromise.
We can do the same today.
Both of these couples remind us of the words
recorded at Hebrews 13:6:
“Jehovah is my helper; I will not be afraid.
What can man do to me?”
Jehovah truly was the Helper
of our brothers and sisters in the former Soviet Union.
Despite all the waves of persecution that our brothers faced,
they remained faithful and their numbers grew.
For example, in 1949, there were about 10,000 Witnesses
in the countries that formed the Soviet Union,
and most of those were in Western Ukraine.
Now the number of publishers in those countries
is over 380,000!
Truly, Jehovah helped them.
In the late 1970’s and 1980’s,
I worked very closely with the brothers behind the Iron Curtain.
I saw not only their faith
but also the many ways that Jehovah helped them.
Jehovah always made sure they had the spiritual food they needed.
The brothers really appreciated the importance of attending meetings,
even though these were held in small groups.
And they loved to sing theocratic songs,
learning many of these by heart.
They had to risk their freedom and even their safety
in order to attend in-person meetings,
but they always made the effort.
Even though the Devil tried to break their integrity,
I saw again and again how Jehovah prospered our brothers
and helped them to remain faithful.
The Russian government can liquidate a legal entity,
but they can never liquidate Jehovah’s organization.
What will happen to the king of the north?
Daniel 11:45 tells us:
“He will come all the way to his end,
and there will be no helper for him.”
“There will be no helper” for the king of the north.
But who will be our “helper”?
What did Hebrews 13:6 say?
“Jehovah is my helper.”
Brothers and sisters, be determined, come what may,
to put your full confidence in Jehovah and be faithful.
Jehovah will be your Helper!
We dearly love each one of you.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

我们的弟兄姐妹

在恢复面对面的传道工作后
一位姐妹说
“这种感觉就像经历了复活一样
我们好像一起走了
然后又一起回来了”
一个弟兄说
“这就好像骑自行车一样
虽然好久没有骑了
但是马上就找回感觉了
我们真的很开心”
美国分部委员会的一个成员
跟几个弟兄姐妹一起续访了一些
疫情之前认识
但没有机会再次见面的人
他说
“刚开始我担心这些人会有不好的反应
或者害怕被传染
但情况完全不是这样”
在跟这些人进行了很好的讨论后
这个弟兄说
“我真的太开心了
因为我们现在可以在住户的门口
向他们传道”
最近
我在街头作见证时
也有类似的经历
一个年轻女子留意到
跟我在一起的弟兄有《守望台》杂志
就主动跟我们说话
她说她很高兴见到耶和华见证人
后来我们开始了一个很好的讨论
也安排了一个姐妹以后继续续访她
能再次回到街头作见证
真是太棒了！
在赞比亚（尚比亚）
一个公共汽车司机看到弟兄们
在街头作见证
就把车停下来
他向弟兄们要了一本杂志
还请弟兄们向公共汽车上的乘客传道
车上的所有乘客都很高兴听到圣经的信息
也接受了杂志
2022年6月25日的周末
是我们翻译工作的一个里程碑
因为在这个周末
有十三种语言版本的《新世界译本》发行了
这些译本中
有的是圣经的部分经卷
有的是希腊语部分的所有经卷
还有的是整本圣经
之前我们在一个周末发行的圣经译本数量
最高的纪录是六种
所以
真的感谢耶和华赐给我们这些宝贵的礼物！
欧洲人权法院在21起案件中
全都作出了对耶和华见证人有利的裁决
这都是在一天之内发生的
在此之前
我们在一天之内赢得胜诉最高的纪录
是在1943年5月3日
当时我们在美国最高法院赢得了12场胜诉
我们衷心赞美耶和华
帮助我们取得这些胜利
在这个月的21起案件中
有20起是跟俄罗斯当局
迫害耶和华见证人有关的
这些判决是历史性的
法院作出了什么裁决呢？
在下面的短片中
几位在世界总部法律部工作的弟兄
会为我们解答这些问题
弟兄们
这是个历史性的裁决
欧洲人权法院对我们提交的20个案件
做了一致的判决
最后的裁决都是对我们有利的
欧洲人权法院在这份196页的裁决书里
详细地指出
俄罗斯迫害我们的弟兄、禁止我们的活动的
所有指控都是谎言
沙恩弟兄，具体来说
俄罗斯受到哪些谴责呢？
好的
裁决书清楚地指出
俄罗斯对正确崇拜
和参与正确崇拜的人
进行的有计划的
残酷的迫害
都是违法的
比如
在裁决书的第254项
欧洲人权法院指出
俄罗斯当局对耶和华见证人的信仰
当然，我们知道他们的计划完全失败了
实际上
人权法院宣判我们完全无罪
比如
俄罗斯指责我们的出版物和网站
包含极端主义思想
就因为我们相信自己的信仰是真理
关于这一点
欧洲人权法院指出
沙恩弟兄，还有别的对我们有利的判决吗？
欧洲人权法院确认我们享有这些权利:
挨家挨户传道
父母教导儿女崇拜耶和华
拥有和使用崇拜场所
拒绝服兵役
拒绝输血，也有权选择其他疗法
保持政治中立
在以上这些方面
欧洲人权法院都承认
我们的信仰和活动都完全是倡导和平的
我们应该享有信仰自由的权利
在判决书里

When I learned that I was invited to work

But that excitement quickly turned into anxiety
because of what I had to do.
I prayed to Jehovah for weeks to give me the strength
to have the conversation with my employer.
All right, Sarah, come in!
So?
I wanted to, first of all, say thank you
for taking the time to meet with me, . . .
I began to explain about the construction project
and how I had been invited to volunteer.
. . . and I would really like the time to . . .
So you want time off
during the busiest time of our year?
Well, yes, but . . .
It’s your choice, but under no circumstances will I hold your position.
Suddenly, this beautiful privilege felt like a huge risk.
Was I making my life more complicated by doing this?
I read the account about the people in Nehemiah’s day.
Their willing spirit demonstrated faith,
and Jerusalem’s walls were built by people
who “put their heart into the work.”
I didn’t want to miss out
on the opportunity to serve Jehovah in that way.
This is my resignation letter.
I had to have faith that Jehovah would bless my decision.
I’m not sure what the future holds when I get back,
but I know Jehovah will take care of me.
For now, I’m going to focus
on putting my heart into the work.

어떻게 사탄이 인간 이전의 예수를 알면서도 자신을 숭배하라는 이러한 대담한 제안을 할 수 있었느냐 하는 겁니다.
그가 얼마나 정신이 나갔는지 알 수 있죠.
예수께서는 사람들이 그분을 왕으로 세우려고 했을 때에도 비슷하게 반응하셨습니다.
사람들은 예수께서 평화를 가져다주실 것이라고 생각했지만,
그분은 여호와께서만 그렇게 하실 수 있다고 분명히 밝히셨습니다.
하느님의 왕국이 가져올 평화는 인간이 가져올 수 있는 그 어떤 평화보다도 훨씬 더 우월한 것입니다.
그리고 인간 통치를 없애고 죄도 없애실 것입니다.
지상의 평화를 방해하는 모든 요인이 없어질 것입니다.
제가 항상 감사하는 것은 그분이 모든 문제를 없애실 것이라는 점인데요.
그 가운데는 고통의 모든 원인들이 없어지는 것도 포함됩니다.
그분은 신체적인 고통뿐만 아니라 감정적인 고통도 없애실 것입니다.
우리의 아버지 여호와와 아들 예수께서 주시는 평화가 이 땅에 가득할 그 날이 정말 기다려지지 않습니까?
이제 다음 영상을 보시면서 한 자매가 이 세상이 약속하는 평화가 가짜라는 것을 어떻게 깨닫게 되는지 유의해 보십시오.
이게 예수님의 복음과 어떻게 부합한단 말입니까?
하지만 목사는 한마디 답도 하지 못했어요.
그래서 전 정치에서 답을 찾으려고 했죠.
당시에 평화 운동 단체들이 많이 생겼고
내가 바라는 건 사람들을 추앙하는 게 아니라
하루는 커피 한 잔 하려고 친구 집에 갔는데
성경에 대해 알려 주러 왔다고 했어요.
그 후 정말 친절한 여자 분이
이 조직이야말로 평화를 진정으로 갈망하는 조직이야’ 하고 생각했어요.
그랬더니 다들 저를 미친 사람 보듯 쳐다보았죠.
전 새로운 인생을 살게 되어 정말 기뻤어요.
이사야 14:7의 말씀은 제 인생에 큰 영향을 주었습니다.
하느님께서 평온하고 평화로운 세상을 가져오겠다고 약속하시기 때문입니다.
자매는 정치와 시위를 통해 세계 평화를 이루려고 했습니다.
하지만 그 모든 게 가짜 평화라는 것을 깨달았습니다.
진정한 평화를 가져다주실 수 있는 분은 여호와뿐이십니다.
지금까지 이 연설에서 세 가지 형태의 가짜 평화에 대해 살펴보셨는데요.
마지막으로 강조하고 싶은 점은 예수께서 주신 평화를 지키기 위해 노력하시라는 겁니다.
잘 아시는 내용이지만 6절에 나오는 한 가지 표현에 초점을 맞춰 보겠습니다.
나를 통하지 않고는 아무도 아버지께 올 수 없습니다.’”
특히 강조하고 싶은 것은 예수께서 “진리”이시라는 것입니다.
우리는 그분의 모든 약속을 신뢰할 수 있습니다.
그분은 지금까지 평화를 주셨고 미래에는 더 큰 평화를 주실 것입니다.
그들이 어떤 어려움을 인내해야 했는지 생각해 보십시오.
사도 바울이나 베드로 그리고 그 밖의 사람들은 참으로 엄청난 박해를 인내했습니다.
예수께서 주신 평화가 없었다면 결코 그럴 수 없었을 겁니다.
예수께서는 오늘날에도 여러분에게 평화를 주실 것입니다.
그러면 여러분은 계속 여호와의 뜻을 행하고 그분을 기쁘시게 해 드릴 수 있을 것입니다.
따라서 형제 자매 여러분, 예수께서 우리에게 주신 평화를 잘 지키시기 바랍니다.
사탄은 이 세상을 사용해서 여러분에게 가짜 평화를 약속합니다.
여호와께서는 그분의 아들을 통해 우리가 영원히 평화를 누리게 해 주실 것입니다!

en.text: Jesus taught us that Satan
is “the father of the lie.”
We recall that he deceived Eve, a perfect woman.
He lied about our precious Jehovah.
Now, you’re familiar (many of you) with Revelation chapter 12.
I invite you to find that
—Revelation chapter 12.
And in this chapter, verses 7 and 8,
it addressed the fact that “war broke out in heaven.”
But notice
that after he’s kicked out of heaven,
in verse 9 we read:
“So down the great dragon was hurled,
“the original serpent, the one called Devil and Satan,
“who is misleading the entire inhabited earth;
“he was hurled down to the earth, and his angels
were hurled down with him.”
Now, I read it that way specifically,
but what it doesn’t say is
(in the middle part of verse 9):
“Satan, who is [trying to mislead]
the entire inhabited earth.”
No, he “is  misleading
the entire inhabited earth.”
That’s crucial to understand when we think about the theme of this talk,
not to be misled by imitation peace,
because as “the ruler of the world,”
that’s what he’s out to do—mislead.
In fact, it’s an interesting point here in 2 Corinthians chapter 11
to appreciate
how he goes about misleading, or at least it’s addressed here
to serve as a good warning for us.
And an interesting point with the revision
of the New World Translation
(for those of you in the truth before 2013
when it was revised, you’ll remember this)
in verse 14 of 2 Corinthians chapter 11:
“And no wonder, for Satan himself keeps disguising himself
as an angel of light.”
Now, the New World Translation
used to say before the revision
“[transforms] himself into an angel of light.”
Well, the very English word “metamorphosis,”
like for a caterpillar transforming into a beautiful butterfly,
that’s where it comes from, the Greek language.
And that word was not in verse 14.
No, because Satan can’t transform himself
into “an angel of light” (so it’s an improved translation),
but he does disguise.
He’s a masquerader.
And he does that with the subject of peace.
His world offers a sort of peace,
but it’s imitation peace.
Now, Jesus is distinguished, though, with the peace that he gives.
And if you’ll follow along here
in John chapter 14,
he himself explains it to us.
And we treasure the Gospel accounts,
verse 27: “I leave you peace;
“I give you my peace.
“I do not give it to you the way the world gives it.
Do not let your hearts be troubled nor let them shrink out of fear.”
So Jesus gives us his peace, see.
And the peace that Jesus gives us,
it’s this inner calm once you know the truth and Jesus gives us the peace.
We have this confidence that he loves us and Jehovah loves us,
so that we enjoy a good, peaceful relationship with them
and a good conscience.
And we look forward to the Kingdom removing all war and death.
Now, a point to make here:
Satan wants us to trade
the peace that Jesus gives
for his imitation peace
that he has advertised in the world.
Now, in this talk,
we will consider three forms of imitation peace
and why the peace that Jesus gives is superior.
The first one has to do with material things
—how they’ll not bring true peace.
And to help us with that, turn to Matthew chapter 4,
and we’ll be referring to this chapter
throughout this particular talk about not being misled by imitation peace.
And this one is connected with material things
—how they don’t bring true peace—
in the example Jesus sets forth here.
So in Matthew chapter 4:
“Then Jesus was led by the spirit
“up into the wilderness to be tempted by the Devil.
“After he had fasted for 40 days and 40 nights,
“he felt hungry.
“And the Tempter approached and said to him:
“‘If you are a son of God,
tell these stones to become loaves of bread.’
“But he answered: ‘It is written:
“‘“Man must live, not on bread alone,
but on every word that comes from Jehovah’s mouth.”’”
Isn’t that a beautiful rebuttal?
See, Jesus refused to trade
his peace for material things (in this case, bread),
even though he was hungry.
So serving Jehovah was more important to him
than material things, see.
In the world, they have this thinking,
‘Well, you need
a certain amount of money to retire,’
and they’re constantly focused on material things
—not Jesus, see.
It’s superior peace from Jehovah God.
So it’s only temporary anyway,
the material benefits that people seek
and pursue throughout their lives.
Now we can enjoy true contentment
because Jehovah God is going to care for us.
We know that many have personal experiences to prove that.
Now, in the following video,
see what a brother learned about the so-called peace
that the world promises.
As a family, we were doing very well spiritually.
We did family worship, went preaching,
and went to the meetings together.
After some time, we began
to encounter financial problems.
At times, we did not even have money to buy food
for each day.
Many people in our area were going to South Africa
to provide basic needs for their families.
So I decided to go as well,
leaving behind my wife to take care of our seven children.
This affected me spiritually
because I did not know the language, I was unable to preach,
and I did not benefit from the meetings.
Being so far from my family
caused me to neglect my responsibility as a family head.
As a result, my family grew weak spiritually
and we all missed each other very much.
I realized that I had made a wrong decision going abroad.
My conscience started to trouble me greatly.
Then I remembered the example of Baruch
found at Jeremiah 45:5.
Baruch may have wanted to pursue material riches as I had.
When he was helped, he returned.
I decided then to put Jehovah in first place
instead of searching for material things.
So I started to make changes to go home
and help my family spiritually.
When I left South Africa and reached the border of Malawi
(after leaving my family for about six months),
I felt great happiness in my heart,
and I am still happy till now.
Studying the Bible has helped me.
We still encounter financial problems,
but I remember that in Satan’s world,
there is nowhere we can go and have no problems.
Now I serve as an elder.
My family is progressing spiritually.
And this makes me very happy,
because my relationship with Jehovah is strong.
Yes, he learned a hard lesson.
He goes to South Africa
—meetings interrupted and no field service.
And then he remembers Baruch,
secretary for Jeremiah.
And he returns to be with his family, putting the Kingdom first,
and we appreciate him being truthful and sharing that experience.
That’s imitation peace, going after material things.
Now this next one, it’s quite interesting.
So pay close attention
because there may be some listening who need this counsel.
Satan’s world says that we
can ignore Bible standards
and that we might need to ignore some of them to gain peace of mind.
Here are two examples that we’re going to analyze in this talk.
A person may reason that marrying an unbeliever
or obtaining an unscriptural divorce
will make life easier.
And they start reasoning this way,
‘I just want to get married,
and he’s an unbeliever, but he’s a nice person.’
Things like that go on with the treacherous heart.
Again, we go to the example of our Lord and Master, Jesus.
We’re going to read verses 5-7 of Matthew 4:
“Then the Devil took him along into the holy city,
“and he stationed him on the battlement of the temple
“and said to him:
“‘If you are a son of God, throw yourself down,
“‘for it is written:
“‘“He will give his angels a command concerning you,”
“‘and, “They will carry you on their hands,
“so that you may not strike your foot against a stone.”’
“Jesus said to him: ‘Again, it is written:
“You must not put Jehovah your God to the test.”’”
See, Jesus made that very clear.
He was going to be obedient to his Father
and wasn’t going to worry about being testy
with such an experience as the Devil proposed there.
So obedience
—Jesus twice (in a moment we’ll read another one) said: “It is written.”
He sticks with the Scriptures —Jehovah’s thinking—
and he refused to disobey Jehovah.
Now here’s the question,
Why is the peace that Jesus gives
superior to the pursuit
of unscriptural solutions to our problems?
Let that sink in.
Why is the peace that Jesus gives
superior to the pursuit
of unscriptural solutions to our problems?
For example, marrying an unbeliever
—that will likely bring (and it has happened time after time)
that person greater pain
than the longing they felt when they were single.
I’ve personally seen that
all too many times in various congregations
that I’ve had the privilege to serve in.
You see, the other one is an unscriptural divorce.
It often leads to immoral conduct.
It certainly leads to a troubled conscience,
emotional damage and, of course, a loss of privileges.
Now, this is very important to keep in mind.
It’s true that with two imperfect individuals
married to each other, well, there are going to be difficulties
and there are going to be challenges.
But stop and think about this:
When you’re having difficulties,
don’t forget that marriage
is a sacred arrangement.
The world totally has forgotten that.
So Jehovah will strengthen
both to make a success.
You have to keep that in mind: Jehovah will strengthen and help
so that you can succeed because this is his sacred arrangement.
And the Devil has been attacking the family arrangement
all through the last days of this system,
and he’s intensifying it
as he gets closer to being thrown into the abyss.
Now, in the following video,
notice the results of pursuing imitation peace.
Newly married life came with a lot
of unexpected challenges.
You dream about the way your marriage will go,
but then the reality is quite different.
All we ever did was argue,
or we wouldn’t speak to one another.
We never ever went to the elders.
We just didn’t want to bother them.
We just felt, you know, we needed to figure it out ourselves.
We decided that if the house sold,
then we would separate.
The separation wasn’t a good thing,
because in some respects it made things worse.
It did have an impact on the boys.
They started acting out.
They got into some trouble with the police one time.
And there was a loneliness because you’ve gotten married,
and now you don’t have that, and you’re by yourself.
And the same old routine went on where you’re
cooking and cleaning and doing laundry and working.
I felt sick to my stomach.
I had a hard time getting up every morning and facing the world.
At that point, I felt that I needed
to have the elders help out a little bit.
I did pray for Jehovah’s help to direct me,
and I kept wondering why Jehovah wasn’t really
answering my prayers.
But I kind of realize now that it was because we were separated.
The expectations of the separation were not at all what I was thinking.
I reflected on the marriage vows.
One of the things I thought
about was a sister in our congregation.
She was married to an unbeliever, and then she learned the truth.
And he was so violent.
He would beat her; he would burn her books; he would burn her clothes.
He did not allow her children to attend the meetings.
And I thought about the problems that Darrel and I had.
And I thought: ‘Well, Darrel is a kind person.
He’s never done that.’
And I thought:
‘You know, this is something
‘that we need to really work on.
‘We need to really put forth the effort
‘to start applying Bible principles
‘to put Jehovah first in our life
so that we can bring our marriage back in union with Jehovah.’
I realized that it wasn’t what I wanted,
but it was what Jehovah wanted.
There was just no other choice.
Jehovah wasn’t going to bless us unless we got back together.
When we got back together, our marriage was still a work in progress.
You can’t have a perfect marriage in this world,
but you can sure make it better when you put Jehovah first.
We enjoyed the feelings we had toward each other.
I felt closer to Debbie.
Debbie and I have been married now for 48 years.
Separation does not make anything better at all.
If you even have an inkling of love for one another,
you want to work on that, and you want to make it bloom
so that Jehovah can bless it.
The blessings have been endless.
Our children are all doing
fantastic in the truth.
Jehovah said: “Taste and see that [He] is good.”
So we’ve got to do that.
We really appreciated this couple sharing
their experience with the brotherhood.
He learned, you know.
They were always arguing,
and that’s all they did was argue, argue, argue.
It affected their children.
They decided to separate and finally have peace.
‘I don’t have to be around her,’ or ‘I don’t have to be around him.’
But then he realized his relationship with Jehovah
was being interfered with here,
and he went to the elders.
His prayers were affected.
The things he noticed —he was honest about that.
And our precious sister was so nice to honestly explain.
She said what she learned was that ‘this is not about me;
it’s about Jehovah.’
When you finally come to that realization,
Jehovah will strengthen you
to enjoy peace with your marriage partner.
Now, the next one, I never tire of speaking
about these particular couple of verses
or reading about it or hearing another brother give a talk about it.
See, here’s what’s coming soon.
Turn with me to 1 Thessalonians chapter 5.
And many of you are going, ‘Oh, yeah, I know
what he’s going to read about.’
And this is one of the prophecies
that is yet to be fulfilled.
So it’s just invigorating
to know that soon here’s what’s going to happen
—1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
verses 2 and 3:
“For you yourselves know very well
“that Jehovah’s day is coming exactly as a thief in the night.
“Whenever it is that they are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
“then sudden destruction is to be instantly on them,
“just like birth pains on a pregnant woman,
and they will by no means escape.”
Yes, see, “Jehovah’s day”
—this has to do with the day of the outbreak of the great tribulation
when Babylon the Great is destroyed
and Armageddon finishes it off.
In this context, that’s “Jehovah’s day.”
And what happens before then
is this proclamation, “peace and security!”
Will religious leaders be involved?
Well, they’re part of Satan’s system; that’s very possible.
We’ll have to wait and see.
Will it be one announcement or a series of announcements?
That we don’t know.
But this is coming.
And those who are staying close to Jehovah
and enjoying the peace from him and his Son, Jesus,
will not be deceived
by this imitation proclamation of peace
—imitation peace.
And again, back in Matthew chapter 4,
we’re going to see how Jesus handled
this type of test from the Devil
and what we learn from it here
in verses 8-11 of Matthew chapter 4.
“Again the Devil took him [in verse 8]
“along to an unusually high mountain
“and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
“And he said to him:
“‘All these things I will give you
“if you fall down and do an act of worship to me.’
“Then Jesus said to him [without hesitation]:
“‘Go away, Satan!
“‘For it is written: “It is Jehovah your God you must worship,
and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.”’
“Then the Devil left him, and look! angels came
and began to minister to him.”
Right away, a third time: “It is written.”
Jesus was having nothing to do
with this offer of the kingdoms —this imitation peace.
‘You’ll have all the glory and rule.’
And it’s always boggled my mind
that this one who knew
Jesus in his prehuman existence
would have the audacity to try to get Jesus to bow down and worship him.
It shows you that he’s obviously insane.
Now, he wouldn’t allow it either
when they tried to make him an earthly king.
Jesus wasn’t having any part of that.
They were thinking he could bring them peace.
But Jesus said there’s no peace except by Jehovah’s way.
And the peace from God’s Kingdom is so superior
to anything they could try to come up with —their imitation peace.
Here’s why.
Think about this:
Jesus will remove the Devil.
Jesus will remove human rulership.
Jesus will remove sin.
So the earth’s peace will never again be disturbed.
And I appreciate very much that he’s going to get rid of all problems,
and that includes undoing all causes of pain
—and not just physical pain,
emotional pain as well.
It’s wonderful to look forward to that time
with that beautiful peace
from our precious Father, Jehovah, and his Son, Jesus.
Now, in the following video,
see what convinced this sister
not to believe the world’s promises of peace.
My father always taught me that we needed God in our life
in order for there to be peace.
And he always wanted to know,
Can Christians go to war?
How is this consistent with the Gospel of Jesus Christ?
But the pastor could never give us an answer,
and so I thought I’d have to look to politics to find it.
A lot of peace movements were being formed at that time,
so I joined one of them.
We decided where the protest marches would be
and which pamphlets we would use.
But after the protests were over,
everyone was so excited
and they all started applauding
and cheering for the leaders.
I thought: ‘That’s not what I wanted.
‘I don’t want to honor people.
‘I want to have world peace.
And that still hasn’t happened yet.’
Then I started to feel very alone,
and it made me feel unsafe in this world.
With no peace in sight,
I thought, ‘What is the purpose of life?’
While visiting friends for coffee, I saw a man I’d never met before.
My friends told me he wanted to talk to us about the Bible.
So I asked him:
“Sir, what do you think?
Can Christians join the military?”
And the man said, “No, that’s not allowed
because the Bible says you should ‘love your [enemy].’”
It made me think about what my father always said
—that we need God to bring peace.
Then a really nice lady came to my door,
and she had an orange book in her hand.
And it said: True Peace and Security.
After reading it, I thought:
‘This is it!
This is the organization that truly wants peace.’
So I went to those involved in the peace movement.
I told them that I believe that God will change this world
into a beautiful earth where there’ll be true peace.
They all looked at me like I had lost my mind.
I was so happy with my new life.
I felt like I was part of a family
who truly cared about one another
and really wanted peace with each other.
Isaiah 14:7 had a major impact on my life
because there God promises
a calm and peaceful world.
Wasn’t that nice how she learned?
She’d looked to politics and protests for world peace.
Obviously, she was sincere.
But she learned that’s all imitation peace.
True peace and security comes from Jehovah God.
So wrapping it up with these three different types
of imitation peace that we’ve emphasized,
we want to encourage you in these last minutes
to safeguard the peace that Jesus has given you.
In John chapter 14
(you know this, but I want you to really focus
on a particular point), in verse 6:
“Jesus said to him:
“‘I am the way and the truth and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through me.’”
Isn’t that beautiful?
Particularly we want to emphasize Jesus is “the truth.”
We can trust all of his promises.
He is “the truth.”
He’s going to give us peace —already has—
and will to a greater extent in the future.
Yes, our Master is “the truth.”
And he gave the early Christians that peace.
The things that they were able to deal with are just mind-boggling.
As we read the apostle Paul’s experiences and Peter’s and others’
—the persecution they endured— they did it,
enduring with joy.
It’s amazing!
It can only be a supernatural provision of peace.
And just remember,
Jesus will likewise give you the peace you need now
to keep doing Jehovah’s will and to make Him happy.
So, brothers, please,
safeguard the gift of peace
that Jesus has given you.
Satan uses this world
to offer you promises of imitation peace.
Do not be misled!
No, rather, “Let the peace of the Christ rule in your hearts.”
“And show yourselves thankful.”
Yes, through his Son,
Jehovah will bless us all with peace forever!

cn.text: 耶稣告诉我们撒但是“谎话之父”
他欺骗了完美的夏娃
他也说谎诋毁耶和华上帝

title: 마크 누매어: “평화의 군왕”을 충성스럽게 지지하십시오

ko.text: 당신이 친구들과 사랑하는 선생님과 함께 겟세마네 동산에 있는데,
앞장서 오는 사람의 낯이 익은데, 가룟 유다입니다.
그가 예수께 다가와 뺨에 입을 맞춥니다.
유다가 물러서자 사람들이 몰려와 예수를 체포합니다.
어떻게 이런 일이 있을 수 있지?
베드로가 칼을 뽑아 휘둘러서 대제사장의 종의 귀를 잘라 버립니다.
칼을 잡는 사람은 모두 칼로 망할 것입니다.”
예수께서 그 남자의 귀를 고쳐 주시죠.
분명, 베드로는 하느님의 아들을 위해 싸우는 것이
예수께서는 “칼을 제자리에 도로 꽂으십시오”라는 짧은 말로
우리 모두가 어떻게 베드로가 그랬던 것처럼
이 세상에서 벌어지는 분쟁에 휘말리게 될 수 있는지에
또 그런 심각한 실수를 피하는 법도 살펴볼 것입니다.
왜 아버지께 ‘열두 군단의 천사들’을 보내서 도와 달라고 하지 않으셨는지
다 함께 성경을 펴서 이사야 9:6을 보실까요?
우리는 그중 하나에만 초점을 맞춰 보겠습니다.
그의 어깨 위에 통치권이 있을 것입니다.
그의 이름은 ‘놀라운 조언자’, ‘위력 있는 신’, ‘영원한 아버지’,
여호와의 천사들이 들에서 목자들에게 선포한 내용을 생각해 보시죠.
땅에서는 선의를 받은 사람들 가운데 평화.”
평화의 군왕이 될 분이 태어났을 때,
예수께서 땅에 계실 땐 이루어지지 않았죠?
오늘날에도 우리는 평화를 볼 수 없습니다.
세계 주도권을 잡기 위해 싸우고 있습니다.
이사야 9:6의 말씀은 꿈에 불과한 것이 아니죠.
이사야 9:7의 마지막 부분에서 어떻게 알려 주는지 보겠습니다.
“만군의 여호와의 열심이 이 일을 이룰 것입니다.”
여호와께서는 마지못해서가 아니라 열심히 평화를 이루실 것입니다.
우리는 여호와께서 약속을 반드시 이루실 것임을 확신할 수 있습니다.
전 세계 수많은 사람이 자주 말하고 외우고 있는 문구에 들어 있습니다.
영원한 평화가 이루어지는 것이 바로 이 성구의 성취에 달려 있는 것이죠.
단지 종교적 지식을 전하기 위해서가 아닙니다.
모든 사람이 하느님의 이름을 알고 거룩히 여기고 존중해야 합니다.
그 이름에 돌아간 모든 모독이 제거되어야 하죠.
사실, 온 우주와 모든 피조물의 미래가
여호와의 이름이 거룩해지는 것에 달려 있습니다.
아버지의 뜻이 하늘에서와 같이 땅에서도 이루어지게 하십시오.”
하느님의 왕국은 인류 역사상 가장 강력한 정부가 될 것입니다.
그 어떤 나라나 제국도 하느님의 왕국에 대적할 수 없습니다.
어떤 나라가 하느님의 왕국이 오는 걸 막으려고 하는 것은
마치 개미 한 마리가 기찻길 위에 버티고 서서
다가오는 기차를 향해 손을 내밀고 이렇게 큰소리 치는 것과 같습니다.
오늘날의 모든 폭력적인 정권을 없앨 힘이 있습니다.
그분은 그들이 더 이상 전쟁과 분쟁을 일으키고
영원한 평화와 관련하여 매우 중요한 성구입니다.
하느님의 왕국은 영원한 평화를 가져올 유일한 수단이죠.
예수께서는 평화를 방해하는 모든 것을 없애실 것입니다.
이 성구에 담긴 예언을 깊이 생각해 보면,
행복해지고 미래에 대한 희망을 갖게 될 겁니다.
“조금만 더 있으면 악한 자들이 더는 없으리니,
[조금만 더 있으면] 그들이 있던 곳을 살펴보아도 없을 것이다.”
아이들은 여행할 때 부모에게 묻곤 하죠.
악한 사람을 찾아 보아도 찾을 수가 없을 겁니다.
풍부한 평화 가운데 더없는 기쁨을 얻을 것이다.”
이웃과 하느님과 평화를 누릴 때를 묵상해 보십시오.
평화로운 신세계에 있는 자신의 모습을 그려 볼 수 있습니까?
그때 우리가 듣게 될 뉴스는 오직
나는 누구에게 여호와에 대해 가르치도록 배정될 것인가?” 하는 것들이죠.
문화가 다를 뿐 아니라 시대도 다른 사람들과 연구하면서
그들의 시각을 이해하고 그들이 여호와를 사랑하도록 도우면서
머지않아 평화의 군왕이 이 세상을 기쁨에 넘치는 세상으로 바꿀 것입니다.
국경도 없고 위협도 없고 걱정도 없고,
형제 자매들과 누리는 풍부한 평화만 있을 것입니다.
우리는 어떻게 평화의 군왕을 충성스럽게 지지할 수 있습니까?
지금 그렇게 할 수 있는 몇 가지 방법을 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
하지만 정말 조금도 속해 있지 않을까요?
나와 관련이 있는 정치적인 이슈들을 보면
그러다 보면 마음의 평화를 잃을 수 있고, ···
어느 한쪽 편을 들게 될 수 있습니다.
··· 저는 세상에 속해 있지 않기 때문입니다.
여러분이 사는 나라에서 평화를 앗아가는 것은 무엇입니까?
예민한 사회적 이슈들이 평화를 앗아갈 수 있죠.
두 형제와 한 자매가 어떻게 평화의 군왕을 충성스럽게 지지했는지 보셨습니까?
부당한 세금 인상, 노골적인 불공정, 환경 파괴.
해결하기 위해 노력할 가치가 있는 문제들로 보일지 모릅니다.
우리 모두에게는 베드로와 같은 순간이 있을 수 있죠.
우리가 중요하게 생각하는 이슈 때문에 감정이 끓어오르고
부당한 일을 봤을 때 우리에게 무엇이 도움이 됩니까?
평화의 군왕이 베드로에게 하신 말씀을 기억하십시오.
싸우는 것보다 훨씬 더 나은 일,
우린 예수의 통치를 지지한다는 걸 나타내는 겁니다.
우리가 왕국의 좋은 소식을 정말로 믿는다면
그 소식을 전하는 데 방해가 되는 행동은 그 무엇도 하지 않을 겁니다.
우리가 왕국의 좋은 소식을 정말로 믿는다면
그 소식을 전하는 데 방해가 되는 행동은 그 무엇도 하지 않을 것입니다.
우리가 좋은 행실을 유지해야 하는 이유를 알려 줍니다.
“이방 사람들 가운데서 여러분의 행실을 훌륭하게 유지하십시오.
그러면 그들은 여러분이 잘못을 범한다고 비난하다가도
여러분의 훌륭한 행실의 목격 증인이 되어
하느님이 검사하시는 날에 그분께 영광을 돌리게 될 것입니다.”
사람들이 여호와를 보는 시각에 영향을 주죠.
우리가 섬기는 여호와가 어떤 분인지 생각합니다.
또 우리의 말을 들을 때에도 그런 점을 생각하죠.
우리가 정치적인 이슈에서 한쪽 편을 든다면
말의 자유를 가지고 하느님의 왕국에 관해 말하기가 어려워질 수 있습니다!
사실 이런 상황이 가족들과 있을 때, 직장에서, 학교에서 있을 수 있죠.
사탄은 우리가 베드로처럼 ‘귀를 자르는’ 행동을 하게 하려고
우리의 감정을 끓어오르게 하는 상황을 이용합니다.
우리가 격한 감정에 빠져서 그런 미끼를 물게 되면
사탄이 원하는 대로 끌려가게 될 것입니다.
모든 선한 일을 위해 준비하고, 아무도 비방하지 말고,
모든 사람에게 온화함을 온전히 보이게 하십시오.”
우리는 나라의 법을 지키고 세금을 냅니다.
또 위에 있는 권위에 대해 부정적으로 말하지 않습니다.
정치적인 이슈에서 한쪽 편을 들지 않죠.
하지만 정말 조금도 속해 있지 않을까요?”
물론, 우리는 카이사르의 법과 하느님의 법이 충돌할 때
“사람이 아니라 하느님께 순종”해야 한다는 걸 잘 압니다.
하지만 우리는 무기를 들고 온 말고의 귀를 고쳐 주신 예수처럼,
이 세상의 불공정이나 잔혹함을 볼 때에도 온화하게 대처하기로 결심해야 합니다.
우리는 평화의 군왕에게 영예를 돌리는 놀라운 특권을 누리고 있습니다.
부당한 일이 벌어질 때 우리가 느끼는 감정을
하지만 예수께서 겟세마네 동산에서 베푸신 중요한 교훈을 기억하십시오.
영원한 왕이신 여호와와 평화의 군왕이신 예수께서는
머지않아 이사야 9:6, 7의 예언이 온전히 성취될 것입니다.
정치적인 이슈에서 편을 드는 것처럼 보일 수 있는 행동을 하지 마십시오.
이 세상의 불공정이나 분쟁 때문에 ‘칼을 휘두르는 일’이 있어서는 안 됩니다.
그는 겟세마네 동산에서 배운 중요한 교훈을 결코 잊지 않았죠.
지금이야말로 평화의 군왕에 대한 충성스러운 지지를 적극적으로 나타내고
베드로 후서 3:14의 이러한 말씀을 따라야 할 때입니다.
“마침내 점도 없고 흠도 없이 평화 가운데
[여호와와 평화의 군왕] 앞에 나타날 수 있도록

en.text: Imagine the scene: It’s nighttime.
You’re in the garden of Gethsemane with your close friends and beloved Teacher.
Suddenly, you hear a crowd coming.
They’re being led by a man you know, Judas Iscariot.
He approaches Jesus and kisses him on the cheek.
He then steps aside as men move in to arrest Jesus.
Your emotions churn inside you.
Your Master and Lord is being arrested —the Son of God.
How can this be happening?
What do you do?
Before you can even decide what to do,
Peter draws his sword
and chops off the ear of the slave of the high priest.
Then Jesus says to Peter:
“Return your sword to its place,
for all those who take up the sword will perish by the sword.”
And then you watch the unbelievable,
as Jesus heals the man’s ear.
Peter must have thought that it was a great and noble thing
to fight on behalf of the Son of God.
But Jesus didn’t think so.
With six words
—“return your sword to its place”—
Jesus taught his disciples an important lesson.
This was not their fight;
nor was it the time to fight.
So in this talk,
we’re going to focus our attention on an insidious way
that any of us, like Peter,
can become inadvertently involved in this world’s conflicts
without even realizing it.
And we will talk about how we can avoid making that serious mistake.
But first,
let’s discuss why Jesus did not ask his Father
to send “12 legions of angels”
to help him when being arrested.
It has to do with Jesus’ name.
So please open your Bible to Isaiah chapter 9,
and let’s read verse 6
—Isaiah 9:6.
Now, we know Jesus has many titles,
but in this verse, we’re going to focus on just one.
Verse 6:
“For a child has been born to us,
“a son has been given to us;
“and the rulership will rest on his shoulder.
“His name will be called Wonderful Counselor,
“Mighty God, Eternal Father,
Prince of Peace.”
Why is Jesus called “Prince of Peace”?
Well, consider what Jehovah’s angel declared to the shepherds in the field
at Jesus’ birth at Luke 2:14.
They said: “Glory in the heights above to God,
and on earth peace among men of goodwill.”
How appropriate for the angels to announce
that at the birth of the destined Prince of Peace,
there would be divine peace for those who have God’s goodwill!
But when will this become a reality?
It didn’t happen when Jesus was on earth,
and we certainly don’t see peace today.
Instead of peace, what do we see?
We see the nations that are locked in hostilities and aggression
in a competition for world dominance.
We see global violence and bloodshed.
But please don’t lose heart.
Because we don’t see peace now does not mean it’s not coming.
Isaiah 9:6
—it’s not just wishful thinking.
It’s a promise from Almighty God, and Jehovah cannot lie.
All his prophecies come true.
In fact, let’s read the last portion of verse 7
in Isaiah chapter 9.
The last verse (the last portion of verse 7) says:
“The zeal of Jehovah of armies will do this.”
What does that mean?
It means that Jehovah does nothing in a half-hearted way.
He’s zealous to bring peace, and he will.
We can be sure that whatever Jehovah promises,
he will fully accomplish.
So how will peace come to the earth?
Did the Prince of Peace give us a clue?
Yes, he did.
In fact, the key to everlasting peace
is on the lips of millions of people throughout the world.
They know it by heart.
But let’s read it at Matthew 6:9, 10
—Matthew 6:9.
What a beautiful thought for us!
This is how everlasting peace is going to come through.
It depends on the fulfillment of these verses.
Verse 9:
“You must pray, then, this way: ‘Our Father in the heavens,
let your name [the name Jehovah] be sanctified.’”
The emphasis that we place on the name of God
is not merely a matter of religious knowledge.
Everyone must know God’s name
and treat it as something holy and respected.
It has to be something sacred.
It must be cleared of all the reproach that has been heaped upon it.
In fact, the well-being of the entire universe and its inhabitants
depends upon the sanctification of Jehovah’s name.
Now, let’s look at verse 10:
“Let your Kingdom come.
Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.”
God’s Kingdom —two words but so important.
God’s Kingdom is the most powerful government
humanity will ever see.
There is no nation or empire
that can withstand the might of God’s Kingdom.
And any nation who thinks they can block the coming of God’s Kingdom
is like an ant who plants itself firmly on the railroad track
and with his hand raised defiantly shouts to the oncoming locomotive:
“Stop! You can’t run over me.”
Well, God’s heavenly government has the power
to destroy all present-day violent regimes.
They’re like ants to Jehovah.
And he will eliminate their ability
to wage war, to foment conflict, and to shed blood.
So, yes, Matthew 6:9, 10
—it’s that valuable and important for lasting peace.
God’s Kingdom is the only road to lasting peace.
And in his role as King,
Revelation 19:15 describes Jesus
as ‘striking the nations with an iron rod.’
Soon, Jehovah will give the command to his Son,
and he will destroy all the things that disrupt peace.
Gone will be the terror that we have grown accustomed to living with
day in and day out.
So, what will happen next?
This is what will happen
Let’s open our Bibles here to Psalm 37:10, 11,
and just allow this prophecy to absorb
and to thrill our minds and our hearts
and give us a hope for the future.
Verse 10 of Psalm 37:
“Just a little while longer,
“and the wicked will be no more [a little while longer];
you will look at where they were, and they will not be there.”
“Just a little while longer.”
It’s just like children saying to their parents
when going on a trip “Are we there yet?”
and the parents say “Just a little while longer.”
And that brings comfort to them, and it’s the same with us.
So imagine that!
This means you go into the streets,
you’re looking for a wicked person,
and you will not be able to find even one.
“The wicked will be no more.”
“But the meek will possess the earth.”
That’s what we’re speaking about in verse 11.
Let’s read that: “But the meek will possess the earth,
and they will find exquisite delight in the abundance of peace.”
We love reading that.
Men will be at peace.
They will be at peace with themselves, with their neighbors, with their God.
How does that sound to you?
Meditate on that.
Can you see yourself there in a peaceful new world
where the only news to tune into
is regarding who’s getting resurrected today
or which new person you will be assigned to teach about Jehovah?
Can you imagine the joy of studying with a person,
not just from a different culture,
but from a different time period,
seeing things through their eyes
as they come to love Jehovah as you do?
Well, soon the Prince of Peace
will turn this world into one of sheer delight
—no more borders, no more threats, no more worries—
just an abundance of peace with your brothers and sisters.
Do you want to be there?
Me too.
So how can we show our loyal support for the Prince of Peace?
Please watch the following video,
and notice the different ways we can do this right now.
“I am no part of the world.”
But is the world a part of me?
I’m pressured every day
to get involved in political issues that affect me socially,
. . . environmentally,
. . . and economically.
That pressure could rob me of my peace of mind
. . . and influence how I think.
I could take sides in my heart,
even if I’m not aware of it.
But I know that Jehovah
will care for all of mankind’s concerns
. . . by means of his Kingdom
ruled by his Son, Jesus Christ.
I show my support for him in my prayers,
. . . in how I think and feel,
. . . and by teaching others
what the Kingdom will do for mankind.
I know there are millions
of brothers and sisters all over the world
. . . who loyally support the “Prince of Peace”
just like me, because I
. . . I am no part of the world.
So, what takes away the peace in the country where you live?
in your community? in your town? in your society?
Most likely, it’s the hot-button social issues.
Did you notice how our two brothers and sister
showed their loyal support for the Prince of Peace?
What issues affected them?
Unfair tax hikes, blatant injustice, a disregard of the environment
—all things in themselves seemed like noble causes worthy to get involved.
‘How can they get away with this?
It’s not right. We should do something.’
Does that sound familiar?
We may not have a literal sword in our hand,
but we all have our Peterlike moments.
And if we’re not careful, issues that are close to our heart
can charge our emotions and we can lose our spiritual balance.
So, what can help us when we see things that are wrong?
Remember what the Prince of Peace said to Peter
in that highly charged moment:
“Return your sword to its place.”
In other words, this is not your fight.
So, what do we do?
We do something far better than fight.
We preach.
Each time that we share the Kingdom news,
we proclaim our support for Jesus’ rule.
But here’s the thing:
If we truly believe in the good news of the Kingdom,
we will not do anything that hinders our ability to tell it.
Once again, it’s so important
that if we truly believe in the good news of the Kingdom,
we will not do anything that hinders our ability to tell it.
Why?
Well, let’s find out.
Let’s open up to Peter’s words himself
at 1 Peter 2:12
—1 Peter 2:12.
Peter helps us here with why we need
to maintain our conduct properly.
First Peter 2:12:
“Maintain your conduct fine among the nations,
“so that when they accuse you of being wrongdoers,
“they may be eyewitnesses of your fine works
and, as a result, glorify God in the day of his inspection.”
So Peter had to learn this.
But do we see the connection?
Our actions and words are directly linked to Jehovah.
When people see us, they see a people that worships Jehovah.
And when people hear us, they hear a people that worships Jehovah.
Imagine how our freeness of speech to speak about God’s Kingdom
would be hindered if we were to voice a position for a political issue!
And it can happen so easily.
It can happen at work, at school, with relatives, and so forth.
Satan sets the trap masterfully.
He’s just waiting.
If he could only make us “chop off the ear” of anything in this world
that causes hurt and indignation in our heart
or if he can hook our heartstrings by getting us emotionally charged,
he can then step back and reel us in.
The new world, our hope for true peace,
all starts to fade into the background.
Don’t give him that chance!
Be determined to do
what Titus 3:1, 2 tells us.
Let’s read that
—Titus chapter 3,
verses 1 and 2.
Here is the Scriptural admonition:
“Continue reminding them to be in subjection
“and to be obedient to governments and authorities,
“to be ready for every good work,
“to speak injuriously of no one, not to be quarrelsome,
but to be reasonable, displaying all mildness toward all men.”
‘Be in subjection
and be obedient to governments and authorities.’
Well, now let’s break that down.
In practical terms, what does it mean?
It means to obey the laws of the land and pay taxes,
to not speak negatively about the superior authorities,
and to be careful not to take sides on political issues
(not even in our hearts).
Do you remember that expression from the video?
“I am no part of the world.
But is the world a part of me?”
Of course, when we find ourselves
between Caesar’s law and God’s law, we know what to do.
We apply Acts 5:29 and “obey God as ruler rather than men.”
We know that.
But like Jesus, who healed the ear of the armed guard Malchus,
we’re determined to react with mildness
when provoked by an injustice or cruelty in this world.
In conclusion,
we have the indescribable privilege to honor the Prince of Peace.
And how reassuring it is to know that Jesus understands our feelings!
He understands our emotions when we see things that we know are wrong.
He knows these things hurt our heart.
We just want to make things right.
But remember the critical lesson
he taught his apostles in the garden of Gethsemane:
This is not your fight.
Rather, Jehovah, the King of Eternity, and Jesus, the Prince of Peace,
are telling us: “This is our fight. Leave it in our hands.”
Soon, the prophecy at Isaiah 9:6, 7
will be fulfilled completely.
In the meantime, keep preaching about the Kingdom.
Avoid saying or doing anything
that suggests taking sides on a political issue.
Don’t allow yourself to “chop off the ear”
of the injustices and the causes of conflict of this old world.
Peter tried that, but it didn’t work.
He learned a big lesson that day in the garden,
and he never forgot it.
May we never forget it either.
Now is the time to show your active and loyal support
for the Prince of Peace
as we echo Peter’s words at 2 Peter 3:14
and “do [our] utmost to be found finally by [Jehovah and the Prince of Peace]
spotless and unblemished and in peace.”

之后，不可思议的一幕发生了
耶稣治好了那个人的耳朵

“把剑收回原处！”

这既不是他们的战争

这个演讲会讨论
为什么说我们可能会被阴险的诡计蒙蔽？

不经意间就卷入了这个世界的冲突
我们也会谈谈
我们可以怎样避免犯这样严重的错误
不过，首先
我们会谈谈当耶稣被逮捕的时候
他为什么没有请父亲
派12个军团的天使来帮助他？
答案跟耶稣的一个头衔有关
请翻开你的圣经到以赛亚书第9章
我们来看一下第6节
我们都知道耶稣有很多头衔
不过在这节经文中
我们只重点讨论一个
第6节说
“因为有一个孩子为我们而生
有一个儿子赐给我们
他要肩负领袖的重任

永恒的父亲、和平的领袖”
耶稣为什么被称为“和平的领袖”呢？
让我们看一下耶和华的天使在耶稣出生时
向牧人宣告的话
在路加福音2:14，天使说

在和平的领袖出生时
天使做这样的宣告多么适时啊
受上帝认可的人将会享有平安
这什么时候会应验呢？
这件事没有发生在耶稣生活的时代
也没有发生在我们的时代
我们的时代并不和平
我们看到很多国家彼此竞争
敌对、互相侵犯
世上也发生了很多流血冲突

现在没有和平

这是来自全能上帝的承诺

以赛亚书9:7的最后部分

我们深信，无论耶和华做什么承诺
他都会实现

和平的领袖向我们透露了重要的线索
我们从世上数百万人经常说的话

这些话就记在马太福音6:9,10

这节经文非常有力量
这就是永久和平将会实现的原因

也就是耶和华的名

我们在这里强调上帝的名字
不只是希望大家知道这个名字而已
也希望每个人都尊重这个名字

所有诋毁上帝名声的谎言都要被清除
事实上，全宇宙以及宇宙众生的未来
都有赖于耶和华的名字彰显为圣
现在请看第10节
“愿你的王国来临

短短5个字，但至关重要

世上没有哪一个国家可以跟上帝的王国对抗
任何一个想阻止上帝王国来临的国家

永恒的君王耶和华，还有和平的领袖耶稣

不要让自己在比喻意义上削掉别人的耳朵
也就是不要参与世上的纷争
彼得就在这个问题上犯了错
他在客西马尼园学到了重要的教训
他永远不会忘记，愿我们也不要忘记
我们继续热心而忠贞地支持和平的领袖
就是在实践彼得后书3:14的劝勉
我们要竭尽全力
最终使自己在耶和华和耶稣眼中
毫无污点、毫无瑕疵
和睦安宁

title: 존 에크란: 평화로운 가정을 이루는 비결—함께 여호와를 섬기십시오

ko.text: 하지만 ‘너희가 평화롭기를 바란다’고 말씀만 하시지 않고
어떻게 평화로운 가정을 이룰 수 있는지 구체적으로 알려 주시죠.
여호와께서 길을 알려 주시는 것과 같습니다.
가는 길에 이정표가 몇 개 있어.
그걸 따라가면 잘 도착할 수 있을 거야.”
이제까지 우리는 몇 가지 이정표를 지나왔죠.
가족이 함께 여호와를 숭배하면 평화를 이루고 축복을 받게 됩니다.
가족 중에 여호와를 섬기지 않는 사람이 있더라도
좋은 영적 습관을 유지하면 평화로운 분위기를 만드는 데 도움이 되죠.
가족이 함께 여호와를 섬기는 데 무엇이 어려움이 될 수 있는지 보시겠습니다.
이번 주 가족 숭배 때 뭐 할 거예요?
이 특성의 의미를 이해하는 데 도움이 되지.
성경에는 복종하는 태도를 나타낸 사람들의 예가 많이 나옵니다.
그런 훌륭한 본으로 누가 좀 떠오르니?
현대에도 훌륭한 본들이 아주 많이 있지.
이 내용이 애들한테 잘 맞는 건지 모르겠네.
가족 숭배가 원활하게 진행되는 것 같진 않았죠?
진정으로 가족이 함께 여호와를 섬기기 위해
좋은 습관을 들이고 유지하려면 굳은 결심이 필요합니다.
여러분의 가족도 그렇게 할 필요가 있죠.
가족이 함께 여호와를 섬기겠다고 굳게 결심해야 합니다.
“이제 여호와를 섬기는 것이 여러분에게 좋아 보이지 않으면,
아니면 여러분이 살고 있는 아모리 사람들의 땅의 신들이든,
여러분이 누구를 섬길 것인지를 오늘 스스로 선택하십시오.
그러나 나와 내 집안은 여호와를 섬기겠습니다.”
가족이 함께 여호와를 섬기는 일이 가정생활의 중심이 되어야 합니다.
매주 가족 숭배를 하는 것 말고도 해야 할 일이 더 있습니다.
가족이 함께 여호와를 섬길 수 있는지 알아보겠습니다.
부모 여러분, 여러분의 기도가 자녀들에게 미치는 영향을 과소평가하지 마십시오.
자녀는 부모가 여호와께 마음을 쏟아 놓는 것을 들으면서
여호와께서 부모에게 매우 실제적인 분이라는 것을 느낍니다.
어렸을 때 아버지의 기도를 듣던 기억이 나는데요.
그땐 아버지의 기도가 너무 길게 느껴졌죠.
아버지의 기도 내용에 주의를 기울이게 되었고,
아버지가 여호와와 얼마나 가까운 사이인지 알게 되었습니다.

en.text: Jehovah wants your family to be happy and peaceful.
But Jehovah does more than simply say,
“I hope you have a peaceful family life.”
He explains exactly how we can get our family there.
I want you to imagine Jehovah laying out a map in front of you
and saying: “See these landmarks?
“Look for them on the road to peace.
And if you see them, you’re going in the right direction.”
So far in this symposium, we’ve passed
the landmarks of showing love and respect,
improving communication,
and working together as a team.
The last landmark we’ll consider in this symposium
is worshipping together as a family.
Worshipping together as a family
promotes peace and brings his blessing.
Even if not all in your family are worshippers of Jehovah,
you can promote peace by maintaining a very good spiritual routine.
In the following dramatization, notice some common obstacles
to worshipping Jehovah as a family.
Hi.
Hey, babe.
So, what’s for family worship this week?
I think I got some good ideas.
Yeah?
Mm-hmm.
Thank you for reading that.
Um.
Let’s just go ahead and ask the question. We’ll just do that.
So paragraphs 13 and 14: “How can we be generous?”
Anybody?
Now, the footnote that we just read really helps us to appreciate
the definition of that quality.
Without the definition, we’re left to wonder
exactly what it is and how it connects to the other things
that we’ve discussed this evening.
Gabe, can you go ahead and read the next one for us?
Mm-hmm.
Thank you.
The Bible contains many examples of submissive individuals.
So are there examples?
Sue.
Yeah.
That’s right.
When we talk about examples, where do we start?
There are examples in the past;
there are even examples presently.
And we could even be examples.
That’s—that’s the power of them.
Let’s keep going.
That was a lot of reading.
I know, right?
I want to enjoy family worship, but
I feel like the things that we are covering
are just really not what I need right now.
Yeah.
You know, I just don’t know if this is what they need right now.
Hmm.
We’ll keep working on it.
I think we’d all agree that family worship was difficult to watch.
It was uncomfortable for everyone.
Clearly, Max and Irene had some obstacles
they needed to overcome to really worshipping Jehovah as a family.
To start and keep a good habit going
requires determination and resolve.
So that’s where you need to start for your family.
You need to resolve
that you’re going to worship Jehovah as a family.
Notice the resolve in Joshua’s words
at Joshua 24:15.
That’s Joshua 24:15:
“Now if it seems bad to you to serve Jehovah,
“choose for yourselves today whom you will serve,
“whether the gods that your forefathers served on the other side of the River
“or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are dwelling.
“But as for me and my household,
we will serve Jehovah.”
Yes, worship of Jehovah as a family
needs to be at the very center of your family life.
Now, weekly family worship
is not all that’s involved in worshipping together as a family.
Let’s consider five ways
we can worship Jehovah together as a family.
(1) Prayer.
Parents, do not underestimate the impact
that your prayers have on your children.
When a child hears their parents pour out their hearts to Jehovah,
that tells them that Jehovah is very real to their parents.
I can recall growing up listening to my father’s prayers.
Now, when I was young, I thought his prayers were very long.
But as I grew older and really listened carefully to what he was saying,
I could see how much of a close relationship he had with Jehovah.
(2) Discuss the daily text.
It’s an excellent habit
and a very spiritual way to start the day.
(3) Attend meetings.
Now, we’re not just making sure our family is there at the meetings
but that they’re involved and engaged.
And work hard to prepare so that all family members
can have a meaningful comment at the meetings.
(4) Share in the ministry regularly as a family.
Now, sharing in the ministry together as a family
draws us closer to our family members.
When we hear them speak about the truth,
we listen to their phone calls,
or we read their letters,
we can feel their faith.
I loved going in the ministry with my mother
and listening to her skillfully use the Bible
to answer questions.
And (5) have a consistent,
enjoyable, and meaningful Family Worship program.
Let’s consider what that means —first of all, consistent.
In the video, Max was trying to have
the family worship consistently each week.
Is your family worship consistent each week?
Is your family worship enjoyable?
In the video, the kids were bored.
They were looking at their phones and checking the time.
And week after week of kind of a question-and-answer style
led to the young people giving sort of one-word answers.
It did not look enjoyable.
Now, would your family describe family worship as enjoyable?
How about meaningful?
What Max was using for material
was material that he thought was meaningful.
But did it look like it was meaningful to the family?
Does your family worship use material that is meaningful to your family?
Now, after reviewing these five points,
we don’t want you to be discouraged
if it’s a struggle to maintain a good routine.
Life in this system has many challenges,
trials, and unexpected events.
So stay positive.
And when your good routine breaks down from time to time,
consider what adjustments you can make
to be successful and get your spiritual routine back on track.
Regularly ask Jehovah for his help, and don’t give up.
Now, as you watch the following dramatization,
notice how Max and Irene and the family worked together
to make family worship successful.
March 15, 2014, Watchtower,
“Family Worship —Can you Make It More Enjoyable?”:
“The worship of Jehovah should not be boring. . . .
Address the needs of each family member.”
Babe, what do our kids need?
What’s actually going on in their lives?
Family worship needs to include that.
Yeah, maybe we need to pay more attention to what’s going on with them.
Talk to them; listen to them.
I’m going to send you a link to a great Watchtower  article.
I can’t wait to read it.
Max and I changed our approach.
We found out what mattered to our kids
—like friends,
. . . adjusting to a blended family,
. . . dating.
So we turned things around and used family worship
to focus on what our kids really needed
and to prepare ourselves for possible future trials.
Good night, y’all.
Good night.
Good night.
Good night.
Um,
family worship was—was cool.
It was.
I’m glad you liked it.
Thank you.
Good night, y’all.
Night.
Good night.
Hey! Guess what?
What?
What?
I applied to Bethel.
You did?
Yep.
That’s really exciting.
I’m proud of you.
Thanks.
Aww, congratulations.
Thank you.
Hey, it’s selfie time, everybody. Come on, let’s get together.
All right. On three we’re going to say Bethel, OK?
All right.
One, two, three.
Bethel!
We’ve come a long way.
And through it all,
Jehovah has taught us to love
and he’s given our family
peace.
We can see that Max and Irene analyzed what was wrong with family worship
and decided to change their approach.
Let’s examine how they did that and what it means for us.
What did they do to make their
family worship more meaningful?
Well, Max and Irene had to ask themselves
what was going on in their kids’ lives.
What topics could they discuss at family worship
that would truly be useful to their kids?
Did you smile when you saw Max almost drop the glass
when his daughter talked about dating?
But what a difference their efforts to listen
and really understand what was happening
with the kids made in the family worship!
How did Max and Irene make family worship more enjoyable?
Did you see how the family was reacting at family worship now?
What a difference!
The kids were smiling.
They looked engaged in the discussion
and touched by what they were discussing.
So do what you can to make sure that your family
feels relaxed and happy
and that your family worship reflects
the kind of happy and joyful God that Jehovah is.
Remember, your family will often remember
more about how they felt during family worship
than maybe the exact details of what they learned.
Keep worshipping Jehovah as a family.
Make your family worship consistent,
enjoyable, and meaningful.
And work together to overcome obstacles,
just like Max and Irene and the kids all worked together to solve problems
and create a very peaceful family life.
It was really beautiful to see how far
they had come by applying Bible principles.
In review, this symposium has taught us
that Bible principles can be used
as a road map to family peace.
Work hard to show love and respect,
to improve communication, to work together as a team,
and to worship Jehovah together.
And please be patient with one another
as you form habits that lead to peace.
With Jehovah’s help, you and your family
will enjoy peace that only he can provide.
