지상의 평화를 방해하는 모든 요인이 없어질 것입니다.
제가 항상 감사하는 것은 그분이 모든 문제를 없애실 것이라는 점인데요.
그 가운데는 고통의 모든 원인들이 없어지는 것도 포함됩니다.
그분은 신체적인 고통뿐만 아니라 감정적인 고통도 없애실 것입니다.
우리의 아버지 여호와와 아들 예수께서 주시는 평화가 이 땅에 가득할 그 날이 정말 기다려지지 않습니까?
이제 다음 영상을 보시면서 한 자매가 이 세상이 약속하는 평화가 가짜라는 것을 어떻게 깨닫게 되는지 유의해 보십시오.
이게 예수님의 복음과 어떻게 부합한단 말입니까?
하지만 목사는 한마디 답도 하지 못했어요.
그래서 전 정치에서 답을 찾으려고 했죠.
당시에 평화 운동 단체들이 많이 생겼고
내가 바라는 건 사람들을 추앙하는 게 아니라
하루는 커피 한 잔 하려고 친구 집에 갔는데
성경에 대해 알려 주러 왔다고 했어요.
그 후 정말 친절한 여자 분이
이 조직이야말로 평화를 진정으로 갈망하는 조직이야’ 하고 생각했어요.
그랬더니 다들 저를 미친 사람 보듯 쳐다보았죠.
전 새로운 인생을 살게 되어 정말 기뻤어요.
이사야 14:7의 말씀은 제 인생에 큰 영향을 주었습니다.
하느님께서 평온하고 평화로운 세상을 가져오겠다고 약속하시기 때문입니다.
자매는 정치와 시위를 통해 세계 평화를 이루려고 했습니다.
하지만 그 모든 게 가짜 평화라는 것을 깨달았습니다.
진정한 평화를 가져다주실 수 있는 분은 여호와뿐이십니다.
지금까지 이 연설에서 세 가지 형태의 가짜 평화에 대해 살펴보셨는데요.
마지막으로 강조하고 싶은 점은 예수께서 주신 평화를 지키기 위해 노력하시라는 겁니다.
잘 아시는 내용이지만 6절에 나오는 한 가지 표현에 초점을 맞춰 보겠습니다.
나를 통하지 않고는 아무도 아버지께 올 수 없습니다.’”
특히 강조하고 싶은 것은 예수께서 “진리”이시라는 것입니다.
우리는 그분의 모든 약속을 신뢰할 수 있습니다.
그분은 지금까지 평화를 주셨고 미래에는 더 큰 평화를 주실 것입니다.
그들이 어떤 어려움을 인내해야 했는지 생각해 보십시오.
사도 바울이나 베드로 그리고 그 밖의 사람들은 참으로 엄청난 박해를 인내했습니다.
예수께서 주신 평화가 없었다면 결코 그럴 수 없었을 겁니다.
예수께서는 오늘날에도 여러분에게 평화를 주실 것입니다.
그러면 여러분은 계속 여호와의 뜻을 행하고 그분을 기쁘시게 해 드릴 수 있을 것입니다.
따라서 형제 자매 여러분, 예수께서 우리에게 주신 평화를 잘 지키시기 바랍니다.
사탄은 이 세상을 사용해서 여러분에게 가짜 평화를 약속합니다.
여호와께서는 그분의 아들을 통해 우리가 영원히 평화를 누리게 해 주실 것입니다!
예수의 약속을 더 굳게 신뢰하게 되었네요.
여호와께서 어떻게 우리를 평화로 축복하시는지 살펴보았습니다.
주제 성구는 베드로 후서 3:14의 이런 말씀입니다.
“점도 없고 흠도 없이 평화 가운데 ··· 나타날 수 있도록 최선을 다하십시오.”
우리가 모든 기회에 “평화의 좋은 소식”을 전할 준비를 갖추도록 도와줄 것입니다.
또한 청소년들을 위한 아주 특별한 연설이 있는데요.
자연재해 등의 여러 가지 어려움을 당하면서도
어떻게 평화를 잃지 않는지 볼 것입니다.
따로 마치는 기도를 하실 수 있습니다.

en.text: We are overjoyed that you are among the millions around the world
who are viewing this convention.
An infirm Bible student named Joyce,
who lives in Southeast Asia,
expressed her appreciation for these arrangements by saying:
“With the convention being streamed online,
“I don’t have to miss a single talk!
“I can watch the program with the rest of the brotherhood worldwide.
I am so thankful to Jehovah for this arrangement.”
Perhaps you can relate to her expressions.
Thank you for the generous donations you have made online
at donate.jw.org and by other means,
which help make these streaming services possible.
During these critical last days,
many families lack the affection
that Jehovah designed us to give and receive.
However, God’s Word contains principles
that, when followed, lead to peace.
We’re sure you will enjoy the fine talks and dramatizations
in this next symposium.
Brother Joel Dellinger, a helper to the Service Committee,
will deliver the first talk,
“Follow the Road Map to Family Peace —Show Love and Respect.”
Family peace is precious.
It’s even as the Bible proverb says:
“Better is a piece of dry bread where there is peace
than a house full of feasting along with quarreling.”
But what exactly is family peace?
Someone might say, “As long as we’re not arguing, our family is at peace.”
But is that real peace?
We might think of two countries that were fighting
but have now agreed to a cease-fire.
Does the cease-fire mean that they’ve become
real friends who love one another?
No.
We know that genuine peace takes more work.
That’s true in the family as well.
Our heavenly Father knows that the most satisfying family peace
involves more than an absence of arguing.
It involves a family’s well-being and unity.
Is such peace in a family today really possible?
Although none of us have a perfect family, the answer is yes.
While it requires work —perhaps breaking bad habits
that disrupt peace and adopting new ones that promote it—
those efforts are worth it.
In this symposium,
we’ll see how Bible principles can guide families to peace,
just as a road map
guides travelers to a beautiful destination.
In each of the talks, we invite you husbands, fathers,
wives, mothers, children, teenagers
to be the traveler who studies the map
and then goes in the right direction.
The focus of our first talk
is showing love and respect.
Why would you say these two qualities
are so important to family peace?
Well, it’s simple:
because family members who love and respect one another
feel secure and appreciated.
As a result, our relationships
are warm, close, and peaceful.
Of course, showing love and respect can be a challenge these days.
In the following dramatization notice why.
Irene.
Aww,
you look so handsome there.
Oh, you look beautiful.
Those came out so nice.
Look at you.
Crazy, right?
That’s the day!
Look at us.
You’re so surprised.
I just knew you were going to do it.
Sorry, Olivia.
Are you OK?
Yeah, it’s OK, Sue.
I’m so sorry.
No worries.
Um, I’m all moved in.
That was the last box.
Dad, are those the wedding photos?
Yeah.
Let me see.
Look it. Here’s . . .
Oh, you all look beautiful.
That dress looks so nice.
You look so good.
Aww, look at you.
Aww, that suits you.
Very nice, you guys.
Yeah, it all came together.
It really did.
Yeah.
Olivia?
I know this is all new, baby.
Be patient.
Can I cut in?
Yeah, sure.
Thanks.
What’s wrong?
Where’s the desk?
We had to get rid of it.
This one is better for everyone.
You mean it’s better for him!
For Max?
What are you saying?
What do you care?
Don’t talk to me like that. Get back here!
Hey, Olivia, what do you think about the desk?
Come here, sweetie. Come here.
So you never forget that I love you.
I hope you like it.
Today, every family faces challenges of some sort.
So let’s consult our road map together
in the Bible at Romans 12:10.
Would you read it with me, please?
That’s Romans 12:10:
“In brotherly love
“have tender affection for one another.
In showing honor to one another, take the lead.”
Now, what’s the point?
Regardless of the role we play in the family,
each of us needs to treat our family members with love and respect.
We need to “take the lead,” or initiative, to do so.
To help us, let’s consider four good habits
that all of us should work to develop more fully.
Habit number one:
Regularly express tender affection.
When conveyed with sincerity,
expressions of affection
are like sunshine and water to plants.
They help everyone in the family grow and thrive.
In the video we just watched, did you note how Olivia
cherished her father’s gift (that green desk) and his tender words?
He told her, “So you never forget that I love you.”
We also saw warm affection
as the newly blended family of Max and Irene looked at wedding photos.
That was encouraging.
Well, here’s a question: How are we doing
in expressing tender affection in our family?
If that’s not one of our strengths,
we might relate to a husband who mustered up the courage
to say “I love you” to his wife.
It brought her to tears—tears of joy.
And she said this, “I love you too,
but this is the first time in 25 years you’ve said it like that.”
Well, what’s the point?
We don’t want to wait that long, of course,
but even an awkward attempt at expressing affection in our family
is an act of love, and it can do so much good.
That’s a habit we all want to cultivate.
Let’s consider a second habit:
Be kind in your actions,
tone of voice, and choice of words.
In the video, we recall Irene’s reassurance to her daughter, Olivia.
She said: “I know this is all new, baby.
Be patient.”
Mom was kind
in what she said and how she said it.
A little later, though, Olivia was upset.
While we know she was hurt,
her speech and actions were not so kind, were they?
During the pandemic,
all of us have been under tremendous stress,
and likely we didn’t always treat others
in our family as kindly as we would have liked.
Well, that’s in the past.
But what can we all do now?
We can pray to Jehovah to help us “take the lead”
in showing kindness.
For example, every day greeting one another kindly,
every day saying “please” and “thank you,”
sharing little gifts, making time to talk, really listening
—all of these are acts of kindness.
That’s a good habit we all want to cultivate.
What’s habit number three?
Be quick to apologize and forgive freely.
In the video, Olivia’s new stepsister, Sue,
apologized after she bumped into Olivia with a box by mistake.
That apology promoted peace.
When you and I realize we’ve hurt someone
even unintentionally, what should we do?
We should make amends quickly.
A mother named Marina said this:
“We try to set a good example for our children
“in forgiving others . . . and not getting offended.
“When I am wrong, I apologize to my children.
I want them to learn to do the same in their dealings with others.”
That’s a good habit, wouldn’t you agree?
Well, let’s consider one more, a fourth habit:
Help your family members feel respected.
An article in the Awake!  magazine once made this insightful comment:
“Respect is in the eye of the beholder.”
What does that mean?
Even if we think we’re showing respect in the family,
good questions to ask ourselves are:
‘Do my family members feel that I respect them?
‘Is there more I can do to help my mate, my children, or my parents
feel loved and respected?’
Brothers and sisters, when we fulfill our God-given role in the family
by developing good habits such as these,
we show respect both for Jehovah and for all of our family members.
Now, let’s think about Olivia and her mom.
In the next video, note how peace can be restored
by showing love and respect.
It’s OK, Mom.
You didn’t know.
Dad did that for her just before he died.
Anything I can do to help?
Romans 12:10:
“In showing honor to one another, take the lead.”
Olivia?
I made your favorite tonight.
Thank you.
I wanted to tell you that I didn’t handle that so well today.
You had good reason to be upset about the desk.
Mom, you didn’t know.
It’s just one of those things that Dad did just for me.
I know he’s my stepdad now, but
I just wish he would have checked first.
It wasn’t Max.
It was me.
I wanted to surprise Max with a place for him to do his work.
So he didn’t make you get rid of the desk?
No.
I just thought you both didn’t care.
I will never ever stop caring about you.
What a beautiful outcome!
The well-being and unity of the family were restored.
The mom, Irene, applied the principle at Romans 12:10.
She ‘took the lead,’ or the initiative, to talk kindly with her daughter.
Though Olivia was upset, she too showed love and respect
by being willing to listen to her mom.
As a result, the misunderstanding was cleared up,
and Irene used the opportunity to reassure her precious daughter of her love,
saying, “I will never ever stop caring about you.”
And how our hearts were touched
to see their warm embrace!
When we “take the lead” in applying Bible principles,
we promote genuine family peace.
So may all of us be determined
to keep showing our family that we truly love and respect them
in word and action.
Now please listen as Brother Robert Luccioni,
a helper to the Publishing Committee, considers the next talk
of this symposium, with the theme
“Follow the Road Map to Family Peace —Improve Communication.”
Our previous talk reminded us
that it’s possible for a family to enjoy peace,
but it takes work.
Let’s look at one more step that can help us stay on the road to peace,
and that is good communication.
A family promotes peace when all the family members communicate
in an open, calm, and honest manner.
But how does communication help with peace?
Well, a pattern of good communication keeps a family close.
It helps us to identify and address problems
before these reach a point that they take peace away.
Now, that may seem obvious.
But isn’t it true that we may find that between work and school,
the meetings and ministry, and recreation and just life in general
it’s hard to find time to communicate as a family?
Is that a challenge in your family?
In the following dramatization,
notice what habits hinder family communication.
Hey, Steve.
Yeah, I’m sorry I was late to the meeting.
I should have been there to help out with my assignment.
Yeah, we got delayed.
We’re late!
Let’s go, kids!
We’re coming! Sorry!
Yeah, the family is fine.
Everybody is adjusting really well.
Anyone seen my glasses?
Anyone?
I mean, we might be a little out of sync,
but I don’t know
—every family has their issues, right?
You going outside in those?
Mm-hmm.
Hey, well, thanks for understanding.
All right.
OK. Take care.
All right, bye-bye.
Did you notice some habits that hinder family communication?
In the case of this family, it seems like
technology is stifling their communication.
And they obviously have some things they need to communicate about
—punctuality, dress and grooming— but it’s not happening.
Now, while the scenes of them
all looking at their devices and ignoring one another
may have been a bit humorous,
did it remind you of your family at times?
What a good reminder for us not to let the use of technology
rob our family of our time and attention!
So how can we develop habits
that promote good communication?
Let’s consider the second Bible principle of this symposium.
Let’s turn together, please, to Ephesians chapter 5.
And let’s read verses 15 and 16
—Ephesians 5:15, 16:
“So keep strict watch that how you
“walk is not as unwise but as wise persons,
“making the best use of your time,
because the days are wicked.”
Now, let’s look at two ways that this Bible principle can help us.
The first is by making time
to have meaningful communication.
Did you notice there in verse 16
it says “making the best use of your time”?
Now, the study note for this phrase indicates
the need to ‘buy out the time’ for important things
from other pursuits.
So how can this apply to family communication?
Well, this could include having a plan, or a routine,
for when we spend time together as a family each day.
And during those times, we may choose to limit
our use of technology so that it does not interfere with communication;
perhaps it’s in the evening or at a specific mealtime.
One brother named Aaron stated,
“We have our evening meal together,
“which allows us time to talk and hear what’s important
to each member of the family.”
He says: “My wife and I have arranged our schedules
“so we take the boys to school and pick them up.
This allows us to spend more time with them.”
And then he says, “My wife and I regularly take walks
and freely talk about our concerns.”
What’s the point?
Well, they’re making good use of their time.
However, to do this, they’ve had to buy that time out from other pursuits.
But they have a plan; they have a routine.
So, what plan, or routine,
does your family have for meaningful communication each day?
If you don’t have one, can you start now?
Let’s look at the second way that this Bible principle can help us.
And that is by determining when and how
to deal with problems when they do arise.
You notice verse 15 in Ephesians chapter 5
says that we should ‘walk as wise persons.’
It means we need to choose our paths carefully,
knowing when to go, when to stop, when to take another route.
Well, how can that help us when problems arise?
Well, a wise person
generally knows when is and when is not
a good time to address a problem.
For example, we all can attest that when emotions are high,
it’s probably not the best time to bring up an issue.
One father states:
“Sometimes we need to wait and let things cool.
“Often a night’s rest with prayer makes a big difference
when we address the issue the next morning.”
That’s a wise person.
A wise person also listens.
James 1:19 reminds us to “be quick to listen,
slow to speak, [and] slow to anger.”
Thus, we can go to Jehovah in prayer
and ask him to help us to really listen,
to stay calm, to stay humble.
One sister named Dawn states,
“When there are problems, the first thing I do
is ask Jehovah in prayer to help us resolve the problem calmly.”
Then she says, “Then we talk with the family member privately
and really try to listen to their side of the issue.”
That’s a wise person.
A wise person will also consider the approach
and the words that he or she uses.
For example, rather than telling our family member that they have a problem,
can we turn it around so that it’s something that we all need to work on together?
Do you reassure your family members
that you really love them and you want to understand
their side of the issue or the problem?
See, now, doing this, we’re not attacking the family member
but, rather, showing that we’re all in this together.
So we see benefits of this Bible principle
in communication in our family, don’t we?
You notice the two points: (1) making the best use of our time
and (2) walking as wise persons.
Now, communication will always be a work in progress,
but it’s worth the effort, as it will go a long way
to bringing peace to your family.
Let’s watch more of our dramatization
and notice the benefits of developing habits
that promote good communication.
I don’t know.
What do you think?
We all have to work on it. I know I need to.
Why don’t we approach it that way with the kids
—just be open with them?
That sounds like a good idea.

communication
in our family.

Sue,

“So keep strict watch that how you walk
“is not as unwise but as wise persons,
making the best use of your time, because the days are wicked.”
So
how do you think we’re doing with our phones and other devices?
It isn’t that what you’re doing on your devices is wrong.
Exactly.
But could it be taking time away from more important things
—like talking to each other,
and in that way affecting even how we’re talking to each other?
Yeah, I think it’d be smart
to have some boundaries then.
Yeah, OK.
OK.
OK.

Hey!
Hey, Olivia.
Hey.

Hmm.

I got this one.
I know,
but it’s all about good spiritual judgment.

I know that you’ll do the right thing.
OK.

Yeah, of course.
Mm-hmm.

I know we all have different views on punctuality,
but
I really need your help
so that I can take care of some of my responsibilities.
You think we can meet in the middle?
OK.
Yeah.
All right. Great.
Now, this symposium has been discussing
four Bible principles that can guide families to peace.
Brother Dellinger considered the first one
at Romans 12:10.
And in this part, we considered Ephesians chapter 5,
verses 15, 16.
Now, did we see how this scripture helped our family in the video?
Well, we saw that they knew down deep that they were not making
the best use of their time, so they made changes.
They saw that they needed to set boundaries
so that they could improve their communication.
We also saw how the family —the parents—acted as wise persons.
How?
Well, by determining when and how
to address the problems that needed to be addressed,
such as the use of technology, dress and grooming,
and punctuality.
Well, can this Bible principle help your family
—help my family—to improve communication?
Would this be a good scripture to include
in your next family worship?
Now, it takes time to learn how to communicate well as a family.
But it is worth the effort.
Why?
Well, if we strive to communicate well each day,
then communication will come more readily
when there are problems.
So be determined to look for ways
to improve communication in your family.
And by taking this initiative and sticking with it,
you will be following the road map
to family peace.
Please listen now to Brother David Splane, a member of the Governing Body,
as he considers the next talk of this symposium,
“Follow the Road Map to Family Peace —Work as a Team.”
Jehovah intended married couples to work together.
That’s why Jesus used the expression we find
at Matthew 19:6.
Let’s read this from the Bible —Matthew 19.
And I’ll give you a moment.
Matthew chapter 19 —now, we’re going to read verse 6.
Now, first of all, Jesus quotes
from Genesis 2:24.
Speaking of married couples, he says:
“So that they are no longer two, but one flesh.”
Now, you remember, Jehovah made that comment in the garden of Eden.
But now Jesus adds something that isn’t in Genesis.
He says: “Therefore, what God has yoked
“[yoked] together,
let no man put apart.”
When we think of a yoke, we may think of a team of horses
plowing a field or pulling a heavy wagon.
Well, if they pull together, they can be a powerful force.
The same is true when family members work together.
Mom, Dad
—you have excellent reasons to work together.
When you work together, you contribute to the peace of the family.
And think of the effect it has on the children.
By working together, you’re teaching that fine young son of yours
how to be a caring husband and father,
and your beautiful daughter how to be a supportive wife and mother.
But what happens when teammates begin pulling in opposite directions
or when one puts on the brakes?
Let’s watch a video.
Now, here’s the setup.
For a long time, a sister raised her two children as a single parent,
and she did a great job of it.
Then she married a very kind brother.
The family has a new head.
Let’s see how well the sister is adapting to her new role.
The last few weeks of family worship have been nice,
right?

Rather, Jehovah, the King of Eternity, and Jesus, the Prince of Peace,
are telling us: “This is our fight. Leave it in our hands.”
Soon, the prophecy at Isaiah 9:6, 7
will be fulfilled completely.
In the meantime, keep preaching about the Kingdom.
Avoid saying or doing anything
that suggests taking sides on a political issue.
Don’t allow yourself to “chop off the ear”
of the injustices and the causes of conflict of this old world.
Peter tried that, but it didn’t work.
He learned a big lesson that day in the garden,
and he never forgot it.
May we never forget it either.
Now is the time to show your active and loyal support
for the Prince of Peace
as we echo Peter’s words at 2 Peter 3:14
and “do [our] utmost to be found finally by [Jehovah and the Prince of Peace]
spotless and unblemished and in peace.”
Thank you, Brother Noumair, for strengthening our determination
to give our undivided support
to God’s appointed King, Christ Jesus.
This brings us to the final talk of today’s session.
Jesus promised to give his followers peace.
Why is the peace that Jesus gives far superior
to any peace that this world promises?
And how can we safeguard the gift of peace
that Jesus has given us?
Please follow along as Brother Anthony Morris,
a member of the Governing Body,
delivers the talk, “Do Not Be Misled by Imitation Peace!”
Jesus taught us that Satan
is “the father of the lie.”
We recall that he deceived Eve, a perfect woman.
He lied about our precious Jehovah.
Now, you’re familiar (many of you) with Revelation chapter 12.
I invite you to find that
—Revelation chapter 12.
And in this chapter, verses 7 and 8,
it addressed the fact that “war broke out in heaven.”
But notice
that after he’s kicked out of heaven,
in verse 9 we read:
“So down the great dragon was hurled,
“the original serpent, the one called Devil and Satan,
“who is misleading the entire inhabited earth;
“he was hurled down to the earth, and his angels
were hurled down with him.”
Now, I read it that way specifically,
but what it doesn’t say is
(in the middle part of verse 9):
“Satan, who is [trying to mislead]
the entire inhabited earth.”
No, he “is  misleading
the entire inhabited earth.”
That’s crucial to understand when we think about the theme of this talk,
not to be misled by imitation peace,
because as “the ruler of the world,”
that’s what he’s out to do—mislead.
In fact, it’s an interesting point here in 2 Corinthians chapter 11
to appreciate
how he goes about misleading, or at least it’s addressed here
to serve as a good warning for us.
And an interesting point with the revision
of the New World Translation
(for those of you in the truth before 2013
when it was revised, you’ll remember this)
in verse 14 of 2 Corinthians chapter 11:
“And no wonder, for Satan himself keeps disguising himself
as an angel of light.”
Now, the New World Translation
used to say before the revision
“[transforms] himself into an angel of light.”
Well, the very English word “metamorphosis,”
like for a caterpillar transforming into a beautiful butterfly,
that’s where it comes from, the Greek language.
And that word was not in verse 14.
No, because Satan can’t transform himself
into “an angel of light” (so it’s an improved translation),
but he does disguise.
He’s a masquerader.
And he does that with the subject of peace.
His world offers a sort of peace,
but it’s imitation peace.
Now, Jesus is distinguished, though, with the peace that he gives.
And if you’ll follow along here
in John chapter 14,
he himself explains it to us.
And we treasure the Gospel accounts,
verse 27: “I leave you peace;
“I give you my peace.
“I do not give it to you the way the world gives it.
Do not let your hearts be troubled nor let them shrink out of fear.”
So Jesus gives us his peace, see.
And the peace that Jesus gives us,
it’s this inner calm once you know the truth and Jesus gives us the peace.
We have this confidence that he loves us and Jehovah loves us,
so that we enjoy a good, peaceful relationship with them
and a good conscience.
And we look forward to the Kingdom removing all war and death.
Now, a point to make here:
Satan wants us to trade
the peace that Jesus gives
for his imitation peace
that he has advertised in the world.
Now, in this talk,
we will consider three forms of imitation peace
and why the peace that Jesus gives is superior.
The first one has to do with material things
—how they’ll not bring true peace.
And to help us with that, turn to Matthew chapter 4,
and we’ll be referring to this chapter
throughout this particular talk about not being misled by imitation peace.
And this one is connected with material things
—how they don’t bring true peace—
in the example Jesus sets forth here.
So in Matthew chapter 4:
“Then Jesus was led by the spirit
“up into the wilderness to be tempted by the Devil.
“After he had fasted for 40 days and 40 nights,
“he felt hungry.
“And the Tempter approached and said to him:
“‘If you are a son of God,
tell these stones to become loaves of bread.’
“But he answered: ‘It is written:
“‘“Man must live, not on bread alone,
but on every word that comes from Jehovah’s mouth.”’”
Isn’t that a beautiful rebuttal?
See, Jesus refused to trade
his peace for material things (in this case, bread),
even though he was hungry.
So serving Jehovah was more important to him
than material things, see.
In the world, they have this thinking,
‘Well, you need
a certain amount of money to retire,’
and they’re constantly focused on material things
—not Jesus, see.
It’s superior peace from Jehovah God.
So it’s only temporary anyway,
the material benefits that people seek
and pursue throughout their lives.
Now we can enjoy true contentment
because Jehovah God is going to care for us.
We know that many have personal experiences to prove that.
Now, in the following video,
see what a brother learned about the so-called peace
that the world promises.
As a family, we were doing very well spiritually.
We did family worship, went preaching,
and went to the meetings together.
After some time, we began
to encounter financial problems.
At times, we did not even have money to buy food
for each day.
Many people in our area were going to South Africa
to provide basic needs for their families.
So I decided to go as well,
leaving behind my wife to take care of our seven children.
This affected me spiritually
because I did not know the language, I was unable to preach,
and I did not benefit from the meetings.
Being so far from my family
caused me to neglect my responsibility as a family head.
As a result, my family grew weak spiritually
and we all missed each other very much.
I realized that I had made a wrong decision going abroad.
My conscience started to trouble me greatly.
Then I remembered the example of Baruch
found at Jeremiah 45:5.
Baruch may have wanted to pursue material riches as I had.
When he was helped, he returned.
I decided then to put Jehovah in first place
instead of searching for material things.
So I started to make changes to go home
and help my family spiritually.
When I left South Africa and reached the border of Malawi
(after leaving my family for about six months),
I felt great happiness in my heart,
and I am still happy till now.
Studying the Bible has helped me.
We still encounter financial problems,
but I remember that in Satan’s world,
there is nowhere we can go and have no problems.
Now I serve as an elder.
My family is progressing spiritually.
And this makes me very happy,
because my relationship with Jehovah is strong.
Yes, he learned a hard lesson.
He goes to South Africa
—meetings interrupted and no field service.
And then he remembers Baruch,
secretary for Jeremiah.
And he returns to be with his family, putting the Kingdom first,
and we appreciate him being truthful and sharing that experience.
That’s imitation peace, going after material things.
Now this next one, it’s quite interesting.
So pay close attention
because there may be some listening who need this counsel.
Satan’s world says that we
can ignore Bible standards
and that we might need to ignore some of them to gain peace of mind.
Here are two examples that we’re going to analyze in this talk.
A person may reason that marrying an unbeliever
or obtaining an unscriptural divorce
will make life easier.
And they start reasoning this way,
‘I just want to get married,
and he’s an unbeliever, but he’s a nice person.’
Things like that go on with the treacherous heart.
Again, we go to the example of our Lord and Master, Jesus.
We’re going to read verses 5-7 of Matthew 4:
“Then the Devil took him along into the holy city,
“and he stationed him on the battlement of the temple
“and said to him:
“‘If you are a son of God, throw yourself down,
“‘for it is written:
“‘“He will give his angels a command concerning you,”
“‘and, “They will carry you on their hands,
“so that you may not strike your foot against a stone.”’
“Jesus said to him: ‘Again, it is written:
“You must not put Jehovah your God to the test.”’”
See, Jesus made that very clear.
He was going to be obedient to his Father
and wasn’t going to worry about being testy
with such an experience as the Devil proposed there.
So obedience
—Jesus twice (in a moment we’ll read another one) said: “It is written.”
He sticks with the Scriptures —Jehovah’s thinking—
and he refused to disobey Jehovah.
Now here’s the question,
Why is the peace that Jesus gives
superior to the pursuit
of unscriptural solutions to our problems?
Let that sink in.
Why is the peace that Jesus gives
superior to the pursuit
of unscriptural solutions to our problems?
For example, marrying an unbeliever
—that will likely bring (and it has happened time after time)
that person greater pain
than the longing they felt when they were single.
I’ve personally seen that
all too many times in various congregations
that I’ve had the privilege to serve in.
You see, the other one is an unscriptural divorce.
It often leads to immoral conduct.
It certainly leads to a troubled conscience,
emotional damage and, of course, a loss of privileges.
Now, this is very important to keep in mind.
It’s true that with two imperfect individuals
married to each other, well, there are going to be difficulties
and there are going to be challenges.
But stop and think about this:
When you’re having difficulties,
don’t forget that marriage
is a sacred arrangement.
The world totally has forgotten that.
So Jehovah will strengthen
both to make a success.
You have to keep that in mind: Jehovah will strengthen and help
so that you can succeed because this is his sacred arrangement.
And the Devil has been attacking the family arrangement
all through the last days of this system,
and he’s intensifying it
as he gets closer to being thrown into the abyss.
Now, in the following video,
notice the results of pursuing imitation peace.
Newly married life came with a lot
of unexpected challenges.
You dream about the way your marriage will go,
but then the reality is quite different.
All we ever did was argue,
or we wouldn’t speak to one another.
We never ever went to the elders.
We just didn’t want to bother them.
We just felt, you know, we needed to figure it out ourselves.
We decided that if the house sold,
then we would separate.
The separation wasn’t a good thing,
because in some respects it made things worse.
It did have an impact on the boys.
They started acting out.
They got into some trouble with the police one time.
And there was a loneliness because you’ve gotten married,
and now you don’t have that, and you’re by yourself.
And the same old routine went on where you’re
cooking and cleaning and doing laundry and working.
I felt sick to my stomach.
I had a hard time getting up every morning and facing the world.
At that point, I felt that I needed
to have the elders help out a little bit.
I did pray for Jehovah’s help to direct me,
and I kept wondering why Jehovah wasn’t really
answering my prayers.
But I kind of realize now that it was because we were separated.
The expectations of the separation were not at all what I was thinking.
I reflected on the marriage vows.
One of the things I thought about
was a sister in our congregation.
She was married to an unbeliever, and then she learned the truth.
And he was so violent.
He would beat her; he would burn her books; he would burn her clothes.
He did not allow her children to attend the meetings.
And I thought about the problems that Darrel and I had.
And I thought: ‘Well, Darrel is a kind person.
He’s never done that.’
And I thought:
‘You know, this is something
‘that we need to really work on.
‘We need to really put forth the effort
‘to start applying Bible principles
‘to put Jehovah first in our life
so that we can bring our marriage back in union with Jehovah.’
I realized that it wasn’t what I wanted,
but it was what Jehovah wanted.
There was just no other choice.
Jehovah wasn’t going to bless us unless we got back together.
When we got back together, our marriage was still a work in progress.
You can’t have a perfect marriage in this world,
but you can sure make it better when you put Jehovah first.
We enjoyed the feelings we had toward each other.
I felt closer to Debbie.
Debbie and I have been married now for 48 years.
Separation does not make anything better at all.
If you even have an inkling of love for one another,
you want to work on that, and you want to make it bloom
so that Jehovah can bless it.
The blessings have been endless.
Our children are all doing
fantastic in the truth.
Jehovah said: “Taste and see that [He] is good.”
So we’ve got to do that.
We really appreciated this couple sharing
their experience with the brotherhood.
He learned, you know.
They were always arguing,
and that’s all they did was argue, argue, argue.
It affected their children.
They decided to separate and finally have peace.
‘I don’t have to be around her,’ or ‘I don’t have to be around him.’
But then he realized his relationship with Jehovah
was being interfered with here,
and he went to the elders.
His prayers were affected.
The things he noticed —he was honest about that.
And our precious sister was so nice to honestly explain.
She said what she learned was that ‘this is not about me;
it’s about Jehovah.’
When you finally come to that realization,
Jehovah will strengthen you
to enjoy peace with your marriage partner.
Now, the next one, I never tire of speaking
about these particular couple of verses
or reading about it or hearing another brother give a talk about it.
See, here’s what’s coming soon.
Turn with me to 1 Thessalonians chapter 5.
And many of you are going, ‘Oh, yeah, I know
what he’s going to read about.’
And this is one of the prophecies
that is yet to be fulfilled.
So it’s just invigorating
to know that soon here’s what’s going to happen
—1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
verses 2 and 3:
“For you yourselves know very well
“that Jehovah’s day is coming exactly as a thief in the night.
“Whenever it is that they are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
“then sudden destruction is to be instantly on them,
“just like birth pains on a pregnant woman,
and they will by no means escape.”
Yes, see, “Jehovah’s day”
—this has to do with the day of the outbreak of the great tribulation
when Babylon the Great is destroyed
and Armageddon finishes it off.
In this context, that’s “Jehovah’s day.”
And what happens before then
is this proclamation, “peace and security!”
Will religious leaders be involved?
Well, they’re part of Satan’s system; that’s very possible.
We’ll have to wait and see.
Will it be one announcement or a series of announcements?
That we don’t know.
But this is coming.
And those who are staying close to Jehovah
and enjoying the peace from him and his Son, Jesus,
will not be deceived
by this imitation proclamation of peace
—imitation peace.
And again, back in Matthew chapter 4,
we’re going to see how Jesus handled
this type of test from the Devil
and what we learn from it here
in verses 8-11 of Matthew chapter 4.
“Again the Devil took him [in verse 8]
“along to an unusually high mountain
“and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
“And he said to him:
“‘All these things I will give you
“if you fall down and do an act of worship to me.’
“Then Jesus said to him [without hesitation]:
“‘Go away, Satan!
“‘For it is written: “It is Jehovah your God you must worship,
and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.”’
“Then the Devil left him, and look! angels came
and began to minister to him.”
Right away, a third time: “It is written.”
Jesus was having nothing to do
with this offer of the kingdoms —this imitation peace.
‘You’ll have all the glory and rule.’
And it’s always boggled my mind
that this one who knew
Jesus in his prehuman existence
would have the audacity to try to get Jesus to bow down and worship him.
It shows you that he’s obviously insane.
Now, he wouldn’t allow it either
when they tried to make him an earthly king.
Jesus wasn’t having any part of that.
They were thinking he could bring them peace.
But Jesus said there’s no peace except by Jehovah’s way.
And the peace from God’s Kingdom is so superior
to anything they could try to come up with —their imitation peace.
Here’s why.
Think about this:
Jesus will remove the Devil.
Jesus will remove human rulership.
Jesus will remove sin.
So the earth’s peace will never again be disturbed.
And I appreciate very much that he’s going to get rid of all problems,
and that includes undoing all causes of pain
—and not just physical pain,
emotional pain as well.
It’s wonderful to look forward to that time
with that beautiful peace
from our precious Father, Jehovah, and his Son, Jesus.
Now, in the following video,
see what convinced this sister
not to believe the world’s promises of peace.
My father always taught me that we needed God in our life
in order for there to be peace.
And he always wanted to know,
Can Christians go to war?
How is this consistent with the Gospel of Jesus Christ?
But the pastor could never give us an answer,
and so I thought I’d have to look to politics to find it.
A lot of peace movements were being formed at that time,
so I joined one of them.
We decided where the protest marches would be
and which pamphlets we would use.
But after the protests were over,
everyone was so excited
and they all started applauding
and cheering for the leaders.
I thought: ‘That’s not what I wanted.
‘I don’t want to honor people.
‘I want to have world peace.
And that still hasn’t happened yet.’
Then I started to feel very alone,
and it made me feel unsafe in this world.
With no peace in sight,
I thought, ‘What is the purpose of life?’
While visiting friends for coffee, I saw a man I’d never met before.
My friends told me he wanted to talk to us about the Bible.
So I asked him:
“Sir, what do you think?
Can Christians join the military?”
And the man said, “No, that’s not allowed
because the Bible says you should ‘love your [enemy].’”
It made me think about what my father always said
—that we need God to bring peace.
Then a really nice lady came to my door,
and she had an orange book in her hand.
And it said: True Peace and Security.
After reading it, I thought:
‘This is it!
This is the organization that truly wants peace.’
So I went to those involved in the peace movement.
I told them that I believe that God will change this world
into a beautiful earth where there’ll be true peace.
They all looked at me like I had lost my mind.
I was so happy with my new life.
I felt like I was part of a family
who truly cared about one another
and really wanted peace with each other.
Isaiah 14:7 had a major impact on my life
because there God promises
a calm and peaceful world.
Wasn’t that nice how she learned?
She’d looked to politics and protests for world peace.
Obviously, she was sincere.
But she learned that’s all imitation peace.
True peace and security comes from Jehovah God.
So wrapping it up with these three different types
of imitation peace that we’ve emphasized,
we want to encourage you in these last minutes
to safeguard the peace that Jesus has given you.
In John chapter 14
(you know this, but I want you to really focus
on a particular point), in verse 6:
“Jesus said to him:
“‘I am the way and the truth and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through me.’”
Isn’t that beautiful?
Particularly we want to emphasize Jesus is “the truth.”
We can trust all of his promises.
He is “the truth.”
He’s going to give us peace —already has—
and will to a greater extent in the future.
Yes, our Master is “the truth.”
And he gave the early Christians that peace.
The things that they were able to deal with are just mind-boggling.
As we read the apostle Paul’s experiences and Peter’s and others’
—the persecution they endured— they did it,
enduring with joy.
It’s amazing!
It can only be a supernatural provision of peace.
And just remember,
Jesus will likewise give you the peace you need now
to keep doing Jehovah’s will and to make Him happy.
So, brothers, please,
safeguard the gift of peace
that Jesus has given you.
Satan uses this world
to offer you promises of imitation peace.
Do not be misled!
No, rather, “Let the peace of the Christ rule in your hearts.”
“And show yourselves thankful.”
Yes, through his Son,
Jehovah will bless us all with peace forever!
Thank you, Brother Morris, for strengthening our trust in Jesus’ promise
to give us peace now and during the events that will shortly take place.
The second session of our convention has truly helped us
to see how Jehovah blesses us with peace.
What can we look forward to in the next session?
The scripture theme will be from 2 Peter 3:14:
“Be found . . . spotless and unblemished and in peace.”
The program will begin with a symposium that will help prepare us
to share the “good news of peace” at every opportunity.
Young ones can look forward to a special talk just for them
given by a member of the Governing Body.
We’ll also see how brothers and sisters are maintaining their peace
even when suffering from illness, economic problems,
natural disasters, and other difficulties.
And of course, our next session includes the baptism talk,
after which those who have been approved
will be baptized locally.
We have much to look forward to!
To conclude today’s session,
let’s sing song number 112, entitled
“Jehovah, God of Peace.”
Again, that’s song number 112.
After the song concludes, you may have your own closing prayer.

之后，魔鬼就离开了
有天使来服侍耶稣”
耶稣第三次说
“圣经上写着”
他断然拒绝撒但的引诱
因为他知道这是虚假的
万国和万国的荣耀都是虚假的
你知道吗？
我常常想
撒但以前在天上就认识耶稣
但是他胆敢让耶稣跪下来崇拜他
由此可见
撒但真的疯了！
后来犹太人也要拥护耶稣作王
但是耶稣也断然拒绝了
犹太人以为耶稣会带来和平
但耶稣知道只有耶和华才能赐给人和平
上帝的王国带来的和平
远远超过人所能够想象的虚假的和平
为什么呢？
因为耶稣会消灭魔鬼
耶稣会消灭人间的政府
耶稣也会消除罪
地上的和平将永远不会再被破坏
我很感谢耶稣
因为他会消除人类所有的难题
以及难题的根源
他会治愈所有的伤口
不只是身体上的
也包括感情上的伤口
我们真的非常期待
我们的天父耶和华和他的儿子耶稣
赐给我们这样的和平安宁
接下来请观看短片
请留意这位姐妹怎样看出
世人承诺的和平都是虚假的
我爸爸常说
我们要有世界和平就必须依靠上帝才行
他一直很想知道
基督徒能不能参与战争
参与战争真的符合耶稣基督的教导吗？
牧师并不能给我们合理解释
所以我觉得只有通过政治途径来追求和平
当时有很多和平运动
我就加入了其中一个
我们会策划要在哪里游行
还有要分发什么册子
但是抗议游行结束之后
大家都很兴奋，情绪高涨
为那些带头的人鼓掌欢呼
我想，这并不是我想要的
我不想要推崇人
我只想要和平安宁
但它并没有实现
我开始感到非常无助
得不到安全感
我觉得和平安宁是不可能实现的
于是我想
“活着到底是为了什么？”
我去朋友家的时候
看到了一个我从没有见过的人
朋友说，这个人想跟我们谈谈圣经
我就问他
“基督徒能加入军队吗？
你觉得怎么样？”
他回答说
“不行，因为圣经说，要爱你的敌人”
这让我想到我爸爸说的
只有上帝才能带来和平
后来有一位友善的女士来找我
她手里拿着一本橘色的书
书上写着“真正的和平安全”
读完后，我就想
这是我要找的！
这个组织是真正在追求和平的组织
我就去找那些以前跟我一起游行抗议的朋友
我跟他们说
上帝会把这个世界变得非常美好
他会让这个地球充满和平和安宁
他们都惊讶地看着我
觉得我疯了
现在我过得非常快乐
我很高兴我属于一个温暖的大家庭
大家都彼此关心，追求和睦
以赛亚书14:7的经文
对我的人生有很大的影响
因为上帝保证
大地会安宁太平
姐妹真的学到了很多
以前她以为政治运动能带来世界和平
虽然她很努力去追求
但她后来才发现这都是虚假的
真正的和平与安宁是来自于耶和华上帝的
现在
我们来总结一下
刚才讨论过的三种虚假的安宁
我们想鼓励大家要紧紧持守
耶稣赐给我们的安宁
大家都很熟悉约翰福音14章
但我想请大家留意其中的一个要点
第6节，经文说
“耶稣说
我就是道路、真理、生命
要不是通过我，谁也不能到父亲那里去”
说得多么好！
我们想特别强调耶稣就是“真理”这一点
因为他就是“真理”
所以我们可以相信他的承诺
耶稣已经赐给我们安宁
以后还会赐给我们更多的安宁
没错，主耶稣就是“真理”
他赐给1世纪的基督徒安宁
让他们能够成功地应对各种考验
我们读到使徒保罗
使徒彼得以及其他人的经历
面对迫害他们仍然保持忍耐和喜乐
真的不可思议
因为他们得到耶稣所赐的安宁
不要忘记
耶稣今天也会赐给你安宁
让你能够继续遵行耶和华的旨意
让他欢喜
所以，弟兄们
要保护耶稣基督赐给你的安宁
撒但通过这个世界给人虚假的安宁
千万不要上当！
“要让因基督而有的安宁支配你们的心
要显出感恩之心”
耶和华上帝会通过他的儿子
赐给我们永远的安宁！
谢谢你，莫里斯弟兄
你的演讲帮助我们确信
耶稣在现今和大患难期间都会赐给我们安宁
第一天下午的节目
帮助我们看出耶和华怎样赐人和睦与安宁
第二天上午又有哪些精彩内容呢？
第二天的主题经文是彼得后书3:14
你们要毫无瑕疵、和睦安宁
第一个节目是一个系列演讲
帮助我们抓紧每一个机会
跟人分享“关于和睦的好消息”
一个中央长老团成员
会发表一个特别为年轻人准备的演讲
敬请期待
我们也会看看弟兄姐妹
在遇到健康问题
经济压力、自然灾害
以及其他难题时怎样享有安宁
不要忘了
第二天上午也会有浸礼演讲
之后被批准受浸的人会在本地接受浸礼
我们真的满怀期待！
在节目的最后
请大家一起唱诗第112首
赐平安的上帝耶和华
诗歌第112首
唱诗结束后
请各自在现场祷告

title: 열왕기상 소개

ko.text: 이 책은 약 129년 동안 있었던 일을 다루는데
솔로몬의 통치 아래 평화와 번영을 누립니다.
솔로몬의 봉헌 기도에 대해 알려 줍니다.
그는 솔로몬의 지혜와 번영을 본 뒤에
“내가 들은 것은 그 절반도 안 됩니다”라고 말합니다.
이방 신들을 믿는 이 아내들로 인해
아스도렛과 밀곰 같은 신들을 섬기게 됩니다.
르호보암은 유다 지파와 베냐민 지파만 다스리게 됩니다.
여로보암은 백성이 예루살렘으로 가서 숭배하지 않도록
북쪽 왕국에는 우상 숭배가 만연하게 되고
그로 인해 압제와 권력 다툼과 암살이 있게 됩니다.
르호보암과 그의 뒤를 이은 아비얌의 통치 기간에
남쪽 왕국에서 거짓 숭배가 성행하게 됩니다.
순결한 숭배라는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
아사의 뒤를 이어 왕이 된 아들 여호사밧도
북쪽 왕국을 다스린 악한 왕들을 언급합니다.
그 결과 아합은 전쟁에서 죽임을 당합니다.
그리고 그의 아들 아하시야가 이스라엘의 왕이 됩니다.
어떻게 거짓 숭배가 큰 고통을 가져오고

en.text: An introduction to 1 Kings.
First and Second Kings were originally one volume,
which was later made into two.
Jeremiah is believed to be the writer.
First Kings continues
where Second Samuel leaves off.
The account covers a period
of some 129 years,
beginning about 1040 B.C.E.
with King David’s final days
and ending in about 911 B.C.E.
when King Jehoshaphat dies.
In the first part of the book, after the death of King David,
Israel enjoys peace and prosperity
under Solomon’s rule.
In the second part, false worship takes root
and Israel is split into two kingdoms.
In chapter 1, Solomon is anointed as king.
In chapter 3, Jehovah blesses King Solomon
with extraordinary wisdom,
along with riches and glory.
In chapter 4, God’s people prosper
under Solomon’s rule.
Chapters 5 through 8 discuss
the construction of the temple,
the making of its utensils,
and Solomon’s dedication prayer.
In chapter 10, the queen of Sheba
hears a report about Solomon
and then travels to Jerusalem to see him.
After observing the king’s wisdom
and prosperity, she says:
“Look! I had not been told the half.”
In chapter 11, Solomon,
in disobedience to Jehovah,
“loved many foreign women.”
These pagan wives gradually incline Solomon’s heart
to worship other gods,
including Ashtoreth and Milcom.
After reigning for 40 years, Solomon dies
and his son Rehoboam takes the throne.
In chapter 12, Rehoboam promises
to add to the already heavy burden on the people.
Ten tribes revolt and make Jeroboam their king.
Rehoboam is left with the tribes
of Judah and Benjamin.
Jeroboam sets up the worship of golden calves
to discourage his subjects from worshipping in Jerusalem.
Idolatry becomes entrenched in the northern kingdom,
and this leads to oppression,
power struggles, and assassinations.
In chapters 14 and 15,
Rehoboam and Abijam after him
allow false worship
to take root in the southern kingdom.
Did you know?
About 33 years
after Solomon inaugurated the temple,
Jehovah allowed Pharaoh Shishak
to plunder its treasures.
This shows that Jehovah is pleased,
not by impressive buildings,
but by pure worship.
In chapter 15,
Asa becomes king in Jerusalem
and he does what is right in God’s eyes.
He is succeeded by his son Jehoshaphat,
who imitates his good example.
The next chapter mentions
a number of wicked kings
in the northern kingdom.
These include Ahab,
who marries the pagan princess Jezebel.
She and her husband bring Baal worship into the kingdom.
In chapter 18, the prophet Elijah
proposes a test on Mount Carmel
to show who is the true God—Jehovah or Baal.
Jehovah demonstrates that he is the true God.
In chapter 19, Elijah flees for his life
when he receives a death threat from Jezebel.
Jehovah appears to Elijah at Mount Horeb
and comforts him in “a calm, low voice.”
He gives Elijah further assignments.
In the final chapter, Ahab disregards
the prophet Micaiah’s warning against fighting Syria.
As a result, Ahab is killed in battle.
His son Ahaziah takes the throne in Israel.
Later, Jehoshaphat also dies,
and his son Jehoram becomes king in Judah.
As you read 1 Kings,
note how false worship
leads to great suffering,
see how true worship promotes
peace and happiness,
and take comfort that Solomon’s wisdom
pales in comparison to that of Jesus Christ,
the incorruptible King of God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 列王纪上下原本属于同一卷书
之后被分为两卷
一般认为执笔者是耶利米
列王纪上接续撒母耳记下记述以色列的历史
列王纪上涵盖的时期是大约129年
从大约公元前1040年大卫离世前
到公元前911年左右约沙法王去世为止
这卷书的第一部分描述在所罗门的统治下
以色列国繁荣昌盛、国泰民安
在第二部分，错误崇拜开始蔓延
以色列分裂成两个王国
在第1章，所罗门被任命做王
在第3章，耶和华赐给所罗门王非凡的智慧
以及财富和荣耀
第4章描述了在所罗门统治下的繁荣景象
第5到8章记述了建造圣殿，打造圣殿器具
以及所罗门在圣殿呈献礼的祷告
在第10章，示巴女王听到所罗门的名声
就到耶路撒冷拜访他
看到所罗门的财富以及表现的智慧，她说
“［我］才发现别人告诉我的还不到一半呢！”
在第11章，所罗门没有听耶和华的话
“爱上了许多外族女子”
这些妻妾使他的心离开上帝去崇拜别的神
包括亚斯他禄和米勒堪
所罗门统治以色列40年后去世
他的儿子罗波安继位
在第12章
罗波安决定要加重人民的苦役和重担
结果，十个部族反叛
另立耶罗波安为王
罗波安则统治犹大和便雅悯部族
耶罗波安为了不让人民前往耶路撒冷崇拜上帝
就设立了金牛犊像供人崇拜
偶像崇拜开始在北方以色列国盛行
这引发了压迫、争权夺利以及暗杀
在第14和15章
罗波安和接续他做王的亚比央
纵容在南方犹大国的错误崇拜
你知道吗？
圣殿启用大约33年后
耶和华允许埃及王示撒
夺去圣殿内的所有财宝
从这点可以看出
耶和华看重的不是辉煌的圣殿
而是正确的崇拜
在第15章，亚撒在耶路撒冷做王
他做耶和华眼中看为对的事
后来约沙法继位并效法他父亲亚撒的好榜样
第16章描述了北方以色列国几个邪恶的王
其中就包括亚哈
他娶了信奉异教的公主耶洗别为妻
他们二人在国内推行巴力崇拜
在第18章
先知以利亚在迦密山和巴力的先知较量
让人民看出谁才是真神
后来耶和华证明他才是真神
在第19章，以利亚知道耶洗别要杀他
就赶紧逃命
耶和华在何烈山向以利亚显现
用“平静低微的声音”来安慰他
并交给他更多的任务
在最后一章
亚哈不听米该雅发出的警告
执意去跟叙利亚交战
结果战死沙场
他的儿子亚哈谢继位
之后在犹大国的约沙法也去世了
他的儿子约兰继位
当你阅读列王纪上时，请留意
错误崇拜给人带来痛苦
正确崇拜则给人带来快乐和安宁
身为上帝王国的君王
耶稣的智慧远胜所罗门
他也会永远忠于上帝
值得我们全心信赖！

title: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 겸손의 길로 걸으십시오

ko.text: 그런데 생각해 보면, 겸손을 나타내는 면에서 어떤 때는 잘하다가도
또 어떤 때는 그렇지 않은 경우도 있지 않습니까?
예를 들어, 평일 집회 때 연설을 잘하거나
파수대 연구 때 좋은 해설을 해서 누군가에게 칭찬을 들으면,
그 모든 것이 여호와와 우리가 받은 훈련 덕분이라고 생각합니다.
하지만 어떤 경우에는 잘 안 될 때도 있습니다.
우리의 겸손이 시험을 받는 상황이 때때로 생기는 것이죠.
베델에서는 우리 모두 서로 밀접하게 연합해서 함께 일합니다.
학생 여러분 가운데는 팀으로 일하는 자매들이 있고,
형제들 모두는 회중이나 베델에서 또는 둘 다에서 책임을 가지고 있습니다.
이 모든 상황에서 필요한 것은 겸손입니다.
여호와 하느님과 예수 그리스도의 사도들이 나타낸 겸손을 통해
무엇을 배울 수 있는지 생각해 보겠습니다.
범위를 좀 좁혀서 몇 가지 부면만 살펴보겠습니다.
첫 번째 점이 좀 의외라고 생각되실 수 있는데요.
겸손에는 다른 사람에게 자비와 동정심을 나타내는 것이 관련된다는 점을
다른 사람에게 자비와 동정심을 나타낸다는 것이 포함되죠.
다시 말하면 필요한 경우에는 예외를 허용하는 것입니다.
성경에서 그분이 다시 생각해 보신 예를 여러 번 보지 않으셨습니까?
여호와의 법칙은 완벽하지만 때때로 그분은 다시 생각해 보십니다.
예를 들어, 이스라엘 백성은 약속의 땅을 정복할 준비를 하고 있었습니다.
여호와께서는 그들에게 다음과 같은 아주 분명한 법을 주셨습니다.
“그들과 계약을 맺어서도 안 되고 그들에게 호의를 베풀어서도 안 된다.”
계약을 맺어서도, 호의를 베풀어서도 안 됐죠.
여호수아는 그 도시로 두 정탐꾼을 보냈고
보통 라합의 믿음에 대해 이야기를 많이 하는데,
두 정탐꾼의 믿음에 대해서는 어떻게 생각하십니까?
그 도시로 가기 위해 그들이 나타냈을 믿음에 대해 생각해 보셨습니까?
그들이 40살이 안 되었다면 광야에서 태어난 것입니다.
그들은 실제로 얼마나 집에 들어가 봤을까요?
기껏해야 요르단강 동편에서 몇 사람 정도였겠죠.
그들이 도시에 들어가자마자 무슨 일이 있었습니까?
우선 그들은 가나안 복장을 하고 있지 않았죠.
당시에는 인터넷으로 옷을 주문할 수도 없었으니까요.
아마도 그들은 광야에서 죽은 아버지에게서 물려받은
가나안 사람처럼 보이지 않았고 금방 눈에 띄었습니다.
그리고 그들이 입을 열자마자 사람들은 “여기 말을 하지 않네요.
가나안 사람이 아니군요” 라고 했을 겁니다.
여호와께서는 라합의 마음속에서 뭔가 좋은 것을 보신 걸까요?
정탐꾼들이 예리코에서 여호와께 믿음을 둘 만한
네, 라합은 정탐꾼들을 숨겨 주기로 했지만 조건이 있었습니다.
가나안 말과 히브리 말이 많이 달라서
몸짓을 많이 사용했겠지만 어쨌든 서로의 말뜻을 이해했을 겁니다.
그들에게 속한 모든 자를 살려 주셔야 하며,
예외를 허용해 줄 것을 요구한 겁니다.
‘그들과 계약을 맺어서도 안 되고 그들에게 호의를 베풀어서도 안 된다.’
라합은 상당히 큰 예외를 요구한 겁니다.
모든 가족의 생명을 보존해 줄 것을 요구한 겁니다.
라합과 그의 가족이 죽지 않을 것이라고 약속했습니다.
정탐꾼들이 예외를 허용한 것에 대해 성경은 나쁘게 말하지 않죠.
라합에 대해서 뭔가 좋은 것을 보시고 살려 주기를 원하셨을 수 있죠.
기브온 사람들과 계약을 맺어 지침을 따르지 않았을 때,
지금 이 두 정탐꾼들과 관련해서는 그런 언급이 없습니다.
그처럼 예외를 허용한 것에 대해 여호와께서 동의하셨습니다.
그분이 라합의 가족이 살던 부분의 성벽은 보존하셨기 때문입니다.
여호와께서는 자신의 완벽한 규정에 예외를 허용하신 것입니다.
그리고 대부분 규칙은 우리의 상황에 잘 맞죠.
하지만 때로는 규칙에 예외를 적용해야만 하는 경우가 있습니다.
저는 베델 가족이 브루클린에서 이사를 나오던 때가 생각나는데요.
많은 베델 성원들이 인근 회중에서 장로와 봉사의 종으로 섬기고 있었습니다.
그래서 대대적인 조정이 뉴욕시에 있는 회중들에 필요했습니다.
각 회중의 장로, 봉사의 종, 전도인 수를 적절하게 맞춰야 했습니다.
그렇게 해서 전도인들은 여러 회중에 배정되었죠.
이 조정에는 다음과 같은 적절한 규칙이 따랐습니다.
개인적인 감정을 다 고려할 시간이 없습니다.
그런데 독신인 두 자매가 한 회중으로 배정되었습니다.
배정받은 회중은 그곳으로 가는 대중교통편이 없었습니다.
그런데 왕국회관이 위치한 지역은 매우 위험한 곳이었죠.
그리고 많은 경우 불완전한 규칙이라도 대부분의 형제들에게 잘 적용됩니다.
때때로 예외를 허용해야 하는 경우가 생길 수 있습니다.
라합이 예리코에서 죽지 않은 것에 대해 누가 감사했을지 떠올릴 수 있습니까?
앞선 연설에서도 나왔는데, 룻의 남편인 보아스입니다.
라합이 예리코에서 죽었다면 다윗이 태어날 수 있었겠습니까?
여호와께서는 가나안의 일곱 민족을 없애라고 명령하셨고
먼 곳에서 온 사람인 것처럼 가장했습니다.
그래서 장로들은 여호와께 묻지 않고 기브온 사람들과 계약을 맺어
그렇게 계약을 맺고 얼마 되지 않아 이스라엘 사람들은
속아서 맺게 된 계약이었지만 이스라엘 사람들은
이스라엘 사람들과 기브온 사람들이 계약을 맺었다는 걸 알게 되었고
그래서 그들은 모든 기브온 사람들을 죽이기로 작정했고
사실 그것은 여호와께서 처음에 의도하신 것과 같았습니다.
너희 손으로 기브온 사람들을 죽이지 않겠다고 했으니
아모리 사람들이 죽이도록 내버려 두면 되겠구나.’
그들 중 한 사람도 너에게 맞서지 못할 것이다.’”
여호와께서는 이스라엘 백성이 잘못 맺은 계약도 지킬 수 있도록 도와주셨습니다.
이제 예수의 사도들을 생각해 볼 텐데요.
그들이 벌인 논쟁에 관해 말할 때가 많은데 대부분
오순절 이후로 사도들은 어떤 특성을 나타냈습니까?
그들은 어떤 일에 대한 공을 자신에게 돌리거나
마태는 예수 그리스도의 생애에 관한 첫 번째 영감받은 기록을 썼습니다.
마태 본인이 그 기록에서 자주 등장할까요?
마태가 공개 연설을 하고, 기적을 행하고, 양 치는 방문을 하고.
그의 이름은 마태복음에 두 번밖에 나오지 않죠.
그 두 번도 자신을 세금 징수원으로 묘사합니다.
한 번도 사도 요한을 가리킨 적은 없습니다.
거의 매번 침례자 요한을 가리킨 것이죠.
할례 문제에 관해 모인 적이 있는데 중요한 모임이었을까요?
사도들과 연로자들이 있는 자리에서 누가 주재했습니까?
사도도 아닌 예수의 동생 야고보가 모임을 주재했습니다.
그리고 결정이 내려진 후에 누가 그 결정을 발표했습니까?
“아주 중요한 결정이니까 우리 둘 중 하나가 발표하는 게 좋겠어”
사도들은 겸손해야 한다는 교훈을 배운 겁니다.
순회 방문 때 그들의 본을 기억하십시오.
여러분이 베델에서 중책을 맡고 있을지 모르지만
순회 방문 때는 순회 감독자가 그 주를 책임집니다.
그의 수고에 얼마나 감사하고 있는지 주저 없이 알려 주십시오.
이곳 미국의 베델 가족은 이 면에서 훌륭한 본이 됩니다.
순회 감독자들은 베델 성원들이 많은 회중을 처음 방문하면 좀 긴장하죠.
하지만 베델 가족은 받은 조언에 매우 감사한다는 걸 나타내는데,
어떤 땐 순회 방문이 끝나고 여러 주 동안 그에 관해 이야기하기도 합니다.
베델 가족은 순회 감독자의 방문에 깊이 감사하며
겸손한 사람은 어떤 식으로든 왕국 활동에 기여할 수 있다면
그들은 특권이나 맡은 책임이나 위치에 연연하지 않습니다.
이와 관련해서 사도 바울에 대해 좀 이야기해 보겠습니다.
바울은 자랑하기를 좋아하는 사람이 아니었다고 했죠.
예수께선 아나니아에게 바울이 큰 특권을 받게 될 거라고 말씀하셨습니다.
그 사람은 내 이름을 이방 사람들에게
즉시 예루살렘에 가서 중앙장로회로 일하겠다고 했나요?
“이젠 나도 기름부음받았으니까 그럴 수 있다”고 하면서요.
다마스쿠스에 머물면서 계속 좋은 소식을 전했습니다.
드디어 기원 36년에 그는 예루살렘에 있는 세계 본부로 갔습니다.
그는 예루살렘에 와 있던 사도 베드로와 15일간 함께 지냈습니다.
바울은 겸손하게 좋은 소식을 계속 전파했습니다.
어느 날 그가 성전에 있을 때 예수께서 나타나셨습니다.
그분은 바울에게 예루살렘을 즉시 떠나라고 말씀하셨는데,
제가 떠나 버리면 그들은 어떻게 일 처리를 하죠?
그는 신권 지침에 순종하여 예루살렘을 떠났습니다.
그곳은 중앙장로회가 있는 예루살렘에서 800킬로미터나 떨어져 있었죠.
어떻게 중앙장로회가 그의 탁월한 특성들을 알 수 있겠습니까?
바울이 거기 갔을 때 회중이 있었는지는 알 수 없습니다.
앞서 들었던 회견에서 한 형제가 결국
어떻게 순회 활동을 하게 되었는지 말한 기억이 나는데요.
순회를 하기 전에 여호와께서 훈련을 베풀어 주셨죠.
아마 사도 바울도 그랬던 것 같습니다.
여러분은 바울이 타르수스에서 8년 동안이나 전파했다는 걸 알고 계신가요?
바울이 개종한 지 11년이 지나서야 바나바가 그를 찾아왔습니다.
그때부터 바울은 더 많은 책임을 맡기 시작했습니다.
5년 뒤에 바울은 우리가 지금도 소중히 여기는
그들 가운데 계수되지 않은 것에 못마땅해하지 않았습니다.
야외 봉사 모임을 사회해 달라는 요청을 받는다면,
그것을 여호와의 사랑의 표현으로 생각하고 소중히 여기십시오.
겸손의 시험이 되는 여러 상황이 생길 것입니다.
여러분이 그 시험을 통과할 것이라고 확신합니다.
속으로는 별로 마음에 안 들 수 있죠.
그 일이 잘 될지, 시간 낭비만 하는 것은 아닐지 의문이 들 수 있습니다.
하지만 여러분은 그 일을 제쳐 두면서
나중에 시간 나면 하겠다는 식으로 하지 않을 겁니다.
오히려 마음을 다해 그 일을 할 것입니다.
여호와께 그 일을 축복해 달라고 기도할 것입니다.
처음엔 마음에 들어 하지 않았던 그 일을 말이죠.
어떤 추천을 해 달라는 요청을 받았는데
선택할 수 있는 모든 옵션과 각각의 장단점을 얘기해 줄 것입니다.
이렇게 생각하며 선호하는 방법을 강조하지 않을 겁니다.
형제들이 결정을 내리도록 돕는 것은 성령이라는 점을 인식하고
올바른 결정을 내리도록 성령이 도와줄 것임을 확신하십시오.
그럴 때 여러분은 마음속으로라도 내 의견이 가장 좋은 의견이기 때문에
다른 사람들의 의견을 친절히 듣기는 하겠지만,
사실 내 의견이 정답이고 그래서 다른 사람들이 내 의견을 따라야 한다고
아무도 항상 맞을 수는 없기 때문에 그렇게 생각해서는 안 되죠.
여호와의 영은 함께 일하는 모두에게 작용할 수 있습니다.
여러분이 한 제안이 혹시 채택되지 않더라도 실망하지 마십시오.
다음번 회의에서는 여러분이 한 제안이 받아들여질 수도 있습니다.
‘채택도 안 되는데 이제 어떤 제안도 안 할래.’
영 시원치 않을 수 있다는 걸 인정하십시오.
사실 저도 바보 같은 제안을 할 때가 있는데
그럴 때 중앙장로회가 참을성을 나타내 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
평일 집회에서 해설하거나 프로를 다룰 때
편안히 앉아서 집회를 즐기고 영적 양식을 섭취하십시오.
형제 자매들이 여러분을 위해 준비한 내용을 즐기십시오.
모두에게 필요한 내용을 상기시켜 드린 거죠.
하지만 항상 겸손할 때가 오기를 우리는 기도합니다.
그렇게 한다면 여호와께 계속 사용될 것입니다.

en.text: All of you are humble people.
If you weren’t, you would never have been invited to Gilead.
Have you ever noticed, though, that where humility is concerned,
we do well in some situations
and not so well in others?
For example, if someone commends us
for a good job on a talk in the midweek meeting
or perhaps a comment on the Watchtower  Study,
we give all credit to Jehovah and to the training we’ve received,
and that’s good.
But in other situations,
we might get into trouble.
In other situations,
our humility might be put to the test.
Now, at Bethel, as has been mentioned
on this program already,
we all work with people;
we all work closely with others.
Now, some of you sisters work on a team; you work with others.
And you brothers all have responsibilities
in the congregation or at Bethel or perhaps both.
But in all situations, humility is needed.
So I thought that this morning
we might consider what we can learn about humility
from Jehovah God
and from the apostles of Jesus Christ.
Now, humility is a broad term,
so let’s narrow it down a little bit.
Let’s consider a couple of aspects of humility,
and the first one I’m going to mention might surprise you.
Insight on the Scriptures tells us that humility includes
the ability to show mercy
and compassion to others
—the ability to show mercy
and compassion to others—
the ability to make exceptions where that is warranted.
Well, that’s Jehovah, isn’t it?
Jehovah isn’t rigid.
Jehovah knows when to make exceptions.
How often did you read in the Bible as you went through
that Jehovah reconsidered?
Jehovah makes perfect rules,
and yet at times he reconsiders.
Now let’s illustrate:
The Israelites are getting ready to conquer the Promised Land.
And the first up is the city of Jericho.
Now, there’s a rule
—a rule of engagement— and it’s very clear.
Jehovah says:
“You must not make any covenant with them
nor show them any favor.”
No covenant, no favor —that’s the rule.
It’s a perfect rule because it’s Jehovah’s rule.
Joshua sent two spies into the city,
and they went to the home of a prostitute named Rahab.
Now, wait a minute;
let’s think about that.
Pretty easy to say, isn’t it?
Joshua sent two spies into the city.
They went into a house of a prostitute named Rahab.
Now, we often think about the faith of Rahab.
But what about the faith of those two spies?
Can you imagine the faith that it took for those men
(the Bible says they were young men) to go into that city?
Now, if they were under 40 years of age,
they were born in the wilderness.
How many cities had they ever seen?
Had they ever seen a city before?
How many actual houses had they entered?
How many foreigners had they ever met?
Maybe not very many—maybe a couple on the other side of the Jordan,
but not very many.
So now, as soon as they enter the city, what happens?
Someone calls the police.
They’re recognized right away.
And no wonder!
First of all, they weren’t dressed like Canaanites.
You couldn’t order your clothes from Amazon in those days, you know.
They were dressed like Israelites.
They probably had on 40-year-old hand-me-downs
from their fathers who had died in the desert.
So they didn’t look like Canaanites; they didn’t blend in.
And as soon as they opened their mouth, people would say:
“You’re not from around here, are you?
You don’t speak the Canaanite language.”
So no wonder they were discovered.
They had to get off the street.
They had to get out of sight.
And you wonder if Jehovah directed them to Rahab.
You wonder if Jehovah saw something in Rahab,
something in her heart that he could work with.
Or do you believe that it was a coincidence
that the spies were led to the only family in Jericho
that was worth saving?
It could be that Jehovah was involved with that.
Well, Rahab decides
that she’s going to hide the spies, but she has a condition.
And if you’d like to turn to Joshua chapter 2,
we’ll see what that condition was.
I’ll give you a moment.
We’re going to read Joshua 2:13.
This is Rahab.
Now, we don’t know how she communicated with them
—must have been a lot of sign language.
We heard about sign language a minute ago.
There must have been a lot of sign language going on
because the Canaanite language wasn’t quite like Hebrew, you know.
But anyway, somehow they got the point across.
And here’s what she says in verse 13:
“You must spare the lives
“of my father and mother,
“my brothers and sisters,
“and all who belong to them,
and you must save us from death.”
What’s she asking for?
She’s asking for an exception.
There’s a rule:
You must not make any covenant with them;
you must not show them any favor.
And she is asking for an exception —and quite a broad exception.
She is asking not just for her own life
but for the lives of all of her family members as well.
Some might have thought that she was pushing it.
But she asked for that.
And the spies showed favor to Rahab.
They made an exception.
And they promised that when the time came,
Rahab and her family would be spared.
The Bible doesn’t criticize the spies for making that exception.
So it may be that Jehovah had something to do with it.
Maybe Jehovah moved the spies in that direction.
Maybe Jehovah saw something in Rahab that he wanted to save.
Now, later on, Joshua and the elders
didn’t follow instructions,
and they made a covenant with the Gibeonites.
The Bible does mention that,
but it doesn’t mention this when it comes to the spies here.
They made the exception.
And we do know that Jehovah agreed with that exception.
How do we know that?
Because when he made the walls of Jericho fall,
he preserved the section of the wall
where Rahab’s family lived.
Jehovah agreed to an exception
to his perfect rule.
Now, you know where I’m going with this.
We need rules.
And most of the time, a rule will satisfy our needs.
But in a few cases,
it only makes sense to make an exception to the rule.
I’m reminded of the time not too long ago
when the Bethel family moved out of Brooklyn.
Now, there were a lot of Bethelites in the congregations
who were elders and ministerial servants.
And so a massive reorganization of congregations
was necessary in New York City.
And the elders and the circuit overseers
had to make sure that each congregation
had a balanced number of elders, ministerial servants, and publishers.
And so publishers were assigned to various congregations.
Can you imagine hundreds of thousands of assignments that had to be made?
And so there was a rule, and it was a pretty good rule,
and the rule was: “Go where you’re assigned.
“We don’t have time to consider the personal feelings
“about every publisher in New York City,
so please go where you’re assigned.”
That was the rule.
Now, there were two sisters (single sisters)
who were assigned to a congregation.
They didn’t have a car,
and you couldn’t reach the congregation they were assigned to
by public transportation.
So they were going to have to walk to the Kingdom Hall,
and the area where the Kingdom Hall was located
was very dangerous.
Their safety would have been involved.
Well, you had a rule to go where you were assigned,
but the circuit overseer lovingly made an exception.
So the point is, we do need rules.
And most of the time, our rules, even our imperfect rules,
will serve most of the brothers.
But let’s use common sense.
And there are times when we have to consider an exception.
Now, can you think of anyone who is grateful
that Jehovah made an exception for Rahab
and that she didn’t die in Jericho?
Can you think of someone?
He was mentioned in this program.
It’s Boaz, the husband of Ruth.
Rahab was his mother.
And think of this:
If Rahab had died in Jericho,
would there ever have been a David?
Let’s go on.
Jehovah directed that seven nations in Canaan
were to be eliminated, and the Gibeonites were among them.
But they had a plan.
They pretended to be from a far-off nation
that wasn’t slated for destruction.
And so the elders, not consulting Jehovah,
made a vow that the Gibeonites would be spared.
They made a covenant with the Gibeonites.
Well, it wasn’t long, but what the Israelites realized
is they’d been tricked.
But even though their oath had been obtained under false pretenses,
they agreed to keep their word.
But it’s what happens next that’s interesting.
Five kings of the Amorites find out
that the Israelites and the Gibeonites have made a covenant,
and they are furious.
And so they are determined to kill all the Gibeonites,
which was really what Jehovah had intended in the first place.
What did Jehovah do?
He could have said: ‘Well, that solves your problem.
‘You promised the Gibeonites that you wouldn’t put them to death,
so you can sit back and let the Amorites do the job.’
But what did Jehovah do?
Joshua 10:8.
Now, remember, he had had a rule.
He’d had a rule that everyone was to be destroyed.
Joshua 10:8:
“Jehovah then said to Joshua:
“‘Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over to you.
Not one of them will be able to stand against you.’”
Imagine the humility.
Jehovah helps the Israelites to keep a promise
that they had no business making.
That is humility.
Well, let’s talk about Jesus’ apostles.
We can really learn humility from them as well.
Now, we often talk about the disputes they had,
but mostly that was before Pentecost.
When you think about it, after Pentecost was a different story.
What do we find out about the apostles after Pentecost?
Well, they weren’t interested in taking credit for things,
and they weren’t searching for the limelight.
They were really very self-effacing apostles.
Matthew wrote the first inspired book
—the first inspired history of Jesus Christ.
Do we see Matthew’s picture on every other page?
Matthew giving a public talk?
Matthew performing a miracle?
Matthew shepherding?
No, his name is only mentioned twice in the whole Gospel,
and both times
he describes himself as a tax collector
—not a very flattering portrayal.
And what about the apostle John?
The name John appears 23 times
in his Gospel,
but it never refers to the apostle John.
It almost always refers to John the Baptist.
When the apostles and older men met to consider the matter of circumcision,
was that an important meeting?
Would you agree that that was a landmark meeting?
The apostles and older men are there.
Who presided?
Who of the 12 was jockeying for position?
James, the brother of Jesus, wasn’t even an apostle.
He’s the one who presided.
And then later on when the decision was made,
who announced the decision?
Again, James.
You don’t find Peter or John saying:
“Well, you know, this is a pretty important decision.
We think that one of us should announce it.”
The apostles had learned their lesson.
Well, remember that when the circuit overseer visits.
You may have heavy responsibilities at Bethel,
but when he visits a congregation, he’s in charge that week.
Follow his direction.
Don’t be critical of the circuit overseer,
and don’t be afraid to let him know how much you appreciate his service.
And you know, our Bethel families here in the United States
are such a wonderful example of that.
When the circuit overseers first visit a Bethel congregation,
they’re a little bit nervous for about ten minutes.
But the Bethel family shows
that they appreciate the counsel so much,
and sometimes they talk about the circuit overseer’s counsel
for weeks after his visit.
They really deeply appreciate the visit of the circuit overseer,
and they respect that man.
And we know that you’re going to do the same.
Humble people are happy to contribute to the Kingdom work in any way they can,
just so they can contribute.
They’re not hung up on privileges.
They’re not hung up on prestige or on position.
They don’t seek the limelight.
And in this regard, we’re going to talk a little bit about the apostle Paul.
Now, Brother Lippold mentioned in his talk
that Paul was not a man to boast, and that’s quite true.
Actually, Paul was a very humble man.
Now, think about this: At the time Paul was converted,
about 34 C.E.,
Jesus told Ananias
that Paul was going to have a wonderful privilege.
Let’s read about it in Acts chapter 9.
Acts 9:15
—Acts 9:15 (and this is Jesus to Ananias):
“But the Lord said to him: ‘Go! because this man
“‘is a chosen vessel to me
“‘to bear my name to the nations
as well as to kings and the sons of Israel.’”
“A chosen vessel.”
How about that!
How did Paul react?
Did he let that go to his head?
Did he immediately go up to Jerusalem
and volunteer to be on the governing body, saying,
“Well, now that I’m anointed, I can be on the governing body”?
No.
He stayed where he was in Damascus,
and he kept preaching the good news.
Now, in 36 C.E., he did go up to world headquarters in Jerusalem.
And how did he react?
Did he say: “Here I am, the chosen vessel.
I’m here to help you run the place”?
He stayed with the apostle Peter for a couple of weeks.
Apparently, Peter had moved to Jerusalem.
But he kept preaching.
He just put his head to the ground, and he kept preaching the good news
until one day Jesus appeared to him
when Paul was in the temple.
And he told Paul that he had to leave Jerusalem immediately
because the Jews were out to kill him.
How did Paul react?
Did he say: “But the governing body is going to need me.
“If I leave, how will they manage without me?
They need my wisdom”?
Paul obeyed theocratic direction,
and he left.
He accepted a new assignment
—Tarsus.
Tarsus?
What kind of assignment is that for a chosen vessel?
It was out in the boondocks.
It was 500 miles (800 km) from the governing body in Jerusalem.
How would the governing body get to know his wonderful qualities
if he was 500 miles (800 km) from Jerusalem?
Paul went to Tarsus, and he kept preaching.
We don’t even know if there was a congregation of Tarsus
when Paul got there.
But Paul kept preaching.
I was thinking of the lovely interview we just heard
where the brother talked about how he eventually ended up in the circuit work.
But before that time, Jehovah gave him a little training.
And perhaps that’s what happened to the apostle Paul.
Do you know that Paul may have remained in Tarsus
for eight years preaching?
And then Barnabas came along
11 years after Paul’s conversion.
Barnabas came along and invited him to Antioch.
And from that time on, Paul started to have privileges.
And five years after that,
Paul wrote his first inspired letter
that we cherish to this day.
Paul worked hard all his life.
He did more than any of the 12 apostles,
but he was never upset that he wasn’t counted among them.
Paul appreciated the privileges he had.
He viewed them as undeserved kindness.
And we know that you brothers and sisters are going to do the same.
You’re invited to conduct a meeting for field service
—treasure the privilege.
Any privilege that you receive,
treasure it as an expression of love from Jehovah.
Well, when you go to your assignments,
many situations are going to test your humility.
And I know that you brothers and sisters are going to pass the test.
The branch asks you to work on a project,
and deep down you don’t quite agree with it.
Deep down, you really wonder if it’s going to work,
and you wonder if it’s not going to be a waste of your time.
But you’re not going to put it on the back burner and say,
“Well, I’ll get to it someday if I get time.”
You’re not going to do that.
You’re going to put heart and soul into the project.
You’re going to pray to Jehovah to bless the project,
the project that you didn’t quite agree with.
Or if you’re asked to make a recommendation
and you favor one option over another,
humility is going to move you to present all of the options,
all of the pros and cons equally.
You’re not going to slant things, thinking:
‘Well, you know, I’m going to have to help these brothers to make this decision.
‘So I’ll put a really heavy weight on the pros,
and I’m going to make it really light on the cons.’
Don’t do that.
I know that you’re going to present everything honestly,
and you’re going to recognize that it’s the holy spirit
that helps brothers to make decisions.
Trust the spirit to move the brothers to do the right thing.
Suppose you sisters are working on a team
or you brothers are working on a body of elders.
I know that not even in your heart of hearts
are you going to think that you have the best judgment on the team
and that, well, you can listen politely to the expressions of others
but, really, yours is the only sensible conclusion,
and you hope that the brothers and sisters are going to go along with you.
You’re not going to think that, because nobody is right all the time.
Jehovah’s spirit can work on any member of the team.
Don’t get discouraged if every suggestion you make in a meeting
gets shot down.
It happens to the best of us.
And there will be other meetings,
and hopefully some of them will go better for you.
Don’t get discouraged, and don’t decide: “Well, I’m not going to say anything anymore.
I’m not going to contribute anymore.”
Be humble and recognize that at times
we may make suggestions that don’t make very much sense.
I certainly appreciate the kind way the Governing Body deals with me
with some of my lamebrained suggestions.
In your comments and your assignments on the midweek meeting,
use the knowledge you’ve gained at Gilead to build up.
And I know you won’t proofread the meetings.
‘I don’t think that was a good illustration.
‘That scripture wasn’t applied right.
That isn’t the right word.’
You won’t do that.
Just sit back, relax, and enjoy the meetings.
Take in the spiritual food.
Rejoice in whatever the brothers and sisters have prepared for you.
Well, I haven’t told you anything you don’t already know.
You’re all humble people.
These are just reminders that all of us need.
All of us are humble most of the time.
We pray for the day when we’ll be humble all of the time.
And in the meantime, let’s work on it, you and I.
Let’s work on it together.
Let’s follow the course of humility.
If we do, we’ll continue
to be used by Jehovah.
We love you.
May Jehovah bless you richly.
