ko.text: 데이비드 스플레인 형제의 연설을 들어 보겠습니다.
그런데 생각해 보면, 겸손을 나타내는 면에서 어떤 때는 잘하다가도
또 어떤 때는 그렇지 않은 경우도 있지 않습니까?
예를 들어, 평일 집회 때 연설을 잘하거나
파수대 연구 때 좋은 해설을 해서 누군가에게 칭찬을 들으면,
그 모든 것이 여호와와 우리가 받은 훈련 덕분이라고 생각합니다.
하지만 어떤 경우에는 잘 안 될 때도 있습니다.
우리의 겸손이 시험을 받는 상황이 때때로 생기는 것이죠.
베델에서는 우리 모두 서로 밀접하게 연합해서 함께 일합니다.
학생 여러분 가운데는 팀으로 일하는 자매들이 있고,
형제들 모두는 회중이나 베델에서 또는 둘 다에서 책임을 가지고 있습니다.
이 모든 상황에서 필요한 것은 겸손입니다.
여호와 하느님과 예수 그리스도의 사도들이 나타낸 겸손을 통해
무엇을 배울 수 있는지 생각해 보겠습니다.
범위를 좀 좁혀서 몇 가지 부면만 살펴보겠습니다.
첫 번째 점이 좀 의외라고 생각되실 수 있는데요.
겸손에는 다른 사람에게 자비와 동정심을 나타내는 것이 관련된다는 점을
다른 사람에게 자비와 동정심을 나타낸다는 것이 포함되죠.
다시 말하면 필요한 경우에는 예외를 허용하는 것입니다.
성경에서 그분이 다시 생각해 보신 예를 여러 번 보지 않으셨습니까?
여호와의 법칙은 완벽하지만 때때로 그분은 다시 생각해 보십니다.
예를 들어, 이스라엘 백성은 약속의 땅을 정복할 준비를 하고 있었습니다.
여호와께서는 그들에게 다음과 같은 아주 분명한 법을 주셨습니다.
“그들과 계약을 맺어서도 안 되고 그들에게 호의를 베풀어서도 안 된다.”
계약을 맺어서도, 호의를 베풀어서도 안 됐죠.
여호수아는 그 도시로 두 정탐꾼을 보냈고
보통 라합의 믿음에 대해 이야기를 많이 하는데,
두 정탐꾼의 믿음에 대해서는 어떻게 생각하십니까?
그 도시로 가기 위해 그들이 나타냈을 믿음에 대해 생각해 보셨습니까?
그들이 40살이 안 되었다면 광야에서 태어난 것입니다.
그들은 실제로 얼마나 집에 들어가 봤을까요?
기껏해야 요르단강 동편에서 몇 사람 정도였겠죠.
그들이 도시에 들어가자마자 무슨 일이 있었습니까?
우선 그들은 가나안 복장을 하고 있지 않았죠.
당시에는 인터넷으로 옷을 주문할 수도 없었으니까요.
아마도 그들은 광야에서 죽은 아버지에게서 물려받은
가나안 사람처럼 보이지 않았고 금방 눈에 띄었습니다.
그리고 그들이 입을 열자마자 사람들은 “여기 말을 하지 않네요.
가나안 사람이 아니군요” 라고 했을 겁니다.
여호와께서는 라합의 마음속에서 뭔가 좋은 것을 보신 걸까요?
정탐꾼들이 예리코에서 여호와께 믿음을 둘 만한
네, 라합은 정탐꾼들을 숨겨 주기로 했지만 조건이 있었습니다.
가나안 말과 히브리 말이 많이 달라서
몸짓을 많이 사용했겠지만 어쨌든 서로의 말뜻을 이해했을 겁니다.
그들에게 속한 모든 자를 살려 주셔야 하며,
예외를 허용해 줄 것을 요구한 겁니다.
‘그들과 계약을 맺어서도 안 되고 그들에게 호의를 베풀어서도 안 된다.’
라합은 상당히 큰 예외를 요구한 겁니다.
모든 가족의 생명을 보존해 줄 것을 요구한 겁니다.
라합과 그의 가족이 죽지 않을 것이라고 약속했습니다.
정탐꾼들이 예외를 허용한 것에 대해 성경은 나쁘게 말하지 않죠.
라합에 대해서 뭔가 좋은 것을 보시고 살려 주기를 원하셨을 수 있죠.
기브온 사람들과 계약을 맺어 지침을 따르지 않았을 때,
지금 이 두 정탐꾼들과 관련해서는 그런 언급이 없습니다.
그처럼 예외를 허용한 것에 대해 여호와께서 동의하셨습니다.
그분이 라합의 가족이 살던 부분의 성벽은 보존하셨기 때문입니다.
여호와께서는 자신의 완벽한 규정에 예외를 허용하신 것입니다.
그리고 대부분 규칙은 우리의 상황에 잘 맞죠.
하지만 때로는 규칙에 예외를 적용해야만 하는 경우가 있습니다.
저는 베델 가족이 브루클린에서 이사를 나오던 때가 생각나는데요.
많은 베델 성원들이 인근 회중에서 장로와 봉사의 종으로 섬기고 있었습니다.
그래서 대대적인 조정이 뉴욕시에 있는 회중들에 필요했습니다.

여러분이 받게 될 수 있는 특권 때문에 자기만족에 빠지지 마십시오.
여러분과 우리를 얼마나 친절하게 대해 주셨는지를 기억하면서
방패와 그 밖의 모든 중요한 갑주를 잘 관리하는 부지런한 군인이 되십시오.
여러분이 길르앗 학교에서 배운 내용에 계속 초점을 맞춘다면
늘 “믿음을 위해 훌륭한 싸움을 싸울” 준비를 갖추게 될 것입니다.
앞서도 말했지만 우리는 여러분이 그렇게 할 것이라고 확신합니다.
여호와와 그분의 아들의 축복이 함께하기를 바랍니다.

en.text: Well, at this time, we have the pleasure
to hear from another member of the Governing Body, Brother David Splane,
and the title of his talk is
“Follow the Course of Humility.”
All of you are humble people.
If you weren’t, you would never have been invited to Gilead.
Have you ever noticed, though, that where humility is concerned,
we do well in some situations
and not so well in others?
For example, if someone commends us
for a good job on a talk in the midweek meeting
or perhaps a comment on the Watchtower  Study,
we give all credit to Jehovah and to the training we’ve received,
and that’s good.
But in other situations,
we might get into trouble.
In other situations,
our humility might be put to the test.
Now, at Bethel, as has been mentioned
on this program already,
we all work with people;
we all work closely with others.
Now, some of you sisters work on a team; you work with others.
And you brothers all have responsibilities
in the congregation or at Bethel or perhaps both.
But in all situations, humility is needed.
So I thought that this morning
we might consider what we can learn about humility
from Jehovah God
and from the apostles of Jesus Christ.
Now, humility is a broad term,
so let’s narrow it down a little bit.
Let’s consider a couple of aspects of humility,
and the first one I’m going to mention might surprise you.
Insight on the Scriptures tells us that humility includes
the ability to show mercy
and compassion to others
—the ability to show mercy
and compassion to others—
the ability to make exceptions where that is warranted.
Well, that’s Jehovah, isn’t it?
Jehovah isn’t rigid.
Jehovah knows when to make exceptions.
How often did you read in the Bible as you went through
that Jehovah reconsidered?
Jehovah makes perfect rules,
and yet at times he reconsiders.
Now let’s illustrate:
The Israelites are getting ready to conquer the Promised Land.
And the first up is the city of Jericho.
Now, there’s a rule
—a rule of engagement— and it’s very clear.
Jehovah says:
“You must not make any covenant with them
nor show them any favor.”
No covenant, no favor —that’s the rule.
It’s a perfect rule because it’s Jehovah’s rule.
Joshua sent two spies into the city,
and they went to the home of a prostitute named Rahab.
Now, wait a minute;
let’s think about that.
Pretty easy to say, isn’t it?
Joshua sent two spies into the city.
They went into a house of a prostitute named Rahab.
Now, we often think about the faith of Rahab.
But what about the faith of those two spies?
Can you imagine the faith that it took for those men
(the Bible says they were young men) to go into that city?
Now, if they were under 40 years of age,
they were born in the wilderness.
How many cities had they ever seen?
Had they ever seen a city before?
How many actual houses had they entered?
How many foreigners had they ever met?
Maybe not very many—maybe a couple on the other side of the Jordan,
but not very many.
So now, as soon as they enter the city, what happens?
Someone calls the police.
They’re recognized right away.
And no wonder!
First of all, they weren’t dressed like Canaanites.
You couldn’t order your clothes from Amazon in those days, you know.
They were dressed like Israelites.
They probably had on 40-year-old hand-me-downs
from their fathers who had died in the desert.
So they didn’t look like Canaanites; they didn’t blend in.
And as soon as they opened their mouth, people would say:
“You’re not from around here, are you?
You don’t speak the Canaanite language.”
So no wonder they were discovered.
They had to get off the street.
They had to get out of sight.
And you wonder if Jehovah directed them to Rahab.
You wonder if Jehovah saw something in Rahab,
something in her heart that he could work with.
Or do you believe that it was a coincidence
that the spies were led to the only family in Jericho
that was worth saving?
It could be that Jehovah was involved with that.
Well, Rahab decides
that she’s going to hide the spies, but she has a condition.
And if you’d like to turn to Joshua chapter 2,
we’ll see what that condition was.
I’ll give you a moment.
We’re going to read Joshua 2:13.
This is Rahab.
Now, we don’t know how she communicated with them
—must have been a lot of sign language.
We heard about sign language a minute ago.
There must have been a lot of sign language going on
because the Canaanite language wasn’t quite like Hebrew, you know.
But anyway, somehow they got the point across.
And here’s what she says in verse 13:
“You must spare the lives
“of my father and mother,
“my brothers and sisters,
“and all who belong to them,
and you must save us from death.”
What’s she asking for?
She’s asking for an exception.
There’s a rule:
You must not make any covenant with them;
you must not show them any favor.
And she is asking for an exception —and quite a broad exception.
She is asking not just for her own life
but for the lives of all of her family members as well.
Some might have thought that she was pushing it.
But she asked for that.
And the spies showed favor to Rahab.
They made an exception.
And they promised that when the time came,
Rahab and her family would be spared.
The Bible doesn’t criticize the spies for making that exception.
So it may be that Jehovah had something to do with it.
Maybe Jehovah moved the spies in that direction.
Maybe Jehovah saw something in Rahab that he wanted to save.
Now, later on, Joshua and the elders
didn’t follow instructions,
and they made a covenant with the Gibeonites.
The Bible does mention that,
but it doesn’t mention this when it comes to the spies here.
They made the exception.
And we do know that Jehovah agreed with that exception.
How do we know that?
Because when he made the walls of Jericho fall,
he preserved the section of the wall
where Rahab’s family lived.
Jehovah agreed to an exception
to his perfect rule.
Now, you know where I’m going with this.
We need rules.
And most of the time, a rule will satisfy our needs.
But in a few cases,
it only makes sense to make an exception to the rule.
I’m reminded of the time not too long ago
when the Bethel family moved out of Brooklyn.
Now, there were a lot of Bethelites in the congregations
who were elders and ministerial servants.
And so a massive reorganization of congregations
was necessary in New York City.
And the elders and the circuit overseers
had to make sure that each congregation
had a balanced number of elders, ministerial servants, and publishers.
And so publishers were assigned to various congregations.
Can you imagine hundreds of thousands of assignments that had to be made?
And so there was a rule, and it was a pretty good rule,
and the rule was: “Go where you’re assigned.
“We don’t have time to consider the personal feelings
“about every publisher in New York City,
so please go where you’re assigned.”
That was the rule.
Now, there were two sisters (single sisters)
who were assigned to a congregation.
They didn’t have a car,
and you couldn’t reach the congregation they were assigned to
by public transportation.
So they were going to have to walk to the Kingdom Hall,
and the area where the Kingdom Hall was located
was very dangerous.
Their safety would have been involved.
Well, you had a rule to go where you were assigned,
but the circuit overseer lovingly made an exception.
So the point is, we do need rules.
And most of the time, our rules, even our imperfect rules,
will serve most of the brothers.
But let’s use common sense.
And there are times when we have to consider an exception.
Now, can you think of anyone who is grateful
that Jehovah made an exception for Rahab
and that she didn’t die in Jericho?
Can you think of someone?
He was mentioned in this program.
It’s Boaz, the husband of Ruth.
Rahab was his mother.
And think of this:
If Rahab had died in Jericho,
would there ever have been a David?
Let’s go on.
Jehovah directed that seven nations in Canaan
were to be eliminated, and the Gibeonites were among them.
But they had a plan.
They pretended to be from a far-off nation
that wasn’t slated for destruction.
And so the elders, not consulting Jehovah,
made a vow that the Gibeonites would be spared.
They made a covenant with the Gibeonites.
Well, it wasn’t long, but what the Israelites realized
is they’d been tricked.
But even though their oath had been obtained under false pretenses,
they agreed to keep their word.
But it’s what happens next that’s interesting.
Five kings of the Amorites find out
that the Israelites and the Gibeonites have made a covenant,
and they are furious.
And so they are determined to kill all the Gibeonites,
which was really what Jehovah had intended in the first place.
What did Jehovah do?
He could have said: ‘Well, that solves your problem.
‘You promised the Gibeonites that you wouldn’t put them to death,
so you can sit back and let the Amorites do the job.’
But what did Jehovah do?
Joshua 10:8.
Now, remember, he had had a rule.
He’d had a rule that everyone was to be destroyed.
Joshua 10:8:
“Jehovah then said to Joshua:
“‘Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over to you.
Not one of them will be able to stand against you.’”
Imagine the humility.
Jehovah helps the Israelites to keep a promise
that they had no business making.
That is humility.
Well, let’s talk about Jesus’ apostles.
We can really learn humility from them as well.
Now, we often talk about the disputes they had,
but mostly that was before Pentecost.
When you think about it, after Pentecost was a different story.
What do we find out about the apostles after Pentecost?
Well, they weren’t interested in taking credit for things,
and they weren’t searching for the limelight.
They were really very self-effacing apostles.
Matthew wrote the first inspired book
—the first inspired history of Jesus Christ.
Do we see Matthew’s picture on every other page?
Matthew giving a public talk?
Matthew performing a miracle?
Matthew shepherding?
No, his name is only mentioned twice in the whole Gospel,
and both times
he describes himself as a tax collector
—not a very flattering portrayal.
And what about the apostle John?
The name John appears 23 times
in his Gospel,
but it never refers to the apostle John.
It almost always refers to John the Baptist.
When the apostles and older men met to consider the matter of circumcision,
was that an important meeting?
Would you agree that that was a landmark meeting?
The apostles and older men are there.
Who presided?
Who of the 12 was jockeying for position?
James, the brother of Jesus, wasn’t even an apostle.
He’s the one who presided.
And then later on when the decision was made,
who announced the decision?
Again, James.
You don’t find Peter or John saying:
“Well, you know, this is a pretty important decision.
We think that one of us should announce it.”
The apostles had learned their lesson.
Well, remember that when the circuit overseer visits.
You may have heavy responsibilities at Bethel,
but when he visits a congregation, he’s in charge that week.
Follow his direction.
Don’t be critical of the circuit overseer,
and don’t be afraid to let him know how much you appreciate his service.
And you know, our Bethel families here in the United States
are such a wonderful example of that.
When the circuit overseers first visit a Bethel congregation,
they’re a little bit nervous for about ten minutes.
But the Bethel family shows
that they appreciate the counsel so much,
and sometimes they talk about the circuit overseer’s counsel
for weeks after his visit.
They really deeply appreciate the visit of the circuit overseer,
and they respect that man.
And we know that you’re going to do the same.
Humble people are happy to contribute to the Kingdom work in any way they can,
just so they can contribute.
They’re not hung up on privileges.
They’re not hung up on prestige or on position.
They don’t seek the limelight.
And in this regard, we’re going to talk a little bit about the apostle Paul.
Now, Brother Lippold mentioned in his talk
that Paul was not a man to boast, and that’s quite true.
Actually, Paul was a very humble man.
Now, think about this: At the time Paul was converted,
about 34 C.E.,
Jesus told Ananias
that Paul was going to have a wonderful privilege.
Let’s read about it in Acts chapter 9.
Acts 9:15
—Acts 9:15 (and this is Jesus to Ananias):
“But the Lord said to him: ‘Go! because this man
“‘is a chosen vessel to me
“‘to bear my name to the nations
as well as to kings and the sons of Israel.’”
“A chosen vessel.”
How about that!
How did Paul react?
Did he let that go to his head?
Did he immediately go up to Jerusalem
and volunteer to be on the governing body, saying,
“Well, now that I’m anointed, I can be on the governing body”?
No.
He stayed where he was in Damascus,
and he kept preaching the good news.
Now, in 36 C.E., he did go up to world headquarters in Jerusalem.
And how did he react?
Did he say: “Here I am, the chosen vessel.
I’m here to help you run the place”?
He stayed with the apostle Peter for a couple of weeks.
Apparently, Peter had moved to Jerusalem.
But he kept preaching.
He just put his head to the ground, and he kept preaching the good news
until one day Jesus appeared to him
when Paul was in the temple.
And he told Paul that he had to leave Jerusalem immediately
because the Jews were out to kill him.
How did Paul react?
Did he say: “But the governing body is going to need me.
“If I leave, how will they manage without me?
They need my wisdom”?
Paul obeyed theocratic direction,
and he left.
He accepted a new assignment
—Tarsus.
Tarsus?
What kind of assignment is that for a chosen vessel?
It was out in the boondocks.
It was 500 miles (800 km) from the governing body in Jerusalem.
How would the governing body get to know his wonderful qualities
if he was 500 miles (800 km) from Jerusalem?
Paul went to Tarsus, and he kept preaching.
We don’t even know if there was a congregation of Tarsus
when Paul got there.
But Paul kept preaching.
I was thinking of the lovely interview we just heard
where the brother talked about how he eventually ended up in the circuit work.
But before that time, Jehovah gave him a little training.
And perhaps that’s what happened to the apostle Paul.
Do you know that Paul may have remained in Tarsus
for eight years preaching?
And then Barnabas came along
11 years after Paul’s conversion.
Barnabas came along and invited him to Antioch.
And from that time on, Paul started to have privileges.
And five years after that,
Paul wrote his first inspired letter
that we cherish to this day.
Paul worked hard all his life.
He did more than any of the 12 apostles,
but he was never upset that he wasn’t counted among them.
Paul appreciated the privileges he had.
He viewed them as undeserved kindness.
And we know that you brothers and sisters are going to do the same.
You’re invited to conduct a meeting for field service
—treasure the privilege.
Any privilege that you receive,
treasure it as an expression of love from Jehovah.
Well, when you go to your assignments,
many situations are going to test your humility.
And I know that you brothers and sisters are going to pass the test.
The branch asks you to work on a project,
and deep down you don’t quite agree with it.
Deep down, you really wonder if it’s going to work,
and you wonder if it’s not going to be a waste of your time.
But you’re not going to put it on the back burner and say,
“Well, I’ll get to it someday if I get time.”
You’re not going to do that.
You’re going to put heart and soul into the project.
You’re going to pray to Jehovah to bless the project,
the project that you didn’t quite agree with.
Or if you’re asked to make a recommendation
and you favor one option over another,
humility is going to move you to present all of the options,
all of the pros and cons equally.
You’re not going to slant things, thinking:
‘Well, you know, I’m going to have to help these brothers to make this decision.
‘So I’ll put a really heavy weight on the pros,
and I’m going to make it really light on the cons.’
Don’t do that.
I know that you’re going to present everything honestly,
and you’re going to recognize that it’s the holy spirit
that helps brothers to make decisions.
Trust the spirit to move the brothers to do the right thing.
Suppose you sisters are working on a team
or you brothers are working on a body of elders.
I know that not even in your heart of hearts
are you going to think that you have the best judgment on the team
and that, well, you can listen politely to the expressions of others
but, really, yours is the only sensible conclusion,
and you hope that the brothers and sisters are going to go along with you.
You’re not going to think that, because nobody is right all the time.
Jehovah’s spirit can work on any member of the team.
Don’t get discouraged if every suggestion you make in a meeting
gets shot down.
It happens to the best of us.
And there will be other meetings,
and hopefully some of them will go better for you.
Don’t get discouraged, and don’t decide: “Well, I’m not going to say anything anymore.
I’m not going to contribute anymore.”
Be humble and recognize that at times
we may make suggestions that don’t make very much sense.
I certainly appreciate the kind way the Governing Body deals with me
with some of my lamebrained suggestions.
In your comments and your assignments on the midweek meeting,
use the knowledge you’ve gained at Gilead to build up.
And I know you won’t proofread the meetings.
‘I don’t think that was a good illustration.
‘That scripture wasn’t applied right.
That isn’t the right word.’
You won’t do that.
Just sit back, relax, and enjoy the meetings.
Take in the spiritual food.
Rejoice in whatever the brothers and sisters have prepared for you.
Well, I haven’t told you anything you don’t already know.
You’re all humble people.
These are just reminders that all of us need.
All of us are humble most of the time.
We pray for the day when we’ll be humble all of the time.
And in the meantime, let’s work on it, you and I.
Let’s work on it together.
Let’s follow the course of humility.
If we do, we’ll continue
to be used by Jehovah.
We love you.
May Jehovah bless you richly.
Well, thank you very much, Brother Splane,
for the excellent Scriptural examples in that talk
(including, above all, Jehovah’s example)
and for the reminders that humble people follow rules
and that humble people, though, are reasonable
—beautiful reminders and examples through that talk.
Well, now for the presentation of the diplomas.
And I will be assisted in this
by Brother William Malenfant, a helper to the Teaching Committee.
First of all, we have Brother and Sister Cheung,
and they will return to the Canada branch.
And here we have Brother and Sister Ciupek.
They’ll return to the Central Europe branch.
Brother Ciupek has been appointed to serve on the Branch Committee.
And we have Brother and Sister De Chavigny.
They will return to the France branch.
Brother and Sister Dolev will return to the Bulgaria branch.
And Brother and Sister Eisa have been assigned
to world headquarters at Warwick,
where Brother Eisa will work with Hospital Information Services.
Brother and Sister Grim have been assigned to the Ghana branch.
Brother Grim has been appointed to serve on the Branch Committee.
Brother Kitts has been assigned to the Central Europe branch,
where he will work under the oversight
of World Headquarters Office of Public Information.
Brother N’Gwete will return to the Suriname branch.
Brother and Sister Peltonen have been assigned
to the Central Europe branch.
Brother Peltonen will work under the oversight
of World Headquarters Office of Public Information.
Brother Velev will return to the Bulgaria branch.
Brother Vita has been assigned to the Albania branch.
Brother and Sister Weaver will return to the Spain branch.
Brother Weaver has been appointed to serve on the Branch Committee.
OK. Well, that was wonderful to share in.
Now they’re graduates.
So at this time, we’re pleased to present
the graduates of the 151st class of Gilead.
There’s a lot of love here today.
That’s wonderful.
Well, we have a letter to be presented
by one of the now graduates of the 151st class.
Brother Davide Vita
from Italy and going to Albania will read that now at this time.
“To the Governing Body and Bethel family.
“Dear Brothers: For the past five months,
“we have traveled through the Bible from the first page to the last.
“We experienced the heat of the Sinai
“and found ourselves in the depths of the Red Sea,
“in the narrow alleys of Jerusalem,
“and high up on Mount Hermon.
“We met the prophets, visited the temple,
“saw the awesome celestial chariot,
“and enjoyed the precious company of Jesus and the apostles.
“What is the result of our journey?
“The very same that resulted for Job
“after he encountered his God —great astonishment!
“Although he recognized that he would only be able to understand
“‘just the fringes of his ways,’
“it was enough to make him marvel at Jehovah.
“‘Now I know that you are able to do all things.’
“At the same time, the experience humbled him
“so that he ‘put [his] hand over [his] mouth.’
“That is how we feel today.
“Gilead leaves us in its wake,
“filled with awe, humility, and gratitude.
“Studying the Bible is studying about Jehovah himself.
“And what we have learned has impressed on our hearts
“the depth of Jehovah’s love for each one of his servants.
“We saw this love not only in numerous Bible accounts
“but in those who imitate him and his Son, Jesus
“—the Governing Body, our guest instructors,
“our Gilead instructors, and the Bethel family
“here at Patterson and the other complexes.
“Your example is the living answer
“to the question of how to define Christian love.
“We express our heartfelt thanks to you, the Governing Body,
“and all those who made this unforgettable experience possible.
“We know that our divine education is not our possession alone.
“We received it to share it.
“The end of Gilead School for our class is the close of a chapter.
“And we are determined to write the next chapter of our story
“by showing the same love
“and personal interest we have experienced.
“It is our prayer that as we apply what we have been taught,
“we inspire others and make Jehovah’s heart rejoice.
“As the psalmist expressed at Psalm 106:48:
“‘May Jehovah . . . be praised throughout all eternity. . . . Praise Jah!’
Your brothers and sisters, the 151st class of Gilead.”
Thank you for that beautiful letter.
And those heartfelt expressions are something we will remember too.
Well, in closing, we just have a few things to say to you now.
You are graduates
—graduates of the 151st class of Gilead.
I used the word “students” a few times earlier on
because you didn’t have a diploma in hand yet.
Now you have them.
And that’s just such an encouraging and wonderful thing to see.
You may know that back in 2011,
the Governing Body adjusted the objective
of Gilead School training a bit.
Now the training is even more focused
on strengthening and stabilizing
the field and branch organization.
Since that time, a good number of graduates
have been appointed to a Branch or a Country Committee.
And so with Jehovah’s blessing, the training is working.
But not all graduates from Gilead
are brothers who may someday receive such responsibilities.
We have many sisters in each class too, don’t we?
So then, how might the goal
of strengthening and stabilizing the field and branch organization
be reached through each one of you
graduating brothers and sisters?
Well, the goal is reached when others can look at what you do and say
and they see a man or woman of strong faith.
Just as Paul wrote at 1 Thessalonians 1:8,
where he said in part:
“Not only has the word of [God] sounded out from you . . .
“but your faith in God
has spread abroad in every place.”
And that’s exactly what happens, isn’t it?
Yes, such examples are priceless.
Your schooling was designed to strengthen your faith,
and we’re confident that it has done just that.
You are ready for what is ahead.
Our faith keeps us strong, though.
And at 1 John 5:4, the apostle John wrote:
“This is the conquest that has conquered the world,
our faith,” right?
With that in mind, for just a few minutes
let’s consider how you can keep your faith strong
when you get to your assignments,
so that you can be that powerful force for good
in strengthening and stabilizing the field and branch organization.
So when you’re settled into your assignments, perhaps with new responsibilities,
remember to remain focused on what is most important,
namely, the doing of God’s will.
What could cause a person to forget this if not careful?
Well, we get into danger if we ever start to feel
like we have achieved everything
that we’ve wanted to achieve as our spiritual goals.
See, if we allow that to happen,
our interest could turn to other things.
We never want to allow that to happen.
We want to remain focused on Jehovah —his work.
It’s always about Jehovah and helping other people.
Never become distracted by losing sight of the need
to keep advancing spiritually day by day.
Never become content with what this empty system of things has to offer.
Remain fixed on Jehovah’s promises and on the doing of his will.
Keep your “large shield of faith” strong.
In Bible times, soldiers repaired their shields between battles.
If a soldier found damage or weakness to his shield,
he diligently made the needed repairs.
In this way, he was always ready to fight the next battle.
He never let down his guard.
We need to keep this up in a spiritual way.
Over time, a brother or sister might lay down his or her shield of faith
and go after things that have no lasting value.
The Devil wants nothing more than to see us neglect our faith,
because that will pull everything down if he can do that.
We show that we’re strengthening our faith in God
when we take time to give attention to our spiritual need.
The basics always count.
The basics always count.
So then be certain to regularly attend Christian meetings
(which we know you’ll do and soon in person—right?),
to zealously speak to others about Jehovah’s name and his Kingdom,
to maintain strong faith by reading God’s Word every day,
and then to apply its counsel prayerfully in all that you do.
Those are the basics that never fail us
and help us to keep our faith strong.
So in summary, don’t take liberties with your spiritual routine
now that you’ve graduated from this wonderful, beautiful school.
Never neglect those basic things.
Never become self-satisfied because of resting
on a privilege that you may come to enjoy.
And finally, keep growing as a godly person
because you remember how kind Jehovah has been to you and to all of us.
Be like the diligent soldier who worked hard
to care for that shield and all of his vital armor.
As you remain focused on what Gilead School has now strengthened you to do,
you will always be ready
to “fight the fine fight of the faith.”
As mentioned earlier, we have confidence that you will do just that.
May Jehovah and his dear Son bless you
—each one of you— for it.

cn.text: 接下来
我们会听到另一位中央长老团成员

title: 제151기 길르앗 졸업식—인사이드 스토리

ko.text: 이제 길르앗 졸업식에서 많은 분들의 사랑을 받고 있는 프로를 즐기시겠습니다.
길르앗 학교 강사인 제임스 코손 형제가 이 프로를 다룰 때
인생에도 높은 음이 있고 낮은 음이 있죠.
충실한 숭배자들의 음악을 여호와께서 마음으로 들으시죠.
그분은 우리가 살면서 달성한 일만이 아니라
우리 삶의 여정 자체를 소중히 여기십니다.
오늘은 151기 길르앗 학생 3명의 이야기를 들어 보겠습니다.
그들은 자신들의 여정을 통해 어떤 노래를 만들었을까요?
첫 번째 손님은 조엘 그림 형제와 에이드리엔 그림 자매입니다.
어릴 때부터 영적 목표가 있었다고 들었는데,
네, 부모님 덕분에 어릴 때부터 여호와를 섬기고 싶었어요.
젊은 독신 파이오니아 자매 5명이 저희 회중을 도우려고 이사 왔어요.
한 자매는 미국 수어를 할 줄 알았는데,
청각 장애인을 위해 성서 연구를 사회하고 집회를 통역했어요.
저도 그 자매한테 수어를 좀 배워서 도울 수 있었죠.
그런데 몇 년 후에 제가 아직 십 대였을 때
그래서 자매가 하던 성서 연구를 제가 도우려고 최선을 다했죠.
하지만 쉽지 않았는데, 그때는 수어 출판물이 없었거든요.
한쪽 무릎엔 「파수대」를 놓고 한쪽 무릎엔 수어 사전을 놓고
네, 그땐 할 수 있는 게 그것밖에 없었죠.
청각 장애인들이 정말 친절하고 참을성 있게 저를 잘 도와주었거든요.
한번은 왕국회관 뒤에서 제 또래 여자애랑 수어로 대화를 나눴어요.
그때 그 애가 수어로 뭔가를 얘기했는데 못 알아듣겠더라고요.
그래서 다시 해 달라고 했는데, 그래도 이해가 안 갔죠.
그래서 그 애는 어떻게든 절 이해시키려고 온갖 방법을 써 봤지만,
전 이해가 안 되고 눈물만 나더라고요.
그래도 포기하지 않았고 전 결국 이해했어요.
그처럼 친절과 참을성을 나타내는 걸 보고 또 보면서 깊은 감동을 받았어요.
그림 형제는 당시 월킬 베델에서 봉사하고 있었고,
두 분은 결혼한 뒤 함께 베델 봉사를 시작했습니다.
나중에 두 분은 수어 회중으로 가기로 결정했는데,
그림 자매는 이미 미국 수어를 할 줄 알았고
고린도 전서 9:22을 전과는 다른 시각으로 보게 되었어요.
고린도 전서 9:22이 언어를 배우는 것과 무슨 관련이 있죠?
그 성구에서 바울은 “모든 부류의 사람에게 모든 것이 되었다”고 했는데요.
사실, 언어를 배우려면 정말 그래야 하죠.
언어란 단지 단어들을 모아서 말만 통하게 하는 게 아닙니다.
언어가 생각하는 방식에 영향을 미치는 건 사실인데,
예를 들어, 두 사람이 대화를 나누고 있는데
그 사이를 지나가야 한다고 생각해 보죠.
먼저 두 사람에게 다가가 양해를 구한 뒤에야 그 사이를 지나갈 수 있습니다.
두 사람이 수어로 대화를 나누고 있다면
눈의 접촉과 대화의 흐름을 끊지 않는 게 더 중요하기 때문에,
제가 생각하는 예의 있는 방식으로 접근하면 안 되죠.
수어에서는 그냥 지나가는 게 예의 있는 거죠.
괜히 애매하게 이것저것 할 것 없이 바로 지나가면 되죠.
애매하게 이것저것 하지 말고 바로 한다.
학급에서도 적용해야 할 점인 것 같은데요.
물론, 처음에는 적응하기가 쉽지 않았지만 나중에는 익숙해졌죠.
그리고 문화와 관련해서 적응해야 할 점들이 더 있었습니다.
언어와 문화는 밀접한 관련이 있다는 겁니다.
서로 절대 뗄 수 없는 관계죠.
적응하기 위해 노력하고 기꺼이 바꾸려고 해야 합니다.
성경 원칙이 관련된 게 아니라면, 원어민의 문화와 생각을 받아들이는 것입니다.
‘모든 부류의 사람에게 모든 것이 되라’고 한 바울의 말이 이런 의미이죠.
물론 바울은 이 면에서 훌륭한 본이 되죠.
그럼 두 분이 수어 봉사를 하다가 또 무슨 일이 있었나요?
우린 베델에 있었지만 길르앗 학교에 가고 싶은 마음이 있었어요.
하지만 먼저 함께 파이오니아를 하는 게 좋다는 말을 들었죠.
그래서 베델을 떠나 테네시주에 있는 수어 집단에서 봉사했습니다.
테네시에서 좋은 형제 자매들을 만났고 멋진 경험도 했습니다.
몇 년 뒤에 순회 감독자 형제가
텍사스주로 이주해 그곳의 수어 회중을 도울 수 있냐고 물었습니다.
그곳에서 또 훌륭한 형제 자매들을 만나 좋은 경험을 했죠.
그런데 1년밖에 안 되었을 때 우린 월킬 베델로 다시 초대됐어요.
그런데 몇 년 뒤에 형제들이 저를 불러서
현지 번역 사무실에 가서 봉사할 수 있는지 물어보았습니다.
그 사무실에서는 출판물을 미국 수어로 번역합니다.
그곳에서 5년 동안 봉사했는데, 사진은 숙소 건물의 모습입니다.
제가 수어 봉사를 시작했을 때는 수어 출판물이 없었다고 했잖아요.
그게 수많은 사람들의 삶에 큰 영향을 미치는 걸 직접 볼 수 있었죠.
그런데 번역 사무실에서 그 출판물을 만들기 위해
형제 자매들이 얼마나 많은 사랑을 쏟고 수고를 하는지 보면서
지금 사진에서 보시는 건 첫 집회 교재인데요.
미국 수어로 집회 교재를 번역하고 있었죠.
모든 사람에 대한 여호와의 사랑을 놀라운 방식으로 볼 수 있었습니다.
그곳에서 좋은 경험을 하면서 훌륭한 교훈을 배우셨네요.
그림 형제, 수어 봉사를 하면서 어떤 유익을 얻으셨나요?
한 가지 분명한 건 이해심을 나타내는 법을 배웠죠.
프레드라는 청각 장애인과 성서 연구를 했어요.
프레드는 여러 교회를 다녀 봤지만 만족하지 못했죠.
그 지역의 전도인이 봉사하다 그를 만났고
특히 미국 수어로 된 성경을 보는 걸 좋아했죠.
그럼 우린 ‘지금 “ㅇ”을 읽고 있구나’ 하고 생각했죠.
한번은 프레드의 아내가 이런 얘기를 해 줬는데요.
침대 가장자리에 앉아 눈을 감고 수어를 하고 있었대요.
그래서 아내는 문제가 있는 줄 알고 다가가서 뭐하는 거냐고 물었죠.
그 이야기를 듣고 마음에 깊은 감동을 받았습니다.
프레드는 강한 믿음을 기르고 있었던 거죠.
그의 기도를 보고 계시다는 걸 알았던 겁니다.
이 사진은 프레드가 침례받은 날 찍은 겁니다.
그러면 침례받은 후 모든 게 순조로웠나요?
특히 프레드는 점점 시력을 잃고 있었습니다.
수어 동영상을 통해 영적 양식을 즐겨 왔는데,
60대의 나이에 점자를 배웠고, 촉각 수어도 배워야 했습니다.
그가 손으로 수어를 느끼고 내용을 이해할 수 있게 해 주는” 거죠.
기꺼이 도움을 주려고 하는 희생적인 형제 자매들이 아주 많았어요.
그의 집으로 가서 집회를 예습하게 도와주었습니다.
집회 때 다룰 내용을 미리 알 수 있게 도와주었죠.
프레드를 위해 모두가 돌아가면서 집회 내용을 촉각 수어로 통역해 주었어요.
사진은 프레드가 수어 회중 집회를 보고 있는 모습입니다.
두 분과 회중 형제 자매들의 강한 의지를 느낄 수가 있네요.
프레드는 집회 내용을 잘 따라가고 있다가
사회자가 질문을 하면 손을 번쩍 듭니다.
‘와, 프레드가 집회를 이해하고 여전히 해설도 하다니
수어 봉사를 하면서 하게 된 경험이
어떻게 앞으로 받게 될 임명에 잘 대비하는 데 도움이 되었나요?
네, 잘 적응하는 법을 배울 수 있었고
어떤 일을 하는 방법이 한 가지만 있는 게 아니라는 걸 알게 됐어요.
새로운 사람을 만나면 그 사람의 진짜 모습을 보려고 하는 거예요.
프레드는 자신의 상황이나 어려움 때문에 실망감을 표현할 때도 있었지만
그분이 어떻게 어려움을 이겨 내도록 도와주시는지에 초점을 맞췄죠.
프레드를 알게 되면서 저는 이해심이 더 많아졌어요.
어려움 속에서도 포기하지 않는 태도를 보았죠.
저도 그런 특성들을 계속 길러 나가고 싶습니다.
두 분의 이야기를 들려 주셔서 감사합니다.
형제는 길르앗에 오기 전에 흥미로운 임지에서 일했는데요.
열심히 봉사하면서 보낸 어린 시절에 대해 이야기해 줄 수 있을까요?
그러면 이 사진은 몇 살 때인가요?
양말에 샌들을 신은 게 특히 매력 포인트인 거 같아요.
어릴 때부터 봉사하는 걸 좋아하셨던 것 같은데,
네, 저는 봉사하는 걸 늘 좋아했어요.
어릴 때 어머니가 학교에 와서 저를 태우고
다른 파이오니아들과 함께 봉사를 하곤 하셨어요.
전 침례받고 나서 보조 파이오니아를 시작했죠.
그리고 고등학교를 졸업하자마자 정규 파이오니아를 시작했습니다.
그리고 어릴 때부터 영적 목표가 있었다고 알고 있는데요.
당시 순회 감독자는 리처드 애시 형제였죠.
“크리스토퍼, 너는 크면 나처럼 순회 감독자가 될 거야.”
그때 그분이 해 주신 말씀이 어린 제 마음에 깊이 남았습니다.
그리고 순회 감독자가 되는 걸 제 목표로 삼았죠.
하지만 그 전에 많은 걸 배워야 했죠.
그곳에서 3년 동안 있다가 아미시 지역으로 가게 되었죠.
닐스빌이라는 더 작은 마을에서 6년 동안 봉사했어요.
그 후 저는 워소라는 작은 도시에서 3년을 보냈죠.
여호와께서는 그런 경험들을 통해 저를 놀랍게 훈련시켜 주셨어요.
저 자신에 대해 많은 걸 배웠고,
여호와께서 저의 모난 부분을 많이 다듬어 주셨죠.
그런 임지들에서 여호와께서 언제나 일과 지낼 곳을 마련해 주셨거든요.
그리고 제 성서 연구생들이 잘 발전해서 침례받는 걸 보았고
영원히 지속될 우정을 맺을 수 있었죠.
그리고 2018년에 버지니아주 리치먼드에서 순회 활동을 하도록 초대되었습니다.
저는 그곳에서 약 1년 동안 순회 활동을 했습니다.
그리고 베델을 방문했다가 약 30년 만에 애시 형제를 우연히 만났습니다.
형제가 한 말이 맞았다고 말씀드릴 수 있었죠.
또 그분이 어린 제게 얼마나 큰 영향을 주셨는지 알려 드렸어요.
영적으로 장성한 사람이 청소년들에게 큰 영향을 줄 수 있다는 걸 깨달았죠.
청소년들이 목표를 세워서 최상의 삶을 살도록 도울 수 있어요.
이렇게 훌륭한 경험을 말씀해 주셔서 감사합니다!
그런데 그 후로 어떤 놀라운 임명을 받으셨죠?
제가 선교인 임명을 받아서 동아프리카 지부로 가게 되었습니다.
탄자니아 다르에스살람에서 순회 활동을 하도록 임명되었죠.
그리고 저는 그곳 언어를 몰랐기 때문에
스와힐리어도 배우고 탄자니아 수어도 배워야 했죠.
그래서 제가 회중에서 회중으로 갈 때마다 통역자가 따라다녔어요.
여호와와 함께 새로운 문화에서 새로운 모험을 하는 거였죠!
그곳에 도착한지 얼마 안 돼서 무슨 일이 있었다고 하신 거 같은데,
그래서 저는 직접 가서 회중을 방문할 수 없게 되었습니다.
형제 자매들을 대면해서 만날 수 없었죠.
임지에 온 지 6개월쯤 되었을 때 아침에 일어났는데,
제가 이 마을에 나타났을 때 팬데믹도 동시에 시작되었는데,
저는 외국인인 데다 언어도 안 통하니까
마을에 사는 몇몇 사람들과 문제가 생기기도 했습니다.
제가 해결책을 찾을 수 있게 즉시 도와주셨죠.
제가 맡은 일에 너무 많은 힘을 쏟고 있었어요.
여호와와 단둘이 있는 시간이 더 필요했죠.
잠이 많은 저에겐 아주 이른 시간이죠.
커피 한 잔을 들고 밖으로 나가서 아프리카의 일출을 보았어요.
해가 뜨는 걸 보면서 마음의 평화를 느꼈습니다.
여호와께서 바로 옆에 계신 것 같았어요.
성경 읽기를 위해 정신을 준비할 수 있었죠.
그리고 읽기 전에 기도로 여호와께 이렇게 청했어요.
그렇게 성경을 읽다가 제게 적용되는 점을 찾게 되면,
잠시 멈춰서 묵상하고 생각해 본 뒤 여호와께 말씀드렸죠.
그렇게 성경을 읽다 보면 그 말씀이 제 마음에 확 와닿을 때가 있었죠.
예를 들어, 어느 날 아침에는 예레미야 애가 3장을 읽고 있었는데
“우리가 멸절되지 않은 것은 여호와의 충성스러운 사랑 때문이니.”
‘그분의 자비는 끝이 없고 아침마다 새롭다’고 알려 주죠.
전 아침마다 그분의 자비를 받고 있었죠.
그분의 과분한 친절 덕분에 해가 뜨는 걸 또 볼 수 있었어요.
이 성구를 읽고 나서 마음이 아주 평온해졌습니다.
매일 아침 그 일과를 유지하는 동안에는 우울감을 느끼지 않았죠.
형제 자매들을 위해 사용할 수 있는 활력이 더 많이 생겼습니다.
양치는 일을 더 많이 할 수 있었죠.
그리고 토요일에는 줌에서 청소년들과 시간을 보내면서
그들이 어떻게 팬데믹을 헤쳐 나가고 있는지 알게 되었고,
우리에게 아름다운 아프리카의 일출 사진을 보여 주신다고 했었죠?
네. 실제론 이것보다 훨씬 더 아름다워요.
그리고 예레미야 애가는 보통 위로의 책이라고 생각하지는 않는데,
음악처럼 높은 음과 낮은 음의 굴곡이 있었죠.
사랑이 언어의 장벽을 뛰어넘는다는 걸 배웠습니다.
우리가 나타내는 사랑이 상대방의 마음속 깊이 이를 수 있습니다.
저는 제 말을 통역해 줄 통역자가 필요했지만,
형제 자매들은 제가 언어를 배우느라 애쓰는 걸 보면서 제 사랑을 느꼈죠.
참을성 있게 저와 일하며 저를 도와주었거든요.
그들에 대한 여호와의 사랑도 볼 수 있었죠.
형제들에게 읽어 준 성구들에 그 사랑이 분명히 나타나 있었죠.
또 그들이 여호와를 사랑한다는 것도 볼 수 있었는데,
저는 창조물을 통해 여호와를 볼 수 있다는 것도 배웠어요.
또 성경을 읽으면서 그분의 음성을 들을 수 있죠.
그리고 줌을 통해서라도 형제 자매들을 만나며
또 제가 이 임지에서 배운 점은
또는 교도소에 수감되어서 고립되었거나 외롭다고 느낄 때에도
학생들은 여호와를 섬기면서 각자 독특한 여정을 거쳐 왔습니다.
하지만 그럴 때마다 여호와를 온전히 의지했고
우리 삶의 여정 자체를 소중히 여기시니까요.
그 점을 기억하면 지금도 위로와 희망과 기쁨을 얻게 됩니다.
이사야 30장에서 이 사실을 잘 보여 주는데요.
축제를 위해 준비하면서 밤에 부르는 노래와 같고,
너희의 마음은 여호와의 산으로, 이스라엘의 반석에게로,
피리를 불며 걸어가는 사람처럼 기쁠 것이다.”
포기하지 말고 계속 아름다운 음악을 만들어 나가시기 바랍니다.

en.text: Well, at this time, we have a regular
and much loved feature of the program that we’ll enjoy
—The Inside Story.
Please pay close attention to this as it’s presented by Brother James Cauthon,
one of our Gilead School instructors.
Life is often compared to music.
It has high notes as well as some low notes.
Isn’t that true?
But together they compose a melody that is unique to ourselves.
Where does that melody go?
For faithful worshippers, it goes directly to Jehovah’s heart.
You see, he greatly values,
not just the accomplishments in our lives,
but the journey itself.
So today we’re going to hear from three students
in our 151st Gilead class.
As you listen to their journey, can you hear their song?
Let’s get started.
I’m sure you’ll enjoy meeting our first guests, Joel and Adrienne Grim,
on this edition of The Inside Story.
Adrienne, your theocratic goals started at a very early age.
Can you tell us about that?
Yes, my parents helped me to know that I wanted to serve Jehovah early,
and then when I was around 11
there were five young, single pioneer sisters
that all moved into my congregation as need-greaters.
So, of course, they were my heroes.
And one of them knew some American Sign Language,
and she started conducting Bible studies and interpreting the meetings
for the deaf in the area.
And she started teaching me a little bit too.
I was trying to help out.
Is that you there at 11 years of age?
That’s me and my little brother. I think about that time—yeah.
So a few years later, when I was a teenager,
the sister had to leave the area, and so there were Bible studies there.
So I was trying to help out as much as I could,
but it was challenging then because there were no sign-language publications yet.
Yeah, so how did you do that without any publications?
I tried different things.
One thing is that every Saturday night, you would find me sitting
with The Watchtower  on one knee
and a sign-language dictionary on the other knee,
and I would just look up every word.
You mean you looked up every  word?
Yeah, it was the best I could do at the time,
but I got a lot of help too, because the deaf were so kind
and so generous in helping me and so patient.
I remember this one time having a sign-language conversation
with a young girl about my age in the back of the Kingdom Hall,
and she signed something, and I couldn’t understand.
So I asked her to repeat it.
She repeated it, but I still wasn’t getting it,
and we just went back and forth with her trying
every way she could think of to try to get me to understand
until I just had tears going down my face.
But we kept at it, and finally I got it,
and I remember we just hugged because I finally understood.
But it was that kind of patience and kindness
that I saw over and over again that just really touched my heart.
Yeah, well, that experience touches our heart too.
Later you met Joel.
And Joel, you were serving at Wallkill Bethel at the time,
and things worked out —Adrienne, you became a Bethel bride.
And then later you both decided to join the sign-language congregation.
Now, Adrienne already knew (ASL) sign language, right?
But, Joel, you had to learn it.
So how was that for you?
Well, after learning sign language,
for one thing, I will never look at 1 Corinthians 9:22 the same way again.
So, what does 1 Corinthians 9:22 have to do with learning a language?
Well, that’s where Paul says that he became
“all things to people of all sorts.”
And that’s very true when you’re learning a language.
Language is more than just collecting vocabulary
so that you can communicate with someone.
You have to get to know the way that person thinks.
Well, there’s no doubt that language can affect the way we think,
but can you give us an example?
Sure.
Imagine there are two people having a conversation,
and you want to get to the other side.
Now, the way I grew up, my culture, is that I need to approach them
and excuse myself, be acknowledged, and then I can move on.
But in sign language it’s different.
If two people are having a signed conversation,
they value their eye contact and the flow of their communication
much more than they value my idea of what’s polite.
So in sign language, you just move on
straight through the conversation with minimal distraction
and no weaving and dancing and bobbing.
No, you just go straight on through.
No weaving, no dancing,
no bobbing, just straight through
—we should have applied that to your assignments in class.
There’s probably some truth to that.
So it was difficult to adapt.
But, of course, you know, after some time, I got the hang of it.
And there were other adjustments, of course, that you have to make for culture.
And I learned a valuable lesson,
and that is that language and culture are intrinsically linked.
You can’t really have one without the other.
And if you’re learning a new language,
you have to just adapt.
You have to be willing to change,
and the best thing to do is that if there are no Scriptural principles involved,
just adopt the culture and the value of the native language users.
And that’s what Paul meant when he said:
“Become all things to people of all sorts.”
Well, no doubt Paul was an excellent example in that regard,
and it sounds like you were too.
So where did your journey in sign language take you next?
Well, there we were at Bethel, but we really were hoping
that we would get a chance to go to Gilead.
But we were advised that it would be a good idea to pioneer together first.
So we left Bethel, and we moved to Tennessee
and joined a sign-language group down there,
and we really did love that group.
We sure did.
We met some wonderful brothers and sisters,
and we had some great experiences there in Tennessee.
After a few years, the circuit overseer asked us if we would be willing
to move to Texas to support a sign-language congregation there,
and so we did
—and, again, just wonderful times and great brothers and sisters.
But we were only there about a year,
and then we got invited back to Wallkill Bethel.
So we went back to Wallkill and after a few more years there,
the brothers called us one day
and asked us if we would be willing to transfer to the RTO,
the remote translation office,
in Fort Lauderdale, Florida,
where they translate
into American Sign Language.
And we were there for five years.
This is a picture
of the residence buildings there.
It looks very beautiful.
So how did you like that assignment?
I loved it!
Remember I told you that when I first started in sign language,
there were no sign-language publications.
So then as they started coming out,
we had the opportunity to see the impact
that those publications had on so many people’s lives.
So we already treasured those.
And then to get a chance to kind of get a glimpse behind the scenes
and see how much love and hard work
goes into all of those translations really was powerful.
I loved it!
And so, what publication are we looking at here?
So this is when we were working on the very first meeting workbook,
and this is when we were working on the sign-language version of that one.
Really, working in the Translation Department
was such a beautiful way to see Jehovah’s love for all people.
I’m sure that was excellent, and you learned good lessons there.
Joel, how were you affected by supporting the sign-language field?
Well, in many ways, but one way is definitely
that I learned to be more empathetic.
Do you mind if I share an experience that I had?
Well, we’d be pleased to hear it.
OK,
well, when we were in Tennessee, we had the privilege
of studying with a deaf man named Fred.
Now, Fred had been to many churches, but he was unsatisfied.
The local publishers found him in the ministry,
and he agreed to a Bible study.
And Fred loved to learn.
He especially loved watching the ASL Bible,
the portions of it that we had available at that time.
And he also loved to read the Insight  volumes.
He just had an insatiable desire for knowledge.
He would show up to the meetings, and he would ask us questions about them.
So he might come and say, “OK, I have two questions:
about Elijah and Elizabeth.”
And we’d think, ‘Oh, he’s in the e’s now.’
One day, Fred’s wife told us a little story.
She said that she had found him
in the bedroom at home sitting on the edge of the bed
with his eyes closed just signing.
And she thought something was wrong with him,
so she interrupted him and said, “What are you doing?”
And he told her that he was praying.
When I heard that, it touched my heart.
It was so beautiful to know
that Fred was developing strong faith
and that he knew that Jehovah knows sign language
and that he was watching his prayers.
It was really something.
This is a picture of Fred on the day that he got baptized.
So that’s great. Thanks for sharing that.
But now I ask you, Was it smooth sailing for Fred after that?
No.
No, he had many challenges, and one of those was
that he was losing his eyesight gradually.
And that was tough for him.
Here was a man who loved to learn.
He relied on the sign-language videos for spiritual food,
and he was going blind.
But he didn’t give up.
In his 60’s, he started to learn braille,
and he also had to learn tactile signing.
Now, “tactile”—could you explain that?
Sure.
Now, on its most basic level, “tactile” is “signing into another person’s hands
so that they can feel the signs and understand what’s being communicated.”
So that congregation there in Tennessee
was just full of self-sacrificing brothers and sisters who would help him.
They would go over to his house and help him prepare for the meetings
by signing the information into his hands
so that he could know what was going to be discussed.
And then at the Kingdom Hall
during the meetings, we would all pitch in and do tactile signing for him
so that he could keep up and follow along with the meetings.
This is a picture of him there
listening to one of the congregation meetings in sign language.
You know, that shows a lot of determination
not just by Fred but by those in the congregation,
yourselves as well.
Thank you for that.
Now, Fred was determined,
and he would be there following along with the meetings.
And you know, there might be a question.
And so his hand would just shoot up.
He wanted to comment, and I would see that and think,
‘Wow, you know, Fred is getting it, and he’s still able to participate.’
It was beautiful.
Yeah, it is inspiring. We appreciate you sharing that.
So now in conclusion,
how do you think your experiences with the sign-language field
have helped you to prepare
for any future assignments that may come your way?
I feel like it’s helped me to learn to be adaptable
and to remember that there’s not just one way that things should be done,
and also, when you’re meeting new people,
to really work to try to see the person and not just what you see at first glance.
Joel?
Yeah, I think about Fred a lot.
He would express frustration
at his situation and the challenges he was facing, but he wouldn’t dwell on it.
He would very quickly redirect his attention to Jehovah
and how Jehovah was supporting him to get through those challenges.
Getting to know him helped me to be more empathetic.
But I also saw his humility
and the fact that he would not give up in the face of adversity.
So those are some qualities that I want to continue to develop
wherever our journey takes us.
Those are great expressions. Thank you both.
Thank you for sharing your story.
And by the way, how do you sign
“thank you”?
Thank you.
Our next guest is Brother Christopher Kitts.
Before he came to Gilead, he had a very interesting assignment.
Please welcome Chris.
Chris,
before we talk about your most recent assignment,
I’d like to talk about your early years as a zealous evangelizer.
OK.
So in this picture, how old were you?
I was about four years old right there.
Four years old
—and I see even back in the day
that you were very fashion-conscious.
Thank you.
Personally, I think
it’s the socks with the sandals
that brought that whole outfit together.
Yeah!
Well, we love the picture,
and we understand you have a love for the ministry too.
So tell us a little bit about those early years.
Yeah, I always had joy in the ministry.
I loved it!
It was my happy place.
My mother would pick me up from school as a kid,
and she would take me out with her and the other pioneers.
And when I got baptized, I started auxiliary pioneering.
Then as soon as I graduated from high school, I started regular pioneering.
Wow, that’s excellent, Chris!
Now, I understand that you also have a theocratic goal from a very young age.
Yeah, I got baptized at 10,
and my circuit overseer at the time was Richard Ashe.
And he got down on his knee, and he said to me,
“Christopher, when you grow up,
you’re going to be a circuit overseer just like me.”
And his words had a big impact on my little heart.
I cherished them.
And I actually set circuit work as a goal.
Well, did you meet that goal?
I did, but we had a lot of work to do before we got there.
In 2005, I went to the Ministerial Training School,
and then after that, I got assigned
from where I grew up in Long Island, New York,
to the potato farms of Wisconsin
in a little town called Antigo.
I spent three years there,
and then I went to Amish country.
I spent six years in an even smaller town called Neillsville.
And then I spent three years in Wausau, a little city.
And that experience was amazing
because that’s where Jehovah gave me my training.
I learned a lot about myself.
Jehovah rubbed off a lot
of the rough edges.
I learned about faith, because in those assignments,
I saw Jehovah always provide me with work and places to live
in areas where sometimes there weren’t.
And I saw some of my Bible students progress to baptism,
and I made friendships that will last forever.
And then in 2018, I was invited into the circuit work
down in Richmond, Virginia.
And that was amazing!
I was in the circuit work there for about a year.
And it was about 30 years later
that I ran into Brother Ashe when I was visiting Bethel,
and I got to tell him he was right.
I got to share with him what an impact he had on me
as a child.
And it really made me think of the impact
that spiritually mature ones can have on young ones,
helping them to set goals
that can help them have the best life now.
That’s an excellent experience!
Thank you for sharing, Chris.
So it must have been a great moment for the two of you.
But, now, what surprising assignment followed that?
Yeah, I was appointed as a missionary,
and I was sent to the East Africa branch,
and I was assigned to circuit work in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
So from Virginia to Tanzania —that’s quite a jump!
Yeah.
So how did you feel about that?
I was excited!
It was a new adventure.
I didn’t know the language, so I’d have to learn Swahili.
I’d have to learn Tanzanian Sign Language,
so I would have an interpreter that would travel with me
from congregation to congregation.
So it was a new adventure for me with Jehovah and with a new culture.
I couldn’t wait!
There must have been challenges, though, and I think
you related one or more to me
that happened soon after you got there.
So can you tell us about that and the effect it had on you?
Yeah.
Yeah, as soon as I arrived in my assignment in Dar es Salaam,
the COVID-19 pandemic started.
And so now I wasn’t going to be able to visit the congregations in person.
I would not meet the brothers and sisters face to face.
I would have to serve them over Zoom and over the phone.
And about six months into my assignment,
I woke up one morning
and I had some pressure on my chest.
And I was feeling anxiety
because I was alone —I was isolated.
My interpreter lived six hours away.
He connected over Zoom and over the phone.
And because I showed up to this little village
at the same time the pandemic started
and as a foreigner not knowing the language,
it created some real difficulties between me and some of the villagers.
So I was feeling anxiety.
I was feeling alone.
There were times I was scared,
and for one of the first times in my life, I was feeling depressed.
So I went to Jehovah in prayer,
and I asked him:
“Did I do something wrong?
Should I go home?”
Chris, that must have been such a difficult time.
How did Jehovah help you?
Jehovah is amazing!
He helped me right away to see what the solution was.
I was giving so much in the assignment.
I needed more time alone with Jehovah.
So I started waking up at 5:30 in the morning,
and that’s early for me.
I like my sleep.
But it was what I needed.
I’d make my coffee, and I would go outside,
and I’d watch the African sun wake up.
And as I would watch the sunrise,
I felt peace
because I felt like Jehovah was right there with me.
And it grounded me;
it put me in the right frame of mind to start my Bible reading.
And so before I started, I would say a prayer to Jehovah,
and I asked him: “Jehovah, talk to me.
Let me hear your voice.”
And then I started my reading,
and I would read until I found something that applied to me.
And then I’d stop,
meditate, think about it,
and talk to Jehovah about it.
And that really brought me peace.
That helped calm me down.
I would be reading,
and there were times when it was as if the words would pop off the page.
For example, there was one morning
when I was in the book of Lamentations chapter 3,
and I was reading verse 22.
And it said there: “It is because of Jehovah’s loyal love
that we have not come to our finish.”
And when I read that, I thought,
‘Jehovah is protecting me in my assignment.’
And then it said next: “For his mercies never end.
They are new each morning.”
And that was true.
I was seeing Jehovah’s mercy every morning.
His undeserved kindness was painting me a new sunrise.
But verse 24 is what changed my life.
It says: “Jehovah is my share.”
Jehovah was with me.
And it says next: “That is why
I will show a waiting attitude for him.”
And it was like Jehovah was saying:
‘Chris, just wait.
Don’t give up.’
That brought me so much peace after I read that scripture.
My anxiety went away.
The fears that I had were gone.
And as long as I maintained that routine, I didn’t feel depressed.
I just continued in my assignment.
I found that I had more energy to give to the brothers and sisters.
I was able to spend more time shepherding.
And on Saturdays, I would spend time with the young ones on Zoom
and listen to their stories
and find out what they were doing
to help them get through the pandemic.
And their answers built my faith.
Chris, I believe you were going to share one of those
(a picture of one of those) beautiful African sunrises with us.
Is that not true?
Yeah, that picture doesn’t even do it justice.
Yeah, I can see why that would help you.
And, you know, we don’t typically think of the book of Lamentations
as a book of comfort,
but that’s a great scripture to remember.
So thanks for sharing that with us.
Now, Chris, as you look back on your journey,
you definitely had some high notes and some low notes.
So, what lessons have you learned?
I learned that love transcends language.
Love has the ability to bypass the mind
when words are formed into sentences,
and it can pierce right into the heart,
where emotions and feelings come from.
I needed an interpreter to translate my words,
but love needs no interpretation.
Those brothers and sisters could see how much I loved them
as I struggled to learn their language.
And I saw how much they loved me
as they patiently worked with me and helped me.
And I could see Jehovah’s love for them.
It was coming off the pages of the Bible as we read them scriptures.
And I could see their love for Jehovah as they
implicitly followed the direction from the Governing Body.
They viewed it as coming from Jehovah,
and they followed it even if it came to them at a cost.
And I also learned
that you can see Jehovah in creation
and that you can hear his voice in your Bible reading
and that you can feel his love
coming from the brothers and sisters even over Zoom.
And this assignment taught me
that even if you feel lonely
or if you’re isolated
because of a pandemic
or you’re in prison bonds,
you’re never alone.
Chris, thank you for sharing your illuminating story with us.
Thank you very much.
So could you hear it, friends?
As you saw, each of our students
had a unique journey in their service to Jehovah.
Things didn’t always go as planned.
There were some setbacks, and there were some tears.
But in each case, they fully relied on their Father, Jehovah,
and with his help, they got past those low notes,
and we can too,
because Jehovah greatly values not just our accomplishments
but also the journey itself.
Your faithful service is like a pleasing melody in Jehovah’s heart.
He cherishes all that you do for his name.
And remembering that should give us comfort, hope, and joy even now.
The words of Isaiah chapter 30 echo this thought.
Let me read this for us.
This would be Isaiah 30:29.
It says: “But your song will be
“like the one sung in the night when you prepare for a festival,
“and your heart will rejoice like one who walks with a flute
on his way to the mountain of Jehovah, to the Rock of Israel.”
So, brothers and sisters, don’t give up,
and don’t stop making beautiful music.
Till the next time on The Inside Story.
Well, those comments were priceless.
Thank you very much, Brother Cauthon,
and you students, soon-to-be graduates,
who were involved with that program.
That was delightful.

title: 재방문: 하느님의 목적—사 55:11

en.text: Last time, we discussed that God’s purpose
was for the earth to be a paradise,
and we left you with the question,
How can we be sure that God’s purpose for humans
here on earth will still be fulfilled?
Um, I’m not really sure.
We find the Creator’s assurance here at Isaiah 55:11.
Tina, would you please read that for us?
OK.
“So my word that goes out of my mouth will be.
“It will not return to me without results,
“but it will certainly accomplish whatever is my delight,
and it will have sure success in what I send it to do.”
Thank you.
Now, since these are the words of God himself,
how do we know that his purpose will be fulfilled?
Well, he says: “It will have sure success.”
Isn’t that interesting?
Our heavenly Father guarantees it.
Absolutely!
And looking again at this verse,
God says that his word will “accomplish whatever is [his] delight.”
So how does he feel about accomplishing his purpose?
He wants to accomplish it.
Yes, he delights to.
He’s really looking forward to bringing mankind happiness.
So we can be sure he will fulfill his purpose for the earth.
That’s very touching.
We think so too.
But what will life be like when God fulfills his purpose for humans?
Let’s discuss the Bible’s answer next time we talk.

다른 옛날 번역판으로 성구를 낭독하려고 하는데요.
전자 기기가 있다면 여러분도 다른 번역판으로 보실 수 있습니다.
20절 숫자를 누르면 다른 번역판으로 성구를 볼 수 있습니다.
그들의 말하는 바가 이 말씀에 맞지 아니하면 그들이 정녕히 아침 빛을 보지 못하고.”
이 성구를 읽고 깊은 감동을 받은 어머니는 연구를 계속하기로 결심하셨습니다.
‘이 성구에 나온 “증거의 말씀”이 뭐지?’ 하는 생각이 드실 수 있죠.
이 성구를 「신세계역」 개정판으로 보면 이해하기가 더 쉬울 것입니다.
이 말씀에 따라 말하지 않는 자들에게는 빛이 없다.”
생각해 보니까 어머니는 자신을 찾아온 두 사람이
성구는 하나도 보여 주지 않았다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
그냥 여호와의 증인에 대한 자신들의 생각만 늘어놓았죠.
그러한 점들을 생각한 어머니는 큰 용기를 얻었습니다.
「“하나님은 참되시다 할지어다”」 책 1장에서 알려 주는 것처럼,
하느님에 대해 우리가 믿는 모든 점은 그분의 말씀인 성경
즉 기록으로 확증된 것이어야 한다는 점을 깨달으셨죠.
사람들이 우리에 대해 무슨 말을 하든, 어떤 악의적인 비난을 늘어놓든,
우리는 언제나 확신을 가질 수 있습니다.
우리의 신앙은 성경에 확실한 근거를 두고 있기 때문입니다.
또 제가 보여 드리고 싶은 두 번째 출판물은
제가 사무실에 없을 때 이걸 보셨다면
‘아, 이 잡지가 나오고 몇 주 뒤에 잭슨 형제가 태어나셔서
이걸 갖다 놓으셨나 보다’ 하실지 모르는데,
이것 역시 제 어머니가 진리를 받아들이는 계기가 된 출판물입니다.
첫 번째 기사의 제목은 “단 하나의 참종교”입니다.
“밀을 살 돈을 내고 지푸라기를 받을 것인가?
포도주를 살 돈을 내고 물을 받을 것인가?
물을 마시고 싶은데 누가 흙탕물을 주면 만족할 것인가?
당신이 그런 식으로 사기를 당하고 있다는 걸 누군가가 증명해 준다면,
당신은 그에게 화를 낼 것인가, 사기꾼에게 화를 낼 것인가?”
오늘날 여호와의 백성이 하느님의 말씀에 담긴 진리를 가르치고 있다는 걸 보여 줍니다.
그리고 이 잡지에는 제 어머니에게 도움이 된 두 번째 성구가 있습니다.
그들은 거짓말을 하는데, 꿈을 꾸고 나서 자신의 꿈을 설명하려고 합니다.
자신들의 가르침으로 백성들이 ‘하느님의 이름을 잊게 만들려고 한다’라고 알려 주죠.
“‘꿈을 꾸는 예언자는 그 꿈을 이야기하도록 내버려 두어라.
그러나 내 말을 가진 자는 내 말을 진실하게 전해야 한다.
중요한 점은 우리가 하느님의 말씀을 진실하게 전하는 것입니다.
이 잡지에서 제가 소개할 두 번째 기사도 흥미로운데요.
사람들이 참종교를 선택해야 한다는 걸 보여 주는 내용입니다.
이 기사에서는 일부 사람들이 하는 이러한 말을 소개합니다.
‘이 많은 종교를 어떻게 일일이 다 조사해?
건초 더미에서 바늘을 찾으려고 하는 것과 마찬가지지.’
근데 이 잡지에서는 앞서 나온 예레미야서에 근거해 이렇게 말합니다.
건초를 한 가닥씩 다 살펴보아야 하는 것은 아니다.’
그런 다음 다소 과격한 제안을 하죠.
‘건초더미를 불태운 뒤 자석으로 바늘을 찾을 수 있다.’
쓰레기를 태워 버리는 불이라고 할 수 있죠.
그러니까 우리가 다양한 종교의 모든 가르침을 알아보려고
그건 건초 가닥을 전부 살피는 거죠.
하지만 우리가 성경을 연구하면서 순수한 진리를 배우면,
네, 이런 방법을 통해 우리가 진리를 갖고 있다는 확신을
이를테면, 여호와의 이름도 모르는 사람들의 말을 믿을 필요가 있을까요?
특히 그들이 여호와의 백성을 공격하면서 하는 말을
때때로 그러한 자문을 해 본다면 유익할 것입니다.
제 경우에는 어머니가 가르쳐 주신 두 가지 점을 생각합니다.
우리가 믿는 것이 성경에 근거해 있는지 확인해야 한다는 것입니다.
그리고 둘째로, 우리가 듣는 이야기들을 전부 알아보아야 하는 것은 아닙니다.
우리는 무엇이 옳고 그른지 알 수 있습니다.
거짓의 아버지의 말을 들을 필요가 없죠.

en.text: This morning, we’re going to discuss the thought
of keeping “the belt of truth”
tight around our waists.
Now, why is that so important?
Well, we see in the world today
there’s just no end to the misinformation,
the lies, the falsehoods that are being spread.
But in addition to that, as Jehovah’s people
we face all sorts of verbal attacks, don’t we?
People accuse us of horrific things,
and this can be very discouraging.
So that’s why we need to make sure
that we’ve got “the belt of truth”
firmly around our waist—tight.
But how can we tighten it?
Well, of course, there are many different ways
that we can reassure ourselves of the truth.
But this morning, I thought we might talk about just one thing that may help us,
and that is to go back to the basics.
From time to time, think about this question,
What was it that convinced me or my family
that this is the truth?
And if we meditate on that,
it can help to strengthen our resolve
to continue in the truth.
And in this way, figuratively speaking, it’s as if we tighten the belt.
And we all know, those of us who wear belts,
you need a tight belt for it to be effective.
Now, with that in mind, if you ever visit me in my office,
you’ll notice that I have two things
that from time to time I’ll look at.
One is this publication.
Now, when you look at it, you might say the same as my wife did a few days ago:
“Don’t you have a better copy of that edition?
It’s not really looking so good.”
So why is this in my collection of books in the office?
Well, because this is the book, “Let God Be True,”
that my mother started studying in 1956
when she was contacted in the door-to-door work.
Now, I have a connection to this because at that time I was 18 months old.
And as you can see in the front,
I had no potential whatsoever
of being in the Writing Department or the Art Department.
But I guess it did prove that at an early age,
I was interested in books.
Anyway, this book is close to my heart
because it helped my mother
at a time when she faced some opposition.
She’d just started using this book
when a minister from the Methodist Church and a missionary
came along to her house to try to force her
to stop studying with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Now, what did they do?
Well, they berated the Witnesses.
They said all sorts of falsehoods.
And they said everything they could
that was negative about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Once they left, my mother said that she felt
very discouraged and disheartened
after being the victim of this verbal abuse.
So, what did she do?
She took her King James Bible
and turned to a scripture
that she had just studied in paragraph 5
of this book in the first chapter.
Maybe you’d like to read it with me, if you would.
If you have an electronic device,
you have an advantage this morning because I’d like you to turn
to the book of Isaiah 8:20.
But I’d like you to read it from the King James Version.
So Isaiah 8:20
—and if you tap on verse 20,
you’ll see that the King James Version  may come up.
It says: “To the law and to the testimony:
“if they speak not according to this word,
it is  because there is  no light in them.”
Now, that touched her heart
and helped her to make the decision to continue studying.
Now, if you’re like me, you are probably trying to work out:
‘What is “the testimony”? What’s this all about?’
But if you look at the revised text
of the New World Translation  in verse 20, it helps us, doesn’t it?
There, it says: “Instead, they should inquire of the law
“and of the written confirmation!
When they do not speak according to this word, they have no light.”
So she realized that these two who had come to visit her
did not show her anything from the Scriptures.
Rather, they just said what they felt
about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
So that helped her because she realized,
as the “Let God Be True”  book says in chapter 1,
that everything we believe about God
needs to be based on the Word of God, the Bible
—in other words, written confirmation.
So that’s the first lesson—the first point that is a good reminder to me personally.
No matter what people say about us,
no matter what negative comments are made,
we can always take comfort in the thought
that our beliefs are solidly based on the Bible.
Now, the second thing that you might notice in my office
is this Watchtower  magazine.
It’s from February 15, 1955.
So if I’m not in my office and you see it, you may think,
‘Ah, he’s got that there because he was born
just a couple of weeks after this.’
No, that’s not the reason it’s there.
The reason is that this was the second thing that helped my mother
to take a stand for the truth.
There were two beautiful articles in this Watchtower.
The first one was entitled
“Only One Right Religion.”
And notice how it starts off:
“If you pay for wheat will you settle for straw?
“If you buy wine will you accept water?
“Or if you thirst for water will you be satisfied with mud?
“What if someone came to prove
“that you were being defrauded in these ways?
Would you be angry with him or with the one who was cheating you?”
What a great start to the article!
And then it went on to show how the truth of God’s Word
is being taught by Jehovah’s people today.
But there’s a second scripture
that was in this magazine that really helped my mother.
So if you’d like, turn with me to the book of Jeremiah
—Jeremiah chapter 23.
Now, in the context of this,
we’re going to read verses 28 and 29.
But in the previous verses, it mentions false prophets
—those who tell lies, who are dreaming,
and who try to explain their dreams.
And verse 27 says that these are the same ones who teach people
or ‘intend to make them forget my name.’
So, what do verses 28 and 29 say?
“Let the prophet who has a dream relate the dream,
“but the one who has my word
“should speak my word truthfully.
‘What does the straw have in common with the grain?’ declares Jehovah.”
Do you see how the Watchtower  article was tied in there about grain and straw?
But the point is that we need to speak God’s Word truthfully.
Now, the second article in this magazine, which is equally good,
helps persons to see the need to select the true religion;
it is “Choosing the One Right Religion.”
In this article, it raises the point that sometimes people will say:
‘Well, I just don’t have time to investigate all the religions in the world.
‘How can I find the truth?
It’s just like trying to find a needle in a haystack.’
Well, this magazine, building on what was said in Jeremiah, said,
‘Well, if you go to a haystack looking for a needle,
you don’t have to look at every straw in the haystack.’
Actually, they recommend quite a radical move,
‘Burn the haystack, and then with a magnet, you can find the needle.’
Now, what’s the point?
Well, as it goes on to say, you see, as Jeremiah said,
‘God’s Word is like a fire.’
You see, in verse 29, it says it’s like a fire that consumes the rubbish.
So we don’t have to go around investigating
all the various teachings of different religions.
That would be like a huge haystack.
But rather, when we study the Bible
and we see the pure truth in the Scriptures,
then we can identify anything
that’s virtually rubbish or straw.
And we have the real thing.
Yes, that helps to really convince us that we have the truth.
Because if people don’t even know Jehovah’s name,
why would we believe them?
And if they believe that people are going to hellfire,
why would we believe everything that they say
—particularly if they’re criticizing Jehovah’s people?
So, what about you?
What was it that convinced you
that you found the truth?
Well, it’s good from time to time to think about that question.
In my case, I think of those things that my mother taught me.
The first one from the book of Isaiah:
to make sure that what we believe is based on the Bible.
And then the second thing: We don’t have to investigate
every story that’s told to us.
Once we have the truth from the Bible,
we can recognize what’s right and what’s wrong.
Yes, we don’t need to listen to the “father of the lie,”
but we certainly believe in “the God of truth.”

cn.text: 今天早上我们会一起谈一谈
为什么我们必须把真理当作腰带紧紧地束上
这样做很重要
因为在今天的世界里
我们的周围充斥着各种各样的谎言
和不实的报导
除此之外，作为耶和华的子民
我们还受到人们言语的攻击
很多人指控我们做很糟糕的事
这真的容易让人灰心
所以我们必须要确保
自己把真理紧紧地束在腰间
那我们可以怎么做呢？
当然有很多的方法可以帮我们确信
自己拥有真理
但今天早上，我想跟大家谈一个方法
就是沉思基本真理
我们要不时地问问自己这个问题
是什么帮助我和我的家人看出这是真理呢？
如果我们常常思考这个问题
就能让自己更有决心继续持守真理
这样做仿佛就是帮我们在束紧真理的腰带
我们大家都知道
要束紧腰带，它才会有作用
如果你有机会到我的办公室看一下
你会看到有两个东西，我常常会看一看
其中一个是这本书
看到它，你的反应可能跟我妻子一样
几天前，她问我
“这本书又破又旧
你不能换一本好一点的吗？”
我为什么要保存这本书呢？
这本《以上帝为真实》是我母亲的
弟兄姐妹在挨家挨户传道时找到她
她就开始学习了
这本书也跟我有一点关系
当时我18个月大
如果你打开，看这里
你会发现我没有潜力
在写作部或美术部服务
但你也可以看出，我从小就很喜欢书
我非常喜欢这本书
因为它对我母亲帮助很大
我母亲刚刚开始用这本书学习圣经
没过多久
一个卫理公会的牧师和一个传教士
就来到了我们家
想要阻止我母亲和耶和华见证人学习
他们怎么做呢？
他们开始攻击耶和华见证人
说了许许多多耶和华见证人的坏话
几乎把能想到的所有的坏话都说了
他们离开后，我母亲感到很沮丧、很灰心
因为牧师和传教士说得太难听了
但她怎么做呢？
我母亲就拿起圣经，打开一节经文
这节经文是这本书第一章
第五段里面提到的经文
我们可以一起读一下这节经文
如果你有电子设备
你可以打开圣经到以赛亚书
我母亲读的是一个比较老的译本
所以我想请你看一下一个以前的译本
怎么翻译这句话
以赛亚书 8:20
如果你点击20节
就会在旁边看到其他的译法
有一个译本这样说
“人当以训诲和法度为标准
他们所说的若不与此相符，必不得见晨光”
这节经文打动了我母亲
让她下定决心，继续学习圣经
很有可能，我们读完都不明白
这里说的“训诲”到底指什么呢？
如果我们看一下《新世界译本》（修订版）
就会明白了
经文这样说
“他们应该从法律和作证的文件中
寻求指引才对！
如果他们说的跟上帝的话语不符
就不会看到亮光”
这节经文让我母亲想到
那两个人没有让她看一节经文
他们说的
只不过是自己对耶和华见证人的看法
我母亲看出
《以上帝为真实》的第一章说得很对
就是所有关于上帝的真理
都必须根据上帝的话语圣经
换句话说，圣经就好比“作证的文件”
这是我今天想说的第一点
这一点对我帮助也很大
就是无论别人说我们什么
无论他们对我们有多么负面的看法
我们都可以确信
我们的信仰是完全以圣经为根据的
你在我的办公室留意到的第二件东西
是这本《守望台》
这是1955年2月15日刊
你看到这本杂志可能会想
他保存这本杂志
是因为这本杂志发行之后没几周
他就出生了
不，不是这个原因
这本杂志
是帮助我母亲在真理中站稳的
第二个出版物
这本《守望台》里有两篇很好的文章
其中一篇是《只有一种正确的宗教》
文章开头这样说
如果你付了钱买麦子，你会肯接受稻草吗？
如果你买的是酒，你会肯接受水吗？
如果你口渴要饮水
别人给你些泥，你会满意吗？
如果有人向你证明你这样地受了欺骗
你会怎样呢？
你会恼怒他呢？
抑或恼怒那欺骗你的人呢？
引言的部分写得多好！
接着这篇文章就谈到，耶和华现代的子民
教导别人上帝话语的真理
这本杂志里引用的经文对我母亲帮助也很大
我们可以一起看一下这两节经文
耶利米书23章
我们会一起读28, 29节
请也留意经文的上下文
前面几节的经文谈到假先知
他们说谎话
他们做了梦
也向别人解释自己的梦
第27节说，这些假先知
企图让上帝的子民忘记耶和华的名
请看28, 29节的经文
“就让做了梦的先知把梦说出来好了
可是得到我话语的先知
必须把我的话原原本本地说出来
耶和华宣告
干草和谷物怎么能相比呢？”
你明白了吗？
为什么文章会谈到干草和谷物
要点就是，要原原本本地传讲上帝的话语
这本《守望台》里还有另外一篇文章
写得也非常好
文章指出，选择信仰很重要
这篇文章的题目是《选择唯一正确的宗教》
这篇文章谈到很多人有这样的看法
就是，我没有时间去研究世上所有的宗教
怎么能找到真理呢？
这就好比在干草堆里找一根针啊
这篇文章主要是讨论耶利米书的
它说，如果你要到干草堆里找一根针
你不需要仔细检查每一根草
文章提出一个激进的做法
烧掉干草堆，用吸铁石就能找到针了
是什么意思呢？
文章接着引用29节的经文
上帝的话语就像火一样
火能够把废料都烧掉
所以我们不需要仔细研究
各个宗教的不同教义
它们的确像一个干草堆
如果我们仔细研读圣经
和上帝话语里纯正的道理
就能分辨出哪些是谬论和谎言
然后就找到了真理
这真的能帮助我们
让我们确信自己拥有真理
如果他们都不知道耶和华的名字
我们为什么还要听他们的呢？
如果他们觉得，人死后会在地狱里受苦
我们为什么还要听他们讲别的道理呢？
特别是他们还批评耶和华的子民
那你呢？
是什么帮助你确信自己找到真理呢？
我们最好常常想想这个问题
对我来说，就是我母亲教我的两件事
第一是来自以赛亚书
要确保我们相信的道理都是基于圣经的
第二，我们不需要去调查所有听到的传言
一旦我们拥有圣经的真理

是的，我们不需要听“谎话之父”说什么
