title: 크리스토퍼 메이버: 여호와께서는 자신의 백성을 사랑하십니다 (이사야 54:5)

ko.text: 서로 더 가까워지는 데 도움이 되는 점들을 다룹니다.
앞으로 결혼 생활을 하다가 갈등이나 어려움이 생기면
그들이 그러는 이유는 우리 하느님 여호와를 모르기 때문입니다.
그들은 여호와께서 결혼 서약을 얼마나 중요하게 여기시는지 모르죠.
결혼에 대해 이 세상의 많은 사람들이 생각하는 것과 매우 다릅니다.
단지 편의나 개인의 이익, 자녀 출산을 위한
법적인 계약에 불과한 것이 되기를 원치 않으셨습니다.
예를 들어, 창세기 2:24에서 최초의 결혼식을 주례하실 때
‘두 사람은 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 서로에게 평생 잡혀 살 것이다.’
이 구절에 나오는 여호와의 말씀을 읽어 보면,
얼마나 큰 사랑과 애정을 갖고 계셨는지 알 수 있습니다.
“그러므로 남자가 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내에게 고착할 것이며
이 기록을 통해, 우리는 사랑이 참으로 여호와의 주된 특성이며
사랑을 나타낼 수 있도록 창조되었다는 걸 알게 됩니다.
따라서 아담과 하와는 서로에 대해 그런 사랑을 기를 역량을 가지고 있었고
그렇게 하는 것은 결혼 생활에서 정말 중요합니다.
“마지막 때”를 살고 있는 불완전한 부부들에게 특히 그렇죠.
그들은 ‘육체의 환난’과 오늘날 결혼 생활에 따르는 다양한 어려움을 극복하기 위해
그리고 그분이 자신의 백성들에게 얼마나 깊은 사랑을 갖고 계신지 알 수 있습니다.
그렇게 말할 수 있는 이유는 무엇입니까?
여호와께서 고대 이스라엘을 어떻게 여기셨는지 함께 살펴보시죠.
“너를 만든 위대한 이가 너의 남편이니, 만군의 여호와가 그 이름이다.”
여호와께서는 자신의 백성인 고대 이스라엘과 계약을 맺으셨는데,
여호와께서는 자신의 백성과 계약을 맺으실 때
그 점을 그들에게 분명히 밝혀 주셨습니다.
여호와께서 모세를 통해 뭐라고 말씀하시는지 보시죠.
“여호와께서 여러분에게 애정을 나타내어 여러분을 선택하신 것은,
여러분이 모든 민족 중에서 수가 가장 많아서가 아니었습니다. …
[그리고 8절 끝에 그분이 그들을 선택하신 이유가 나오죠?]
여러분의 조상에게 하신 맹세를 지키셨기 때문입니다.”
여호와께서는 사랑에서 우러나와 아브라함과 계약을 맺으시고
이삭, 야곱, 그리고 나중에는 다윗과 같은 충실한 사람들과
그분은 자신과 같은 생각과 마음을 가진 사람들을 찾으시고,
인류에 대한 그분의 뜻을 이루기 위해 그들을 사용하셨습니다.
여호와께선 자신의 백성을 위해 최선을 다하셨습니다.
그런데 그분과 계약을 맺은 백성 즉 비유적인 아내가 불충실해지고
그분을 저버렸을 때 그분의 마음이 얼마나 아프셨을까요?
그들의 행동에 배신감을 느끼시고 가슴이 찢어지는 것 같으셨을 겁니다.
그분은 그 점을 백성에게 분명히 밝히셨죠.
특히 열 지파 왕국에게 그렇게 하셨는데,
그들은 영적으로 완전히 타락해서 더 이상 여호와를 신경 쓰지 않았습니다.
그들과 그들이 한 행동에 대해 그분이 어떻게 느끼시는지
그분은 예언자 호세아에게 아주 힘든 임명을 주셨습니다.
여기 2절을 보시면, 호세아가 해야 할 일이 나옵니다.
‘가서, 매춘 행위를 할 여자와 결혼하고 매춘의 자녀들을 취하여라.
이 땅이 매춘 행위를 하여 여호와를 따르는 길에서 완전히 돌아섰기 때문이다.’”
여러분이 한 번도 결혼한 적이 없는 처녀나 총각인데,
여호와께서 앞으로 바람을 피울 것이 분명한 사람과 결혼하라고 하신다면 어떨까요?
그들 때문에 자신이 얼마나 고통스럽고 마음이 아프신지
이것은 배우들이 아니라 실존 인물들이 보여 준 드라마죠.
호세아의 이웃 사람들이 어떻게 생각했을지 상상해 보세요.
그의 아내가 바람을 피우고 남편에게 몹쓸 짓을 합니다.
영성이 있는 사람이라면 그걸 보고 마음이 몹시 아팠겠죠.
여호와께선 그 마음 아파하는 사람들에게 이러한 희망의 소식을 전하십니다.
‘이 땅이 멸망되고 너희가 유배되어 갈 것이지만,
다른 남자의 사랑을 받으며 간음을 저지르고 있는 그 여자를 사랑하여라.
이스라엘 백성이 다른 신들에게로 향하고 건포도 과자를 사랑하는데도
여호와가 그들을 사랑하는 것처럼 그렇게 하여라.”
하느님을 사랑하는 사람들은 유배지에서 예루살렘으로 돌아와
여호와께선 그들을 당장 없애 버릴 법적 권리가 있으셨습니다.
하지만 그렇게 하지 않으신 건 다른 점들이 관련되어 있었기 때문입니다.
이스라엘과의 관계에는 정말 중요한 문제가 달려 있었습니다.
인류에 대한 여호와의 목적을 이룰 메시아가 이 민족을 통해서 나올 것이었죠.
그래서 이스라엘 백성이 이방 민족들에게 가고
바알과 같은 거짓 신들을 섬기면서 온갖 불충실한 일을 저질렀지만,
‘내가 다시 그를 데려오겠다. 내가 계속 그와 함께 일할 것이다’라고 하셨죠.
이스라엘 백성이 이 땅에 오신 하느님의 독생자인 예수를 죽음으로 내몰았을 때,
그분을 닮으신 예수의 말씀에서 그 점을 엿볼 수 있죠.
예루살렘에 가까이 이르러 그 도시를 보고 울며 말씀하셨다.
‘오늘 네가, 바로 네가 평화를 가져다주는 것이 무엇인지 분별했더라면—
그러나 그것이 지금 네 눈에 숨겨져 있구나.’”
마음 아프게도, 이스라엘과의 결혼 관계는 곧 끝날 것이었습니다.
여호와 하느님께서 자신의 백성과의 관계를 결혼에 비하신 점을 생각해 보면
이런 비유를 통해 우린 여호와께서 인류를 얼마나 사랑하시는지,
또 사람들을 돕기 위한 자신의 목적을 얼마나 중요하게 여기시는지 알게 되죠.
그리고 배우자의 배신으로 고통당하는 사람들의 마음을 이해하십니다.
여호와께선 그들이 느끼는 모든 감정과 고통을 온전히 이해하시죠.
그들이 유익한 결정을 내릴 수 있도록 도와주십니다.
또한 일부 사람들은 여호와의 축복으로 새로운 임명을 받게 되거나
여호와를 사랑하는 새로운 배우자를 만나서 함께 그분을 충실히 섬기며
따라서 우리가 결혼에 대한 하느님의 생각을 이해하고
여호와께선 우리가 결혼 생활이나 그 밖의 임명을
감옥살이나 무거운 짐처럼 여기길 원하지 않으시죠.
어떤 상황 속에서도 튼튼한 결혼 관계를 유지하고
진정한 행복과 기쁨을 누리는 삶을 살 수 있습니다.

en.text: If we stop and think about this
scripture text for today,
it was taken from an article
that dealt with how to help couples
who are perhaps having difficulties
in their marriage to resolve them
and to move forward.
We contrast that with the world.
You know, in the world, when they get married,
they anticipate they’re going to have problems and conflicts,
and they’ve already mapped a route for leaving the marriage if things are
too inconvenient for them or are just not working for them.
And that’s really because they don’t know our God, Jehovah, do they?
They don’t know how he feels and the depth of his feelings.
When we stop and consider marriage and the institution of marriage
that he inaugurated back in the garden of Eden,
we see a great contrast.
He did not want marriage just to be a contractual agreement,
something for convenience or personal interest
or even just for procreation purposes.
He didn’t want it to be a heavy burden.
For instance, at Genesis 2:24
when Jehovah did perform the first marriage,
he didn’t say: ‘That is why a man will leave his father and mother,
and they will be stuck with each other for the rest of their lives,’
as if committing them to a life sentence or punishment.
No.
But when we read Jehovah’s words in this scripture,
we hear in Jehovah a great deal of affection
and even sentiment about the couple, Adam and Eve,
when he says: “That is why a man will leave his father and mother
“and he will stick to his wife,
and they will become one flesh.”
You see, from this we learn about Jehovah
—truly, love being his dominant quality
and how he conveyed that dominant quality
to his earthly creation, humans made in his image.
Adam and Eve had the capacity, then, of developing such a love
for one another that they would literally cling
to one another —hold on to one another.
And this is an important aspect of marriage,
especially as imperfect people living in “the time of the end”:
We have to cling to one another
in order to get through the ‘tribulation of the flesh’
and other difficulties that come upon married people today.
So we see, though, in analyzing this
that we get to know our God, Jehovah,
and the deep love that he himself has
and conveys to his people.
Jehovah is the superlative example of a man,
if you will—a person—
who clung to his wife.
And why do we say that?
Consider how he viewed ancient Israel.
Open your Bibles, please, to the book of Isaiah
chapter 54 and verse 5.
Here we read: “For your Grand Maker
“is as your husband,
Jehovah of armies is his name.”
Now, true, we think of the covenant that Jehovah initiated
with his ancient people, Israel.
They were bound together in a covenant agreement.
But what was behind it?
It was love.
Jehovah made that clear to his people
when this contract
—this covenant—was inaugurated.
At Deuteronomy 7:7, 8,
notice what Jehovah through Moses said.
It says: “It was not because you were the most numerous of all the peoples
“that Jehovah showed affection
“for you and chose you,
“for you were the smallest of all the peoples.
“Rather, it was because of Jehovah’s love for you
and because he kept the oath that he had sworn to your forefathers.”
Love was behind this.
Love is what motivated Jehovah to make a covenant with Abraham
and pass that on to Isaac, to Jacob,
and to other faithful men, like David later on.
It was love that moved him to engage in this covenant.
He found someone that was of the same mind and heart as him
who he could use to work out
his purpose on behalf of mankind.
Jehovah gave them his very best.
He clung to them and looked after them.
And how deeply it pained him
when his covenant people
—wife, if you will—
turned unfaithful to him and rejected him!
Jehovah’s feelings are pure and deep.
So Jehovah felt truly betrayed
and deeply cut to the heart.
Now, he really wanted to make this clear to his people,
especially the ten-tribe kingdom who were so spiritually bankrupt
that they lost total sense of what Jehovah was all about.
So before he pronounced judgment upon them,
he made very clear to them just how he felt
about them and what they had done to him.
And how did he do that?
He commissioned his prophet Hosea
with a very difficult assignment.
Turn with me, please, to the book of Hosea
in chapter 1,
and notice right away what Hosea was to do
—chapter 1 and verse 2.
It says: “When Jehovah started to speak his word through Hosea,
“Jehovah said to Hosea:
“‘Go, marry a woman of prostitution
“‘and have children of prostitution,
“‘because by prostitution the land
has turned completely away from following Jehovah.’”
Can you imagine getting that assignment?
Here you are a virgin —never been married before—
and you’re told now to go marry someone that you know
is going to be unfaithful to you.
And Jehovah did that.
He wanted to show in a very real way
to this hardhearted people
just what his feelings were and what
he was going through in dealing with them.
This was a drama, not of actors, but of real-life people.
We can just imagine those in the village of Hosea and what they were thinking.
Here is this prophet of God, and here this woman was just cheating on him
and treating him very, very badly.
Anybody with any kind of spiritual sense would have been cut to the heart.
Jehovah reached out to those who were cut to the heart
because he said, ‘This land is going to be destroyed;
you’re going to be exiles, but I’m going to call you back.’
And Hosea 3:1 says:
“Then Jehovah said to me: ‘Go once again, love the woman
“‘who is loved by another man and is committing adultery,
“‘just as Jehovah loves the people of Israel
while they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes.’”
Jehovah loved them.
And those that loved him, after exile, returned
and went back to Jerusalem to continue worshipping God there.
Certainly, when we consider the history of Israel,
we feel, or know, that Jehovah definitely had
a legal right to just do away with them.
But he didn’t.
Why?
Because there were things to be considered.
There was a great deal riding on this relationship.
He was working out his purpose on behalf of mankind.
The Messiah was going to come through this nation.
So despite all the immorality
that the people of Israel committed by going to the nations
and worshipping Baals and whatnot
—all this unfaithfulness—Jehovah said, ‘I’m going to take her back
and continue working with her.’
However, there was a limit to this.
And when Jesus came to the earth, we know that Jehovah
had reached his limit with his people,
especially when they put his only-begotten Son to death.
And we can see the remorse and the pain of heart
that Jehovah had was perfectly reflected in Jesus.
At Luke 19:41, 42,
here it says: “When [Jesus, that is, when] he got nearby
“[that is, to Jerusalem], he viewed the city
“and wept over it, saying:
“‘If you, even you,
“‘had discerned on this day the things having to do with peace
—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.’”
It was too late—too far gone.
The relationship—the marriage— was going to come to an end,
and it hurt deeply.
You see, in understanding the marriage relationship
and how Jehovah uses this relationship in a very real way,
we can understand Jehovah better.
We get to know how deeply he feels
about mankind,
how he treasures mankind,
and also how he treasures his purpose
in wanting to help people.
He feels for those who are going through ‘tribulation in the flesh,’
and he especially feels deeply
for those whose mates have proven unfaithful.
Jehovah knows completely the emotions —the gamut of emotions—
that such ones go through.
And he is there to help them work through this
in making appropriate decisions that are good for them.
Oftentimes, with such ones, we see how Jehovah has blessed them
with new assignments and, yes,
even a new mate that loves Jehovah.
And they’re off faithfully serving their God together,
easing their pain.
So by imitating God’s love —cultivating God’s love—
in our marriages and understanding marriage,
we understand Jehovah better.
He does not want any of us to view marriage or any assignment
as something that is a life sentence, a drudgery, or a burden.
No, but through love,
we are able to cultivate our marriages and have a life
—whatever situation we are in—
that would truly bring us joy and happiness.

cn.text: 我们今天讨论的内容
摘自一篇《守望台》文章
是跟婚姻有关的
文章谈到夫妻之间如果出现问题
可以怎样解决
加以改善
对于一般的人来说
他们结婚的时候已经预料到
有可能会遇到难题
产生矛盾
他们也早就想好
如果婚姻过得不顺心
或者自己觉得不幸福
就结束这段婚姻
他们这样做
是因为他们根本不认识耶和华
他们不知道耶和华有多么重视婚姻
如果我们回想一下
当初在伊甸园里
耶和华怎样创立婚姻安排
我们就能看出
耶和华不希望婚姻
只是为了个人利益和方便签定的合同
甚至婚姻也不仅仅是为了生儿育女
上帝不希望婚姻是个重担
比如亚当夏娃结婚后
在创世记2:24
上帝不是说
“所以人要离开父母
一辈子都必须和妻子绑在一起”
这样的话，结婚就好像被判无期徒刑
实际上
我们阅读上帝的话语就会发现
耶和华对第一对男女亚当和夏娃
怀有非常深厚的感情
他是这样说的
“所以人要离开父母
与妻子长相厮守
二人合为一体”
这段经文真的帮助我们更加认识耶和华
爱是他最主要的特质
他按照自己的形象创造了人类
让人类也能够有爱心
亚当和夏娃可以建立起非常深厚的爱
让他们乐意长相厮守
二人仿佛合为一体
夫妻都不完美
又生活在“终结的时期”
所以必须加深彼此间的爱
这样他们才可以在“身受患难”时保持忍耐
并成功应对其他常见的婚姻难题
如果我们仔细沉思
就会更加认识我们的上帝耶和华
他非常有爱心
也向他的子民表达爱心
我们可以说
耶和华在对待妻子方面
为丈夫们树立了最佳的典范
为什么可以这样说呢？
请考虑一下他怎样对待古代的以色列人
以赛亚书54:5
这样说
“你伟大的创造主就像是你的丈夫
天军的统帅耶和华是他的名号”
这节经文让我们想起
耶和华跟古代的以色列人立下的约
这是一个非常严肃的承诺
为什么要立约呢？
是因为爱
耶和华跟古代的以色列人立约的时候
就清楚地告诉了他们这一点
现在请打开申命记到7:7,8
请留意耶和华通过摩西说的话
“耶和华关心你们
挑选你们
不是因为你们在万族中人数最多
其实你们在万族中人数最少
耶和华是因为爱你们
并履行向你们祖先发的誓”
是因为爱
因为爱
耶和华和亚伯拉罕立下了约
之后
他又和以撒、雅各
大卫等忠心的人立约
因为爱
他和古代的以色列人立下了约
耶和华看到那些衷心爱戴他的人
就任用他们来实现自己对人类的旨意
耶和华把最好的给他们
他照顾他们
亲近他们
与他立约的子民就仿佛是他的妻子
他们对他不忠
离弃他的时候
耶和华都非常伤心
耶和华的爱
又纯洁
又深厚
所以他的子民背叛他的时候
他非常悲痛
上帝希望他的子民了解这一点
但后来北方的以色列国背叛了他
他们完全忘记耶和华是怎样的上帝
在宣布判决之前
耶和华告诉以色列人他们做了哪些恶事
以及他有什么感受
他是怎么做的呢？
他委派给先知何西阿
一个非常困难的任务
请打开何西阿书
到第1章
读的时候请留意何西阿是怎么做的
“耶和华开始通过何西阿传达他的话
耶和华对何西阿说
你去娶妻子吧
她将来会淫乱
你会抚养她淫乱生的儿女
因为这片土地的人民也淫乱
完全离弃了耶和华”
你可以想象吗？
何西阿非常贞洁
还没结过婚
但现在却要去娶一个女子
而这个女子以后会背叛他
这就是他收到的任务
耶和华用一个非常特别的方式
让叛逆的以色列人知道他的感受
以及他们的行为给他带来多大的伤害
这不是演戏
而是真实的人物
我们可以想象
何西阿的邻居会怎么想、怎么看
何西阿是上帝的先知
而他的妻子
却一再欺骗他
背叛他
这样的事会让任何正义的人都痛心不已
耶和华帮助那些因为这样的事而痛心的人
他说
“这块土地会被毁灭
你们会被流放
但我会把你们领回来”
何西阿书3:1说
“耶和华对我说
尽管那个女人继续跟情夫通奸
你还是要去爱她
就像以色列人虽然归附了其他神
贪爱葡萄饼
耶和华还是爱他们一样”
耶和华很爱他们
后来
那些衷心爱戴上帝的人
从流放之地又回到耶路撒冷
可以继续崇拜耶和华
如果我们沉思以色列人的历史
就能够看出
耶和华绝对有正当的理由弃绝他们
但他没有这样做
为什么呢？
因为还有别的因素要考虑
耶和华和以色列人之间的关系非常重要
他要实现自己对人类的旨意
而弥赛亚会从以色列人中产生
所以，尽管以色列人跟周围的民族来往
并崇拜巴力等其他假神
变得不忠
耶和华还是说
“我要领她回来，继续善待她”
但是
耶和华的容忍也是有限度的
上帝的独生子耶稣来到地上时
以色列人甚至把他处死
这让耶和华再也不能容忍他们了
从耶稣的反应
我们就能清楚知道
耶和华有多么痛苦和难过
路加福音19:41,42这样说
“快到耶路撒冷的时候
耶稣看着城，为城哭泣，说
但愿你今天看出关系到平安的事
但这些事现在是隐藏的
使你看不见”
到这个时候已经太晚了
耶和华和以色列人的关系快要结束了
这真的令人伤心
耶和华用夫妻之间的关系
来比喻他和以色列人之间的关系
这真的帮助我们更加认识他
我们看出耶和华多么爱我们！
他非常珍视我们
而且他也很渴望实现自己的旨意
帮助全人类
耶和华很关心那些“身受患难”的人
他特别关心那些
因为配偶不忠而受到伤害的人
耶和华完全理解他们的感受
而且他也会帮助他们
从伤痛中走出来
并帮助他们作出明智的选择
很多时候，耶和华都会赐福给他们
委派给他们新的工作岗位
甚至赐给他们一个同样爱耶和华的配偶
让他们能摆脱痛苦
继续忠心服务
所以我们要效法上帝培养爱心
以他的观点看待婚姻
这样我们就能更加亲近耶和华
耶和华不希望我们把婚姻
或者自己的工作岗位
看作重担或无期徒刑
不管我们处于怎样的环境当中
如果我们不断地培养爱心
就能够让我们的婚姻
带给我们幸福和喜乐

title: 첫 방문: 하느님의 목적—창 1:28

en.text: Today, we’re discussing
what God’s purpose is for humans.
What’s your opinion?
Hmm. I think we’re here to help
each other cope with life’s problems.
You know, that’s a thoughtful viewpoint,
and it’s understandable because life today is filled with tests.
But the Bible shows that the kind of life we live today
is not what God intended.
Really?
Yes.
In fact, notice what the Bible says here
at Genesis 1:28.
Morgan, would you please read the first part of the verse?
Sure.
It says: “God blessed them,
“and God said to them:
“‘Be fruitful and become many,
fill the earth and subdue it.’”
Thank you.
So according to this verse,
what did God want Adam and Eve to do?
Hmm. “Be fruitful” and “fill the earth.”
That’s right.
In other words, God’s purpose was for Adam and his descendants
to expand the garden of Eden until the whole earth was a paradise.
Of course, things didn’t work out that way.
But does that mean God’s purpose failed?
Or will it one day be fulfilled?
Maybe we can talk about that on our next visit.
OK, sounds good.

我平时都得上班, 只能周末陪陪她 Wǒ píngshí dōu děi shàngbān, zhǐnéng zhōumò péipei tā

title: “값진 진주”를 발견한 사람들

ko.text: 하지만 사람들을 위해 봉사하고 싶은 마음이 있었기 때문에
하지만 여러 교회들의 거짓 교리와 위선 때문에
이제 더 이상 종교를 알아볼 일은 없을 거라고 생각했지만요.
그러다 캘리포니아 포튼저 요양 병원에서 일할 때
드디어 그토록 찾아 헤매던 진리를 발견했죠.
죽은 사람의 상태에 관한 성경의 진리를 알려 주었죠.
여기저기서 연이어 켜지는 것 같았다고 말했습니다.
메리는 의료 분야에서 품었던 목표를 뒤로하고
전 시간 복음 전파자로 살아가는 삶을 선택했습니다.
어떤 사람들은 적극적으로 진리를 찾는 반면,
제가 진리를 찾고 있었던 것은 아니지만,
힘든 선수 생활을 하며 꿈꿔 왔던
전 지금 다른 사람을 돕는 일을 하면서

en.text: Some individuals search for years
before finding Kingdom truth.
Consider Mary Kennedy.
She came to the United States from Scotland
in the early 1900’s at the age of 18
and found work as a housekeeper.
She dreamed of becoming a missionary.
She found flaws in religion.
Still wanting to help others,
Mary began training in the medical field.
And in 1910, she graduated
from the Boston City Hospital Training School for Nurses.
She continued to search for truth
but was disappointed by false doctrines
and the hypocrisy she found in many churches.
She kept reading her Bible
even though she thought she was finished with religion.
While working at the Pottenger’s Sanatorium in California,
she found
what she’d been looking for.
She came in contact
with a nurse and Bible Student
named Nellie Hanford.
One day,
Nellie shared with her
what the Bible says
about the condition of the dead.
Mary said that it was like
a telephone switchboard in her mind,
with one light after another turning on.
Instantly she knew she’d found the truth.
She abandoned all her ambitions in medicine
and began a lifelong career
as a full-time minister of the Bible.
Some, like Mary,
actively search for the truth.
Others find it even though they weren’t looking for it.
My life revolved around volleyball at the highest national level.
Training every day, traveling regularly,
and playing matches
meant that everything else
had to take second place.
I wasn’t really searching for the truth,
but my girlfriend started studying the Bible.
I thought, ‘I’d really like to know more about this.’
I discovered that it’s just like a jigsaw puzzle,
where all the pieces fit neatly into place.
Daniel chapter 2 in particular intrigued me,
and I realized that it was important to do more with what I was learning.
So I had to decide between a temporary life in this world
or eternal life under God’s Kingdom.
I needed to make changes in how I spent my time and in my priorities.
I was quite self-centered.
Right when I decided to stop,
I got a lucrative offer to play with the defending champions for a year.
I could finally achieve all the things
I had been working hard for all those years:
recognition and a good income.
But I still decided to refuse their offer.
Before I came into the truth,
I thought I knew how to achieve success.
But Jehovah knows the best way to succeed in life.
I’m very glad that I’m now able to spend my time helping others,
and that’s what brings true happiness.
And now my wife and I serve Jehovah full-time,
which is the best way you can use your life.
Jehovah drew both Mary and Björn to the truth.
Both of them
focused on the value, not the cost,
of Kingdom truth.

cn.text: 有些人用了好多年的时间才找到王国真理
一位女士名叫玛丽·肯尼迪
她在上个世纪初从苏格兰来到美国
找到一个家务员的工作
当时她18岁
她的梦想是成为一名传教士
但却发现教会有很多问题
不过，玛丽仍然很想帮助别人
于是，她接受了医疗方面的培训
在1910年，她从波士顿的一个护理培训学校毕业
当时她继续寻找真理
但是她对教会的错误教义和虚伪行径特别失望
她仍然喜欢读圣经
不过她觉得自己不会加入任何教会
她在加利福尼亚的一所疗养院工作的时候
终于找到了一直渴求的真理
她认识了一个护士
是一位圣经研究者
名叫内莉·汉福德
有一天
内莉跟玛丽分享了圣经中人死后的情况
玛丽说
她的内心好像电话的线路都接通了一样
心中的结一个又一个地打开
她立刻就看出自己找到了真理
于是放弃了在医疗方面的追求
并且从此开始全时传讲圣经真理
有些人，像玛丽一样
热切地寻求真理
也有些人没有寻求，但是也找到了
我曾经是一个职业排球运动员
我每天训练，经常到不同地方比赛
对我来说，没有任何事比排球更重要
我当时并没有在寻找真理
但是我的女朋友开始学习圣经
所以，我也很想了解一下
我发现，真理就像是拼图一样
每一块部件都能放在合适的位置上
我对但以理书2章的预言特别感兴趣
后来我看出，我应该实践所学到的真理
我也要在这个世上的短暂一生
和上帝王国里的永远生命之间作出选择
我当时的生活都只顾自己
所以我需要改变
调整生活的重心
正当我打算退役的时候
国内最好的球队想跟我签一年的高薪合约
看来我这么多年的努力
终于有机会得到回报
可以名利双收
但我还是拒绝了这份合约
认识真理之前
我以为我知道怎样获得成功
但耶和华才真正知道什么才是成功
我非常高兴现在能付出时间帮助其他人
这为我带来真正的快乐
现在我和妻子都全时为耶和华服务
这真的是最棒的生活方式！
耶和华吸引玛丽和比约恩认识真理
他们两个关注的
不是付出的代价
而是王国真理的价值

title: 케네스 쿡 2세: 여러분은 앞에 놓인 일들을 직면할 준비가 되었습니다

ko.text: 오늘은 여러분이 절대 잊지 못할 특별한 날입니다.
사실 학교의 전체 과정을 잊지 못하시겠죠.
오늘 영적 프로그램을 통해 우리 모두가 유익을 얻게 될 것입니다.
참석한 모두가 유익을 얻게 될 것이지만,
이 프로그램은 특히 여러분을 위해 마련된 것입니다.
모든 연사가 기도하고 묵상하면서 여러분을 위한 연설을 준비했습니다.
하지만 우리 모두도 프로그램을 통해 유익을 얻게 될 것입니다.
오늘 프로그램은 여러분에게 두고두고 깊은 인상을 남길 것입니다.
여호와께 영광을 돌리고 그분의 사랑을 확신시켜 줄 것입니다.
많은 성경 기록에서 원칙을 이끌어 내는 훈련을 받았습니다.
여러분은 성구를 보는 새로운 방법을 배웠습니다.
여호와께서는 우리가 성구의 내용을 주의 깊이 살피고
그 기록들은 여러분처럼 하느님의 도움을 받아
그분의 뜻을 성공적으로 수행한 그분의 종들에게 초점을 맞추고 있습니다.
여러분은 그리스도인 생활, 다른 사람을 어떻게 가르치는지,
일을 어떻게 조직하는지 등에 관한 원칙들을 조사해 보았습니다.
이 졸업식에서도 원칙들에 초점을 맞출 것입니다.
제가 간단히 말씀드릴 내용의 주제를 알려 드리죠.
“여러분은 앞에 놓인 일들을 직면할 준비가 되었습니다”입니다.
유의할 점은 앞에 놓인 일들을 직면할 준비가 되었냐고 묻는 것이 아니라
그처럼 자신 있게 말하는 이유가 뭘까요?

en.text: Well, class 151,
you seem excited, and you should be.
This is a very special day for you —one you’ll never forget.
Just as with the entire course of Gilead, you’ll never forget.
And we’re happy to be with you today.
And we will all benefit from the things that are said today
at this spiritual program.
But even so, we know that although this will benefit everyone involved,
the program has been designed with you in mind.
So with every talk given,
the brothers have prayerfully considered what can be said to encourage.
And as you listen, just be certain that the brothers have had that in mind.
But all of us listening today will benefit
from the good things that will come out in this program.
When the day is over, you’ll look back and recall a program
that honored Jehovah and confirmed his love for you.
And again, you’re never going to forget it.
During the past five months of your schooling, you were asked to draw out
principles from many different Bible accounts.
And you worked hard to do that, didn’t you?
You learned new ways to do that,
to see the Scriptures
as something that Jehovah wants us to listen to very carefully
and then apply its fine points in our lives.
So those accounts focused on genuine servants of God
who with his help succeeded in doing His will.
And you were doing the same.
You examined principles for Christian living,
you examined principles for teaching others,
you looked at principles
about how to organize the work, and so forth.
This graduation program will do the same.
With that in mind, I have a theme for these brief introductory comments.
I thought it would keep me focused.
So here’s my theme:
“You Are Ready to Face the Things Ahead.”
Now, notice that it’s not a question: Are you ready?
It’s a statement: You are ready to face the things ahead.
Now, why can we say this with such confidence?
Because we see your faith.
We see your deep love for our heavenly Father, Jehovah,
and his Son.
You’ve trusted in Jehovah, you have done well,
and you’ve made it to graduation day.
I know some of you wondered if you would make it, but you did.
Here you are.
You’re graduating with the 151st class of Gilead.
What a delight!
You undoubtedly agree more than ever before with what the apostle Paul wrote
at Philippians 4:13,
where he said: “For all things I have the strength through [who?]
the one who gives me power.”
And we know who that is.
Jehovah has surely helped you during these months
to make a success of Gilead school.
And we’re very proud of you for that.
You can be certain that Jehovah is just delighted to see that
because you love him
and you went through this course, you’ve gone through it
with that in mind, true?
Jehovah gave you what you needed,
and that’s a blessing you must never forget.
By remembering it, you will put that blessing to work for you
wherever you are in your service to Jehovah
in the weeks, months, and years ahead.
Really, these things you learn and that all of us learn now
will serve us well forever.
For example, whenever you face a task in the future
that seems almost too large for you to tackle or handle,
you’ll remember how Jehovah helped you in this school.
Your experience in going through Gilead
now adds to your extensive experience,
the experience you already had in serving Jehovah,
but this just enriches it that much more.
It will help you as you face
trials and tests ahead
in that you’ll know you can make it through what you may view as difficult times
because Jehovah will help you to do it.
You are growing ever more and more ready to face the things ahead.
You already are, but you’ll grow more and more so, like all of us will,
as you reflect on and remember what Jehovah has done for you,
such as helping you to complete this Bible school course.
Here’s an example of things you must be ready to handle or you may face.
Soon after your graduation, you will be off to your assignments.
And as you go,
have in mind Jesus’ words, where he taught his disciples to pray:
“Do not bring us into temptation,
but deliver us from the wicked one.”
Now focus on the words
“temptation” and “wicked one.”
They go together, don’t they?
Temptation and wicked one.
Satan, “the wicked one,” doesn’t like your success here at Gilead.
You can be certain that he hates this school
and all the good that it has accomplished through the years in honoring Jehovah
and benefiting His people and those in the field.
So, then, what temptations or stumbling blocks
might Satan try to place before you
now that you’ve graduated from this school?
Well, here are a few things, and they are things
that all of us must face.
For example,
if you’re not careful, you might be tempted
to become self-satisfied with what you have accomplished.
Don’t ever let that happen to you.
Never be self-satisfied.
Keep setting goals for yourself.
Strive to please Jehovah more and more each day
in all that you do.
It’s the principles that we draw from God’s Word
that help us to do that.
Yet, here’s a caution: Your healthy desire to keep setting goals
must not be allowed to lead you into the next temptation.
And that is this: the temptation to give in to pride.
That can happen.
It can happen to a person when he or she forgets
who has truly helped them to succeed
—and that is Jehovah.
Those who forget about Jehovah may become
ambitious and try to outshine others.
We must never allow that to happen to our heart and mind.
We must never become like that.
In fact, we must fight against pride.
And one key way to do this
is to remember that in all that you do —in all that we do—
it is always about Jehovah.
When we have that focus,
we will succeed in doing things his way, the right way,
no matter what we face in the future.
So we reflect on his blessings.
We see how he’s strengthened us.
We’re confident he will continue to do so, and he will do that for you.
But we never forget that he’s in charge.
It’s always about Jehovah.
And so we do everything out of love for him.
And that, of course, leads into love for others,
because he loves others.
If a person fails to remember how Jehovah has blessed him or her,
that person might become big in their own eyes, like King Saul did.
You’ll recall his example.
Where did that eventually lead Saul?
It led him away from Jehovah’s favor and blessing.
People like Saul fail to maintain faith.
They fail to remain humble.
What about your faith and your humility?
Well, we see those good qualities in you,
and that’s why we confidently state that you’re ready to face the things ahead.
Along with Jehovah’s blessing, your faith will help you to conquer
any temptation that the wicked one, “the Tempter,” may place before you,
and your humility will help you
to remain unbreakable.
You will be able to defeat the Tempter.
Along with resisting temptation,
your Gilead training will also help you
to continue supporting our vital work for Jehovah’s Kingdom,
his people, and for those who will yet listen.
In fact, for all of God’s people,
this is the greater purpose behind any training
that we receive from him, right?
So, then, wherever you serve,
never forget the purpose behind the blessings
that you have experienced in this school.
Trust in Jehovah and in his Son to help you at all times.
Use your Gilead training in the branches and territories where you are going.
Keep in mind that with God’s help, the One who gives you power,
you are ready to face the things ahead.
Well, we will say a little bit more about this at the conclusion of the program.
Now we’re going to enjoy a series of encouraging talks that for all of us
will strengthen our faith, build up our trust in God,
and highlight his wonderful purpose that we support.

titles.ko: 케네스 쿡 2세: 여러분은 앞에 놓인 일들을 직면할 준비가 되었습니다

title: 게리트 뢰시: 결코 없어지지 않는 사랑을 기르십시오

ko.text: 아기들, 청소년들, 부부들도 사랑받을 때 더 잘 살아갑니다.
사랑은 받는 사람을 행복하게 해 줄 뿐 아니라
우리가 생명을 누리고 그분을 사랑할 수 있도록 창조하셨습니다.
우리의 사랑을 필요로 하지 않지만 그 사랑을 소중히 여기십니다.
우린 다른 사람들에게 좋은 일을 하고 그들을 사랑하는 걸 사랑하죠.
사랑은 늘 존재해 왔고 사랑에는 시작이 없습니다.
하느님이 존재하시는 동안 사랑도 늘 존재했습니다.
여호와께서는 사랑을 갖고 계실 뿐 아니라
여호와께선 그분의 형상에 따라 우릴 창조하셨고,
우리는 그 사랑을 반영할 수 있는 놀라운 역량을 갖고 있습니다.
세상의 책, 영화, 노래도 사랑을 자주 다루죠.
오늘날 하느님과 이웃에 대한 진정한 사랑은 찾아보기 어렵죠.
“마지막 날”에 관해 묘사한 디모데 후서 3:2의 예언과 일치하게
내가 먼저라는 태도가 널리 퍼져 있죠.
‘우선 나 먼저, 그다음엔 또 나, 그다음엔 뭐 다른 누구.’
디모데 후서 3:2에서 바울은 사람들이 “돈을 사랑”할 것이라고도 했습니다.
또 같은 예언에서 대부분의 사람이 “하느님을 사랑하기보다는
많은 사람의 삶에서 오락과 스포츠는 가장 중요한 부분을 차지하죠.
두 가지 사랑이 서로 경쟁하고 있다는 걸 알 수 있는데,
여호와에 대한 사랑과 세상에 대한 사랑입니다.
우리는 세상에 대한 사랑을 더 잘 물리칠 수 있습니다.
하느님에 대한 사랑을 최대한 키우라고 권하셨죠.
“네 마음을 다하고 영혼을 다하고 정신을 다해
왕국 진리의 씨앗이 뿌려진 우리의 마음이라는 좋은 흙을
두 사람 사이의 사랑은 어떻게 자랍니까?
여호와께서는 우리에게 성경과 그분의 조직을 통해 말씀하시죠.
우리가 매일 성경을 읽고 공부하고, 회중 집회에 참석한다면
그분에 대한 우리의 사랑은 계속 자랄 것입니다.
곧 여러분의 사랑이 … 더욱더 풍성하게 되는 것입니다.”
어느 정도만 사랑하는 게 아니라 사랑이 풍성해져야 합니다.
1만 달란트의 빚을 기꺼이 탕감해 주려는 왕에 비하셨습니다.
우리에 대한 그분의 큰 사랑을 잘 보여 주죠.
예수께서는 우리의 죄를 위해 죽으심으로 사랑을 보이셨습니다.
더 많이 용서받은 사람은 더 많이 사랑합니다.
하지만 죄를 용서받아야만 사랑하는 것은 아닙니다.
용서를 받아야 하는 죄를 단 하나도 짓지 않으셨죠.
하지만 그분은 여호와와 우리 모두를 사랑하셨습니다.
그분은 죽기 전 밤에 요한 14:31에서 “내가 아버지를 사랑한다”고 하셨죠.
하느님의 사랑에 보답해 우리도 어떻게 그분을 사랑할 수 있습니까?
온 마음을 다해 그분을 섬김으로 그렇게 할 수 있습니다.
“전파하고 가르치는 가장 중요한 이유는 이웃에 대한 사랑 때문이다.”
전파하는 가장 중요한 동기는 무엇보다 여호와에 대한 사랑입니다.
그리고 전파하는 가장 중요한 목표는 여호와를 찬양하는 것이죠.
우린 여호와를 영광스럽게 하고 그분의 주권이 입증되기를 바랍니다.
그래도 우린 형제들에게 사랑을 보여야 합니다.
한 회중에서는 몇몇 자매들이 매일 돌아가면서
몸이 마비된 형제를 위해 따뜻한 음식을 준비해 주었습니다.
사랑이 전파 활동으로만 나타나는 게 아님을 보여 주죠.
강도의 공격을 받아 다친 남자를 돌봐 준
사마리아 사람은 강도를 당한 남자에게 전파한 것은 아니지만
예수는 이웃에 대한 사랑에는 적들을 사랑하는 것이 포함됨을 알려 주셨죠.
여러분을 박해하는 사람들을 위하여 기도하십시오”라고 하셨습니다.
적들까지 사랑한다면 우리의 사랑이 완전해질 것입니다.
여호와께선 악한 반대자들에게까지 햇볕과 비를 주십니다.
한 전도인은 병원에 입원한 한 자매의 반대하는 남편을 찾아갔는데,
그 남자는 이러한 친절한 행동에 깊이 감사했습니다.
그분은 이유 없이 미움과 박해와 모욕과 죽임을 당하셨습니다.
예수께서 우리를 위해 하신 일에 감사를 나타내도록
관심자들에게 대속 때문에 여호와께서 우리의 죄를 용서하시고
영원한 생명의 길을 열어 주셨다는 점을 알려 주십시오.
대속에 관해 이야기할 때 단지 법적인 측면에서만 설명하지 마십시오.
“저울 한쪽에는 아담이, 다른 한쪽에는 예수가 있는데요.
아담이 잃은 것을 되찾기 위해 생명을 바쳐야 했죠.”
그 일에 대한 감사와 사랑을 기르도록 도우십시오.
예수께서 처형되기 전에 어떤 일을 겪으셨는지 함께 살펴보십시오.
피가 흐르는 살점이 너덜거리는 모습을 상상해 보도록 도와주십시오.
그분이 어떻게 조롱을 받으셨는지 상상해 보게 하십시오.
고통스러운 채찍질 후에 군인들은 그분을 조롱하며 이렇게 말했습니다.
또 그분에게 침을 뱉고 그분의 뺨을 때렸습니다.
군인들이 그분의 손과 발에 큰 못을 박는 모습을 상상해 보게 도와주십시오.
형주를 똑바로 세우자 고통은 극에 달했습니다.
체중으로 못이 박힌 상처가 찢어졌기 때문입니다.
하지만 예수께서는 로마 군인들을 위해 이렇게 기도하셨습니다.
… 자기들이 무슨 일을 하고 있는지 모릅니다.”
예수께서 우릴 위해 하신 일을 묵상해 보면
그분에 대한 사랑이 더욱 깊어지지 않습니까?
그리스도께서 보여 주신 사랑이 지식을 초월하며
우리의 마음속에 깊은 울림을 준다는 것입니다.
예수께서 하신 일은 우리에게 깊은 영향을 줍니다.
그리스도께서 우릴 위해 하신 일을 생각해 보면
병 고침이나 방언과 같은 영의 선물에 관해 언급한 다음
왜냐하면 예언과 같은 영의 선물들은 없어질 것이기 때문입니다.
여호와께서는 영원히 계시며 그분의 사랑은 결코 없어지지 않을 것입니다.
“믿음, 희망, 사랑, 이 셋은 남아 있습니다.
그런데 이 중에 가장 큰 것은 사랑입니다.”
또 바울은 ‘사랑은 결코 없어지지 않고, 모든 것을 인내한다’고 썼습니다.
그리고 오늘날 러시아와 같은 나라에서 고통을 겪어 왔죠.
오늘날 여러 정부들이 진리를 억압하고 있습니다.
마지막 때에 살고 있는 우리에게 놀라운 일이 아니죠.
큰 환난이 가까워 올수록 더욱 심해질 겁니다.
많은 나라에서 상황이 점점 악화되고 있으며
결코 없어지지 않는 사랑의 탁월한 길을 추구하고 있습니다.
우리는 영원히 살 뿐만 아니라 영원히 사랑하고 영원히 사랑받을 것입니다.

en.text: Do you want to be loved by others?
Naturally, we all want to be loved.
Love is a basic human need.
Babies thrive on it. Teenagers thrive on it.
Marriage mates thrive on it.
Bethelites and Gilead students thrive on it.
It makes us happy to be loved.
What about loving others?
Love is unselfish.
Loving others makes the receivers happy,
but it also makes us as givers happy.
Love is the reason why we exist.
Jehovah created us out of unselfish love
to let us share not only life
but also the privilege to love him.
Jehovah does not need our love since he does not depend on anybody else,
but he appreciates our love.
He loves to be loved by us.
He created us also with the ability
to love others besides him.
We love to do good to others.
We love to love them.
Since when does love exist?
It always existed.
It had no beginning.
Why?
Because “God is love.”
And we know God had no beginning,
so God’s love had no beginning.
There was no time in the past when God existed but love did not.
Jehovah not only has love,
but he is love personified.
Jehovah created us in his image.
This is why we have this superb privilege
to reflect his love.
In the world, books, movies, and songs often deal with love.
But what kind of love?
Usually romantic love—love that often fails.
Genuine love of God and of neighbor
is widely lacking today.
When describing “the last days,”
the prophecy at 2 Timothy 3:2 has come true
that people are often “lovers of themselves.”
Me-ism and egotism is widespread.
One journal carries the title Self.
People think, ‘First me, then nothing,
and then me again, and then perhaps somebody else.’
At 2 Timothy 3:2, Paul also wrote
that people would be “lovers of money.”
In the same prophecy, it says that the majority
would be “lovers of pleasures rather than lovers of God.”
For many, entertainment and sports
have become the dominant aspect of their lives.
Furthermore, 1 John 2:15 indicates
that there is a battle between two loves
—love of Jehovah and love of the world.
The stronger our love for Jehovah is,
the better we will be able to resist the love of the world.
At Matthew 22:37,
Jesus encouraged cultivating love for God
to the fullest extent possible.
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
and with your whole mind.”
How does love for Jehovah grow?
We must tend to the good soil of our heart
where the seed of Kingdom truth was sown.
How does love between two persons grow?
One way is by communication.
We communicate with Jehovah through prayer.
Jehovah communicates with us
through the Bible and his organization.
If we study the Bible and read it daily
as well as attend the congregation meetings,
our love for him will continue to grow.
Love needs to grow.
It is not a matter of how much we know
but how much we love what we know.
Head knowledge is not enough.
There needs to be heart knowledge.
Growing in love is a process.
A plant grows when it is watered;
love grows if it is watered with the water of truth.
At Philippians 1:9, Paul says:
“And this is what I continue praying,
that your love may abound yet more and more.”
Love grows gradually.
It is not enough to have a little love;
we should abound in love.
Jehovah sets the example.
He expressed his love by providing the ransom.
In Matthew chapter 18,
Jesus compares Jehovah with a king who was willing to forgive a debt
of 60 million denarii,
or 10,000 silver talents.
This certainly impresses his love for us.
Jesus expressed his love by being willing
to die for our sins.
This stirs our love in return.
The more one has been forgiven, the more one will love.
But love is not dependent on having one’s sins forgiven.
Jesus loved Jehovah so much
but had not a single sin that needed to be forgiven.
But he loved Jehovah, and he loved us.
The night before he died, he said at John 14:31:
“I love the Father.”
Do we not (all of us) feel the same?
How can we demonstrate our love of God in return?
We can do so by serving Jehovah with all our heart.
This includes preaching and teaching.
True or false?
The most important reason for preaching and teaching is
love of neighbor.
It sounds good, but it is wrong.
The most important motive for preaching
is, first of all, love for Jehovah.
And the most important objective
is to praise Jehovah.
We want to glorify him and to support the vindication of his sovereignty.
Love of neighbor comes second.
But we also need to show love to our brothers.
In one congregation, several sisters
took daily turns to prepare a hot meal
for a quadriplegic brother.
This shows that our love extends beyond preaching.
It is like with the parable of the Samaritan
who cared for the man who was assaulted and hurt by robbers.
The Samaritan did not preach to the man who fell among the robbers.
He just showed unselfish love to him.
Jesus emphasized that our neighborly love
should include even enemies.
At Matthew 5:44, he said:
“I say to you: Continue to love your enemies
and to pray for those persecuting you.”
Our love will be perfect
if we love even our enemies.
Jehovah gives sunshine and rain
even to wicked opposers.
One publisher went to a hospital to visit an opposing husband.
The man appreciated this kind gesture very much.
Think of what Jesus has endured.
He was hated without cause, persecuted, reviled, and murdered.
Help people to develop their appreciation
for what Jesus did for us.
Show interested ones that because of the ransom,
Jehovah forgives us our sins
and opens the way to everlasting life.
When you talk about the ransom, don’t do it just in a legalistic way
by saying: “See, like on scales,
“on one side was Adam and on the other side was Jesus.
“God’s justice required that by giving his life,
Jesus restored what Adam had lost.”
Rather, make the student meditate
and develop heart appreciation and love for what Jesus did.
Review with a student what Jesus went through prior to his execution.
Help him picture in his mind how Jesus was flogged,
producing quivering ribbons of bleeding flesh.
Help the student sense how Jesus was mocked.
After his tortured beating,
soldiers said to him mockingly:
“Good day, you King of the Jews!”
Also, they spit on him and slapped him in the face.
Remind the student how the soldiers later pounded large nails
into his hands and into his feet.
With the stake swung upright, the pain was excruciating,
for the weight of the body tore all the nail wounds.
Yet, rather than threaten, Jesus prayed for the Roman soldiers:
“Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”
Meditating on what Jesus did for us,
does this not greatly deepen our love for him?
At Ephesians 3:19, Paul wrote:
“The love of the Christ . . . surpasses knowledge.”
It is not the love for the Christ but the love that Jesus displayed
that surpasses head knowledge
and strikes a wonderful chord in our figurative heart.
Jesus’ course stimulates a response in us.
As we think about what Christ has done for us,
our love for him deepens.
In fact, 2 Corinthians 5:14 says:
“For the love the Christ has compels us.”
After mentioning gifts of the spirit, such as healing and speaking in tongues,
Paul explained at 1 Corinthians 12:31:
“Yet I will show you a surpassing way.”
What is this “way”?
The way of love.
In what way is it surpassing?
In the sense that the gifts of the spirit,
including prophesying, would be “done away with.”
But love would always be there.
Jehovah is eternal.
His love will never fail, never end,
but will continue forever and ever and ever.
Therefore, Paul wrote: “There remain
“faith, hope, love, these three;
but the greatest of these is love.”
He also wrote: “Love never fails.”
Love “endures all things.”
Many brothers suffered a lot during World War II
and also today in Russia and other countries.
Today, there are a number of governments in the world that suppress the truth.
As we live in the time of the end, this is not surprising to us.
It will get worse as the great tribulation comes closer.
World conditions are also getting worse in many parts of the world,
and COVID has claimed many human victims.
But we Witnesses keep enduring
by pursuing the surpassing way of love
that never fails.
We shall not only live forever
but also love forever and be loved forever.

cn.text: 你希望别人爱你吗？
当然
我们都想感受到爱
爱是人类的基本需求
婴儿需要爱
年轻人需要爱
夫妻需要爱
伯特利成员和基列学员也都需要爱
有了爱，我们才能生活快乐
爱别人又怎样呢？
爱是不自私的
爱不仅让接受的人感到快乐
也能让施与的人感受到快乐
爱是我们存在的理由
出于无私的爱，耶和华创造了我们
他让我们不仅享受生命，也能够爱他
耶和华不需要别人爱他
因为他根本不需要我们任何人
但他很珍视我们的爱
他喜欢我们爱戴他
上帝创造我们的时候
让我们不仅能爱他，也能爱别人
我们喜欢帮助别人，向他们表现爱心
什么时候有了爱呢？
爱没有开始，它一直都存在
为什么呢？
因为“上帝就是爱”
既然上帝没有开始
那上帝的爱也没有开始
上帝一直都存在
因此爱也一直都存在
耶和华不仅拥有爱的特质
他本身就是爱的化身
我们是按照耶和华的形象被创造的
因此我们能够反映出他的爱
世上有很多书籍、电影和歌曲
都是关于爱的
什么样的爱呢？
通常都是浪漫的爱
这种爱很难持久
今天，世上很少人会真的爱上帝、爱别人
提摩太后书3:2
谈到“最后的日子”时预言说
人会“专爱自己”
这个预言真的应验了
很多人都只关心自己，而不关心别人
一本杂志鼓励人取悦自己，叫《悦己》
对很多人来说
“最重要的是我，之后还是我
再之后才轮到别人”
在提摩太后书3:2保罗也说
到时人会“贪爱钱财”
在同一个预言里，圣经也说
大部分的人都会“爱享乐不爱上帝”
在很多人看来
生活中最重要的事就是娱乐和运动
约翰一书2:15也指出
会有两种彼此对抗的爱
对耶和华的爱和对世界的爱
我们对耶和华的爱越强烈
就越能够抵抗对世界的爱
在马太福音22:37，耶稣鼓励我们
要竭尽全力加深对上帝的爱
怎样让对耶和华的爱茁壮成长呢？
我们要保护好内心的土壤
让王国真理的种子可以生长
人和人之间的爱怎样加深呢？
一个方法就是经常交流
我们通过祷告跟耶和华交流
耶和华通过圣经和他的组织跟我们沟通
如果我们每天都研读圣经
并且参加会众的聚会
就能不断加深对耶和华的爱
爱需要成长
重要的不是我们学到多少
而是我们有多么喜爱自己学到的
光有知识是不够的
还要让知识打动我们的心
爱的成长是一个过程
要浇水，植物才能生长
爱也需要接受真理之水的浇灌才能生长
在腓立比书1:9，保罗说
爱会逐渐地成长
只有一点点爱是不够的
我们要越来越有爱心
耶和华为我们树立了榜样
他表现爱心，为我们提供了赎价
在马太福音18章
耶稣把耶和华比作一个国王
他赦免了一个奴隶6000万银元的债务
也就是1万塔兰特
可以看出，耶和华有多么爱我们
耶稣也表现爱心，甘愿为我们的罪而死
这激励我们以爱还爱
被赦免的罪越多，爱也就越多
但这并不是说，只有罪被赦免的人才会去爱
耶稣很爱耶和华，但他从来没有犯过罪
也就不需要获得赦免
但耶稣很爱耶和华，他也爱我们
在牺牲前的晚上
他在约翰福音14:31说
“我爱父亲”
我们大家也都爱耶和华
那么，我们可以怎么表明我们爱耶和华呢？
就是要全心全意为他服务
包括努力去传道教人
是非题
我们传道教人主要是出于对别人的爱
听起来不错，但这是不对的
我们传道的最主要原因
是因为我们爱耶和华
我们传道教人最主要的目的
就是赞美耶和华
我们很想荣耀耶和华
支持他的宇宙至高统治权
接下来就是爱别人
我们也需要对弟兄姐妹表现爱心
在一群会众，有几个姐妹
每天都轮流为一位瘫痪的弟兄做饭
可见，我们爱别人不只是向他们传道
在耶稣的比喻里，撒马利亚人很有爱心
他帮助那个遇劫的人
撒马利亚人并没有向这个遇劫的人传道
但他表现了无私的爱
耶稣强调，我们要爱的人
甚至包括我们的敌人在内
在马太福音5:44，他说
我们必须爱我们的敌人
我们的爱才会完全
耶和华甚至让不义的人也能享受阳光雨露
一个传道员去医院探望一个姐妹的丈夫
他本来反对妻子的信仰，但这次他非常感动
请想想耶稣的经历
他无缘无故地被人憎恨和辱骂
被人迫害和杀害
我们不仅要告诉别人耶稣为我们做了什么
也要帮他们培养感激之情
让感兴趣的人明白
通过赎价，耶和华可以赦免我们的罪
让我们有机会得享永远的生命
在解释赎价时
不要只是从法律的角度解释说
“这就好比一个天平，一边是亚当
另一边是耶稣
按照上帝的公正标准，耶稣献出生命
所以可以赎回亚当失去的”
相反，要让学生沉思耶稣经历的事
从而在内心里充满感激和爱
跟学生一起讨论耶稣被处死前发生的事
让他在脑海里想象耶稣怎样被人鞭打
被打得皮开肉绽、遍体鳞伤
帮助学生想一想，耶稣怎样被人辱骂
罗马士兵毒打过耶稣之后，还嘲笑他说
“犹太人的王啊，万岁！”
之后，他们还向他吐唾沫，并打他的耳光
让学生想象
罗马士兵把钉子钉进耶稣的手和脚的画面
木柱被竖起来时，耶稣有多么疼痛
因为他全身的重量都悬在钉子上
但耶稣不仅没有恐吓罗马士兵，反而祷告说
“父亲啊，求你宽恕他们
因为他们不知道自己在做什么”
沉思耶稣为我们所做的
能够大大加深我们对他的爱，对吗？
以弗所书3:19说
基督的爱是“超越知识”的
保罗说的不是我们对基督的爱
而是耶稣表现出来的爱，超越了知识
能够深深打动我们的心
耶稣所做的深深地影响了我们
沉思耶稣为我们所做的
我们就会更爱他
实际上，哥林多后书5:14说
“基督的爱仿佛催逼着我们”
在哥林多前书12章
使徒保罗列举了各种恩赐
包括治病救人和说外语
但在第31节他说
“我要告诉你们什么是至善之道”
是什么呢？
他说的就是爱
爱怎么是“至善之道”呢？
耶和华给人的许多恩赐
包括说预言的恩赐，都终必消失
但爱会永远存在下去
耶和华是永恒的，他的爱也绝不会停止
而是会永远、永远、永远地存在下去
因此，保罗写道
“现在存留的，有信心、希望和爱
这三样当中，最大的是爱”
保罗还说
“爱是永恒的”
爱“凡事忍耐”
二战期间，很多弟兄都受到迫害
今天在俄罗斯等国家也是这样
现在，世上的很多政府都限制我们的工作
这也毫不奇怪
因为我们生活在最后的日子
随着大患难越来越临近
在世上很多地方情况都会越来越糟糕
很多人已经死于冠状病毒病
但我们耶和华见证人会保持忍耐
并继续追求至善之道，就是永恒的爱
我们不仅会永远活着
而且会在爱和被爱中享受永远的生命

title: 가유스 글로켄틴: 여러분은 얼마나 자주 “실로”로 갑니까?

ko.text: 사람들은 그녀가 집을 떠나 전 시간 봉사를 하러 간다는 말에
이스라엘 여자들이 보통 추구하는 흔한 목표나 꿈이 아니라
사람들은 그녀를 지원하기 위해 어떻게 할지 생각합니다.
누가 등장하고 그들이 무엇을 했는지 알아보겠습니다.
그들이 한 일은 곧 졸업할 여러분이
임지로 가서 성공하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
1년에 4일씩 길르앗 사람 입다의 딸을 칭찬하러 갔던 것이다.”
이스라엘의 젊은 여자들은 입다의 딸을 칭찬하고 격려하기 위해
칭찬은 여호와를 섬기는 이 전 시간 종에게 힘을 주었습니다.
여러분도 다른 사람에게 힘을 주고 싶으시죠?
여러분은 정기적으로 다른 사람들을 칭찬하고 격려함으로
그들을 강하게 하고 조직을 안정시킬 것입니까?
다른 사람을 강하게 하는 데 어떤 칭찬이 효과적일까요?
이스라엘의 젊은 여자들을 어떻게 본받을 수 있습니까?
다른 사람을 강하게 하는 데 어떤 칭찬이 효과적일까요?
예수께서 세우신 본을 살펴보기 위해 마가복음 5장을 보겠습니다.
그분은 자신의 겉옷을 만지고 두려워하는 아픈 여자를 칭찬하셨습니다.
효과적으로 칭찬하는 데 도움이 되는 5가지 요소를
예수께선 그 여자가 한 일을 칭찬하셨습니다.
그 여자는 실제로 정말 큰 믿음을 나타냈습니다.
그 여자가 율법을 어긴 것에 대해 조언하지 않으셨죠?
그러셨다면 그분의 칭찬은 진실하게 들리지 않았을 것입니다.
여자에 대한 그분의 따뜻한 관심이 녹아 있는 표현입니다.
예수께서는 그 여자의 필요를 아시고 병을 고쳐 주심으로 행동하셨습니다.
예수께서 여자를 칭찬하신 건 자신을 돋보이게 하려는 것이 아니었죠.
그 여자에게 관심을 가지셨고 그를 안심시키려는 것이었습니다.
어떻게 이스라엘의 젊은 여자들을 본받을 수 있는지에 대한 답을 찾아보죠.
네, 여기에는 “정기적으로, 계속해서”라는 의미가 들어 있죠.
젊은 여자들은 입다의 딸을 반복해서 격려한 것입니다.
여러분도 임지로 가면 베델이나 회중이나 야외 봉사에서
함께 일하는 사람들을 반복해서 칭찬할 수 있습니까?
예를 들어 그들이 나타낸 열심, 노력, 사랑의 행동에 대해
이런 격려적인 메시지도 보낼 수 있습니다.
아마 간단한 말도 함께 보내면 좋겠죠?
이런 메시지는 많은 시간과 노력이 들지 않지만,
다른 사람을 계속 칭찬하는 것은 좋은 일이죠.
1년에 4일씩 길르앗 사람 입다의 딸을 칭찬하러 갔던 것이다.”
가족적인 책임을 뒤로 하고 그렇게 하는 데는 희생이 따랐을 것입니다.
그들은 실로까지 여행해야 했고 선물도 가져갔을 겁니다.
때때로 약간의 시간과 노력을 들여야 하거나
개인적인 희생을 치러야 할 수도 있다는 점을 생각나게 해 줍니다.
네, 누군가에게 전화를 하거나 그 사람을 방문하려면
형제 자매들과 시간을 보내는 건 선물을 주는 것과 같습니다.
형제 자매들과 함께 봉사하고 그들과 함께 일하고
그들을 기쁘게 해 주고 크게 칭찬하는 것과 같습니다.
“때에 맞게 하는 말이 어찌 그리 좋은가!”
입다의 딸이 즉시 필요한 지원을 받았다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
기회가 생길 때 바로 하는 것이 가장 좋습니다.
단지 간단한 몇 마디 말이라도 말입니다.
보통 누군가에게 긍정적인 말을 빨리 해 줄수록,
그 사람은 불안감이나 의구심을 빨리 떨쳐 내게 됩니다.
또한 그만큼 빨리 행복해지고 기분이 좋아지죠.
따라서 너무 오래 기다리지 말고 즉시 행동하십시오.
이제 세 번째이자 마지막 질문으로 왜 정기적으로 칭찬하는 것이 좋습니까?
여러분이 임지로 가면 “입다의 딸”과 같은 많은 사람들을 만나게 될 것입니다.
그들은 바로 희생적으로 여호와를 섬기는 충실한 전 시간 종들입니다.
여러분은 회중에서 이런 형제 자매들을 만나게 될 것입니다.
불안과 염려가 많은 사람들을 만날 겁니다.
때때로 그들은 자신이 무가치하다고 느끼기도 하죠.
그들은 여러 어려움에도 충실을 유지하기 위해 최선을 다하고 있습니다.
자신의 불완전성, 실수로 인해 겪는 일들
그리고 때로는 여러 상황으로 인한 낙담과 싸우면서요.
선한 일을 하려는 우리의 열망을 강하게 해 줍니다.
또 우리가 계속 최선을 다하도록 격려해 주죠.
형제 자매들과 가깝게 일하다 보면 무엇을 보게 될까요?
아니면 우리에게서 좋은 점을 찾으시는 여호와를 본받으려고 할 것입니까?
좋은 점을 찾는 습관을 기르고, 그 점에 대해 칭찬해 주십시오.
우리에게 불평하는 경향이 있었다면 그것이 칭찬하는 태도로 바뀔 것입니다.
칭찬하는 사람은 다른 사람의 좋은 점에 초점을 맞추고,
주위에 있는 사람들의 아름다움을 보기 때문입니다.
여러분이 불평하기 보다는 칭찬하는 사람이 된다면
곧 졸업하게 되실 151기 길르앗 학생 여러분,
칭찬과 격려가 여러분의 몸에 배어서 자연스럽게 흘러나오도록

en.text: They were speechless when they heard
she would leave home and join full-time service.
Instead of pursuing their common goals, dreams, and hopes,
she would do whatever she was told to do.
What a sacrifice!
They were so proud of her.
And they started thinking about what to do in order to support her.
Whom are we talking about?
Let us open to Judges 11,
and let’s find out who they were
and what they did.
Dear soon-to-be graduates, what they did
is something that will help you
to succeed in your assignment.
Let’s read, please, Judges 11:40:
“From year to year,
“the young women of Israel
“would go to give commendation
“to the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite
four days in the year.”
The young women of Israel
went to the sanctuary in Shiloh in order to give
commendation and praise to the daughter of Jephthah.
Commendation strengthened this full-time servant of Jehovah.
Is this not what you want to do too?
So that’s why we have the question for you,
How often will you “go to Shiloh”?
Will you strengthen others and stabilize the organization
by regularly commending and praising others?
Let us, therefore, ask the following questions:
What type of commendation is effective in strengthening others?
How can you imitate the young women of Israel?
And why do you want to give commendation regularly?
Let’s start with the first question,
What type of commendation is effective in strengthening others?
And let us, please, look at the example that Jesus set
as we turn to Mark chapter 5.
Here he commends
the frightened, sick woman who touched his outer garment.
As we read Mark 5:34,
please watch out for five elements
of effective commendation
—Mark 5:34:
“He said to her:
“‘Daughter, your faith has made you well.
Go in peace, and be healed from your grievous sickness.’”
Did you note what made this commendation effective?
First, effective commendation is specific.
Jesus commended the woman for what she did.
Her faith moved her to act.
Effective commendation is sincere.
The woman’s faith was real
and outstanding.
Did you notice that Jesus did not use the opportunity
to counsel her for violating the Law?
This might have made his commendation sound insincere.
Third, effective commendation is personal.
Jesus used the expression “daughter.”
That expression emphasized his tender concern for her.
Fourth, effective commendation is more than words.
Jesus acknowledged the needs of the woman
and followed up with deeds.
He healed her.
And fifth,
effective commendation is unselfish.
Jesus did not commend the woman in order to make himself look good,
but he was concerned about her
and wanted to make her feel good.
Now, can you do the same?
Let’s go back to Judges 11,
and let’s look again at verse 40.
So this is Judges 11:40, and let’s answer the second question,
How can you imitate the young women of Israel?
So the verse started here in verse 40 by saying
“from year to year,”
so this means regularly,
repeatedly.
The young women would praise the same person
again and again.
In your assignment as you work with others in Bethel, in the ministry,
or watch them in your congregation,
can you repeatedly praise them?
For instance, could you praise them for their zeal,
their fine efforts,
or for their acts of love?
Could you send an upbuilding text message saying
“Great job,” “Well done,” “Thumbs up,” “Loved it,”
maybe along with a brief comment?
These messages do not require a lot of effort and time,
but they can go a long way.
One time is not enough.
Do it again and again.
Don’t worry that the person could get a big head.
In the Bible,
Jehovah praised and commended
the persons whom he loved repeatedly.
Commending others again and again is a good thing.
Now, the verse continues here, saying:
“The young women of Israel would go to give commendation
“to the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite
four days in the year.”
Being away from their family obligations
must have been a sacrifice.
Somebody else must have taken over their usual work.
They had to travel to Shiloh
and they may also have brought a gift.
Now, could this serve as a reminder
that giving commendation might sometimes require
a little bit more time and effort and can come at a personal cost?
Yes.
Calling somebody or visiting him
requires time and effort.
Spending time with your brother and sister honors them.
Being out with them in the ministry, working together on a project,
or asking them for advice
really makes them feel good and can be a powerful commendation.
It’s worth all it costs.
Timing is important too.
Proverbs 15:23 states:
“A word spoken
at the right time—how good it is!”
So, what is “the right time” for commendation?
The verses leading up to our theme scripture here
mentioned that Jephthah’s daughter
right away got much needed support.
So generally speaking, commendation is of greatest value
when it’s given as soon as the opportunity comes up,
even if it’s initially just a brief comment.
The sooner somebody receives positive feedback,
the quicker feelings of insecurity or doubts will vanish
and the sooner the other person will be happy and feel good.
Please do not wait too long,
but act right away.
Now, this leads us to our third and final question,
Why do you want to give commendation regularly?
As you go to your assignments,
you will be surrounded by many “daughters of Jephthah”
—faithful, full-time servants of Jehovah
who made sacrifices to serve.
This auditorium is full of them, and you are among them.
You will meet
brothers and sisters in the congregation,
and some of them are insecure—worried.
Sometimes they doubt that they are worth anything.
They are giving their very best to stay faithful despite challenges
—fighting with their own imperfection,
dealing with the results of their own mistakes,
and are sometimes discouraged
because of setbacks.
They need commendation.
We all need commendation
because commendation enhances a person’s self-esteem,
it builds confidence and motivates to action,
it reinforces our desire
to do good things,
and it encourages us to keep on doing our very best.
Please “go to Shiloh” as often as possible.
Now, there’s another important aspect.
The reality is
that when you work closely with brothers and sisters,
you see their flaws and mistakes.
So, what are you going to do?
Will you ignore that person?
Or will you try to imitate Jehovah,
who is searching for the good in us?
Make it a habit to search for the good,
and then give voice to the positive.
Now, what happens to us
if we are doing it that way?
It can change us.
It can change us from being a complainer
to being a commender.
A commender focuses on the good in others.
He sees others
with Jehovah’s eyes.
A commender is very happy because he sees
all the beauty around him.
So if you gain a reputation
for commending rather than complaining,
you will succeed in your assignment
because others will love to work with you.
Dear soon-to-be graduates of the 151st class of Gilead,
please make commending and praising others
part of your personality —something that comes naturally.
So how often will you “go to Shiloh”?
Please “go to Shiloh” as often as possible.

cn.text: 听说她要离开家，参与全时服务
她们都很惊讶
她不再追求以前的目标、梦想和希望
而是把自己完全献了出来
这是多大的牺牲啊！
她们都为她感到骄傲
也开始想自己可以做些什么来支持她
我们说的是谁呢？
请打开士师记11章
我们看一下她们是谁以及她们做了什么
亲爱的基列毕业生
了解她们做了什么
能帮助你在新的岗位做得更好
现在请打开士师记11:40
经文这样说
“以色列的女子年年都去称赞
基列人耶弗他的女儿，每年四天”
这些以色列的女子
每年都去位于示罗的圣幕
去鼓励和称赞耶弗他的女儿
这让耶弗他的女儿得到很大的力量
你们也很想这样做，对吗？
另外，我们还想问你们另一个问题
你们多久去示罗一次呢？
你们会常常称赞和鼓励别人
在分部和会众发挥稳定的作用吗？
在这个演讲里，我们会讨论以下几个问题
什么样的称赞能让人受到鼓励？
你们可以怎样学习以色列女子的榜样
以及为什么需要常常称赞别人？
我们先看第一个问题
什么样的称赞能让人受到鼓励？
我们会先看一下耶稣基督树立的榜样
马可福音5章记载
耶稣称赞一个生病的女子
她摸了耶稣的外衣，所以惧怕颤抖
读马可福音5:34的时候，请你留意
耶稣称赞女子的话
有哪五个要点值得我们学习
马可福音5:34
“耶稣对她说
女儿，你的信心使你痊愈了
回去吧，愿你平安
你的恶疾已经治好了”
你留意到耶稣的称赞包含哪五个要点吗？
第一，耶稣的称赞非常具体
耶稣因为这个女子所做的而称赞她
她的信心让她采取行动
第二，耶稣的称赞是发自内心的
这个女子真的有很大的信心
你留意到吗？
耶稣并没有趁机批评这个女子违反摩西法典
耶稣如果这样做
就不是真的称赞这个女子了
第三，耶稣真的关心这个女子
他称呼她“女儿”
从这个称呼看出耶稣真的满怀温情
第四，耶稣不只是称赞她，还采取了行动
他看出这个女子的需要，就施行奇迹
治好了她
第五，耶稣的称赞不是出于自私的目的
耶稣称赞这个女子，不是为了抬高自己
而是因为他真的关心她，希望她感到安舒
你们也可以这样做吗？
我们再看一下士师记11:40
我们要讨论的第二个问题是
你们可以怎样学习以色列女子的榜样？
第40节的经文说
这些以色列女子
“年年都去称赞”耶弗他的女儿
这意味着她们会常常地
定期地去称赞同一个人
不论是在伯特利还是在会众里
或者跟别人一起传道时
你可以常常称赞周围的弟兄姐妹吗？
你可以称赞他们很热心、努力做对的事
以及向别人表现爱心
你可以给他们发一个简短的信息
说他们“做得好”、“太棒了”、“赞喔”
并加上几句简短的话吗？
这样的信息不需要你花费很多时间和精力
但可以发挥很大的作用
只称赞一次是不够的，要常常称赞他们
不要担心这会让别人变得骄傲起来
圣经记载
耶和华常常称赞和鼓励那些他所喜爱的人
要经常称赞别人，这样做很重要
我们再看一下士师记的经文
“以色列的女子年年都去称赞
基列人耶弗他的女儿，每年四天”
她们要离开家，不能照顾家人
这是个很大的牺牲
她们的工作也需要有别人替她们做
她们到示罗也需要长途跋涉
很可能她们也需要准备礼物
这也让我们知道
有时候称赞别人的确需要
花一点时间和精力
甚至需要作出一点牺牲
是的，给别人打电话
去探望他们都需要花时间和精力
但花时间陪伴别人本身就相当于一个礼物
和弟兄姐妹一起传道、跟他们并肩服务
并主动问他们的意见和建议
都会让弟兄姐妹感到安舒
并受到很大的鼓励
这样做很值得
什么时候称赞也很重要
箴言15:23的经文说
“说话合时，多么美好！”
什么时候称赞最恰当呢？
士师记11章前面的经文告诉我们
耶弗他的女儿在最需要帮助的时候
马上就得到了所需的支持
所以通常来讲，只要有机会
就要马上称赞别人
哪怕只是简短地说几句称赞的话也可以
因为如果他们很快得到积极的反馈
就不会一直感到担心和忧虑
也很容易感到安舒和快乐
所以，不要拖太久，要马上称赞别人
现在，我们来到第三个，也是最后一个问题
为什么我们要常常称赞别人？
你们到了新的工作岗位后
周围会有很多“耶弗他的女儿”
就是作出牺牲、忠心的
全时为耶和华服务的人
今天在场的也都是这样的人
你们自己也是这样的人
你们在会众里会认识很多弟兄姐妹
他们有些人觉得忧虑、不安
有时候他们觉得自己没有任何价值
他们尽自己最大的努力保持忠贞
但他们有很多难题
包括因自己的弱点和犯过的错而感到灰心
因为发生在他们身上的事而觉得失望
他们需要称赞和鼓励
我们都需要称赞和鼓励
因为称赞和鼓励会让人有自尊
会让人有自信，也会激励人采取行动
让人得到力量去做那些对的事
还能激励一个人坚持下去
所以，请你们常常“去示罗”
还有一点也很重要
当你们和弟兄姐妹并肩服务时
你们会留意到他们的缺点和毛病
你会怎么做呢？
不理会那个人吗？
还是你会效法耶和华，积极地看待别人呢？
要养成习惯，多留意优点
然后称赞别人做得好的地方
如果我们这样做
会带来什么美好的结果呢？
我们会改变
我们将不再总是抱怨，而是会常常称赞
称赞别人的人会留意别人的优点
他会用耶和华的观点
去看待身边的弟兄姐妹
他会非常的快乐
因为他看到的都是积极的、美好的东西
同时，他也会因此得到一个很好的名声
你们会在新的工作岗位做得很好
因为别人会喜欢跟你们一起服务
所以，第151届基列毕业生
亲爱的弟兄姐妹
请让称赞和鼓励别人成为你品格的一部分
要养成习惯去称赞别人
你多久“去示罗”一次呢？
请你们常常“去示罗”

titles.ko: 가유스 글로켄틴: 여러분은 얼마나 자주 “실로”로 갑니까?

title: 루서 조지스: 여호와께서는 우리를 인정해 주십니다

ko.text: 여러분이 깊이 존경하는 사람이 잘했다고 한다면
여러분의 노력이 가치를 인정받고 있다는 확신이 들지 않겠습니까?
그런데 151기 학급의 우리 형제 자매들이 임지로 가서
형제들을 돕고 격려하기 위해 최선을 다했는데,
잘했다는 말을 해 주지 않는다고 생각해 보십시오.
그것은 여러분의 노력이 가치가 없다는 뜻입니까?
예수께서 이 문제에 관해 무엇이라고 하셨는지,
몇 가지 성경의 예에서 무엇을 배울 수 있는지,
이것이 우리 각자에게 의미하는 바를 알아보겠습니다.
인정을 받기를 바라는 것이 인간의 정상적인 욕구이지만,
예수께서는 마태복음 6장에서 균형 잡힌 견해를 갖도록 도와주십니다.
“자비의 선물을 베풀 때에는 오른손이 하는 것을 왼손이 모르게 하여.”
이 “자비의 선물”은 가난한 사람들을 위한 기부였습니다.
이 말씀을 통해 예수께서는 자신의 제자들에게
당시의 진실하지 않은 종교 지도자들을 본받지 말라고 권고하신 것입니다.
그들은 사람들의 인정을 받기 위해 자신의 자선 행위를 널리 알렸죠.
3절에 있는 예수의 말씀을 따르려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?
즉 보이지 않게 여러분이 행한 친절과 신권 임명들을 생각해 보십시오.
예를 들어 여러분은 아픈 형제나 자매에게 여러 번 전화하거나
그들을 방문해서 사랑과 관심을 나타내고 함께 기도했을 것입니다.
또는 회중에 있는 그리스도인 청소년을 영적으로 돕기 위해
또는 고통을 겪는 형제나 자매를 격려하고 실제적인 지원을 베풀기 위해
여러분은 이 모든 일을 “보이지 않게” 하셨죠.
하지만 예수께선 여러분이 깊이 존경하는 분이
‘당신의 아버지께서 보이지 않는 곳에서 보고 계시다’고 하셨죠.
여호와께서는 인간이 볼 수 없는 하늘에 계시기 때문에
우리가 보이지 않게 하는 행동도 그분은 보이지 않는 곳에서 보고 계십니다.
여러분의 선한 행동을 유의해서 보시고 승인해 주십니다.
성경에는 충실한 남녀노소의 본이 많이 나옵니다.
여호와께서는 그들의 선행과 마음을 다한 정성을 보시고
한 가지 예는 악한 왕 아합의 집안 관리인이었던 오바댜입니다.
그는 슬기롭고 조심스럽게 여호와의 예언자 100명을 숨겨 주어
악한 이세벨에게 죽임을 당하지 않게 해 주었습니다.
다른 사람 모르게 빵과 물을 가져다주었습니다.
이 충실하고 관대하고 동정심 많은 사람을
여호와께서 보이지 않는 곳에서 보시고 승인하셨다는 것을
그의 용기 있는 행동이 성경에 기록되어
대대로 읽어 볼 수 있게 하셨다는 것을 보면 알 수 있죠.
하느님을 믿는 가족과 함께 살다가 시리아 사람들의 포로로 잡혀 갔죠.
이 그림에서 볼 수 있는 것처럼
이스라엘 소녀는 거짓 숭배자들에게 둘러싸여 있었지만
용기 있게 나아만의 아내에게 여호와의 예언자 엘리사에 관해 말했습니다.
그로 인해 나아만의 나병은 기적으로 치료되었고
그리고 그 일로 분명 여호와께 찬양이 돌아갔을 것입니다.
우리는 이 소녀의 이름을 모르지만 여호와께서는 아시죠.
그분은 보이지 않는 곳에서 이 소녀를 호의적으로 보고 계셨습니다.
이 두 예와 성경의 다른 많은 예들은
여호와께서 여러분의 선한 행실을 보고 계시다는 걸 확실히 알려 줍니다.
단지 보이지 않는 곳에서 우리를 보고 계시기만 한 것이 아닙니다.
“그러면 보이지 않는 곳에서 보고 계시는 당신의 아버지께서
많은 경우 여호와께서는 예상치 못한 방법으로
훨씬 더 가치 있고 의미 있는 방법으로 갚아 주십니다.
여러 가지 방법으로 그렇게 하시지만 그중 세 가지만 살펴보겠습니다.
“자비로운 사람들은 행복합니다. 그들이 자비를 받을 것이기 때문입니다.”
그분과 따뜻한 개인적인 관계를 누리게 해 주십니다.
그분이 갚아 주시는 두 번째 방법이 마가 10:29, 30에 나옵니다.
거기서 예수께서는 우리가 여호와를 섬기기 위해 무엇을 희생하든
계속 늘어나는 사랑 많은 영적 가족이라는 축복을 주십니다.
신세계에서의 영원한 생명이라는 소중한 희망을 주심으로
그리고 선한 일을 했지만 이 제도가 끝나기 전에 사망하는
그들은 그들의 선행에 대한 여호와의 인정과 축복을
다른 사람은 전혀 모를 수 있는 다양한 어려움들을
여러분의 임지에서 자비의 선물을 계속 베풀 수 있을 뿐만 아니라
여호와에 대한 마음을 다한 정성을 나타내게 될 것입니다.
하지만 여러분의 선행과 친절과 희생과 인내에 대해
다른 사람들의 인정과 “잘했다”는 칭찬을 받지 못하더라도
여러분을 인정해 주시고 승인해 주실 것임을 계속 확신하십시오.

en.text: How do you feel when you have exerted yourself in some way
and someone you deeply respect says to you,
“Well done”?
Don’t you feel assured that your efforts
were recognized and appreciated?
However, when you dear brothers and sisters
in the 151st class of Gilead
arrive at your assignments and you exert yourself
to accomplish the work you’ve been given
and give of yourself to encourage and help others,
suppose you don’t always receive
an audible “well done” from others.
How will you feel?
Does that mean that your efforts were not appreciated and recognized?
To answer those questions, we are going to consider:
first, what Jesus had to say on the subject;
second, what we can learn from some Bible examples;
and third, what this means for you personally.
Although the desire to receive recognition from humans is normal,
Jesus helps us to have a balanced view in Matthew chapter 6.
Please turn to Matthew chapter 6, and note verse 3
—Matthew 6:3:
“But you, when making gifts of mercy,
do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.”
Now, what did Jesus mean?
Well, these “gifts of mercy” were really donations for needy ones.
But with these words, Jesus was exhorting his disciples
not to imitate
the insincere religious leaders of his day
who publicized their gifts of mercy
just to be recognized by humans.
Now, what would be the result of heeding Jesus words here in verse 3?
Well, Jesus explains in verse 4.
He says: “So that your gifts of mercy may be in secret.”
Now, for a moment, think of the gifts of mercy
—the kindnesses and the theocratic assignments
that you have performed in secret.
For example, likely you’ve many times telephoned or visited
an ailing brother or sister just to reassure them
of your love and your concern,
and you’ve even prayed with them,
or perhaps you spent considerable time
being a spiritual mentor to a Christian youth,
or you may have given generously of yourself
to encourage and provide practical assistance
to a distressed brother or sister
—all of this you did “in secret.”
However, Jesus said that someone that you deeply respect did take note.
Look there at Matthew 6:4.
He stated in the B  part:
“Your Father who looks on in secret.”
The point is that Jehovah, who resides in the heavens,
is invisible to mankind,
so he remains in secret as far as humans are concerned.
But your good deeds
are recognized with approval by Jehovah.
Now, how can we be sure of that?
Well, there are many Bible examples
of faithful men and women, young and old,
whose good deeds and heartfelt devotion
were recognized with approval by Jehovah.
One example is Obadiah, the household steward
of wicked King Ahab.
First Kings chapter 18 explains
that he discreetly, secretly, and cautiously hid
100 of Jehovah’s prophets
so they would not be killed by wicked Jezebel.
Now, as illustrated here, Obadiah supplied them with bread and water
in groups of 50 in caves
without being observed by others.
How do we know that Jehovah in secret recognized with approval
this faithful, generous, compassionate man?
Well, we know because his courageous acts are recorded in the Bible
for generations of people to read about.
Another example is the young, nameless Israelite girl
mentioned in 2 Kings chapter 5.
She was taken away from her God-fearing family by the Syrians.
Now, as can be seen in this picture,
although surrounded by false worshippers,
she courageously told Naaman’s wife
about Jehovah’s prophet Elisha.
That led to Naaman’s miraculous healing of leprosy,
it led to Naaman’s becoming a worshipper of Jehovah,
and it certainly contributed to Jehovah’s praise.
We don’t know the name of that little girl —do we?—
but Jehovah does, who in secret
looked favorably on that young girl.
So these two examples and many others in the Scriptures assure you
that your good deeds are noted by Jehovah.
Please note, though, that Jehovah does more
than just look on in secret.
Look again, please, at Matthew 6:4.
The B  part read in its entirety says:
“Then your Father who looks on in secret
will repay you.”
Often, Jehovah repays us in unexpected ways
—in ways that are better and more meaningful
than humans could ever give us
in the way of recognition.
But how does Jehovah repay us?
While there are many ways,
we’re going to focus just on three significant ones.
One way is mentioned at Matthew 5:7
—Matthew 5:7.
Jesus said: “Happy are the merciful, since they will be shown mercy.”
So by our being kind and merciful,
Jehovah mercifully forgives us and allows us to enjoy
a warm, personal relationship with him.
A second way he repays us is mentioned
at Mark 10:29, 30.
There Jesus promised that we would receive “100 times more”
than anything we sacrifice to serve Jehovah.
And one resulting, tangible reward that Jehovah provides
is our ever-expanding, loving spiritual family.
A third way he repays us is by means of his promise
of the priceless reward of everlasting life in God’s new world.
And regarding righteous ones
who perform good deeds but fall asleep in death
before the end of this system,
Jesus at Luke 14:14 gave the assurance
that they will be repaid in the resurrection.
And then they will see the full effect
of Jehovah’s recognition and blessing
on their good deeds.
In addition to your gifts of mercy
in your new assignments,
your heartfelt devotion will be reflected
as you, with Jehovah’s help,
face and successfully endure various challenges
—many of which others will know nothing about.
But even though you may not receive recognition
or a complimentary “well done” from others
for your good deeds, your kindnesses,
your sacrifices, and your endurance,
please remain confident
that you will be recognized with approval
by a loving Father, Jehovah.
And as Jesus promised:
“[Jehovah] who looks on in secret
will repay you.”

cn.text: 请想一想你会有什么感受
你付出努力
然后有一个你非常尊敬的人对你说
“做得好”
你是不是会觉得自己的努力
得到了别人的赏识和认可呢？
但是第151届基列学员，亲爱的弟兄姐妹
如果你们到达新的岗位
并且付出努力完成自己的工作
也尽己所能帮助和鼓励身边的弟兄姐妹
但是
并不是每次都有人对你说
“做得好”
你又会有什么感受呢？
你会不会觉得自己的付出
没有人赏识和认可呢？
要回答这些问题，我们会考虑
第一，关于这件事，耶稣是怎么说的
第二，我们可以从圣经中的榜样学到什么
还有第三，这对你有什么影响
虽然我们所有人都很希望得到别人的认可
但耶稣在马太福音第6章提醒我们
要有合理的看法
请翻到马太福音第6章，请看第3节
经文是这样说的
“你接济穷人时
不要让左手知道右手所做的”
这是什么意思呢？
“接济穷人”意思是
帮助那些生活困难的人
耶稣这样说
是鼓励他的门徒不要像当时
那些虚伪的宗教领袖一样
那些人喜欢在大庭广众之下行善
因为他们只想得到人的称赞
我们听从耶稣的吩咐就会怎么做呢？
紧接着在第4节，耶稣说
“要暗中资助他们”
请想一想“暗中资助”
你可能表现爱心并努力完成你的工作
而这些别人并不知道
比如说，你看望生病的弟兄姐妹
给他们打电话
让他们知道你关心他们、爱他们
你也和他们一起祷告
再比如
你花很多时间帮助和关心会众里的年轻人
或者你慷慨地献出自己的时间和精力
为那些伤心难过的弟兄姐妹提供实际的帮助
这些你好像都是在“暗中”做的
但耶稣说
你的好行为
还是会被你深深尊敬的一位留意到
请再看一下马太福音6:4
下半节的经文这样说
“你父亲暗中观察”
耶稣说的就是耶和华
他住在天上，对人类来说他是看不见的
所以说耶和华仿佛是在暗中观察
他看到并认可你的好行为
为什么我们可以确信这一点呢？
圣经记载了很多忠心的人
他们有男有女，有老有少
他们的忠贞和好行为
都得到了耶和华的认可和嘉许
其中一个例子是俄巴底亚
他是邪恶的亚哈王的管家
列王纪上18章记载俄巴底亚
偷偷地把耶和华的100个先知藏了起来
因此这些先知
才没有被邪恶的耶洗别王后杀害
现在请看这幅插图
俄巴底亚把这些先知50人一组藏在洞里
并供应饼和水给他们
俄巴底亚真的又忠贞、又慷慨
又富于同情心
但我们怎么知道他得到了耶和华的认可呢？
耶和华让人把他的英勇的行为记载在圣经里
让以后的人都可以读到
列王纪下第5章提到的一个
以色列的小女孩
她的父母敬畏上帝
但她被叙利亚人掳走了
请看这幅插图
虽然身边都是崇拜假神的人
但是小女孩还是勇敢地告诉乃缦的妻子
耶和华的先知以利沙的事
结果乃缦的麻风病被神奇地治好了
而且乃缦也开始崇拜耶和华
这无疑为耶和华带来了荣耀
我们不知道这个小女孩叫什么名字
但耶和华知道
耶和华仿佛在暗中观察这个小女孩
并且非常认可她
这两个例子以及圣经中其他的许多例子
都能让你确信
你的好行为耶和华一定会留意到
请再留意
耶和华并不只是暗中观察
他还会怎么做呢？
我们再看一下
马太福音6:4
下半节的经文这样说
“你父亲暗中观察，就会回报你”
耶和华常常以意想不到的方式回报我们
得到耶和华的嘉许和认可
比得到人的嘉许和认可
更有价值、更有意义
耶和华怎么回报我们呢？
有很多方法
但这次我们会主要讨论其中的三个
第一个记载在马太福音5:7
耶稣说
“富于怜悯的人有福了
因为他们会得到怜悯的对待”
如果我们待人仁慈、富于怜悯
耶和华也会仁慈地宽恕我们的罪
并让我们有机会跟他建立亲密的友谊
耶和华回报我们的第二个方法
记录在马可福音10:29,30
耶稣保证说
耶和华会“一百倍”地回报我们
我们为了崇拜他，作出任何牺牲都是值得的
举例来说，现在
耶和华就让我们拥有一个全球的大家庭
和越来越多的弟兄姐妹
他回报我们的第三个方法
就是让我们有机会
在新世界里享受永远的生命
有些正义的人常常行善
但他们在这个制度结束之前就去世了
在路加福音14:14，耶稣保证说
他们会复活过来，得到回报
到了那个时候
他们就会看出
自己的好行为得到耶和华的认可
会带来多大的福分
在新的工作岗位
你们会继续帮助身边的弟兄姐妹
也会继续全心全意地崇拜耶和华
靠着耶和华的帮助
你们能够成功地面对各种各样的考验
而你们的付出可能别人并不知道
但就算你们没有得到别人的认可
也没有人称赞你们说“做得好”
请记得你的好行为、你待人仁慈
你作出的牺牲、你保持忍耐
这些都会得到
仁慈的天父耶和华的认可和嘉许
就像耶稣保证的那样
你父亲耶和华暗中观察
就会回报你

titles.ko: 루서 조지스: 여호와께서는 우리를 인정해 주십니다
titles.en: Luther Georges: Does Jehovah Recognize You?
titles.cn: 卢瑟·乔治斯：耶和华认可你吗？

title: 리처드 칠턴: ‘누가 나를 위해 일어나겠습니까?’

ko.text: 먼저 패터슨 베델에 있는 한 형제의 경험을 이야기해 드리겠습니다.
그 형제는 정말 사랑하는 어머니를 끔찍한 사고로 잃었습니다.
그는 자신의 고통스러운 심정을 털어놓을 사람이 절실히 필요했습니다.
그 형제는 마음이 몹시 혼란스러워서 도움이 필요했죠.
그래서 월킬 베델에 있는 친한 친구에게 전화했습니다.
그 친구는 그때 대화를 나눌 수 있는 상황이 아니라고 했습니다.
여러분도 비슷한 경험을 해 본 적이 있으신가요?
마치 깊은 물에 빠져서 누군가의 도움이 필요한 상황 말입니다.
저와 함께 시편 94편을 펴서 그가 한 질문을 보겠습니다.
시편 94:16에서 그가 한 질문의 일부분만 보겠습니다.
“여호와께서 나를 도와주지 않으셨다면, 나는 이미 사라지고 없을 것입니다. …
우리가 그처럼 여호와께 마음에서 우러나온 기도를 드릴 때,
그리고 우리는 어떻게 그분을 본받아 다른 사람들을 위해 일어날 수 있습니까?
과거로 돌아가 한 가지 예를 살펴보시죠.
보아스라는 부유한 토지 소유자가 살고 있었습니다.
그의 밭에서 떨어진 이삭을 주울 수 있게 했습니다.
하루는 밭에서 일하는 한 여자가 눈에 띄었는데,
곧 그는 그 여자가 외국인인 룻이라는 걸 알게 됩니다.
그때까지만 해도 룻에 대해 얘기만 들었었죠.
이삭을 주우려고 다른 밭으로 가지 마시오.
다른 곳으로 가지 말고, 내 밭에서 일하는 젊은 여자들 곁에 있으시오.
그들이 수확하는 밭에서 눈을 떼지 말고, 그들과 함께 다니시오.
내가 젊은이들에게 그대를 건드리지 말라고 명령해 두었소.
목이 마르거든, 물 항아리가 있는 데로 가서
젊은이들이 길어다 놓은 물을 마시도록 하시오.’”
보아스가 어려움에 처한 사람을 도와주고 보호해 주는 걸 볼 수 있습니다.
외국인인 자신을 도와주는 이유가 무엇인지 묻습니다.
이때 보아스가 어떤 두 번째 방법으로 룻을 위해 일어났는지
‘그대가 남편이 죽은 후에 시어머니에게 한 모든 일과
또 그대의 아버지와 어머니 그리고 친족의 땅을 떠나
전에는 알지 못하던 백성에게 온 일에 대해 내가 다 들었소.
여호와께서 그대가 행한 일에 대해 상 주시기를 바라오.
그대가 그분의 날개 아래로 도피처를 구하려고 왔으니,
이스라엘의 하느님 여호와께서 그대에게 완전한 삯을 주시기를 바라오.’
‘내 주여, 제가 당신의 눈에 호의를 얻게 해 주십시오.
저는 당신의 종들 가운데 하나만도 못한데,
당신의 종에게 안심시키는 말을 해 주셨습니다.’”
보아스가 룻에게 안심시키는 말을 해 주었다는 표현이
각주에서는 그가 룻의 “마음에 말해 주었다”고 되어 있죠.
그의 말은 단지 일반적인 칭찬의 말이 아니었습니다.
룻의 개인적인 상황에 맞는 구체적인 칭찬이었죠.
그가 한 모든 희생을 잊지 않으실 것이라고 안심시켜 주었습니다.
이처럼 위로와 격려가 되는 보아스의 말을 들은 룻은
아무것도 염려할 필요가 없다는 걸 확신하게 됩니다.
하지만 보아스는 안심시키는 말만 해 준 게 아니죠.
그가 룻을 위해 일어난 세 번째 방법을
죽은 친척인 엘리멜렉의 상속 재산이 그 집안에 계속 남아 있을 수 있게 했습니다.
기룐과 말론에게 속한 모든 것을 나오미에게서 사겠습니다.
그리고 말론의 아내인 모압 여자 룻도 내가 아내로 맞아들이겠습니다.
죽은 사람의 이름으로 그의 상속지를 보존하여,
죽은 사람의 이름이 그 형제들 사이에서
그리고 그의 고향 성문에서 끊어지지 않게 하려는 것입니다.
첫째, 보아스는 자신이 돌보는 사람들을 보호했습니다.
둘째, 그들에게 안심시켜 주는 말을 했습니다.
도움이 필요한 걸 보고 일어난 것입니다.
보호해 주고, 안심시켜 주고, 행동을 취했죠.
우리도 그렇게 해 주어야 하지 않을까요?
앞서 언급했던 형제 얘기로 돌아가 보겠습니다.
패터슨 베델에 있는 이 슬픔에 잠긴 형제는
다음날 아침 일을 하러 나오자마자 로비에서 걸려 온 전화를 받았습니다.
월킬에서 일하는 바로 그 친구에게서 온 전화였죠.
그 친구는 그날 아침 일찍 일어나서 8시까지 도착하기 위해
월킬 베델에서 패터슨 베델까지 1시간 넘게 운전해 온 것입니다.
그는 슬퍼하는 형제와 대화를 나눌 수 있는 회의실을 예약해 놓고
형제를 도울 방법을 알고 싶었던 거죠.
저는 그때 그 일을 한 번도 잊은 적이 없습니다.
그 친구가 나를 위해 일어나 준 그날의 일을 말이죠.
그 형제가 행동을 취해 준 덕분에
그리고 이 프로그램을 보고 계신 모든 분에게 드리는 질문입니다.
그와 같은 상황에서 여러분 한 분 한 분이

en.text: I’d like to start by telling you an experience
of a brother at Patterson Bethel.
He had recently lost a loved one
—a parent, in fact—
in a horrible accident.
And he desperately needed to talk with someone
about what he was going through and how he was feeling.
He was, in a word, unraveling, and he needed help.
So he called a close friend of his at Wallkill Bethel
but, unfortunately, the brother said that at that time
he was unable to talk.
Have you ever found yourself in a similar situation
—that is, feeling like you’re drowning
and in need of assistance?
The psalmist did.
Please read with me his words in the 94th Psalm
and note his question.
It’s Psalm 94:16.
The psalmist asked in part:
“Who will rise up for me?”
“Who will rise up for me?”
He goes on to answer his own question
in verses 17 and 19.
He says: “If Jehovah had not been my helper,
“I would soon have perished. . . .
“When anxieties overwhelmed me,
you [Jehovah, you] comforted and soothed me.”
Well, when you and I send up such heartfelt prayers to Jehovah,
how does he rise up for us?
And how can we imitate him
by rising up in behalf of others?
Let’s go back in time and consider an example.
During the days of Israel’s judges,
there lived a wealthy landowner named Boaz.
In obedience to Jehovah’s Law,
he made sure that in his fields
gleanings were left for the afflicted and poor.
One day,
he observes a woman working in his fields
that he does not recognize.
And soon he learns that she is the foreigner Ruth,
who up to this point, he has only heard about.
Well, what does Boaz do?
Notice how he rose up for her
at Ruth 2:8
—Ruth chapter 2,
starting with verse 8:
“Boaz said to Ruth: ‘Listen, my daughter.
“‘Do not go away to glean in another field,
“‘and do not go anywhere else;
“‘stay close by my young women.
“‘Keep your eyes on the field that they harvest,
“‘and go with them.
“‘I have commanded the young men not to touch you.
“‘When you are thirsty,
go to the water jars and drink from what the young men have drawn.’”
Clearly, Boaz protected Ruth.
He brought her under his loving care.
We see him looking out for, shielding,
defending the one in need.
And when Ruth, according to verse 10,
questions his motive for helping her, a foreigner,
notice a second way he rose up in her behalf
at Ruth 2:11:
“Boaz answered her:
“‘A full report was made to me
“‘of all you have done for your mother-in-law
“‘after the death of your husband
“‘and how you left your father and your mother
“‘and the land of your relatives
“‘to go to a people whom you had not known before.
“‘May Jehovah reward you for what you have done,
“‘and may there be a perfect wage for you
“‘from Jehovah the God of Israel,
“under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.’
“To this she said:
“‘Let me find favor in your eyes, my lord,
“‘because you have comforted me
“‘and spoken reassuringly
“‘to your servant,
although I’m not even one of your servants.’”
When Boaz spoke reassuringly to Ruth,
the footnote says that he ‘spoke to her heart.’
How so?
His words were not just general expressions of praise.
They were specific to Ruth
and to her personal circumstances.
He reassured Ruth that Jehovah loved her
for all the sacrifices she had made
and that she would not be forgotten.
Those comforting, encouraging words of Boaz
convinced Ruth
that everything was going to be OK.
But Boaz did more than offer reassuring words.
Notice the third way he rose up
at Ruth 4:9.
By taking swift action,
Boaz ensured that the inheritance
of his deceased relative Elimelech
would remain in their family
—chapter 4, verse 9:
“Boaz said to the elders and all the people:
“‘You are witnesses today
“‘that I am buying from Naomi
“‘all that belonged to Elimelech
“‘and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.
“‘I am also acquiring Ruth the Moabitess,
“‘the wife of Mahlon, as a wife [for what reason?]
“‘to restore the name of the dead man
“‘to his inheritance,
“‘so that the name of the dead man
“‘will not be cut off from among his brothers
“‘and from the city gate of his home.
You are witnesses today.’”
Jehovah used Boaz
to rise up for Ruth and Naomi
in three main ways.
One,
he protected those under his care.
Second,
he spoke reassuringly to them.
And third,
he took action.
Seeing the need, he rose up to meet it
—he protected,
he reassured,
he took action.
Well, how about you and me?
Should we not do the same
for those in need of assistance?
And what can result when we do?
Well, before you answer that,
let’s go back to our opening experience.
You see, the very next morning
upon arriving at his work assignment,
our distressed brother received a phone call
from the Patterson lobby.
It was the brother, the friend from Wallkill.
He had gotten up early that morning
and had driven over an hour from the Wallkill complex
to reach the Patterson complex by 8:00 a.m.
He had arranged for a private conference room,
and he was there waiting for that distressed friend
so that he could find out, “How can I help?”
That was 22 years ago.
But I can tell you now,
I have never forgotten
what that friend did for me
when he rose up for me on that day.
By means of the action that he took,
I felt reassured,
I felt protected, and I felt loved.
So the question
for you 24 students—
In fact, the question for all of us
in our hearing audience is this:
What will you do
to rise up for someone in need?
We have every confidence
that each and every one of you
will answer that call when it comes,
saying: “Here I am.
“I will rise up for you. How can I help?”

cn.text: 我想先给大家讲一个弟兄的经历
他在帕特森服务
他刚刚失去了一个亲人
就是他的母亲
在意外中丧生了
他真的很需要找个朋友来聊一聊
说说自己的感受
因为他非常难过
很需要帮助
于是他打电话给一个好朋友
这个朋友在华基尔服务
但朋友说他当时很忙
不方便讲话
你也曾经遇到过这样的情况吗？
你觉得自己像一个溺水的人
很需要帮助
诗篇执笔者遇到过
我们可以看一下诗篇第94篇
看看他提出的问题
他这样问
“谁会为我起来？”
“谁会为我起来？”
然后在第17节和19节
他这样回答自己的问题
“要不是耶和华帮助我，我早就没命了
每当我多忧多虑
你［耶和华］都安慰我
使我安心”
当我们向耶和华恳切地祷告时
他会怎样为我们起来呢？
我们又可以怎样学习他的榜样
为别人起来呢？
我们可以看一个古代的例子
在士师的时代
以色列有一个非常富有的人
名叫波阿斯
他服从耶和华的法律
在收割的时候
他会在田里留下麦穗
让贫穷的人可以捡
一天，他在自己的田里
看到了一个不认识的女子在捡麦穗
后来他知道这个女子是外族人路得
他以前只是听说过路得的事
那波阿斯怎么做呢？
请留意他怎样为路得起来
我们一起来读一下路得记
路得记第2章
我们会从第8节读起
“波阿斯对路得说
女儿啊，听我说
不要到别的田里去捡麦穗
也不要离开这里
就跟着我的女仆吧
你看见她们在哪块田里收割
就要跟着去
我已经吩咐手下的年轻人不可以欺负你
你渴了
可以到水缸那里喝他们打来的水”
你看，波阿斯保护路得
仁慈地照顾她
波阿斯主动地帮助
和保护那些有需要的人
在第10节
路得问波阿斯
为什么要帮助她这样一个外族人
请留意第二个
波阿斯帮助路得的方法
在路得记2:11
“波阿斯回答她说
你丈夫死后
你怎样对待婆婆
怎样离开了父母和家乡
跟陌生的民族一起生活
别人全都告诉我了
愿耶和华照你所做的奖赏你
你来投靠以色列的上帝耶和华
留在他的翅膀底下

请再看第13节，她就说

具体地称赞路得
